There are some food, drinks and souvenir shops within the area for you to rest or shop at. Once you enter the area you can also visit other places of interests, some at additional fee (eg HCM museum).Wear long pants and covered shoulders (no sleeveless) if you plan to visit HCM’s body. The other museums are not as strict on dress code.

reviews.author: Tassie Carly
reviews.title: Very interesting experience - go early
reviews.content: Got here nice and early as I was expecting a queue. Took me a while to find the entrance as it was right around the back behind the mausoleum. Very few tourists about - it was only 8am so I was able just to walk straight through the line to the front with no waiting. They were doing some sought of quick ceremony when I got up to mausoleum and about 20 military officers walked through ahead of me. That was very interesting to watch them silently salute the body as they stopped in front of it. Only did the mausoleum and one pillar pagoda before heading off elsewhere. As I left there were masses of school students lining up at the entrance waiting to come through so I was glad I was there early.

reviews.author: Rahul M
reviews.title: Fast Queues. Good value for money. Interesting
reviews.content: Very interesting experience. Good value for money. Wear long pants and tops with covered shoulders. Come at 0700hrs to secure a spot in the mausoleum viewing queue.

reviews.author: logo369
reviews.title: Historic point of view
reviews.content: I did not not only go to the mausoleum, but the grounds gave it a 5 due to historical value. There is a lot of beauty in the grounds.

reviews.author: Aditya
reviews.title: Hanoi Museum Experience
reviews.content: Amazing place to understand more about the History of Vietnam and what the people have gone through! Hien from Hanoi Free City Tour Guides was super amazing and took us through the museum with a lot of patience and details

reviews.author: AylwinKearney
reviews.title: Closed
reviews.content: The mausoleum is closed until August 15th. Very unclear information from our hotel and when we searched online.Still worth while visiting the grounds and premises where Ho Chi Min lived and worked.

reviews.author: Corentin
reviews.title: Closed for annual maintenance in summer 22
reviews.content: Everywhere I read that the mausoleum is open, but in fact closed to the public from June 13 to August 15 (2022) for annual maintenance, no clear information about that 😅 you can walk around, and continue with the presidential palace and Hô Chi Minh house (not free) and finish by the one Pilar pagoda.

reviews.author: Eddie T
reviews.title: Thank u to the English tour guide Huyen
reviews.content: Our family with young children visited the Ho Chin Minh museum on 19 June, Monday. We took up the free tour guide service provided by the museum and was assigned to Kelsey. She spoke fluent english and explained each of the exhibits clear enough for the children to understand. Kelsey was really passionate when bringing us around the museum, and was very warm and friendly towards us tourists. Our visit to the museum was very educational and informative because of this tour!

reviews.author: Nitin Tulsian
reviews.title: Must visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: There were atleast a thousand people in queue when we reached and it took around 30-40 minutes of dragging to reach to chamber where the body of their great leader is preserved. The time and the pain was worth at the end and I will recommended visitors to definitely include this place in their itinerary.One should start early when the mausoleum opens to get quicker access. Also visitors with sleeveless tops or short pants/skirts are not allowed entry. Men with knee length shorts are Ok. Will recommend sober full clothing to avoid disappointment.

reviews.author: Stuart B
reviews.title: We’ll worth the waiting.
reviews.content: Very interesting visit to see the preserved body of the revered leader of Vietnam.Strict control and run by the military. No loitering or talking photos inside the chamber.Cannot take photos inside. But outside of the building & gardens ok

reviews.author: David
reviews.title: A monolith of impressive scale.
reviews.content: If you want to go inside you will need to come early - check the hours on Google Maps.I looked at the outside only. The building and the grounds outside are quite impressive in scale, all watched over by White-uniformed guards.As you wilk see from all the picture, the Mausoleum is a very stark edifice. The wide open space and straight, clean edged structure contrast quite a lot with the rest of central Hanoi.

reviews.author: IndochinaTraveler
reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.content: Had a blast while visiting here!i like the freindlines of the people here,and the architecture here.Would visit again!

reviews.author: Katy Santos
reviews.title: Historical Mausoleum
reviews.content: I went here before the pandemic - Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is the resting place of President Ho Chi Minh. You can enter the mausoleum to view his embalmed body on a glass guarded with soldiers. You must be quite early to get in the queue. I didnt go inside and just took a photo outside

reviews.author: Andrew Perry
reviews.title: Interesting place worth a visit
reviews.content: Peaceful and lovely place to visit, which locates right in the center of Hanoi capital. Our walk there was so interesting, with a connection visit to Westlake and Tran Quoc pagoda

reviews.author: N21dx
reviews.title: Great Leader - Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: This is where the Great Leader, Ho Chi Minh is resting. You can see the body of Ho Chi Minh, resting in the glass case. Its a nice place to go and pay respects. Its very strict there, no loitering around, you can't take pics inside the mausoleum and talk too loudly. All this shows how much of love and respect is given for Ho Chi Minh. If you are there, please do show some respect for the Great Leader. There are soldiers in white uniforms on guard duty and marching around the Mausoleum. I did try to ask permission to take a photo with one of the soldier stationed there. He politely told us that he is on duty and he cant take pictures. We respected that and we moved on.

reviews.author: LuizDutraNeto
reviews.title: The solemn and revered Mausoleum of President Ho Chi Minh in Hanoi ...
reviews.content: I wouldn't say "Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum" is a tourist attraction, but it is certainly one of the most revered monuments by all Vietnamese. At Hanoi's "Ba Dinh Square",  President Ho Chi Minh's (*May 9, 1890 +September 2, 1969) embalmed body lies inside a glass case with dim lights. Outside the impressive marble building, inspired in "Lenin's Mausoleum" in Moscow (but with Vietnamese architectural elements), huge queues and honor guard. Before going, check its visiting hours, as it changes according to seasons. Dress properly, join the queue, keep the pace, be silent and respectful. No pictures, no stops and no entry fees. Enjoy!

reviews.author: essdon2017
reviews.title: I would not bother, TOO COMMUNIST CONTROLLED, l was surprised how strictly the Tourist Guides were so censored.
reviews.content: Do not bother, guards are too strict, outside if you walk too close to line in allowed path, because you want to get past a group walking too slow, you are told off by guards using sign language. Also if inside building walking upstairs to view Ho Chin Ming dummy body(he is cremated), when l stopped to wait for my wife again l was told off.

reviews.author: Frances L
reviews.title: Sobering
reviews.content: The Mausoleum in Ba Dinh Square is the resting place of Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam's most popular leader. The site is very heavily guarded and when entering the Mausoleum there is no opportunity to stop and linger as the visitors must continuously "flow" through. It is important that you dress with respect and cameras are forbidden. The Mausoleum is closed to the public  between September and December and also some days of the week.

reviews.author: Erik Karlsson
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: We had such a lesson of Vietnam's history on our visit to the Mausoleum. The campus looks so nice, peaceful and solemn. We had great time to get inside the Mausoleum, visit the stilt house and one pillar pagoda. Memorable!

reviews.author: omega132857
reviews.title: A must in Hanoi
reviews.content: If you are lucky enough to Visit Hanoi, then you must go and see Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Our guide Khan took us to see it. It is secure and you will have your bags searched. We were lucky as the changing of the gaurd was taking place as we arrived. In there starch whit uniforms, they looked great. One tip, do not cross the yellow line. It was not very busy because of the covic 19, so it was so good for us to see it all, with only a few other tourists about.

reviews.author: Gmglcfc
reviews.title: A must see
reviews.content: Didn’t want to go into the actual mausoleum and anyway it was either closed due to coronavirus or due to time/ day we visited . Cant’t quite understand why foreign tourists would want to actually view the body. Impressive building and grounds, rather ‘ Stalinist’ looking. The main guards changed whilst we were there, very smart all in white uniforms and precise marching etc. The soldiers/guards were all, or seemed to be, much taller than your average Vietnamese! A must see in Hanoi but not that memorable.

reviews.author: depressed frog
reviews.title: Heavy hearted and Remarkable Trip
reviews.content: I last came to this place a long time ago, and I had just visited it again, to see Ho Chi Minh and feel the cold atmosphere, a strange feeling of gratitude. It's horrifyingly quiet, you can hear yourself thinking. The guards are like silhouettes. The visit was lovely and I cant wait to find an opportunity to go again.

reviews.author: Cindy P
reviews.title: Recommended
reviews.content: Very interesting place to visit. Ensure you check that it is open the day you go as we went on a Friday and the you could only go in the grounds so we went back the next day. You need to dress respectful and behave respectfully. We had to wear a mask the day we went and not sure if this is standard practice but go prepared.

reviews.author: Craig E
reviews.title: Slightly morbid!
reviews.content: The mausoleum has a very grand appearance from the outside, with a large square for ceremonies at the front. The guards that patrol the area around the mausoleum are very regimented and quite hostile. Seeing Ho Chi Minh’s embalmed dead body was quite a strange feeling, as he looked just like a Madam Tussauds wax work. Worth a quick walk by the outside of the mausoleum, but that’s it in my opinion.

reviews.author: ireddi2018
reviews.title: Worth a visit.
reviews.content: Impressive building and grounds. The actual mausoleum is sombre and respectful as it should be. No photos and some dress rules (sorry cant remember these).No admission charge. Almost no queues as we visited during the COVID 19 outbreak (March 2020).The mausoleum was only open in the morning until 12:00 (I Think)

reviews.author: nadiak97
reviews.title: Must Visit! Highly strict environment.
reviews.content: -Must visit attraction in Hanoi-Free entry-Open for a limited time so arrive early to go through security checks etc-Very strict (Water was thrown away, camera was taken before entering, no sunnies allowed to be worn inside)-Have to queue (low peak we queued for 10 minutes) -One downside was you had to keep walking inside the Mausoleum so you only had a few minutes to view the body (very rushed)-Other attractions in walking distance

reviews.author: Justnitid
reviews.title: Respect and remembrance
reviews.content: If you are in Hanoi, make it a point to visit the mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh. It is important to respect the nation you are visiting. The mausoleum is a modern structure, cubic and gigantic. There is heavy security and long queues for viewing the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh. Maintain decorum and do not do anything which can be construed as disrespectful.The arrangements are quite efficient and the queue moves quickly. Open only between 8 - 11 am, except Monday. Once done, you can walk and explore the entire area. There is much to see - the presidential palace (you can only see from outside), the house where Ho Chi Minh lived and worked and the revered One-Pillar-Pagoda. Soak up some atmosphere in the large square in front of the mausoleum and watch the change if guards.

reviews.author: Gordon S
reviews.title: Worth a quick visit
reviews.content: Visited the Mausoleum and it was a site to see. It was on huge grounds and I am unsure if we allowed in as it was closed. Worth a quick visit as not much to see.

reviews.author: MattGlick
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: My friends and I toured Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum during the Corona Virus outbreak which meant that it was fairly empty. Even with it being so empty it wasn't that impressive. If you have some free time, it's worth a visit. But it's not something you need to see.

reviews.author: JPA-2009-SEA
reviews.title: A must do in Hanoi
reviews.content: What an amazing place. The atmosphere is sombre but you can sense the respect and love that the locals hold for this great man. Obviously you need to be dressed in a suitable manner, covering shoulders etc. Take your cameras with you cos although you cant use them in the first part of the tour, you can in the grounds and his house etc, which you get to see after passing through the mausoleum. We were lucky enough to have a very informative guide who gave us an insight into this mans life.

reviews.author: kingvikramaditya
reviews.title: Respect
reviews.content: A visit to Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum in Hanoi would make you aware of the respect Vietnamese people attach to this towering personality. From September for a couple of months every year, it gets closed as Ho Chi Minh's body is taken to Russia for getting embalmed again. Photographs are allowed but it'd be great if you pay a visit to the Mausoleum first. Entry here is free for all.

reviews.author: André K
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: This is really worth to visit. Very beautiful complex to visit. The guards look very impressive in their uniforms and the other buildings around the Mausoleum is also very impressive. The one pillar Pagoda is also worth the visit. We were there during the Coronavirus outbreak and therefore had the place to ourselves. Really glad we visited this attraction.

reviews.author: Jane T
reviews.title: Recommended
reviews.content: Lonely Planet's guide says it is a place of pilgrimage, and it is.  Because I was there during the coronavirus outbreak, the single-file line took only about 30 minutes to get in.  There are lots of immaculately-dressed, unsmiling guards to make sure people are dressed appropriately, wear no hats, and do not take photographs.  "Uncle Ho's" pale body is encased in glass.  The air is kept chilly.  The whole edifice is a monument to communism.  The man himself wanted a simple cremation.  There are other sites in the complex that are worth seeing, like the Stilt House, where Ho Chi Minh lived, and the One Pillar Pagoda.

reviews.author: TerryH
reviews.title: Glad we did it, but...
reviews.content: A must do to see guarded body of revered leader Ho Chi Minh. Been embalmed since 1972. Told to wear masks although not everyone wore them. No queues due to impact of corona virus. Glad we didn’t queue for this.

reviews.author: Meuok
reviews.title: D
reviews.content: A visit to Hanoi wouldn't be complete without a shuffle round Uncle Ho's body.The rather surly soldiers order you into a single file procession and you're in and out in a minute.Then to walk around the grounds đ50,000 where you're made to walk without stopping and view his house on stilts, cars ans so forth.It's  not a bad couple of hours.WATCH OUT FOR ENTRANCE TIMES. THEY VARY.

reviews.author: UV1951
reviews.title: very impressive
reviews.content: This place is very impressive place, and I think it must to visit.   Amazing place to go around and see how Ho Chi Minh live there. also the garden and building around.

reviews.author: flighttime
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: We did not go in just stopped for a visit. The area is beautiful,well maintained and as you will see very respected. They change the guard every  hour try to catch that. We were there during the virus outbreak so no one there.i am sure during peak season it is packed. No real need to go in,not sure of the cost but we were not interested.

reviews.author: Beth
reviews.title: Strange place
reviews.content: Very strict entry, currently must wear a mask for Coronavirus,but we did remove it once we were inside the compound as it was empty of people and therefore were not going to catch or pass anything on. The building itself was quite plain, we had expected lavish decorations and fold etc, but I guess as a place of mourning, plain is better? We were probably here no longer than 5 minutes.at least it was free!

reviews.author: Khushbu Mehta
reviews.title: Amazing experience
reviews.content: Located inside the Ba Dinh Square. Make sure u enter from the right entrance. We went to the wrong entry point, so walked around 15 minutes to reach the right one. The Mausoleum is open to visit only for certain hours during the day. Make sure to be informed of the time beforehand. U have to behave in an orderly manner,walking in a straight line to enter the Mausoleum. Once ur in the whole atmosphere inside gives u goosebumps. Soldiers standing in attention around the remains of Ho Chi Minh without moving a single muscle. In my opinion its a must visit place. No food allowed inside, u can leave it at the counter outside

reviews.author: Nicolas P
reviews.title: Like Robot
reviews.content: When you had been complex, don't move, don't shake, do not wear sunglass, do not wear hat even the sun is like fire, do not speak each other. The guards check and look to  see  to visitors like as a terrorist. I am going to think about never visit to there.

reviews.author: PamBeale
reviews.title: Worth doing but all a bit strange!
reviews.content: Just do what you are told basically! Very strict. The seeing Ho Chi Minh bit is over very quickly. You can't stop and look for long. No photos of course. Gardens and house etc quite pretty. Need a face mask, and cover up too, out of respect etc. Can't take water/drink in so don't bring, otherwise you have to leave it at a 'luggage drop' place and collect on way out.

reviews.author: Mr-Poisson
reviews.title: A memorable visit
reviews.content: The highlight was seeing Ho Chi Minh. Memorable. Also enjoyed visiting the Museum. Learnt alot about the ideas of Ho Chi Minh. We went on a Sunday morning. Little queue.

reviews.author: Phoebesmum10
reviews.title: Lots of walking
reviews.content: We were not going here on our tour. We had just wanted to meet our group at the end but miss communication with our guide, we ended up going through it. Lots of soldiers and security, although 1 did leave his post to help my husband up the steps. I was surprised by the size of the whole place. So much open space but not allowed on the grass!!!! Saw some people on grass and next thing a guard blows a whistle and signs for them to get off. Interesting place though.

reviews.author: Arthur415
reviews.title: No Mask/No Entry
reviews.content: Temporarily due to Corona concerns there is a policy visitors must wear a mask. Two drug stores sell them across the street. About half a block away from the entrance next to a hardware store is a little shop with a better cheaper variety.

reviews.author: Cary L
reviews.title: rare glimpse at the father of modern day Vietnam
reviews.content: We went to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum to go to the museum and of course to see Ho Chi Minh lying in state.   He is in air tight glass case and it is a very somber and quiet moment as you walk around the glass case viewing his body.   Now some people would think this is kind of weird but I saw Lenin in Moscow and it is still a part of history.   They are open only in the mornings and woman must be dressed in a sedate and respectful manner.  No shorts, no sleeveless blouses and or flip flops.  Men..no dago tees, flip flops or running shorts.   There are honor guards all along the walk ways and going up the stairs and into the mausoleum.  No cameras are allowed so don't plan to bring one in.   The entire viewing will take about 30 seconds because they will move you along but it is still a chance to see Ho Chi Minh lying in state.   The rest of the grounds, the stilt house, the museum, and the parade grounds is worth seeing.  Allow at least 2 to 3 hours.   Have a good tour.

reviews.author: timbisto
reviews.title: A place full of history
reviews.content: An impressive palatial building and square which feels at the heart of Hanoi.The final resting place for Ho Chi Minh and the parliamentary buildings around. Then into the grounds where the traditional french design led building followed by the more simple but equally beautiful former house of Ho Chi Minh.There is a lot of history information here and plenty to take in. We walked down a little further and also saw I’m the one pillar pagoda which is also an amazing feet of design. You are surrounded by history and it brings all the elements of Vietnam together.

reviews.author: JanCorb
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Very militaristic with lots of security and soldiers.  Close to the Citadel and parliament. Square is completely open so there is no shade

reviews.author: AlfK60
reviews.title: INTERESTING! SORT OF
reviews.content: A vast sprawl of a place and the mausoleum itself is huge!  Ho Chi Min is treated like a god with dozens of guards patrolling and managing visitors.  Cameras and sunglasses aren't allowed - I even had to remove my prescription "reactolite" glasses which is a trifle over-the-top.

reviews.author: George C
reviews.title: George from Toronto
reviews.content: Worth a visit.   I don't  know if Icould say I enjoyed visiting  Mausoleum. But, it certainly was interesting

reviews.author: Annie H
reviews.title: Bit Weird but a MUST SEE
reviews.content: Found this experience slightly strange but impressive with guards standing like statues in respect.  Was told to take my hands out of pockets which I fully understood.  The country obviously have heard just one side of the story of his "reign".

reviews.author: Guy T
reviews.title: Huge imposing landmark
reviews.content: A striking large Mausoleum built in a Russian Style.Sitting on the edge of the large parade Square. Very Interesting regardless of your political views. Just as a sight to see from outside it is good. You must pass through a security check point to get into the parade Square.Only open in the mornings (except Monday & Friday) for 2-3 hours from 0730.

reviews.author: Jillian F
reviews.title: Fascinating insight from guided visit
reviews.content: The guide who took us was very knowledgable and this definitely made the visit worthwhile. Having the explanations and understanding the history was essential to get full benefit from the visit

reviews.author: feyms
reviews.title: Stoic and Iconic
reviews.content: Our guide brought us past the Presidential palace to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.After passing through security to a large square, we walked up to this huge and stoic monument only to find it closed.However, not feeling a great need to see a tomb, walking past it was good enough.Hanoi, for all its claims to be a communist city was more like a democratic place, or at least the people have a bent for democracy.  I don’t think it will be too long before the people throw out the communist party and it’s elite in favor of power to the people.

reviews.author: Jerome B
reviews.title: Imposing Tomb
reviews.content: Ho's preserved body (a la Lenin in Moscow) lies inside.  Didn't go in, but the building is imposing and the site worth visiting.

reviews.author: harrybee
reviews.title: ......probably worth the long queuing time..........
reviews.content: Be prepared for a very long time in a queue. We arrived early in the morning, knowing  there could be a long queue, but were amazed at the sheer size of it - we walked for perhaps a quarter of a mile and didn't reach the end, so we gave up and visited the museum ( in the same park ) , which was very good. Recommended. When we came out, we could see the end of the queue, so decided to join it. We didn't get into the mausoleum for another 35 minutes - not much fun in the rain..... Inside, uncle Ho looked very  serene in his glass case, surrounded by immaculate and totally statue-like guards. Quite impressive.

reviews.author: TriciaBishop
reviews.title: Interesting part of history
reviews.content: The mausoleum is a beautiful building, kept respectfully peaceful with young sentries always on guard around the body of Ho Chi Minh. The body itself is extremely well preserved and they apparently take very good care of it. I think that this place would have far greater significance for the Vietnamese people who worship him and what he did for their country. It was a good experience to learn more about this great leader and see his resting place.

reviews.author: NikiG1948
reviews.title: Inspiring
reviews.content: Makes you understand how one individual changed the course of history. A reverential place worthy of respect. Museum somewhat confusing and surreal but provides a thorough framework of modern Vietnamese history.

reviews.author: DoctorDerm1
reviews.title: Closed sometimes
reviews.content: It is a very stirring building from the outside, reminding me of the Lincoln Memorial in Washington DC. We were there on a Monday and it was closed. Every 2 hours they do have the changing of the guard which we saw, complete with goose-stepping marching. Directly across the square from the Mausoleum is the beautiful Vietnam parliament building.

reviews.author: Steve S
reviews.title: Respectful History of a World Leader
reviews.content: Must do while in Hanoi to pay respects to the culture and history of a great leader. Interesting history, commitment and accomplished life’s work by Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: JuH
reviews.title: great complex but awkward process
reviews.content: walking down from Tran Quoc pagoda/west lake allows views of outside of the Mausoleum and royal palace.I am not sure what the bag policy is and this made my visit uncomfortable.  After the initial security screening I was told to check in my small back pack.  (many people were carrying much larger bags inside).  At the luggage window they said I should take my camera, phone and wallet with me.  This was actually all that was really in my bag.  I then went through in the queue to see Ho Chi Minh.  At the electronics window they did not want to take in my camera as it was too small.  So i ended up carrying in my hands all my stuff.  I put my wallet in my pocket and was a bit worried about pickpockets in the queue but was then told off for putting my hand  in/near my pocket which is not allowed by Ho Chi Minh.  so I am very unclear what the policy is and what to advise people planning a visit.  I get the impression they wanted to identify anyone with a camera/electronic device at initial security and then store these at the camera storage window later on but clearly the different teams are not working to the same policy?Overall it is very interesting to go to this complex but due to all the confusion about the bag policy, difficulty carrying my stuff in my hands rather than conveniently in my bag and attitude of the staff/guards it was not a reverent experience - lacks reflection and peace I expected for a final resting place.

reviews.author: John W
reviews.title: Probably better when it's not raining
reviews.content: An impressive monument which was slightly spoiled for us due to it raining the whole time we were there. The gardens are exceptionally well maintained and the guards obviously took their duties very seriously.The mausoleum itself is somewhat austere and very soviet.Worth a visit if only to say you have seen it.

reviews.author: mhiom2018
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Impressive building and site that lets you feel some of the history of the country. Very clean tidy and well worth visiting.

reviews.author: Chris_JNP
reviews.title: Interesting is a bit creeped
reviews.content: A place that most tour companies seem to take you, a bit creepy walking past the corpse. You will need to show respect, cover shoulders and knees , no hats no talking or taking photos. Walk past in single file. Interesting to see where he lived “ no mod cons very basic”. The complex is interesting with some very nice bits . Nice to see and hear the history.

reviews.author: Greg W
reviews.title: Interesting visit to HCM tomb
reviews.content: Beautiful grounds surrounding the Mausoleum.  Actual tour went swiftly as we visited Ho Chi Minh’s body lying in state.  Worth a visit for this historical figure.

reviews.author: Bec Campbell
reviews.title: Ho chi minh
reviews.content: The mausoleum was definitely eye opening it Is honestly amazing to pay respects to such a great man and to see him laying there left me speechlessHighly recommended viewing and paying respects

reviews.author: Oystein l
reviews.title: Been there, done that
reviews.content: Just a big, guarded building, nothing special to see or do in the surrounding park either. Been there, done that.

reviews.author: Lauren
reviews.title: Long queues
reviews.content: When I visited there were long queues to get into the Mausoleum, so we were advised by our tour guide to give it a miss as it would impact on the rest of the sightseeing we could do that day.  So if visiting leave plenty of time.  All I  managed was to get some photos of the building when visiting the square.

reviews.author: Lorine R
reviews.title: Immaculate and beautiful
reviews.content: What a tribute this is to Ho Chi Minh. The grounds and building are very well-groomed. An excellent piece of history to witness.  Very interesting to watch the guards walk the grounds.  Beautiful.

reviews.author: Pontinha2015
reviews.title: Entrance location
reviews.content: This was my first mausoleum visit and at the same time that it is very strange also it is very interesting. It is a place of highly respect so no hats, no hands in pockets, conservative clothes too. The visit is very short but after the mausoleum you have the opportunity to see some of other buildings of importance. It was very unclear how to get to the entrance, so I had to do extra walk to find it. Getting there: the entrance is located on the corner of Le Hong Phong and Ngoc Ha. You will go thru security and if you have electronic such as cameras you will have to check then in before proceeding to the visit. You can take cellphones with you but they have to be putted away. I also heard that liquids were not allowed so I left water, hand sanitizer at the hotel to prevent any delays. I arrived around 7:40am and the line was with about 35 people, highly recommend early arrival. My hotel told me that the mausoleum opened at 8 but I was glad I followed google and went with 7:30.

reviews.author: Dan W
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Although I was unable to visit inside the mausoleum, just to be in the expansive square and seeing the building is impressive. The grounds are extremely well kept and the Congress building across the street equally interesting.  Seeing the honor guard out front, the surrounding area, and the impressive seriousness of it all makes for a good visit and a good photo op   I would like to return and see the inside of the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Deborahve17
reviews.title: A visit to the mausoleum
reviews.content: When you are in Hanoi you have to visit the mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh a very imposant building. It’s on a very large square and in the neighborhood you find diverent  ambassades and the home of the primeminister and the presidential building.

reviews.author: Boomeranger
reviews.title: Worth going - Very interesting
reviews.content: Thousands of people queued but it was so well organised , you kept moving and were in / out within 45 minutes. Very tight security No cameras Videos etc   - VERY STRICT . We went with out guide and glad we went as it was very informative.

reviews.author: Maurice B
reviews.title: The mausoleum is a must for your visit
reviews.content: Has to be visited if you visit Hanoi. The most important leader in Vietnam for a century is honored in a magnificent memorial. Appropriate dress and manners required

reviews.author: Jay P
reviews.title: A worthwhile stop
reviews.content: The mausoleum was closed but the building is impressive, the grounds pretty and the Congress building across the street.  Good place for a photo or two.

reviews.author: Lorelie F
reviews.title: A must when in Hanoi
reviews.content: If interested in the history of Vietnam this is a must. Be careful  about timing as the Mausoleum, palace complex and museum all close in the middle of the day at slightly different times then open  again later in the day. It takes about 40 mins from the gate to file through the Mausoleum. No water allowed in Mausoleum but is allowed in museum.

reviews.author: Wilcockg
reviews.title: Almost ghoulish
reviews.content: It was spooky to witness Vietnamese coming to pay their respects to the man who gained independence in 1953.It it many ways was their thank you for freedom.I had seen Lenin in 1983 and it was just as eerie.The grounds and historic displays were fascinating.

reviews.author: GRLUK
reviews.title: Somewhere you have to go
reviews.content: To understand better Vietnam and its people it really helps to spend a few hours in this widespread mausoleum.  The queues to see the body can be long so our guide got us there quite early in the morning and the rest of the visit went smoothly after that.To learn about the country's great leader and feel his presence around the gardens, the small ponds and his domestic buildings was a great history lesson.You may not agree with his politics but this was such a major character in the nation's history that you understand why his mausoleum is so popular.There's plenty to see and the site is well run, though the entrance security was a bit more stern than necessary. A must-do on any tour of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Egle K
reviews.title: nice place
reviews.content: Very nice place to walk around. There are a lot of local people walking or running. We ere on friday, so mausoleum was closed

reviews.author: SHo_13
reviews.title: Check out history
reviews.content: There's a museum but within walking distance. It's a must for sight seeing in Hanoi to have a bit of understanding of history.

reviews.author: Steviep
reviews.title: A must see when in town
reviews.content: This really is a must, what a fascinating insight into the life of Ho Chi Minh. No photos are allowed when in the mausoleum and Ho Chi Minh really does look like he is sleeping. While there you can also see the stilted house he lived in, which is a must see too.

reviews.author: Dan6482
reviews.title: Daniel 🇸🇬
reviews.content: I had booked with Hanoi Transfer service and on one day city tour, we had visited to Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and its was worth place to visit and knowing about Lated President Ho Chi Minh history

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Have to visit
reviews.content: You have to visit the mausoleum - our guide used as a base for the recent history of Vietnam.Yes it is a dead body but it's your way of showing respect to a country that is so welcoming and respectful to you

reviews.author: Woodedelk234
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: This is an interesting place to visit. A stroll past the mausoleum (heavily guarded) and lots of instructions where to walk and where not to! Lovely gardens and ancient pagodola behind. Worth visiting if you are in Hanoi

reviews.author: SteveByfleet
reviews.title: Would be a must see if you could get in
reviews.content: We decided against the long wait to enter. The mausoleum itself is a beauty from the outside probably not worth waiting to see a dead body. Go see HCM's house nearby instead

reviews.author: Michael W
reviews.title: Big surprise
reviews.content: I don’t know whether we inadvertently latched on to someone else’s tour but we had read that a) we would have to pay for entry and b) wouldn’t be allowed anywhere near the mausoleum itself. Imagine then our surprise, when we found ourselves filing past the body of old HCM himself. Quite the experience and not even much of a line to wait in.

reviews.author: Roslyn v
reviews.title: Hanoi experience
reviews.content: If you come to Hanoi it seems a fitting part of Vietnam history to visit the Mausoleum. Only there is no time to ponder over Ho Chi Minh and history as you just have to keep walking past and I guess this is because of volume of visitors.  The Mausoleum was free entry but the surrounding grounds were a small fee for entry.  We enjoyed our visit, no photographs permitted and was all over quite quickly.

reviews.author: George R
reviews.title: Mr. George W. Riley
reviews.content: We went there yesterday and It is a lengthy excursion. Be prepared to walk around and no shorts or straps for clothes. The admissions place closes at 10:30 and it is a lengthy event. Watch the taxi drivers to and from and get a firm price for where you are going and have the exact amount in hand beforehand. They are pros at getting to you and you are an amateur.

reviews.author: Compass59566
reviews.title: Hanoi Adventure
reviews.content: Our guide toured us through the Mausoleum and was very knowledgable. The guide gave us a very good narrative of the historical importance

reviews.author: Ian
reviews.title: Ho Cho Minh
reviews.content: I thought the whole place was properly and respectfully arranged. An important place to visit if you’re visiting Hanoi.

reviews.author: Andy87
reviews.title: The Greatest Ho Chi Minh!
reviews.content: Felt great seeing his body and feel his soul.Great man! The greatest! I recommend visit it for sure!

reviews.author: malomax
reviews.title: Definitely worth visiting!
reviews.content: Another must-do when visiting Hanoi.  We went in winter so crowds weren’t a problem.  Just note that the entry is at the back of the complex and if you walk there (like we did), we had to walk nearly another 30min to get to the entrance.The only caution is that it’s free to get in, but once you exit the mausoleum, the only way out that we could find was to pay to go through to the Golden Palace and gardens.  We looked around but didn’t see any other way to exit.

reviews.author: betteskid
reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit
reviews.content: I stopped here during my recent visit in Vietnam. I did not have time to wait in the incredibly long line to enter the building, but I got a feel for importance of Ho Chi Minh to the people of Vietnam. As someone who came of age during the Vietnam era it was very interesting to get a broader perspective on this period in history through my visit and also understand a bit more about Ho Chi Minh. I would recommend going.

reviews.author: ozallan
reviews.title: A Must See in Hanoi
reviews.content: The holy of holies for Vietnamese. This is the mausoleum for Uncle Ho and a solemn place. You walk past the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh in full view (or is it really him?). Also in close proximity is the old French designed Presidential Palace & also the simple 2 room house Uncle Ho lived in while he was President. All a must see when in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Keith W
reviews.title: Part of our tour
reviews.content: Quite an experience , to think how long he has been laying in state & you can walk past close to the casket

reviews.author: julia b
reviews.title: Not an enjoyable experience, no time given to pay respect to Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: I did not enjoy this experience, as you begin with having to check your belongings including your camera and water. Make sure ladies, you are covered or you will be denied entry. You are then lead in 2 single file lines in silence for over 1km in the direct sun. As you go there are several armed guards around and will whistle at you if your caught taking photos of the grounds. You are then taken into the mausoleum, again several armed guards and get to do one pass around Ho Chi Minh. I totally understand the guards and being silent but you don't even get to stop and pay respect to Ho Chi Minh, which was what I was there for. Then you get pushed out to the gardens to buy water as by this time you're super thirsty and souvenirs. The grounds are very large and the majority of it was off limits to the public. The areas that were open were very lovely and it was the only place I saw free birds flying around. The museum of Ho Chi Minh is also on the grounds and I'm sure it has some amazing things in it, however we did not go through it.

reviews.author: Alan R
reviews.title: A strange but unique place
reviews.content: This was an experience that very few people can say they have done. As it can only be done in very few countries. When in Vietnam be sure to wake up early and take part in the visiting of Ho Chi Minh in his embalmed state. Watch the changing of the guards and enjoy the beauty of the area around the mausoleum. Be sure if you want to go into the mausoleum to go to the entrance near the ho chi Minh museum about an our before it opens, depending on the time of the year it's either 7:30 am or 8:00 am. Entrance is free.

reviews.author: Pip L
reviews.title: Kind of strange but a must see
reviews.content: Weird but totally worth a visit.Well manicured gardens surround it.Well organized queuing at entry.You walk past him cant stop, no hats or as I learnt donot hold yr hands together (I got a slap from a guard for this!)

reviews.author: jwgbusiness
reviews.title: Interesting, Historical but not manned by welcoming people
reviews.content: The historical aspects of seeing Uncle Ho's final resting place is a must-see for its historical and architectural aspects.  However, to see the entombed body, you have to line up and wait in the hot sun, so be sure to have head-wear.  In addition, the entire buidling and its compound is manned by miliatry outfitted guards who are very unfriendly, stern and regimental. Perhaps, they like to put on a show of "strength".  Next door is Ho Chi Minh's house on stilts and lying to one side of the Mausoleum is the One Pillar Pagoda, which was founded by King Ly Thai To in 1049 - an important symbol for the people of Hanoi.

reviews.author: 71emma
reviews.title: unfriendly
reviews.content: When we entered, we were told we couldn't bring in our backpacks.  The unsmiling guards shoved our belongings into a bag and shooed us away, handing us a tag to claim our belongings later.  As we followed the other people, walking forward into the open space in front, we were yelled at to retrace our steps, to enter through another way.  And yet, those others could do it ...?Ok, so we obeyed and walked into the other pathway with a canopy overhead. Further on, we saw the toilet sign and moved to visit it.  The guard there stopped us and signaled us to keep walking, with a cold expression on his face. We were bewildered at all the unfriendly treatment.  If we had done anything wrong, at least we should be accorded some politeness being shown.  Body language and facial expression can really hurt.We decided to leave.

reviews.author: Walt D
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: It was quite an interesting visit and worth while seeing though be prepared to stand in line for a while and listen to the guards as they’re very strict.

reviews.author: myeden88
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: Very nice and large area. Learned a lot from Vietnam History. If you go in the summer make sure u wear hat, mister... you will be outside and walk in the sun a lot.

reviews.author: JMB50
reviews.title: Closed on Mondays
reviews.content: Guess what, I visited on a Monday so was unable to visit the mausoleum itself but was able to spend time wandering around a very attractive site.  The pagoda supported by just one beam is beautiful and I would really recommend the cold fresh coconut juice drinks when you have finished your visit.  The old cars on display are fabulous and it really is a very tranquil place.  Be warned some of the visitors to the site do push you around but try and stand your ground if you can.

reviews.author: Eveline E
reviews.title: Eye opening
reviews.content: The body of Ho Chi Minh is preserved so well. Definitely a must visit. Also do dress conservatively to visit this place

reviews.author: carmen_from_canada
reviews.title: A very controlled and serene environment
reviews.content: Clearly great pride is had! The gardens are stunning, the environment is well controlled by staff, and the hall is serene. Don't forget to check out the buddhist temole too. Worth the visit!

reviews.author: XavierNY
reviews.title: Pretty Amazing
reviews.content: It was pretty amazing seeing Ho Chi Minh and his resting place. Don't you dare try to take a photo. Nice how it was free also. At the end we opted not to see the presidential palace, as you can't go in it, it's just a money grab in my opinion. Enjoy.

reviews.author: Georgina C
reviews.title: Interesting & worthwhile!
reviews.content: We went here to pay or respects to Ho Chi Minh and it was well worth the trip! We went to the Temple of Literature first as we were too late to go inside the Mausoleum but the structure was still exciting to see from the outside. We saw the changing of the guards and then went to the museum which was also great! Although we both knew who Ho Chi Minh was we had a much better understanding of his importance to Vietnam and the person he was after the visit.

reviews.author: ByronP
reviews.title: Traditional tourist stop in Hanoi
reviews.content: It is interesting to see once.  It is a long process to get through the lines and into the mausoleum - took us about 30 minutes or so and it didn't seem to be that busy.  You are directed by stoic soldiers who scold you for taking photos or talking very loud as you are walking - one must be reverent!!  Once inside you keep moving slowing around HCM's body and out - about 2-3 minutes walking around the case where his body is - much like Lenin's mausoleum in Moscow.  Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Mary-Jo J
reviews.title: Fine for wheelchair visitors
reviews.content: We went with a friend who was in a wheelchair due to an injury. The courtesy shown was amazing. We were expedited through the lines with the staff pushing the wheel chair. Although the lines seemed to be moving pretty fast even without the helpful assistance. When we neared the mausoleum building a collection of white-uniformed guards appeared and carried the wheelchair with friend in it up the numerous series of steps in and out of the mausoleum. Incredibly thoughtful and kind.

reviews.author: LoBommer
reviews.country: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
reviews.title: Magnificent Mausoleum
reviews.content: We arrived just after 10.00am and it was too late to enter into the mausoleum. The edifice is magnificent and befitting. It was also highly guarded. While this is a revered place, it's majestic presence commands respectable awe.Well worth a visit but check the opening times!

reviews.author: John D
reviews.title: Important Monument to Vietnamese people.
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh is revered by the Vietnamese and was humbling to see his body. Extremely well organised and efficient queuing. This site is well worth a visit whilst in Hanoi. Also, worth checking out Ho's house on stilts which is nearby. Very large complex and not far from Old Quarter.

reviews.author: mrsbrodcb
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh mausoleum
reviews.content: Free to get in to see him. It shuts quite early, about 10 or 11am. As taxi dropped us off at 9am we caught a glimpse of changing of guard. Hoped to see it again but didn't. No kids under 3 allowed in. The guards outside mausoleum very strict about not taking photos of mausoleum (outside). You walk through fairly quickly so don't be put off by queue. Pay VND40k to access his house on stilts and walk round lake. Cheap food available in this area.

reviews.author: Craig
reviews.title: Highly revered visit
reviews.content: Amongst other places, my family and I visited was the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum where the preserved body of Vietnam’s first President Ho Chi Minh is on display. He is highly revered - and I mean extremely high. Queues of mainly locals & school kids blended with tourists like us attended this location. I must admit, it is a very solemn moment when you walk around his body which is well policed by the local military (all immaculately dressed) to ensure everyone’s behaviour is in check. President Ho Chi Minh died in 1969 and I respectfully say that he looks very well cared for. Photography in the building is a huge NO.

reviews.author: pelagiadlc
reviews.title: informative of Vietnam history
reviews.content: it was nice, very organized. he was loved and well respected by the proud people of Vietnam, this place is a must visit.

reviews.author: Elin L
reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.content: We arrived too late to enter into the mausoleum, but boy were we treated with the lit up structure and changing of the guards was an added bonus!  While this is a solemn place, it's majestic presence commands respectable awe.

reviews.author: Bob B
reviews.title: Very different
reviews.content: We visited the Mausoleum during a recent trip to Hanoi.This is obviously a very important place in Vietnamese history and they very jealously guard respect and proper decorum.The queue took circa 45 minutes and the grounds are lovely.At the Mausoleum you are filtered into two lines to walks past in total silence the preserved body of Ho Chi Minh.As i say in the title “very different”.  Pleased i went - but would not go again.

reviews.author: Lia Linh
reviews.title: Extraordinary
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh is a humble but extraordinary, hugely popular and most respected leader of the nation. This feels exactly like a pilgrimage. A must visit place.

reviews.author: John Walker
reviews.title: Fascinating place for any fans of Vietnam and history
reviews.content: As a child with a passion for US history and with one of my biggest passions the cold war I came to Vietnam to learn more about learn more about the history of the country and to see important historical sites.  This was a fascinating chance to see the last resting place of perhaps the most important person in Vietnamese history.  Was truly amazing to be able to see Ho Chi Minh and this Mausoleum and is a day I won't forget.

reviews.author: Julie M
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum vsHoa Lu Prison- which is worth seeing?
reviews.content: Don’t waste your time on this alleged attraction. You have to slowly march in long lines to get to the Mausoleum, and when you finally get there you’ll get a two second glimpse of his dead body. There is no history or information poster anywhere. Then you are shepherded to his house viewing which costs 40,000 Duong per person just to view a few random rooms from the outside.The Hoa Lu Prison on the other hand is well worth the visit- there are excellent preserved areas of the original prison, many letters , statues of prisoners in the cells, letters and many photos.There is an excellent audio guide available for a small fee which tells you many stories of prisoners experiences and takes about two hours.

reviews.author: Shashvisits
reviews.title: Well worth a visit.
reviews.content: It’s a very imposing building, beautifully  maintained and lovely gardens around. You can’t go inside this building.

reviews.author: MaryNML
reviews.title: Nice monument
reviews.content: Nice walk but we couldn't come in. Good to know it's part of the Hanoi visit because that area worth the visit.

reviews.author: Ray
reviews.title: Our visit to Uncle Ho
reviews.content: This is a must do for anyone who visits Hanoi. It is a very solemn experience to see Ho Chi Minh lining in state 50 years after his passing.

reviews.author: B H
reviews.title: Walking to Mausoleum from Hoan Kiem.
reviews.content: If approaching from Dien Bien Phu, make a left at Le Hong Phong (embassy row).  After the security check (no water allowed), follow the crowd and direction of uniformed guards.  No charge for mausoleum.  The stilt house, working house and garage need a ticket.(40000 vnd).  The museum is another fee of 40000 vnd.  Follow signs to exit to return to entry gate.

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: It’s ok at best
reviews.content: Massive space and lawn area that you can’t enter not sure why!!! For me the strict rules, regulations and armed guards are a complete over kill and dampens your experience.Remembering he’s not a king, for the Vietnamese people a great warrior from past history and should be remembered but to this scale!!!!For the wait and how uncomfortable security makes you for me not a must do in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Jeri F
reviews.title: Historically and culturally important monument
reviews.content: The mausoleum is not open to tourists.  The area does contain Ho Chi Minh's house and other government buildings.

reviews.author: okiejer
reviews.title: Important historical site
reviews.content: This is an important historical site that also contains gardens and the living quarters of Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: Boss0079
reviews.title: Once in a lifetime
reviews.content: Very strict upon entry. No bare shoulders and no short skirts. Take a jacket to cover up. Any liquid bottles you take in are confiscated, opened or not.You have to check in your cameras and they are returned to you after you exit the mausoleum.Definitely a must do if your around the area. The mausoleum part is free but the other section you have to pay for.

reviews.author: Herbert C
reviews.title: Eternal memorial to a Vietnam icon
reviews.content: Love him or hate him, no one can deny that Uncle Ho has a special and permanent place in the hearts of the Vietnamese population, and this mausoleum is perhaps the ultimate tribute to Vietnam’s iconic leader. His body, which has been embalmed for the past 50 years since his death in 1969, is a must-see for visitors to appreciate this larger-than-life figure. This attraction only opens for a few hours in the morning, so best to be there early when it opens at 7:30 a.m. Entrance is free, but be prepared to endure stringent airport-style security checks and 20 minutes queue, monitored by disciplined white-uniformed guards who disallowed any form of photo-taking. Once near the mausoleum, the line moves quickly as visitors are not allowed to hold the queue when walking past the serene corpse.

reviews.author: Ian R
reviews.title: Unique memory of an Iconic Figure in Modern History
reviews.content: It's been over 50 years since the death of Ho Chi Minh and the end of the Vietnam War only a few years later, so to visit this mausoleum and see Uncle Ho lying in state was.....incredible!  Regardless of the politics and the arguments about the war, Ho Chi Minh was a mighty leader for what he believed in, and again, whatever one may think about it all, the reunification of Vietnam was something to which he  devoted his life.

reviews.author: jack M
reviews.title: A MEMORIAL TO AN ASIAN RULER
reviews.content: Aesthetically it's like many of the memorials erected throughout the world to commemorate worthy (or not so worthy) individuals. This commemorates a man without whose passion, devotion, and determination Vietnam would not exist.  For its historical significance this is a place to visit in Vietnam.

reviews.author: Lizzy T
reviews.title: Free activity
reviews.content: Free activity to do everyday 5am and 9pm where you see the troops raise and pull down the Viet Flag with marching parade.

reviews.author: AdrianS2403
reviews.title: One place you have to visit.
reviews.content: We choose not to get up early and queue to see Ho Chi Minh's body. However walking around the outside of the Mausoleum is very interesting.  Guards in white military dress on their whistles when tourists cross the yellow lines. Very strict airport style security to enter the park, you can collect items at the end.

reviews.author: Mawa N
reviews.title: Colosseum to preserve history
reviews.content: Beautifully build in front of big green lawn. This site is one of most important site to preserve Vietnamese history! The site itself is now becoming the instagramable site in Hanoi. Come and have a visit!

reviews.author: Nelson L
reviews.title: Very grand and must do in Hanoi
reviews.content: They are closed from 12pm to 2pm and the museum was also closed at different times. Be aware to avoid disappointment

reviews.author: Josefer M
reviews.title: Great!
reviews.content: The most important thing, It is a historic piece that keeps the spirit who guides and projects the actual Vietnam. When you are there the emotions will come and showing you the Great's Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: Yasmin Tavaria
reviews.title: Ms. Yasmin Tavaria
reviews.content: A good place to visit when in Hanoi. But don’t visit on Monday as it remains closed to visitors for inside visit. Also view the adjacent Presidential Palace and the stilted house where HCM lived. Do not miss the Pagoda visitalso.

reviews.author: HouAzn Traveler
reviews.title: History
reviews.content: A part of history and worth seeing. The different areas can be confusing and there is a walk from the front to the actual Mausoleum. The hours are limited so check before you go

reviews.author: lawlessrose
reviews.title: Maybe not on a sunday
reviews.content: The Mausoleum was the first sight we were to visit today, however even before 9 am the line was winding around the corner, I think we would have to have edited already an hour to get in. Decided to miss to mausoleum and comeback latter just to visit Ho Chi Minh palace. The mausoleum closes at 10 am. So we just got to see the outside, I was ok with that.

reviews.author: Shirzccy
reviews.title: Interesting highlight
reviews.content: A place to pay respect to their local great politician. Quite crowded with locals and tourist. It is a solemn and respectful environment so please dress appropriately and abide to the rules.

reviews.author: Tracey W
reviews.title: Great place to visit but closed Mondays
reviews.content: Great place to visit but watch for the closed days which are Monday and I think Fridays. Free to walk around but not sure if cost involved to enter the Mausoleum. Watching the guards changing is with waiting around for (they are regular).

reviews.author: David W
reviews.title: Good experience to walk around
reviews.content: This was a good experience to do. We saw the mausoleum and visited the garden.To enter the main grounds is free, but none Vietnamese have to pay a small amount to view the garden and memorabilia of Ho Chi Minh.Worth doing if you are in the city.

reviews.author: IGor A
reviews.title: Big complex
reviews.content: The mausoleum is located in a big area where you can find the one pillar paogda and also the presidential Palace.

reviews.author: Myra Brian
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: Formal atmosphere, strict security. Inside quiet, fresh air. Some sections have soft, soothing music. In the mausoleum slightly cold.

reviews.author: Stephen C
reviews.title: Must visit in Hanoi but not much to see
reviews.content: This is a must see if you are in Hanoi although there is actually not much to see apart from Ho Chi Minh’s body. There was a long line of visitors when I went and you have to go through in two lines so it takes a while to go through the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Freddieh
reviews.title: Day visit
reviews.content: Great site to visit Ho Chi Minh Buriel site well maintained and great sight seeing venue in a great location.

reviews.author: WilliamWillieWilson
reviews.title: A worthy and historic stop
reviews.content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is not one of those sites that leaves you breathless, like the view from Brazil’s Christ the Redeemer, or standing in front of India’s Taj Mahal, or beholding Zimbabwe’s Victoria Falls. It’s the historical significance that is worth considering when standing here.Walking through Hanoi’s Ba Đình Square, it is immediately reminiscent of Moscow’s Red Square and Beijing’s Tiananmen Square, those massive public spaces that punctuate major communist cities. It took me back to previous trips in far flung lands.Before you stands a mighty mausoleum containing the body of Ho Chi Minh, the president of North Vietnam at the time they went to war with the United States. This ostentatious burial site is ironic, given that Ho Chi Minh asked to be cremated before dying in 1969. But here he lies, across from the National Assembly in a building for all to see.

reviews.author: Anthony0909
reviews.title: Good experience
reviews.content: Good to experience and walk around there. Only too crowd on the day I visited. Worth to visit and know more

reviews.author: Bharly
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: Very strict security. Beautifully maintained gardens and building. Interesting to see. Many tourists.

reviews.author: chezfijez
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Huge queues but go down very quickly worth a visit just to say you’ve been. Ho Chi Minh is so revered here still and there were many Vietnamese visiting along with holiday makers

reviews.author: TTP89
reviews.title: A Must See if you’re in Hanoi
reviews.content: We decided to visit the mausoleum after seeing the imposing but beautiful building from the road. Having visited though, I thought it was an amazing cultural experience for the entire family and would recommend a visit for any travellers in Hanoi. It’s an important part of the Vietnamese national identity and we felt very humbled by the experience. Save yourself some time and read the dress code online (don’t wear shorts or short skirts, and cover your shoulders) and don’t bring any baggage (you will have to check in anything bigger than a small ladies bag).There was already a long queue when we arrived (fairly early in the morning) however it moved surprisingly quickly as everyone was politely but sternly shepherded by the guards. There was a palpable sense of solemnity as we approached the mausoleum itself. The grounds and surrounding gardens are meticulously (or perhaps militantly) kept, it was beautiful though it felt disconcertingly too square and too organised. The building itself is an amazing piece of architect, and you can take pictures outside but no photography was permitted inside. The guards kept a very brisk pace so viewing time was very short but more than enough to catch sight of the man himself.

reviews.author: Anna M
reviews.title: Interesting and unusual
reviews.content: Really interesting.  We visited on a weekday morning arriving around 8:30am.  The mausoleum visit took about 30 mins from security screening to exit.  Very efficient.  The line moves quickly and the soldiers ensure no-one steps out of line - a few people were told off for their lack of line discipline - so pay attention or that will be you.  The actual viewing of the body is brief as you walk around it.  Then before you know it you are walking down the stairs and out. I really recommend it as an unusual and interesting place to visit. We also went to the museum on the same site (5 minutes walk from the mausoleum). That was excellent too.  Possibly we got lucky as when we asked about audio guides they were all out.  No problem there was a volunteer guide available - Lyn (Lin?) a law student with a very keen interest in Ho Chi Minh who volunteers when she has time.  Wow what she didn’t know about the man and the museum exhibits would not be worth knowing.  Absolutely fascinating and we learnt so much.  Highly recommend the museum and if there is a volunteer guide available even better.

reviews.author: Dr. Issa Abu-Dayyeh
reviews.title: Closed Monday Evening
reviews.content: Went there to check out the body of Ho chi Min which is supposed to be kept inside. Closed Monday evening, so be careful!

reviews.author: Susan
reviews.title: An Organised Outing
reviews.content: The Mausoleum is very dominant along the strip. Always being watched by the guards. Just looking at it from outside wasn’t very exciting.

reviews.author: Courtney
reviews.title: Really interesting
reviews.content: If you’re visiting Hanoi you should visit the Ho Chi Mingh complex. There are a lot of pieces to the site. The mausoleum is interesting although not the most interesting part of the visit. You will need to take hats off and prepare to be quiet and respectful during your visit. Also know that there can be quite a line and they will keep you moving - so your visit will be short. No photography is allowed inside the mausoleum and you will have to check bags and big cameras at the desk on the way in.

reviews.author: Gita Yubilate
reviews.title: Unique building
reviews.content: This Mausoleum Ho Chi Minh had a unique style of building and located same with One Pillar Pagoda in the center of Hanoi.The ambience is very calm and we can get relaxing time in the park.

reviews.author: Dennis ES T
reviews.title: Militant but Marvellous
reviews.content: The place was strictly run by the military but you can understand why when they are guarding the preserved body of President Ho Chi Minh. I did not expect to see him so the feeling was momentous indeed. Then a tour to the Presidential grounds to how he had lived. A truly remarkable yet humble man whatever your political slant

reviews.author: Sunspotter2016
reviews.title: definitely worth a visit if in Hanoi
reviews.content: If time allowing, do visit this site. Open skies and lovely plants. Well preserved architecture and interesting history.

reviews.author: Sudeep Chatterjee
reviews.title: Grand monument
reviews.content: Ho Chin Minh masouleum is a must visit with stately body preserved of uncle Ho along with well maintained gardens

reviews.author: Emma
reviews.title: Very nice surroundings
reviews.content: We only saw the Ho Chi Minh-mausoleum from a distance, but the atmosphere surrounding it was very nice. People were singing, soldiers were training and tourists were walking around.

reviews.author: cliff1608
reviews.title: Somber
reviews.content: Not what you’d call a fun day out and definitely didn’t expect the view inside, the whole experience was like a day out in the USSR in the 1970s. But historical and part of the reason we visit foreign countries.

reviews.author: iamnewanda
reviews.title: The founding father of modern Vietnam
reviews.content: Seeing "Uncle Ho" was a very unique experience, and a highlight of my tour to Vietnam.  Do yourself a favour. Research the man before you arrive at the mausoleum, so that you understand his journey and how he united Vietnam. It is a powerful story, and he is a very interesting man. Yes, the queues are crazy, but as you get 30 seconds to see him, everything runs very smoothly. Just follow the rules! Seeing the place where Ho Chi Minh lived was also very interesting.

reviews.author: Debi P
reviews.title: Uncle Ho is back!
reviews.content: So we read that “uncle Ho” goes to Russia to be restored from Oct to Dec - luckily we went today and he’s back. The most humbling and amazing experience to see him you are not allowed to loiter or take photos and you must be dressed respectfully and walk in two lines around him- 3 minutes us all it took tops but would highly recommend you to do this - just not in Oct to mid Dec!

reviews.author: Amar K
reviews.title: Solemn; sense of history
reviews.content: My second time back to visit, this time with our adult children. Though the lines are Long, they move at a steady pace and the wait does not feel long. The mausoleum and embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh succeed in providing respect and conveying a sense of gravitas for a man who embodied the struggle of a people’s will and desire to be free from colonialism and foreign subjugation. Be sure not to miss the nearby museum, where Ho Chi Minh lived and worked in a one-bedroom house.

reviews.author: Scot
reviews.title: Unique experience
reviews.content: I came to appreciate this tour more over the course of our visit through Viet Nam.  Of course the government reveres the man who started the movement to unite Viet Nam, but as we travelled south, it is became clear to me that whatever issues Viet Nam has, they are happier that at least they are making their own decisions - not the French, not the Chinese, not the Americans.  You begin to appreciate the impact that this man had on the future of the country - and why so many people come to see him.

reviews.author: 2014NG
reviews.title: Something to appreciate while in Hanoi
reviews.content: If you can dodge the crowds here, then this would great experience. We had a personal guide who walked us through the key highlights of the site. Since all tour groups get routed via a one way path, there are some bottlenecks to contend with especially around the private residences as pond. The gardens were also a welcome reprieve from the afternoon sun. Plenty of tacky souvenirs to choose from on the way out.

reviews.author: Andi
reviews.title: Long wait for a short viewing
reviews.content: The line was very long, but tolerable. This is likely due to going on a weekend, so going during a weekday would probably be preferable. The viewing of Ho Chi Minh was very short, we were probably in there for 30-60 seconds. Afterward, there are some pagodas, vendors, and a museum that is an extra charge.

reviews.author: Miondon
reviews.title: Not sure why it was so busy
reviews.content: We went at 7am and already there were hundreds in the lines including children on trips. I was quite surprised. Having said that, the lines moved quite quickly. The mausoleum area is well maintained. There are a lot of staff around and all tourists are monitored closely. No photos allowed of the inner area and you have to check in cameras if you bring them with you.

reviews.author: susan a
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Military efficiency at it's best despite the long queues we went through very quickly. Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: Rashid Isa Rishi AlHeddi
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: A really great Tribute to the First President of Vietnam who held the country together. Fascinating to see the Masoleum, His house, cars and office . also the simple private quarters attached to a Bunker! Great watwr lake and flowers around it, makes for a fascinating days tour. Must visit when in Hanoi.

reviews.author: DRW44
reviews.title: IMPRESSIVE HISTORY
reviews.content: The whole outdoor complex is called the Ho Chi Minh Museum comprising the Mausoleum, Ho's two houses, the One Pillar Pagoda and a large park area with lakes and streams. The Mausoleum is a very large, solid edifice even bigger than Lenin's Tomb and the parade area outside is even bigger than Red Square. If visiting on your own, you may not have been told not to walk inside the yellow lines in front of the Mausoleum. TIP: There is a small changing of the guard ceremony every hour, on the hour.

reviews.author: bluehive
reviews.title: A Reflection of History
reviews.content: The mausoleum has remains of the most iconic leader of Vietnam. It's a vast space, green and well organized. You have to deposit your bags at the entry. You can't take pictures inside the mausoleum. Expect to spend about 45 minutes here. You can proceed to the One Pillar Pagoda from here. Tip: please check the time and day of mausoleum open schedule. The mausoleum is closed on Monday by the way.

reviews.author: Anjana
reviews.title: Respect
reviews.content: Respect us the word that comes to the mind when one visit this place. No food water big cameras allowed. One is not allowed to speak its complete silence. That’s how they pay homage to the leader when u enter it feels that The great leader is just lying down and would be with us any moment. No hats or sunglasses on....... all I can say is hat off

reviews.author: Aarón G
reviews.title: History
reviews.content: Interesting experience as you make the Disneyland-like lines (which move quite fast) towards the mauseoleum.  Do follow the security guard's instructions / hand gestures.  Inside, the experience is surreal as you witness the body of Ho Chi Minh dimly lit in a unique glass and wood-carved display case.  You solemnly parade in and out in about 20 seconds.  No photos or video allowed.  This experience is free and definitely worth it.

reviews.author: jasfitz1969
reviews.title: Strange experience
reviews.content: We went with a tour group today to see Ho Chi Minh’s mausoleum today, and was surprised at the level of security and seriousness around it. The guards in the crypt were in full white dress uniform, which would be uncomfortable at best in the humid conditions, and they physically push you past the crypt, definitely no photos with Uncle Ho here. The level of respect and love they have for HCM is everywhere, but he does look a bit plastic, but he has been dead for 50 years.

reviews.author: Sonya S
reviews.title: Bit disappointed
reviews.content: We were primarily there to see Ho Chi Minh’s house and go to the mausoleum but the way-finding was non existent and the grounds are large. Even the brochure hasn’t a map. When we asked for directions we were sent to the Ho Chi Minh Museum which was interesting but not where we intended to go. By the time we found his house, we couldn’t find the entrance so we wandered around the mausoleum only to discover it wasn’t open. There was no information online to indicate this. We still enjoyed it but it wasn’t what we had hoped it to be.

reviews.author: Ruth B
reviews.title: Ho Chi Min Mausoleum
reviews.content: Long line ups and guards usher you through to the mausoleum. Once through you are able to wander through the gardens and other buildings, Lovely way to spend a morning.

reviews.author: Ev_kka
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Actually, this was interesting. First, I was a bit worried because of the long line, but it moves really quickly, so it took line 30 minutes only to get to the mausoleum.You can't take your camera, but you can have your phone. Taking photos isnstrictly prohibited inside.You can't wear any sunglases (even in the line outside the soilders told to get them off), no sleevless shirts or shorts or short skirts.The mausoleum is free of charge (you pay only the entrance to the komplex after the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Waqas M
reviews.title: Lame.
reviews.content: They didn't let us in cause we had a baby with us, which would have been ok except I saw others with same age babies going in. The guard clearly had his own interpretation.

reviews.author: baghdadlian
reviews.title: Excellent Place
reviews.content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and Its area is outstanding.  I spent 3 hours going around and admiring everything.  The body of Ho Chi Minh was in Russia which it is sent once a year for preservation uptake.  But enjoyed the stilt House where he lived .....the pond....the main building parliament from outside ( no visitors Inside).  It is a place you should come.

reviews.author: Buzz B
reviews.title: Nice trip full of history
reviews.content: Despite arriving near 11am closing time, we managed to enter the mausoleum and say Ho Chi Minh's body which was very amazingly embalmed. There wasn't any queue on Sat so I was pleasantly surprised.

reviews.author: Zheng JF James
reviews.title: Important sight for tourists
reviews.content: Needless to say, the mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh deserves a visit by all tourists to Hanoi, at least for picture taking. Sadly, during this period, I am fully aware that the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh cannot be viewed as I have ever read somewhere that during the month of Oct/Nov of each year, the body would be sent to Russia for 2-3 months for restoration. Anyway, I will be visit Hanoi again and hence there will be an opportunity to view the embalmed body in the near future.

reviews.author: Ruth C
reviews.title: Ho chi minh
reviews.content: We had been warned to be here early to avoid queuing but we slept in!! Arrived at 9am and the queue was very long, wrapping around the side and out to the main road. Despite this it moves very quickly because you're not allowed to stop inside. We ended up leaving 40min later which isn't too bad. You have to leave all cameras at a drop off point. Lets just say it was interesting to see although unusual.

reviews.author: Simone B
reviews.title: Visits to Ho’s Mausoleum
reviews.content: Worth’s visit , guards are very smart and gardens are beautiful . Bit creepy though especially as it wasn’t what he wanted

reviews.author: JrnyJunkie
reviews.title: Impressive structure.
reviews.content: Unfortunately the mausoleum was closed the day that we visited...I would have thought that our guide would have known in advance...very disappointed.

reviews.author: Steve_of_N21
reviews.title: Well, that’s something I have never done before.
reviews.content: I have to omit that I have never seen the fascination in visiting a mausoleum to see a dead body, be they an important historical figure or not. But the reverence the Vietnamese show to their favourite son is quite moving.The Mausoleum is quite an impressive building in its own right, being modelled on Lenin's mausoleum in Russia, and you can obviously view it from the outside without visiting inside. The organisation for you to visit inside is very well done but does involve queuing and several layers of security removing you of liquids and cameras, but the queue does move quite quickly and it probably took about 30 minutes from the initial security scanners to entering the mausoleum. The dress and behaviour codes to visit are quite strict, even to the level that I had to remove my glasses because, being reactolite, they looked too much like sun glasses to the guards. Fortunately the Mausoleum is dark inside and I could soon put them back on to be able to see Uncle Ho. I have to say his annual trips to Russia for maintenance obviously agree with him and I hope I look half as good when I have been dead for 50 years.I have to say it’s not something I would have chose to do if it hadn’t been a major item on our tour company itinerary, but I am glad I actually experienced it. But for me personally the visit after to the Presidential Palace complex was more interesting.

reviews.author: YY C
reviews.title: Rude security personnel at baggage drop
reviews.content: You need to be properly attired, no sphagetti straps, no shorts, flip flops.You need to drop your bags at a security counter.Long queue... unfriendly staff & guards.Visit to HCM Mausoleum spoiled by very rude security at the baggage drop area and unfriendly guards who seemed to discriminate against foreighers and were surly & unfriendly.At the Security counter baggage drop windows, the women security staff were shouting instead of telling us nicely to go to a different window counter. A local Vietnamese girl (who spoke English)   & who were trying to help us was also scolded by the security staff!The reason they were shouting at us, because we were at the foreigner window counter to drop our bags.
