reviews.content: we visited the old town of Anoï with LUCI our guide who first taught us to cross the road between cars and scooters the motto cross the road without ever running the first time ..🫣Of course there is a world of scooters🤪 it is a must 😂LUCI made us discover The streets and alleys of Hanoi While making us discover the stories of the city 💕after these exciting stories We had lunch not far from the train street Enjoy an excellent egg coffee do not leave without having tasted it 💕  Coconut coffee 🥥💕-~~~Hanoi market is open all day until late at night 💕orchids ,artificial flowers , flea markets ,memories , offerings to honor the dead ☠️ and more.~~~ Hanoi is a friendly and human city 💕Street food I admit we did not venture 😬~~~~For brand hangers-on Uniqlo 😉😉~~~~typical Vietnamese brands that are not exported such as: bascket of the brand bitis ,tried city : shirt carta postal , poster ...    ~~~~The city center is very well visited on foot or the cyclo pushes 5€ + - for an hour

reviews.author: FrameTheWild
reviews.title: Hanoi City - great few days sightseeing
reviews.content: We had a private tour of Hanoi around the key places to visit, and had an absolutely wonderful time. What an amazing city - and although we arrived at the tail end of 'Tet' - the busyness of this made it an even more special visit.  Our guide took us to the Temple of Literature - definitely not to be missed; we also visited the mausoleum and paid our respects. With a visit to Ho Chi Minh's stilted house and also the One Pillar Pagoda.  Our tour included the Ho Loa prison - but due to the free entry because of New Year the queue was too long so we settled for a narrative and history of the prison from our tour guide. We also managed an inside visit of St Joseph's Cathedral.  The following morning we experienced a cyclo ride through empty streets (5.30am) and what a different view of Hanoi.  We saw the flag raising at the Mausoleum and then experienced local Pho noodle breakfast - not to be missed. And our final stop was the Hoan Kiem Lake and the Ngoc Son Temple. We were only in Hanoi for a few days, but managed to see all of the highlights.  And not to be missed was Train Street - which we were able to time perfectly with a track side seat in a local cafe, and an experience most definitely not to be missed.  All in all we had a wonderful time in Hanoi, and stayed in a wonderful hotel - The Capella.

reviews.author: Jeremy C
reviews.title: Charmingly Chaotic
reviews.content: All the noise, colour and activity is something of a shock to the senses and with so much to see my advice is take a deep breath, walk slowly (you might not much choice on that one) and look around and when it comes to crossing the road: -- step out confidently.- maintain a steady pace.- walk a straight line.- do not stop or try to turn back.Once you start you will have been spotted and the traffic is honour bound to drive around you and not over you and you will make it.I wouldn't want to live here but for a couple of days, what an experience.

reviews.author: Damian Byrd
reviews.title: Chaotic Crosswalk
reviews.content: The area was crowded, and crossing the street felt somewhat risky—vehicles zipped by with little regard for pedestrians, making it tricky to navigate safely through the busy traffic.

reviews.author: Christina Z
reviews.title: The Old Quarter is best for first time visitors to Hanoi
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is the best place to stay for first time travelers to Hanoi or for a mix of sightseeing, shopping, walking around  the Hoan Kiem Lake and relaxation amid noisy streets. The Old Quarter is alive far from the quiet atmosphere around the West Lake area. Don’t forget to haggle with  vendors who sell their wares at 100 to 150 percent up the price. When eating out along the small restaurants that line the streets be aware that the price on the menu is different from the final bill where they add 10 percent  more supposedly as service charge. Lastly, use grab when going around as many taxi drivers tend to scam tourists, well, even the one who was commissioned by our hotel to bring us to the airport. Also, be careful in crossing the street as motorbikes and cars hardly stop to give way to pedestrians.

reviews.author: Ivan
reviews.title: Nothing to see
reviews.content: Just a lot of shops with cheap knockoff clothes.  Ton of people and scooters. Bad air and terrible noise. There isn't much to do unless you want to buy a knockoff Beckham jersey or want to get ran over by a scooter. You won't miss out if you don't visit.

reviews.author: Fico R
reviews.title: Stability is necessary! Shop carefully!
reviews.content: There is so much to shop for! Prices are generally similar, so if you adjust well, you can buy at a decent price. However, there are places where things are not in good condition, check carefully before buying!

reviews.author: Steve_Grant1
reviews.title: Nice area
reviews.content: This is a nice area that is well worth visiting. Before walking we took a ride on a Tuk Tuk through and this was very pleasant. Recommended,

reviews.author: Mr9xx
reviews.title: Street View
reviews.content: Spring in Hanoi!A lovely place with street coffee everywhere.Traffic jams can be difficult to manage, but it’s all part of the city’s energy.I’ll bring my family here to visit soon.

reviews.author: Shoshanna O
reviews.title: Chaotic charm: scooters, smiles & smart bargains
reviews.content: What a thrilling, chaotic whirlwind of a city! If you love the buzz of crowds and the electrifying madness of streets alive with scooters weaving like schools of fish, you’ll adore it. The people are genuinely warm and kind—smiles everywhere—but stay sharp when shopping! Ask around, compare prices, and don’t be afraid to bargain; it’s all part of the vibrant, exhilarating dance of daily life here.

reviews.author: caroleen78
reviews.title: Crawling
reviews.content: Our first day in Vietnam the capital 10 million inhabitants and 7 million scooters ...It honks from everywhere pedestrian cars bicycles and scooters omnipresent in this capital.We had taken a hotel in the old town central point and stayed two days doing the tourist activities and walking around the city. The train street, the reconstituted sword garden, puppets on the water, neighborhood restaurants and especially a catfish restaurant, a canteen with plastic stools where we ate very well. Another show the quintessence of tonkin is 40 minutes from Hanoi, temples, pagodas, communal houses. The city is very safe, no beggars! Everyone's on their own in a joyous, teeming folklore. That's really the word that describes this town. A foot massage for 30 minutes very pleasant and a manicure for 15€.Getting lost in the city with a smile...

reviews.author: Abbie Kelly
reviews.title: Vibrant streets, endless charm
reviews.content: It’s brimming with energy—packed with locals and travelers alike, dotted with travel agencies, cozy cafés, inviting restaurants, soothing massage spots, and striking architecture that’s full of character.

reviews.author: Aurea UK
reviews.title: Stroll through Hanoi’s soul
reviews.content: Enjoy a relaxed walk through the lively streets and soak in the vibrant atmosphere of Northern Vietnam’s capital.!!!!

reviews.author: Dim DeL
reviews.title: Hanoi old quarter
reviews.content: Buzzing with scooters, markets, and local life, the Old Quarter offers a fascinating glimpse into Hanoi’s culture and traditions.Don't overnight there if you can't stand the noise!!

reviews.author: Joell Louise
reviews.title: Night market & beer street magic!
reviews.content: This place is absolutely vibrant and full of life! The atmosphere is electric, especially as the sun goes down. The night market buzzes with colorful stalls, mouthwatering street food, and local crafts, while Beer Street comes alive with laughter, clinking glasses, and a laid-back yet energetic vibe that’s impossible to resist. Whether you're a foodie, a culture seeker, or just looking to soak in the local scene, this is a must-visit destination!

reviews.author: lindagn1
reviews.title: Amazing City - Do not skip
reviews.content: A must visit.  I didn't do a tour.  We just planned our trip around food. :)You cannot come to Hanoi and not visit/stay in the Old Quarter.  Tue An has the BEST pho I've ever had, sorry mom.  North style Pho hits different.  Stay within walking distance of the lake and you've got access to cafes, shops, restaurants, people watching, etc.  Such a lively city and seems to change every time I visit.  Keep your eyes peeled when you go out at night, as it's a different experience during the day.  The shopping here is much better (cheaper) than in the south.  Negotiations are expected but don't low ball them, as they are trying to run a business.  I can't wait to come back.  Notable places: Tue An for pho, 4Ps for pizza, Bun Cha (Obama), Ha Noi Croissant and Coffee (hot coconut coffee), Tam Vi (best food).

reviews.author: Josh
reviews.title: Very Chaotic but Organized and Charming!
reviews.content: Vietnam is a beautiful country, and the Old Quarter is one gem out of many in Vietnam. The streets are very, very busy, not a lot of personal space. However, if you just embrace the culture and go with the flow, it’ll be very smooth. This is a MUST go to when you are here in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Amber C
reviews.title: nice but wear a mask
reviews.content: Nice for shopping (try local fruits, coffee, food, souvenir, and more), but very crowded. I would wear a mask because of all the waste gas from motorbikes and cars.

reviews.author: Barret Hampton

reviews.content: What a vibrant, joyful corner of the city! Bursting with cozy little bars and the infectious energy of people having a great time—it’s impossible not to smile as you wander through. Don’t miss it, even if just for a magical evening stroll through this utterly charming neighborhood! 🌃

You still have to see him to understand that life is not rosy for everyone. Go off the beaten track.

reviews.author: Mandel Williams
reviews.title: A sensory delight!
reviews.content: Hoan Kiem Lake radiates timeless charm, surrounded by bustling pedestrian streets alive with energy! Every corner invites discovery—sizzling street food stalls, delightful souvenir shops, the majestic Cathedral, and so much more. It’s an absolute feast for the senses and the soul!

reviews.author: Albertina Sol
reviews.title: Hanoi’s happiest hideaway!
reviews.content: An absolutely delightful place to unwind! The vibrant night market is perfect for browsing and buying, the food is mouthwatering, and the massages are pure bliss—everything here just feels joyful. Without a doubt, it’s the happiest, most uplifting spot in all of Hanoi! 🌟

reviews.author: Culture201920
reviews.title: Magical and Vibrant
reviews.content: The Old Quarter in Hanoi is an absolute must-see! The narrow streets are full of life, amazing street food, local shops, and so much character. Every corner has something interesting to discover. Yes, it's busy and chaotic, but that's part of the charm. The energy is incredible, the food is delicious, and the people are welcoming. Don't miss the evening atmosphere – it's truly magical. One of the highlights of our Vietnam trip!

reviews.author: Travel@1964

reviews.author: Durga M

reviews.author: Marni Lowis

reviews.author: Celia Cicilia

We wandered for hours, utterly enchanted, tasting pho that tasted like home and breathing in the city’s raw, joyful energy. It’s chaotic, lively, and beautifully overwhelming—in the very best way. This is the heartbeat of Hanoi, and we loved every second of it!

reviews.author: Brander Vance
reviews.title: Explore the heart of culture & cuisine
reviews.content: A lively blend of culture and history—with plenty to see and delicious food to enjoy! Absolutely worth exploring. I went last week and loved wandering through the streets.

reviews.author: Marshal A

reviews.content: A delightful neighborhood—best enjoyed from a corner café soaking in the ambiance. That said, the streets are buzzing with motorbikes and the sidewalks are uneven, making leisurely walks a bit tricky.

reviews.author: skid g

reviews.author: Pauly-101

reviews.title: A beautiful discovery
reviews.content: Come and discover this picturesque neighborhood.You will be able to roam the alleys avoiding motorcycles , bicycles or taxis .dozens of restaurants , massage parlours and all kinds of souvenir shops in the evening the whole streets turn into a restaurant terraceFrom Friday to Sunday evening you can visit the night walk where you will have the choice to find all kinds of booth shoes souvenir clothes etc...

reviews.author: Shyamal B
reviews.title: Enchanting Hanoi Old Quarter at Night in the Rain
reviews.content: It rains and rains hard in Hanoi...don’t let the rain stop you; it makes the experience even more special!...stroll in the streets of Hanoi’s Old Quarter at night, it is absolutely magical, and the rain only adds to its charm. The streets glisten under the soft glow of lanterns and neon signs, creating a romantic and vibrant atmosphere. The sound of raindrops mixing with the hum of scooters and chatter from cozy cafés makes the experience unforgettable. Walking through the narrow lanes, the countless street food stalls serving steaming bowls of pho, sizzling skewers, and sweet treats, the air filled up with the aroma of fresh herbs and grilled meat, so tempting as we passed through. Small shops selling souvenirs, shoes and sandals, and handmade crafts, some closes early and some  stay open late, making it perfect for a leisurely stroll.We enjoyed a warm cup of Vietnamese coffee by the side of the lake watching the rain fall, it’s pure bliss. The Old Quarter in the rain feels like stepping into a living postcard—colorful, lively, and full of character.

reviews.author: AbhimanyuSinghi
reviews.title: Old City Charms
reviews.content: This part of Hanoi is famous for its old city charms. For an Indian its like Purani Dili. Crowded with lots of cheap shopping options where you need to bargain like crazy. Difficult to get around in a car. So you need to stop at one place and then walk around the area to actually enjoy it.

reviews.author: Bertrand C
reviews.title: Cleanliness, catch-up economy. Each for himself.
reviews.content: Having been born in Saigon 60 years ago, the culture of cleanliness is still not there.The city is noisy, and the traffic is each for himself. A lady fell on the roadway, with her child in her arms, no one stops to help her. People with their motorcycles go forward without yielding. Too bad.

reviews.author: tesh
reviews.title: Old quarter Hanoi
reviews.content: It’s been a pleasure visiting Hanoi’s old quarter ,places like Ho Chi Minh & Ninh binh was great experience.I highly recommend taking the half day Jeep tours in Hanoi it’s arguably the most underrated yet one off the best things to do .

reviews.author: Valentina
reviews.title: A place to come back
reviews.content: We stayed there for a few days before catching a bus to Ha Giang loop, the city, which feels a bit too touristic, but it also has lots of local stalls, shops, and restaurants. Additionally, our hostel is just a short walk from the lake, and we enjoy walking around it.

reviews.author: Bree S
reviews.title: The vibrant soul of old Hanoi
reviews.content: Hanoi’s old quarter is full of history, culture and energy. Narrow alleys, shops, cafes and street food make it an ideal place to explore on foot. Certainly animated and noisy, but that is all its charm. The combination of ancient architecture and modern life creates a unique atmosphere, typically Hanoi.

reviews.author: Song Mi-rae
reviews.title: Charme of Hanoi Old Town
reviews.content: Hanoi's old town is a vibrant area of history and culture, a city full of continual life. Every narrow alley has shops, cafes, and street food packing cars, which makes it ideal for walking. There's a lot of people and noise, but that's the charm of this place. The combination of old architecture and modern life creates a unique atmosphere where you can feel the true emotion of Hanoi.

reviews.author: 李强
reviews.title: Lost and happy Millennium Street
reviews.content: A few of our friends wandered around Hanoi's old quarter all day, winding down narrow alleys flanked by old French buildings and handicraft shops. The coffee scent is mixed with street rice flour, and it's a retro blockbuster in a snap. Though lost twice, but accidentally found a great little bar! Perfect for friends to walk and talk while immersing themselves in Lao Hanoi fireworks.

reviews.author: Emma
reviews.title: 🏮 A real Vietnamese experience in the heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: A beautiful place full of life! 💛 Hanoi's Old Town is an absolute must for any visitor. The small streets, old houses and colorful street stalls tell so much history. I especially liked the Dong Xuan market – here you can find great bags, souvenirs and friendly sellers who always have a smile on their faces. 🌸 I bought some beautiful gifts for friends here. Just authentic, lively and warm – I will definitely be back! 🇻🇳✨

reviews.author: 渡辺 愛子
reviews.title: Love deepens in a maze of alleyways
reviews.content: Walk hand in hand through narrow alleyways and share Vietnamese coffee. Even in the hustle and bustle, there is quiet time between us. The old town is a fusion of romance and chaos!

reviews.author: browncondo2102
reviews.title: Take a taxi to get there
reviews.content: Tuk Tuk's are really not available to get to this area of Hanoi so I recommend a taxi.  Once you are there, you will see how the Vietnamese people shop and what they buy.  This to me is really not a place for tourists to shop but more for locals.  If you do decide to shop here then the streets are named for what you will find there.  Example: Hang Gai (Silk Street).

reviews.author: Chirag Gupta
reviews.title: Immersing in the Soul of Hanoi: A beautiful Chaos
reviews.content: Stepping into Hanoi's Old Quarter is like entering a living museum of Vietnamese heritage. With its labyrinth of narrow lanes, centuries-old architecture, and vibrant street life, this historic heart of the city captures the true essence of Hanoi. By day, the neighbourhood hums with the energy of daily life—street vendors, scooters weaving through tight alleys, and the aroma of fresh fruits and Vietnamese street food.But it's after dark that the Old Quarter truly comes alive. The transformation is remarkable—softly lit, buzzing cafés, and an almost cinematic glow cast over the colonial facades. The atmosphere becomes electric, yet intimate, offering a deeper connection to the rhythm of local life.For those visiting over the weekend (Friday through Sunday), the night market is a must-experience. Stretching through the main thoroughfares, it’s a delightful blend of food stalls, local crafts, and live performances. More than just a shopping experience, it’s a lively, authentic way to engage with Hanoi's residents and soak in the spirit of Vietnamese culture.

reviews.author: Dhaya M
reviews.title: Vietnam Coffee is love!
reviews.content: I know it is located in Hanoi. But regardless how traffic around the area,  we enjoyed there! We love that everywhere you look there are foods! I super love the coffee, bahn mi and buhn cha!!! Even the sausage and vietnam pizza on the streets where yum!!! Most of the locals are nice too! I will definitely go back!

reviews.author: elfin27
reviews.title: A must see place!
reviews.content: Decided to stay here with other half while visiting other friends who worked in Hanoi. Amazing place. We loved wandering around the lake and the side roads. Lots of charming buildings, snacks, food, fruits, drinks, shopping.

reviews.author: Morrissey
reviews.title: It's not a tourist spot, it's a real people breath.
reviews.content: I mention it here because it is a tourist destination, but the beauty of Hanoi's Old Quarter is that it is a city for residents that is never flattered by foreigners. It's exciting just to walk around and see all the vegetables, fish and meat that are sold on the road. It's a good idea to venture into the labyrinthine alleys alone.

reviews.author: Cordy
reviews.title: A labyrinth of love and lantern light
reviews.content: The scent of street food, the hum of motorbikes, and colorful silk lanterns above—every corner felt like a shared secret. Quaint cafes and hidden temples made perfect pauses between laughs. It’s chaotic, yes, but together, it felt like magic.

reviews.author: みるく
reviews.title: I want you to experience it.
reviews.content: I was staying in a hotel in the old city of Vietnam, so I spent time feeling the power of the old city. Bike waves, tremendous horns, , (although noisy at night) lively and awesome!! You can also enjoy the traditional cityscape.

reviews.author: Xing H
reviews.title: Romantic Encounters Between Ancient Rhymes and Night
reviews.content: We both indulged in the traditional architecture of the Old Town as if we were going through time. Stroll through narrow alleys by day and indulge in vibrant nightlife at night, with street stalls scented and beer bars music. The combination of ancient and modern makes our world of two more poetic and is definitely a romantic place for couples to visit!

reviews.author: Masela Fadjar Pratiwi
reviews.title: Festive Charm of Hanoi’s Old Quarter During Tet
reviews.content: Visiting Hanoi's Old Quarter during the Tet Festival is a vibrant experience. The streets are full with colorful decorations. Many of shops, making it an excellent destination for shopping enthusiasts. Additionally, there is a wide array of restaurants and cafes offering diverse culinary options. The pleasant weather during this period further enhances the experience, as the Old Quarter becomes a hub of activity, attracting visitors who come to immerse themselves in the cultural festivities.Overall, experiencing the Old Quarter during Tet offers a unique insight into Vietnamese culture and traditions, making it a memorable visit for anyone in Hanoi during this festive season.

reviews.author: Huntington Cindy
reviews.title: The Old charm
reviews.content: Timeless charm meets vibrant energy, with an abundance of delicious food, refreshing local beer, unique shopping finds, and historic atmosphere—all available in endless supply. Whether you're strolling through cobbled streets or hopping between cafés and boutiques, there's something for everyone.

reviews.author: rahul
reviews.title: Crowded
reviews.content: Crowded, hustle and bustle, and have to endure lot of heat. have to be careful with interacting people otherwise be ready to lose money.

reviews.author: J.Colodoveo
reviews.content: On my second day in Hanoi, after work, I went to visit the Old Quarter. First of all, the weather here was extremely hot and dusty. I was wandering around wanting to buy gifts for my two young daughters when I saw two saleswomen arguing over customers. It was horrible!

reviews.author: francesca g
reviews.title: The chaos that fascinates
reviews.content: Not to be missed if you are in Hanoi. The experience is worth the incredible chaos that characterizes it. Low tables and chairs / stool for food scattered everywhere, restaurants, shops, beauty spa, nails and on the backrooms some faux luxury well done... watch out for the life moped and cars do not stop even on the strips... crossing the road puts a derà anxiety, this is the old town that fascinates. There are also beautiful and very quiet hotels just look...better if a 5 star! From here you reach everything

reviews.author: Safari50371395366
reviews.title: Hà Nội
reviews.content: We are really like here with good food, nice people, friendly ,many place we visited there,but too much traffic jam here.

reviews.author: Lee K
reviews.title: Great

The streets are full of energy, with scooters buzzing past, vendors calling out, and the delicious smell of street food everywhere. Every corner feels like a piece of living history, from the ancient architecture to the small family-run shops that have been there for generations.

reviews.author: wang2383

reviews.author: linece91
reviews.title: Must-see
reviews.content: First night in Vietnam. A joyful bazaar of street food, scooters everywhere and in all directions.Numerous clothing and other shops by neighbourhood A quick dive into the universe of this country that did not leave us indifferent throughout our 14-day stay. Not to mention the train street which is really amazing

reviews.author: Harlene L
reviews.content: The traditional architecture, with its narrow shophouses and French colonial touches, whispered stories of the past. But it was the vibrant art scene that truly captivated us—hidden galleries, colorful murals, and spontaneous performances added a modern pulse to this historic heart.

reviews.author: Holt Sour
reviews.title: Charming streets and warm smiles
reviews.content: A maze of hidden gems—tiny cafés, local shops, and peaceful courtyards tucked between the hustle. The friendly locals made us feel welcome, offering smiles and tips that turned our trip into a heartfelt adventure. A must-visit for travelers who love authentic charm.

reviews.author: Giuseppe S
reviews.title: Wonderful.
reviews.content: Located in Hoan Kiem Urban District, a short distance from Hoan Kiem Lake, Hanoi Old Quarter – The Old Quarter – represents Hanoi’s Old Town.Located in the vicinity of the Imperial Citadel, Old Quarter was the main commercial center of the city.

reviews.author: Eliane S
reviews.title: Extraordinary journey!
reviews.content: The Old Quarter of HanoiHalong BayHOI AN and the Lantern Festival (full moon)SAPA etc......Extraordinary!!!!@

reviews.author: Oby L
reviews.title: Explore the vibrant cityscape with your family!
reviews.content: I was really surprised by the vibrancy of the old town! It was a bit overwhelming at first, with so many bikes and people, but I also felt that was a very Hanoi attraction. It was a lot of fun to explore the city with my family, looking for delicious food and choosing souvenirs.

reviews.author: Deva Venga
reviews.title: You dont need a ticket to visit this place
reviews.content: Great food and great shopping.Dont be ripped off without a bargain.Haggle everything.. yes that's right everything unless its the food items at the foodaries.You will be surprised what you can get away with.

reviews.author: BalkrishnaShroff
reviews.title: Not to be missed in Hanoi !!
reviews.content: After finishing our daytime sightseeing, we were brought here by our guide. We were 30 of us. We got down and took cycle rikshaw since the streets are so narrow that big buses can't go inside. Only two adults can sit in rikshaw. Old Quarter is a combination of 40 streets who once upon a time used to sell different crafts. It was a great fun to ride in a rikshaw going through many streets enjoying the cultural and  historical architecture of Hanoi. Certain streets are almost for pedestrians with bars and restaurants on both sides. The entire area was very crowded with great vibe. It was full of life. After sometime we got down and settled in a restaurant for drinks and dinner. No doubt it was the best attraction of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Neile Nuri
reviews.title: An intoxicating maze where we loved each other! ❤️
reviews.content: The incessant ballet of the scooters, the smells of street food and the smiles of the inhabitants create a unique atmosphere. Each alley hidden a charming café or craft shop, perfect for our moments together.

reviews.author: Hallie J
reviews.title: Crowded, Noisy but worth a visit!
reviews.content: We stayed here for 2 nights. It's very crowded and busy with lot of scooters, but an amazing city with lot of things to see. It's safe to walk around at night to anywhere you go. Lot of good & cheap restaurants with great food to try. It's different from any cities we have ever visited.

reviews.author: Maarten V
reviews.title: The Old Quarter in Hanoi is definitely a unique place
reviews.content: The Old Quarter in Hanoi is definitely a unique place with a lot of character. The narrow streets, old buildings, and buzzing atmosphere give you a real sense of local life and history. There’s always something happening, and the street food is a highlight – delicious and cheap!However, it can be overwhelming. The traffic is intense, with motorbikes coming from all directions, and walking around can feel chaotic and stressful at times. It’s also quite noisy and crowded, especially in the evenings.Overall, it’s worth a visit for the experience, but be prepared for the hustle and bustle. Not ideal if you’re looking for peace and quiet.

reviews.author: Strike_right
reviews.title: Old Quarter, Hanoi on a Weekend Night
reviews.content: If you're in Hanoi on a weekend night, the **Old Quarter** becomes an unforgettable experience—a vibrant, chaotic, and deeply atmospheric immersion into Vietnamese urban life.### 🌃 AtmosphereAs night falls, the Old Quarter transforms. What by day is already a busy maze of narrow streets turns into a carnival of colors, sounds, and smells. Streets are closed to vehicles from Friday to Sunday night, allowing crowds to spill into the roads. The air buzzes with live music, laughter, and the clang of street vendors preparing food. Bright lights from lanterns, beer stalls, and souvenir shops give the place a magical, almost surreal energy.### 🍜 Street Food & DrinksThis is a paradise for food lovers. You'll find everything from steaming bowls of *pho* and sizzling *banh xeo* to exotic snacks like grilled quail eggs and sweet sticky rice. Plastic stools crowd the sidewalks where locals and tourists sit elbow-to-elbow drinking *bia hoi* (fresh beer) for less than a dollar. For those feeling adventurous, the food tour possibilities are endless—and delicious.### 🎶 Entertainment & CultureThere’s live music in the street, both traditional and contemporary. Impromptu dance circles form around performers playing Vietnamese instruments or acoustic guitars. The weekend night market, stretching from Hang Dao Street to Dong Xuan Market, offers clothes, handicrafts, and quirky souvenirs, often at bargain prices.### 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Crowd & VibeExpect crowds—lots of them. It’s loud, energetic, and sometimes overwhelming, but that’s part of the charm. You’ll see families, young locals, travelers, and backpackers all mixing in one pulsating cultural cocktail. While it’s generally safe, watch your belongings and avoid scams, especially around bar areas.### 💬 Final ThoughtsA weekend night in Hanoi’s Old Quarter isn’t just an activity—it’s an **experience**. Whether you’re sipping beer on a low stool, listening to a street band, or weaving through the market crowds, it offers a rare blend of sensory overload and authentic cultural engagement. Not for the faint of heart, but absolutely essential for anyone wanting to feel the true heartbeat of Hanoi.**Rating: 9/10**(Best enjoyed with open senses and a flexible schedule.)

reviews.author: Susan L
reviews.title: Hanoi in June hot and humid
reviews.content: Hanoi temperature and humidity very high, keep up fluid and electrolyte intake. Take care when walking to avoid the many uneven surfaces. Hold on to your belongings. Grab is a cheap alternative if you are tired from walking. Train street is interesting, as are the various streets, selling lots of same same. 2-3 days is more than enough.

reviews.author: Joe C
reviews.title: Hanoi's Old Quarter Soul
reviews.content: Hanoi's Old Quarter pulses with history and charm. Wander its narrow streets, sample street food, and browse traditional shops for an authentic taste of Vietnamese culture. Don't miss this essential district to truly experience Hanoi's soul.

reviews.author: Annalise Cole
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Hanoi Old Quarter is amazing, especially on weekend nights (after 7 pm) when it's a walking street around Hoan Kiem Lake. Full of history and tradition. Worth a visit!

reviews.author: Keen Louie
reviews.title: Great vibe, watch for traffic
reviews.content: The atmosphere was incredible, making for a great overall experience. Just be mindful of the somewhat chaotic traffic, particularly if you're on foot.

reviews.author: Windy2512
reviews.title: Good vide
reviews.content: Every weekend, there would be a night market, but unfortunately, when we were there, it was raining heavily. But overall experience was great! But be careful with the traffic around. A little bit chaotic, especially for the pedestrian.

reviews.author: Sebrina
reviews.title: Must-try vietnamese delights: pho, banh mi, and egg coffee!
reviews.content: The food here is fantastic! Don't miss the famous pho and delicious banh mi from street vendors, and be sure to try the renowned egg coffee at cozy cafés!

reviews.author: Dion P
reviews.title: Bustle and hustle area.
reviews.content: Visiting Hanoi Old Quarter was a whirlwind of energy, sights, and sounds that I won’t forget. The narrow streets were always buzzing—scooters weaving through traffic, street vendors calling out, and the constant hum of life all around. It felt chaotic at first, but there was a rhythm to it that grew on me quickly.I loved wandering through the maze of alleys, discovering hidden cafes, old temples, and tiny shops selling everything from handmade crafts to street food. The smell of pho, grilled meats, and fresh herbs filled the air—it was a feast for the senses. The Old Quarter has this gritty charm that’s both intense and fascinating. It’s not polished, but that’s what makes it feel so real. Every corner had something new to see or taste. It was overwhelming at times, but completely unforgettable.

reviews.author: Paton Kante
reviews.title: Unique culture
reviews.content: The old town was incredible! We could’ve easily spent days soaking up its unique atmosphere. We will definitely come back for sure.

reviews.author: Sightseer51244447655
reviews.title: Aah the old quarter of Hanoi...
reviews.content: Each street is a "specialty" of craftsmen... street of cooks, street of bamboo, wood craftsmen...the lake of the sword restored... and the street of the train.There is so much to see, and to buy!

reviews.author: Lacy Henna
reviews.title: A must-visit
reviews.content: Hanoi's Old Quarter is a vibrant historic district known for its narrow streets, bustling markets, and iconic Vietnamese dishes like pho and banh mi. Blending tradition with modern charm, it features ancient temples, boutique shops, and a lively weekend night market. A must-visit, it offers a rich glimpse into Hanoi's culture and heritage.

reviews.author: Cleve A
reviews.title: Perfect Vietnam Experience – From Street Food to Ba Be Lake!
reviews.content: Our Vietnam trip was full of surprises and amazing moments, thanks to BC Family Tour. We started with the Hanoi Street Food Adventure, and it was fantastic! The guide was friendly and spoke great English. He took us to try many local dishes we never knew existed — all super yummy and very clean. Everything was organized perfectly, we didn’t have to worry about a thing.Then we did a trip to Ba Be Lake, and it was one of the most peaceful places we’ve ever been. The itinerary was smooth, accommodation was lovely, especially the soft bed! Our guide was professional and told us beautiful stories about the people and the area. A huge thanks to Daisy, Sam, Le, driver Minh, and the Luxia team for helping us save so much money. We were 11 people and booked a very cheap but high-quality tour with comfortable and safe transportation.We booked all our tours through bcfamilytour.com, which is now our go-to site for Vietnam. We also recommend contacting them directly via WhatsApp: +84886559609. 10/10 service!

reviews.author: Conan Billy
reviews.title: Charming place
reviews.content: This place offers an amazing atmosphere with a vibrant and lively setting. There are numerous seating options, including tables halfway down, allowing for a comfortable dining experience. The food is delicious, catering to a variety of tastes, and the overall vibe is fun and inviting.

reviews.author: Norway Ken Jesus
reviews.title: The Heart of Hanoi – Where Culture, Chaos, and Food Collide
reviews.content: Staying in the Old Quarter was probably the best decision we made in Hanoi. It’s where you feel the pulse of the city—no filters, just pure local life. From the early morning buzz of vendors to the late-night street barbecues, this district offers a full immersion into the Hanoi experience.There’s an endless lineup of coffee shops tucked into corners, streets lined with pho stalls and smoky barbecue grills, and more than enough cheap local buys. You’ll constantly be surrounded by movement and noise, but it’s all part of what makes the Old Quarter unforgettable.Tips for travelers:	•	Bring comfy shoes—you’re walking a lot here.	•	Don’t hesitate to sit on those tiny stools at street food spots; that’s where the best meals are.	•	Mornings are a little quieter if you want to ease into it.	•	It gets lively at night—perfect if you want a street food crawl.

reviews.author: AMsays
reviews.title: What a Wonderful City....
reviews.content: Hanoi’s Old Quarter is sensory overload, mayhem really, but it works. You can’t escape the honking motorbikes, petroleum smells, food stalls, sidewalk hustle, unique buildings and more. It is vibrant, colourful and lively. Restaurants abound, so too markets, hotels, tourist stops and even more. Watch yourself crossing at chaotic corners where screeching traffic comes from all sides. But still, what a wonderful city….,

reviews.author: Nadya Henry
reviews.title: Beautiful and vibrant
reviews.content: Great area to stay in with easy access to food, tourist attractions, and the French Quarter. Plenty of hotels and spas nearby, plus a night market and excellent dining options. It’s lively and vibrant, making it a fantastic choice for experiencing the city center.

reviews.author: Boycey dean
reviews.title: Great place!
reviews.content: It's a great place to wander and explore the streets. There are countless small shops and restaurants. A must-visit when you're in Hanoi!

reviews.author: Clerissa Dario
reviews.title: Chaotic yet interesting
reviews.content: Hanoi's Old Quarter thrums with chaotic energy—endless honking, roaring café music, and gridlocked traffic crescendo at night. Yet this messy vitality is precisely what gives the neighborhood its soul.

reviews.author: Phil R
reviews.title: Hectic
reviews.content: Another example of a hectic old part of a city.  You need to take your time and explore slowly.  Visit at different times, early morning in the calm, the chaos of the day and then the nighttime activities

reviews.author: Richard P
reviews.title: Old Quarter comes to life after 6pm
reviews.content: Old Quarter comes to life after 6pm especially near Hang Bac, Ta Hien street and 'Beer corner' virtually everywhere it is either a bar or a restaurant, often spilling out into the road, car drivers often at a standstill as a result of the crowds and tables.Food is excellent and abundant, our favourite was the Bar-b-que for two, (three, four) people, cooked on a slow heated dish in front of you coupled with a couple of beers, excellent! all at stupid prices, so incredibly cheap!

reviews.author: Rodrigo Elsie
reviews.title: Chaotic in the best way

You can also enjoy tasty local Vietnamese food with the guide's help in choosing. I strongly recommend having a guide, as they are very helpful.

reviews.author: 坂本 由美
reviews.title: Review Body:
reviews.content: I visited Hanoi Old Quarter for the first time. The local pho and banh mi are also excellent, making it a fun area to just walk around.It is a tourist destination, but it is also a place where people can feel their lives. It is also a great place for adult women to walk around town.

reviews.author: John N
reviews.title: Great place to explore
reviews.content: Wow great area to stay in, so many wonderful options and affordable food! Most things close at 10pm and open at 7am. There are so many areas dedicated to textiles, foods, souvenirs all kinds of fun things to do and areas to explore

reviews.author: Maxie Bunz
reviews.title: Interesting place
reviews.content: Vibrant and vivid, it stands out as a captivating destination. Packed with stores, street eateries, and cafés, the ongoing hustle and bustle creates a delightful atmosphere.

reviews.author: BarbAndJohnB
reviews.title: Great Area to Immerse Yourself in Hanoi
reviews.content: Such a bustling part of town! Within walking distance to Train Street and Hoan Kiem Lake. Lots of great restaurants, cafes, markets, and bars. Plenty of fun things to do around here.

reviews.author: Raye B
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: The area has almost everything you want. The hotel was pretty nice and affordable in this area. A lot of tourists and busy most of the time

reviews.author: Susie D

In this neighborhood the Vietnamese in this neighborhood are not very friendly

reviews.author: Todd S

reviews.content: The Old Quarter experience was an incredibly good adventure in living amidst the mass of humanity and motorbikes. But to see the Hanoi residents living their daily life was such an enjoyable experience that I enjoyed being a part of during our visit for a week.

reviews.author: Curious56604451762

reviews.content: A fascinating labyrinth of narrow streets, old houses and lively clubs. The atmosphere is authentic and full of life. Sometimes it can be crowded and noisy, but it is still a must-see to discover the soul of Hanoi!

reviews.author: Atonie Dupont

reviews.content: I really wanted to love Hanoi’s Old Quarter, but honestly, it was a bit too chaotic for me. If you enjoy a fast-paced, noisy, and packed environment, you might love it. But if you prefer a more relaxed vibe, this place can be overwhelming.

reviews.author: aurlea1963

reviews.author: Foodie_Bakabon

reviews.author: SB01

reviews.content: My son and I spent 3 days in 2 hotels in the old Town. We could easily have spent a couple more days as there is so much to see and do. I don’t think I’ve ever been anywhere like this and for sure it won’t be for everyone. Yes, it’s dirty, noisy, chaotic, overcrowded. But it’s also friendly, authentic, great value, colourful and buzzing. The old quarter is a compact area, but other interesting sites - West Lake, the French Quarter, Ho Chi Min’s mausoleum are all within walking distance, or a low cost Grab - so it makes a good base. There are lots of good places to eat, with decent meals being available for less than £10/head. Or go for a blowout on one of the rooftop bars, where you may spend £30-40/ head. There are plenty of bars with beer around £1 a pint. You can pay less in the very congested bia street, but this is also the one part of the area that feels a bit sleazy and where you might get hustled to buy things. At night stroll over to train street and join the crowd flirting with disaster.

reviews.author: Voyage60924171737
reviews.title: Charming & Full of History
reviews.content: Old Quarter of Hanoi is full of life and culture! The narrow streets, local shops, and street food make it a unique experience. A great place to soak in the atmosphere and explore Vietnam’s rich heritage!

reviews.author: GIZMOKI
reviews.title: In Vietnam it is to stop sidewalk bikes.
reviews.content: In Vietnam sidewalks are there to stop bikes. You can't walk in Vietnam unless you get used to walking on the road. I think the old town is Hanoi, which is the original. There are no big hotels in the old town. But there are many nice small hotels, good shops and Vietnamese shops. Please enjoy it.

reviews.author: NickGi
reviews.title: I have visited many city in the world, each are special - but Hanoi has a number of different experiences.
reviews.content: The old part of Hanoi is the hart of the city. I personally would advise to stay in a hotel just outside of the old quarter because it is very busy and load. The streets and old architecture are wonderful to look at. We stayed for 7 days and could explore most of the the places to go. If you enjoy the exciting pace, are used to busy city’s and want the next level, then Hanoi is for you. Trying to cross a road is an experience you need to do , but be careful!! If your an experienced traveler in Asia you will be fine alone , if not use a guide!!!! Train Street will definitely blow your mind !!! Fantastic city to visit for at least 3 days.

reviews.author: Dana A-C
reviews.title: Good Old Hanoi
reviews.content: Love the city, it's fast, and same time so calm living. People are amazing. There is so much to love there. Love to walk along streets of Old town.

reviews.author: Sue M
reviews.title: Best to See from an Electric Golf Cart
reviews.content: This is a colorful and very busy, old section of Hanoi.  Viking made arrangements for us to ride in golf carts with a driver well versed in negotiating the traffic of mopeds, hand pulled carts, pedestrians, etc.  It was a lot of fun to ride around in an open vehicle, not traveling very fast, taking in the sights.

reviews.author: akio9jp
reviews.title: Good old townscape
reviews.content: Various shops are lined up in a miscellaneous manner, and products are arranged so that they protrude from the storefront. Motorcycles are also cluttered on the sidewalk, so you have to walk along the roadway. I was scared until I got used to it, because of the constant traffic of cars and motorbikes.Motorcycle engines and horns are loud, but this hustle and bustle may symbolize the vibrancy of Vietnam.

reviews.author: alessandra_biondi3
reviews.title: Hanoi, beautiful town
reviews.content: Hanoi is divided into two parts, one modern and the other ancient. The old part is preferable, I liked it more for the activities and the few architectural evidence of its history..

reviews.author: vinayak
reviews.title: Old quarter walk
reviews.content: You should definitely walk around here and explore the region, lots of small shopping centres with really cool stuff, preferably take a walk instead of a scooter

reviews.author: Chang C
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.content: Nice place. We came here on weekend so they have the night market with a lot of things you can buy. A place you should walk around when you come here

reviews.author: francesco b
reviews.title: calm chaos
reviews.content: funny for the amount of people, shops, street vendors, bikes, scooters, restaurants, etc. You get lost, in the literal sense of the word!

reviews.author: gfsc5
reviews.title: Chaotic delight
reviews.content: Situated at the northern end of Hoan Kiem Lake, the Old Quarter is a must-see destination for tourists.  Chaos abounds with motor bikes and scooters parked over the footpaths and whizzing along the streets with gay abandon.  They do tend to avoid running into people so the trick to crossing a road is to look straight ahead and walk at a steady pace from one side to the other.  Don't try to dodge them - they'll dodge you.Apart from the traffic (and the large number of people) there is lots to see.  Small shops abound with many of the streets specialising in particular goods whether that be silk or paper/decorations or shoes or whatever.  There is no grid pattern in the streets so it’s easy to get disoriented and lost.  That’s part of the adventure, of course.A great place to visit.

reviews.author: OnAir38937315268
reviews.title: Bursting With Energy
reviews.content: Full of locals and tourists, the streets exude energy as well as all manner of retail (including many places to get massages and similar treatments). Though known as the French Quarter, there's not much left of French architecture, but it has that rabbit warren of streets vibe and is great fun. Spend a few hours walking round, or get a pedicab tour.

reviews.author: Le Jardin Haute Couture
reviews.title: Hanoi old quarter
reviews.content: Hanoi's Old Quarter: Chaotic charm! Buzzing streets, delicious street food, and hidden temples. A sensory overload, but a must-see for its vibrant, historic atmosphere.

reviews.author: PatB56
reviews.title: A walking tour to do
reviews.content: Must do during a stay in Hanoi.Walking in this district of a corporation allows you to soak up local life during a quiet walk.

reviews.author: S&O
reviews.title: Time travel
reviews.content: Woooow! What an interesting city. Like 100 years ago ... ;-). Just let yourself drift and become part of it. Solid footwear is an advantage.

reviews.author: arunabet
reviews.title: Old quarter best
reviews.content: Rame, good for walking, nongkrong, jajan, the food price is cheap, lots of cafes too, caves more than the old quarter of hanoi vietnam than china town bangkok anyway.

reviews.author: Joel D
reviews.title: Out and about in Hanoi Old City
reviews.content: Fascinating food, alley ways, culture, people.Lots to see, do and experience by day or night. Go with someone with local knowlege till you get your bearings

reviews.author: Alek - Indonesian Traders
reviews.title: The safe place to make a pedestal
reviews.content: Sorganya for walking tourists. During your stay in Hanoi's Old Quarter area, cheap hotels are available at almost every street corner, even in narrow hallways. Very safe and comfortable. Walking anywhere won't be boring for you!

reviews.author: OmanRob
reviews.title: Greta location to stay
reviews.content: Lots and lots of fake clothing stores but also lots and lots of great places to eat and drink so on balance a lovely place to base yourself on Hanoi - do understand it will be noisy though and bring ear plugs. We chose an Airbnb just north of the lake and this was a pretty much perfect position Rob

reviews.author: Noa H
reviews.title: Amazing food, but chaotic
reviews.content: Street vendors sell everything from pho to bun cha, and the smells are irresistible. It’s an authentic taste of Hanoi. The noise can also be overwhelming at times, with motorbikes zooming by on the sidewalks.

reviews.author: Donaugh Q
reviews.title: Unique culture
reviews.content: Quaint shops lined the narrow streets, each one brimming with character and charm. Around every corner, hidden gems revealed themselves—artisan crafts, aromatic street food, and cozy cafés.

reviews.author: Inspire820983
reviews.title: Stay near The Old Quarter
reviews.content: West Lake was serene and beautiful. Road was closed to traffic on weekends. Weather was nice. Easy to walk around the Old Quarter. Lots of things to do and experience such as local food, sights and also cafe culture

reviews.author: Inger B
reviews.title: Bustling streets
reviews.content: The air was filled with the aroma of street food, and the sounds of laughter and chatter surrounded us. It felt like stepping back in time. We marveled at the ancient architecture, stopping to take photos and soak in the vibrant atmosphere. The markets were a riot of colors, and we haggled over souvenirs, feeling like locals.

reviews.author: Global43434286807
reviews.title: Old Quarter is a must shopping location
reviews.content: The street market is the place to shop. You will get everything from souvenir to clothes and at very reasonable rates. Though you need  bargaining skill..

reviews.author: Isac V
reviews.title: Very fun
reviews.content: We had a good time at old quarter in Vietnam! We tried good foods and saw a lot of local unique stuff. It was a definitely good experience.

reviews.author: Uyên N
reviews.title: Perfect City
reviews.content: Wandering through the charming alleys of Chân Cầm, you can feel the heartbeat of Hanoi come alive. This vibrant street weaves a tapestry of culture and history, where every corner tells a story. The aroma of delicious street food fills the air, mingling with the whispers of the past, creating a unique atmosphere that’s both nostalgic and lively. Chân Cầm is a hidden gem, capturing the essence of Hanoi’s timeless beauty, inviting you to explore its rich heritage and vibrant life…

reviews.author: Yvonne K
reviews.title: Chaos but unmissable
reviews.content: Visiting Old Quarter is a must  it is lively noisy and full of character Yes the motorbikes are annoying and you cannot walk on footpaths as they seem to be the motorbike parking area but it shows the real Hanoi and you soon get used to it waving your hands in an effort to cross the road in a land where traffic lights and zebra crossings are merely artefacts added to street corners with no instructions provided on how they are to be usedNight market provides a wonderful array of goods and crafts which you can haggle for experience street food and meet some wonderful Vietnamese peopleYou can take a break and get refreshments and view the madness that is Old Quarter from a balconyIn my view it is a must

reviews.author: Shafinah J.
reviews.title: A Chaotic Symphony You’ll Want to Get Lost In
reviews.content: The 36 ancient streets that make up Hanoi’s Old Quarter are a maze of chaos and treasures. The streets are narrow and so are the houses, but that doesn’t stop the constant crush of motorbikes and, in an increasing number, cars mixing with bicycles, tourists and rickshaws known as cyclos. Despite the craziness, the Old Quarter should not be missed. Its lanes overflow with everything you need to fill your suitcase back home, from colourful kitschy trinkets to Vietnamese crafts to fine silks to hardwares and more. To fully explore the Old Quarter in Hanoi, prepare your feet for a day of walking street to street and taking in the locals’ daily life amidst these old-style narrow streets and houses. And if you have spare change, dining on these streets is a culinary requisite. more than just a tempting and adventurous bid – it’s actually required for a complete culinary excursion in Hanoi. It doesn’t take much effort to trace down an absolutely great bowl of humble Pho at ridiculously low prices.

reviews.author: Strike_right
reviews.title: Weekend Night Market
reviews.content: Must try at least once. Weekend Night Market is a really interesting,Nice people, no haggling, crowded, bargains welcome, good food.

reviews.author: Dalia U
reviews.title: A must place to walk about and eat
reviews.content: Absolutely a must. Colourful, interesting, fun with lots of restaurants, small shops, little fruit markets and massage parlours. Some French Arquitecture.

reviews.author: Hailey S
reviews.title: Old Quarter in Hanoi
reviews.content: The unique culture is palpable, from the bustling street vendors to the charming cafes. As night fell, the vibrant nightlife came alive, with locals and tourists mingling over delicious street food. We enjoyed exploring the narrow streets, each turn revealing something new. While it can be chaotic, the energy is infectious and made our visit unforgettable. We left with a deeper appreciation for this lively area and its rich history!

reviews.author: Damian A
reviews.title: Bustling street life
reviews.content: Every corner revealed hidden gems, from quaint cafes to local artisans. We loved wandering through narrow alleys, soaking in the lively atmosphere. The scents of street food wafted through the air, tempting us to try everything. While it was crowded, the energy of the place made it all worthwhile. Each moment felt like an adventure, and we left with unforgettable memories and a desire to return.

reviews.author: Giorgio
reviews.title: Night Charm in the Old Town
reviews.content: Rich history is felt in every corner, and vibrant culture completely engulfed us. As night falls, vibrant nightlife comes alive with lights and music. We enjoy romantic walks and delicious street foods. It was an unforgettable experience that captured the essence of Hanoi perfectly. Recommended for couples looking for adventure and charm!

reviews.author: debsum123
reviews.title: Loved Hanoi
reviews.content: I enjoyed Hanoi far more than I expected. The Vietnamese Women’s Museum, the War Jail, Train Street, the food. It was all marvellous! Busy, loud but marvellous!

reviews.author: 이준호
reviews.title: Hanoi Old City Explorer
reviews.content: There were many baby shops, and there was fun watching. But there was nothing as special as I expected. The vibrant night culture was good, but it was too loud to talk. The historical background was interesting, but there was a lot to enjoy as people in North America. Next time we'll find a quieter place!

reviews.author: Slawomir

reviews.author: Ray P
reviews.title: A cultural delight

We immersed ourselves in the unique culture, sampling street food and sipping coffee at cozy cafes. The friendly locals welcomed us with warm smiles, making us feel right at home. Old Quarter is a treasure trove waiting to be discovered!

reviews.author: Nealson Florence
reviews.title: The Charms of Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: The traditional architecture took us back in time, and we loved wandering through the bustling markets. We stumbled upon hidden gems, from quaint cafes to local artisans. The vibrant atmosphere was infectious, and we enjoyed tasting street food along the way. Each corner had a surprise waiting for us, making our trip unforgettable. We can't wait to return!

reviews.author: Fletcher M
reviews.title: Chaotic Walk
reviews.content: The narrow road was full of motorcycles and was magically chaotic. But that's what's interesting again. Cafes all over the place were bustling, and Vietnamese coffee was delicious. It was exciting to feel a vibrant culture, but I was a little tired. Well, it was a good memory.

reviews.author: Myranda W
reviews.title: Charming Atmosphere
reviews.content: We stumbled upon cozy cafes, where we savored the tastiest coffee we've ever had. Each sip was a perfect blend of rich flavors and local charm. The energy of the area, combined with the warm smiles from locals, made our visit truly special. We can't wait to return!

reviews.author: Gabbie V
reviews.title: An Unforgettable Journey to the Ancient Quarter of Hanoi
reviews.content: From the moment we arrived, we felt a peaceful atmosphere, where each alley tells a story. During the day, vibrant markets and lively cafes immersed us in local culture. At night, the magic happens: the twinkling lights and music create a festive atmosphere. We enjoyed tasty dishes while walking hand in hand. This mix of tranquility and vibrant nightlife made our stay an unforgettable one.

reviews.author: $age
reviews.title: Busy, street life galore but touristy
reviews.content: Street life is incredible. Find a spot and order some spicy noodles or a coffee and watch the thousands of scooters speed by!Very touristy though. I estimate half the people in the old quarter were tourists when we were there. I actually prefer the other areas nearby which are less touristy.Shopping is great. Find a a street that seeks what you need, toy street, bag street, light street etc, they have so many streets selling all sorts of cheap quality goods.

reviews.author: Keslie Tee
reviews.title: Chaotic Charm
reviews.content: Rich history oozing from every corner, but also, like, a million scooters. We loved getting lost in the maze of streets, and the bustling cafes were perfect for people-watching. So much energy! Definitely a must-see, even if it's a bit chaotic. We'd go back for the coffee alone!

reviews.author: Lancelot Clinton
reviews.title: Chaos, charm & questionable souvenirs
reviews.content: Hanoi's Old Quarter is a wild ride! One minute we're dodging scooters, the next we're stumbling upon peaceful parks that feel like a different world. The traditional architecture is gorgeous, like stepping back in time, but then BOOM - a motorbike almost takes you out. We spent hours wandering, getting lost in the maze of streets, popping into quaint shops selling everything from silk to questionable "designer" bags. We bought some random stuff, mostly because we were overwhelmed. It’s a sensory overload in the best way. Definitely an experience. Would recommend

reviews.author: 지후 한
reviews.title: Hidden jewels, vibrant culture!
reviews.content: The old town of Hanoi, we were both completely off! There are many shops like hidden jewels, and a lively culture is felt! Every street is full of charming atmosphere, and there is a lot of delicious food! 😋 I want to come again next time! It made you a truly unforgettable memory!

reviews.author: Tety Gints
reviews.title: A Perfect Blend of Old and New!
reviews.content: The Old Quarter in Hanoi is simply enchanting! It’s where history and modernity come together, creating a vibrant atmosphere full of life and charm. The narrow streets, bustling markets, and colonial-era buildings tell stories of the past, while trendy cafes, shops, and street food stalls bring a fresh, modern vibe.If I were a city, I’d probably be the Old Quarter—it feels so alive, full of character, and endlessly fascinating. Wandering these streets made me fall in love with Hanoi. A must-visit for anyone who wants to experience the soul of this incredible city!

reviews.author: Schuyler Wii
reviews.title: Quaint Chaos
reviews.content: We got wonderfully lost in the Old Quarter's narrow streets! Quaint shops spilled onto the sidewalks, a totally eclectic mix of old and new. It was a sensory overload in the best way. Definitely bring your walking shoes (and maybe a map, haha!).

reviews.author: chamilaherath78
reviews.title: Horrible place on earth
reviews.content: Horrible dirty unfriendly city.Don't speak english and very hard to communicate with these people.Never come back.The traffic is really bad.People at shops are very rude.Dirty street food places.We all got sick few times.Even in good hotels the staff is very rude.Not good hospitality.

reviews.author: Jeni Helen
reviews.title: History and modernity.
reviews.content: We lovEd the eclectic mix of old and new, from traditional street food stalls to chic cafes. Every corner offered a new delight, making our time here an unforgettable adventure. It truly felt like a hidden gem waiting to be discovered!

reviews.author: Abdullah Al-Muyeed
reviews.title: My love, Old Quarter Hanoi
reviews.content: The old quarter is my old memorable place. You can have a great Hanoi experience just walking round you. I can see the changes happening in Hanoi, but the Old Quarter is like a place where I shall stay again and again when I visit. Love you, Old Quarter Hanoi...

reviews.author: Krupa R
reviews.title: Exploring the Old Quarter and Night Market in Hanoi: Bargaining is the name of the game
reviews.content: The bustling streets are filled with vendors selling everything from fresh produce and street food to souvenirs and artisanal goods. Walking here, you’ll encounter the heart of Hanoi’s culture: scooters weaving through pedestrians, locals enjoying steaming bowls of pho on tiny plastic stools, and the hum of life that never seems to pause.The Night Market: A Shopper’s ParadiseWhen the sun sets, the Old Quarter transforms, and the night market comes alive. Stretching across Hang Dao Street and its surrounding lanes, this market is a must-visit for anyone in Hanoi.The night market offers an array of goods: clothing, accessories, handicrafts, and souvenirs, all at bargain prices. It’s a fantastic place to shop for gifts or pick up unique items that showcase Vietnamese artistry. Be prepared to haggle—it’s part of the fun and adds to the authentic experience!If you are a foodie, there is lots to experience.

reviews.author: Daydream23787093660
reviews.title: Evaluation of the Tour Plan: "Hanoi 6 Hours: One Journey, A Thousand Experiences" Overview
reviews.content: Evaluation of the Tour Plan: "Hanoi 6 Hours: One Journey, A Thousand Experiences"OverviewThe proposed tour plan for a 6-hour exploration of Hanoi is well-structured, offering a blend of cultural, historical, and culinary experiences. The itinerary is designed to provide tourists with a comprehensive view of the city, showcasing its rich heritage and vibrant lifestyle.StrengthsDiverse Experiences: The tour effectively combines various aspects of Hanoi, including traditional transportation (cyclo), historical sites (Temple of Literature, O Quan Chuong), and local cuisine (egg coffee, Bun Cha). This diversity caters to different interests and enhances the overall experience.Cultural and Historical Significance: Each stop on the itinerary is carefully chosen for its cultural and historical importance. For instance, the Temple of Literature is not only a beautiful site but also a significant educational landmark in Vietnam's history.Culinary Highlights: The inclusion of local delicacies, such as egg coffee and Bun Cha, provides tourists with an authentic taste of Hanoi's culinary scene. This aspect is crucial for a well-rounded travel experience.Scenic Locations: The tour includes visits to picturesque locations like West Lake and Tran Quoc Pagoda, allowing tourists to enjoy the natural beauty of Hanoi while learning about its history.Estimated Costs: The breakdown of estimated costs for entrance fees, transportation, and meals is practical and helps potential tourists budget their trip effectively. Offering both budget and mid-range options makes the tour accessible to a wider audience.Practical Tips: The recommendations regarding the best time to visit, essentials to bring, and appropriate clothing are valuable for tourists, enhancing their overall experience and comfort.Areas for ImprovementTime Management: While the itinerary is packed with activities, the time allocated for each stop may be tight, especially considering travel time between locations. It might be beneficial to allow for more flexibility or to prioritize certain experiences.Transportation Details: While the plan mentions various transportation options, providing more specific recommendations or arrangements for tourists (e.g., pre-booking cyclo rides or taxis) could enhance convenience.Cultural Etiquette: Including a brief section on cultural etiquette, especially regarding dress codes and behavior at religious sites, would be beneficial for tourists unfamiliar with local customs.Interactive Elements: Incorporating interactive elements, such as a brief workshop on traditional crafts or a cooking demonstration, could enrich the experience and engage tourists more deeply.Sustainability Considerations: Addressing sustainability in tourism practices, such as encouraging the use of eco-friendly transportation or supporting local artisans, could enhance the tour's appeal to environmentally conscious travelers.Overall, the "Hanoi 6 Hours: One Journey, A Thousand Experiences" tour plan is a well-thought-out itinerary that effectively showcases the cultural, historical, and culinary richness of Hanoi. With minor adjustments to time management, transportation logistics, and the inclusion of cultural etiquette, this tour could provide an even more enriching experience for visitors. The combination of diverse activities and practical information makes it a strong offering for tourists looking to explore Hanoi in a limited timeframe.

reviews.author: Thủy Nguyên Đ
reviews.title: Review: A Remarkable 8-Hour Journey Through Hanoi
reviews.content: Review: A Remarkable 8-Hour Journey Through HanoiRating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4.8/5)What I Loved:This tour exceeded my expectations and offered a seamless way to explore Hanoi’s rich history and culture in just one day. The breakfast at Bun Cha Huong Lien was a fantastic start – the flavors were authentic, and the connection to President Obama’s visit added a special touch.The itinerary was well-crafted, covering Hanoi’s most iconic landmarks, such as Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the serene One Pillar Pagoda, both of which left a deep impression. The Temple of Literature stood out with its tranquil gardens and beautiful architecture, while the Hoa Lo Prison visit was an emotionally impactful highlight, offering a profound glimpse into Vietnam’s past.The cyclo ride through the Old Quarter added a touch of charm and authenticity. It was wonderful to slow down and absorb the vibrant streets and unique energy of the city. The guide was knowledgeable and friendly, making the experience all the more enriching.Minor Improvements:While the pacing was generally good, I felt a little rushed at the Temple of Literature, where more time to explore would have been ideal. The lunch was delicious but could have included an extra dish or two to showcase more of Hanoi’s culinary diversity.Overall:This tour is an excellent choice for anyone looking to experience the essence of Hanoi in a short time. The balance of historical landmarks, cultural immersion, and local flavors was spot on. A few minor tweaks could make it absolutely flawless, but as it stands, it’s a must-try experience!

reviews.author: Huyền Ngọc
reviews.title: Hanoi’s Vibrant 8-Hour Tour: A Day as a Capital Resident
reviews.content: Are you ready to immerse yourself in the heart of Vietnam’s culture, history, and flavors in just one day? This 8-hour tour of Hanoi is a must for travelers seeking a perfect blend of adventure, history, and culinary delights. Here's my experience:Morning BeginningsWe started the day with a steaming bowl of Phở at Phở Thìn—an unforgettable taste of Hanoi’s culinary soul. Then, visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum was a humbling experience, allowing us to pay respects to one of Vietnam’s most revered leaders. The grandiose structure and serene gardens set a reflective tone for the morning.Mid-Morning ExplorationThe Temple of Literature was my next favorite stop—a tranquil oasis showcasing Vietnam’s devotion to education and Confucian values. I even tried my hand at traditional calligraphy! This serene escape in the middle of the bustling city was both peaceful and inspiring.Afternoon AdventuresDong Xuan Market was an explosion of energy, colors, and aromas. Bargaining for trinkets and sampling street foods like bánh cuốn and chè was so much fun! The highlight, however, was bún đậu mắm tôm—a dish packed with bold and distinctive flavors.The Imperial Citadel of Thăng Long was another highlight. Walking through this UNESCO World Heritage Site felt like stepping back in time. The history here is tangible—from ancient relics to the underground command center used during the war.The Grand FinaleWe ended the day with coffee at Hanoi Train Street. Watching the train pass by as I sipped on cà phê trứng (egg coffee) was surreal! It perfectly captured Hanoi's unique blend of tradition and modern charm.Why You Should GoThis itinerary is packed with Hanoi’s top highlights and hidden gems, offering a well-rounded experience of the city. The balance of cultural landmarks, delicious food, and unique experiences (like the cyclo ride through the Old Quarter) makes it perfect for first-time visitors.With costs ranging from $20 to $40, it’s affordable, flexible, and unforgettable. Don’t miss this opportunity to see Hanoi at its best—you won’t regret it!Have you been to Hanoi? Share your experiences below! 🌟

reviews.author: Georgina Pep
reviews.title: Exploring the Charm of Old Quarter Hanoi
reviews.content: The rich history enveloped us as we strolled through bustling cafes and quaint shops. We savored delicious street food and enjoyed the vibrant atmosphere. Every corner held a new surprise, making it a perfect spot for our romantic getaway!

reviews.author: linh chi
reviews.title: Exploring Hanoi, the thousand-year-old cultural capita in 8-hour
reviews.content: Hanoi, the thousand-year-old capital of Vietnam, is a blend of tradition and modernity. The city stands out with its bustling Old Quarter, the serene Hoan Kiem Lake, and historical landmarks like the Temple of Literature and the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Additionally, Hanoi attracts visitors with its diverse cuisine, featuring dishes like pho, bun cha, and the unique egg coffee. The city's atmosphere exudes rich culture, combining a leisurely pace of life with vibrant energy, creating a charm that's uniquely its own.This one-day Hanoi itinerary is ideal for those looking to explore the city's highlights in a short amount of time. 07:30 – 08:00: Breakfast at Banh Mi B+The day starts perfectly with a banh mi from Banh Mi B+ (71 Hang Non). This spot is famous for its crispy baguettes filled with flavorful and meticulously prepared ingredients in true Vietnamese style. It's a delicious and convenient meal to fuel your journey.08:30 – 09:30: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum & MuseumThe Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a must-visit destination in Hanoi, where you can learn about the life and legacy of Vietnam’s great leader. The serene and spacious surroundings, coupled with the Ho Chi Minh Museum, provide deeper insights into the nation’s history.09:45 – 10:15: Temple of LiteratureIn just 30 minutes, you can marvel at the Temple of Literature, an iconic symbol of Vietnam’s tradition of learning. It exudes a sense of timelessness and preserves the cultural heritage of the nation.10:30 – 11:00: Hanoi CathedralThe St. Joseph's Cathedral, with its unique Gothic architecture, is a quick yet worthwhile stop. It's an ideal place for photography and enjoying a moment of peace in the bustling city.11:30 – 12:15: LunchThis is the perfect time to indulge in Hanoi’s culinary delights. Although the location is not specified, options like pho, bun cha, or fried spring rolls are always a satisfying choice.12:30 – 13:15: Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son TempleHoan Kiem Lake is another iconic symbol of Hanoi, offering a serene setting and picturesque views. The Ngoc Son Temple provides cultural and historical significance, making this stop both peaceful and educational.13:30 – 14:30: Hanoi Old QuarterThe Old Quarter is the perfect place to experience the daily life of Hanoians. Its narrow streets and bustling markets offer an authentic glimpse into local culture and traditions.14:30 – 15:30: Cafe Giang – End of TourThe journey concludes beautifully at Cafe Giang (39 Nguyen Huu Huan) with a taste of their legendary egg coffee. This unique drink is not only a culinary highlight but also a memorable experience to end the day. This trip offers a well-rounded experience, combining the exploration of Hanoi's history, culture, and distinctive cuisine. I can delve into Vietnam’s traditions and history through landmarks such as the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the Temple of Literature, and Ngoc Son Temple; immerse themselves in the vibrant energy of the Old Quarter and Hoan Kiem Lake; and savor iconic dishes like banh mi, pho, and egg coffee. Moments of relaxation in green spaces and the blend of modernity with tradition create an unforgettable journey, offering a comprehensive and profound perspective of the thousand-year-old capital.

reviews.author: Explore36690758678
reviews.title: An Amazing Day Exploring Hanoi
reviews.content: This six-hour tour focuses on Hanoi’s rich cultural and historical heritage, blending iconic landmarks, authentic local cuisine, and immersive experiences.Hanoi, the heart of Vietnam, gave me an unforgettable experience in just one short day. From starting the journey at Thong Nhat Park to ending it at St. Joseph's Cathedral, I felt a perfect blend of history, culture, and the vibrant modern life of this city.Timeline:8h15- 8h30 Gather at Thong Nhat Park and move to the first location9h00-10h00 Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum10h00- 11h00 Move to Thang Long Imperial Citadel11h00- 12h30 Lunch and rest12h30- 13h00 Visit Hoan Kiem Lake13h00-14h30 Visit and explore the Old Quarter14h30- 15h00 Visit the Cathedral and end.The Day’s JourneyMorning:We gathered at Thong Nhat Park at 8:15 AM. The morning air was refreshing, filled with birdsong and the rhythmic sounds of people exercising. Soon after, we moved to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, where I felt a deep sense of reverence and national pride. Remember to dress modestly when visiting this sacred site.Next, we explored the Thang Long Imperial Citadel, which felt like stepping into a giant history book. The ancient architecture and serene atmosphere made me forget I was in such a bustling city.Midday:After our explorations, we rested and enjoyed lunch. A steaming bowl of Hanoi pho and a glass of iced tea were just what I needed to recharge for the afternoon.Afternoon:Hoan Kiem Lake and its surroundings were our next stops. Seeing the red Huc Bridge standing out against the blue-green water was a breathtaking sight. Then came the Old Quarter, a lively maze filled with artisan shops, traditional eateries, and the energetic buzz of Hanoi’s streets.Finally, we visited St. Joseph's Cathedral, where the classic Gothic architecture amidst a modern city provided a perfect conclusion to the day.Tips for Traveling in HanoiTransportation:Wear comfortable walking shoes because you’ll be doing a lot of walking.Use ride-hailing apps or taxis to save time when traveling between destinations.Weather:If visiting in summer, bring a hat, sunglasses, and water to stay cool.In winter, pack a light jacket as mornings and evenings can get chilly.Food:Don’t miss iconic dishes like pho, bun cha, banh cuon, and egg coffee.Try eateries tucked away in small alleys—they often have unique and authentic flavors.Sightseeing:For sacred sites like the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the Temple of Literature, dress modestly.Avoid visiting the Old Quarter during rush hours to steer clear of crowds.Shopping:When shopping in the Old Quarter, be ready to bargain for reasonable prices.Hanoi is truly a city worth exploring, and I can’t wait to return to discover even more of its wonderful charm!

reviews.author: Phương Anh T
reviews.title: HA NOI 8 HOURS: ONE JOURNEY, A THOUSAND EXPERIENCES
reviews.content: A Perfect One-Day Tour in Hanoi: History, Culture, and Unique ExperiencesIf you only have one day in Hanoi, this itinerary is perfect for immersing yourself in the city's rich history, vibrant culture, and iconic landmarks. From historical sites to unique local experiences, here's how I spent a memorable day in Vietnam's capital:Morning: A Glimpse Into Vietnam’s Past- Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and One Pillar PagodaMy day began at the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, an iconic symbol of Hanoi and Vietnam. The solemn atmosphere and grandeur of the site were deeply moving, offering a glimpse into the life of one of Vietnam's greatest leaders. Just a short walk away is the One Pillar Pagoda, a small but beautiful structure steeped in Buddhist symbolism and history.- Temple of Literature (Văn Miếu - Quốc Tử Giám)Next, I visited the Temple of Literature, Vietnam’s first university. The peaceful courtyards and ancient architecture made this an inspiring stop, showcasing the importance of education and Confucian values in Vietnamese culture.Afternoon: Learning and Savoring Hanoi’s Delicacies- Hoa Lo Prison (Maison Centrale)Hoa Lo Prison Museum offered a sobering insight into Vietnam's colonial history and the resilience of its people during difficult times. The exhibits are well-curated, providing a balance of historical context and personal stories.- Lunch with Hanoi’s DelicaciesFor lunch, I enjoyed a bowl of bun cha, accompanied by nem cua be (crab spring rolls). The combination of savory grilled pork, fresh herbs, and sweet-sour dipping sauce was an explosion of flavors. I highly recommend trying this dish when in Hanoi!Traditional Arts and Unique Cafes- Thang Long Water Puppet TheatreThe evening began with a mesmerizing water puppet show at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre. The performance, accompanied by live traditional music, was entertaining and gave insight into Vietnam’s rural life and folklore.- Train Street CafeMy last stop was Hanoi’s Train Street, a narrow alley where trains pass just inches away from local houses and cafes. Sipping a traditional Vietnamese egg coffee here while watching the train pass by was an unforgettable experience, blending thrill and tranquility in a way only Hanoi can offer.Overall ExperienceThis one-day itinerary was a perfect introduction to Hanoi’s culture and history.
