Each stop was thoughtfully planned, and the experiences were diverse yet cohesive. Whether you’re a history buff, a foodie, or just looking for something unique, Hanoi has something for everyone.Would I recommend this tour? Absolutely! Hanoi left a lasting impression on me, and I hope to return one day to explore even more of this charming city.

reviews.author: Martainn W
reviews.title: A bit of everything, really
reviews.content: We wandered through the streets, checking out all the quaint shops. Some were cool, some were... not so much. You can feel the rich history, though, with all the old buildings. We stopped at a few bustling cafes, which were pretty fun. It's a bit chaotic, but that's part of the charm, I guess.

reviews.author: ttlhttl
reviews.title: Hanoi: 8-Hour Journey: Breathe in Hanoi Touch its Soul
reviews.content: Hanoi: 8-Hour Journey: Breathe in Hanoi Touch its SoulI recently had the opportunity to experience an incredible afternoon and evening in Hanoi, and I’d love to share my journey on TripAdvisor. The itinerary lasted 8 hours, starting in the afternoon and ending late at night. This schedule is perfect for those with limited time who still want to fully immerse themselves in the charm of Vietnam's capital.1:00 PM - Hoa Lo PrisonThe afternoon began with a visit to Hoa Lo Prison, a historical landmark that is a must-see. The space vividly recreates stories of patriotism and great sacrifices during the resistance periods. What impressed me was the discount policy: 50% off for students and senior citizens, free entry for children under 15 and war veterans, making the experience even more meaningful.3:00 PM - Hoan Kiem Lake Walking StreetAfter visiting Hoa Lo Prison, I moved to Hoan Kiem Lake Walking Street, which is about 3 km away and takes around 30 minutes to get to. This was the perfect time to explore Hanoi’s street food. Snacks like crispy bánh gối (fried dumplings), sweet bánh rán mật (glutinous rice doughnuts), warm bánh đúc (savory rice cake), bánh trôi tàu (sticky rice dumplings in ginger syrup), and the iconic Tràng Tiền ice cream left a lasting impression. Don’t miss trying egg coffee – a unique specialty of Hanoi!4:00 PM - St. Joseph’s CathedralThe next stop was St. Joseph’s Cathedral, only about 2 km from Hoan Kiem Lake. With its ancient Gothic architecture and serene atmosphere, this spot offers a sense of calm amid the bustling streets. It’s also a fantastic place for photography or simply taking a rest.6:00 PM - Dinner at Bếp Prime or Nearby RestaurantsDinner was a relaxing time after a busy afternoon. I chose Bếp Prime, located 5 km from the cathedral (15 minutes by car), to enjoy delicious dishes such as coconut shrimp salad, grilled goby fish with chili salt, and pigeon sticky rice. If you want to try other local specialties, nearby restaurants offer dishes like chả cá Lã Vọng (grilled fish with turmeric and dill), fried spring rolls, and crab hotpot.7:00 PM - Night Tour at Thang Long Imperial CitadelAs night fell, I joined a nighttime tour of the Thang Long Imperial Citadel, about 30 minutes from the dinner spot. With shimmering lights and vivid historical storytelling, this journey into the past was truly magical. The night tour includes great discounts: 50% off for children under 12 and free for those under 5, making it ideal for families.9:00 PM - Flag-Lowering Ceremony at Ho Chi Minh MausoleumThe itinerary concluded with the solemn flag-lowering ceremony at Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, 2.5 km from the Imperial Citadel. This special moment evoked a deep sense of national pride and respect for the values left by President Ho Chi Minh.ConclusionAn afternoon-to-evening journey in Hanoi is not only exciting but also deeply meaningful. Combining historical exploration, culinary experiences, and cultural discoveries, this is an itinerary I highly recommend for anyone looking to make the most of their time in the capital.

reviews.author: Willy A
reviews.title: The duality of Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: The perfect combination of seeing historic buildings by day and toasting with beer hoi by night! The French colonial architecture lining the narrow alleys is retro cute and I was super excited to visit 36 different ways! At night, the street was packed with food stalls and bars, and the sounds of motorcycles and the aroma of local food mingled with beer hoi in one hand :-) It was a blast! It's a perfect tourist destination, where the good old Vietnam meets the modern!

reviews.author: LSQRD1
reviews.title: A unique aspect of Hanoi
reviews.content: This aspect of our visit to Hanoi was very authentic.  There were all manner of seafood, fruits and meats for sale in the narrow streets.  There was a lot of activity including the very present motor banks.  This was definitely a very unique experience.

reviews.author: Sightsee46512244701
reviews.title: A memorable evening in Hanoi
reviews.content: I just had the opportunity to experience a wonderful evening in Hanoi, and wanted to share my itinerary on TripAdvisor. The schedule lasts 8 hours, starting in the afternoon and ending in the late evening. This is a suitable itinerary for those who have little time but still want to fully experience the beauty of the capital.1:00 - Hoa Lo PrisonThe afternoon begins with a visit to Hoa Lo Prison - a historical landmark not to be missed. The space here vividly recreates stories about patriotism and noble sacrifice during the resistance period. What's impressive is the 50% discount policy for students and seniors, free for children under 15 years old and veterans, making this experience even more meaningful.3:00 - Hoan Kiem Lake Walking StreetAfter visiting Hoa Lo Prison, I moved to Hoan Kiem Lake walking street. This is the ideal time to explore street food. Snacks like crispy pillow cakes, sweet and fragrant honey donuts, hot Duc cake, Chinese cake, and Trang Tien ice cream really impressed me. Don't forget to try egg coffee - a unique specialty only available in Hanoi.4:00 - Hanoi CathedralThe next stop in the evening is Hanoi Cathedral. With ancient Gothic architecture and peaceful space, this place brings relaxation in the heart of bustling streets. This is also a great place to take photos or simply stop to rest.6:00 - Dinner at Prime KitchenDinner is a time to relax after an afternoon of walking. I chose Bep Prime restaurant to enjoy delicious dishes such as coconut shrimp salad, grilled goby fish with salt and chili, and pigeon sticky rice. If you want to try other specialty dishes, you can visit the surrounding restaurants to enjoy La Vong fish cakes, fried spring rolls or crab hotpot.7:00 - Thang Long Imperial Citadel night tourWhen night fell, I joined the night tour at Thang Long Imperial Citadel. With shimmering lights and vividly told historical stories, this is truly a magical journey back into the past. The night tour has attractive incentives: 50% discount for children under 12 years old and free for children under 5 years old, very suitable for families.9:00 - Flag lowering ceremony at Uncle Ho's MausoleumThe journey ends with a solemn flag-lowering ceremony at Uncle Ho's Mausoleum. This is a special moment, evoking national pride and respect for the values ​​left by Uncle Ho.This afternoon-to-evening itinerary in Hanoi was not only enjoyable but also deeply meaningful. Combining historical exploration, culinary delights, and cultural experiences, it’s a schedule I highly recommend to anyone looking to make the most of their time in the capital.

reviews.author: Anh Thư
reviews.title: Touching the Soul of Hanoi: Strolling Through Its Streets
reviews.content: If you want to truly experience the soul of Hanoi, this day-long itinerary has everything you need! From serene lakes and ancient temples to bustling streets and mouthwatering local dishes, every stop offers something unique.Morning Highlights:Start your day at Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son Temple. The legend of the Sword Lake will transport you back in time, and the iconic red Huc Bridge is a perfect spot for photos. Want a touch of local life? A cyclo ride around the streets is both fun and relaxing.Next, we visited the Temple of Literature, Vietnam's first university. The stone steles and ancient architecture are awe-inspiring, making this a must-see for anyone interested in history and culture.Historical Wonders:The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is an emotional journey into Vietnam’s past, and the One Pillar Pagoda showcases stunning Buddhist architecture. Both sites are perfect for those looking to learn more about Vietnam's roots.Lunchtime Delight:Hanoi’s food is legendary, and Cha Ca Thang Long did not disappoint. Their grilled fish with vermicelli (Cha Ca La Vong) was the highlight of our culinary adventure—don’t miss it!Afternoon Adventures:We then explored the chilling history of the Hoa Lo Prison, a site that will give you deep insights into Vietnam's revolutionary struggle. The Thang Long Imperial Citadel, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was a stunning dive into the grandeur of Vietnam's feudal era.A Sweet Ending:The day ended at St. Joseph's Cathedral, where we sipped coffee and enjoyed sticky rice while soaking in the peaceful Gothic beauty of the church. It was the perfect conclusion to a perfect day.Tips for Visitors:Dress modestly for the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.Take plenty of photos at the Temple of Literature and St. Joseph's Cathedral.Don’t rush—every location has a story worth exploring.Costs:Entrance fees for all locations are reasonable, averaging around 320,000–370,000 VND If you’re up for a panoramic view of the city, hop on a double-decker bus for 450,000 VND—it’s worth it!If you’re visiting Hanoi, this itinerary is a fantastic way to explore the city’s charm in just one day. I can’t recommend it enough!

reviews.author: Bettina S
reviews.title: Surprisingly Charming
reviews.content: The beautiful temples were, like, actually beautiful. And the whole eclectic mix of old and new? It somehow works! We wandered around for hours and loved it. Definitely a 5-star experience. Go check it out, you won't regret it

reviews.author: 鈴木 花子
reviews.title: The vibrant charm of Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: We were captivated by the bustling city life in Hanoi’s Old Quarter! I met friendly locals and experienced a unique culture. It was a great time to explore the colorful markets while enjoying street food. I want to go again.

reviews.author: Sadye H
reviews.title: Adventures in the good old Hanoi Old Quarter
reviews.content: This is a place with a rich history, where we visited quaint shops and touched on local culture. The narrow alleyways and colorful shops made us feel like we were back in time! I have so many fun memories.

reviews.author: Morgun Elie
reviews.title: Bustling Chaos in Old Quarter
reviews.content: Lots of motorbikes and persistent vendors, but that's part of the experience. Found some decent street food, though hygiene might be questionable. Better to visit in the early morning to avoid crowds.

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: Cheap and cheerful
reviews.content: Absolutely wonderful. Interesting during the day and wonderfully vibrant at night. Great street food and great people. Good little hotels. Loved it.

reviews.author: Essy K
reviews.title: Lost in Translation
reviews.content: We loved getting lost in the maze of streets, dodging scooters and slurping down delicious pho. The art scene is definitely vibrant - we stumbled upon some cool galleries tucked away down tiny alleys. The lakes offer a bit of serenity amidst the chaos, and the whole area has a charming, slightly chaotic atmosphere. It's not always relaxing, but it's definitely an experience!

reviews.author: Lavinie Hye
reviews.title: Our getaway in the Old Quarter of Hanoi
reviews.content: Markets are lively and abundant. We enjoyed delicious local dishes and discovered picturesque shops. An authentic experience, although sometimes a little confusing.

reviews.author: Evangelia Brian
reviews.title: whirlwind of sights, sounds, and smells
reviews.content: The narrow streets are a chaotic mix of scooters, shops, and street food vendors.  We loved soaking up the charming atmosphere and trying all the delicious food, but be prepared to bargain hard and watch your step!

reviews.author: Alberto G
reviews.title: Pulsing and busy neighborhood of Hanoi.
reviews.content: Neighborhood with almost palpable culture in the air. Agitated, many motorcycles (as throughout the country). Great for a walk and to make a street food experience - always very good and clean.

reviews.author: Julianne L
reviews.title: Old Quarter's Chaos
reviews.content: We spent two days exploring the maze-like streets. Some great local food spots, but also plenty of tourist traps. The traffic was overwhelming at times - watch out for motorcycles! Found some decent cafes and shops, though bargaining is a must. Atmospheric but exhausting after a while.

reviews.author: Terrance
reviews.title: Lost in Hanoi's Maze of Old World Charm
reviews.content: We spent two days wandering these narrow streets. The bustling cafes serve decent Vietnamese coffee, though some felt too touristy. Found some quaint shops selling everything imaginable - watch out for inflated prices! Food scene is vibrant; tried some delicious street food but stick to busy spots. Chaotic but worth experiencing.

reviews.author: Nomad08095101122
reviews.title: Solo in the City
reviews.content: Hectic but expected, exciting and watch yourself crossing the road; the city needs more bins..the people welcoming and helpful.

reviews.author: Petronella Amul
reviews.title: A labyrinth of life and culture
reviews.content: We fell in love with the winding streets of the old quarter! The atmosphere is indescribable - everywhere street kitchens, scooters and friendly people. The coffee in the small cafes is fantastic. An authentic experience not to be missed.

reviews.author: Tybalt Z
reviews.title: The vibrant heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: Lost in the maze of the alleys of the Old Quarter, we loved to soak up the unique atmosphere of this timeless place. The smells of street food, the colourful stalls, the endless ballet of scooters... A total immersion in the hectic life of Hanoi!

reviews.author: BTS1972
reviews.title: Like Thailand or China 30 Years ago
reviews.content: Hanoi is still trying to catch up with the rest of Asia. This offers the unique opportunity to feel the atmospehere of Asian citites decades ago. All the small houses, little shops and myriads of motos can still be found here today. May not anymore in 5 to 10 years time. So you should rush to still discover this atmosphere.

reviews.author: Jonis Hasta
reviews.title: Hanoi's Ancient Heart
reviews.content: We lost track of time exploring the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter, ducking into tiny cafes and browsing traditional shops. The atmosphere is electric, especially at dusk when the lanterns light up. Such a magical place to get wonderfully lost with your loved one!

reviews.author: Judy T
reviews.title: Still a must to go whilst visiting Hanoi
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is just very busy and hectic for my liking. It was chaotic with cars and scooters and no one actually followed any lights. For local Hanoians, it’s their routine. For tourists, can be feeling frustrating at first. Needed a few days to get used to the vibe

reviews.author: Greta S
reviews.title: Hanoi Old Quarter - a feast for your senses!
reviews.content: A buzzing vibrant town that tantalises all the senses!  So much to do and see, restaurants, cafes, bars, spas galore and shopping for just about anything.We took a tuk tuk when first arriving and did not regret, it was a great way to get our baring - our driver took us on a tour of all the best streets. There are 36 themed streets each selling a particular kind of ware such a flower street, fruit n veg street, shoe street etc. We spend 3 days exploring the old quarter and had some great massages, ate good food and we did get a taxi to visit the museum of ethnology which was well worth it. The restaurant Duongs was excellent we had the best Pho in Vietnam. Mets restaurant also good. Stayed at The Apricot Hotel which was in the best location easy walking distance to all and lovely service and Buffet breakfast.Would highly recommend visiting the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Burgess D
reviews.title: A maze of charming chaos
reviews.content: The mix of scooters, street food aromas, and local life was intoxicating. Found the cutest coffee shops and bought amazing souvenirs. The evening atmosphere was particularly magical with all the lanterns lit up.

reviews.author: rosa m
reviews.title: Fantastic experience
reviews.content: Spend at least 4 hours.Lot{s of good shopping. The only thing is that you have to be careful with the mopeds as they rule the road. Coffe places are very nice and bathrooms are clean.

reviews.author: Germaine Kope
reviews.title: A maze of culture and chaos in Hanoi's heart
reviews.content: The narrow lanes packed with vendors, the mix of aromas from street food stalls, and the constant buzz of motorbikes created an intoxicating atmosphere. We loved exploring the traditional tube houses and discovering hidden cafes. Despite the chaos, there's an undeniable charm that kept drawing us back.

reviews.author: hana
reviews.title: Journey to discover the ancient beauty of Hanoi Old Quarter
reviews.content: Hanoi Old Quarter is a great place to experience the traditional culture and bustle of the capital. Small streets, ancient houses and long-standing eateries create a space that is both classic and vibrant. Strolling through streets such as Hang Ngang and Hang Dao, you will see the rhythm of Hanoi people's life with bustling night markets, fragrant pho, and a unique cup of egg coffee. An unforgettable experience in the heart of Hanoi

reviews.author: Tấn Trung L
reviews.title: some self-service laundromats in the Old Quarter of Hanoi
reviews.content: There are some self-service laundromats in the Old Quarter of Hanoi, such as those at 10 Hang Non and 16B Hang Ga. The cost is around 40,000 to 60,000 VND per load, with a maximum of 10 kg per load. Detergent and fabric softener are provided, making it convenient for travelers who want to wash and fold their clothes themselves.

reviews.author: Rard Raebe
reviews.title: Love and chaos in Hanoi's Heart
reviews.content: We got wonderfully lost in the maze of streets, dodging motorbikes while hunting for the perfect pho. The mix of ancient architecture, street food aromas, and constant bustle was intoxicating. Between sipping egg coffee on tiny stools and bargaining at local shops, we fell in love with this chaotic charm.

reviews.author: soup suphachai
reviews.title: old guarter
reviews.content: So many shops, so many vibes, so easy to walk, so busy nights, so much fun, so much good food.

reviews.author: Hoi An Free Walking tour & Cycling tour
reviews.title: Center of HaNoi
reviews.content: A busy place in HaNoi, where you will see the gap between the Rich and the Poor in HaNoi.  However,  the hospitality of the people is amazing.  They are helpful. On the other hand,  the traffic is crazy 🤪, so you need to learn from the local people how to cross the road. Just walk slowly and surely,  the motorcycles will be slow down and then go around you. Do not run to cross the roads , it will be more dangerous if you do that. Safety first.

reviews.author: Massimiliano B
reviews.title: Routes off the tourist route
reviews.content: A lively, colorful and hectic neighborhood. Many markets and corners of a city that, at times, seems to forget itself, in alleys that turn into the corridor of a large apartment building.

reviews.author: Jon Lajom
reviews.title: Visiting Old Quarter in Hanoi
reviews.content: The place is an old district in Hanoi which features the historical past if Hanoi...It is usually quiet in the morning up to around 6 pm, and the place turns into a vibrant place at night.  The streets will then be filled with people dining and drinking in shops mostly selling food and beer.  Hundreds of massage parlors, coffee shops, souvenir stores and specialty shops open in the afternoon until around midnight.  A night market also opens on weekends selling all kinds of stuff from food, clothes, toys, souvenir items etc

reviews.author: 鍾曉儀
reviews.title: A Lost Journey in Hanoi's Old Street
reviews.content: Walking the streets of Hanoi's Old Street, I was drawn to the colourful stalls and lively crowds. Surprises were at every corner, and the scented street snacks made me stop. Talk to friendly locals, hear their stories about the city and feel the culture. Despite being alone, here I found a sense of belonging, as if I were exploring the depths of history every step of the way.

reviews.author: Alex K
reviews.title: The Old Quarter
reviews.content: We stayed 2 nights in Hanoi and did a street food tour by scooter. Lot of things to do around the Old Quarter. Great place for food lovers. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Mark
reviews.title: Ha Noi old quarter
reviews.content: The Hanoi old quarter is an amazing vibrant place to hang out. It’s a real treat for all your senses!The Old Quarter is an intriguing neighborhood, home to a mix of Vietnamese architecture, ancient shops, and fresh-as-it-gets street food, and can be easily explored on foot. It's very chaotic and its constant motion is part of the charm. You'll see bicycle vendors selling fruits, and fresh flowers. Explore hidden alleyways, secluded pagodas and temples, and cosy coffee shops.

reviews.author: Lucy
reviews.title: nice
reviews.content: amazing place, friendly people. You should come here to visit. Having many street with thousand years old history. Look very nice......

reviews.author: Junkee u
reviews.title: unforgettable 4-day adventure from Hanoi to Halong Bay and Cat Ba Island, linking two world heritage sites
reviews.content: We explored Hanoi’s Old Quarter, enjoying the local food (yummy:) and searching for a Halong Bay tour but couldn’t find the right one. After days of online searches and asking friends, we finally discovered an unforgettable 4-day adventure from Hanoi to Halong Bay and Cat Ba Island, linking two world heritage sites. The trip revealed the serene beauty of Cat Ba Island and Lan Ha Bay, a peaceful alternative to the crowded main areas.The itinerary let us soak in Halong Bay’s stunning scenery, kayak in hidden lagoons, and relax on scenic beaches. Perfect for travelers looking to avoid crowds and experience authentic Vietnamese beauty! Having visited Halong Bay twice before, we wanted a unique experience, so we contacted the organizers for a custom itinerary. While I don’t remember their WhatsApp, you can reach them on their website, bcfamilytour.com, for bookings or more info.

reviews.author: Damien
reviews.title: A must
reviews.content: A very vibrant area Plenty to see and do No Irish bars though!A must see in Hanoi The bar street does get very loud though Enjoy

reviews.author: Cassey S
reviews.title: The charming chaos of the Old Quarter!
reviews.content: Between street vendors magically popping up and scooters doing their daily dance, it was our favorite little circus. We feasted on phở on every corner, and we fell in love with art galleries so much that we had to buy an extra suitcase!

reviews.author: Dulce W
reviews.title: Unique Vietnamese culture
reviews.content: Wow, Hanoi's Old Quarter was an experience!  The energy of the place is contagious, with scooters zipping around, vendors hawking their wares, and delicious smells wafting from every corner.  We loved getting lost in the maze of narrow streets, discovering hidden temples and charming cafes.

reviews.author: Olwen H
reviews.title: Ha noi
reviews.content: Hanoi with many beautiful sceneries and friendly people here. I had a very happy trip. I will come back next time.. see yah

reviews.author: werner g
reviews.title: Top
reviews.content: It’s fun to walk through the vibrant city in the morning and discreetly watch the marchers Since my last visit in 2018, a lot has changed. A fearer see pictureattacked us with a laser pointer while I was negotiating with him for the price of a photo. He wanted more than 200,000 dong on the bamboo ladders

reviews.author: 佐藤五郎
reviews.title: Attractive culture and hidden gems
reviews.content: Walking around the city, there are hidden, jewel-like spots everywhere, and there is no shortage of fun to explore. This charming area blends history and modernity, and each visit brings new discoveries. It's a place that offers a special experience when traveling with friends.

reviews.author: Morgun
reviews.title: Exploring Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: This historic area, known for its peaceful atmosphere and beautiful traditional architecture, offered us a glimpse into Vietnam's rich cultural heritage. We wandered through narrow streets, each dedicated to specific trades, observing local artisans at work. The well-preserved shop-houses and temples showcased the area's architectural charm. Despite the bustling activity, we found tranquil moments in hidden courtyards and by Hoan Kiem Lake. The Old Quarter provided our children with an immersive experience in Vietnamese history and daily life, making it an ideal destination for families seeking both learning and leisure.

reviews.author: Federico
reviews.title: Flavors and Landscapes
reviews.content: The streets are full of tasty dishes that have delighted our taste buds, from smoking phở to crispy bánh mì. After tasting these delights, we strolled around the picturesque lakes, enjoying the soothing view.

reviews.author: Angus
reviews.title: Our enchanting escape
reviews.content: We loved getting lost in Old Quarter Hanoi's maze-like streets! The beautiful temples tucked away in unexpected corners were a treat. The charming atmosphere had us feeling like we'd stepped back in time. Sipping coffee at tiny cafes and browsing quirky shops made for the perfect getaway.

reviews.author: Changnoi94
reviews.title: Tourist trap full of scammers
reviews.content: Awful. As a solo man you are incessantly harassed by scammers, they follow you down the road and as soon as they finally leave another one rides up to bother you. Touts stand in your way and forcibly try to drag you into bars. Shops are very pushy and demand that you BUY SOMETHING RIGHT NOW NOW NOW! The liquor in the bars is mostly fake, made from fusel oil, flavorings and water. Large numbers of vietnamese regularly die from drinking it. Like the rest of Vietnam, everyone is smoking all the time and the stench is everywhere. You have to walk in the street with the gazillion motorcycles and you have to be prepared to leap out of the way.The lake is pretty and there a few decent restaurants. A few people are actually nice.

reviews.author: Londoto
reviews.title: Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: Wandering the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter was an adventure!  We loved soaking up the atmosphere, bargaining for souvenirs, and indulging in delicious street food at every turn. A must-do for any visitor to Hanoi!

reviews.author: Tommy
reviews.title: Discovering the charm of Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: The narrow streets are lined with galleries, street performers, and traditional shops selling everything from silk to souvenirs. However, be prepared for the crowds, especially on weekends when the area is bustling with locals and tourists alike. We enjoyed getting lost in the winding alleys, sampling street food, and taking in the sights and sounds of this fascinating neighborhood.

reviews.author: Vietnam Tourist Sim
reviews.title: Best way for Hanoi Old Quarter discovery
reviews.content: From Noibai airport, we can reach to Hanoi by public bus No 86, it costs 45k VND for a ticket, and take 1hr driving.Meter taxi: There are 4 official taxi companies at the airport, the distance is around 40km and it costs almost 500k/way.The grab is available and the cost is comparative with meter taxiThe prepaid taxi. You can reserve taxi at the counter in arrival halls. They will issue ticket and you will safe to go to your hotel.Hanoi Old Quarter is an amazing choice for cuisine. We will have local food as the local often does everyday. In Hanoi, you must try:- Pho = Noodle: with beef, chicken …- Bun = Vermicelli: with pork, fish, eel …- Spring rolls: deep fried/ freshWe can’t count enough how many dishes but step by step to try it all.Hanoi also good for drink- coffee (egg coffee is the best)- beer; the famous street for beer is Ta Hien- rooftop bar all around the Old quarter- sightseeing: Hoan Kiem Lake, Catheral, Opera house, temples, pagodas and museums Be enjoy Hanoi by your own way, too.

reviews.author: 田中春人
reviews.title: The Adventures of Lovers Across Time and Space
reviews.content: Every time I walked down the lively street, I discovered something new. The old building and the contemporary café harmonized beautifully, making it feel like we were traveling through time. Watching the hustle and bustle of the streets while enjoying Vietnamese coffee in a lively cafe was a great experience. Every day was an adventure, shopping in traditional markets and exploring alleyways. A mix of old and new, the city is an ideal destination for couples.

reviews.author: oliver
reviews.title: Getting Lost in the Old Quarter
reviews.content: The streets are a maze of traditional architecture and vibrant energy. We loved getting lost exploring hidden temples and trying street food. The locals were so friendly and welcoming, making the experience even better.

reviews.author: Barbs25
reviews.title: Lots to see
reviews.content: So much going on in the hustle and bustle of the old quarter. Lots of character in the buildings, decor etc all around. Hard to miss while you’re exploring the city

reviews.author: Zaninka
reviews.title: Moved by the vibrancy and taste!
reviews.content: Traveling to Hanoi with friends! The old town is still the best! Old buildings lined up, all of them picturesque everywhere you look! 🤩 There are also many fancy cafes, where we can take a break over Vietnamese coffee ☕ It’s exciting just to walk through the vibrant streets! It’s even better lit up at night ✨ A must-visit place when you come to Hanoi!

reviews.author: parisina_8
reviews.title: organized madness
reviews.content: It is ideal for eating, shopping, you can find anything, even if your suitcase is repaired, it is a very authentic neighborhood.

reviews.author: bettye
reviews.title: A plunge back in time!
reviews.content: Traditional architecture, with its colourful tube houses and hidden temples, is truly magnificent.  We strolled the craft shops, sniffed out street food scents and sipped delicious Vietnamese coffee on the terrace.  A unique and authentic atmosphere not to be missed!

reviews.author: Rachelle C
reviews.title: Great place if you like being in the middle of it all...
reviews.content: This place is nuts, but the shopping is great.  Mopeds everywhere, including the sidewalks.  We were there in August and the heat and humidity were oppressive.  We stayed in a hotel three nights here.  I think I would have given Old Town 5 stars if I had come in the spring or fall when the heat wasn't so intense. My husband loves to haggle and for him it was a kind of paradise.

reviews.author: Daryl
reviews.title: Charmingly chaotic!
reviews.content: Hanoi’s old town immediately captivated us with its charming atmosphere! The bustling markets, the abundance of street food and the teeming crowds of people - life is pulsating here!  It was a bit tight at times, but that's exactly what made it so appealing. An unforgettable experience for us as a couple!

reviews.author: WCOB
reviews.title: Changed a lot
reviews.content: A visit to the old quarter is a must. However, I was here last about 20 years ago and it's changed for the worse. I remember having a cup of tea and listening to the blacksmiths working. Now it's all cars and motorbikes and horns. Guess it's called progress.

reviews.author: Marius
reviews.title: Hanoi’s Old Quarter
reviews.content: The vibrant streets teem with life, from bustling cafes to friendly locals offering delicious street food. We were captivated by the area's rich history and charm, evident in its ancient temples, traditional shops, and the energy of daily life unfolding around us.

reviews.author: OneTrip with local
reviews.title: The best part of Hanoi to discover.
reviews.content: The busy part of Hanoi with lots of great local restaurants and hidden gems. Hanoi in September is much cooler so it's easier to get around without worrying about the heat.

reviews.author: Michelle Drexler
reviews.title: Getting lost in the right direction
reviews.content: We dove head-first into the chaotic charm of Old Quarter Hanoi and emerged with huge smiles. This historic neighborhood is a treasure trove of hidden gems, from quirky shops to mouth-watering street food. We geeked out on the rich history and traditional architecture, and even got lost in the narrow alleys (in the best way possible).

reviews.author: Kelly T
reviews.title: Old quarter
reviews.content: Old quarter is must to stay in we stayed on Hang Bong right in the middle of it all! So much fun so busy! You would not stay anywhere else

reviews.author: Anne
reviews.title: Unforgettable
reviews.content: Pho co Ha Noi is a true historical and cultural treasure that captures the soul of the Vietnamese capital. A contourable for Tour Traveler in Vietnam!

reviews.author: Wells Alabama
reviews.title: Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: This historic district, with its quaint shops and charming atmosphere, offers a captivating glimpse into Vietnam's cultural heritage. The bustling street life provides an authentic immersion into local customs and daily routines. We found the narrow alleys lined with traditional shophouses particularly fascinating, each dedicated to specific trades. The area's vibrant energy, combined with its architectural charm, creates a unique urban landscape. For couples seeking a blend of history, culture, and commerce, the Old Quarter presents an ideal destination.

reviews.author: yac ine B
reviews.title: A love affair with Hanoi's heart
reviews.content: The bustling cafes and unique culture captivated us at every turn. We lost ourselves in the labyrinth of narrow streets, each one revealing beautiful surprises. The blend of French colonial architecture and traditional Vietnamese charm was mesmerizing. We savored aromatic pho, shopped for handcrafted souvenirs, and watched local life unfold from quaint balconies. The energy was infectious, and we couldn't help but fall in love with this vibrant slice of Hanoi. A must-visit.

reviews.author: Antonia Garner
reviews.title: Hanoi
reviews.content: Walking through the Old Quarter, you’ll encounter bustling markets, street vendors selling delicious local food, and shops offering a variety of handicrafts and souvenirs. The area is also home to several historical sites, including the ancient Bach Ma Temple and the iconic Dong Xuan Market.Whether you’re exploring during the day or enjoying the lively nightlife, Hanoi’s Old Quarter offers an unforgettable experience that captures the essence of Vietnam’s capital city. It’s a must-visit for anyone looking to immerse themselves in the rich heritage and dynamic energy of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Patrick P
reviews.title: Chaos but lovely city!
reviews.content: We spent 2 nights here and did really love it. Lot of things to do just around your hotel (ensure that you stay in the Old Quarter). We did city tour by scooter and tried all most popular streed food. It's noisy and busy all the day and so much different from the atmosphere we had in our hometown. It's great and unique.

reviews.author: DouglasBaxter51
reviews.title: Fantastic taste of Asian city living.
reviews.content: Fabulous few days in Hanoi after 10 days touring. It is vibrant in a way that is unique. EVERYBODY was so helpful and friendly.My wife and I intend to return

reviews.author: dawn3103
reviews.title: Comfy shoes are a must as you can walk miles.
reviews.content: Definately worth a trip, facinating just watching the world go by. Lots of shops, restaurants,cafes etc. You are free to browse and dont get hassled to buy. Drop into any of the Bun Cha places to eat. They usually have chairs that look as though they have come out of nursery, but the food is delicious and so tasty and costs around £3.00. Great experience.

reviews.author: Jolyn
reviews.title: A Labyrinth of Culture and Flavors
reviews.content: Scenic lakes, such as Hoan Kiem Lake, offer moments of tranquility in the heart of the bustling city. Lively street vendors animate the narrow streets, selling everything from spices to souvenirs.Delicious food is everywhere: we tasted authentic pho and crispy banh mi. French colonial architecture blends harmoniously with traditional Vietnamese temples.To get your bearings, we recommend a Map or Guide. Despite the chaos, the Old Quarter offers an authentic immersion in Vietnamese culture.

reviews.author: lucycan
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: This is a larger area in central Hanoi, maybe 8 blocks by 10 blocks.  Its called the old quarter but there is very little historic buildings.  Mostly shops, restaurants and hotels.  And LOTS of people and scooters!  Some great areas to do your shopping, get your nails done, and each lunch but OTHER than the train road (area) it was not that special compared to even other old areas in SE Asia.

reviews.author: Saretto
reviews.title: Wonderful in chaos
reviews.content: Hey! Hanoi’s Old Town is crazy! We were both lost in countless alleyways, but we found cool shops hiding every corner, small coffee shops on narrow balconies that had to climb the stairs, but the views were gorgeous!This bustling neighborhood is bursting with street beers that are cheaper than empty water!In summary, if you want a quirky experience here, don’t forget to take a map or you’ll be lost.

reviews.author: Teodoor
reviews.title: A Dive into the Heart of Vietnam 🇻🇳
reviews.content: We strolled for hours through the narrow streets, admiring the traditional architecture that made us feel like we had gone back in time. The rich history of this place is felt on every corner. But the real star? The food! We tasted everything from banh mi to pho, and each bite was more delicious than the last. Street vendors and small local restaurants drove us crazy with their inviting scents.

reviews.author: Dany
reviews.title: A Crazy Cocktail of Old and Modern!!!
reviews.content: We found ourselves in an eclectic mix of old and new, as if past and present had decided to party together. The bubbling coffees thrilled us more than our fifth espresso. What about the locals? So friendly that we almost left with an adopted family! We zigzagged between the scooters, haggled like pros (well, we think), and laughed with people we didn't understand a word about. A Trip Tip: Come with an empty stomach and a full sense of humor!

reviews.author: Wilona
reviews.title: An unforgettable journey through the heart of Hanoi!
reviews.content: The bustling coffees we loved, the aroma of Vietnamese coffee is irresistible! The unique culture left us fascinated, from street vendors to ancient temples. Every corner surprised us with something new. Definitely the vibrant soul of Vietnam! We can't wait to get back.

reviews.author: Paton
reviews.title: Love and chaos
reviews.content: We survived the Old Quarter, folks! Talk about a wild ride. Dodging scooters became our new couple's sport. The vibrant street vendors had us stuffing our faces with everything in sight. We embraced the unique culture by getting lost approximately 37 times. Who needs a gym when you've got these narrow streets?

reviews.author: Consuelo Steuber
reviews.title: a mix of tradition and modernity
reviews.content: We had the pleasure of discovering the ancient district of Hanoi, a place where tradition and modernity come together harmoniously. Lively markets and narrow alleyways allowed us to experience the daily life of the inhabitants, while magnificent temples, such as the Bach Ma Temple, offered us a glimpse into the history and culture of the city. We were impressed by the rich architecture and the variety of Things to do. The ancient district of Hanoi is a must for any Traveler wishing to discover the essence of the Vietnamese capital.

reviews.author: Peacocke
reviews.title: The unique culture of Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: The narrow streets bustled with activity, offering glimpses into traditional Vietnamese life. We sampled delicious food from street vendors and local restaurants, experiencing authentic flavors. The blend of history and modernity made for an unforgettable exploration of Hanoi's cultural core.

reviews.author: Sandee
reviews.title: Hanoi Old Quarter Adventure
reviews.content: This maze of narrow streets had us laughing at our terrible navigation skills. We stumbled upon quaint shops selling everything from lucky cats to, well, unlucky rats (eek!). The unique culture hit us like a motorbike - which, by the way, we narrowly avoided about 100 times! We played "guess that smell" with street food and "dodge the vendor" became our new favorite sport. Despite getting lost, found, and lost again, we fell head over heels for this chaotic charm!

reviews.author: Krisha
reviews.title: Unique culture
reviews.content: The traditional architecture transported us back in time, with narrow streets lined by ancient tube houses. We learned about the 36 guild streets, each specializing in specific trades . The blend of history and modern life made for an informative and captivating experience for us.

reviews.author: Olivia
reviews.title: A journey through vibrant culture and traditional architecture
reviews.content: The vibrant culture enveloped us as we wandered through narrow streets lined with traditional architecture. The sight of numerous Vietnam flags fluttering in the breeze, especially during Independence Day, added a patriotic charm to the atmosphere. As a couple, we found the blend of history and modernity captivating. From bustling markets to serene temples, every corner of the Old Quarter tells a story. It's a must-visit for anyone looking to immerse themselves in the heart of Vietnam.

reviews.author: Naser
reviews.title: Old quarter hanoi
reviews.content: Nice place to visit and try some traditional food and coffee, i stayed in the old quarter and it was good area to stay as a solo traveler.

reviews.author: Reynolds
reviews.title: Hidden gem
reviews.content: The street food scene blew me away – I'm still dreaming about that PHO! From tiny alleyways bursting with local life to secret rooftop cafes, this place is a treasure trove.Definitely a must-visit for any adventurous traveler.

reviews.author: Robinson
reviews.title: Exploring the charms of Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: The narrow streets, bustling with life, led us to hidden gems around every corner. We were captivated by the vibrant art scene, where local artists showcased their talents in colorful galleries. Each meal we enjoyed was a delightful exploration of delicious food, from street vendors to cozy restaurants, offering authentic Vietnamese flavors.

reviews.author: Nakashima Minako
reviews.title: Experience the rich history of Hanoi Old Quarter
reviews.content: When we visited Hanoi's Old Quarter, we were blown away by its rich history. The landscape of old buildings and traditional markets is like stepping back in time. I was able to enjoy the wonderful couple moments while feeling cultural attraction.

reviews.author: MissL219
reviews.title: Crazy busy area
reviews.content: Lots of businesses and shops and more mopeds than people.Train street is a must. It's utter chaos when the traffic is stopped and the crowds can be a lot but if you can get a space it's really fun to watch the train pass by.

reviews.author: Kathrine
reviews.title: What a crazy adventure!
reviews.content: What a place! So many shops, cafes, restaurants and motorbikes! They are all over and crossing the streets each time is an adventure. Somehow the motorbikes, pedestrians and cars have their own navigation on these narrow streets. Fun to watch. We found no harassing from shopkeepers; they were pleasant to meet. Wander around and take in the sights.

reviews.author: lola
reviews.title: Exploring the Heartbeat of Hanoi
reviews.content: The bustling cafes drew us in with their aromatic brews and cozy atmospheres. We wandered hand-in-hand through the vibrant streets, soaking in the rich history that seemed to whisper from every corner. The street life was a lively tapestry of sights, sounds, and flavors, making every moment an adventure. From the charming architecture to the friendly locals, the Old Quarter offered us an unforgettable experience that well cherish forever.

reviews.author: Coyote-Travelerz
reviews.title: Wonder and View
reviews.content: The old section of Hanoi is small, but offers a wide variety of shopping, food, and attractions. Wondering around you will see a mix of architecture (old to new). The area is worth visiting, especially for the night market which is interesting.

reviews.author: Dee Dee
reviews.title: Vibrating
reviews.content: Old Quarter of Hanoi was a vibrant and unforgettable experience. The narrow streets are full of life, with colorful markets, charming shops and a rich gastronomic offer. French colonial architecture and historic temples add a special charm to the neighborhood. Ideal for those seeking cultural immersion and authenticity, the Old Quarter is a must-see destination to explore the essence of Hanoi and feel the pulse of the city.

reviews.author: Beka Travel
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: Everything was fine! My friend and I came to coffee train and wlked along the lines to old quarter! The drink at there quite expensive

reviews.author: Iván C
reviews.title: I'd come back again
reviews.content: I liked the city, and the markets, good place also to eat at night and good atmosphere at night too , all perfect

reviews.author: Shimwell
reviews.title: Buckle up, buttercup!
reviews.content: We loved the vibrant energy, the amazing street food, and the unique culture.  Just be prepared for the chaos of a million motorbikes coming at you from every direction!  An unforgettable experience!

reviews.author: SHAHIDA
reviews.title: A sensory overload (in the best way!)
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is a whirlwind of sights, sounds, and smells! We loved getting lost in the maze of streets, haggling for souvenirs, and trying all the delicious street food (so cheap!). The locals were super friendly, too. Don't be afraid to wander and see where you end up!

reviews.author: Nom
reviews.title: Lost in the Old Quarter's Charm
reviews.content: The Old Quarter totally stole our hearts! Wandering hand-in-hand through the narrow streets, we were blown away by the energy of the bustling markets and the peaceful beauty of hidden temples. It's a feast for the senses: the aroma of street food, the vibrant colours, the constant buzz. We loved getting lost in the maze-like alleys, stumbling upon hidden gems and soaking up the charming atmosphere. A must-do in Hanoi!

reviews.author: markusw147
reviews.title: There's a lot to see!
reviews.content: Lively neighborhood with sometimes intense impressions for the nose. Colorful mix of restaurants, cafes and shops of all kinds. Always well attended. Offer a lot of interesting impressions.

reviews.author: Anima05
reviews.title: Colorful place
reviews.content: Colorful place. Very noisy, crowded, concentration of mopeds through the roof. Lots of different shops and cafes. Every Traveler Must Visit the Old Quarter

reviews.author: Kaenda
reviews.title: Hanoi’s beating heart 💓
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is a whirlwind of narrow streets , bustling with vendors and motorbikes. We were enthralled by the chaotic and abundance of the street food option at every turn. This historic district is a feast for senses, offering a glimpse into local life and traditional crafts. While overwhelming at times, exploring the Old Quarter is a must for any Hanoi visit.

reviews.author: Shauna i
reviews.title: City tour by scooter
reviews.content: We did half day tour by scooter. It's a real adventure.  We enjoyed the food and train street. Lot of cheap and good restaurants. Traffic in Hanoi was so crazy but fun. Noisy and busy all the time!

reviews.author: Timmy Mulbery
reviews.title: Living Breathtaking Cultural Heritage !!!!
reviews.content: Hanoi Old Quarter preserves the vibrant culture of Vietnam. A narrow alley between traditional architectures stretches like a maze, causing the mistake of leaving Trips in time in the past. For couples who care about cultural experiences, this is a living museum.

reviews.author: Kolacz
reviews.title: Charm overload!
reviews.content: We loved getting lost in the maze-like streets of Hanoi’s Old Quarter ! Friendly locals, scenic lakes, and beautiful temples around every corner. It’s a photographer’s dream, with something interesting to capture in every direction.

reviews.author: Jo J
reviews.title: Old Quater, HANOI
reviews.content: The best thing about the Old Quarter is the opportunity to visit the Mosuleaum and the neighboring museums. The Old Quarter is rich with history, food galore, and coffee galore. You will find a great abundance of travel agencies vying for your business for various tours. I went with Adventure Indochina Travel and they were excellent. I'm sure they're all good, they all offer the same tours for relatively the same prices. You will be met with street vendors and massage girls on every street calling out to you for your business. This gets to be annoying as you cannot walk down the street without being solicited. Whatever you do, you must try the famous Egg Coffee at The Note coffee shop. If you are American, I recommend that you use the HSBC in the center of the OLD QUARTER to withdraw funds from the ATM as it is otherwise difficult to find an ATM that works with our debit cards.

reviews.author: carra
reviews.title: Vibrant exploration
reviews.content: The traditional architecture, with its charming old buildings, transported us to a bygone era. We loved strolling around the scenic lakes, which offered a peaceful respite from the bustling street life. The vibrant atmosphere, filled with lively markets and street vendors, made every moment exciting. As a couple, we found the blend of history and modernity absolutely enchanting. Highly recommended for an unforgettable cultural experience!!!

reviews.author: Antonia
reviews.title: A must visit
reviews.content: Here you can experience a very authentic vietnamese lifestyle with a lot of restaurants and cafés. Although a visit is a must, some may find it a bit littered and chaotic.

reviews.author: Dewana
reviews.title: Hanoi'd it Out in the Old Quarter!!!!
reviews.content: We spent our days dodging motorbikes (couples therapy on wheels!) and our nights getting lost in a maze of alleys bursting with delicious smells. The locals were so friendly, we almost got adopted (twice!). And don't even get us started on the temples - jaw-droppingly beautiful. Hanoi's Old Quarter: come for the hidden gems, stay for the organized chaos!

reviews.author: Mundy
reviews.title: A foodie’s paradise
reviews.content: Hold on to your taste buds and prepare for a hilarious food adventure at Old Quarter Hanoi! The vibrant street vendors will lure you with their delectable treats, and their antics will leave you in stitches. From pho to banh mi, every bite is a burst of deliciousness. Just be ready for some unexpected surprises along the way! A must-visit for couples who love good food and a good laugh!

reviews.author: kate
reviews.title: Our hearts were captured!
reviews.content: Wandering hand-in-hand through Hanoi's Old Quarter was pure magic! The charming atmosphere, quaint shops, and incredibly friendly locals made us fall in love. Every corner held a new discovery. Don't miss it!

reviews.author: Puff D
reviews.title: Culinary symphony
reviews.content: Our culinary journey through the narrow streets of Hanoi’s Old Quarter was nothing short of a symphony. Sizzling works, fragrant broths, and crispy spring rolls composed a melody that left our taste buds singing praises. From savory pho to delightful banh mi, each alley revealed a verse in this gastronomic opera. A must-visit for food enthusiasts! 🍜🥟🎶

reviews.author: Timothy H
reviews.title: Beautiful place to spend time
reviews.content: Wether it's the people, food, or shopping the old quarter was something fpr everyone. Beer street, the vendors, market were amazingly nice and made the time spent very pleasant

reviews.author: Ben G
reviews.title: Vibrant neighborhood
reviews.content: This neighborhood is full of restaurants, bars, stalls, food vendors, historical landmarks, and even Hoan Kiem Lake. Walking around, you can fully experience the vibrant street life. I recommend staying in this district as your base, as there are plenty of walkable options everywhere.We were here during the weekend when they close the streets to traffic, which is an added bonus as you can freely walk around without worrying about traffic or scooters. During this time, they also host live music performances on the streets. I highly recommend timing your stay to coincide with the weekend.

reviews.author: Stefan
reviews.title: Amazing energy, not to be missed
reviews.content: All the reviews are right, about the lovely chaotic energy that suffuses this district. Don’t fret about walking in the street (but keep your eyes peeled for scooters going against traffic) and sample everything you can. Some highlights: the night markets, talking with young students practicing English at Hoan Kiem Lake, Beer Corner, and Train Street. Give yourself a few days here to soak in the vibe.

reviews.author: pate
reviews.title: Hanoi's charming chaos 😲
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is a whirlwind of sights, sounds, and smells! We loved getting lost in the maze of narrow streets, lined with beautiful temples and traditional architecture. It's a photographer's dream, and the perfect place to experience the heart of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Travel 2291
reviews.title: Love this place
reviews.content: We loved our time in old quarter. We found ourself returning everyday to eat, shop and drink. Always something happening and the chaos is overwhelming, but you can always find somewhere to take a timeout and cool down. It’s amazing how bikes,cars, buses and pedestrians navigate the tiny streets. Loved it

reviews.author: Mẫn N
reviews.title: Highly recommended
reviews.content: The food was delicious, and the recipes were easy to follow. We're now looking forward to spoiling our friends at home with self-cooked Vietnamese dishes!

reviews.author: Chu Thị N
reviews.title: What a great trip!
reviews.content: Our guide was not only funny but also incredibly knowledgeable, enhancing the experience even further. I highly recommend this tour to everyone looking for a memorable adventure!

reviews.author: OHKSO
reviews.title: There are many attractive general stores and cafes, and foreign tourists stand out
reviews.content: I took a walk here and there without any particular purpose, but there were many attractive general stores and cafes, and foreign tourists stood out. In particular, many foreign tourists gathered in front of the Banh Mi store, which is Listing in the Guide, so that they did not miss the place. Incidentally, there was a call for cyclo, but it was not that easy to back down.

reviews.author: Namely
reviews.title: Love Hanoi
reviews.content: Nice place to come and stayBetter to come in the weekend and joining the night market and drink beer on the beer streetFood all very nice

reviews.author: Nguyễn Hoàng Th... M
reviews.title: Exploring
reviews.content: Without a doubt, we wholeheartedly recommend this tour to anyone eager to immerse themselves in the vibrant spirit of Hanoi. Amazing adventure!

reviews.author: Vũ N
reviews.title: Navigating the bustling streets
reviews.content: Without hesitation, we wholeheartedly endorse this tour to anyone seeking to delve into the vibrant essence of Hanoi. Amazing trip!

reviews.author: Carol G
reviews.title: Glad we went but would not return
reviews.content: Went first to an opticians - within in an hour my friend had her eyes tested and came away with a pair of glasses. Very cheap compared to the UK and Australia.Walked around a little but very hot so hopped on a bus tour and sat on top deck. Unfortunately, the English audio was not working so we only had the map to look at. However, after we saw the main sights from the bus we did not feel that inspired to return.

reviews.author: Alexander K
reviews.title: Scott and Deborah Hanoi 2024
reviews.content: Stayed in the Babylon Hotel in the Old Quarter where the staff were extremely polite and helpful so would definitely recommend if your visiting Hanoi

reviews.author: Tracy
reviews.title: Must visit destination this summer
reviews.content: Looking for Your Next Trip Destination? Hanoi is a Must!🏠Historical Landmarks: Explore iconic sites like the Hoan Kiem Lake, the Temple of Literature, and the ancient Old Quarter. Each corner of Hanoi tells a story of its thousand-year-old history.⛩️Cultural Richness: Immerse yourself in Vietnamese culture with visits to traditional water puppet shows, bustling markets, and local craft shops.🍜Delicious Cuisine: Savor Hanoi’s world-renowned street food, including pho, banh mi, and bun cha. Foodies will delight in the array of flavors and culinary adventures.👉🏻Must-Visit Spots in Hanoi: • Hoan Kiem Lake • Old Quarter: narrow streets packed with history, shops, and local eateries • Temple of Literature: Vietnam’s first university • Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum • Hanoi Opera House👉🏻Tips for Travelers: • Accommodation: From luxurious hotels to cozy homestays, Hanoi offers a variety of lodging options. • Getting Around: Use Grab (ride-hailing app) or rent a scooter for convenient travel.

reviews.author: Fidelia L
reviews.title: Hanoi'd our hearts in the Old Quarter!
reviews.content: This place is BANANAS (in a good way)!  The Old Quarter is a wild ride of vibrant street vendors hawking everything from silk pajamas to durian fruit.  We dodged motorbikes, slurped delicious street food, and stumbled upon beautiful temples tucked down hidden alleys.  Don't miss the scenic Hoan Kiem Lake - we even saw a turtle!  Hanoi, you stole our hearts (and maybe our sanity, but worth it!).

reviews.author: Razon
reviews.title: Where culture and energy collide
reviews.content: The bustling street life kept us energized, while the vibrant art scene added a creative flair to our days. We marveled at the beautiful temples, each offering a serene escape amidst the city's lively atmosphere. Perfect for any couple seeking a blend of culture and excitement! 😄

reviews.author: Barnes
reviews.title: Hanoi's enchanting heart 💕❤️
reviews.content: We loved wandering through the labyrinthine streets, discovering quaint shops and beautiful temples around every corner. Delicious street food, hidden cafes, and the vibrant energy made it a highlight of our trip as a couple.

reviews.author: Hannah
reviews.title: Sensory overload in the best way!
reviews.content: We ate our way through delicious street food (so cheap!), got lost in quaint shops overflowing with treasures, and soaked up the energy of the bustling markets.  A perfect blend of chaotic charm for adventurous couples!

reviews.author: Jones
reviews.title: Hanoi's heart & soul
reviews.content: The Old Quarter buzzes with vibrant culture and friendly locals always ready with a smile (and directions!).  We loved getting a little lost down charming alleyways, stumbling upon hidden gem cafes and shops. A must-do for families seeking an authentic Hanoi experience!

reviews.author: Voyageur590
reviews.title: A bike ride pushes!
reviews.content: It's exotic, alive, there are restaurants on every corner, as alive day as night. For a few euros (of course they accept euros contrary to what you can read), you can take a push bike ride.

reviews.author: Trendonz
reviews.title: A lot to do
reviews.content: The name Old Quarter is somewhat misleading as it’s filled with streets with cars and motorbikes rushing by, so not the old world charm of small alleys and bizarres in other parts of the world. However there’s lots of shops to duck into that sell all kinds of souvenirs and things. Lots of tourist offices as well and temples that are hidden away. The lake in the Quarter is a bit quieter in the day although the cafes around it are pricey compared to those further away. Bartering is expected. The train street, when the train comes, is a must. There’s not much else like the experience elsewhere in the world so take the time to check when the train will pass through. We got there 25 minutes before and secured good seats at a cafe and ordered drinks. Ignore the touts and choose where you want to sit. Definitely worth a visit when you’re in Hanoi.

reviews.author: saikumardxb1972
reviews.title: Hanoi experience
reviews.content: If you want to enjoy a real Hanoi then take a scooter and tell them to drive your around the city. It is one of the most fascinating cities in this planet which I absolutely love exploring.

reviews.author: Alcin
reviews.title: Lost and reused in the Old Quarter!!!!!
reviews.content: We had fun getting lost in the labyrinthine alleys of the Old Quarter!  Between two crazy laughs trying to find our way back, we came across little hidden wonders: a beautiful lacquer workshop, a coffee shop overlooking the rooftops... and what about food? Delicious and cheap! We drove (literally) with happiness.

reviews.author: Athena P
reviews.title: Hoian Old Quarter!
reviews.content: It's like no other cities we ever visited - crowded, noisy, chaos, funny, safe and friendly. We came here at weekend and enjoyed time walking around. Lot of good small restaurants, shops. It's so safe. The guide took us to walking around to small lames, drinking local beer on the streets. People were extremely friendly. All smiled and said "hello" when seeing us. Love staying here.

reviews.author: 서윤 강
reviews.title: Hanoi Old Quarter Hang with a fascinating atmosphere and vibrant nightlife
reviews.content: We were completely immersed in the charming atmosphere of Hanoi Old Quarter. With a rich history, at night, the vibrant nightlife captivated us. The jewelry-like cafes and bars hidden in every hillside made our trip even more special!!!!

reviews.author: Kym C
reviews.title: Discovering the charms of Old Quarter Hanoi.
reviews.content: We explored the scenic lakes and hidden gems of Old Quarter Hanoi, captivated by its bustling street life. The vibrant energy and rich history made our couple's trip unforgettable. From quaint cafes to lively markets, every corner held a new adventure....

reviews.author: Summertrip14047762376
reviews.title: A fun place to hang out at night in Hanoi
reviews.content: Has the best beer I've ever tried. Fun place to have a night out with friends. We strolled around the walking streets and tried plenty of food. You must try Trang Tien ice cream!!

reviews.author: nzwestie
reviews.title: Relax and just wander around and enjoy!
reviews.content: We enjoyed walking around Old Quarter.  Get amongst it and just wonder - it is nice.  The market they have in Old Town at night is by far the best market to go to as well.

reviews.author: Passenger48173273905
reviews.title: Old Quarter
reviews.content: The old quarter in Hanoi is a captivating blend of history and vibrant culture. Winding streets lined with centuries-old architecture transport visitors back in time, while the bustling markets and lively street food scene offer a tantalizing taste of modern Vietnamese life. Exploring this enchanting district is a must for anyone seeking an authentic Hanoi experience.

reviews.author: Molly Durnas
reviews.title: Old Quarter Hanoi 🫶
reviews.content: Vibrant and fun! Great to walk around, lots of cute coffee shops and restaurants. Who cares if it’s slightly touristy - you’re a tourist. Great vibes.

reviews.author: Beau W
reviews.title: Market Centre
reviews.content: It's an interesting place to walk around, with plenty of things to see buy, and barter for. Lots of restaurants to try the fantastic local food.

reviews.author: tinkle_24
reviews.title: Very touristy but some interesting architecture
reviews.content: Interesting area with numerous shops. Exceptionally good in the night with the night market. However Hanoi is full of interesting side streets and certainly a lot less touristy. Try and find them to get a better local experience!

reviews.author: Explore60587237549
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Many delicious restaurants and friendly people. Everyone can experience riding a cyclo to go through many neighborhoods, each neighborhood will sell a typical item corresponding to the street name!

reviews.author: Tilly P
reviews.title: Loved it, vibrant, exciting, authentic.
reviews.content: This area is wonderful.  Trees in the narrow streets provide shade and colour, not sure what they are but very pretty.  At night it goes off!   Busy market streets, lots of places to eat, people everywhere, so much to see.  Street corner eating is cheap and tasty and the people watching is fun.  No one really hassles you, except maybe the rickshaw drivers are a bit pushy.  We took one and  agreed a price then when we arrived he tried to increase it.  Bit cheeky!  Easy to get a taxi if you need one but it would be quicker to walk through the district as there are so many bikes.  Get a map as it is really easy to get lost, although that can be fun too!  Tiny shops and tiny buildings all squeezed in, really interesting. It was really hot when we went (May) so be prepared.

reviews.author: Helen W
reviews.title: Peridot Grand Luxury Hotel Hanoi
reviews.content: Beautiful hotel to stay in The staff were brilliant. With particular mention to  Stella who checked in on and provided assistance to us. It was most appreciated. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to others. Cleanliness, breakfast hotel rooms were to an exceptional standard. We loved the rooftop bar that had such a beautiful view. Returning from shopping in the hot streets to the air conditioning was so nice. Could not recommend enough. Will stay here again should I visit Hanoi in the future

reviews.author: THE LIGHTHOUSE AN BANG RESTAURANT & BAR
reviews.title: cool city with big lake and some activities
reviews.content: we have been here last time. it is big city with many traffice but we got a great time to walk along the lake . it is very cool and many activities .

reviews.author: santravel
reviews.title: A few words about the trip to Hanoi
reviews.content: My trip to Hanoi was wonderful. Beautiful ancient city with small streets, houses with mossy tiled roofs, and peaceful Sword Lake. Diverse cuisine, from pho, bun cha to banh cuon, fried spring rolls are all delicious. Visiting the Temple of Literature, Uncle Ho's Mausoleum, and museums helped me understand more about Vietnamese history and culture. Hanoi's autumn is poetic with the scent of milk flowers and falling yellow leaves. Hanoi is truly a charming destination that I want to return to.

reviews.author: iayzit2
reviews.title: Good area to stay in Old Quarter
reviews.content: Nice place to stay and stroll around. Everything is close but be aware of motor bikes. It feels like there are millions of them. Crossing a street or road is a challenge. Worth staying in Old Quarter many attractions in walking distance.

reviews.author: Kristin
reviews.title: Enjoyed good beer and good food in Old Quarter
reviews.content: The quarter is nice, busy but lovely in its own way. many ancient relics around and it is super near Hoan Kiem lake. We drank beer at Ta Hien street and ate some amazing food too. Highly recommend this place when you visit Hanoi

reviews.author: Dimitris L
reviews.title: Busy place
reviews.content: Hanoi Old Quarter is quite an interesting area. There are about 39 streets that make up this quarter. They are narrow, full of small shops and restaurants and full of life! This may not be everyone's favourite destination but many people choose to visit. We enjoyed our visit but were apprehensive with the street food on offer and the busy traffic on the roads. Cars and bikes everywhere and no footpaths to walk on.  A nice place full of history with lovely people everywhere.

reviews.author: Wildon Bank
reviews.title: Buzzing and beautiful.
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is the vibrant heart of Hanoi, brimming with many renowned restaurants and cafes. The atmosphere of Hanoi, especially in this area, was really charming. My dining and shopping experiences there were exceptional, and the highlight was meeting the warm, kind and hospitable locals, who were accommodating despite language differences.

reviews.author: Tommy
reviews.title: The Old town
reviews.content: Amazing old town, lot of street food, lot of cafe shop. I loved ice coffee in Hanoi. It is very strong and tasty 😋 😘😘😘😘😘

reviews.author: Blenkinsopp C
reviews.title: A maze of culture and charm
reviews.content: We were completely captivated by the Old Quarter's charming atmosphere! From the traditional architecture to the vibrant art scene, there's something to discover around every corner. It's a fantastic place to immerse yourself in the unique culture of Hanoi. We loved getting lost in the maze of streets and exploring all the shops and cafes!

reviews.author: The Travelling Chef
reviews.title: One of the best parts of Hanoi
reviews.content: One of my favourite parts of Hanoi, I think I visited the old quarter almost every other day over a month and went every weekend evening to explore the vast night market which is full of something for everyone.Street food galore, a sea of people, music, a show in the centre, famous ice-cream.It has a special feel that can't be described only experienced.Gorgeous architecture, so many little nooks, shops, people and stalls to see and believe me I saw them all.The locals who have lived there all their life have some fascinating stories to share so I recommend finding one of the older bars, restaurants or cafe's to spend time watching the world go by and chat with the owners, they'll appreciate your interest and the business.An absolute must if you're in Hanoi.

reviews.author: mana
reviews.title: Where chaos meets charm
reviews.content: We braved Hanoi's Old Quarter – a whirlwind of vibrant street vendors, super friendly locals (even when we almost got run over by a scooter!), and this crazy mix of old and new. The traditional architecture is gorgeous, but good luck trying to cross the street! It's an adventure for sure, and one we oddly kind of loved.

reviews.author: Dave C
reviews.title: Great halong cruise booked from HALONG BAY CRUISE HUNTERS tripadvisor
reviews.content: We got pickup at our hotel in Old quartee in morning,  it was a bit slow and delay but not a matter cauz traffic. All servuces during tours included jayak, island, cave, food. Everything was set smoothly and turned out excellent.

reviews.author: Navin Francis
reviews.title: Mesmerizing old world charm
reviews.content: Great architecture, food, and people. It was truly an amazing experience staying and soaking in the atmosphere.  Four days weren't enough. We will be surely going back another time.

reviews.author: George Severin
reviews.title: A major attraction in Hanoi
reviews.content: The "Old Quarter", the old town of Hanoi, is a main attraction in itself in this big city. Small alleys, one small shop next to the other, thousands of scooters and old architecture characterize this district. You can buy everything imaginable, eat at kindergarden tables and stools and just let yourself go. Yes, it is loud and can be exhausting. If it gets too much, just treat yourself to a coffee break and maybe carry on. The old town is a "must" in Hanoi.

reviews.author: foodymad
reviews.title: Hanoi holiday
reviews.content: After coming from Ho Chi Min City this was very  easy to get around. The weather was a little cooler but not much. No rain at all. The old Quarter had a lot of little shops. You could buy a lot of pearls at jewellery shops. Plenty of money exchange shops. We got a SitLo to get us around and stop at shops of interest like the famous train street. Plenty of restaurants. Three days is  probably enough.

reviews.author: Sepsi
reviews.title: Charm and Effervescence
reviews.content: We loved the unique atmosphere of the Old Quarter of Hanoi! The labyrinth of streets, the traditional architecture, and the constant activity make it an unmissable place. And when night falls, the neighborhood lights up and offers a festive and vibrant atmosphere. A real favorite!

reviews.author: Oliver
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: The old town is always so beautiful, always poetic and attractive. The 36 streets are a specialty of the capital. Go there at least once in your life.

reviews.author: Stuart
reviews.title: Must Do !
reviews.content: Amazing and so interesting .. still has retained much of its original charm. great to just get lost in the many many streets available

reviews.author: Jun
reviews.title: A big experience Hanoi
reviews.content: Hanoi is a very unique Town, a lot of store with a tons of things, a lot of things to do, even in the night is perfect to walk, i always feel secure. A lot of beautiful hotel s with affordable prices. Very good food and fresh fruits. Alway be careful with the transit but is a complete experience

reviews.author: Maria L
reviews.title: HALONG BAY CRUISE HUNTERS agent is excellent
reviews.content: Overnight cruise trip from Hanoi was fabulous and we had wonderful time. Tour guide is friendly and told us many things to do and see during the trip.

reviews.author: Chris J
reviews.title: Be pampered with a fantastic massage by lovely professionals
reviews.content: Very skilled masseuse, extremely friendly welcome. You will immediately be pampered with a cooling cloth and a delicious jasmine tea. After a light script of the feet you will be massaged according to your choice. In my case, head, shoulders and back, quite intense, a bit on the pain threshold, but extremely beneficial. My masseuse Kik had 20 years of experience and that was clearly palpable. This immediately found the places that needed the most attention and I came out feeling reborn. Another tea and a cookie to end this fantastic experience... Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Huaxin
reviews.title: Noisy, chaotic
reviews.content: Nice tourist spot. But it is losing its authenticity of Hanoi and Vietnam. It's too crowded. It's a normal shopping street. There's nothing special about it.

reviews.author: Liễu
reviews.title: old Quarter
reviews.content: The old town has many specialties, many entertainment spots, and many types of people. Sometimes I still go to the old town to eat and drink coffee. A characteristic of Hanoi that cannot be found anywhere else

reviews.author: Howard L
reviews.title: It's crazy busy but it's historic Hanoi!
reviews.content: It's an adventure visiting Hanoi's Old Quarter but it is well worth seeing life can be like in a still developing country.  There are a ton of motorbikes and a few cars,  but here pedestrians have to share the street with them.  That's because the sidewalks are all fully occupied by the vendors which use the side walk as an extension of their storefront.  You will need to learn how to cross the street - just keep moving, raise your hand, walk steadily, and don't stop or go backwards!   You're in Hanoi - you might as well check it out for yourself!

reviews.author: Rowan M
reviews.title: Too busy but Must See!
reviews.content: It's too crowded and noisy but a must-see city. Lot of good and cheap restaurants. We did cyclo tour around the old Quarter. Great experience!

reviews.author: dianedinky
reviews.title: The Old Quarter IS Hanoi so you have to visit
reviews.content: I had a picture of Vietnam and Hanoi in my head of hectic rickshaw and scooter traffic, vibrant stalls and vendors in conical hats.  And the Old Quarter is exactly that.  Even if you just go to see the design of the old French colonial buildings it is fascinating.  Very easy to get lost but always a friendly hotel desk or person nearby to ask for help.I was surprised at all the foot massage parlours, they are everywhere!  There are also lots of souvenir outlets but I found the quality to be low and things overpriced.  Wait and buy things elsewhere if you can as mainly tat in this bit of town.

reviews.author: えいこおばさん
reviews.title: Free tours by local university students are recommended.
reviews.content: It was my first time in Hanoi. I went sightseeing using a free tour guided by university students who learned the language. I applied for a half-day tour in Japanese, but the male student who came to the hotel on the day spoke English. "I thought he spoke English." He called the club on the spot, but he was not there and I could not get hold of him. He said, "I'll guide you if you don't mind," so I asked him. He listened to my wishes and made a schedule while translating it into Japanese on my smartphone, even though I can hardly speak English, and he fulfilled all of my wishes. Church, train street, wall art, lake, market. He also listened to my wishes for transportation, called Grab and negotiated the price for a cyclo. He also listened to my wishes for lunch and took me to a local shop. Since I was traveling alone, he took a lot of photos, which was helpful. At first I was nervous and worried about what would happen, but I'm glad I requested him. It was fun to get to know the local young people. I was able to make very good memories. There seem to be several companies that offer similar tours, and the club I requested at first requested a month before the trip, but I didn't get a reply. I contacted them a week before the trip and they replied, but they said, "There is no suitable person." I thought it was irresponsible, even if it was free. The circle I used this time applied four days before the trip, and got a response three days later.

reviews.author: Solo
reviews.title: A cultural tapestry of history and modernity
reviews.content: We loved getting lost in its maze-like streets, each specializing in a unique trade, a testament to the city's rich history.  While exploring, we stumbled upon a vibrant art scene tucked away in hidden galleries and studios, showcasing works by talented local artists.Beyond the bustling markets, we were surprised to find pockets of tranquility in peaceful parks like Hoan Kiem Lake. Locals gather here for morning tai chi or a relaxing stroll, offering a glimpse into daily Hanoian life.  Of course, no visit to the Old Quarter is complete without experiencing the café culture.  Quaint coffee shops line the streets, perfect for people-watching and enjoying a strong Vietnamese coffee.

reviews.author: Soumya Nayak
reviews.title: Happening part of the city
reviews.content: If you want to shop, visit the popular temples, get massages, have street food or drink cheap beer, then Old Quarter is the place to visit. Maybe for this same reason, there are a lot of affordable hotel & hostel stays in the area.My family & I visited the Ngoc Son Temple, did street shopping & got foot massage. You can easily spend 3 hours & want to explore more. Wearing comfortable shoes is a must. Definitely worth a visit, if you do not mind super crowded streets.

reviews.author: Malika B
