reviews.author: AVIDTRAVELLER53
reviews.title: Must visit for a true HaNoi experience
reviews.content: Wonderful place just to walk around and shop. Do not miss the great street food. A wonderful experience.

reviews.author: Stuart B
reviews.title: Busy & hectic
reviews.content: We’ll worth a visit to see how the real street life and businesses operate.  Everything from fruit & veg. Sales to shoe repairs. Street food, jewellery shops, banks and small hotels line the streets.  The walkways are covered by motorbikes so be prepared to brave walking on the road.  Very interesting and some of the best & tastiest food cafes.

reviews.author: Dirk W
reviews.title: The heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: The old quarter is the main attraction of Hanoi. Every square meter is turned into a little business or shop and the energy pumps non-stop. It pains me to see how much these entrepreneurial people have suffered during the last 2 years of Covid lock-downs ; a great number of shops are still shuttered up, possibly never to open again. Although it is the same everywhere in Vietnam, it baffles me that they still block all footpaths with parked scooters, forcing pedestrians into the crazy traffic on the road. They even park their scooter in the entrance of their own shop !! Not a place for those obsessed with "health & safety" either : because the shops are so small, all work is done on the footpath, exposing live wires, tools and sharps . . .It is all chaotic, but fun and interesting. Invariably, you will find a little shop with the perfect souvenir !

reviews.title: The true bustling heart of Hanoi!
reviews.content: Come, feel and enjoy the true bustling heart of Hanoi! At any visit to Hanoi, its "Old Quarter" cannot be missed! Stroll along its narrow streets and alleys - dating back 1,000 years, ride a rickshaw  or join a cyclo tour. So many things to see as "Hoàn Kiêm" (the Lake of the Restored Sword), "Thê Hûe" (the Bridge of the Morning Sunlight), "Ngoc Son" (the Temple of the Jade Mountain), "Tháp Rùa" (the Turtle Tower), "Dông Xuân (the Spring Field Market), the Hanoi Opera House, Ba Ding Square, One Pillar Pagoda, the Hanoi Post Office and many other attractions. Enjoy the colonial architecture, the Buddhist temples and pagodas, the charming outside cafés, tea houses and restaurants, and the amazing spicy street food. If shopping, don't forget to haggle, at least a little bit. And one last remark, as a pedestrian, crossing streets in Vietnam is no easy task and please ask help in learning correctly how to do it - basically always keep the same pace and never, absolutely never, make a "U" turn! Enjoy!

reviews.author: Veronica Morra
reviews.title: So much to do and see.
reviews.content: I was in Hanoi on and off from January to July. I stayed in the Old Quarter at Hanoi Family Home Stay on Ly Nam De, which was the perfect location to explore the Old Quarter. I found it fascinating with the streets that are specialized, like the fabric street,  the flower street, and the plumbing street... All the alleys to be in explored for unique Cafes and food street. The place is alive 24/7. Not a minute to be bored. The people are friendly and patient. I have to communicate through the translator on my phone and everyone understood and was helpful. It was my second time to Hanoi in  five years and I will be back.

reviews.author: sher88
reviews.title: Great area to explore
reviews.content: Walk around and explore the area. Tons of cute shops to see! If you need sportswear like hiking gear and sports shoes, plenty of shops to choose from. For me, I enjoyed the cafes and visiting the church!

reviews.author: donnagough17
reviews.title: Amazing bustling city
reviews.content: Spent three days exploring this amazing place, people are very friendly the food is amazing its amust do if you go to Vietnam.

reviews.author: Tran Hien
reviews.title: really like the chilly air here
reviews.content: I live in a hot area all year round so when I go to Hanoi in October, I am really impressed with all the food and drinks for the cold season here as well as the atmosphere of Hanoi Old Quarter. Since I only stayed for 1 day, so I haven't explored them all, so I'll definitely come back next time.

reviews.author: Mansur M
reviews.title: Most central location
reviews.content: Old quarter is the area every tourist must stay, every tourist attraction, food alleys, currency exchange are within walking distance, take the airport shuttle bus from Hanoi Airport, get down at last stop thats hanoi railways station and viola, ola, ala, you are all set to experience the beauty of Hanoi

reviews.author: rayontime
reviews.title: Always something happening and something to see
reviews.content: One of my favourite places to visit and walk around whenever I am in Hanoi. There is always something happening or something to see. It's also fairly safe and full of character.

reviews.author: markllydselby
reviews.title: The Best Location to Stay When Visiting Hanoi
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is the place to be for restaurants, shops, landmarks, and street-life. It also felt very safe walking around at at night time

reviews.author: Susan Carol L
reviews.title: Definitely the Place to Stay During a Visit to Hanoi
reviews.content: Vibrant, fascinating, and safe. Excellent restaurants to suit all budgets and great shopping even for someone like myself for whom shopping normally has no appeal.

reviews.author: Chris Pierce
reviews.title: Hanoi Old Quater
reviews.content: Nice place to go shopping and grab some beautiful Authentic Vietnamese food. Would definitely recommend a visit.

reviews.author: Frances L
reviews.title: Bustling
reviews.content: This is a bustling area overflowing with shops and restaurants. The architecture dates back to the 13th Century and each street in the old quarter specialises with merchants selling silk, wood, silver etc.

reviews.author: ndcoach
reviews.title: Love it or hate it
reviews.content: You either love Hanoi or you do not I happen to love it here every street has a different theme it has adventure excitement and surprise if you love good food and you have adventure in your blood this is your town

reviews.author: Cherie H
reviews.title: A rush of senses and a delight of new finds
reviews.content: Wow, what a rush. This area of Hanoi is a feast. Busy, noisy, crazy mopeds everywhere and rickshaws, market venders, gorgeous architecture,  friendly locals, tasty treats, 3 nights here was not enough!

reviews.author: Bernard
reviews.title: Night walks
reviews.content: A great and safe place to hang out at night. On weekends they make the whole area pedestrianised, and it becomes like a mini festival of music and dancing for all generations. Magical.

reviews.author: Beth Hodgkinson
reviews.title: Awesome area
reviews.content: I stayed at a hostel in the Old Quarter. The area is bustling - with all the comings and going of this metropolis! There are plenty of street food options as well as coffee shops to watch the world go by.

reviews.author: Khushbu Mehta
reviews.title: Charming locality
reviews.content: Its the best part about Hanoi, infact the main characteristic of Hanoi. Most of the tourist attractions are located here. Most of the hotels are located here. Infact most tourists stay in this area. Its a cultural hub, where u can watch people living their everyday life. The whole vibe of the old quarter is fascinating. There are atleast a thousand cafes here,each as amazing as d other. The Coffee Culture here is amazing. We spent every evening exploring cafes. I can just keep going on and on.

reviews.author: Veronica Morra
reviews.title: You can walk the.streets for hours!
reviews.content: There is something for everyone in the old quarter:  definitely the heart of Hanoi, it is definitely a must visit while in the city. You can do it on your own but I suggest a guided tour with a private guide. It is affordable and you will get so much more from the experience.

reviews.author: Culture560036
reviews.title: Old Quarter
reviews.content: We stayed in the Old QuArter district,close to Beer Street not far from lots of eateries and bars. We were able to walk to many attractions when not on the tour. We walked around the lakes stopping at cafes. We found several roof top bars to enjoy a cool drink in thee endings. Loved the price of beer in the minimarts.

reviews.author: Mark S
reviews.title: Intensely Urban
reviews.content: We spent six days walking around the old quarter in Hanoi, en route to various sites, or just walking around. It's an exciting experience, seeing the great variety of businesses, shops, stands, residences.... Just beware the motor-scooters everywhere. I've heard they're worse in HCMC, but it's hard to imagine anything more intense than the traffic in old Hanoi.

reviews.author: dustythoughts
reviews.title: Visual and auditory love
reviews.content: Wandering through the Hanoi Old Quarter was a wonderful visual and auditory experience.  There's so much to hear and see that it was impossible to take in everything, but it's still a worthwhile place to visit, as it really captures the cultural heart of Hanoi.  There are plenty of restaurants and shops to explore as well; keep an eye out for vehicles.  It's best to explore on foot (rather than taking a driving tour).

reviews.author: BillMcAdam
reviews.title: Wonderful Urban Walk
reviews.content: Just an incredible part of Hanoi to enjoy on foot- visual diversions everywhere. South of the Lake- Colonial Architecture is more prevalent.  Pay attention to the diversity of architectural facades on homes along the streets.  Do not walk in fear of the motor cycles. Just start walking across the street slowly and don't stop, the drivers will avoid you- when you stop is when the trouble begins!

reviews.author: Helena
reviews.title: Nice Place
reviews.content: This is nice place, near the lake and crowed with motorbike though the food around is very good. You should book hotel in here to walk around

reviews.author: Eridere
reviews.title: Sensory Feast
reviews.content: Great to walk through, shop, and eat. Vibrant and alive. So much to see and explore. Think Chandni Chowk but a bit more organized, buildings are newer and without the animals.Very fun.

reviews.author: SteveRDay
reviews.title: Not as good as I expected
reviews.content: I was expecting the old town to be fantastic - but I would rate it as very good. Maybe a little dirty for my liking.

reviews.author: Hogan M
reviews.title: Wacky place!
reviews.content: Place that is great, remained here three nights. Website traffic is insane, the street is as a sea of mopeds, it's a leap of faith when crossing the street! They actually ride on the pavements! Though it's an incredible site, every block offers various products, therefore in case you desired a digital camera you will visit the Camera or maybe perhaps electrical street. Restaurants are abundant in which you are able to get a banh mi along with a beer at insane low prices. The Lake is a great place to stroll around and chill out.

reviews.author: Hubbard R
reviews.title: Ha Noi
reviews.content: Hanoi Old Quarter, really helpful folks, Old streets offer all sorts of products, food, and nature very beautiful... Therefore in case you arrive at the existing Quarter, I suggest you try eco-friendly rice, meat Beef, chicken noodle soup, then hotpot tend to be unique food items in Hanoi in Vietnam and around the planet.

reviews.author: Donald
reviews.title: Amazing Place to visit
reviews.content: If you want a nice place to have a night walk this is the perfect place for you to visit. It has many shops around it.

reviews.author: Brenda Chenu
reviews.title: Nice Place
reviews.content: Very nice place to stay and explore when visiting Hanoi. There are Hoan Kiem Lake, Old Quarter lives and French quarter worth a visit. Love the place

reviews.author: handyman111
reviews.title: Just about everything
reviews.content: If you want to stay in an interesting, affordable, walkable area then this is the place. It's touristy and lots of businesses are oriented to tourists, small hotels with exceptional service, fantastic small restaurants, shops, easy walking (be brave), scenic. I loved the old quarter. It was exceptional

reviews.author: Zenaida
reviews.title: Loved staying in old quarter
reviews.content: An excellent place being lost in, from excellent local foods to knockoff clothing as well as this way the place has everything. As an individual man going, however, beware of the motor scooter riders which will stop and also provide you with anything from females to medications.

reviews.author: Glendora C
reviews.title: Hustle and Bustle!
reviews.content: We stayed in the center of the existing quarter at Hanoi Trendy Spa and Hotel, so we enjoyed the resort. It's the greatest place for anyone to remain. The old quarter is quite busy, lots of coffee houses, food stops as well as shops.

reviews.author: Taddeo
reviews.title: Amazing Part of Hanoi
reviews.content: This's a really hectic location day and night. The old quarters tells you the vibrancy of Hanoi. There are lots of older buildings, with streets filled with stores, peddlers, eateries, and naturally motorbikes!! We should go to in Hanoi!!

reviews.author: DaniBastidas
reviews.title: Picturesque area
reviews.content: Very picturesque area where you can find everything. The only problem is that it is a little dirty.It is like a giant market where you can appreciate the normal life of Hanoi. It is better to visit it at night and be careful with the food stalls, they are not very clean.

reviews.author: Ode
reviews.title: Honeymoon
reviews.content: We remained in the existing quarter in Hanoi. Loved it. Endorse. You're directly in the center of the stress that's the soul of Hanoi. We stayed with the 7-year-old child of ours. She enjoyed checking out this particular component of the city.

reviews.author: Jules
reviews.title: Taking walks around in tie Old part of Hanoi
reviews.content: An excellent spot to find out, it provides you with a great impression of the City, flat today. Really excited to view the busy life within the clock, but watch for scooter everything around. You might try out a little street meal on the way of yours with the community, and also it tastes good and new.

reviews.author: RG02
reviews.title: A hectic experience
reviews.content: The streets of Old Hanoi are worth a look but you take your life in your hands with traffic ignoring the traffic lights and coming at you from every direction. Just when you think it’s safe to cross the road after looking every which way and step out, another scooter comes hurtling towards you. Lots of shops if you’re a shopaholic, many selling the same things. If you can get on the pavements they are very uneven but quite often you are forced to walk in the road because of the scooters parked there, along with the other debris. We were quite glad to get back to our hotel just a short stroll away.

reviews.author: Ambler_12
reviews.title: Must spend time there - unique Asian vibe
reviews.content: Stayed in the old quarter - Adamas Hotel.  The area has so much history - good and bad. Ask guides for background if you haven't read up on it or if what you read was confusing without the context.  Look out for all the little alleys and explore inside.We were there just at the start of Corona, and things were shutting down from Hanoi down to the south.  We were so lucky - all the way down to HCMC - only having one trip cacelled  on our last day.  Many Hanoi people were not very friendly / approachable.  90% of tourists were caucasian and I believe locals felt we were bringing in the virus (?).  The small tourist numbers were definitely a boon for us!   Wander about, explore restauarants - found really nice ones,  check out street food vendors - some appear absolutely tip top whils others appear a bit dugies in terms of health.Shopping - lots of similar items all over.  Bargain!!! (about 60%?)Still have a lot of French arcitecture.  Narrow buildings but look up.  each floor often houses a different business - so you havw to climb.Cabs are cheap. Ask your hotel to call them -  Mai Linh and - they're there in no time - with a stated fare up front!  Streets are narrow, congested and doni't necessarily follow a grid pattern - taxis are much easier.  explore and enjoy!

reviews.author: Julie D
reviews.title: Amazing area for wandering around
reviews.content: We stayed at the Bonsella Prestige hotel in the old quarter and just walking outside the front door you become immersed in the bustling street food scene. There are so many shops, restaurants, massage locations, street vendors and everywhere is just bustling. It’s great to stop in one of the many coffee shops to just watch the crazy world go by!

reviews.author: Linnell T
reviews.title: The existing quarter will be the beating heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: Hanging out there in the existing Quarter, morning or maybe evening is excellent. A lot of colors, of course, people and, bustle, sounds, a lot and shops...

reviews.author: Peggie R
reviews.title: Beautifull
reviews.content: Full-On expertise of originality Old Hanoi. Noisy, chaotic full-on fun to see the atmosphere. Has from street food, bars, restaurants, shopping & marketplaces in close proximity to most Hanoi attractions.

reviews.author: Joanne B
reviews.title: Food tour of teh Old Quarter
reviews.content: Had an exceptional night our with the locals. We did a Food tour of the old Quarter with a local guide. 5 different restaurants. A great balance of the local cuisine and local delicacies. Fantastic value and a great way to mix in wit hthe locals

reviews.author: ceterpaple
reviews.title: crazy fast paced
reviews.content: this place is crazy /lively /and is a must we were there at the corona virus pandemic and it was bizzy enough and tourism was down about 50% so i would hate to see it at peak times, you must do it, and if your a candy lover do not miss candy lane , get lost go into the back streets you wont be disappointed

reviews.author: Pradeep Thacker
reviews.title: Good place
reviews.content: Good place for shopping, local food. We did cyclo, joined night market and made friends with a lot of people. The locals are very friendly as well.

reviews.author: Kelowna Guy
reviews.title: Busy streets
reviews.content: There are few main roads in Old Town that can have 2 way vehicle traffic, if it was not for the scooters. Most roads look like alleys. Walking the streets, and you do walk the streets as the sidewalks are full of parked scooters, offers a view into the life of the residents,but you have to be aware of the traffic. Old Town offers everything a resident needs from tin smith to bamboo ladders to food.

reviews.author: tatiana118
reviews.title: Very nice place
reviews.content: We booked hotel in this area and were happy with our chose. A lot of interesting place to visit, very good restaurants.

reviews.author: Lovetravel59
reviews.country: Yorkshire Dales National Park, United Kingdom

reviews.author: Hemant_Ggn

reviews.author: Emma C
reviews.title: Walking around the Old Quarter
reviews.content: Interesting  place, footpaths are used to park motorbikes and used for cleaning , cooking and whatever.So then when you walk on the street you have to avoid getting run over by this mad traffic coming from all directions.

reviews.author: NickyU
reviews.title: Explore on foot
reviews.content: Wonderful to wander around and just soak up the atmosphere, find a street bar and watch the world go by.

reviews.author: Martin S
reviews.title: Old Quarter Walking Tour
reviews.content: This was our first visit to Vietnam and the old quarter in Hanoi is a great place to experience everyday life and get immersed in the culture. Highly recommend starting a trip to Hanoi with a walk through the old quarter.

reviews.author: dandynette
reviews.title: touristic area mix poor poeple
reviews.content: It can be nice if you try any walking free tour (around 3 hours), otherwise you can go there randomly, but if you're not here for a long time, maybe the traffic gonna lost you. But it's a small part and finally since the second day, you find easily your way .

reviews.author: Kim T
reviews.title: Great
reviews.content: We went for a visit during the virus’s. We walked around town and had a great time. Watch for pick pocketed and the walk around town was part of the adventure.

reviews.author: Jean-Paul V
reviews.title: Two days well spent strolling down the alleys of Hanoi's old quarter
reviews.content: My wife and I found it really nice to just walk, observe, enjoy the scenes and look and the very very nicely specialised shops.

reviews.author: shaman baloch
reviews.title: Beautiful old qatar
reviews.content: Beautiful old Qatar and a lots of different shop and have a lots of Vietnamese food and Indian And Pakistani food and also have lots of luxury good rated hotel and apartment and lots of spa and also lots of coffee shop

reviews.author: Niall Dublin
reviews.title: a lively place
reviews.content: The part of the city is just amazing to walk around. there is plenty of activity, looks like chaos, but it is not. - you must visit it if you are in Hanoi

reviews.author: Richard Hyde
reviews.title: Quite charming
reviews.content: As an old quarter there is nothing in particular to distinguish it from that of other cities. The old lake is nice (and the illuminations beautiful). As our French friends would say 'bof! but interesting from the point of view of seeing a different culture and the people going about their day to day trades.

reviews.author: chipsmiths
reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.content: Fabulous place for a walking tour with a good guide who knows what works. We sampled delicious street food, egg coffee, yes it sound disgusting but it tasted delicious, a roadside bar complete with barrels and low stools for some home brew at ridiculous prices, passed the market stalls with really fresh produce, and some that you really wouldn’t want to eat.

reviews.author: Alan R
reviews.title: Loud, hard to cross street, lots of low quality clothes with names like North Face(some locals call it North Fake).
reviews.content: Very noisy, polluted city. It is the capital so you have some interested historical museums to visit. Would limit it to 2 or 3 nights.

reviews.author: TheFeenee
reviews.title: You'll get to love it!
reviews.content: We have explored many places in this world including Cairo, London and Istanbul but we had never seen anything quite like Hanoi!the pavement culture and the number of scooters is unlike anywhere else we have seen and we thought that it would be a very strange place to explore.But after a day or two it becomes an exciting and vibrant city that is a delight to explore!there are two hop-on hop-off bus tours the yellow one uses the same stops and is slightly cheaper than the red one. It was a great way to be introduced to the city.

reviews.author: Adrian F
reviews.title: Busy and culturally interesting
reviews.content: Really enjoyed walking through the Old Quarter. Arrive early in the morning (6-7.30am) and you will find very few tourists and lots of locals selling fruit and other goods in a calmer environment before the mass of people and motorbikes arrive.

reviews.author: Margaret S
reviews.title: so different
reviews.content: Noisy, frantic, interesting, wonderful shopping for all sorts of goods.  Local life writ large and wonderful food easily available.

reviews.author: Jenny M
reviews.title: Shopping in the Old Quarter
reviews.content: Essential to get out and about in this area. There is so much to see and the colours are amazing. Local people are so friendly.

reviews.author: André K
reviews.title: Very average rea
reviews.content: We spend the afternoon here but it was nothing spectacular. Lots of shops selling fake goods and lots of scooters. We have seen better Old Quarter areas in other cities.

reviews.author: Anthony G
reviews.title: The Organised chaos of the city
reviews.content: We stayed here for two nights after travelling from the south and what can I say about Vietnam it’s a wonderful place . The people are so friendly the foods amazing and we just love the place .

reviews.author: DaHo57
reviews.title: very autentic old town
reviews.content: It's just great to walk around in this old town with many great shops, good restaurants, very reasonable and cheap massage places. Enjoy the vietnamis coffee!

reviews.author: gemmeta
reviews.title: 100% vietnam
reviews.content: We loved the old quarter. Bikes amd motorbikes everywhere, smells, shops, little bars, food, crazyness... markets, old ladies with bikes carrying whatever you can imagine... We loved The Old quarter, just crazy!

reviews.author: Muzaffar
reviews.title: Muzaffar
reviews.content: It was the first timethat I was going to visit Vietnam and had no idea at which hotel to stay. I by chance chose one of them, Hangmy Boutique hotel, later I realised that my choice was a brilliant one. The staff were very good, especially young lady, Lisa, was very friendly and helpful, her english was perfect. The only negative moment of my trip was not being able to visit Halong bay because of current situation in the world but it is a reason one more time to come back to Vietnam, visit Halong bay, definetely.

reviews.author: Pembrae
reviews.title: Beautiful area of the city
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is definitely the classic side of Hanoi. It’s a beautiful area and feels safe.We went on food tour with Hanoi Street Food tour (hanoistreetfoodtour) which we really enjoyed. She took us to 7 different places and we tried lots of different things.We also did a walking tour using Withlocals. We chose “The True Essence of Hanoi: Highlights & Hidden Gems” with Sung, who was an excellent guide.We took a taxi to the HCM mausoleum and then walked to a temple on West Lake on our own and also went to Temple of Literature.Enjoyed a drink at a sky bar at night and another in a restaurant on the lake.

reviews.author: Laura L
reviews.title: Can get a little crazy with the crowds and traffic
reviews.content: It's the heart of the city and not to be missed.  Be careful walking but not fearful.  You must be on the street to feel the city and be a part of it.

reviews.author: thetztraveller
reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.content: Loved walking around this. Full of vibrant colour and the locals going on with their day to day activity.

reviews.author: LeanneSM
reviews.title: We'd only allowed a day, and should have allowed at least a week or two
reviews.content: Great vibe, easy to walk around, very pretty, lots of shopping and eating and drinking variety.  Gorgeous locals who were always quick to help despite language barriers

reviews.author: Beth
reviews.title: Busy and noisy!
reviews.content: Only visited for an evening, stayed a little way away and we're glad we did! It's very noisy and exciting! Lots of bars, restaurants and shops. Worth a visit, but go prepared!

reviews.author: Thibaud J
reviews.title: Near Hanoi's lake
reviews.content: Go there for a walk if you're around, in evening or night if possible, but you will meet more tourists than locals.

reviews.author: Explorer
reviews.title: Good place to chill at night
reviews.content: Ample of local food stalls and pubs. very crowded place to be at night especially weekend. Basically meant for local crowd and cheap hangout area. Many foreigners aswell.

reviews.author: MissT_HongKong
reviews.title: Busy bustling. Unique
reviews.content: Every time I visit Hanoi I love to wander into round the corner old quarter. The shops, the food, the smells are so evocative. The traffic is awful. But it is all part of the charm of the place.Take a deep breath, step boldly out and be absorbed into the flow

reviews.author: tripleespresso2go
reviews.title: Busy, beautiful and a must-see in Hanoi
reviews.content: We had a fantastic cyclo tour around the Old quarter of Hanoi. Our driver took us past the lake, red bridge, the oldest building in Hanoi, in and around streets filled with hooting scooters, sizzling street food and it was an experience that our 3- year old thorougly enjoyed.

reviews.author: Phoebesmum10
reviews.title: Ride on tuk-tuk
reviews.content: Went for a ride around the old quarter on a tuk-tuk. So worth doing. Was very interesting to see the electricity wires everywhere,

reviews.author: robyn b
reviews.title: Old quarter
reviews.content: Stunning colourful and vibrant part of town. Something for everyone. Visited several times and can highly recommend.

reviews.author: Vu Trung Thanh
reviews.title: A real Hanoi
reviews.content: It's simply come and see people around and drink local beer and you will feel happy.Drinks and Foods are cheap

reviews.author: nyasnono
reviews.title: Food walk through the Old Quarter
reviews.content: We spent three very interesting hours experiencing multiple family run restaurants and many booths with a multitude of wares (vegetables, fish, meat, seasonings, bamboo food products, pho, etc)!

reviews.author: Cary L
reviews.title: Absolutely buzzing
reviews.content: the Old Quarter of Hanoi is alive and well.  Shops line the streets and you are walking the streets because motor scooters are all parked on the sidewalks.   You have to keep your head on a swivel because traffic comes at you from every angle.  If you decide to cross the street...once you see your opening you go for it and don't stop or hesitate.   Just keep your eyes wide open and you will do fine.  After the second day it becomes like second nature to you and you get into the groove of the city.   It is incredible.  Buildings that go back 150 to 200 years are still occupied and being lived in and worked in.   Once you check into your hotel get a street map and walk every square inch of the city.  We did!   We walked 16 miles one day and close to 12 the next day just up and down streets and side streets.   7.5 million people live in Hanoi and you definitely feel it.  People are everywhere and moving all the time.  Motor scooters are flying by and everyone has something to sell.   You definitely want to go to the big open central market.  They have everything you can think of and if you are into exploring then this is the place to go.   Incredible history and incredible buzz.  Have a great tour. Cary

reviews.author: Tony Grahame
reviews.title: Old quarter
reviews.content: Much nicer than Saigon. Pleasant and full of character. You have to try Pho when there. And walk round the lake

reviews.author: Miroslav
reviews.title: Great city
reviews.content: Great city that lives 24 hours. Fantastic  restauraunts and street food. A lot of people on the streets, motobikes and cars that make an awful crowded. Hanoi is unique

reviews.author: idreamoftravel
reviews.title: Beautiful and Lively Area!
reviews.content: A beautiful and lively area in Hanoi, and perfect for walking around!  Lots of great restaurants and bars in this historic area, including beer corner.  A food tour is a great way to see the area and experience the local food.  Ha Food tours with Chris is a great option if looking for a tour!

reviews.author: Catha
reviews.title: People everywhere
reviews.content: Really good community, with a beautiful old town. In case you require clothes, anything is achievable. check out the museum history Hanoi as well as the food industry. Grab taxi is an affordable and good approach to take around. You require a 4g tourist sim card.

reviews.author: 1RichardBrighton
reviews.title: Charming old world delights
reviews.content: We enjoy this trendy wonderful area with superb restaurants hotels and spas. Delightful street food. Basically if you are in Hanoi you must visit it

reviews.author: Rach
reviews.title: Cool place
reviews.content: It’s a cool place to walk around, there’s lots to see and so much culture!! Highly recommend if you got time to kill

reviews.author: richard
reviews.title: Old Town, Hanoi
reviews.content: I am not overly fond of markets, and this is a busy almost chaotic environment. Here in Vietnam stopping for red lights for the 45 m motor cycles/ mopeds is dependent on how the driver feels. You can be run down standing on the pavement so place little faith in the green man safe to cross lights, always look everyway possible and never relax.  The old town has an interesting street by street specialism. We asked our hotel to send us to the money change market but out taxi dropped us off in thr street that repairs motor scooter seats! All very confusing. The okd town market is open 7 days a week so dont wait for the evening! Overall not my cup of tea.....

reviews.author: Santhosh Gnanasurian
reviews.title: Must visit place in hanoi
reviews.content: The old quarter and its neighborhood has something for everybody -food,massages,coffee,nightlife,theatre,It would be fantastic if you can stay in the locality.Lot of places to see incl the ancient house,the hoan kiem lake,night market etc

reviews.author: RaquelPonsati
reviews.title: Amazing experience
reviews.content: Old town is a very interesting and peculiar part of Hanoi to visit, lots of stores, street food, the chaotic tráfic of motorcicles, bikes, cars and pedestrians and the noise of peddlers selling evrything you can imagine! Hardly advise to choose a hotel In this área!

reviews.author: Dennis Z. Magers
reviews.title: Mix of Old and New
reviews.content: Old buildings, mixed in with the vibrant night life. Largely frequented by foreign tourists, but it was a good opportunity to get a taste of the local cuisine as well.

reviews.author: Anne M
reviews.title: Local atmosphere at it's best
reviews.content: Little shops,  tiny streets,  crazy motorbikes,  everything is happening. Life goes on literally in the street,  cooking their own food as well as yours, directly on the pavement. A must to visit. Just walk around and soak up the atmosphere.

reviews.author: AlfK60
reviews.title: GREAT IF YOU CAN FIND A PAVEMENT TO WALK ON!
reviews.content: Hanoi is a seriously busy city.  There are millions of scooters, mopeds and motorcycles, most of them parked on the pavements or heading the wrong way dow a one-way street.  All this adds to the fun of the place.  Just keep walking and draw in the atmosphere but try to avoid the exhaust fumes!

reviews.author: nichoj19
reviews.title: Great place to visit
reviews.content: If you get a chance get out and walk around the old quarter.  We spent a couple days there and really enjoyed walking around seeing the different shops, people and places.  If your in Hanoi, don’t miss it.

reviews.author: Raphael K
reviews.title: Bustle bustle and careful how you cross the road
reviews.content: A city of charm, great street food, character and indulgence. And not expensive as everything is a copy or a fake. Just enjoy the buzz and have fun

reviews.author: Gussy
reviews.title: Love the old quarter
reviews.content: so much shopping, but barter and even move on the other shops in same street and barter with the price you found down the road.  Look up the architecture is amazing, you get use to crossing the crazy roads.  At first I was scared but got so use to just walking across and the traffic goes around you, their is a rhythm. But if you panic you will cause havoc. Imagine when you decide to cross the drivers can predict your course, if you suddenly stop, they cant prdict your route.

reviews.author: Wendy M
reviews.title: Fascinating to explore
reviews.content: Around every corner is something new, from egg coffees, pho, local food stalls or small eateries, boutique hotels, clothes, souvenirs, artwork, pot street, tailors, buttons, hardware, to the lake. Great place to spend a couple of days

reviews.author: Martin A. Kelly
reviews.title: The real Hanoi
reviews.content: What a great experience just streets of lively people selling their wears and you can negotiate great prices and have them work hard to sell. Shops of like goods are bunched together in the same street so makes it easy to compare.

reviews.author: Poonon
reviews.title: Leisure
reviews.content: It’s always a lovely time to visit Hanoi. My “homemade” is always at the Essence Hanoi Hotel and Spa. Incredible staff.

reviews.author: hilary262015
reviews.title: An amazing place.
reviews.content: Walk in and out of the alleys to see the real life in Hanoi.Lovely people always with a smile.See the bustling market with everything you could wish to buy.Moost of the food restaurants are on the street and the thousands of motorbikes cover the pavements making walking quite difficult at times but a great experience.

reviews.author: Jerome B
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: The Old Quarter in Hanoi has a little bit of everything from street food shops to water puppet theatres to fast food (western style) and much more.  Great for wandering around!

reviews.author: Gary Nguyen
reviews.title: Great cultural value
reviews.content: Noisy, but lots of history and culture, many life activities is going on. Love the restaurants, shops and coffee stall around it. Cyclo is available for the people to try. Very French influences too

reviews.author: ParisCelt
reviews.title: Must See
reviews.content: The old Quarter is a blend if Vietnam and old French colonial buildings, shopping was excellent, pubs were good, street food wasexcellent

reviews.author: Pwncjn1
reviews.title: Wonderful shops and restaurants
reviews.content: Good for buying lots of clothes and bags at very cheap prices. You can buy anything as you walk around never seen towers of sellotape before.

reviews.author: DeMauier
reviews.title: Chaotic and fabulous
reviews.content: Too much to see and do.Just enjoy Hanoi.  Shop at Tammy Designs for authentic, handmade women's clothes and art and ceramics.

reviews.author: Brady M
reviews.title: Beautiful city!
reviews.content: It's great to explore and walk, the street food is delicious, you'll have to be amazed about motorbikes here, crossing roads is a game. Worth exploring!

reviews.author: TriciaBishop
reviews.title: Great area
reviews.content: Our hotel was situated in this lively quarter. It is very easy to get lost amongst all the shops and cafes. There is lots of hustle and bustle and the traffic is crazy.You can reach the railway track here and the lake.It's lovely to see all the street vendors.

reviews.author: Aaron L
reviews.title: My favourite place in Nam
reviews.content: This place has the feeling like stepping back in time, of you come to Vietnam is a must visit, busy and full of hussle and bustle  but it's by far my favourite place here

reviews.author: TMOH8
reviews.title: Wild, just wild
reviews.content: If you've never been to an Asian city before then you'll either love or hate the frenetic activity of the Old Quarter.The streets are alive with cars, bikes, scooters, people, dogs etc. Markets pop up and disappear at different times of the day and street food vendors and their stools block the pavements. You'll spend half your time walking in the road but just go with the flow, walk confidently and you'll be fine. It's real.

reviews.author: Michael Coughlan
reviews.title: beautiful place
reviews.content: Personally I love wandering around these old colourful streets. It's not for the faint hearted; there's a lot of strange sights, sounds and smells, there is plenty of traffic to negotiate and there are few rules to crossing the busy roads, plus pavements are full with families eating and scooters everywhere, so sometimes you are stepping into the road. But if you like a city adventure ... this is a really good one. And don't forget your camera.

reviews.author: Mario
reviews.title: Must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: Top Location in Hanoi! A lot of excellent streetfood, markets are a must-see, perfect for shopping, beer street excellent for long nights, walkingtour recommended!

reviews.author: Colin W
reviews.title: Busy,busy,busy
reviews.content: So much happening it this tightly packed area. Traffic is hectic and noisy, even so there are quieter corners and if you look carefully you can see the structure of the place behind the superficial brash commercialism.

reviews.author: Nana_JP
reviews.title: Not impressed
reviews.content: The streets are too crowded and the traffic is dangerous. Cars and motorbikes are not careful with pedestrians.  There are plenty of places to eat and a uninteresting night market. But, the area around the lake is very pretty and easy to walk.

reviews.author: Chris
reviews.title: A chaotic, fantastic pleasure on the senses
reviews.content: There’s no way to sum up the Old Quarter of Hanoi. We hadn’t been given great encouragement by people about Hanoi but we loved it, especially the Old Quarter. The noise, the traffic, the markets, the bars, the restaurants, the people were all fantastic. We had three nights & wouldn’t hesitate on revisiting. Thanks Hanoi, we’ll be back.

reviews.author: A K
reviews.title: Slum quarter
reviews.content: When I see its called the Old Quarter, I had an idea that I might see some original building, genuine Vietnamese architecture and nice sites. How wrong I was, this is a horrible dirty part of town.. advertising everywhere, facades covered any glimpse of the buildings. Dirt and filth, poorly designed traffic system, scooters blocking pavements force pedestrians into dangerous roads. Constant harassment from scooter sellers shoving dirty pictures into your face for "girls' or massage.Much racist attitude from locals.I imagine this was once a reasonable area but unless you like the worst a city has to offer, stay away. Better areas to stay only a short walk away and then you can visit the old part if you must.

reviews.author: Pratima
reviews.title: Get the feel of True Hanoi
reviews.content: Walk around the narrow bustling streets that curiously are named after the row of shops that sell particular merchandise! A whole street for shoes! Scarves! Jackets and sports wear !!! Nestled in between would be small eating places that serve delicious food!

reviews.author: baz657
reviews.title: So much to see
reviews.content: Lots to see, lots to buy, so much to barter. Many shops together doing the same stuff so you have to look around to see what you might want.

reviews.author: mhiom2018
reviews.title: At home with the locals.
reviews.content: We stayed in this area at a fantastic boutique hotel. The hustle and bustle really makes this area a must visit.

reviews.author: MandM5960
reviews.title: Really good architecture
reviews.content: We had a walking tour of the Old Quarter and French quarter really good, impressive architecture amazingly clean and we felt very safe here. Walked out at night no problems at all.

reviews.author: Bec Campbell
reviews.title: Old q
reviews.content: The old quarter of hanoi is truly a sight all the shops, restaurants, buildings to see will keep you busy for a week, with plenty of accommodation to choose from you will not be sorry staying, dinning and shopping in the old quarter

reviews.author: Bob G
reviews.title: Fascinating cultual experience,
reviews.content: Safe area, courteous people, excellent hotels, food outlets. Be careful of eating the street food if you are a westerner, lots of bacteria and easy to get sick.

reviews.author: Corinne M
reviews.title: It's normal to feel overwhelmed
reviews.content: Great experience on a weekday but weekends there is a higher risk of death due to traffic levels.  Food walking tours are a great way to try new foods.  Coconut coffee is my new favorite

reviews.author: dancethrulife
reviews.title: Get Your Camera Ready and Get Ready to Shop
reviews.content: It was so fun walking around and just soaking in the culture here.  People watching and watching the shop and restaurant owners go about their day.  There are so many shops to stop into, restaurants to grab a bite, and gorgeous photos to be taken everywhere!  Give yourself time to really explore this area at your leisure.

reviews.author: ValMacCalgary
reviews.title: Interesting and crazy
reviews.content: Life happens on the sidewalks including grinding, welding, cooking and parking. Interesting to walk through and see.

reviews.author: Dan W
reviews.title: Not To Be Missed!
reviews.content: Hanoi’s Old Town has everyone!  Literally.  One could spend a week, a month exploring all it has to offer and not tire of its  discoveries.  Food, items usable and not, cafes, market goods and inexpensive massages are just a few of the many, many reasons to spend time here!

reviews.author: Lorelie F
reviews.title: Great to explore
reviews.content: Lots to look at and experience. Short streets interesting architecture especially the tube houses.  Braving the traffic is a challenge but quite satisfying when one succeeds in crossing from  one side to the other in one piece!

reviews.author: Phuong L
reviews.title: Great time with friends
reviews.content: Excellend rooftop bar in the old quarterWith nice view to the centerFood and drinks were amazing, served by friendly staff Highly recommend if you are staying in Hanoi

reviews.author: Kapil Jalwal
reviews.title: Hanoi old Quarter is Best place for stay
reviews.content: If you are planning for come in hanoi and don't know where you stay you may prefer Old Quarter This area is called old city and available all the food items cheap hotel and it's nearly all the attractions in hanoi

reviews.author: Boomeranger
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: Loved the hussle and bussle of this area , not much influence by the West. lots of restaurants bespoke shops bars . Fun vibrant area

reviews.author: Kim G
reviews.title: Ba Dinh District: Hanoi's Most Beautiful & Historic Area
reviews.content: Exceptional experience walking the streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter where so much history can be found. The traffic and humanity is overwhelmingly congested, proceed with caution as you walk the streets; however at night and on weekends many of the streets become pedestrian friendly with traffic blocked off. Walk the lush trail surrounding Hoan Kiem Lake and visit its Ngoc Son Temple, the 18th century pagoda accessed by a wooden pedestrian bridge.   Visit St. Joseph's Cathedral, The "Hanoi Hilton" (Hoa Lo Prison), and most definitely spend time  exploring the Dong Xuan Market and street markets. Many great restaurants in this area and lots of interesting architecture.  We stayed at the Apricot Hotel on Hoan Kiem Lake and fell in love with the Ba Dinh District and all that it has to offer.

reviews.author: Marlene V
reviews.title: Shopping heaven
reviews.content: For shopping and walking around this area is top notch. Find everything you need at bargain prices coupled with old city experience.

reviews.author: DGB
reviews.title: Nice place to visit in Ha Noi
reviews.content: Green, accient and convenience! We could easily find good foods here. People are so nice and friendly

reviews.author: Ruth G
reviews.title: fun area to stay in
reviews.content: We enjoyed being close to the old quarter. We felt park of the local experience, walking alongside the street vendors and bring close to the Lake.

reviews.author: JasonfromJoplin
reviews.title: So named for what it feels like when you walk around
reviews.content: It was a fun place to explore, see period buildings, mixed with modern life.  I am sure it is much like many other Old sections of cities around the world.

reviews.author: Stephen M
reviews.title: Brimming with character
reviews.content: Personally I love wandering around these old colourful streets. It's not for the faint hearted; there's a lot of strange sights, sounds and smells, there is plenty of traffic to negotiate and there are few rules to crossing the busy roads, plus pavements are full with families eating and scooters everywhere, so sometimes you are stepping into the road. But if you like a city adventure ... this is a really good one. And don't forget your camera.

reviews.author: Anderson
reviews.title: Good trip
reviews.content: Old quater is good place to go. Many things to do and have many restaurant street Food to try. Thanks for everything

reviews.author: Robert L
reviews.title: Great fun
reviews.content: Walked through here today and had a very enjoyable timeClearly need to be careful about the motorcycles everywhere and going in all directions If you are crossing the road walk very slow and steadyThey will calculate where you will be and miss you Never step backwards or go to fastLots of very interesting shops and sights

reviews.author: Clive R
reviews.title: Rough, dirty, noisey
reviews.content: Hanoi is a dump. Crowded with cars and scooters that have no regard for pedestrians. Massive smog. Mostly rude people. Great poverty.Few redeeming features. Give it a miss.

reviews.author: Natascha
reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.content: If you are staying in Hanoi make sure you stay in the old quater! It‘s really noisy and untidy but this is what makes hanoi to the city it is. Everything important is in the old quater.

reviews.author: Celeste M
reviews.title: Loved Old Quarter, Hanoi
reviews.content: So much fun!  All the best action, street food and shops are in this area.  Rent a scooter for about $10 a day and experience Hanoi like a local.

reviews.author: Christina Towle
reviews.title: Busy Old Quarter
reviews.content: Buzzing and very busy with the night market at weekends and traffic free around the lake. We loved the atmosphere and sampled some street food.

reviews.author: Sofie B
reviews.title: Cozy place
reviews.content: Nice but hectic area. To cross the streets are a challenge - especially with kids. When you explore the small hidden streets - you will really see the local Hanoi.

reviews.author: Vineet M
reviews.title: Veitnam honeymoon
reviews.content: Awesome.Must visit without Fear.Good For street shopping. Wonder three wheel rikshaw ,that helps u roam around entire old quarter with ur better half on the same rikshaw.Puppet show is amazing

reviews.author: Madelein L
reviews.title: Old Quarters
reviews.content: Its a really busy place and to loud for me but a lot to see and shop for those who like it. Wouldnt go there again but if you like busy streets go ahead.

reviews.author: johndrinkersinLAO
reviews.title: excellent
reviews.content: more than excellent in city bus and we had a chance to be there thanks the organizers for the time in hanoi by the tour alisa group

reviews.author: Joel Love
reviews.title: Sensational. A must.
reviews.content: Don't miss this destination. Some amazing  hotels, food everywhere, bars, cafes, shopping, shopping and shopping. Go to Silver Street for a bargain. This is a real little hub of activities.

reviews.author: GuidoHongKong
reviews.title: GO!
reviews.content: This is a wonderful part of Hanoi - very genuine and very accessible.  See ‘life in the open’ here, and take your time!

reviews.author: audrey m
reviews.title: Love this area
reviews.content: Lots of things happening in this area, can walk the lake, old timers are dancing in the street early morning, lots of people running, walking safely. Many restaurants to choose from

reviews.author: Mike M
reviews.title: Sensory overload
reviews.content: To the uninitiated Hanoi runs at 100mph and the old quarter is at its heart. Packed with restaurants, bars and shops you can find anything you wantYou quickly get used to the traffic and take the pace of the city in your stride Great location to stay with some fantastic hotels in the very centre of the heart of Hanoi. Be adventurous and get out to it,

reviews.author: Noel B
reviews.title: An amazing Maze of Humanity and Commerce
reviews.content: As part of a Wendy Wu tour we did both cyclo tour and a walking street food tour through this area. It was jam packed with people selling just about anything you can imagine. Quite overwhelming and intriguing at the same time.

reviews.author: Egle K
reviews.title: nice
reviews.content: very cosy place, with lot of shops, restaurants and great architecture. Nice just to walk and take some local food

reviews.author: Gina
reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.content: Lovely neighborhood full of cultural treasures. Lovely accommodations, variety of popular food places, authentic local life scenes.

reviews.author: walkerpayne
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Thought provoking quite sad but well worth visiting You can get an English audio guide for 50000 vndEntrance is 30000 pp The film is very short but good The lifelike exhibits are excellent very realistic Toilets and a shop on site Defo go

reviews.author: Michael P
reviews.title: Stayed in the old quarter
reviews.content: Our hotel was in the old quarter, close to shops, restaurants , bars and attractions very handy to eat local food for breakfast, lunch or dinner or all three.

reviews.author: Charliev1970
reviews.title: Crazy busy, scooters everywhere, take a rickshare around - that's an experience!
reviews.content: Great place to spend an evening, watching the world, mostly on 2 wheels, rush by.  It's so busy, buzzing.  Lots of bars, street food, and people!Look up, we found a bar with a 'Northern Soul' light advertising on a rooftop - went up in the lift, a little oasis of calm, sitting outside watching the world down below - a real highlight.

reviews.author: Daniel Elliot
reviews.title: Great place to stay
reviews.content: Lots of good street food, vibrant at night and safe part of the city where most tourists stay.Prices can be more expensive than in other parts.

reviews.author: Chris L
reviews.title: Great to see
reviews.content: Was lovely to walk around to learn about the history and see the beautiful buildings and meet the lovely people in hanoi.

reviews.author: Alan Smith
reviews.title: unique and delicious street foods
reviews.content: During the business trip with my son, I had 2 evenings in this warm and joyful Old Quarter. My son enjoyed very much the street foods and street art, especially the local dancers and singers. Such a beautiful and peaceful place

reviews.author: DedreTrip
reviews.title: A hive of continuous activity
reviews.content: We loved Hanoi's Old Quarter.  It is so delightfully busy and full of life.  Hanoi Chic Hotel was very central and the ideal spot to explore from.

reviews.author: specter308
reviews.title: Beautiful area.
reviews.content: The Old Quarter is a beautiful area to walk around with a maze like network of street's. Wide variety of shopping depending on what one is looking for. Easy access to restaurants, coffee shop's etc.

reviews.author: Clay S
reviews.title: Hanoi
reviews.content: If you are going to stay in Hanoi this is the place to do it. Close to markets, food, restaurants, and the Hanoi Hilton.

reviews.author: SupratimPal
reviews.title: Best for Food
reviews.content: Awesome place for food and shopping! We had very good dinner, typical Hanoi style — virtually on the pavement.

reviews.author: Deborahve17
reviews.title: Must visit the old quarter if you go to Hanoi
reviews.content: It is recommanding to visit the old quarter. Enjoy the food and drinks, the people and be surprised about the Trafford.

reviews.author: Marlie
reviews.title: The best area of the city!
reviews.content: The old quarter structures have a lot of character and lovely to take a look at. At night time, the spot is buzzing with individuals shopping and eating. To cross the path is practically death and life however, Hanoi traffic may be the craziest.

reviews.author: Catherine B
reviews.title: A good walk
reviews.content: A good distance to walk for an hour or so because there's a nice wooden bridge at the end. Stopped and had a coffee at lpatissier.

reviews.author: Jscinny
reviews.title: A must in Hanoi
reviews.content: The old quarter in Hanoi is a great place to stay and/or tour. Old world charm, walkable sights, shopping, cafes.....its all here.

reviews.author: K&M rates plates
reviews.title: Lovely place
reviews.content: Came here for a little mooch around and it’s really impressive and very authentic. There’s lots of small shops, coffee shops and street food vendors. It’s definitely worth a visit

reviews.author: SteveByfleet
reviews.title: Great walking area
reviews.content: Take in all the atmosphere of old Hanoi, stop for coffe and cake, great little streets to experience

reviews.author: WRB_Kawakuchi
reviews.title: Great food and fun
reviews.content: Strolling around the streets absorbing the hustle and bustle. We ate in 3 different places including a family owned “ baguette” small takeaway where they do lovely light baguettes, ours with pork and other things. Finished off with beer from a keg and then a Egg coffee house that was established in 1946. Great fun.

reviews.author: Jaime G.
reviews.title: Great Stop to say you've seen
reviews.content: The old quarter is a great spot to visit - it has a lot of charm with a decent balance between old and new that does not disappoint. I will say it is very tourist-centered. Our local guide noted that it has become tourist oriented, so make sure to visit other spots on the map that might now be as known to get the real Ha Noi experience.

reviews.author: Gareth D
reviews.title: What a charming place . Full of history character and wonderful people
reviews.content: My favourite city of Vietnam .  Particularly the old quarter with colonial building . Narrow tree lies street . Great food and charming people

locationDesc: Colloquially known as Hanoi Hilton, this famous prison has been mostly torn down. A museum occupies the remaining structure.

reviews.author: petethepipe
reviews.title: Great history lesson
reviews.content: Well worth a visit, very informative I recommend hiring the headsets for the full experience

reviews.author: Eric G
reviews.title: Must See for Historians
reviews.content: John McCain and many other American pilots were imprisoned here.  This prison was also used to house Vietnamese who fought against the communist regime.While far from uplifting, the exhibits are well done (and in English) and just fascinating. This is well worth an hour or two if you are interested in the war or the revolution.   Prices are reasonable and audio guides are available.

reviews.author: Patty B
reviews.title: Glad We Went
reviews.content: This was an informative tour.  Lots of interesting depiction of the war as well as the exhibits.  People from my generation remember stories of the Hanoi Hilton and of course John McCain taken as a POW and held many years. We appreciated seeing this first hand.  We felt it was well done and appreciated seeing the aspect of the Vietnamese people against the French.  Photos, cell blocks among other items were sobering  to see.  We went in February and it wasn’t too bad temperature wise.  No A/C must be brutal during the summer.  There was a section that was closed off but we had seen enough.We would recommend especially to anyone who remember the war and John McCain.

reviews.author: Chris
reviews.title: Agent Orange is not a trendy cocktail
reviews.content: No “Há Nôi Hilton” without the Ho Chi Minh City War Museum! ??One thing sheds light on another. It explains without justifying.History always repeats itself. One power dominates another, and vice versa: the French, the Vietnamese, the Japanese, the Americans, and the Vietnamese.The attention given to the pilots is well-deserved; their return in ’73 to their loved ones was a once-in-a-lifetime event.But they, too, were (partly) responsible for 80 million liters of Agent Orange and 7.8 million metric tons of bombs. Laos and Cambodia were also heavily bombed.So…… a subtle distinction between good and evil is in order. Although the museum downplays the treatment of these pilots, suggesting that they (the pilots) didn’t have it that bad, physical and mental torment were the order of the dayP pop s

reviews.author: 301隊長
reviews.title: toilet
reviews.content: It was shocking that the toilet, made with a bucket-like can, was constructed so that everyone in the room could see it.

reviews.author: Scamp88
reviews.title: Top Museum
reviews.content: We had a great trip to the old prison today. The set up is excellent, and the audio guide is one of the best ones I have had. To go around takes 1 to 1.5 hours. It is beautifully designed, and there are several moving moments as you go through. The room that houses the guillotine highlights the stark reality of colonial rule. The story of the Hanoi Hilton is covered well but there is a definite partisan aspect to it. I do think this is a must see when in Hanoi.

reviews.author: VNORVI
reviews.title: Humans are cruel
reviews.content: Although perhaps we should not need reminding, this is another reminder that humans are awful. The displays make the borrow come to life.  Up to the Vietnam war.  And then it is just a few pictures of the prisoners gardening, eating, getting medical help and playing chess.  I think our guide believes it all

reviews.author: DayTrip45109522386
reviews.title: History of fireworks.
reviews.content: The historical monument of Fire Lò preserves true and moving war memories. Intuitive presentation, vivid theory listening helps visitors to feel deeply the strong spirit of the warriors....I love every time I visit the fireplace

reviews.author: Katchamata
reviews.title: Well organized but historically very biased
reviews.content: The tour route is clear, the signs are interesting as are the exhibited objects. The main flaw of this museum is that one generally expects a factual and honest approach to history from a museum. Yet here the narrative is extremely biased, even misleading. They display on one hand the cruelty of the prison under the colonial regime, and claim elsewhere that under Vietnamese control, the prison resembled a sort of vacation center. They present themselves as saints.While it is clear from the numerous testimonies of American prisoners (of which nothing appears in this museum) that they suffered abuse and torture there

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: A very interesting historical visit that explains the detention conditions of dissidents during the era of French colonization.Period objects and reconstructions are offered to visitors.Some images and other sets may offend the sensitivity of some visitors.

reviews.author: jh0rnsey
reviews.title: A very interesting and thought-provoking visit.
reviews.content: A very good value for money experience - 50k Dong per person - we were inside for 1.5 hours. This was a very interesting and thought-provoking visit.

reviews.author: 4kksandme
reviews.title: Maybe?
reviews.content: Interesting but biased presentation of the treatment of American prisoners. French treatment if Vietnamese prisoners was the focus however.

reviews.author: jodaneida
reviews.title: Interesting but onesided info
reviews.content: This museum was interesting in regards to its history, both during colony times and the war. But for me the info look very onesided. They forget that a conflict has two sides. The info about the POWs make it look like they where attending a summer camp.I am very shure that this is not the case.

reviews.author: Ben
reviews.title: Impressive and historically significant
reviews.content: A visit to the Hỏa Lò Prison (historically known as the 'Hanoi Hilton') is an impactful and thought-provoking experience. The museum provides a deep insight into the site's history, focusing heavily on the struggle of Vietnamese prisoners against French colonial rule, as well as the period during which American POWs were held here.The exhibits, including the preserved cells and the guillotine, are powerfully presented. The available audio guide is of high quality and provides essential historical context that truly enhances the visit; using it is highly recommended.Keep in mind that the information is presented from a specific national and political perspective, which is particularly noticeable in the section regarding the American pilots. Nevertheless, it remains an absolute must-see in Hanoi for anyone interested in Vietnam's recent history. The complex is well-maintained, and a visit takes approximately 1 to 1.5 hours.

reviews.author: Hailstorm12
reviews.title: Worth a visit for the Vietnamese narrative
reviews.content: This is mainly valuable to learn something about the Vietnamese view of this prison. With a western education, my knowledge of this prison is a place of POWs from the Vietnam War (which they call the American War). That's not what you will see here. The focus is when the prison was used by the French to house political prisoners. This is the history told there. There are a couple rooms set aside that talk about the American POWs including John McCain. This mainly tries to highlight how great they were treated, with photos of them playing sports and decorating Christmas trees. Our guide, a local, specifically commented on the difference of how the French treated the Vietnamese and how the Vietnamese treated the US. I've have my serious doubts about how the lucky the American POWs were, but I think learning about how other people tell their history is worth learning. I'm glad we went.

reviews.author: David G
reviews.title: Not Our Favorite Hanoi Attraction
reviews.content: After lunch was the visit to the Hoa Lo Prison Museum (Hanoi Hilton). It is probably on many Americans must see list, especially Vietnam War Veterans, but it was very disappointing for me. Much of the prison is not accessible (off-limits), including the underground areas where the Americans were held. Multiple buses had just arrived, so it was “wall to wall” with little room to move and difficult to view the few exhibits and cells.

reviews.author: Fairy S
reviews.title: Interesting but a bit underwhelming overall
reviews.content: I went to Hoa Lo Prison expecting a really heavy, eye-opening visit, and it was a mixed bag. Some of the exhibits were genuinely moving, especially the old cell blocks and the photos of prisoners, and I could feel how cramped and dark the place must have been. But a lot of it felt a little too polished and rushed, with some sections reading more like a quick history lesson than a deep experience. It was pretty crowded when I went, so it was hard to take it all in. Worth a stop if you're in Hanoi, just don't expect to be blown away.

reviews.author: Lewis R
reviews.title: Heavy history, worth a thoughtful stop
reviews.content: I went to Hoa Lo Prison expecting a quick stop and ended up spending a lot longer than I planned. The place is heavy, in a good way if that makes sense — the old walls, the cramped cells, the iron shackles, and the photos really hit you. Some of the exhibits were genuinely moving, especially the sections about Vietnamese prisoners and the later war history. I could almost feel the damp, stale air in the old rooms. My only gripe is that a few displays felt a bit repetitive and the crowd made it hard to linger in some spots. Still, I’d absolutely recommend it if you want something more reflective than a typical museum.

reviews.author: Wanderlust
reviews.title: Well Worth the Visit
reviews.content: I spent around two hours exploring Hoa Lo Prison, and it was one of the most fascinating and thought-provoking experiences I had in Hanoi. If you're interested in history and culture, this place is definitely worth visiting. I highly recommend renting the audio guide as well—it was worth every penny and really brought the stories to life.

reviews.author: Cosmopolitan826271
reviews.title: Captivating experience
reviews.content: Personally, I found it a moving visit ...Especially the cruel torture techniques and the real photos of the captured, the destroyed villages and fleeing families were very confronting....However , they were only war crimes committed by the Americans .Outside in the courtyard of the museum, there are several helicopters and planes of the Americans who stayed behind after their departure.

reviews.author: Travel Girl GR
reviews.title: History of Vietnam
reviews.content: The prison is a little away from the center but pass for a visit.You learn what happened during the war to many civilians.It has images of the prisoners, the cells and objects from the torture.

reviews.author: Ratigan
reviews.title: Interesting, but not a must-see for me
reviews.content: I stopped by Hoa Lo Prison while exploring Hanoi, and it was a mixed visit. Some of the exhibits were genuinely interesting, especially the old prison cells and the sections about the French colonial period. It felt sobering walking through those narrow, damp-looking rooms. That said, a lot of it felt a bit rushed and repetitive, and I didn’t always find the layout easy to follow. It was also pretty crowded, so it was hard to spend time with the displays. I left with a better sense of the history, but not really blown away. Glad I went once, but I wouldn’t say it was a highlight of my trip.

reviews.author: Francesca Cruz
reviews.title: A look into Hanoi’s Past
reviews.content: I was hesitant to visit as I have read that when you visit you would be depressed but still I dropped by here. So before heading for our lunch I decided with my brother to visit as going here with kids is not recommended. So entrance to Maison Centrale or Hoa Lo Prison is about  2 usd and upon entering you would be asked if youd like a guided audio which u just press and play to have information of what you are looking at - cost around 4 usd. The area that is sad is the torture cell where a prisoner is positioned in a reverse reclined so in long time blood would rush to head unless you support yourself using your elbows. the main prison cell where prisoners are chained on ankles is also sad and that prisoners have to use the toilet in front of other prisoners. Some prisoners i think 3 only escaped through an underground sewer. So yeah a bit of history. we didn’t really stay long maybe 45 mins only but yes we got to learn a bit of their history.

reviews.author: Pia S
reviews.title: Interesting history, but the visit felt thin
reviews.content: I wanted to like Hoa Lo Prison more than I did. There is definitely a heavy history here, and a few of the preserved cells and old photos were sobering to see up close. I could feel the dampness in some areas and the dark, cramped rooms made the place hit harder. But the visit felt a bit rushed and patchy overall. Some signs were hard to follow, and I kept wishing there was more context and better organization. It’s worth a stop if you’re in Hanoi, but they could do a lot more to help visitors understand what they’re looking at.

reviews.author: Jovan P
reviews.title: Heavy history, worth a thoughtful visit
reviews.content: I spent about an hour at Hoa Lo Prison and came away glad I went. The exhibits do a good job showing the prison’s brutal history, and some of the old cells and photographs really stuck with me. It was quiet inside, a little damp in places, and that made it feel more serious. I liked that it wasn’t overly long and I could take my time reading the displays. My only gripe is that a few sections felt a bit repetitive, and the signage could be clearer in spots. Still, if you’re in Hanoi and want a dose of history, it’s definitely worth visiting.

reviews.author: Karie C
reviews.title: Interesting history, but the experience feels rushed
reviews.content: I went in expecting a sobering history stop, and parts of Hoa Lo Prison definitely delivered that. The preserved cells and the old artifacts were the most memorable bits, and I did get a chill walking through some of the darker rooms. But overall, it felt a bit cramped and hard to follow. Some of the signs were small or not very clear, and at times I wasn’t sure what I was looking at. It also got crowded quickly, which made it hard to really take it in. There’s value here, but I think it could be much better with more context and a less rushed layout.

reviews.author: Claudette B
reviews.title: Sobering and well worth a visit
reviews.content: I spent about an hour at Hoa Lo Prison and left feeling pretty moved. The exhibits do a good job of showing the prison’s history, and some of the preserved cells and photos were hard to look at in a good way — very sobering. I especially liked the mix of artifacts and translated explanations, though a few signs felt a little uneven and I wished there was a bit more context in some sections. It wasn’t a light or fun stop, but it was definitely memorable and gave me a better sense of Hanoi’s past. If you’re into history, I’d recommend it, just don’t expect a huge place or a super polished museum experience.

reviews.author: Mckenzie K
reviews.title: Interesting history, but a bit underwhelming
reviews.content: I stopped by Hoa Lo Prison while in Hanoi and had mixed feelings about it. The history is definitely heavy, and some of the exhibits were well done, especially the older photos and the prison cells that give you a real sense of the place. I also liked that it was easy to walk through on my own without feeling rushed. That said, parts of it felt a little repetitive, and a few displays were hard to follow or needed  context. It wasn’t crowded when I went, which helped, but overall I left feeling like it was worth a visit, just not a standout for me.

reviews.author: Joetta C
reviews.title: Interesting history, but the visit felt rushed
reviews.content: I wanted to like Hoa Lo Prison more than I did. The history is obviously important, and some of the original cells and old walls were genuinely striking to see, especially with how cramped and cold the spaces felt. But the whole place was crowded and the flow was a bit confusing, so I kept bumping into people and missing bits of the story. More English explanations and better signage would help a lot. Some sections felt repetitive too. Still, a few displays were powerful and I’m glad I went. It’s worth a stop if you’re already in Hanoi, but I left feeling like the museum could do a much better job with the visitor experience.

reviews.author: Sacha B
reviews.title: Interesting history, but a cramped visit
reviews.content: I went to Hoa Lo Prison hoping for a deeper look at the history, but honestly it felt a bit rushed and crowded. A lot of the rooms are pretty small, so when there’s a group in there it’s hard to take anything in properly. The signs were helpful in places, but I wish there was more context and a clearer flow through the exhibits. Some sections felt a little one-note, too. That said, the preserved cells and old photos were powerful, and I did come away with a better sense of the place. If they improved the pacing and added more detail, it would be much stronger.

reviews.author: William Tan
reviews.title: cool
reviews.content: Located right near the city center, this spot attracts plenty of tourists. It’s a must-visit!

reviews.author: The Wandering Pair
reviews.title: A Powerful Insight into Vietnam’s Past
reviews.content: A monument to a troubled past, Hoa Lo Prison Relic is a must-visit in Hanoi for anyone wanting to learn more about not only the Vietnam War, but also the hardships endured by the Vietnamese people under French colonial rule.As you move through the cell blocks and read about the harrowing conditions faced by political prisoners, from overcrowded cells to accounts of torture and execution, it serves as a poignant reminder of the suffering many endured. The exhibits are well presented and help bring the stories of the prisoners to life.As you continue through the prison, you learn about the women who resisted colonial rule, the freedom fighters, and the revolutionary soldiers who dedicated themselves to the fight for Vietnamese independence. Their stories are both fascinating and humbling.The later sections focus on the prison’s use as a POW camp for captured American pilots during the Vietnam War and provide insight into this chapter of its history. Beyond this, the story of Hoa Lo continues through memorials and exhibits dedicated to those who fought for modern Vietnam.Visitors should dress appropriately, particularly when entering areas containing shrines and memorials. Shorts above the knee are not permitted, and it is important to remember that this remains a place of remembrance as much as a historical attraction.The museum is well laid out and easy to navigate, although be prepared to spend more time reading than walking. In a place with this much history, that’s certainly not a criticism.For anyone interested in history, Hoa Lo Prison offers an excellent opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of Vietnam’s past and a greater appreciation of the resilience of its people.Admission was 100,000 VND (£2.80) for two people, with an audio guide available for an additional 100,000 VND per person.Excellent value and a very worthwhile way to spend a couple of hours in Hanoi.

reviews.author: PareshR
reviews.title: Must do
reviews.content: Well managed and informative

reviews.author: April c
reviews.title: Didn’t use audio and worked well, plenty translation on pics, not a long time to finish
reviews.content: We went and didn’t use the audio, I didn’t feel like we needed it as there was plenty signs in English. But we may have lost a lot of information as we had finished it. Very busy when we went so suggest not to go peak time. They have videos in a few rooms which was interesting. It wasn’t a proper cafe so bring drinks with you

reviews.author: Travelosivi
reviews.title: Lots to see and learn. Audio guide available
reviews.content: This place is much bigger and with lots more exhibits than we imagined. We came with a guide that gave us interesting facts but I felt like I missed out on listening to the details from the audio guide.We were hesitant to bring our young kids here but other than some terrified looking mannequins, the place wasn’t really scary for them as they didn’t understand. Definitely go to learn more about the Vietnamese history and all they suffered!

reviews.author: Lsrgirl
reviews.title: Very interesting and moving place
reviews.content: This was incredibly interesting and very thoughtful and respectful in presentation. Highly recommend to pay for headphones to hear in English as you learn so much more. We did in morning so was cooler and some parts have fans and air conditioning and plenty of seating to be able to sit and reflect and listen and honour their stories. Such brave and resilient people.

reviews.author: Ceciledelanewyorkie
reviews.title: A must-do
reviews.content: A very interesting visit to make  Do not hesitate to take the audio guide; it is great and allows you to truly understand the history of the place without rushing.

reviews.author: Pheobe
reviews.title: Very exciting experience.
reviews.content: I have two daughters, 12 and 9 years old. A very sacred historical experience. There are speakers in both Vietnamese and English very chin chu to better understand about prison

reviews.author: Cheryl L
reviews.title: Even if museums aren't your thing, make an exception for this one
reviews.content: Maison Centrale — known to Americans as the Hanoi Hilton — is one of those places that stays with you long after you leave. Built by the French to house Vietnamese political prisoners, it was later used by North Vietnam to hold American POWs during what the Vietnamese call the American War. The museum tells both stories with care and unflinching honesty.The audio guide is essential — don't skip it. It transforms what you're seeing from a collection of rooms into something deeply human. This is an emotional experience, but it is absolutely not one to miss. Arrive when the doors open; the rooms are small and fill quickly, and the quieter it is, the more the place speaks to you.Even if museums aren't normally your thing, make an exception for this one.

reviews.author: Pippa Jones
reviews.title: Informative and eye opening
