reviews.content: I was recommended this place by a friend who used to live in Hanoi as a must go and see. The layout of the prison told the story from start to finish. Each room had information about the history and what the prisoners endured when in the certain areas. There were some parts of the prison that was reconstruction of what the prisoners endured had looked like and original structures and  actual parts. You could feel and understand the history of the pain that prisoners suffered and an eeriness in the air because of the information that was on the wall to read. There were 3 different languages to read. Vietnamese, English and French, so it catered for a few different nationalities. I learnt a lot about why it happened and it was a deep dive into thought process. Definitely a place to go if you have a spare few hours, it’s very eye opening.

reviews.author: David L
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton's dark past
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a historic monument that provides a moving and fascinating glimpse into Vietnam’s troubled past.  After Vietnam's independence in 1954, the prison was converted to hold criminals and later became famous for housing American pilots captured during the Vietnam War.  Known as the "Hilton of Hanoi", this prison holds stories of resilience, sacrifice and the struggle for independence.  Very well exposed.  Highly recommended

reviews.author: bbrady962
reviews.title: Well worth a visit for those who have an interest in history
reviews.content: Well worth a visit for those who have an interest in history. Well laid out in both text and audio. Centrally located as well

reviews.author: Nigel C
reviews.title: Interesting history lesson!
reviews.content: Interesting visit and not to be missed for historical reasons. A hot history lesson mainly about the French Administration with the American PoW’s thrown in.

reviews.author: Сергей С
reviews.title: Without Russian
reviews.content: Turns out - nothing in Russian, not even an audio guide.... I had to cancel my visit.

reviews.author: Dream64132638193
reviews.title: Historic visit
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a very interesting place to visit if you want to learn more about history. There was no live guide during my visit, but they provide an audio device that explains the exhibits well and helps you understand the stories behind each area. It’s a meaningful and informative experience.

reviews.author: Der_Humboldt
reviews.title: Memorable exhibition about a notorious prison
reviews.content: The "Hanoi-Hilton" is a legendary prison in Hanoi that has gained fame as Vietnam's notorious central prison for housing and displaying American prisoners of war. But its history goes back much further: it was already used to detain political prisoners under the French colonial administration. The inhumane prison conditions are shown here, as is the further story during the Vietnam War. Everything very vivid and memorable, unfortunately some areas were not accessible due to modernization work, therefore only 3 stars

reviews.author: grard2314
reviews.title: Why not?
reviews.content: Former prison built by the French administration. Living conditions there were particularly difficult.It also shows the guillotine used in death sentences.The second part, less interesting, exhibits photos of American soldiers prisoners.It's black with people and admission costs 15€. Without headphones. Which is expensive.If we are willing to endure the obviously one-way speech (I am thinking of the "Death March" inflicted on French soldiers after Dien Bien Phu, the good guys instantly becoming the bad guys), why not?

reviews.author: Daflee
reviews.title: An interesting insight to our past
reviews.content: Unfortunately the goal is going through a bit of a refurbishment at the moment so about 30% isn’t open. We were told before we bought our ticket.It’s sad to hear how the past were treated, it’s also interesting to read the stories of those captured in the Vietnam war

reviews.author: Jazz Gumbo
reviews.title: Fascinating place
reviews.content: Important to find some of the history & culture of a location you visit, very interesting & also sad to see how some inmates were treated. Some exhibits were closed during our visit, buck temporary replacements were provided, also you are claerly advised by staff in advance.

reviews.author: Margarita D
reviews.title: Grear experience in the prison
reviews.content: Visited Hoa Lo Prison during my time in Hanoi and it turned out to be one of the most impactful places I went to. The exhibits are well organized, and walking through the preserved cells really gives you a sense of the harsh conditions prisoners endured.  The atmosphere is quite heavy and emotional, but in a meaningful way—it makes you stop and reflect. I spent about an hour here, and that felt just right.  It’s centrally located and easy to visit, so I’d definitely recommend it if you’re interested in history. Not the most “enjoyable” attraction, but absolutely worth experiencing.

reviews.author: Demetri
reviews.title: Get the Headset
reviews.content: You MUST select a headset. I returned to this place the next day after coming with family as I really felt one does not have the luxury of time when one is travelling with others who may not be as passionate as one on human history.The cost was more than worth it. I originally lost my wallet near reception, but the staff there were great and I recovered it 20 minutes later when I discovered I had lost it. I found the whole experience to be pretty emotional.

reviews.author: WillRod321
reviews.title: Trip round The Hanoi Hilton as it is nicknamed (Hoa Lo Prison)
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit, this prison has a lot of history behind it.

reviews.author: johnhp702
reviews.title: Fascinating history
reviews.content: Most people of a certain age have heard of the Vietnam War and how this prison was known as the Hanoi Hilton but prior to that this prison was used for political prisoners who were against the local government/French. Not sure that the story told here is actually what occurred inside of these wall, but it is fascinating.

reviews.author: Jeremy C
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Anyone with any knowledge of what is understandably referred to here as the "American War" will have heard of the infamous "Hanoi Hilton", but it seems somewhat strange and a surprise that in the middle of this bustling, modern city it is still here, albeit as a museum. However, if you are in Hanoi, you really should come here and even if you don't necessarily agree with the historical narrative put forward, be grateful that you can now visit this beautiful country and wonderful people.

reviews.author: iainb
reviews.title: A very worthwhile and interesting visit.
reviews.content: A very worthwhile visit to this prison. The cost is 50,000vnd per person and an additional 100,000vnd for the headset which was invalueable. The tour through the different areas of the prison took approx 1 hour and the headset talks you through the history of the establishment including American airmen and vietnamese political prisoners. Tickets can be purchased on the day at the entrance.

reviews.author: Stephanie
reviews.title: To do
reviews.content: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison is a deeply poignant experience. We plunge into the dark hours of colonial history and war, with a staging that makes the atmosphere particularly heavy. Despite the gravity of the place, access remains very affordable with a low entry fee, making it an essential and accessible step to understand Vietnam's past. A necessary place of memory that marks the mind long after the release.

reviews.author: Dave Woods
reviews.title: A chaotic place to visit
reviews.content: What a chaotic place to visit. Crowds of people, all coming and going in different directions.Why they can’t make it all follow in one direction only, I’ve no idea. Sure it would involve some planning and the odd bit of construction work, but it’s just a joke as it is.For example, the cells are located in a narrow corridor with a dead end. So you have those trying to go in, struggling to get pass those trying to get out.Do yourself a favour, don’t bother to visit. You can read about it online.

reviews.author: Murton68
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: It was very busy when we visited which is a pity but I think we saw most things.We learnt a lot about the welfare of the prisoners although the section that dealt with the American POW made it sound like a holiday camp so I don’t think this was a true reflection of their imprisonment.  Senator John McCain spent some time here.Overall it is a sobering experience because being held there must have been a living hell.

reviews.author: Alexis P
reviews.title: Must visit but might be one sided
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a must-visit when in Hanoi. The site recounts several harrowing episodes in Vietnamese history, from the French colonial period to the Vietnam War.The exhibition is clear and thoughtfully organized, making it easy to grasp the significance of what you are seeing. The museum effectively recreates the atmosphere experienced by prisoners, notably through the use of life-sized figures placed in reconstructed detention areas. The artifacts themselves are presented with restraint and honesty — few words are needed to convey the reality of their use.The captions accompanying the photographs are equally informative and provide helpful context throughout the visit.That said, I would approach the section on American imprisonment with some caution. Looking more closely into the background of certain prisoners suggests that parts of the narrative may reflect a degree of bias.Even so, this remains an essential visit for anyone wishing to better understand Vietnam’s complex history.

reviews.author: Francois T
reviews.title: Not what we expected
reviews.content: A part of the Prison was under construction and whilst they said you see enough photos of this area it was disappointing. Areas we could see were small and too crowded to spend enough time there. If you in the area and have nothing else to do it could fill a gap, but not recommended to go there specifically for a visit.

reviews.author: Michelle2013
reviews.title: Crowded, awful museum
reviews.content: We couldn’t get past the pictures of American soldiers receiving mail, celebrating Christmas, playing sports, getting health checks etc. they tried to make it look like summer camp for captured soldiers. Yes, what Americans did in Vietnam is terrible, but it was difficult to see this propaganda.

reviews.author: Passport12061120810
reviews.title: Great
reviews.content: Although the audio guide costs extra, I highly recommend getting it.The museum tells history from a Vietnamese point of view, which helps you understand Vietnamese values and mindset.

reviews.author: Colin Swann
reviews.title: Visit to Hua Lo Prison
reviews.content: Interesting morning visiting this infamous place, originally built by the French for political prisoners and became famous for housing US military prisoners. The tour guide was good and gave a different perspective of the how the prisoners were treated during the Vietnam War

reviews.author: Abbie Kelly
reviews.title: Awakening through history
reviews.content: As the saying goes, those who remain unaware of the past are bound to relive its mistakes. A visit to this museum has the power to awaken both hearts and minds, fostering understanding and reminding us to see each other—truly—as fellow human beings worthy of dignity and respect.

reviews.author: Isobel D
reviews.title: Interesting but biased and misleading
reviews.content: The first half focuses on the Vietnamese prisoners under French rule, which was very informative and interesting to learn about. However, don’t expect to learn anything about the treatment of American POWS during the Vietnam War. The American section was extremely biased. The museum mentioned absolutely nothing about how they were tortured, or their living conditions. It showcased propaganda images from the War, which showed prisoners having fun, and engaging willingly in interviews, stating this was their general experience. However this was actually something that prisoners were tortured for until they agreed to take part. I personally don’t agree with many of Americas actions throughout the war, however I felt this exhibition was extremely misleading so I was very disappointed.

reviews.author: elleberk
reviews.title: Hanoi hotel
reviews.content: Museum is under restoration so many rooms partially closed  but even so a very informative and thoughtful presentation of the history of the Hanoi hotel. The audio guide provides a useful and in depth explanation of the artifacts and rooms.  Would recommend.

reviews.author: Bernard W
reviews.title: About the Captured and Tortured - Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Only a section of the large, notorious prison remains, but it packs a lot of information though signs and exhibits about the captured and tortured political prisoners, as well as the physical conditions.  An important, historical place to visit and a good place to learn about the effect of French colonialism.

reviews.author: Wanderlustaustralia
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit, especially to learn about the French colonists and what they did to political prisoners. When we visited it was undergoing renovations, but a staff member informed us of this before we purchased the tickets, so we could decide whether to go in or not. We didn’t do an audio tour, so I feel we missed out on a lot of information.

reviews.author: Silke105
reviews.title: Journey into the past
reviews.content: Admission 50,000 dong, audio guide 100,000 dong.According to our knowledge, representations are somewhat one-sided perhaps precisely for this reason a good experience.

reviews.author: The Pilot Wife
reviews.title: Well worth it
reviews.content: What an interesting and humbling experience here. It’s definitely worth getting the audio tour as it gives more information than the boards. Some exhibits are closed due to renovations but boards have photos on and the audio gives you good description of things. Well worth it.

reviews.author: Cheston Jean
reviews.title: Vietnam war insights with audio guide recommended
reviews.content: Insightful Vietnam War history site—partly under renovation (disclosed in advance). Audio guide recommended; English labels are available, but crowds can obstruct views.

reviews.author: Livsnyderen2014
reviews.title: Facts and harsh realities
reviews.content: One of the safest prisons in Asia from 1893 to 1953 during the French colonial period.Today's museum tells harsh stories about how prisoners were treated with torture and neckline in the guillotine.During the Vietnam War, defeated American pilots were placed here, and they named the Hanoi Hilton prison.Although it was one of the safest prisons, there are stories of fatal escape attempts.A symbol of how humanity has treated each other, even in our time count.

reviews.author: Leonie
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: This is a really interesting place to visit to understand how the prisoners lived and how american prisoners were treated during the war.

reviews.author: Kassia
reviews.title: Compelling, but parts were off-limits & history glossed over
reviews.content: Fascinating, though a significant section was closed for renovations—and they somewhat downplayed the harsh treatment of American POWs. You’ll get a vivid glimpse into the prison’s history—the lifelike statues bring the past to life so convincingly, it almost feels like you’re standing there in that era. The site is exceptionally well-preserved, with informative details displayed throughout.

reviews.author: Alex B
reviews.title: Good historical venue
reviews.content: Very clean and organised. Sequentially good with the narrative. Very helpful staff. Would be amazing if there were an app/digital guide to use. But overall very good!

reviews.author: philip w
reviews.title: Hoa lo prison Hanoi November 2025
reviews.content: We went there and it is a bit commercial and a bit one sided regarding the Vietnam war. It is quite a small exhibition and compared to other prisons I have been in below par. Not one I would visit again.

reviews.author: Emmery Z
reviews.title: Prison museum with depth
reviews.content: I didn't take an audio guide because many exhibits already offer clear explanations in English. It was fascinating to learn about the history of the prison and the lives of both Vietnamese and American prisoners. The exhibition is clearly arranged and offers deep insights into a significant part of Vietnam’s past – a must for history buffs.

reviews.author: Departure44001634851
reviews.title: Very interesting historical site in Hanoi
reviews.content: As someone who really enjoys learning more about history this is was a very informative experience, visiting Hoa La Prison is one of the highlights of visiting Hanoi.

reviews.author: HillCountryTxn
reviews.title: Not worth your time if you're interested in 'Hanoi Hilton'
reviews.content: The museum is nothing more than the gate to the colonial French prison which help political prisoners through the first 50+ yrs. Everything for 1964-1973 has been destroyed and replaced by a few posters of POW years.  I would consider this information as semi-fiction with numerous inaccuracies.

reviews.author: Deb S
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: It was interesting - but I fear we missed a lot by not spending the extra money on the audio tour. I found the captions to the photos superficial.

reviews.author: Louise
reviews.title: Too loud and too busy
reviews.content: This visit could have been very interesting but was spoiled by two elements:1. They let way too many people in. It’s difficult to circulate and see the exhibits.2. Tour guides speak very loudly, which prevents us from hearing the rented audio guides. I went on a Monday and thought that traffic would have been limited. I can’t imagine going on a Sunday!

reviews.author: Liam R
reviews.title: Excellent - Rent the headphones!
reviews.content: Excellent tribute/exhibition/museum about this prison. I’d recommend getting the headphones as you go in (cost more but worth it).

reviews.author: Carpentier
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: You can take headphones with explanations in French in addition to the entrance ticket but in reality there are many explanations in French in the museum.It’s really a great onePlace to visit , filled with history and culture .

reviews.author: Lindekilde
reviews.title: A historical view in Hanoi
reviews.content: Of course we had to experience one of the major tourist attractions in Hanoi – Hoa Lo prison. There is not much left of the prison itself, but we paid the entrance fee and spent about an hour watching the entire exhibition.It was interesting to get an insight into the history of the prison. But overall it was not an experience that stands out markedly or was excessively exciting.Good to see, but if we had opted out of it, we would have managed it too.

reviews.author: Vương Đ
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.content: Great experience. The audio guide was so nice. I enjoy this one a lot. The staffs are also nice and helpful and they are very attentive to their customers. Gave me water also. Good

reviews.author: Emily
reviews.title: Very Good Museum
reviews.content: Very well done museum with good exhibits & information. Can also get an audio guide.Well laid out with a lot to see. A good range of items covering the full history of the museum, as well as memorial. Important to see but be mindful a few topics are not pleasant. Ticket good value, but felt audio guide was overpriced.

reviews.author: Tim F
reviews.title: Hardships of Hanoi
reviews.content: We were charged twice. Once for entry another for headphones. No refund on headphones. Some sections are small so you to wait for entry. Very educational, about the local political prisoners. Once again show the resilience of the local people through historical hardships.

reviews.author: browncondo2102
reviews.title: Vietnam War Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: The Hoa Lo Prison was better known as the Hanoi Hilton.  One of its most famous residents was John McCain who was an American Pilot who was shot down in Hanoi and spent his time here.  There are many mock ups of what life was like here and it wasn't kind to its residents.

reviews.author: Paul F
reviews.title: A history lesson from a Vietnamese perspective.
reviews.content: Really enjoyed the tour guided by a head set in English. Wasn’t really necessary as every display had an English board describing the display.Get there at opening time as tourist groups and local schools get their soon after!

reviews.author: loonylou78
reviews.title: Worth a visit.
reviews.content: Interesting visit to the prison. Visited on a hot day and loads of tourists, so moving round was slow..Interesting things on show , pictures/photos objects etc.  Plenty of information available too, you can also get an audio guide if you would like.

reviews.author: Nadia S
reviews.title: Museum prison
reviews.content: Former prison with personalized status and photos of former prisoners documentary about political prisoners who suffered terrible living conditions photos of Vietnamese revolutionaries in hoa lu prison

reviews.author: Elena W
reviews.title: Visit to the ‘Hanoi Hilton’- Hoa Lo Prison.
reviews.content: This was very educational and visceral reminder of war. The audio in English was exceptional. Seeing an actual guillotine and pictures of victims is confronting. Would recommend to all.

reviews.author: Marie F
reviews.title: Interesting activity for a rainy day
reviews.content: I found this visit really interesting. I would say the audio guide is a must, especially if you are not a French or Vietnamese speaker. I spent over 2 hours here and felt I needed that time to see everything.

reviews.author: Angela C
reviews.title: Really well presented and informative
reviews.content: The prison exhibition is well laid out, provides Vietnamese, English and French for most exhibits plus audio guides and (blissfully for those of us whondon't cope well with the heat) is EXCEPTIONALLY well equiped with large fans and airconditioners throughout.  The experiences of the Vietnamese under the French are grim but it provides insight into why the Vietnamese fought so strongly for their independance.

reviews.author: Phip Pulp
reviews.title: A poignant and essential visit
reviews.content: An intense and moving dive into Vietnamese history. We didn't expect to be so affected. Some cells are chilling. A visit that marks and opens the eyes, essential to understand the country.

reviews.author: Magali L
reviews.title: Mixed
reviews.content: Interesting on the path of Vietnamese history... On the other hand, very questionable on the side of propaganda exacerbated...

reviews.author: yvefreeman@gmail.com
reviews.title: A tour worth the effort
reviews.content: A really great experience. It is worth taking out the audio tour. It is well written and personal. There is a lot to absorb so be prepared. Approx 2 hrs if you follow all the modules and worth getting there early before it gets overly busy.

reviews.author: Smithzc
reviews.title: Excellent audio guide
reviews.content: Very interesting museum. Clear engaging audio guide. The audio guide is 2x entry fee but worth it imo.Worth visiting with children old enough to understand the context.

reviews.author: Rebecca Charles-Myers
reviews.title: Interesting museum
reviews.content: Interesting museum and worth a visit when in Hanoi. Highly recommend you purchase an audio guide to understand what you are seeing. There are in depth stories around the whole museum. Some of the text is extremely small and even more difficult to read when there are larger crowds.

reviews.author: Danielle R
reviews.title: Ok museum
reviews.content: The museum cost 50,000 per adult to get in which was cheap!The exhibition was ok and you need about 45 mins to go round if you don’t have the headsets (100,000 each extra).Nothing spectacular still worth visiting

reviews.author: Belec R
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Very impressive prison memorized and reminding of vietnam war. We did not know that how nightmare was the war, did not know as many people were killed as the guide informed, and never heard such impressive stories of vietnamese people

reviews.author: Adventure05703998509
reviews.title: Interesting but obviously biased museum
reviews.content: We toured the remains of the prison with audio guides that give a lot of context (I strongly advise them). The history of the prison is traced from colonial times to the Vietnam War. However, the influence of pro-Vietnamese propaganda is felt. Prisoners under the colonial regime are shown as examples of bravery locked up for their opinions while the Processing of American pilots has passed under a candy pink filter that totally ignores the war crimes and torture of the time.

reviews.author: Caroline WSL HYZ
reviews.title: Hỏa Lò Prison (Hanoi Hilton)
reviews.content: Visiting Hỏa Lò Prison is a sobering but very insightful experience. The museum gives a glimpse into Vietnam’s complex history—from colonial resistance against the French to the Vietnam War era when American POWs were held here.Highly recommend taking the audio headset, especially if you’re in a couple or small group. It’s well-organized and adds a lot of valuable context as you move through the exhibits. The narration really helps bring the stories to life and makes the visit much more meaningful.It takes about 1 to 2 hours to go through the museum depending on how much time you spend at each section. Some parts can be quite moving, especially the preserved prison cells and the personal stories.If you’re interested in history and want to understand more about Vietnam’s past, this is definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: Jaydeedee
reviews.title: Prison Museum
reviews.content: We wanted to visit one place to learn some Vietnam history with our limited time in Hanoi, and are glad we chose this museum. It gave an in-depth perspective, lots of information, and stories. Entry price was reasonable. My husband hired the audio guide and recounted some extra stories to me, but I found the information boards everywhere provided in English were adequate.

reviews.author: aurelieBou
reviews.title: Nice visit for family with teenagers
reviews.content: This is a museum I recommend for family with teenagers on Hanoi.It is the cultural side of Vietnam that must be remembered here.The indications are also in French to know about this prison in Vietnam. You do not have to take a guide or audio guide. The price is 50,000 dong per adult. Our teenager didn't pay for admission.Ps. This remains a sad place because it is a prison.

reviews.author: Em Happy Travelling Folks
reviews.title: Prison Visit - Cool guillotine!
reviews.content: An interesting read when walking through prison. Quite a humbling and impactful time to reflect on the resilience of the human spirit to resist, survive, and the complex nature of human experience due to colonisation, occupation, and wars in general. We were a bit rushed. Lady at the door rude re the ages of our children (one I wouldn’t even call tall) and us needing proof to be carried on us. Other than that, quite enjoyable and some undercover if you get rain. Worth it visit IMO.

reviews.author: Xem Số Mệnh
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison – A Haunting Remnant of Cruelty and the Unyielding Spirit of Revolutionaries
reviews.content: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison is not merely a historical excursion — it is an emotional reckoning. The moment I stepped inside, a chilling silence wrapped around me. It wasn’t the air that made me shiver, but the weight of suffering, resistance, and unspoken screams that still linger within these cold, oppressive walls.Built by the French colonists to incarcerate and break the will of Vietnamese patriots, Hoa Lo was designed as a living hell. Narrow, airless cells, heavy wooden shackles, and rusting iron bars speak of the torment inflicted. Instruments of torture — including the infamous guillotine — are preserved like grim witnesses to the brutality of a regime that sought to crush the human spirit through pain and fear.Yet amidst that horror, what struck me deepest was not just the cruelty, but the courage.As a traveler representing Xemsomenh.com, where we explore the fate, soul, and resilience of the Vietnamese people, I was deeply moved by how the revolutionaries transformed this prison into a cradle of strength and ideals. Names like Phan Boi Chau, Nguyen Duc Canh, and Nguyen Van Cu echo through the halls — not as victims, but as symbols of heroic resistance. Within these bleak cells, they turned darkness into light, turning torture chambers into classrooms, and nurturing hope in places meant to extinguish it.Hoa Lo is no longer just a museum. It is a place of remembrance — a shrine to sacrifice, and a testament to the iron will of those who laid the foundation for our independence. It reminds us that while colonists may have wielded chains and swords, they could not imprison the human spirit nor destroy the dream of freedom.Walking through these corridors, it is impossible not to feel humbled. You don’t just see history — you feel it. The pain is palpable, but so is the pride. Each rusted chain, each crude wooden door, tells a story that demands not only respect, but also reflection.At Xemsomenh.com, we believe that destiny is shaped not only by stars and numbers, but by the courage of those who dared to change their fate. Hoa Lo Prison is living proof. Here, fate was rewritten — not by surrender, but by sacrifice.If you come to Hanoi, don’t skip this place. Come with an open heart. Leave with a deeper understanding — not just of Vietnam’s painful past, but of the extraordinary spirit that rose from it.

reviews.author: lilybt
reviews.title: The air is heavy.
reviews.content: This facility was established during French rule to house Vietnamese political prisoners and activists. It was used to house American prisoners of war during the Vietnam War, and was apparently referred to by American soldiers at the time as the Hanoi Hilton. The exhibition is mainly colonial, with instruments used for torture and a guillotine table with a blade attached, and there is a rather heavy atmosphere. It is impressive that the air conditioning crisis is bad for a lot of tourists, and it is so hot and humid that you might think it is a production.

reviews.author: Global Wanderers
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: 50,000 vnd well spent.It’s well structured and covers a lot of history. You pay extra for the audio guide but we didn’t feel as though we missed out without one.Well worth it - and a short walk to old town.

reviews.author: Windy2512
reviews.title: For anyone seaching history
reviews.content: (Cash only) Ticket: 50,000 VND; Guided tour: 100,000 VNDIt takes about two hours to complete the tour with a guide, and there are chairs along the way to sit and listenYou can better understand the history of Huolu Prison through pictures and sounds, recommended👍It's very crowded on Monday afternoon, but you can see the exhibits by waiting for each otherIncredibly informative and interesting exhibition of the sufferings endured by the Vietnamese people. I wish there is more staff around as some visitors were being insensitive and disrespectful.

reviews.author: Creeping_Death_LA
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton not a five star
reviews.content: The price of admission is so low it would be a crime not spend at least one hour inside this historic prison. Once we went inside of a couple of the rooms we thought that's it and decided to leave but there was lot more to see. We kept wandering around the grounds and there was a lot of information about the history of the prisoners and escape attempts.

reviews.author: Jan T
reviews.title: Insight into French Colonization - and man's inhumanity to fellow human beings
reviews.content: Relatively small but interesting museum, providing an insight primarily into the French Colonization period but also Vietnam War. Disturbing and moving, well worth a detour and visit

reviews.author: Bernie T
reviews.title: Great
reviews.content: Fascinating museum detailing the political prisoners,  their lives, imprisonment,  resilience of the prisoners. Well worth a visit

reviews.author: Spaghetti and Meatballs
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: Very interesting reading about all the prisoners and learning history of Vietnam. Very cheap to get in. Go for a look if you’re close

reviews.author: german_taliesin
reviews.title: Interesting, not entirely objective
reviews.content: Interesting museum, well done, informative, friendly, audio guide Charging stations...Covers colonial times and American War.The American War is probably not entirely objective. Definitely worth seeing

reviews.author: sarah zeke
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: You’ll learn a lot about the culture & history of Vietnam by visiting. Kinda spooky but the place is pretty small so you can check it out quick.

reviews.author: TUMBO10
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Ashamed to say I don't really know the history of Vietnam, and I thought this prison was only for American Pilots from the Vietnam war.It was actually built by the French, an interesting piece of history and well set out museum. It was the entrance fee, plus an additional fee of the headphones.It will take you approximately 90 minutes with the headphones on, to get round.

reviews.author: Tim-1664
reviews.title: Great museum
reviews.content: This is a great museum to learn allAbout the history,  a great walk around with lots of information and things to look at.Well laid out and there are places to get a drink with the heat,  I would definitely recommend this to anyone who is going and has a couple of hours spare.

reviews.author: maho
reviews.title: Japanese audio guide is difficult to understand
reviews.content: It was very crowded, probably because I went to a holiday in Vietnam, and I was not in a position to calm down and watch the exhibition.We used an audio guide in Japanese, but it was difficult to hear who was speaking, and there were many mistranslations, so we couldn't hear them (especially male voices, which were often inaudible).If you listen to all of the audio guides, it takes about two hours in 35 places, so I recommend doing some research in advance and watching without them.

reviews.author: AMsays
reviews.title: Light an incense stick to hopefully inspire a more peaceful future.
reviews.content: Sarcastically known as "Hanoi Hilton," this infamous prison was renowned for its harsh treatment of prisoners. French built in 1896; it is now mostly torn down and transformed into a museum with stark reminders of the era of its prominence. It was hard walking through there knowing some of the history which included the incarceration of Senator John McCain.  Originally the prison had 4 areas (A-D). Within those areas were the cramped cells, torture devices and the Guillotine Room. Today we see articles of oppression, the sewer used to escape and the POW exhibition area. Significant artifacts including haunting photos and prison objects. There’s newly created artwork and sculptures of prisoners. You can light an incense stick to hopefully inspire a more peaceful future. I did.

reviews.author: Simon M
reviews.title: Another must see
reviews.content: You can't visit the city and not come here. Such sad history for the people of Vietnam here and I advise you get a tour guide to explain it all in detail.

reviews.author: SB01
reviews.title: Grimly Engaging
reviews.content: Most western visitors will gravitate here due to its place in fairly recent history. Overall it is very well done, giving a grim sense of the experience of the inmates. History is written by the victors, and I suspect this is the case with a some of the description of the treatment of the US pilots. It was not a hotel.Everything is in immaculate condition and treated with reverence by the staff and visitors. Even without the audio guide there was plenty of information available. You will spend at least an hour here and possibly twice that.

reviews.author: Clerissa Dario
reviews.title: Excellent museum
reviews.content: This site is an essential stop for any visitor—not only does it play a pivotal role in Vietnam's and Hanoi's historical narrative, but it also serves as a profound window into the region's heritage. To fully appreciate its context, I strongly suggest opting for the audio guide, which adds depth to the exploration. The concise one-hour tour makes it an ideal addition to your itinerary, blending education with efficiency.

reviews.author: valentina
reviews.title: a meaningful journey
reviews.content: A truly wonderful and meaningful journey, I cried listening to the stories that happened here and their courage. In this place full of history and pain, I rediscovered the value of resilience, love for one’s land and freedom.

reviews.author: Alice R
reviews.title: An important visit of you want to understand the complex history of Vietnam
reviews.content: Visiting Hoa Lo prison was one of the most memorable parts of our trip. The museum offeres a deep look into the history of Vietnam. There're different sections, presented from the Vietnamese perspective, so some of the information may seem biased or sanitized, but it's still fascinating to see. The signage is mostly in Englsih and Vietnamese so it's quite easy to follow.Took us about 1 hour to go through everything. Entry was cheap snf worth the price.

reviews.author: Phil R
reviews.title: Worth a Visit
reviews.content: Another opportunity to see a different view of Vietnams colonial and wartime history.  Compare how the French treated prisoners to how the Vietnamese treats POWs.  Well worth a visit but take your time, get an audio guide and expect lots of people

reviews.author: capsicum0620
reviews.title: Why not...
reviews.content: Useful information, some striking photos but propaganda drowns everything in a partial and indigestible emotional bath. Remains a beautiful architecture.

reviews.author: Ruth C
reviews.title: Great audio guide
reviews.content: A really good museum and very much worth getting the excellent audio guide to make the most of its story. Give yourself a good 2hrs to explore. We found that using the audio guide and doing it on your own allowed you to go at your own pace. Little benches in each space are good so you can sit and listen comfortably. It got quite busy with big groups occasionally but wait a few minutes and they passed through quickly.

reviews.author: Trip U
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: Wonderful architecture in Hanoi, Vietnamese history. Encourage people to visit . There are many places to take pictures and there should be an interpreter.

reviews.author: chillyandKeith
reviews.title: Well worth a visit when in Hanoi
reviews.content: Well worth a visit, very moving and grim seeing the conditions the pow’s lived in but all very well presented. But the audio it’s a time saver rather than reading everything. An interesting experience.

reviews.author: Harirajan Varatharajan
reviews.title: A tragic past
reviews.content: Visiting Hoa Lò Prison was a deeply moving experience. The historical significance of the site, both as a place where Vietnamese revolutionaries were held by the French and later used during the Vietnam War, struck me profoundly. The exhibits, from the dark, confined cells to the stories of the prisoners, really brought the past to life. Despite the somber atmosphere, I found it to be an insightful and important part of understanding Vietnam’s history, and it left me with a deeper respect for the resilience of those who endured such hardship.

reviews.author: Egon V
reviews.title: excellent
reviews.content: A fascinating experience full of history! The visit was really interesting, with many details to discover along the way. However, the cost of the audio guide does not seem fully justified, as the information provided does not add much to that already on the information signs. To better enjoy the site, perhaps it is better to rely on reading and direct observation!

reviews.author: corinne_prevost
reviews.title: LEARN THE STORY
reviews.content: It is very well done and everything is very well told. An excellent history lesson. To see and review because everything is very well explained

reviews.author: mion369
reviews.title: History in pictures
reviews.content: Interesting and oppressive, as long as it deals with the conditions in prison during the French occupation. The Vietnamese prisoners were treated inhumanely. Later, American pilots were trapped here during the Vietnam War. Nothing is told about their circumstances, except propaganda where you wonder if all that is true... it looks like a holiday camp with volleyball, walks, medical care etc... But when you poke through the propaganda it is very interesting!

reviews.author: Bp-np-travelling
reviews.title: God not great location
reviews.content: Decent and cheap. The hard set was cheap and easy and explained things well. Not heaps to see. Pretty basic but some interesting.

reviews.author: DTWtravellers
reviews.title: Vietnam’s version
reviews.content: I’m so surprised at the complaints about this museum.  Museums are made from the country where they are located.  I’m sure the museums in the USA do not 100% accurately depict the military actions during that time period.  We found the museum interesting to see.  Both my wife and I had researched this before we went so we had a basic understanding that this would be from the view of the Vietnamese.  To hear the history was interesting but saddening as well.  Living conditions, tortures and executions were real despite the point of view of the country.  I would suggest going to this museum but please do some research so you are not disappointed by the point of view

reviews.author: Ian R
reviews.title: Interesting and sombre place to visit
reviews.content: Came across the prison by chance whilst walking around the old and french quarters. There are plaques around the prison in English and French that help guide you around the prison.It would appear that it was an exceedingly tough life / death if for detainees.US pilots were apparently treated quite well whilst they stayed at the Hanoi Hilton.I'd definitely suggest visiting.

reviews.author: MrDream688
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: Known as the "Hanoi Hilton," this former prison offers a powerful insight into Vietnam’s past. Exhibits detail its use during French colonial rule and the Vietnam War, making it a poignant historical site.

reviews.author: Peter1199
reviews.title: Worth a visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: Worth a visit if you are Hanoi. The Museum is small and we entered before the 5 pm closing and we appreciated the ability to stay in the Museum until 6pm.

reviews.author: Sue M
reviews.title: Grim Reality
reviews.content: It is worthwhile to see this prison that American POWs had to endures as well as Vietnamese political prisoners of the French.

reviews.author: pf1sh
reviews.title: Great exhibition
reviews.content: This is a must for visitors to Vietnam and Hanoi. Important lesson in how not to behave as foreign powers. Well laid out exhibition and photos

reviews.author: Naomi B
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: Hoa Lo prison is within walking distance of the old quarter. It’s really done well and gives a good sense of what life must have been like for the prisoners. The audio guide costs about double what the entry fee is (and is on top of entry).  I think it would be worth it if you are interested in much more detailed history. The exhibits do have short explanations in Vietnamese and English and actually that would have been enough for me as I found the audio guide didn’t move at my pace and really detracted from me being present in the moment but I think this is just down to how we individually interact with these things.

reviews.author: Caroline C
reviews.title: an interesting visit
reviews.content: This was an interesting, pro-Vietnamese/pro-Communist story of Hoa Lo prison. Most of the original building has been destroyed, but you can still walk through parts of the original prison. The audio guide was well worth it. I spent an hour and a half there and it was the perfect amount of time.

reviews.author: OnAir38937315268
reviews.title: French Prison -- Grim Place
reviews.content: One of the key places to visit, there's much to see about the (very bad) treatment of political prisoners by the French. Not so much about how the American POWs were treated. Lots of historical displays and information -- again, mostly on Vietnamese prisoners. Not a big place. A visit takes an hour.

reviews.author: Chantal R
reviews.title: An informative and poignant visit
reviews.content: This visit is important to understand part of the history of Hanoi. This visit is both informative and poignant. It reveals cruelty, resilience and human creativity. In short, the human being in all that he has good and bad. We liked it. To really enjoy the visit you really have to take the audio guide.

reviews.author: Thomas S
reviews.title: Don't go here. Wasted time.
reviews.content: This place is full of propaganda. Dropp guide, and make your own preparations so you can understand the story correctly. This is one of many places in Vietnam that repeat untruths in historical context. Not impressed.

reviews.author: JensLundgaard
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Very interesting and informative. The place is kept to a high standard and the displays are scaringly good.  I absolutely recommend spending a little extra on the audio guide.

reviews.author: Simon
reviews.title: Nice learning but a little one-sided view
reviews.content: We selected audio guide as recommended. Nice historical review of history, but lacked more authentic details. Most of it was designed to demonstrate, and gave a clear mark of this. A lot of focus on how they treated American prisoners, and it was something unilateral. Nice details about the French colonial era.

reviews.author: Keelyimps
reviews.title: Well worth a visit.
reviews.content: Very interesting to walk around. I would recommend the ear phone information pack for a little extra cost, you get so much more interesting facts about the prison. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: chaosandcandy
reviews.title: Crowded but Interesting
reviews.content: When we visited in morning (around 10am) the museum was extremely crowded. It was really hard to read any of the information presented. The info was interesting, if not perhaps a bit one-sided. Either way, it was interesting, but a bit stressful to navigate the crowds crammed into the small rooms.

reviews.author: eliza248
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Well laid out and an interesting museum. Worth getting the audio  tour too. Would allow 1.5 to 2 hours. Provides some useful background information to the wars the Vietnamese people have gone through relatively recently and it's impressive they seemingly hold no grudges against their invaders.

reviews.author: OmanRob
reviews.title: Very cool museum / exhibit
reviews.content: This is a must see in Ha Po I’d say, I also liked how the main focus of the history was about political prisoners rather than Americanized - do get the audio tour which is informative and interesting Rob

reviews.author: Deano1967
reviews.title: How to re-write history, Vietnamese style.
reviews.content: By all means visit the "Hanoi Hilton" but do your homework beforehand to learn the real stories of what went on in here because you certainly can't rely on the Vietnamese version of the truth being told.Making themselves out as latter-day saints, it's all the fault of the French and the Americans committing atrocities and torture against the valiant native population who were just freedom fighters.There isn't a single mention anywhere of what the Vietnamese did by way of torture to the American pilots who ended up here (do a Google search for "strappado" for one of the torture means, but you won't find a single reference to it in the totally one-sided presentation of history.We left feeling utterly at a loss because of the outright lies being told in this place. Yes, it's a Communist country but if you want Western money you're going to have to tell the truth because the truth is so very easy to find for those willing to see it.

reviews.author: R958_James
reviews.title: a useful way to spend an afternoon
reviews.content: We took our kids around - and they enjoyed it as much as we did - well worth a visit if you find yourself in this part of the city and don't have other plans

reviews.author: joe v
reviews.title: "History" museum filled with falsehoods
reviews.content: As a museum on the history of Hoa Lo prison, there is a shocking lack of actual history. Instead the museum is dedicated to shameless propaganda for the Communist Party of Vietnam.The start of the museum showcases the horrors inflicted on Vietnamese prisoners when the museum was run by French colonials. You can walk through the inhumanely cramped rooms and see the barbarism of how prisoners were kept. Clearly the French built a nasty prison and committed numerous attrocities here and it would be a crime to continue it's use.However, skip forwards a few years, and the prison is now being used to house American POWs. Surely Americans being housed in the same prison must have also faced terrible conditions? They nicknamed the prison "Heartbreak Hotel," but no, according to the museum, American prisoners were treated like honored guests. They were free to enjoy Christmas feasts and games of basketball (as long as a cameraman was nearby to record for propaganda purposes).The museum that could be used to present history is now just a house of propoganda and untruths. This is somewhat unsurprising, as even during the war they concealed what was occurring here. Admiral Jeremiah Denton had to blink "torture" in Morse code while telling interviewers how great a time he was having for any information to get out.Tldr; The museum is preserved well and has a good setup, but any attempt at teaching history is overshadowed by posting blatant lies (that can be facts checked with a 10 second google search) all over the information boards

reviews.author: Hugary1
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: A must to see the prison where US pilots were held in very difficult circumstances. If the place is busy the corridors can be difficult as the in is also the out route.A courtyard with memorial is a relief to get to after the cramped conditions

reviews.author: Douglass Y
reviews.title: Harrowing history together
reviews.content: This wasn’t just another tourist stop; it was a raw dive into Vietnam’s harrowing history, told from a poignant Vietnamese perspective. The exhibits—photos, artifacts, and stories—pulled at our hearts in unexpected ways. We stood silently before rusted shackles, imagining lives once bound by them. It was somber yet enlightening, as if the walls whispered tales of resilience and pain. As a couple, we found ourselves reflecting deeply, discussing what freedom truly means. Some sections felt hard to digest, almost intrusive, but that’s the point—it forces you to remember, not forget. For all its emotional toll, Hoa Lo is unforgettable, leaving us with more questions than answers about humanity’s past mistakes.

reviews.author: Wendy W
reviews.title: Such a wonderful way to see both sides of this history
reviews.content: This was a great morning spent looking at how the Vietnamese kept their fighting spirit alive even under great pressure form the invaders from many countries.There are  sad, fascinating & proud moments to witness Please allow 2-3 hours to really take it all in

reviews.author: zhou
reviews.title: It's worth seeing.
reviews.content: I went to the French colonial prison in Hanoi and felt the misery of the colonial era, and the overall feeling of experience was still good, but the downside was that the prison wasn't much, the experience was 30; the minutes were basically over.

reviews.author: Hiroko M
reviews.title: Worth Visiting
reviews.content: Worth visiting while in Hanoi. Great exhibition of the French colonialisation resistance. The American intrusion of the Vietnam War is exhibited.

reviews.author: Alexandra N
reviews.title: Very interesting.
reviews.content: Very interesting and informative. Only a small part of the prison is left but the exhibits and audio guide really paint a picture of what it was like, and a really valuable lesson in some of the history of Vietnam. Definitely worth it.

reviews.author: Otto S
reviews.title: I recommend making this visit
reviews.content: The visit is recommended. The whole prison story. From when it was founded to when a group of prisoners escaped.I recommend taking the audio guide to understand each room

reviews.author: Mareike
reviews.title: Through misinformation we unfortunately doubt the entire museum
reviews.content: We are divided, because the depictions of the prison are very well made and poignant. The audio guide was also well done.However, the reappraisal of the Vietnam War period is historically wrong and completely twisted. Unfortunately, this is where the lack of press freedom becomes apparent. The torture that took place in the prison during this time is completely covered up and the conditions as described in the hotel. Just as Americans used the term “Hilton Hanoi” ironically, the “museum” portrays this term as true.

reviews.author: Rolls Grant V
reviews.title: A must do in Hanoi if you love to learn about culture and history
reviews.content: It is a moving experience. It is interesting to learn the Viet history. The audio guide is a must to appreciate more the visuals.From 🇵🇭

reviews.author: James O
reviews.title: Eye opening demonstration of man's inhumanity to man
reviews.content: We visited mid-morning to avoid the tour crowds, and I would suggest the earlier the better, so as to experience the displays with the level of solitude it requires.I was astounded by the number of people who wouldn't pay a paltry fee for the self guided audio headset as it added so much clarity to the experience.It was shocking to see how a supposedly civilised country such as France treated their fellow humans, but then again, how many empires behaved in such a manor ? and how many countries still are today ?The displays were well laid out and numbered for ease of understanding with the audio  headset.I realise that this is Vietnam's story to tell, however, I thought it was a little cheapened by the constant maintenance of the party line through the French area when human emotion must have been to the fore of the poor Vietnamese, and the assertion that, in general, the American POWs were treated with such gentleness and compassion during that conflict. Obviously, the pictures and displays are authentic, however, I imagine selective portrayal was extensively used.I thought the narrative was weigted unnecessarily heavily in one direction, as what I assume would be a more accurate portrayal, would certainly be understandable to most people today.For me, both the story and site were lessened a little by such.I'm glad I went and would  recommend a visit to anyone visiting Ha Noi.Also, maybe it's just me, but I noticed a few people openly sobbing ??? Whilst its eye opening for sure, I certainly didn't achieve such emotion.

reviews.author: Louise
reviews.title: An Insight into Vietnamese Prisons
reviews.content: A little out of the way but if you have time and are into history I would put this on the to do list. Entrance fee is around $4 AUD and the audio guide is another $4 per person. We had read the audio guide was worth while but didn’t really want to spend the extra so just got one guide and shared a pair of headphones! Worked out fine - the museum is quite busy but still enjoyable and not too crowded. You could still enjoy the museum without the audio guide but the guide did provide access to some great stories throughout. If I were to go again I would still only purchase the 1 guide but I would only bother listening to the audio attached to the personal story pictures these are easily earmarked and I would also listen to the guide around all the torture devices. Some of the information about the treatment of American soldiers was definitely brushed over/ selectively included - as an Australian teacher who has taught Year 10 history the perspective was interesting however, selective.Would recommend going especially if you like prisons or war!

reviews.author: jim d
reviews.title: Worth a visit to get a different prospective
reviews.content: Very informative, though suspect based on the info provided around the American POWs treatment that it’s very one sided. That said, the French treatment of the Vietnamese people was horrible.

reviews.author: memee08
reviews.title: Fascinating history
reviews.content: We paid for an audio guide and, although pricey relative to the entrance ticket, it was easy to use with clear language, and provided lots of extra detail that wasn’t available within the museum. Of particular interest were the personal accounts portrayed. The museum was very interesting, detailing numerous atrocities that were bestowed upon political prisoners that ended up here. As mentioned before, the American POW section did present a very positive perspective of how they were treated. Was this the case? Maybe? One thing I loved about this museum was the numerous benches provided to sit on, everywhere! Very nice to be able to sit and listen to the audio guide in peace as people filtered past.

reviews.author: Cyndie
reviews.title: A must visit
reviews.content: A must visit. It is not pleasant, but the history is so fascinating. What the French did was unforgivable to these poor people I felt the negative energy the moment I walked in.

reviews.author: Schuyler Wii
reviews.title: Heavy History
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison was a powerful experience, a sobering look at a harrowing history. The weight of the stories, a symbol of resistance, was palpable. It's not a lighthearted visit, but definitely impactful. We left feeling a bit somber, but glad we went.

reviews.author: Voyage29672267144
reviews.title: Experience the Tour "Hanoi Essence: 6 Hours of Magic" - An Impressive Journey to Discover the Capital
reviews.content: Recently, I had the opportunity to join the tour “Hanoi Essence: 6 Hours of Magic” – a short but emotional and memorable journey to discover Hanoi. As someone who has participated in many tours, I was really impressed by the meticulousness and scientific arrangement of the schedule as well as the quality of service that the organizer provided.The tour started at 13:20 at Hoa Lo Prison – a famous historical site in the heart of Hanoi. Right from the gathering, I felt the professionalism when the tour guide briefly introduced the schedule and important notes. I was quite impressed with the way the staff took care of the tourists, from ensuring drinking water to welcoming them warmly. Hoa Lo Prison carries within it painful but proud historical stories. Under the guidance of the tour guide, each story and each artifact seemed to come alive before my eyes. Leaving Hoa Lo, the group quickly moved to Thang Long Imperial Citadel by comfortable and cool means of transport. The shuttle bus was very punctual, clean and fully equipped with drinking water for each passenger. At Thang Long Imperial Citadel, I felt like I was stepping into a space of the past, where the vestiges of ancient dynasties are still imprinted through each brick and each gate. The tour guide not only introduced historical information but also told interesting stories, making the tour not dry at all. After hours of exploring history, the group moved to Hanoi Old Quarter to enjoy the typical cuisine here. The time for cuisine was arranged reasonably, not too rushed. The tour suggested a few famous restaurants in the Old Quarter and I chose a small, pretty restaurant with typical dishes such as pho, bun, and spring rolls. Each dish had a strong Hanoi flavor, was fresh and delicious, and was served very attentively.In the late afternoon, the group experienced the feeling of sitting on a cyclo around Hoan Kiem Lake. This was probably the most romantic and memorable moment of the trip. When the city began to light up, Hoan Kiem Lake appeared sparkling with Turtle Tower and the bright red The Huc Bridge. Sitting on a cyclo, watching the narrow old streets, the street stalls, and the flow of people created a peaceful picture of Hanoi amidst the hustle and bustle of life.Next, the group stopped by Thang Long Water Puppet Theater to enjoy a traditional art performance. The wooden puppets were skillfully manipulated under the water, combined with traditional music to create an artistic space imbued with Vietnamese identity. The performances tell familiar yet captivating folk tales. The last stop on the journey is Indochine restaurant. The restaurant space is luxurious, cozy and the menu is diverse and attractive. I really like the attentive service of the staff here, always ready to meet all the guests' requests.Dinner took place in a comfortable, cheerful atmosphere. Delicious food, beautifully presented and especially a relaxing time after a long day of exploration.The tour ended at 19:30 and the tour guide did not forget to say goodbye and introduce other tours for those who want to explore Hanoi more deeply. Hanoi Essence: 6 Hours of Magic" is truly a short but extremely complete journey. From historical relics, cultural spaces to cuisine and art, all are arranged harmoniously and carefully. If you are looking for a tour to explore Hanoi in a short time but still full of experiences, do not hesitate to book this tour right away.

reviews.author: Hany G
reviews.title: A must for history enthusiastic!
reviews.content: It was part of our free walking tour and we glad that we visited the prison. It is located in the French quarter to scare the rebellions. The prison was built since the French colonial and continued to serve during the Vietnam War. It has many stories about the prisoners.I highly recommend getting a tour guide to explain to yiu the history and the stories behind these walls.

reviews.author: Giorgos-Rodos
reviews.title: One of the city's attractions worth visiting
reviews.content: They are the prisons built by the French conquerors and used by the Vietnamese to detain American prisoners during the Vietnam War, as well as political prisoners. It's worth a visit.

reviews.author: Almacsixtyeight
reviews.title: Educational visit
reviews.content: I don’t doubt that this visit is part of the school curriculum in Vietnamese schools. However there is a lesson for all of us here, because atrocities against fellow humans continues today. I do admire Vietnam for owning its history. I think that makes for a better nation, has allowed healing, reconciliation and understanding. If a visit here makes fight for human rights and dignity a much needed voice. Then the lesson has achieved much.

reviews.author: Phương Anh T
reviews.title: A Fascinating and Sobering Experience at Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: Visiting Hỏa Lò Prison in Hanoi was a truly eye-opening experience. As a tourist, I appreciated the well-preserved historical artifacts and the detailed information provided throughout the museum.What I liked:- The museum offers a balanced narrative about the prison's history, from its use during the French colonial period to its role in the Vietnam War.- The exhibits are engaging and immersive, with a mix of photographs, documents, and reconstructed prison cells that give a vivid sense of the harsh conditions faced by prisoners.- The storytelling was powerful, particularly the section on the resilience and determination of Vietnamese revolutionaries held there.- The air-conditioned interiors provided a comfortable environment for learning, even on a hot day in Hanoi.But I didn’t like something as:- Some parts of the museum felt a bit crowded, especially during peak visiting hours, which made it challenging to fully enjoy the exhibits.- While the displays were informative, I felt that certain narratives were a bit one-sided, particularly in the section dedicated to American POWs during the Vietnam War. Adding more perspectives would enrich the storytelling. Overall, Hỏa Lò Prison is a must-visit for history enthusiasts and anyone interested in understanding Vietnam’s complex past. It’s a sobering reminder of the struggles and sacrifices made during pivotal moments in history.

reviews.author: houndy11
reviews.title: And interesting look into the prison past
reviews.content: This prison is near to Hanoi towers which is actually built on some the site as well. Get the audio guide to listen to the stories to get a look of it from colonial times to the war times.

reviews.author: Paul Lee
reviews.title: Impressive place
reviews.content: The historical stories are amazing. Precious historical documents provide a lot of unique information. One of the best places if you want to learn about Vietnam

reviews.author: Philip H
reviews.title: A must for Hanoi
reviews.content: A must if you visit Hanoi.  Very well presented compact and informative.   Covering many different conflicts in Hanoi’s history. Suggestion. Take your time going round and absorb the atmosphere

reviews.author: Gerri Jane
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: Not the most cheerful tourist spot, but we felt it was important to see. The exhibits about Vietnamese prisoners were extensive, while the American POW section seemed selective in its narrative. The guillotine display was particularly chilling. Informative but heavy experience.

reviews.author: Andrea C
reviews.title: Historical
reviews.content: Great visit, all very interesting.I think the price of the audio guide is not justified (it tells nothing more than information signs).

reviews.author: Aaron S
reviews.title: Great Experience
reviews.content: Great experience, very informative and quite emotional  a real eye opener. The Vietnamese people have been through it and come out smiling, positive and forward looking

reviews.author: JOHN H
reviews.title: Inspiring
reviews.content: This is more than a museum it's a testament to strength of conviction and character.  It's of Ghandi and Mandella proportions and it deserves a visit in respect of the struggles to achieve goals and survive in the process.

reviews.author: Teresina Hughes
reviews.title: A poignant and educational tour
reviews.content: The exhibitions are well organized and tell the dark but important history of this place. The audio guides in French allowed us to understand everything. A moving experience that marked us.

reviews.author: David Roy P
reviews.title: Tells a very poignant story
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison was formally a prison during the French occupation of Vietnam and was occupied by Vietnamese political prisoners . This museum , as it is now tells the Brutal story of the French Rule of Vietnam and the Vietnamese struggle for independence .During the American War ( Vietnam War) It was occupied by American Prisoners who gave it the nickname , the Hanoi Hilton . To truly understand why the War was fought you need to visit this prison as it tells a very poignant story .

reviews.author: Frannie Dig
reviews.title: Historical site
reviews.content: Though the exhibits are haunting, they tell important stories that need to be heard. A profound experience that made us appreciate our freedom and peace together even more.

reviews.author: Judy T
reviews.title: Great way to learn about Viet history here
reviews.content: Modern bright building (nice) on the outside. In the inside, it’s gloomy and filled with dark glimpse of Vietnamese history. Great place to learn a little bit about Vietnamese history, Indowar and American pilots who were prisoned there

reviews.author: Cord Bury
reviews.title: A journey through history together
reviews.content: Walking through the somber halls, we felt the weight of history. The exhibits were thoughtfully curated, showcasing the resilience of those who endured such hardships. We shared our thoughts and emotions, deepening our connection. It was a poignant reminder of the past, and we left with a greater appreciation for freedom and love.

reviews.author: Caley
reviews.title: Not for everyone
reviews.content: Stomach churning and left halfway through the tour. Something about taking pictures of old prison cells does not sit right.

reviews.author: Rajesh
reviews.title: Hoa Lo - An impressive and touching historical relic
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is not only a museum, but also a journey back to Vietnam's painful past. From the narrow, stuffy cells to artifacts such as handcuffs and shackles, all recreate the extremely harsh living conditions that prisoners had to endure. I was especially impressed with the display of revolutionary soldiers who sacrificed their lives for the ideals of independence and freedom. In particular, this place also preserves stories about American pilots imprisoned during the war, a part of history that not everyone knows. Visiting Hoa Lo Prison made me feel very emotional and grateful for the sacrifices that previous generations made for the country to be what it is today

reviews.author: Luskas
reviews.title: A must-see trip to better understand Vietnamese history
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is one of the historical destinations that cannot be missed when coming to Hanoi. During the tour, I was able to admire historical artifacts such as handcuffs, shackles and photos of prison life under the brutal rule of the French colonialists. Every cell, every corner in the museum brought a heavy feeling, as if I was reliving the difficult days of the revolutionary soldiers. A special part was the exhibition about American pilots, including John McCain, which gave me a deeper insight into the Vietnam War. This is an ideal place for those who want to learn about the history of the country.

reviews.author: John
reviews.title: Discover a part of Hanoi's brutal history
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a special and profound place to visit, where you can learn about a painful part of Vietnam's history under French colonialism and war. The museum holds many valuable artifacts, such as handcuffs, shackles and documents reflecting the brutality of detention and torture of prisoners. I was very impressed with the display of revolutionary soldiers and American pilots imprisoned here during the Vietnam War. The space of the prison clearly recreates the harsh life of prisoners. A visit to Hoa Lo will help you understand more deeply the difficulties that the Vietnamese people had to go through to regain independence."

reviews.author: Lea
reviews.title: An emotional tour
reviews.content: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison helped me understand more about the hardships that the revolutionary soldiers had to face. I was most impressed with the display of artifacts such as handcuffs, shackles and the guillotine - the horrifying torture tools of the French colonial period. The stories about the indomitable spirit and sacrifice of the prisoners moved me deeply. This is a great destination to learn about the arduous but proud past of the Vietnamese people.

reviews.author: Jonathan
reviews.title: A place to preserve heroic historical stories"
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a place that preserves the painful but also heroic historical stories of Vietnam. The dark, stuffy space of the cells gives a creepy feeling, helping me to imagine the harshness that prisoners had to go through. I was very impressed with the exhibition area about prison life, escape attempts and the solidarity of revolutionary soldiers. This is truly a place worth visiting to learn more about the history of Vietnam's struggle for independence

reviews.author: Maria
reviews.title: An emotional tour of Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a must-see if you want to understand more about Vietnam’s painful history. Here, you will see artifacts such as handcuffs, prison cells, and documentary photos that document the harsh lives of political prisoners. The stories of resilience and indomitable will of those who were imprisoned here are truly touching and deeply impressive. Don’t forget to take the time to read the detailed descriptions of prison life, which will help you better understand this difficult period in Vietnam’s history

reviews.author: Sherpa441005
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: Very good place to visit if you like history places. All you need to know about years ago with the vietnam wars with the french and Americans

reviews.author: Hannah
reviews.title: A place to tell stories of resilience and patriotism
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a must-see destination when visiting Hanoi. It holds many tragic historical stories about the French colonial period and the Vietnam War. The museum is well-preserved, with galleries detailing the harsh lives of prisoners, including American soldiers captured during the Vietnam War. Walking through the cramped cells and hearing the stories of the revolutionary fighters really moved me. A meaningful experience for those who want to learn about Vietnamese history.

reviews.author: james
reviews.title: the pain of the revolutionnary soldier
reviews.content: I recently visited the Hoa Lo Prison Relic, and it was a thought-provoking experience. The site is rich in history and provides deep insights into Vietnam's past, particularly during the Vietnam War. The exhibits are well-organized and informative, featuring photographs and artifacts that tell powerful stories. The atmosphere is both somber and reflective, giving visitors a chance to understand the struggles faced by those imprisoned there. The ticket price is reasonable, and the staff were friendly and helpful. I recommend taking your time to read the displays and absorb the history. If you're in Hanoi, Hoa Lo Prison is definitely worth a visit!

reviews.author: 中村 拓也
reviews.title: A place where you can feel the weight of history
reviews.content: We learned about the hardships of the past through exhibitions. We held hands in a quiet atmosphere and had a memorable experience. Visiting this place reminded me of the importance of love and freedom.It was a precious time to think about our future at this site, which has a heavy history.

reviews.author: Tiler G
reviews.title: A Shadowy Glimpse into the Past
reviews.content: The exhibition on American prisoners of war and French colonial history was very striking. The exhibits are well organized and very informative. A moving reminder of human endurance.

reviews.author: Damien
reviews.title: V good
reviews.content: It is smaller then it was on my last visit as most of land sold to developers But still a good visit Good to see the Hanoi Hilton and the good french construction

reviews.author: Les Y
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: You will get a very different perspective as viewed through the eyes of the Vietnamese people as compared to the eyes of the Americans

reviews.author: Stay44289736243
reviews.title: Prison Tour was Profoundly Moving.
reviews.content: I’m a retired prison officer and counselor from Arizona and Washington State Corrections Agencies and I was very impressed with all of the exhibits and information provided.  It was as informative as it was interesting and I learned a lot about the prison history.  All the staff were friendly and helpful and it was busy but not too crowded.  Some of the artwork was very moving.  The French Colonial government was responsible for the barbarity depicted in the early days of the prison which later became known as the Hanoi Hilton because of its relatively comfortable environment compared to other POW camps run by the Vietnamese during the war with USA.

reviews.author: mickey448
reviews.title: Disturbing but well worth the visit
reviews.content: A disturbing place to visit but well worth it.  We rented the audio presentation and listened to each stop.  This prison was built by the French.  The history of the prison and the country was important to hear

reviews.author: Kristy D
reviews.title: Well worth a visit!
reviews.content: Very interesting stories and descriptions of the treatment of prisoners, war captives and political prisoners.Well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Marcel K
reviews.title: Good experience
reviews.content: This is a very good historical experience for 3/4 of the venue. Very insightful presentation of the prison and its standing in Vietnam history and culture. Unfortunately the last 1/4 of the venue leads us to believe a false narrative suggesting that US prisoners were treated with humanity and fairness. It is highly implausible and unbelievable that US prisoners were not exposed to some form of torture and inquisition. But if one can step past that aspect, this is a worthwhile opportunity to visit.

reviews.author: Kristy B
reviews.title: Average museum .
reviews.content: Very basic museum, took about 1 hour from start to finish, had lots of written information but nothing more than what we already knew about Vietnam. Headset an additional 100VD to hire for your tour.

reviews.author: Pang O
reviews.title: Interesting museum
reviews.content: This museum, in Hanoi city, is definitely worth a visit.  It gives some insight into the history of Vietnam during the French colonial days.

reviews.author: Passenger791696
reviews.title: Good museum- get the translation headsets!
reviews.content: Would recommend getting the headphones to listen to the stories (100K VND per headset) from actual people that were in the prison and hear the intriguing commentary. It’s a really decent guide from actual escapees and people who were held in the prison. Without it I think you’d go through in about 30 minutes but we ended up being there for a good hour and a half as it was so educational. It can be confronting for some people. We were fine with our children as we explained this is all a part of history and it’s not always a nice story. They enjoyed taking turns with the headset and going through the exhibitions. We shared one headset between us four (2 adults and 2 kids). I would say if there are two adults it’s worth getting one each to go through together. Some of the stories can be 5-7 minutes. Overall if you like history, it’s a good quick trip.

reviews.author: Tommy599
reviews.title: The prison is only one of three location in Hanoi worth visiting.
reviews.content: We are on a 23 day OAT tour of Vietnam.The prison is only one of three location in Hanoi worth visiting.The prison dates to 1896 when it was used to hold and torture anyone (local Vietnamese) who opposed the French government (Back then the French held power in Vietnam as THEIR colonial interest).Most of the prison was demolished in 1990 to make room for a high rise (Hanoi Towers). Asmall corner of the original prison still exists dedicated to the history of the prison’s past.There was lots of propaganda media, but mainly about how the French used the prison in the firsthalf of the 1900s as a place of incarceration and torture for anyone that opposed the Frenchgoverning.
