Why there is even a Guillotine on display and pictures of severed heads.Only as a side feature is there information about the 600 American prisoners of war that wereheld there (some over 9 years), during the Vietnam / American War.A dreadful place and we only went there because we heard so much about it during the war.

reviews.author: Ightham1
reviews.title: Excellent visit
reviews.content: We arrived shortly after opening at 8.30, no queue on a Saturday. Paid for the audio which was very informative. Well laid out and a good mix of artefacts and anecdotes. As others have said, the narrative is slightly imbalanced but it didn’t take away from it being a good trip

reviews.author: Alessandro
reviews.title: Interesting visit from the historical point of view
reviews.content: Interesting visit from the point of view of history. The living conditions imposed by the French were poor and the interiors prove this fact

reviews.author: Nomad09762738686
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Interesting visit. Shows the resilience and determination of the Vietnamese people. Paid extra for the headphones and audio. Gives some extra insight. A bit dubious about how well the US prisoners were treated while in Hoa Lo Prison by the Vietnamese. Only a small portion of the prison remains today.

reviews.author: FrequentT1280
reviews.title: See if you have time
reviews.content: It was an interesting visit. However, the museum was not well laid out in terms of viewing and access.Though signage was made to accommodate English speakers, the amount of commentary was rather sparse. Also tilted toward propaganda rather than providing only historical fact.

reviews.author: AdventuresOnPlanet
reviews.title: A must-visit location in Hanoi.
reviews.content: This is a clear example of how people treat one another in times of conflict. Very gloomy location to witness firsthand. Even though the Vietnamese account of how they handled American POWs is obviously highly dubious, you absolutely have to see this place if you're in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Tam C
reviews.title: Must do tour
reviews.content: When in Hanoi this is a 'must do' tour. After paying the admission charges there is an option to pay a small additional charge for an audio tour which we highly recommend.Seeing the inside of what is left of the prison is quite daunting and finding out how the political prisoners were treated and suffered is something we should all learn about.The tour also tells you about the US Pilots who were detained there after being shot down during the US/Vietnam War. Very interesting and tour takes about 90 minutes.

reviews.author: sandler
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.content: Amazing place, worth every pennies. U should buy the headphone service for understanding better the story behind……….

reviews.author: Resort18211189263
reviews.title: A CASUAL VISIT
reviews.content: It’s a great historical place to visit if you’re coming to Hanoi, although it can sometimes be disconcerting to younger audiences. XD

reviews.author: Dr Kulkarni Mohina S
reviews.title: Prisoners museum hanoi
reviews.content: This prison was a great visit in hanoi.The design by french colonial rulers for prisoners...now it is a museum. Later after french left..north Vietnam used it for american prisoners.. there are gender wise cells...depict ung inhuman treatment. The miniature in the entry itself gives a complete view.Great gift shop and restrooms facilities

reviews.author: Akiko_short
reviews.title: As a path to peace.
reviews.content: Honestly, I can only think of war and colonial rule as something that happened somewhere unrelated to me, but that is why I thought it was so meaningful to be exposed to the reality of our institution.Listening to the audio Guide's explanations of living in poor conditions, torture and executions there, inside the actual facility, makes you think about how much sacrifice was made and how far away it was to get a peaceful life today.It was as if the monuments and the trees that had been there since then were telling us not only about the cruelty and the misery, but that everything was connected to the peace that we have today and we must continue to do so.

reviews.author: Russ Lacuata
reviews.title: Gruesome
reviews.content: Former Hoa Lo Prison turned museum and nicknamed "Hanoi Hilton" by American POW's. I recommend this museum to everyone who wants to learn from history so the horrors of the past may not be repeated.

reviews.author: lucycan
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton!
reviews.content: I went here on a full day city tour.  I spent about an hour inside.  Interesting to see how the French treated the prisoners.  By contrast the Vietnamese were quite accommodating to the Americans in the 60s and 70s.

reviews.author: WCOB
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: This little museum has a lot packed into it. There are plenty of displays which are well labelled. It's quite popular and there were a lot of people crammed in. There are also the courtyard, guillotine and cells to explore. Definitely a visit as it displays early Hanoi history under the French rule.

reviews.author: vip_foodie
reviews.title: Actual prison turned into a museum
reviews.content: I visited this museum during my Hanoi visit. This museum used to be an actual prison. It now showcases the hardships Vietnamese freedom fighters had to endure when they were put in prison. If someone is a history buff, they should definitely check it out.

reviews.author: Stephanie M
reviews.title: Interesting experience
reviews.content: We went to see Hoa Lo prison with very limited knowledge around the Vietnam war. We found the beginning parts very interesting and thought there was enough information on the placards (as we opted not to go for a guided audio tour). The walkthrough offers a lot to look at and read, and depicts what it was probably like to have been a prisoner of war in those times.

reviews.author: vicnot
reviews.title: Very interesting; good way to learn about French colonization and the American War.
reviews.content: I didn't really want to visit this prison, but had booked a 'Tour with a Local' who was a bit dogmatic about the itinerary (but she was right!). It is easy to get to, with plenty of info/signage in English. It was really interesting to hear about the French colonization of Vietnam and the history of the prison, and to see artefacts and history from the 'American War'. This was obviously from the Vietnamese experience and point of view, and most illuminating and fascinating. Seeing a guillotine was gruesome but also interesting (don't think I've seen one before despite being to France on many occasions).

reviews.author: chatonette
reviews.title: Sobering (If You Ignore the Propaganda)
reviews.content: Maison Centrale was a horrific prison, and it’s worth a visit (but the communist propaganda should be taken with a grain of salt). It was opened by the French during colonial times to imprison and punish those who rose up against the French regime. Inmates had their legs bolted to wooden beds, where they could not move position, or even move to use the toilet. Mothers along with their children were also imprisoned here. It was a brutal place. The propaganda, however, is outrageous. Yes, after the French pulled out of Vietnam, the Americans believed that supporting the South Vietnamese in their fight for a democratic republic against the Communist North Vietnamese was the right thing to do. Yes, it all went pear-shaped, and in retrospect, perhaps the US shouldn’t have gotten involved and instead allowed the South to be taken over by the North (which is what happened at the end of the war anyway). The museum purports that the American prisoners of war were basically in a good-time summer camp, complete with a full medical team and a Christmas feast. The reality, however, is that when Jeremiah Denton was forced to make a propaganda video, he secretly blinked “TORTURE” in Morse Code. Inmates were not allowed to speak with each other, so they used a tapping code to communicate. The museum message is that that John McCain was treated well. However, he was in solitary confinement for 2 of his 5.5 years here, lost 50 pounds in weight, his hair went completely grey very quickly (likely due to his trauma), was tortured, was forced to make false confessions, and was denied proper medical treatment and nutrition. He was never again able to raise his hands above shoulder height, and Hillary Clinton from the opposition once famously helped him fix his hair before an appearance because he was unable to reach it himself. All in all, it’s a sobering visit. It was an inhumane place for any poor soul to spend their days. This is true for both those imprisoned by the French colonialists and those imprisoned by the North Vietnamese, despite the museum’s message that it was fun for the US POWs.

reviews.author: Abbys M
reviews.title: Very interesting.
reviews.content: My family esp. our 14 year old son is a history buff.  He took his time here, listening to the audio headset guide we rented.  It was very interesting and sad.  The materials or displays was awesome.  Some are realistic which made it sadder yet very interesting for history sake.  Lots of emotions here while we go through the tour.  It's a must visit when visiting Hanoi.  The museum over all was well-kept, clean and organized.  Staff or volunteers running the place speaks English.  They are also friendly and accommodating.  The museum have vending machine, gift shops available.  Restroom is also clean.  There's no time constraint so you can go through the museum at leisure or at your own pace.  We are specially thankful for the A/C cool atmosphere.  It was a reprieve from Hanoi's summer heat.  Truly an amazing and historical museum full of interesting displays.

reviews.author: Jolie
reviews.title: Good experience
reviews.content: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison in Hanoi is a profoundly moving experience. Walking through the grim, high-walled corridors and peering into the small, stark cells gives a tangible sense of the harsh conditions faced by prisoners. The exhibits, filled with personal stories and historical artifacts, evoke a deep empathy and connection to those who suffered there. The somber atmosphere and the historical weight of the site leave a lasting impression, making the visit both unsettling and enlightening.

reviews.author: Coyote-Travelerz
reviews.title: Legacy of Colonialism
reviews.content: While only a fraction of the original structure remains, the section open to visitors provides a stark view of justice under French colonial and Vietnamese rule.

reviews.author: ilp3
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: A very informative tour on the difficult history of Vietnam. Makes it possible to understand the conditions of detention during and after French colonization

reviews.author: GM Tran
reviews.title: HOA LO NIGHT SHOW
reviews.content: The Hoa Lo Night Show is truly exceptional. It was so emotional and moving that it brought me to tears. The performers are incredibly talented and made the experience unforgettable. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Will C
reviews.title: Hoa Lo prison
reviews.content: Remarkable experience, very hot and sweaty, but exhibits are informative in English, French and Vietnamese. We used an audio tour guide, but everything they say in the audio guide, that you pay 100k VND for, is on the signs infront of the exhibits

reviews.author: Shimwell
reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison offers a sobering look at Vietnam's history, particularly its French colonial period.  We were moved by the prisoner artwork and personal stories.  While somber, it's a chance for reflection and understanding.

reviews.author: Zurdar
reviews.title: Educational
reviews.content: For what it cost, it’s worth it. Very informative. Kinda graphic at one point, but loved all the history and explanations behind everything. We didnt do the audio tour, there is plenty to read. It was easy to enjoy because we went at opening and basically went ahead of everyone else.

reviews.author: Lachlan Reynolds
reviews.title: Interesting!!
reviews.content: Really interesting museum! They give you headphones to walk around and listen to, however they are quite time consuming and can get a little boring. The experience was really cool and I learned a lot whilst being here!

reviews.author: tieganblake
reviews.title: Go early - it gets very busy!
reviews.content: We spent 50,000VND (about £1.50) for two entry tickets, and we decided not to buy the audio guide. The prison was a decent experience, it had lots of photos/paintings and sculptures to look at and you do learn some interesting things about the war. Unfortunately, they do not control how many people go in at once, and we found it was so busy inside that we were struggling to see things, and people were standing in front of us when we were trying to read/take photos. Thankfully it is quite cool inside, due to lots of fans and air conditioning being used, but we would recommend to go early (we visited at dinner time) to avoid crowds as most people had the same idea as us - to visit during the hottest hours to avoid the heat.

reviews.author: Jayden C
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison Audio Tour
reviews.content: The prison is fascinating and informative. We did the Audio Tour of the prison which is available for 100k VND (per person). The audio tour provides narration through headphones as you walk through the prison and key in exhibit numbers into the device they give you. The narration includes personal stories of people kept in the prison, and explanations of objects in the exhibits and their significance. Hoa Lo prison is full of historical objects and insane stories of escape and determination. I highly recommend going and doing the audio tour.

reviews.author: Tung N
reviews.title: Love Vietnam
reviews.content: The place woth to visit.You will learning much about Vietnam War, seeing how did they can fight again 2 big countries...Vietnamese should pround of their country.We love Vietnam.

reviews.author: Marjorie M
reviews.title: Explore history in Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: Before going to Hanoi, I’ve been eyeing to visit this museum because it’s part of the history of Vietnam. The museum was very immersive and well-presented. You can avail the audiobook to deeply understand each representation per room. Overall, it was a great experience to know this part of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Camper19338800412
reviews.title: Speechless
reviews.content: I am speechless after having the opportunity to visit this place and witness firsthand a small part of Vietnam's dark history. I highly recommend everyone to come here.

reviews.author: JAnneBNYC
reviews.title: Important to see, moving and gives you perspective on Vietnam’s long term struggle
reviews.content: This is the famous Hanoi Hilton. It is very moving and the audio tour is really really good. While seeing the artifacts of American POW’s (including John McCain) is moving, it is most important to be here because the long struggle and bravery depicted against the French colonialists helps you understand how very very long the Vietnamese struggled for self determination

reviews.author: k.s w
reviews.title: It's worth it!
reviews.content: Impressive to see what took place in Hanoi. It is not expensive 50,000 per person and children under 16 are allowed free of charge on presentation of ID. There are audio recordings in different languages that take you on a journey through the prison.  Definitely worth a look.

reviews.author: jesintha r
reviews.title: Hao lo prison
reviews.content: Went as a family. Bigger than expected and worth the visit. 50000 dong per person entrance fees.  They did not charge my sonwho is 6yrs old.

reviews.author: Yvonne S
reviews.title: OK but not what we expected
reviews.content: The prison dates to 1896 when it was used to hold and torture anyone (local Vietnamese) who opposed the French government (Back then the French held power in Vietnam as THEIR colonial interest).   In the mid to late 20th century (US War), Hoa Lo was then used by Vietnamese locals to imprison American POWs who gave the site the nickname “Hanoi Hilton.” Most of the prison was demolished in 1990 to make room for a high rise (Hanoi Towers).  A small corner of the original prison still exists dedicated to the history of the prison’s past.   There was lots of propaganda media, but mainly about how the French used the prison in the first half of the 1900s as a place of incarceration and torture for anyone that opposed the French governing.  Why there is even a Guillotine on display and pictures of severed heads.Only as a side feature is there information about the 600 American prisoners of war that were held there (some over 9 years), during the Vietnam / American War.Besides the citadel this was the only other location worth historical viewing in this very crowded and trash covered city.   Yes there are some sights and experiences in this city but based on the pollution and many motor bikes we have no desire to visit the area again.

reviews.author: Matt M
reviews.title: Ha Lo Prison- incredible history - a must
reviews.content: A must do in Hanoi. I got the audio tour (highly recommend) and my wife and daughters (18, 15), didn’t get the audio. The audio was great, adding prisoners’ stories to the tour and getting a true sense of what it was like. At time it was devastating and other times uplifting with the courage of the prisoners. American part showed well looked after prisoners, so take that how you want to due to the two different sides of the story. Whole family appreciated the information presented in this well set out tour.

reviews.author: Aditya M
reviews.title: An insight into Vietnamese History
reviews.content: There is a lot you can learn about the treatment of Vietnamese political prisoners during the French Colonization. You can also rent an audio device that I believe explains the details. However I didn’t rent the audio device. They are numbers mentioned on each section and I believe you can play the audio according to the number. There are lot of fans and coolers placed throughout the area but it was still a bit hot for me. There are a couple of souvenir shops inside the prison as well.

reviews.author: nzwestie
reviews.title: Do go and you will learn so much history
reviews.content: We learnt so much going through here.  Would def put it on your to do list.  A very good experience.  We did not get the audio - but rather read our way through which we were more than happy with.

reviews.author: Ana Sofia D
reviews.title: Shocking and informative
reviews.content: It's a place where we can have a perspective on past times, not so distant. It's a little shocking.It has a lot of information and several visiting rooms.

reviews.author: Onas
reviews.title: Simple museum
reviews.content: Although it's cool to see, it's a very simple museum. There are several murals with information, but old items are scarce.

reviews.author: Ludo V
reviews.title: Sad image of French colonization
reviews.content: Built in 1896 by the French colonizer with the name: 'Maison Centrale', for 450 prisoners, that number increased to 2000 around 1930. Mostly political prisoners and opponents. During the American war (we call it the Vietnam War), Hoa Lo became infamous as a prison for downed American pilots, who gave their place of incarceration the ironic nickname Hanoi Hilton. The original nameplate still hangs above the entrance, but a large part of the cell complex was demolished in 1997. The preserved part is furnished as a museum, which mainly refers to the colonization period. The museum exhibits consist of chains, whips and other torture instruments and some preserved cramped isolation cells. In a small section there are some photos and material from the American period. The whole thing actually doesn't amount to much.

reviews.author: Betsy S
reviews.title: Sobering and Worth Visiting
reviews.content: Fascinating history.  A larger touring experience than I expected.  I rented the audio guide and was glad I did.  Interesting insight into the Vietnamese perspective on the Vietnamese/American war.

reviews.author: Joe V
reviews.title: Mostly enlightening
reviews.content: The Hoa Lo prison was an eye opener for the treatment of criminals and political prisoners during the French colonisation of Vietnam .  This is an era of which I knew very little, except that France was going to great lengths to suppress a population deserving of independence.  It’s not an uncommon story of western colonisation/suppression in general.  The museum is well done - I highly recommend the audio guide; a bargain at 100 dong; and if the topic interests you, you’ll find the audio compelling, especially the inmates stories.  The ‘comradeship’ is pretty central to each display.  It’s ironic when you consider how horrendous the French treatment of the Vietnamese was that they should ignore the true conditions in which American POWs were held.  Make no mistake, the US involvement in the Vietnam War was a dark chapter in its history and the destruction it ‘rained’ down upon  the Vietnamese people in chemicals and weaponry was horrific.  But to suggest POWs were treated humanely with respect, allowing them to mingle together and enjoy holiday dinners isn’t even close to accurate.  It’s a shame as this  inaccuracy undermines the truth of all the stories. Still, it’s well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Marc B
reviews.title: Best Paid Attraction in Hanoi
reviews.content: This place is really cool. Easily my favourite paid tourist attraction in Hanoi. Would recommend. I didn't get the audio guide but heard from others that it's worth it.

reviews.author: Dimitris L
reviews.title: The "Hanoi Hilton"..... a must visit!
reviews.content: A visit to Hoa Lo Prison is a must. The prison, or what remains of the original structure, was built by the French (who ruled Indochina-Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia-up until 1954) in the late 19th century and was used to incarcerate mostly political prisoners who lived under inhuman conditions. The appalling conditions used by the French are evident in the various displays throughout this museum . Even if the story may be "one-sided" one cannot help but despair at the thought that human beings can be so cruel to others. The prison was also used by the North Vietnamese  during the Vietnam War, to hold enemy prisoners, mostly Americans. During that time it came to be known as the "Hanoi Hilton"..... However not much is displayed about the Vietnam War years.

reviews.author: CARLOS S
reviews.title: TO NOT LOSE
reviews.content: A visit not to be missed for its historical weight, but ALSO FOR THE EMOTIONAL IMPACT..The entire exhibition is done with very impactful realism. There is no chance of not being affected. It is common to find former prisoners visiting with their families, which further reinforces the emotional nature that the visit imposes.The exhibition respects the temporal evolution of the prison and the most relevant events that took place there.

reviews.author: CNT_09
reviews.title: Historically informative and good to escape some of the heat
reviews.content: Okay place to visit. Gives a person a good understanding of the poor conditions of prisoners. Also of the long history of the prison from when the French built it in the late 1890’s. It’s understandable that they want to focus on the long history of oppression and atrocious conditions prisoners were kept under by the French up until 1954, but there then is a vast silence on the history after that. 1898-1954 Very bad things happened. 1954-1973 …………. (Guess it was an empty building?? A play ground for kids?? Who knows?). 1973 American pilots released at end of the war and all were very happy.

reviews.author: Stuart
reviews.title: Must Do !
reviews.content: Must Do !!! This is so interesting and thought provoking. some real insights into how life would have been like (and its brutal).

reviews.author: Edouard L
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: This is a must visit place for history aficionados in Hanoi.  Good for someone that really love to study about Vietnam history. So proud to be vietnamese when you see this place.

reviews.author: Valigessa
reviews.title: Arrive there already "studied"
reviews.content: Prison built by the French to detain Vietnamese political prisoners, then used to detain American soldiers who sarcastically named it “Hanoi Hilton”: the American prisoners were subjected to terrible torture that the Vietnamese government still denies today. During the visit, in fact, it was clear that they wanted to make it appear that the American "guests" were treated in a more than humane way.Explanatory signs in English and French.Interesting visit.

reviews.author: Dianna O
reviews.title: An interesting, informative afternoon.
reviews.content: Very informative visit.  Individual headset to hear the commentary for each exhibit.  The information in the rooms were well presented.  It was busy, but we were able to get around easily and see everything.  Some of the rooms had seats so we were not constantly standing.  There was a shop on site although we didn't buy anything.  Although not air conditioned, there were air fans in most of the rooms.

reviews.author: Chris318i
reviews.title: Impressive prison
reviews.content: Impressive prison museum in Hanoi. You will find out a lot of details about the history of Vietnam. It's definitely worth a visit!

reviews.author: Keonyoung P
reviews.title: place of history
reviews.content: It was truly a meaningful place where I could learn a lot about Vietnamese history!!! If I have another opportunity in the future, I will definitely come with other friends and family to share what I felt and increase the value of the trip. Hanoi, the center of Vietnam, is the best!

reviews.author: Keith Munn
reviews.title: Hanoi prison tour
reviews.content: Had a great time and there was an outstanding exhibition there, documenting the history of the prison. I would advise anyone visiting Hanoi to go

reviews.author: SEALS
reviews.title: I recommend a guidebook, but the exhibits are shocking. A testament to history.
reviews.content: I visited this place because it was recommended in the guidebook. The exhibits are so painful and shocking that you can't help but look away when you enter. Facilities like this should be preserved for future generations. Many visitors stopped to look at the exhibits. They seem to have earphones for foreign languages, so why not use them? As an aside, I was surprised to see that the Ho Chi Minh sandals I had been looking for were on sale at the shop, and although they were the regular price, they were cheaper than I expected, so I bought them. Also, while there are many tourists from Western countries and Asia, such as France and the United States, in Vietnam, I saw many young Japanese tourists here.I went there as a set with a famous and popular Asian restaurant and chocolate shop nearby.

reviews.author: Angelo M
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: Was interesting and glad I went but nothing overly exciting.Lots of history here and some good explanation vietnam history.

reviews.author: Kyle
reviews.title: Quick tour through the prison
reviews.content: Good little tour that roughly lasts an hour  or less depending on your movements40000VND entry fee with optional 100000VND for the audio tho the subtitles on the photos and visuals are in both Vietnamese and english.Good insight with information in regards to vietnam war and a look back in history of facts you or might not known with the history of it with lots of showings of how the p.o.w were detained and captured and how they were treated in there time of prison life.Souviner shops also here and a good little attraction to visit to knock off a bit of time near the old quarters

reviews.author: hemismom
reviews.title: Very enjoyable visit
reviews.content: We had an enjoyable morning at the museum, but highly recommend. The only thing I would suggest is that you bring insect repellent with you as sometimes the bugs are quite bad I got about 30 bites during my visit.

reviews.author: Millie Bawden
reviews.title: HOI AN PRISON - MUST DO
reviews.content: I went with my parents who are super interested in history- me, not so much, however I had a fantastic time. We walked through individually, without a tour or the audio and loved it. Extremely touching and really glad I saw it. No line for the tickets, just buy them outside the prison on the day.

reviews.author: Matt Ferguson
reviews.title: Worth a visit, but tour with eyes wide open
reviews.content: I visted the Hoa Lo Prison. First, the good. I learned so much about the French occupation and the following repression of the Vietnamese Rebles. Now the bad. The American Vietnam War section was not balanced. I would say the museum did not address the harsh treatment of American POWs, but nor did I expect it to shine a light on that dark history.

reviews.author: Cheryl M
reviews.title: One of the best experiences in Hanoi
reviews.content: This was our number one half-day out in Vietnam (along with the water puppets).  You had audio in several languages and easy to find your way around.  It is not for the faint hearted though, the conditions that the Vietnamese and US prisoners experienced was horrific.

reviews.author: Sshuddho G
reviews.title: Must visit for all Veterans.
reviews.content: This is a must visit place for history aficionados. Also known as the Hanoi Hilton by the American prisoners' of war captured by the NVA.

reviews.author: shaishavv
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: This museum gives an inside view of the life of the prisioners - where they lived, how they were treated etc. It has the orginal prision gate  & the guillotene on display. It has nice pictures & other items thru which visitors can experience the prision life.NIce museum worth visiting once.

reviews.author: vaugkimb
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: Interesting site to visit.  While there is a fair amount of info on the Vietnam (American) War, the education is rightly focused on the entire history of the prison, built by the French, which includes significant mistreatment of Vietnamese political prisoners by the French prior to liberation from being part of French Indochina. Other reviewers comment on the propaganda around how well cared for the American POWs were while in custody.  It’s true that it is definitely prominently displayed and is hard to read; however. It should be kept in mind that this is told from the Vietnam government’s point of view.  The information is highly patriotic in nature as a site like this in any country would be.  As an American, if you don’t remember that cultural context, you will be irritated.  You are in another country after all, and one that has significant restrictions on free speech and free press to boot.One thing is clear, anyone who spent time as a prisoner here over the approximately 100 year history of the prison lived a nightmare in awful physical and  psychological conditions.

reviews.author: sariver
reviews.title: A great place to learn history
reviews.content: It's a wonderful place to learn about Vietnamese history. It's heartbreaking to think of how cruelly the prisoners were treated. After seeing the actual size, darkness, cruel torture and execution equipment of the cells, I'm impressed that they were able to build a facility called the Hanoi Hilton.

reviews.author: Johnnie C
reviews.title: Am interesting stop in Hanoi
reviews.content: We came to the "Hanoi Hilton" on a drizzly afternoon. The audio guide is well worth doing to provide some insights as you tour around. Some of what occurred during the French occupation was sadistic, the models and exhibits help you to imagine the conditions.  Of particular interest to me was the prison use during the Vietnam/American War, probably as it is recent history within my lifetime, as expected there is a good section dedicated to this and it was interesting to hear how well American prisoners of war were treated, so much so I wonder if they were sad to return to the US (sarcasm). This said it's worth a visit and easy enough to get to and from using Grab.

reviews.author: DotsGirl2
reviews.title: A lot of propaganda
reviews.content: This place is interesting but was ruined for me by the heavy propaganda on all of the explanations. As with any place that tells of inhumanity and war it is a sad place to visit.

reviews.author: howardxp1
reviews.title: Should be on everyone’s “to-do” list.
reviews.content: The historical dates. timelines and general accounts are valuable, especially since most people under age 60 don’t really know much about the Vietnam wars. I agree with so many previous reviews about making the treatment of the Americans seem like a resort and not a “hell on Earth” as it really was. Leave a couple of hours to go through it thoroughly.Howard S.

reviews.author: Lori M
reviews.title: don't miss but look out for serious propaganda
reviews.content: Super cool to see and don't miss but the propaganda was a joke. Showed two chunks of history... when the French imprisoned the Vietnamese resistance and when the Vietnamese imprisoned American POWs. Showed the French as ruthless torturers but presented the way the Americans were treated like they were on a vacation. Sitting in the cell was chilling.

reviews.author: BrakiWorldTraveler
reviews.title: Underwhelming after the Phu Quoc's prison and Saigon's "War Remnants Museum"
reviews.content: I must admit I expected more from the capital's museum.As a history buff, during our 15 days Vietnam tour, we've visited Phu Quoc's prison and Saigon's "War Remnants Museum", along with this one in Hanoi as the last one.Maybe if the sequence was opposite I'd rate it higher, but this Hanoi's is in a shade of those.Likewise the Phu Quoc's prison this one was also built by the French for captivating and torturing Viet freedom revolutionary fighters and dissidents.After, during the Vietnam War it served as a prison for US POW.Viet prisoners from colonial era are presented tortured, chained, in solitary confinement,....US POW are represented like they were in a resort vacation reading books, practicing sports, listening to music, writing to their loved ones,....

reviews.author: Gigi C
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: So impressed with the audio guide service at Hoa Lo Prison! They had multilingual options that made the history accessible to international visitors. A great touch to enhance the overall experience!

reviews.author: David M
reviews.title: Great History museum!
reviews.content: Outstanding museum. Very highly recommended. The torture of Vietnamese by the French appears well documented.  However, the treatment of USA pilot POWs is not presented accurately. They were tortured and treated quite badly. It is a shame that the Vietnamese government leadership can't admit the truth about the treatment of the American POWs.

reviews.author: Stephan Biel
reviews.title: Hoa LoDi Prison tích Nhà tù Hỏa Lò
reviews.content: It is worth visiting to learn about the history of Vietnam and its occupation by the French. We did it on our own, and with the audio guide you are well informed.

reviews.author: Shannon
reviews.title: Hanoi's Dark Past
reviews.content: Great immersive spaces that gives great insights of life as a prisoner. The area can be covered in under an hour but for audio tours which I would recommend might take much longer due to the variety of content. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Tu-Anh P
reviews.title: Maison Centrale
reviews.content: Hỏa Lò Prison was a prison in Hanoi originally used by the French colonists in Indochina for political prisoners, and later by North Vietnam for U.S. prisoners of war during the Vietnam War.During French era Hỏa Lò was known as Maison Centrale. During Vietnam War, it's was known as Hanoi Hilton from the film The "Hanoi Hilton".

reviews.author: Jenny Nguyen
reviews.title: January fire
reviews.content: Fire Prison is one of many must-visit places when you travel to Hanoi. There is a new night tour open to everyone but the ticket price is not worth it.

reviews.author: Yella
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Impressive, sickening and respectful of everyone who has been imprisoned and tortured here. What hell.Still good to see.

reviews.author: Merlin Alejo
reviews.title: Informative
reviews.content: Good for someone that really love to study about Vietnam history. Need to pay more if you want to hear audio for explanation. Or else a little bit less information from the poster. Somehow creepy.

reviews.author: Bettoli Rocco
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: A very interesting look at history . This is an old prison built by French while occupying Vietnam. Great audio tour at a cost of $100,000 dong.

reviews.author: HkkS
reviews.title: Love it Or Pass
reviews.content: You will like it or just another visit to a museum. You need to have a bit of love in history to appreciate this museum, they try their best to give perspective on the history of the prison and the prisonners. Informative and a lot of photos and videos references inside. It is worth your time and money. Good for children to see what a prison lookalike especially in the old days.

reviews.author: Alex Phạm
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Hilton
reviews.content: A place worth experiencing when you travel to Hanoi. Currently there are also very interesting night tours. Ticket prices are a bit more expensive but still reasonable.

reviews.author: Chloe S
reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.content: Audio tour (100,000 vnd) was well worth it. Some sections of the exhibition were outside and it was raining when we went (though there were umbrellas provided) so byo jumper! Took about 2hrs to listen to all 30 audio chapters.

reviews.author: Monique L
reviews.title: Solo prison tour
reviews.content: The museum, history, and collections are rich. The prison and their events were beyond barbaric- evil. Emotional experience.

reviews.author: andrea2359
reviews.title: Eye-opening
reviews.content: It was very crowded when I was there. War sites always leave one heavy-hearted but this was an eye-opening walk if you are a war buff. There are audio-guides so you can DIY and learn about the oppression faced by the Vietnamese on your own.

reviews.author: Sophie G 🏖🧚🏻‍♀️☀️🌴
reviews.title: You have to see it to know ☺️
reviews.content: I loved this visit, it was fascinating! Terrible to see the life of these prisoners in this prison and the survival in these dungeons!! I learned a lot of things that I didn't know... the whole story is explained on panels but you also have the possibility of taking audio (for a fee) very nice too, that's what I did in French .I really recommend this visit, you will not regret it!

reviews.author: Donald F
reviews.title: Well worth it
reviews.content: Very interesting visit giving insights to the French colonial period and of course the Vietnam war. Well worth s couple of hours. Every story has two sides - interesting to see the Vietnamese view of the imprisonment of Vietnamese during the 1930s as well as their view of the US inmates during the 1960s/1970s - suspect that the museum authorities might have a generous view of how the US servicemen were treated.

reviews.author: Coscojar
reviews.title: An important part of Hanoi’s past
reviews.content: It was a very informative and moving experience about the history of Hanoi and what took place here for many prisoners of war.  Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: khaled Youssef
reviews.title: Unavoidable
reviews.content: Not to be missed to remember the horrors of colonialism (here French) and part of the sad history of the country, the sewers which allowed certain prisoners to escape and change history. Well documented and well done. The building was built by the French by razing a village that lived on crafts.

reviews.author: EmilyMorin
reviews.title: Should visit
reviews.content: This relic is part of Vietnam's painful past and exploring it helped me understand more deeply the history and spirit of the Vietnamese people. Detailed stories, especially together with the photos of actual people who has been executed. I think it is an interesting historical place and worth experiencing for not only history lover.

reviews.author: egwanderlust
reviews.title: Important to Remember
reviews.content: The Hanoi Hilton, is possibly one of the hardest museums I have ever visited. This establishment has seen many deaths, hardships, and torture. It is important to remember the history despite how painful it is. The museum is huge and not even the full size as it once was. Visit on a weekday, the weekends are quite busy and crowded.

reviews.author: adrenalinejunkie007
reviews.title: Informative on Hanoi's past
reviews.content: Feels wrong to say I enjoyed the visit given the site's historical purpose, but it does capture Vietnam's history dating back before colonization. The site is only around half what it once was, but does a good job at capturing the experience of the prison as well as the purpose. Do keep in mind it presents a certain historical perspective, but nonetheless a must visit in Hanoi.

reviews.author: LackyTravels
reviews.title: Impressive experience
reviews.content: The museum is well worth seeing. You get a good impression of the conditions of the past. The many information boards in Vietnamese, French and English tell you a lot and you don't necessarily need the expensive audio guide. The entrance fee is 30,000 dong. Only recommended to a limited extent for children.

reviews.author: Quân Đ
reviews.title: Hoa Lo
reviews.content: tbh, i was exploded with tears and emotions after visiting this place, so proud to be vietnamese!!!!

reviews.author: TonyB
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Very much worth the visit here. Used for political prisoners during the french occupation, and later for american prisoners during the war.

reviews.author: Mary S
reviews.title: Excellent Historical Presentation
reviews.content: This is the prison known to Americans as the Hanoi Hilton when US airmen were detained there and there is an exhibit on that period.  But far more interesting is the way the struggle for independence from the French is depicted through the prisoners detained during the French occupation and their stories.

reviews.author: petersQ2306YZ
reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.content: Very cost effective museum tour.  Good to see inside the cell blocks, experience the conditions and be educated about recent history

reviews.author: Mohit Mangal
reviews.title: Ha Loa Prison Relic
reviews.content: This is one of the best place to be in hanoi. You get to relive the struggle of the Vietnamese people against French and Americans.It makes you remember about the heroes of the country. It is must to be in here as understanding a country's history is the best way to start your trip.The place is at walking distance from st Joseph's cathedral.

reviews.author: Katie2690
reviews.title: Important to visit
reviews.content: A really important place to visit. Very informative and gives those who visit an insight into the history of the prison and the conditions that the prisoners endured.

reviews.author: Harry
reviews.title: Unforgettable memory
reviews.content: I was truly impressed by the comprehensive exhibits and the haunting stories they tell. The prison's transformation from a place of suffering during the French colonial to a poignant reminder of resilience and determination during the American War is striking. The attention to detail in the exhibits and the informative audio guide made my experience much more worth it. Walking through the solemn halls and cells, I feel a sense of reverence for the strength of the Vietnamese people!!! Hoa Lo Prison is an essential stop for history buffs and curious travelers alike!

reviews.author: GoPlaces51924752933
reviews.title: Propaganda / museum
reviews.content: Part Museum, larger part propaganda. Even though Vietnam's leaders have not acknowledged maltreatment if American prisoners of war the outright misrepresentation of their treatment as very kind and jolly is too much. Some acknowledgement of other stories is needed in any historical museum / exhibition.The statements that only 1 to 2 dozen Hanoi citizens died in the December 72 bombings are contradicted later in the museum and literally incredible. One can therefore credit nothing

reviews.author: wintercolleen
reviews.title: Great
reviews.content: Loved it and wave scary then port Arthur in Tasmania Australia. I loved the death cell and the women one. Great audio tour at a cost of $100,000 dong. Lovely staff and also great gift shop.

reviews.author: Jodie Shannon
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Very interesting place. We paid the 50,000vnd for the audio guide and found it very helpful. Signs do have English translations but I think without the audio guide I would have been a bit confused so definitely worth hiring.

reviews.author: Eva EG
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Interesting to see. Partly scary, for example the dead cells. As long as you are aware that the story is quite lopsided (French who condemned Vietnamese = evil. Vietnamese who held American prisoners of war = kind) our family appreciated the museum.

reviews.author: Black_Father
reviews.title: Terrible and instructive history
reviews.content: A prison is rarely a positive experience and even here you get to experience an extremely frightening handling of convicted persons. At the same time, it is useful to see how it can be as there are still today prisons with equivalent standards and management.The conditions are well described but also show the prisoners' creativity in order to have a slightly easier life and also continue to communicate internally and externally.To get the most out of the visit, you should hire an audio guide.The prison is a gruesome monument well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Matthew H
reviews.title: Good attraction in Hanoi
reviews.content: A very interesting look at history and the difference between how the Vietnamese prisoners were treated compared to the American. Worth getting the audio guide!

reviews.author: Shari M
reviews.title: All about French and Vietnamese brutality
reviews.content: It’s a prison that shows you how the French were brutal to the Vietnamese. At the end there is a brief photo of John McCain,,,, but this is not about the Hanoi Hilton as i thought,,,its all about the French brutality.

reviews.author: James N
reviews.title: Important to visit, but sad and awful to reflect on
reviews.content: For anyone with even a passing interest in history. Sad and sombre, it's an important site to visit, to truly understand what the Vietnamese were fighting, to see France's near 70-year 'colonialisation' legacy and what a western country was willing to do, even up to the 1950s. The brutality, even against teenage resistance fighters, and the young toddler children of female prisoners, is awful to grasp. It puts some things into perspective.

reviews.author: NeoAsian
reviews.title: Hỏa Lò Prison given nickname was The Hanoi Hilton where captured American P.O.W’s where housed during the Vietnam War.
reviews.content: It’s an amazing tour very detailed and a great guide in assistance learning about the history of the people and Vietnam War.

reviews.author: André K
reviews.title: Informative museum
reviews.content: This museum is worth visiting. It tell you the story of how brutal the French were. It is informative but also sad. Looking at the guillotine in the execution room is very dramatic, especially together with the photos of actual people who has been executed. This is just a reminder how cruel humans can be.

reviews.author: Culture13607538725
reviews.title: Propaganda at its best
reviews.content: Summary of this place: French treated the Vietnamese prisoners with extreme cruelty. No food no clothing, etc. Vietnamese treated US POW with wholehearted kindness.  US soldiers were given food, cigarettes, party time, etc

reviews.author: chris h
reviews.title: Headsets informative
reviews.content: The English speaking Headset was helpful. Maybe just average for me as I work in a Prison. Subjective view.

reviews.author: Hamish S
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: It was one of the few things on the Hanoi circuit we wanted to see, it was interesting but not memorable. A bit to read o. The walls so bring your glasses if you need them.

reviews.author: maughams
reviews.title: A place of memory
reviews.content: The colonizing power or not puts its intelligence, its methodology and its rigor to create the perfect place to lock up its political opponents. In this respect, this prison is a success. Buildings still standing that seem to defy the years. The visit is fascinating, we opted for the audio guide and the explanations are an undeniable plus. We must recognize that the French authorities have great contempt for the Vietnamese people and it is incredible to see that the scandalous conditions continued after the Second World War. This prison was also used by American soldiers. Obviously, as in other places of history in Vietnam, the historical facts are reviewed according to the Vietnamese prism and certain assertions should be more nuanced but the fact remains that it is an essential visit which sets a framework history and allows you to acquire new knowledge.

reviews.author: libbbond
reviews.title: Worth a visit if you’re in Hanoi
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area! The museum is laid out really well and is very informative and interesting

reviews.author: Susan C
reviews.title: Crowded on Independence Day
reviews.content: This was my second visit to Hoa Lo Prison but the first for my husband. It was open on Independence Day but was incredibly busy because of that. Last time I came away with an understanding of the horrible conditions Vietnamese people suffered under French colonialism but this time the actual prison area was so crowded it was difficult to stop and read anything. It was less crowded in the section about the American pilot prisoners and in the outside area. There were two new displays there that replaced the ones I had seen last time: one on the 1972 bombing of Hanoi and one on Vietnamese youth involvement in the resistance. These were primarily photos and written material (including English) an both contained quite graphic material.

reviews.author: Zimminaroundtheworld
reviews.title: Sad History, I did Learn a lot though
reviews.content: I visited Hoa Lo Prison during the week in the morning when they opened and it was not busy. I say, plan an hour max to visit the prison. There are many interesting exhibits here with information that includes English text. This prison has a lot of history, unfortunately nothing good. Life was rough here, especially during the French occupation.

reviews.author: Loud1Canberra
reviews.title: A small insight into man's inhumaity to man
reviews.content: One of the sites included by our guide. The original prison dates back to the French occupation of Vietnam and the imprisonment of political prisoners seeking Vietnamese freedom. It is much smaller than you think with only two blocks of the original prison still standing. That said it gives you an insight into the terrible conditions experienced by the prisoners. It also is renowned for being the prison for American airmen during the Vietnam War. While their conditions were much better it was still bad. Be prepared for the propaganda video!

reviews.author: orrdin
reviews.title: Fascinating exhibit
reviews.content: Excellent exhibit on the infamous prison and what life was line in it. Expect to get a healthy dose of propaganda but still worth the visit. Need at least an hour.

reviews.author: Rob & Ronan & Lucy
reviews.title: Understanding the past of Vietnam
reviews.content: It was a great experience to see what the poor people of Vietnam went through. When Americans thought they were being helpful. At that time. It gives you a greater understanding and respect for such an amazing culture in Vietnam today. We thank you for your amazing hospitality and your kindness I was enjoying your stay here.

reviews.author: Hanoi Best Tours
reviews.title: Great tour
reviews.content: A place full of heroism and showing the fighting spirit of the Vietnamese people and a lesson for everyone in the world to appreciate peace more.

reviews.author: Cushard G
reviews.title: Interesting experience
reviews.content: Put it on the list of things to do in Hanoi. We didn't participate in the audio guide and it took us 1-2 hours to tour the museum. There are many signs explaining the history of the museum and exhibits. You are allowed to move freely around the prison and cells and it is both interesting and challenging. There are stories of some of the people held at the prison and they have been presented in a way that will hold your attention and make you want to read everything. We had a really good time for 30,000 VND, definitely worth the trip, it's also within walking distance of the city so easy to get to on a day trip to Hanoi.

reviews.author: EndlessTravels
reviews.title: Fascinating but do own research
reviews.content: Fascinating prison that shows the struggles the Vietnamese people went thru under various colonial oppressors. Some of the exhibits (the ones about American POWS) are laughable propaganda though and need to be taken with a grain of salt. Still well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Akan S
reviews.title: Hoa Lo – such a great place
reviews.content: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison is a must when visiting Hanoi. It is a very important historical relic where you can learn more about the stories of the struggle of the Vietnamese people

reviews.author: Garfieldluvr
reviews.title: Educational Stop in Hanoi
reviews.content: My boyfriend and I visited the “Hanoi Hilton” for around an hour during our stay in Hanoi. I really enjoyed our visit as a learned a lot about not only the use of this building in WWII, but also before that when Vietnamese prisoners were held here.  I recommend getting an audio guide, to at least listen to exhibits that interest you, as they provided some great information. Like other reviewers here, the stories about how WWII prisoners were treated is just one side of the story, but still an interesting and educational stop.

reviews.author: Akshay Sharma
reviews.title: An old prison museum - French Occupation of Vietnam
reviews.content: This is an old prison built by French while occupying Vietnam. It shows how the locals were kept in confinement and tortured by the French police. There is an audio guide and an entrance ticket.

reviews.author: Michael S
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: The existing museum is located in the remaining sections of the prison. Entry price is pretty cheap, as is the audioguides, which are available in several languages. On google maps, it says the museum closes at 5pm, but we learned that it is open until 6pm, but the last entrance is 5pm.  It was an interesting and informative museum.

reviews.author: Steve P
reviews.title: Informative tour
reviews.content: Very informative and well laid out tour, air conditioning welcomed too.  About the right length of your for a family and good value.  Under 15’s free

reviews.author: Marcela Kane
reviews.title: Great experience - not sure why it was not in our tour….
reviews.content: After reading “things to do” in Hanoi we asked our tour guide to accommodate a stop to the prison. We are so happy we did! Great experience and helps understand part of history. Chilling and en lighting at the same time. Would strongly recommend making time

reviews.author: NT
reviews.title: Fascinating experience
reviews.content: Chilling and fascinating experience. The prison has lots of different sections with plenty of information and artifacts. Highly recommend getting the audio headset for more in-depth knowledge of the prison and its history.

reviews.author: Ali_Royal_2015
reviews.title: Chilling experience.
reviews.content: A well presented prison museum with lots of interesting things to see and read. Some chilling moments as you see the reality of living conditions and learn a little about the history of the place.

reviews.author: mr g
reviews.title: Well worth going
reviews.content: My family enjoyed the museum.  You have to look past the nationalistic propaganda (Vietnamese prisoners were tortured and treated horribly but American prisoners were treated really well and played basketball and volleyball all day; not quite how the American POW's describe it).  Worth going for sure, however.

reviews.author: GaryandLesleyTravel
reviews.title: Political Prison to see or not to see.
reviews.content: The original Prison was built by the French in 1896 to hold Vietnamese patriotic & revolutionary fighters. What remains of the original Prison is interesting as is the way they have staged the exhibits. It does contains historical photos and documents from the turn of the 20th century. If you are in to prisons and in particular political prisons then you’ll enjoy this if not if not skip it or view it from the outside.

reviews.author: mrbrentharris
reviews.title: Glad I visited
reviews.content: As many have written. This museum is from the Vietnamese perspective. It was very interesting and a sad reminder of the original use of it by the French to imprison the Vietnamese.Before we saw the the 'American' side, our tour guide thankfully warned us, that what we were about to see was prob not an accurate portrayal of how the Americans POW's were treated. I did spend some time after I left the prison reading the stories of those who were held there.

reviews.author: Steven H
reviews.title: Interesting and informative tour.
reviews.content: Went to see the infamous " Hanoi Hilton", whilst only a small part remains, there was enough to see the conditions etc they had to endure. We used the audio tour for about $6, found this very informative and easier than reading all the info on site.Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Yvonne C
reviews.title: Best tourist attraction in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Best tourist attraction in Hanoi! The museum is well-designed, where you can learn the history of Vietnam from the French colonial period till the end of the Vietnam War. There's a lot to see in the prison, with clear description. There's also sufficient space to sit and enjoy the AC throughout the entire visit which is very nice during summer. There's also a small shopping mall and supermarket beside the prison which you can grab some snacks after the visit.

reviews.author: Luh K. A. Mega Andhini
reviews.title: The Truth
reviews.content: What a place to make you realize how hard was life way back then, how the France colonization pretty much just make Vietnam and its people suffering. Can't say much, as the chill of the prison, the history of the people who trying to protect their country and what was happend with all of that torture just make you in silence, you can not even imagine!

reviews.author: JMW
reviews.title: Family visit
reviews.content: Great museum- if you want to see and read everything you may want to do it over two days as it is so interesting and there is so much info.  We took two teenagers who both enjoyed the experience.

reviews.author: united9999
reviews.title: A must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: I didn’t realise how good it was until we visited it, really captures the horrors of the prison. Some of the torture techniques were grizzly.

reviews.author: jackbonsell
reviews.title: Very powerful and very well done.
reviews.content: The exhibit was done very well.  The history was interesting.  However, if you are miltary buff and wanted a perspective of the american side it was very little.  Most of the exhibit was dedicated to  the imprisonment of the vietnamese during the French control.

reviews.author: Samantha B
reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.content: This is a must visit in Hanoi and I was glad to have read the suggestion to get the audio tour. It was informative and interesting. As many others have noted it is very much from the Vietnamese perspective. It is their right to tell their story. It is good to have this in mind as you listen to the stories. There is information about the construction of the prison, use by the French to house political prisoners and then by the Vietnamese to house American pilots.

reviews.author: mfkstf
reviews.title: Top Notch
reviews.content: This is a must when in Hanoi it is  so so interesting .I read a review before we went and they said to do the Audio tour and they were not wrong makes the whole place come to life in your head would recommend at a drop of a hat as we had been to Saigon first it gives a great perspective on the North & South  views

reviews.author: JamesS
reviews.title: Add the audio guide!
reviews.content: The audio guide may seem expensive (compared to the ticket price) but is well worth the money.  The introductions to each part of the prison is clear and informative whilst being complimented with personal accounts of inmates.   It is a pity that barely 4/10ths of the prison remain -- how the rest "disappeared" under the neighbouring hotel remains a mystery!

reviews.author: Lozza1uk
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: As with every location in Vietnam the story presented is quite one-sided (their home, their right to present their version of the story!) but I thought this was a well laid out museum and larger than I was expecting. Found it interesting and would love to give a massive thank you to the visitor that found my husband’s money belt he had dropped, and handed it into security. We are incredibly grateful and delighted to see there are still lovely people out there!

reviews.author: Ethan J
reviews.title: Interesting but has gaps
reviews.content: Interesting exhibits that focuses more on the French imprisonment of Vietnam people rather then how the prison was used for POW during the war whilst there is some information available they have left out key parts of the prisons history. I left feeling as though I hadn’t got the who history of this place.

reviews.author: Han M
reviews.title: Very interesting to learn the history of the war !
reviews.content: Very interesting museum, describing the history of the war in great detail. Audio guide was very worthwhile otherwise it would have been difficult to follow.

reviews.author: Murray A
reviews.title: Memorable
reviews.content: Good to be reminded of the horrors of war. Very realistic displays and lots of information boards. Bigger than expected.

reviews.author: jason m m
reviews.title: Interesting but falls short
reviews.content: You will leave here thinking the French and Americans were the only barbarians connected to this place. The shocking conditions, torcher and malfeasance towards the revolutionary prisons by the French is described in great and shocking detail. The treatment of the US prisons by contrast is critiqued from the perspective of compassion towards the captives!  Nothing on the treatment of POWs. Nothing. Disappointing.

reviews.author: Stacey P
reviews.title: Revolutionary prison in Hanoi
reviews.content: Our tour of the Hoa Lo Prison was a deeply impacting experience. We gained understanding of Vietnam's history and the beautiful people of this country.

reviews.author: Frodo_10
reviews.title: Eye opening .. a must do
reviews.content: This was so worth visiting to witness and see the oppression by French Colonists and the atrocities committed by the Americans. One can see and visualise what the wonderful, kind Vietnamese people have had to endure and yet have emerged as a united nation moving forward and without any ongoing adverse feelings towards either of the latter , with a forward positive mindset .One can see and hear the narrative  of the cells , oppression and suffering , yet see the positives whereby American ex soldiers have met and seen their previous victims, captors and indeed saviours . One can see how Senior John McCain was recused from Truc Bach  lake , and although imprisoned and tortured , came to meet his rescuers and ended up making friends and ended up being a benefactor for the Vietnamese people

reviews.author: gregsf11
reviews.title: Testament to the unbreakable spirit of the Vietnamese people
reviews.content: When you consider all the horrors that went on here during the French colonial period, discussed in great detail in the audioguide, it really starts to sink in how determined the Vietnamese people have been in their struggle for freedom and independence. Definitely get the audioguide, btw, because without it you miss a lot. Unfortunately the struggle had to continue against the Americans, some of whom served time within its walls after being shot down while bombing their cities, and there's an exhibit on that as well. Americans tend to complain that the information presented here is biased. No doubt all countries try to put themselves in a favorable light. How well or badly the Americans were treated, is in the eye of the beholder, but some facts remain facts. American planes were bombing Vietnamese cities, not the other way around. Vietnamese civilians were getting torn to shreds by American bombs, not the other way around. Take the exhibit on John McCain. McCain wound up here because he was bombing civilian infrastructure -whether a power plant or a light bulb factory. For this act, a group of Vietnamese civilians pulled him out of a lake after his plane was shot down, saving his life at the risk of their own. There's a moving photo of that event on display. Many of the Vietnamese who were here under colonial occupation, were here for much less, and received a fate that was much worse.

reviews.author: Biffro
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: We read that this was a worthwhile thing to do whilst in Hanoi. It was interesting to visit this place to see what the prison was like before the Vietnam war. It was also harrowing to see how some prisoners were treated and to see what incarceration was like for them. After walking through the prison, there is a final section focused on the Vietnam war and whilst it was interesting, we found it was content heavy with boards and boards of text and it could have been more succinct; especially as this area was outside with no air con.  It was an interesting visit and good to get some history, and it was reasonably priced to get in. Do bring water and a fan if visiting this attraction as it takes a good 1 - 2 hours. You also don’t need the audio guide for your visit as there is plenty of text to provide context.

reviews.author: InternationalPillow
reviews.title: Average experience
reviews.content: Pros- interesting to be able to walk in the prison and great English explanations. We also used the audio headphones.Cons- super biased and a little inaccurate.

reviews.author: lady_muckfish
reviews.title: Audio Guide is a must - be aware that the information is biased.
reviews.content: Definitely get the audio guide, you get more in depth stories of what happens at each place and a better understanding of the horrific conditions the prisoners were in.Whilst the prison was very interesting and it was awful hearing the treatment the prisoners had, please note that the information presented is VERY biased. All of the information is about Vietnam vs the French or the Americans, with very little mentioned about the actual divide between North and South Vietnam.Some of the accounts which were presented regarding how they treated US prisoners was also very selective, showing them in a favourable humane light, but when. you read the actual accounts online it's drastically different.The tour wasn't in chronological order, and went back and forwards in time which made it quite confusing at times.It's still definitely worth a visit though.

reviews.author: Sharon S
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: Really interesting and well done. Make sure you get the audio tour and headphones for the best experience. Really reasonable entry and audio tour- a must if you’re visiting Hanoi.

reviews.author: formeryogi
reviews.title: Short visit.
reviews.content: It was one of those things that we felt like we had to do.   Very little information about Vietnam War role during first part of tour.    Mostly information about the prison's French past.    Later, when the Vietnam war is mentioned, it shows American prisoners celebrating Christmas.    Obviously, North Vietnam won the war, and it gets to present the narrative it wants.    But, it does not take much imagination to realize the prison was not a pleasant place.   Less than an hour.   Audio tour is not necessary.

reviews.author: ctm7944
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: Walked from Military History Museum to Hoa Lo Prison (Entry 30KVND Open 8AM - 5PM). Very interesting to learn the Prison's history. And the significance of the location.BTW - there is a VP Bank No Fee ATM nearby. Walked back to my hotel (Hanoi Flora).

reviews.author: Ali B
reviews.title: Definitely worth visiting
reviews.content: Worth getting the audio guide. Good museum / exhibit and still has ~1/5th of the original buildings. Took around 2 hours. Covers the prison during French colonisation  (Vietnamese prisoners) and during the war (American prisoners); take the latter period with a pinch of salt in terms of the conditions the Americans were imprisoned in…

reviews.author: Shelley M
reviews.title: Creepy place
reviews.content: I had done a bit of research before going here, even reading the book by John Mc Cain.  It was still an interesting visit and whilst not entirely accurate, still had a lot of information and worthy of a visit.  Quite creepy in places and I wouldn't take small children to a place like that.  I liked the motorbike parking valet had towels placed on all the seats of the bikes, so owners wont get burnt butt, thought that was a nice touch.  Was easy to find and you had to pay in VND, didn't seem to accept cards for payment.  We spent an hour walking around and that was enough time.

reviews.author: GLB103
reviews.title: Confusing Information!
reviews.content: Interesting museum but too full of propaganda! Pictures of American prisoners enjoying putting up a Christmas tree and playing pool did not sit easy.  I certainly did not agree with the Americans getting involved with the war in any way but like to see how they were treated!  I decided to research on my return to the UK and this prison, known as the Hanoi Hilton, was the worst POW camp - and the Americans were not treated well at all.  I prefer the truth when visiting a museum and this was not!

reviews.author: foodieMelbourne
reviews.title: Great way to spend an hour or two. Well worth a visit.
reviews.content: Well worth a visit. We did the audio tour with our 8 and 10 yr old kids. They got through 2/3 before getting bored which was pretty good going.Highly informative and interesting tour. A great way to spend an hour or two learning about Vietnam’s history.We took cyclos there. If coming from the old town there is a big and very busy road to cross and we wouldn’t have fancied doing that as a pedestrian.

reviews.author: dph1966
reviews.title: Great museum
reviews.content: Just spent a couple of hours here which is enough time. Great place to go to find out the history of the prison from when the French ruled it to the time it was the Hanoi Hilton

reviews.author: devina1991
reviews.title: Well worth paying a visit
reviews.content: Worth visiting and spending some time here. The condition of the prison and the prisoners who lived there during their imprionment is well depicted. The entrance fee is also very reasonable

reviews.author: Joanna
reviews.title: Worth a visit!
reviews.content: Centrally located and worth a visit. Some parts of the story certainly missing but interesting all the same. Went with 13 and 10 year olds and they enjoyed it, took around an hour.

reviews.author: irina j
reviews.title: Interesting part of sad history
reviews.content: Glad we’ve seen this place! So much history and so sad. I was shocked actually how Vietnamese prisoners were kept. Very awful conditions! So cruel.

reviews.author: Jaroslav Nečas
reviews.title: Interesting exhibition
reviews.content: Interesting exhibition of prison and its history as there were many different kind of prisoners over the years started with French occupation to Vietnamese war. English audio guide is for extra price, still basic descriptions are in English language for admission price.

reviews.author: Jashon S
reviews.title: good place to visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: Very good place to visit in Hanoi to understand about history of Vietnam. It is not so far from Hanoi Old Quarter so we can get a taxi easiy.

reviews.author: Tc voyageur
reviews.title: Atmospheric. Very comprehensive descriptions of the French n US war period
reviews.content: Thorough about the horrors of the French occupation and the US bombing.  They describe a bit out of context the horrors of the S VN “tiger cage” system.   However they barely mention any hardships endured by the US aviators.   They say the aviators were provided food that reflected the poverty of the North then but fail to even mention the allegations of torture by the North’s prison guards, which were convincingly made IMOQuite unbalanced IMO.

reviews.author: RoseFeather
reviews.content: Decent museum. Can be completed quite quickly. I’d say go because it’s cheap and there’s something to learn for sure. I would’ve given it a 3.5 if that was an option.

reviews.author: Anne D
reviews.title: Atmospheric prison museum
reviews.content: A fascinating exploration of how this building became a prison throughout French occupation and the American war. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Ali07London
reviews.title: Interesting museum with a lot of history covered
reviews.content: An interesting place to visit with lots of history.  It is worth visiting to get more of the history of the country.  It helps you to understand the war time not just the war against the Americans but also the French - who often seem to be forgotten about.  There is a very tasteful memorial on the site.We chose not to have an audio guide and there are English signs and information throughout the museum

reviews.author: prathamesh
reviews.title: Prison with a lot of history. French and American wars.Visited on
reviews.content: Impressive and a must see as long as people understand that 1964 - 1973 period is 100 % propaganda narrative!For example a statement that US prisoners of war had more food than they could eat is obvious disinformation.I took audio guide which is 100 000 VND extra (ticket is 30 000 VND). I recommend to take it. Without you would loose a lot of information at least from the earlier French occupation time

reviews.author: S Sewpersad
reviews.title: "Interesting and painful"
reviews.content: Visited the Hoa Lo Prison during a city tour of Hanoi. Commonly known as Hanoi Hilton. Historic prison where political prisoners were kept during the French colonisation and the American/Vietnam war. Vividly depicts the harsh conditions that Vietnamese political prisoners were kept. I found it interesting and painful. A must visit as it forms a crucial part of Vietnam's history. Well documented and preserved for the next generation.

reviews.author: Jain G
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison museum
reviews.content: Here are my recommendations . Hoa Lo museum is intersting if you like history. We had an amazing time in Hanoi

reviews.author: Asia Mystika Travel
reviews.title: historical places during Vietnam war time
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison, also known as the Hanoi Hilton, is a historic prison complex in Hanoi that was used for political prisoners during the French colonial era and later for American prisoners of war during the Vietnam War. Today, it serves as a museum and a reminder of Vietnam's turbulent history.

reviews.author: KTP310
reviews.title: Insight into Vietnam’s history
reviews.content: When visiting the vibrant city of Hanoi it is easy to overlook the history of the country, from French colonisation to the Vietnam War. A visit to the prison explains this well, and vividly depicts what life in the prison was like.

reviews.author: Steve Buckley
reviews.title: Integral Part of Hanoi’s History!
reviews.content: My wife and myself are currently holidaying in Hanoi staying at the excellent Boutique Hotel Lasiesta (see separate Review) and earlier today visited Hoa alo Prison/Museum - better known as the Hanoi Hilton.It is an old property opened by the French but our main interest was to learn more about the US pilots who were held captive there during the Vietnam (or American - depending on who you’re talking to!) War. In this regard, the services of a good guide are a must accompanied by a keen eye for details!All in all, it was a most informative visit and one that I would strongly recommend to any visitors looking to learn more about Hanoi’s history.

reviews.author: Leeyoungon
reviews.title: Nice place for history
reviews.content: Very good place to understand about history of Vietnam. We learn a lot from guide Thang from Vietnam Escape Tours Travel. Thank you so muvh

reviews.author: LCPEN
reviews.title: Very Interesting
reviews.content: What an interesting place. It tells the history of the time of the French occupation and shows how prisoners were treated. It was also used for US POWs during the Vietnam war but their “stay” seems to have been less violent than the Vietnamese people’s “stay” under the French. It is well worth a visit but be prepared for the heat inside the buildings.

reviews.author: Ahsan a
reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.content: Must visit during Hanoi visit for little bit of history. A lot to learn about some of the history. Expect to spend around 1 to 2 hours.

reviews.author: Sinéad N
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: Very interesting museum. We learnt a lot. We didn’t get the audio guide and still found it very informative. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Sunny eng
reviews.title: Nice place to understand history
reviews.content: Nice place to understand about history of Vietnam. Very amazing place and we could not understand why people could live there. Had a great time trip arranged by Vietnam Escape Tours.

reviews.author: Omni F
reviews.title: Very sobering experience
reviews.content: If you're over the age of 55, you can probably relate to a visit here.  I went early in the day, just as they opened, and it was nice that there were no crowds and I had plenty of time to process all the displays.  When I was leaving, there was a long line waiting to enter the prison.

reviews.author: Jonathan C.
reviews.title: hoa lo prison
reviews.content: The exhibits offer really interesting interpretation of this prison, ranging from French colonization to American POWs. Lots of interesting displays on the history of this site from the perspective of Vietnam and how different world events have impacted the local community.

reviews.author: debcox
reviews.title: Worthwhile visit.
reviews.content: This is a very worthwhile place to spend an hour and understand how the Vietnamese were treated in the colonial times and what drove them in their long  fight for freedom. It’s separated into two conflicts really, the early colonial period and then the US/Vietnam war.
