This does have a slight propaganda twist to it but nevertheless this all happened and the bombing happened and atrocities happened. every country engages in some propaganda and as I write this Ukrain has been  been invaded by Russia , all repeating itself again. You cannot fail to learn something about Vietnam from this place.

reviews.author: Alex H
reviews.title: Definitely use the audio guide
reviews.content: Entry is 30,000 I think from memory, but the key to having the best experience here is by getting the audio guide for 100,000. There are many signs around the prison but the audio guide goes into so much more detail, which really makes the experience much more chilling and real. There are even accounts from former prisoners on the audio guide.We spent around 2 hours here in total although we took our time.This prison is well worth visiting if in Hanoi, highly recommend.

reviews.author: Miles Archer
reviews.title: HISTORICAL PRISON
reviews.content: Very interesting. Lots of history, including American prisoners here. There's propaganda for the visitor to deal with. Not crowded when I was here.

reviews.author: Tabitha Paige
reviews.title: Not bad, if you don't mind a bit of propaganda
reviews.content: Highly recommend buying the audiobook, it definitely gave some extra information that was really useful. However, we found only the first half was informative. From there, you get expected propaganda on US POWs. I do not condone either side of the war.. but it's far from an accurate rendition. Disappointing.

reviews.author: Leonhkny
reviews.title: Local take on recent history
reviews.content: The former French prison is a perfect place to understand more about colonial rule. The informative museum provides an often-graphic overview of French suppression of the local independence movement as well as a platform for patriotic learning. Each prison cell is well-maintained to re-create the horror of inmate life. The part on American POW is also remarkable. Do devote enough time to explore.

reviews.author: Terry M
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Spent a couple of hours visiting the old prison in Hanoi Paid to hire headphones with audio description of exhibits which was well worth it and very well doneA really well put together museum explaining how the prison was used first by the French and later by Vietnamese to house prisoners including political prisoners and later captured American airmenWell worth a visit

reviews.author: Geoff M
reviews.title: Torture, propaganda, with a little bit of history
reviews.content: I'd say this is a site worth visiting, but keep in mind its purpose is Communist propaganda.  It's divided roughly into 2 sections:  Vietnamese prisoners under the French who were treated abominably, and U.S. prisoners under the Vietnamese who were treated with the utmost compassion and respect.I learned a lot about resistance against the French.The section on U.S. POWs was a horrific whitewash.  The photos and narration show them being treated incredibly well, and the uneducated visitor might swallow this.  The reality was starvation, torture, and outright murder were the norm for most of the time there, until the fear of bad publicity forced a change.I of course do not mind, and even welcomed, reading the Vietnamese view of the war.  I do mind propaganda and outright lies to cover up brutality.

reviews.author: Nomad
reviews.title: Good place to visit
reviews.content: Good place to visit when you are in Hanoi. Many objects there and a lot of info we get. Just 15 minutes for walking from Hanoi Old Quarter

reviews.author: Jodie W
reviews.title: Informative, interesting piece of Hanoi’s History
reviews.content: An informative, interesting place to visit.  We all took away a lot of information about the history of the prison.  Plenty of varied information about the Vietnamese prisoners & then later the US pilot prisoners. The place is well maintained, information in multiple languages.   No need to purchase the audio, everything has written information.   Entry was 30k per adult, well worth it.

reviews.author: Joseph M
reviews.title: Itchin for beer hoi r’after
reviews.content: Seemed alright, just I hadn’t showered for a few days and a serious bout of itchy balls. Didn’t really get what it was about, any suggestions on how to catch up?

reviews.author: EdM
reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit
reviews.content: Well preserved and presented, this is an interesting visit.The commentary was clear throughout the exhibits. It was interesting to note that the French tortured and brutalised the Vietnamese nationalist insurgents, but the VC supported their US prisoners by letting them play volleyball and basketball.That aside, this is well worth a visit and why shouldn’t the victors rewrite history? 😂

reviews.author: Pierre F
reviews.title: If only one place to visit in Hanoi, this one.
reviews.content: A must to see place. Difficult not to be upset after a visit to this historical place but important for a better understanding of Vietnam and its recent past.

reviews.author: PEkBJ
reviews.title: Learn from the past…. A must visit
reviews.content: An eye opener and must see visit in Hanoi. Very good site to revisit the past and learned from it. So heartbreaking to see the pain of the past. Would recommend to visit this in Hanoi. Only VD 30k or USD1.2 for admission.

reviews.author: Ali921
reviews.title: Popular attraction of an old French prison
reviews.content: A popular attraction kept in good condition. Don't pay much attention to the message that they are trying to convey. I think it's very tongue in cheek, they know, they are just having fun with us tourists especially French and US. See it for the construction, size of cells and how prisoners were kept. Their main message is anti-French. If you want to know what it was really like, buy a book, written overseas.

reviews.author: Mitchell D
reviews.title: Disappointing.
reviews.content: They just want you to hear one side of the story, just like the War Remnants in Saigon! I find it disrespectful that they painted out like the American POW enjoyed their time in this dark dingy prison! They spent more time telling us about how the Americans enjoyed basketball here and parading photos of them decorating the prison for Christmas! Not one word about the torture of them at all. I recommend just watching a video on YouTube about this place and the Vietnam war in general! I do not agree with the Vietnam war and the atrocities from both sides but just tell the history how it actually was.

reviews.author: AlwaysTurnLeft
reviews.title: Very interesting to learn about the history of the prison.
reviews.content: Very interesting to visit and learn more about the history of the prison over the years. Lots of information provided as well as being able to look in cells. Definitely worth visiting!

reviews.author: Danny L
reviews.title: Sad but memorable
reviews.content: This was a great tour. It was sad because so many American pilots were there. There were numerous pictures in a flight suit. They revere John McCain especially since he came back to Vietnam in 96 and re establish relations with America which dramatically improved Vietnamese life.

reviews.author: wombatdavid
reviews.title: Interesting place but don’t bother with audio guide
reviews.content: This is the so called Hanoi Hilton with interesting history about French colonialism and USA POWs. The entry fee was 30,000ḏ for adults and 15,000ḏ for students. She accepted my Australian student card after a bit of scrutiny!Please don’t worry with the audio guide. They tell you at the entrance that you need it as there is limited information inside, but we found there was more than enough info in English and French to meet the needs of most. The audio guide is 100,000ḏ so I really would not bother.An interesting place to visit and inexpensive without the audio guide.

reviews.author: Face_The_Elements
reviews.title: Interesting and heartbreaking
reviews.content: This is an interesting and heartbreaking place. Used for political prisoners from 1886 to 1990s, this place has stories and artifacts from a dark time within these prison walls. It was worth spending time at.

reviews.author: MikeH98
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Enjoyed an hour’s visit here. Exhibition is well presented. I quite liked the way that the French are portrayed as the really bad guys when they ran the prison but when the Americans were held there it was all volleyball, letters from home and medical treatment! Nothing wrong with a bit of patriotism…

reviews.author: NA181920
reviews.title: Experience the Patriotism of the Prisoners incarcerated there!
reviews.content: It was great that the gallery was presented in the way how it was like for the prisoners so that visitors can have an experience of it. The exhibits were well presented with sufficient information in Vietnamese, English and French. Recommended time to be there 90 minutes.

reviews.author: Jim Milton
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Good place to visit with a real insight to Vietnam history. Good value for money and would recommend the audial tour. It doesn't cost much and worth it. To walk around the museum takes about 2hrs. If in Hanoi -worth a visit.

reviews.author: MNataro
reviews.title: Sobering testament to history
reviews.content: Definitely a sobering testament to history. Whitewashed by the Vietnamese as these magnanimous victors, completely neglecting the fact that John McCain could never raise his arms high enough to comb his own hair.

reviews.author: Rahul M
reviews.title: Quick tour. Informative and well curated museum
reviews.content: Well curated museum. Place-cards on exhibits in English. You don’t have to buy the audio tour if you’re on a budget. The information on the exhibits can suffice. Spend 1-2 hours here.

reviews.author: travelqueenNi
reviews.title: A thought provoking museum
reviews.content: If you enjoy 20th Century History you will like this museum. Entrance is only 30,000 but the audio guide is 100,000; we found it worth it for the extra information, although we tired a little towards the end.  The exhibits are all very well presented, and you can enter the former prison cells.

reviews.author: samitdeb
reviews.title: A well maintained part of the dark colonial past
reviews.content: Well maintained, informative and best enjoyed with the audio guide. Ticket is 30,000 vnd for the foreigners and audio guide is 100,000 vnd but recommended. Gives a factual overview of the darker colonial past that many Asian countries had to endure and one really feels for the tortured, oppressed political prisoners when you get to exhibit 21 which celebrates  the undaunted vietnamese spirit.

reviews.author: CatgAspersions
reviews.title: Sad but hooray for the courageous Vietnamese!
reviews.content: This is really worth a visit. Rent the audio guide. Walk through the rooms and listen to the horrific conditions and torture of what the prisoners went through.  Very sad but you learn about the courage and patriotism of the Vietnamese. At the end of the journey, I felt like waving their flag!

reviews.author: OneTrip with local
reviews.title: Historical landmarks are filled with interesting facts & relics
reviews.content: Historical landmarks are filled with interesting facts & relics. You will learn a lot about the history & struggles of the people for both French, American & locals. It is an excellent place to spend an hour (or two). Highly recommended! Tickets are required for anyone above 15 years old.Openining hour: All week (8 AM - 5 PM)

reviews.author: Nancie
reviews.title: Bizarre & biased museum
reviews.content: Quite a bizarre yet harrowing experience. The information was limited so I would advise getting the audio guide to give you more insight (we were googling things on our phones). Also, very very biased side of history depicting the American prisoners of war attending a ‘holiday camp’ and saying that they did not want to leave. Altogether, still very interesting.

reviews.author: emalice9
reviews.title: Get the audio guide
reviews.content: Very interesting museum documenting Vietnam's difficult but inspiring history. Definitely get the audio guide, I wouldn't have learned much without it. You can easily spend a few hours here.

reviews.author: Clevelang
reviews.title: Sobering experience
reviews.content: If you are in Hanoi I think you should try to fit this in. Coming from Australia I was well aware of the brutality of European colonialism in times gone by. I was not aware of the actions of the French in Vietnam such a short time ago.We visited with friends from Hanoi. To talk about what happened in this prison with them and how the period of history shaped the people was quite humbling.Having local friends and a world of information available online we did not bother with the audio guide but many other people did. A very cheap (100K dong) but very rewarding experience. You could spend as much or as little time as you like here.Yes if you want to be moved and educated. No if you're looking for a Hollywood version of history. Go with an open mind and kind heart.

reviews.author: ataylor
reviews.title: Limited information and unbalanced view of history
reviews.content: It is interesting to see the building and the different cells but the information written on the walls is not that informative and I get the impression that it is a rather biased version of history (especially when it is portrayed that the Americans had a luxurious stay involving decorating Christmas trees and playing card games). We didn’t take an audio guide as we were told the information was written on the walls. But I would recommend getting an audio guide as the information on the walls is pretty vague. Several rooms mentioned the Hanoi poisoning case but there was no further detail on what this was until later in the museum.

reviews.author: JU
reviews.title: Highly recommended
reviews.content: What initially seems to be an intimate account of the horrors experienced by individuals held captive here unravels into a national history much wider in scope. The freedom fighters and patriots once imprisoned and tortured by the French colonialists would become government and military figures; the very things they stood against were encapsulated within the confines of the prison. Expectedly, there is a downside to this. If you’re looking for an accurate portrayal of the experience US POWs, look away. I was almost jealous of their Christmas parties, sports, feasts, and top class medical care… But this is not the focus of the museum, to be sure and, if anything, it makes it all the more fascinating.Go in with an open mind and at your own pace. It’s definitely recommended if you have a few days in Hanoi.Don’t bother with the audio guide, which costs over 3x what the entry ticket costs (they’ll try to persuade you to buy it). The information you need is all well-presented on boards in Vietnamese, English, and French.

reviews.author: Travelly HN
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison, a new perspective on the strength of the Vietnamese people
reviews.content: I believe this is an important cultural stop while visiting Hanoi. Although it is difficult to imagine the war years, this building and its history can serve as a helpful reminder of what occurred, who was involved, and other pertinent details.Unsurprisingly for a building with such a history, some displays are slightly grisly—such as recreations of rooms showing prisoners with their legs in stockade-like shackles, and the guillotine used by the FrenchI'd highly recommend spending a little extra on an audio guide to enhance the experience and clarify everything you are looking at.

reviews.author: Pera168
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: A real history, we respect much our peace today. The audio guide in many languages can help us to know other stories, well presented.

reviews.author: CKF
reviews.title: Important to visit
reviews.content: Even though many parts of this prison are disturbing, Hoa Lo Prison, a.k.a. "Hanoi Hilton", is historically important and a recommended stop on any Hanoi itinerary.  The displays are well done with good English descriptions on labelling.  There is a small section regarding the time frame when it was used to house American POWs, such as John McCain.  There are both interior and exterior displays.Allow one hour.

reviews.author: Anna L
reviews.title: Worth A Visit - Keep In Mind Biases
reviews.content: This gives a very good history of Vietnam's fight for independence.  The prison was originally built by the French and used to imprison Vietnamese "freedom fighters".    The first part of the tour focuses on this part of Vietnam's history. The 2nd part showcases the experiences of POWs during the Vietnam War.  The contrast is quite interesting in that it tries to portray through photos and descriptions a place where POWs were treated well - this is propaganda and does not marry with the first hand accounts of the men who were held here.Hence I would say that you need to go with this in mind although I wouldn't go so far as to say it makes the whole experience irrelevant.  As others have commented, you do not need a headset.  I had one and my husband did not and yet we both came away with the same information.It started to get busy while we were there so in the height of the tourist season, I imagine this could make the experience a little frustrating as there isn't much room to move around. So perhaps get there as early as possible.What does hit you - as history and present times show us time and again - is how cruel and inhumane human beings can be to each other.  In some places the cruelty and resilience of the prisoners moved me to tears.

reviews.author: Stuart B
reviews.title: Good experience, well presented.
reviews.content: Very interesting visit to this grim and grisly prison of the old Vietnam war period.Well maintained with lots of written information in 3 languages along with photos and images.  Plus life size replicas of men & women in chains and stocks. You can visit the actual cells where 10 + people were held in one call. A horrible place of misery & torture for both Vietnamese and American prisoners of war.

reviews.author: K Wang
reviews.title: Nothing fantastic but informative
reviews.content: I didn't rent the audio guide and felt the English explanations were sufficient for my understanfing about the dark history. It reminded me of how recent our "civilization" is and there is no lack of evidence of how evil human beings are.

reviews.author: Flo G
reviews.title: Sobering Experience
reviews.content: As tourists, I believe its always important to be interested in a country’s history. Hoa Lo Prison was an excellent visit for this. Very extensive and informative visit. I agree with other reviews saying that there is no need to purchase a headset. Everything is written in Vietnamese, English and French.

reviews.author: Suzi G
reviews.title: Interesting history of a famous prison
reviews.content: Interesting to see the famous Hanoi Hilton. No need to hire a headset as all the information boards are in English, Vietnamese and French. Lots of other visitors there. Facts are slanted against the French who imprisoned the Vietnamese communists and make the American Vietnamese war pilots look like they had a great time in the prison! 30,000 dong per adult.

reviews.author: Kibble992
reviews.title: Great trip but emotional
reviews.content: I really did not have much of an idea of what happened in Vietnam with the French. But this prison gives such a clear picture as to what happened all those years ago which when you put into perspective, really was not long ago. The treatment that those prisoners went through to try and get independence was so tragic.Prepare yourself for an emotional experience, it is something which really will hit you. A very good visit and very well explained. You can have a tour guide or you can read all the plaques on the wall which are in English and watch the videos throughout which explain it all perfectly. Fantastic trip and for 30000 Vietnamese dong it's well worth it.

reviews.author: N21dx
reviews.title: The Hilton Hanoi.
reviews.content: A very sad moment in Vietnamese History, of the events of the war and what went on in Hoa Lo Prison. Arrested US pilots called it the 'Hilton Hanoi'. You can see how prisoners were treated and how they lived in the prison cells. A good morale lesson on why we don't need wars and the why we need the whole world to leave in harmony. The tickets are 30.000 VND for entry. You can also purchase the 'Hao Lo Prison: Historical Relic' publication for just 20.000 VND. The publication contains interesting facts and pictures. There is a souvenir shop in the prison, the souvenir there cost cheaper than compared to official souvenir shops in the city.

reviews.author: Tom R
reviews.title: Worth a visit for a bit of history
reviews.content: At only 30k VND entry (50k VND for the audio guide, which is very good) this is definitely worth a trip to experience some of the horrors faced by Vietnamese prisoners during colonial rule.I say Vietnamese political prisoners because very little mention is given to "normal" prisoners and even less about why people were in there in the first place. Regardless, the prison is quite disturbing and they've done a great job in recreating some of the horrors, whilst also not going for "shock value".Any Americans who want to learn more about US captives will probably be disappointed. Whilst a lot of the audio guide is given over to individual cases, the framing is very much around how well they were treated. Somewhat at odds with what went before under the French.If you can look beyond some of the propaganda (which is true of any museum about Nationalist heros) then there is a lot to learn and admire here

reviews.author: k3iiferz56
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton, a place I never want to serve time at.
reviews.content: Seeing first hand the Hanoi Hilton was very eye opening. You experience the brutal lifestyle of the people serving their time in Hoa Lo Prison makes you realize how much better life in the modern world really is. French Colonial prison exhibit is what I found the most interesting. Seeing artifacts left behind, the guillotine used for sentencing, and parts of the sewer system in which political prisoners used to escape was definitely an experience.

reviews.author: Beth Hodgkinson
reviews.title: The history of the Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: A sobering visit to the Hoa Lo Prison is in order when visiting Hanoi. Although the original buildings have long since been demolished, the museum is a harrowing reminder of the atrocities that have taken place here. I would recommend getting an audio guide when visiting.

reviews.author: Linda B
reviews.title: Very sobering experience
reviews.content: With the history behind it related to the "American War"...it was a site I wanted to visit. People of a certain age (me) know the story of the "Hanoi Hilton" as it pertained to captured US serviceman and their time spent here. I had no idea about the previous history when it was under French rule. Lots of history. Lots of sadness and pain for so many.

reviews.author: amanda5805
reviews.title: The Hanoi Hilton. John McCain, was imprisoned
reviews.content: We spent about an hour here which cost 30,000D a person which is about $1.75CAD. More if you want a guide or head set. Everything was labeled so I wouldn’t recommend the headset.Hoa Lo Prison was used by the French colonists  for political prisoners, then later by North Vietnam for US prisoners during the Vietnam War.  The prison was demolished in the mid 1990s but the gate still remains as a museum.This building house a lot of nasty history. There are many Exhibits that show how it was used during the French colonists & Vietnam War. Which  including the guillotine room. Artifacts from  prisoners are on display, including  flight suit and parachute of John McCain.It was very educational but very graphic. I was shocked to see people with small children.

reviews.author: Traveler O
reviews.title: Propaganda Expo
reviews.content: Heavy on the history of French colonial rule but scant info about the horrible mistreatment, torture, and death of U.S. prisoners kept here. All that remains is the gatehouse as the prison itself, which took up the block behind, was razed to construct office buildings and other modern structures within the last 20+ yrs. It's safe to say this is a part of history the Vietnamese want to forget as well, but it's unfortunate there's a gross omission of what really happened here. Take it with a grain of salt. Due to some gruesome pictures, best not to bring kids under 12 yrs old here.

reviews.author: Mark S
reviews.title: Not A Fun Place
reviews.content: Yes, it's among the obligatory tourist sites in Hanoi, this remnant of the old prison now turned into a museum/propaganda house. We visited partly out of curiosity--to see how things were represented--and partly out of respect for the US prisoners housed there, not least the late Senator and patriot from Arizona. It's an emotional experience, so much suffering, especially under the French; and also the accounts of the American war and its prisoners...very much contested ground, historically. Much food for thought here, but not a fun place.

reviews.author: LisaEstella
reviews.title: Interesting and emotional history
reviews.content: Came here after a tour of Vietnam finished. This was our spare day. Interesting history and sad. Not sure if small children should see this.

reviews.author: feltroneu
reviews.title: Horror experience
reviews.content: Actually the building now was only maintained part from its original which is now opened as a museum. When walked further inside you will see those horrible rooms that really make you scare and crazy. Can't imagine those prisoners lived there as being buckled in the bed. I don't like the feeling being there because I really felt sad to see the people being tortured and how many lucky one can get out from there alive!

reviews.author: Joel K
reviews.title: Maison Centrale ... Hanoi Hilton .... A place of historical mistreatment
reviews.content: This prison of horrors was built by the French in 1886. Originally a prison for Vietnamese by the French and then for Americans by the Vietnamese. Many, many American combat soldiers such as John McCain were imprisoned here. Here is where torture was commonplace throughout the history of this Prison.

reviews.author: Mr Joe Does Asia
reviews.title: Very Limited Original Building Not Much Offered
reviews.content: Although somewhat interesting, for the most part a bit boring! Seventy five percent of the original prison building has been torn down. A few interesting artifacts are displayed but very few. If you decide to go it’s ok but, if you decide to skip it you aren’t missing much!

reviews.author: joannegray
reviews.title: Interesting biased views but well worth a visit
reviews.content: It's bizarre to read that American prisons of war were apparently kept quite comfortable and treated well... in a way almost offensive but then who's to say what's correct and what's not?! The prison has been well kept and reflected the entire history from the point of view of the Vietnamese. It's quite eye opening and well worth a visit. I'd say an important part of the countries history.I'd highly recommend spending the little extra on an audio guide to enhance the experience and clarify everything you are looking at.

reviews.author: Gordon S
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Visited Hanoi "Hilton" which was only partially remaining, The visit was eye opening as it showed how the prisoners were kept in cramped quarters. John McCain was also kept as a prisoner here. Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Khushbu Mehta
reviews.title: Disturbing yet must visit
reviews.content: This memorial prison has been well conserved and gives u a glimpse into Vietnam s struggle for freedom under the French and the atrocities suffered by them. Hoa Lu Prison is also called Hilton Prison because during the South/North Vietnam War , American pilots who were captured were prisoned here. But they were not treated as prisoners,rather they lived a comfortable life here,with every facility available to them. U can spend an hour here easily. There’s a lot to see and observe. And a plethora of knowledge about the French Rule and Vietnam s Independence. Some sections are quite disturbing about how the Vietnamese suffered under the French. Entrance is 30,000 VND. Must Visit

reviews.author: kingvikramaditya
reviews.title: A gem for getting acquainted to contemporary Vietnam
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a testimony to the countless innocent Vietnamese souls who wanted nothing but to lead their lives with independence and respect without any colonial intrusion. The prison cells show the brutality of the colonial administration in the treatment meted out to those who raised their voices against the injustice carried on by the French. A serious visitor could spend hours and end up with tears in their eyes! A must visit when in Hanoi!

reviews.author: Biggest backpack
reviews.title: It’s a prison
reviews.content: If you don’t get the audio tour your kind of waiting your time. This is an interesting way to spend a half day at most. It explains not just about the prison but will gives you a little insight into what the Vietnamese people have gone through.

reviews.author: Rachel
reviews.title: Thoughtful
reviews.content: According to what I learnt from the exhibition, the prison mostly showcases the French colonization time in Vietnam. It was only at the end of the tour did I know about the US pilots involvement, which was pretty interesting but rather a bit biased and propaganda-like. It was the exhibitions that struck me with the huge amount of information. At the end, the visit is totally worth it. Would definitely recommend it to my friends

reviews.author: Jane T
reviews.title: Informative, but disturbing
reviews.content: How do you rate a prison museum?  The audio tour had a lot of information, especially about the earlier history where the French held the Vietnamese, but I found myself just wanting to see where John McCain was held for five years.  There is a display case just about him, with English descriptions of how he was "saved" from Truc Bach Lake and given medical care.  The actual wing where Americans were held is no longer standing, but you can get an idea of how grim, depressing, and deplorable the conditions had to have been.  Group detention and single cells in the remaining part, at the front, have been filled with life-size mannequins.   There is a gift shop.

reviews.author: Rus5ty
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Quite interesting. The focus is mainly on what the French did to the locals. It is only after you finish the tour that you get to see the American involvement. I would have like to see how they treated the American POWs.

reviews.author: AfricanQueen6
reviews.title: Interesting but a propaganda filled tour
reviews.content: A very interesting and informative tour giving the history of the prison from the time of French colonialism. Audio tour is full of propaganda and I felt like I was listening to a communist era speech about the evil of the western world and the glory of communism but atrocities were committed by both sides in that prison and the presentation was pretty one sided. It is a reminder of how horrifically man can treat their fellow man and if you can look past the propaganda, it’s a must visit.

reviews.author: NikiG1948
reviews.title: Alas closed due to CV controls.
reviews.content: Vietnam has been vigilant in putting in restrictions to reduce the risk of infection and it is working as they have on 16 cases nationwide. We were able to walk around the building and get a sense of the horrific place during colonial and war times. Another monument to Vietnamese resilience.

reviews.author: UV1951
reviews.title: interesting place
reviews.content: the prison since the France be in North Vietnam and later this place use for USA soldiers, place which call "Hilton Hanoi" . It is not simple to see what was there - but it must to visit.

reviews.author: Cary L
reviews.title: intense history with a brutal past
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison aka  The Hanoi Hilton was started back during French colonial occupation and presents you with a history that is intense and brutal.   For the baby boomer generation this is a part of history that is deeply ingrained in your psyche and when there brings you back to the time when you saw pilots being held and when that wench Hanoi Jane (Jane Fonda) betrayed our American pilots when she handed over the secret notes to the prison guards.    What is important, had but important is to step back and look at this place through the historical lenses  and then you can begin to slowly separate your personal feelings and then understand why the Vietnamese fought like they did to throw off French oppression.    This place was in operation for more than 120 years and it was a place that was feared by everyone.   Today it is museum and it does a very good job of presenting its history and the stories of those people that came through it and the stories of those who didn't.   If you are going to Hanoi this is a must see destination.  It is somber and sobering but it is history and it gives you some serious insight as to why they fought so hard. Have a good tour.

reviews.author: DiPi
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Very interesting and impressive museum, showing the different ways in which the prison was used. The section dedicated to peace was a nice touch

reviews.author: timbisto
reviews.title: A glimpse into the horrible brutality of war
reviews.content: A glimpse into the horrible brutality of the french on the Vietnamese and later the prison for the US military. It is very well organised with so much information. It shows how long the Vietnam people have been at war!

reviews.author: BTG
reviews.title: Basic but interesting
reviews.content: Very basic museum with not much information around though it is interesting and there are some noteworthy displays. Worth a visit if you have time to kill.

reviews.author: Justnitid
reviews.title: A chronicle of the brutality of man
reviews.content: Hoa Lo prison was built by the French by taking over and displacing an entire village community. Over the years it was the place where Vietnamese freedom fighters were interred in the most inhuman conditions possible. There are lots of stories here; stories of brutality and death; and stories of heroism, like those who escaped through the sewers. The prison was also used to house American PoWs. This prison museum is open till 5 pm. Photography is allowed; however out of respect for those who suffered here I took only 3 - one being the shadow of the guillotine.

reviews.author: tintin 69
reviews.title: Interresting place not to miss
reviews.content: Very well organised and discover many things there .   Firts time we saw a real guilotine . Impressive and the way it has been presented is really great . Learnt a lot of things with the exhibition path .

reviews.author: Guy T
reviews.title: Interesting, thought provoking
reviews.content: Put it on the list of things to do whilst Hanoi. We didn’t partake in the audio guide and it took us 1-2Hours to get round the museum. There are plenty of boards explaining the history behind the museum and the exhibits. You are allowed free roam on the prison & the cells and it’s both interesting and thought provoking. There are stories of some of the people held at the prison and it has been presented in a way that keeps your attention and makes you wanted to read it all.We really enjoyed ourself at for 30,000 VND it’s definitely worth a look it’s also in walking distance to the town so easy to get to during a day tour of Hanoi.

reviews.author: G2Kpauly
reviews.title: Ok for a look
reviews.content: I had a look around here and found it vaguely interesting. I didn't bother with the audio tape as I just wanted to read and go at own pace. For 30000 dong it's worth a look

reviews.author: David W
reviews.title: Really interesting
reviews.content: Probably more known by westerners as the POW camp for the American airmen during the Vietnam war but this is much more. This tells of the rough times that the Vietnamese people had to endure before that period. Well worth the visit

reviews.author: Moltys73
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: A very good self tour, that shows you the history of the Prison. Recommend a couple of hours to look at all the Prison has to offer.

reviews.author: b h
reviews.title: Great time in Vietnam
reviews.content: Visiting the prison was one part of a three week trip. Guide was great and informative. Thanks Linh for putting together a great trip.

reviews.author: TMOH8
reviews.title: We only visited the exterior but still worthwhile.
reviews.content: I wish that we'd had time to go inside as I'd heard good things about it but time didn't allow.We were however able to look around the exterior and I'd recommend the very informative display of the history of Vietnam and Hanoi that lines the walls and is free for all.

reviews.author: Pwncjn1
reviews.title: A must see in Hanoi.
reviews.content: A very chilling place to walk around and see and read how the Vietnamese people have put up with many hardships, especially during the French time.

reviews.author: Liz H
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton - moving
reviews.content: Very interesting and moving, particularly of the prisoners held here in such terrible conditions.  Need more than an hour here to take in all the exhibits.  Wish we’d visited separately from our tour to have more time here.

reviews.author: Tony
reviews.title: Confronting view of Vietnam's recent history
reviews.content: Fascinating and confronting experience of a very cruel past. Insight into the harsh conditions for prisoners male and female. Stories of escape was incredible.

reviews.author: Mikemycroft
reviews.title: Visit to the “Hanoi Hilton”!
reviews.content: We spent a very informative morning visiting the Hoa Lo prison, dubbed the Hanoi Hilton by the American POWs who were imprisoned there during the Vietnam war. The prison is an easy place to visit, the flow of the exhibits is very good, and it is a bit of an eye opener when you realise that although there was a lot of criticism aimed at Vietnam for there I’ll treatment of some prisoners, they suffered just as badly under the French regime when the prison was called Maison Centrale. Well worth a visit if you are in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Jlogez
reviews.title: Very Interesting Tour
reviews.content: Great tour and a little confronting in some parts. Get the Audio headphones. Loads of information and stories from inmates. Well worth it to visit.

reviews.author: A K
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Now a place of peace, this is a useful insight into the political imprisonment in days gone by.Its a shame much of the original building js no longer there. Some of the printed information is a little confusing \ contradictory but I found no one available to discuss this with. All in this was s good experience.

reviews.author: Amanda C
reviews.title: Thought provoking
reviews.content: A well presented representation of the history of this prison, built by French to house political prisoners who opposed their occupation.They had actually brought a guillotine with them before the construction of the prison.The treatment of the prisoners was barbaric and continued well after the atrocities of the Second World War that France underwent!Cost 30,000dong (£1) excellent value. There is an audio guide, but if you choose not to use one there is plenty of information in the various stages, these are within the remaining cellsHighly recommended

reviews.author: Michael W
reviews.title: Not so much left
reviews.content: Although the ‘Hanoi Hilton’ is a must visit, it’s really just for the name these days, as the majority of the place has been built over. Nevertheless, there are some interesting exhibits and it’s worth taking 30/40 minutes to take a look round and try to get a feel of what it was like to be taken there in the war.

reviews.author: Karens
reviews.title: Shocking truth
reviews.content: We had a free day , and as it was raining I looked on trip advisor to see if there was something close by our hotel to fill in a couple of  hours, which is when I came across Hoa Lo Prison... it was about a 10 minute walk but once inside you actually feel the oppression these poor prisoners must  have suffered, the absolute inhumane conditions in which they were held  and in many cases lost their lives is felt as you walk through and read the way they  treated.   Very sad but I’m glad I had the experience

reviews.author: Kim G
reviews.title: Highly Recommend; Although Upsetting & Confusing
reviews.content: Written above the entry to Hoa Lo Prison are the words: "Maison Centrale", or Central House, however Vietnamese prisoners referred to it as "the Monster's Mouth". This is but the small southern section of the remaining prison more commonly referred to as the Hanoi Hilton by American POW's (prisoners of war), during the Vietnam War.  In 1990, the missing portion of the prison was demolished to make way for the Hanoi Towers hotel and offices. Built by the French Colonialists in 1886-1901, the most striking sense of brutality are the scenes and literature revealing torment and torture of the Vietnamese by the French Government. The period of American captivity is "whitewashed", when the Vietnamese were in control of the prison. The visitor will feel humbled, upset and confused; nonetheless, I highly recommend a tour of this historic prison.

reviews.author: Heather M
reviews.title: Great history and site, but beware of brutal truths
reviews.content: We hadn't planned on going here, but our 13-year-old daughter chose it to fill an afternoon. She got into the audio tour while the rest of the family took in the atmosphere of the harsh prison and whatever printed English stories were available. Halfway through our 10-year-old was quite upset by the nature of the content. It was one of the most emotionally challenging historic sites I've been to, but reality is like that.

reviews.author: Lorine R
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: I am so thankful the city left part of this prison standing so visitors can witness a piece of History. This exhibit is very well done and contains much information. The recorded walking tour is excellent. So thankful I visited and step back in time to feel and see what the prisoners experienced in this place.

reviews.author: Janet A
reviews.title: Thought provoking museum
reviews.content: Recommend this prison museum for introduction to neo colonial and 20th century Vietnamese history. Well curated and visual.

reviews.author: Peyroutel
reviews.title: Historical
reviews.content: Worth a visit so to remind us how cruel humans can be to each other. The whole tour is bias and a lot of the stated information has to be taken with a pick of salt. Still worth a visit.

reviews.author: Brenda N
reviews.title: Hilton Hotel
reviews.content: Spend some time there and get the headset for the walking tour.  Very informative.  Not too crowded   Worth while

reviews.author: GRLUK
reviews.title: Not much talking going on, just people taking it all in, quietly
reviews.content: When you have heard of a place so often the actual experience of visiting can be a let down, but not here, this was just as sad as we expected. The prison elements made you realise what life and death had been like there, and then the images and statistics and general horror of war and conflict made us sad, and very quiet as we spent a long time taking it all in.The most memorable was actually seeing the messages and coverage from around the world showing how people at the time felt about the Vietnam/American war.Has to be visited, look out also for the stories of the escapes from this Hilton.

reviews.author: Ruth G
reviews.title: Amazing documenttion
reviews.content: Eventhough the visit to the prison was a heavy afternoon, it's an amazing piece of history.  The documentation was was very well done with many photos as well.  Plan for about two hours to see all.

reviews.author: Claudia R
reviews.title: Very moving
reviews.content: A great place to visit to understand how prisoners (both Vietnamese and Americans) were treated during their incarceration at this prison. The propaganda is interesting and pictures are moving. For an entrance fee of 30,000 VDN it’s worth it. You can also hire an audio guide for an extra 50,000 VDN.

reviews.author: Dan
reviews.title: A should “Visit” if you are here !
reviews.content: Cheap to enter, will not take long, interesting and insightful ! A view to not letting past history repeat its self ever !! Taken by two FREE tour guides, to young students who spoke very good English...100 of them in the city membership.....please look the college scheme up !!

reviews.author: Cynthia
reviews.title: Interresting
reviews.content: This museum is not too big but its filled with important information and if you love history it's worth a visit.

reviews.author: Sofie B
reviews.title: Cultural trip
reviews.content: An interesting and historical tour. There is a lot of reading and if you read it all it will take a long time. But a good break from the busy streets of Hanoi.

reviews.author: GuidoHongKong
reviews.title: Worth the time
reviews.content: Definitely a place you should stop in Hanoi.....doesn’t take long, but very impactful.  Gives a real view of what ‘colonialism’ really meant to many in VietNam.

reviews.author: Stacy K
reviews.title: Interesting Stop
reviews.content: It was interesting to see the remaining portion of the prison that the French built to hold Vietnamese political prisoners and then used by the Vietnamese to hold Americans during the war. Harrowing conditions. At the end there is a Garden of Peace that is full of Vietnamese propaganda claiming that all the nations in the world were against "imperialist American aggression" Audio guide is extra cost.

reviews.author: killerdwarf
reviews.title: Good insight to the prison history
reviews.content: This is a good tour offering some interesting insight into the history of the Hanoi Hilton.I thought the audio tour was well worth the extra couple of pounds to get a full understanding.

reviews.author: Steviep
reviews.title: Put this on your list of things to do in Hanoi
reviews.content: We asked our tour guide to put this on our itinerary, and we are so glad we did. It’s not just about the Americans that were incarcerated here, it’s so much more than that. Please make sure that you get the audio guide at the start of the tour, as this explains things that you will miss without it. Allow yourself around 2 hours for the tour. Please be aware that it was a prison for political prisoners and some of the pictures and audio descriptions are not for the squeamish.

reviews.author: Lardie
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: We visited this as part of a walking tour with Hanoi Kids. Helped having a guide to explain a little about the place. Having said that lots of signs on the exhibits . It whiles away a couple of hours.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: A scary place ( as you'd expect), the broken glass topped walls give an initial taste in what is to come.Intimidating conditions from the French rule through it's time as the Hanoi Hilton.Never seen a guillotine before!

reviews.author: udontnomee3e
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: This was worth a visit,  wasn't to expensive.  Wish they had tour guides to explain it more as all of the areas need to be read about.  They did have an audio guide but there was 4 of us & didn't want us all to be walking around with head phones in.  Had it been more expensive I might not have been so impressed but for the price we paid it was interesting. It doesn't take very long to go around,  no more than an hour.  Which is a good time frame with kids.

reviews.author: JD666
reviews.title: Interesting History
reviews.content: The history and Vietnamese perspective are very interesting and informative.  Much of how modern Vietnam has come to be is apparent... The museum/prison itself however isn’t really all that riveting.  Definitely worth a visit but temper your expectations.

reviews.author: Pete B
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Former prison in the centre oh Hanoi built by the french when Vietnam was a French colony, later used during the Vietnam war to captured American pilots well worth a visit .

reviews.author: WhiTe Angel
reviews.title: A must visit and understand more about Vietnam's history!
reviews.content: This prison visit truly give me a deep impression about how the Vietnamese people suffered during the French period & wars. So sad how the prisoners been tortured in the cell. The dark spirit in the prison was devastated for freedom and new life! This is how I learnt more about Vietnam history! No more war!! Freedom & Peace for Vietnam!!

reviews.author: George R
reviews.title: Mr. George Riley
reviews.content: We have been here twice. We went too late the first time and had to leave before going upstairs. It was so interesting and we went back today. I may have overthought it all but it took me 4 to 5 hours total. I wouldn’t have missed the Hanoi Hilton. This historical place was top on our trip to Hanoi.

reviews.author: Barry W
reviews.title: Well Worth A Visit
reviews.content: I would recommend getting the headphones, which cost 50,000VND per person, as the commentary is really informative. 30,000VND per person entry fee, which is very good value for money considering, what you get to see.

reviews.author: malomax
reviews.title: A great way to understand more of the country’s history
reviews.content: A visit to the ‘Hanoi Hilton’ is almost a must when visiting Hanoi.  Most of the displays are about the French period, but there are a couple regarding the ‘guests’ that stayed there during the Vietnam War.  I think it was quite eye-opening for our kids (11 and 14).

reviews.author: TICKY
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: A must go to when in Hanoi. Really had my eyes open to the history of Vietnam the occupation of the French and of course the American war. Being a child of the 70’s and growing up with the Vietnam war on the news daily I found this place fascinating, although strange to say a really enjoyable visit.

reviews.author: Caacer1
reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.content: A must see place, interesting to get another perspective of the war!  Horror that people endured!  It was an eye opening experience,!  The details of the cell and how they were kept in irons.

reviews.author: TMRoot
reviews.title: great place for history
reviews.content: The audio guide is a bit long winded....but it's good information much more than the signs alone. Don't buy the paper guidebook.  Good information and it doesn't feel like propaganda.

reviews.author: Alan R
reviews.title: Very in depth museum
reviews.content: This museum really did a great job telling the story of this prison during the French colonial times and the horrors that took place. It is worth the trip and is located near many different other areas of note, such as St. Joseph cathedral and the women's history museum. So create a nap and spend the day exploring.

reviews.author: Feenixwest
reviews.title: Historic Place of Man’s Inhumanity to Man
reviews.content: In spirit this is an ugly place. Of course crimes are ugly but political repression and retribution are uglier. The focus was on a time when the French were incarcerating political prisoners. There was also some information on the American pilots shot down in 1972 but mostly on the day they were released after their six years of “temporary” and indefinite stay. A lot of propaganda on how kind the Vietnamese were shown by staged pictures of happy American prisoners. Hmm.

reviews.author: UK Adventure Seeker
reviews.title: Essential visit
reviews.content: A sobering reminder of the past, however it’s essential to visit. I didn’t feel that the stories portrayed a balanced reflection of the history behind the war though

reviews.author: Johan K
reviews.title: Interesting to see first hand the infamous Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: The Hoa Lo prison is easy to access, well organized and easy to grasp. Used during both French and Vietnamese control, the prison holds a certain political role. Well worth an hour or a little more. (Get the audio tour - $2.5 - with 35 pre-recorded tracks for each exhibit in the prison.)(Our seven year-old was a little intimidated by the prison, but there are no strong graphics etc.)

reviews.author: deviina
reviews.title: A lot of history !
reviews.content: Very interesting. I learned a lot about the vietnamese war. However, I reccomend before going to read up about the basics of the war if you are quite clueless about the topic as you may get confused.

reviews.author: Julie
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: This was simply £1 pp to get in, well worth it. A lot of history attached to the prison, it is an interesting place I enjoyed it.

reviews.author: Benrubi
reviews.title: Get ready for some heart wrenching stuff
reviews.content: This is a must see... the conditions, the treatment and the fortitude of these men.... you have to see the deplorable conditions and the limited amount of freedom they had

reviews.author: XavierNY
reviews.title: Must Visit
reviews.content: Definitely a must visit, to learn about this prison and Vietnamese History. Museum is organized well, which I appreciate a lot.

reviews.author: Lise B
reviews.title: Difficult to see
reviews.content: We knew this would be a difficult place, but the stories at the end of the exhibit about the Viet Nam war were so difficult to read.  I highly recommend a visit here, but be prepared to feel some pain.

reviews.author: Martha D
reviews.title: A New Perspective
reviews.content: I’m so glad we took time to do this tour. So interesting to learn about the “American War” as opposed to the “Vietnam War.” It certainly offered a perspective I hadn’t considered much. We rented the audio tour and it was excellent. Lots of good information that we would not have gotten from simply reading the markers at each display. The personal stories/memoirs were particularly moving. If you like history and you’re interested in a side of it you may not have been exposed to, I highly recommend.

reviews.author: ByronP
reviews.title: The "Hanoi Hilton" is a must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: This former prison is now a museum that is pretty much dedicated to show how badly the Vietnamese prisoners were treated by the French during colonial times (I don't know much about what the French did) and how well the American prisoners were treated by the communists during the Vietnam war.  You'll see pictures of US prisoners smiling, playing ping pong, going to church, eating well, etc. - the world knows US prisoners were tortured, not well taken care of but the Vietnam government propananda machine is still putting out the lies and propaganda.   Overall, it's worth a visit but I think that most people about 1 hour is good.  If your the type of person that reads everything (some stuff in English) and wants to do the audio guide then plan on 2 hours.

reviews.author: 73Chelle73
reviews.title: Good Half Day Tour
reviews.content: We did the prison on our last day in Hanoi to fill in the day before leaving for home.  We all hired the headsets for a small fee, I feel you get a lot more out of the experience if you do.  There is a lot of information in English you can read but listening allows you to walk around & observe a lot more, took us a few hours to get around, no food options available within other than vending machines so take it with you.  My 20 & 16 year old kids got a lot out of it but I wouldn’t take small children.

reviews.author: Jason
reviews.title: Prison visit
reviews.content: Very powerful experience. Very well done. I didn’t use the headset guide and there was plenty of information to read in English. I think this is an important place to visit.

reviews.author: AnnLouiseBigPineKey
reviews.title: A must for Hanoi visitors
reviews.content: Excellent museum and historic site. A very meaningful glimpse of colonial persecution of Vietnamese who wanted independence and democracy for their country. This is not just a museum but you enter the cells, touch the walls. Gift shop is very well done. Displays regarding Sen. John McCain and other US POWs are excellent. Lots of content here.

reviews.author: Hello in 10 Languages
reviews.title: Well Presented
reviews.content: We travelled for the full length of Vietnam from Hanoi to Saigon, via Danang, taken in most of the 'War' history. Hoa Lo Prison a.k.a Hanoi Hilton proved to be the most friendly and non-biased war associated site we visited. The museum mainly concentrates on the French occupation, guillotine provided, and also how the museum has been used by a prison. All the information is well presented.

reviews.author: Curtis G
reviews.title: Interested
reviews.content: The museum is very good. You need a good few hours if you want the in-depth knowledge and would recommend it. You can get a headset in English and walk around learning it all

reviews.author: zarniwoop
reviews.title: Very Enlightening
reviews.content: A testament to the evils of colonisation and the horror and futility of war. An essential insight into Vietnamese history

reviews.author: Misst
reviews.title: Must see!
reviews.content: Great museum. I spent 3 hours there!!! Grab the audio tour as it adds a lot to the displays. Great personal stories that really bring it to life.

reviews.author: umaramanan
reviews.title: Worth a visit when in Hanoi
reviews.content: Learnt a lot about Vietnamese history since early 19th century to 1975..Went with 2 “almost” teenagers who were pretty apprehensive. But we walked away pondering about history of Vietnam and pledged to watch a documentary or two about it together as a family! Also makes one wonder and feel sad about how this friendly country had to endure so many years of violence. 100% Worth a visit We had a local guide with us so didn’t take the Audio guide. But this is available. The visit itself lasts between 2-2.5 hours depending on how much you stop to read..

reviews.author: BecAndyB
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: We spent a good hour here exploring the prison and imagining the horrors that had taken place. Good to get some history and fill in an hour or more in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Caitlyn M
reviews.title: An absolute must
reviews.content: This museum was fabulous.  I learned a lot about the history of Vietnam and the the prison itself. Although it definitely is slanted towards the good of the country  even taking that bias into consideration it is very interesting. I highly recommend getting the audio guide, it is worth the price.

reviews.author: Barb2travel
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison -Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Excellent Museum. Inexpensive and rent the English audio guide as it was well done.  Some local bias in the story telling but this was worth the visit!

reviews.author: robilaz
reviews.title: Eye-opening attraction
reviews.content: An interesting, dark, eye-opening museum that explores the history of the prison and looks back at the war with the USA. Very insightful and it succeeds in helping you realise how horrific a place it would have been to have been locked up in. And, some of the awful things that people are capable of doing in the name of punishment.

reviews.author: Ryan L
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: Prison was smaller than I imagined. Was plenty to read and see but it seemed to repeat alot of it. Definitely a place  you need to visit In Hanoi.

reviews.author: Sydneysider888
reviews.title: Interesting and enlightening visit
reviews.content: Visited this prison museum in late December 2019.  Only a small portion of the original jail has been preserved. I found the visit very interesting and informative, a real eye-opener. It gives an insight into Hanoi's history, through French colonial rule, local rebellion, and the Vietnam war. Of course there will be some local bias, but it sparked interest for me to look in to those historical events further after the visit. It is a fairly somber journey through the jail, but does end on a lighter note.The price of the visit is nominal, 30,000VND or there-abouts. Probably allow about an hour or so, depends on whether or not you read all the information presented. We found it easy and cheap to travel to different sites using Grab while in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Ian R
reviews.title: Historical site with a link to the American War
reviews.content: Right in Hanoi the Hanoi Hilton where US pilots shot down during the war were held, but it's history goes much further back to the French era where the inmates were Vietnamese and treatment bordered on the barbaric.Interesting reflections on the times during the American War era.

reviews.author: dekalbill
reviews.title: Important Museum
reviews.content: If you have expectations before visiting this site, you will come away with a new perspective of the many conflicts in Vietnam's history.  Much of the prison is now gone, but the displays in the prison which is now a museum are thought provoking and could be hard to look at. It could be depressing, but there are displays providing hope for the future.

reviews.author: Love to travel
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: I think many people think this is going to be all about Vietnam war and it’s not. It covers centuries of troubled times and harsh conflicts, its a must if you are in Hanoi. Very interesting when you see  what this country has been though in the last 2000 years. I did feel at the end there was a lot of propaganda especially with the relationship with Russians, but all in all it was very interesting trip

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: Very well done and informative
reviews.content: It was very good to walk around the prison and see the cells, conditions etc that prisoners went through.Most of it focused on the French time of running the prison with how brutal they were to the political prisoners with the cruelty, executions and mistreatments.They have several areas that have pictures with timelines and history of prison in multiple languages which was really good.Wouldn’t say this is a must visit but it’s a good visit.

reviews.author: Wills
reviews.title: An historic Relic of significant importance and great interest
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison, aka Hanoi Hilton, spans the history of Vietnam from French Colonialism through to the Vietnam War. Built in 1896 by the French to house political and revolutionaries fighting against the French occupation. After North Vietnam's liberation in 1964, the Vietnamese Government imprisoned criminals behind its walls. Between 1964 and 1973, American pilots shot down over North Vietnam were held captive and tortured there as POWs. It was these POWs who gave it the name, Hanoi Hilton.Today, a section of the original prison forms the Historic Relic, housing an impressive museum and Memorial Monument.Given the atrocities and executions that took place here, the exhibitions are remarkably neutral, yet factual. Even the exhibit dedicated to the American Vietnam War is empathetic. The journey through the museum is well thought out. The majority of the exhibits are on the ground floor and easily accessible except for access into the cells themselves. There are also exhibits on a second floor, accessed via a steepish staircase. The Memorial Monument is a peaceful garden on the ground floor.If you are in Hanoi - don't miss it.

reviews.author: Julian M
reviews.title: Another Perspective.
reviews.content: Obviously a visit to a notorious prison like the "Hanoi Hilton" isn't on everyone's typical holiday to do list. However it is surely impossible to visit Vietnam and not want to see an alternative perspective on the history of the French colonialism and Western/American involvement in the Vietnam war. A visit to this prison is thought provoking and disturbing but should be done. It isn't unbiased but then neither is the history that we in the west have grown up with.

reviews.author: Nik_Braitch
reviews.title: A Fantastic bit of History
reviews.content: This prison tour is a great way to spend a couple of hours understanding Vietnamese history. They have audio tours for you to hire inside. I would highly advise taking one as this explains the full history of Hoa Lo Prison and also case studies from people captured and imprisoned here.

reviews.author: hejhopptopp
reviews.title: Interesting and important
reviews.content: Very interesting and memorable. However, most of the information is very scewed in favor of the Vietnamiese.

reviews.author: Karol J
reviews.title: History in the pill
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is memory place that you should visit if you are in Hanoi. It will take through the history of Vietnam and open your eyes on what happened to the nation. Exibition can be creepy at times as you will encouter life sized statues of prisoners in dimly lit cells. Spend some time to read description on each exibition. You can book a tour with audio or with a guide. Entry fee is really cheap

reviews.author: RodKou
reviews.title: Small, cheap and worth it.
reviews.content: Nice place, it took us around 30 minutes to visit. It makes you understand the conflict better, its repercussions, international support/views, and how it all ended up.

reviews.author: okiejer
reviews.title: Sad reminder of man's inhumanity to man
reviews.content: The prison highlights the suffering primarily of the Vietnamese under French rule.  The resilience of the prisons was astounding, given the torture and conditions.  While some reviewers were offended in how American prisoners were portrayed, remember that this is the Vietnamese narrative of the war.  For them, the American were just another invading foreign force to be repelled.  I think the museum allows empathy for all those prisons who suffered.

reviews.author: DaleB
reviews.title: Grim, but good, glad I visited.
reviews.content: I wasn’t going to visit the prison as I didn’t think it would appeal to me, but went and enjoyed it. I too, the hop on hop off bus tour and visited late morning. I found the history interesting and the stories about how it was used to house American pilots during the Vietnam war very factual. Like any site associated with war, it was grim, but I thought it was well preserved and definitely worth visiting.

reviews.author: Carli R
reviews.title: Hanoi “Hilton” prison
reviews.content: A really informative insight into the political history of North Vietnam. Well preserved architecture and a time line story that leaves you feeling sad but strangely optimistic for the future.

reviews.author: Natalie A
reviews.title: Not that great-could be improved with better audio guide
reviews.content: We spent 60-70 minutes and had the audio guide but it was hard to hear the voice over the ‘background’ music. Definitely interesting to see how the French Colonialists mistreated the Vietnamese during their occupation, and the Americans who were captured and held here appear to have had good conditions for a prison. I wouldn’t recommend this as a must do in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Praveen K
reviews.title: Well maintained
reviews.content: We got a slice of history first thing in 2020 when we visited the prison. The facility has been maintained fairly well and the audio guide has loads of information about the place.

reviews.author: lynder78
reviews.title: Interesting and not a huge time commitment
reviews.content: The audio was a little wordy and not really sure it was exactly necessary. Tip: if you have an extra set of earbuds that fit standard phones (not the new iphone ear buds) you can connect to the audio set and only pay for one. There’s an extra outlet which we noticed after the fact.

reviews.author: Ausausbaby
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Quite interesting, especially the early history with the French. Like the others we recommend the audio tour as well

reviews.author: Michal M
reviews.title: Exceeded Expectations, but Beware of Propaganda
reviews.content: We found the museum to be very informational and moving. The audio sets are definitely recommended, they really add to the experience and are easy to use. They cost 50,000 dong extra ($2), but it's worth it.There are plenty of benches to sit and rest / listen to the audio guide.The only disappointment was that the room about American prisoners of war was entirely propaganda. I hoped that they would be a little more honest in their depictions of American imprisonment. It is interesting to see the Vietnamese perspective, but I would recommend educating yourself further on the subject after your visit.

reviews.author: Paintme02
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Definitely worth the visit. Doesn’t take too long. Best to do independently and hire head sets. You don’t have to wait for others to take their photos..

reviews.author: Shirzccy
reviews.title: Great place to understand Vietnam History
reviews.content: Entrance fees: 30kd per person. Among all the rest of museum, my whole family enjoyed this the most.

reviews.author: Paddy F
reviews.title: Han lo prison
reviews.content: Great tour with good guidance. Not the usual America war style prison that u might think. More backdated to French colonial times and only a small section for America war but still a fantastic insight to what the jail would have been like for prisoners

reviews.author: Alan S
reviews.title: A little confronting
reviews.content: A tour of the prison provides a great opportunity to learn more about the fascinating history of Hanoi.  Especially the French occupation and the treatment of the political prisoners.Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: E9N20
reviews.title: Major History in Hanoi
reviews.content: Excellent well spent time, and history lesson.  Museum is not that big but in the originallocation. Must see

reviews.author: VickyT_TravelBug
reviews.title: Very informative tour
reviews.content: We spent an interesting afternoon doing the audio tour and found it very interesting and emotional.You learn the history of the conditions the Vietnamese were kept in under the French rule and the way the Americans were treated after being captured during the vietnam war when it was referred to as the Hanoi Hilton.A must see activity in Hanoi.

reviews.author: hanauerl
reviews.title: Interesting but biased
reviews.content: Interesting visit, but the focus is overwhelmingly on the experience of Vietnamese prisoners under the French. The small section about US prisoners is whitewashed. Skip the audio tour, which is informative but loaded with propaganda.

reviews.author: Ashish J
reviews.title: Dark History of the city of peace
reviews.content: Place takes you back in time when Vietnam was under French occupation. A must visit for tourists to appreciate what the country has gone through. If you go through all the rooms and read the material carefully then it might take a good part of half a day for you otherwise couple of hours are sufficient. A good place to visit in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Stephen C
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: The building is interesting historically although you need to read all the information to appreciate it.

reviews.author: WilliamWillieWilson
reviews.title: Most important site in Hanoi
reviews.content: While visiting Hanoi, tourists will find historic sites, great restaurants, and open markets. But only Hoa Lo Prison (a.k.a. the “Hanoi Hilton”) will truly take your breath away. Nobody should come to Hanoi without stopping here and considering its significance.Vietnam is a rapidly developing country, becoming more tourist friendly and cosmopolitan by the day. But the country is noticeably, and understandably, reluctant to embrace historical sites from the Vietnam War. It seems to be a period they’d like to forget.Hoa Lo Prison is a rare site we found in the whole of Vietnam that paid tribute to the ugliness of this war. Walking through the museum, you’ll see the conditions endured by political prisoners and American troops including John McCain. It is shocking, fascinating, and poignant all at the same time.

reviews.author: Denis T
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Very cheap entrance fee. It is well laid out and very informative. Staff are friendly and helpful. Can view in about an hour but could spend longer if you absorb everything

reviews.author: chezfijez
reviews.title: Interesting part of Vietnamese history
reviews.content: Very interesting part of Vietnamese history. Would have liked more information on the American servicemen held here. But interesting to read about the ‘ comrades’ held here and the conditions they endured. Quite horrific .

reviews.author: 88UK
reviews.title: Interesting and inexpensive
reviews.content: I found the prison interesting, shame that most of it was knocked down for development. There are a lot of informative displays. I’m not sure how biased the information is though.

reviews.author: Ghentfreak
reviews.title: A must have seen in Hanoi
reviews.content: An very interesting place to visit in order to understand the Vietnamese history of the previous century. A bit shocking but realistic again it makes us aware of what mankind can cause to each other. Belgium has been the battlefield of Europe, Vietnam of that part of Asia!

reviews.author: steverichhudd
reviews.title: Spent longer here than expected
reviews.content: We thought we would go to this museum to pass a bit of time, but ended up being here almost 2 hours. We didn't get an audio guide, but did get the booklet (20k) when we got our entrance tickets (30k each).The main prison was demolished a long time ago to enable the commercial tower next door to be built, but there entrance and first part of it remain for historical legacy.The exhibits are basically done and we had a really interesting time here and felt we learnt a lot from reading the information panels across the site.Definitely a must see museum when you visit Hanoi

reviews.author: Jessie L
reviews.title: Worth a visit.
reviews.content: We got the audio guide and found it very interesting. Took about 1.5hours to go through with the guide. We went at about 9am and it was very quite and enjoyable.

reviews.author: Rahul S
reviews.title: Prison shown with real description
reviews.content: Prison visit gives you and leaves you with great experience. You learn a lot about the Vietnam war and many other aspects..

reviews.author: Mike E
reviews.title: Thought provoking
reviews.content: Our visit to Ho Loa gave us a lot to think about. The exhibition presented a graphical representation of the horrors the Vietnamese political activists had to endure as they fought for the independence of their country. We'll worth the visit.

reviews.author: Sansanee V
reviews.title: An important fragment of Vietnam’s History
reviews.content: First of all I need to say that this place is not family friendly, the place contains scary pictures and the tool that the French use to torture the proud Vietnamese peace fighters, do not bring young toddlers with you on your trip:Lets start at the front, you will see a yellow gate that says “Maison Centralle” which is French for  The Central House ( I guess ). You can take some pictures at the gate. Next, you must buy the ticket at the ticket booth, a black little building at the left of the entrance. Then you will follow the directions to the prisoner’s cell. You will see life sized statue around the room. Afterwards, you will enter the Caqchot or the Dungeon. Prisoners are locked with their feet positioned higher than their head to create stress, not only that, they are torture in an inhumane ways such as Cold Water torture in the winter, fatal diseases, and extreme hunger from the French. Walking out, you will see the jailyard or garden. There are displays of monuments and relics that are too large to fit inside. Walking out to the second floor, you will see the list of Vietnamese fighters, politicians, and civilians that have died or extremely tortured here in Hanoi Hilton ( another term for the place ). If you read this review, I didn’t wrote all I could but I wanted you to be surprised because there are about 60% of this prison for you to discover! Bye and have a nice trip.( If you read to this part of the review, you are so good at reading)

reviews.author: Gary J
reviews.title: Reflective Visit
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit. You need to be in a reflective mood to view some of the sadness that is a part of history. Initially, a prison constructed by the French colonial power to suppress any hint of independence. Later used by the North Vietnamese to imprison captured US Airforce personnel during the Vietnam War. A clear message that suppression and war has no real winners.

reviews.author: Dr. Issa Abu-Dayyeh
reviews.title: Cultural visit
reviews.content: This is a French prison initially used to confine Vietnamese political prisoners, and later used by Vietnamese communist party to imprison American pilots captured during the war.A big part of it was demolished to develop the area, and a small part was left as a museum. You can visit detention areas, solitary prisons, and and read and see relics related to the history of this prison which wa once called Hilton- Hanoi and represented hell on earth for many.Audio guide available inside for an extra charge.Well worth a visit!

reviews.author: Amy S
reviews.title: Interesting and educational
reviews.content: A great way to break up the day and learn a bit about how the American war here in Vietnam is seen by many of the Vietnamese and the rest of the world today. Moving exhibition at the end of that explained the 10 years and aftermath – worth an hour of your day and while seemingly spun on the view of the Vietnamese and how they want the perception of the prisoner of wars to be seen, there is truth to how the world viewed the war and its tastefully told.

reviews.author: Liz S
reviews.title: A good history lesson
reviews.content: If you are a history buff then this might be your thing... it wasn't ours. We went with teenagers and they were ready to leave in about 10 minutes... we were ready in 30. A good reality check, terrible to see how people are treated, but could live without the experience.

reviews.author: Courtney
reviews.title: Interesting but not a must see
reviews.content: If you have interest in the American Vietnam war this has a lot of interesting history. In some ways even more interesting than the Vietnam war was the French occupation and some of those stories. Frankly it’s interesting enough but not a highlight or a must see.

reviews.author: fairreadx
reviews.title: CREATIVE MEMORIES
reviews.content: Interesting take on some parts of history but goid none the less, more interesting to see visitors of a certain age from certain countries fighting with their memories. Must of been so difficult. Place worth a visit.

reviews.author: JPollock311
reviews.title: Good exhibits / little pricy
