reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Prior to my trip, I watched the Ed Burns documentary on the American/Vietnam war, and this prison has the prominent role as the Hanoi Hilton, where the captured airmen were kept.  The museum primarily focuses on the Vietnamese who were detained in the prison by the French/Chinese, but there is a section focusing on the "Special Guests" being the US airmen.  Get the audio guide to walk you through, it's worth it!

reviews.author: Suered
reviews.title: An interesting museum highlighting the treatment of political activists
reviews.content: Most of the prison is gone as a high rise has been built there but the gatehouse and death cells remain. The museum is interesting and informative about how political prisoners were treated in terrible conditions. There is  a little information about the captured american pilots  .There are models pictures and relics including the guillotine used to behead the prisoners. There is a memorial area highlighting the war at the end.  You need about an about to 90 minutes.

reviews.author: Aussie Travelers
reviews.title: Prison Hanoi
reviews.content: What they were able to project was the Hanoi Hotel atrocities by not only the displays but by pictures and video tapes. It was difficult to see some of the information especially involving children but what the overriding factor is that these prisoners never gave up and stayed united. I did learn a great deal today. You can book a tour or hire headphones, or like us just go on your own as there is English signs giving details too

reviews.author: KGB777
reviews.title: An interesting small museum
reviews.content: This small prison museum was located right next to our hotel, and so it was an obvious choice to visit. The kids were a little scared by some of the exhibits, and especially the darker cells and the guillotine, but for adults this is a fascinating place. The display on the captured U.S. pilots was also quite informative (although it's hard to know what is truth and what is propaganda).

reviews.author: Latif T
reviews.title: Heart touching
reviews.content: Really a must do one of our best experiences here. Really interesting about history and info about the past. Not expansive at all. Peace n Love to Vietnam

reviews.author: D.j. B
reviews.title: The experience is worth the price of the ticket
reviews.content: Tickets were cheap to get in, from what remember roughly around 30,000 Dong (around a dollar 50 American). Do not fall for paying to rent the earphone system, you dont need it as long as you speak English. Most, if not all, of the signs in the old prison have English included on them explaining what went on in the different locations of the prison. We had our 2 year old son with us and had no issues pushing him around in a travel stroller. Might have to lift it up a few times here and there but nothing a strong buck cant handle. The reason I gave it a lower scoring is because I found out that about 70% (if not more) of the prison was not the original. So basically you are on the same grounds of all that torture but the majority of the building itself was not the original and felt a little disappointed. Call me petty I suppose but all in all it was a great experience for the low cost.

reviews.author: Phil B
reviews.title: Great history lesson
reviews.content: You want to understand Vietnamese people and why they have such a deep culture. Visit this place. A great place to learn and understand the history of these great people.

reviews.author: Yel R
reviews.title: Worth to visit
reviews.content: We visited this on our last day since it's just few blocks away from where we stay (Malo Botique Hotel). I recommend this place even though it's kind of sad and depressing how Vietnamese suffered during that time. It would still good to know their story. Entrance fee is only 30k dong.

reviews.author: Pitter Do
reviews.title: I'm a little disappointed with the audio guide
reviews.content: I am the anti-French overseas Vietnamese, when I visited Lo I was almost crying when I recalled the days of suffering the aggression. I really don't want to use the Orpheo audio guide when knowing where it came from. You should use a device that does not remind others of the past

reviews.author: leeoliver2018
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton - horrific
reviews.content: The colonial prison was terrible - not sure whether it was that much better when it served as the Hanoi Hilton - the information obviously has a slant to it. Well worth the visit

reviews.author: WanderAlex
reviews.title: Comprehensive and informative
reviews.content: Very informative tour of the Hanoi Hilton prison . We opted for the walking audio guide at 50k Dong . Which was very informative with extra stories recounted from inmates . But in hindsight we could have done the tour and been just as informed without the audio guide. Otherwise very eye opening and informative tour and a must see on any visit to Hanoi

reviews.author: Marie B
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: We walked here few min away from the lake. It was extremely interesting and gave a good overview to just how awful it was to spend any amount of time here.

reviews.author: Tracy A
reviews.title: History
reviews.content: We visited this prison whilst in Hanoi as it has a lot of history and we wanted to know more. It is not all there now but going in and seeing where the prisoners were shackled in the different cells was informative. Two of us had audio guides but to be honest you didn't really need them , all the information was there and the only thing that seemed different was someone reading first hand accounts.

reviews.author: WyFly
reviews.title: Prison Interest
reviews.content: This was very interesting and fitted in well with the other attractions that we visited.  Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Hilla B
reviews.title: Thru Their Eyes
reviews.content: It was interesting and worth the time.  The prison was built by and used by the French to confine, torture and kill Vietnamese during the French colonialism of Southeast Asia.  During the Viet Nam or American war North Viet Nam used it as a prison for shot down American pilots who named it the Hanoi Hilton.  Information presented is the view of Socialist Republic of Viet Nam.

reviews.author: hairypott3r
reviews.title: Dark, grim and heavy hearted
reviews.content: They succeed in giving visitors a tiny glimpse of how bleak life can be, confined to death in a prison. Walls of the exhibition was dimly lit, with an air of grim and sadness. I had a moment of nausea walking through the compound especially where the death row prisoners are locked. It’s a good place to visit for history buffs and those keen to experience Hanoi’s lesser known side.

reviews.author: Alejandra LAG
reviews.title: Interesting with a clear bias
reviews.content: It’s interesting to hear the story of this prison, but beware of the obvious anti French and anti American bias. However, it does allow its visitors to image the horrible conditions of imprisonment for locals and foreigners during war time.

reviews.author: julian nabozny
reviews.title: very historic
reviews.content: Even though the truth about how US pilots were tortured, in the past, at this prison is not shown, we can imagine that experience as we walk through the prison. We must also appreciate  the fact that the Vietnamese government has dedicated many photographs and posters praising the new constructive relationship with the US. They highlight the diplomatic work that has been done by the past six US Presidents in Vietnam to build a stronger bridge of understanding and further business interests between our two nations.

reviews.author: Andrew T
reviews.title: Historical Prison worth a visit
reviews.content: Suggest to have a guide with you or a listening device before you going in.There are a lot of historical stories worth to listen to. It is at the city center, if you ever drive pass by and have at least 30 min to 1 hour, might worth the time to visit.

reviews.author: walkasone
reviews.title: Interesting and is mostly air cond
reviews.content: Quite well preserved section and main entrance of the original French prison. The majority is air conditioned or is cool so good for the middle of the day. I can’t comment on the audio tour, but my guide told some very interesting stories about the prison. For example why the isolation cell floors are on a incline...

reviews.author: AWCostless
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Quite eerie and even frightening at times, as prisons go. Interesting exhibition about the Vietnam war.

reviews.author: Euan
reviews.title: Must visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: Informative and insightful exhibit for the main wartime prison of Hanoi. If you are interested in the history/wars of Vietnam, you have to come here.

reviews.author: Kalyani G
reviews.title: Provides good overview
reviews.content: A good place to explore the sad lives of the prisoners that had to experience hardships. They have a nice display of prisoners full of sad and distressed expressions. A sad piece of history

reviews.author: elei73
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: It was an interesting place. The history, the stories. Very sad to read about the experiences prisoners had, but at the end there was a really lovely and positive display called the 'Diary of Peace'.

reviews.author: JimOtto
reviews.title: Great tour of "Hanoi Hilton"
reviews.content: Enjoyed visiting this prison.  The history of the place was very interesting, and eye-opening.  The displays were realistic.  I was not aware of the full history of the prison.  Only aware of the use of it during the Vietnam War.

reviews.author: Emma C
reviews.title: Very interesting!
reviews.content: Very interesting visit! Learnt a lot about the history of the prison and the Vietnamese prisoners of war. Definitely recommend getting the audio guide, don’t know how much we would have got from it without .

reviews.author: Psynaut
reviews.title: Pretty cool place if you have ever studiesd the Vietnam war.
reviews.content: I think this is where Senator John McCain was kept.  If you go, be sure to read the propaganda plaques on the wall.  It really gives you a sense of the mindset of Hanoi during what the Vietnamese call "The American War."

reviews.author: 255100Foodgirl66
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: Great place to visit and learn a lot about Hanoi history. The option for audio tour is great and provides a lot of information cost is 100000 dong and cost to get in is about 40000 all areas are providing very readable boards.

reviews.author: Febe N
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: If you are in the old quarter of Hanoi, you should visit this! We thought it was impressive to see and read the history of this prison. Everything is also explained in English. I think we paid around 30.000 VND /pp. Really worth a visit

reviews.author: Mark M
reviews.title: Worth a couple of hours
reviews.content: The former prison complex for Hanoi gives a historical journey through it's working life and a good understanding of the conditions in which the prisoners were kept. It costs only VND30k (approx. 1£) for an adult. You can pay extra for an audio tour, but the info boards do have English descriptions.

reviews.author: YouAreWhatYouIs2
reviews.title: Impressive!
reviews.content: Our visit to Hoa Lo Prison, or 'HaNoi Hilton' as it's called, was very impressive. The museum is very well structured and tidy and the audio guide - which is a must - was the best we ever experienced in a museum.Yes, of course there are signs of political propaganda here and there, but not disturbing at all.

reviews.author: Elynn10sg
reviews.title: Interesting but depressing
reviews.content: Interesting and educational history for my kids, audio guide is very thorough. However it was depressing finding out the cruelty in the prison of Hoa Lo during the Vietnam war

reviews.author: Melanie S
reviews.title: Very interesting with good exhibition
reviews.content: We found this museum and former prison very interesting to visit. It showed history from different perspectives to us. Our 9 year old son was impressed, but it was not too much for him.

reviews.author: Brent
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Hoa Li prison was good. Nothing over the top that makes it fascinating. Walk yourself through in about 40 min as it’s not that big. 40k dong per person to enter. You can also get a audio tour with headphones for a additional 50k dong per person if you want.  We didn’t get it as every sign had English on it. It’s a pretty cheap way to kill a hour and learn a little about the prison and some history plus it air conditioned which was a bonus when it’s 34 degrees out.

reviews.author: Jimmy H
reviews.title: Busmans holiday
reviews.content: Visited while in Hanoi.Worth a look if you like history.Well marked out and easy to follow tour.Showed history from both sides.

reviews.author: FrequentExplorer
reviews.title: Definitely do the audio tour
reviews.content: The audio tour provided the ability to give a great insight to the prison. If attending I would definitely pay extra and pay for this option.

reviews.author: HappyMarga
reviews.title: Must see!
reviews.content: Though they say it's not d real one anymore, it is still a must see for a historical junkie like me. One would appreciate how Vietnam fought during those times. The displays will give u goose bumps. Also, it's just within the Hanoi downtown area, so one can easily walk.

reviews.author: Elizabeth C
reviews.title: Informative albeit biased
reviews.content: We went here on a raing day and booked into the audio tour which takes just over two hours from start to finish. We found it really informative and it includes personal testimonials which makes the tour more engaging. However I did feel at times that the information was a small bit biased. Nevertheless, a worthwhile tour and excellent vakue for money.

reviews.author: Luke and Krissy S
reviews.title: Sad piece of histiry
reviews.content: Well worth the visit, make sure you get the audio commentary you will get more out of the experience.Provides a very good understanding about the long struggle for independence and the sacrifice of many individuals.

reviews.author: Stephen B
reviews.title: Interesting and Informative
reviews.content: Good place to spend a few hours in Hanoi very informative if a little one sided of the Vietnamese struggle over the last 150 years or so . Some great artifacts on display and roughly takes 2 - 2.30 hrs to visit

reviews.author: MW72
reviews.title: 1 Hour
reviews.content: We popped in to waste some time one afternoon. Took about an hour to get around the whole site. 100,000 dong entry then extra if you wanted to hire audio guide - we didnt. Plenty enough written commentary around the site. Was good to get an idea of conditions prisoners lived in and their resilience.

reviews.author: Aino H
reviews.title: Must see!
reviews.content: We heard lot of the Vietnam war when at school and want to learnt more about it when coming to Vietnam. It's worth the visit and really what I expected. Did enjoy time there.

reviews.author: Patrick
reviews.title: An old soldiers perspective
reviews.content: Let me preface this by saying that I have read many accounts from previous guests of the "Hanoi Hilton", so I arrived already thinking one way. Even though a lot of the prison has been destroyed you can get the feel of the horrors that were inflicted on the prisoners here. I spent over an hour wandering through the prison and found some really interesting things. The tour allows you to see the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese prospective. Overall it was a really good experience and I highly recommend taking your time and actually learning about what happened here.

reviews.author: AlanM
reviews.title: Really interesting
reviews.content: A chance to look at the war from the Vietnamese side - interesting to see how it is portrayed. especially the info on John Maclean

reviews.author: RRVNV
reviews.title: Viet Nam’s view
reviews.content: Interesting to see the history of a prison built by the French in 1886 and to experience Viet Nam’s version especially during the last war.  Regardless, experiencing this history is worthwhile.

reviews.author: LinLing03
reviews.title: Do the Audio Tour Guide
reviews.content: You’ll need more than 1 hour if you do the audio tour, which is highly recommend. Lots of information and amazing to see the perseverance of many people through the decades. Worth a visit.

reviews.author: jimmy
reviews.content: Explication en Français très bien.giải thích bằng tiếng Pháp. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️explanation in English and French and cheap.

reviews.author: NaomiGoldcoast
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: Definitely worth a look, doesn’t take long to go through... had a bit of trouble finding each point on the Audible tour as many numbers not in sight.

reviews.author: Kiwi_Bliss
reviews.title: A must in Hanoi
reviews.content: As somber as it was the prison was well worth visiting. Small fee to get in and another for an audio tour but this was excellent. It took a few hours, but to be there right in the moment learning about the atrocities that had taken place right where you stand gave me a real understanding of Part of Vietnamese history and the people. I have the utmost respect for the Vietnamese! Very moving and informative, but do allow a couple of hours.

reviews.author: Nelida Stone
reviews.title: Enlightened
reviews.content: Must see in Hanoi, Cannot change history only learn from itVietnamese Culture is ResilientI recommend paying for audio

reviews.author: bactowers
reviews.title: A must see!
reviews.content: We paid a short visit here & didn’t bother with the headphones as we were short of time. You have to see this, an important part of history, and to remind us how we cannot treat people, prisoners or not. Well looked after & not too big so easy to fit into a busy tour. Staff helpful but not intrusive. Make time for this if you’re near Hanoi.

reviews.author: souLondon_england
reviews.title: Such an insight at war imprisonment
reviews.content: A local place to visit while in Hanoi.This well presented and emotional place describes life as a prisoner from the Vietnam wars. The remaining front entrance block is packed with interesting facts and reconstructed enclosures. Audio guides are available but we didn’t feel the need for one.

reviews.author: michaelkS1933CR
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Very interesting visit. As Americans, we know it is as the Hanoi Hilton, but have now learned the longer painful history of the prison when the French help Vietnamese political prisoners here. Hard to go through and see the "other side" of the story when our soldiers were held here, but in the end, a great reminder that no one wins in war. Many thanks to the people of Vietnam for keeping this available to see and for their friendliness.

reviews.author: Stephanie Kate
reviews.title: So interesting
reviews.content: Great value for money, spend an hour or so walking round with a guidebook or audio guide and learn all about the prison and what it was used for. Nicknamed the Hanoi Hilton by the American Prisoners of War, it’s definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area or have some time to kill.

reviews.author: travelengnancy
reviews.title: A must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: Great exhibit on the Vietnam war.  I was so moved and emotional when I read the letters from American POWs and saw life size exhibits of soldiers shackled to pipes.  It's a haunting story and I read most of the museum panels, which I normally don't.  It can be a short visit, I spent an hour, and you get a lot out of it.

reviews.author: klitgaardj
reviews.title: Daunting insight to the life in Hoa Lo
reviews.content: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison gives a daunting insight to what it must have been like to be a prisoner here.The visit allows you to see the prisoner quarters, death row and isolation cells along with proving details on the history of the prison and the inmates.Some of it is a bit constructed with prisoner mannequins in the quarters and cells but in a way it gives an idea of the size and space they had.

reviews.author: sammy1239
reviews.title: wow
reviews.content: if you have any interest for the Viet Nam war this is the place for you a lot of visual of the way they torture people in back of the days , not really recommend for bringing your kids here .

reviews.author: Stephanie H
reviews.title: Eye Opener to Prison Days of Yesteryears
reviews.content: A very well layout facility to depict prison days of yesteryears. You will need 1 hour to cover everything. There is a guillotine on display with pictures of gory heads being chopped off. Cells are interesting to view but the feeling of despair and hopelessness fills the atmosphere.

reviews.author: David M
reviews.title: Visit
reviews.content: To do in Hanoi. Pricw to visit: 30.000 dongs. Audio guide not included but for 50.000 dong (with 50.000 as bail).

reviews.author: Angie
reviews.title: Pretty informative and self-sufficient
reviews.content: For people who don't want to hire a guide or pay for the audio guides services, this museum is pretty self-sufficient in the information provided to people who visit. At the ticketing, the staff will sell you the entrance ticket and also up sell you a small little booklet about the history of the museum for 20,000 dong. If you are more into reading, this little booklet provides details comprehensive enough about the prison itself.I think I spent a total of 2.5 hours in the museum itself. Totally worth it!

reviews.author: Zuzka123
reviews.title: Reminder of shocking behaviour of French colonists
reviews.content: The prison museum reminds us of the incredibly cruel conditions the political prisoners were subjected to. Clearly milked for propaganda purposes but quite shocking all the same. Worth visiting to remind yourself how horrible humans can be. Exhibition on the American airmen held there during the Vietnam war is unintentionally hilarious. Apparently, it was all like a big fun summer camp. Hmmm.

reviews.author: Andydjp
reviews.title: Interesting museum
reviews.content: We stopped here as part of a motor bike tour we were doing. The prison is now a museum and has many interesting and informative displays. It details the capture and imprisonment of John McCain and other US war prisoners during the Vietnam war as well as historical details of prisoners throughout its history. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Stan1000000
reviews.title: Interesting museum
reviews.content: Creepy and interesting in equal measures, the museum manages to get over some of the horrors that occurred there. It's a shame that only a fraction of the original prison remains, most of it disappeared in the 90s to be replaced by a hotel and office complex.

reviews.author: Vanessa H
reviews.title: An amazing place to visit
reviews.content: This was an amazing place to visit. We wandered through and did the audio tour, which was great, and very informative. It was very emotional and and interesting to see how the prisoners were treated and to hear their stories.

reviews.author: Eden C
reviews.title: Interesting.
reviews.content: This was a very interesting trip to do with the family. It was nice a clean inside (as much as an old prison could be😂). Their were audio guides available which we did not use because of a review on here saying they dragged on. I am glad I didn’t because some places I wanted to stay longer and some just walk through. You can easily do it without the audio guide as there are posters and videos and information everywhere. The one thing I would be aware of when coming here is it could definitely be distressing to younger children or anyone for that matter. There is one room with a guillotine and pictures of severed heads in baskets. Also models of men in the prison cuffed up and locked up. It is all very interesting but just be wary of this issue.

reviews.author: Deez773906
reviews.title: I thought this place was cool
reviews.content: As an American, I thought this place was cool, but my fiance was bored out of her mind. John McCain was shot down and captured and held prisoner at this place known as the "Hanoi Hilton".  The place was rich with history and if you do the audio guide you will learn some stuff, but it is eye opening to see how these prisoners lived.  I think it's worth checking out but since my fiance was bored out of her mind I'll give it 4 stars. If you want to see where John McCain was held prisoner then check it out or if you want to just learn the history of the place then it's not a bad idea to stop in. There is an entrance fee but just look it up online, the price wasn't bad.

reviews.author: Raymond D
reviews.title: Must do in Hanoi
reviews.content: The prison has done well for tourists .It portrays the history of despair and violent abuse and is full of information.I would say a must in Hanoi .

reviews.author: Tim L
reviews.title: Wow - fantastic place to visit
reviews.content: If you are after some history of prisons in Vietnam this is the place to go. The audio tour was very good up until the end where it dragged on a little. Overall a great experience and brings us back to how lucky we really are.

reviews.author: Troy M
reviews.title: Invest in the audio tour!!
reviews.content: A great and informative look at the rebellious past of Vietnamese people. The artifacts are mind blowing. One of the greater sites in Hanoi that one should not miss out. Can be reached by foot if your lodging is in the old quarter. Invest in the audio tour for a more immersive experience.

reviews.author: Ric Travels
reviews.title: Sad history of colonial past
reviews.content: The prison gives you an idea of the horrible conditions prisoners experienced. Harsh and unforgiving. There is little to no translation of information.  It is very interesting though because this was probably the incubation ground for the revolution.Records show the names of all the prisoners Which I thought was very interesting.This included the names and photographs of men and women who were incarcerated over time. At the end of the exhibition is an area dedicated to future peace with all countries around the world which I thought was quite touching.

reviews.author: Gordo C
reviews.title: A very narrow view, but fairly interesting.
reviews.content: The Prison was an interesting place to visit, however has a very narrow focus and really hammers home a few key pointers. These are the injustice faced by Vietnamese prisoners under the french rule, and the above average treatment received by American POWs. A little more variety in information would really benefit the place, and the English is almost non existent unless you buy a guidebook.

reviews.author: Benjamin93
reviews.title: Good insight into injustices of prisoners
reviews.content: Provided a good insight into the prisons history during French occupation and the revolution period. Touched briefly on American POWs and had a memorial too. It would of been good to have more detail into the day to day life of a prisoner. It gives you a feel on how they were treated by the guards but not so much life in pristine.Instead it is quite heavy on the injustices against the pro-revolution Vietnamese prisoners there which is understandable of course. It is a memorial as well as a museum for them. It outlines the resolve of the people and how they took secretive measures to provide political teaching in the prison. Focuses mainly on the organisation of a political party inside the prison and how they remained focused on independence and overcoming French rule.

reviews.author: Shane P
reviews.title: Moving
reviews.content: We enjoyed our visit. The exhibition is confronting at times but does not hide the truth of the realities faced by prisoners. Really informative and worth spending an hour exploring this piece of history

reviews.author: TODNewcastle
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: Well worth a trip. Recommend getting the audio commentary for a very small additional payment as it completely brought it to life. Very atmospheric with combination of artefacts, testimony and modern exhibition.All 5 of my family (kids 22,20 and 17) enjoyed it and found it educational and sobering.

reviews.author: darrenparker1980
reviews.title: Eye opening
reviews.content: A great intake in to how prison life was for the Vietnamese many years ago. A must visit for any traveller

reviews.author: Donna
reviews.title: The kids enjoyed it
reviews.content: My young kids really enjoyed the prison. It’s well worth paying for the Audio tour guide, headphones, especially for the kids as they walk around. It’s a great learning experience for the kids. Wasn’t too expensive to enter and we all enjoyed our visit. It’s not as big as I thought it would be,so it doesn’t take too long to get through and see it all.

reviews.author: grimsbygirlusa
reviews.title: Amazing historical site
reviews.content: This was an amazing tour get the audio version.Allow 2 to 3 hours to do this properly. I had no idea how fantastic this would be . Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Ashton D
reviews.title: Informative audio tour
reviews.content: I took the audio tour of the prison and easily killed a lot of time doing that one morning. What’s left of the prison to tour is smaller than I expected but they did a good job maximizing space.

reviews.author: Lauren N
reviews.title: Worthwhile Visit
reviews.content: One can’t come to Hanoi and not visit Hoa Lo Prison. It’s an example of how wonderful and how terrible humans can be. I learned a lot about the spirit of the Vietnamese people, getting stories of perseverance and hope from prisoners that first inhabited the prison despite their conditions. It was also nice to give some context to what you learn in US History when you hear about Hanoi Hilton.

reviews.author: Diogo R
reviews.title: A lot of info. Take the audio guide.
reviews.content: Great tour but you need the audio guide. It’s a fantastic tour if audio guided. We liked learning about the harsh conditions prisoners lived.

reviews.author: maryntessa
reviews.title: Shocking!
reviews.content: Hỏa Lò Prison was a prison used by the French colonists in French Indochina for political prisoners, and later by North Vietnam for U.S. prisoners of war during the Vietnam War. So interesting to see "Hanoi Hilton" after hearing about it for so many years.

reviews.author: Barry C
reviews.title: Propaganda but worth a visit
reviews.content: This is the famous prison often called the Hanoi Hilton. It is small and located off a side street.  An interesting visit but the propaganda about how well American POWs were treated is over the top.  A visit here will also help you understand that the methods of POW mistreatment were learned from the French.  The French built and ran this horrible place when they occupied Vietnam.  Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Karen B
reviews.title: Very interesting and memorable
reviews.content: We had 2 days to tour Hanoi and spent one of them walking through the old quarter and visiting the prison. It's well laid out, good signage and videos. Very informative. We chose not to use the headsets just because of the children's ages. Nothing too traumatic for the children to see (aged 9&11) but enough for them to start to appreciate the horrors endured and the resilience of the prisoners. Very good displays. Definitely recommend including this on your itinerary when visiting Hanoi.

reviews.author: MaelleB
reviews.title: A Great Piece of History
reviews.content: This is a must visit when in Hanoi. It is a well preserved prison with audio guide option for those who want to. We did not take the audio guide and still got through the tour very well. There’s an actual guillotine and photos and a good explanation of the history. Highly recommend this.

reviews.author: J3nnE
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: The entrance fee for the prison is very cheap. The audio guide is available for 50k dong + 100k dong deposit which you get back once you return the device. There are additional stories and more information with the audio guide but a lot of information is around the prison. There are few areas remaining in the prison due to them being pulled down and a tower built in it's place. A lot of history inside and good place to visit.

reviews.author: brockd001
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: Most of the original prison has been torn down, like 90 percent. Has a couple jail cells to look at with some wax like prisoners on display for effect. Has some newspaper articles on display but all in all it was very boring and staged.

reviews.author: Helen G
reviews.title: Enlightening
reviews.content: Well worth a few hours of your time in Hanoi.Exhibits that show clearly what the prison was like at various periods in it's history.

reviews.author: Frank A
reviews.title: Eye Opener
reviews.content: This place gives an amazing insight into the brutality inflicted on Vietnamese citizens , held in this place as political prisoners by their colonisers .This tour is a must so people learn from our history .The government should be congratulated on the way they have presented the exhibition and respective story telling .

reviews.author: Rebecca
reviews.title: Back in time
reviews.content: Well presented historical viewpoint on Vietnam and the French and American occupations. Chilling reminder of days gone by

reviews.author: bkdas82
reviews.title: A must visit place in Hanoi for history lovers
reviews.content: It was actually a prison when Vietnam was under rule of France. Now it has been converted into a museum. Many statues are displaced there to show the brutal punishment given to Vietnamese activists. Hats off to the hero’s of Vietnam

reviews.author: Grey Nomads from Oz
reviews.title: History
reviews.content: An insight into the history of French settlement and rule in Vietnam along with some history of the Vietnam War .

reviews.author: fozjon
reviews.title: Not about the American POWs
reviews.content: OK, yes, I wanted to see the Hanoi Hilton. My thinking was more in the lines of John McCain and the American POWs. But the displays here are much more about Vietnamese freedom fighters and French colonial autrocities. All the same, it was worth the visit

reviews.author: Steve W
reviews.title: So much more than the 'Hanoi Hilton'.
reviews.content: Although it became synonymous with PoW USAAF pilots as the 'Hanoi Hilton' during the Vietnam War it has a much longer and sinister history.Well worth a couple of hours walking through the whole museum and learning the events that took place here.

reviews.author: DoctorDrej
reviews.title: Interesting History
reviews.content: Would recommend the audio guide to give you personal accounts of prisoners. Only the front section is left. Built during colonial rule by the French, the prison underwent many different owners who all used it to emprison political prisoners. Some amazing Shawshank style prison escapes occured and they have the route which they used on display. POWs from the Vietnam war were also hosted in what was called the Hanoi Hilton.

reviews.author: Govindan N
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Hanoi Hilton -MaisonCentalle or Hoa La Prison Museum is where the American POW"s were kept during the war. The centre has exhibits relating to prisons use and some relating to American prisoners of war.

reviews.author: Maxine G
reviews.title: prison
reviews.content: We visited this place in 2015 and found it to be very interesting as well as moving, especially to see how prisoners was kept whilst their duration of their sentence, would recommend this place.

reviews.author: LondonDynamic
reviews.title: The Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: A very interesting couple of hours. Invest in a head set rather than a tour and go at your own pace.

reviews.author: steadfast90
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Worth a visit. Different experience but worthwhile.Quite thought provoking. You can get an audio tour we were very lucky to have a local guides expertise at hand.

reviews.author: TrailBlazer782712
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: It is interesting enough even without an audio guide, though recommended. With all the items and scenes shown, the history of human torturing each other is vivid enough. PS: 这个地方和渣滓洞差不多。不过这边展示物品的尺度要比国内大...阴森森的氛围营造得很成功。

reviews.author: Ed Longley
reviews.title: Get the audio guide
reviews.content: Without the audio guide, a lot of detail would be lost, so pay the extra for audio.There is good signage in Vietnamese, English, and French. There are toilets, drinks, a gift shop, and most of the rooms have air-con or fans - making it much nicer to visit.Probably worth allowing 90 minutes for a decent visit.Only one section, right at the end, and oddly easy to miss, references the American War. The exhibit is largely about the time prior to the 1960’s.

reviews.author: Sydney243
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: It is frightening to see what human beings can do to each other. Pretty scary but it should be remembered.

reviews.author: BristolMelly73
reviews.title: Thought provoking
reviews.content: Fascinating and thought provoking visit, excellent look at the history of the prison and life in it over the years.

reviews.author: rowdyfox
reviews.title: worth a look
reviews.content: Thought provoking experience. I didn’t do the audio tour but there was planet to see and read. Unfortunately some of the written exhibits have not been translated from Vietnamese but I expect the detail of these is in the audio tour. I visited when it was raining heavily and most of it is indoors so it was a good choice. It’s relatively small mall so I can’t imagine how it would be when busy and hot! Perhaps go first or last thing. Tickets are cheap; £3GBP so don’t disregard. Its interesting.

reviews.author: Michael D
reviews.country: La Manga del Mar Menor, Spain
reviews.title: Thought Provoking
reviews.content: This is a place that is worth seeing. If only to prove that there are some very terrible people in this world. The inhuman treatment inflicted on the prisoners was mind boggling. The average life expectancy in this place was very short due to sickness and lack of food. Built by the French, and I can only hope that the whole nation is ashamed of what it put other humans through.

reviews.author: Victor H
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: It's not a nice place but you should have a look. It is impressive what people are able to do to other people.

reviews.author: walter
reviews.title: Good to see
reviews.content: Good to see what the French did to the Vietnamese, and thereafter the Americans. Good historical ace to visit, also with teenage children. 45 minutes is all you need.

reviews.author: Gokhan B
reviews.title: Amazing. Breath Taking
reviews.content: One must not skip this place to understand Vietnam. We did it by ourselves and it is enough. Bu the way leave around 90-120minutes for here

reviews.author: Jonathan D
reviews.title: Great museum
reviews.content: Great museum to lean more about the conditions during war in Vietnam. As a French it is also more interesting because it is part of our history too.

reviews.author: Glen M
reviews.title: Feel the history.
reviews.content: The prison is now very small and can be easily missed. Entry fee is very reasonable.This for me was the place i most wanted to visit, but it was not as haunting as i had expected. Museum is pretty much split in two, with the majority devoted to the Vietnamese political prisoners suffering during French occupation and a smaller section for the US aircrews.  We did not purchase the headphones as we arrived close to closing time and hurried our tour. The terrible conditions are detailed in English with lots of information boards describing conditions suffered by the local prisoners.The US aircrews treatment as described seems a little unbelievable but then again we head their side first.Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Travelsteph2018
reviews.title: Interesting and harrowing
reviews.content: The prison is tucked behind a big government building and so we walked past it a few times. The entrance fee was very cheap (under £1.50 per person) and we decided not to get the audio tour as most of the plaques were in Vietnamese, English and French. The main exhibition focuses on the political prisoners during the period of French colonization and was both interesting and harrowing. There is a graphic photo of the heads of executed prisoners in baskets in the guillotine room (if you have young children). The prison also served as a holding for the American POWs during the Vietnam war and there are a few rooms dedicated to this. I'm not convinced that they were treated quite as well as advertised, but overall we really enjoyed our visit. Good way to spend 90 mins.

reviews.author: Felicity K
reviews.title: Fascinating insights
reviews.content: My advice- pay for the headset as it provides an excellent narrative for the Hoa Lo Prison. Also, invest in a hand fan as you will need it in the heat. This is a fascinating timeline of Hanoi and Vietnams history- many excellent artifacts, photos and stories from a recent past. Some very sad stories but also incredibly interesting.

reviews.author: Gavin M G
reviews.title: Worth the time
reviews.content: It is hard to be in Vietnam and not visit these places. The museum stands as a brutal reminder of how political prisoners were treated.

reviews.author: Romulus
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: The Hoa Lo prison is a  marking monument in the Viet Nam history.  It offers a view from the Vietnamese perspective of the French and subsequently to the American war.Also known as Maison Central (French) or the Ha Noi Hilton (for US prisoners of war), it is a moving rexperience.Even though only a small portion still exists, it is a place to visit (close to the Old District).

reviews.author: Alan J
reviews.title: Fascinating glimpses, on the actual site, into Hoa Lo Prison's infamous past
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison "hosted" many brave Vietnamese political prisoners during the French period, sometimes with their entire families. A few escaped through sewers, as documented by the exhibits, which also show its use during the American war. As with other museums in Hanoi and in Ho Chi Minh City, you get a visceral sense of the inanity of colonialism and war.

reviews.author: Luke E
reviews.title: Very intense experience
reviews.content: Enjoyed learning about the difficulties and troubles faced by the Vietnamese people and American pilots. It was nice to learn from their perspective. The audio tour was good but at times you had to stand in front of a bucket for quite sometime until the recording finished. Got a bit long towards the end.Worth visiting.

reviews.author: Australia
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: We went and found the prison tour very interesting. We learnt alot about the history of Hanoi and the French. Worth doing.

reviews.author: Varun
reviews.title: Great educational place for everyone
reviews.content: We went with 2 young kids to this place and were glad. It's a great educational place for kids to learn about Vietnam's history through the decades, the colonial period, struggle for independence, communism and the cold war era. The whole museum is nicely built around the old prison with every section being interesting and different.

reviews.author: Mike G
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Visited as part of things to do in Hanoi.  Great little souvenir shop inside.  Gives you a good feeling for how it was for prisoners during the war.

reviews.author: _vco_mcivor
reviews.title: Important part of Viet Nam history
reviews.content: Well worth visit - probably the most interesting museum we visited in Ha Noi.  The prison has a long history and through it can be discovered the history if much of Viet Nam.  That this is from the Vietnamese perspective makes it more valuable.

reviews.author: Maps362921
reviews.title: A Sobering Experience
reviews.content: It was sobering to hear the stories of the imprisonment of Vietnamese from years gone by and to also listen to the stories of some of the American Pilots that were shot down during the war.

reviews.author: Sarinah O
reviews.title: Very informative visit
reviews.content: I visited this with my ‘History Teacher hat’ on and I found the whole experience fascinating. It is on the surface a very good display of artefacts and information, but at the same time it is often harrowing to be a spectator in a place that was the site of so much suffering and trauma. You get, also, a sense of how the people endured, and in the end, manage to triumph. A testament to sheer willpower, pride and optimism. Definitely thought provoking.

reviews.author: JohnnydiScozia
reviews.title: Certainly worth a visit
reviews.content: With 10,000+ reviews ahead of this there's not much I can add without simply re-phrasing the key elements.I would, however, wish to reiterate that a visit is instructive and informative, especially when you use the hand-held recorded guide.  It really helps you to relate much more closely to the city and the people by knowing more of their turbulent, at times terrible, past.For this reason I'd strongly recommend a visit.

reviews.author: Jacki H
reviews.title: Important historical record worth visiting whilst in Hanoi
reviews.content: We visited as part of a day tour including other sights. The prison had a well curated exhibition explaining the historical development of its inmates including Vietnamese political prisoners by the French colonialists, and later, US pilots held as prison arts of war during the Vietnam conflict. I came to Vietnam knowing little about it’s history and conflicts, other than what has been portrayed by the Western World, so welcomed learning from the Vietnamese perspective . There are interesting exhibits of artefacts, lots of photographs and images laid out in various areas, and you get to see inside the cells and holding areas. Some mind blowing information about the the prisoner were treated awaits you. I think this is an important historical venue and should be visited by tourists. We can all learn from these places that have held so much suffering and conflict, to make the world a better place.

reviews.author: Matthew P
reviews.title: Awful Truths of French Colonialism
reviews.content: Scary truths of the treatment many poor Vietnamese people experienced at the hands of French Colonial power but probably not much different to the suffering of many thousands under British Colonial rule of the same period. Very interesting exhibitions and displays which also covers the period when the north was under attack from the South of the country.

reviews.author: gunnagale
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: A very informative insight into some more of Vietnam's history. We used the voice guided tour and highly recommend this. Well worth the visit.

reviews.author: kathleen s
reviews.title: Also known as the Hanoi Hilton, it's definitely worth seeing
reviews.content: Sadly this prison was used against the Vietnamese people who protested against the French.  Later it was used to house John McCain and other Americans caught during the US war against North Vietnam.  It's very graphic as they have models of prisoners in the various cells etc.  Special section devoted to the women who were held there. The propaganda used in connection with McCain and his fellow inmates is very interesting too-apparently all they did was play volleyball, cook thanksgiving dinner and decorate their Christmas tree!  Different twist on a familiar story.

reviews.author: Laura Danny
reviews.title: Enjoyable!
reviews.content: Interesting! Good way to kill time if your bored. Staff are friendly and the audio guide is worth purchasing

reviews.author: redrob1742015
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: So called by US prisoners of war. Very interesting place & well worth a visit if in Hanoi. Informative with exhibits as part of the tour

reviews.author: JesusLives67
reviews.title: Insightful
reviews.content: We thoroughly immersed in the history and stories. Aside from the charms in Old Quarters, quaint shops, bargains and amazing street food. A visit to the Hoa Lo Prison is a must. Gives the visitor insightful understanding on the suffering, perseverance and personal cost of victory experienced by people of Vietnam. Well choreographed, and exhibits meaningfully arranged. Worth a visit .. indeed “the nature of the war and the struggle of the people of Vietnam” should be highlighted as in the words of Bertrand Russell.

reviews.author: Samantha E
reviews.title: Cheap and educational
reviews.content: Entry was only 30.000d, even without an audio guide we received lots of interesting information from the signage and videos around the prison. Very informative and worth an hour of your time.

reviews.author: Kerry A
reviews.title: Most interesting place we visited
reviews.content: A must when in Hanoi... also known as the Hanoi Hilton.... only about a pound to get in and very informative..... takes about an hour to look around

reviews.author: masagero
reviews.title: Interesting tour with audio guide
reviews.content: Myself and the kids enjoyed this tour which brings to life the harsh conditions of the prison - particularly in the 1940s and 50s. The audio guides were very engaging for the kids.

reviews.author: Tonia K
reviews.title: Audio tour was great
reviews.content: Very confronting. The displays are well presented and along with the audio commentary, allow you to begin to imagine the conditions for those imprisoned there. Recommended for families but it was a bit much for my 7 year old, who lost interest quickly. 13 year old was engrossed in the detail and enjoyed it.

reviews.author: Mike
reviews.title: Very educational
reviews.content: What a fantastic place. It's not an easy thing to see and it's a very Vietnamese based story but you really get a sense of how the country has recovered from a brutal justice system. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Steven H
reviews.title: An Insight Into Vietnamese History
reviews.content: The prison teaches about the history of Vietnam that many don't hear about. It shows the harsh conditions prisoners were kept in and the stories of some individuals. It also shows how it was used during the Vietnam war to hold POW's. It was an insight into the reality of life for the Vietnamese and how tough they are. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Mario&Sandy
reviews.title: The Resiliency of the Vietnamese
reviews.content: I was really looking forward to visiting this site to gain a better perspective and learn the history of this prison. My wife and I decided on the audio tour (can’t remember the price) but well worth it. The audio tour takes about an hour and is very helpful as it explains each exhibit in detail. An amazing look at what the Vietnamese people went through for standing for what they believed in. A true testament to the resiliency of the men, women, and children that had to endure this dreadful and very torturous prison. An eye opener for sure and I feel a must visit!

reviews.author: Qwest94
reviews.title: Interesting Place
reviews.content: Just a portion of the prison has been retained, and the history of the prison is divided between the time it was used to house Vietnamese revolutionaries and then American downed pilots.  It was pretty hot, but if you are interested in the Vietnamese revolution or the Vietnam war it is definitely worth visiting.  The audio tour was particularly well done.

reviews.author: we_love_holidays_9
reviews.title: Memorable visit
reviews.content: Visited with our 13 yo son and did the audio tour. Best history lesson ever! The story of the prison was traumatic, shameful and so moving. We will never forget it and the stories! Why must humans be so dreadful to human kind? Hard to comprehend.

reviews.author: World Traveler
reviews.title: Interesting History of The Vietnamese-French Conflict
reviews.content: We planned to stay here for 30 minutes, but we stayed an hour and a half. Super interesting to see how the French treated the Vietnamese and learn more about the rise of communism. Definitely slanted to glorify communism and the revolution, but it’s unique to have this experience in Hanoi. Also great exhibit on worldwide peace at the end. Skeptical on the glorified treatment of American POWs. Records show they didn’t experience the spa treatment exhibited in Hoa Lo. But again, important to recognize perspective.

reviews.author: Felice Santiago
reviews.title: Educational experience
reviews.content: You can purchase and audio guide when you enter to make the tour more educational. I didn’t but it was overall alright. The museum has been restored 70 to 80% of it and they did a good job. So much history of suffering but its good to know about this and remember those people and events.

reviews.author: Johannes B
reviews.title: Worth a visit.
reviews.content: You learn alot about how the french oppressed the vietnamese people. Didnt use the audiotour but they have good information plaques.

reviews.author: Jon9344
reviews.title: Good attraction, worth a visit.
reviews.content: My partner is an ex prison officer so she was interested in going to see the remains of Hoa Lo prison. Pleased we did as its a really good attraction with good exhibits from the french era through to housing american POW's during the war. Some of it is quite sobering when you realise the brutal conditions prisoners were held in. Worth a visit.Costs the equivilent of about £1.50 each for entry.

reviews.author: Cookie
reviews.title: “The first casualty of war is the truth “....
reviews.content: We were aware when going that the story would be told from one perspective and this certainly was the case. Nevertheless an interesting hour on a rainy afternoon .

reviews.author: BrittanyB
reviews.title: Interesting Way to Spend an Afternoon
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison was very interesting to learn about, from its use to house Vietnamese political prisoners during the French invasion, to its use to keep POWs during the Vietnam war. Walking through the prison definitely gives you an interesting perspective as there are still steel leg locks used on prisoners and even a guillotine. The only thing I found slightly annoying is that they want you to pay essentially the price of the admissions ticket for a headset that gives a guided tour. It’s not much money but you may as well just charge 60,000 up front instead of buying a ticket and then having to go buy a headset 20 feet away.

reviews.author: Joey & Co
reviews.title: Fascinating yet brutal
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison was told through the stories of the inmates, first the Vietnamese then American POWs. The exhibits brought the pain and suffering of those inmates to life especially solitary confinement and death row cells. People were certainly tougher in those days. I felt suffocated after standing in the solitary confinement cell block - lasted 3mins (and there was a air cooler on!)

reviews.author: Karan
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Extremely beneficial to understand the tectonics of vietnamese culture history and suffering from the wars. Audio guide recommended. Although now the prison places itself admist modern architecture influenced by the western world and the Hoa Lo prison was a space where you would want to forget the torment of the westerners.

reviews.author: Sam A
reviews.title: Interesting insight into colonial Vietnam.
reviews.content: Was very interesting to see the troubles Vietnamese went through under french rule. Completely worth getting the headsets for the walk around.

reviews.author: Mags133
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Really interesting & informative visit to Hoa lo prison. Purchased the audio guide which was inexpensive, easy to use & well worth getting made it easy to go round & understand the background & use of each of the areas. Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: VoVan11
reviews.title: A true history lesson
reviews.content: Most of us born in the time of peace know little about the wars that Vietnam went through in the past. That's why a trip to Hoa Lo gives a such an impressive and informative experience on me.You will treasure more the peace you are enjoying when you know how harsh and unjust the wars were.

reviews.author: Cruunchy’s Fly
reviews.title: “History Tales”
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a must if you are in Hanoi, this is a famous prison where you will learn the true history of this place.When French ruled this place, Vietnamese people suffer like hell, they where punished and tortured by the French in the indochina’s war.Then later when Vietnamese take control with Ho Chi Minh this prison was called “Hilton Hanoi” cause when Vietnamese capture Americans, they treated them as equals and even teach them their culture, this place teach occidental side how rich can be the other side of the bed.

reviews.author: Millie D
reviews.title: VERY affordable trip...
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison was so cheap to enter which made the experience more accessible. A student discount is available which reduced the ticket price to just 15 000 Vietnamese Dong! A more modern perspective was also provided, which certainly led to more engagement. At an additional cost, an audio tour is available. We did not do this and the experience was still very interesting and easy to understand.

reviews.author: nicolecampbell92
reviews.title: Absoloutely incredible
reviews.content: Thia is the best historical museum/landmark i have ever been to. They have individual audio devices (mp3 players) in multiple languages that takes you around the prison.  A must do if visiting this city. In my top 3 experiences of all Vietnam

reviews.author: Hans H
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: Quite interesting place that makes you think and reflect back on the horrors that took place when the French occupied Vietnam.Definitely worth a visit

reviews.author: ghp3
reviews.title: Moving, but don't expect an even-handed approach
reviews.content: Not much of the prison remains as most of it was torn down several years ago, but what remains is well worth a visit.  The tour includes a couple of cell blocks, the "death row" and a memorial space.  The emphasis is on the use of the prison by the French to house "revolutionary comrades" during the early through mid-20th century.  It's use as the "Hanoi Hilton" for U.S. POW's is downplayed and very one-sided.  Don't go expecting a balanced history.

reviews.author: Mila
reviews.title: Left me speechless
reviews.content: America doesn’t talk about the Vietnam war AT ALL, never, ever. To be honest, o have never been interested in learning anything about it; so when my husbanded suggested we visit, I was a bit hesitant. But I am SO glad o listened to him and we went. It was a huge learning experience for me. The museum/prison is well designed - it really takes you through the suffering of the Vietnamese people. Vivid descriptions, personal diaries, historical narratives really make everything come alive. I think I literally cried when reading the young people’s diaries and background stories. I left with a newfound appreciation of Vietnam, the resilience and positivity of its people. Truly worth a visit.

reviews.author: Lori N
reviews.title: Worth a stop
reviews.content: If in Hanoi, must see.  Bigger than I thought it would be.  A couple of the rooms have excellent A/C-key if in Hanoi in the summer.  There is a gift shop on site.

reviews.author: Josh
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: There are two parts to this place. First part and larger portion shows the place when the French were in charge and the conditions that were there during the occupation period. The second part is during the American/Vietnam War in which the Americans called it “Hoa Lo Hilton”. The difference is amazing between the two. This is a great place to go on a hot day as there is A/C available.

reviews.author: asw71
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Entrance fee is a few dollars Australian - the signs are translated into English. We didn't do the audio tour but probably would've stayed much longer if we had (we wanted a quick visit). Audio guide is 50,000 VD. Interesting to learn about the prison's significance during different periods in Vietnam's history.

reviews.author: Sundncr
reviews.title: Monument to remember the struggle for freedom
reviews.content: Hoa lo prison was built by the Colonial French to suppress the Vietnamese freedom movement.  The prison was purposefully built in the middle of town to serve as a reminder.    Nowadays, only a small portion of the Hoa Lo prison is left, which is a museum.  The other part is a huge tower.   Serving as metaphor to the changing economy of Vietnam.   There is an entrance fee to the museum.   Hanoi has many lakes, and probably the prison is close to Hoan Kiem lake near the Hanoi old quarter.   The ticket counter also sells a guide book and an audio book to take on you tour.  You will see some of the Prison cells on display and the conditions of prisoners are sad to realize.   The prison conditions were purposefully kept dire and harsh to deter freedom moments among the Vietnamese population.   One should definitely visit this museum to learn how life can turn cruel if people do not realize their freedoms.

reviews.author: danibrown113
reviews.title: Interesting museum
reviews.content: This museum is worth a visit for any American in Hanoi. Seeing many of Vietnam conflicts through Vietnamese eyes was quite interesting and thought-provoking.

reviews.author: Michelle P
reviews.title: Historical must
reviews.content: I came here with my fiancé as I am a history geek and so is my girlfriend. We weren’t disappointed as it was very informative for us, as we didn’t and aren’t aware of Vietnam’s history, and it was great to learn and be less ignorant about the struggles and steep history that Vietnam has. I think everyone should visit this place to understand colonization and how the French impacted Vietnam for so many years. Ignorance is not bliss, knowledge is king/queen.

reviews.author: Epic-Traveller
reviews.title: Very Informative
reviews.content: Having travelled SE Asia extensively and seen many war memorials, prisons, war remnants museums etc I decided not to buy the audio tour for this one.Information dotted around the prison on boards is enough to give you a picture of what life and conditions were like for Vietnamese political prisoners during French colonial times.Whilst not the most horrific I’ve seen, it was still pretty bad. It is an eye opening experience visiting these types of attractions in SE Asia and I highly recommend tourists visit.

reviews.author: Dean S
reviews.title: Surprising good!
reviews.content: We intentionally avoided all of the Vietnam War memorials, museums, etc. on our trip to Vietnam but one day we found ourselves near the Hanoi Hilton and decided to give it a try.  This museum was far better than anticipated.  Beyond the Vietnam War the history of this museum extends back to French Colonial times.  Very interesting and informative displays and artwork.  Well worth a couple of hours of your time to learn more about colonialism in Vietnam.

reviews.author: Jeanie
reviews.title: Thought provoking
reviews.content: Visiting the "Hanoi Hilton" challenged my view of the Vietnam War by offering a different perspective of the Americans' involvement.  The trip wasblazing hot (at the end ofJune 2019), which helped to illustrate the conditions of the inmates.  The audio tour is excellent, well-laid out and very informative.  I highly reccommend this as a stop in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Sheltie2/16
reviews.title: Worth a visit during a trip to Hanoi
reviews.content: An interesting way to spend a couple of hours in Hanoi. We visited earlier in the day, around 10am, and the museum was fairly quiet and easy to navigate. Well worth getting the audio guide as the information and stories are fascinating. We visited in June and it was very hot and there is not a lot of airflow in the museum so would recommend taking a few bottles of water with you.I would definitely recommend this as a must do if you visit Hanoi.

reviews.author: Tansendoc
reviews.title: Tragic History
reviews.content: This is a very important stop for any visitor to Vietnam if you want to understand the history of colonialism and oppression of the people of Vietnam.Very good value, excellent displays and information.I was not aware of how much the Vietnamese suffered during French rule and also during the American war.

reviews.author: adventuresofkaymay
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: After the police museum we wandered across the road and visited Hoa Lo Prison. Entry was 30k dong for adults and free for kids. This was very educational to walk around and has been set up quite well with manicans to show what life was like for the prisoners at that time. The kids 8yo and 4yo handled the prison quite well as some areas are dark.

reviews.author: Mr-MrsDubbs
reviews.title: Hoa Lo (Hanoi Hilton) prison
reviews.content: A must see on a trip to Hanoi. Very informative and very well set out. First part is all about how the French mid treated the Vietnamese when it was once  French colonial. Second part is how well they treated the US forces during the VietNam war. So go with an open mind but well worth a visit. 400000 VND entry.

reviews.author: anne jovaras
reviews.title: The Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Another brutal but intriguing insight to Vietnam’s past. Included a comprehensive narrative on the history of a prison reserved for political prisoners until ‘the American war’ when the guests included pilots from fallen enemy planes. There was also a very informative commentary on Ho Chi Minh. This was one of my highlights and worth visiting in spite of the heat

reviews.author: Smashcbe
reviews.title: Good insight into history
reviews.content: Hop on hop off buses have stops just by the side of this prison. There is a kiosk at the entrance to buy tickets. Ticket rates are 30,000 VND per person and is worth it. The museum has a detailed display of the torture during French colonist rule. Mannequins in iron shackles is a sad sight. Also shows how well the Vietnamese treated the American Pilots including McCain. His parachute, jumpsuit and a piece of the aircraft that was shot down are also among displayed articles. The torture house has a few cells retained as such. Two underground sewers are also exhibited through which a few escaped to join the resistance base. Worth a visit if you want to get a sense of the countryside history.

reviews.author: Tony M
reviews.title: A quick visit
reviews.content: It seems there is very little left of the original prison, but there's enough for you to get a sense of it's history. Exhibits go through its foundation by the French and use by both the French during the revolutionary war and North Vietnamese during the 'American' war. There are some interesting exhibits and photos relating to the war with the US and the captured US pilots. Definitely worth a visit and they have a reasonably priced souvenir shop. Only 1.50 euro entrance fee and kids 15 and under are free.

reviews.author: JackieC
reviews.title: Very interesting!
reviews.content: We found this museum fascinating. Our local guide took us through and gave us a good tour. However, as an American and having studied the war, we know our American POWs were treated way worse than they would have us believe.

reviews.author: Carole M
reviews.title: A must see
reviews.content: Spent time going through the prison and found it very informative. Be sure to spend time looking at the McCain memorabilia.

reviews.author: alexa19
reviews.title: Overall an okay place
reviews.content: We went here after going to the one in Cambodia- the Museum of Genocidal Crime (S21). In our opinion you can skip this and go to Ha Long Bay, Sapa, or other sightseeing spots in Hanoi. We used the audio tour and it really wasn't what we were expecting. We ended up walking out before finishing up the prison. If you're in Hanoi and have nothing to do then sure go for an hour but I wouldn't recommended it as a must do.

reviews.author: Nora M
reviews.title: Excellent place to see how our US military POWs lived while captive during Vietnam War.
reviews.content: Very centrally located in Hanoi so very easy to get to by foot from our hotel. We used the audio set to get more info but I will say most was very interesting. However, as an American, I didn't really care to hear all the stuff about their political prisoners, but interesting none-the-less. I specifically came to see/learn/hear about the American POWs and came away very satisfied with the info displayed and shared by the museum. This is a must visit place if you crave info on the Vietnam War and our American POWs.

reviews.author: Li B
reviews.title: Fascinating 2 hour tour
reviews.content: Our family (14 and 8 year olds) did this amazing tour.  Cost is about $4.00 AD to enter and It is best that you hire audio headsets $12.50 AD which you listen too as you walk around this prison. Interesting and the 2 hours fly’s by.  Visit the different aspects of the prison and get an understanding of life was under French rule.

reviews.author: memcey
reviews.title: Interesting and sad relic
reviews.content: Informative museum. Holds the heat on hot days. Can only imagine what it was line for prisoners. Great to check out and reasonably priced. Allow an hour or so

reviews.author: SunDaze1
reviews.title: Interesting perspective
reviews.content: Very interesting to see where both Vietnamese and American prisoners were held. Definitely intrigued by the way it was presented from a Vietnamese perspective. Opened up an opportunity for our kids to understand a POWs’ life.

reviews.author: Lee C
reviews.title: Eye opening
reviews.content: If you are in Hanoi and interested In History then the Hanoi Hilton is a must see destination. The information you receive while wandering the prison are eye opening and in some instances horrific but also very informative making the experience worth while. Like most tourist places in Hanoi it is not expensive to enter and will probably only take an hour to walk round the entire place.

reviews.author: Traveler
reviews.title: Very good experience
reviews.content: Very well set up. Get the audio because it is super informative and adds to the experience. It’s long so I wish I would’ve gotten there earlier so I could’ve had more time, because it was very interesting and I really enjoyed it!

reviews.author: Adrian Lee
reviews.title: Amazing Prison - Mr. Adrian Lee
reviews.content: Fascinated and amused by Thai prison. They still preserved the architectural buildings and its texture. It was a-bit of scary and creepy to see how the prisoners was executed during the French Colonials day’s. Some past political secretary was the prisoners of this prison before. Amazing place to visit to know the historical of Vietnam and its rulers during the days of Ho Chi Minh. Great leader of Vietnam. Worth every penny to visit☺️

reviews.author: N_i_b_a_r
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: Another stop of our city tour. We actually liked coming here. Interesting place to visit and offered so much information during what happened in 1886 when the French built this prison. Real artifacts are used like the sewer where the prisoner escaped from. The machine they used for the death penalties. Should go!

reviews.author: heeminjeong
reviews.title: Authentic history background
reviews.content: Quick description on the board for tourists, enough to understand with the video inside, although quite hot inside

reviews.author: Francis Martino
reviews.title: Small but well done
reviews.content: The things are very interesting contrast between the treatment of Vietnamese prisoners by the French and the treatment of American prisoners by the Vietnamese. If you're a foreigner decide in advance if you want their booklet because if you say nothing they automatically charge you 20,000 dong for it when you buy your ticket.Great place to visit and understand the history of the city and country.  Only a small part of the prison remains but the space is well laid out and has plenty of signage/explanations around in English as well as Vietnamese.There is plenty of propaganda woven in to the choice of exhibits and how they are presented, but then history is written by the winners as they say.Really do the audio tour adds so much to the overall experience! Have the pay 50K dong and a 50K deposit ,are refundable.

reviews.author: Zoe903
reviews.title: Sad and quite one sided
reviews.content: Very interesting to visit, quite a lot of horrible history here. But they are at pains to point out that the French were horrible jailors while the Vietnamese treated the Americans with care - and that's simply not true. Still wort a visit!

reviews.author: Clive-Cherie W
reviews.title: If in Hanoi then spare the time to visit
reviews.content: Known as the Hanoi Hilton to some, this very old prison stands in the middle of town and has a gruesome past. The history in here was well documented and very stirring, glad we came in to check it out, tickets are reasonably priced and it will take about 2 hours out of your day. Some of the guests in here were brutally tortured including being beheaded.

reviews.author: peteandbarb9
reviews.title: Good place to visit
reviews.content: This was a last minute decision to visit, interesting place and I would recommend paying a little more and getting the audio tour it explains a bit more.

reviews.author: HuahinCharlie
reviews.title: The sewer breakout must have been interesting
reviews.content: Political prisoners and others were not treated all that well here compared to the almost luxury 21st C digs in many "enlightened" countries. I wonder why?Go and visit this site. Worth the effort.

reviews.author: Corinne Lau
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: One of the places of interest to understand about the history of Vietnam. You need to spend at least 1.5 hrs there to go through all the exhibits and you can loan a recorder set in English which will explain to you on the Exhibits.

reviews.author: NickT
reviews.title: Well worth a visit.
reviews.content: Well worth visiting this somber location and learning its history from the French to the American POW’s in the “Hanoi Hilton”.

reviews.author: DHook
reviews.title: Great musuem, expected propaganda
reviews.content: We really enjoyed our visit to Hoa Lo Prison (aka the "Hanoi Hilton").  This prison has housed both Vietnamese prisoners during the French phase, and then US prisoners during what we call the "Vietnam War" and they call the "American War".Yes, there is an element of propaganda, but the information and exhibits are outstanding.  Not to be missed.

reviews.author: Givparis
reviews.title: Beware - A tale of two stories.
reviews.content: Excellent museum. Only thing to point out is the uncomfortable amount of propaganda in favour of communism and the north during the war. First part of the exhibition (1930’s to mid 50’s) had the French soldiers damming/torturing any Vietnamese prisoner they could get their hands on. Second part of the exhibition (actual US Vietnam war - 60’s onwards) showed how well treated the US pows were? All about history however it is highly skewed. Definitely recommend a visit however as entrance fees extremely cheap!

reviews.author: Paddleboardbb
reviews.title: Do it , didn’t disappoint
reviews.content: Wow , what a fab morning . Stunning architecture and great history . Very well done and quite confronting . One of our faves . Thanks , so clean and organised .

reviews.author: leanneb310
reviews.title: Doing the tourist route
reviews.content: It is an amazing place to visit but also rather sad. The cruelty of the place is terrible. Glad we went - but not a nice place. Historical site done well, little bit of propaganda. How anyone survived living here in those conditions. Terrible. My son listened to the audio with actual stories from survivors. He was fascinated.

reviews.author: Declan H
reviews.title: Well presented
reviews.content: We decided to visit as part of our tour of the French and old quarter. We were really glad we stopped here. A well presented exhibition and museum which really allows you to appreciate the gravity of what happened. One of the exhibits we saw at the war museum in Saigon, however we actually appreciated it more and understood it clearer after seeing the prison. PRICING:Entry: 30,000 VND Guide Book: 20,000 VND

reviews.author: Camper820600
reviews.title: Very worth seeing
reviews.content: An amazing experience, great to learn about some Vietnamese history. We took our time here and we really did learn a lot between the French liberation and the American war. Extremely worth a visit

reviews.author: Travelingjohn123
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: Excellent museum and definitely worth a visit. Total propaganda,  but it must be viewed from a communist North Vietnamese viewpoint (evil French colonialism and kind Vietnamese looking after their American guests)In both cases it must have been absolute hell to have been a prisoner here and Im fairly sure the US pilots imprisoned here, for years, didn’t enjoy their stay like in the photos, playing volleyball and smoking donated cigarettes. Definitely worth a visit, but be open minded to the truth.

reviews.author: Sam Yates
reviews.title: Insightful experience
reviews.content: Very moving and insightful experience into one of Hanoi's sadder moments in history. A well looked after place with a good, clear layout. Informative signs in English. Didn't pay for the audio guide and still feel like I got a lot out of the experience.

reviews.author: WorldTravelManTerry
reviews.title: Good perspective of this former prison and what it stood for historically
reviews.content: It is stunning, surreal and mind boggling in terms of what type of history transpired in this part of the world, the pain, the suffering people had to go through to achieve independence. . Shocking , maybe even disturbing but worth  the time to see a part of our world history that we can all learn from to make us understand that peace in this world is priceless. The prisoners throughout the history of this prison suffered so that this part of the world finally achieved peace, independence and freedom, whether you were American or Vietnamese protestors of the colonial system.

reviews.author: Carly
reviews.title: Something to do if you have an extra hour or two
reviews.content: The museum was interesting and a good way to pass some time but I would not say is a must for a visit to Hanoi. If you do go, I would recommend the audioguide because the posted plaques do not provide very much reading/information. They have air conditioning and a student discount.

reviews.author: R M
reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit
reviews.content: Very interesting and haunting museum. My second visit in about 7 years, has improved since the first time (better signage, new exhibits detailing peace). There is some propaganda, but it's a fascinating place and also goes into more detail about how the prison was built now, meaning more insight into history of Ha Noi.

reviews.author: Tenaj & Tino
reviews.title: A Prison Tour You Must Visit
