If you're not interested in purchasing something (mostly apparel is offered in the many stalls in the center of two streets), you can still take part in the energy and the carnival-like atmosphere... I especially enjoyed the classical Vietnamese "opera style" performances and live music, at the center of the Market; this included folks dressed in traditional regalia, and a fire dancer as well.  Small presents, and even VNDs are distributed to the children in the audience (very nice touch!).  The pubs and bars are filled with young tourists (so if you seeking nightlife with fellow travelers, this is the place to come to during the weekends... the Hanoi Backpacker Hostel was really jumping).  If you're not into the "drinking scene", you can stop at a cafe for a meal, coffee, dessert, etc. and also just stroll with the crowds, and enjoy the activities & cheerful buzz of the Night Market :)NOTE:  If you're staying at a place that's a bit distant from the Night Market, you can have your taxi driver drop you off at one of the main entrances.

reviews.author: SSDelhi
reviews.title: Visit the market only for the sake of it...
reviews.content: Comprising of unending stalls majorly of cheap and sub-standard goods, this market was way below my expectations. Being a foreigner was definitely a set back with the shop keepers demanding exorbitant price for goods that fell below quality standards. I purchased souvenirs and other gift items at much reasonable price from the streets in Old quarter on regular working days. I was actually scared of visiting the place after my hotel and my colleagues from Vietnam warned against the frequent pick-pocketing in the night market. Kept clinging to the little cash I carried after all I had heard about it. Over-crowded and not at all children friendly.

reviews.author: DebbieBridge
reviews.title: Nice stroll, but didn't but
reviews.content: I love night markets, so if you like to just wander and take in the atmosphere, then by all means do that here.I did not find that what was on sale was well made or would be likely to fit.  I never got to the haggle stage, so can't comment on price.It's huge, but can't say there was much of interest for a tourist, but, maybe it's more for the locals?

reviews.author: Duffmondo
reviews.title: Sizes and clothing - TAKE CAUTION!!
reviews.content: If your a bit bigger than the average local be carful that the ticket telling you it's your size fool you. If it has a sticker on top of the original ticket. You get home only to find it's too small. This only happened with a single pair of shorts in my experiance. They were only $10 but it still tarnished the good vibe of the market as a whole. Got plenty of honest people to. Just peel back those stickers before you buy and see what they have to say. IF you get ripped you can alway give it to a friend (small friend) as a present.Otherwise it was great found heaps of cool gadgets, nicks and nacks, plenty of snacks and much much more!

reviews.author: John K
reviews.title: Woolworths it's not
reviews.content: We walked the length of the market and back. It is supposed to be pedestrian friendly, however the occasional scooter barrels along. There is a variety of tat for sale and food stalls at the far end. The most interesting thing was a small temple beside the market where they were having a service and being able to listen to the chanting in the courtyard beside the temple. Would I rush back, no. If you found the review helpful please let me know.

reviews.author: Raintree_Thailand
reviews.title: Something for everyone!
reviews.content: It takes a pretty hardened shopper to walk the full length of the night market and not to find something to buy.  Lots of crafts, clothes, shoes,  bags, folk art, food, drinks.... the list goes on and on!!  Have to bargain hard for discounts, but always an opportunity to find something you need or want.

reviews.author: pieata
reviews.title: Another market, but in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Open.  Fri to Sunday , after 6pm.To me, just another  night market,  CHEAP.  GOODS, but to me, is it really  cheap?In Asia, cheap to me is Normally, SMILES on purchase, TEARS after  use!!!Buyer beware!NO REFUNDS (you can try).  I walked  1/2  way up, then. Turned back(no purchases)About 30 mins, others may be more interested !

reviews.author: yensta
reviews.title: Unfortunately, full of cheap tat
reviews.content: I went to the night market and left after 10 minutes. It was full of poor quality, unattractive merchandise, and was very very crowded.Considering how much Hanoi has to offer in the way of shopping, I was really surprised to find the market so disappointing.

reviews.author: RohitMonserrate
reviews.title: Almost got pick pocketed
reviews.content: The night market was nice to browse just for the experience. Almost got pickpocketed at the end the food was nice though.

reviews.author: Oller46
reviews.title: Big but not that good
reviews.content: The market is big but there are just a few food places and the goods are not nice showed to the people. Also there are not really nice things to buy. Just 50 booths with handy covers and other stuff. There are no nice clothes or nice accessories as we know it from other markets in Asia. There are a lot of people around (also a lot of locals) which is nice. But the most of the sellers are unfriendly and do not really understand what you want ...

reviews.author: Brooke R
reviews.title: Busy atmosphere
reviews.content: I went on a Saturday night, the night markets were packed. Tried some of the street food which was good but didn't buy anything from the stalls

reviews.author: shilpa swami
reviews.title: It's big!!!
reviews.content: The night market is really big.. We did not but anything, we went there just for the experience n I must say it was good.. There are lot of food stalls all around so if u can eat non veg go ahead n discover. We did not eat much cos we are vegetarians.. U should visit the night market to get a feel of Vietnam, the people and their lifestyle. But everyone advised us to be safe with our valuables, we were lucky enough to not experience anything bad, but I guess it's good to be cautious..

reviews.author: RTT
reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.content: We actually went on a Thursday night to find plenty of stalls and shoppers around, so not sure it is actually 'weekends only'. It was nice to walk around for a while, although a lot of the stalls seemed to sell very similar items. Worth a look and I'd probably go again, I wonder if there's more on offer on the weekends although there was multiple streets worth as it was. Expect high pedestrian/scooter traffic.

reviews.author: William L
reviews.title: Best shopping in Hanoi!
reviews.content: If you are in Hanoi try & make it to the weekend night markets in the centre of the old quarter (Friday-Sunday nights). These markets offer the best items from Hanoi's shops at bargain prices. I also felt that perusing these markets was less intimidating that walking into a shop & getting bombarded by the owner. Definitely aimed at tourists but attracts large crowds of locals & has a great vibe!

reviews.author: LakeComoExpert
reviews.title: Huge, amazing, a must!
reviews.content: Only open at the weekends - Friday, Saturday and Sunday, this huge market stretches for miles you can buy clothing ( handy if you are there in the winter when hanoi is cold  - thick jackets for £7.50), food, jewellery, shoes, electronics etc.Be careful with the electronics though, we bought a selfie stick and it broke after 2 days. We didn't buy a cheap looking one either!Get there around 7pm  as  between 8-9 it gets so busy y can hardly move. Do it ina logical manner to get the best out of it, start at the top, do the right side, then go as far as you can stand and walk back up the other way.Hang onto your bags and don't have an easy access ruck-sack on your back. It's a busy place, so easy to get pick-pocketed. Just be aware, it's by no means scary. And is great fun.

reviews.author: Mdayyana
reviews.title: bargains, bargains
reviews.content: Really value for money and spoiled for choice. Good place to get all those authentic handmade pouches or bags as souvenirs.

reviews.author: FormerCaliBoy
reviews.title: Ok to see once, but not impressive
reviews.content: We headed over to the night market to see if we could find any good deals and maybe find something for dinner.  Once we got to the main street it was packed with people bumping into you and it did not make for a pleasant evening.  The vendor booths, I felt, did not really offer any great deals of interest to me.    There were a couple of areas that severed food, but we decided to just go to another area of town for dinner.  We did need to use the bathrooms at the night market and there were pay toilets (tourist price) and they were pretty dirty and disgusting.  We walked back through the market to get back to our start point and were more than happy to move on.  I had no desire to return again during our stay.

reviews.author: nObOdY007
reviews.title: It Has All What You're Looking For
reviews.content: Such A Wonderful Place To Shopping At Night. It However So Busy All Time. Everything is Cheap With Good Quality. You Can Find Many Many Stuffs During The Way. Such A Long Way To Walk And Could HardLY Find The End Or Way Back. Overall, It's Good.

reviews.author: Zee S.Puad
reviews.title: Long way
reviews.content: A very very big night market.. You can't even find the end.. Located in old quarter near Dong Xuan market.. The goods is awesome.. They sell lots of things.. Went there at 11pm and it is still open.. Nice!

reviews.author: Vestfoldgirl
reviews.title: Mostly crap
reviews.content: This place sells low quality items and badly made copies of designer clothes and bags. We didnt really find anything that we wanted to spend money on, we were debating on buying a selfiestick, but decided against it in the end :-) This is a big market covering several streets, but is not the kind of market that I enjoy visiting, I would rather go somewhere they sell some genuine handicrafts and not the sort of crap and bad quality you find here. Basically I waste of time.

reviews.author: jaci55555
reviews.title: Good deals among the pushing
reviews.content: You will be pushed and shoved. Clothes are Vietnamese sized except for t shirts. Lots of other pretty things though. Definitely worth a walk through the throng! Not much bargaining, a few vendors will try rip you off, first check prices at a few places. Got some great deals!

reviews.author: Tyson M
reviews.title: Rudest people in Vietnam
reviews.content: Having travelled Bali, Cambodia and the south of Vietnam before arriving at Hanoi and seeing plenty of markets along the way this place was a real disappointment for us. The markets are basically filled with the same old crap. There is no way I would wear any of this stuff back home. The stuff is far to pricey compared to the other markets in Asia I have been to… The vendors are not willing to budge at all… Not even a few thousand dollars… They don't acknowledge you… When locals are buying things they hide the money so you don't see how much they are paying.Even though this is street is 'closed off to scooters' they seem to stream through the markets beeping there horns with an angry face when you fail to move.AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.

reviews.author: HoneycombDreamers
reviews.title: Leave Your Motorcycle at Home
reviews.content: For us the night market was a little disappointing, as the products sold were no different from the Old Quarter during the day. The bonus was the freedom to walk down the streets without watching for traffic and no tooting horns could be heard, only the hum of chatting friends.Though the odd annoying motorcycle did try to squeeze past the crowds of people to just keep us on edge. The bright lights and the locals did give off a happy vibe. We were also warned by our guide that pick pockets were active in the area too. The night market is only open Friday, Saturday and Sunday, so we thought we'd take a peek, as we had a free Saturday night.

reviews.author: CanberraDiner
reviews.title: Fun night market
reviews.content: Ok so the wares at the night market are your typical flea market offering. But the atmosphere is very fun. Prices seem to start a little higher than what you'll be asked during the day in the Hanoi Old Quarter but sellers are happy to bargain.The main selling point for this night market is that they close off the streets to traffic. Which is a plus if you're tired of dodging hundreds of motorbikes, cars, scooters and push bikes while you shop.

reviews.author: joltt
reviews.title: Big night market with many stalls
reviews.content: This is quite a big night market with about 3 - 4 blocks of streets lined with many stalls selling all types of items.  The night market operates on every Friday, Saturday and Sunday.  Stalls start setting up at 7pm and the road is closed to traffic for the night market to be set up.  However, do watch out for motorbikes as many riders on motorbikes still try to scoot on the road even though it is closed to traffic.  Some stalls are clear in their pricing and state pricing clearly, others, probably need to bargain.  This round, I realised that I was unable to buy any items at 50% of what was quoted.  So do have some idea of how much things cost before bargaining to know what is a fair price to pay.Should visit.

reviews.author: Celebr8_8
reviews.title: Not very good... But not too bad
reviews.content: The night market, which runs on Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights from 7pm to 11pm, was one of the bright sparks for my family during our stay in Hanoi. The stuff sold there are not as junky as some described them to be. A little touristy... but IMHO it's way better than Dong Xuan Market which is too cramped and messy for me. Have fun...

reviews.author: NinaTom
reviews.title: Not the worst, not the best.
reviews.content: There is a lot of repetition along the long line of stalls in the Hanoi Night Market, but there are also some nice buys to be found amongst the clutter. The atmosphere in the whole was good and it was pleasant enough to stroll around. The whole area around the night market is scattered with small bars and food stalls to take a break. There are always going to be people trying to nick stuff but no more here than any other big city across the world, just be sensible with your belongings; we ensured we put all valuables in inside zip pockets and didn't take any bags out with us.

reviews.author: Harry R
reviews.title: 'Great atmosphere, but the cheap fakes lack any quality'
reviews.content: Recently visited the markets on Sunday night and was great to see the typical hustle and bargaining taking place in the vast amounts of stalls. However, recently coming from Ho Chi Minh and Hoi An the quality of product is much poorer and even though the price maybe a little lower, these markets have made fakes that are very tacky and with the exception of some products are not worth the low prices.These markets are definitely worth having a walk around for the vibe of a Vietnamese night market and the risk of pickpockets is unlikely providing you are wary of your possessions, with police also frequent in the area. However, unless you are happy with cheap and cheerful stuff you probably won't buy much, with other cities and the day time shops through Ha Noi selling much better quality items for reasonably similar prices.

reviews.author: Tegan R
reviews.title: A typical night market
reviews.content: We took a walk through the market while recently in Hanoi. It is your typical market found in Asia full of atmosphere and, of course, an infinite number of stalls selling souvenirs, copy clothes, and numerous other wares. My advice is if you're going to go to the market then go hungry so you can check out the food! We had unfortunately eaten before we stopped by but managed to fit in some bbq pork and it was delicious!

reviews.author: Oliver S
reviews.title: A night market like any other, but...
reviews.content: still worthwhile to stroll through it and just to observe other people haggling and bargaining for the same-same fake watches, clothes or other useless nick-nack. Or just sit down in one of the street food stalls, enjouy a cold Tiger or a feww bites and enjoy the scenery. I don't quite understand some of the negative ratings mentioning the pick pockets and thieves. On this market there aren't any more or less thieves then on any other market in the world, be it in Paris, Cartagena, Mumbai or wherever. I personally have no sympathy for those blue eyed touristst that lost their property although they knew better. Next time better keep your belongings (wallets, I-Phones etc) in the hotel.

reviews.author: Ten P
reviews.title: Affordable and Negotiable
reviews.content: The place is generally clean. The night market is not one compact place though. It is a long stretch of stalls along a few streets in Hanoi. Poor in geography, I only remember treading a short  street, crossing to the other side, walking straight a narrow street, turning left, turning right, crossing again, and taking a cab back to the hotel. But I got to buy nice bags at really affordable prices, with good quality, and warm, smiling, gentle people of Hanoi, Vietnam. Do not get fooled, though, I was able to chat with an old woman who I learned to be a revolutionary during the Vietnam war.  She was in her early 20s when she fought during the Vietnam-American war. No one would guess she was a guerilla - she is a woman of courage and righteousness hiding behind her soft eyes, gentle smile, and meek bearing. I feasted on beautifully colored tops, bonnets, shirts and masks, but bought only what I needed -uh oh, you have to have strong discipline to control impulsive buying in Hanoi because there's just a lot to want.  Prices are already affordable - but a good negotiation can bring it a few cent lower. Happy shopping :)

reviews.author: SaltyDogz
reviews.title: Worth a look and check out the street food
reviews.content: All that is said in the other reviews re the lack of traffic etc. But the stalls are nearly all cheap average quality clothing, bags, sunglasses, fake watches etc aimed at the local buyers and Vietnamese tourists.The saving grace are the lack of traffic and the many and interesting street food stalls and the plentiful cheap beer. Street side vendors with tiny stools for you to sit on (not good for the elderly or frail) will fill you up with yummy food cooked in front of you and endless cheap beer. What's not to like about that.

reviews.author: Ira S
reviews.title: Crowded, Noisy and the place to be on a Weekend Night in Hanoi
reviews.content: The night market is open on weekend nights.  We went on a Saturday night.  The vendors have  stalls set up in the street, traffic is prohibited and a cadre of police make sure the motor bike riders keep off the streets and the vendors adhere to the rules.The streets are packed with tourists and locals.  The vendors sell mostly stuff that no one seemed to want to buy, t-shirts, tourist items, purses, and so on.  There are also food vendors.  We bought  some food from a street vendor, I have no idea what it was, but it was tasty and inexpensive.To me, it was all about the atmosphere and not the items being sold.  It is a great place to people watch and worth the visit.

reviews.author: Lity M
reviews.title: Good place and Bargain
reviews.content: Good to see many things you can bargain and get a good deal. Really cheap and reasonably good stuff for the money you pay.

reviews.author: Itinerant Ozzie
reviews.title: Bustling Night Market - Limited Variety
reviews.content: The Hanoi night market takes place on Hang Dao street in the old quarter after 7pm a few nights a week (definitely Friday and Sat night). The street is blocked off to vehicular traffic during the market operation which makes a huge difference as most of the shopping streets are swamped with traffic most of the time.The market is quite large extending for at least 3 blocks and it is certainly attracts a lot of interest with large crowds.The thing that lets this market down is the relatively narrow range of goods being offered. Having said that it is quite an experience and any visitor to Hanoi should visit at least once.

reviews.author: Jack P
reviews.title: Better than expected
reviews.content: I read a lot of bad reviews on here, but I'm not quite sure what everyone was expecting. It's your typical asian market - and it's unlikely you will find a huge amount to buy, but soaking in the atmosphere is a really nice experience.In the end we ended up buying a pretty reasonable selection of things - from decorative post cards to new phone cases.Don't expect the best thing in the world, but be realistic and you'll enjoy it. As for pickpockets - we didn't see any but with any situation like this - just be wary and you will have no problems at all.

reviews.author: morgandeller
reviews.title: A fun night out
reviews.content: We went to the night market twice while in Hanoi. Lots of stalls, bustling atmosphere, street food, a decent shopping opportunity and definitely lots of fun. Dodging the motorbikes can be a little annoying as can the masses of people, I'd suggest going a bit earlier in the evening, around 7:30, if you want to avoid the crazy crowds!

reviews.author: Mahendra A
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: The market is full of stalls selling cheap quality clothes, bags, accessories, belts and souvenier items at the same price as the other regular shops in Old Quarter. There is nothing special that you would miss if you do not visit this place. Also, I was warned by the hotel staff that due to the heavy crowd in the market, there is a good chance you might get pickpocketed.

reviews.author: Prudence W
reviews.title: Busy Market not the best for shopping
reviews.content: Hanoi seems to be full of authentic knock offs and cheap clothes. The people of Hanoi seem to like this. As a tourist it's great to see local people doing what they do (great outfits from promenading couples dressed uo for the night!)But as a westerner the clothes were nowhere near my size (UK 12) as the female frame here is soooo petite. Good for people watching and wandering, but not great for shopping either for travel clothes, souvenirs or gifts.

reviews.author: Tim S
reviews.title: Bustling market but lacking in variety.
reviews.content: I live in Hanoi now so I'm used to the crowds, in fact I love being in a crowd. That's what visiting a real market is all about and this one is certainly bustling at it's peak times.What lets this place down is the lack of variety in the stalls.

reviews.author: Jeanette W
reviews.title: More for the experience!
reviews.content: It's definitely worth coming out for The Night Market on Friday, Saturday night to check out the items on sale.Take in the experience and you never know, you might see a few things that would make perfect souvenirs for your friends and family back home. P.S.Make sure you are aware of your belongings at all times.

reviews.author: Juliana788
reviews.title: BEAWARE!! WALLET THEIVES
reviews.content: whilst having an okay time looking through the many stalls and waking through the pushy crowds I was alerted that my bag had been slashed and my wallet stolen! i went to the police but they did not care! the crowds are so pushy, that if you go make sure you take no valuables and a bag in which you can hold! my friend also had her wallet stolen the night before! would never go back. you can buy anything at the market during the day at the many shops on the streets of Hanoi

reviews.author: Lasse R
reviews.title: Your average market
reviews.content: Rather crowded and nothing especially interesting. Picked up a little stuff for the kids. It's only open in weekends and closes at 22:30.

reviews.author: DanielaKLI
reviews.title: Not very different from what you see during the day
reviews.content: The night market offers the same products that you can buy in the Old Quarter during the day. No big surprise. It's good if you have an idea of the 'normal' prices, to negotiate effectively (ex: if you know that a kid's souvenir t-shirt costs around 100.000 VND maximum, when you are approached and offered a t-shirt for 200.000, you know how to react). The market can quickly become unpleasant and overcrowded. Go there at the beginning of the night.

reviews.author: ivan l
reviews.title: long stretch of shops with repeated products
reviews.content: most of the shops sells similar items and are repeated throughout the night market. not many street food choices at this night market compared to that in HCMC or Taiwan. 5 of the vendors we encountered were not open to price negotiations. not even 10% off. it leaves us wondering if the price quoted in the first place is inflated or not? most guides and even our hotel says we should bargain from 50% off and pay no more than 70%. once in a while you can find something for a real bargain. there are men's belt going for 20K, 30K, 50K VND. some children and adult clothes going cheap too. only good enough for a once in a lifetime visit to experience.

reviews.author: HairdresserAbroad
reviews.title: longest night market I've ever seen
reviews.content: This night market is amazing so many vendors lots of people it's buzzing I made a couple of good buys, there's clothes sun glasses, souvenirs, there's something for everyone

reviews.author: Brad R
reviews.title: Mostly junk
reviews.content: The atmosphere is lively but most of the stalls are selling the same junk you've seen in most of the tourist shops throughout Hanoi. It's a good place for a wander after dinner but I was repeatedly warned about pickpockets, however I saw no evidence of this - then again I am extremely cautious. Don't feel like you've missed something if you don't get around to visiting, unless you're in the market for some cheap shirts shoes or other 'bargains'

reviews.author: James S
reviews.title: Like cartoon background scenery
reviews.content: WARNING!  Keep you wallet/money out of your pockets, keep nothing in your pockets full stop - unless you want it stolen.  I caught a lady trying subtly to undo the buttons on my trouser leg pockets attempting to get at my wallet.  I managed to prevent it being stolen.  From then on my wallet stayed in my shoulder bag which remained fastened and held over shoulder but towards the front of my body in my sight, NOT on my back and out of sight.  It can be a pain when buying something, having to keep going into the bad for money but worth it in the long run so you don't lose all your cash/bank cards etc. That said, despite the warning it's still worth a short visit and it's not a bad market for picking up some cheap t-shirts or other clothing.  Also, there's some knock off rucksacks to be had (North Face) which aren't bad and came in handy for me as I was seeking out a new one anyway - got a new one for about VND200K (about £6GBP).  There's the usual sunglasses, hair accessories, shoes, t-shirts, stand-up greeting cards, but it is a bit repetitive especially as it's quite long it doesn't change much from end to end, and some of the stall holders aren't up for much negotiation over the prices.  By all means have a look, but don't expect to find anything different, including any changes in price, the further you head down.  If you see something, get it, leave.

reviews.author: kalimah
reviews.title: Hanoi Night Market
reviews.content: I was able to buy embroidered bags. It was cheaper there than the regular shops in the Old Quarter. There were combs made of carabao and buffalo horn that looked very nice. No haggling. Fixed price. There were some handicrafts too. Lots of clothes.

reviews.author: SSQuah
reviews.title: Cheap but nothing really special
reviews.content: This is just like a night market in many of Asian cities and towns. Some roads would be closed up to traffic, allowing traders to set up their stalls. The items sold weren't that much different from what I would find in my hometown: cheap clothing, shoes, handbags, sweets, fresh and dried fruits, decorations, toys, stationery, sundry goods and roadside food, except that some of the branded goods may turn out questionable. The night market stretched for about one kilometre or so, but we gave up after walking along the Hàng Ngang Street. All the goods looked more or less the same, and if you see one, chances are that you would have seen them all.

reviews.author: Sue C
reviews.title: Beware pickpockets!!!!
reviews.content: We happened to stumble across this market after a walk after a meal one night. After venturing a small way into the market and seeing that it was generally a pretty crappy market with very average things on offer, and with very grumpy smallholders, we decided to leave. I was aware of some pushing a shoving around the entrance of the market and within seconds realised that my phone had been stolen from my bag. The 'pregnant' woman who had brushed past me and stolen the phone had disappeared as quickly as she had appeared. When I put in a police report the next morning there was a Singaporean couple in front of me at the police station reporting the same crime at the same place. Unfortunately  we had not been warned that pickpockets were rife here but I do tend to keep my things close and at the front of me. These guys are well versed at their 'craft' so do be very very careful at this location.

reviews.author: JohnF47
reviews.title: Great place to buy 3D cards
reviews.content: There is a lot of market here!  And it gets jam-packed.Having read the reports/advice, I went early evening before it became too crowded.  I loved the atmosphere, the buzz.  I carried no bag, no camera, no phone - better safe than sorry - and I did feel safe, even when it became more congested and people were jostling me at every turn.  This is NOT a place for back-packs!Had been looking to buy some 3D origami cards, and this was where I found the best selection (small and larger size), and the starting prices were lower than I had seen in regular stores.  Had fun bargaining (successfully) with a very friendly vendor.As expected, there is quite a range of product quality and price on offer, however bargains are to be had.Really glad I experienced this vibrant market.

reviews.author: Carrie N
reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.content: I was here at the beginning of April. I went to a few markets across Asia, and this one was by far the worst. My hotel warned me of pickpockets. I saw a couple sketchy individuals, and as I watched them make their through the crowd, eyeballing the purses some ladies were carrying, I am certain they were not there to shop. It’s a big market yes, but every booth has the exact same very cheaply made garbage, and vendors were not willing to negotiate at all.

reviews.author: KiwiDriver
reviews.title: Cooler time to shop, pickpockets are rife
reviews.content: The market goes through the Old Quarter, it goes for 8 blocks.  Nothing different to buy here.  But nice to shop when it's cooler at night, you can get clothing, sunglasses, DVDs, handbags, etc here.I was 2 seconds away from losing my wallet though.  It was in the main part of my backpack, not the front zip.  The lady must have watched me buying something and putting my wallet away.  Then just steps down the market, I felt a slight nudge or bump, I turned around and saw a lady move her hand a little.  I quickly took my backpack off and the main zip, which was fully closed was half open!  I went to follow her but she was gone, very quick and into the crowd.Plse do be careful in Hanoi, from reading, it seems that pick pockets are aplenty up here.  Either have your backpack on the front of your body or put some money near your body and go out without a wallet.

reviews.author: Ida D
reviews.title: Interesting Night Market!
reviews.content: Hubby and I were lucky to have arrived on Saturday as we only found out about the market on the day itself. It had the feel of both the 'Pasar Malam' in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia except you can bargain here. We ended up buying our souvenirs here and everything was pretty cheap. You can find souvenirs, toys, clotjes and shoes.Although on the downside, in my opinion, there are a lot of repetitive goods sold in the whole stretch of the market.I don't mind going there again to shop in I choose to visit Hanoi again. :)

reviews.author: Kerry C
reviews.title: Similar to daytime shopping but streets are 'closed'.
reviews.content: We enjoyed the night market. It sells clothes, souvenirs, jewellery and general stuff.  They close the streets for the market but not everyone follows that, there is still the occasional motorbike that  comes through. My son liked the cheap helicopter toy that a lady was demonstrating - it lit up in the night and cost a whole 50c.  It was also cooler and had a nice atmosphere with the lights.  Worth a stroll.

reviews.author: travelafeme
reviews.title: Great bargains
reviews.content: We were lucky that we were there for the weekend night market.  I bought clothes, souvenirs, scarf.  There were lots of cheap items.  They close a stretch of the street of Hang Dao, but still you can encounter few motorcycles entering the street.  There were grumpy salesladies, we just walk away from them.  There were nicer ones and made our shopping a pleasure.

reviews.author: MrGoh
reviews.title: Lovely evening outing on weekends
reviews.content: The night market operates every weekend only. It is an enjoyable way to spend the evening after dinner. We visit the night market every night when we were in Hanoi. The place is ordering (one way in, one way out) and there are many stuff to see and buy. Some of the stalls change over the days.

reviews.author: ShawnLiv
reviews.title: Dong Xuan Night Market
reviews.content: Hanoi night market, also known as Dong Xuan night market, held on weekend evenings in the Old Quarter of Ha Noi. Basically, I went because the night market is very close to my stayed hotel. Overall, I think it is worth a visit to experience the local lifestyle. You can see locals and tourists mingle along the streets. People were everywhere and the locals like to push their way through the crowd.As a whole, many stalls were selling the same things and isn’t much unique stuffs being sold here. Therefore, walk back half way. However, I still managed to buy some souvenirs, clothes, hand make Christmas card and etc. On the other hand, many reviews and my tour guide do remind me regarding the pickpocketing issues. Therefore, I keep all my valuables at the hotel.

reviews.author: Shawn_Storm
reviews.title: Detailed review of the Hanoi Night Market.
reviews.content: After reading the other reviews on here I decided to contribute an in depth review that addresses all aspects of the night market and hopefully clears up a few things.  Here goes.GENERAL INFO:This night market operates only on the weekends (Fri-Sunday).  It is decent sized and starts near the Northwest Corner of Hoàn Kiếm Lake on Hàng Đào Road.  It runs north along Hàng Đào Road for roughly 8 blocks and ends at the edge of the old quarter where the railroad tracks go above the street.  It also has a side extension that runs east along Hàng Khoai Road on the north side of Chợ Đồng Xuân Market.  The roads are blocked off and popup booths are erected in the center of the streets creating two lanes of foot traffic.  There are also booths on the sides of the street, so while walking down either of the two lanes you will usually have booths on either side of you.  To see all the booths you can traverse the length of the market on one side and then return to the beginning on the other side.  Foot traffic generally runs in one direction (north in the east lane and south in the west lane).  The market starts setting up around 6pm and really gets going sometime between 7-8pm.AMBIENCE:The majority of people at the night market are local Vietnamese.  It has a somewhat festive atmosphere.  Some of the stalls play techno or dance music (which I actually like).  It can be very crowded and there are definitely moments when the foot traffic flow comes to a standstill.SHOPPING:Most of the stuff being sold is geared towards the locals (such as basic clothing, jackets, belts, handbags, cell phone cases, etc).  For the most part it is basically the same kind of stuff found along the street during the day.  There are also some booths more geared towards tourists that have handicrafts, t-shirts, etc.  In general there isn't much unique goods being sold here that can't be found around the old quarter during the day.  Pricing also didn't seem any better from what I could tell.FOOD:There isn't much food being sold here.  I would recommend getting dinner at a restaurant before going to the night market because it doesn't have much to offer.  With that said, there are some food booths and strolling food venders scattered along the length of the market.  They mostly offer snacks such as grilled meat on a stick, french fries, cotton candy, snack pancakes, steamed corn, etc.  There is also a small food court with roughly 8 restaurants located at the northwest corner of Chợ Đồng Xuân Market (near the north end of the night market).  These restaurants don't seem to be anything special and have similar pricing and selection as other normal restaurants in the old quarter.PICK POCKETS:After reading all the reviews on here about pick pockets, I decided to leave my valuables at the hotel and came to the night market with empty pockets and a small amount of money tucked in a hidden pocket in my jacket.  I traversed the length of the market numerous times and never encountered any thieves.  I was actually hoping to find some and was looking forward to potentially busting them in the act.  Perhaps the issue is subsiding, or perhaps I am not a likely target, or perhaps I just wasn't in the right place at the right time.  However, I can see how pick pockets could be successful at this market because the tight packed crowds create an ideal environment for such things.  So be aware, but chances are you will be fine if you take normal precautions.MOTORCYCLES:Yes, there are occasionally motorcycles that attempt to use the footpaths which creates a logistical mess.  However, the streets are closed off to traffic and they aren't supposed to be there.  I only saw it happen a few times and it was because their motorcycle was already parked along the street before it got shut down to traffic and they were trying to get out.  There were also security guards at every intersection who were giving the motorcycles a hard time and preventing other ones from entering the walking paths.SUMMARY:Compared to other SE Asia night markets that I have visited, this one is nothing special.  I was actually kind of surprised because I would think Hanoi would have a great night market.  However, I still think it is worth a visit, especially if you happen to be staying in or near the old quarter on a weekend.  It may not be amazing, but it is something to do.  I personally wouldn't come to the night market to shop or eat, but rather to simply wander the market in a crowd of Vietnamese locals taking it all in.

reviews.author: Richard S
reviews.title: Big but limited
reviews.content: I've been to a number of markets before but this is by far the largest. It takes a good hour just to see everything and could easily occupy several hours if searching the stalls and buying things.Unfortunately, there is a fairly limited range of products available. Most of the stalls are selling similar selections of clothes and trinkets with the odd different shop here and there. I hardly saw anything that interested me but if you like touristy t-shirts then you'd probably love it. You can find most (if not all) of the same stuff at the shops nearby any time.Apparently the market only runs on Friday-Sunday nights but again, you aren't missing much if you don't see it.

reviews.author: AlnAbroad
reviews.title: It's a market
reviews.content: I didn't have any trouble or problems with people at the night market, and don't know why other people did.  Just like anywhere else in the world, use common sense and don't make yourself a target!  That being said, the market isn't spectacular.  It's always fun to mingle with crowds and take in the sights and sounds of a Southeast Asian market, especially at night, but don't expect to come across any great finds in the stalls.

reviews.author: beach132
reviews.title: Nothing special, Unfriendly traders
reviews.content: The things that selling in the night market are nothing much different from other Asians country's night market.  Some of the traders were unfriendly and not happy if you touched their products.  A lot of motorbikes, noisy and need extra careful when crossing the road, the cars and motorbikes likes to make hon from their vechicles and if you are not prepared, can get shocked.

reviews.author: Tan S
reviews.title: Skip this, nothing but thieve!
reviews.content: I went there on my arrival day , didn't know there is a night market, we passed by and just to check out the place, it was a very long haul of stalls selling low quality and fake stuffs. I noticed a decent look lady standing kinda close to me, but I thought she was one of the store owner, because of those bikes passing by, she was trying to avoid the bike, but after a few meter passing through the stalls, I noticed the same lady was still behind me and I thought she was a shopper, suddenly I felt someone pushing me at my side, and consciously I just hold my bag tight and looked back, the lady was next to me with a guy, but they were not looking at me, pretending they didn't realize that they pushed someone, it didn't strike me at that time, but I just didn't feel comfortable and calling my husband who was a few meter away from me.  I was tired when go back to hotel, didn't realize my bag got snatched a big hole until the next morning, lucky that I only bring my hp in the bag and it was safe, they didn't manage to get anything from me. The next day, my cousin who happened to go there, same place, her cash, hp and ID card got stolen, someone opened her bag even though she was careful with it!

reviews.author: BMDunn03
reviews.title: Locals market
reviews.content: This is more of a locals market from my view. Still interesting for a look and to kill the curiosity. Wouldn't need to go again. And it goes FOREVER

reviews.author: Phil W
reviews.title: Not worth the effort
reviews.content: Many stalls selling exactly the same stuff as the shops in Old Quarter sell during the day (hardly surprising). Crowded and I felt a little uncomfortable at the number of 20ish male pairs who were mingling. I believe they were there for shoppers not the shopping. Go if you want to but shopping opportunities are abound (and in my view are safer and possibly better value) during daylight hours in the multitude of Old Quarter shops.

reviews.author: Carolloo83
reviews.title: Not just for tourist
reviews.content: I went looking for a good morning Vietnam tourist tshirt but had to walk quite a bit before I found it. I'm not sure why this place has got such awful reviews because I actually found it to be genuinely for the locals. And if the locals (with the income) do find shopping for fake goods etc as part of their shopping experience and we tourist go there WANTING to experience the local lifestyle, then we shouldn't discount it just because they have fake goods and cheap stuff on sale. That's the real deal guys. I like seeing the little street side stalls although I wasn't brave enough to risk it since I have a weak tummy. If u wanna see the Vietnamese lifestyle, what the locals do at night (if not in a st side bar), this is a good place to start walking around.

reviews.author: Stefanie089
reviews.title: Night Market in the Old Quarter
reviews.content: The night market is on friday, saturday and sunday nights, starts at about 7 pm and slowly starts closing around 10 pm. You find plenty of food stalls, clothes (fake brands and cheap, even second hand), lamps, shoes, accessoires, candles, incents, whatever you may looking for. it's frequented by tourists and locals of all ages which makes it a nice mixture.

reviews.author: james i
reviews.title: Hanoi annoy
reviews.content: Those giving any more than a 3 star ratings for this pitiful excuse for a market need to get their heads examined. I'll give you the layout. Trust me I can map it out, and you can too if youre unfortunate enough to go. Ok....here goes: fake leather purse stall, stereotypical t shirt stand, cheap sunglass stall, followed by happy-mealesque plastic toys, pirate dvds and finally a fake leather purse stall. Hang on a second. De-ja vous anyone? Seriously this "market" is a kilometer long and is literally a rinse and repeat job. On top of that their is a rather grim atmosphere. Hot, sweaty, narrow, foul tempers and shoulder barging. Others on here have pointed out a pickpocketing problem but I didnt run into this problem (result!). It really is a shame. It seems that finding qaulity goods is like finding a needle in a haystack here. Save your time, money and feet. Avoid it.

reviews.author: lastminaroundworld
reviews.title: Cheap and bad quality
reviews.content: The night market was a bit of a dissapointment after being all up for it, it turned out to be nothing but a road with a few stands offering bad looking fake products. Do not get to excited and keep your money and belongings close to yourself as it appears to be filled with pick pockets!

reviews.author: HelenaGuerra
reviews.title: Pick Pockets, fake items
reviews.content: It's crowded with locals buying contrefait clothes and bags. You can barely stretch your arm. It's awful. Unless you are interested in fake clothes and bags skip that. Awful street food (tons of cockroaches).Very rude and aggressive locals.

reviews.author: 313globetrotter
reviews.title: NIGHT MARKET, HANOI
reviews.content: HANOI is trying to do more tourist attraction doing the "NIGHT MARKET" concept like many of the Asean Countries. The Night Market only operate on weekend (ie Friday--Sunday nights). It runs from Hang Dao street ( North of Hoan Kiem Lake) all the way to Hang Gai street; crossing several intersecting streets. The main streets where the Market stalls operate are closed to traffic. Most of the stalls sell clothings, shoes, cosmetics, electronics, watches  etc; while the end part of the market sell food and drinks. The items can be found in most of the stalls and shops around the city; and the prices are higher!!! The locals take this as an weekend night outing and jammed packed the streets. Nothing exceptional for the tourists; except the crowds!!! Visit this as an experience and nothing else.

reviews.author: Chrissut
reviews.title: Very Busy BEWARE of pick pockets !!!
reviews.content: I have been to this market twice now and it gets busy to the point where browsing the stalls becomes difficult, I would definitely reccomend getting there early as it is quite pleasant to begin with.My second trip however was marred by an attempted pick pocketing experience.Three ladies blocked my way while one undid the buttons on my shorts, luckily I was able to get her hand out before anything was taken. I normally wear a money belt, however didn't on this occasion, please don't be complacent as it nearly cost me !

reviews.author: TravellingBeet
reviews.title: We were disappointed even when we went with low expectations
reviews.content: We heard many mixed reviews about this market and had really low expectations when we decided to visit but yet it managed to disappoint us. This market is unlike the street markets of Bangkok where you are able to not only shop and find bargains for souvenirs and clothes, but also enjoy some local street eats, neither is it like the organized mess of Hong Kong's street markets.There was virtually zero street food, the variety of the souvenirs there were limited, the local stall keepers were unfriendly and the prices quoted to us were exorbitant. To make matters worse, we were rudely brushed aside when we tried asking for a discount for some t-shirts. Overall, it really wasn't a pleasant experience. We were much better off shopping for souvenirs at the shops along the lake which we deemed "tourist traps" when we first arrived. There, we were offered better prices. I guess that makes sense since the market stalls are only able to operate on weekend nights and they would have to make their profit somehow.

reviews.author: FireSpitter
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: This one is different to the ones found in other Asian cities. Go there at least once to experience it.

reviews.author: Ang Thomas
reviews.title: Hanoi Night Market
reviews.content: A really long stretch of streets filled with stalls when night falls. They are really different, as they are selling the same kind of items next to each stall, before you can find another stretch of stalls selling the same type of items. Narrow walkway with motorbike coming in & out of it as they transportation their goods.

reviews.author: mikiamil
reviews.title: Beats shopping in the day
reviews.content: I reviewed the Old quarter and commented that most shops are being rude and ripping off customers with sky-high prices. This market is different. Because locals visit this market as well, the goods seems to be of better variety and prices are definitely a lot better. As it is open only on weekends (Fri-Sun), the crowd is massive and I will not recommend overly young children and elderly with mobility issues to WALK (the crowd pushes you at times and there are still some motorcycles even when the street is sealed off to traffic).While shopping, one can also enjoy some dessert by the roadside which are quite tasty. Do it Hanoi style and sit on their tiny stools on the pavement, its an experience!

reviews.author: Thanh Cong V
reviews.title: Wonderful atmosphere
reviews.content: Dong xuan night market is wonderful place to see the movement of young generation in Hanoi. The market only open at the weekend from 7pm therefore dont try to find it during the week days. In the night market, there are many things to buy from souvernir things, cloths and many other interesting and cute items. The prices are often cheaper than the day shops. However the most interesting thing for me in the night market is atmosphere created by many young couple, many beautiful girls.

reviews.author: ArunSikka
reviews.title: The Night Market in the Old Quarter
reviews.content: Four reasons to go to the Night Market: The atmosphere: Explosion of sound and light and movement  The price: Magically changes to suit your quote!  The range: Unbelievable variety of things  The experience: Matches the magic of any bazaar, souk, market anywhere in the world.Yes if you’re in Hanoi, definitely make time for the Night Market. More at http://arunsikka.blogspot.com

reviews.author: Roachie1961
reviews.title: Nice intro to Hanoi
reviews.content: Different to other night markets I've been to in other Sth East Asian countries. Sellers don't hassle you to buy. They actually don't seem overly interested to sell. Beware of scooters. They are everywhere and beep their horn and push their way through the crowd. Limited range of goods. Some watches, bags, belts. Didn't see sporting items like runners or tops. For buying ordinary. For the experience, great.

reviews.author: sowpow
reviews.title: "night" market!?!?
reviews.content: This is def not a night market - I have no idea why people advertise it that way - we walked in the same area during the day and there were waaaay more stores open during the day...and the stores that were open at night were starting to shut down by 7pm so def a day market

reviews.author: Attila J
reviews.title: Busy market
reviews.content: Being around just before Lunar New Year was exceptionally busy place with pick pockets around. Be careful, carry as less as possible camera some cash and maybe a CC. My girlfriend bag been slit with a sharp item but luckily nothing stolen. Over all average but you can definitely get your souvenirs here as long you negotiate around 50-30%.

reviews.author: Judith G
reviews.title: worth it
reviews.content: everything sold in the night market is cheaper than what they are sold in the stores in the day time. remember to keep your valuables close to u all the time and bargain like nobody's business.

reviews.author: jimburns4u
reviews.title: Awful
reviews.content: Just the same old tat you can buy at all the other crappy stores for tourists.. same stores over and over again the only entertainment is watching the pickpockets.

reviews.author: Jhsan
reviews.title: Could be better arranged
reviews.content: It was a very crowded place, with many stalls and hawkers but kinda dull since most of them sell regular clothings,accesorries,footwear n stuff. It's just my opinion though, since I was a tourist,I guess it's mostly providing for the locals. Very different from halong bay nite market that sells mostly souvenirs/gifts and typical vietnamese items. However, it was a lively place to be,just be careful woth yoyr belongings!

reviews.author: SiowThiamKong
reviews.title: Get your souvenir items here!
reviews.content: The night market will only do business on Sat. and Sun. night. The item's price here was cheap and the quality was fine. No point you pay more at the others souvenir shop.

reviews.author: Cecdior
reviews.title: Hanoi night market
reviews.content: The night market has many stalls selling the same stuff so it can get a bit boring after walking through the street.  Be careful of pickpockets cos my Longchamp tote bag was slashed by a woman carrying a fake baby and she used a penknife to cut open my bag.  Her tactic was to keep pushing me (penknife hidden in her hand) and get a group of teenage girls to surround me.  I didn't realise my bag was cut open till I reached the end of the street!  Thank God my wallet was not stolen and nothing was lost.  Unfortunately, I had to buy a replacement bag the next day cos it couldn't be repaired.  Wish police could patrol the area...

reviews.author: aghasek
reviews.title: “An interesting place”
reviews.content: it is a very busy market, first level sell mostly of shoes and dried food stuff, decorative items, 2nd floor is mostly clothing it is a good market to find cheap stuff, it is cheaper to shop there compared with the market at the hoan kiem lake. but the lane between each stalls are very narrow, you really needs lots of skill to move through[6:01:12 PM] Hannah: it is a very busy market, first level sell mostly of shoes and dried food stuff, decorative items, 2nd floor is mostly clothing it is a good market to find cheap stuff, it is cheaper to shop there compared with the market at the hoan kiem lake. but the lane between each stalls are very narrow, you really needs lots of skill to move through

reviews.author: choymp
reviews.title: Less interesting than expected
reviews.content: It was not very interesting to begin with except the very long stretch of stalls and the huge crowd. After an encounter with pickpockets, I was more busy looking after myself than to look around. Make sure to hold your young children.

reviews.author: ubermum_lisa
reviews.title: Good way to see what locals do
reviews.content: Enjoyed the fact this is not a touristy attraction. Locals and tourists mingle along traffic free streets. However, you will get the occasional vespa trying to get through. Bargain at least 50% if there are no signs telling you how much things cost. I enjoyed eating the kebab banh mi. Great place to replenish your tee shirts and slippers. If your back pack breaks, you can get a Northface knock off at just SGD3!!!

reviews.author: Mel H
reviews.title: Amazing Experience
reviews.content: Even if you dont want to buy anything, just walking through these huge markets filled with 1000s and 1000s of people is awe inspiring.  You can buy anything your heart desires at these markets but just be wary of pick pockets

reviews.author: benzberry
reviews.title: Lower your expectations
reviews.content: Same stuff over and over and over again. Not the best quality nor rock bottom cheap. If it is not a hot night and you are bored with nothing else to do, then give it a try.The best thing about it was the lack of motorized traffic; they actually closed it off. The most irritating was some idiotic motorbikes still manages to get past the barricades .... If you are into streetside food, can find decent selection here especially at the Dong Xuan end.

reviews.author: havaholiday
reviews.title: more things to buy
reviews.content: It seemed to be nothing you couldn't find in a shop in the daytime, and many stalls selling the same stuff, so after a bit of a look we grabbed a cab to a restaurant elsewhere. We had been warned that there there was danger of pickpockets so this did not make us want to hang around.

reviews.author: chocolatealbury
reviews.title: amazing
reviews.content: Theres nothing you cant buy there absolutley everything you could possibly think of and more. Most recomended, but be wary of pickpockets.

reviews.author: dubbs2012
reviews.title: Hanoi Night Market
reviews.content: Busy and nothing that I was really looking to buy. We were warned by several people about pickpockets but had no trouble personally. It is funny that motorbikes came through the market despite it supposedly being closed to traffic.

reviews.author: Abuhasans
reviews.title: Average night market
reviews.content: This night market cannot be compared with Bangkok night market or similar. Narrow streets make it worse when it is crowded. Beware of prices. They may ask 10 times more than the actual price.

reviews.author: sadein
reviews.title: Blocks and blocks of uninteresting stuff
reviews.content: We went to the night market hoping to score some warmer clothes to wear. We found everything to be of poor quality and overpriced. I'm not sure what would interest foreign travelers at the market. There are no crafts and the only decent clothing we found was Chinese and much more expensive than the local products.So, unless you just like the hustle and bustle of the street market, there is really no reason to go here.

reviews.author: Zara S
reviews.title: BEWARE!! PICK POCKETS GALORE! @intersection of Hang Dao & Cau Go
reviews.content: Market is too crowded..lots of locals pushing and shoving. Stalls selling the same old stuff, low quality though...but be careful as you approach the END of the market at the barricade just before the 3 FRUIT STALLS (at intersection of Hang Dao & Cau Go).A very 'organised' group of women (well dressed) will aim for their targets and as you are walking along with the flow of other pedestrians, they will (as what happened to me & my husband) come in between you&your spouse/friends...pushing and shoving and before you know it, they have robbed you of whatever u have in your bag, or pocket or backpack. (in our case, my husband's wallet and iphone) I had a front sling Tumi pouch (they couldn't get to it) :)I recognised the pickpockets, went back to the spot, and watched as they tried to pickpocket an American tourist with the same tactic. my husband and I caught them in the act at which point i demanded our stuff back....they were shocked & scattered, but a few minutes later, an old woman pointed something to us...and there was my husband's wallet, (minus his CITIBANK credit card, bt everything else in tact..scattered all over the road) but iphone-gone forever!Don't bother trying to report to the authorities, i tried to as they were only yards away from where it happened...they gave me a blank stare.Best thing is...DON't bother with the night market...you are better off finding deals at the many shops....I decided to go to Hoi An the very next day...much..much..MUCH better experience.

reviews.author: fg42
reviews.title: Just so-so
reviews.content: Nice to have a night-time activity like this in the Old Quarter.  But the range of products was very limited; lots of "sameness."  Not the variety of stuff like you'd see in a Hong Kong night market, for example.  And it's supposed to be a pedestrian zone for the night market -- so what is it with all the motorbikes weaving in and among all the foot traffic?

reviews.author: RenataTavares
reviews.title: Not the best place to eat in Phu Quoc
reviews.content: We went there to have dinner... They have a lot of restaurants and they look all the same! :) I don't know if we asked for wrong plates or if the food is not that good, but it was kind of a deception... :( may be we have to give it another chance! :)

reviews.author: GRM
reviews.title: Very average, seen much better!!
reviews.content: This is a by average market. I expected so much more and when you consider how big it is, it is quite disappointing. It is very repetitive with stall after stall selling the same thing. I also noted a reluctance for vendors to negotiate prices (i.e. one item 250,000 dong, two items the same 500,000 dong). I expected much better in Hanoi!!

reviews.author: jollyguy_11
reviews.title: typical Asian market
reviews.content: Very hectic, crowded with more locals than tourists.  Watch out for pick pockets

reviews.author: yaapeet11
reviews.title: Little to spend your tourist money on
reviews.content: Nothing wrong with the market as such, just that its not very big, and there are better deals to be had elsewhere.

reviews.author: Travel_bugle
reviews.title: Not a great night market
reviews.content: This night market is a bit rubbish to be honest, there is nothing to buy.  You can get some cheap dvds, some of which will work quite well, but that is about it.  Go elsewhere for markets...Hoi An is a better spot if you're in Vietnam.

reviews.author: LED6
reviews.title: Dried fruit shop at Hang Duong
reviews.content: Looking for dried fruit snacks? Try a shop along Hang Duong. Number 11 I think.  Shop name is called Hong Lam. It's usually got a crowd. The dried plums in various flavours are great. So are the sugary coconut strips. I'm told the dried longans are good but I didn't buy them. Somewhat disappointed with the pistachios though which were small and unopened.

locationDesc: Focused on the contribution of women to Vietnam's history and culture, this museum highlights their roles in Vietnam's many military conflicts as well as in commerce, including features on female street vendors, women's role in the family, and more recently, single mothers in Vietnam.

reviews.author: kisha m
reviews.title: Best of Night Market Experience
reviews.content: We were lucky enough to visit during the  festival and it was beautiful to see all the lighted boats and lanterns on the water. Worth a visit but be prepared for crowds. Still we hardly ever waited to order or eat at the restaurants or street vendors.

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: Somewhat mixed review
reviews.content: Very large night market that gave us a mixed impression. There is a good atmosphere there and it is pleasant to look at the different stalls.On the other hand, the choice for dining is very limited compared to the night markets we visited during our vacation in Malaysia in 2025. Here, you should expect a lot of clothes, jewelry, and souvenirs for tourists. The stalls sell roughly the same items (inexpensive, it is true) and in the end, there is nothing very authentic.Furthermore, the space to move around is very limited and unfortunately, scooters continue to drive in the street. I dare not imagine the chaos in high season.

reviews.author: Chrissie H
reviews.title: Fun shopping experience-bring cash!
reviews.content: Lots of great clothes, shoes and souvenirs and super fun atmosphere. Don’t forget to bargain and take cash :)

reviews.author: Travel Girl GR
reviews.title: You must be a weekend in Hanoi
reviews.content: The night market is held on the weekend only on the main street.You'll find everything, clothes, shoes, bags, souvenirs, food...

reviews.author: Rimjhim R
reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.content: Amazing vibes and goves the feel of vibrant Hanoi

reviews.author: thila2015
reviews.title: Safe, careful and comfortable.
reviews.content: Can get lots of stuff and souvenirs with reasonable price.

reviews.author: Jatin V
reviews.title: Hanoi taxi fraud
reviews.content: I have been to so many countries in europe and asia ...but in  hanoi i was told that there are so many pickpocketers and fraud.. i had terrible fraud experience in night matket grab taxi scam.. i took taxi from night market to my hotel ..that was showing grab lebel on the taxi...so i trusted...but when the driver dropped us ..He insisted to pay me without going out of the car and turned on blue light...and when i payed exact amount, he denied that it is not and asked me to show me my purse so he can help...and in the fraction of seconds he took big notes and put on the floor...and i caught him and he told me that accidentally fell ...and i saved my money..but that was the first experience in my life of this kind of fraud..

reviews.author: Jacqueline
reviews.title: If you enjoy markets, you'll love this.
reviews.content: We walked through the market but as markets and crowds aren't really our thing, it wasn't really for us.

reviews.author: Ray Yantch
reviews.title: Better night markets in Vietnam
reviews.content: The market was the same as all the other night markets there wasn't as much food and with all the motorbikes cutting through we made it difficult to walk I would not recommend this one in Hanoi. The one in Da Lat was a lot better

reviews.author: Mohit B
reviews.title: Lots of people and a lot more vendors
reviews.content: Crowded but lots of stuff to buy! Don’t forget to bargain but be respectful. Most of them sell similar stuff but prices might vary

reviews.author: Jacky D
reviews.title: Bustling Market
reviews.content: Wonderful experience of the local market here. Amazing food n music to experience. Had fun interacting with the locals and knowing about their products.

reviews.author: ATH Theatre
reviews.title: Spacious but a Bit Rough Around the Edges
reviews.content: I visited Dong Xuan Market in Hanoi with my friends. The market has an old design, but it feels spacious and familiar. Inside, it looks quite nice, though the surrounding area is a bit dirty. This place mainly sells wholesale goods, so it’s hard to buy just one or two items. It’s a pity that the vendors weren’t very friendly. Still, it’s worth a visit to experience the atmosphere.

reviews.author: loonylou78
reviews.title: Night market.
reviews.content: Very large,busy but repetitive market.Great to wander along at the weekend.If you're lucky you can grab a bargain!Street food readily available too!

reviews.author: Shalini Lalwani
reviews.title: Great deals if you have the patience to crack it!
reviews.content: Huge walking market to be discovered on foot. Loads of food and things to be haggled on… colourful and vibrant street shops with great bargains.

reviews.author: Simon S
reviews.title: Hoi An Night Market
reviews.content: Really enjoyed a stroll through the night market in Hoi An. A good selection of merchandise. As you'll find throughout the world at night markets, some vendors were really pushy, others were good. Be prepared to say no thank you more than once at some stalls.

reviews.author: Matvl
reviews.title: Bustling market
reviews.content: The Night Market is great to explore. Sure mostly cheaper items, knock offs etc but this isn’t a market geared up for tourists. It was very busy. Plenty of food options too - both market stalls and small eating places that operate out of market times too. It’s definitely worth exploring if you’re in Hanoi over market opening days. Nice to combine with a walk around the lake too.

reviews.author: Sharnee K
reviews.title: Atmosphere and food
reviews.content: The atmosphere was amazing and highly recommend for a look and great food choices but if you’re going for shopping it’s all the same things on repeat store  after store.

reviews.author: Thanh Xuan
reviews.title: Nơi mua sắm trải nghiệm tuyệt vời
reviews.content: Shopping at the night market was an unforgettable experience!The moment I stepped in, I was greeted by the colorful lights, the buzz of chatter, and the irresistible aroma of street food. Every corner was alive – with rows of stalls selling everything from handcrafted souvenirs to trendy fashion and quirky accessories. I found unique items I wouldn’t see anywhere else, and the best part? Bargaining with the friendly vendors made it all the more fun!There’s a kind of charm here you can’t find in big malls – it’s raw, real, and full of life. The energy, the people, the variety… if you’re in Hanoi (or Vietnam), don’t miss out on a night market walk – it’s more than just shopping, it’s a cultural adventure!

reviews.author: Willem B
reviews.title: Busy, busy market.
reviews.content: All markets in Vietnam seem alike, all items sold seem alike, but the experience is why I go the various markets. you see all kind of people trying to get the best deal, and that is what this market is all about. Very lively vibrant market, worth a try.

reviews.author: Remi A
reviews.title: Okay experience
reviews.content: Nice but a little underwhelming when compared to other night markets. It does like variety in the goods being sold and some of the foods were not tasty. However, I will still recommend as it is a change in pace and something to do.

reviews.author: corinne_prevost
reviews.title: HORROR
reviews.content: A night market where mopeds pass everywhere, nothing is controlled, an endless broom of mopeds that honk non-stop to pass. Prices are no more interesting than elsewhere

reviews.author: Kenlly Bowne
reviews.title: Overpriced and Too Crowded
reviews.content: The Hanoi Night Market is lively but overly crowded. Prices are quite high, especially for tourists, so be prepared to bargain. The atmosphere is fun, but the experience is not the best if you dislike large crowds. Worth a visit, but not a must-see.

reviews.author: akio9jp
reviews.title: Negotiating prices is imperative
reviews.content: The night market is held only on weekends (Friday, Saturday and Sunday) with traffic restrictions of approximately 700 meters from the rotary intersection on the north side of Hoan Kiem Lake to Dong Xuan Market.The area is packed with local citizens and tourists, selling a variety of goods such as clothing, accessories, household goods and souvenirs. However, there are many without price tags, and you basically have to negotiate a price to lose money, so you need wisdom and guts to get a good deal.

reviews.author: netnut2008
reviews.title: A nice change in the evening.
reviews.content: The Night Market is a nice change from the shops open during the day. Here you will find a lot and sometimes at significantly cheaper prices than during the day. However, the many fake brands have annoyed us a bit.

reviews.author: Keelyimps
reviews.title: Worth a visit, lots of nice things to buy.
reviews.content: Huge street market selling all sorts of stuff. Well worth going to and walking along looking at the different stalls. Grab yourself a bargain. 😄👏

reviews.author: Louise
reviews.title: Worthwhile But Tourist Traps Lie Within
reviews.content: The first 50 or so meters of the market is great! However, the rest is the same - pretty much all sellers are selling the same products but it’s still worthwhile! You can get some great bargains, don’t pay more than 100k for a branded T shirt and 150k for a branded windbreaker - definitely lots of tourists traps here with sellers overcharging, just know your prices and you can get some great trinkets for back home.

reviews.author: BenZ
reviews.title: 100% Go Visit
reviews.content: If you want to visit a really good market visit this one in Hà Nội. There is so much to see and lots of bargains, it’s amazing to see how good the copies are they are literally 10/10. Amazes me how they do it, the market has a good buzz and always haggle. They will always give you a high price but most of the time you can get them down to 50%

reviews.author: Sandrine F
reviews.title: A must do in Hanoi
reviews.content: Nice to see, great atmosphere, loads of good bargains. Perfect to buy souvenirs, do not hesitate to negotiate the price.

reviews.author: Rita N
reviews.title: Hanói night market, not to miss
reviews.content: Hanoi night market happens every friday, saturday and sunday. Hang Dao street is where you have to be. Busiest hour is between 19.00 and 20.30. I whas in Hanoi for 3 days and i found there all the best deals: under wear, sun glasses, sport wear (north face, Nike...), scarfs, souvenirs. No food strolls in this night market but in the streets around it. It is sure a "don't miss it" .

reviews.author: Sunil D
reviews.title: Great shopping experience in night market
reviews.content: great place to get some nice bargains for souvenirs and other stuff . the quality of clothes is good and this is one of the cheapest places in vietnam to shop ... YES... HCM is more expensive than this market

reviews.author: Ros C
reviews.title: spectacular
reviews.content: exceptional a night visit must not miss The inhabitants are really welcoming Here you can eat and buy lots of fresh fruit

reviews.author: Alessandro
reviews.title: Great for Evening Shopping
reviews.content: Characteristic Point of Sale where objects, clothes and food are sold. Famous brands Made in Vietnam are frequent for which the authenticity is doubtful. It remains open until about 11.30 pm Definitely worth a visit

reviews.author: Rachelle C
reviews.title: Fun pedestrian zone, weekends in the evening
reviews.content: We kind of stumbled onto the night market in Old Town in Hanoi but were glad we did.  The lights were so much fun and the streets reserved for pedestrians  (finally no mopeds!) were filled with young families.  It was amazingly hot and humid in August, even at night, but we still had a great time.

reviews.author: RIchard035
reviews.title: Weekend night market
reviews.content: The night market in Hanoi takes place at the weekend and extends from Ho Hoan Kiem lake at one end along Hang Dao and Hang Duong streets. It a large market that seems to go on for ever. It is very well lit and seems very safe. We were there in the summer when the area around the lake is closed to traffic in the evening at weekends and the were many families with young children walking around. The market sells food, clothing, souvenirs, etc. Prices are cheap, particularly if you bargain. However, I found there seemed to be more items with fixed pricing than in other markets I have visited in Asia.

reviews.author: Julie M
reviews.title: Hanoi.
reviews.content: Due to the effects of the typhoon, the Yash Market has not been opened for 2 times. Follow schedule.

reviews.author: Coyote-Travelerz
reviews.title: Pleasant
reviews.content: Compared to other night markets in Southeast Asia and Vietnam, this isn’t the best. Don’t let that discourage you from taking time out to enjoy the market. Each one is different and offers its own unique opportunities. We found wondering the streets and soaking up the atmosphere to be a very pleasant experience. It wasn’t too crowded (we didn’t feel like sardines) and we saw some interesting things on our stroll. It’s also a good opportunity to visit some of the historical places in the old section (like the gate or temples). As noted in other reviews, there are a lot of vendors selling knockoff products (which makes it a tacky experience) and not nearly as many street food vendors as you might see in other night markets.

reviews.author: these boots are made for walkin'
reviews.title: Tragic
reviews.content: Redundant (and oddly overpriced) fake garbage imported from China. The grossly underwhelming experience is tragically worsened by cranky retailers. I recommend a trip to Bangkok for anyone  interested in a good day/night market.

reviews.author: D McNeish
reviews.title: Steer clear market
reviews.content: A market full of plastic junk  . Worst market I have ever been to . I Couldn’t leave quick enough. Not a pleasant experience.

reviews.author: Skeets54
reviews.title: Average market for fake clothes
reviews.content: If you’ve never been to a night market before in any other part of Southeast Asia, you might think that this is really great however if you have been to other markets like those in Bangkok, Thailand or other parts of Thailand this market was quite poor in comparison. Firstly the street is not closed to motorbikes and they are still driving up and down incessantly whilst you were trying to shop which is really annoying. They should stop the street For All traffic including bikes. Secondly the stores are mainly clothing and fake goods which is fine if you want some counterfeit crocs handbags wallet belts and sportswear stuff but it wasn’t like other markets that had cute dresses or other types of interesting items. There were very little handcraft as well but the usual tat that you can find everywhere .Thirdly we found the market was significantly lacking in food options compared to other markets we’ve been to in Southeast Asia. There were a lot of reviews about the food so we came without eating hoping to to try a few things but we really couldn’t see anything apart from a few stools selling octopus tentacles and other things on a stick.  We were so disappointed by this market we thought that we went to early so then we went away and had some beers and came back again later in the night thinking that maybe more things would be open then however it was still exactly the same so all of the other reviews that we read about this market Were quite confusing. There were also very little places to sit and enjoy a drink or beer and watch the world go by all of the shops on the sidelines are clothing shops there’s only really one coffee shop but we saw that had a small balcony all in all probably one of the poorest, experiences.

reviews.author: AJ2000
reviews.title: Fun night out with family of teenagers
reviews.content: So much fun with the family! Great for picking up some bargain clothing or cute souveniers. Gets very busy but is easy to navigate. Recommend finishing with a relaxing walk around the lake soaking up the atmosphere and enjoying some fun performances along the way. Also great after the intensity of the market.Teenage kids cut their teeth bargaining and picked up some decent bargains at the market (I think the stall owners were being kind!). We stopped at an ice cream stall on the lake during our walk which finished the night perfectly. Very squashy at the market and not recommended for prams, wheelchairs etc however plenty of space around the lake which would be wheelchair / pram friendly.

reviews.author: The Travelling Chef
reviews.title: A Must in Hanoi
reviews.content: Prepare for a pleasurable assault on the senses.If you love great food, street side grills of questionable tasty meats on a skewer, a bustling chaotic atmosphere, market stalls of counterfeit designer brands, garments, fruit and veg, fresh juice, toys, electronics just too many to list, live performances of traditional and modern music and pantomime, endless streets of packed bars and restaurants all inviting you in ,photo opportunities and a warm scenic walk around the lake.I highly recommend the night market to all travellers to experience.

reviews.author: Amy
reviews.title: Pocket Thieves
reviews.content: One of the better night market in Vietnam. Lots of vendors and activities. We got 15 toddler clothes set. 1 set (shirt & pant) for under $1 USA or 25k dong.
