reviews.title: Impressive museum of the year 0 to date
reviews.content: Very impressive museum of the military history from the year 0 to the present. My main interest is the Vietnam War. This is recorded from the point of view of the communist North and that is understandable. Lots of photos and utensils, film and maps showing operations. Recommended

reviews.author: Juan C
reviews.title: NEW Military Museum
reviews.content: In this place you only find the old imperial city. Very interesting and very nice, however, the military museum is NOT in this place. Hanoi has a new museum just outside the city.

reviews.author: Stu
reviews.title: Impressive Museum well worth a visit.
reviews.content: This is a newly constructed building away from the centre and not pictured correctly atm.We caught a Grab Taxi and visited this impressive museum which was surprisingly free entry for us at around 12:30pm during January 2025 and afterwards another cab to  the Lotte Deck for the sunset view over Hanoi.. Well worth doing!

reviews.author: Me_n_my_rucksack
reviews.title: New location out of town - a new modern museum well worth the visit.
reviews.content: Importantly - this Museum has moved ! It is no longer in the middle of the city.  It is now in the suburbs a 20 to 30 min drive out of the middle of town. (Using the Grab App its still only a few pounds) Head for the Vincom Megacity Smart mall (A moders shopping Centre) and its the other side of a dual carriageway with an underpass.The new museum is large - massive comcrete multi story building with large galleries (some of which were not finished when we visited.  The external displays are generally the ones which were previously displayed in the old museum in town.  As you enter the museum grounds to the left are US Aircraft and tanks, to the right Vietnamese aircraft SAMs and Radars.Fortunateley some of the political propoganda of the old museum has been toned down - after all somewhere claiming to be a Museum presents facts and artefacts not a one sided biased account.  The new museum is still a long way from being an impartial account of history but its better than the old one.When we visited the museum had been open a week, some of the galleries were empty and the escalators didnt work.  It was free for the first month and it was heaving with visitors.   The obvious bias aside this is an excellent museum displaying the tanks aircraft etc with lots of space around them and very accessable.  Very well worth the trip out of the City to visit it.

reviews.author: Analiese E
reviews.title: War !!!
reviews.content: We had mixed feelings about this one. Some exhibits were interesting, especially the aircraft collection outside. Labels weren't always clear in English, and some sections felt outdated. Worth visiting if you're into military history.

reviews.author: Sarah E
reviews.title: Huge museum that’s worth visiting
reviews.content: They recently changed locations and the new museum is massive. Has three outdoor areas with US planes, and USSR planes and statues. The inside is giant as well. The museum shares their side of the history which is of course a little different then how the other sides portray it but very interesting to learn.

reviews.author: 건우 권
reviews.title: A Journey Into History
reviews.content: The various exhibits and materials were impressive, and we could feel the pain and hope of the war. It was a special time to share thoughts and deep conversations with each other and a meaningful place to learn a lot.🪖⚠️⚠️🪖🪖🪖🪖⚠️⚠️🪖⚠️ 🚁🚁🚁🚁🚁 🔫🔫🔫🔫🔫

reviews.author: Michael M
reviews.title: Oct 24. Read before you visit the museum.
reviews.content: Read the attached photo before visiting. Oct 24. Please read the attached photo before visiting. Museum has moved. As of 1 October.

reviews.author: Jorge G
reviews.title: Much of the exposure is missing
reviews.content: The courtyard of the museum, where it was most interesting, is completely empty. So it's not very worth it... the rest of the museum is pretty simple.

reviews.author: Andy S
reviews.title: Brings it all to life
reviews.content: Fascinating Military Museum focusing heavily on the US war but also highlights the turbulent history of this country. A must for military history fans.

reviews.author: Uzi H
reviews.title: Good but times wrong.
reviews.content: Class however shuts earlier then says. Didn't even reach the war against America. Very gutting considering it's importance.

reviews.author: Fabienne
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: I was very disappointed. Little information. The War Remnants museum in Ho Chi Minh City is much better because it gives much better information about how everything went in reality.

reviews.author: Stefano M
reviews.title: In transfer
reviews.content: The visit totally disappointed me because the "highlights" of the collection were removed pending a new set up elsewhere. Some "iconic" things are therefore no longer visible. Too bad, really.

reviews.author: Lachlan Reynolds
reviews.title: Cool experience
reviews.content: This was a really cool experience and saw a lot more than expected. The signs to get everywhere are quite poor but it is really special and I would certainly recommend

reviews.author: JFib
reviews.title: Total waste of time
reviews.content: DO NOT COME - they have moved all of the interesting exhibits and all of the tanks/aircraft etc to a new museum on the other side of town. I have searched extensively for the new museum’s address and have located the street but cannot find it on Google Maps - I don’t think it is open yet? Either way, the move is not signposted on the museum website or at the gates in front of the existing museum - they should tell you BEFORE you pay for a ticket to see this totally gutted museum. To the existing (now old) museum curators - why on earth have you replaced the now-moved exhibitions with an exhibition about the Belarus’ resistance of the Nazis during WW2? How is that relevant to Vietnam’s military history? Complete waste of time - don’t come here.

reviews.author: DranaiNguyen
reviews.title: The place to know the difficulty of Vietnam during the war
reviews.content: The place to know the difficulty of Vietnam during the war and the way to win of Vietnam. More over you can find the b52 airplane which was drop in hanoi

reviews.author: Timothy H
reviews.title: Avoid. Go see new museum
reviews.content: Very little here. Most of the key exhibits have been moved to the new museum. Make sure you visit the new museum when it opens

reviews.author: Bud R
reviews.title: Vietnam Military Museum
reviews.content: Museum shows exhibits realte to wars in Vietnam .Ideally located 15 mins walk from Old Quarter .Shows war memorial clothes/armour expkained well what occured .30000 dong to enter per person

reviews.author: Mark K
reviews.title: Don't Bother
reviews.content: Don't bother - most of the exhibits have been removed but they still charge full price to get in. Save your money - extremely disappointing!

reviews.author: Marley_Lew22
reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.content: All aircraft monuments on the outside of the museum have been removed. Some interesting exhibits on the inside of the museum but not worth visiting. Instead visit b52 victory museum, which features more interesting monuments and is overall better and free.

reviews.author: John R
reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.content: Place is run down half it’s not translated to English no clear order in which to walk so end up skipping sections and have to go back go to hoa lo prison much better experience

reviews.author: nzwestie
reviews.title: Visit just for the plane monument will make it worth is
reviews.content: It gets 'very good' only because of the plane monument outside.  So well done.  You can walk around it and get such different angles and each is great, also looking at the size etc of the bombs and shells.  The museum inside I was not fussed over, there were a few displays interesting.  All the other planes etc that are in the ad picture are not there, but as I stated - the one plane monument that is there is worth the visit.

reviews.author: Tanemahuta Gray
reviews.title: A must experience in Saigon
reviews.content: An awesome museum with very powerful images and storytelling of the tragedy of the different occupations and wars within Vietnam. A must experience!!!

reviews.author: Grace
reviews.title: Average Experience
reviews.content: This museum was a little underwhelming and didn't have the greatest first impression of the site.  The information inside the building is very informative and gives you a lot of information and detail although when we visited they had started to remove some displays outside.

reviews.author: ボボ
reviews.title: Vietnam War History
reviews.content: Here, a wide range of artifacts from the Middle Ages, the wars leading up to the founding of the country, and the Vietnam War are on display and explained. Outside, destroyed US military aircraft and bombs recovered from the Vietnam War are on display.

reviews.author: Javier P
reviews.title: Disappointment
reviews.content: When I went to visit the museum, the patio was empty, that is, there were no tanks or airplanes or anything, therefore I consider it totally expendable.

reviews.author: Michelle P
reviews.title: It's on the move!
reviews.content: Unfortunately the museum is currently moving to a different location, When we went there was no outside exhibitions. However, if you are interested in the Vietnam war, it is still worth a visit.

reviews.author: Michael
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.content: Very interesting museum, unfortunately no longer has an outdoor exhibition. Vietnam's fight for freedom is presented here (although in a rather propagandistic way, I think!). Lots of original artifacts, from the 9th to the 20th century.

reviews.author: Shane
reviews.title: Wouldnt bother
reviews.content: All the heavy equipment has been removed Its only a few rooms with small arms weapons. Not worth it. The B52 Victory museum and the air force museum are a better experience

reviews.author: Stijn R
reviews.title: Not special. Little information.
reviews.content: To be honest, the museum was a bit disappointing. The pictures also did not match what it actually was.The information given was largely a summary of dates and numbers. There wasn't really a common thread. Also, not all information could be read in English.The museum looked good and there were some nice attributes.

reviews.author: Thomas
reviews.title: Misleading pictures online, the planes and tanks had been moved
reviews.content: Really disappointed, the pictures on trip advisor still display tanks and the planes, only after arriving discovered they had been all moved

reviews.author: Jim B
reviews.title: Went for the Monument and the aircraft exhibits, only got the Monument (but it was worth it)
reviews.content: This is an iconic monument in Hanoi made up of parts of US aircraft downed over Hanoi during the war against the Americans and along side is the flag tower which is also situated in the grounds. However, the aircraft exhibits which formed part of the museum are no longer there and have been removed.😢 There are some display rooms and items recounting the French occupation and the war against America which is very interesting and well documented. Cost of entry is 30K (Dong) pp. I have given it 3 out of 10 as I really wanted to see, not just the monument, but also the aircraft as I am a bit of an avgeek so feel a bit shortchanged that they were no longer on display. Glad I went though!

reviews.author: bellemonde
reviews.title: What's the point of running this museum? Not worth your time and money
reviews.content: tiny amount of content for a national military history museum, atrociously little useful content and numerous historical inaccuracies such as geographic conflicts and even artefact descriptions. Minimal mention of the role of the Soviets, Vietnam War (aka American War), Cambodian–Vietnamese War, and the relation with the Chinese etc.Even at 30k VND ticket it is not worth the time, effort and money.

reviews.author: pfd104
reviews.title: Not really worth the effort
reviews.content: Unfortunately the static display of vehicles has been removed, the displays inside the buildings consist mainly of photos on the wall, that if you’ve been to any similar museum in Vietnam, you’ll had already seen.  Not really worth a visit in my opinion but having said that it’s only $2 - $3 to enter.

reviews.author: phil
reviews.title: Oh dear, oh dear
reviews.content: Only went to see the impressive looking display of aircraft and vehicles outside as per all the pictures - only the scrap plane statue remains 😢 - rest of museum is a bit dull

reviews.author: Adam
reviews.title: Great visit
reviews.content: Great place of information more related to the North. All the aircraft and vehicles are gone, unsure where or the future plan, no staff could tell me.Still worth a visit

reviews.author: Jacques
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Very cheap entry fee. Plenty of exhibits. Found it very informative. Takes approximately 90 minutes. Within walking distance to historic quarter and other tourist attractions.

reviews.author: nasser
reviews.title: Vietnam heroes
reviews.content: An excellent museum rich in the conflicts that Vietnam went through. It is worth visiting and seeing the Vietnamese heroes who sacrificed themselves for their country. It is not very large, but it contains many historical eras.

reviews.author: David S
reviews.title: All the planes and outside stuff moved away.
reviews.content: Most of the outside exhibits have been moved to another location. So not such a good visit now. This was a must visit museum before, but the interesting exhibits have now been moved some distance away. I suspect they may be repairing them as they must be deteriorating outside in the elements. Plenty of other military museums around Vietnam.

reviews.author: BrakiWorldTraveler
reviews.title: Good but HCMC War Remnants museum is better
reviews.content: This was a very similar museum to HCMC War Remnants museum we've visited two weeks earlier in Saigon. This one looks more like a showcase of ceased weaponry, so I preferred the HCMC one.Anyway, I suggest visiting and it's in the center of Hanoi in vicinity of the Flag tower.

reviews.author: Nico
reviews.title: 2Days in Hanoi
reviews.content: The exhibition was a bit “out of shape” also were some objects moved to an other exhibition. Definitely a big highlight is the crashed aircraft.

reviews.author: Shannon
reviews.title: Great Content
reviews.content: Way much better than the War Remnants museum in Ho Chi Minh. The museum is quite big so in terms of proper coverage expect to take more than an hour, maybe two. There's so much information and the building is well maintained, some of the toilets on the other hand are like construction potty, this needs improving. Highly recommend and remember they close for lunch from 11am to 1pm.

reviews.author: pieata
reviews.title: A history of how VIETNAMESE peasants, defeated a modern US army!!!
reviews.content: The foto history of The weapons etc, used by the Vietnamese Over their  war history!interesting  to see how a 3rd world nation  armed itself, to fightThe USA during the  1950s … armed with pop guns, pitchforks etc, and homemade rifles, etc, etc…against the modern weapons, the howitzers, tanks, etc, etc..the cluster bombs, agent Orange, Napalm, and other horrific weapons!Their country was scarred by indiscriminate bombing, Millions killed, and wounded.. with many scarred with horrendous injuries from NAPALM SPRAYED INDISCRIMINATELY FROM ABOVE.. INDESCRIBABLE   , HERIDITARY BODY MALFORMATIONS.. PEOPLE BORN WITH INTESTINES HANGING OUT FROM NO “ stomach walls, at birth”, and other malformedBody parts…But the Vietnamese hung on, until the ALMIGHTY USA finally Departed, DEFEATED, BY A RAG TAG MISFIT ARMY OF PEASANTS!!!!!But those scarred, will live on in a hell hole life!An interesting thought provoking museum..I did not think / believe that I spent over two+ hours here!

reviews.author: Shruti Pramod Reddy
reviews.title: educational
reviews.content: Visited here on the morning of Dec-23,2023.Interesting to learn about the fort, weapons, equipment, documents & vehicles of that time well preserved and captioned/explained.

reviews.author: Gert V
reviews.title: Disappointment
reviews.content: To our disappointment there were no planes and the tanks were no longer there.Adjust the photos if you please!!!!

reviews.author: kchJJ
reviews.title: Okay-ish Museum
reviews.content: A moderately engaging museum experience, showcasing an extensive collection of loot and weaponry captured throughout the centuries. Currently they seem to be in the process of moving the outdoor exhibition pieces to a new location, so a few of them were missing. History buffs might get a kick out of it, but for the average tourist it’s probably an okay-ish experience.Also you get access to the flag tower, which is a plus

reviews.author: Black_Father
reviews.title: Interesting but lacking in information
reviews.content: A military history museum that could have been so good but has now been neglected. There is a very large number of interesting objects here, but the English-language signs say nothing or in some cases are completely incorrect. However, with a good AI app or Google image search, you can get good information about most objects.The info that does exist reflects a different interpretation of history than the one normally taught in schools in Europe. Interesting to broaden the views.

reviews.author: Art S
reviews.title: An interesting museum
reviews.content: We were in the museum for several hours. The exhibits are interesting. especially airplanes. The museum is full of weapons and vehicles.

reviews.author: Susan C
reviews.title: A history of resistance
reviews.content: This was the first war museum we visited in Vietnam though not the last. It is an extensive museum that ended up taking the whole morning to complete. In the outside sections there are many examples of planes, tanks, rockets and artillery with clear signage. There are also interesting sculptures with some made out of the wreckage of bombers. This is also a simple way of visiting the Hanoi Flag Tower which gives you views over Hanoi and the museum from its first two levels.In the multiple buildings there are exhibits about the wars with China from 214 BC to 1789 and then the resistance against the French from 1858 to 1954 and the Americans 1954-1975. We saw again information on the 1972 bombing of Hanoi (there was also a temporary exhibition in Hoa Lo Prison). We sat through some tactical reconstructions of battles with AV presentations that lit up with lights showing offensive and defensive actions though the dialogue was only in Vietnamese. However, many of the signs include English explanations. On a practical note, some of these rooms are air conditioned and some use fans which were a relief in the September weather. This museum encapsulates the Vietnamese history of resistance to invasions and gives details of how they did it and the weapons and methods they used.

reviews.author: D13O
reviews.title: Good overview of the military prowess of Vietnam
reviews.content: Too be honest, it was a bit boring after also visiting the national museum and Hoa Lo Prison. A lot of images get recycled. However it does show that it is not a good idea to invade Vietnam in winter or any other season for that matter. Lots of exhibits and military material either home or Russian made and captured US material. Good place to spend an hour or 2.

reviews.author: Michael S
reviews.title: Cool things to see, good historical info.
reviews.content: Excellent museum, with a fair bit to see.  Several parts of it are outside, and when we went, it was hot.  Some of the indoor exhibits have some air conditioning, but some have just fans.  I would recommend it.

reviews.author: Paulo N
reviews.title: Warrant went to Vietnam, to fight with Viet Cong
reviews.content: I liked the quantity and quality of History on site, however I noticed that some rooms were disabled and a good part of the interactive material (maps with electronic subtitles) were not working. Another point that needs to be improved is the signage of rooms that are in other buildings. Without it, it is very easy to lose the chronological order of wars.

reviews.author: Alice S
reviews.title: Really enjoyed this museum
reviews.content: So so interesting. Plenty of English for those who don't understand vietnamese. Very enjoyable experience

reviews.author: mr g
reviews.title: Decent museum but too many exhibits were closed
reviews.content: 1/4 of the museum was closed but what they had was pretty good.  You have to look past the nationalistic  propaganda

reviews.author: TanjungBaraDiver
reviews.title: Fascinating look into Vietnamese history
reviews.content: This is a very interesting tour of Vietnamese history.  As a foreigner it's always fascinating to hear the "other" side of events that were big in your life.It's quite extensive but doesn't take too long to get around.  A guide may be useful.  Most displays have English (or close enough) descriptions of the items.  There's some amazing original military planes and armored vehicle used in the "American" war and since then as well.Take your time and wander around.  Be warned it's summer and very, very hot.  You'll need to take a few breaks in the air conditioned halls.  Take the time to read the signs.  It's very informative.

reviews.author: swexplorers2018
reviews.title: Vietnam's war history on display
reviews.content: Informative and inexpensive.  Lots of photos and war memorabilia. They will ask you to leave backpacks in free lockers. Cafes on site which was great for cold drinks on hot day.

reviews.author: Mark D
reviews.title: Good not great visit.
reviews.content: Only outside of the museum was open the day we visited. We got in for half price. Many cannons, bombs, a a few tanks and planes. Good not great.

reviews.author: ctm7944
reviews.title: Military History Museum
reviews.content: Rode GRAB Motorcycle to Military History Museum (30KVND/85 cents). FREE lockers for backpacks. You take the key with you. Bathrooms. This is where you can see the scraps of a B-52 and lots of other War artifacts. Open 8-11AM + 1-430PM. Entry 30KVND.

reviews.author: Gary M
reviews.title: A bit underwhelming. Could be so much better.
reviews.content: Like so many, I felt the museum to was a bit underwhelming and poorly laid out. It is 3 stars at the very best. I didn't mind the propaganda as it made it slightly more interesting.  It felt like a missed opportunity with mainly artefacts labelled and surrounded by pictures. This could be far more interesting with video footage and audio tours. Talks by veterens would be amazing. That said, to see one of the American helicopters on display was worth the entrance money alone.

reviews.author: Ali B
reviews.title: Worth a visit if flush with time
reviews.content: Covers full military history not just recent history. Good selection North Vietnamese and American equipment from the war. Downsides: not great flow around the museum I.e. easy to accidentally miss sections or go outwith chronological order. Be aware of bias in the telling of the French and American wars.

reviews.author: Shelley M
reviews.title: another museum
reviews.content: Think I had enough of museums when we arrived here.  I wanted to see the flag tower but husband and sons wanted to check out the museum too.  A few things labelled strange or incorrectly and not as well laid out as the one in Saigon, but the boys enjoyed it.  There is quite a few rooms to see and we found clean bathrooms which was a bonus.  Large coffee shop outside and a park opposite with a lot of young ones riding, skateboards and having fun.

reviews.author: intrepidtravelerfla
reviews.title: Humbling
reviews.content: In a word depressing.  Understand it was written in a different era but it is hard to accept that we treated other human beings as bad a this.  Not for the faint of heart.

reviews.author: Will B
reviews.title: Very interesting- not all that accurate
reviews.content: It was an interesting experience in Hanoi, and included a lot of impressive artifacts from the wars with France and the USA. It does a good job of showing the hardware used by the Vietnamese in their resistance.However- when it comes to impartiality and overall accuracy- it falls a tad short. Some of the claims made on the displays are interesting to say the least and the information about the individuals and the weapons do not always match up. A certain number of artifacts have the misleading labels and information attached to them, with some being blatantly incorrect.If you are going as a casual tourist to see the sights- it’s a brilliant stop and a nice slice of history. However, if you have more insight into the conflict you may find some of the information sketchy. It is interesting to see the other side, regardless.

reviews.author: Tc Vagabond Foodhound.
reviews.title: Great exhibits but captions need a lighter, less propagandistic hand.
reviews.content: Good exhibits.  Perhaps the US war was too recent to expect impartiality but as an earlier reviewer noted, that was interesting in a “meta” way.  Especially interesting: While the caption writers are pleased to condemn the US and France, they never use the “C” word (China), regardless of discussing ancient wars, the war with China following the US war, or current tensions in the S China Sea.   The whole place could use a renovation but the assets are very impressive and the English is mostly understandable.   (85%? )

reviews.author: Angela G
reviews.title: A must see.
reviews.content: Great museum with 2 main sections. Indoors covering the history of occupation of Vietnam over 1000 years from the Mongols up over and outdoors a display of military equipment. This place is extremely busy with bus loads of children arriving mid-morning, so go early. The display inside is written almost as a PR exercise for the Peoples Liberation Army. Don't expect impartiality. However, that was interesting of itself.

reviews.author: Steve Buckley
reviews.title: Rather Disappointing!
reviews.content: As members of the 20-strong Anglo-Thai Society Regional Tour Group, my wife and myself visited the Vietnam MilitaryHistory Museum this afternoon - something, after visiting both the Hoa Lo (Hanoi Hilton) Prison/Museum and Dien Bien Phu, I was much looking forward to.In the end it all fell rather flat as - despite some interesting hardware - the video of the famous 1954 Battle of Dien Bien Phu was largely inaudible! Not somewhere I would personally pay a return visit.

reviews.author: Alex H
reviews.title: Closes at 4:30pm so time your trip
reviews.content: We came here after visiting the Hao Lo Prison and arrived around 3:15, so perhaps didn’t give ourselves enough time due to the closing time of 4:30.Nevertheless there are some really interesting and cool things in the museum, such as real tanks, aeroplanes and vehicles, and military weaponry and guns. There are 5 sections in total with plenty of signs in English. Worth a visit if in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Kavinmcthurn
reviews.title: Learn a lot
reviews.content: Great musuem for our family with kids. Our kids learnt a lot about the wars happening in Vietnam and how much terrible the Vietnamese had to suffer during the war time and that is the reason our tour guide always told us that no more wars to Vietnam and other countries in the world

reviews.author: Rbansal2014
reviews.title: History packed in centre of Hanoi!
reviews.content: The Military museum in Hanoi has information about the different era of Vietnam and the struggle for independence from foreign rule, followed by the Vietnam War.The entry ticket can be purchased right at the entrance for 30.000/- VND.The museum displays a variety of weapons used by the Vietnamese people over time.It displays tanks and machine guns used in the war with USA.A good place to visit with kids and whoever is interested in the history of Vietnam.It is very informative and interesting!

reviews.author: John C
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: This museum was good, worth a visit, perhaps not the most dynamic, bits of used and captured military equipment to look at, reasonable displays, tidy and well maintained.

reviews.author: Olivia H
reviews.title: Enjoyable visit with our guide
reviews.content: We spent a few hours here walking around and taking everything in. There is a lot to see and read! We would recommend visiting if you’re in Hanoi and interested in history/the Vietnam War.

reviews.author: David M
reviews.title: Must see for the Military History Enthusiast
reviews.content: This military museum, while is needs a renovation, still is a great museum for Vietnamese military history with rooms for each chapter of Vietnam's past going back to antiquity.  Alot of great artifacts, maps and information inside the air conditioned museum. This includes 2 light up dioramas:  Battle of Dien Bent Phu and the Fall of Saigon. each has a 20 minute or so video presentation that illuminates the diorama as the ballet progresses.  Outside is a great set of military hardware on display.

reviews.author: wombatdavid
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: We enjoyed a walk around inside and outside. The Chinook helicopter is interesting as are the MiGs. Lots of interesting information in English and understandable pride in the victory over the imperialist USA. Entry ḏ40k and also got half price for student.

reviews.author: Jim Milton
reviews.title: Good place to visit
reviews.content: Worth a visit, a well laid out museum and good value for money. This place gives a good insight to the history of Vietnam, and the conflicts which have happened. The exhibits are well put together and displayed.

reviews.author: Tassie Carly
reviews.title: Definitely a must see
reviews.content: A fantastic collection of war equipment displayed proudly for the world to see. The exhibits were very good too and it was interesting to learn about the ingenuity the Vietnam people employed to win the war.great to be able to climb the tower too and get a better aspect on the ware equipment. The set out of the exhibit rooms was a bit confusing and could do with some better signage or maps.

reviews.author: N21dx
reviews.title: Superb collection of Military Artifacts
reviews.content: This was one of the best military's museum that I have visited before. Simply wonderful. They have exhibits of US's aircrafts that was taken down by the Vietnamese Army. They have amazing exhibits of how the Vietnamese Army fought and chased away the invading armies. After a trip here, I truly admire and respect the people of Vietnam more.

reviews.author: markllydselby
reviews.title: Very Good Museum With Unique Exhibits
reviews.content: Spent a great morning here. Unsurprisingly much of the focus is upon the French and American conflicts. I can't imagine that there's collection anywhere else in the world of US helicopters, planes, and other military vehicles to rival the one that the museum has

reviews.author: The flying Canuck
reviews.title: Military museum and citadel
reviews.content: Any museum of military history will peak an enthusiasts want to see coupled with the citadel makes for a great couple of hours. Yes things are dated but great representations of the major conflicts that Vietnam has endured, coupled with a visit to the citadel you will spend a good portion of the day, if your a history buff.

reviews.author: Khushbu Mehta
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: It was walking distance for us from the imperial palace. The sight of huge aeroplanes and helicopters and fighter jets and missiles just adds to the whole excitement. Once u enter the museum its a plethora of knowledge. They’ve displayed extensively about all the wars Vietnam has suffered over the ears. Must visit. Do hike the flag tower for some amazing views

reviews.author: Gmglcfc
reviews.title: Good photo opportunity
reviews.content: Military museum mainly covering the French and especially American conflicts . Quite a lot of army and airforce hardware including ex US as one would expect. The internal exhibits weren’t really that exciting . The Flag Tower is within the museum grounds which is worth a look. Overall, ok for a visit, good for photos of the planes and tanks etc but I thought the similar museum in HCMC was better.

reviews.author: cody
reviews.title: Should go to for military history
reviews.content: I've constantly been captivated by Military and war history, watching films and also playing games based war. It was a total treat for me to find out all of the military equipment along with ammunition. Everybody may not like it almost as I did. Though its an extremely cool spot to enjoy.

reviews.author: Hodges M
reviews.title: A great deal of history
reviews.content: it was fascinating to check out the edge of Vietnam. it is split in areas that are different plus you've to move around. a couple of trucks and also jets. and helicopters simply stay away from the toilets extremely horrible. you are able to spend in USD also.

reviews.author: Moss
reviews.title: Extremely informative
reviews.content: We enjoyed the tour of the museum, it's a lot to take a look at. You will find scores of artifacts, military equipment, along with war info. The museum is affordable, you have to time the go to of yours as there's a lunchtime break for approx. An extremely great must-do activity.

reviews.author: Eldredge
reviews.title: Great museum
reviews.content: Great museum of Vietnamese army history (which to ninety nine % of individuals would mean the French and american Wars) Dien Bien Phu area of French history great but Im guessing many people are simply enthusiastic about the US (and puppet South) vs North Vietnam. Really one sided propaganda version of events, that is really at odds with the typical US version of history - although North won, so in this instance they're permitted to create the story! Fascinating displays and also a lot of planes and tanks outside. It's a little overlooked as well as the US jets, particularly, would use a layer of paint and a little TLC, But usually, a fascinating museum in case you'd like historical past from an alternative viewpoint.

reviews.author: Obie
reviews.title: A Must see to recognize the country
reviews.content: An anticipated 1 hour visit considered three in addition. it is not a great deal the weighty equipment outside, It is the graphic photo's & the stories & volumes that choose them in this particular museum. I went out of the top part of Vietnam on the bottom part by train, passing through the farms & villages & this's what made it much more confronting to believe what a lot of Vietnam's individuals have lived through. check out the Museum & I am certain you will have different perspective on both the country and the folks.

reviews.author: Ephrayim
reviews.title: One more worth watching place
reviews.content: I went here and also discovered it truly informative. there's a replica of the last fight with the French, told in numerous languages such as English, along with demonstrating the way the Vietnamese wont the fight for independence, together with a different area focused on the war against America as well as the south.well well worth seeing.

reviews.author: Jacques d
reviews.title: Good but was expecting more
reviews.content: Not much info on the wars. Some firearm info was very limited and they called a m16 a ar15.. was expecting a lot more

reviews.author: AweSam87
reviews.title: Dissapointing
reviews.content: The museum itself is pretty good for 40k entrance fee, with 3 buildings each with 2 floors of exhibits and two outside displays of tanks and aircraft. However we were disappointed that none of the tv/videos were playing including the huge war map upstairs which looked impressive. The museum closes at 430pm and staff start locking rooms and buildings at 4pm so if you arrive after 3pm don't bother. I think you would need at least 2 or 3 hours to read all the exhibitions.

reviews.author: Toralin
reviews.title: Very interesting museum!
reviews.content: We recently visited this museum. It was pretty quiet due to the corona virus scare so we did not encounter any crowds. It's an interesting museum displaying a wide range of military artefacts, machinery and weaponry.Allow about 2 hours to view the exhibits.

reviews.author: Moltys73
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Give yourself a couple of hours to visit the Museum that closes for lunch. Some interesting information presented.

reviews.author: K&M rates plates
reviews.title: No logical layout
reviews.content: Quite disappointed with this as I was looking forward to it and it wasn’t the best. No logical layout to museum or indication where to stop and start tour. I would recommend getting a tour guide as most of the information is written in broken English. Tanks and planes outside are pretty cool

reviews.author: Graeme D
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Was good lots of interesting things to see and of course the other side of the story.Plenty of interesting info pictures, was good.

reviews.author: Kevin H
reviews.title: Military museum
reviews.content: The museum was well worth  the visit ,it was tidy and kept up lotts of info and good signage reasonable priced good value

reviews.author: Rincewind
reviews.title: Great displays, especially the outdoor displays.
reviews.content: There are many museums in Hanoi covering different branches of the military (infantry, air-force, B-52 defense, etc). This one is the most centrally located, just to the west of the Old Quarter near Hanoi Train Street and Lenin Park. The museum has is split over several buildings with displays on the ground and upper floors as well as several areas outside for larger exhibits such as tanks and aircraft. Most of the museum covers the colonization by, and war with, France. Only a fraction covers the war with the US or China, although the outside exhibits are mostly from the war with the US.There is a general lack of narrative to the museum. It is mostly just a display of stuff in roughly chronological order. Here's a thing, here's its name, that's it. The only exception is the audiovisual display about Dien Bien Phu which does a decent job of illustrating the order of battle.The best part is the outdoor exhibit. There are a decent number of airplanes, helicopters, tanks and artillery pieces. Make sure to go right to the back of the museum because there is more tucked around the corner that you might miss.

reviews.author: Thomas W
reviews.title: INteresting
reviews.content: An interesting presentation of Vietnam´s recent war historiy, with a lot of tanks, airplanes and other military equipment.

reviews.author: Chris & Tina
reviews.title: Worth a Visit
reviews.content: The visit here to this museum helped to put some perspective to Vietnams past both recent and ancient. The museum itself is quite disjointed and maybe a little sterile, however still worth a look if you are interested in history and understanding what makes the Vietnamese people unique.

reviews.author: digitalroc
reviews.title: For the Vietnamese people
reviews.content: The admission is only 40K VND, however the place was overrun with several busloads of Chinese tourists.  It is interesting to view Vietnam’s perspective of the war, however knowing that this is a tourist spot, English signs may be warranted.  The attraction was decent but really caters to the Vietnamese people, still worth a visit.

reviews.author: Artur
reviews.title: reorganization of the space and timeline
reviews.content: - Historical sequence is somehow confusing- A lot of interesting historical artefacts- need modernization on the display of information- need more contents in english

reviews.author: ChicoRanMan
reviews.title: Nicely Done
reviews.content: Enjoyed this museum with its large outdoor display of aircraft, tanks, helicopters and artillery. Inside, the museum displayed many photographs, documents and weapons of past modern wars in Vietnam. Not a lot of descriptions in English, but most items were identified in English.I felt it was a worthwhile visit.

reviews.author: mgantman
reviews.title: Cool, but not a must see
reviews.content: It was pretty cool to see some of the machines of war used during the Vietnam War, and the tower is beautiful, but not a must see.

reviews.author: Andrew C
reviews.title: Very Interesting
reviews.content: Very interesting artifacts and especially the photos. It’s laughable reading negative reviews about too much propaganda and not enough English translations. First off - it’s a museum for the Vietnamese people not Disneyland for westerners and hearing “too much propaganda” from anyone vaguely American is rich irony. Worth the money and you will leave w an appreciation for the Vietnamese spirit.

reviews.author: patli2015
reviews.title: Military Museum Hanoï
reviews.content: To understand Vietnamese’s history, you have to visit this place. It is very well done. The first time I was there, was more than 20 years back. The place is very well preserved maintained and updated. I am French, my grandfather was part of the colonialists, they wanted part of the cake: the Opium route. He stayed in Saigon 20 years. One of my uncle was born there. They left in 1911. When France lost Vietnam in 1954 (with USA help). America took over telling us, you French you don’t anything, we are taking over, and you’ll see how to handle the problem! It’s going to be quite fast. What they did, sorry, a shame! To end the war in 1973. Then to put an embargo during 20 years! Then to say sorry! No! Sorry my Vietnamese friends.

reviews.author: Simone B
reviews.title: Military Museum
reviews.content: Enjoyed the aircraft and helicopters but in the museum itself not all the exhibits were translated into English ( most were ) . Loved the statue of plane wreckage . Very enjoyable

reviews.author: DaisyM777
reviews.title: Interesting museum
reviews.content: There is a lot to see and learn in this museum.If you are in Hanoi in September( like us)visit the museum as early as possible,we went in the early afternoon and the heat was unbearable.      Definitely must see in Hanoi!

reviews.author: John E
reviews.title: Interesting War Museum
reviews.content: This is worth going to visit if you have an interest in war history. There are many planes and tanks from war with America as well as France. Recommended.

reviews.author: Bill C
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Not a bad collection. Price is cheap to get in. Interesting, as an American, to experience the war from the Vietnamese point of view. Layout is a bit confusing as you go to different buildings and the signage is not that great. Worth a look if you have time.

reviews.author: WileyCoyote2
reviews.title: Nice compact museum ,good exhibits of Vietnam war
reviews.content: Good range of equipment artillery,helicopters,tank and personnel carriersInteresting equipment of general infantry soldierLots of propaganda postersInteresting collection

reviews.author: Philip D
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: Very interesting museum to visit, well worth the entrance fee of about £2! Various rooms with the story of Vietnam and the wars. Great collection of war memorabilia.

reviews.author: Jim W
reviews.title: Military Musem Visit Hanoi
reviews.content: This was about a 20min walk from our accomodation & we decided to have a look at the musem.It has a morning sesion & afternoon sesion, we went in the afternoon, we arived at 2:30pm & left at closing time, 4:30pm. I would sugest getting there at 1:00 pm & taking your time, there is quite a lot to look at & read about if you have time. It has many displays describing the many wars/conflicts Vietnam has had through it's colourful history, much more than what I was ever aware of.There is a heavy influence in the displays from the Vietnam war, the descriptions are very one sided & that is to be expected. I throughly enjoyed looking through this musem & it has various displays upstairs & downstairs in each of the buildings, not to hard to figure out where you need to go.If you like military history, looking at the tools of war I would go & take a look at this musem.

reviews.author: chiangmaicharlies
reviews.title: Looks good, but .................
reviews.content: It's probably a good to very good war museum, but like many of Hanoi's museums, you have to be careful when you visit. Many are closed on particular days of the week, and for a longtime at midday. We arrived at Vietnam Military History Museum at one of these times so could not look inside.We were able to view some of the outside exhibits from the entrance, but guards stopped us going any closer. Shame!I'm sure it's worth a visit, but not worth waiting hours for it to open.

reviews.author: _clesste11
reviews.title: Check It Out if in Hanoi!
reviews.content: If you’re a lover of war history then this is a must. It isn’t just photographs and text, but actually planes and a couple tanks. Yet it’s still difficult to imagine that men got wounded or even died in such old relics. Also amazed that a few of the guns were actually handmade. Note that the place closes from 11:30 am to 1 pm for lunch, but there’s a coffee shop right next as a place to wait. Hopefully war history will teach us or remind everyone that war is horrible.

reviews.author: Loïc G
reviews.title: Impressive display of military equipment
reviews.content: I went to this museum very skeptical about what to see there but I actually had a very good surprise.The rooms about the different wars are well detailed with many interesting objects to see but the most impressive is the quantity of military equipment that you an see outside! It is actually quite rare to see such a great collection of planes, tanks, canons...Great visit for a very cheap price, only 40k for an adult ticket!

reviews.author: Mark
reviews.title: The Big One
reviews.content: I visited every military museum I could during my exploration of Vietnam and none even came close to the Vietnam Military History Museum, aka the "Army Museum". Hardware galore featuring as a centerpiece the distorted remains of an American B52 Stratocaster bomber shot down over Hanoi--grotesque modern art. It's a location you could easily spend an afternoon visiting. I slowly and methodically went through every gallery and spent an hour outside and felt I had seen it all, but it took nearly four hours. Right outside the gate I had a fantastic cup of coffee, but then--that's everywhere in Vietnam. Visiting Hanoi and missing this museum would be a big mistake. If you only see a single military collection, this is the mother of them all.

reviews.author: Antonieta
reviews.title: Only on the outside
reviews.content: I didn’t enter, only wandered on the outside, that is totally worth it!So many USA planes!And learning that the US dropped more that 5kk tons of bombs on Vietnam is scary!

reviews.author: Pushpal P
reviews.title: Nice collection of aircrafts from Vietnam war
reviews.content: This place has a good collection of aircrafts from vietnam war. Will give you good feel of what was the air power then. They even have some destructed b52 bomber. The SAMs tanks mig 21 and helicopter. You can also climb the flag tower for a brids eye view. Good place military aircraft lovers

reviews.author: Raymondale
reviews.title: Learn something about military
reviews.content: This museum presents the First and second Indochina wars from a Vietnamese perspective.there are plenty of authentic war relics, weapons...Interesting attractions include the wreckage of an American B-52 bomber, an M107 self-propelled gun, and a military tank that had ploughed through the gates of Saigon’s Presidential Palace...even i am not a fan of military,still learn something from the museum.the Flag Tower is beside the museum,admission is free from the highlands cafe.Opposite the museum,it is Lenin park,if you have time can relax there.

reviews.author: BelgiumWdb
reviews.title: Amazing stop in Hanoi
reviews.content: For all who like military history. Interesting displays, impressive collection of airplanes and helicopter from the Vietnam war. A bit one sided: who can blame them. :-)

reviews.author: Susannah P
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: Was rather looking forward to seeing the Vietnamese take on the war with America.  However this section of their history wasn't particularly well covered.However, it was reasonably interesting for a couple of hours

reviews.author: Mark M
reviews.title: Interesting collection
reviews.content: A great collection of military articles spanning the history of Vietnam, from tribal weaponry, cannons through to planes and helicopters from the American (Vietnam) War. Also some relevant modern sculptures and access to the flag tower.

reviews.author: KGB777
reviews.title: Interesting collection
reviews.content: We visited here together with the flag tower. There's a good collection of aircraft to see outside, which kept the kids entertained for a while.

reviews.author: Joe Clarke
reviews.title: Nice attraction but needs refining
reviews.content: After studying the History of Vietnam at university, my partner and I decided to visit this museum whilst on holiday in Hanoi. Whilst it was a lovely museum, with great indoor and outdoor exhibits. There are a few things which are incorrect; a lot of the aircraft plaques had generic captions such as calling numerous aeroplanes “helicopters” which was actually quite comedic after the tenth occurrence. Numerous pieces of military equipment were also labelled incorrectly such as calling an American M14 Rifle a “Vietnamese Rifle”. Other than these infrequent errors, my partner and I enjoyed our visit and would recommend it to others who are interested in military history.

reviews.author: leeoliver2018
reviews.title: The view from the other side
reviews.content: Quaint displays and a great explanation of Dien Buen Phu. Very interesting to see history from the other side’s perspective.  So this wasn’t a ‘Vietnam War’ museum and the US is the imperialist invader and its allies, including South Korea and South Vietnam, are puppet troops. Fascinating

reviews.author: John K
reviews.title: Worth A Visit - If Only For The Sculpture
reviews.content: a tremendous work of art - aesthetically rich - it's all there - form - texture - color - conflict - tension - balance - symbolism - and packed with triggers - whether intended or unintended - that hit you at your deepest - an intangible rightness prevailing - this gloating sculpture - of terror - of victory - of national pride - of humiliation - of destruction - of hubris - of ignorance - of death - this pile of junk - wreckage of French and American aircraft shot-down by Vietnamese troops in the resistance war against the French Colonialists and also in the United States Sabotage War in North Viet Nam - it's a big flip-off - perhaps rightfully so - and it is glorious -- so riveted - I was compelled to circle it - numerous times - and even after stepping away from the area - returning - to see it from all sides again - and again - as a whole - and then in sections - and finally small details - cracked windows - some equipment operating text - in English - spray-painted on what was the outside of a plane - the amount of smash in the smashed engines - element-worn wing-stars - scrapes and scratches - a head-height propeller jutting out beyond the guard line - long thin sheets of metal - able to catch enough wind to flap and sway but unable to tear themselves away - an - almost annoying in its nature-always-wins cliched self plant that has taken root amidst this chaos - and cherry-topping the entire heap - as if locking this all together - should you have any further questions - the torn-off - ill-divined - tail-end of an aircraft - a dunces cap - a peak - a shape - that from the symbols pounded into my head since before I am able to remember - conjures both Brazil's Christ the Redeemer - and Lebanon's Our Lady in Harissa - all here in this defiant - breathtaking work - in this bold abstract representation - of the other side of the story - on the other side of the world -

reviews.author: Kieron Ball
reviews.title: History in front of your eyes
reviews.content: For years I had heard from my instructors about their time in Vietnam during the war so it was like seeing their history come to life for me as I hadn’t seen most of the hardware before . The exhibits are described in English as well as Vietnamese and it was awesome .

reviews.author: Steve W
reviews.title: Brilliant museum.
reviews.content: An excellent collection of artifacts from Vietnam's military history that starts with internal fights during the formation of Vietnam, the several wars with different Chinese dynasties, French colonisation (twice), the Japanese in WWII, and finally the Vietnam War, (or the American War as it is known).Considering its size Vietnam has certainly held it's own throughout this history, surviving occupation and invasions.

reviews.author: Govindan N
reviews.title: Excellent Museum
reviews.content: The Vietnam Military History Museum Hanoi houses a collection of weaponry that was used in Vietnam War. Notable attractions include the wreckage of an American B-52 bomber, an M107 self-propelled gun, and a military tank that had ploughed through the gates of Saigon’s Presidential Palace, thus ending the Vietnam War in 1975. You can also find improvised weapons and exhibits of artefacts dating back to the Hong Bang Dynasty.Entry ticket to Museum -VND 30,000  Camera charges – VND 20000 Museum Opening Hours: Daily 08:00 - 11:30 Tuesday – Thursday, Saturday & Sunday 14:00 – 16:00

reviews.author: HistoryTravelSte
reviews.title: Interesting - Vietnamese perspective!
reviews.content: I really enjoyed the visit to this museum; it is well laid out, with a chronological approach to Vietnam’s military history. There is a fascinating range of artefacts on display, and some good models displaying key areas of the French and American Wars. As noted in many reviews already, much of the coverage is from the North Vietnamese perspective, but this doesn’t take away from a fascinating insight into the mindset of the Vietnamese people toward their military history. Highly recommend this museum for any fan of history.

reviews.author: Matthew P
reviews.title: Planes Tanks and Choppers
reviews.content: Interesting place to while away a good few hours learning all about the many atrocities that took place in what was the Vietnam war from the start, with conflicts with the French Imperialists from the early 1950's through to the 1975 liberation of Saigon and the reunification of this wonderful land.  There are also loads of old planes and other military hardware to look at from the US, China & what was the USSR.

reviews.author: Vignesh Srinivasan
reviews.title: Excellent museum with great displays
reviews.content: The museum had excellent open air displays of tanks, flights etc that were very realistic replicas of wartime. They also had a tall tower from where its excellent to view all the outdoor displays. The indoor displays depict wars from several centuries ago. There are 2 indoor museums. The only issue is that visitors may need to time their visit well - the museum opens late and closes by 4.30 PM.

reviews.author: 181ShellBell
reviews.title: Good Display and History
reviews.content: I took my 15 year old son to this museum which is in the same area as the Flag Tower.  We found this place interesting and enjoyed looking and reading what it offered.  I think it's worth a visit.

reviews.author: Denise S
reviews.title: Warmongering...... recent and past.
reviews.content: This Museum contains a lot of vintage, decommissioned, seized and destroyed machinery and vehicle from the different eras of the wars that occurred throughout the history of Vietnam. There was a lot of historical interest to be seen here,especially with the  remnants and whole machinery relating to the Vietnam War which mainly displayed captured American items.  There were also examples of Russian planes and equipment displayed. However there were artifacts and displays that encompassed from early precolonial history through to the First Indo -China war and the second. For me who loves old architecture, I was drawn to the Flag Tower of Hanoi which was built in 1812. I love flying so I was drawn to the planes and in particular the remnants of Aircraft wreckage assembled as monument. Quite sobering to look at the mangled machinery etc.There is a Highland Cafe, which is good for lunch or a coffee, and to have a rest before exploring the museum some more.  I would highly recommend visiting this museum as you can absorb the history through the Vietnamese perspective.

reviews.author: Jerzy N
reviews.title: Complete waste of money
reviews.content: All what’s interesting is outside for free. What you pay for is a propaganda how cruel French were and how humane Viet cong was. All on few photos and banners. Not worth money we paid.

reviews.author: John H
reviews.title: their side of the american war
reviews.content: this was rather too full of american hardware, although parts of a B52 have been used to make a sculpture.

reviews.author: HuahinCharlie
reviews.title: The American War
reviews.content: A nice walk from my hotel and stopped of to see the Flag tower and the incorporated Vietnam military history museum. If you are interested in this conflict and have seen Burns' documentary (among other things) then this is of interest with some 70's and earlier implements of war. The T34 inside was in great condition as was the A/C on the day I visited after depositing small rucksack at front desk. An APC was being worked on during my visit - must have been 40deg C + inside the hull.The downed US bomber was artfully arranged and there are a number of stalls for eats and drinks on site.

reviews.author: Craig D
reviews.title: Very different to the War Remnants Museum in Ho Chi Minh- worth a visit
reviews.content: The Vietnam Military History Museum is not as polished as the War Remnants Museum, nor is it as 'in your face'. This museum highlights the strengths of the Vietnamese and the wars and struggles that they have endured and won over the millennia. The War Remnants Museum is a reminder of the atrocities perpetrated by the US and allied forces during the Vietnam/US conflict.

reviews.author: Noam W
reviews.title: Good for those who have some knowledge
reviews.content: After 10 episodes of the epic Vietnam War documentary, by Ken Burns, this is a must see visit for the history of this sad war. Feel it from the eyes of the Vietnamese side. Exhibition it self isn't very much of a thrill, so an hour or two will be definitely enough to get the vibe

reviews.author: Travelingjohn123
reviews.title: Nice museum
reviews.content: Nice museum of Vietnamese military history (which to 99% of people means the American and French Wars)Dien Bien Phu section of French history very good but I’m guessing most people are just interested in the US (and puppet South) vs North Vietnam. Very one sided propaganda version of events, which is at odds with the common US version of history - but the North won, so in this case they are allowed to write the story! Interesting displays and lots of tanks and jets outside. It is a bit neglected and the US jets in particular could use a coat of paint and some TLC, But otherwise an interesting museum if you want history from a different perspective.

reviews.author: David Fredericks
reviews.title: Hanoi military museum
reviews.content: For anyone interested in the military history of Vietnam this is a must see. Many people will only comment on the Vietnam War (or more precisely the American War to the Vietnamese people) aspects of the museum but it covers the Vietnamese people's experience with war going back to the Chinese thousands of years ago and more recently the French in the 50s and 60s.Take your time to see all the exhibits and learn a bit about their rich history, not just the Vietnam War

reviews.author: TheDaddyP1967
reviews.title: Great to walk round and see items and stories of the past history of this beautiful country
reviews.content: Lots of artefacts and articles about the wars the country has been through some great war items they had a mig Russian fighter as well as some scraps of American bombers and different tanks and weapons. Hot day walking around but really enjoyed it.

reviews.author: Ian G
reviews.title: Worth Visiting
reviews.content: Lots of interesting things to see, a lot of artefacts from the American war on display as static displays. What i found fascinating is the displays devoted to the struggle for Independence against the French and how a grass roots movement grew into something that overthrew not only their colonial overlords but also succeeded in the American war as well.Interesting also to see a different slant on the American War to that of Hollywood and the popular media that we've been fed.i particulary like the central monument made from the remains from shot down aircraft, very effective i thought...

reviews.author: Cathee
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: There's an extended history of warfare in Vietnam. There's a saying " you've to be powerful or others are going to take you land". The museum houses parts from different wars were armies have taken the land of theirs and the Vietnamese have battled back. This extends back a quite a while. The greater recent Vietnam war is just a part of it.

reviews.author: Osgood
reviews.title: A must to see
reviews.content: I liked the museum as much as a place but at this point I'd gone to a few museums of the Military, Groundbreaking and Ho Chi Minh form in different locations in Vietnam and definitely the Prison Museum in Hanoi therefore I was somewhat tired of the propaganda and also the anti-American and anti-French bias as well as identical pictures. I suspect it will have made much more of an influence on me in case it was the very first one I'd been to. Nevertheless, it's a great museum of the kind of its, particularly in case it's the first of the kind that you visit.

reviews.author: Red
reviews.title: worth a visit
reviews.content: Interesting slant on Vietnamese military historical past from the early past to the current day. Nevertheless, in case you're extremely restricted, you are able to enter for free as there's a coffee shop adjacent with access from no restriction and the road on entering the museum campus. Once inside, your ticket isn't checked. having gone to the Hanoi Hilton earlier in the day' we paid our quid. You will find signs letting you know not to get on the exhibits, though I assume in case you cannot read English or maybe Vietnamese then you may think you are able to run riot! Hardly any information on the American war in this particular museum, virtually all of the exhibits are from the Chinese and french conflicts, nonetheless, the automobiles and planes come from the later battle. The Vietnamese are thin on specifics, exhibits simply let you know what the point is and often who donated it or maybe that glorious unit liberated it. Very little on the story of conflicts or perhaps any explanation of timelines or battles. Worth the coffee and an hour was excellent. The museum has toilets as well, which happens to be a bonus.

reviews.author: Eziechiele
reviews.title: Museum worth it
reviews.content: we have to see all points of reference to the history of ours. And it is not only around the impact on the war on Vietnamese but additionally the Americans and the children of theirs. The truth is quite thought provoking about companies and the contribution of theirs to wars as well as the American options in just how we battle them.

reviews.author: Carmen T
reviews.title: Biased
reviews.content: Cost about 40 000 VND to get in .  There are alot of things to see such as aircrafts, tanks,  weapons and even a flag tower. Its a cool place to check out the history however it is very biased so take it as a grain of salt.  Some images may be gruesome to see. It is worth checking out and reccomended to spend 90 mins there to see it all.

reviews.author: CSQUARED
reviews.title: Cool museum and exhibits, very hard to navigate and too much propaganda
reviews.content: The museum has extremely cool pictures from the wars against the French and Americans. However, the text descriptions of what occurred during the wars were extremely vague and in embarrassingly broken english for a museum. Also, the propaganda in the way they portrayed the war against the Americans while dismissing the Southern Vietnamese as simply puppets was a little ridiculous. Was hoping to get the North Vietnam perspective of the war, instead just got a bunch of lies and misinformation.

reviews.author: paul w
reviews.title: Very well organised and interesting museum
reviews.content: I must confess having a father in the military I tend to always be particularly interested in military history and artefacts. The museum is laid out across several buildings and floors in a chronological order (if you enter by the wrong door you’ve suddenly find you’ve skipped twenty years). Almost all of the exhibits have English translation - some incredible historic photos and a lot of very interesting facts and information provided. Found it very well balanced and for me, minimal propaganda against the various enemies they have faced over the centuries (and beyond). The are a number of tanks, planes etc in immediate view but don,t miss the hardware on display behind Building 3 ( it’s not that obvious)

reviews.author: aaong86
reviews.title: Interesting history of Vietnam
reviews.content: The museum consists of various buildings. Different eras of Vietnamese military history are showcased in different buildings. The Flag Tower of Hanoi is within the bounds of the complex as well.The entire complex was huge and I spent quite a few hours walking around. There were thousands of exhibits (mostly artifacts) with English explanation.A must visit when you are in Hanoi!

reviews.author: Gary E
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: We enjoyed the tour of the museum, it has plenty to look at.There is lots of artifacts, war information and military equipment. The musuem is reasonably priced, you need to time your visit as there is a lunch break for approx. 1 1/2 hours. A really excellent must do activity.

reviews.author: Patrick D
reviews.title: Vietnam Military History Museum
reviews.content: The Museum of Military History makes it possible especially to understand the Vietnamese history since 1945 until now. More than 2 thousand documents and precious objects give a glimpse of the evolution of the country from the time of the Hung kings to that of Ho Chi Minh. But it is especially the period of the wars of Indochina and Vietnam during which Vietnam sought to regain its independence against the French and then the Americans which is highlighted.The museum is divided into six parts: the Vietnamese heroic mothers, a heroic nation, the heroic people's army of Vietnam, the traditions of the Vietnamese People's Army, weapons and weapons manufacturing, the support of the international community in Vietnam during the war and relations between the Vietnamese People's Army and other countriesNational relics are exhibited such as the MIG 21 aircraft driven by Pham Tuan during the 1972 battle of Dien Bien Phu. tank 843 which broke the gates of the Independence Palace on April 30, 1975, ending the Saigon regime See also the citadel of Thang Long and the Flag Tower which offers a panoramic view of the city i. This observation tower built in the 19th century is one of the few ancient Vietnamese buildings that were not destroyed during the French colonial period. Very interesting museum because it presents the military strategies put in places, and one discovers there the technical dimensions of a warThe museum is opposite Lenin ParkEntry fee for foreigners: VND 40,000 / personSupplement for a camera, phone: VND 30,000Next to the museum, there is a cafe with a very large shaded terrace, possibility  to have a drink, (  very good pastry,)  restaurant

reviews.author: Polisgirl
reviews.title: Really interesting
reviews.content: This is great for anyone interested in history.  The exhibits were really informative and the photo opportunities with the tanks and helicopters were good.

reviews.author: Christy V
reviews.title: Great place to visit
reviews.content: Interesting military history to learn about with many exhibits to view. A large outdoor collection of aircraft as well. We were glad we stopped by to tour.

reviews.author: Bangoe
reviews.title: Glimpse of history
reviews.content: Interesting place to visit to learn about the history of Vietnam. Rather well laid out. I just do not understand why they charge extra for "camera". Almost as much as for a person. Especially as taking photos with your phone seems to be free (everyone did it).

reviews.author: Mike K
reviews.title: Cheap entry and worth a visit if your in Hanoi.
reviews.content: Spent a couple of hours here, lots to see including planes, helicopter, tanks and other vehicles.  The flag tower is also incorporated in this area.

reviews.author: gastronaut_11
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Good chronological history of the military struggles that Vietnam has undertaken through the ages. Most relics relate to the French colonialism era. Certainly worth a visit. Cheap entry fee. Watch out for the buses, which park immediately adjacent to the outdoor sited planes and armour.

reviews.author: Andreaobrien1
reviews.title: History of wars in Vietnam
reviews.content: This museum takes you through all the history of conflicts that have impacted Vietnam from the Chinese occupation, french and Vietnam war in the 60s, 70s. Some great photos and images, like the prison much propaganda but you can see the struggle of the people and the country. Plenty of Russian, Chinese and USA military artefacts.

reviews.author: lucasjnl
reviews.title: Must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: Various buildings with extensive displays. Big choppers outside. Especially the French colonial war section was an eyeopener. The Dien Bien Phu presentation is very striking with a complete lightshow of strategic moves. Beware of the curious siesta opening hours. Complementary to the War Remnants Museum down in Saigon.

reviews.author: PETER J
reviews.title: A Must see to understand the country
reviews.content: An expected 1 hour visit turned to 3 plus . It's not so much the heavy equipment outside , it's the graphic photo's & the stories & numbers that go with them at this museum . I went from the top of Vietnam to the bottom by train , passing through all the farms & villages & this is what made this far more confronting to think what so many of Vietnam's people have lived through . Visit the Museum & i'm sure you'll have different outlook on both the people & the country .

reviews.author: Badger
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: Well worth a visit depicts the history of Vietnam for thousands of years and of course the 60’s:70’s , obvious North bias with references to the Puppet south but a very interesting visit that I recommend

reviews.author: ZBH88
reviews.title: Grizzly
reviews.content: A very deep and matter of fact portrayal of the war in Vietnam. Accurate as war is war and it doesn't discriminate. It's 40000 to enter each and younger children are free. Children of all ages are allowed but it's your choice if you feel it suitable as there are many colour photos and grapgic descriptions of deformities resulting from the use of agent orange, torture being carried out and dismemberment/dead bodies. We took our 2 year old but he is too young to pick up on it. There are a number of militarty planes, helicopters and artillery in the yard outside of the museum. There are toilet facilities on site and the odd gift shop.

reviews.author: pratikshahi
reviews.title: Must visit for military history
reviews.content: i have always been fascinated with Military and war history, watching movies and playing games based war.  It was an absolute treat for me to see all the military equipment and ammunition. Everyone might not enjoy it as much as i did. But its a very cool place to explore.

reviews.author: Karina P
reviews.title: War is over
reviews.content: I don't find war that intertaining, think it is sad. Costs 110.000 in all for 2 people with camera. It is quiet a big place, and guess you could spend a couple of hours there, 2 hours was enough for us. Non of the videos and audio worked. The most interesting was all the old airplans, choppers and tanks. You can also see the flagtower on this trip.

reviews.author: Vasudev68
reviews.title: A must visit
reviews.content: Located in old Hanoi city area, it houses various military equipment. It also has planes, helicopter, ammunition seized from Americans during their long battle. It has an in-house theater showing  small movie clip on early wars.

reviews.author: BC
reviews.title: Really Good
reviews.content: This was a really good visit, showcasing such of the military history of Vietnam, with many big planes and tanks to look at too. It was very sobering in places as it detailed the horrible acts of the americans, which really made you think. A must see.

reviews.author: Carolyn C
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: Whilst we aren’t military people, we visited the museum whilst in Hanoi and OMG, this place blew my mind. It has so many artefacts and the history displays are so informative. My 11 year old son learnt so much and so did I. If you have time, make sure you visit, but note that it is closed at times during the day.

reviews.author: Alex C
reviews.title: Badly organised and uninformative
reviews.content: Really disappointed by this museum. The layout was so unclear we found ourselves skipping around chronologically quite a bit.I wanted to go to find out more about the first and second Indochina wars. To be honest, I learnt nothing (certainly nothing I didn't already know - which isn't much). There's a lot of pictures of Uncle Ho meeting with various parties, signing documents etc. but not enough content/text to really get an idea of what is going on. The second Indochina war (the Vietnam War) got a little bit tedious to be honest. Being neither American nor Vietnamese, I don't have ultra strong views on the war and I do have some sympathy for a Hanoi museum showing a bit of a one-sided picture. That said, there's a limit to how many times you can be presented with VC weapons used to bravely, annihilate the enemy excellently while similar looking US weapons were used to torture and kill and not got a bit bored.Of course, facts and artifacts don't lie. There were a number of military vehicles to look at. If you enjoy watching hoards of Chinese tourists trample over 'Do not cross' signs and clamber into the museum's private property (jeeps and planes) then this museum is a must see.

reviews.author: GWYN33
reviews.title: Sobering visit
reviews.content: Superb collection of military artefacts greet you - People forget that the Vietnamese were involved in a series of wars of liberation from the French and later US intervention - this is all chronicles here in an excellent museum. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: ESVincent
reviews.title: Everyone goes and there is a very good reason...
reviews.content: This Museum is very much on the tourist trail both Vietnamese and International but having said that it never feels over whelming. The story told is unsurprisingly one of throwing off Colonial oppressors whether those are Thai from the 14th C, the French or later Americans. It is of course the French and American conflicts that dominate but their is long history of independence struggle and you do wonder how both the French and Americans misread the tide for independence for so long. The atrocities are one sided though and don't show the total picture.The Museum has an amazing range of vehicles, planes and items but not everything is explained. This is a worthwhile visit if only to look at historical folly . Fascinating

reviews.author: Granduelle
reviews.title: Interesting but more explanations in English would be great
reviews.content: It's worth a visit, collection of some heavy machines like war planes and tanks, plus various smaller items like weapons, clothes and loads of pictures. A little effort in translating more if what's there into English would be nice.

reviews.author: Chris J
reviews.title: Great amount of Military History
reviews.content: Worth a visit to walk around and view the Historical Military machines, good amount of literature in the museum

reviews.author: Paul O
reviews.title: Good, but not great...too one sided
reviews.content: The planes, tanks, helicopters and more were all in excellent condition and really impressive to look at. The narrative of the war history of vietnam was extremely one sided though. In both the French and American wars in Vietnam there was great victories and terrible loses on both sides but you only hear about Vietnamese victories in this museum so not really getting the full facts. Found the French war narrative much better too (albeit one sided) where it went through the various years and events and how it started and ended. American war narrative just started in the middle and had no ending so if you didn’t know the full info of the war prior to going in you’ll be none the wiser coming out of here. Very cheap to enter though (40k pp), worth a look if you’re nearby.

reviews.author: Richard B
reviews.title: A Fair Four
reviews.content: Vietnam is synonymous with the American war of aggression that last a considerable time.The museum doesn't glamourise events or attribute any blame.  It just presents information,  photographs and exhibits. Very interesting and sad in equal measure.   Well worth a visit.  Maximum 1-2 hours would be suffice for this attraction.Some tanks, planes, weapons etc.  Relatively inexpensive too.

reviews.author: Jalal Iqbal
reviews.title: proud history of Vietnam
reviews.content: not a big museum. yet nicely kept war crafts, clean and well maintained. entry fee could have been a bit less comparing the prices in VN. liked it much to see the proud history of a nation who defeated the aggressors.

reviews.author: StuandSue23
reviews.title: vietnam military museum
reviews.content: The museum buildings were closed but we were able to walk around the outside for only 20 Dong each.Was a great couple of hours. The plane statue was quite moving.It was raining but plenty of shelter.

reviews.author: kevin r
reviews.title: Quite small but very interesting.
reviews.content: You pay 40k/VND and you have 2-3 hours of walking around. Start from 1940 until the end of 1980s. 4 buildings with 2 floors with things, weapons and information. They also show you a movie for 20 minutes of the war that was quite interesting. It was a little bit hard to understand where you go after the first building to follow the path. We walked from old town and it took 15-20 minutes, no need to take a taxi.

reviews.author: Sheffield_Boar
reviews.title: Slightly one-sided
