reviews.content: An interesting museum with the display of military hardware the obvious draw. The information about the war and the exhibits are definitley from a Vietnamese viewpoint. Some would call it propaganda but I found it fascinating. Why shouldn't it be from a Vietnamese point of view...it's in Vietnam.

reviews.author: jamie R
reviews.title: Missed opportunity
reviews.content: Propaganda all over and very little substance or proper information to tell the story of the vietnam war.Some interesting photos and a bunch of harware stacked outside but a badly put together presentation and distorted dialogue. Visitors deserve better.

reviews.author: Gary
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Came to visit the tower and did not even know the museum was here. We were drawn in by the exhibitions and ex military vehicles on display and spend an interesting hour or two here.

reviews.author: Grahame H
reviews.title: An Insight into the Military History
reviews.content: A fascinating place to visit. I was there to see the aircraft and I was not disappointed. many of the items could do with renovation but never mind that may come one day.

reviews.author: Maytrea
reviews.title: See the planes
reviews.content: This is a must-see on all tourist visits to Hanoi, and puts a very clear point of view on the war. The mangled B52 sends a clear message, but for this reason and others, it is an interesting place to visit. Less shocking than its counterpart in Ho Chi Minh City. It isn't a big exhibition, and can be done in an hour. Look out for the guy outside selling  Bao inh's book, which is worth reading.

reviews.author: Anil L
reviews.title: Only if you are interested in Museums
reviews.content: Its only for those who love to go to museums. And also who are interested in weapons. Otherwise, it can be a very boring place.

reviews.author: William K
reviews.title: Gross omissions
reviews.content: This museum presented an excellent overview of the American and French Agent Orange. What was glaringly missing was an account of the mayham created by the Viet Cong and VCN against the Americans.  The French were properly villified.

reviews.author: DAVID L
reviews.title: Military History on View ...
reviews.content: This museum tells and shows the military history of Vietnam with displays of military items from all periods of history. Heaviest on items from the French and American wars.

reviews.author: SouthPerthAustralia
reviews.title: A timely reminder of the resilience of the Vietnamese people
reviews.content: We only saw the outside exhibits and climbed the tower but that was itself sobering.Recommended for a perspective of 1965-75.

reviews.author: Northern Correspondent
reviews.title: Part of Vietnam’s History
reviews.content: This museum is worth stopping at if you are touring the City.It’s relatively inexpensive and provides a useful insight to Vietnam’s history and struggles with invaders as well as a background to colonial France and the American intervention in the 60’s and 70’s.There are plenty of artefacts to look at including military apparatus within the outside viewing areas.

reviews.author: Gee Gee
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Great museum to visit. Great display of war air crafts and weapons. Everything is translated in English which made things easy. Allow 1.5 to 2 hours for the visit. A few gifts shops are on site and a great Highland coffee shop just outside.

reviews.author: aljoneill
reviews.title: Interesting but lacks detail
reviews.content: The weaponry, aircraft and vehicles were interesting to see but if you’re a person that wants specifics, you’ll be disappointed. The firearms, aircraft etc... had random information noted, regarding who they supposedly belonged to and what battle they were used in but no technical info. There were also odd display pieces like a “hand bag, documents were carried in” which didn’t really seem to fit. It was still interesting to see and the heavy weaponry and vehicles especially in the outdoor area but if you’re a big military history buff you may find it slightly lacking.

reviews.author: Simone B
reviews.title: Military Museum
reviews.content: Enjoyed the aircraft and helicopters but in the museum itself not all the exhibits were translated into English .Saw wedding day event in park next door too

reviews.author: KenVicLee
reviews.title: A Different Perspective On The War
reviews.content: This museum frames the Vietnam War as one of independence. It is housed in a three story building with a number of tanks, jets and other armament outside as you walk up to the museum. I started on the third floor and worked my way down. Events that American history depicted as being one thing are depicted completely different in the Vietnamese telling. This was less about the government being socialist and more about being abused by the French during colonization as they raped the land of natural resources. I wish I had more time to read every description of the events show in photographs throughout the museum. It just goes to show there are different perspectives on many things.

reviews.author: R K L
reviews.title: Old relics of bygone era...
reviews.content: The Vietnam Military History Museum was interesting from the standpoint of seeing how many confilcts have dominated the country's history. The crowning achievement of this museum was to memorialize Vietnam's wars. Our local guide insisted that we see this "magical" museum which was average at best. Our observation is that it was neither worth the entry fee nor time spent.

reviews.author: D_and_G_2008
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: Very unorganised and most materials do not come with details information or information in English.  Thus, difficult to browse around & make sense of the history.

reviews.author: Ian D
reviews.title: Eye opening!!
reviews.content: More confronting than I had expected, but very worthwhile for the lessons in recent history. So much to read, so much to see. Ensure that you allow enough time......

reviews.author: noodlepillows
reviews.title: Informative and lots to look at
reviews.content: This museum surprised me with how many aircraft's, tanks and helicopters there are to look at. I wasn't expecting any. The museum has a lot of different buildings to go into and upstairs also. No maps were available when we visited so make sure you poke your nose into all the buildings to make sure you don't miss out on anything.  Very informative and eye-opening.

reviews.author: MiniBanner
reviews.title: Great place to learn about Vietnam war
reviews.content: This museum is just about a 15 min walk from Hanoi Old quarter. It's a great way to spend a couple of hours looking at the various Vietnam war weapons (tanks, a chinook, torpedos, US bombs etc.) they have on display . They also have some memorabilia from earlier battles with the french but the recent historical artefacts are more well preserved. The entry is cheap at 40,000 dong and no guide required since there is enough documentation everywhere. Thoroughly enjoyed my time time here and it got me more interested in reading about Vietnam war history.

reviews.author: amber g
reviews.title: Must DO
reviews.content: Take  a local tour guide when visiting. The details can matter a lot .We are a  family of 5 and contacted Hanoi Free Walking Tours who provided us a local guide named Peter, extremely friendly and informative and eager to share details. Loved the trip and insights provided.

reviews.author: AndyPG
reviews.title: Fascinating history
reviews.content: The museum starts with old Vietnamese military history and artefacts. Very interesting as they managed to kick out the Chinese on multiple occasions. Then it moves to the Vietnam war. It’s closed from 11.30- 1.30. Also I walked to the place from pub street and wasn’t that far but looked further on the map. Some of the presentations are a little over the top re propaganda but they have extensive military hardware and exhibitions. It’s a little bit sporadic with the buildings but just remember when you’ve been to S1, S2 etc. There is a big coffee, drinks and food snack area attached.

Really good museum! 40,000 vnd entry fee (£1.30), I visited assuming that it would just be full of the American Vietnam war artefacts, but there is a broad range of items dating back centuries. Vietnam has a really fascinating history and this museum is well worth a visit. Outside there's plenty of planes, tanks and am American helicopter. Awesome!

reviews.author: Jess G
reviews.title: Let down by lack of open exhibitions
reviews.content: My partner has just left the military so when we walked past the museum and spotted the outdoor display of tanks we decided to go in and take a look around. The display of vehicles and weapons is really interesting and it was nice to climb up the ancient flag tower - but that was about all we could actually see. The front doors to the museum were locked with no sign or explanation as to why, and we could only access one exhibition room as the others were also shut. Having paid 40,000VND- which is more than most other museums and sights in Hanoi - and not being told it was partly closed beforehand we were pretty disappointed.

reviews.author: Wandering Traveler
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Interesting! Beware at 11:30 you are out of all buildings. Everyone goes to lunch 11:30 A.M. till 1:00 P.M. Staggered lunch hours are unheard of I guess. Shows the warfare history of Vietnam from ancient China's Dynasties to present day as a socialist country. Plenty of photos showing armed female soldiers. But their enemies always killed unarmed woman & children. The Ha Noi Flag Tower is on this property.

reviews.author: Peter F
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Has some interest for teenage son to check out too. Interesting and quick and easy to walk around. Outside display of planes and choppers. Don't get a taxi by metre reading- ask for price upfront or refuse ride.Otherwise the metre reading is a major rip off.

reviews.author: stewartgt
reviews.title: Interesting for a broad range of military exhibits
reviews.content: Museum houses a broad range of different artifacts with many large pieces on display.The bias is understandably anti-imperialist/US as would be expected, but its not too heavy handed and you can still enjoy looking at the various displays for an insight into the military conflicts that have taken place over time.In the center forecourt there is what I understand is a downed B52 bomber complete with jet engines and the rest which is quite interesting. Also various planes, helicopters, ordnance and tracked vehicles that you can get right up next to and underneath. Again pretty interesting to see the technology up close.The museum also has the Flag Tower of Hanoi you can enter (free) which gives a nice view of the area.Guided tours are available but not really necessary in my opinion if you prefer to explore at your own pace.Well worth a few hours especially for military buffs. Also they don't charge for photos if only using your phone. I'd suggest if you were discreet on entry you could use an DSLR without any issue as well.

reviews.author: khm2412
reviews.title: For Military History Buffs
reviews.content: We visited on a Monday, when the main museum was closed. Access to the external exhibits was possible, but not enjoyable due to a rainstorm. Several Vietnamese War era aircraft and fighting vehicles are on show in various states of decay, surrounding a symbolic pile of aircraft wreckage, evoking the futility of war.  I plan to return some time when the weather is kinder.

reviews.author: Joseph The Don
reviews.title: Worth a visit even just to see the tanks
reviews.content: The museum itself and story of the Vietnamese fight against the French and Americans - is very difficult to follow. The museum houses a selection of captured and collected 'stuff' with bits of story built around it - so it is very difficult to follow the historical flow of events. The Dien Bien Phu diorama is suprisingly educational though - so give it 5-10 minutes - it feels very odd at the start. But where the historical value is very poorly organised and curated - the ability to walk amongst the military vehicles and aircraft from the wars (both Vietnamese and captured American) is worth the few bucks. You can touch the tanks, and get a feel for their size and peer into an American Chinook helicopter. Where do you ever get to do that! A good pit stop on the way to the Mausoleum.

reviews.author: TonyPullen
reviews.title: A good educational museum
reviews.content: Wasn't a place I planned to visit but our guide took us there and it seemed rude to say I wasn't interested. Came away with a better understanding of just how much the Vietnamese were used as a pawn in the power game between USA and Russia as well as an appreciation of how industrious and resilient the Vietnamese people have turned out to be. Its definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: NickP22
reviews.title: Avoid
reviews.content: I prefer not to give poor reviews, but unless you are really into your Vietnamese history, I would avoid. There is no discernible organisation here, I don't know if we saw 25% , 50% or what of the exhibits.. no signs to say where to go next or what the room is about.. there are a few old planes a Huey and a Chinook, and some really aged of Viennese jets.. like everything here, the cost in minimal, so if you have time to kill, give it 30 minutes, no more

reviews.author: gr87_13
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Visited on a recent trip to Hanoi. Would recommend going if you are interested in history. The old aircraft outside was particularly good

reviews.author: TheLeongOhana
reviews.title: War from Vietnamese Perspective
reviews.content: This was one of a couple museums I cobbled together during a walk around Hanoi on a Sunday.Outside the museum is quite an assortment of military vehicles, bombs, misled and aircraft.  They are in fairly good condition.  In the center of the outdoor display is a remarkable monument pieced together from many different airplanes downed by the Vietnamese during the war with the United States.The museum is comprised of two buildings.  Both buildings cover displays about war heroes, epic battles, armaments and uniforms and dioramas.  On the second floor of the second building they have a short movie and a diorama that covers one of the battles against the French.  As the battle progresses you can see the LED lights blinking on and off showing troop locations, movements and the advances of the Vietnamese as they overrun the French.  As an FTI, they do turn off the lights in the room during the show.There is a cafe nearby if you want to grab a Vietnamese coffee or food.  It seems common at museums here.  Bathrooms are located in between the buildings on the first floor.  Condition was ok.

reviews.author: Tony C
reviews.title: Interesting but nothing special!
reviews.content: Interesting but nothing out of the ordinary.  Huge display of actual military vehicles, planes and helicopters used in their various wars.  Exhibits in doors with buildings throughout the area of the museum.  Displays and exhibits of various equipment and memorabilia in & outdoors!

reviews.author: Liam T
reviews.title: Very disappointing not like a UK museum
reviews.content: This must be the worlds smallest museum inside the actual building. It was very basic and my girlfriend saw a rat running across outside from inside. Which made her not really want to look around the outside. The outside is ok. The big Tank and War Plane can draw you in. However they are maybe the best things to see.  Outside they then have a viewing tower which looks nice but is nothing special and then some Army Vehicles that were caught by the Vietcong. They are ok to look at but tbh you could Google them. And if you are from the US you could see them most likely in the US, same with UK the imperial war museum in London is much better. I can't remember entrance fee but it was most likely more than it should have been. They have a nice sculpture of a falling place. Which was Most likely the highlight of the trip If you have money to spend/ free time then go for it. Or if you are a lover or studier of these type of Vehicles.  If not then give it a miss

reviews.author: Guillaume B
reviews.title: Nice museum!
reviews.content: The museum part is not so nice and look very old.. but the flag tower and also the exhibition of plane and tanks,.. is very interesting!

reviews.author: Jazzy1995
reviews.title: Great museum to visit!
reviews.content: It is located within a great walking distance from the Old Quarter, is opposite a statue of Lenin. There is a small entrance fee, but you will have to pay slightly more to take pictures which is still very reasonable. There are lots of tanks, planes, guns, helicopters, and other weaponry to see outside (from both the Vietnamese and American armies which were seized). Inside the museum there is lots of information on the Vietnam war, and is a great place to spend a 1-2 hours. In the same complex there is also a flag tower which you can go up, and this provides a nice view of all the vehicles and machines at the museum.

reviews.author: Dave
reviews.title: Chaos
reviews.content: We went here after we went to the old jail in Hanoi a couple of blocks away.The first thing when you come on the terrain is that you need to pay to park your scooter here besides paying for entering the museum. Found that a bit odd because it's not public ground, you come there to visit the museum...When you bought the ticket you're on your own.. which is not a bad thing if there is good guidance threw signs etc.. but that's not the case.We found ourselves entering certain exhibitions at the wrong end and not knowing where to go next.It's a very bad organized museum..The war machines are stuffed in a corner, and the, as they put it on the signs, "national treasures" old fighter jets are next to a scooter parking place next to the busy road.Overall a not very good experience.We were done with the exhibition very quick and wanted to get a drink, but you pay the jackpot on the terrace there, so we left.

reviews.author: David F
reviews.title: Propaganda plus
reviews.content: Found it fascinating. The early stuff was not my thing but the war against the US was superb - lots of captured hardware and some artwork too. Not wishing to generalise but males may find it more interesting than females.There's some great propaganda of support from nations around the world - mainly communist states such as Bulgaria, Cuba etc but also protests in the US, UK and Australia. There are good views from the bell tower and although you're not supposed to take photos from the top, you can get a great one of the helicopter and planes at the bottom.I enjoyed it but it won't be everyone's cup of tea!

reviews.author: Andrew B
reviews.title: Good Museum
reviews.content: Enjoyed looking around museum showing history about Vietnam .Would recommend a visit and it does not cost much to get in.

reviews.author: AKB
reviews.title: COOL AF
reviews.content: Firstly it was quite hard for the uber driver to find the entrance so make sure you have the right address! I arrived at 12:30 but the museum is closed from 11:30 - 1:00. I paid 40'000 dong entry, but it is an extra 30'000 if you want to take your camera in (iPhone camera is okay). To be completely honest I just hid my camera in my bag and took it out when I was out of sight of the gate and no one cared. The museum is spread across three buildings, an old fort, and a yard full of old tanks, canons, planes, and other weaponry. I throughly enjoyed the exhibit but remember that everything here is from a Vietnamese socialise perspective so maybe it would be best to brush up on your Vietnamese history before you go. There is no aircon so it's hot as balls even inside the museum so maybe take a fan and a bottle of water. A super cool way to spend a morning or afternoon in Hanoi. Loved it!

reviews.author: Thomas S
reviews.title: Good fun
reviews.content: This was a good way to spend the morning and enjoy some good photos of tanks and planes ... has a very impressive outdoor section however the exibits inside where not the best ... worth the trip for the outdoor section however 1 or 2 hrs max

reviews.author: Caroline R
reviews.title: Just the outside...
reviews.content: Walked past on a Friday in August when it was shut, but for 20,000 you could walk around the outside artefacts. The tanks, cannons and planes were interesting to look at, especially the wreckage. Worth a look, even if it just the outside bits! Highlands coffee shop is right next door, with wifi, with an enterance way to the street and the outside section of the museum, in hindsight I probably could have just walked in there..

reviews.author: LexEnglish
reviews.title: Very Interesting
reviews.content: It is a great museum, very interesting and with some great things to see.  I have to say I preferred the war museum in Ho Chi Minh City but both are worth a visit.

reviews.author: Sharlene C
reviews.title: Gave a complete history of Vietnams resistance
reviews.content: Pretty interesting if you like to learn more about Vietnams resistance to all foreign invaders not just the French or Americans. They had a great display of army tanks and aircraft including one of their National Treasures, one of the first tanks to crash through the gates of the Presidential Palace in Saigon. If you enjoy history, you will enjoy this museum.

reviews.author: hsbeloshi
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: If you like history, you will love this museum. There is a good collection of weapons used throughout Vietnam years of warfare. There are indoor and outdoor displays. It is a very interesting place to visit to look into the Vietnamese struggle against invasions.

reviews.author: hanpinn
reviews.title: Saw what I wanted to see.. given very short time!
reviews.content: I was in Hanoi for a 1.5 day business trip and happened to saw a Vietcong Air Force MiG-21PFV fighter standing majestically at the entrance of this museum! Being a fan of Russian military aviation, here came my chance! It was around 8.45am in the morning and I just had 15minutes left before rushing off for my business appointment. I hence took the trouble to enter and given the limited time, viewing the retired aircrafts and ordinances on display was sufficient for me! Hell, I was rewarded with details and closeup of the VAF MiG-21 fighter jet, together with the SA-2 missile on display and other items such as the Russian made Illyushun IL-18 turboprop civilian airliner. There were also many other displays available which are housed inside the main museum building which I may explore on my next trip here. I'd recommend this place to those who love to see Vietnam war relics life such as the MiG-21, USAF Skyraiders or even the Soviet build SA-2 missile system!

reviews.author: Amnon A
reviews.title: Museum presents old weapons
reviews.content: The museum is mainly dedicated to the communist fighters against the French, with some mention of earlier history. Some weapons are presented, but the whole exhibit is not very interesting. Learn more from Wikipedia...

reviews.author: phoonies
reviews.title: Great Place to Start Knowing Modern Day Vietnam
reviews.content: This museum was my first stop upon arrival in Hanoi. I am glad I did it as it helped me appreciate the freedom that Vietnam enjoys now that came at a high cost with a lot of determination and sacrifice of their people.

reviews.author: Nathan A
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Try to go on a cooler day, it is only cooled by fans and majority of the better stuff is outside. There is a rather cheap Cafe on the grounds and heaps of cool military stuff.

reviews.author: Ollie S
reviews.title: It was ok. Not as interesting as I had hoped.
reviews.content: We went here after visiting the Hoa Lo Prison. I have to admit I didn't find the military history museum as interesting as I had hoped.  There wasn't a great deal of information. There is quite a fun interactive video bit in one of the rooms though.  We did visit on a very hot day and there was no air conditioning which made walking around a little bit harder. For the price and things to see its not so bad. It took us about an hour to walk around.

reviews.author: babiesquuensland
reviews.title: very interesting
reviews.content: very  interesting, well set out , could do with a bit more of other language signs on the exhibits, enjoyed the citadel, a lot of stairs here

reviews.author: rajanishp
reviews.title: Delightful place to visit
reviews.content: A must on your visit to Hanoi. There is a lot of history about Vietnam to be learnt at this place. The display of fighter aircrafts was wonderful

reviews.author: WanderingAngeus
reviews.title: Interesting way to pass a few hours if you like war toys
reviews.content: To be honest if you are like me, once you have seen one T-34 to T-55 or M-48 to M-60 yort eyes glaze over but in fairness although there is a lot of armour but there are other aspects too that save it from being just a war junk yard. I found the 1945-1960 material very interesting & there is an entire room with a very large model of the surrounding hills -to recreate the Battle of Dien Bien Phu, complete with sound effects and original film footage and lines of different coloured light to indicate the movement of the different groups. One drawback for me was, it was all in Vietnamese! But I got the jist. There are also exhibits on the ingenuity of improvisation in war that are both nasty but fascinating.  There is also a wonderful eye catching piece of sculpture made from a crashed US plane in the middle of all the other exhibits. War art not art of war, I suppose.

reviews.author: Dave111962
reviews.title: How the Vietnamese won their freedom.
reviews.content: If in Hanoi you should spend a couple of hours at this museum. Some interesting artifacts and decent english explanations.

reviews.author: Paul C
reviews.title: Good, worthy and has models
reviews.content: Although War Remnants in HCMC wins by a nose, this is a good museum and goes into a bit more detail on the 46 to 54 French war.Unique semi animated models with movie screen above bring to life Dien Bien Phu and the fall of Saigon.

reviews.author: CYY_sg
reviews.title: Large museum detailing the military history of Vietnam
reviews.content: Whether it is a family with young children or a group of friends who are looking for places of interest to keep themselves occupied, this museum has a wide enough range of exhibition to keep the casual visitors entertained and should have enough details and information to keep the history buffs happy.

reviews.author: Soren S
reviews.title: A lot of important information about a terrible war...
reviews.content: It's very informativ and intersting to watch, read and listening about the Vietnam war. I was getting very emotionel when i was walkie-talkie around the museum watching the photos and reading about all these tragical stories which have been heading a lot of people during the Vietnam war, suddenly it's coming much more closer to you. War is cruel and there is no winners that was my own experience visiting Vietnam Military History Muse...

reviews.author: purpleneenor
reviews.title: Interesting and intricate
reviews.content: The museum hosts multiple exhibits that range across decades, and is suitable for those whose knowledge of Vietnamese war history is advanced or basic.The only drawback that we came across on our visit was the lack of clear routes for an effective tour of the different exhibits - it's all arranged in a somewhat incoherent way, due to which visitors might miss some of the show rooms.

reviews.author: Cecilia N
reviews.title: So cool!
reviews.content: The big planes and tanks as soon as you get in are quite impressive. The whole exhibition is really interesting to see, and it´s kinda funny how they use music to generate different feelings.It's a must to get to know more about the history of Vietnam

reviews.author: GregL
reviews.title: Very good Museum
reviews.content: Very enjoyable museum the displays are very good, and is very central to Ho Chi Minhs Mausoluem,Gives  a very good account of Vietnams involvement in conflicts over the years,

reviews.author: Bruce F
reviews.title: You have to know Vietnamese history to really appreciate this.
reviews.content: the Vietnamese Military History Museum is interesting to visit, but it has brief captions in English, so you have to know the story behind them to fully appreciate it. In the past I have read reviews that accused it of being full of propaganda, but I would disagree. there are many aspects of Vietnam's military history that give good grounds for propaganda, but this museum largely avoids these (especially when compared to its counterpart in HCMC.

reviews.author: QuinnyGG
reviews.title: Good but could be updated
reviews.content: We 'enjoyed' this experience although somewhat harrowing, as it explains a lot of what is fundamental to current Vietnamese culture. There is exciting hardware in the exterior - like the tail end of a B52 bomber, MiG jets etc. Not propaganda as some people suggest but things which have shaped this nation's culture. Would benefit from some investment as the internal exhibits are poorly displayed, and the text could be improved. Worthwhile if you are interested in history/ politics.

reviews.author: travelling4experince
reviews.title: History of Vietnam
reviews.content: This museum gives you a nice insight of the history of Vietnam. Even though most of the information are kept very simple and basic. Was definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: AungMyo S
reviews.title: A Place tells the History....
reviews.content: This is a authentic place to know about resistance history of Vietnam people from various intruders over a thousand years ago.Also learn about famous Vietnam war against French and American accordingly in the past. Most of exhibit item has their own history background so that grab the interest of all visitors.Entrance fees are about 2US$ and another 1.5 for camera fees then you can stay as much as you can. There are nice coffee shop at the corner of the museum compound so that visitor can take some rest during their visit.

reviews.author: Nilesh Patil
reviews.title: A little Gem - must visit if you're in Hanoi
reviews.content: It's a little Gem although it doesn't have a very high ranking in Hanoi attractions. They've real planes and tanks used in famous Vietnam war. One of the most interesting thing is the wreckage of a bombardier. My son loved the visit. It inspired him to know more about Vietnam war. They probably need to give more information on the war.Since my daughter couldn't join us for our first visit we went there again only to find that it's closed ok Monday and Friday which I think is very strange for a tourist attraction. They should consider to keep it open 7 days a week.Overall I rate it as a must visit place if you're in Hanoi.

reviews.author: ash b
reviews.title: Interesting insight into War History
reviews.content: Great walk around the museum. Highlight definitely the multiple planes and vehicles displayed in various conditions. Fabulous views of the museum and surrounding areas from the climb up the flag tower. Close to other tourist destinations. Local hang out across the road where we were lucky enough to see groups of street dancers. Great atmosphere in the area!

reviews.author: PatH13
reviews.title: Very cool
reviews.content: The military museum in Hanoi is much better than the one in Ho Chi Min. Lots of tanks, a destroyed B52 and planes and helicopters. A lot of maps inside to look at. Well worth the visit

reviews.author: Chriswakeford
reviews.title: The museum is JUST ok compared to the Saigon museum.
reviews.content: This place is just Ok and for 2 entire bucks worthwhile.On the plus is the MIG 21 and a few great Russian tanks and the BONUS SAM missile.Saigon's museum is way way better.Period.Chriswakeford.com

reviews.author: tjess2
reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.content: We thought we would only spend an hour or so here but ended up spending the afternoon. It was very interesting to see a different perspective on the military history in Vietnam, war had been a part of the country for such a long time. Highly recommend you allow a few hours to take everything in.

reviews.author: Glen T
reviews.title: Interesting military museum
reviews.content: We spent a few hours wandering around the Vietnam Miliary History Museum on a rainy day back in March. As is common in Vietnam, this museum has a lot of interesting indoor and outdoor displays, albeit with the usual propagandist point of view in respect of the US involvement in Vietnam and other conflicts involving Vietnam over the centuries. If you're not into military history, this museum would  have much less appeal. Given that it is close to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and the entrance fee is only around 40k VND, this museum is worth a short visit in our view.

reviews.author: Timohawk
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: The Vietnamese storey of the Vietnam War is graphic in places with hard hitting images throughout the Museum. You will need a few hours to take it all in but well worth the visit. I would like to see the difference in the American take on the war, which I'm sure would be completely opposite to the Vietnam version. Captured American planes and military equipment on display around the perimeter of the museum.

reviews.author: Issac33
reviews.title: Good Museum
reviews.content: This museum charts the history of Vietnam since the first invasion by the Chjnese. It seems the poor Vietnamese have spent most of their history fighting for independence. the museum boasts an exceptional collection of weapons and aircraft unto and including the USA conflict

reviews.author: Christian T
reviews.title: Great collection of war relics
reviews.content: Tickets here are around 40,000 VND and I would say the museum is worth the price.  Plenty of war relics to get up close to and a few buildings to look around.  There is plenty of history here documenting the war and weapons used.Similar to the war museum in Saigon, the descriptions can be seen as mild propaganda but nothing over the top. The descriptions are in depth and if I remember correctly there are some areas that don't have English descriptions.  I would say the Saigon museum was better than this one but if you're in Hanoi I would say this is a worth while visit.

reviews.author: Alf
reviews.title: Not much of a museum
reviews.content: The museum cost about 40,000 VND to get in. The best part is seeing a few Vietnam war relics outside. Huey & Chinook choppers couple APC's, US Skyraiders and a  few Russian built Migs and Anti aircraft middle launchers. Inside is mostly propaganda stuff about defeating the French in the 1950's. A few French and American captured guns. Not much on "American War" which is a bit of joke. Only go if you only have nothing else to do.

reviews.author: gottagothere525
reviews.title: Propaganda Galore with a Good Intro to the Length of their History of Defense
reviews.content: The museum is spread out over several buildings in the Old Quarter with the outdoor Citadel and military equipment as its focal point.  Surprised by the towering sculpture of wreckage (mostly American jets) which is very thought provoking to say the least.  If you like to see tanks, tracked vehicles and helicopters (American and 2 Russian tanks) along with some old jets and planes then this is the place for you.  They start your tour looking back to 200 BC and the defense of Vietnam against the Chinese.  There are some good exhibits here showcasing ancient weapons used in their long battles with the Chinese, French and Americans.  Also a very nice display of cannons discovered around Hanoi in various excavation projects dating back to ancient China through modern times.  You don't see the depth of historical explanations in the displays that you would like and the grounds are pretty worn down. So I have to give it 3 stars for being a less than attractive and not very dynamic museum.  Worth a visit if you really like military history but don't expect Smithsonian level exhibits or restorations.

reviews.author: amichael
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: What a great experience to see the Military Museum and very educational to see what Vietnam had to endure during the wars.

reviews.author: chris19531955
reviews.title: A good afternoon spent here
reviews.content: Admission cost is reasonable. Gives a good account of the American War and all the other wars involving Vietnam. Of particular interest to me was the USA built war hardware that was captured by the NVA.

reviews.author: summerluva222
reviews.title: war atrocities make you feel depressed
reviews.content: this museum is very interesting and it shows the other side of the story of the war. and the horrible atrocities  that happened to the women and children in Vietnam. There is always 2 sides to any story   Warning do not go unless you are prepared to witness shocking pictures  I came away feeling very depressed .

reviews.author: GERMAN ALBERTO P
reviews.title: Great place for History
reviews.content: It's a must in Hanoi, great display of artifacts from the War between USA and Vietnam mainly. It gives you a close experience with what was the war at that time and the terrible numbers of losses and many other bad things that brought this war to both parties. The display of aircrafts is impressive

reviews.author: kapsbell
reviews.title: To much propaganda
reviews.content: Visited the military museum but it ONLY showed or told one side of the story. As always , there are 2 sides to every story or event but in this place, you only ever got one side - disappointing.

reviews.author: 40countrytraveler
reviews.title: You do not need to go into the building. All is outside
reviews.content: You do not have to buy a ticket to tour the inside of the building.  We watched all the tour buses stop, walk through the outside displays and then leave.  We did the same.  You do not need to spend any money to walk around the outdoor displays nor do you have to wait till they open. You can sit in the huge outdoor coffee shop if you want, like we did, then walk in and enjoy the outdoor displays of French and Vietnam war relic's.

reviews.author: apatasaurus
reviews.title: Our Teenage Son Loved This Place!
reviews.content: The military museum was fantastic and our son especially loved it!  We spent a fair bit of time there as he was so fascinated with absolutely everything - all the different weapons and the aircraft.  A very interesting place to visit - definitely recommend.

reviews.author: ImaginativeNameHere
reviews.title: Really interesting
reviews.content: I really enjoyed this museum.  They have an outside area filled with helicopters, tanks, planes, etc., and an inside area where the museum is.  There is a large flag tower you can climb up and who doesn't love having a climb somewhere historical and then looking at the view!  I can't remember how much it was but it was very reasonable to go in and well worth the money.  It really informs visitors, as well as Vietnamese, just how resilient the Vietnamese are and how many occupiers they've had to overcome.  On a less serious and more practical side there is also a HIghlands Coffee cafe on site.

reviews.author: kam a
reviews.title: flag tower
reviews.content: I intended to go to the flag tower and looked over the Citadel, but ended up going to the museum because I could not get to the Flag tower without purchase the tickets of the museum. Later I found out you can just walk through the museum gate to the tower without the ticket or going through the neighbor Highland coffee shop. The Museum is fine, and typical old war artifact, and not exciting to a nonmilitary person.

reviews.author: Usman M
reviews.title: I loved this as it showed the resilience of the Vietnam during the war
reviews.content: When I went the museum was closed from inside; however for half price you can see the items on display.I loved seeing the helicopters, tanks and aeroplane parts as for me I felt it showed how the War was won by the Vietnamese; appreciate their resilience during the war.Was great to see these real life historical machinery; ie the tanks.  Well worth the visit.

reviews.author: lovesweets2
reviews.title: Chinook, airplanes, tanks, bombers - Instruments of destruction
reviews.content: It was interesting to see all these up close and personal where I would only normally see these war instruments from the movies or history documentaries.Entry fee of 40k VND that is all worth it for the exhibits they have on display.  I highly recommend to go there early before 10am and beat the crowd so you can enjoy the exhibits peacefully.

reviews.author: joy L
reviews.title: Histoy
reviews.content: This is interesting but if you are like me war is not something I like.   Yes there is a lot of information there and believe it or not there were other countries involved in this war but all you see if American pictures.  There are some terrible pictures which will bring you to tears.  Be prepared.  Overall it was interesting but a biased look.

reviews.author: Sanjay
reviews.title: A must to see
reviews.content: The Military museum is worth seeing. They have alot of history there of a war, which went on for 19 years, 5 months and 4 weeks. North Vietnam was in combat with South Vietnam. America, Australia and New Zealand and other countries joined forces with South Vietnam to stop communism from spreading through out South East Asia. North Vietnam had the support of the Soviet Union. North Vietnam celebrated their final victory on 15th of May 1975. Entrance fee is 30,000 Dong, NZ$2.00.

reviews.author: Smurphy49256
reviews.title: Afternoon visit
reviews.content: Worth a visit if military history is your thing. Nice to see some tanks, aircraft and bombs. Very exposed outside but they do have two buildings with information and weapons on display.

reviews.author: Dominikam1991
reviews.title: Very chaotic with little information
reviews.content: Reasons to visit this place: it is close to many other attractions in the area and it is very cheap to enter 40 000 so it's worth giving it a go. It has a lot of exhibits and it would be great for somebody who likes planes and tanks. Minuses: very little to non information. If you do not know the history you will not learn anything as there are just pictures with little to non explanation. Also, it is very chaotic, you don't know where to go next and end up doing things not in the historical order. Also, there is no air con and you need to move between buildings and a lot of exhibits are outdoors so on a hot day it is not that pleasant. On a last note, we got there at 10:30 and we've been kicked out at 11:30 as they were having an hour and a half break. So we had to wait in a cafe to finish our visit. To sum up, it is worth popping in if you are in the neighbourhood but I would not recommend going out of your way to visit.

reviews.author: r0bertpk
reviews.title: The winner writes the history - propaganda at its finest!
reviews.content: If you are interested in being bombarded with stories of America's "imperialist aggression" and endless photos of wounded children and other victims, you will like this place.  They also re-write the history, including changing the outcomes of several important battles.  There is an interesting collection of aircraft and tanks, but they are not being well maintained.  As a Vietnam war vet, I was a bit disgusted.  Most displays describe the North Vietnamese and Viet Cong as patriots, while describing their opponents, including South Vietnamese troops as criminals and worse.

reviews.author: Allie_k9090
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Spent an hour here.. plenty of exhibits and things to see, a 40,000 dong entry fee. Enjoyed seeing the US military planes and wreckage.

reviews.author: LovinLifesJourneys
reviews.title: Must See !
reviews.content: This was an eye opening experience to see the perspective view of American involvement.  Harsh realities but a absolute must see.

reviews.author: Teresa
reviews.title: Fascinating museum
reviews.content: Travelling with 4 very young children (2,4,6 and 8) they loved all the tanks and aircraft, my husband and I really appreciated the history behind it all. A great experience for everyone!

reviews.author: William D
reviews.title: See the military equipment used by the U.S. during the Vietnam War.
reviews.content: This museum tell what the war was like through the eyes of the Vietnamese.  I spent a lot of time looking at everything, and I must say, it was worth the trip.

reviews.author: Rubir_sharan
reviews.title: Overhyped but still does the job
reviews.content: This place is overhyped. Though it has got some very good collection of tanks,planes and war equipment but still soul is lacking. The crashed plane made up of war remnants is amazing. Do watch the video if you have patience to watch it,its seriously is a deal breaker. The outlay of the things is not very impressive but still it gives you a very thorough understanding of the types of weapon used.

reviews.author: palawanismyhome
reviews.title: Don't forget to visit this war museum
reviews.content: We spent two hours here and it could have been more but we had other things to see. There are several buildings with various displays starting from 1000 years ago when the Vietnamese got rid of the Chinese. Of course i grew up watching the American Vietnam war on the news so i was interested in that period. Outside the buildings are planes, helicopters, tanks, artillery , cannons and more. The exhibits are American, Russian and Chinese if i remember correctly and is a great place if you are interested in military hardware. Besides the entrance fee there is a camera fee but i did not notice this until i left, but nobody seemed to bother us while we were taking photos.

reviews.author: Stu7C9F
reviews.title: For the price...it's great
reviews.content: The main attractions here are the outdoor exhibits; which have pretty much been covered in the trip advisor pictures. (Huey, Il-14, 2x sky raiders and a Mig21 are the aircraft) numerous missiles, ordnance, tanks, mobile artillery etc. They are in a tatty state and there is very little information available on them regarding their historyYou can go onto the stand of the flag tower which is also good for pictures. The internal exhibits are to a reasonable standard with some interesting artefacts relating the the US-Vietnam era but again the information available is sparse. IT COSTS ABOUT 60p TO ENTER. How can that not be worth it. Expect to be there an hour or so. The info boards are in English. There are toilets and a couple of shops that don't really sell anything worthwhile. Located bang in the middle of Hanoi, just opposite the entrance is the statue of Lenin which is also worth a quick look

reviews.author: Msiatravel_lover
reviews.title: A museum for military history lover
reviews.content: I give it a 5 star rating for the outdoor exhibits and a 3 star rating for the indoor exhibits with a rundown museum. I will start with the outdoor exhibits. Many collection of the military airplane and tanks. If you love military history, you gonna love this place. Get a spectacular view over the outdoor exhibits by going up to the flag tower. The museum in the other hand i have to be honest, it was a little bit rundown. They could at least do better with the museum with an entrance fees of 40.000 vnd. No air conditioning is being open during my time of visit. Making the visitor felt hot and stuffy inside the museum. Lacks of information of the exhibits in the museum. Only two floors. Having been to HCMC War Remnants Museum, i would said i like HCMC War Museum far more better than this.

reviews.author: Sharyn M
reviews.title: All things military
reviews.content: If you want to get a lesson in the military history of Vietnam then this is the place to go.  From ancient times to the present - a broad overview will keep you occupied for a good few hours.

reviews.author: visanana
reviews.title: History Buffs
reviews.content: Must see for those interested in the history of the time. Spend as little or as much time as you want wandering around the museum.

reviews.author: bhavik1803
reviews.title: Not very interesting
reviews.content: They should do a better job with this place, such a waste.Right next to hanoi flag towel and opposite a beautiful park

reviews.author: Sprockett666
reviews.title: Certainly worth a visit if you are military minded
reviews.content: Our husbands spent a good 3/4 hours in the museum and found it very interesting albeit the history being a little bit one sided .

reviews.author: ch6006hc
reviews.title: Good collection of Vietnam war era hardware
reviews.content: Airplanes, helicopters, tanks, cannons and guns are the core of this place. It´s an ample collection and the museum could improve the experience considerably by providing more explanations and putting into context the collection. English explanations on everything would be great.

reviews.author: niekselis666
reviews.title: Very informative and entertaining
reviews.content: Really nice museum with pretty informative boards and expositions aldo with military maps showing history of battles from 200b.c. to 1979. Pretty inpressive outdoor exhibition with tanks and planes from american and vietnamiese sides. Nice attraction while staying in town

reviews.author: Yvonne R
reviews.title: Thought provoking display
reviews.content: It is easy to spend a few hours learning of the Vietnamese history at this place. We enjoyed the displays and buildings.

reviews.author: SimonDabbs
reviews.title: A very comprehensive museum
reviews.content: This museum gives a great insight into the many conflicts that Vietnam has faced, especially in recent times. I like the way that reference is made to the social side of wars, not just to the technology, of which many aspects are covered.One word of warning. Try to arrive early. By about 10.30am, hoards of rather noisy people seem to turn up by the bus-load!

reviews.author: 558splat
reviews.title: More of a time filler
reviews.content: It was getting towards the end of the week of my parents visit and my dad likes history and planes so I took them to the museum. The outside displays of the planes and helicopters are superb but the exhibitions inside are ok. We exited the museum and walked around the grounds outside before realising we had missed half of the museum. There was a LOT of construction happening and items were easily missed. Lack of sign posts. You would think there would be an apology if parts of the museum were under construction. Slightly disappointing

reviews.author: Liz W
reviews.title: A place for people who love history
reviews.content: A pleasant experince information was great and many things were detailed.If you are young or old you will enjoy the surroundings exhibits and all the information within.

reviews.author: Hilary C
reviews.title: Moving visit
reviews.content: Great place to visit, very moving when you read the stories and look at the pictures of what happened, need 2 hours to visit

reviews.author: justvacati0n
reviews.title: Not informative
reviews.content: Not a lot of stuff to see. There are no signs or information about the pieces. You need to read about it before you come or just skip it.

reviews.author: Andrew W
reviews.title: Similar to the one in HCMC
reviews.content: This museum is similar to the one in HCMC but has more old war machines. I was pleased to see that the level of support for the Vietnamese round the world was highlighted including our own efforts in Melbourne.

reviews.author: juliestego
reviews.title: Julie and mark
reviews.content: Well worth a visit. If in Hanoi , really cheap to enter and lots to see also a nice little cafe/bar if you need a rest

reviews.author: George-and-Peggy
reviews.title: Good to visit but not a must.
reviews.content: Its OK but not a must stop. Displays are OK. The museum part was well done. Its a good stop to get out of the traffic for a while. Go into the flag tower that gives you a good view.

reviews.author: Laura J
reviews.title: Rough to get through
reviews.content: A Lot of interesting things and objects but with a lack of introduction to each room og time period. Kind of hard to navigate around the different years and wars when there Are No "headlines" or introductions. I needed more overall info on what objects or things that belonged to which time period

reviews.author: Jules69P
reviews.title: Good exhibits
reviews.content: The day we visited the inside was closed so we had a reduced rate to see the outside exhibits. Planes,helicopters, tanks,canons etc. It was very interesting and good value

reviews.author: Bunditit
reviews.title: Well keep tourist place, nice to take a look..
reviews.content: If I am not wrong they close on Monday(please recheck) tourist also can walk and see many military aircrafts and taks outside the building, I think inside the building can have a lot of good historic story to tell, will be back again if I am back to Hanoi..

reviews.author: Bhuvaneswari R
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: The museum gives insight about Vietnam War. Information is available in english. Easy walk from Old Quarter.

reviews.author: 358tr_nh
reviews.title: Great!
reviews.content: The first time I've come here was in 2016 that I had a training lesson with my group. We were surprised by everything here... becasue I could know mỏe about our History during the War time!!!! And I went here several times with my guests and I told them about the ones I learnt! All of those tours are interested!

reviews.author: Peter C
reviews.title: Historic
reviews.content: Very interesting museum,strong on struggle with France.Not as gruesome as Ho Chi Minh .On the way to ho chi minh mausoleum.

reviews.author: motherdoran
reviews.title: Military muesum
reviews.content: I am old enough to remember this war bought into our homes nightly on TV.    Here Iearnt about the war from Veitnam's view.    The displays were very graphic and thought provoking

reviews.author: DRLuxury
reviews.title: Really cool, inspite of communist propaganda
reviews.content: I loved the tanks and planes exhibited in the yards. So cool. Too much commie propaganda but fortunately all in vietnamese lol.Nice guns and important facts depicted. The exhibits very lively. The jungle traps, the uniforms...pretty impressive.Fridays closed, and the have a 2 hr siesta. Unbelievable lol

reviews.author: ncw2
reviews.title: Great outdoor display
reviews.content: The indoor display on Vietnam war vs US was a interesting and detailed one. Many weapons were on exhibits. There was even a letter for US pilots to give to locals if they were shot down. It explained in various languages to keep the pilots in safety and the rescuers will be rewarded. I was expecting more infor and exhibits on the various war fought with Chinese, but it was very short and limited. The resistance war started against Qin Empire in 217 BC and the most recent against the Qing dynasty in 1789.It would be a good visit for family with young children or teenagers.

reviews.author: Chloe L
reviews.title: lots of equipment and vehicles on show but not much content about vietnams history
reviews.content: has lots of tanks, planes and machinery etc on show outside which is done really well (don't miss the machinery which is right at the back of museum - easy to miss)wanted a bit more information about vietnams history!!! video was in chinese

reviews.author: johannes977
reviews.title: brings back Memories of the Viet War days
reviews.content: So much to see. Get there early and enjoy a leasurely Walk A Bout   Most interesting. So many great Exhibits

reviews.author: Craig M
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: An interesting perspective on the establishment of Vietnam through wars with Japan, France and USA.As would be expected a little one sided but they won.

reviews.author: williampugh
reviews.title: Worth a short visit
reviews.content: This was certainly worth doing but dont allow too much time as the maximum you will need would be 2 hours. Be careful as it closes for lunch - a bit strange for a museum.

reviews.author: Daniel L
reviews.title: One of the better musea in Hanoi
reviews.content: Many helicopters, tanks and jets outside the museum and don't miss out the back and second floors. Many interesting facts about the complete history of Vietnam his wars.

reviews.author: Bawdseysue
reviews.title: Many artefacts but lacks flow and context.
reviews.content: This museum shows the what but not the why. There is a lot of military hardware, large and small, and many photographs. Explanations are in English and French as well as Vietnamese. Progression around the exhibits is not always obvious. I came away feeling none the wiser about the cause of foreign incursion onto Vietnamese soil, nor about the impact on the Vietnamese people. There are no eyewitness accounts of the American war. I found it all just a little sterile.There are toilets and a cafe on sight plus a couple of gift shops.

reviews.author: NayAllen
reviews.title: Very interesting.
reviews.content: History goes right back before the French colonisation. It's very interesting to see how the military changed over the years. The story in the north is very different to the south. Definitely go at either end to compare. The "wreckage" sculpture is amazing.

reviews.author: Dave S
reviews.title: RAMS Adventures
reviews.content: A living history lesson which was informative and very interesting sharing the experiences of the American war from a Vietnamese perspective .Which I found extremely interesting and able to understand the suffering now from both sides of this 10,000 day conflict.

reviews.author: larksfam
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: Museum is segmented by period of time - we missed the American part since it closes at 11:30am (promptly!!) for lunch.  Perspectives from the Vietnamese are very interesting.

reviews.author: Paul N
reviews.title: Lots of History
reviews.content: If you have an interest in all things military, this is worth a visit. There are exhibitions detailing Vietnam's historical past with China/France etc and there are also more recent exhibitions from the Vietnam War.There is a selection of military equipment from the Vietnam War which is split into 2 outside areas, and also 1 of the 2 tanks that broke down the gates at the Independence Palace is preserved here which has been identified as a national treasure.

reviews.author: damovdanger
reviews.title: Military Museum
reviews.content: Worth a look to see how Vietnam has struggled to remain independent and the amazing war history and culture.

reviews.author: johnee40
reviews.title: Very graphic photos.
reviews.content: This museum was packed.  There were visitors from all over the world.  There were graphic photos of what went on during the war and there were people there with deformities from being exposed to agent orange.  It was very sad...;(

reviews.author: TandJen
reviews.title: Great for the history buffs, but not a great deal for anyone else
reviews.content: Interesting for the history buffs but not a huge amount of stuff to do / see - 40 000 enterance feeThe view from the tower was pretty good although I'm sure there are much better places.

reviews.author: Mosaic Images
reviews.title: Vietnam Military History Museum
reviews.content: An encompassing museum that includes not only items from The Vietnam War... AKA The American War or the Second Indo China War. But it also has many items from earlier conflicts. The museum also features cafe facilities that are very welcome on a warm day, some of the relics have put put together in such a way that they stand up with anything in Modern Art... I would love to have one of them in my garden. As before this will be part of any escorted tour around the Military sites of Vietnam

reviews.author: Angela Rose S
reviews.title: Well presented
reviews.content: Presented from a take it as you see open air Museum. Very good pieces to look at and information about each exhibit. Amazing from an tourist point esp if you are interested in history.

reviews.author: nadia089
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: We got here only half an hour before it closed but that was ample time to wander around the outdoor exhibits. There are us planes on display from the Vietnam war and lots of cannons from much earlier times. The thing I found most powerful was the metal sculpture made up of many pieces and fragments from planes used during the war in Vietnam .

reviews.author: edwardvanboer
reviews.title: Very average
reviews.content: A collection of different kind of weapon, served in a very boring way. You can see a machine gun with a description like "used on the hill 531 in March 1969, by this division, that regiment and unit, to destroy an enemy post" Nothing about killing real people, nothing about the horror of war and destruction of humanity. Cold numbers, nothing less, nothing more.

reviews.author: 1jwilko
reviews.title: Not informative enough!
reviews.content: It takes you right through the years of Vietnamese wars and history and had really good weapons and other items used in each year - was really impressed by the tanks and planes etc. Only problem there wasn't enough information about the actual wars. Unless you're a history buff, it can be a bit boring!

reviews.author: Chris
reviews.title: Takes you back to the war times
reviews.content: Spent over 3 hours in this amazing place. Such a proud nation with so much history bend them. advice any one visiting Hanoi to spend some time to get an understanding of the rich past this country has to offer.

reviews.author: _drjackson40
reviews.title: Lots of reckage
reviews.content: It was presented in an interesting way. It does have lots of airplanes in the back to see also. The water tower was nice and the coffee shop next door a must. Keep this on your list to see for history sake

reviews.author: DaleDale2
reviews.title: An Amazing Place To Visit
reviews.content: I had an amazing time learning about the Vietnamese Peoples' views and take on the War in Vietnam in the late 1960s and 1970s My father really enjoyed getting to relive and revisit the sights, sounds, and times of his younger years and replayed his part in the the United States' involvement in Vietnam

reviews.author: davevond
reviews.title: Will need most of a quiet afternoon
reviews.content: Very illuminating to see it from the Vietnamese voice. I learnt way more than I thought that I ever would.

reviews.author: Alan G
reviews.title: Great Museum in Hanoi
reviews.content: We were in Hanoi last April , what a fabulous city , hot , busy ,interesting , food good .We went to this museum out of total interest for the past , I was brought up as child with almost daily to news broadcastsOf the war in Vietnam , so to visit here was like reliving the past ! It was really interesting to see and hear the views and comments from the other side , not American one ! Well worth a visit !

reviews.author: Catherine
reviews.title: Not what I would not recommend
reviews.content: I think its a museum more for the local people as it is not very tourist friendly. Not much translation and there are some old military flights display. I don't think its very interesting.

reviews.author: iansomauroo
reviews.title: a must see place
reviews.content: This is a great place to be at.  Be prepared to be shocked by what happened in the war of 1970.  Great amount of information to read whilst you troll around.

reviews.author: pramrath
reviews.title: Vietnam Military History Museum
reviews.content: Very educative, The Vietnam War is now long enough in the past, so that we can take an objective view. Certainly worth a visit.

reviews.author: managercers
reviews.title: Blast from the past
reviews.content: This museum is well worth a visit, it has a number of exhibits and lets you into a brief window in time, of some of the history of Vietnam, cost in English currency £2 entry fee

reviews.author: David S
reviews.title: Good for war buffs ,
reviews.content: A walk through the history of Vietnam at war, numerous old guns and stories of War time leaders, became a bit repatitious and unless your a history buff I would give it a miss.

reviews.author: Abhishek
reviews.title: Well kept with some amazing pieces
reviews.content: Full scale tanks and helicopters along with debris of destroyed American aircrafts present a somber picture yet offers you a close view of the hardships of a long war fought by vietnam. Number of exhibits, generally well marked and a lot to see, it's a must-see.

reviews.author: Roni_Stanbul
reviews.title: For fans of vestiges of the war
reviews.content: Too bad most boards are in vietnamese... but you can at least see and touch all these remnants of the past warThough you cannot understand much, you can still get a grasp on the influence of former ussr on the conflict and on the extent and of the conflictthe site is remote from the city center

reviews.author: Bart N
reviews.title: Outside is ok, inside is a bit boring.
reviews.content: Went here with my finace. She isn't into musea at all so she didn't like it one bit. I'm really into them but I didn't think this was a good one either. Its mostly old weapons shown in show cases, tons of riffles throughout the ages, mostly with the information when they were found or when they were made etc. What I was missing the most is a story as a whole. I hardly learned anything about the Vietnam war or any other war by visiting the museum. The first few rooms have English information, the last bunch only have Vietnamese which makes it even less interesting for tourists.  The yard is kinda fun with tanks, planes and a chopper but again little information. Entrance fee is 40.000 Dong per person and 30.000 dong if you want to bring a camera. Just use your phone if you want to make pictures and leave your camera in your bag. They will make you stow it in a locker (for free, you get to take the key with you)

reviews.author: Mark P
reviews.title: some war relicts worth a shor visit
reviews.content: Some planes and other heavy war equipment from the Vietnam war. Open air area attached to a an indoor museum that gives some information about the wars in Vietnam.

reviews.author: Armando P
reviews.title: can be skiped
reviews.content: Military is not my favorite field, having seen the war museum at CHM, this one was a bit too much, many photos, but few artifacts, except the planes and tanks on the outside yard.

reviews.author: Max P
reviews.title: Not as good as it was 10 years ago
reviews.content: Went there in 2006 and was impressed, sadly commercialisation has taken precedence over preservation.  An area previously used for displays is now used as a Highlands Coffee shop even though there is a large Highlands Coffee shop right next door.  The outside displays particularly the aircraft are differently showing aging being left out in the elements.  The battle of Dien Bien Phu diorama was not working and in darkness.  There use to be a system of lights built into the diorama that showed the progress of the battle. While still interesting, I left disappointed knowing how much better it was 10 years ago.

reviews.author: YFL
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: I was already born during Vietnam war so I have adequate knowledge of that event and made me really interested to visit this place. I love history and seeing things like what they have makes one feel that they are somewhat part of the events that transpired.

reviews.author: Joe
reviews.title: High high quality
reviews.content: Thus displays inside tell a good story.  Information in many languages.  But the highlight is the machinery. The planes and tanks.  Excellent. This needs to be one of the top things to do in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Kate M
reviews.title: Lots to See
reviews.content: We visited this with our 2 young boys on a day that they were both 'grumpy'. The planes and vehicles outside cheered them up but they had little to no interest in any of the indoor exhibits which was too bad for me.  There is a cool exhibit inside depicting life in the jungle during the war.

reviews.author: Mark W
reviews.title: If your interested in the long fight the Vietnamese people endured
reviews.content: Its sad but interesting to see. The remnants of war, a reminder of the struggle but one that can help to prevent future conflict. Many artefacts, vehicles, planes, tanks etc

reviews.author: georgejacob45
reviews.title: Seeing Is Believing!
reviews.content: You have seen movies on the Vietnam war. Now get ready to see the military hardware face to face. It gives you a complete different perspective on the war and the military hardware used. It is a history lesson and a place to spend time. Though the hardware looks old, in some cases not well maintained it is still a place to experience.

reviews.author: Oenological terroiriste
reviews.title: Good topic, reverential about HCM and the wars but run down
reviews.content: Rusty captured planes and munitions, main diarama of Dien Bien Phu was unlit and almost invisible, that is what we came to see.

reviews.author: Nadnerb2
reviews.title: Good Museum
reviews.content: A good selection of aircraft here for history buffs, while the indoor museum had a great range of exhibits to whet the appitite.

reviews.author: Jipatcherdchu
reviews.title: History
reviews.content: This museum was interesting place to visit and to know about the Vietnam history. Lot of items and photographs of military hardware

reviews.author: Theminimalistbackpacker
reviews.title: Great Museum
reviews.content: Spent a few hours here looking around and taking photos of the old military vehicles. Also has a cafe there which is good for a small rest before going out to see more sites.

reviews.author: Alamgir Farhad
reviews.title: History of invasions
reviews.content: It is an interesting place to visit, and to know the history of conflicts with the French, Japanese and Americans. Lots of photographs and an impressive collection of military hardware including a couple of MIGs. The most interesting (and symbolic) thing is a pile of twisted metal which are the remains of American planes that they've turned into a kind of tower of war junk.

reviews.author: faysie2015
reviews.title: Interesting Enough
reviews.content: Vietnam Military Museum was on the list for my history buff husband - it was quite well done but a bit disjointed for someone who didn't really know much about Vietnamese History. A tour guide would have been very helpful to get an overview.

reviews.author: James G
reviews.title: WEll worth a visit for anyone interested in history
reviews.content: This museum has some interesting exhibits. It heavily emphasizes the war with the French. It seems to me that the American war area has been "sanitized"  for American tourists. However, I found only two errors of fact.

reviews.author: Scott M
reviews.title: Good museum, but better structured exhibitions and English signage would help.
reviews.content: This was a superb museum which covered the 2200 years of Vietnamese resistance to foreign domination. Particular emphasis is on the French and American wars. Many interesting exhibits, but they need to be grouped together around themes or some overarching narrative needs to be provided, along with better English signage.

reviews.author: BenSmith21
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: A really great museum with some great artifices going back a long way. Not just US war relics but the citadel and ancient artifacts found throughout the city are amazing. Great couple of hours for anyone who likes a bit of history.

reviews.author: aditya k
reviews.title: Nothing Great
reviews.content: Ok ok. here they have displayed the different things used for wars in past , divided in to three four section , old war , war equipment in the recent past , covered and closed. Good time pass.

reviews.author: MichaelJT19
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: A good visit which includes a lot of information regarding Vietnam's military history since their inception. Recommended for any military buff.

reviews.author: Maggie K
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Exhibits were well laid out and were very interesting; mixture of indoor and open air. Kids will love all the big planes and tanks.

reviews.author: Schlepper1939
reviews.title: An excellent place to view weapons of war
reviews.content: Both the indoor and outdoor collections are worth the time and effort of a visit if you are interested in the history of the Vietnam war.Indoors are exhibits of all kinds of arms, while outdoors there are aircraft, tanks, bombs, missiles etc. Inside in a separate area is also the tank that broke through the palace gates in Saigon at the end of that war.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: History of a Victorious Army
reviews.content: The Vietnam Military History Museum, often called the Army Museum, is significantly located on Dien Bien Phu Street, which was the ultimate battle of the Vietnamese victories over their French colonial masters in 1945.The Museum traces the development of the Peoples Army of Vietnam, and as  is the usual case when the victors are telling the story, there is obvious bias here and there.That aside, this museum is worth a visit for anyone interested in military history, or even the history of Vietnam, which for millennia has been soaked in military blood.If you intend to visit, make note that it is closed on Mondays.

reviews.author: sandypearce
reviews.title: Step back in history
reviews.content: We came across this museum whilst looking for the entrance to the Citadel. What an amazing nostalgic eye opening experience into Vietnam's sad past. It is a must see whilst in Hanoi. The boys in the family, young and old really were excited at seeing the historical war planes and helicopters.The grounds were a nice haven away from the hustle & bustle of Hanoi. Not to be missed!

reviews.author: jalee77
reviews.title: Understanding the revolution and seeing the Flag Tower !
reviews.content: I wanted to visit the Flag Tower. And the entrance fee allowed me to visit the military history museum as well. There is a short video of the Dien Bien Phu war in the museum. There is also an awesome display of a downed B52 jet on display just outside the museum !You can climb halfway up the Flag tower to see the surrounding view.

reviews.author: BrandingExpert
reviews.title: Up close view of weapons both large and small and the Vietnamese take on the "American War"
reviews.content: All sorts of weaponry are displayed from knives and spears to rifles to tanks, fighter planes and rockets.  Plus, video presentations of some battles against the French and Americans.

reviews.author: krys_k
reviews.title: Not engaging enough
reviews.content: Very old school style museum in the sense that exhibits are displayed with a perfunctory explanation. And that's all you get. I found the captured US hardware  (planes, armaments, tanks) and loaned military stock (from the Soviet Union) to be interesting (reminds me of similar military museums in the former Soviet block) - it's all displayed outside. The interior museum is less interesting since you're looking mostly at small weapons and photos. Not too much context, but what there is, with a definite pro Vietnam communist tinge, and why not - they won. For me, the atmosphere was best, hot day, slightly muggy, South East Asia, old buildings, contents hacking back to an almost forgotten time (who worries about communism now), in the distance the honking on horns and the smells of freshly cooked pho.

reviews.author: RebelTravel
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Me and my gf had that one on "to do" list in Hanoi. It was easy to get to from The Old Quarter. Entrance was 40 k vnd and camera fee was 30 k vnd ( although to be fair you probably could easily not pay it). It has exposition rooms about different wars that Vietnamese people had been in throughout the centuries. Unfortunately descriptions look like they used Google translate and are also of poor quality ( for example description could just say "rifle" and then what it was used for, often wro g type of weapons shown, sometimes same description would be for 3 different items. It does however have good pictures and some interesting dioramas. Main attraction however is all types of tanks, armoured cars, planes, helicopters and guns that you can see up close and it was worth coming just to see that. Plus flag tower is in the museum area as well and it's worth going on top of it for some nice views. All in all worth checking out if you are even a bit into military history.

reviews.author: GohYH93
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: This museum portrayed mainly the victories of the Vietnamese army.  Saigon museum showed the effect n cruelty of war. The museum showed Vietnam was in many wars- Chinese (Qin,  Tang,  Han, Song),  Genghis Khan,  French n US.  Previously the museum showed old world maps including Trung Quoc n Campuchia.  But couldn't find such maps now.  Maybe removed?

reviews.author: Mark L
reviews.title: Okay... Goes through all conflicts
reviews.content: Interesting, Almost everything is in Vietnamese so it's rather difficult to fully understand but easy to fill in misunderstandings by looking.

reviews.author: 170minr
reviews.title: Great toys to see
reviews.content: Isn't as good as the one in Saigon but this one has many toys to see and get up close and personal with, many planes, vehicles, tanks, choppers, artillery.Could do with a bit more information though and clearer signs.

reviews.author: Michael C
reviews.title: Propaganda
reviews.content: It's funny to see how the museum makes propaganda how amazing their warriors were against the enemy the western people. It makes the stories mostly fake

reviews.author: Oldjack
reviews.title: Interesting But Not Special
reviews.content: It has a good range of exhibits with an emphasis on planes and other stuff taken from the Americans and accepting it may have some bias it is worth a visit.The Hanoi Flag Tower is in this complex and not the Citadel next door so that is an added benefit.

reviews.author: Leong Khar Woh
reviews.title: In need of a major makeover.
reviews.content: There were a lot of artefacts on display but lacking a good categorisation system, they are unable to tell a cohesive story. The lack of good english translation was also a major let down as we couldn't figure out the context of the exhibits. There was a "multimedia" presentation of a major battle (Dien Bien Phu) in english but it was also another disappointment as the narration was draggy andmonotonous.The only plus point that I could give is the whole bunch of  real T54s tanks, artillery guns, wreckage of american helicopters outside that you can take photo of to your heart's content.

reviews.author: BobsWorth1
reviews.title: Lots to see and well worth a visit
reviews.content: Visited last week:Opening hours 07:30 - 11:30 & 13:00 - 16:30 (07:30 - 11:30 on Mondays). Admission fee 30,000VND/about £1. I read on some websites there was an additional fee to take photos - didn't see it listed there myself and nobody asked for it.
