Tons of great exhibits, small and large, both indoor and outdoors, all with English translations. Probably best to go early or late as lots of tour buses started turning up around 10:00 hours. Good coffee shop with free wifi on site too. I spent around 2 hours there but could easily have stayed longer.

reviews.author: caroworcester
reviews.title: A bit old fashioned but worth a visit
reviews.content: The museum contains a lot of artifacts relating to Vietnam's history and the wars they fought with both the colonial French and the Americans.  Some of the exhibits are a bit dusty!  And there are no translations or audio tours available which make some of the material very obscure to an English speaker.  But we passed an interesting afternoon here.

reviews.author: AyeMyaMyaCho
reviews.title: Recommend to go
reviews.content: Vietnam Military History Museum was for people who were interested in Military related treasures. Even the military used big tanks, helicopters and aeroplanes were displayed. Very interesting place.

reviews.author: NorthK1954
reviews.title: Great afternoon!
reviews.content: The only reason that I didn't give it a 5, is due to the lack of English translation and background information. As a Canadian, I'm not as intimately familiar (that being said I have done some reading on the subject) of the US involvement in the Vietnam war. I would've liked a bit more in terms of story line along the way, however the artifacts and size of the museum were excellent. For sure check it out.

reviews.author: RobDog33
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: lots of planes and tanks from past wars, very interesting to see, gives a good insight into the Vietnam war

reviews.author: Viet T
reviews.title: It is all about the Modern History of Vietnam
reviews.content: So you should visit.  It explained why Vietnam won the wars with French, Japanese and American to unite the country in 1975. You can see the remains of B52 Fortress together with weapons and military equipment used during the wars.  The museum is located at the Hanoi Flag Tower area. If you are lucky, you could find the gate to the Tower open and you could climb to the top where you can see 360o view of the surrounding area of Vietnam's supreme power centre.  Highlands Coffee there is a good place for gathering .

reviews.author: Alejandro Q
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: It was a very average museum without too much things to see. Lack of information in English makes it considerably better with a tour guide, but it is more expensive to hire one. The airplanes and tanks outside of the building are the biggest highlight in my opinion. If you are only for a couple of days in Hanoi and want ti save some time you cam easily avoid this museum.

reviews.author: Sebastien G
reviews.title: Time for some Bombing
reviews.content: Nice museum with a good amount of things, giant tanks, big planes which i would advice not to climb of course. You also see things taken from downed planes and other military equipment from US military. Worth the visit.

reviews.author: Phil G
reviews.title: Okay for 40k VD
reviews.content: Everything in vietnamese. Not a lot in english. No guides.Outside a lot of planes, tanks, and helicopters to see and inside the whole of the vietnamese military history in chronological order.Camera costs 30k extra but no one seemed to check.

reviews.author: 164ulysses
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: I'm not a huge museum fan but it was great to hear the Vietnamese perspective of the conflict and I loved the outdoor exhibits - don't miss the tanks and planes out the back, there are no clear directions to the second outdoor area.

reviews.author: Glenda T
reviews.title: a must see
reviews.content: Really interesting. History going back through Vietnam's past. Planes, tanks, helicopters from the 70's and inside showing many conflicts from history. For anyone who is interested in History,

reviews.author: HelenCopestake
reviews.country: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
reviews.title: More than you expect
reviews.content: This is in a large building that keep going, being a little dry at first with older military history but improving as you work your way through, and with an impressive "back yard" of relics from the US involvement in the war from 1963-75

reviews.author: VickiMcQuade2016
reviews.title: Highlighted the destruction that this war created
reviews.content: Going through the museum I was saddened to the core to see what a war can do on both sides, the destruction and the aftermath of a war that should never have been fought in the first place.  It was extremely interesting to see the pictures and the story telling of events, places and the cruelty that prevailed. It humbled me in many ways.

reviews.author: Kimberly B
reviews.title: Enough to see but not much information
reviews.content: It's a nice museum that's remembering the past of Vietnam but I would only advise to go there if you have some spare time. It's not on the top list of things to do when you are only a few days in Hanoi. There are far better museums. They do have some aircraft and there is enough to see but not all the information is translated into English and I had the feeling a lot of signs were missing unfortunately.

reviews.author: Adam L
reviews.title: Lots of things to see but very little information about them
reviews.content: I'd say this museum is worth going to but it's not very informative, lots of weapons and artifacts and military vehicles but basically no back story or explanation of exactly what things are or what they were used for. If there were more parts explaining the military history in Vietnam it would make it a lot more interesting but it was mainly just guns and planes and tanks with no information If you like military history then check it out but don't expect to learn much

reviews.author: IVY PAZ A C
reviews.title: Remembering the Past
reviews.content: I cannot help but feel super sad for what the effects of war inflicted to the abyss of my emotion having my generations before me felt the same as what Vietnamese felt. These war remains tell me that NEVER AGAIN will this happen to my generation and hopefully to the rest of the world; too much greed for power makes a leader forget the true good values that THE ALMIGHTY teaches us ; leaders become blind FOR THE GOOD OF ALL  mantra once the evil sides of their persona reigns over the GOOD GOVERNANCE which should be their MANTRA in order to work harmoniously  and on which should anchor how they lead and act. May PEACE be on our planet earth.

reviews.author: Jessica S
reviews.title: Eye-opening look at the resilience of Vietnamese people
reviews.content: This museum, which at first glance seems small, has many artifacts and photographs from myriad wars.  It shows the nearly consistent struggles for independence and against invasion that Vietnamese people have endured.  This was a great way to spend a beautiful afternoon!

reviews.author: LFDMinnesota
reviews.title: History Museum
reviews.content: I am a history teacher and found the Military Museum very informative providing a view from the people of Viet Nam which was helpful to me, from the USA.

reviews.author: Chris H
reviews.title: Another Great Museum
reviews.content: If you are interested in the history of Vietnam starting from the very early times up to when Vietnam became one country again then you must visit this museum.The museum is very well laid out in different section reflecting the different periods of time and the various wars they fought.They have many exhibits inside and outside, from a MIG 21 fighter, tanks both Russian and US as well as the wreckage of a B52 and a SAM 2 Missile, as well as many other things on display you can touch and take photos with.My partner and myself spent hours walking around the different sections and also looking at the out side exhibits, there is one section that explains and shows movies and details about the battle at Dien Bien Phu, this gave us good insight into what happened to the French during that battle. The whole museum both outside and inside gave us a much better idea of the different conflicts that Vietnam has gone through over time.From the grounds of the museum you can also go into the old fort next to it and climb the stone stairs through the narrow passage ways to the top level where you are able to take some great photos.If you would like to relax there is an out door coffee shop where you can sit and relax and then return to look at more displays.The entry fee is 40,000 dong per person, you will need to leave your bags or back packs in a looker when you buy your ticket, the lockers are free and you can lock them yourself and return at your leisure.If you want to understand more about Vietnam then take time and visit this museum as it is easy walking distance from the city.

reviews.author: cristina j
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: The military museum has two separate parts: the first which is more of a museum of the people and the history of the wars, and the second, which is the items of war (planes and others). The visit is very interesting because you see the real pieces of few wars suffered in Vietnam

reviews.author: Karly M
reviews.title: tired and worn out
reviews.content: this museum is quite tired and worn out, some of the translations to english make no sense.  Annoyed by the fact myself and fiancee were not allowed to take our backpacks in but they allowed other Asian visitors their backpacks.  Also you need to pay the same admission fee for your camera.  Was told by 2 separate employees to put my phone away or they would remove it.  Not the nicest or friendliest place I've been to in Vietnam

reviews.author: Sarah K
reviews.title: Good if you like War items
reviews.content: There's not too much English or any audio guides so it is a case of reading what you can. My partner loved it though and loved looking at the outside exhibits.The outside bit was cool to be fair. A few planes, tanks, and a tower you can walk in. For these reasons I wouldn't necessarily do it on a rainy day but we did it on one of their coldest days and it wasn't too bad.They also have a couple cafes on site and a shop for drinks to take around. There's also an ATM outside on the corner if you need it.

reviews.author: satchn
reviews.title: Group of friends tour
reviews.content: I would recommend Vietnam anytime to those who want to travel to Southeast Asia.We were totally amazed by its post war beauty and the beautiful islands which are fast becoming a tourist attraction.Make that trip to Vietnam soon !!🙏👍

reviews.author: KitsuneCole
reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit
reviews.content: We had planned on seeing this museum for a while after seeing the centrepiece on tv somewhere! The museum is 30,000VND to get in (just over £1) per person. You first see a MIG plane and a tank before going into the first building. This is full of very old and interesting artefacts from Vietnamese resistance over the years, particularly against Chinese invasion. The sheer list of resisted invasions is impressive in itself. We missed on upstairs section of the museum due to the heat on the day we went, we just needed a cold drink! However the outside display is worth the extra nice fee alone as you can ascend the Hanoi Flag Tower which is a pretty impressive monument, and then walk amongst the plethora of planes, helicopters, tanks, armoured vehicles, bombs and missiles on display. All of the signage was also translated into English which was a really great surprise as it really added to the trip - for instance we had no idea that the Vietnamese shot down over 4000 planes! It was really interesting to see just how massive the anti-aircraft missiles are. Particularly after we (completely by accident) stumbled upon the Ngoc Ha Ho B52 the day prior. This is a memorial in the maze of tiny backstreets behind the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum to a B52 shot down into a tiny lake. You can see the wheels and undercarriage above the water still. The main centrepiece is incredible, comprised of engines from a Hellcat and B52 along with an array of bits from various planes. The main photo in the centre is pretty powerful too. A really fascinating little museum, really showing just how much the Vietnamese have resisted over the years. I'm glad we made the effort to see it.

reviews.author: pauline o
reviews.title: Interesting place if you like military history
reviews.content: Enjoyed this place, well worth a visit to see close-up remains of planes, tanks etc. from the Vietnam war.  Not as spectacular as the museum in Saigon/HCMC but good nonetheless.

reviews.author: bangkokmissy
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Worth a visit, they accept admission with either dong or dollar, mainly of interest to ex American service personal I would suspect, involved in the Vietnam war. Shot down helicopter, and planes. There were much older artefacts dating back to wars with the Chinese dynasties

reviews.author: Karsten H
reviews.title: Learned a lot
reviews.content: This is a very impressive and historically informative museum, which added to my knowledge of Vietnam's military history, including important events before and after the end of the well-known Vietnam war.

reviews.author: Tom M
reviews.title: Interesting, worth going to!
reviews.content: Great place to go if you're interested in the wars that have happened in Vietnam. Loads of artefacts and information. Would definitely recommend to go there irrelevant of the ages in your party!

reviews.author: JMWG
reviews.title: Tanks Planes Rockets and guns !
reviews.content: Great place to take the kids. Plenty to see and do and they can climb in some old tanks n stuff. Lots of great photos and relics from the Viet war etc.

reviews.author: PamnNeil
reviews.title: Very interesting and moving museum
reviews.content: Of course this is telling the story from the view of the Vietnamese but it is quite comprehensive with many photos and exhibits.

reviews.author: TogoYovo
reviews.title: Spellbinding and Must See
reviews.content: I was awestruck at the suffering Vietnam has endured for centuries. And in the 20th century alone having to repel the Japanese, French and Americans. The story is told over several buildings and covers centuries of struggle. The military artifacts are stunning, including the wreckage of an entire B-52 bomber, the tank that broke through the embassy gates in Saigon, a Huey helicopter fully in tact and several U.S. tanks and Soviet planes. Very much worth a trip to understand the incredible resilience of a determined people.

reviews.author: sydneyite1111
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: A good collection of military hardware with, as you would expect, commentary written from the Vietnamese perspective

reviews.author: Miriam G
reviews.title: Missing information
reviews.content: You can see some interesting weapons and tanks, jets...but there were not sufficient information to introduce each room. Room for improvement

reviews.author: Rob S
reviews.title: Great little museum
reviews.content: Loved being able to get so close to all the exhibits. Something you often can't do back in UKMore propaganda....but hey, it's vietnam 🙂Needed to pay to enterNice cafe onsite also for drinks and snacks

reviews.author: Nick A
reviews.title: Exceptional Military History Location
reviews.content: If Your Interests include Military History, then this is A Definite "Must See", During your visit to Hanoi.This place has Everything, From a Downed USAF B52 Bomber, to All Forms of Military Hardware, mainly from the US/ Vietnam War period.Indoor static Displays of Uniforms, Weapons, First person accounts, of various battles and actions.All Indoor Displays areas have Excellent Lighting, and Easily readable plaques in both English and Vietnamese. If your a Military History Buff, then Allow plenty of time to take All of this place in.Outdoor display areas include many Armoured Vehicles, including Tanks and Personnel Carriers, from both sides of the conflict. Soviet and U.S Aircraft, A Large Display of the Many forms of Military Hardware from the Conflict.Entry to the Military History Museum, is 40, 000 VND per Person.Be Aware, that the Museum Is NOT OPEN , On Mondays And Fridays. It Opens at 8:AM, closes at 11:30AM, Then Re-Opens Between 1:PM And 4:30PM.

reviews.author: Adventurer652033
reviews.title: Boys toys galore.
reviews.content: Some great military exhibits littered all around the grounds plus many displays of weaponry upstairs. Fascinating cinema showing archive documentary film about the building and occupation of the legendary tunnel system. Well worth a visit even if it is to explore mans inhumanity to man.

reviews.author: Linda M
reviews.title: you have to visit
reviews.content: if you enjoy militaria you will enjoy this,there are tanks,planes,bombs etc all outside,but more to see and read inside,be careful what time you visit as it closes for lunch (there is a nice outdoor cafe on the premesis if you need it while waiting)

reviews.author: Mo-ni-Aonghusa
reviews.title: A must for military buffs
reviews.content: Beware of walking on the wrong side of the road as you approach!!! We nearly had a run in with the authorities as we did not notice the signs!

reviews.author: Fadamos
reviews.title: A brilliant collection of artefacts and history
reviews.content: Full with flavour of the North Vietnamese story of the war, the museum has a fantastic collection of both artefacts and history - albeit with narrow optics. A great eye opener for anyone familiar with the romanticised war rhetoric outside of Vietnam.

reviews.author: jeff1955malaysia
reviews.title: very interesting
reviews.content: it is a very good and interesting place to learn more of the wars from a different perspective. it is the remnants of the war. some old russian planes and pic and relics of the war.

reviews.author: valerio c
reviews.title: Excellent place to learn how stupid is the war
reviews.content: Any war is silly and a nonsense, this place is good to teach young people that something like Vietnam wars should never happen again!

reviews.author: lordticklish
reviews.title: See the other side
reviews.content: As an American who fpgrew up during the Vietnam war it was a great thing for me to vist this museum. One because it signified that it's better to be friends than enemies. Two because it's healthy yo try and see the other side. I am very grateful I had the chance.

reviews.author: Donald M
reviews.country: Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park, United Kingdom
reviews.title: Worthwhile visit
reviews.content: Enjoyable visit on our first day in Hanoi. Interesting to see the authentic relics and the aircraft displayed.

reviews.author: Azcavator
reviews.title: Nice to walk around
reviews.content: An easy way to spend an hour walking around. There is not a lot to see but some interesting items that have signboards written in English.Entry was 40,000 VND and there is a small shop with drinks, ice creams etc.It has strange opening hours: 8-1130 and 1-430. Closed Monday and Friday.

reviews.author: michelleJ3212NS
reviews.title: Military enthusiast heaven
reviews.content: The weapons display and stories behind the war is a must do. We learnt much more of Vietnam war and how depressing it much have been

reviews.author: QueenslandTommy
reviews.title: History inside & outside
reviews.content: Spend a 1 1/2 understanding the pride the Vietnamese people have for their country from video / visual presentation (only in Vietnamese ) to picture , posters and artefacts in several display rooms . Outside you have tanks , artillery , planes and helicopter , worth a visit check the website for opening days & times.

reviews.author: henribio
reviews.title: stir emotions
reviews.content: is a good way to see a litlle part of history of war and her catastrofick and your legacy in this country

reviews.author: SandyCinOZ
reviews.title: Amazing Place and great exhibition
reviews.content: The museum is full of interesting artefacts and you can easily spend a few hours there.The museum does close for lunch for 1 hour for the staff (12.00 - 1.00pm)Some of the museum artefacts are outside so wear a hat and sunscreen

reviews.author: Ji10101
reviews.title: outside of the facility was also great
reviews.content: actually when I arrived at Vietnam, I was not that interested in the American war. but after visiting here, I've got interested in it.especially outside of the museum was impressive for me. broken airplains and helicopters were movingI recommend you to visit this museum especially too hot summer or rainy season. it would be efficient. furthermore there was a Vietnam local brand cofe. it was good place to take a rest

reviews.author: umwakichwa
reviews.title: Important experience
reviews.content: I felt like we just had to go and see this, though I knew it would be quite depressing.  There are old planes and inside, each floor shows a different thematic area.  When we were there, Americans that fought in the war were volunteering as docents at the museum and explaining things to groups of tourists.  It was very humbling to see how well they portrayed the complicated nature of war at this site.

reviews.author: Boolag666
reviews.title: Must visit for history buffs!
reviews.content: Venture thru the museum buildings first prior to checking out the displays outside..plenty to see, although we got a little lost goin from building to building. There is an exhibition of modern patriotic art representing the Indochina wars that is worth seeing.The torpedo tube from one of the torpedo boats that engaged the USS Maddox is found in the rear courtyard, alongside a crazy looking sea mine countermeasure device & several armoured vehicles. Beware the MiG-21 & MiG-17 sitting side by side as they are not the actual examples they are painted to represent..these will be found at the Airforce museum at Bach Mai airfield.There is a decent open air cafe with good food on the museum grounds.

reviews.author: HO D
reviews.title: Vietnam War History
reviews.content: A must for all tourist as it is difficult to see old war planes, helicopters, ships, etc left by the USA army during the previous Vietnam-American war.  The museum gave a total history how the Vietnamese fought during the war to defend their country.

reviews.author: Paolo T
reviews.title: Very interesting museum
reviews.content: We were very impressed by the content exposed in the museum. Many important documents relevant to the wars against foreigners occupation of Vietnam can be found and you can became aware of important historical events

reviews.author: 562aashishp
reviews.title: Poor customer service
reviews.content: We reached the place to find out the main building was closed for renovation. Only the 1st floor was open. The second building was locked up even though we could see some fans and lights running inside and no works were going on. The lady in charge of audio visual theatre was chatting on mobile and when we asked her to put the show. She just said " NO". We asked another lady in the other room and she gladly obliged. Request the management to change this grumpy person and replace with someone less rude.The outside exhibits of aircrafts and armored vehicles were good although we found a person claiming be be a red cross volunteer asking for donations after filling a stupid survey on tourism. Paid him 10,000 VND just get off our backs.Overall not happy.

reviews.author: Tweeter1952
reviews.title: Tailings of war
reviews.content: Lile a sculpture garden museum, a record of man's ingenuity in the persuit of killing other men. Remanents of the American War in Vietnam from uns and rockets to planes and bombs, its a museum to the blunders of war. It;s like a car accident, you know you should'nt look but you cant look away. Once seen can never be unseen. Thats the beauty of this place. A must when in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Russ514
reviews.title: A good day out
reviews.content: Although politically directed this is a good place to visit with equipment outside.The wording of the displays is directed at the sacrifice of the people, which is understandable after what they have been through.

reviews.author: Lisa O
reviews.title: An interesting hour can be spent here.
reviews.content: The actual war planes and tanks are very interesting too. Inside, many of the larger signs and information posters are in Vietnamese, however subheadings for pictures were translated to English.

reviews.author: Yann M
reviews.title: Totally worth the 1$ investment
reviews.content: I am (totally) not a fan of war or guns... But this museum was very interesting. A lot of great artefacts and interesting pictures or facts are explained.This totally worth the 1$ investment

reviews.author: John J
reviews.title: Historical Journey
reviews.content: until recent times Vietnam has unfortunately suffered decades of conflict.From the wars with Japan, France and in more recent times the Americans.  So, its important to gain an understanding of the Vietnamese make up and to do this can, in part be achieved by a visit to this museum. (note it is closed for lunch 11.30-2pm each day)The museum has an extensive outdoor area to the side and the rear of aero planes, helicopters and tanks.Inside, the halls are arranged in sequence -1945, (WW2)1956 (French) and 65-72 (USA) It takes about 2 hours to view most of the artifacts. So, I recommend a visit on your trip to Hanoi.

reviews.author: lcrause
reviews.title: Enigmatic displays
reviews.content: There is an amazing outside display of aircraft wreckage.  Unlike the museum in Ho Chi Minh City, this one is not as graphic.

reviews.author: Garth117
reviews.title: MUST DO
reviews.content: An awesome museum for a super cheap price!If you have a few spare hours this is a must do! It has a great collection of machines, weapons of war and shows history from the vietnamese side.

reviews.author: Vidi
reviews.title: An interesting visit
reviews.content: A big museum, a lot to see if you don't mind the propaganda and the slight distorsion of facts. Still, a worthwhile visit.

reviews.author: 정오 박
reviews.title: 2000won per person,so so
reviews.content: we dropped by that museum from hochimin museum.It s really hot so we just took a rest for a while at there. but The entrance fee is expensive more than I thought. even I was not interested for us

reviews.author: Pat L
reviews.title: great place
reviews.content: we found this place very interesting. if you are in to militaria or history a must. lots of historical displays and war stuff from documents, to tanks to guns. A great coffee shop with fierce aircon for a rest from the battle

reviews.author: stuartml2015
reviews.title: YOU'LL LIKE THIS
reviews.content: This is a very interesting museum and a must see if you're visiting Hanoi.  The best exhibit is the living 3 dimensional account of the battle of Dien Bien Phu - this brings the battle totally to life and makes it completely understandable.  There is of course a useful insight into the US war in Vietnam - perhaps not up to the level of the War Remnants Museum in Ho Chi Minh but if you're visiting both cities then both museums are well worth a visit to learn something about this proud country.

reviews.author: ArtistKev
reviews.title: Must see museum
reviews.content: I think this was well worth the visit for those with a sense of Vietnamese history from the victors point of view. The descriptions made us smile but the victors write the history as was the case. An excellent panorama of Diem Bin Pho Battle is worth seeing. A large quantity of equipment and munitions were on display. Abstract displays were also present using wrecked equipment.

reviews.author: Flolam
reviews.title: good historical place
reviews.content: it's a good historical place, location is easy going, worth visiting & I think it's a must go place.  Bad thing is the cafe besides the museum is a bit noisy.

reviews.author: Lynsie F
reviews.title: Dusty and confusing
reviews.content: I didn't get much out of it. The place was dusty and in need of a complete refresh. Nothing seemed to make much sense. My husband loved the planes in the outside display.

reviews.author: mike j
reviews.title: a developing museum
reviews.content: This is a relatively new museum - still under construction in areas - builders working around you.It was interesting and we managed to spend about 90mins - 2 hours easily .Not expensive - but ensure you check the opening hours before attending

reviews.author: Simon de C
reviews.title: It brings balance to the Vietnam story
reviews.content: The most thought provoking sculpture i have ever seen.Non judgemental exhibition of planes and history of the war seen through the Vietnamese eyes. Really makes you think, respect and admire all the people caught up in a horrible war.

reviews.author: Dan B
reviews.title: Comprehensive breakdown of the impact of war
reviews.content: A really fascinating visit. So much history and information to absorb.Complete military hardware exhibition complete with many items, and detailed and comprehensive displays explaining aspects of the war.Coffee shop on the grounds to stop and consider the visit.

reviews.author: Karl L
reviews.title: Important museum in heart of Hanoi.
reviews.content: Stumbled across this important piece of history in Hanoi.   From the real life war pieces out front of the main complex, to ruins of war and the agent orange exhibit.   It really reminds of you of what this country has endured to be what it is todayWe love Vietnam.

reviews.author: Profguy
reviews.title: The Vietnam War from Another View
reviews.content: It was fascinating seeing this museum as an American and son of a Vietnam Ware veteran. There is clearly a different perspective and one worthy of a look. I walked this with my daughter and gave her a history lesson. I cannot imagine a better place to teach history than in a place dedicated to a different version. It was more than educational, it was emotional for me.One building is dedicated to what they call "The American War" and the other to the French War.  This is a source of tremendous national pride since they defeated two global powers.

reviews.author: Edwin J
reviews.title: Vietnam Military Museum
reviews.content: First of all, it's not called the B52 Victory Museum.  A lot of people are going to be confused with that title.  It's called the Vietnamese Military Museum.   There is an entrance fee for adults. Children are free.  If you go when its closed, maybe they let you walk around inside the grounds for free.   I didnt find the attractions inside very interesting.  There are two landscaptes set up where the announcer recalls some military victories while watching a tv monitor.  The first was against French forces.   I wanted to see the Vietnam war landscape against the US in action, but it was not on and no time schedule was posted.  The outside is a mishmash of military relics and broken planes.  Not very exciting.  Small kids would probably enjoy it more.  I am sure I missed something there.  Guidance was pretty bad.

reviews.author: TN007
reviews.title: Better than HCMC
reviews.content: A lot more information and armour to see here than the War Remnants in HCMC. My husband and boys particularly enjoyed this museum.

reviews.author: szkut
reviews.title: Still seems more work being done
reviews.content: Place seemed to be going through a bit of a renovation when we arrived. Not to mention that it was closed when we got there at 12 (between 11:30-1pm it's closed). But we came back and ended up doing it in reverse. It's all very interesting and for anyone who loves a bit of history will love it. If a bit more money is spent (which it seems) it may just give that bit more it needs.

reviews.author: Fiona M
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Enjoyable hour here, interesting museum. Nice coffee shop on the grounds, Highland Coffee, for a stop before you leave.

reviews.author: Stuart B
reviews.title: Disturbing
reviews.content: This museum certainly gives the other side of the Vietnam War. It doesn't hold back and some of it is very graphic and quite disturbing. We couldn't read all of it as it really is very upsetting. You have to visit this place as it is so much part of recent history.

reviews.author: Stu B
reviews.title: Has potential, lacked finesse!
reviews.content: The museum itself has some great exhibits about the Vietnam War which are both fascinating and historically important. The variety of planes, tanks etc is also very good- however, as previously mentioned, the inside of the museum had poorly presented exhibits, some of which weren't translated into English. This could be great museum, but sadly is not. They are carrying out a lot of maintenance work at the moment too, maybe we can hope for improvements?

reviews.author: amadeus11190382
reviews.title: Lots of interesting captured USA hardware and planes!
reviews.content: An interesting museum inside and out . Will appeal to military historians and those who remember the Vietnam war. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: 111boopatrick
reviews.title: The suffering of Vietnam in the hands of the American
reviews.content: This Museum showed the war planes used during the Vietnam war by the American and the weapons used were displace inside the building.There is a Tiger chamber that shows the suffering of the people during the wars with the American Murderers. The conflicts of Vietnam was between the North which is communist with the South which was ruled by the French.But the American BIG Brother got involve to show their military might with their weapons of air power and bombs including Chemical Bombs.North Vietnam, Hanoi under it greatest leader, Ho Chi Ming fought  the American with underground tunnels. This is the only American defeat in the history of wars by the American.The staffs are unprofessional as most visitors are foreigners who speaks mostly English, but the staffs mostly do no even understands English.Although Nuclear bombs was not use, the Chemical bombs killed many mericlessly and the damaged to the land and forest were long terms.More than million of people were killed by the Murderous Americans which was never their business as it is just an internal conflicts of the Vietnamese themselves.

reviews.author: lloyd b
reviews.title: Great raw material; could make for an exceptional experience
reviews.content: What with all the hardware available and the overwhelming interest in how Vietnam vanquished the greatest military in history, this could be a world class museum. Unfortunately it is not.  Once you leave the outside exhibits and wander in doors, the exhibits go from great to muddled and poorly presented and even more poorly documented. What a shame.

reviews.author: swaby_commander
reviews.title: The American War and Invasion of Vietnam
reviews.content: This museum is not open on Mondays and Fridays, and is excellent value for money.   Mig 21 jet fighter plane with 14 kills marked on nose, tanks, and lots of military stuff from the Vietnamese perspective.   One of the things that stuck in my mind was the number of American planes downed during that war - something like 4,189.   This is about double the figure that the US government claims was shot down.   I would believe the Vietnamese personally.

reviews.author: Janine7Craig
reviews.title: Great for the Military Enthusiast
reviews.content: A friend on our trip was a great military enthusiast and he said he thoroughly enjoyed the visit, so if that is your thing, then this is the place to see.

reviews.author: Mauveen T
reviews.title: An interesting stop.
reviews.content: Worthwhile spot to look around. The aeroplanes were impressive as were the majority of artefacts on display.

reviews.author: Linda K
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: My husband wanted to go here, I wasn't that bothered as I know very little about the wars in Vietnam, but I did actually find it quite interesting. There is obviously lots of military hardware here and to be honest I never realised quite how big some of it is. The chinook in particular is huge as are some of the planes and guns.  They also have exhibitions in the big halls which were interesting to walk around and find out more about the history of the country.  The military hardware is now considered to be National Treasures (since October 2012) which I found amusing but not quite sure why!!The museum costs 40,000 per person to get into and 30,000 for cameras but I never saw anyone checking that. There is also a really old flag tower on the site which is worth looking at.  You can walk here from the old quarter, it takes about half an hour. It is quite straight forward but you probably need a map if you're not sure where you are going.If you want to go to the temple which is behind the museum then make sure you turn right when you come out - if you go left it is a huge walk al the way around!!

reviews.author: N. Asokan
reviews.title: Covers the military history of Vietnam's independence struggle and the American war
reviews.content: Most of the exhibits have English explanations (sometiimes the translations are really quaint!). Some of the exhibits are eye-opening, like rubber sandals (rather than boots) worn by soldiers, fashioned out of car tyres and "helmets" that are essentially Vietnamese conical bamboo hats covered with camouflage cloth. This was a ragged army that made do with whatever was available. There is a faint whiff of propaganda throughout, which is not unexpected and does not detract from the experience. The 200-year old flag tower outside seems to be peeling apart (but this may be due to last night's storm). I was hoping that the museum would give an overall view of Vietnam's perspective and narrative about the American war. This it didn't (instead it focused on specific objects, events or personalities).

reviews.author: Spad2014
reviews.title: The debris of war
reviews.content: Focused on the many struggles of the Vietnamese to be free of Japanese, French, American and Chinese oppression the museum is largely for the Vietnamese but there is sufficient English and French signage to follow most of the displays. The sheer volume of material is impressive, especially from the American war. A big plus is the old flag tower which is part of the compound

reviews.author: Giugmsk
reviews.title: Great Museum with good information
reviews.content: This museum was so full of information and knowledge about Vietnam history and events so we chose to visit it but not others when we had a chance to choose which in our city tour. The flag tower and ancient citadel of Hanoi , both also and the 2 hours were really well-spent.

reviews.author: kcslkcsl
reviews.title: I enjoyed the visit here
reviews.content: It might not be for everyone but I enjoyed the visit, taking pictures with the cannons, tanks, & planes that were on display.

reviews.author: ravipsk
reviews.title: Tribute to the Military Struggles that Forged Vietnam
reviews.content: Aptly located on Dien Bien Phu Street, this museum encapsulates the decades of warfare that the nation had to undertake to win its freedom. The centre piece is the wrecage of a B52 bomber with the iconic picture of a Vietnames girl dragging the orignial wreckage away.

reviews.author: Michael P
reviews.title: A must for anyone traveling to Điện Biên Phủ
reviews.content: The Military History Museum is a fantastic place for history buffs in general and should be of particular interest to anyone planning a journey to Điện Biên Phủ. The museum has an excellent diorama of the Điện Biên Phủ battlefield which is displayed with an audiovisual presentation narrated in both Vietnamese and English.

reviews.author: lisbet h
reviews.title: Great place to visit with children
reviews.content: Went there with my husband and two boys aged 10 and 12 in the beginning of july. Many things to see. Not all written in english at the displays, but still very interesting, with lots of photos, things from the different ages. Outside the museum big displays of airplains, helicopters, tanks, vehicles etc fromVietnam and Sovjet Union from the vietnam war .....worth a visit!

reviews.author: Schuyler E
reviews.title: A great history of warfare equipment, planes, tanks, bike etc
reviews.content: The displays are both indoors and the larger equipment such as tanks, helicopters and planes outdoors. There is an air-conditioned cafe within the complex so you can have a break in between exhibits. Make sure to obtain a copy of the printed guide as the exhibits are on two floors within various buildings as well as highlighting staff administration offices and toilets.

reviews.author: noravoorwald
reviews.title: waepon museum
reviews.content: a place full of war toys out of different wars from centuries ago until the last war. Nice restaurant next to it.

reviews.author: BRUCEANNETT1
reviews.title: A reminder to the USA
reviews.content: After visiting this museum, and also getting to know the culture and the history of the Vietnamese, it is easy to see how the American government got their just rewards from the war. It is hard not to feel sympathy for all the American troops sent over here, as they were up against a population which was battle hardened by many previous wars, and which, quite frankly, were all prepared to die for their country. A moving experience, and one which will remain with me.

reviews.author: Narasimha Prasad G
reviews.title: Superb
reviews.content: Her you can see the spirit of the Vietnamese in War how they won in all wars even they were very small in budget and weapons compare to their envies.it's also one of the top tourist destination

reviews.author: Annie F
reviews.title: Military enthusiast heaven
reviews.content: Visited with three kids and while some of the displays were a little dry my 2sons and husband loved being up close to the planes,helicopters and tanks.Cafe next door has nice shade and cool drinks as a lot of the  museum was outdoors or very hot.Check opening hours as they close for lunch.

reviews.author: Catherine J
reviews.title: Great for people interested in the war, especially the Vietnam-American War
reviews.content: If you're interested in war history, this is definitely a place to visit. While the exhibits aren't fantastically done, it's always fascinating to see how the wars are explained. Lots of B52s and other artifacts as well.

reviews.author: speedyyen
reviews.title: Amazing blast from the past history lesson
reviews.content: the weapons display and stories behind the war...all told ...is a must do .we learnt much more of the viet war and how depressing it must have been

reviews.author: Greyhound77
reviews.title: Large war planes and helicopter
reviews.content: This was enjoyable as it told the history of Vietnam's war history, from their perspective, as they've been invaded by the Chinese, Japanese, French and America. The highlights are the large flag pole, planes and wreckage of the Vietnam War, and the art gallery in one of the rear buildings, including a great portrait of Khe Sanh.

reviews.author: Kevin_One_Man_Show
reviews.title: AMAZING TOUR
reviews.content: It is an amazing tour - informative, interesting, shocking and emotional.There can be little lingering doubt left in most people as to how unjust and brutal and inhumane the Vietnam war was - and this day will remove any doubt that was left.Beware taxis that charge extortionate amounts that hang around the exits hoping to trick first timers - and take advantage of how vunerable they may be feeling after this tour

reviews.author: Mga1500
reviews.title: Sad old museum
reviews.content: As many others have said this is only worth visiting if you really have nothing to do. A fairly tatty collection of planes and lots of guns, early history interesting. But as also said already it is in particular order. Highland coffee shop open air and inside is good though, however the toilets are disgusting

reviews.author: james p
reviews.title: dont go here high
reviews.content: not great for when youre high.  Turns out America was really naughty and did some very very bad things to VIetnam.

reviews.author: Yvonne M
reviews.title: Good for a brief visit
reviews.content: Our visit to the museum was good but not great. It does very little to explain anything about the war as a whole but does display artefacts well. The planes and tanks on show outside are very impressive. There is a charge for entering at the main gate but if you go into the coffee bar next door you can go through their gate and avoid the cost. Nobody asked us to produce a ticket but if they do you will just need to pay them then. I am glad that we didn't pay for the trip to be honest.

reviews.author: handymann69
reviews.title: Remembering Vietnam's Unforgettable Past
reviews.content: Entering the Vietnam Military History Museum, you will see the horrible reminders of the violent Vietnam war. Different weapons of war from Mig-21's to B-52's are displayed inside. Helicopters, canons, tanks and other weapons used during the Vietnam war are available for public viewing. You will be able to feel the difficulties that the Vietnamese encountered during the war. I recommend that travelers visit the museum to see the difference between the beauty of present day Vietnam and its violent past.

reviews.author: mj68fr
reviews.title: Emotional
reviews.content: This museum is really particular. You can see and understand two points of view: Vietnamese and American... The pictures are sometimes terrible, but this is the real story of the war... Must be see...

reviews.author: romi1331
reviews.title: In need of some TLC
reviews.content: Opening: Everyday except Monday and Friday. 8-11.30 then 13-16.30. Buy tickets a the box office to the right as you enter through the gates. This place does not flow at all. Exhibitions are scattered and in need of some refurbishment. We got there at opening but it was still not quite what you expect with displays often not in English which made it hard to understand it all. It also doesn't have air con which sounds silly but I thought it would be a refuge from the 37 degree heat but it had a few fans dotted around which made the whole experience tiresome. The outside exhibition is cool. It requires you to have a lot of prior knowledge and does little to explain things to those who may not know a lot and therefore I did not gain as much from this attraction as I would have liked to.

reviews.author: Ian Goh
reviews.title: Not a fan of military history, but this museum feels in need of refreshment
reviews.content: I'm not a fan of military history, nor history. But the exhibits were interesting enough. Couple of tanks, canons, airplanes on display.Note: rooms can get very warm, and they do smell a little musty. Also, take a lil climb up the flag tower, its breezier and a good view.

reviews.author: John K
reviews.title: Interesting artefacts but no flow...
reviews.content: I'd echo the previous reviewer's comments - unless you're a reader of Vietnamese it's really hard follow what's going on here. The only bits in English or French are the labels for each artefact; all the other information hasn't been translated so you don't really learn any history here - it's just 'here's a gun, here's another gun...' A shame as they could make the place really fascinating, like the War Remnants Museum in Saigon. Also, the toilets are disgusting :-/

reviews.author: Paul M
reviews.title: Good to have a view on the history
reviews.content: A museum like many others. This one was not very special. It was okay, but not complete as I can imagine. Translation was poor and some stuff was exposed twice. But visit it and have a look in the history.

reviews.author: Chimp Ran
reviews.title: The exhibits did not flow.
reviews.content: Walked in & presented with a jumble of items from various time lines with little or no connection. Story boards were in Vietnamese only with minor details in English & French.Little effort to convey the sequence of events & connect the pieces of history.30k vnd for pictures, get real!Go to the history museum for a class act instead.

reviews.author: Laurent M
reviews.title: Interesting history of Vietnam's wars
reviews.content: They cover early wars from the 1200 Mongolian invasions up to tye American war. Lots of artefacts on display. The airplanes and tanks outside could use better maintenance though. Not a lot of info on what the airplanes or other equplipment were designed for, just when they captured it. Lots of propaganda though but interesting to see their side of the story

reviews.author: simon w
reviews.title: Close during midday! Worth a visit
reviews.content: They have a huge collection of all kind things from the war! The collection they have a planes, hilicoptors and tank are very interesting. However, you get a little tired of the almost propaganda like view they take on the war. It's a bit too one-side.

reviews.author: ComplicatedDisaster
reviews.title: Interesting, I guess.
reviews.content: I guess in hindsight it should have been obvious that the Vietnamese would call the war the American War.  The museum is interesting but a lot of the interpretation is only in Vietnamese so it's hard to understand a lot of what is on display.  There's a poignant sculpture made out of parts of crashed US aircraft.  You also get access to the flag tower.  40K to get in.

reviews.author: Meranbloom
reviews.title: Not a must on your attraction list
reviews.content: a small place. we went there on Friday afternoon and the museum was closed. but you can still pay an entrance fee, abt 20k or 10k dong to see some of the machineries used in war and parts of a destroyed warcraft plane. we saw tourist buses there, so i guess it is a must go visit place for them in their itinerary. the entire place can be combed in less than 30 min.

reviews.author: Werner1979
reviews.title: Interesting museum but it needs some maintenance
reviews.content: Our 5 year old son was very interested in all the planes and tanks that you could see.It was interesting but there was almost no information in English so the visit didn't take that much time.

reviews.author: Hyppe
reviews.title: Old Planes and Tanks
reviews.content: This attraction is very old, not well kept. You have to pay a fee to enter. They have tanks, guns, a few jet planes. Some of the vehicles are falling apart. Not much evidence of american war equipment. If you really have no place to go, then visit this place.

reviews.author: Jonny W
reviews.title: Interesting but run down museum
reviews.content: Highlight was the recovered tanks, planes and artillery outside. Shame it's starting to rust in the heat and rain but still great impact. The 2 internal sections (war against colonialist French and the US "sabotage" war as its referred to throughout) could do with an upgrade but the cuttings and artefacts are good.  Downside is the lack of English translations for many of the the artefacts and pictures. As with many of the museums in Hanoi it is at times comically partisan on its explanation of events. Part of the charm I guess.

reviews.author: Pete
reviews.title: Great museum
reviews.content: This place has strange opening hours as its open in the morning up until 11:30am and then closes until 1pm when it opens again. Aside from that, the museum is interesting and has some great things on the outdoor section including planes, bombs and helicopters. We loved walking around and would recommend a visit.

reviews.author: Neil M
reviews.title: Interesting Collection of War Artefacts
reviews.content: As expected, this visit gives a somewhat partisan version of events for both French & American conflicts. It is worthwhile, although possibly bettered by the Saigon version?

reviews.author: Sam From Canada
reviews.title: A History Buff's Delight
reviews.content: We came on a Monday when everything is closed. But, you are still able to tour the outside, which was amazing to say the very least. A history buff myself, I was in heaven. They have many captured American military vehicles and equipment, including the engines and remains of shot down B52 bombers! It was a great way to experience the military history of the Vietnam War.

reviews.author: Glyn G
reviews.title: Military history museum
reviews.content: You have to visit this place just to understand the atrocities and hardship that these people went through during the American war. The building is air conditioned so was a welcome break from the 39deg heat outside. We were warned not to catch a taxi outside the museum as apparently they are notorious for ripping off Westerners so we walked 1k and got one.

reviews.author: Neil S
reviews.title: Sad
reviews.content: I think one must visit to see war from the Vietnamese perspective.Very sad to see the results of war and bombing and of course agent orange! There is no nice part in war, so don't expect to not have a tear or two at some point.

reviews.author: Pekka S
reviews.title: War is always brutal
reviews.content: But if you want to see how Vietnam people have defended their own country against many countries, go and see the long period of different wars. They have never underestimated the enemy which is very important.  Some things are a bit overestimated but still you can find out lot´s of interesting things. Of  course museum is mainly concentrated to last wars and I think there is a lot to learn about that. Very educating visit.

reviews.author: Nick C
reviews.title: Tad one sided
reviews.content: Very informative regarding past conflicts but very one sided.  Worth a visit as not expensive. Artifacts quite good.

reviews.author: Sven W
reviews.title: Lacks international character
reviews.content: The museum is easily found due to the big aircrafts in the exterior of the building. Inside the museum there are several buildings with all their own theme. The biggest problem is that only a few of the pieces showcased in the museum are accompanied with an English text. So for a lot of the pieces it's hard to place it in perspective. The museum is primarily for domestic public. Furthermore the history is being told from one side. This makes it interesting to see how the current day propaganda in Vietnam works.

reviews.author: Incense Travel
reviews.title: Best place to learn about Vietnam wars
reviews.content: If you want to know more about how Vietnamese manage to fight in their two main war: French colonial war and the Vietnam war then this is the place for you. This is a large museum with two mains sections related to those two wars. Lots of broken war fares displayed. The pieces of a broken B52 is impressive. You should really have to go to the back of the museum to see the tank and war craft collection.

reviews.author: Lara M
reviews.title: Cool planes and tanks
reviews.content: The stuff inside the building is boring. I won't lie. The stuff outside and the tower were awesome! Really interesting to see how many choppers and planes they managed to take from the US and the French. They definitely put up a good fight!Must do military museum

reviews.author: bruno l
reviews.title: impressive war museum
reviews.content: quite an impressive war museum with so many pictures and artefacts. you can spend quite a while if you go into all the details. English explanations are sometimes missing or poor.

reviews.author: jackmoore93
reviews.title: Really cool museum!
reviews.content: Really cool museum with an outside area full of American/Vietnamese and soviet jeeps, planes and helicopters etc. Inside the buildings are good exhibitions telling you the history of Vietnamese military aswell as giving you an insight to influential people. We paid 40k dong to enter

reviews.author: chicagobizjetpilot
reviews.title: B-52
reviews.content: When I went there I was the only person there. I walked freely around the remains of the B-52 and other aircraft

reviews.author: RATZnz
reviews.title: Best Museum we went to
reviews.content: This Museum wasn't top on our guides list so we weren't sure if it was worth going to.  There's lots to see with interesting facts about various bits of equipment.  Really glad we made the effort to go see this.

reviews.author: Hammad A
reviews.title: Gives you an idea about Vietnam War
reviews.content: This was a must visit place in my list and I would say the Vietnamese have tried to maintain it as best as they can. The only issue seems to be that no one cares about translating or explaining the stuff inside in English. You can always request for a guide if you inform them at the beginning of the tour while buying the ticket but don't expect the level English to be high. Maybe the authorities need to place the helicopters and planes in some kind of shade rather than leaving them in open air where sun, rain and sea wind is affecting them.

reviews.author: Robert P
reviews.title: Interesting visit.
reviews.content: It was a very good side trip during my city tour. The displays are very well organised and labeling is also done in English.

reviews.author: ScottAfghanistan
reviews.title: Good museum.
reviews.content: A good museum of the Vietnam war albeit if offers a one sided opinion.  It's worth a visit, especially for military history buffs.  A good indoor activity that takes several hours to see.

reviews.author: Iryshe
reviews.title: An Interesting Place to Visit
reviews.content: An interesting collection of military history, focusing mostly on the Indochinese Wars of the 20th century. The interior contains many photos and artifacts while the exterior has displays of many pieces of military equipment, including a sculpture of shot down American and South Vietnamese aircraft. Be aware that the museum closes down for an hour for lunch - though the grounds remain open during that time.

reviews.author: Ngan H
reviews.title: Expensive entrance fee
reviews.content: The entrance fee is expensive. Really! So I don't go in the museum. Hope the fee can be lowered so that more people can afford to visit the museum.

reviews.author: LouenStephan
reviews.title: nearly only documents and photo's of unknown people
reviews.content: we visited this part of the history museum, because it was included in the entrance fee.  There are so many documents and photos, only interesting maybe for local people

reviews.author: 960kaseyb
reviews.title: Military museum
reviews.content: Recently went here with the family. Was a good day; really enjoyed it. We learnt a lot about the Vietnam war between them and the French. It was really awesome. Saw heaps of cool planes and cannons they used in the war. Great for young kids, my 2 year old brother absolutely loved it!

reviews.author: Tom W
reviews.title: Interesting afternoon
reviews.content: Don't get me wrong this is a really good museum but it didn't come close to the war remnants museum in Ho Chi Minh city......

reviews.author: pata157
reviews.title: Very interesting place
reviews.content: An interesting place which catalogue Vietnam ' s history of conflicts going back many hundreds of years. Very proudly displayed is a collection of US military aircraft and ground craft.

reviews.author: SBoyle9416
reviews.title: Worth the Dong
reviews.content: A lot to see at this museum! There is photo exhibitions, videos, interactive activities as well as a lot of relics from the many conflicts and wars that Vietnam has been involved in. This is also opposite the Lenin statue and the flag tower so definitely worth the trip.

reviews.author: Russell C
reviews.title: Be careful it's in 2 parts and easy to miss the other part
reviews.content: Some interesting history of the Vietnamese during the various wars. A bit propaganda-ish in verbiage but what countries don't tell things from their viewpoint.

reviews.author: Poosan
reviews.title: Great Museum
reviews.content: The museum is a great to have a walk round for a few hours. Yes like others have said some of the English translation is a bit off but you can muddle through to understand. Some (most!) of the interactive stuff wasn't working on our visit which was a shame.There's a outside section that houses planes and tanks which is interesting. The price is so cheap, only a few £ for a visit.

reviews.author: Joy
reviews.title: Not enough information
reviews.content: I would have love to know the stories behind the conflict of the wars but I just could not find any information regarding it.  There were documentaries that were in the local dialect.  I suspect the stories of the conflicts were there.I like the outdoor exhibit a lot :-DI was quite surprised with the lunch break where visitors were asked to leave.  It was a good thing there was a nice cafe at a distance where my friends and I went for lunch.  When we left the museum there was a man outside asking for our tickets.  I feel like he is going to recycle the tickets.  They are not strict with people going in and out the place plus the ticket do not have a date.

reviews.author: JLC-1972
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: This museum gives a great view of the Vietnam War seen from Vietnamese perspective. The exhibits have recently been updated and includes numerous artifacts and good texts in English. The collection of planes in the front is also quite cool to view - as is the view from the Flag Tower.

reviews.author: Genepy
reviews.title: Indoor and outdoor exhibits
reviews.content: Spend about 2 hours here, tanks, choppers etc outside with smaller artefacts inside. The signage is in Vietnamese and therefore hard to follow. As one would expect the stories are heavily biased towards the Vietnamese. The museum in Saigon is better and its not a patch on the Cu Chi tunnels!

reviews.author: Dan L
reviews.title: Well worth the visit
reviews.content: The history of Vietnam since 1945 has been dominated by war, and this museum showcases the conflicts in which the country won its independence.  It`s not an "objective" analysis of the conflicts, but it doesn't have to be.  This is the story told by the victors, and it's a pretty good one.  Of special note is the diorama of the Battle of Dien Bien Phu, which ended the French colonial era in 1954.  In a large relief display of the area, supplemented by audio and visual displays, the battle plays out, as little red lights show the progress of the Vietnamese forces until the final moment of victory.  It's well done.In much of the museum, the signage is only in Vietnamese, which limits its usefulness to tourists.  But there's enough here to make one wonder about the various strategists and tacticians who continually underestimated the Vietnamese.  This museum has a lot packed into a small amount of space and repays a visit.  It's one of a number of military museums in Hanoi, and is probably the best.

reviews.author: SOH KIEN PENG
reviews.title: Arrogant display of military hardware
reviews.content: I stayed at the Old Quarters and I walked my way to this military history museum. The museum is open everyday from 8 am to 11.30 am and from 1 pm to 4.30 pm. A huge billboard of the typical communist propaganda type with praises for the Army was proudly displayed at the front entrance. I did not access into the museum through the main door. I entered from the side door of a café near to the Flag Tower. It was free entry. A row of artillery cannon used during the Nguyen Dynasty was on display near the entrance. Walked further in and I saw the display of numerous war planes, helicopters, truck, cannons, etc and the display of giant planes extended further to the perimeter walls.  Vietnam is always proud to showcase her military museums. Whether you are in Ho Chih Min, Dien Bien Phu or Hanoi or Hoi An, the artifacts displayed in the military museums in these places tell only one story: the `Great Victory' of the `Invincible' Vietnamese Revolutionary Army  against French colonialism, US Imperialism and foreign subjugation and oppression.'One display board in this museum stated: `In the Vietnam War, the US used 29 kinds of destruction bombs, 13 kinds of anti-personnel bombs, 25 kinds of manual detonators and 10 kinds of electronic detonators. Between 1965 and 1972, the US dropped 5,382,000 different types of bombs on both the North and South of Vietnam. The US bombardment killed more than 80,000 of people and injured more than 200,000 others.' The Vietnam War miserably turned Vietnam into an experimental arsenal and human destruction laboratory. Despite having sophisticated and technological advanced military equipment and hardware, US lost the war. It was an epoch of the titanic show of forces between the democratic bloc led by the US and her allies and the communist bloc led by China and Soviet Union. Vietnam was the playground and the focus of the battlefield of the two opposing forces. While the conventional war theory in Vietnam attributed the victory to great military planning and strategy and the support and unity of her people, I am quite skeptical over this finding. Could Vietnam has won the war against the French and US if China and Soviet Union were not directly supporting her from behind. China had always back up Ho Chih Min giving him the advantage of having unconditional and continual supply of military reinforcement and supplies from the north. While I do not deny that the Vietnamese Army has great strategists and battle tested trained soldiers, the outcome I think would be quite different if the support of the two communist giants were not there then. If a war would to broke out now on the same scale as that in the Vietnam War between an isolated Vietnam and the US `Imperialists', Vietnam may not be so lucky.    The number of US bombers, planes, trucks, helicopters that clustered around the base of flag Tower show the glorious past and Vietnam is always happy and proud to be in that dream. As I walked out of the museum and crossed over to the other side of the road, I saw the statute of Lenin loom like a fiery fighter in front of me. Vietnam was born out of the shadow of this great communist leader. He stood guard and kept watch on this museum so that the glorious victory history continued to be sung.

reviews.author: Nigel W
reviews.title: Selection of militaria
reviews.content: We came across better war museums in Vietnam, notably in Ho Chi Minh or Saigon if you are interested in the history.

reviews.author: BeeB
reviews.title: Lots of items behind glass, not much English.
reviews.content: There were some really interesting artifacts behind glass cases, and a bunch of aircraft, tanks, trucks, etc. however, the museum doesn't present much at all in English. It's closed from 1130-1300, and I showed up around 1215 and was told I couldn't get in yet... So I walked over to the coffee shop (inside the walls of the museum) and was able to spend 45m looking around outside, climbing up the flag tower, and taking photos of the aircraft and trucks for free. That was by far the best part - after 1300, I bought a ticket (40k dong, I think) and spent maybe 30m walking through the exhibit halls. There's not much English at all except in the "American War" section, and even that is minimal, only translating the labels on various items in the cases.  There's no perspective on any of the stuff, no real story to be told - just lots of guns, canteens, uniforms, and documents in French and Vietnamese with no translations.  I'm told a tour guide may be very useful here.

reviews.author: Thwamy
reviews.title: Disorganized
reviews.content: Other than the large planes surrounding the building, the exhibits were mostly disappointing. A lot of the displays lacked English descriptions and there didn't seem to be any chronology to the rooms. I recommend skipping this museum.

reviews.author: DeadlyddPerth
reviews.title: An amazing experience
reviews.content: This complex consists of a ancient tower, grounds and buildings. Everything is very informative and professionally presented. You can examine the military past of Vietnam from ancient times to the American war, and you will certainly find American exhibits including bombs, planes, guns, etc.   There are also many planes, carriers and Viet Cong war materials/actions.   It is very well presented and sign posted. Allow about 2 hours. But it closes for lunch - be aware of this.

reviews.author: Sidneeman
reviews.title: Depends on your interest in history
reviews.content: As a museum goes it's not such a high rating but it covers very well the modern history era and has a good collection for the post 1954 era as well. Interesting display outdoors as well although from a distance it looks a pile of junk, would also appeal to the younger kids as you get up real close.Very much worth a visit but keep an open mind to the representation obviously made from the perspective of the Vietnamese.A bit of a pity that they don't get some professional help with their English translations as this is an International show piece - how hard or costly would this be?

reviews.author: g0girlmelb0urne
reviews.title: Spend a few interesting hours seeing war from the 'other side'
reviews.content: This museum, although small, houses an interesting collection of photos and military equipment.  Explanations are sometimes sad, and seen from the Vietnamese perspective. The collection of tanks, helicopters and pieces of a shot down American plane is quite extraordinary.  The visit helped explain Vietnam's quest for self rule. Well worth a visit. Entrance fee a very reasonable $2.40 (Aus dollars)

reviews.author: Stephen C
reviews.title: Worthwhile to see the history of the last days of South Vietnam
reviews.content: Well maintained museum of the old palace. Living quarters of the King and offices and command centre for use during the war. There is a bunker in the basement (think Cabinet War Rooms in London) and a helicopter on the roof.

reviews.author: Cynthia C
reviews.title: well worth visiting
reviews.content: This was quite an experience not sure what to expect Felt sad at seeing what war does to people wish we had more time

reviews.author: dontstopthetrip
reviews.title: small but interesting
reviews.content: nice museum, with a lot of artifacts and actual war vehicles from the Vietnam war.I loved the outer part with the exposition of tracks and cannons

reviews.author: Travel obsessed
reviews.title: War history
reviews.content: This was a very interesting morning, some insightful information which did have a bias in it as you would expect, but very hands on, great planes and tanks

reviews.author: fjab
reviews.title: Extensive comprehensive collection
reviews.content: Visited with my husband who has an interest in military history. Very little money to get in. Wide ranging exhibits with lots of arms related hardware, much of it displayed within the grounds. Several galleries over two floors.  Beware that the toilets are dreadful, and I do mean really really dreadful.

reviews.author: JLHavinfun
reviews.title: Very interesting...
reviews.content: Another museum where you see the other side of the Vietnam war. It was once a palace that is frozen in time. You see lots of rooms decor from the 60's and then a military under ground bunker.

reviews.author: TomJeffery_123
reviews.title: An interesting attraction
reviews.content: Worth a visit if you're in Hanoi. Easy to tie-in with a walk around town. Plenty of exhibitions to see and an excellent collection of vehicles outside. The museum could have more English information boards, and an audio guide may be able to provide more interaction for the visitors. As many have posted already, it is possible to gain access 'free of charge' from the café next door. However, the already inflated price of 40,000 VND is hardly going to break the bank, you're paying a small fee to access an entire museum. Give something back to the Vietnamese people and appreciate the history of the many periods of conflict.

reviews.author: multi v
reviews.title: Interesting to see the planes on the outside
reviews.content: This museum is closed on a Monday. Unfortunately this was the only day we had to visit. However we were able to photograph the planes on the outside of this museum. It is not far from The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Duncan B
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: Rather dull and dreary, with not much to see. Some Vietnam war planes and tanks for the kids, but definitely don't go to the loos here !!!

reviews.author: loveturkeyLancashire
reviews.title: worth a visit
reviews.content: interesting visit only downside is the opening hours the are closed mon, fri  and shut for 1 1/2 hours over lunch i would give a good 2 hours to see everything so check times before you go they do shut over lunch which means you have to leave even if you didnt get to see every thing

reviews.author: craig094
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: After visiting the military museum you develop a sense of respect for these people who fought the might of the us  and won very interested to see the helicopter on the roof and all the old radio gear in the basement the chinese tanks are also verry cool

reviews.author: MrFood&Wine
reviews.title: A nice visit for some history
reviews.content: When we got here they told us that the building insides was reserved for a larger group. We got a peek of the canons, tanks and planes that where outside though. I think it would been really nice to go inside to get more information and to see the photos and films they provide

reviews.author: EarlyRetirementAbroad
reviews.title: Saw only outside
reviews.content: We could not go inside the museum, but spent some time outside studying the tanks, weapons, bombs, etc. and reading the explanation.  It is good to know the other side of the story.  You’ll appreciate more how nice and friendly Vietnamese people are towards the foreigners.

reviews.author: Charlie_Wondersteen
reviews.title: Poorly executed
reviews.content: Old and not very well-maintained. Has some vintage military gizmos but the museum does not do a good job of educating its visitors or telling a story. The museum in HCMC is much better.

reviews.author: James H
reviews.title: Hanoi War Museum
reviews.content: I really enjoyed walking round the museum. It was good to get the story from the other side of the war. I loved looking at the equipment and vehicles used, it really gave it some perspective of how awful the war was. I will say it is quite a small museum with most of the attractions being outside, there are some bits too look at inside but not much.

reviews.author: sleepybexhill
reviews.title: Visitors to Vietnam should see this museum.
reviews.content: You've had all the American propaganda about the Vietnam war. Now you need to see the other perspective. The museum sets this out in graphic detail. Makes you realise the 20 years of fighting was for nothing. What a waste of life on both sides.

reviews.author: luckylou56
reviews.title: very interesting
reviews.content: This really is a must see.. such history for both the US and Vietnam. Growing up at the beginning of the war in 1970's it make things much clearer to understand.

reviews.author: Simon H
reviews.title: Shut monday and friday but you can still look round outside
reviews.content: This shut at 11.30 on Friday when we went. However you can still look round the outside military tanks, guns and planes .....for free. Good collection of captured hard ware. Toilets on site for those with a strong stomach. Coffee bar by gate was nice.

reviews.author: SangIl oh
reviews.title: there are so many spectacles.
reviews.content: you can learn about the Vietnam war through this place. while i did not expect spectacles in a Vietnam museum, there were so many spectacles. you can visit several sections for tour.

reviews.author: georgeyboy714
reviews.title: very interesting and informative
reviews.content: Lots to see. Quite a comprehensive history of vietnamese military from hundreds and hundreds of years ago to more recent history. sculptures of military heroes past and present as well as scene displays and documentaries make sure the information is gotten across in numerous different ways to keep it interesting. also plenty of war vehicles to see out in the yard ranging from aeroplanes and helicopters to big tanks. To rooms dedicated to the conflict with the US which im particularly interested in so worth a visit for me for sure. 40,000 to get in so just over £1 - well worth it. enjoy.

reviews.author: Paola Grace T
reviews.title: Impressive museum
reviews.content: A must-visit if you are interested in Vietnam war history. It was very informative and we had fun taking pictures at their exhibits. A must visit!

reviews.author: Andrew P
reviews.title: Vietnam's history of conflict
reviews.content: This site gives the full deal of Vietnam's history of armed conflict, from muzzle loading cannons to jet  fighters and SAM missiles.

reviews.author: Zalsapehuh
reviews.title: History & wide collection of weaponries
reviews.content: Indoor and outdoor collections of weaponries from the war. It includes the flag tower with it. There is an entrance fee of 30,000 i think? But you can sneak in from the museum from Highlands Coffee Cafe next to it. No one seemed to care. The building(s) are pretty run down. Much of the information need to reviewed. Wrong spellings everywhere.

reviews.author: Sifex
reviews.title: Impressive military museum featuring planes and guns from the war
reviews.content: The Museum documents the history of the conflict from beginning to end and outside are a variety of planes - Russian Migs and US F2 fighter jets, a Chinook , numerous guns and a rare collection of stone cannon balls.

reviews.author: John L
reviews.title: I Cried
reviews.content: This place is heavy. Don't miss it if you care anything about history. Only half was open, the part about the French years. Excellent Dien Bien Phu battle display.

reviews.author: Jim P
reviews.title: Very Complete Collection
reviews.content: Nice collection, a great walking tour of hardware along with descriptions. Takes you on a logical journey

reviews.author: Gidieh
reviews.title: You get what you pay for.
reviews.content: I'm not that into history, but it was an interresting experience. At first I didn't think we would be that long. The english signs was flawed and sometimes non-existant.It was bigger than it looked with many different parts so make sure you are not in a hurry when you go here.We stayed for 2 hours.

reviews.author: woodfinbrown
reviews.title: Tour of the Vietnam Military History Museum
reviews.content: Was initially reluctant to go but very glad I did.  Very moving, very sobering very important to be reminded about the horrors of war.  Even knowing we were Americans, the Vietnamese could not have been more kind, more hospitable, more gracious..

reviews.author: ErinLK88
reviews.title: Extensive
reviews.content: There are heaps of exhibits, all with labels in English as well as Vietnamese, and a wonderful audio visual display on the final battle against the French. The extensive collection of munitions, tanks and planes was impressive. If you want to know how the exhibits fit together though, you might need a guide - there were no longer explanations. It's also a bit difficult to find your way from building to building.

reviews.author: travelnomadNZ
reviews.title: Not as good as Ho Chi Minh War Remnants
reviews.content: I visited Ho Chi Minh War Remnants first. I found myself comparing it to that building. It covers a lot of history for Vietnam and Ho Chi Minh . But it was not as well organised as Agent Orange section in Ho ChinMinh.It is still worth a look at.
