If you want to understand the Vietnamese people you need to understand their past and their neighbours. For me it also filled in some missing pieces for Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos. It also clarified the French connection.Tip : allow good length of time to visit; take a tour guide it's much easier to understand

reviews.author: manonspot
reviews.title: Disapointed.
reviews.content: We walked to the mausoleum and it took the same amount of walking to find entrance,after you walk around Ho chi mins hose and gardens you come to war museum.pay40000 dong then walk round.No doubt there is plenty of interesting reading mostly about Ho chi min himself but it is not a patch on the one in Saigon and I wish I'd gone to the b52 victory museum instead

reviews.author: EdA27
reviews.title: Difficult to view
reviews.content: Yes, it's pro Vietnamese, but the Agent Orange room with the pictures of birth defects and other damage is real enough. Plus it hurt both sides and nobody was held accountable.

reviews.author: dave b
reviews.title: War history of Vietnam.
reviews.content: Entrance fee 40,000vnd. Closes for lunch 1130 each day.Interesting exhibits from Vietnamese viewpoint.Cafe and souvenir stalls.

reviews.author: markmik
reviews.title: More than the Vietnam War
reviews.content: Lots to see here for about 40000 dong. both indoor and outdoor displays. Indoor with Vietnam war and other wars prior to this. Outside a range of items cannons, aircrafts, tanks and planes.

reviews.author: Cassie W
reviews.title: Lots of info about the war, visit when you are not tired from walking all over the city
reviews.content: There were rooms in here dedicated to the various conflicts and wars and there was a large tower from the war that we explored. They have a large collection of planes and missile launchers as well as the wreckage of a downed plane.This complex was actually quite large and as we had been walking non-stop for 3 days we did not make it through the whole thing.  There are several buildings with different displays which tell similar stories as in the prison and other museums.  Overall we enjoyed looking at the tower and climbing it and looking at the planes and tanks but found the "information" parts a bit long.

reviews.author: SBS63
reviews.title: N interesting and at times shocking representation of hisory
reviews.content: Overall the museum is very informative, but perhaps a little biased.  I did find, as did others with me, that there was an over exposure/concentration on the photographic evidence of the outcomes from the orange gas and Ne pam.  This served I think to somewhat lessen the sympathy  one truly feels as there is too much space dedicated to the atrocities , and it was perhaps a little imbalanced.

reviews.author: DamienBwood93
reviews.title: It was pretty average
reviews.content: The history wasn't too bad however, the war remnants museum was better and more interesting, had a good collection although if museums are your thing, then this is second on the list of things to do

reviews.author: BrianMellor
reviews.title: Good Museum
reviews.content: A good place to go if you are interested in Vietnams war history.The model and film of the battle with the French is brilliant.Relics and information on the war with Americans is also available to view.

reviews.author: Angus M
reviews.title: Excellent collection!
reviews.content: I visited the war remnants museum in Ho Chi Minh city a couple weeks ago and I can honestly say that I liked this place better. It's twice the size and has a lot more equipment on display including a couple of Russian T54 tanks and an array of aircraft and weapons. If you're a history/war buff like myself you'll enjoy every minute of your visit here.

reviews.author: Pun
reviews.title: The history is amazing
reviews.content: If you're interested in learning about the history of this amazing country, the Vietnam Military History Museum is a must. Steeped in artefacts and the violent history of Vietnam, it takes you through a journey from the early days, through the French and American attempts to sabotage the country, and to the modern day. The plane and tank remains are fascinating. A must visit when in Hanoi

reviews.author: Steveprattnz
reviews.title: Some interesting exhibits - but no story
reviews.content: It was difficult to piece the exhibits together - signs say "this weapon taken from captured soldiers and later used to kill 15 enemy".  Not overly believable history and it didn't give a sense of the trials and tribulations of the last decades in Vietnam.  It would be OK if you knew a lot already - but as a learning experience not-so-much

reviews.author: Klas B
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Nice museum but as always you should have a guide. They have quite a lot of items  and tell the story (from a Vietnamese perspective of course) but coming from a country that was not involved in the war it's good the heat both sides of the story

reviews.author: MARKRUN100
reviews.title: Good History
reviews.content: If you are a war history buff you need to see this. Lots of overviews with pictures and narratives. Very worth the trip. Lines were not too bad and there were lots of schools there for graduatoins.

reviews.author: rodja2016
reviews.title: curious
reviews.content: Interesting place to visit, if you are army or historical fan. Tickets costs aint so much, but you can see a lot for that price. As a minus, I can say that it is hard to get what place to go next. As plus - you can touch and phot some army vehicals, helicopters, you can go to the Flag tower etc. You can see Lenin's monument at other side of the road )

reviews.author: vinojeff
reviews.title: Westerners will get a better understanding of the 'Viet Nam' war by visiting and watching the film strip.
reviews.content: Not only are the aircraft worth the visit, but the film strip gave a chilling perspective and made 'one' think hard about America's participation in the 'Vietnam War'.

reviews.author: jce123
reviews.title: Average museum
reviews.content: The museum is smaller than expected and can be visited in under an hour. The only interesting displays are the aircraft and tanks outside. If you intend visiting the excellent War Remnants museum in HCM City, a visit to this museum could be skipped.

reviews.author: Thewanderingpassport
reviews.title: Cant miss this... really
reviews.content: The main highlight for me were bodies of the tanks and planes and other misc war paraphernalia, it was really interesting! I was there for around 2hours and learnt a lot - its always crowded as its a pretty touristy spot but its well worth seeing

reviews.author: Sheila R
reviews.title: Historical War Museum
reviews.content: I expected to see more detailed information about the Vietnam War. It represented what a war museum has, but I wanted to see and gain more information about the past. There was a memorablestatue outside made of destroyed war planes. Thatrepresented the ugliness of war.

reviews.author: Dishaa S
reviews.title: military museum
reviews.content: as you enter the courtyard, you are reminded of the terrible past that vietnam has gone through in its war against the french, americans, cambodians and the chinese through military equipmens, weaponry, fighter planes. a moving place to see

reviews.author: Kevin6333
reviews.title: Not just for military buffs.
reviews.content: Listed on our map as "Army Museum". Displays of Vietnamese military history from ancient times to the defeat of the US 40 years ago.

reviews.author: pepics
reviews.title: War is never nice
reviews.content: The end of the war is still quite close so these war museums surely raise some sad feelings in some people. There are lot of details and authentic photos on display, including the photo of the first American POW. Questionable honor. Outside some bigger memorabilia, you can view them from the citadel also. Also, there is a cafe outside. You cannot take your bag inside the museum.

reviews.author: Jayme B
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: The museum provides a brief overview of the war through old equipment and poorly written informative signs.The real winner here is outside where there are planes, tanks and missiles on display, some of which you can climb on!

reviews.author: abundancetree
reviews.title: A Moving Experience
reviews.content: A moving and sad morning spent at the Vietnam Military History Museum.  The photos and factual accounts of the Vietnam War were harrowing but helped understand what occurred during the period of Vietnamese history.  See history from a different perspective and realize that war is a waste of time, money and most importantly human life.

reviews.author: mumtaz kassim
reviews.title: insight into the war
reviews.content: was a great experience viewing the collections of old and modern warfare used in vietnam...artifacts were kept in good shape ..worth the visit!

reviews.author: Traveler-O-World
reviews.title: Museum of Military History
reviews.content: The Vietnam military history museum gives one an overall view of Vietnamese history particularly from the militaristic angle. There are a series of pictures, maps and artefacts depicting the various military campaigns over the ages.

reviews.author: Sir_Gaurav
reviews.title: Another War Museum
reviews.content: Most well maintained of all museums in Hanoi. Most tourists visit here to know about the military history of the nation.

reviews.author: ramiaj197
reviews.title: Great and comprehnsive
reviews.content: One of the best museums in Hanoi. It has great collections from different eras. I think it is a must for tourists.. The only problem is the lunch break. They close the galleries in the noon time..

reviews.author: haomai
reviews.title: A place can be added to your visiting list
reviews.content: For the open time,you can checked with the hotel or hostel you stay and ask receptionist to help for the way getting there. You can include in your travel list if you are around Ha Noi in few days.

reviews.author: wilburb
reviews.title: A Different Perspective
reviews.content: An interesting location with military hardware  large and small. Stories of individuals and groups.Measure what you see and read against what you already know. It is as interesting as the American perspective.  It will educate many Americans as to what happened in their war in Viet Nam, not only in Viet Nam but in Laos and Cambodia.

reviews.author: Karl S
reviews.title: Fascinating collection of military ordnance mainly American.
reviews.content: There is a large collection of planes ,surface to air missiles, artillery , bombs, tanks , from the French & American wars .Mainly American , Soviet & Chinese ,but also some Vietnamese equipment .

reviews.author: Shane L
reviews.title: Visit with an open mind
reviews.content: The military museum is the Vietnamese side of its history. Including the Vietnam War in 1962-1975. As like any other national military museum, there is just the one side portrayed. Take everything you know about the war, add in what you can learn here and somewhere in the middle is the truth.Meanwhile, the actual museum itself has many displays of hardware and pictures from various historical wars, not just the Vietnam War.There is a theatre room upstairs with a light display and video presentation of the war through Vietnamese eyes.I recommend spending a good 2 hours here to take everything in and don't miss out on the Chinook helicopter hidden away towards the back!

reviews.author: Tasha H
reviews.title: Typical Communist Propoganda
reviews.content: Go but keep an open mind. Recommend doing your own research ahead of time on the Vietnam War to see the glaring issues with their data. War is a horrible business with the effects long lasting for all involved but world leaders have a duty to tell history how it happened and not manipulate the facts to best benefit their side in an attempt to manipulate the population and the museum goers. Do not believe everything you read...

reviews.author: Dongxing S
reviews.title: Interesting presentation of Vietnamese military
reviews.content: The place showcases many old weapons in the modern history of Vietnam, generally those used in the wars. The museum also gave some insights on the history and development of the Vietnamese military. Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Jo P
reviews.title: An interesting insight into the Military History of Vietnam
reviews.content: The museum exhibits are set in a series of old colonial buildings with fighting equipment set out in the grounds.  An interesting insight into military history from the Vietnamese side.

reviews.author: Roland M
reviews.title: So So
reviews.content: We found the Military History Museum not so interesting and had much more to offer but nobody seams really care to much to keep it clean and interesting. The washrooms was not cleaned at all for months or years. To us was a waste of time.

reviews.author: Ted O'Connell
reviews.title: A bit one sided but worth the visit
reviews.content: You may find this place a bit one sided and heavy handed in their attempt to try and glorify the Communist vision of warfare.They have lot of exhibits showing how they shot down the US planes, liberated oppressed peoples and won every battle they fought. Of course there is no talk about the Communist atrocities like the mass killings in Hue, or towards ethnic minorities in the south but this is part of their history and it's great to see so many displays on the different fighter jets, bombs, helicopters and military toys....etc.

reviews.author: manucanuck
reviews.title: Another must see for the military lovers
reviews.content: You may find this place leaning favours towards the communism as they have lot of exhibits showing how they shot down the US planes, what bad influence they have towards the then citizens etc but none the less this is part of their history and it's great to see so many displays on the different fighter jets, bombs, helicopters etc. this is where the Hanoi flag tower is also!

reviews.author: Zarin S
reviews.title: Vietnam Military History Museum
reviews.content: You come to know the History of Vietnam by visiting this Museum.  A 20 minute documentary is also showed to get an idea about Vietnam.  The weapons used were also displayed along with the photos.

reviews.author: Geert-JanTelkamp
reviews.title: Not what was expected.
reviews.content: Most of the exhibits don't have a proper explanation. Very, very biased. We just did not like the museum at all.

reviews.author: Barb F
reviews.title: Lots to see
reviews.content: There are lots of full sized air craft, including crashed remnants outdoors, plus various weapons and bombs.  Indoors there are various displays and pictures from wars gone by.  There's quite a bit of ground to cover.  The flag tower, seen from the mausoleum area across the street, is also located on the military museum grounds.  You can go up some fairly steep steps and get a good overview of the grounds and some city views from the tower.  Entrance fee is 40,000 VND plus another 30,000 if you want to take pictures.  As most sites in Hanoi, this one also closes between 11:30-1.

reviews.author: Andrew G
reviews.title: Interesting tour through military history
reviews.content: Some good exhibits of the conflict with the French and the Americans. Naturally part of the fun is to spot some of the biased or subjective descriptions, exhibitions and focus of the Vietnamese but it does work well if you have an open mind!

reviews.author: Leung W
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: The exhibition covers the ancient military history to modern Vietnam war.  However, not all display has English explanatary note.  Better to have some very basic information on the Vietnam history before your visit this museum.

reviews.author: david j
reviews.title: So much information to take in, superb place
reviews.content: This was the first place on our itinerary, and was quite an eye opener. There are a lot of war planes and tanks here as well as a lot of American wreckage from the American War. IT was here that I first found out about Agent Orange that the Americans used to defoliate the jungle to prevent the Viet Cong from hiding out. Sadly the effects of exposure have had serious consequences for the population with deformities and health problems. I learned a lot that I didn't know about this war, as we've only really heard the American side before.

reviews.author: BladeKandahar
reviews.title: Interesting, but you'd better study ahead!
reviews.content: Great place to visit and, like all the attractions, super cheap, but the place desperately needs a good curator. If you didn't know the history of the Vietnam war - the central part of the multi-building exhibition - you'd just see a bunch of relatively context-free photos, guns and maps. As just one example, the exhibit on the short Sino-Vietnamese 'war' in 1979 consists of a couple of pictures and a caption about 'defending the Northern border' - without mentioning China!  A few explanatory posters for each section, in a couple of common languages, would be a cheap way to improve an otherwise interesting collection.

reviews.author: Tracois29
reviews.title: A junkyard of history
reviews.content: Found in the Ba Dinh District of Hanoi, the Vietnam Military History Museum is a relic in itself.  Established in 1956 following the Vietnamese defeat of the French at Dien Bien Phu, the museum is in need of revitalising.There are many relics, particularly weapons from the many conflicts that have passed through Vietnam.  All have stories attached of the heroic deeds of their owners.Particularly interesting is the fact that someone decided to keep the table and chairs that Ho Chi Minh and the politburo had their strategy meetings at to defeat the French in 1953/54.There is an interesting diorama with lighting and accompanying video that tells the story of the battle of Dien Bien Phu.  On the day we were there, some cadets from the military academy were also present.  Apparently this is part of their military history training.The museum is part of the larger Hanoi Citadel which covers a large part of this district.  The most impressive part of the museum is the Hanoi Flag Tower.  Constructed in the early 1800’s it has flown the Vietnamese flag daily from the mid-1950’s.  You can no longer climb to the very top of the tower.  This decision was made following a visitor falling to their death whilst leaning out from the tower.  You can climb to the top of the base which still allows for some good views of the scale of the citadel.The grounds of the museum are like a military junkyard with lots of captured and downed aircraft from the various wars.Overall, an interesting site to visit to see some of history, but it does need some help to maintain its exhibits.

reviews.author: Benjamin_Martyn
reviews.title: Great place for military hardware sightseeing
reviews.content: The tour itself is a bit ordinary but is self guided and the museum is rather spacious. There is great military hardware on display and they are very interesting to see.

reviews.author: ABA27
reviews.title: Histort
reviews.content: Went with a vetran and did not really want to go BUT I learned so much that I still despise what races do to races and now I have gained som knowledge about this country and its relentless attacks from so many other countries, these people really fought hard to hold on to their country, everyone fights hard in war, kill or be killed, sad the world is not learning from the horrors of war. even one that finished in Vietnam in just 1975!

reviews.author: Travelthew0rld79
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: More like a graveyard for a few captured French and US military hardware, with some Vietnamese military hardware. Most articles in Vietnamese. Shame, as it'd be great to understand as a foreigner.

reviews.author: David M
reviews.title: Really impressive
reviews.content: I hadn't expected to enjoy this as much as I did. Really beautiful interior and incredibly cool and peaceful feel to it. Who knew that 60's architecture could beso good!

reviews.author: Paul P
reviews.title: War displays and icons
reviews.content: Enjoyed the afternoon exploring the remnants of the war. Lots of aircraft to view, including jets, prop planes, helicopters and rockets. Many different types of vehicles to inspect, such as tanks and jeeps.Spread across a number of buildings with many displays of information, photos, weapons, hand guns, rifles, machine guns, missile launchers and bombs. There was a scaled down model display of the tunnels used during the war.

reviews.author: Coljosh
reviews.title: Very moving and well laid out with lots to see up close
reviews.content: Both snide and outside exhibits with lots to read and see. Lots of graphic pictures so not really a place for young children

reviews.author: Colum S
reviews.title: Well wort a look!
reviews.content: Glad I went to see this. I was also at war remnants museum in HCMC which I thought was very interesting and this is every bit as good. A lot of exhibits so allow a couple of hours to see everything. Closes for lunch too so check times before you go there. Not far from Hanoi centre.

reviews.author: 816terry
reviews.title: different view of the war
reviews.content: everything is labeled the aggressive American war, I never knew the bad things  the Americans did, but interesting to see the equipment the Americans left behind

reviews.author: Rachelle W
reviews.title: Very moving
reviews.content: One would visit here for the planes, helicopters, tanks and missiles set up for display rather than what is inside the museum.  Many of the internal displays are Vietnamese-language only so non-native speakers can't get too much out of it.The outdoor displays of military machinery is amazing though.  You can't help but feel overwhelmed at times, especially when standing before the reconstructed mess of metal that is a crashed US bomber plane recovered from a lake.  The equipment displayed are real machines flown/ shot/ driven by real people and the weight of that on the heart of those visiting cannot be truly captured in a review like this.  Real pain and hopes are attached to them and this visit was the most emotional thing we did the entire time we were in Vietnam.

reviews.author: JVS1956
reviews.title: Must see...
reviews.content: Wonderful relics, data, exhibits, all presented without too much jingoistic fervour.......as much concerned with the war with the French as with the U.S. Of A.

reviews.author: 365Weathers
reviews.title: A must for Military minded traveller
reviews.content: An excellent presentation of the military history of the Vietnamese people, the museum is well worth a visit when in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Michael W
reviews.title: Great history lesson
reviews.content: Spent a few hours at the museum and learnt a lot about the history of the military in Vietnam and the conflicts they endured.

reviews.author: luxultima
reviews.title: The bloody face of war
reviews.content: Many war/military museums I've visited find it difficult to glorify war. I guess that's why some of them call themselves "peace" museums. This museum, on the other hand, is unapologetic and very visceral. You will get an interesting timeline of Vietnamese conflicts, and a glimpse of all sorts of awful weapons. You'll also see a graveyard of the twisted metal of crashed planes. There are also triumphant displays of signs of the revolutionary spirit: instruments and banners. Basically, this museum is unique, but not for those of sensitive stomach or disposition. There is much that is grim and upsetting, but war itself is grim and upsetting, so it's really only appropriate.

reviews.author: Tim M
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: To be honest I can spend all day wandering around these military museums, this was great to see it from the Vietnamese point of view. Some really interesting exhibits to look at as well.

reviews.author: Kimberlie J
reviews.title: War Museum
reviews.content: This experience was incredible, I cannot express enough that all visitors to Hanoi should spend some time here.  It is definitely something I would do again

reviews.author: MrMattiAleksi
reviews.title: History and war, planes, tanks and guns
reviews.content: If you are interested in history and machines like planes, tanks etc. this is place for you. I enjoyed and I think this is specially place for men! Of course ladies also if they are interested in such a things. A Lot of information about guns, tanks, history of Vietnam. I recommend this! It takes approximately 1-2h visit. Entrance fee 30k dong (2,5-3 US dollars)

reviews.author: Daiseaview
reviews.title: An Interesting and Worthwhile Visit
reviews.content: A very interesting experience which identifies the conflicts from the other side and we left with a different understanding of the wars we had some previous knowledge about.

reviews.author: E S
reviews.title: Suprisingly interesting, proud exhibits
reviews.content: Despite a lot of the main text being in Vietnamese, the museum gives an interesting account of the countless battles the Vietnamese army has dealt with.

reviews.author: karol452
reviews.title: War Buffs
reviews.content: If you are a Vietnam war buff this is a must see.  A lot of interesting exhibits,  Outside there are helicopters, cannons, and tanks.

reviews.author: Andrew M
reviews.title: Poorly set out
reviews.content: Sorry to be a Debbie Downer but this was boring. I was very excited about this tour but it was actually just bad. Skip the displays inside, they are set out at random and it's hard to stay interested. Go out the back and look at the cool artillery (the only highlight) and then head home.

reviews.author: Amiad H
reviews.title: A must for anyone interesting in military history
reviews.content: Very interesting museum that covers much of Vietnamese history, but the modern period is much more heavily covered than the older periods.

reviews.author: etai s
reviews.title: The worst museum I have been to
reviews.content: I am quiet a military enthusiast and as such was very disappointed, that is after 3 weeks in Vietnam and some understanding of the local standards:1. Generally the museum and mainly the artifacts are in bad condition and crumbling.2. The info is totally missing without logic through the exhibition.3. Nothing really to see there. The place is boring.4. Even as a propaganda museum it was not convincing.5. Half of the halls were not even air conditioned.Bottom line, Save your time and 40,000D and do something thing else.

reviews.author: Charlie T
reviews.title: one time visit
reviews.content: i thought this is the good place to visit as i heard they said the Vietnamese government have keep the body of Ho chi minh inside but went there can't really see the body look like made from wax and security guards yelling at people to keep moving with out stop and no photo allow to take at all .

reviews.author: Leonard S
reviews.title: Great Experience!
reviews.content: This museum is worth to visit if you're really into military or stuff. Here you can see some war leftover guns, planes, etc.. They also got souvenir shop on the second floor. And you can watch a movie about the war history too on the second floor. I go to the some kind of watch tower and go up, careful for the head room, when I go inside the tower, I thought I ducked low enough, but my head still hit the stone, pretty hurt. The watch tower looks kinda dirty with all the marker and paint from visitors (their name, signature, signs, etc.) Too bad the management should pay more attention to maintain this. There's also a Highland Coffee connected to this place, it's pretty cool to chill at this place.

reviews.author: Perry F
reviews.title: Extended HIstory
reviews.content: Like all museums in Vietnam, it is obviously biased. However, the first few rooms are excellent to get a more thorough understanding of pre-French colonial rule. It seems so much is focused on late 1800's to today.

reviews.author: Joe M
reviews.title: Worth seeing
reviews.content: Full of history, providing a visual of the traumatic journey Vietnam endured to achieve independence.  Found to building to be somewhat dated, however worth seeing for the military hardware

reviews.author: Bikehikers
reviews.title: Welcome, 'Comrade'...
reviews.content: I have a real interesting all things Military so was very much looking forward to this visit but I left disappointed. The theme throughout the displays is the French and American roles in various wars in Vietnam, fair enough but thats where the info stops. It would ave been more objective to continue the story with information regarding the communist re-education camps that housed over 1,000,000 (mainly ARVN) and approx. 165,000 died. I felt like i was in 1960's Soviet Union and given its advertised as a museum then I think more objectivity is needed. The complex is also in need of a makeover and the toilets are best avoided...

reviews.author: Worldlycouple
reviews.title: A MUST SEE
reviews.content: I went with the expectation of seeing mostly the US/French Vietnam war effort and walked away with a completely different view of Vietnam.  These people have been invaded since he beginning of time!  They have a rich history of occupation and defeat, yet they somehow continued with their traditions and hung onto their ideals.  For everything you may think you know about this country, the military museum will enlighten you some.  Although the context is military, I do not believe you can examine the history of Vietnam without examining the conquests of foreign powers.  And that is what this museum does best; puts this out there for you to decide.  I thoroughly enjoyed the time and the amount f information given; and although nearly all the static displays deal with the US portion of the war in Vietnam, the exhibits vary greatly over the history of this country.  You can easily spend a day here if you are interested in learning about this country.  And regardless of what you may think of Ho Chi Min he did unify the country and got back their national dignity; I can see why he is hailed as the father of modern day Vietnam.  I truly left this country with a new appreciation and a thorough understanding of their rich history.

reviews.author: Bickykid
reviews.title: Welcome to propaganda!
reviews.content: There is plenty to see, which all is definitely spun with a communist twist, which is understandable, but for me it lacked a narrative taking you through the journey of what happened and why. This would have greatly improved the experience as it seemed like a disparate set of items without knowing the full story

reviews.author: keith B
reviews.title: Military museum
reviews.content: This was a great musuem with lots of great history and information about the military history of Vietnam.

reviews.author: Carlos R
reviews.title: Interesting artifacts from the war
reviews.content: If you like war history or if you are a pilot, then this is a must-see, otherwise you might be disapointed. The ticket is around 30000 VND, and you have access to two main areas: the museum, with some relics from Ancient Vietnam (although most of them are fake) and the outside area, where some planes and tanks are on exhibition: a MIG-21, a tank, two american Skyhawks, a helicopter (a Huey, of course). You have also a soviet missile used in air defense in Hanoi, wich was used to shoot a B-52, which remains are also on display (well, it's more like a pile of scrap metal than the remains of an aircraft, and additionaly, there were a few parts that do not belong to a B52). Considering the price (less than 2 USD), I consider this to be an interesting visit and would recomend it

reviews.author: S T
reviews.title: An insight in to the Vietnamese War
reviews.content: This place gives you a real sense of the Vietnamese war from a communist perspective. We visited with our daughter who is currently studying Vietnam for her GCSE history. The propaganda is prolific and understandable. The artillery and weapons on display really make you pause for thought.

reviews.author: Mary Anne
reviews.title: You need to be strong to see some of the War pictures
reviews.content: A must place to see what the War bring to human and generations after. No ones is right 100% for doing all of the actions we saw with the brutal killing, torturing and haphazard bomb

reviews.author: PennyPie
reviews.title: A Must See
reviews.content: This place is just somewhere you must go to get lots of the real history of Vietnam. Well documented, easy to get around and some scary photographs. Could have spent lots more than the hour and a half we got allocated.

reviews.author: roamingmark1
reviews.title: Outside displays the hi lite...for the aficionado and the boys.
reviews.content: Like many of these  Museums the displays are in poor condition and are for the history aficionado.Inside I wanted to know more about the battle campaigns but the displays and maps are all in Vietnamese which is a common occurrence. My Teenage boys enjoyed the outside war memorabilia but these are the hi-lite of the museum. Entry is 40,000 Vietnamese dong each.10 minute walk south  from "Ba Dinh Square" and another 10 minute walk south to the "Temple of Literature" (which is outstanding).Makes for an interesting morning

reviews.author: Sizzlin S
reviews.title: Very Interesting
reviews.content: Very Interesting tour. Unfortunately could not go into museum that day (closed mondays). Fantastic tour guide..Clean and beautiful buildings.

reviews.author: Martin H
reviews.title: Excellent collection of Military equipment
reviews.content: This was one of the first places that we visited whilst in Hanoi. A real eye opener as to to all the weapons that were used by both sides during the American war in the 60's & 70's.  Well worth a visit for around 50 pence each and this is a better collection / museum than it's equivalent in HCMC.

reviews.author: Tancredi C
reviews.title: A surprise
reviews.content: Interesting museum full of original military gear dating back to the 40s. Way better than its equivalent in HCM. Unfortunately there's little info and explanations in english. Still a valid museum to see.

reviews.author: Tom M
reviews.title: Poorly designed for non-Vietnamese
reviews.content: There are cool examples of military hardware outside the museum, but inside the exhibits are fairly boring, with no, or very little, explanations in English. 40,000 dong entrance. Very disappointing.

reviews.author: Urgenta
reviews.title: Interesting place
reviews.content: Very affordable entrance fee at 40,000VND A great place for children to learn more about Vietnamese war history. Lots of aircrafts and tankers makes the place much more interesting to visit. A place worth visiting.

reviews.author: Chris101111
reviews.title: Very good.
reviews.content: A good insight to the wars of the country, lots of exhibits and one of the few places you can get up close, touch and climb in and over the many war machines that are on show. Closed on Mondays, for the low price it's well worth the trip to visit this museum.

reviews.author: Puppy
reviews.title: Lots of attractions in this area
reviews.content: The museum is right next to the Flag Tower of Hanoi, opposite Lennon Park, beside the citadel and very close to HCM mausoleum so lots to see in one area. If you want to see all of these attractions go to the mausoleum first (it can be hard to get in), then the Military history museum and flag tower before visiting the citadel. You can get a coffee, food and souvenirs.

reviews.author: Gavatron07
reviews.title: Interesting but could be better
reviews.content: The Vietnam Military History Museum is interesting if you are keen on military history but could be so much better if more information was provided in English.  This is a not an expectation but rather a reflection that many people visiting it are visitors to Vietnam not locals. There are interesting exhibits but it would have been a better experience to have understood more about the context of what I was seeing.  I think the War Remnants Museum in Ho Chi Minh City does a better job of catering for visitors even if the focus of the two museums is different.

reviews.author: robinson25261
reviews.title: Some interesting exhibits
reviews.content: It's worth a trip to the museum to see the old tanks, planes and helicopters but the language used in the exhibits is 'unusual'. It's certainly good value and there's a lot to see.

reviews.author: Kyl J
reviews.title: Good to see
reviews.content: Good little set up to see.. needs to be a bit more from all aspects of the  war. Great condition artifacts and remnants. . A must see in the city

reviews.author: Mark W
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: Went here hoping to help our teenage children understand the history of the country and the various wars. I found that the museum lacked information, story telling and basic signs to guide the visitor. If you are pressed for time during your visit, you will not miss anything if you don't go here. If you have time, then worth a visit to see the collection of articles from the wars and to listen to the projection of the defeat of the French army. It doesn't take very long to walk around. The children liked the tanks and stuff.

reviews.author: Christy M
reviews.title: Very real - a must for history geeks
reviews.content: Spent about 2 hours in here for an afternoon in Hanoi. Had studied the Vietnam war to second level education and so loved every minute of this museum's displays. Great showcasing of real machines and weapons which were taken from the French and U.S armies, and a good section on guerrilla warfare used by the Vietcong. If you're from France or the U.S, be prepared for some biased language in the displays, but it is only 40 years since the war which divided this country for 21 years finished so things are very close and very visceral.

reviews.author: Rumsby
reviews.title: Still great when it's closed!
reviews.content: When we got there is was closed.  It was Monday.  However, you can still access the outside area which displays military aircraft, tanks and rocket launchers from different conflicts.  We spent an hour here ( for about £1 each) and learnt lots.  There is also a very nice cafe in the grounds.  Well worth a visit even if it's closed!!

reviews.author: Gill_tripping
reviews.title: Propaganda museum
reviews.content: I spent most of my visit trying not to laugh at the crazy captions. The one the stays with me is of a heroic tank. This isn't the most inspiring museum around, I'd not really recommend it. I didn't learn anything I didn't already know.

reviews.author: John Daunt 🇮🇪
reviews.title: Not providing enough for tourists
reviews.content: This could be a fascinating place to visit given the extensive military history of Vietnam. However, there is little information available in English or other languages and the various plans/tanks etc. seem to be scattered around in no apparent order and again with little information as to their history. We still enjoyed spending an hour here but without more info and no air con we soon had to leave for a cold drink. Tip: closed Mondays and Fridays, visit whilst on the way back from nearby Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Max-zeene L
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: The outside of the museum provides many interesting artifacts to engage you as a viewer. However, inside the text is mostly in Vietnamese and there's too much in too little space to wrap your head around. It's interesting nonetheless but there's a lot which can get a bit confusing or jumbled. Still worth a visit and it doesn't charge.

reviews.author: rtc31293
reviews.title: Easy to do on your own
reviews.content: This is a nice exhibit that does not require a guide. The signs are informative and the exhibits are cool. Worth a strop after hi chi Minh mosuleum.

reviews.author: macneillfamily
reviews.title: Also worth a visit if you have time
reviews.content: Good introduction, into the Vietnamese war with the French, and then with the Americans, good exhibitions and narrative of the struggle against the foreign invaders! Will only take you an hour to go around

reviews.author: Mario S
reviews.title: go for it
reviews.content: If you are interested of Vietnam history, you will get very good overview about latest history and Vietnamese war. Tanks, planes etc in outside is experience itself, its very amazing. Dont visit it in very hot day, because AC in rooms are very low and walking outside is also exhausting during very hot day. I expected this museum is bigger but its good enoughAlso take opportunity to climb top of flag tower also to get great view

reviews.author: Kyle K
reviews.title: Incredible Value and Display
reviews.content: The best part about the museum is its' large collection of warplanes and large weapons, both Vietnamese (Soviet built), and those captured from the French and the Americans.  The Hanoi flag tower adds even more allure to the site.  Entry is less than $2 USD.

reviews.author: Sam B
reviews.title: Worth a visit for the price
reviews.content: Quite a cheap attraction in Hanoi at 40,000 dong for entry. Had maybe 3/4 planes, a few of tanks, a helicopter and miscellaneous war paraphernalia (mixture of US, Vietnamese and Russian). Plenty of propaganda which is interesting to read too. Won't really take more than an hour or two to see everything. Good for something to do when you've got time to kill on an afternoon.

reviews.author: David W
reviews.title: Fan of war vehicles and equipment? You have to go!
reviews.content: Being from England we have loads of war museums with large collections of vehicles and equipment so going here was a no brainier! The museum is fantastic especially for the price. There's loads to see in the way of tanks, planes, helicopters, guns, rockets. Good to see a lot of South Vietnamese and American displays in Northern Vietnam too.I loved every minute in here and you get a great view of the Flag Tower too!

reviews.author: Tammy F
reviews.title: Average - kids liked the planes
reviews.content: We travelled as 2 adults and 2 kids aged 18 months and 4 years. The kids enjoyed running around and touching the jeeps and planes.The museum had interesting displays that went through the various wars of Vietnam.Overall a good museum and an easy way to spend 2-3 hours.

reviews.author: John W R
reviews.title: Military History
reviews.content: Good for a half day visit this museum gives the history of Vietnams wars and has many displays with actual tanks and planes used in these wars. For those interested in history well worth a visit. The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is close by (5 min walk) so this trip can easily be combined with a visit there. Just watch the taxis as they will try to take an extended route to get you there rather arrange through your hotel.

reviews.author: Melv82
reviews.title: Photo and storymuseum
reviews.content: First we don't wnt to do this because the good weather, but when it starts to rain like hell, we get there...and we don't regret. It's a story and photomuseum...but it's get's you until your bones in your body.

reviews.author: nootnoot6
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: It was amazing to see bombers, helicopters and wreckage up close. A fascinating insight into the realities of war.

reviews.author: Untoldwanderlust
reviews.title: Worth a visit for sure!
reviews.content: it's 40,000vnd for entry. The most for a museum I've known during my visit across Vietnam.However the price you pay makes up for the amount there is to see. There are several building with things to see including outdoor exhibits also. Tanks, planes, helicopters, weapons, guns, uniforms ect

reviews.author: Naylorsontour2015
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: Perhaps need to have a basic understanding of Viet history before going as exhibits not necessarily in chronological order. Closes for lunch Nice Highland café on site

reviews.author: AndyL83
reviews.title: Step into the Vietnam War
reviews.content: My partner and I walked to the museum from the old quarter ( a mean feat in the 38 degree heat).As you approach, you can see what looks to be a MIG jetfighter in the courtyard - being a military history fan, I started to get very excited.............until the guard informed us that it was closed and frogmarched us out of the courtyard where my partner and myself spent 10mins trying to dissuade two moped tour touts to take us on a tour of the city - no thanks.However, we did discover a convenient life hack for this - after being turned away and admitting defeat, we both went for a consolatory drink in the Highlands Coffee next door. I was cursing our rotten luck, (as you can see the citadel tower in the war museum's courtyard and the tip of the B52 wreckage over the wall - I thought this was the closest I would get) when I caught a couple walking through the courtyard next to the MIG before turning into the seating area of Highlands Coffee - no one seemed to challenge them or did they seem to be any problem about walking being the two.Grabbing my camera and partner, we managed to time our run when the guard at the gate ( about 150-200 yards from where the two courtyards meet) turn his back and we dashed into the war museum courtyard where we were able to take some pictures of the excellent military machines on display. Huey choppers, tanks strike fighters, artillery pieces and the colossal wreckage of a B52 shot down over Hanoi, it was superb. We were eventually rumbled by the guard who politely asked us to leave. Although we didn't see inside, the external displays were amazing.Well recommended

reviews.author: wilanmedia
reviews.title: an excellent display of military artifacts
reviews.content: The only problem we had with the Museum was a timing issue as the building housing the "American War" was closed for renovation, but seeing Bell "Huey" choppers intact was a surprise.

reviews.author: Judit731
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: This museum has a good collection of memorabilia and  in most cases is labelled and has the history. If you like this sort of thing it is well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Jose Luis B
reviews.title: 100% Vietnamese
reviews.content: After months living in Hanoi (2012), finally i decided to enter in the Military Museum. It has been designed in a Vietnamese way, cos you can find so many things, so many objects. Not recommended for any lover of Museography or Museology. Because it is not a "Museum" it is just a place they found to put a piece of each american war-object that they capture. Special mention to the Hall of Fame of war heros they have in the inside of the building. Amazing soldiers with unbelievable stadistics, only possible to learn from them coming to the Museum. Lets try, you cannot complain about the price. ( And you will be able to climb any Helicopter or tank that you want! )

reviews.author: HugoColle
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: We heard all about the war from the Western side but here you see and hear the Vietnamese side...bit of propaganda..ofcourse but didnt we do the same..Alot of things to see here from history, war, peace,.. You find weapons, tanks, airplanes, guns,...everything what was used in the war. Learn more from their founder Ho Chi Minh, he was a great leader thats for sure. A must see when one loves history and wants to know more.

reviews.author: James T
reviews.title: Not too bad at all
reviews.content: I was going to visit this place while I was in Hanoi and I stumbled across it while I was wandering around the French Quarter looking for the Hanoi Hilton. Being late morning the indoor displays were about to close for lunch, but I still had time to see what I wanted to see and photograph. The T.54B tank that broke through the gates of the Independence Palace in 1975 is there, plus torpedo tubes, a metal discharging boat, numerous planes and the remains of a B52-D bomber placed almost in an artistic display. I "loved" the stone cannonballs. Unfortunately the Tower had closed for lunch, so that was a bit disappointing as I had wanted to climb to the top and take some pics. As I was taking photos of the aircraft a nice young lady walked within a few metres of me, gave a 'V' so I took her photo too. That's what gets me about the Vietnamese, the people always seem happy to have their photo taken. I thought the Museum was quite good and for the admission price being so cheap, that makes it all the more rewarding.

reviews.author: Jeffkhs
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: We visited the museum on a Friday morning and was told by the ticket counter that the indoor exhibit was closed.  Anyway, we were told that we can alternatively visit the outdoor exhibit for a discounted ticket price (20k Dong).We did so and was quite impressed with the planes, tanks and other military hardware that were on display. You had Russian and American hardware displayed side by side.Some of the equipment was in a state of decay though but all in all an interesting visit.  Leaves me to think what would be contained in the indoor exhibit.

reviews.author: Gary99Numan
reviews.title: It's OK
reviews.content: Some good USSR style hard where. Most of the information is only in Vietnamese. If your passing worth a visit. Good coffee shop Highlands next door.

reviews.author: Manchestertiger
reviews.title: ok to kill some time
reviews.content: this place is ok to kill a bit of time while you are on the general tourist route. It is about the same standard as most tourist attractions in vietnam. That probably says enough, dont expect to be wowed.

reviews.author: James L
reviews.title: Lots of things to see
reviews.content: Really enjoyed seeing all the military equipment and vehicles. Just wished there was a bit written information to explain the war.

reviews.author: rodjenks
reviews.title: Watch out for lunchtime closure !
reviews.content: Open Tuesday to Saturday:8.00 am- 11.15 am & 13.00 pm- 16.15 pmWe were tricked by locked doors before we realised they had closed for lunch !There is an air conditioned coffee shop  where you can while away the time., strangely the waitresses here go out to get your order from somewhere outside.The "American War" display is in the far left corner, We saw someone with a much needed map but have no where they got it  Sign posting is minimal.As expected it celebrates the glorious victory of the Peoples Socialist Republic over the US aggressors.Most exhibits have a paragraph in English . Look for the small windmill that winds a string to detonate a grenade when helicopters land, and handbags used to signal VC that US forces were nearby.We could not find any reference to Australia's involvementin the war (571 Ozzies were killed ) Very well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Rev-D
reviews.title: Personally I found this place to be amazing.
reviews.content: Someone from America asked my why i wanted to go here. I replied, ive spent my life listening to Americas propaganda... i just wanna hear someone elses for a change. and to be honest, there isn't much propaganda. Just pictures of the struggle between different powers. During the war, the Vietnamese army fought off the French, the Chinese, and the Americans. It doesn't matter that you believe politically, thats one hell of a feat for any army. This museam documents in English, French and Vietnamese much of Vietnams warrior culture. Very interesting...

reviews.author: Becky Gibson
reviews.title: Great overview of Vietnamese Army history
reviews.content: A great place for a military enthusiast with two large buildings containing a large amount of original weapons and tools of war dating back as far as 2,500 years. There is also a large amount of military vehicles both Vietnamese and U.S. A place one could easily spent a day browsing. Alongside the museum is the Hanoi Flag Tower, completed in 1812 is absolutely magnificent. The only thing this place would fall down on is extensive explanations of the historical warfare the occurred in Vietnam. Otherwise a great place of history and inexpensive at 40,000VND ($2US)

reviews.author: Steph F
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: Was very informative, don't go during there lunch as it closes.  Not well signed as its all over the place so you can miss sections.

reviews.author: Andrew S
reviews.title: The student and the Teacher
reviews.content: Interesting to say the least maybe you find a slightly changed story but hey you must expect it they were the student and we were their teacher

reviews.author: annanic16
reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.content: Extremely unimpressed with this museum. Nothing is translated and is all in Vietnamese. I came here expecting to learn about the history but could not understand a single word. I found it was like most museums in Vietnam where they present pictures and artifacts left behind but don't educate on the history or talk about the war. I definitely don't recommend. Waste of time.

reviews.author: Kenneth S
reviews.title: Vietnam Military History Museum
reviews.content: Liberation Day/Reunification Day . . .what do you do a day before these important milestones for Vietnam, and two days before International Labour Day/May Day? You visit the Vietnam Military History Museum! It's a delicious irony for an old anti-war campaigner and pacifist. This is a monument to (mainly) the twentieth century victories that closed the book on French colonialism and the post WW2 western irrational fear of communism. The museum is a beautifully curated collection of war memorabilia, photography and documents - in short propaganda. The beauty is that it is the propaganda of the winners.The places of key political and military leaders - Ho Chi Minh, Giap, Van Thai and many more - are well documented. The central and overarching influence of 'Uncle Ho' is, without fanfare, given its importance in a parallel, underlying storyline.Some of the 1973-75 closing pieces - the Ho Chi Minh campaign particularly - are showcased with spectacular, 'soviet-style' art installations like the captured enemy hardware and the surrealistic centrepiece created from the remains of a B52 bomber - fantastic.You will also find the story of the last millennium of dynastic warfare - interesting mostly because over the period there is very little of it relative to some of the bloodier places on the canvas of history. Throwing off the yoke of Sino-suzerainty over 1000 years ago led to a stability yearned for in many parts. And of course we visited two days after Vietnamese Kings Commemoration Day which heightened the meaning.A satisfying philosophical and historical visit. Expect patchy airconditioning and airless spaces as is the norm for these seventies monuments in Vietnam - it doesn't detract.

reviews.author: Nick B
reviews.title: Many guns, no history
reviews.content: Even though it has the words "History" and "Museum" in its name, this place is none of both. Plenty of guns are showcased and all the museum tells about them is their name and when/where they were used/manufractured. It barely tells anything about any of the Indochina Wars. The tanks and planes outside also don't have any information written. This place has a lot of potential but really just satisfies people with an interest in big guns. If you want to learn something about the military history of Viet Nam, go to the War Remnants Museum in HCMC and the Hoa Lo Prison in Ha Noi.Admission was 40,000D and you pay an additional 20,000D to bring a camera for taking pictures in front of some tanks and planes.

reviews.author: Bjorn O
reviews.title: Good military museum with plenty of arms and aircraft
reviews.content: Interesting place to visit although the history is sad.The number of aircraft in good condition is impressive and so are the indoor photo displays and small arm displays.A word of warning,some of the taxis nearby are running with bent meters

reviews.author: FotoMike
reviews.title: An unexpected flash back to 1970s
reviews.content: We accidentally discovered the Museum while we were walking the streets of Ha Noi.  We noticed the F5 American firghter jet sitting next to the Mig 17 Russian fighter and tanks side by side behind a high wall.  Curiosity led us to the front gate where, for a mere 2$ USD, our journey transported us back 200 years to the construction of the Citadel and forward to 1960-70s and the days of my experience during the American intervention in Viet Nam's civil war.  For two hours we went from exhibit to exhibit of ancient warfare (canons, knives, and spears) to 20th century warfare involving France and the USA.  Standing tall inside the front gate was the Mig 21 that won fame during its service.  Inside exhibit halls were artifacts, photos, and explanations of the life and times of Viet Nam in those decades of foreign intervention.  When we thought we had seen it all, a new door was opened and more came into view.  Videos, diaramas of battles and living conditions during those times helped bring the tenacity and strength of the Vietnamese combatants to mind.The outdoor exhibits were a forest of 20th century war machines: tanks, helicopters, airplanes, fighter jets, mag tugs, and more. All of them up close and personal with ladders ascending to the cockpits to view the tight buckets and instrument panels pilots used to lead their machines into their deadly missions.Perhaps the only disappointment was our timing.  We leave mid April but there was a flurry of activity of building and installing sound and light for the upcoming celebration of liberation on 30 April when Viet Nam celebrates their 40th anniversary.

reviews.author: Damspost
reviews.title: Interesting History (with big toys0
reviews.content: Loads of equipment from the wars of the last 100 years but the main highlight was the array of guns, aircraft, helicpoters, vehicles, etc in the yard of this place. It was great if you like big old military vehicles!

reviews.author: TheCoach25
reviews.title: One of the better museums
reviews.content: One of the better war museums in Hanoi. Out the back are the planes and tanks. For 40000 dong, it is a good 30 minutes of interesting war memorabilia. Anything written in English advises how the gun, motar, bazooka was used to kill Either the French or U.S. troops. Bit one sided and glorifies the war, as if all the Vietnamese people were heirs and happy to be fighting. All a bit wrong. Anyway, the place is worth a look, especially if you compare it to the b52 museum which is a dive.

reviews.author: savvy2olympia
reviews.title: A Mix of Good and Biased Information
reviews.content: If you are in the area (near the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum) it is worth a 1 or 2 hour visit.  Some of the information and displays are, from an historical viewpoint, noteworthy while others are one sided.  The museum experience got the 4 of us thinking about the Vietnam War again and made for some interesting discussions after our visit.  It was good to see what the museum had to offer.  It made us think about current world unrest issues and the alternatives we all face in resolving them.English explanations on what you are looking at are limited.  There's an additional fee to take in your camera.

reviews.author: Pierce_Rekk
reviews.title: A good amount of military hardware to look at
reviews.content: A view of the war that westerners are sure to find odd. I really enjoyed the museum, and to see up close hardware that fought in such a pivotal part of my countries history. I highly recommend a look, but don't expect to see a traditional western military museum. It can seem a little jumbled but the message is clear. War has been a part of their history since the countries first settlement. Its for the Vietnamese people not tourists. But a goos tourist attraction none the less.

reviews.author: Ducatibabe
reviews.title: Eerie, a little odd, & a definite jumble.
reviews.content: A big part of recent history, but still a bit odd to see a MIG jet, a Huey, a Chinook, & various tanks etc, kind of randomly scattered around, plus all the photos. Not a lot of info, but some good photos.The tower is from an entirely different era & nothing to do with the war, as is the citadel which you can't see anyway as it is a military base.All in all, pop in if you are in the area & interested in war, but I wouldn't make a specific trip.

reviews.author: Chandranath S
reviews.title: The relics of the Vietnam war.
reviews.content: Why  did the Americans fought this long war, leaving havoc for generations to suffer? For the first time we were seeing a variety of mines that killed thousands of people, bombs of different kinds, a variety of ammo and vehicles, taks of all kinds.The guides were  people who actually participated in this war and suffered through their lives with shrapnel, ball bearings in their body.

reviews.author: kiwihatters
reviews.title: Hard if you dont understand Vietnamese....
reviews.content: The tour guide from another tour we went on recommended we go here, and so we did. Looked good from the outside, and was cheap to enter (although there was an extra fee if you wanted to take a camera), so we ambled in excited to learn the history of the many wars throughout Vietnamese history. Unfortunately, once we got in there we found it to be not particularly well laid out and rather difficult to understand a lot of what we were looking at because there was very little in English. All the old tanks, planes and weapons outside were pretty cool though.All in all, I probably wouldn't go again if I were in Hanoi, but I'm sure people who were extremely interested in the war(s) would find it interesting.

reviews.author: CarysC006
reviews.title: Go for the diorama
reviews.content: The main reason for visiting this museum is to see the diorama depicting the Vietnamese assault on Dien Bien Phu, ehic is an excellent way of seeing how the events unfolded and great for kids. Be aware that we were the only people there and when I asked them to turn it on they said they only do so for groups of 10 or more?! On seeing my sons face as this was the reason we had come the lady did relent and she was much warmer when she realised that they were genuinely interested. The rest of the museum is just ok ( but nowhere near as weird as the Ho Chi Minh museum )  though the kids loved the planes and tanks outside as well..

reviews.author: Daniel A
reviews.title: Disorganized and propaganda filled
reviews.content: If you want to learn about Vietnamese military, read a book or watch a movie produced by the History Channel. Do not go to a museum in Vietnam as it is disgusting, only in Vietnamese and so filled with propaganda and so very biased.If you want to go and laugh at how ridiculous Vietnamese Museums are set up then go ahead and have a blast. Otherwise, avoid at all costs.The museum cost 15,000 Dong, is in or near Old Quarter, and the flag tower is also set up there behind the scrap metal they call exhibits.

reviews.author: Helen G
reviews.title: A very strong view of the Amercan War
reviews.content: The photos were at times very graphic and powerful.  They highlighted the destructive power of war, but also the resilience of the Vietnamese people.

reviews.author: Tony3357
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: There is plenty to see and take in at this museum. However, it is all a bit jumbled and haphazard. Plus, as others have said, you get very little explanation in English or French about what you are looking at. It's quite interesting to see the old photos. But you need to have an understanding of Vietnam history to get much out of it, and to put the photos etc into context. I only managed to work out the significance of the items where a date (year) was given. A pity, as this could be so fascinating.

reviews.author: Greg S
reviews.title: Like a junkyard of military scrap
reviews.content: I arm bled across this place walking through the streets. Inside the buildings are some of the memorabilia from past conflicts, unfortunately labels are not in English so you don't know why they are about.Outside are wreckages of a B52 shot down and other captured military scrap.Further to this is a collection of captured and abandoned military vehicles at the end of the Vietnam War.

reviews.author: Jasmin J
reviews.title: Not much
reviews.content: I've been here with my friends for my trip. To be honest, prefer to go to the president house to enjoy rather than spend the time in here. Although it was free but ...

reviews.author: Banksideman
reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit
reviews.content: The museum is spread over several buildings and together give one a good background to the wars that have been set against a country made up of disparate villages that make up Vietnam as a whole. After the brutal French occupation Communism seemed to offer the people a unifying and caring solution to their plight however the Americans saw a Communist threat and persecuted the Vietnam war using modern day weapons and Napalm supplied by Monsanto (agent Orange) against a largely uneducated village peoples. That the Vietcong defeated the Americans is an amazing achievement. The museum has many armaments mostly captured from their enemies as well as several aircraft including a Huey helicopter (think Muss Saigon). I found this a compelling exhibition and suggest you allow 3 hours to read about the exhibits.

reviews.author: Allan E
reviews.title: a must go visit
reviews.content: As a tourist the Vietnam Military History Museum is a must go visit.. This is a fascinating look into the way the Vietnamese have defended their country against foreign invaders. The focus is on Resistance Wars of the Ho Chi Minh era.

reviews.author: Hanna A
reviews.title: Much to see
reviews.content: This museum offers a view from the "other side" of the wars against the French and USA, which is quite refreshing. If you've been to the war museum in Saigon though you need not bother, we found that one to be of a bit higher standard. I found it disappointing that not all signs were in English and some English descriptions were quite basic as well. My boyfriend though, who is quite a history enthusiast, found many interesting things to look at here. We spent around 2h here so it is worth the visit. Entrance is 40k dong.

reviews.author: Stuart H
reviews.title: Interesting to see the other side of the military history of Vietnam
reviews.content: Not expensive to enter and as always the staff were friendly and helpful though they could not speak English but then I can't speak Vietnamese and that's where we were. A range of militaria from swords to canons to tanks and aircraft including a crashed B52. The most interesting thing was to see how the story of Dien Bien Phu and the Vietnam war from the Vietnamese side. Yes some of this is propaganda and tells many stories of 'heroes' of the war but to be fair no more so than the plethora of films from the American view. The exhibits all have english translations and many are attributed to the named individuals who used them.I am really pleased we did not miss this.Walking around talking English and being clearly western in a museum largely about a war that ended not that long ago I wondered if we would experience any animosity or bad feeling but it was just the opposite.

reviews.author: brit-us-sports
reviews.title: Viet Nam 2015
reviews.content: very good and i found it to be very propaganda exercise and the tank on the forecourt was photographed alot as it was one of the tanks that broke the gates down.

reviews.author: Leo D
reviews.title: Getting thorough understanding of Vietnam’s great victory
reviews.content: Visiting the museum, tourists can see thousands of exhibits, photographs, maps, scale models of the past Vietnam war. Thanks to this, visitors will have a good general knowledge of the process of the birth, growth and victories of the Vietnamese people's armed forces for the cause of peace, independence and freedom.

reviews.author: Walter k
reviews.title: Few English signs
reviews.content: Few signs in English make this a fragmented site. There are captions on pictures, but the museum fails to tell a story or narrative. And mostly you're looking at pictures and maps unable to make the connection to history. There's an impressive display of planes, helicopters, tanks, and debris from shot down planes, but i don't think this makes it worth the price of admission.

reviews.author: Zee S.Puad
reviews.title: 40,000VND for adult
reviews.content: They even got charges for your camera if you want to bring it in.. But it was worth it.. Lots to see here.. The flag tower and what I like the most is thr plane debris plus the tanks.. Just beautiful.  A very beautiful history.. ^^

reviews.author: berrnardz
reviews.title: Plenty there
reviews.content: I spent about three hours here and enjoyed this museum a lot. There is plenty to see. The exhibits were interesting. I liked the way you could actually get onto the old tanks, guns and planes right up close unlike so many Western museums were you have to stand so far away that you cannot see the details. The staff were very friendly too.

reviews.author: michael19251927
reviews.title: A look at the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective
reviews.content: A truly anti-American edifice this museum contains photos, weapons, planes, tanks and much more from the War. It is an interesting museum as it tells much more than many people might want to know about the horrors of that war but it is at times so rabidly anti American that it can be hard to understand the narrative . But an essential part of Hanoi to anyone with an interest in this lovely country's past

reviews.author: Kevin M
reviews.title: great place to spend a few hours
reviews.content: loved this place a lot  very interesting place lots of old weapons planes and such great information about the Vietnam war from the view of the other side of things

reviews.author: Arne B
reviews.title: Another perspective on the war
reviews.content: History is written by the victorius. When the Vietnamese express their side of the war you'll get their side of the story. The museum starts with the struggles back in earlier days with the Chinese invasion. There are artifacts dating back almost a thousand years displayed.For the war against the French and Americans you will find a clear propaganda feel to the display. There are artifacts displayed with information on where it was obtained (taken from French officer) and used in attacks or killings elsewhere. As a lot of museums around the world it's mostly information in the local language and with some limited quality translations to English. If you have limited knowledge of the war and the change of power in Vietnam, this might not be the place where you will learn it. What you will find are items with a history, newsletters (in Vietnamese) that circulated during the war, weaponry and a larger elements like a US tank, A Russian Mig, a helicopter and anti aircraft guns and cannons. I liked and spent about an hour and fifteen minutes walking through the museum.Note: you're not allowed to bring a backpack into the museum, as all the other museums we visited in Hanoi. The storage units are a bit small, but I got to place my pack in the ticket sellers office.

reviews.author: Stephen-O
reviews.title: A dud
reviews.content: With such a lengthy history where the Vietnamese have had to defend themselves against all comers, this museum is a dud. The cost of VND40,000 is over priced  for what is on offer. The external displays are of various planes, cannons, the odd tank etc. with a pile of debris that used to be an F111, that's the good part. The internal displays are a series of poor, grainy photographs of "glorious" soldiers standing around. The history behind the displays is not done any justice by them. To make matters worse, the museum's workers are quite happy to speak and act as if they're on the street. Such noise in Australia's War Memorial would cause instant action. The highlight of the museum is a model of the battle plan of Dien Bien Phu. A movie is flashed onto the rear wall but you can't see it because the light is too bright. The politics of a re-united country finding its way into a capitalist world have shaped the presentations, they are bland and generally of little importance. Those who made this history deserve better, Vietnamese as well as their previous foes. This is more a propaganda statement than a museum. The toilets here must have been used by the Viet Cong while on campaign. All in all, very disappointing.

reviews.author: mynameisbeau
reviews.title: Don't bother
reviews.content: Tired exhibits many of which overlap those of the national museum. Tickets are 40k dong (approx $2.50AUD) which is just about what it is worth.

reviews.author: nathan b
reviews.title: Definitely a worthwhile experience, but...
reviews.content: It is really a great experience to see the Vietnamese experience of their wars.  The museum covers the early wars against the Chinese, the resistance against the Japanese, and then the more widely know (in the West) French, and American conflicts. There are many displays with artifacts, but it is hit and miss on the labeling.  Generally, you'll see large wall panels with some background information of a major event, but in Vietnamese.  Then the individual items in the display cases will be labeled ("This rifle was captured by XX Regiment"), but they really aren't tied together.  The labelling seems to be the biggest issue in the museum.  It's not as much a translation issue, but a mindset issue.  For example, the ARVN is never referred to by name - just Southern puppets.  On the outdoor displays, vehicles that have placards indicating capture from S. Vietnamese forces, the Southern markings have been replaced with US markings.  Even then, the S. Vietnamese flag is visible on at least one vehicle (CH-47) under the paint.  In the Dien Bien Phu room, there is a really good terrain map with LEDs and explanatory film to go with it.  It would really help though if you know beforehand the Vietnamese designations of the strongpoints.  For instance, the vast majority of foreign visitors will have heard of Eliane, Dominique, or Beatrice.  But the Vietnamese refer to Eliane 2 as just A1 for instance (I'm pretty sure it's Eliane 2, but you get the gist).  If you can get past the "Socialist Heroic" aspect of the labeling and explanatory placards, then you will really enjoy the museum.  The cost is 40K dong, with another 30K on top if you want to take pictures - so under $4.  You can also go up to the Flag Tower too.  I'd have to say I got my money's worth.

reviews.author: BabyCParis
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: You have 4 sections to visit + the outside showroom of the tanks, planes, helicopoters. It's very interesting and you get to learn a lot of things!

reviews.author: fotoamazonas
reviews.title: If you really have nothing better to do...
reviews.content: ...then spend the money and a couple hours here. Otherwise, save the few bucks and walk around the outside wall. You can see most of the old Vietnamese and captured US military equipment without entering the complex. Also, I had heard the tower was great, but the gate to climb stairs to the top was locked.

reviews.author: lia97a
reviews.title: A learning & humbling experience!
reviews.content: They have a few interesting visual display of vietnamese war or wars. Different weapons used for different eras. While I was exploring the place, a lady almost lock me up. I looked out & saw  the lady just locked the door one by one, passing by, stared at me without an apology or a smile. I rushed towards the last door!  As I went downstairs, I met 2 groups of Europeans. They were quite disappointed. Why on earth they sold the tickets if it was the closing time?

reviews.author: Daniel G
reviews.title: Get to da Chopper
reviews.content: Not a bad little number. It's good to kill some time and see some relics from the war. A good look into the history of the Vietnam war. So if you have an hour or two to fill, then I recommend a quick look around.

reviews.author: Merilyn_S_12
reviews.title: An interesting insight into vietnamese history from their perspective
reviews.content: A very interesting place to get an insight into vietnamese history from their perspective. Only thing I found was that it was very english friendly. There were loads of great historical artifacts, including papers, equipment, historical photographs, and even a movie for the kids to watch.  A great interactive place to take children, but as a non vietnamese speaker, I may have got more value had there been some more english translations.  I'm glad that I went though, because for later museums that I saw in Vietnam, it started piecing together a story of the greater Vietnamese psychology and history that they value as important.   They have storage facilities to put your bags in whilst you go through, and you will have to pay extra to take photographs in the museum. Very interesting if war museums are your thing.  Oh, and beware the bathroom, it's stinky squat facilities! So if you don't want to squat, wait until you get to other museums in Hanoi.  One more thing, make sure you walk up the stairs to the top of the spikey thing. It has an awesome view across to the imperial citadel, and you can see more of the centre of Hanoi. Well worth doing.

reviews.author: DVDPlayer
reviews.title: Great collection of Vietnamese and captured US military equipment
reviews.content: This is a total bloke fest. Interesting displays inside explaining the Vietnamese point of view regarding the war. Really eye opening for people born after the 60's like me who had no idea how wrong it was for the US to be in Vietnam.  But the real show stoppers are the planes tanks and helicopters outside - including a B52 that looks as though it has just crashed head first in the carpark

reviews.author: Helen T
reviews.title: Provides Insight
reviews.content: The museum was especially helpful in understanding the war against the French Imperialists.  The photographs and paintings depicted the exploitation of the Vietnamese people by the French and the feudal lords.  The "American War" as called by the Vietnamese also has photos and displays.  It did not come across as propaganda, but simply as factual.

reviews.author: Clive H
reviews.title: A 1000 years of conflict
reviews.content: This is a must for anyone interested in the history of Vietnam. It takes the visitor through a 1000 years of struggle starting in the 10th century with the war to drive out the Tang Empire; fighting off invasions by the Siamese, the Mongols and so on and just when they think they are free the French turn up. The French Colonial period was one of sporadic uprisings often savagely put down. There is a very good diorama plus contemporary film of Dien Bien Phu. Obviously the American War is covered in detail and museum is home to a number of captured tanks, aircraft and artillery pieces as well as kit used by the North itself. The gate guard is a North Vietnamese fighter jet credited with more than a dozen kills during its operational career. We combined a visit to the museum with a look round the Ancient Citadel as they are on the same site. There is a very good café between the two of them. Please note the Military Museum is closed on Mondays.

reviews.author: 19Jack64
reviews.title: A bit too much propaganda
