reviews.title: So unique
reviews.content: Please include this in your Hanoi sightseeing !Kind of strange being able to walk along the tracks and stop for a drink or chat ! . Night is great with the lights of the cafe bars but daytime is great too . Check the train times

reviews.author: alessandra v
reviews.title: Don't miss it!
reviews.content: It will be a tourist thing but after all what is not now?! X we are not to be missed because it is not every day to drink a beer with a train that passes so close to you that you can touch it!

reviews.author: Vy H.
reviews.title: Train Street in Hanoi, Vietnam
reviews.content: Definitely a must go place in Hanoi!!  The street is beautiful with tons of lovely cafes to choose from.  Check the schedule for the train and come early, grab a drink and watch the train go by.  When it’s safe, you can take pictures on the train track!  I recommend coming at night, with all the lights, it’s much prettier.

reviews.author: Sharul M
reviews.title: Train street - My POV
reviews.content: Worth a try to just see the train passes by. Love it and unique experience.It's free so you can just explore without a guide. I just stayed for less than an hour depending on how long you finish your cuppa.It is busy but that's the whole atmosphere. It adds up. Just worth the visit whilst you are in Hanoi.The black rooster and chicken are cute... Lol. Look out for them

reviews.author: 749David
reviews.title: Once in a lifetime experience; everything you've heard/read, and more. Details inside.
reviews.content: Simple amazing. Something you won't experience anywhere else. You need to get the train schedule in advance, then turn-up 15 mins in advance. Just walk along the tracks and the bar owners/servers will direct you to seats. Don't worry, there's no such thing as a good or bad seat; they're all the same. The prices of the beers are all the same. Take a 33 beer, it's the cheapest and just as good as any Heineken. 5 mins before the train arrives, the servers will push you back against the wall (in your seat) and sound a bell. Then wait for the Train to arrive and wonder at it all. A great experience.

reviews.author: sekjr0521
reviews.title: Fun!
reviews.content: This is fun. But if you're going to be in the restaurant area you will have to take a seat and order something like a beer for a 50 cents USD. Otherwise you have to leave the area before the train arrives. That doesn't mean that you'll miss the train. Because you can stand out on the street with everyone else. Guards will pull a gate across the road and you will be squished among everybody including all the traffic that is backed up... .

reviews.author: Johnny Alice
reviews.title: Railside charm after dark
reviews.content: It’s a truly unique spot—charming cafés line the railroad tracks, and the whole area is incredibly picturesque. At night, the tracks take on an especially magical glow.

reviews.author: Max S
reviews.title: Tourist trap
reviews.content: Very crowded place with tourists, with café owners who jump on you and want you to take a seat next at their place. A more interesting place to visit are the quarters next to the train street, where Hanoi inhabitants spend their daily life in narrow streets.

reviews.author: Sparklep0d
reviews.title: Mental but excellent
reviews.content: This is legitimately bonkers but everyone should probably do it! Worksafe NZ would have a cow.Train came at about 4pm, apparently a reliable time to see it. Do not stick out your elbows if sitting on outside seat!

reviews.author: Toneupascotaesthetics
reviews.title: Avoid Caffee on train street
reviews.content: We have been really excited about this historical experience and went back to see the trains on a few times while in Hanoi. My experience is to be really careful where you sit. We had a coffee in Caffee 94, which is a must avoid!!! We got a drink made out of powder and she has made more cups and wanted to charge us extra for the cups. We said no, she got really angry and started to shout front of everyone and wanted us to leave. Very unpleasant experience. Just walk around before you get a drink anywhere.

reviews.author: Thano T
reviews.title: Splendid evening in train street
reviews.content: Went to catch the train planned for 21.15.. the atmosphere was electric with all the lights and tourists posing on the tracks, YouTubers live streaming, it was just spectacular. We set in a bar having drinks. The 1st train arrived around 9.30.. the cafes and bars have a bell to notify the public the train is approaching. After the 1st train which was a passenger train, 15 mins later another passenger train went by and about 10 mins later a goods train went. Amazing sitting close to the trains … health and safety in the UK will have a field day. With the cost and have a drink or something to eat to support the cafes in that area.

reviews.author: The Pilot Wife
reviews.title: Definitely a site to see in Hanoi
reviews.content: Wow ! This place is amazing. It’s our second time visiting this area and never disappoints. Even though it gets busy it’s still very safe. Lots of bars and restaurants to choose from. Well worth the visit to see the train pass by. Ask local cafes the exact times because the times do vary from what’s published online.

reviews.author: Durga M
reviews.title: Unique experience
reviews.content: This is very popular place in Hanoi. It's not easy to find as it is nestled Between rows of shop.Though we went there but missed seeing the action however I fell without the train you can appreciate the place more as the place is less crowded.Recommend

reviews.author: Rhi3
reviews.title: Unique Experience!
reviews.content: This does seem to get closed by the authorities quite often and doesn't appear in the guidebooks... if it is open it is worth a visit. We went in the day. there are touts meeting you and directing you follow them to certain cafe's etc but just ignore and sit where you want. You are very close to the train so just be careful. The cafe owners make sure people stand back but you should also take your own precautions.

reviews.author: jw6969
reviews.title: Must do!
reviews.content: It’s such a famous attraction that we had to go and see for ourselves. We decided it might be more colourful at night and it was. Our hotel suggested a bar and fortunately there were couple of stools sitting empty. We bought a couple of beers each (about $4 each). Then the action of the train itself - it really is quite extraordinary! Zero “health & safety”, just a sodding great train trundling by! Loved it. Unmissable.

reviews.author: Sandy W
reviews.title: Incredible experience!
reviews.content: Incredible experience in Hanoi. Food and drinks on the railway line, wait for the train to pass every hour.Delicious food at ChuChu Railway cafe.Would definitely return.

reviews.author: possagol
reviews.title: Particular and colorful
reviews.content: Very colorful little street. We only took a walk because the train only runs in the evening or morning only at the weekend. Full of places to have a coffee or a drink. To see

reviews.author: Alison S
reviews.title: Adrenaline fueled coffee.
reviews.content: Fun place to stop for mid morning coffee. Even more enjoyable to watch the proprietors chase people off the rails and out of seats they think they can have for free!

reviews.author: Ashwin k
reviews.title: One crazy night at train street with family!!
reviews.content: Very excellent and must visit place when you plan trip to Vietnam (City name is Hanoi). It is a dream come true moment to all of us when we saw actual train just crossing so close to us which used to function as normal market place just before actual arrival of train. Beautiful planning of street indeed which is a blend of so many markets on either side of the train track and train just passes in that street (on track) and all activities in that street just freezes for a moment except train moving fast in style. Passengers inside the train waves hands from inside in joy to people outside and also tourists, locals, store people and others who ever present in that street also enjoys in so much in joy. No one is actually disturbed but that moment just gives immense pleasure and happiness to everyone around. Salt & egg coffee is also an highlight of that train street and it is very famous in the entire city. We felt like spending lifetime with short stint of hour may be. It is more of everyone coming together to celebrate as a big occasion and giving tourists like us an awesome experience which is also culture of Hanoi and eventually Vietnam as a whole.

reviews.author: Jimmy HW Y
reviews.title: Get the fixed seating in front of the cafes
reviews.content: It was an amazing experience to feel a train passing through a narrow street packed with people and cafe on both sides. I believed is is a unique experience that you must try in Hanoi. If you want to secure a good front seat in a cafe, 1. you must get there as least half an hour before the train schedule, and 2. Find fixed seats, but not folding tables or chairs along the rail, as these would be removed before the train arrives.

reviews.author: Grace-Aguiar
reviews.title: Captivating & Travel-Inspired
reviews.content: Visiting the famous Train Street in Hanoi is one of those experiences that stays with you long after you’ve left. Tucked between narrow houses and lively cafés, the railway cuts straight through a tiny neighbourhood where life carries on just inches from the tracks. When the train approaches, you can feel the energy shift—locals pull in their stools, tourists press against the walls, and suddenly the whole street hums with excitement.The moment the train passes is both thrilling and surreal. It’s loud, close, and heart-pounding, yet there’s something strangely beautiful about watching daily life pause and then instantly return to normal once the train is gone.Beyond the train itself, what makes this place special is the atmosphere. Friendly café owners invite you in, offering egg coffee or cold drinks while sharing stories about the street’s history. It feels authentic, chaotic, and uniquely Hanoi.

reviews.author: Sandy T
reviews.title: Interesting experience and worth a visit
reviews.content: Interesting experience to have a train drove past us in such proximity. We got a drink from one of the cafe and sat along the tiny strip and waited for the train to arrive. We are thrilled.

reviews.author: Alexandru-Ionut E
reviews.title: ​No. 8 Duong Tau: Egg Coffee and Adrenaline.
reviews.content: ​You have to try the Egg Coffee here—it's pure creamy perfection. But the real star is the location. Sitting on the Hanoi Train Street as the train rumbles by is absolutely wild. Seriously, this place is not for the faint of heart, but it’s an experience you'll never forget. Go for the coffee, stay for the rush!

reviews.author: Shweta Rajat T
reviews.title: Life time experience
reviews.content: The staffs are good.. but for vegetarians the menu is limited.. there are timings of the train in train street go accordingly.. it’s a life time experience, scary but new experience… must go

reviews.author: Deb S
reviews.title: Own being a tourist!!
reviews.content: This is such a place for tourists! But it was fun and worth it. I will confess being a bit nervous when the person from the restaurant shouted watch out for your knees. But they knew what they were talking about, and I did not need to worry about getting mooshed by a train.

reviews.author: Ginkai Silver
reviews.title: Touristy, but great experience
reviews.content: It’s touristy thing to do, but it’s not often that one can get to experience this. It’s great to see this stretch of old houses built right up close to the railway track turn into an attraction that attracts visitors to its hole-in-the-wall cafes and shops, and generating income for the little neighborhood. Found a little shop that prints T-shirts and tote bags right at the end, and selling them at half the price of shops in the streets.

reviews.author: Kate H
reviews.title: What a wild ride!
reviews.content: A very interesting experience, sitting right next too, I mean right next to a passenger train running through Hanoi. Lined with lined cafes serving food and drinks. It’s an experience for the senses. Get there 30 mins before the train to give yourself time to order drinks and find a chair.

reviews.author: Beppe Marini
reviews.title: Unmissable attraction
reviews.content: Tourist attraction not to be missed. Recommended in the evening because if the train is late you can sip some cocktails or enjoy coffee in one of the many bars that literally overlook the tracks and the lights and colors become suggestive and atmospheric.

reviews.author: 138Paul138
reviews.title: Crazy thing to see
reviews.content: Located in the Old Quarter of Hanoi, Train Street is easy to find. You can look up train times via websites. We saw the 15:15hr train and were told another left at 17:00hrs.It is a crazy tourist fuelled scene.Cafes line the side of the tracks with tables and chairs inches away from the track. You have to walk along the track to find a seat, it is uneven in places so take care. Loads of traders past by trying to sell souvenir tat but that’s to be expected. As the time approaches the cafe owners will take away tables and become animated as to where you must stand. They do have your safety at heart. The Police close the ends of the street prior to the train passing through.The train is huge, and you are honestly inches from it when it passes by. It’s quite an experience and well worth it. Do try and get there 30 minutes before the train as it is very popular.

reviews.author: Liam R
reviews.title: Must do - Worth the hype (Better at night)
reviews.content: Must do in Hanoi, nothing prepares you for the massive train coming within inches of your seat.There are a lot of workers trying to get you into their cafe (best option for front row seat, coffee is only a bit more expensive than normal).

reviews.author: Emily
reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.content: I found this street to be a little overrated, I appreciated this is an unusual experience for some, but its over very quickly, the street is very busy & you could be waiting a while. Plenty of bars / coffee to choose, prices a little high, but expected for tourist location.

reviews.author: Stephen B
reviews.title: Unique and fun way to spend a Hour
reviews.content: A fun way to spend a hour or so don't overthink it yes its touristy but that's sometimes what its all about . Its nice to have a stroll along and choose a spot to view the train ( Best to check the timetable ) and have a drink or snack . Prices are slightly inflated but still very reasonable considering your location and effort the locals put in.  Great atmosphere to be fair and we found most people sitting and waiting to be very chatty and friendly.

reviews.author: sylviet t
reviews.title: should try
reviews.content: Its a super animated place, always. There are tons of tourists coming to catch the train moment. Nice vibe, should try. Coffee shop owners hunt customers in every second. Sometimes cannot choose one shop you like

reviews.author: loonylou78
reviews.title: Bright and colourful train street!
reviews.content: Had a great evening along train street. Very vibrant and loads of cafes/bars to choose from. We were lucky and had 3 trains pass through which was a great experience. Yes it's very touristy but worth a visit. All the local people we came across were all so friendly and accommodating!

reviews.author: Tom
reviews.title: A colourful and vibrant street with the defining feature of the train
reviews.content: Hanoi's Train Street  is a tourist attraction that is bursting with vibrant  colours and proud Vietnamese vendors. One of the vendors was quite rude I was excited to  order coffee for the first time in Vietnamese and as I approached I said Vui long and he interrupted me before my third word to ask if it was just me (solo traveller so yes) I said yes please table for one  and he told me no no no and then to get out so I found another vendor. The train passed and were a great photo opportunity train street provides a great chance for photography and getting pictures of yourself there

reviews.author: John B
reviews.title: 28 Train Street Hanoi - the place to go
reviews.content: 28 Train Street is the place to go when visiting here. Owner is So hospitable she elevates the whole experience. Excellent coffee, great drinks & food. Went twice during our 3 day Hanoi visit. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Michelle N
reviews.title: Unique and exciting experience
reviews.content: Very unique street with lots of cafes and restaurant with seating where you can watch the train go past less than a metre in front of you. Incredible experience

reviews.author: Maureen M
reviews.title: Fun experience but be wary of the locals at the entrance
reviews.content: We were dropped of by our ride at one of the entrances to the Train tracks. Upon alighting a man immediately tried to engage us. I read about a couple of reviews warning us about the locals who will try to bring you to their cafes insisting that you have to go to where they will take you. My friend and I just went ahead and was again stopped at the entrance of the rail tracks by a lady. She tried to bully us and telling us we had to wait as the train will pass by already and attempted to show me photos on her phone. I largely ignored her and after a few attempts I decided enough was enough and just pushed ahead to find our own cafe. We managed to secure a good spot and also found the server named Vesper at the Spot 09 Cafe who was helpful and polite. It was a good save from our earlier negative experience of the rude and pushy lady at the entrance. I advise anyone going to the Train Street to be aware and don’t let anyone dictate on you. I was informed that there are multiple entrances and only a few have these locals who will try to bully you to go to their cafes. Hopefully, this practice won’t be encouraged by the local authorities as it dampens the experience of tourists who are there whose only objective is to have a good time while contributing their bit to the local economy.

reviews.author: Aivlis
reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.content: Just live the experience! Fantastic!! To watch the train pass, it is mandatory to sit in the chairs, next to the houses, as it is also mandatory to consume drinks. In any case, it is a means of subsistence for those who live there. Before the arrival of the train, there are immense people around, either to find a place or to sell crafts. The Mood is very interesting. Just before the train arrives, there are warnings with whispers and everyone has to sit down. As the train approaches, it whispers loudly and insistently! It is appalling by our proximity! 😄 And it is filmed, and you admire the long train passing. It is an unforgettable experience in Hanoi!

reviews.author: Anne A
reviews.title: Oh wow, what a must do experience !
reviews.content: How crazy is this, but you need to step out of your comfort zone & get involved. It’s something l’ve wanted to do for a long time & it really was worth it. Get there early, choose your spot & relax & wait with a cold beer or a coffee

reviews.author: Samson1971
reviews.title: Unbelievable
reviews.content: This is an unbelievable experience. You sit along the tracks in a small coffee shop and watch a passenger train pass by while sipping your drink. 🍹 You wonder how this street came about being, all the coffee shop owners own the space and live on the upper floors and close by. Seems to me that they would have encroached this land and build on it to stay by the tracks years ago and this turns out to be a huge tourist attraction now…It’s just my opinion 🙄😬🙏

reviews.author: Gregg F
reviews.title: Great experience, no reason not to go there!!! (although might avoid if in wheelchair for example)
reviews.content: Visited as mum, dad and 11 year old son.  We had WhatsApp’d ‘Hanoi 1990s’ before making our way there approx 19:30.  Really friendly staff who got us seated with drinks in a great spot to see the train going past. (They also have toilets which not every establishment along there does)We spent just under an hour there (you probably wouldn’t want to stay longer than that) and saw three trains VERY close-up of course!.. brilliant experience!  Highly recommended!  Something to note is that you’re expected to buy drinks from whichever place you stop at to watch the view.. but this was a very nice experience for us and no reason you wouldn’t want to in any case.

reviews.author: Sharnee K
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.content: We loved this. I recommend getting there early and get a good seat on the shady side. The seating is a little squishy but it’s a good chance to chat to the person next to you.

reviews.author: StJ651
reviews.title: A must in Hanoi!
reviews.content: I’d highly recommend going at night when it’s all lit up. So beautiful and just lovely to see the buzz of the street. Everyone is in great spirits. We went at around 8:30 on a Saturday night and we were lucky enough to have 2 trains come past at around 9:20 and 9:30.

reviews.author: Caroline WSL HYZ
reviews.title: Hanoi Train Street – A Unique Experience with a Few Tips
reviews.content: Visiting Hanoi Train Street is definitely a must-do when you’re in the city. The atmosphere is vibrant, and the experience of watching a train rush past just inches away is unforgettable. To make the most of it, I recommend arriving at least one hour early. This gives you time to grab a good spot, snap some great photos before the train arrives, and enjoy a cocktail or coffee at one of the local cafés.There are many cafés and bars along the tracks. Some places have upstairs seating for a better view, but personally, I’d suggest sitting downstairs to really feel the excitement up close — it’s much more immersive.Toilets are usually available at the shops, but don’t expect them to be very clean or well-maintained. If that’s a concern, plan accordingly.You’ll also find many souvenir vendors nearby. Prices can vary a lot, so bargaining is a must. Once you’ve made a purchase, it’s a good idea to let other vendors know — some can be quite persistent, even a bit pushy. In general, interactions with shop owners can be hit or miss; some are friendly and welcoming, while others may come off as rude.Overall, Train Street is a fun and unique slice of Hanoi life — just come prepared, be patient with the crowds and vendors, and enjoy the ride (figuratively)!

reviews.author: Ashok kumar S
reviews.title: Bad staff i have seen first time
reviews.content: Disappointed by Rude and Disrespectful ServiceWe had a very disappointing experience at one of the shops along Train Street. Before we even made a booking or ordered anything, we were approached by a Vietnamese girl working there who was extremely rude and disrespectful. There were clearly empty seats available, but she refused to let us sit without any proper explanation, speaking in a very unkind and dismissive way.What made it worse was that, at the same time, another staff member from the same shop was actively calling and inviting other customers in. The inconsistency and unprofessional behavior left us feeling very unwelcome. We understand rules and limitations, but basic politeness and respect should never be too much to expect.

reviews.author: Redback_Venom
reviews.title: An experience not to be missed
reviews.content: We walked to the train street from the Vincom Centre not too far away. It was a hot and sticky day, and when we neared the railway crossing, a lady bustled us down the street and toward what we can only suggest was her family's cafe. We were quickly given seats and small tables, and were served on quickly for food or drink. We ordered smoothies and soft drinks - all reasonably priced for a cafe in the area.We were initially told the train was not far away, but then after 30min had elapsed, were told it was still 45 min away! Oh well. More drinks!Our family of 5 (3 kids) fell in love with the cafe owner's small dog which thankfully kept them occupied as we waited. And then, the train came, and went in the flash! Was it worth it? Yes it was as there is no way you would ever be able to do this in Melbourne or anywhere in Australia!

reviews.author: Lily
reviews.title: A thrilling encounter with trains
reviews.content: The thrill of trains zooming past just inches away was exhilarating! We loved sipping coffee at a tiny café, watching the world go by as the vibrant energy of the street enveloped us. A must-see

reviews.author: Chris Anderson
reviews.title: Thriller on Train Street
reviews.content: We visited at 9.30 in the morning - no crowds, good egg coffee and a thrilling experience. I'm sure it's great  at night when it's all lit up but fewer people made it better for us.

reviews.author: Evered Cincinnati
reviews.title: Hanoi's craziest coffee break
reviews.content: The chaotic and crowded atmosphere is part of the charm, we suppose. Seeing the trains passing surprisingly close is both thrilling and a little terrifying. We squeezed into a small cafe right on the tracks. It felt like a scene from a movie. It's a bit touristy, but definitely a unique memory from our trip.

reviews.author: Rachel H
reviews.title: Cool experience in Hanoi, easy to navigate and get a good spot
reviews.content: Worth visiting whilst in Hanoi. We did lots of research but ended up just walking in really easily, finding a table quickly and having a great view. The cafe prices weren’t as high as we were expecting either so overall would recommend. We went late in the evening.

reviews.author: Ronan Q
reviews.title: Our visit to train street
reviews.content: Me and my girlfriend visited train street when we first arrived in Hanoi. As you can expect, it’s a street where a train passes by you. It’s cool. The bars are a bit more expensive but it’s not that dear, about 50K VND for Hanoi Beer. Although you can put the cap on the track and keep that as a memory. It’s a cool first time experience, would do it once and then probably not again as you can expect.

reviews.author: divya
reviews.title: One time experience.
reviews.content: * It was a 15-20 mins walk from our hotel * Get there 30minutes early to get a good spot with a seat at a cafe/restaurant. * Check the train timings on google(could change) .They have additional trains running on weekends in the evenings. Just pick a bar to sit you are comfortable in. You can enjoy a beer,coffee or something to eat while you wait for the train. Very pricey

reviews.author: Global Wanderers
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Lower quality coffee at twice the price as elsewhere but it is a pretty unique experience. Watch out for the locals who help you cross the busy street then show you the best coffee shop. We sat and watched it happen time after time.

reviews.author: Gina R
reviews.title: A must-do in Hanoi's Old Quarter
reviews.content: If you're in Hanoi's Old Quarter, it's a unique experience that you shouldn't miss. Trains mostly run in the afternoon and evening, so just text one of the many cafés — we loved Hao Hao Coffee — to find out the exact time and, if you want, book a table. Make sure you arrive early, as the road is closed when the train is about to arrive. If you are in the curved section of the street, choose the café well to get a better view. Trains arrive from both directions, and the bars usually also have an upper floor from which the view is completely different, with the atmosphere changing a lot with light and darkness.

reviews.author: John V
reviews.title: Unique tourist attraction
reviews.content: Original idea. Everything is on the pricey side but we were willing to drop some dough to support this interesting tourist attraction. It is a lot more organized than we imagined even with a guard to call people out and clear the area ahead of the train passing. We arrived at about 2:30pm and the train does come as predicted at 3:20. It’s worth it coming in a bit earlier to get a spot because there are lots of folks popping up really close to the train time. Be nice and support the locals, spend a bit of money here.

reviews.author: Creeping_Death_LA
reviews.title: As Ozzy sang Crazy Train
reviews.content: This is a must see while in Hanoi, you can get the schedules from your hotel staff. We went a couple of times during the day and each time was an experience. Expect to see many tourists kicking back along the route either drinking beer, coffee, you name it the locals serve it. Just be aware that mixed drinks are pricey compared to a local cheaper bottle of beer. We could never have this train experience in the USA because too many stupid locals would get drunk fall on the tracks end up dead and the family would sue due to negligence.

reviews.author: Christopher L
reviews.title: Better than Thailand
reviews.content: Such a fun thing to see. Deff better than the one in Thailand. Just don’t fall for the street people trying to show you were to go. Walk up the ramp and pick a bar to sit in. They will cram you in the closer the time gets. I hit the 330 train and wasn’t too busy.

reviews.author: Desiree
reviews.title: Hanoi Street train
reviews.content: Tom our guide took us to the Hanoi Train street. What an experience. Highly recommended. This is an experience you must have!

reviews.author: Dao Matcha - 143 Phung Hung Train Street
reviews.title: Hanoi Train Street
reviews.content: Nice places, good drinks, i love Matcha at 143 Phung Hung streetNice staffs and servicesThis place is perfect for watching the train pass by

reviews.author: Bernie T
reviews.title: Brilliant
reviews.content: What an exciting experience.  You arrive,  loads of great restaurants on the track. The staff know the train time and adjust the seating to protect visitors. There was a near miss some yrs ago, the Vietnam equivalent to health and safety closed the street to visitors.  We arrived not that long after the resteraunters requested it reopening. They certainly look after you as its in their interest to do so.

reviews.author: Laura B
reviews.title: Ignore the hustlers
reviews.content: The train tracks run straight through the cafes and shops of this street.  We sat on a shop on the second floor and enjoyed some sodas while people watching.  The train comes 2-3x per day; while we were there, the schedule of the day was 11:50am, 3:20pm, 7:40pm.Just make sure to ignore the people hounding you and preventing you from getting close to the train to take photos even though they are just shop owners trying to "trade" your going to their shop with train access.  We figured this out later after the train had sadly passed us by.

reviews.author: Linda H
reviews.title: Silly, but fun.
reviews.content: This is so fun.  It’s a train that runs down a street of shops.  A lot of the shops serve food and drink while you wait for the train.  I have to say that the coffee I had in both shops was the best coffee I had in Vietnam.  They get it from Saigon.

reviews.author: sarah zeke
reviews.title: Too crowded
reviews.content: Too crowded and food was expensive there. There’s limited time when train pass by and its only short. Worth the visit but wont be coming back again, not worth the hype and trouble.

reviews.author: TUMBO10
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: This is a great thing to see. Initially I thought it would be quite Instagrammy and over hyped but I actually enjoyed it. We went at night and seeing the lights from the bars either side of the track made for a great atmosphere.Staff from businesses will try and get you into their bars - prices are double what we found nearer the lake but still only 50,000 VD for a beer, which is just over £1.70 is still good.We got lucky and arrived about 2 minutes before a train arrived but I recommend seeing what times trains are - your hotels typically know this answer.

reviews.author: Lee_family_219053
reviews.title: Overhyped and don't get conned by the eateries that you gain entry only thru them
reviews.content: We were at the Train Street Mural and followed the rail track to train street to see what the fuss was about. When we approached a few people started asking us to go ro their drinking places as that's the only way to get access to the train track. We saw a barrier and someone controlling access up to the track. DO NOT get conned or follow them but walk further down and you'll gain free access to the train track and walk along the narrow alley with drinking places on both sides. The owners will try get your business by saying train coming and sit down have a drink. Do note the train timing and be ready to get out of the way. Enjoy your time there taking photos and the atmosphere.

reviews.author: Hugary1
reviews.title: Hanoi Train Street
reviews.content: One of the most unique tarin experiences in a major city of 92million you will ever see. Train comes on schedule and some people lock up their doors. The shop owners are obliged to keep you out of harms way. You can have a beverage and food inside along the track and watch the train pass, around 30 sec's. Can't imagine how people sleep as the trains run all the time. The Unification railway was completed after the war and connects Saigon and Hanoi.

reviews.author: KAVITA BERRY
reviews.title: Electrifying
reviews.content: It was an electrifying experience -- a must do  for everyone---the train passed so close-- atmosphere was charged with excitement

reviews.author: AMsays
reviews.title: A Moment of Magic, but overall, I think it is overrated...
reviews.content: Yes its unique, sitting trackside as a train goes by, but its momentarily magical.  There's the hustle beforehand, the jostling for position, the uneven sidewalk, the expensive drinks and what of the surly service. I don't know, maybe my server was having a bad day but overall, I think its overrated....

reviews.author: vtex001
reviews.title: Please research carefully and be patient!
reviews.content: Reviews of the various cafes are difficult to use because individual experiences vary considerably and there are hundreds of themscattered across several areas where trains come through.I have attached a screen shot from google maps of the area we would recommend but be careful because lots of people will try to convince you that you are in the 'wrong' place and they can get you to a better place for a small (inflated) fee via taxi or scooter. The train times seemed about right but don't be surprised if it's late. Get there a little early (45 mins) but be prepared for some of the train street cafes to be closed or setting up. We were about to accept one when lots of local people appeared and started pulling tables and chairs from everywhere, this resulted in crowds heading down the previously quiet street. The prices are fairly standard and all of the reputable cafes will give you a menu to choose from. Don't buy unless see a menu with prices.You will also see the late-comers trying to push in to cafes where there is clearly not room. The staff are excellent at moving them or'encouraging' them upstairs.Even though I had seen videos I was still surprised at how close the train passes. While it is 'touristy' I would definitely recommend it, the staff at our cafe were excellent hosts and it is their livelihood. They played their part in the safety aspect too as the police are swift to kick people out of the street for non-compliance. We had a guy offer a 'back-street' view which was genuine but had we been caught the police would have moved us. Stick with the bigger streets with lots of cafes. The guy got very worked up and started shouting when we looked sceptical and he told us to leave - don't take offence, smile and wave!Overall, it will take an hour and a half all-in. It is safe and easy, the most difficult part will be timing and choosing a drink!Highly recommended.

reviews.author: corinne_prevost
reviews.title: NOTHING TO SEE
reviews.content: A passing train, expensive drinks, I don't see the point. A call to tourists nothing more, they found the vein

reviews.author: Nick Epps
reviews.title: A must for Hanoi
reviews.content: Such a great experience, health and safety is out the window here. We based ourselves in the southern part and half an hour before the train was due we were set. You have to experience how close the train is to you and the speed which it passes. Must see

reviews.author: Funlovinfella
reviews.title: Natural Laxative!
reviews.content: We rocked up as part of our food tour, had a great egg coffee from Cafe 76, then waited for the train to pass and wondered why you did this in the first place! It’s noisy and a smidgen disconcerting, but fun!One of the best natural laxatives known to mankind but you’ve got to give it a go!

reviews.author: Ian R
reviews.title: A 'Must Visit" experience
reviews.content: We were obviously planning to visit this street having heard so much about it beforehand.As it was we stumbled upon it after visiting the jail and subsequently stopped for a drink. Not expecting to see a train we had another drink and a snack when all of a sudden lots of movement by bar owners ahead of a train coming through.Wow. What an experience to be sat track side as the huge locomotive and carriages rumbled through.Most people left the street at this point, and as we settled in for another beer were told more trains were coming through.Such a great experience.

reviews.author: SB01
reviews.title: A Must Do for Train Enthusiasts
reviews.content: This is an unusual attraction in that it is nothing more than a single line of railway track. However, the proximity to housing and the opportunistic bars that line the passageway make this an edgy and exciting thrill. The train literally passes within centimetres of the punters, including ourselves, who lined the street. At the southern end of the viewing area there are only bars on one side, so the effect is less claustrophobic, so personally I would try and sit further north, where the road crosses the line, as you get a decent view of the train approaching and departing. There are a few chancers who try and direct you to bars, but you could do this without buying anything, but personally I think you get a better view from a chair alongside the track.Train times are erratic,  but usually there are some between 8 - 10 pm. An official blows a whistle and he and cafe owners attempt to clear a path as the train approaches. Make sure you are not in or near an excitable group….

reviews.author: mrsmcdlt
reviews.title: Not again
reviews.content: This was unsettling, and not the way we'd imagined it.  The street is visually amazing, and the train passing by is a thrilling experience, but the night we were there, something wasn't right.As the train was anticipated, a woman appeared, who started screaming at people in the "front row".  She was frantic, and although those people were moving as requested, she continued to bark at them.  A young family near us were attempting to gather their things and their young son, when a police offer came by and started shouting at them (they were not in the first row, so we couldn't understand the problem).  When he didn't feel they were moving fast enough, he grabbed their table, sending their drinks flying, and walked away with it.  Once the train passed (which was awesome), we sat back down with our drinks, only to have the woman return, literally pushing us and yelling that it was CLOSED.  People had full drinks in their hands, and were totally confused, as we were pushed out of the area in a big hurry.We ended up standing on a street corner finishing our beer, and wondering what had just happened.It all seemed terrifically aggressive, and I can only imagine how scared the little guy felt when a police officer yanked away their table and sent his drink flying.

reviews.author: Yo13
reviews.title: What to do See for fun
reviews.content: How not to take an hour of your time and land while enjoying a Hanoi beer or a coffee with egg while waiting for a train, which you will never take.... it is to be seen once in a lifetime, I advise you. I expected the train to idle, but be careful....

reviews.author: Skyrose77
reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.content: This is a highly overrated destination ruined by tourist. I recommend you aave yourself the walk and avoid the utter chaos.

reviews.author: ぴろーしき
reviews.title: There are cafes and bars.
reviews.content: You can also enter from a place not far from Hanoi railway station. Cafes line the tracks. It's a common spot in Asia, but it's by far easier to access than the famous Mae Klong Railway Market in Thailand, so it's not bad in that respect either.

reviews.author: gfsc5
reviews.title: Amazing experience
reviews.content: We stumbled upon Train Street when we were heading back to our hotel after a morning of sightseeing.  Our timing was very good as we only had a 20min wait before the train arrived.Essentially, it's a train track running down a narrow street with small cafes/coffee shops on either side.  The walking isn't easy as there is no real paving.We found a cafe and ordered a Vietnamese milky coffee, peach tea and a chicken banh mi and sat at a table adjacent to the rail line.A warning signal is given before the train arrives to give owners time to move any chairs that are too close to the line.  It also gives people the chance to get to safety.  The train is a full size train with many carriages and it doesn’t go slowly.  And it passes within touching distance.  Amazing.Recommended.

reviews.author: S&O
reviews.title: Especially pretty in the evening
reviews.content: In the evening it is especially pretty, as it is very cheesy, nicely lit. At 7.30 pm and 9.15 pm the train comes through in the evening, at a very decent pace. Very worth experiencing. 1 std before existence and secure a good seat in a cafe in the front row.

reviews.author: Nahid Kaleem
reviews.title: Exploring Hanoi's Train Street: A Must-Visit Experience
reviews.content: Hanoi’s Train Street is a must-visit attraction where visitors can enjoy coffee while witnessing a train pass just inches away. There are two train streets in Hanoi, but the Old Train Street is the most authentic and historically rich.  To make the most of the experience, visitors should arrive 30 minutes before the train’s arrival to take photos and soak in the atmosphere. The most popular section is Phung Hung Street, accessible by foot, motorbike, or taxi. Key train timings vary between weekdays and weekends, so checking the schedule locally is essential.  While the experience is thrilling, safety precautions must be followed, including staying off the tracks, respecting cafe guidelines, and being mindful of the train’s timing. Visitors should avoid gathering in large crowds, sitting on the tracks, or placing objects too close to the railway.  This unique mix of culture, history, and excitement makes Hanoi Train Street an unforgettable experience for travelers.

reviews.author: Keelyimps
reviews.title: Great experience.
reviews.content: Get there early to grab a decent seat outside a café. We asked one of the café owners what time the next train was first and waiting an hour but this was fine enjoying a couple of beers and people watching. The train does come very near you 😀

reviews.author: eliza248
reviews.title: Better than it sounds
reviews.content: Couldn't believe we were sitting there having a coffee and waiting for a train to pass but there was a real sense of anticipation as time of its arrival approached. We were told 3 pm but it was more like 3.20 when it sailed pass us about 1m from us! Would never happen in the UK! Definitely worth going to watch and go about 30 mins earlier to secure any of the cafe seats in the middle of the street.

reviews.author: Happy Eater 😀
reviews.title: Train on time
reviews.content: No20 train street , arrived and had egg coffee at 2pm and advised the train was at 230 , although other places said was at 315 , at 225 whistles started going and train was on time , Lovely coffee and great service

reviews.author: dennisalexandrov1976
reviews.title: One step from the train
reviews.content: This is undoubtedly one of the main attractions of Hanoi, can only be in Asia. In countries where safety standards are at a different level, this is hardly possible when there are dozens of cafes on a narrow street where people sit within a metre of the tracks on which trains of passengers and freight regularly run. And it's not a special show, it's a real road where trains run, for example, to southern Vietnam. There's a schedule, it's best to come in advance to take a comfortable seat in one of the many cafes. We got on two trains: the first day was a very long freight train, and the other time, we barely had time to run into the track area and greet the passenger train. And as soon as the train passes, crowds of people pour onto the tracks, locals even burn things, life boils over and this is how people live with the trains. And nobody's bothering anyone. Be sure to go!!!

locationDesc: The largest lake n Hanoi is a popular spot for gathering, surrounded by many shops, restaurants, gardens, and hotels. It features the Trấn Quốc Pagoda, Vietnamese for Stabilizing the Nation.

reviews.author: Igor Alexeev
reviews.title: West Lake, in Hanoi...
reviews.content: West Lake or Tay Lake (Hồ Tây) - the largest body of water in Hanoi, with a coastline of about 17 km. The lake shores are a great place for walks and relaxation. On these shores, there are, of course, many attractions, including the Chancuo Pagoda (Chùa Trấn Quốc)...

reviews.author: Renate H
reviews.title: Highly recommended in Hanoi
reviews.content: I would be happy to stay at this special hotel with very friendly staff and a delicious breakfast buffet again anytime.

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: Pleasant lake west of old Hanoi
reviews.content: Pretty lake which, as its name suggests, is located slightly to the west of old Hanoi. You will find a pretty pagoda there, but also a very pleasant and well-shaded promenade along the water. Much more peaceful than Hoan Kiem Lake, this lake is also located within walking distance of the embassy district, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, and the One Pillar Pagoda.

reviews.author: Keren W
reviews.title: Nice place for a slow Hanoi afternoon
reviews.content: I spent an afternoon walking around West Lake and liked it more than I expected. The breeze off the water was a nice break from Hanoi’s heat, and there were plenty of little cafes and street stalls nearby where I grabbed a strong iced coffee and some grilled snacks. It felt calm in spots, especially along the quieter sections, but the traffic around the lake can get pretty noisy and crossing streets is still a bit of a hassle. Some parts also looked a little messy, so it’s not exactly postcard perfect. Still, I’d recommend it if you want a slower, more relaxed side of the city.

reviews.author: Eddie F
reviews.title: Peaceful lake with a few rough edges
reviews.content: I spent an afternoon walking around West Lake and really enjoyed the slower pace compared with the busier parts of Hanoi. The breeze off the water was nice, and I liked seeing locals jogging, fishing, and hanging out at the little cafes. I stopped for a cold drink and watched the sunset turn the water kind of silvery, which was lovely. That said, some stretches felt a bit chaotic with traffic and construction, and a few areas near the road weren’t exactly relaxing. Still, if you want a break from the crowds and don’t mind a bit of urban mess, it’s worth going. I’d recommend it, just not for a pristine lakeside experience.

reviews.author: Benjamin A
reviews.title: Hanoi in autumn is truly wonderful.
reviews.content: One beautiful afternoon in Hanoi, I was reminded of my trip there last autumn. Today, as I was going through my travel photos, I found this picture and felt compelled to share a review. Hanoi is truly a wonderful city, with delightful autumn weather and incredible food.

reviews.author: Jazz Gumbo
reviews.title: On a sunny day, its a nice walk.
reviews.content: Came to stroll around the area & even took out one of the swan boats which was reasonably priced and a nice way to wile away an hour. Fascinating architecture surrounds the lake, well worth visiting.

reviews.author: sekjr0521
reviews.title: Enjoyable Walk
reviews.content: No matter where you are in the Old Quarter, it is an easy walk through colorful streets to get to West Lake.,. There is so much activity going on it is hard to keep up with it all.  So no matter how many times you go you'll always find something new to see.  They are always changing different displays that border the perimeter of the lake... Plus, on your walk, you'll find yourself attracted by many other things along the way including the Water Puppet Theater. At the lower end you'll find a number of restaurants including McDonald's, which was my hangout because at least i knew what i was eating.... I think... It is about a 30 minute walk, and more enjoyable at night with all of the lights and music...

reviews.author: AbhimanyuSinghi
reviews.title: Scenic View with Pagodas Around It
reviews.content: The lake was a short walk from Pan Pacific Hotel. We could even see it from our room. The view is quite scenic especially around sunset. A few pagodas line up one side and are worth a shot visit. You can also take a boat ride in the lake I think.

reviews.author: Em Happy Travelling Folks
reviews.title: Pagoda Times - be aware
reviews.content: Visited the pagoda today and a few things there dampened our joy - and it wasn’t the most amazing storm ever as we travelled over in the awesome rickshaws. On arrival we said no to people selling ponchos (as we had umbrellas and our own coats), however it was like no wasn’t acceptable. They “sold” us 4 ponchos, 2 we didn’t want. This made us cranky as we were being respectful. Then after paying different prices for the same product, we got to outside the entrance and a man groused at one of our party for having her phone out.  Ok - so again, judgement re photos. Tourists use phones for everything now, not just  taking pictures - eg using google translate! Sometimes we use them to look up history and information also when there is not English explanation. Anyway, she put it away respectfully. Then when inside we literally walked around for 5–10 minutes, a lady pointed to her watch at quarter to 11 and basically shushed us out of there. So we walked out thinking we had gone to the trouble of ensuring correct clothing and no singlets etc and saw very little for the effort it took to arrange getting out there. Such a shame. Check their breaks times as they matter. The Lake looked beautiful - even with the lightning striking directly down over it!

reviews.author: BalkrishnaShroff
reviews.title: Nice One !!
reviews.content: This beautiful lake is located about 6 km from city center. After visiting oldest Buddhist temple Tran Quoc Pagoda in Hanoi, which is next to lake, we stopped here for some time. It's beautiful lake ideal for photo opportunity. Three were few few vendors around selling souvenirs. We had cold fresh coconut water which was very nice.Worth visiting for few minutes...

reviews.author: AngeK
reviews.title: Best Pho ever!
reviews.content: Went to this place on a food tour and then went back on our own as well just had to try the fried Pho with beef and veggies again. Absolutely 10/10 recommend Pho Cuon Hung Ben! And the Standing Bar has loads of different beers, cider and yummy small dishes to share. Head upstairs for a great view of the lake

reviews.author: Strike_right
reviews.title: West Lake Hanoi
reviews.content: Go for a lively environment, nice picnic, a weekend brunch a beautiful sunset, a lot of sunset pictures, and a long walk.Avoid for evening pollution.

reviews.author: Văn Lâm
reviews.title: I would like to introduce you to a wonderful tour of Hanoi
reviews.content: HANOI CITY TOURDURATION: 8 hoursDEPARTURE: DAILY - MEANS OF TRANSPORT: CAR On this Hanoi City tour, you will visit Uncle Ho's Mausoleum - the great leader of Vietnam. Visit the first university of our country - Temple of Literature, visit and take pictures of Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son Temple - the heart of Hanoi capital, ... A journey to explore the capital of Hanoi promises to bring you the most unforgettable experiences. HIGHLIGHTS OF THE PROGRAM:• Visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum relic site with Uncle Ho's Mausoleum, Stilt House, and Uncle Ho's fish pond and visit the One Pillar Pagoda.• Visit the Temple of Literature - the first university in our country.• Visit Tran Quoc Pagoda - a pagoda with a history of nearly 1500 years, considered the oldest in Thang Long - Hanoi. • Admire the massive architectural work, built by dynasties in many historical periods - Thang Long Imperial Citadel. • Visit and learn about Hoa Lo Prison. • Enjoy the specialities of the capital Hanoi. Tour program8:00 am: The car picks you up at the Hanoi Opera House to start the tour of the capital Hanoi. (Bread and water are provided for you to have a snack in the car)8:15 am: The car arrives at Tran Quoc Pagoda, the group gathers and visits• Tran Quoc Pagoda - located on an island east of West Lake (Tay Ho district). The pagoda has a history of nearly 1500 years and is considered the oldest in Thang Long - Hanoi. The pagoda's architecture has a harmonious combination of solemnity, and antiquity with elegant scenery amidst the tranquillity of a vast lake. It was the Buddhist centre of Thang Long Citadel during the Ly and Tran dynasties.9:00 am: The car picks up the group to go to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum9:15 am: The group gathers at the Mausoleum and visits• The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum relic site with Uncle Ho's Mausoleum, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house and fish pond and visits the One Pillar Pagoda.10:20: The car picks up the group to go to the Temple of Literature - Imperial Academy10:30 am: The group gathers and visits the Temple of Literature - Imperial Academy• The Temple of Literature - Imperial Academy. Vietnam's earliest university is regarded as the Temple of Literature-Imperial Academy. Built on a rather big scale in October 1073, this historic building is still standing today. Confucius, the originator of Confucianism, and Chu Van An, the principal of the Imperial Academy, who stood for the lofty moral concept of Vietnamese education, were worshipped at the Temple of Literature.11:45 am: The group has lunch at the restaurant ... (eat Hanoi specialities)13:00 pm: The car picks up the group to visit Thang Long Imperial Citadel• Thang Long Imperial Citadel is a complex of relics associated with the history of Thang Long - Dong Kinh Citadel and Hanoi city starting from the pre-Thang Long period (An Nam protectorate in the 7th century) through the Dinh - Tien Le period, strongly developed under the Ly, Tran, Le dynasties and Hanoi city under the Nguyen dynasty. This is a massive architectural work, built by the dynasties in many historical periods and became one of the most important relics in the system of Vietnamese relics.14:15 pm: The car picks up the group to go to Hoa Lo Prison14:25 pm: The group gathers and visits Hoa Lo Prison• Hoa Lo Prison was formerly a prison located in Hanoi, Vietnam, also known as the Central Prison or ironically the Hanoi Hilton. It was built when Indochina was an inseparable part of the French Empire. Partially destroyed in 1990, it is now used as a museum. 15:10 pm: The car picks up the group to go to Hoan Kiem Lake 15:20 pm: The group gathers and visits Hoan Kiem Lake• Hoan Kiem Lake, also known as Guom Lake, learns about the Vietnamese and French architecture around the lake area. You will visit and take pictures outside Ngoc Son Temple worshipping Van Xuong Saint and Tran Hung Dao - a famous general in Vietnamese and world history and The Huc Bridge. If you want to go inside the temple, you will pay for the entrance fee. 16:00 pm: The vehicle will return you to the Hanoi Opera House at the end of the Hanoi City Tour, or you can depart independently.

reviews.author: David Roy P
reviews.title: Great Fun
reviews.content: Took a ride on the Pedal Boats on the Lake . Very Cheap for 1 Hour , only $3 AUD .Great Fun but exhausting . Had to give up after 45 minutes as our legs ached too much . The Lake is quite big and is a bit Polluted . Noticed Several Dead Fish floating here & there . Lots of people were fishing

reviews.author: Hoi An Free Walking tour & Cycling tour
reviews.title: The largest lake in HaNoi
reviews.content: The largest lake in HaNoi, where you can cycle. Especially, there are a lot of exercises activities in the morning around the lake. However,  the water of the lake is polluted,  there are a many fishes that died around the lake. Luckily, young generation of HaNoi,  they are taking care of environment at every weekend.  That' s a good point,  more and more people verlunteer to clean the lake. Hopefully,  it will get cleaner in the near future 🙏💯❤️

reviews.author: Chris M.
reviews.title: Beautiful lake. Nice run.
reviews.content: Beautiful lake, did a nice run! Would recommend it to others that are into running abroad. Plenty of shades in the hot weather. Be aware to bring some drinking water because of the humid climate!

reviews.author: OHKSO
reviews.title: Open-top bus tour
reviews.content: This time, we took an open-top bus around the city centre to and from Thanh Nien Street, which divides it from Checkback Lake. Despite the size of Westlake from the bus's 2nd floor window, it was a quiet surface because it was not the ocean. Also, Thanh Nien Street seemed to function as a walking course.

reviews.author: Michelle M
reviews.title: Enjoy the lake view
reviews.content: I found a nice spot for people who love cycling in Hanoi. I could rent a bicycle for $2 and pedal around the serene lake for 3 hours. It was magical, especially at sunset. After cycling, I stopped at a charming coffee shop along the lakeside for a delicious cup of coffee with a stunning view. It's the perfect way to unwind and immerse yourself in the beauty of West Lake.

reviews.author: John L
reviews.title: Walk is interesting but be careful.
reviews.content: You can walk around the lake, which more than 17km. It takes 3-4 hours of walking. Some areas are well planted but others are not. You will walk across some lotus patches, restaurants, schools, cafes, parks etc.. in the summer time lots of dead fishes and it emits bad odor, the water is polluted year round but you still see people swimming in it and fishing even signs everywhere prohibited.

reviews.author: Crumpled Nomad | Travel Intelligence
reviews.title: Largest lake in Hanoi
reviews.content: The biggest freshwater lake in Hanoi. Many hotels and restaurants are located around this lake. We dined at the eastern and oriental tea house which overlooked the west lake from where we were sitting at the cafe. We even went closer to the lake to take more beautiful pictures. Many sites around the lake for picture taking.

reviews.author: Alex Phạm
reviews.title: West Lake
reviews.content: As the largest freshwater lake in Hanoi, if you have time, you should rent a bicycle to go around the lake and enjoy the beautiful sunset here.

reviews.author: Dimitris L
reviews.title: A lake with views
reviews.content: West Lake is a nice area to walk around and enjoy the scenery. There are many sellers selling all kinds of things in the area and many tourists as well. The water however is not something one would admire.

reviews.author: Nami L
reviews.title: West Lake
reviews.content: Windy West Lake on a summer afternoon.The beautiful scenery here is captivating.I'll take you there next fall.Reviewing our old love storyLove Hanoi

reviews.author: Francoise D
reviews.title: Top on the way home
reviews.content: Great hotel! Many facilities. Nice location if you have already done 'old quarter' etc. I stayed here on my way back home. It was still wonderful to enjoy it.

reviews.author: Sofia
reviews.title: Dirty water, unimpressive scenery.
reviews.content: Renting bikes around West Lake was a disappointment. The water was dirty, the air wasn't fresh, and the scenery was pretty boring. We couldn't find a decent spot for our picnic, so ended up eating street food back at our hotel.

reviews.author: Tom Mubarak
reviews.title: A lakeside picnic and bike ride
reviews.content: We rented bicycles and explored the scenic West Lake (Ho Tay). The fresh air and serene atmosphere were perfect for a romantic picnic. We found a quiet spot by the lake and enjoyed delicious street food while taking in the beautiful scenery.

reviews.author: Shruti Pramod Reddy
reviews.title: Walk around
reviews.content: Walked around this lake for an hour on Dec-23,2023, exploring Vietnamese people.Nice insight into the local life as I saw some sunset shoots happening & people sitting & some food stalls and cafes nearby too.

reviews.author: dragonflyazul
reviews.title: 100 % POLLUTION !!!
reviews.content: This is a very big lake ,  lake is very  polluted and full of dead fish.  Lake smell and dirty Not worth the visit. The area around the lake is also not very attractive , the road is dirty very hard to walk around, cause of motorbikes blocking footpath. NOT a tourist attraction.

reviews.author: Monika K
reviews.title: Could be beautiful if cleaned
reviews.content: Unfortunately, slightly disappointed with the lake. There is a nice coffee shop and nice pagoda but other than that- lake is very dirty and crowded. As previous comments mentioned a lot of dead fish and plastic trash floating.

reviews.author: André K
reviews.title: Polluted Lake
reviews.content: Very big lake , polluted and full of dead fish. Not worth the visit. The area around the  lake is  also not very attractive , definitely not a tourist attraction.

reviews.author: Loretta M
reviews.title: Worth riding a bicycle around West Lake👍
reviews.content: Enjoyed our bike ride around West Lake. It was a good challenge and best done clockwise around the lake to be on the lakeside side of the road. Rented bikes from Bike Plus 150,000d for two hours which included helmets. A nice change in activity from walking Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Nick K
reviews.title: Potential but NO
reviews.content: YUKKKKCan't walk around cause of motorbikes blocking footpath.  Lake dirty and smells. Road is busy around and pollution

reviews.author: Annette Dupont
reviews.title: Very beautiful !
reviews.content: Big lake, picturesque landscape. We took many photos here. The sunset is truly magnificent. We also tried the ice cream. But you have to wait a long time before you can queue.

reviews.author: Heidi Watkins
reviews.title: Tranquil Delight at West Lake: A Must-Visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: Just had an amazing time at West Lake in Hanoi. The peaceful vibes by the water and the beautiful pagodas were a treat.Loved how I could take a relaxing stroll, watch Tai Chi, and enjoy the sunset. And the local food around the lake?Delish! If you're in Hanoi, don't miss this gem.

reviews.author: campfamily50
reviews.title: Twin Dragons of West Lake
reviews.content: Twin Dragons of West Lake. This was an impressive sight and if you visit West Lake its a “must-see”.  These twin dragons are colorful, cool and large.  With the back drop of the lake, it almost looks like they are the Guardians of the Lake and welcoming you to this beautiful area. We loved it.

reviews.author: Shelley M
reviews.title: disappointed
reviews.content: Nice to escape the crowds in old quarter.  A much larger lake with a lot of housing and shops around.  The day was so smoggy that you really couldnt see very far and what you could see had so much rubbish floating in it was rather sad to be fair.

reviews.author: Phi Somchai
reviews.title: Peaceful place
reviews.content: One of the most famous place in Hanoi.  It is very scenic with lots of eatery and residences around the lake.The surrounding is rather peaceful here and great place to get away from the chaotic Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Soko37
reviews.title: Famous place
reviews.content: Dominant of Hanoi, neighbouring with Truc Back smaller lake, pagoda or governmental attraction very close near by. Nice to walk around almost in any weather. We walked around a bit and being lucky to have low temperature slightly above twenty degrees. We did walk only part close to another small lake as this is very big one

reviews.author: Jain G
reviews.title: Ha Noi West Lake
reviews.content: There are several places to rent bicycles around the West Lake. You could also rent bikes and start cycling from the Old Quarter.  That was fun

reviews.author: Leonhkny
reviews.title: Lung of Hanoi
reviews.content: This is one of the very few options to escape the crowd in Hanoi. West Lake is a vast waterfront area offering a relaxing, peaceful atmosphere as well as some precious open spaces for a stroll. Good to take a rest when traffic of the Vietnamese capital becomes unbearable.

reviews.author: Ugrid M
reviews.title: Bicycling in Hanoi
reviews.content: This was one of my several times to Hanoi. But the distinguished experience was my first time to ride bicycle in Hanoi where the traffic condition is unique. My experiences  in bicycling in Hanoi was exciting. West lake is a good place for bicycling around. There are good hotels, coffee shops and street food stalls around the Lake. Friendly, hospitality, worth for money at many shops I visited. I took 2 days there before leaving by air back home after finishing 7-day touring bicycling from Thai-Laos border to Laos-Vietnam border and then to SAPA.My impressive accommodation is A25 Hotel 109 Truc Bach, Ba Dinh, Hanoi near West Lake. Clean, well-equipped and hospitality.My impressive bike shop is 2Cycle Bike Shop, 154 Yen How, Tay Ho, Hanoi. Excellent services.

reviews.author: Ali921
reviews.title: Nice views
reviews.content: West Lake itself is not historic in itself. It's probably too large for most people to walk around as well. A lot of the locals just sit down on chairs and look at the view. It's visited mainly because of Tran Quoc pagoda which sits within it. Alongside is another lake Ho Truc Bach - more famous because Senator John McCain was shot down into that lake

reviews.author: wombatdavid
reviews.title: Enjoyable walk
reviews.content: We enjoyed a walk up to the lake from the Old Quarter. It is a bit dirty and the air was very polluted. But we walked around some of the lake and saw the pagoda. A nice spot in Hanoi if they could just clean up somewhat…

reviews.author: G2Kpauly
reviews.title: Nice to wall around
reviews.content: I had a very enjoyable walk around part of this lake. It's worth going to to enjoy some fresh air, take some photos, walk around and watch the locals enjoying life.

reviews.author: Gon Freeces
reviews.title: Best place in Hanoi and I want to live here
reviews.content: The neighborhood consists of some of the best attractions in Hanoi. There are several spots where you can get a great view of sunrise and sunset. Bars, pubs and some restaurants serving the best Vietnamese foods and drinks. Streets are clean.  That’s why some 5 star hotels are located here.

reviews.author: Travelove58
reviews.title: Really it's just a normal lake.......
reviews.content: This is basically just a very normal lake, just as in many places all over the world, with the usual activities people do around & along it. And the usual street seller selling their stuff. Nothing special.Visit only if you have time to spare

reviews.author: Mozzie93
reviews.title: Glad we survived this bike ride!
reviews.content: We rented bikes and cycled round lake. It was a long way (2 or 3 hours) and mixed. Some parts were nice and relaxed, but other parts were on roads and felt a bit dangerous. Lots of cafes to stop for refreshments luckily. Pagoda and interesting buildings. After cycling round, we were too exhausted to go to the botanical gardens.

reviews.author: CKF
reviews.title: Fun but sweaty and a bit dangerous
reviews.content: Our tour company arranged for us to rent bikes to ride around the 17 km perimeter of West Lake.  It was a fun experience, and there are a few temples and statues to stop and see along the way.  Warning: you are on regular traffic rounds with all kinds of vehicles.  Because of this, the experience was more dangerous than I expected.  But we had decent bikes with good gear shifting and we enjoyed the afternoon.

reviews.author: Mawa N
reviews.title: Beautiful sunset at the lake
reviews.content: Amazing sunset overlooking the west lake in Hanoi capital. Drink cocktail and watching the sun disappear in the west so beautiful

reviews.author: LoBommer
reviews.country: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
reviews.title: Not worth a visit
reviews.content: We had walked from the old quarter via the Mausoluem, botanical gardens and the B52 Lake and were looking forward to a nice walk around this large lake, unfortunately there were no lakeside footpaths and the water was dirty and smelly with dead fish floating in it. The Truch Bach lake nearby was marginally better and we found a lovely spot to have a beer and a banh mi.

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: It’s not a must do
reviews.content: West lake is ok to visit love to walk around lakes and parks when I travel to other cities you can get a sense of local life.For me it was ok if staying in area then most certainly go over and walk around the lake or part of it.If staying in old quarter don’t think it’s that special to go and see.Temple and pagoda is a nice touch for lake and it’s fairly dirty and smelly bit that goes for most lakes on Hanoi.

reviews.author: steverichhudd
reviews.title: Didn't get the attraction
reviews.content: We got to the lake from the Botanical Gardens.  We were expecting a beautiful lake to walk around. The part we first encountered smelt terrible and had dead fish floating on top. Some guys were fishing and we saw their catch on the side. We walked past the pagoda but felt no need to go any further. The areas we saw were dirty. Perhaps we had over expectations of West Lake or not seen the best parts (and am very happy to be proved wrong), but this and the Truc Bach Lake next to it were not places I would recommend.

reviews.author: Rajalakshmy M
reviews.title: Beautiful lake with fantastic vibes
reviews.content: Beautiful lake. Amazing atmosphere around the lake activities, tai chi, badminton, runners, tourists. In the weekends it gets even better.

reviews.author: 422iana
reviews.title: Morning run
reviews.content: An enjoyable run towards the lake and there was wide paths around the lake. Head to the pergola. Busy roads to cross.

reviews.author: Raymondale
reviews.title: Biggest lake in Hanoi
reviews.content: it is bigger than Ho Hoan Kien,it is hard to walk around the lake.i went here for Tran Quoc Temple,so no time to admire the lake and its surrounding.better stay close to the lake,then you have time to see the beauty of the lake.be note that there are some peddlers around the lake,they want ask you to try to carry baskets on shoulder pole,and take pics of you,it is not free,and the price is not cheap.if you want to try,ask the price first,and bargain with them.

reviews.author: chiangmaicharlies
reviews.title: Not worth the time
reviews.content: The biggest lake in Hanoi, but it's smelly, dirty and not picturesque.There's a pagoda and temple at one point on the lake, which is where most tourists go.Don't bother unless you have time on your hands and like dirty lakes.It's an easy walk from Hanoi centre, but not worth it.

reviews.author: JimboOz
reviews.title: Tran Quoc pagoda
reviews.content: In the 15th Century, the Emperor borrowed a magical sword from the sacred turtle who dwelled in Hoan Kiem lake.  It's inspiration encouraged the Vietnamese warriors to defeat the invaders from Mongolia . On returning victorious, the Emperor was boating around the lake, and the Turtle rose up from the depths and snatched his sword back from the Emperor's grasp.At this Pagoda I purchased a baby turtle and put it back into the lake, gaining merit for my next reincarnation

reviews.author: parksemin
reviews.title: Nice view
reviews.content: We went to West Lake and really enjoyed the sunset. And then, we walked around, visited temple and pagoda. Nice place to vistit. Should try

reviews.author: Hoang Do
reviews.title: Best Lake in Hanoi
reviews.content: West Lake is pretty big that if you ride a motorbike around the lake it will take 40 minutes. The place is very good for people going on a date. You can ride around the lake and stop at one of myriad coffee shops and restaurants. The lake is truly full of possibility if you stay creative.

reviews.author: michael p
reviews.title: Pretty haven in the city
reviews.content: Hanoi is a busy city ruled by motorbikes which are noisy at all hours and take up any available pathways.  The lake (2 lakes actually) are a haven though even here it is not possible to walk around without using the road and without having motorbikes use the paths. The small lake is good for a 2-3 km run, the big lake is 17km.  There are a few restuarants around the lakes.  The main attraction is the pagoda, which you can visit or take photos of from outside.

reviews.author: Andy Nguyen
reviews.title: Found the fresh air among busy capial
reviews.content: I think most of you know West Lake, Hanoi, Vietnam 🇻🇳 This is the most "fresh" place in Hanoi. I found it when Hanoi was in the worst polution ever and there are many people have to bear it :((Fortunately, Hanoi has West Lake, which bring a lot fresh air to refresh Hanoi. When I reached here, I felt like I escaped successfully from a polluted monster. Really love it 😍 You can visit West Lake if you want to find your own fresh space :)))

reviews.author: John E
reviews.title: Expat hangout
reviews.content: This is the area where most expats live and hangout so there is a lot to do as far as restaurants and stores and hotels. NIce area to walk around and get a feel for lifestyle.

reviews.author: Chunker M
reviews.title: Exclusive!
reviews.content: It absolutely was a breezy and wonderful evening. Strolling on the lake and enjoying seeing neighborhood people dance is a wonderful knowledge. If you are an animal lover you are going to think it's a lot more fascinating because you are able to purchase different species of animals because of their host walking around there. The pet therapy is employed as well as you're competent to possess a peaceful and harmony walk.

reviews.author: Gavin M G
reviews.title: Well it IS a lake:-)
reviews.content: It is good to see any water expense in Hanoi. West Lake is no exception. It is a good place to go and sit for a coffee, and to take a stroll. I could not find any pedestrianised area or quality Western coffee around the lake - still its an OK place to go for an evening walk.... I think that it has massive potential as a really great space to chill and be out, but this potential has not been tapped at all.. that said, sure its OK for a visit.

reviews.author: Epic-Traveller
reviews.title: Ho Tay (West Lake)
reviews.content: This is a large and beautiful lake in a busy part of the City of Hanoi. There is a nice temple at one end and a pagoda with various other things half a mile further.We had a nice stroll along the lake under the shade of trees and visited the pagoda in the middle.

reviews.author: Ajax7925 -Steve W
reviews.title: Ho Tay - west lake
reviews.content: I have been here many times.  It's beauitful to see.  So many high in places to eat .  I have been to Hanoi 4 times and every time I go to West lake.

reviews.author: Elysee
reviews.title: Remarkable beach.. should go
reviews.content: Took a stroll up together with the lake. Such as a lot of Hanoi, the purely organic attractiveness is some spoiled by the litter and additionally the mad website traffic all about you. On the fringes on the lake, it was quite a bit of quieter and we are able to stay on benches and ease up and talk just a little, consequently it was ultimately an enjoyable experience. We in addition walked across the key bridge after which discovered the pagoda which was interesting in the very own right of its. Although I am going to count the in the list of mine of most great waterbodies I've in the past visited.

reviews.author: Conney
reviews.title: Very relaxing place
reviews.content: We walked approximately the sofitel and also took a drink within their roof top bar to view the sunset over the lake drinks were english prices for cocktails but worthwhile for the point of view, we also liked some good tapas there. Nice temple on how though a sign says no shorts so we did not go in therefore in case you're planning that perhaps take a sarong. The walk in place along the lake is extremely great and you are able to purchase a coconut to drink from. More relaxing compared to kiem lake.

reviews.author: Stefan O
reviews.title: West Lake
reviews.content: West Lake in Hanoi is so nice situated so close to the city centre and a great walk along the lake on a sunny day!!

reviews.author: aaong86
reviews.title: Largest body of water in Hanoi!
reviews.content: This is another must visit when you are in Hanoi esp when you are visiting the Tran Quoc Pagoda which is located at the lake. The perimeter of the lake is around 18km which is possible to walk around the entire lake but it will probably take you a few hours to do so. Too bad I didn't have the time to walk around the entire late but i did walked around the the Tran Quoc Pagoda stretch and around the smaller Truc Bach lake which is located besides the west lake. Perhaps you could spend a few hrs to walk around the entire lake.

reviews.author: Bulbul
reviews.title: Ideal to spend time away from the bustling old quarter
reviews.content: The lake is situated in Tay Ho district. The area is posh and clean. Spend a couple of hours in the evening here if you want to experience some peace away from the bustling old quarter. You can also choose to ride swan shaped pedal boats in the lake. The cost is around 100000 VND for an hour.

reviews.author: sangeeta68
reviews.title: beautiful
reviews.content: we were there and loved the sunset one day while strolling down the side, there is not much else to do here

reviews.author: Ellen B
reviews.title: Stroll along the lake and Tran Quoc pagoda
reviews.content: The pagoda is beautiful but today there was too much building going on. The whole footpath was out and lots of drilling. Very dusty. But apart from that it was really nice to see. The lake is huge and has lots of cool coffee places to enjoy. 13 km to bike around if you fancy that.

reviews.author: SeeMoreLiveMore
reviews.title: Know what you are looking for before you come ...
reviews.content: This is more a district around the Lake rather than a tourist spot in itself. The lake is hardly picturesque. But there are a few interesting temples and buildings around it. There are many good local eats in the area as well. But know what you are looking for before coming will make it easier to navigate the area.

reviews.author: Jalal Iqbal
reviews.title: big lake a bit far from the city
reviews.content: the lake is big, clean and nicely maintained lake. located a bit away from the city. has nice walkways beside it. u gonna like it, especially in the afternoon and evening. has a cool pagoda and some nice colorful places around it. i spent a nice evening here and liked the entire place.

reviews.author: Nick Andreeff
reviews.title: Should see
