locationDesc: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology is a unit under Vietnam Academy of Scocial Sciences. Vietnam Museum of Ethnology is both a research centre and a public museum exhibiting the ethnic groups of Vietnam. The mission of the Museum is scientific research, collection, documentation, conservation, exhibition and preserving the cultural and historic patrimony of the nation's different ethnic groups. The museum also serves to guide research, conservation, and technology that are specific to the work of an ethnographic museum.

reviews.author: Myranda B
reviews.title: Full of energy, the food is so-so.
reviews.content: Tahien is a city that never sleeps, always full of energy. The food was just so-so, but drinking a cold Czech beer in the lively crowd was exceptional. It's worth visiting at least once!

reviews.author: Travel Girl GR
reviews.title: Indifferent road
reviews.content: Road with shops for food and drink.Nothing special since you can find decent stores anywhere else in the city

reviews.author: Knuckles
reviews.title: Excellent Hanoi Food Tour with Minh
reviews.content: Excellent Hanoi Food Tour with MinhOur walking food tour with Minh was a real highlight of our time in Hanoi. Minh was informative, relaxed, and incredibly knowledgeable, sharing great insights into the city’s food, culture, and history without ever making it feel formal.What made the experience special was how friendly and genuine he was — it felt more like exploring Hanoi with a friend rather than being led by a tour guide. The food was fantastic, and we discovered places and dishes we would never have found on our own.Highly recommended for anyone wanting an authentic and enjoyable food tour in Hanoi. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

reviews.author: 黄佳琪
reviews.title: Lively beer street for the hustle and bustle of you
reviews.content: It's a beer street crowded at night, so buzzy that it's almost inch-deep. If you love the hustle and bustle and enjoy the beer culture, it's really worth exploring. However, street solicitation is more common and requires psychological preparation.

reviews.author: Mamie F
reviews.title: Vibrant Music Bar Street Safe and comfortable
reviews.content: The ambience is great, the energy is high! The music is pleasant and the environment safe and secure. Bars gather here to pick your favourite tunes and moods, and enjoy one or more great nights~

reviews.author: Vy H.
reviews.title: Bars in Hanoi, Vietnam
reviews.content: Fun area to hang out and drink!  Very energetic vibe, lots of music blasting and tons of people.  If you don’t mind the chaos, this place can be lots of fun!

reviews.author: TravelingFoodie
reviews.title: Fun and worth it
reviews.content: Ta Hien Beer Street offers a fun and energetic glimpse into Hanoi’s nightlife. We visited in the evening and found the street packed with people sitting on small stools, enjoying beers and street food in a very informal setting. It gets loud and crowded, and vendors can be persistent, but this is all part of the experience. A lively place to stop by if you want to see a youthful, social side of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Berte Haul
reviews.title: Perfect pit stop by the night market 🍺
reviews.content: Plenty of seats at 6 p.m., packed by 7! Nearby vendors invite you in but don’t pressure—places fill up fast. Prices are fair, making it perfect for a bite and a beer, a stroll through the night market, and a relaxed drink on the way back.

reviews.author: Furchtlos und Treu
reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.content: I can only think of the following: typical Vietnam... go, order beer, sit and watch the hustle and bustle 😅 There is actually always something to see, you get used to the noise level

reviews.author: Umberto
reviews.title: Worst place we've eaten for 1000000 dong.
reviews.content: Worst place we've eaten for 1000000 dong. The food was just crap and not worth the price.  Attracted by the name, never again.

reviews.author: Lily
reviews.title: Backpacker buzz with heart
reviews.content: We hit Ta Hien Street for cheap eats, cold beers, and spontaneous laughs—and got all three in spades! The energy is infectious, the locals are friendly, and late-night banh mi runs became our group’s favorite ritual. Pure Hanoi chaos, and we loved it!

reviews.author: Song Mi-rae
reviews.title: Hanoi Old Town
reviews.content: In the northern and vibrant city of Hanoi, you must walk through the old streets or by cycling. Through narrow, maze-like alleys, shops and the everyday lives of locals who have preserved hundreds of years of history, you can feel the true charm of the city. Especially in the morning sun or in the evening noise, you'll get deeper into the unique atmosphere of Hanoi.

reviews.author: 李强
reviews.title: A beer, a bunch of friends, an "international street."
reviews.content: Towers Street is a backpacker's paradise! We sat on plastic benches in the evening, drinking ice beer for 20k Vietnamese dong per capita, and watching tourists from all over the world talk and laugh. The street kebabs aroma, the music swirling, lively but not noisy. Laughing late into the night with your friends in the evening wind - that's what travel looks like!

reviews.author: raybrahms1964
reviews.title: Beer Street party section a total abomination!!!
reviews.content: We first visited Hanoi 12 years ago and absolutely loved the place. We are back here at the moment and this review is solely for the god awful section of beer street that is absolutely horrendous. It's like running a gauntlet with elderly men watching girls dancing on tables wearing next to nothing while you are harassed by boys shoving menus in your face trying to drag you into their bar. I don't know what the hell the authorities were thinking of when they gave their approval to this section of the street. It is an absolute abomination  and has no place in Hanoi. Whoever is responsible for allowing this should hang their heads in shame. If Hanoi continues in this direction and decends into a place akin to Pattaya on acid then we will not return. If the authorities read any reviews on TA like this then they need to sit up and take notice as they are overseeing a transformation that has absolutely no place in beautiful Hanoi!!!

reviews.author: Cordy
reviews.title: A chaotic & fun date night!
reviews.content: We grabbed tiny plastic stools, ice-cold Bia Hoi, and just people-watched for hours. It's loud, energetic, and incredibly fun. The perfect place to laughing 😂

reviews.author: Nicolette Torso
reviews.title: Chaotic, fun, and unforgettable!
reviews.content: We dove headfirst into the madness of Ta Hien! Sitting on tiny plastic stools, drinking cheap local beer, and soaking up the insane energy was a highlight of our trip. It's loud and crowded :))))

reviews.author: Nona D
reviews.title: Wild and fun nights
reviews.content: Ta Hien Street is an absolute must-visit for a fun-loving couple! The energy is electric. We squeezed onto tiny stools, drank cheap, fresh beer, and just soaked in the chaotic, bustling vibe. It’s loud and crowded, but it was one of the most memorable nights of our trip. A truly unique Hanoi experience.

reviews.author: MMA Hà Đông
reviews.title: Enjoy night life in Hanoi
reviews.content: Great place to enjoy Hanoi nightlife, there are many private and open bars, especially lively on weekends with walking street with affordable prices and lots of activities. The downside is that it is not for people who like to go to bed early or are allergic to alcoholic drinks

reviews.author: Paul P
reviews.title: Get ready to be pestered
reviews.content: Noisy and annoying. But I guess you have to experience it if you're in this part of the world!!!Beer is cheaper than UK obviously but slightly pricier than other places nearby.

reviews.author: corinne_prevost
reviews.title: THE HOT NEIGHBOURHOOD OF HANOI
reviews.content: We didn't know where the warm neighborhood was we found it while walking. Beers galore + girls + rabateurs. The winning trio on this street. You have to eat, drink and more so affinities.

reviews.author: akio9jp
reviews.title: Nekki Munmun
reviews.content: It is a drinking district in the heart of Hanoi's Old Quarter, with shops, clubs and bars serving alcohol on both sides of the street, just 200 meters long. There's a lot of pop music going on and it's a Fever. I had the impression that there were more Western tourists than locals. It's for energetic young people, and the over-recent father doesn't feel good.

reviews.author: 지후 한
reviews.title: Perfect combination of authenticity and vibrant atmosphere
reviews.content: With our friends, we visited Hanoi's Ta'an Street and it was an unforgettable experience! This place is filled with authentic local atmosphere, and the energy of the lively streets in particular captivated us. Drinking local beer and enjoying the bullshit of the street was a really special experience. It was the perfect place to enjoy a variety of foods and drinks and to spend time with friends and friends. Ta'in Street is a place where you can feel the true charm of Hanoi, and I would definitely like to find it again!

reviews.author: Kent
reviews.title: Street beer so fun
reviews.content: I come here on weekend one time per month with my friends. 9 life for all guys, street beer, street food, street music - The vibrant is so fun. I love it all :))

reviews.author: Willy Sims
reviews.title: Cheers to colorful nights
reviews.content: This vibrant beer street buzzed with life, and we couldn't resist the delicious street food wafting through the air. We sipped cold beers while soaking in the colorful atmosphere, surrounded by laughter and chatter. Each corner offered something new, from mouthwatering snacks to friendly locals eager to share stories. It felt like a celebration every night!

reviews.author: Maddie T
reviews.title: friendly locals and lively beer streets
reviews.content: The street is a lively place, full of tourists and friendly locals. We tasted a variety of delicious beers in the small bar and the atmosphere was relaxed and pleasant. Although it is somewhat touristy, it is this enthusiasm that gives us a sense of Hanoi's unique charm. The night's lights and laughter were intertwined as if time had stood still. If you come to Hanoi, don't miss this vibrant beer street!

reviews.author: Giorgio
reviews.title: Lovely Nights in Ta Hien
reviews.content: Traditional architecture took us back to the past, and the lively Cheap Beer Street was perfect for relaxing with budget beers. The lights and vibrant atmosphere made our visit an unforgettable experience in Hanoi. We'll definitely be back!

reviews.author: Mamie F
reviews.title: Harnoy's Taching Street expedition.
reviews.content: The atmosphere is great, the bars and stalls are full of lively crowds. As a famous beer street, it feels great to have friends drinking beer together! The locals are also friendly and helpful, making us feel warm. Still, the streets are a little crowded, and sometimes it's hard to find a quiet place to rest. Overall, this is a place to experience!

reviews.author: Amara B
reviews.title: Amazingly
reviews.content: A bustling, bustling place in the heart of the old town. There are so many diverse colors in this place. My sister loves dancing to music with bottles of beer at roadside stalls

reviews.author: 周星
reviews.title: The usual experience of lively nightlife
reviews.content: The small bars and stalls down the street offer authentic food and drinks that do give us a hint of the authentic Vietnamese touch. However, the number of tourists makes it difficult to find a quiet corner to enjoy this uniqueness. Although we tasted several local drinks, it wasn't particularly stunning. Overall, it's a great place for tourists who want to feel the nightlife, but don't expect too much.

reviews.author: Jaymee Elf
reviews.title: A night of flavor and fun
reviews.content: We dived into the lively atmosphere, sampling delicious street food and sipping local beer. The vibrant energy was contagious as we mingled with fellow travelers. Laughing and enjoying each bite together made for an unforgettable night filled with flavors and memories we’ll cherish!

reviews.author: Germaine Kope
reviews.title: The heart of hanoi's nightlife scene
reviews.content: Ta Hien Street, aptly nicknamed "Beer Street," offers an electric atmosphere after sunset. We loved sitting on tiny plastic stools, enjoying fresh beer and watching the world go by. The mix of locals and travelers created such a vibrant vibe. It's chaotic and crowded, but that's part of its charm. A must-visit for experiencing Hanoi's authentic nightlife.

reviews.author: Dot P
reviews.title: The vibrant nightlife
reviews.content: The laughter of locals and fellow travelers filled the air, creating an inviting atmosphere. We shared stories with friendly vendors, discovering hidden gems amidst the chaos. It was the perfect blend of culture and fun.

reviews.author: Adriana
reviews.title: Hanoi's Beer Corner
reviews.content: This bustling beer corner came alive at night with endless rows of tiny plastic stools filled with locals and tourists alike. Sipping fresh beer while people-watching and sampling street food made for an authentic Hanoi experience. The energy here is simply contagious!

reviews.author: Blondell C
reviews.title: La Rue de la Bière
reviews.content: Sitting on our little stools, we shared bia hoi with the locals. The atmosphere is electric, especially in the evening. One tip: try street skewers, they are divine with cold beer!

reviews.author: ouchene
reviews.title: The Pulsating Heart of Hanoi’s Beer Culture! 🍺
reviews.content: Wow, what an unforgettable evening on Ta Hien Street! This historic alley in the heart of the old quarter has totally thrilled us. The famous Bia Hoi tastes fantastic here, especially when sitting on the typical small plastic chairs. The atmosphere is electrifying - everywhere cheerful people enjoying life! The mix of tradition and modern nightlife is unique. An absolute must for any Hanoi visitor!

reviews.author: Sue V
reviews.title: Load and chaotic
reviews.content: This place is an assault on the senses. Load music and lights emanating from every venue. Street vendors hassling and hawkers trying to get you in to every bar. Not for the faint hearted.

reviews.author: Krisha
reviews.title: Vibrant nightlife
reviews.content: We were swept up in the lively atmosphere of this iconic Hanoi destination.  Inexpensive local beers flowed freely, making it easy to mingle with fellow travelers and soak in the electric ambiance.  The street food stalls lining Ta Hien offered a tempting array of affordable eats, perfect for fueling a night of revelry.

reviews.author: Explore37315798840
reviews.title: Horrible experience
reviews.content: We visited a few places like this in Southeast Asia (Siem Reap, Phnom Penh, Saigon) and enjoyed the atmosphere, but this one is very disappointing and vulgar. The cacophony generated by the loudspeakers of the multitude of small bars competing as well as the flappers of the latter (which are more harassing than inviting) pushed us to cross it as quickly as possible and go have fun elsewhere. In addition, we were repeatedly asked what we were looking for by putting videos of young girls undressing under our noses. This is a shame because it projects a negative image of the city.

reviews.author: Shtarker
reviews.title: Sheer Craziness
reviews.content: Visited "beer street" in Hanoi's old quarter on a Saturday night.Although we have watched it on YouTube, the crowed, loud technology music & every second vendor trying to drag you into their bar or restaurant was something that we are totally unprepared for.  Finally we sat down at Coco Bar for a drink, seems to have less people around that area, but still have to constantly fighting off street vendors trying to sell items to us, one of them was a kid looked under 10 yrs old selling cigarettes.Definitely not our cup of tea!

reviews.author: Crumpled Nomad | Travel Intelligence
reviews.title: Busy busy busy street on a Saturday night
reviews.content: A famous street in Hanoi where one can find many pubs, bars and drinking holes along the street. They even sat on the road with low chairs sipping ice cold beers. It was extremely busy and packed on a Saturday night and as I walked along, I was constantly bombarded with people touting. I found this rather unpleasant and tried to walk as fast as possible. It’s just not something for me but it’s strictly my opinion. I’m sure many will find this place interesting. For someone who’s not into drinking and loud music, this may not be the place for you. But I enjoyed walking along it, just once to soak in the bustling atmosphere.

reviews.author: Sshuddho G
reviews.title: A diff experience..
reviews.content: ..cold and fresh draught beer sitting on small street side chairs after a long day of touring can be quite therapeutic..cheers

reviews.author: BrakiWorldTraveler
reviews.title: Pattaya style party area
reviews.content: This street is commonly known as Hanoi Beer street and is set in the northern part of Old Quarter. It comes alive at night with dozens of cafes, night clubs, eateries, massage parlors, etc....much reminding on such in Pattaya or Phuket.Music is very loud, coming from every, tiny and small club one by another, so while walking you hear only unrecognizable mixed music noise. We just walked through without any desire to sit somewhere, even our teenage daughter didn't like it.

reviews.author: Departure48409439286
reviews.title: A wonderful experience at Hoang restaurant
reviews.content: The restaurant serves delicious food, super delicious food, friendly and enthusiastic staff. Daisy was the one who took care of my table, she was very kind and friendly. Will recommend the restaurant to many of my friends and will come back again and again

reviews.author: PW14513
reviews.title: chill chill
reviews.content: Busy street and ideal place to hang out with my friends. There were a lot of souvenirs shops and restaurants surrounding

reviews.author: Rutland Auckland
reviews.title: Not worth the effort to go to - it’s just hyped up
reviews.content: Sorry not for us. A tourist trap. Overpriced. Underwhelming. It reminded us of Magaluf or some other seedy European nightlife.Save your money and go to any of the myriad of better places

reviews.author: Mobile40517000222
reviews.title: Bia street for travelers
reviews.content: Such an interesting place for gathering and chilling with friends. Good for Hanoian and travelers to enjoy the bia hoi

reviews.author: HIROYUKI SHIMIZU
reviews.title: Extraordinary
reviews.content: I went there on a Friday and it was crowded with tourists and locals. Cars and motorbikes were passing by nearby so we had to sit and drink on the edge of the seats, music was blaring, people from all over the world, vendors... it was chaos. If you want to feel the power and heat of Asia, this is the place to go.

reviews.author: Siddeeque Hassan
reviews.title: Beer + Positivity = Ta Hian
reviews.content: Ta Hien Corner is also known as The Beer Street, is a great food street. The weekends in Ta Hien is so much positive vibe and positivity. A great place of weekend hangout for both tourists and natives. A must visit place for sure.

reviews.author: Scott W
reviews.title: Beer Street
reviews.content: This place is amazing, bars everywhere and the sights and sounds are an assault on your senses. A great place to go for a drink with lots of 'happy hour' offers.

reviews.author: Vthc4
reviews.title: Great atmosphere
reviews.content: We went on a Thursday evening and it was bustling - a total change of the street in the day. Great atmosphere with loud music with many diners seated on both sides of the street.

reviews.author: SK
reviews.title: Nice area to visit for the nighttime
reviews.content: One of the must-go, it is crowded and fun. Just remember to not drink too much and make sure you always check prices.

reviews.author: Jacky29292
reviews.title: Nice place but very crowdes
reviews.content: Njce place for drink beer and have some food. The price ia a bit expensive. It is very crowded but fun to go there

reviews.author: The Baobab Republic
reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.content: One of the places you must visit when coming to Hanoi is the old quarter of Ta Hien.  Here is famous for the shops selling food, drinks, bars and many specialties of Hanoi.  And there are many delicious dishes.  And Banh Mi Co Nga is one of the dishes that you should try.  A little pate, sausage, chicken eggs are stir-fried in a pan with a little fat.  Add a little soy sauce and chili, serve with bread.  A great experience in the old town.

reviews.author: alebeth
reviews.title: It’s a no from me
reviews.content: Also known as beer street. This place is crazy busy and reminds me of Bangla Rd, Thailand. I really disliked this place and didn’t enjoy it. Maybe better suited to a younger crowd who wants to get on the drink and balloons.

reviews.author: EdM
reviews.title: Everything is happening
reviews.content: A great spot to have a beer and watch the action. We found the junction was better than the bars higher up the street. And cheaper

reviews.author: Pulkit C
reviews.title: Crazy party street, unlike seen anywhere else!
reviews.content: Oh what a street. Extremely crowded, beer revellers filling on the street sitting on small benches. What a vibe! Must visit if you love beer or not. The place to party in Hanoi. Street was alive till midnight on a weekday. Locals as well tourists flocked onto the small drinking joints lining the street, my top rated place in Hanoi for night life!

reviews.author: Rob Nesbit
reviews.title: The place to be on a Saturday night
reviews.content: The place to be on a Saturday night in Hanoi. Might be an idea to let the crowds dissipate after a few hours and wait in a bar, then the fun can begin as the adult-kids go home..........

reviews.author: G2Kpauly
reviews.title: Cool street
reviews.content: A popular street in Hanoi to walk down, chill and eat and drink if you want.  It gets more busy on weekends and you will get hustled by every bar restaurant as you walk down. It's pretty narrow too.

reviews.author: MinT
reviews.title: Great place!
reviews.content: Perfect place to drink and enjoy the crowded people go passing by you on the street. The beer, the street foods, everything from here was great.

reviews.author: alexander
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: The place to be if you want to party in Ha Noi! By night it is a “walking street”  but given so many scooters and the occasional taxi I wouldn’t exactly say it’s a walking street haha. Music can be very loud - but there are strategic spots along the street where you can still have a conversation

reviews.author: Lorraine v
reviews.title: 10k beer nearly gone
reviews.content: 10 k beer is still available but only at few limited places. Most of busy street paying tourist prices for bottled beer. Busy and interesting but probably lot better places to eat. Loud techno and cigarette smoke if you like that.

reviews.author: Michael A
reviews.title: Ta Hien Street , the place to be if I’m Hanoi
reviews.content: Thế street that has incredible numbers and types of food eateries , bars , pubs , gift shops and even boutique hotels . Prices of items sold are value for money , good numbers of service staffs in the Outlets do speak English . Carnival like atmosphere after 6.30 pm right up to mid nite almost daily .

reviews.author: Ashwin V
reviews.title: Fun and eventful
reviews.content: Worth doing just for the experience. Sit outside on the little stools, cook your own food and enjoy the atmosphere.Food is ordinary in pretty much all the establishments but who cares. Wait for the local police to come and clear the street and move you indoors..............give it a few minutes and you're sitting back outside again.

reviews.author: Rajesh Kumar
reviews.title: The best place for night life
reviews.content: Food here was amazing, i loved the way they  provided a  can of margarine for each table. Each pan had aluminum foil to grill your food and they will change once it get burned. Infact when it was served my son looked at me with a question mark that are we here to cook or to eat. But I must confess it was amazing especially with such a happening street and lovely environment.  While planning for Ta Hien you should come a little early and see the Lake area and take stroll to Ta Hien.

reviews.author: burygirlkeeper
reviews.title: Beer street! Lots of bars and cheap meals
reviews.content: We have eaten here twice and had a lot of drinks. Average price for local bottled beer is 30k no need to pay more. Main courses are 70-150k, vegetarian stuff available. Whether you want a quiet chat or to Rave, you will find something fun.

reviews.author: epruuu
reviews.title: Vibrant
reviews.content: This is one of the most vibrant places for night life in Hanoi. There are many pubs with their own craft beers. It is extremely crowded. I suggest to visit this area at weekend from Friday evening. Because it is close to the traffic.

reviews.author: digitalroc
reviews.title: A cool experience
reviews.content: Every large Asian city that I have been too has something similar to this, and Ta Hien Street (Beer Street) in Hanoi is no different.  Even though the area was packed, it was still a unique experience walking down the street with all the chaos around.  This place is worth the effort to get to for a drink, enjoy some nightlife, or just walking the street while you are in the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Amit M
reviews.title: Beer
reviews.content: This street is narrow, no vehicles allowed and has bars and pubs for beer. Its throbbing and full of laughter and music. A lovly place to hang out and have beer and the loal dishes served with a smile. Look out for promotions.  $ 25 is good enough to drink enough beer and eat huge amounts of food.One beeer is $ 1.30. Must visit post 9 pm

reviews.author: jack M
reviews.title: UNIQUE PLACE
reviews.content: Should have been here in my youth.  Too late now.  In this small street one can find all to please your lascivious lifestyle's loves. Food, beer (LOTS of beer), women, and etc.,etc.Most happening outside as one inches his (her) way up the street (tourists and locals). Boy, to be young again.

reviews.author: Steve_of_N21
reviews.title: Ta Hein Beer Street
reviews.content: Its small and crowded, being only 200 meters long but on the street of Ta Hien there are many bars where you can find variety of Hanoi street foods such as Nem chua, Vietnamese bread and noodles alongside a wider variety of beer that you find in Vietnamese restaurants. Most drinking is done outside on the plastic tables and chairs and although the locals get on fine with the small plastic chairs I struggled to sit on them for any great period of time.

reviews.author: E R
reviews.title: Unique experience that is more than just food.
reviews.content: Restaurant after restaurant offer wonderful food to locals and tourists, sitting in the street on small chairs. Then at a moment the waitresses call loudly police, police and wrap in few seconds all the tables, with the food and with the small burning stove, with which they heat their soup or make barbeque. All the tourists make fun of the police, taking pictures of them.

reviews.author: chiangmaicharlies
reviews.title: Good and Bad here
reviews.content: Ta Hien Street is great for people watching and taking photos. You can be sure to get a meal or drink here.On the bad side, it's often frantically busy, with motorcycles winding their way through - and LOTS of people. The food is mostly 'tourist food' (chips, pizzas, burgers, etc) and not much (if any) authentic Vietnamese food. People are often rude and pushy here.Mainly for youngsters looking for a laugh and experience.

reviews.author: Abdur Rahman
reviews.title: Hip Hop... Vietnamese traditional stret foods with ice cold beer.
reviews.content: This is the best street for enjoying the complete nightlife of Hanoi. You will find all kinds of Vietnamese traditional street food with ice cold beer.

reviews.author: edenxo1212
reviews.title: Ta Hien Street
reviews.content: YO! Perfect place to grab yourself a drink and enjoy the crowded people go passing by you on the street. The drink, the side dishes, everything from here was great to me

reviews.author: Srishti Srivastav-Ghate
reviews.title: Loved it!
reviews.content: It's crazy...its chaotic....there are loads of people....loads of two-wheelers...bars all over with outdoor seating on little plastic stools...but its quite an experience.  I would highly recommend grabbing an outdoor seat in one of the numerous bars to just observe and absorb everything.  This spot should not be missed in Hanoi.

reviews.author: vickizig
reviews.title: Yuck
reviews.content: Pretty gross little street, really.  You can't get through without being jumped on by hundreds of shills for the restaurants, trying to get you to stop.  Yucky food.  Overpriced.  Not really a comfortable experience even just walking down the street.  There are so many other fun areas of the Old Quarter - explore the rest and skip this tourist trap.

reviews.author: Annie Hoang
reviews.title: Very crownded with pub and beer
reviews.content: Very crownded with pub and beer. You wanna a place to enjoy Hanoi night life,come here and try some fresh beer, it make your life more beautiful

reviews.author: Samuel Piette
reviews.title: Ta Hien Street
reviews.content: The best street restaurant in Hanoi. A perfect places where you can come and enjoy for the atmosphere as well as the food and the drinks

reviews.author: Yevonne
reviews.title: Good place for dinner
reviews.content: Came to this place randomly when walking around on the streets. My family and I had dinner here in one of the BBQ restaurant. The food is great and price is reasonable. What surprised us is that the shop owners have to keep away the tables and chairs by the roadside when police patrolling, that's really an interesting experience for us

reviews.author: Frogtwo
reviews.title: A meal in Ta Hien Street
reviews.content: This street is extremely crowded, one is constantly harrassed by young men wanting you to tke a meal in the restaurant they work for. At the end the meal, a bun cha, was below average. Grab riders work for prostitutes.

reviews.author: True Vietnam - Gorgeous Local Experience
reviews.title: great place for drinks
reviews.content: It is a hectic street in Old quarter of Hanoi. There is a ton of beer restaurants surrounding this area. Travelers call it as an international square (Ta hien crosses Luong Ngoc Quyen) because it is where the global residents gather. Draft beer is one of the most famous drinks in this place. The price of one cup of beer is cheap (around 5-10,000 VND)

reviews.author: DerriQ
reviews.title: People watching
reviews.content: We came here last Sunday night after the night market.  It was crazy busy and you have to experience it to believe it! I just couldn't believe how many people there were. Its great people watching.  We found a restaurant with a balcony so sat up there and looked down watching the other restaurants trying to get people to stop and eat there. It was funny to watch.  After a bite to eat we moved on to a bar on the street and sat people watching for a while.  We even saw a whole family of bananas (the fruit printed clothing you see at the markets) walk on by which was a funny site and great photo opportunity!

reviews.author: Francis B
reviews.title: 5 Ta Hien
reviews.content: 5 Ta Hien Street is the best street restaurant in this area. Amazing BBQ set up. I have been to this restaurant several times and it has never disappointed me. If you are looking for non-bar non-club street dining experience 5 Ta Hien offers an authentic experience with very attentive service.

reviews.author: Lana H
reviews.title: Not what I was expecting
reviews.content: Atmosphere and buzz of being amongst so many people great but, to be swamped by bar workers to go into their bar was overwhelming. Even when we sat down they tried ordering our beer and food for us! Food and drink, overpriced. Great for people watching and photos but I would not recommend this place.

reviews.author: Anonymous Traveller
reviews.title: Go for Atmosphere - Not food or beer!
reviews.content: We were excited to visit ‘Beer Street’ in Hanoi after some good reviews, it was incredibly busy - which was fine and produced a good atmosphere. However, the food was terrible from 2 different outlets we tried and it all appeared to come from the same kitchen anyway. The beer was not cheap and the whole situation was very rushed and uncomfortable. I’d recommend walking through beer street to sample the atmosphere and then moving on to a nicer restaurant where the beer would be actually be cheaper. If restaurants aren’t your thing and you want street food - there are better places to get much better street food than beer street.

reviews.author: Sajjad
reviews.title: Night Life of Hanoi
reviews.content: It's a great experience to spend quality time with my buddies in the old quarter of Hanoi. All foreigners spend a great time with their like minded buddies with Hanoi beer and snacks.

reviews.author: Tania W
reviews.title: Gotta go!
reviews.content: This street at night on the weekends becomes a market. It is a must do in Hanoi! The usual stuff for sale but just a cool vibe.

reviews.author: Epic-Traveller
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: You get street food all over South East Asia and you can get street beer in beer street.D7,000 for half a pint of Tiger is absolutely pennies. Just outside the Hogaarden Pub a lady sits there with a keg selling 7k beers.

reviews.author: garybush
reviews.title: It’s Ok For A Couple of Beers
reviews.content: We visited Ta Hien Beer St mid afternoon, it wasn’t very busy so the bar’s hawkers were busy trying to get your business. At the end of the day it’s a lane way with a bunch of bars and small restaurants, with several of the bars serving their own home brew, straight from the keg. The beers were 10,000 Dong ($0.60 AUD). The beer was refreshing given the heat of the afternoon. Most of the bars are staffed by young men who can be a touch over the top of passers by,,trying to lure them into their bar.We didn’t try any food, but what we saw come out appeared to be standard local fare.It’s worth a visit when in the Old Quarter, and I’m sure that it gets busy at night and would have a great atmosphere.

reviews.author: Lee C
reviews.title: Heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: Ta Hien is also known / described as food street or beer street and it lives up to its names. During the day the streets are quite quiet but once dark the streets come alive with the copious amount of bars and Small local restaurants. The restaurants may seem grubby and that’s because they are but you will notice they won’t be shy of locals, so give the food a chance and you will be pleasantly surprised.As for the bars the prices are competitive - not cheap but not expensive either. It’s a must see and should be on everyone’s list when visiting Hanoi.

reviews.author: heeminjeong
reviews.title: beer guysss
reviews.content: I love beer and I decided to go here for Vietnamese beer experience. Saigonbeer is so good here for my last night in Hanoi

reviews.author: Joe
reviews.title: crowded area full of people drinking beers
reviews.content: the whole place is overcrowded. too many workers trying to persuade you to have dinner or drink beer in their restaurant which is a bit annoying.  but a great place to experience that kind of atmosphere.  seriously there are just too many bistro, restaurant here that i try to avoid the promoters, at the end i just went into pasteur street brewing co again.  by the time i finished my drink, there are people fighting on the street, and 2 drunk guy push me to the wall and demand me to drink with them.  well, manage to struggle out of their grab and leave the place at once.   chaotic place i would say

reviews.author: Meo Beibi
reviews.title: Would you like to have beutiful nails??
reviews.content: I highly recommend the little shop in Ta Hien street (the best corner for someone that love hanging out at night). Reasonable priceHigh-quality materialsBeautiful young owner

reviews.author: winter
reviews.title: Very busy and crowded local and foreigners
reviews.content: Packed with local and tourist every night, here offers cheap beer and food. Cool to hang out and get drunk with friends, but only if you are a party person. Lots of sellers try to sell fruits and donuts, snacks...can be pushy sometimes

reviews.author: Anas A
reviews.title: Overcrowded
reviews.content: We were recommended to go to this street by our hotel receptionist after we asked about good street food places. It turned out it is packed with tourists and party music. It is not what we were looking for in Vietnam. We wanted to experience it the locals way. After spending a few minutes walking around in the street, we decided to go around in the Old Quarter away from this street and explore it ourselves. We ended up eating a very delicious dish from a local street food store.

reviews.author: Tambonz
reviews.title: Busy
reviews.content: Great street if you're intae cities. Lots of shops to look at and things tae buy.Keep bargaining... Not too much... Just enough so that you're both happy!!!

reviews.author: Betty t
reviews.title: Interesting street in Old Hanoi
reviews.content: My introduction to this street was based on my Walking Tour Guide telling me that this is one of the most popular streets in Hanoi. I saw a lot of small restaurants and small shops in this street. There was even a smart couple taking their wedding photos in the street.It is one of the most visited areas in Old Hanoi.

reviews.author: ZBH88
reviews.title: Awesome and packed
reviews.content: All you would ever want from a party street. Plentiful food of all tastes and palates. Lots of places to drink also. A great place for both tourists and locals especially at the weekends when everyone seems to come out.

reviews.author: David H
reviews.title: Crazy, fun street
reviews.content: Went along to have a look and a few beers. The atmosphere is crazy. Found a bar 3/4 the way up with bar stools instead of tiny little plastic stools. Watched the passing walking traffic and the many motorbikes squeezing through. Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Emily Levert
reviews.title: Must come if you r in Hanoi
reviews.content: Small crazy busy street located in Old Quater where you can enjoy great local food, drink beer and take funny ballons on the STREET (a very special of Hanoian style) There are many bars with reasonable price where u can hangout after meal.

reviews.author: Shane Long
reviews.title: Amazing place to hang out in the evening
reviews.content: I came here with my wife and we love it so much.The street is decorated so beautiful, people are all cheering and having fun.It's maybe a little bit loud and crowded for some people but for us, we really enjoy the vibe of Ta Hien street.

reviews.author: Jalal Iqbal
reviews.title: bright and colourful street
reviews.content: i loved the street and the vibe there.  very bright and colorful. lots of colorful shops and at night a festive look.  crowded and full of local and tourists. a bit loud and many bars and cafes around.

reviews.author: Keshav Khushalani
reviews.title: Night Out
reviews.content: Wow Superb street which is full of fun. Street is full crowd with people ready to fun. Street and near by location are famous for local food. The above place is one of the destination for shopping. Also, pubs and cafes of Ta Hien street are famous.

reviews.author: FYL003
reviews.title: Beer street
reviews.content: Chaotic, crowded, totally packed with tourists for  cheap beer. Vendors trying to pull you into their establishments for beer and food were quite annoying.Go if you are interested in cheap beer or to experience the atmosphere. Avoid if you want good Vietnamese food. Definitely stay away when travel with small children, too crowded to be safe.

reviews.author: JnVSydney
reviews.title: Loud... crowded and pushy vendors
reviews.content: We first walked through during the day quite a calm atmosphere, minimal scooters, however it was peak time for deliveries, came back at night to see what the fuss is about.We found it to be louder than else where, (and believe me that is loud), incredibly crowded with visitors, and vey pushy spruikers, we made it to the end in one piece, and from then on we hung out in the quieter end of old town (if there is such a thing), South of Cửa Ô Quan Chưởng (Hanoi Old City Gate) around Phố Mã Mây, (street), the food is cheaper, as well as the beer, if you are adventurous there are beer vendors on the street, with a keg and a few seats selling a glass for 5.000vn (thats right about US$0.22) See review of old quarter, for more info.

reviews.author: Ирина И
reviews.title: Local food and atmosphere
reviews.content: Try hotpot from local food, drink cheep beer, buy souvenirs. People are so friendly.Easy to catch taxi from there

reviews.author: Geofrey Peterson
reviews.title: Fun fun fun!
reviews.content: Good food, good beer and good people. Fun thing to do to enjoy the local culture. I met many nice Vietnamese here to eat and drink together. And who doesn't want to sit on the little chairs in the street?

reviews.author: Ray M
reviews.title: Chaos but fun
reviews.content: Street vendors take over the streets with tables and chairs. Very busy with foot traffic and the occasional motorcycle. This is until the police come! With calls of “Police” the vendors quickly pack up tables and chairs and stand aside while the police pass by. This happened three times during our dinner. Humorous but a little irritating. The food is good and cheap and the atmosphere somewhat charged. Some menu items leave you scratching your head. Be prepared to move about.

reviews.author: KazFitz
reviews.title: A great place to sit and watch the world go by and the antics of some of the staff
reviews.content: A lively bustling street with multiple drink & food options. Everyone (locals and tourists) very friendly and out to enjoy life. Vendors will attempt to meet your every need. The Police beats were a giggle, clockwork precision in removing and replacing everything on the street.

reviews.author: Sightseer640515
reviews.title: give it a miss.
reviews.content: Altered drinks and synthetic weed are known to be used after hours or during lock in.Foriegners are seen as opportunity for theft.Fine for an afternoon experience  beware of Tet and Tom bars operators.

reviews.author: carloscharmy
reviews.title: Beer street
reviews.content: Crowds of people drinking along the street. If that's your thing, you'll defo enjoy it! This is where the nightlife happens

reviews.author: 814karinar
reviews.title: Lively Atmosphere
reviews.content: Great place to go for some atmosphere. Had a meal and beer at Little Hoi An, we shared the chilli chicken meal, was nice. Then walked further down and had a meal at the Noodle Place. A beef dish, not enough beef, had with a beer. Atmosphere was loud and humming. All the Vietnamese try encourage you into their place to eat. Then we went and chilled out on the MK Rooftop Bar on the couches and had cocktails with Chris and Abby who we met up there. Fabulous night.

reviews.author: ducpham27
reviews.title: International corner in Vietnam
reviews.content: So crowded on weekends, so many people, locals and foreigners, want to enjoy the dynamic, boisterous atmosphere

reviews.author: BLT
reviews.title: Lively street with some great pubs!
reviews.content: This street also called the "Beer Street" comes to life around 5pm in the evening and is a great place to chill and have fun. Many good restaurants around here most of which have a happy hour in the evenings.

reviews.author: 19106secret
reviews.title: Busy street
reviews.content: We came here at night, and it was crowded with both local and foreigners. We took some street food, beer, it was nice. And then walking around here and see something. Good experience.

reviews.author: John v
reviews.title: Po Ta Hien/ Ta Hien street/ Beer street
reviews.content: Pho Ta Hien/ Ta Hien street/ Beer street comes to live about 17pm. In the morning you can have  western and Vietnamese breakfast. You can have luch and/or an early dinner. But  the real action starts about 17pm and lasts  until 00.00 and in the weekend even until later. On Saturday its very crowded. Even the surroundings street are very crowded.This narrow street is full of pubs and restaurants. It seems narrower when the big melting pot  of tourists and locals are packed together on the sidewalk. Sitting on the low stools and at the small low tables. It can get so busy that  there is only a very narrow lane to walk. Some people will/would say "not for me". But for me it was a really pleasant atmosphere. Sometimes the promotors can be very pushy. Even when you tell them firmly that you are not interested.This street has also clubs and danceclubs. Sometimes there are street performers.  According to a Vietnamese guy, this street is very expensive for vietnamese standards and the food is below average. He said that the exploiters are overcharging the tourist. He advised us never to pay with a credit card. Try to pay cash. Because they charge 10% bank fee. That is baloney and a rip off. Watch out for pic pockets.I would advise everyone to go this street in the evening. At least once. Dont forget to try the Bia Hoi. The local type of draft beer that is very popular in Vietnam

reviews.author: Toffee12
reviews.title: Great place to catch Soccer / BPL
reviews.content: I was looking for place to watch soccer on a weekend in Hanoi and what I found was irish pubs that are further off where i were.  Great to have chance across this place while looking for a Truc Bach - great local beer!  There are many pubs and foods there and when i was there at 7, it was barely crowded and when i leave at 11, it was so full in the streets that i could barely walk.Great atmosphere for a drink and food too!

reviews.author: Flying Dutchman
reviews.title: The heaven for street food and beer
reviews.content: Ta Hien Street ıs the meeting point of Hanoi in the evening. People from all social groups and nationalities, from torusits to locals gather around in this street full of beer bars and sit on the street on small chairs. The street turns into a night life festival and the party continues until the late hours of the night. The prices are cheap the food is tasty and the atmosphere is unique. If you want to geel the heart of Hanoi beating, this is the place you must go.

reviews.author: Kristina C
reviews.title: Lively and crowded
reviews.content: Ta Hien street is definitely worth checking out once when you're visiting Hanoi. During the day is not very crazy. But at night everything changes. It's lively and crowded.  The main part is located between Hang Bac Street and Hang Buom Street. There's a fun atmosphere. The bars pretty much only serve bottle beers and light eats (like French fries, peanuts, fried milk, meatball skewers, and other skewers). The crowd is a mix of locals and tourists sitting on low stools at low tables. There are more restaurants and a more western-style bars as you get closer to Hang Buom Street.

reviews.author: ChangBoris
reviews.title: Lively and inexpensive
reviews.content: This is a very lively street with many variety of eateries and clubs. Beers at the eateries starts from Vnd 25k. Very pleasant and cheap night out.

reviews.author: Beesy1950
reviews.title: Disappointing to return here
reviews.content: I guess it was too much to hope that this was still a great place to come for a drink and it was. Draught beer is no longer a feature just overpriced bottles for tourists. I prefer drinking Bia Hoi with locals but this is no longer the place to do that.

reviews.author: purplekitty2016
reviews.title: To do in Hanoi-Beer Street
reviews.content: Ta Hien Street is also known as the 'Beer Street'.  Right at the onset let me tell you it's crowded with foreigners from all over the world sitting outside having their local beer n food at reasonable price.  It essentially wakes up at night (after 6 pm) with what one can call a pub culture. It's fun to just sit outside having a drink, eating some Vietnamese food, listening to music being belted from the pubs, talking to strangers n watching the world go by. U can even shake a leg or two dancing away in one of the happening pubs. The street is narrow n is hardly very long but it is compact with people, pubs n eateries lined up on both sides. Sure to be tried for some fun on one of the nights while in Hanoi n like us might end up going for it for more than one night too 💃

reviews.author: Nguyễn T
reviews.title: Tourists should never ever come to this street
reviews.content: Everything is terrible. Please do not try any kind of food on this steetm full of instance and msg, it is not Vietnamese food that we are normally eat at home.My foreigner friends brought me to this road, and i felt so embarrassing because of what they were served. Felt very sorry for Vietnam with all selfish shops like this.You can consider go to Mon Hue, Cha Ca Thang Long, the gioi hai san,.. so many places to try. Why chose this street???? And beer? Be careful if you got poison!I will rate minus 100 point if i could!

reviews.author: Mayank Agarwal
reviews.title: Low End Pubs, Cafes n Bars
reviews.content: Ta Hien Street also called the beer street lies in the center of Old Quarter of Hanoi. It is the place to be past 6 pm. The street is just 200 meters long but it is one of the most crowded streets I have been to, filled with foreign as well as locals alike. Most people just sit on a small-sized plastic chair right on the street, having beer and food while people watching. There are great varieties of beer available and at reasonable prices. We were here for three nights, one-night having beer n people watching, another trying a Hot Pot and on a third night enjoying sitting in one of the better pubs.

reviews.author: Anil L
reviews.title: Beer Street
reviews.content: Ta Hien street is also called a beer street. The place is full of small beer and snack shops. You can sit on small stools on the road and enjoy a beer watching street performances. On every corner, you will find some performances like local dances, live band, dances etc going on. A beer costs around 1-1.5$. Very lively and happening place. Must visit.

reviews.author: DAVID L
reviews.title: Party and Beer Street ...
reviews.content: What it is in the evening is party and beer drinking street! Lots of locals But seemingly more tourists quaffing down beers and having a good time. Might be right for you?

reviews.author: Xerxes R
reviews.title: Must visit if you are around
reviews.content: There is a little something for everyone here. Food places are a dime a dozen. Shopping deals can be found as well. Small stalls where you can grab a beer drink it while you stroll through the street. Lively music pouring out from clubs even some restaurants. We had a good time hope you do too. Njy

reviews.author: Kristen S
reviews.title: high bank charge for credit card
reviews.content: We ate at Tom's Bar on Ta Hien Street in Hanoi and had a nice dinner. Then, when it came time to pay, and we had a MasterCard, they charged us 10% and said it was a bank fee. Many places do not charge any fee if it's not American Express, and if they do, it's max 3%.  It felt like a scam because they noticed we were foreigners, but by that point, we had eaten and were stuck needing to pay.  We asked our hotel as well, and they said they had never heard of a 10% fee for the bank.  We are very disappointed that this is the last experience we had in Vietnam before heading out of the country. I would avoid Tom's.

reviews.author: Benjamin C
reviews.title: Neat place, must visit at night
reviews.content: Gotta go when it's crazy; hustle and bustle you feel like you're in an ant hill. Cheap beer all over the place. Must experience it for 1 beer at least!

reviews.author: Ajarn Mark
reviews.title: Used to be a place to go
reviews.content: But it is too crowded now. Mostly people have moved from draft beer to bottled beer. It is difficult to walk on the street as it is all encroached by the vendors and restaurants. I did like to go there but it is no longer the case anymore.

reviews.author: Reslimpan
reviews.title: Busy, busy place
reviews.content: Ta Hien street a/k/a beer corner or bar street let you party like a local - Low chairs and table - don't drink too much or you won't be able to get up. Cheap beers and food. I probably wouldn't eat here for dinner but I would save room for some snacks. If Ta Hien as such feels to crowded - try one of the side streets.

reviews.author: huyenht
reviews.title: My favorite place forever
reviews.content: This place is suitable for a couple or the group of friends. The Bia Hoi is very cheap but not sure for quality so you should drink Sai Gon beer or Ha Noi beer in the can is better. They serve the good food here as well. It is nice to take a sit, drink beers and enjoy the local dancing or singing here. It is very kind of you to give some money for tge children or poor people here but should be careful as the others will try to scam you. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: NawtyStupot
reviews.title: CIGARETTE SMOKE. . YUK!
reviews.content: I hated this place. It was awful at night, crowded with western tourists sitting both inside & outside bars / street cafés on both sides of the street smoking.Walking through at night was simply awful & I found myself gasping for fresh air, yes the smoking was that bad!Now, I get that the Vietnamese smoke in cafés & bars because they always have & until the people running the businesses ban it & enforce the law (passed in Vietnam in 2010 banning smoking in public) then the Vietnamese will continue to smoke but what I don't get is the tourists all gathered together in their hundreds from UK / Europe etc (WHERE SMOKING IS NO LONGER ACCEPTABLE IN CAFÉS & BARS) that suddenly think its OK to do so? How does that work? I found it easy to stop the hawkers promoting their bar / café to me on Ta Hien by asking for a no smoking room! They simply turned around & ran to someone else. A heads up for anyone in Ha Noi old quarter wanting to eat / drink without suffering second hand smoke from people who only care about themselves & have no regard for others inside a bar / café suffering their second hand smoke, head over to GREEN FARM RESTAURANT just 2 streets away from Ta Hien & there you will find a restaurant that is smoke free inside & what a pleasure it is!

reviews.author: mmelllyyyy
reviews.title: Small Party Street
reviews.content: If you have been to Ho Chi Minh's Bui Vien Street or Siem Reap's Pub Street or even Bangkok's Khao San Road then you can compare this place with those places I've mentioned above but it's just too small. It's not as huge as those places. But surely, you can have a nice place to party or drink if you're after finding a nice nightlife. People are friendly in this place but of course you have to be careful of your belongings and you need to check out the price twice before ordering them. Ta Hien is walking distance from everything tho and it's usually crowded and packed by locals and tourist which makes it more lively. Go to this place past 8-9pm so you can fully appreciate it. But the sad thing is that, they stop selling drinks by 0100.

reviews.author: Duc Huynh
reviews.title: Different experience
reviews.content: It is such an interesting experience to sit on the pavement, drink beer and look at ppl walking around.Most annoying thing is sometimes the police come and destroy the environment.

reviews.author: nico m
reviews.title: Tour
reviews.content: Beautiful tour with a lot of fun and interesting things. The guide is very prepared and very good.Recommended to everyone.

reviews.author: Nunngo
reviews.title: The best place
reviews.content: The best place for a great look at and a chance to enjoy the night life in Hanoi.  We really enjoyed the entertainment, the local bar scene and dining.  It was awesome to sit and watch the local people having a great time out and about.  This street and several others adjoining attract all sorts, tourists, families, single people, couples and older people.  The Vietnamese know how to have a good time and the 'buzz' in this area is energising and overloading to the senses.

reviews.author: PacoGlasgow
reviews.title: Busy bar area after 9pm
reviews.content: This is a great area to hang out after 9pm, sit back in one of the local bars and watch the world go by. It gets busy so get there early enough to get a seat in one of the many bars. The area is safe and  has a good mix of people from all parts of the world. Great atmosphere the place is buzzing 7 days a week.

reviews.author: Granules2013
reviews.title: Great location for drinks and street food
reviews.content: Spend many hours each night strolling around the Old Quarter down this street looking for drinking spots and places to snack. Great range of bars and heaps of street food. Very lively and great atmosphere.

reviews.author: MaiAnh_Nguyen
reviews.title: Interesting & fun for the young soul!!
reviews.content: I've lived in Hanoi almost since I was born, knowing the development of the city with so many more people. My elementary school teacher used to live here that's why I've had the clear memory of the street 20 years ago. It was quiet, but still the Bia Hoi everywhere. Now the city authority has organized the walking streets, with lots more activities and so much noise, it gives the area new life. It is very interesting experience coming here, I think for both tourists and locals as me. I like the idea and hope that things will be well-organized by time.

reviews.author: thd007
reviews.title: vietnam cafes and street food
reviews.content: part of the old town and near beer corner as well, this is where the vietnam cafes and street food are. must experience the cheap food and drinks.

reviews.author: Michel C
reviews.title: The Street! in Hanoi
reviews.content: The most popular and one of the best example of street for its proposal for tasty north Vietnamese street food.Active quite late

reviews.author: AAS619
reviews.title: Part of Hanoi experience
reviews.content: Saturday night on Ta Hien Street is fun, even if you stay for a little while. It is crowded with tourists and locals alike. The streets are lined with tiny stools and everyone squats around equally small tables dining, drinking and socializing. We had dinner in one of the bars, (I can’t remember the name) stopped at a couple of other bars for drinks and watched the crowd, chitchatted with friendly Hanoian girls sitting next to us. Even if you are not a night owl or don’t like big crowds, hang out on Ta Hein, its nice. We didn’t see obnoxious drunks or any kind of fights. Positive vibes were all around.

reviews.author: Raymond C
reviews.title: lively
reviews.content: Lively place to sit, eat, drink and people gaze. Go for the places where locals sit, they are better value.Toms bar is to be avoided unless you like sitting on rickety stools and being overcharged for beer.

reviews.author: palawanismyhome
reviews.title: Wonderful restaurants where locals and tourists eat
reviews.content: Ta Hien Street is in the Old Quarter and is the place to go to enjoy some of the best food in Hanoi. Restaurants are to be found on each side of the narrow street and small tables with little stools are placed on the street, but you can always dine inside, and maybe this is better as the police come along every night and the restaurant staff remove the tables from the street. Diners are left holding their beer and plates and if they are lucky they will find a seat inside. There are perhaps 20 or more restaurants and while walking along the street restaurant staff shove the menu in your face and invite you to eat. We dined here on five different nights and never had a bad meal. Some of the restaurants are open at lunch time but not all. Could not tell you if they are open for breakfast. Some restaurants ave several different menus and sometimes they will provide you with a meal from another restaurant so they must have some type of agreement.

reviews.author: Marachi72
reviews.title: Fun, lively street - Avoid Tom's bar
reviews.content: I was here on a Friday and Saturday night with a friend. There was lots going on food and drink wise. Loads of Bia Hoi bars - you could grab food from the restaurants next door, perch yourself on a little plastic chair and make friends with your neighbors . There were a few higher end bars which were mainly Vietnamese.For comfort, there were loads of backpacker bar/restaurants with near identical styles and menus to the rest of SE Asia. It also has the most expensive bar in Hanoi - 'Tom's Bar'. I though they were joking when they brought the bill. Tom's hole, so it doesn't really have much of a case for having higher prices than the lakeside rooftops of the classic international hotels.The clubs looked great, but sadly I didn't make it in.

reviews.author: Ferguson M
reviews.title: Center of Hanoi old town center
reviews.content: This place is considered as the crossroads of the world, where convergence of many cultures of the world, so many tourists like this place, we had a good evening, beer here is very delicious, The sidewalk watching people busy, interestingIt is recommended to come in the evening, will be very crowded, suitable for young

reviews.author: Tri T
reviews.title: modern nightlife in old quarter
reviews.content: Like walking street in Bangkok with many bar and street beer shop. The space was quite crowded and small so that we took seats on the street. A good place to chill for both local and expat because staffs speak english so well and we can attend street performances around Hoan Kiem lake at the weekend.Nice place to see.

reviews.author: Lester_Ws
reviews.title: Exciting place for chatting with friends and the local
reviews.content: While walking around Hanoi old Quater, we found this site. The space was quite crowded and small so that we took seats on the street. We heard that Ta Hien street and some nearby streets were shut off to traffic at weekends' nights. We had a lot of fun there like cups of cool beer with some locals. They spoke English very well. They told us about street performances around Hoan Kiem lake at the weekend. Nice place to see.

reviews.author: Ann-Maree A
reviews.title: Great street but don't go to House of Beer
reviews.content: This is a great little street in Hanoi with loads of options however unfortunately we chose the wrong place to eat. After walking up and down for 10 minutes trying to decide we just made a decision after we got pestered to go into this place. The first sign it was going to be a bad meal was when about 2 minutes after I ordered my meal it was brought to me by someone who was also smoking a cigarette. (I am a smoker but come on) We ordered vegetarian spring rolls and they have to be the worst I have eaten and contained meat. Lucky I am not vegetarian. My beef noodle soup was oily and contained about 2 slices of beef and my husbands stir fry noodles were actual 2 minutes noodles thrown together with some tomatoes and chicken which was meant to be a stir fry. The best thing was the beer because it came from a bottle. We couldn't eat our meal and left hastily to head somewhere else after a few bites of our meals. Very disappointed !

reviews.author: Jacqui B
reviews.title: Ken's at number 5
reviews.content: We were walking down this amazing food street and needed a snack, we saw the Ken's was full of locals eating charred birds amongst other things. We were asked if we wanted to eat and a makeshift table for 5 was quickly organised. We ordered drinks while looking at the menu, we decided to try the BBQ option. I can only describe the cooking pot as a single camping ring that had liquid gel as the source of heat. A massive amount of raw meats were brought out, one of the guys showed us what to do and then left it to us. The experience was great and the food delicious. Service was the best. Make sure you eat here.

reviews.author: Beata Maria
reviews.title: eating street
reviews.content: the street fool of bars cafes street food and little resturants.the best to come here for lunch or dinner or just to try great Vietnamese cofffee.

reviews.author: Clairejop
reviews.title: Expensive at toms
reviews.content: We only visited one place down here called tom and jerry bar - v. Expensive for Vietnam and they only offered imported beer on their menu? None of the local beers. I think other places along this street would be cheaper. Fun to perch up on a stool outside one of the bars and watch the madness of the busy street. A lot of people hassle you to buy things - be aware!

reviews.author: Hannah Q
reviews.title: A Must see
reviews.content: A great bustling street for food and drinks - whether you are here to party or here to just enjoy a drink and something to eat, you should definitely visit this street.

reviews.author: Leo_T16
reviews.title: Crazy time but lots of fun
reviews.content: Having great time with my friend and colleague here in 23 Ta Hien. Try local beer and local fruit, especially Truc Bach for beer and Ma Thay (chest nut) for fruit.  Sitting for 4 hours but this place is always crowded and lots of fun.

reviews.author: Sharon M
reviews.title: Tom's Bar
reviews.content: Full of life and plenty backpacker wildness. However, best thing about this particular bar was the manager - jerry (as in Tom and?) Anyway, she runs the bar and street with great precision and attention both to detail and her clients. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Kevhusky610
reviews.title: Great place for a night
reviews.content: Great alley to spend a night. You must try the 5000 dong Beers very god for the price. The little barbecued birds half way up the alley are a other great treat don't be put off. Only time we got ripped of in 3 weeks in Vietnam  was at Tom and Jerry's bar towards the top end (Jerrys bar not the Tom side). Make sure you see the price list and do not go on what the girls tell you or the night may be expensive when you get the bill.Kev

reviews.author: worldiscoverer
reviews.title: Party place
reviews.content: Totally transforms in the evening especially weekend night market. Lotsa people sitting in small stools enjoying beer and hot pot.

reviews.author: tonyhD7219KV
reviews.title: International Corner
reviews.content: A great place for hanging out with friends, meeting new people all around the world, drinking and having fun at night. The International Corner is between Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen Street, famous with Green Pepper Hanoi !

reviews.author: irve2016
reviews.title: The happening place
reviews.content: During the day a shopping strip at night a lively place to be be, join the hundreds of people for a cheap beer or sample one of the many delicious restaurants.15 cent AUD for a beer you can't go wrong join the happy crowds sitting on the small stools on the street drinking a beer watching the world by what more could you ask for? I loved this place.

reviews.author: jeff1955malaysia
reviews.title: at night it beomes a food street
reviews.content: it is at the junction of hang Bo and Ta Hien. At night the whole street transform in a food galore. small tables and chairs and you can order the food all in the menu with pic. prices are a little high compared to other places. there are also a lot of bars along this street.

reviews.author: Roger S
reviews.title: Beer, food and people - what more to have a great evening
reviews.content: Two nights in Hanoi, two nights at Ta Hien Street. Only 200m from our hotel on Ma Mai. Full of life, noise, beer and street food. At the top end of the street (further away from Beer Corner) is Tom and Jerry's bar ( open on both sides of the road). The staff were brilliant - fun to talk to, attentive and great knowledge of local food. We were there in a tropical downpour - watching the staff carry on serving using umbrellas was a scream

reviews.author: Kevin Frank S
reviews.title: Incredible atmosphere that a street has
reviews.content: i had been to many streets in many cities, i was impressed by this street the most. it was so busy at night, at night the street was blocked up at the weekend for all kind of vehicle and only allowed walkers. And that was a chance for many locals restaurant and bars extended there business by putting out our the plastic stools and tables to serve people who wants to sit outside and the prices are very reasonable . I like this ideal, to sit outside was great you could see so much. There are some street vendors came up to you and ask you to buy  clothes, books, cigarettes,,,so if you do not want buy from them , you just need to say "no" with your friendly smile but decisive then they would leave you there with your own business. When you walk from the beginning to the end of the street you see bars, restaurants, hotels gift shops, coffee shop..... Here and there on this street you still could see many old french style houses were  among those local houses.

reviews.author: JasonNguyen24
reviews.title: Dont talk much about this, just come and see
reviews.content: Only 2 minutes from the Hoan Kiem Lake, u will easily find this street. They have many things here. good for seeing

reviews.author: colossalboards
reviews.title: It's all kinds a crazy - bar street
reviews.content: This places is nuts!!!!But you have to go, find a bar, get a cheap beer and watch the chaos unfold! Traffic, people, street sellers, noise!!! Just crazy busy, but we enjoyed it :)

reviews.author: Lee M
reviews.title: Ta Hien Street
reviews.content: A quiet place during the day, but a very busy place at night. Tons of bars with a lot of people (tourists and locals) drinking everywhere you look. Worth a visit, even if it's just for a beer or 2.

reviews.author: ngocdung93
reviews.title: Ta Hien Beer Street - Worthy to visit
reviews.content: Ta Hien Beer Street is mat. Thousands of people concentrate in the intersection and small lanes. They dance, jump and sing. They drink local beer and chit chat. A lot of local people and international tourists, sit on the plastic small chair, a chair becomes the table.It is fun and crazy

reviews.author: BallardBeaver
reviews.title: Crazy, Crazy Scene on Saturday Night
reviews.content: Ta Hien Street -- aka Beer Street -- is just an amazing evening scene, especially on Saturday night. Incredibly crowded (not for the claustrophobic) with people sitting clustered on low stools on both sides of the narrow lane, music booming out of bars all around. There's a bar called Khao San Road Pub, but, really, this tops the original Khao San Road for the sheer intensity of the action. And here, the large majority of the patrons are local, not foreign backpackers. Gotta take a walk through, even if you're not into this kind of oover-the-top scene.

reviews.author: SagarVS
reviews.title: Beer Street
reviews.content: Ta Hien street is also called the Beer street, This street is full of bars and restaurants and hundreds of people sit outside on the street in tiny plastic stools sipping beer. The bars compete with one another in terms of offers to attract customers. It is said that the beer here is fresh and they seldom store it for more than a day. This is a cool place to hang out and socialise with the locals.

locationDesc: For many travelers, the Temple of Literature & National University is a must-visit due to its rich historical significance and serene gardens. This tranquil oasis, with its traditional architecture and beautiful courtyards, is located conveniently near old Hanoi.

reviews.author: BBB-MLJ
reviews.title: Hanoi Must See
reviews.content: A lovely place in the lake. Less than US$2 entry each. Nice city views from the temple island. Not very busy when we visited so plenty of photo opportunities.

reviews.author: 1993Kiwi
reviews.title: Beautiful historical location.
reviews.content: Spent about an hour here walking around. It costs to get in, and you can only pay cash.We walked around the grounds which is beautiful, and has a lot of history.  There’s also someone who will paint a scroll for you - there’s a book of options. There’s no written cost - everyone seemed to be giving around 200k VND.There are bathrooms and a little store as well.

reviews.author: Hozyr
reviews.title: Great inspiration.
reviews.content: Was good to see the focus on education but the place needs repairs and some maintenance.

reviews.author: Beatrice L
reviews.title: A must-do
reviews.content: I loved it, it is a magnificent place. Pretty buildings and a well-maintained garden

reviews.author: Patty B
reviews.title: Worth Seeing Near The Other Sights
reviews.content: Interesting stone structure and nice grounds.  Near the other interesting sights near the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Cecco_Rivolta
reviews.title: Nice, too bad about the weather
reviews.content: We visited this beautiful place on a day of very heavy rain and on a Sunday, so it was very crowded. It was still possible to perceive the beauty and sacredness of the places. Since a good part of the visit is outdoors, I recommend visiting it, if possible, in favorable weather conditions and on different weekdays to find less crowding.

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: A place absolutely to be seen
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature is certainly one of the visits to make in Hanoi, especially for its historical importance: founded in 1070, it is also linked to the Quốc Tử Giám, considered the first great university institution of Vietnam.The entrance ticket costs 70,000 VND per person and is cash only.The complex is quite large and is laid out through a succession of courtyards. The things we liked the most:- the Great Middle Gate, which leads to the different areas of the complex;- the Khuê Văn Các, the characteristic pavilion that has become one of the symbols of Hanoi;- the Thien Quang well and especially the 82 stelae of the doctors, resting on stone turtles, with the names of the scholars who passed the imperial exams;- the temple dedicated to Confucius, which allows for a better understanding of the importance that culture and education have had in Vietnamese history;- the area of the ancient Imperial Academy.Despite this, it is an interesting place, very different from the other temples visited in Hanoi. Allow at least a couple of hours to visit it calmly and read the explanations.Bring water if you go in the summer, it is really very, very hot!

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: In my opinion, the prettiest temple in Hanoi
reviews.content: I am usually not a big fan of temples but this one is clearly worth the detour, both for the buildings themselves and for the surrounding spaces.The temple is close to old Hanoi, about a 15-20 min walk away.Admission is not free: 70,000 Dong.No obligation to cover your knees.

reviews.author: Emmanuel811
reviews.title: A must
reviews.content: Very beautiful place that you really must visit when you are passing through Hanoi. A piece of the country's history.

reviews.author: mvanroy
reviews.title: A haven of peace and greenery in the center of a busy Hanoi
reviews.content: You immediately notice that a piece of history lives here, it is not only Vietnam’s first university but also a tribute to Confucius, a Chinese philosopher and politician who is seen as an example to all teachers. We walked from one courtyard to the other at ease, read some background here and there but mostly soaked up the pleasant and peaceful atmosphere. The different types of trees (from large to bonsai) but also the nice statues (eg the turtles with their smooth rubbed heads) and the beautiful altars were the highlights.

reviews.author: Ben
reviews.title: Beautifully preserved cultural heritage and an oasis of calm
reviews.content: A visit to the Temple of Literature is highly recommended when exploring Hanoi. As the city's oldest university, founded in 1070, it offers an excellent insight into Vietnam's rich educational and Confucian history.The complex is generally well-preserved and divided into five distinct courtyards, showcasing impressive traditional architecture, peaceful gardens, and large stone steles resting on turtles. However, certain areas are currently showing signs of wear and would benefit from some targeted maintenance to fully restore their historical luster.Despite its central location, the grounds offer a remarkably quiet atmosphere away from the busy traffic. For the best experience, renting an audio guide at the entrance is highly recommended to compensate for the limited on-site signage. A visit takes about 1 hour. Arriving early is advisable to avoid tour groups and graduation photo shoots.

reviews.author: David G
reviews.title: The First University of Vietnam,
reviews.content: We also toured the Temple of Literature, the first University of the country that built from 1076, with unique architectural works and some of the oldest historical relics in Hanoi.  It retains much of its original architectural layout, but with restorations made to repair damages caused by wars. There are multiple courtyards with structures (pavilions and stalls), statues and relics depicting the history of the university as well as the religious aspects of the facility. One of the best parts are the huge stone steles on turtle backs bear names of the country’s men who received Doctor Laureate through royal examinations

reviews.author: Maurita M
reviews.title: Peaceful stop in the middle of Hanoi
reviews.content: I really enjoyed visiting the Temple of Literature National University. It felt calm the moment I stepped inside, even though the streets outside were busy and noisy. The courtyards, old stone steles, and red gates were lovely, and I liked reading a bit about the history while wandering around. There was the smell of incense in a few spots and lots of shade from the trees, which made it a nice break from the heat. It does get crowded, especially with tour groups, so it’s not exactly a quiet hidden gem. Still, I’d definitely recommend it if you’re in Hanoi and want a bit of history and a slower pace for an hour or so.

reviews.author: Igor Alexeev
reviews.title: Temple of Literature: a follow-up visit...
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature (Văn Miếu) and the National University (Quoc Tu Giam) in Hanoi is a historical and cultural complex and one of the main attractions of the Vietnamese capital, which is almost 1,000 years old. It was interesting to walk around the complex and appreciate that in the 10 years since his previous visit to the complex, little had changed. As a matter of fact, just like in the previous 1,000 years. During the follow-up visit, it was possible to examine in more detail the structure of all five courtyards of the complex. An exhibition in the fifth courtyard devoted to the Imperial Academy, Vietnam's first national university, was particularly informative. By the way, the infrastructure of the complex is convenient enough to explore: navigation is clear, the routes through the territory are logically arranged, there are areas for short rest. Opening hours (8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.) allow you to choose the best visit time to avoid the densest flow of visitors...

reviews.author: sannamoo
reviews.title: Must-visit historic site in Hanoi
