reviews.content: The Văn Miếu, or Temple of Literature, is a historic site dedicated to Confucius located in Hanoi, northern Vietnam. Built in 1070 during Emperor Lý Thánh Tông's reign, it served as Vietnam's first national university, the Imperial Academy, from 1076 to 1779. The temple is famous for its many stone steles engraved with the names of leading scholars, offering valuable insights into Vietnam's academic legacy. The 82 stone steles at Van Mieu are officially designated as Vietnam National Treasures. Additionally, the temple is featured on the reverse of the 100,000 Vietnamese đồng banknote. If you're planning a trip to Hanoi, a visit to the Temple of Literature is highly advisable. It usually takes about an hour to explore the temple, so visiting in the morning is recommended, especially during summer. If you're planning a trip to Hanoi, a visit to the Temple of Literature is highly advisable. The temple opens daily from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with summer hours from April 15 to October 15 extending to 7:30 AM - 5:30 PM. An entrance fee of 70,000 VND applies. Visitors should note that tank tops and miniskirts are not allowed.

reviews.author: sandydee_7
reviews.title: Beautiful and interesting temple
reviews.content: A nice peaceful oasis in the midst of the busy city of Hanoi.  Lovely area to visit and admire the architecture.  Though busy it did not feel crowded.

reviews.author: Warasit
reviews.title: Discover the Write
reviews.content: Special experience, there is a night tour, should bring an umbrella if you go during the day, to love Vietnam more after this trip, a place not to miss in Hanoi

reviews.author: Ryleigh R
reviews.title: Beautiful and Historic Attraction
reviews.content: A beautiful and well-preserved historical site in Hanoi. The architecture is impressive, the grounds are peaceful, and the cultural significance is remarkable. A great place to learn about Vietnamese history and take memorable photos. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Annie An
reviews.title: Good, progress.
reviews.content: Really interesting weekend experience. There is always artistic and cultural space on Saturdays and Sundays here, worth considering tours

reviews.author: Away
reviews.title: Don't miss!
reviews.content: It is one of the finest places in the world.

reviews.author: bebeThionville
reviews.title: Not to be missed
reviews.content: The most important mausoleum of Confucius in the country It was founded in 1070  Rich in historical and cultural value 😍Our guide Lucy was able to answer our questions ☺️9/2/26

reviews.author: Marc B
reviews.title: Great!
reviews.content: The oldest university in Vietnam. Very nice buildings, shrines and park.

reviews.author: David L
reviews.title: Imperial Academy
reviews.content: Another must-see in Hanoi, passing through the gates of the Temple of Literature, to learn about what was once Vietnam’s first university, teaching place for much of the elite of Vietnamese scholars.  Highly recommended.

reviews.author: AlexSwallow
reviews.title: Interesting rather than spectacular
reviews.content: It was nice to come to this peaceful place and learn some of the history associated with it.That being said, after travelling through more of Vietnam I certainly think there are a lot of temples that are more spectacular than this one. So in my view it felt like a nice to see rather than a must-see.

reviews.author: Hannah
reviews.title: Must do if you’re in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Loved this place, an amazing stop in such a busy area, the building was very unique and beautiful, tha staff were great and had good English, and there were loads of information signs dotted around in several languages, there were also guides that you could pick up and gave you lots of information about what you were looking at.

reviews.author: Nguyen Van Phong
reviews.title: Discover the night in the literature
reviews.content: Excellent and exciting for a night in Hanoi

reviews.author: PM-65-UK
reviews.title: Definitely a key place to visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: Really enjoyed our couple of hours here, aided by an excellent private tour guide.The site is fascinating historically, still ‘spiritually’ important and an oasis of calm in a very busy city. Definitely worth an hour or two to wander around the various parts of the site.

reviews.author: johnhp702
reviews.title: Historical site
reviews.content: Historical site which attracts tourist and locals galore, when we visited it seemed to be a graduation day for all ages of children who were dressed up.

reviews.author: Ria1104
reviews.title: Place of Historical Importance
reviews.content: We visited it as it was listed as one of the top most attractions in Hanoi. But honestly, we did not find much things to do here. The architecture was nice but we had already seen much better architecture in Nihn Bihn. The place stands as the first university of Vietnam and so has a historical significance, hence would only recommend this place if someone is interested in its history.

reviews.author: bask4
reviews.title: Temple of literature, Hanoi
reviews.content: This was recommended as a 'must do' by the hop-on,hop-off bus commentary, and was quite interesting, particularly about the early promotion of education, the doctorate students and the university . There was no information leaflet or audio despite being advertised as such. There was written information inside the display rooms; and calligraphers writing chinese characters representing themes such as hope etc.

reviews.author: Jeremy C
reviews.title: Historic Temple Complex
reviews.content: Delightful temple complex is located in the city centre old quarter and seems popular with both locals and tourists. The temple buildings are beautiful to look at and enter with the bonus of people frequenting the area in folk costumes.

reviews.author: Murton68
reviews.title: Very busy when it’s a public holiday
reviews.content: As was extremely busy as it was a national holiday.  Having said that it was another very interesting place to visit steeped in a lot of history.

reviews.author: HamitGunesli
reviews.title: Confucius’ teachings
reviews.content: Established to teach the teachings of Confucius, this university is an integral and colorful part of Vietnamese culture.

reviews.author: Vietnam immersion
reviews.title: Cultural Site of Hanoi
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature of Hanoi is a place full of history, serenity and beauty. Considered the first university in Vietnam, this iconic site perfectly reflects the importance of Vietnamese knowledge, education and culture.Indoor courtyards, peaceful gardens, lotus ponds and traditional architecture create a calm and inspiring atmosphere away from the hustle and bustle of the city. Each pavilion tells part of the country’s history and invites respect and contemplation.It is a must-see visit to understand the soul of Hanoi and Vietnam. An ideal place to walk, learn and recharge. I highly recommend this site to all visitors.

reviews.author: GlobetrotterMSK
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: The beautiful temple complex is located in the city centre and is very popular with both locals and tourists. Not only the temple buildings are beautiful to look at, but also young people frequenting the area in colourful folk costumes.

reviews.author: FyingKiwi
reviews.title: Accademic
reviews.content: Academic achievement appears to have always been an important part of Vietnamese culture, and this temple certainly provides evidence of this. Vietnam’s first university, established as a Confucius Temple, oversaw the introduction of graduate professionals, such as doctors, emerge. Excellent information provided depicting the entire progress of its establishment, manner in which studies were conducted and examined, and graduation process.

reviews.author: caroleen78
reviews.title: Temple dedicated to education
reviews.content: In this temple of literature five rooms that initially provided education for the kings of the mandarins and children of the court.Then it was open to all children It was bombed during the war and the last building rebuilt with American funds.Many girls have their pictures taken in the gardens.Beautiful architecture

reviews.author: MizLeee
reviews.title: Lovely quiet place
reviews.content: Lovely place to visit. I must admit it was very peaceful there but be warned there are a lot of girls there doing photoshoots so it does distract from the main purpose of the visit but I didn’t mind it.

reviews.author: Dinithi Dabare
reviews.title: Seeking and exploring day in temple of literature.
reviews.content: I really love this beautiful temple of literature. I felt like I was in a historic drama. I was able to learn so many traditions and the history related to Vietnam. This university had one of the smartest scholars back then. They worshiped the Tortoise as a symbol of prosperity. The Temple of Literature consists history of Confucius, books of scholars, attire of scholars, and contributions of scholars. A lot of students and tourists come to visit this temple every day.  This temple is a major landmark in Vietnam.

reviews.author: iPodsolnuh
reviews.title: Beautiful park
reviews.content: A very beautiful place to experience traditional park culture of Vietnam. You can come for a walk and admire the harmony of nature and architecture.

reviews.author: Bernard W
reviews.title: Special, peaceful, highlighting education
reviews.content: Temple dedicated to Confucious.  Different peaceful courtyards and ponds.  First university in Vietnam.  Wonderful stone architecture.  Education is taken very seriously.  Students take their class photos here even if they do not attend.

reviews.author: Wanderlustaustralia
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: The entry fee is more expensive compared with other sites, but you’ll be spending quite awhile here, so it’s worth it! There is plenty to see, and information is plentiful. What ruined the afternoon for us was the huge number of people who came dressed up to have professional photo shoots. It wasn’t a case of them taking a short amount of time for each photo; they posed in the busiest areas with their support crew for 5 - 10 minutes at a time. It was impossible to avoid them, and we weren’t able to see as much as we would have liked because of this. It would be great if staff could encourage the people doing photo shoots to be quicker and not disrupt the experience for others, as this is a site for everyone to share.

reviews.author: JuanMarco31
reviews.title: A visit to this Temple is essential
reviews.content: When one is in Hanoi , it would be a shame not to visit this temple which is dedicated to Confucius . If you have the opportunity to take a French-speaking guide , it will allow you to understand the history of the place and to go around with all the explanations of each nook and cranny .

reviews.author: TheLush101
reviews.title: Temple and artefacts
reviews.content: We spent around an hour here as part of a tour. The temple has beautiful and peaceful gardens. There were several couples having professional photos taken within it whilst we were there. The complex has a large pond at the centre, with different buildings surrounding this. The temple altars are here, and towards the back of the complex is a more modern section which house different artefacts such as ceramics - worth a visit given the history.

reviews.author: possagol
reviews.title: Vietnamese history
reviews.content: Great temple dedicated to Confucius. It is divided into several courtyards and ponds. Admission costs 7000 dong (2 euros and 30 cents more or less) open from 7.30 to 17.30 . Closed Saturday and Sunday is a very crowded temple is not far from the mausoleum of ho chi minh

reviews.author: Sarah H
reviews.title: GIVING US A LESSON!
reviews.content: Stepping into the Temple of Literature was truly an impressive journey back in time. The moment you walk through the ancient gates, you are immediately enveloped in a sense of profound tranquility that feels miles away from the Hanoi bustle. The architecture is simply stunning, with its intricate wooden details and meticulously preserved courtyards providing a magnificent backdrop for reflection. Most powerful of all is the deep history; standing before the Stelae of Doctors and realizing this was Vietnam’s first university gives you a tangible connection to a millennium of scholarly tradition. This site is more than just beautiful; it is a moving testament to the enduring Vietnamese value placed on knowledge and intellect.

reviews.author: Lawrence A
reviews.title: Rich in culture
reviews.content: A place not to be missed when in Hanoi.We do the red bus hop on hop off tourist bus tour to see all the attractions in the city and this is one of my choices to set my foot on.

reviews.author: nicodenheijer
reviews.title: Oasis of peace
reviews.content: Beautiful complex in the middle of the city but still an oasis of peace. Beautiful temples, greenery and ponds. Lovely to stroll around.

reviews.author: Maxxxxx H
reviews.title: Great
reviews.content: Visiting the Temple of Literature and the adjacent National University in Hanoi was a fascinating experience. The temple is peaceful and beautifully preserved, with traditional Vietnamese architecture, serene gardens, and stone stelae honoring scholars. Walking through the courtyards, you really feel the history and cultural significance of the place.The National University area nearby adds to the charm, giving a glimpse into Vietnam’s long-standing tradition of education and learning. It’s easy to spend a few hours here exploring, taking photos, and enjoying the calm atmosphere right in the heart of the city.Overall, it’s a perfect spot for anyone interested in history, culture, or just a quiet, beautiful place to stroll in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Nelson Bolton
reviews.title: The Temple of Literature: Hanoi's Ancient Heart of Wisdom
reviews.content: Stepping into the Temple of Literature was genuinely like walking back in time. I was immediately struck by the tranquil atmosphere and the beautifully preserved ancient architecture, offering a peaceful escape from the bustling city of Hanoi. This complex is a powerful symbol, showcasing Vietnam's profound and historical commitment to education and intellectual development.It’s incredible to think that this site served as the nation's first university, established nearly a millennium ago! Seeing the renowned stone steles, resting on giant tortoises and inscribed with the names of successful scholars, clearly demonstrates the systematic and rigorous education system that flourished during the feudal era. This dedication truly reflects a highly developed civilization.The grounds are immaculately maintained, and wandering through the courtyards gives you a genuine sense of history. If you appreciate culture, history, and stunning architecture, this location is an absolute must. The Temple of Literature is definitely a must-see destination and a deeply enriching experience for any visitor.

reviews.author: Travel Vibes - India
reviews.title: A place of historical significance but not a must see place
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature is a historically significant site in Hanoi, often praised for its peaceful atmosphere and elegant traditional architecture. However, while the site itself is lovely, the experience can feel somewhat underwhelming if you’re expecting a lot of exhibits or interactive elements — it’s more of a quiet stroll than a deep historical immersion. Additionally, there is an entrance ticket required, and the price feels a bit on the costly side compared to what’s actually available to see inside.Overall, it’s worth a short visit if you’re interested in Vietnam’s cultural history, but not necessarily a must-see if you’re on a tight budget or limited time in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Icvrius V
reviews.title: To see as a tourist..
reviews.content: Superb architecture, very well maintained or finally we could read the explanations in English. Why don't we put 5 stars?For beyond that remains a temple like all the others, with no real little extra that makes a difference.

reviews.author: Deb S
reviews.title: Beautiful place amid the City’s chaos
reviews.content: What a beautiful find in the middle of the bustling city! The gardens and architecture were a very pleasant surprise. We very much appreciated walking through the stages of education to enlightenment. It was the highlight of our day!

reviews.author: Dr Navin Machado
reviews.title: Poor Audio- location co-ordination.
reviews.content: This location is on Hop on Hop off bus route,about 3/4th of the way along the route.It is a charming,serene place except when crowds throng.The audio guide is very disappointing. There are specific areas to put on the guide,corresponding  to certain numbered stations in the premises,which then explains the relevant information.These stations are not clearly marked ,they should be visible above clearly,not as small boards,hidden by crods or only visible if you enter from a particular door & there are often,several..This is a basic requirement. One feels let down.

reviews.author: Michel10000
reviews.title: Beautiful and interesting temple complex, which used to serve as a university
reviews.content: Beautiful temple complex to see, where the students used to study and graduate. 11th century with gate in the beginning and 1857, which is mentioned on a banknote.

reviews.author: Lilllie Codey
reviews.title: Love notes in ancient stone
reviews.content: We giggled under mossy arches, pretending we were scholarly soulmates from centuries past. The quiet courtyards, incense-scented air, and stone turtles made our romance feel timeless—even if we totally got lost trying to find the “lucky” turtle. Still, 10/10 for vibe.

reviews.author: Beppe Marini
reviews.title: Striking and unmissable
reviews.content: Another destination not to be missed to breathe the stories of Vietnam and that pays tribute to the philosopher Confucius and other writers. Divided into 5 shorts and still attended by students who come to receive a good omen and thank for the graduation

reviews.author: Mapie G
reviews.title: Very nice visit
reviews.content: A beautiful site well restored. An oasis of zenitude amid the hubbub of the city. Take a paper guide with you to know what it means because little explanation in French inside

reviews.author: Oscardog16
reviews.title: The audio guide is a must.
reviews.content: There are information boards throughout the complex, written in Vietnamese, English and French. The audio guide gives a bit more information and you can sit in the shade and listen to it. Some of the buildings have been reconstructed and or renovated.  It was interesting to hear the statistics about the doctoral candidates from the feudal system.

reviews.author: christiantoulousain
reviews.title: To visit absolutely
reviews.content: Beautiful place not to be missed! the setting is ideal to have a little freshness and beauty is there!We can't be in Hanoi without going there

reviews.author: loonylou78
reviews.title: Lovely place to visit .
reviews.content: We had a very enjoyable visit here even in the heat! It's big enough to wander about and lose yourself in the history and calmness of the place. I liked that there were corners of the complex where you can just sit in the shade and take it all in.There's a lot of information to take in but it's really interesting and so pretty We were appreciative of the small cafe on site to grab a cold drink and chill .Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: Lovejey
reviews.title: Temple of Confucianism
reviews.content: This is the most historic temple in Hanoi and has a magical atmosphere..it is located in the center of the city, yet it is very quiet, a corner of peace!Every corner has very deep and unique meanings! I think studying in this place, was really a unique experience!

reviews.author: Eli
reviews.title: Interesting historical backstory
reviews.content: An ancient temple of literature in Hanoi. Quite peaceful and has that classic historic vibe. Learning more about its backstory was really interesting and surprising. If you’re traveling solo or on your own, you can use the Travellens app to explore it deeper.

reviews.author: Luana S
reviews.title: Beautifull place
reviews.content: It is peacefull even there is a lot od people, you can learn a lot about history, chinese influence on Vietnam People etc.If you actually want to see and learn something (and not just takin photos for Instagram) this is one of the places you shouldnt miss.

reviews.author: doctorfoxtrot
reviews.title: Informative Visit
reviews.content: Nice place to visit. Seeing how the education system works during the ancient time.  How grading and scoring is reflected . There is a small temple inside as well .

reviews.author: Wayne
reviews.title: Good information here
reviews.content: This temple was a good place to visit. It is well set out and cared for. We had a guide with us who was very helpful and made sure we learnt while visiting. Plenty of photo chances too

reviews.author: wang2383
reviews.title: World Heritage List
reviews.content: The Hanoi Temple has a millennium of history and is officially known as the Temple of the National Guard. It was founded in 1070 by the dynasty of Li and is located on the western side of Hanoi, Vietnam. In 1076 it was established as the First High School of Vietnam. The difference from the ordinary temple is that it is a temple dedicated to Confucius.On both sides of the Skywalk well and east, there are 82 monuments on each side. A living, flexible stone turtle raised its head, attached to this fine sculptural monument. The first monument has been carved for over 500 years. After that, each exam, a stone monument is raised. Turtle Negative Stone is long-lived and expects the growing development of Vietnamese education, while confirming that Vietnamese talent is worthy of respect and memory for generations. The inscriptions on the monument are written in Chinese letters, with different pencil. Each monument is a literary work, and the sculptures on the monument are diverse, reflecting the artistic image that evolves over time. Evidence of its wisdom and sophistication by Vietnamese artists. In 2010, UNESCO included the Temple – National Monument in the World Heritage List.

reviews.author: francesca g
reviews.title: The only valid monument
reviews.content: Really fascinating! Very old shows typical architecture of Containerland. The complex is certainly the most interesting thing to see in Hanoi. It is easily reached on foot from the old town.

reviews.author: Caroline WSL HYZ
reviews.title: Temple of Literature – A Peaceful Cultural Stop in Hanoi
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature is one of Hanoi’s most iconic and historically rich landmarks. It offers a peaceful escape from the busy city streets and gives you a glimpse into Vietnam’s academic and spiritual past. If you’re visiting, I highly recommend taking a Grab (or taxi) straight there — it’s the most convenient and affordable option, especially if you’re unfamiliar with the area.I visited in June, and the weather was hot and humid, so be prepared. Bringing a hand fan or small towel can make a big difference in staying comfortable as you walk through the large courtyards and historic buildings.The temple grounds are spacious and beautifully maintained, with ancient architecture, bonsai trees, and quiet reflective pools. If you’re planning to step into the actual temple areas, it’s a nice gesture to bring some small change for offerings — not required, but appreciated if you wish to participate in the local customs.Overall, it’s a serene and meaningful spot to learn about Vietnam’s Confucian heritage. Give yourself an hour or so to stroll around and take it all in — and don’t forget water and sun protection if you go in the summer!

reviews.author: lilybt
reviews.title: Multilayered gardens and buildings
reviews.content: It is close to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, and it seemed on the map to be quite a walk. This is because the entrance gate is on the opposite south side. As the name suggests, it was established as a Confucius Mausoleum and then served as a "Kokugakudo" (literally, school of state) to educate the royal family. Upon entering, you will find five sets of gardens, each with a vertical building, divided by a distinctive gate. One of them, the Kuiwenkaku, is depicted on the 100,000 VND note.

reviews.author: Ames Bury
reviews.title: Surprisingly kid-friendly history that actually held their attention
reviews.content: Took the kids to Hanoi’s Temple of Literature expecting groans—but shockingly, they listened! Ancient courtyards, turtle stelae, and stories of old scholars kept us all curious. It’s peaceful, well-kept, and feels meaningful without being stiff. A quiet escape in the city where history actually felt alive. Great for families who want more than just pho and motorbikes.

reviews.author: Adventure05703998509
reviews.title: A cute but not unmissable monument
reviews.content: The setting and buildings are nice and change from other buildings in Hanoi but you will find much better and more complete elsewhere in Vietnam, for example in Hue. However, it is a good introduction to Confucianists and examinations.

reviews.author: cristoph2010
reviews.title: Confucian influenced education hub
reviews.content: This is apparently Vietnam's first university that was at one point in history for the education of the royals and imperial bureaucrats. You can see the Confucian influences throughout from the writings to the architecture. The temple in the inner courtyard is a treat.

reviews.author: Sayers Houston
reviews.title: Ancient university
reviews.content: The kids were fascinated by the stone turtles, and we all enjoyed the peaceful gardens and traditional architecture. It was a wonderful educational experience for the whole family, offering a quiet escape from the city's hustle.

reviews.author: Shai N
reviews.title: History and Great photos
reviews.content: Serene and nice place to visit. I enjoyed walking around the area and learning about Vietnam's oldest university. The place had lots of history and photo opportunities.

reviews.author: Tedie Peter
reviews.title: A must-see in Hanoi.
reviews.content: We found this to be a beautiful and tranquil escape from the city's noise. The well-preserved traditional architecture and peaceful gardens are lovely. It was a nice, absorbing the history of Vietnam's first university.

reviews.author: Ozzie Lissa
reviews.title: A peaceful escape in the city
reviews.content: The traditional Vietnamese architecture is stunning, and the gardens are so peaceful. It was a nice break from the hustle of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Creeping_Death_LA
reviews.title: Historic neighborhood gem
reviews.content: The prices for entering this historic place is so inexpensive that's worth going even if you only have an hour to spare. It's a popular place and you won't be the only one strolling through it's beautiful grounds and checking out all that it has to offer.

reviews.author: Tracey K
reviews.title: Tranquil place in centre of bustling Hanoi.
reviews.content: This is worth a visit if you are staying in Hanoi for a day or two. Behind the walls on a frantic noisy city is this historical attraction. Audio is offered. You can wander at your leisure with a small map (available once you’ve entered). It has some lovely tranquil gardens, stone carvings, ancient architecture and areas for reflection. There is the temple and huge gong so plenty of photo opportunities. Beside the toilets is a small air conditioned coffeehouse. Also sells food and ice lollies. There is an upmarket quality temple shop near exit as well as several reasonably priced souvenir stalls in the middle of the temple’s main square. Better than those at entrance.

reviews.author: Joe C
reviews.title: Peaceful temple, interesting vibe
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature struck me as quite fascinating and remarkably tranquil. It's a location where visitors and residents naturally blend, with some arriving purely for sightseeing and others for worship. Just between us... I heard a whisper that touching the turtle and crane statues brings good fortune, but whether you give it a go is entirely your decision!

reviews.author: CarSteHolden
reviews.title: Interesting Place
reviews.content: Great place to visit with some interesting things to see.  Small entrance fee and the bus tour stops outside so easy to get to.

reviews.author: Katrin K
reviews.title: Peace and quiet in the middle of Hanoi
reviews.content: A very nice, well-kept complex that offers some peace and quiet amidst the hustle and bustle of Hanoi. A visit to relax is worthwhile.

reviews.author: Rania Homma
reviews.title: Tranquil architectural gem in Hanoi
reviews.content: This location is distinguished by its interesting architecture and offers a serene atmosphere, particularly noteworthy for its setting in central Hanoi. The cost of admission is minimal, and the site can be comprehensively viewed in approximately one hour.

reviews.author: Ana Kampá Tour
reviews.title: Interesting visit to Vietnam's first university
reviews.content: It is the first university in Vietnam, with a very elaborate architecture that reflects Vietnamese tradition. On site there are exhibitions to learn more about its history and culture.At night they offer a special program called "Night at College". Explanations and posters are in English, Vietnamese and French, but not in Spanish.The visit lasts approximately two hours, enough time to appreciate everything calmly.

reviews.author: zaida Luis Z
reviews.title: New experience...
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature in Hanoi is one of my favorite spots in the city—a peaceful, historic place that feels like stepping back in time. Built in 1070, it honors Confucius and became Vietnam’s first national university. The courtyards, old stone stelae, and classic architecture give it a quiet, scholarly charm. Many students still visit to pray for good grades, and it’s easy to see why—it feels deeply connected to learning and tradition. If you're in Hanoi, it's a must-see.

reviews.author: Laura B
reviews.title: Become Erudite
reviews.content: The names of the buildings here make you smarter just by reading them.  With such an extended history of learned scholars coming through here, with their histories recorded so beautifully on the backs of turtles (all the way down), you can't help but think some small bit of all that beauty rubs off on you as you walk through the temple.

reviews.author: Incredible Asia Journeys
reviews.title: Free night tour at Temple of Literature
reviews.content: I took a FREE night tour at Temple of Literature, and so amazing. We admire the 3D mapping, light shows and exhibitions about Vietnam traditional university.

reviews.author: HayKay1
reviews.title: Highly Recommend The Temple Of Literature
reviews.content: I loved this place. It has an incredible history with stellae recording the achievements of outstanding students. The Great Hall of Ceremonies is stunning inside with a large Buddha and a very large golden turtle- a must visit. It is a very calm, peaceful place with 5 courtyards and gardens.

reviews.author: John P
reviews.title: To Help You Understand Vietnam, Go Here to Understand Confucian Learning
reviews.content: Founded in 1070, this extensive Confucian learning and worship complex of squares surrounded by classrooms, temples, exemplary architecture and artifacts has so many stories to tell.  You have two choices for your visit; have a expert personal guide who an unlock understanding of this first university and its deep and lasting impact on Vietnamese society or get - and both study and read while there - a comprehensive guidebook.  My suggestion is to find a highly knowledgeable guide.  Understanding this amazing place is worth the effort and modest expense.

reviews.author: John N
reviews.title: Educational and interesting as education is important
reviews.content: Very clean, nice with a tour guide to explain the history and significance. Great place to take photos and spend the day learning about the importance of literature

reviews.author: corinne_prevost
reviews.title: If you like history
reviews.content: Really disappointed with the place. You have to love history and take selfies in front of monuments. It's not our thing, we prefer people and we didn't like it.

reviews.author: Harirajan Varatharajan
reviews.title: Education excellence
reviews.content: Visiting the Temple of Literature was a highlight of my time in Hanoi. Walking through its ancient courtyards and peaceful gardens, I could feel the deep respect for education and scholarship that has existed here for centuries. The beautifully preserved architecture, from the grand entrance gates to the stone steles honoring past scholars, made the experience even more special. The tranquil atmosphere provided a perfect escape from the city’s hustle, allowing me to truly appreciate Vietnam’s rich academic and cultural heritage. It’s a must-visit for anyone wanting to connect with the country’s history.

reviews.author: Emily Y
reviews.title: Busy but nice
reviews.content: We like this place in Hanoi because not too noisy. It’s bush with lots of school kids but we like the nice buildings and the trees. It’s an old place and the culture is good. Some nice music is also playing and the fish ponds are beautiful. You should see this place if you choose to go to Hanoi.

reviews.author: Anne S
reviews.title: An interesting view of ancient education
reviews.content: We came here as part of a Scenic Cruises tour. Fortunately Scenic had provided a local guide which really helped our understanding of the place. He explained and demonstrated the "exam pods" which would be challenge to modern children, (as would the punishments which included beheading).

reviews.author: SB01
reviews.title: Oasis in Hanoi
reviews.content: Just outside the old town, this is worth a visit just to escape the madness of Hanoi for an hour or so. Once you've paid your entry you progress through a series of courtyards to the main temple buildings. When we went there were several schools also visiting (the children were keen to practice their English with us), possibly making it even more crowded than usual. But if you step off the main central path and walk along the edges it becomes quite peaceful and you can appreciate the splendour. It appears in excellent condition, but that is because very little is original. The temples themselves are mainly modern facsimiles, but I don't think this is an issue. The interiors are a riot of red and gold.There is a reasonable amount of information in English and other languages, but unless you are a scholar of Confucius it may be opaque as it seems to focus on the process of the exams and reference's scholars and mandarins, who would be unfamiliar to the lay person. There are a number of statues of important personalities. I'd be interested in more information about how long the exams took as they seemed to settle in overnight.Well worth a visit in my opinion.

reviews.author: Jacqal
reviews.title: Architecture, serenity and ancient history in the midst of busy Hanoi - fascinating
reviews.content: This place took us by surprise. We walked in out of the noise of on-stop Hanoi into a serene set of gardens, interesting architecture and even more interesting history. There's a lot to take in and even with our excellent guide, we didn't really manage to spend the time it justified. So many interesting facts about how students learnt and were judged - hard to do justice to so many years of history but well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Agota B
reviews.title: New labeled old
reviews.content: Said to be an old building of Hanoi this temple is located in a park and consists of 5 courtyards. It looks nice but is totally rebuild and new. Concrete walls, new wooden structures. This experience did not serve our expectations of “old heritage”. But at least the air was fine…

reviews.author: MrDream688
reviews.title: Temple of Literature & National University Hanoi
reviews.content: This historic site honors scholars and Confucian values. With ancient courtyards, stone steles, and lush gardens, it’s a serene place to explore Vietnam’s academic heritage.

reviews.author: Sue M
reviews.title: Incredible Architecture & History
reviews.content: Amazing to see this complex devoted to Confucius having survived for almost a thousand years.  It was also the home of the first national university in Vietnam.  The complex is so peaceful and serene in the midst of Hanoi.

reviews.author: alessandra_biondi3
reviews.title: Visited by so many youth
reviews.content: It finds existence from 1070. We entered through one of the three doors (heaven, earth, humanity) between the 4 pillars (representing the 4 cardinal orders). Above the pillars are the symbols of reincarnation: phoenix, unicorn . The temple has 5 courtyards (represent the Universe changing with the 5 elements). The first courtyard is dedicated to education and learning, the second built in 1800 is the pavilion of the constellations. the third square filled with water is a well of light between earth and sky because the sky is reflected in the water. the fourth is of the success dedicated to Confucius, the fifth has the Temple for veneration to the first rector of the University.The Temple of Literature wants to teach that life must lead to Wisdom. Sunday, March 9 was very popular with groups of young people and families with children. Nice vital and intellectual place.

reviews.author: Naomi B
reviews.title: You’ll be surprised how peaceful it is
reviews.content: Beautiful buildings and gardens, celebrating the history of learning here. A tranquil spot though buzzing with visitors in the heart of Hanoi, though a little out of the Old Quarter. Approximately 70,000VND per person to visit. Plenty of cafes and souvenir shopping available around the area.

reviews.author: S&O
reviews.title: Temples for students and their success
reviews.content: The famous temple in Hanoi. Worth seeing, traditional and important for all students and their families. The layout itself is less spectacular.

reviews.author: Minadua85
reviews.title: worth a visit!
reviews.content: A beautiful and peaceful historical site! The architecture is stunning, and the lush gardens provide a serene escape. A must-visit to learn about Vietnam’s rich educational and cultural heritage.

reviews.author: Haha.its.Liz
reviews.title: Not a highlight for us
reviews.content: The history of the location was not well told in the audio guide or the signage.  Audio guide went into minutiae.  It listed a lot of names of graduates, unknown to foreign visitors, and possibly locals.  The nuggets of interesting details were hidden among many extraneous details in the signage and the audio guide.

reviews.author: José Antonio
reviews.title: A haven of peace
reviews.content: Amid the chaos of Hanoi a haven of peace. A garden for walking, listening to birds and recharging batteries before returning to the bustle of the capital.

reviews.author: Gwendal L
reviews.title: Flee the audio guide
reviews.content: Skip the audio guide (which is more expensive than the input).The site is superb, there are explanatory signs in French. However the audio guide is to be avoided, text read by teenagers who do not master reading, no insightful info, many mistakes

reviews.author: Liliane M
reviews.title: AUTHENTIC VIETNAM CULTURE.. UNMISSABLE
reviews.content: It's a pickup you can't miss.It is the oldest temple in Hanoi and is considered to be the first university in all of Vietnam dedicated to Confucius.At first it was for nobles and royalty but then it was opened to the brightest students.It is a very nice and well maintained temple with a very pleasant environment..There are stone mats mounted on turtles. Each stele was built to honor the doctoral winning talents.It is a temple that reflects the authentic Vietnamese culture and for me it was an interesting visit.

reviews.author: tanya gupta
reviews.title: Beautiful but not necessary to visit
reviews.content: This place is beautiful and has religious and spiritual significance- but as a tourist I didn’t see the need to go here specially cause of how crowded it was and cause it’s a paid entry. Unless you have a lot of time on your hands- this one is a skip.

reviews.author: RIchard035
reviews.title: Ancient university
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature is a monument to Confucius and Vietnam's first university. It is a vast site situated in central Hanoi. There is a small charge that can only be paid by cash. The temple is a series of courtyards each with pavilions, halls and statues. There is plenty of information on the history of the university, how the exam system worked and the monarch's role in assessing student. There is a small cafe near to one of the courtyards.

reviews.author: Perez L
reviews.title: Very useful discovery
reviews.content: A very beautiful place that preserves the traditional values ​​of Vietnam. it was interesting to visit this place, a useful experience

reviews.author: 加藤 花
reviews.title: A special moment in peaceful beauty
reviews.content: The manicured gardens made me feel as if I was lost in another world. The beautiful architecture gives you a sense of the depth of history. We had a relaxing time in a quiet environment and shared memorable moments. This place will forever be etched in our hearts. I would love to visit again next time.

reviews.author: World best advisor ...!
reviews.title: To be seen...!
reviews.content: interesting architecture and history ... like a small city. to be visited absolutely. avoid pick hours too. don't forget to touch the birds at the temple for good luck!

reviews.author: Julie I
reviews.title: Temple of Literature in its park-like grounds a peaceful, pleasant place to stroll.
reviews.content: Pleasant respite from hectic Hanoi noise and traffic.  Interesting architecture from a by-gone era.  Excellent art exhibition a bonus.  And the toilets clean.

reviews.author: Wolfgang Heurman
reviews.title: Oasis of peace in the middle of Hanoi
reviews.content: This temple is really worth a visit and is a haven of peace (compared to the hectic outside the temple walls) in the middle of Hanoi. Best reached by Hop On Hop Off bus instead of an organized visit to escape the hustle and bustle of Hanoi for several hours.

reviews.author: Gabbie V
reviews.title: Immersion in History
reviews.content: These ancient monuments transported us back in time. Each stone tells a fascinating story, and we were amazed by the delicate architecture. Strolling through the peaceful gardens, we felt the soul of this unique culture.

reviews.author: memee08
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature and National University had a slight feeling of the Forbidden City in Beijing as you walked through one courtyard after another. It was interesting to read about the philosophy of the university where the first lesson for students to learn is how to behave respectfully, and acquiring knowledge comes later. Pleasant gardens, courtyards and religious areas, with some information on the history of the university and students’ examinations. On the day we went we had to navigate around hundreds of young girls dressed in their finest posing for photos, just like around Hoan Kiem lake. Perhaps it’s always the same?

reviews.author: TravelingAnnK
reviews.title: Interesting Temple
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature was the first University complex in Vietnam.It is worth a visit because of it's historical significance and interesting architecture.It is also where students go to pray for luck in their studies and exams.There were many students there the day we visited.I was impressed with the number of libraries next to palaces in Vietnam.

reviews.author: ArpitaS
reviews.title: Beautiful instance of sensitivity towards education.
reviews.content: There are very few places that values knowledge the way Vietnamese people do. Vien Mieu also known as the temple of literature is a beautiful proof of this value. The steles  on the turtles with the names of the illustrious students, the gate with symbolic constellations patterns are also instances of the thoughtfulness of the people towards education. It is definitely our first favourite in Hà Nội.

reviews.author: Schuyler Wii
reviews.title: Ancient Learning
reviews.content: Impressive structures and grand courtyards everywhere. It's steeped in such rich history, you can almost feel the scholars of old. We wandered around for ages, totally captivated. A peaceful escape from the city buzz.

reviews.author: Almacsixtyeight
reviews.title: Another gem within an ancient city
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature delves into another level of knowledge and understanding for all visitors. Situated in the heart of this ancient city there is a richness on beautiful display. I highly recommend you immerse yourself with everything there is to see here. Please add to your cultural and historical tour.

reviews.author: Ilaria S
reviews.title: We walked through the door of talent.

reviews.author: Happiness58079983931
reviews.title: Discovering the Thousand Year Culture of Thang Long
reviews.content: My visit to Hanoi was nothing short of incredible! The city is a perfect mix of old-world charm and modern vibrancy. Walking through the Old Quarter felt like stepping back in time, with its narrow streets, ancient pagodas, and colonial buildings. I especially loved exploring the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the Temple of Literature, which gave me a deeper appreciation of Vietnam’s history and culture.The food in Hanoi is absolutely phenomenal. I couldn’t get enough of the street food—pho, bun cha, and the amazing egg coffee were highlights of my trip. Each meal was an adventure, and the locals were always happy to recommend their favorite spots.While the traffic can be overwhelming at first, I quickly adapted and even found it exciting to cross the busy streets alongside the locals. The energy of the city is contagious, and there’s always something happening, whether it’s a bustling market or a peaceful morning by Hoan Kiem Lake. Hanoi left me with unforgettable memories, and I can’t wait to return someday!

reviews.author: David
reviews.title: The antiquity of the first school inVietnam
reviews.content: After visiting the Temple of Literature (Văn Miếu Quốc Tử Giám), I was deeply impressed by the bustling atmosphere and the ancient beauty of the site. Right from the entrance, there was a large crowd, particularly groups of students from schools inside and outside Hanoi, coming to explore and learn. They gathered in front of the pavilions, attentively listening to the guides introducing the long-standing history of the Temple, once the largest educational center in feudal Vietnam. Not only were there Vietnamese students, but I also saw many foreign tourists eagerly discovering the heritage site. Some visitors were happily engaging in conversations with local students, creating a lively and friendly cultural exchange atmosphere. Within the Temple’s grounds, an art exhibition was being held in celebration of Hanoi's Liberation Day. The paintings vividly depicted the heroic history of Hanoi, from the resistance against the French to the modern era. They were skillfully arranged within the serene, ancient space of the traditional pavilions. The solemn setting, combined with the artful displays, further highlighted the beauty of the Temple, both ancient and modern. With its unique architecture, large shady trees, and the peaceful ambiance of the surroundings, the Temple of Literature is truly a must-visit destination to experience Vietnam's culture and history.

The intricate carvings and the beautifully maintained gardens create a peaceful oasis in the heart of the bustling city.Walking through the courtyards, I felt a deep sense of history and reverence. It was fascinating to learn about the temple’s role as Vietnam’s first university and its dedication to Confucius and his teachings.The staff were incredibly friendly and knowledgeable, providing rich insights into the site’s historical and cultural significance. The facilities were well-maintained, and the informative displays added depth to my understanding of this remarkable place.Overall, the Temple of Literature is a must-see for anyone visiting Hanoi. reviews.author: Ludo V
reviews.title: back in time
reviews.content: Van Mieu or Temple of Literature is the oldest and perhaps most beautiful building in Hanoi. The oldest part dates from 1054, modeled on the Confusius temple in his birthplace. For centuries it was an academy or university for mandarins. The temple complex consists of five courtyards, some of which have beautiful gardens, others large ponds. Each courtyard is separated by walls and ornate gates. A central path divides the complex into two symmetrical halves. Under canopies you will find a number of stelae with the names of the graduates. They are carried by turtles. The last courtyard has a smaller building on the left and right with the traditional drum and bronze bell.

reviews.content: The scene is beautiful and solemn. We really like this place. Our guide recounts the highlights here. It's good that we were here

reviews.author: Alessandro S
reviews.title: Important temple for the Vietnamese
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature is a huge Confucian complex built in 1070 that was built in 1070 by Emperor Ly Thanh Tong. The complex was the site of the first University of Vietnam (1076). Originally it was reserved for the children of noble families, then starting from 1442 the university became the place where students of all social classes, coming from every part of the country, went to learn the principles of Confucianism, as well as the classics of literature and poetry.Starting from 1884, at the behest of Emperor Le Thanh Tong, the names and relative dates of birth of the best students were carved on stone steles and exhibited to the public.The complex is characterized by the Khue Van Pavilion, dating back to 1802, and an artificial basin called the "Well of Divine Clarity".

reviews.author: Wikumj

reviews.author: Seaside25841925893
reviews.title: It's great to add this place to your itinerary
reviews.content: As the first university relic complex in our country, the Temple of Literature is not only a historical and cultural relic but also a place where many scholars and students come here to pray for luck in exams and studies. . reviews.author: IsaacG16

reviews.author: Fie Ka

The histories of the remaining structures are quite interesting.

reviews.author: HMKaren

reviews.author: Lynette Sadleir

reviews.content: Exploring the temple complex was a peaceful and enlightening experience. The beauty of its ornate gates, traditional-style pavilions, and well-manicured gardens captivated me at every turn. The mix of vibrant reds, greens, and golds created a visually stunning atmosphere.

reviews.author: Coopper29

reviews.author: Susan C
reviews.title: Gardens and old architecture
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature consists of five courtyards. The first two are quiet gardens while the last three contain halls which you can enter. There are also five ponds in the first three courtyards filled with water lillies. You can see the tablets which honoured exceptional students in the third courtyard. The two-storey building in the 5th courtyard, destroyed in 1946 and reconstructed in 2000, is the most impressive building. Adjoining the Temple courtyards is another garden open space that stretches its length. It is a quiet space in the bustle of Hanoi and it wasn't overly busy when we visited though you'll always have people posing for photos in front of the gates between each of the courtyards. On a practical note there is a wonderfully air-conditioned café onsite that serves delicious smoothies.

reviews.author: Loud1Canberra

reviews.author: Navigate632731

reviews.author: Vietnam i
reviews.title: Must visit destination
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature & National University in Hanoi is a must-visit destination for anyone interested in Vietnamese history and culture. Built in 1070, this ancient temple was dedicated to Confucius and served as Vietnam's first university for over 700 years.Walking through the temple's well-preserved architecture and tranquil gardens, you can't help but feel a sense of awe and reverence for the scholars who once studied here. The stone tablets inscribed with the names of past graduates are a testament to the temple's rich academic history.The temple is also a great spot for taking beautiful photos, especially during the spring when the cherry blossoms are in bloom. Don't forget to visit the gift shop, where you can find unique souvenirs and traditional Vietnamese handicrafts.Overall, the Temple of Literature & National University is an impressive and educational attraction that should not be missed on any trip to Hanoi.

reviews.author: Dahiru

reviews.author: irina j
reviews.title: Must see in Hanoi

We visited on first Sunday of April when many schools from all over the country come here for graduation. There were thousands of pupils finishing secondary or high school. They all were taking group photos inside of the temple and then were listening for prayer and paid their respects at the temple. This is just wonderful that place established in 1070 has still such an important role to play! It’s not just a brilliant tourist attraction but a significant place for so many! reviews.author: LuizDutraNeto
reviews.title: Remembering Confucius in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Welcome to the "Temple of Literature" ("Van Miêu") and to the "Imperial Academy" ("Quóc Tù Giám")! The temple dates from 1070, was built during the reign of Emperor Lý Thánh Tông and dedicated to Confucius and famous scholars. The academy dates from 1076 and was the very first and largest university in Vietnam until 1779. Visit its pavilions, gates, courtyards, gardens, ponds and altars! The courtyards are numbered from one to five. The first two ("Dai Trung Môn" and "Khuê Vân Các") include gates and beautiful gardens. At the third courtyard ("Thien Quang"), a nice pond known as the "Well of Heavenly Clarity". The fourth couryard ("Dai Thàn Môn") houses the "Hall of Ceremonies" and the "Sanctuary to Confucious". Finally, at the fifth courtyard, the grounds of the "Imperial Academy" ("Quóc Tù Giám") and altars honoring famous professors (on the ground floor) and ancient kings (at the upper floor). Unmissable at any visit to Hanoi! Belore going, check visiting hours (as they may change seasonally) and dress properly for a temple. Enjoy!

reviews.author: skyisblu
reviews.title: Quiet refuge in the heart of a noisy city
reviews.content: This complex is a breath of fresh air in Hanoi - inside its walls, not only will you experience the overwhelming history of the place, but also respite from the hustle and bustle of the city around you. Through several courtyards, boasting lakes and stone structures, you will learn about the temple itself, which dedicated to the teaching on Confucius.This is also the site of the first university of Vietnam, the students and disciples here learned the ways of being a gentleman and living a well-respected life. They wrote poems and essays, and were tested - the most prominent receiving their doctorate and having their names inscribed on large stellae. Presented on the backs of a turtle, there are 42 stellae on site, dating as far back as the 1100s, and all the way up to the 1700s, when the last tests of this temple were conducted.Inside one of the last courtyards, there is a large souvenir shop which also offers snacks and drinks for sale, and there are washrooms available on the grounds as well. There seems to be times when there are live music performances, but I did not see a schedule posted regarding showtimes. A curious observation - watching people tossing coins onto the curved roof tiles from the second story of the main temple building. It's like a mad game of Vietnamese Plinko, and I'm not sure of the significance. Best advice I can give for a great visit? Splurge on the audio-tour, but you only need ONE for 2 people - just remember to bring your headphones with you, as you can plug 2 sets into one base!
