reviews.author: timbisto
reviews.title: One of the most important places to see in Hanoi
reviews.content: This is one of the most important places to see in Hanoi.The history and provenance this place brings is remarkable.The birthplace of universities in Vietnam it is a wonder to see.It was amazing to see see such well preserved historical buildings

reviews.author: Justnitid
reviews.title: A venerable national monument
reviews.content: This is a temple dedicated to Confucius, his disciples and to knowledge. It was also the oldest and most important university of Vietnam from 1076 to 1779. Today it is a venerated place which is visited by students and their families before or after an important examination. The place is huge and consists of five courtyards, each accessed through ceremonial gates. The innermost courtyards have temples dedicated to Confucius and to various monarchs of Vietnam. There are also steles which list down names snd details of hundreds of students who took the imperial examinations. Inspite of the crowds the place has an atmosphere of tranquillity.Once you have finishes your visit, you can also step into the small Ho Van cultural village, located opposite; or step into one of the cafes for a bite and a bit of caffeine. We tried the Ha Noi Cafe and it was quite decent.

reviews.author: Avid Traveler
reviews.title: Great place to visit if you're interested in history
reviews.content: It's mostly an open air university, which adds to the charm of the place. Lots of greenery, not very crowded either.It was interesting to understand the names of the various entrances. I loved the symmetry of the architecture.It's always interesting to understand the history of education in various places, and this gave such a flavor for Vietnam.We did this trip by ourselves using Grab to and from the Old Quarter, and it was very convenient.Overall, a place to visit if you are interested in history, education, and architecture.

reviews.author: Jerome B
reviews.title: Beautiful Historic Site
reviews.content: This is an important historic site in the middle of Hanoi where the bureaucracy of Vietnam was trained.  Lovely Buddhist temples and much more.  Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: NikiG1948
reviews.title: Oasis in the city
reviews.content: Beautiful serene gardens and multiple buildings. Make sure you follow the arrows as there are additional buildings in the back. The Thai Chi practitioners in the adjoining park are a lovely local bonus.

reviews.author: Christopher
reviews.title: Nice place!
reviews.content: A good place to explore in Hanoi city tour. It bears bold Asian culture, but should not stay too long

reviews.author: Pwncjn1
reviews.title: Peaceful place to visit
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit when in Hanoi, lots of info on Confuscious and his teachings, very informative and good for students to visit.

reviews.author: Wanderer
reviews.title: Merit over birthrights
reviews.content: Vietnamese dynasties applied the same selection system as the Chinese to select their intelligentsia : candidates to local, regional and state exams could originate from all layers of society.This fascinating place recalls the merits of past Mandarins, civil and military, whose names are now engraved in stones carried on turtles' backs...Not to be missed.

reviews.author: Liz H
reviews.title: Amazing structure in centre of Hanoi
reviews.content: Visited this as part of our tour of Hanoi.  Very interesting and were lucky to be the first visitors that morning, so quite quiet. Beautiful architecture.  Good insight into history of Vietnam.

reviews.author: ejc-free
reviews.title: Educational and beautiful
reviews.content: A beautiful series of pagodas with gardens in Hanoi dating back a millennium.... a must see.  Educational with the opportunity to see traditional calligraphy

reviews.author: TMOH8
reviews.title: Interesting and enjoyable
reviews.content: We found this place surprisingly interesting. At the end of a four week SE Asia trip we'd pretty much 'templed out', and so a visit to the Temple of Literature hardly warmed the cockles of our heart.Well, we got it wrong. It's thousand year history as the first Vietnamese university was actually fascinating and I found some of the architectural details impressive.I'd recommend a visit here.

reviews.author: ssterling1967@gmail.com
reviews.title: Warning. Outside Museum of Literature at exit vendors swarm, steal money and switch items.
reviews.content: Young woman selling t shirts pulled a 200,000 dong bill from my wallet and returned a 20,000 when I tried to stop her. Basically stole. Another switched the cards I chose and replaced with smaller cheaper cards. Walk away. Buy nothing from them. Deceptively good looking but very dishonest. “Please help me” they say and swarm you till YOU will be the one who needs help.

reviews.author: Michael W
reviews.title: Beautiful gardens
reviews.content: These were the prettiest gardens we saw in Ha Noi. In addition, the temple was in very good shape and interesting. Well worth a visit (when one can find the entrance, although that was not made easy by our rickshaw driver dropping us off some distance away - make sure you’re taken right to the door as it’s a long way round the perimeter).

reviews.author: Núria
reviews.title: A must in hanoi
reviews.content: Peaceful place and interesting in the middle of Hanoi. Special discount for students. We would recommend to take the audio guide.

reviews.author: romina a
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: Great experience being able to see Confucius up close. Appreciated the companion of my tour guide Dzunngg (Zoom).

reviews.author: Amanda C
reviews.title: Lots of interesting buildings set in lovely grounds full of colour
reviews.content: Entrance fee is 30,000dong (£1) so very good value, got here by Grab from old quarter for 27K, no need to use package tourExtensive range of buildings to see, all in good order with some information at each set - or you can rent an audio guide at the ticket office.The grounds are beautiful and worth a visit just for them, huge colourful butterflies and birds flitting about the trees.There are steps into each section and each building which could be a little challenging for anyone with mobility issues.Just by the exit is a small cafe with very clean washroom facilities Highly recommended

reviews.author: Tinky
reviews.title: It's okay
reviews.content: Like any other temple. Nothing extraordinary. It Was part of our tour but I would not have put this on a bucket list.

reviews.author: maureenlogan
reviews.title: Very busy
reviews.content: Lovely area with lots of interesting features, huge drum and  bell and lovely sculptures. We went during Tek very busy as singing competitions going on but still very interesting.

reviews.author: ValMacCalgary
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Interesting to see the evolution of the university over the years. Go with a guide to get the history. I loved seeing students getting their grad photos taken there.

reviews.author: LinhVu
reviews.title: Rich culture
reviews.content: The very first university of Hanoi would have many stories to tell. I was lucky enough to visit Van Mieu together with a friend who is tour guide so have been showed many pieces displayed inside Van Mieu were donated by rich Hanoian families hudreds of years ago.

reviews.author: Jay P
reviews.title: Interesting and peaceful place to visit
reviews.content: Apart from the history, this is a great location to walk through the beautiful grounds and relax located in the middle of a busy city. It is well worth the minimal fee to enjoy and capture some great photos.

reviews.author: Rosemary D
reviews.title: Confuscious was a genius
reviews.content: This Temple of Literature has a serene feeling, embodying the writings of Confuscious and hopefully imparting the moral and intellectual values he taught.

reviews.author: Stacy K
reviews.title: Quick Walk Through
reviews.content: This is worth a quick walk through to see rebuilt traditional architecture. Many locals taking photos in this complex.

reviews.author: Dianne B
reviews.title: Very interesting learning about the history of Confucius.
reviews.content: We visited the University built in 1070 where the temple was dedicated to Confucius. Beautifully coloured  statues showing Confucius and his four best disciples.Desoite wars and other disasters the temple has survived and holds relics from many past dynasties. Well worth a visit. See also the One pillar Pagoda.

reviews.author: SHo_13
reviews.title: Good little tour
reviews.content: Exploring the whole area makes it a worth while. Easily you can spent 1.5hours here. Glad that we came.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.content: Amazing, spiritual, peaceful place to visit.You will learn so much and the buildings are spectacular

reviews.author: Cass E
reviews.title: So glad I came here
reviews.content: I loved the history of the Temple of Literature. I visited alone, got the audio tour and wandered for a couple of hours. Come early to avoid crowds then have lunch at KOTO.

reviews.author: Compass59566
reviews.title: Hanoi Adventure
reviews.content: Our guide took us around the center of ancient teaching and gave us ample time to tour the place. She was very knowledgable

reviews.author: Best Days
reviews.title: So good
reviews.content: Love this amazing historical place and the incredible stories. Visited on a weekend with a lot of beautiful and happy students in graduation gowns taking photos. Will visit again.

reviews.author: kk62
reviews.title: A great facility
reviews.content: It was a recommended place to visit and proved worthy of same. It is very ornate but is showing signs of requiring attention in places.

reviews.author: Ky Nguyen
reviews.title: Vietnam 1st University
reviews.content: What a great, and wonderful  place to visit. I would prefer it to my friends. When they are in Ha Noi.

reviews.author: Terry H
reviews.title: A tribute to knowledge and Confucious.
reviews.content: Entering this serene 'campus' is a wonderful walk back in time.  Vietnam's first national university was housed here, along with wonderful 'stelae' (loose translation:  blocks of what looks like concrete) that reflect the identifying data of exceptional scholars (their names, place of birth and exceptional achievements) .  These blocks sit atop turtles (don't know the significance here - slow and steady and all that?). Originally, there were 116 of these, but 82 remain (not all are visible).Built in 1070, the layout of the buildings is impressive.  There is a wonderful statue of Confucious here and people appeared to be in prayer before it (although Confucious's teachings are not a religion) before it.  If not prayer, certainly paying homage to this great man.A lovely experience.

reviews.author: April A
reviews.title: Sweet spot
reviews.content: Once inside, you could forget you’re in Hanoi. Nice, quiet, beautiful grounds await you. Find the turtle heads that move :)

reviews.author: nina
reviews.title: Architecture Worship Historic Culture
reviews.content: An ancient complexity of history and worship of Vietnamese in a unique architecture & landscape. You will see graduates come here for group photos. Locals come to express their wishes and hope that their wishes are full filled. They have strong belief that their wishes will come true if they virtually write it on a wall.

reviews.author: Keith W
reviews.title: Lots to see
reviews.content: Most interesting temple , a fair amount of walking involved , many places for picture taking on way round

reviews.author: julia b
reviews.title: A sentence and peaceful place
reviews.content: I did enjoy wandering around the grounds, admiring the garden and seeing the architecture of the different gates. As this was used as a centre for learning for centuries, there is so much available information to the history of it and you can get a translation guide to use. In the middle courtyard there is a temple to Confusius, which has a beautifully decorated statue of the philosopher. In the farthest courtyard there are large cast iron urns with great detail, some fine gift shops and a man who specializes in Vietnamese writing and can make personalized pictures.

reviews.author: Alan R
reviews.title: Worth a trip
reviews.content: If your staying in the old quarter the temple of literature is worth a visit. You can combine it with a trip to the citadel and military museum and make a morning of it all. But by itself it is not worth a visit. It was very beautiful, but large crowds from locals make it a challenge to really enjoy the beauty.

reviews.author: jwgbusiness
reviews.title: Serene surroundings that is inviting to reflect on past educational values
reviews.content: It is obvious that there will always be the intellectual in society and Vietnam is no exception.  We visited the Ethnology Museum (various ethnic groups and ancestry), the Literature Temple and Quoc Tu Giam to see Vietnam's first university, constructed in 1070 - it's gardens and well-preserved architecture will offer a relaxing glimpse into Vietnam's past.   We recommend this as a visit especially with its calming effects. The admission price is quite reasonable.

reviews.author: Thomas W
reviews.title: Interesting and inspiring
reviews.content: A quiet and interesting place, filled with the impressive educational history of Vietnam.  Temples and stelas nicely preserved.

reviews.author: JMB50
reviews.title: Calm and beautiful
reviews.content: Such a peaceful place to visit with fantastic architecture.  This temple is dedicated to Confucius and is an inspiring place to see.  Each of the different courtyards is well maintained and laid out.  I left feeling calm and relaxed.

reviews.author: Emilie G
reviews.title: Impressive temple
reviews.content: Impressive temple, well-kept and definitely worth a visit. It has 5 different courtyards, each with its own specific features. So much history there. Plan at least an hour to visit. Cheap entrance ticket of 30k vnd. Fairly busy with tourists.

reviews.author: Elin L
reviews.title: Beautiful site - highly recommended
reviews.content: Allow an hour or so to visit this place.  We were pleasantly surprised with the upkeep of the place. As you enter through the main gate, you'll see a pond in each side of the main path.  They have beautiful lotus flowers in them. The inner courts are beautiful as well.  Good signages to explain the history and the structures within the compound.

reviews.author: Perry H
reviews.title: Vacation
reviews.content: One of my all time favorites from the architecture  and 11th. century beginning to the teaching of Confucius and higher learning. The gardens and grounds are very beautiful. You can easily spend about 2 hours plus here. Good for the whole family.

reviews.author: gamahoz
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds and gardens...
reviews.content: Dedicated to the teachings of Confucious, this complex of historical educational significance is a wonderful experience.  An oasis of calm amongst the hustle and bustle of Hanoi, there are lots of beautiful photo opportunities of the gardens, ponds, temples along with students who love to celebrate their graduation here.  It is a vast complex, so be prepared for a bit of a walk, and stepping in and out of temples - there are however places to sit, rest and reflect on the significance and beauty of your surrounds.

reviews.author: dekalbill
reviews.title: Culturally Significant
reviews.content: The tranquility of the gardens and courtyards welcome you to the Temple of Literature dedicated to education and the teachings of Confucius.  The architecture of the temples and bell tower are representative of Vietnamese style and are beautiful.  Have your guide explain the significance of the many turtle sculptures.  This is an oasis of calm within a busy city.

reviews.author: gomesmano
reviews.title: Temple
reviews.content: Walk through all the courts and listen to the stories of the past students how they got the best PhD to be rulers choices

reviews.author: MaryNML
reviews.title: Beautiful place!
reviews.content: A place with history and much more. Well preserved. The architectural design of the building gave us a sign to drop off and go in to enjoy it.

reviews.author: Raffaele M
reviews.title: Tranquility
reviews.content: This beautiful garden park and structures are the core of the Vietnamese historical respect for learning. You can stroll through gardens and ponds to temples to learning marking the long tradition of scholarship in Vietnam. Students still use the place to have graduation photos.

reviews.author: WilliamWillieWilson
reviews.title: Not much to see here
reviews.content: This was the first stop on our tour of Hanoi. I think they wanted us to start with something less impressive. There is simply not much to see here. As a temple and university, its meaning is obviously important. But the sights inside are uninteresting.If your tour guide brings you here, see it, be respectful, and enjoy yourself. If you have no tour guide and you're making a list of things to do in Hanoi, skip this one.

reviews.author: Boss0079
reviews.title: Great cultural experience
reviews.content: Short but sweet visit to the temple of literature. Not a long time really needed here, perhaps 45 minutes you can finish it all. My 8 year old said it was boring but they endured it.

reviews.author: nilintentum_reliquit
reviews.title: Worth a look of you have time
reviews.content: If you have time you can easily include this in your downtown wanderings. If you have enjoyed Hue then this may be a little of a disappointment but it is still pleasant to see.Thanks for the vote if you found this review helpful.

reviews.author: Virgil C
reviews.title: History and Culture in an Atmosphere of Peace and Tranquility
reviews.content: Be forewarned that there's an entrance fee to this attraction, but it's well worth it. You could spend several hours leisurely exploring the temples and gardens scattered throughout the extensive grounds or simply soak in the restful and relaxing atmosphere of this oasis of peace and tranquility, dedicated to learning and knowledge, located right in the heart of the bustling city. There are places for coffee and refreshments on the premises. An audio guide may be rented for a small fee at the entrance.

reviews.author: AlexfromCanada
reviews.title: Very nice and interesting place
reviews.content: Emperor were very smart choosing the best people of the country to become their mandarins - ministers. Interesting place and pleasant atmosphere

reviews.author: tontonflingueur2020
reviews.title: In the heart of Hanoï, great monument
reviews.content: Temple of literature shows the importance of knowledge and culture in ancient Vietnam, in accordance with writings of Confucius.

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: It was very nice to visit
reviews.content: It’s very nice to walk around and enjoy very picturesque with the buildings, gardens and temples.Lots of history to temple so I think it’s best to get a guide if available they can explain some of it.Lots of primary school kids visiting as well as graduation classes taking photos near the temple nice to see students/kids exploring there local temples and history.I would certainly put visiting this temple in the top 5 things to see in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Ashley G
reviews.title: Must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: This is a stunning temple that you must see while you are here!  The Chinese architecture is beautiful and it was unlike any other temple we saw while we were in Thailand or Vietnam!!

reviews.author: Bruna Iotti
reviews.title: A haven away from the chaotic city
reviews.content: This was a breath of fresh air after the walk to reach it. It was well maintained. I enjoyed the gardens. The audio guide was interesting, just the headphones that were old and not comfortable to use. I would recommend the trip, as it had an interesting old history.

reviews.author: Phils998
reviews.title: A must see.
reviews.content: We visited here with our friends from UK and we got a good deal of useful information by visiting here. Nice architecture also.

reviews.author: Karol J
reviews.title: Great place too see and relax
reviews.content: If you going around the Hanoi looking for some museums or great pictures this is the place you want to visit. Located in good proximity from the city centre. Entry fee is very cheap and there is no long waiting times. Worth visiting if you want to learn about the culture and city history.

reviews.author: Mark
reviews.title: Leave your horse at the gate!
reviews.content: A sign in the front encourages visiting scholars to leave their horses at the gate, which was a quaint and amusing touch. Amazingly, considering the brutal bombardment of Hanoi during the American War, the Temple of Literature is entirely intact although much of what was around it was reduced to rubble in the Christmas Bombings of 1972 (aka "Operation Linebacker I & II). A quiet, peaceful oasis in the otherwise chaotic environs of Hanoi, it features topiaries, reflection pools and a relaxing, park-like environment. It is near many other historical sites which makes it a great place to chill for a while before jumping on a scooter and continuing your exploration of Hanoi. Because of its trees the Temple grounds are cool on even the hottest day which, if you've ever been in Hanoi, is worthy of note.

reviews.author: Mawa N
reviews.title: Temple of Literature in Hanoi
reviews.content: This is beautiful temple and worth to visit while you are in Ha Noi. Looks a bit ancient with its carving and entrance building.

reviews.author: David D
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: Nice place for a short falk of 30-60 minutes, good architecture, nice park, interesting temples. Worth visiting.

reviews.author: Josefer M
reviews.title: Joy in my heart
reviews.content: The Turtles and their patience have taught the most amazing virtue to the Vietnamese people. it's a joy motif when the new generations are ready to share all the effort and knowledge with their country and the Temple have been ready for generations to inspire the wonderful path with his print in every step that the wisdom could fill in the life. You will be amazed. !!!

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: Must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: This was our first sight-seeing place in Vietnam. Awesome. Thoroughly recommend it. We opted for the headphones but in hindsight, not sure you need them. Some of the commentary is just trippy and they have good English signposts around the place. I found myself zoning out a bit from the audio.There are so many courtyards and areas in here and the history of the place is great. We walked in the front gate, and exited via the side exit where you drop off your headphones. Found a great little eatery with Com Ga right across the road. Allow at least 90mns for quick visit, more like 2hours if you pause and take it all in.Compared with the Citadel....not even close. This was the best thing we saw in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Todaku Babato
reviews.title: Historical and cultural stories about the Vietnamese curriculum!
reviews.content: Didnt know this place is the first national university of Vietnam! We took a BonBon bus to experience a whole day trip around Hanoi and they took me to this place. I love the ancient architecture and the stories behind the stone animals, also the development of education in Vietnam. Highly recommended if you love an antique atmosphere and learning about history & cuture!

reviews.author: Rose817
reviews.title: Amazing history over many hundreds of years
reviews.content: As part of our trip we visited this cultural icon in Hanoi. For someone from New Zealand the age of these items is amazing. Many are well preserved and there are translations available for the most important. There is also space to be outside and enjoy the gardens in lovely weather - which was nice for families.

reviews.author: V4889YSmaryd
reviews.title: Beautiful Temples
reviews.content: On our last day in Hanoi we went to visit the Temple of Literature and were impressed with the beauty and peacefulness.Very reasonable entrance fee and immaculate grounds.  I was able to learn a lot about the history of Vietnam.

reviews.author: Dharman H
reviews.title: Amazing history and a great way to spend a couple of hours
reviews.content: Lots of history and reading up about TsunTsu and his disciples and how it affects Vietnamese life was educating. Good place to let the kids run around as well.

reviews.author: nooksoftheworld
reviews.title: A must see historical site
reviews.content: This is one of the main attractions in Hanoi that's worth a visit. This historical site is an old university.

reviews.author: Ken S
reviews.title: A highlight of Hanoi visit
reviews.content: We had a wonderful guide to help us understand the importance of this university in the history of vietnam.  The grounds are very nice, but understanding the history makes it special.

reviews.author: lawlessrose
reviews.title: Good insight into Vietnamese History and Traditions
reviews.content: It is a little oasis in the middle of a bustling city. Very easy to walk around look inside the temples. The shrines are beautifully presented and have statues of Confucius and scholars that then followed in his footsteps.  We spent  no more than an hour here. Definitely worth a look

reviews.author: Stephen C
reviews.title: Fascinating for history buffs
reviews.content: Worth getting the audio guide. It gives you the unique history of the place and explains the significance of the displays in Vietnamese history. Otherwise it would just seem like annoy other temple.

reviews.author: eytanin
reviews.title: Such a pleasant place!
reviews.content: In the Heart of Hanoi, just a stone throw from the hustle and bustle town, you can find this island of tranquility, knowledge, and beauty.  do not miss a visit to the past. many items on display and you will gain a lot of knowledge in this place!

reviews.author: AMMG01
reviews.title: Worth the time?
reviews.content: A bit disappointing. We visited so many temples in Hanoi and this was by far the worst one we visited!

reviews.author: Ann N
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: The Vietnam National University where knowledge and nature blends. An excellent location to relax your body and mind. enjoy a sugarcane juice.

reviews.author: Denis T
reviews.title: Peaceful
reviews.content: Very cheap entrance fee. From the moment you enter there is a peace and tranquility that comes over you. The quietness in the hustle and bustle of the city is amazing. Very informative and extremely interesting facts. Take some time to just sit and reflect. Very well worth a visit

reviews.author: Bag-of-bones
reviews.title: Educational
reviews.content: We had a private guide who explained the origin of the temple and the culture of the people of Vietnam.

reviews.author: Adnan
reviews.title: Great Example of Vietnamese Architecture, Education & Culture
reviews.content: It is a great showcase of Vietnamese architecture, education system, and a peaceful place to escape the hustle and noise of the city. I really enjoyed seeing the temple and the exhibits inside showing the preparation and materials used by the students. There are also some great statues and other relics on display. It is very well maintained.I had a guide (did not get the audio guide so I can't comment) who explained some of the details of the temple and tablets, but her knowledge was not complete as she was part of the city scooter tour I was taking. But, what she did explain was very interesting. So, to really appreciate the historical significance, design elements, and meanings of the various elements you need a guide.

reviews.author: EU family in HK
reviews.title: very interesting, peaceful and educational
reviews.content: a must see when in Hanoi. the audio guide is very helpful to understand the significance and history.

reviews.author: Dr. Issa Abu-Dayyeh
reviews.title: Lovely temple
reviews.content: This is truly a nice temple. 4 pools on sides as you go in, then a middle courtyard with turtles carrying stones with names of students on it. The site seems to be the oldest school in Hanoi.At the end of the space, a Confucius temple is found, quite elegant.The gardens and nature also provide a nice escape from the crowded green less city center.Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Joel K
reviews.title: Beautiful site and great visit... with extra treat
reviews.content: This site was quite informative and great to do on our first day in Hanoi. It was not highly touristed. Calming after an early morning tour of the markets and a Vietnamese breakfast of beef noodle soup. The best part is a photo shoot was taking place of Vietnamese models in beautiful gowns and plumed hats and I was able to take some terrific pictures.

reviews.author: Bette1274
reviews.title: My favorite in Hanoi
reviews.content: This is the most beautiful and peaceful site I visited while in Hanoi.  I would recommend more than one time there because it really has the best of everything, architecture, history, serenity, and beauty.

reviews.author: JPollock311
reviews.title: Cultural Center
reviews.content: The cultural center was worth the visit in this busy city center.  We did the audio tour, but got boarded quickly, I would recommend passing on that, but then we aren’t museum folks.  Found great pho near the exit

reviews.author: Suki P
reviews.title: Temple of Literature & National University
reviews.content: Enjoyed leisure walk around this place built in traditional style Vietnamese architecture. Also, a good place to take some interesting photography

reviews.author: Amityadventure
reviews.title: A great place to see in busy Hanoi
reviews.content: It is an excellent example of the Vietnamese looking after education of their people, this is a 'must do' in Hanoi. Beautiful grounds and headsets with information in English for each of the sections

reviews.author: Dan
reviews.title: Beautiful temple in downtown Hanoi
reviews.content: Beautiful gardens, temples and architecture. Beautiful area to help break up the city vibe. Definitely worth checking out

reviews.author: cliff1608
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: Really lovely place to visit, peaceful walk around gardens and an amazing temple. Nice little break from the mayhem of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Mette P
reviews.title: Green and quite area
reviews.content: This is a nice area with a huge and quite park where you easily can take a break in the very busy city

reviews.author: Rashid Isa Rishi AlHeddi
reviews.title: Temple of Literature - Hanoi- North Vietnam
reviews.content: Temple of Literature & Culture is a Temple paying homage to Confucius in Hanoii. The temple hosts the Imperial Academy, Vietnam's first national university. Its a scenic peaceful site giving respect to the chosen students who are listed on Stone Tablets and the Library . The temple was built in 1070 at the time of Emperor Tong. Its artfully carved has various statues and also large Metal Drums and Bells and has a door through which the King could enter and side doors for others to enter.

reviews.author: Jessie K
reviews.title: confucius!
reviews.content: Very quiet place with a lot of wisdom. I found it interested to hear the stories on the audio. However the quality of it was not that good as i found as the womans museum (which was excellent by the way) it still gave me some more detailed information about the students who where studying there. It was a privilege and they ad to go  through many systems especially values to become a student. Very strict!Also what they owned and had when they studied which was very simple is shown in the museum.

reviews.author: Jason C
reviews.title: A quiet place in the city
reviews.content: A nice little temple in the city. You can take a stroll around the gardens and walk around and explore some of the temples. To fully appreciate the experience I would recommend getting an audio book to fully understand the history of the site.

reviews.author: E.L
reviews.title: A beautiful experience
reviews.content: I was not expecting to be moved but I was. The gardens and half shaded lotus ponds were pretty. The flow between courtyards, gardens and temples felt natural and meditative. And inside the temples the statues and offerings were rich and colorful. A real treat in the midst of a very busy city...

reviews.author: MarkfromtheIsland
reviews.title: Worth a visit - don't expect too, too much
reviews.content: It takes under an hour to visit this site.  Temples in Vietnam are not religious places - rather they are places where one goes to pay tribute to leaders and to those who have made a difference.  This site is mostly a tribute to the teachers and philosophers who brought higher education to the area.  People like Confucius.Worth a quick visit

reviews.author: Courtney
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: I visited the Temple of Literature on my free day in Hanoi with some of my Intrepid tour group. It was super interesting and far larger than I would have imagined.

reviews.author: quavec
reviews.title: Nice compound

reviews.author: Gastronomist52
reviews.title: Review for Solo Travellers - Very Good Audio Guide!
reviews.content: I visited the Temple of Literature as a Solo Traveller. At the risk of duplicating content from the other 10,000 TripAdvisor reviews, I'll focus on the aspects significant to Solo Travellers like myself.The Temple is easy to find, and easy to get into. This is one of the most ornate and beautiful places I visited in Hanoi. If you just like to stroll around and look at the beautiful buildings and scenery, or to do drawings of intricate architecture, or to really dig into the history, this is a great option. (Note that the best architectural stuff is right at the front gate, so you don't even need to pay to get in an see this part.) As a photography buff, I snapped over 200 photos in and around this place!Audio Tour Guide - This was a very good audio guide, almost totally consistent with the actual attraction. The physical guide device was worn out and in poor condition, but at least it used the earpads rather than some gross earbuds that got stuck into a multitude of ear canals before mine.The actual content was very well presented and informative, giving you a real insight into what life was like in Medieval Times. It had a good mix of history focusing on the how the Temple was used, the individual buildings and sights within the Temple, and also some individual stories of historical people who visited and studied inside. I feel it was a good financial value, and definitely recommend this guide if you're going it alone. If you actually want to listen to everything, you'll need at least 3 hours.A few items were out of order, and it was unclear how exactly to access to very back part of the Temple. But eventually I found my way around the side, into the back, to see the final parts.Overall it was a great use of my time, and I definitely recommend that you dedicate half a day at this Temple.

reviews.title: Fascinating piece of History
reviews.content: We went with a tour guide friend and so gained maximum benefit from her knowledge. It is the most beautiful place and a quiet contrast to the bustling city outside. The 5 courtyards have distinct roles from the entrance, to a place of reflection and thought before taking the exams, to the temple devoted to Confucius, the exam courtyard and the university itself. Each stunning in its architecture and laid out gardens. The turtle stones devoted to each year of students listing names, places of birth and exam level achieved..(only 83 remains from the 200 or so originals. Much has been rebuilt to the original form after the damage from various wars. Apparently the high steps into the buildings are designed to make you look down as a sign of respect! Absolutely a must if you have any interest in the origins of universities or just love Asian Historical architecture. Many photo opportunities.

reviews.author: Woon29
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: There are interesting history on the scholars that our guide explained. The different turtles represent different level of scholarship which is interesting. There are a number of bonsai there.

reviews.author: Lynkster
reviews.title: A great example of the Confucian aspect of past Vietnamese culture
reviews.content: Vietnam's first national university established in the 11th century, it has very remarkably, survived wars and time to the present day. Princes and sons of the nobility were educated here, and the names of successful students who passed the difficult exams are inscribed on stone tablets within the inner courtyard. The grounds are quite extensive, containing gardens, courtyards and temples to Confucius and his disciples. Note that guards here will be more stringent in enforcing the "cover-up" rule on visitors showing too much skin, and provide free robes for offenders (which are actually pretty cool, designed like medieval Vietnamese scholar robes). If you're interested in the whole system of education that formed the basis of the University, getting a tour guide might be useful. Otherwise, the few signs that have been installed in each area provide a decent amount of explanation of the buildings and structures.

reviews.author: Brad M
reviews.title: Cultural and peaceful
reviews.content: Beautiful and quiet area in the heart of busy Hanoi. Worth a visit, to enjoy the maximum benefit of the place do a tour or grab a headset at the ticket booth. Get there early before the tour groups rock up for a more peaceful time. Such a wonderful place full of culture and history!!

reviews.author: Nikola S
reviews.title: Nice thing to see
reviews.content: It's nice to learn for how long this University excist. Hole history is fascinanting. It takes about 20 minutes ti go through hole thing...

reviews.author: Kuper_IL

reviews.content: A nice garden and ancient buildings tha demonstrate the importance of education in ancient Vietnam (11th century). You can also see demonstrations of traditional musical instruments used in Vietnam.

reviews.author: Auldprop
reviews.title: Tour

reviews.author: Susannah P
reviews.title: Pretty architecture

reviews.author: Tui Munday
reviews.title: Ancient History Lesson
reviews.content: One of the only urban sites in Hanoi where you can really appreciate that this city is more than 1000 years old.

reviews.author: RobandJoPerth
reviews.title: Amazing and full of surprises.
reviews.content: A fantastic cultural site. There was so much to see and do which gave a deep insight into the life of young men seeking service with king.  Amazing architecture, and the collection of artifacts are the highlights.

reviews.author: Richard P
reviews.title: Much enjoyed

reviews.author: rickalexwestoby
reviews.title: What history a must for Hanoi

reviews.author: Jack T
reviews.title: Star attraction in Hanoi, by far.

reviews.author: Jacob Danner

reviews.content: I enjoyed my visit to the site very much. So much to see. Wonderful architecture and decor. Lots of beautiful plants and trees and some fabulous planters and pots. Lots of history to discover about this 1000-year-old temple.

reviews.author: murielcsmith
reviews.title: Learning a little about Vietnamese history of education.
reviews.content: Well worth a visit, plenty to see and read about. Headphones available at entrance giving description of each numbered item of interest. No need for a paid tour, you can pay at entrance. Much of the site is open so can be very hot.

reviews.author: Wayne H
reviews.title: Intellectual history
reviews.content: Very interesting site to visit. Apparently rebuilt after being bombed during the Vietnam War. Lots of history and amazing how few students actually passed the stringent exams and became honored.

reviews.author: edenxo1212
reviews.title: Temple of Literature & National University
reviews.content: The very first academy in Vietnam, which belongs to a french-built architecture complex. Its own construction traits still able to remain almost identically the same, even after lots of conservation.

reviews.author: Aliana S.

reviews.author: andyarnoldstj
reviews.title: Temple of Literature

reviews.author: poidee77
reviews.title: Literaturtempel
reviews.content: interesting Vietnamese history really worth to visit   so ist easier to understnad this wonderful and charming country

reviews.author: happy tourism vietnam🇻🇳😊🙂
reviews.title: Van mieu quoc tu giam
reviews.content: This is the first university in Vietnam.  When the high school graduates come here to touch the turtle's head, they hope to be lucky in their university entrance exams.😊

reviews.author: NagolNZ
reviews.title: An amazing piece of history!
reviews.content: The oldest university in Vietnam. Spectacular scenery and information!! Visited with Intrepid tour party.

reviews.author: Ian H
reviews.title: Great gardens!
reviews.content: An amazing University where you travel through the levels of acheivement, the history and Prettiness of this place is well worth visiting

reviews.author: Sendilvelan S
reviews.title: Confucius, Bonsai tree Temple of Literature Temple of Culture
reviews.content: Vietnam's first university an interesting history you can enjoy. Confucius, Bonsai tree is the oldest temple of Literature or Temple of Culture. reviews.author: devontravels1
reviews.title: great cultural experience
reviews.content: If you have time this is an inexpensive place to go in Hanoi that's really pretty.  They have lawn animals carved from bushes and you get to see the ancient vietnamese architecture.  A lot was lost during wars but this is still authentic.

reviews.author: Samuel Piette
reviews.title: Amazing exploration into the first ever University in Vietnam

There were tons of sophisticated features in a single one ancient architectural complex. When i get there, i have a chance to maneuver all the way around it, through every single blocks, which is so cool for a person that got a big interest in architecture. Me and my girl also have a chance to put on Vietnam's traditional clothes and taking pictures with it

reviews.author: Tracey G
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Great to see such history. Could be busy. Very peaceful. Good to wander around.  Taking pictures is no problemGood clean toilets

reviews.author: Hoang Do
reviews.title: Great Experience
reviews.content: If you want to get a feel of feudal Vietnamese architecture, this is the perfect place. You can also take great photos at the temple of literature. Beware that the temple is very crowded during national holidays, especially during Lunar New Year time.

reviews.author: Susan M
reviews.title: A peaceful retreat
reviews.content: A peaceful retreat if you go early. It is a STUNNING temple complex dedicated to Confucious and scholarship.

reviews.author: k2711
reviews.title: Pretty
reviews.content: Didn't think it would be very interesting but glad we went as it was bigger and prettier than we thought it would be, worth a visit.

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: Be respectful
reviews.content: When entering any temple do not take pictures Please do not enter if you have shorts onOr shoulders uncovered

reviews.author: HF
reviews.title: Tranquil place in the middle of a bustling business area
reviews.content: Step in the temple and it immediately feels like you're not in downtown Hanoi anymore - so peaceful!

reviews.author: mrswills1
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: I found this temple fascinating. The long, rich history of learning in Vietnam is celebrated. The display of documents is interesting; the statues of the Kings impressive. I was also proud of the contribution the Australian government made towards information boards that educate visitors.

reviews.author: Moimak
reviews.title: Sweaty experience but worth it.
reviews.content: Take an AC taxi and try to visit as early as possible to beat the heat and the obnoxious tour groups who are an invasive species.Better yet... Make friends with a local bigwig and visit outside the official hours.

reviews.author: Sunday
reviews.title: Nice place with an excellent tour guide.
reviews.content: This place is much bigger than some pagodas I visited in Ninh Binh. But the highlight of my day trip is a female tour guide ( Rose) from Swallow Travel. She is very informative and lovely. It seems local pp is very proud of their history 😎

reviews.author: EM-Han
reviews.title: much Ado about nothing

The only reason to go is people watching, I especially enjoyed a rebellious Vietnamese 5 year old that reminded me of my own single mindedness at his age. He was certainly a lot to deal with for his distressed parents.

reviews.author: Bon Olij

reviews.content: If you are interested in ancient Vietnam, this attraction is for you! For an extra 50,000 VND, I highly recommend the audio tour. I wouldn’t have realised the significance of certain parts without it. We spent 2 hours including a stop for a drink.

reviews.author: Dhennver Ng
reviews.title: First university
reviews.content: This is the first university in Hanoi. It's beautiful with well maintained garden and the buildings are well restored. Confucious is worshipped here. There is an entrance fee.

reviews.author: happytwanderer

reviews.author: Ash Mehta

reviews.author: Indonesian-Jetset
reviews.title: They call it the first university

reviews.author: Stephanie J
reviews.title: This is a must do in Hanoi.
reviews.content: Put this on the top of your list. The grounds are beautiful and seeped in tradition. You'll get great photo opportunities and learn something along the way.

reviews.author: MarjofromBrissie
reviews.title: Enjoyable visit
reviews.content: We purchased entrance tickets and audio guides. The audio guides contained a lot more detail than I needed but was useful to understand each of the areas we passed through. The first areas were gardens which were lush and green and the areas further contained buildings with various shrines. We saw some amazing specimens of desert roses which must have been very old. Vietnamese students come here to pray for good luck for their studies.

reviews.author: Momo_yeu_sunny
reviews.title: Absolute highlight
reviews.content: A beautiful 2000 year old complex that was used to train Vietnam's greatest scholars, poets and politicians in ancient history. It's both a beautiful historical relic and a relaxed and shady walk through a garden oasis in the middle of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Sade
reviews.title: Incredibly awesome

The temple of literature is considered one of the most important monuments in Hanoi.  There’s so many beautifully carved statues and stones. Definitely a place not to miss.   Ticket entrance 30,000VD = $1.50 US   Awesomely nice.

reviews.author: bushroda
reviews.title: Fascinating place away from the chaotic motorcycles and cars.
reviews.content: Fascinating place away from the chaotic motorcycles and cars.We spent an interesting couple of hours in this peaceful oasis.

reviews.author: Tracee Edmondson
reviews.title: Historical Gem
reviews.content: I learned of this university in passing as a student leading the free walking tour Hanoi mentioned it.  When the tour concluded I researched the location and walked there two days later.  WHAT ... A ... GEM!!!  So much culture, history and beauty!

reviews.author: Liz W
reviews.title: Favorite site in Hanoi
reviews.content: Hands down my favorite site in Hanoi. The plaques we're informational. The landscaping was beautiful. A wonderful place to sit down and write your postcards or reflect. Must see!

reviews.author: Gordon F

reviews.content: Visit theFirst University in Hanoi and walk through the temple grounds and absorb the history. We spent only half an hour here but there is a 54 minute audio tour of you prefer.

reviews.author: SMK

reviews.author: alex l

reviews.author: ExplorerGabor

reviews.content: Our HanoiKids guides took us to the Temple of Literature and explained the history and key points.  It was interesting and took less than one hour.

reviews.author: BigFoodBigTipsBigFun
reviews.title: It's okay as a time filler. Not sure what the fuss is about.
reviews.content: It's alright. Decent way to spend a couple of hours, a bit overrated though. Nice little walk through the gardens whilst taking in some history. I recommend the audio book.

reviews.author: Heather D

reviews.author: Hanoi Traveler
reviews.title: Interesting history about the temple

reviews.author: terriw1212
reviews.title: Peaceful
reviews.content: It is hard to believe the hustle of Hanoi is outside the walls of this peaceful garden.  The buildings are beautiful, the history fascinating, and the gardens are peaceful. Spend the time (and $) to get the audio guide (if you do not have your own guide) and take it all in, it's worth it!

reviews.author: Aine 🐱
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Popped in to take a look. Well worth a visit, nice and peaceful inside, plus it has a very interesting history. But take an umbrella if you are visiting this time of year!

reviews.author: KGB777
reviews.title: Ancient temple complex in the centre of Hanoi
reviews.content: This is an impressive ancient temple complex in the centre of Hanoi. There's a small entrance fee for adults, but kids are free. We visited in late July in the heat of the day but it was still quite crowded. One of the most significant attractions in Hanoi, so definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: RA
reviews.title: Very Interesting
reviews.content: A MUST see when visiting Hanoi ! Our guide was very knowledgeable and the temple was very interesting to see and learn about !

reviews.author: Meti2
reviews.title: Interesting info about Confucianism
reviews.content: Interesting destonation worth visiting in Hanoi. You get a glimpse of the history and especially of Confucius and his disceples

reviews.author: True Vietnam - Gorgeous Local Experience

reviews.content: This area is the first university in Vietnam. It was built under Ly Thanh Tong’s dynasty more than one thousand years ago. It is a historic and breathtaking place. Students usually come here to pray for luck in their exams.

reviews.author: Ushandra
reviews.title: Confucius...
reviews.content: This is another very historical must-see, even if just for the many awesome Bonzais.It's a university of sorts with scholars chosen being sent here.

reviews.author: fishfamily5
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: Had an interesting history. had a guided tour of this site which helped with all of its past history which we found to be of interest.

reviews.author: matwen2016
reviews.title: well maintained temple area
reviews.content: historic site within the city of Hanoi. A perfect place to wind down from all the noise and traffic.

reviews.author: Madame_Trey
reviews.title: Beautiful dedication to learning
reviews.content: The temple is not only an important piece of Vietnamese history but beautiful in its own right.The grounds are incredibly well kept and well laid out. I would recommend having a guide to show you the intricacies you might otherwise miss. ..

reviews.author: ExVotoFatum
reviews.title: Quiet place in busy city
reviews.content: Take the audio guide and you will learn  a lot about Vietnam’s first „ private“ university , founded about 1000 years ago. A nice day to see, not exceptional, but important for understanding history .

reviews.author: John A
reviews.title: Tranquility in bedlam!
reviews.content: VND30k gets you into a tranquil park and away from the throng of pushy vendors at the front gate. Garden walks with local fauna lead to temples and exotic university buildings. A good 3 hour escape.

reviews.author: doctorfoxtrot
reviews.title: Educational perspective
reviews.content: Another historical place on the educational sense. 30 mins to 1 hour visit would be enough . Tranquil at first then once busloads of tourists come in the morning, everything can be chaotic . One of the early leaders of philosophy and educational, Confucius highlights this place. Afterward , souvenir shops abound for unique gifts . I uploaded some photos .

reviews.author: roselyn
reviews.title: A VERY MEMORABLE
reviews.content: This event is very memorable to me, when i was a second year high school my teacher discuss about the temple and i cant still believe it that i already step up in this temple. The temple is very clean and organized. Thank you

reviews.author: Alex3004
reviews.title: Great place to visit!
reviews.content: Absolutely must when in Hanoi. Beautiful temple with long history ! Great to visit in any any weather.

reviews.author: Liz G
reviews.title: Very interesting visit
reviews.content: We were shown around the place by a local who explained the different parts of the site from the front gate with the small  “fish” who then grow and learn to become a “fierce dragon” as the student progresses through the academic learning structure. The new part behind the main building was a bit of a let down but overall it was an interesting visit and not to be missed as it explains much about the varied culture of Vietnam. Confucius had a lot of influence here! We absolute loved the bonsai trees within the site. Very beautiful.

reviews.author: Michelle B
reviews.title: A beautiful temple, but not much else there
reviews.content: We went to the Temple of Literature just before a massive downpour, but I don't feel like we missed out on much because of the rain. The temple grounds are beautiful, but I didn't learn much about the true historical significance of the site. It seems like there are lots of opportunities for the temple to host educational activities and to create interactive exhibits of some kind. As it was, it was just a very beautifully cared for part of Hanoi's history.

reviews.author: foodie2430
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: This is a very tranquil garden in the heart of Hanoi if you visit it in the morning. In the afternoon there are lots of tourists.

reviews.author: Julianne
reviews.title: Get the audio guide!
reviews.content: The temple of literature is very reasonably priced. Even after springing for the audio guide, I only paid 80,000VND. I would definitely recommend this as you get a lot more detail than if you just read the placards.

reviews.author: Vickie Nguyen
reviews.title: Visit the oldest university in Vietnam
reviews.content: One of the most popular attractions in Hanoi because it invents the first higher education for Vietnamese history, and it is a few architecture still protected since old kingdom.

reviews.author: AthinaK
reviews.title: A Beautiful Temple
reviews.content: This was such an amazing place. The minute you walk inside you find yourself in the middle of a beautiful garden and suddenly all the noise of the city disappears. The Temple of Confucius which was the first university in Vietnam is beautiful but it is the peace and calm of this place that really makes the difference. Not to be missed!!

reviews.author: Harvey S
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Walked up to the sight and was impressed immediately.  This place gives you a level of culture and traditions.  Interesting that it was first a university and now lots of areas to walk and see the different temples.  Nice grounds to wander around and take pictures and move along.  A must to visit.

reviews.author: Natalia M
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Three patios very nicely preserved. Nice buildings. Praying altars. Our girls could play around with ease.

reviews.author: klitgaardj
reviews.title: First university in a beautiful setting
reviews.content: Impressive and well preserved temple that was the first university of Hanoi. Its located in a very beautiful garden which provides a nice break from the busy streets.Beside the main temple and a small lake, inside you will also see lists of previous scholars are encarved in stone templates reciding on large stone turtles.

reviews.author: Jupiter81
reviews.title: Best temple in Hanoi
reviews.content: A place not to miss to understand the level of culture of Vietnam traditions. Very interesting to walk and see all the different temples where old Hanoi scholars went to learn. All in excellent conservation state.

reviews.author: Barry H
reviews.title: Relaxing in a busy city
reviews.content: Beautiful place to visit and get away from the hustle and bustle of the city. The grounds are well-cared for, and there's a lot for everyone to see. We stayed in the Old Quarter, so it was easily accessible by walking.

reviews.author: Sofia
reviews.title: Beautiful place!
reviews.content: This is certainly a beautiful places and can be a serene and calm visit (if you can avoid the big groups). The architecture and the gardens are worth seeing if you have enough time in the city.However, the information given was not great, especially if you come from a different cultural background, so if you're visiting on your own don't expect to understand everything.

reviews.author: Steve
reviews.title: Oasis of calm
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature is an oasis of calm in the midst of a hectic city. Its five courtyards culminate in the Temple of Confucious. This was the site of the first University in Vietnam dating back 1,000 years and huge turtle stellae hold the roll of honour of the institution. We were lucky enough to visit whilst graduation celebrations were taking place but even without this the Temple is of great interest. Some signage in English but audio and English speaking guides are available. Probably worth a stop of between 1 and 2 hours. Situated just south of the "main" sight seeing destinations of The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, Presidential Palace and One Pillar Pagoda, this Temple can easily be included in your own walking tour of the area especially if you are based in the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Nikki W
reviews.title: Beautiful peaceful gardens
reviews.content: I thought this place had the potential to be boring, but it wasn't at all. I didn't get the audio tour, just walked around and read the info boards. I felt like it was a pretty good amount of info

reviews.author: Chandrashekar Naik
reviews.title: Nice one
reviews.content: We had been to this place and experience was good, weather was too humid and didn’t enjoy too much.Otherwise this temple as very interesting story. This temple architecture is part of currency,Vietnam dong.you can click for some beautiful pics surrounding to this temple.Nice to visit during your spare time.

reviews.author: Ivica
reviews.title: Historic place
reviews.content: Having a guide is highly recommended, if you are not familiar with Vietnamese history. Interesting to see students and scholars coming to pay their respect at the Khai Thanh Temple.

reviews.author: FlipViet
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Great historical place. Better to visit with a guide to understand what you are looking at. Bring water, hat/ umbrella, and wear  comfortable walking shoes.

reviews.author: Sharif Razi Al Mahmud
reviews.title: It is again another Historical & Holy Place in Hanoi city
reviews.content: People can visit there to see the old structure. Normally calm place but weather is too hot specially in August.

reviews.author: Tim L

reviews.content: A fantastic site with 2 x temples, many bonsai and a heap of turtle statues. Fairly cheap to enter and some great souvenirs to purchase afterwards.

reviews.author: AEGHOUSTON
reviews.title: Wonderful Experience
reviews.content: I missed this place on my first visit to Hanoi and I’m so glad I went this time. It’s an absolutely lovely place, seeped in history and cultural significance. It’s mostly outdoors, so be prepared for that. Also, there is a dress code, so dress as you would for any temple- longer pants, covered shoulders.

reviews.author: VibrantAurora
reviews.title: Nice if you know how to appreciate
reviews.content: I thought it was quite interesting to see the traditional scrolls of the ancient emperors, ancient banners, structures and photos, etc. of the Temple of Literature. One of the few places we visited as part of our city tour.

reviews.author: Clark Rojas
reviews.title: Ancient Tradition of Education
reviews.content: I was told by my guide that this place is the 1st University in Vietnam, many famous doctors from their history have received education and discipline of the arts from here.Also, the site can be seen in 100,000VND bill.

reviews.author: Gordo C
reviews.title: Only visit if you’re really into temples
reviews.content: This will sound a little crass, however I found the temples to be a little lacking. They are quite pretty to look at but are not particularly engaging or fascinating. I understand this is because I’m not particularly spiritual; however unless you are willing to spend and additional 50,000 VND, and are very into the pursuit of academic prowess this is just another temple. I found the temples dedicated to the 1st and 2nd emperors of Vietnam far more interesting because of their historical significance.

reviews.author: Albert Z
reviews.title: Beautiful historical site
reviews.content: Small, but beautiful.  Definitely worth the minimal entry fee if you're into history or cool photos/photo ops.  If you're not, probably not worth checking out.

reviews.author: sophie d
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: It was a nice visit, especially because accompanied with a local studen on a free half day tour. Her explanations were very useful to understand the constructions, the idea between the draws on  the wall, the gates and orher objects

reviews.author: Mark H
reviews.title: Interesting and worthwhile
reviews.content: The temple allows for a greater understanding of Vietnam history and culture and respect for learning. The temple is fascinating for design and architecture. It allows an understanding of religious aspects in Vietnam. I would suggest going with a local guide . I had a guide book but it was not enough.

reviews.author: Avihay_Efrati
reviews.title: An impressive historical site
reviews.content: Interesting site with historical background. You need to visit it if in Hanoi. Worth visiting with a local guide.

reviews.author: susan1819
reviews.title: Nice place to visit
reviews.content: This is around the corner from the Fine Arts Museum and you can rent an audio guide to take around the compound. It is pretty and shows the influence of the Chinese in early Vietnam. There is a temple to Confucius but what is more interesting is the importance placed on education and scholars.

reviews.author: jaysitt
reviews.title: Hanoi short trip
reviews.content: An amazing historical centre. A calming place. Beautifully manicured gardens. It quite reasonably priced at 30,000 Dong and free for kids below yrs old. A must place to visit in Hanoi

reviews.author: maryntessa

This walled compound with 5 separate courtyards was both interesting and peaceful. Inexpensive souvenirs, beer, coconut milk, etc just outside at the end.

reviews.author: Carrielee
reviews.title: The first National University of Vietnam
reviews.content: I was really supprised to realise that. This site was built before noble Cambridge University. It was for youths of Madarins to join and later they would follow their parents to lead the country.

reviews.author: dbraga5150

reviews.author: heeminjeong
reviews.title: Another temple to go
