reviews.author: Tito Satriyo
reviews.title: Oldest university in Hanoi
reviews.content: This building built as a university in 1070 dedicated to Confucius, scholars and sages, the building is  well preserved and is a great example of traditional-style Vietnamese architectureRed doors, unique books made by the stone, picturesque atmosphere.How to get there? Use your google map and walk or by Grab....easy.

reviews.author: shaily.pate
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: If you love to learn history & architecture of Vietnam. This is a very good place for that. ancient statues & temple was amazing. Atmosphere was very good & quiet amongst busy streets in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Sean P
reviews.title: Historical beauty
reviews.content: Very impressive museum. We enjoyed an English speaking guided tour as part of a 4 hour scooter tour of Hanoi - highly recommend. Dress for the warm weather and keep hydrated, lots of mini marts sell large bottles of water for $11,000VND, try to avoid buying water from people on the street, price is highly inflated.

reviews.author: Travels with my Belly
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: S beautiful place of learning and a monument to knowledge and education. The location of the very first university in the country.It's really beautiful and Interesting. Recommended for a visit. I spent a few hours here as a part of a tour. The guide explained the history and any questions I had.

reviews.author: giji365
reviews.title: One of the must sees in Hanoi
reviews.content: A much revered place with lot of history around it. ?It's the temple of Confucius in Hanoi which hosts their Imperial university - the first one in Hanoi. The temple honours Vietnam’s finest scholars and signifies the beginning of a uniform educational system in Vietnam. It countains 5 courtyards, about 9 ponds and a temple for Confucius and his disciples.

reviews.author: Steve W
reviews.title: Tranquil setting, significant site.
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature or Temple of Culture includes Vietnam's first university; 'The Imperial Academy' and one of the few Confucian Temples in the country.I found the temples the most interesting sights here, but the rest is still very impressive.

reviews.author: Sainesy
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Lovely gardens in the heart of Hanoi. There is enough to see and read, worth a visit for an hour or two (depending on how much you want to see). Great for photos too

reviews.author: Aneta B
reviews.title: Nice place.
reviews.content: A very nice place to visit if you’re in Hanoi. The ticket was 30K Vietnamese dong (very cheap) and it was definitely worth it. Both, the nature and the architecture, are beautiful and you can expand your knowledge by reading one of many different history cards around the area.

reviews.author: fozjon
reviews.title: Historically significant
reviews.content: This is the symbol of Hanoi. The first university in Vietnam. There are a number of Confucian temple type structures. They are interesting, beautiful and ancient. I've never seen these before. Perhaps our tour guide just overwhelmed us a bit with too much information

reviews.author: IAM ADRIANG
reviews.title: A humble suprise in the hectic city
reviews.content: After speaking  to our lovely hotel manager upon arrival the first  thing she recommend  we  visit  was this place...We thought what could be so good about a museum  of literature, a few relics, a bunch of books...big deal. It was just the opposite...that's all I really want to say. Absolutely  mind blowing time periods and fascinating from start to end, we even had authentic scrolls made with words of wisdom authenticated, stamped and all.Defiantly  get down there ...there is a lot of tourists but most are forgiving for you to get a good photo. These are  few photos I don't want to ruin it for you.

reviews.author: Zindabaad
reviews.title: Tour
reviews.content: Worth a visit but you must must have a good guide. Very nice architecture and building  the  story of Confuses and the manner in which the University was established is very endearing. The culture of the Vietnamese is all based on respect and culture.  You just can’t fault these people for the happiness they show. Visit the site and open your minds to how true geniuses once had the best ideas on life.

reviews.author: Prisca
reviews.title: Beautiful temple. Sit down and enjoy the atmosphere.
reviews.content: It's worth it to go early to admire this beautiful spot in Hanoi.The temple is absolutely georgrous and you can take amazing pictures of the architecture, the plants and of yourself of course.

reviews.author: M S
reviews.title: historical place
reviews.content: you can know about the history and culture of Vietnamese and Chinese. can capture the temple area beautiful pictures

reviews.author: Govindan N
reviews.title: A good place to visit
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature is a place of study rather than a religious landmarkThe Temple of Literature is one of Hanoi’s most picturesque tourist attractions. Originally built as a university in 1070 is dedicated to Confucius, scholars and sages. The building is a superb example of traditional-style Vietnamese architecture.Temple of Literature has now become a memorial to education and literature. Originally the university only accepted aristocrats, the elite and royal family members as students before eventually opening its doors to brighter ‘commoners’. Successful graduates had their names engraved on a stone which can be found on top of the stone turtles.There are five courtyards at the temple, two with landscaped gardens, the third having pond and the fourth courtyard is called the Sage Courtyard and features a statue of Confucius and a house of ceremonies, and the last courtyard is Thai Hoc in which stands a large drum and bell tower.The layout of the temple is said to based on the birthplace of Confucius.Opening Hours: Tuesday - Sunday 8:30 - 11:30 & 13:30 - 16:30Entry Fee : VND 10,000

reviews.author: Coolfamily5
reviews.title: Hanoi Confucious Temple of Literature
reviews.content: Many levels of architecture and Gardens and bay, với beautiful traditional Chinese influences on the architecture. Lots of beautiful large bonsai and ponds. Large outdoor city Bell and traditional city drum, beautiful temple right at the back.

reviews.author: steadfast90
reviews.title: Worth a visit.
reviews.content: Lovely gardens in a very relaxing and calming environment.A great way to escape the hustle and bustle of Hanoi itself.  A great shop at the exit with beautiful quality gifts to remind you of your visit. Be careful once leaving as we took a taxi, as we walked there in searing heat and humidity,really tried to rip us off!

reviews.author: Kate09112788
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Visited the temple as we were told it was a must do. Beautiful gardens and very interesting history. Was very hot and muggy though so take lots of water and a fan to keep cool!!

reviews.author: Ian W
reviews.title: So much history in one location
reviews.content: A rich cultural experience in Hanoi. Though it was a very wet day it was worth the soaking to visit this monument to their literature and education system. A slow walk through the gardens and inter linking temples means You can forget the hustle and madness of the city and experience what Hanoi May have looked like centuries ago.

reviews.author: Alexandra H
reviews.title: A serene spot worth a visit
reviews.content: Even in Hanoi's soporific heat, the Temple of Literature remains a serene spot. There is a nice little café with wifi.

reviews.author: BristolMelly73
reviews.title: Beautiful place ⛩
reviews.content: A fabulous place to visit while in Hanoi, stunning gardens and buildings and a great history lesson.

reviews.author: Tran Ngoc Qui
reviews.title: An interesting historical site should not missed
reviews.content: We went their with our guide who has a large knowdge about Vietnam history. There were actually a lot to learn from each kind of attraction!

reviews.author: Kenneth_Pedersen
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: The Tempel of Confucius is located is a beautyful garden, surrounded by the busling traffic of Hanoi. Interesting place to visit, and you should take a guided tour, to get the history of the Tempel and the University.

reviews.author: glb1971
reviews.title: It's a temple....
reviews.content: A nice place if you like temples. You learn about the history of university scholarship in Hanoi. Try and plan your visit early in the morning or late in the afternoon because it will get very hot during the day.Audio tours are provided for a fee.

reviews.author: michelle b
reviews.title: vietnam
reviews.content: this was very interesting and worth a look, plenty to see and it is another temple but is well worth it

reviews.author: OlafJ8531
reviews.title: A taste of older Vietnamese culture
reviews.content: Apart from being beautiful, this is also an old Confuscian temple. Go here to get an insight into a religion that still has a strong foothold in Vietnam as a part of Buddhism; I'm not well versed in Buddhism but I think I've expressed that correctly. Beautiful old historic buildings that were the centre of learning in Vietnam from the 10th century through to 1802, when it was moved to Hue.

reviews.author: BCSinig
reviews.title: Interesting history and okay grounds
reviews.content: The history of the National university is far more interesting than the grounds themselves. Be sure to bring a knowledgeable tour guide with you, otherwise I don’t know that the grounds themselves are worth the stop.

reviews.author: Jonathan Hopsking
reviews.title: Beautiful place for a relaxing stroll in the middle of this busy city
reviews.content: Beautiful and peaceful atmosphere in the middle of this busy city, plus a chance to learn a bit more about confucianism in south east Asia

reviews.author: rickcn
reviews.title: Temple of Literature, Confusius
reviews.content: Very Zen place. The complex consists of 3 courtyards before you get to the main temple, where students get inspiration before they continue to the university to study, which is the next courtyard. The complex is setup in a very Feng Shui way, and allows you to relax and get inspired. Please take a guide with you as it makes the experience much more enjoyable. Learn about the history and be amazed by how long ago in history this was established.

reviews.author: Wisetraveller59
reviews.title: Good place to visit
reviews.content: Enjoyed our visit here and learning about the history of the place. The temples and courtyards are very well maintained and a pleasure to stroll around.

reviews.author: Varun
reviews.title: Surreal experience
reviews.content: The temple of literature located in the heart of Hanoi is the first university in Vietnam. It was great to see that Vietnam's rulers hundreds of years ago paid so much attention to education that they opened the royal university to commoners. The architecture and buildings were unique and interesting to know about.

reviews.author: Jacki H
reviews.title: Important record of Vietnamese history and an oasis of calm
reviews.content: Worth seeing to learn about Vietnam’s  First university, how it was born and the teachings it offered. If you are wanting to broaden you knowledge of Vietnam’s history and particularly in Hanoi, this is a must.

reviews.author: scott4652016
reviews.title: Very Impressive
reviews.content: We had a good look around with our Trails of Indochina guide Kong. The architecture is a amazing. Such history is priceless. Well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Vignesh Srinivasan
reviews.title: Good for insight into Vietnamese history
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature is divided into 5 parts depicting different aspects of Vietnamese history and education. It is better for educational trips - its very quiet and peaceful.Overall, it's worth a visit if you have a lot of time in Hanoi but its not a must-do. If you're not there to learn about the history, it's a decent place to walk around but thats pretty much it.

reviews.author: Daniel19721972
reviews.title: one of the most peaceful places of hanoi
reviews.content: old temples and buildings to discover over different countryyardsespecially just before closing time it is getting nice.

reviews.author: Steven H
reviews.title: Insight into Vietnamese Education
reviews.content: This was the first stop on our Hanoi tour. Here we learnt how the education system works in Vietnam and the history of the temple. Really interesting visit that i' recommend. The turtles with tablet statues are interesting as they have the names of each year on.

reviews.author: Kelly T
reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.content: Being in education, I expected to enjoy this place far more than I did.  We used the audio guide, which I would recommend because there is little printed information elsewhere.  However, the information is not very interesting and the narrator is monotone.  Locations have up to five sections for each place that is not visually engaging.

reviews.author: Mai
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: Very educational learning about this place.  Some much history and nice to seem the name of the scholars who passed the rigorous exam and statues of Confucius and the two emperors who had the place built.

reviews.author: Max, Shie & Migo
reviews.title: Full of History
reviews.content: If you want to learn more of the history, take a guide to show you around. It helps to absorb the history when someone is telling it to you.

reviews.author: Agnes B
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: Loved visiting this Temple, from the plaque to honour Confucius, what a lovely surprise, to the beautiful water ponds with giant water lilies, the Temples, it was truly a wonderful experience, if in Hanoi, definitely make time to visit.

reviews.author: Sam A
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: It was very interesting to see the development of the temple and the importance it had in vietnam. Had our headsets as well which provided some really detailed information about the buildings and their relevance. Had some local children as to practice their English with us which was nice.

reviews.author: Ann O
reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.content: we visited the Temple of Literature and had a great time we were also lucky enough to meet some local children who wanted to up skill their English by asking us a number of questions so we helped them. A great experience

reviews.author: Ian T
reviews.title: Interesting historical place
reviews.content: We were guided through this historical location in central Hanoi as part of a scooter tour. While you do not need a guide to enjoy this oasis of tranquility it will be more enjoyable if the history of the place and its significance is explained as you walk through the 5 different courtyards. Well worth a visit!

reviews.author: canito1963
reviews.title: Over a 1k years old!!
reviews.content: Amazing to see this history 1k year old university ...incredible!! Very nice peices of art to see! Small but make you feel good just to realize how old that is!!!

reviews.author: SajiPrelis
reviews.title: Gorgeous, relaxing place and a temple for Confuscious
reviews.content: This place pays homage to Confuscious. The gardens are gorgeous and relaxing. There is a small entree fee but well worth it.

reviews.author: RheaKB
reviews.title: Was a nice visit
reviews.content: Nice temple, was interesting to go around it and see all the shrines. Wouldn’t spend more than 10 minutes here however. Also, be careful of getting taxis parked outside the temple. One tried to scam us for a lot of money!

reviews.author: ghp3
reviews.title: Beautiful and well done
reviews.content: This was our first major Buddhist facility and it was well done.  The building and grounds were well kept and the small museum was a nice feature as well as break from the heat!  Don't really need more than an hour or so, but a good stop.

reviews.author: Lori N
reviews.title: If in the area, worth a stop
reviews.content: The architecture is beautiful.  Nice place to walk around.  When you get hot, just past the restrooms opposite of the entrance, stop into the small cafe.  Its cool in there! And they have yummy ice coffee drinks and other drinks on their menu.  Gift shop sells retired wooden water puppets.  I knew I wanted to bring one home, and it was easier to buy here than at the water puppet theatre.  You can see it in 30-45 min.

reviews.author: Mick M
reviews.title: Cultural and Educational Heritage
reviews.content: Visited the Temple and was very impressed by the depth and achievements of the Vietnamese people which was evident by the temples and places of learning.Lots to see and experience from a very welcoming and friendly people.

reviews.author: Dave
reviews.title: Visit if you have time
reviews.content: It's relatively peaceful and an interesting spot to visit if you have time in Hanoi. Can walk around the grounds in an hour or so. Some interesting specific sections. We found it definitely worthwhile.

reviews.author: asw71
reviews.title: Worth a visit - book a guide
reviews.content: World recommended a guide to explain the history and significance of each section. Lots of locals visit here to pray.

reviews.author: Todd N
reviews.title: Most beautiful in Hanoi
reviews.content: Definitely a must see for Hanoi. The gardens and temple are very gorgeous and well kept. This was the most well kept temple I saw in Vietnam. The history was interesting, lots of great pictures.

reviews.author: Epic-Traveller
reviews.title: Lovely Confucian Temple
reviews.content: All the temples in Vietnam I have been to seem to be Chinese; including this one.Lots of information around about Confucius and traditional Chinese worshipping. There are lots of skates with information on them but they are so old the writing has worn down.Great to visit and worth the few hours we spent in there.

reviews.author: Shuaib
reviews.title: Beautiful monument
reviews.content: The architecture at this place is mind blowingThe history associated with this building dates back several centuries and is quite interestingNot to forget there are plenty of spots for someone wanting to take nice photographs

reviews.author: Tom E
reviews.title: Beautiful location
reviews.content: Very easy to quickly see around, but at the same time beautiful. You can do audio tours which might be helpful as there isn’t a lot written around, but otherwise beautiful surroundings and a nice way to see authentic Vietnam.

reviews.author: Donna A
reviews.title: Amazing place. Must see
reviews.content: This place is quite large. It so beautiful and well worth visiting. There are lots of sections to view but it really doesn’t take long to do that.

reviews.author: Jeanie
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: This must-see stop in Hanoi highlights the reverence the kings of the period placed on education.  I highly recommend spending the few extra dong for the audio tour and then stopping at the visitors' cafe at the end for a refreshing drink.

reviews.author: Tina O
reviews.title: Wonderful place, so peaceful.
reviews.content: Wonderful place to visit, so beautiful. A definite must for for visitors to Hanoi. Very inspiring and lovely.

reviews.author: Dean S
reviews.title: Best tourist site we visited in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Beyond exploring the Qld Quarter, we found most of the top tourist sites in Hanoi to be somewhat disappointing compared to what is offered in other S.E. Asian cities, that was until we visited the Temple of Literature.  Amazing architecture and history.   A must visit place, great for photo opportunities.  Plan on spending at least 2 hours strolling around the grounds.

reviews.author: 1000Yossi
reviews.title: The nicest place in Hanoi
reviews.content: Very nice place in the heart of Hanoi. Nice garden and halls. Walk in the gardens and enjoy the view

reviews.author: Smashcbe
reviews.title: Art and Architecture through Literature
reviews.content: A peaceful and picturesque place to visit. It’s the first university of Vietnam so of national importance too. The courtyards are very beautiful. The doctor steles with tortoise heads are really interesting. Ticket rates are only 30,000 VND.

reviews.author: emirati_nomad
reviews.title: Ancient university
reviews.content: Beautiful temple and ancient university. It has few water Lili ponds and amazing turtle shaped status. The place is pleasant and great for a quick tour. It has signs which are very informative about the place history.This place is great for families with kids and people interested in history.

reviews.author: john
reviews.title: very Nice
reviews.content: Beautiful serene temple with lovely gardens . Easy walk from Fine arts gallery , HCM mausoleum. We loved the lounge room at the back . Nice rest after the heat . Glad we went .

reviews.author: CTillman
reviews.title: See what is important in people daily life
reviews.content: Well maintained and beautiful temple and garden.  Beautifully dressed graduates to receive their blessings.  Younger students receiving group lessons in rituals and prayers.  You can feel the utmost importance an education is to the people of Vietnam.

reviews.author: ValeriedeL
reviews.title: About the best historical part in hanoi
reviews.content: Really informative about the first university in Hanoi. Also with the really helpful audio guide for the one who travels alone

reviews.author: Matthew G
reviews.title: Peacecful
reviews.content: This place is for those who want to stroll around for a bit.  Very peaceful and charming.  Sit around to enjoy calligraphy scripting or photo shoots taking place.

reviews.author: Steve W
reviews.title: Another area for a peaceful break from the bustle of Hanoi.
reviews.content: This is worth visiting. It is a site of great importance for the Vietnamese and must be shown respect. It is a homage to literature with statues of turtles carrying books and scrolls.

reviews.author: Hanoi Local Guide
reviews.title: Nice place for visitors to Vietnam
reviews.content: It is a nice place for learning more about the history and culture of Vietnam. It takes about 40 minutes to visit the temple and it is good  to have a guide with you. There is a big drum there which mayattract you and there are stone turtles with stelae of doctors may amaze you.

reviews.author: Liliosaandres
reviews.title: Interesting place
reviews.content: I guess we spent about an hour and it was very interesting to see. Not much else to say about it. Fortunately  the guide semed to know a lot about this site.

reviews.author: N_i_b_a_r
reviews.title: 30 mins visit
reviews.content: A big compound with students taking pictures for good luck in their studies (as per our guide). It was nice to see the engraved names of the scholars on the turtles back spanning hundred of years.

reviews.author: Chris braza
reviews.title: A Beautiful Temple Complex
reviews.content: We visited the Temple of Literature on our first day in Hanoi.Visitors must purchase a ticket to enter the temple, our awesome guide Tony did this for us. This temple is beautiful,well kept and well maintained. It's garden and lotus pools are lovely.The complex consists of the temple,  which is an active place of worship.  The huge courtyard and gardens and the School of Literature. The temple has a rich history.  We recommend getting a local guide to explain the various areas of the temple and their importance.This will make your visit more meaningful. Since this place is not just a tourist attraction but an important place of worship for the local people,  we advise visitors to be calm and respectful when exploring and taking photos.  Make time to visit this place when you are in Hanoi. 🌸💕💯

reviews.author: Zoe903
reviews.title: Very interesting!
reviews.content: Although it was super hot and humid on the day of our visit, this was an excellent site. Super interesting history. Our tour guide did a great job explaining the significance of what we we were looking at. Recommended visit!

reviews.author: Noam W
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Nice, easy, and much more interesting than just another temple. Don't forget to get the audio guide. Adds so much to the visit

reviews.author: Cindy K
reviews.title: Pretty Grounds, Worth a Visit
reviews.content: Definitely a worthwhile visit to this little oasis in the city. There were young women celebrating graduation there when we arrived. The ponds, temples, and ancient artifacts are fascinating. The grounds are not huge but well worth a visit.  Clean bathrooms and inexpensive admission help.

reviews.author: mstarzOhio
reviews.title: Beautiful, Calming Area
reviews.content: This temple is right across from the Art Museum although the entrance is about a block away.  The gardens and buildings are beautiful and well worth the time to stop in.

reviews.author: Lindy
reviews.title: Peaceful walk through Hanoi history
reviews.content: Enjoyed visiting the temple of literature - and walking through each of the gates - the gate of talent ... accomplishment ... jade vibrations. Interesting to see the temples and ancient history of education in Vietnam.

reviews.author: Rosco1943
reviews.title: Very interesting and informative.
reviews.content: Really enjoyed your visit here. Was surprised to learn of the influences that Confucius had in Vietnam. This history related tour was excellent.

reviews.author: linda l
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Great place to visit and learn the history of their educational system... the walk around doesn't take long but some great architecture easy stop on the hop on hop off bus

reviews.author: Katherine
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: It was the first time i and my friend have visited Hanoi. It's so nice and peaceful. We will be back here for sure

reviews.author: Paddleboardbb
reviews.title: Fabulous to visit
reviews.content: Beautiful serene temple with lovely gardens . Easy walk from Fine arts gallery , HCM mausoleum. We loved the lounge room at the back . Nice rest after the heat . Glad we went .

reviews.author: tlynn63
reviews.title: Lovely place to wander and spend some time
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature was the first university of Vietnam built in the 11th century.  It was fitting that the May day that we visited many graduates were there also.  Teen girls in long white dresses to preschoolers with their proud parents snapping photos. There was an area that we walked through that the graduation festivities were taking place.  Fee to get in is 30.000 vnd and I suggest also renting the audio guide for an extra 50.000 vnd. There are a few benches to take a break on, restrooms, and an area to buy souveniers and cold drinks (even cans of beer).  Lots of buildings, lots to see.  A lovely area that I very much enjoyed wandering through.

reviews.author: Sam Yates
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Much bigger complex than expected, especially after visiting the disappointing citadel. This location is beautiful, well maintained and showcases different styles of buildings and gardens. Great to be able to go upstairs in a Chinese temple as I've never seen a two storey one before. Great location for taking pictures and soaking up cultural atmosphere.

reviews.author: WorldTravelManTerry
reviews.title: Great historical perspective
reviews.content: I am glad I went, Is absolutely breath taking , adds to your knowledge, history and wisdom of Hanoi and Vietnam. Another best kept secret of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Corinne Lau
reviews.title: Visit Temple Of Literature
reviews.content: Good place to discover and explore. Admission fee is 30,000 Dong, probably takes about 45 mins to finish the site seeing.

reviews.author: R M
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: You can tour here and learn about Vietnamese intellectual history then go to KOTO for a smart meal after. Have been before, but always find this to be a beautiful, serene space with plenty of history and lotus ponds.

reviews.author: HendryD
reviews.title: Beautiful temple complex.
reviews.content: It cost 30.000 VND for 1 adult. Bring your student ID to get 50% off. The complex is quite beautiful with the garden and temple inside. They have the lounge area where you can sit in aircon room and order drinks PLUS free wifi.

reviews.author: Robert P
reviews.title: Very informative and interesting
reviews.content: A lovely tranquil oasis of calm in an otherwise crazy city. We visited here as a group and our guide was excellent.Really informative and interesting place.We were lucky enough to see some young people graduating and having their photos taken.

reviews.author: Tania T
reviews.title: This place is huge
reviews.content: It was drizzling the day we arrived. Need to buy tickets to get in. There are five courtyards connected by gateways. Nice stroll of the grounds and there are a few tiny souvenir shops in one of the courtyards.

reviews.author: Vincent
reviews.title: Visit to the ancient university
reviews.content: An eye opener You can see ancient temple where education is being carried out. The students there take pride in their University.

reviews.author: kkwalia
reviews.title: Ancient university with Confucian's teaching
reviews.content: Visit to this place take you closer to old Vietnamese system of teaching.It use to be very tough for students, you can see lots of inscriptions on stones,small lakes in courtyards serene environment

reviews.author: dan2963eve
reviews.title: Great insight into the education system of the Vietnamese
reviews.content: This place is worth visiting. It is amazing to see the efforts of managing and encouraging education in Vietnam at almost at the same time of the Battle of Hastings. The names of all the scholars carved and preserved for hundreds of years. The records of all previous principals. When we visited there was a convocation photo shots going on. And a group of teachers taking their vows in front of the statue of the first principal.

reviews.author: Valerie R
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Came here as part of an Urban Adventures walking tour. Interesting place. Temple and gardens showing history of past scolars. Made more enjoyable as groups of young school children were there to celebrate their end of term. 5 & 6 year olds dressed in university gowns, sweet

reviews.author: Phillip M
reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.content: Very interesting place, we had a guide so we understood the meanings of the different doorways and the general history of the place, very nice to look around for an hour or so. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: FrenchinLisbon
reviews.title: Beautiful temple
reviews.content: Went there on a rainy day which made the place quieter and more serene. Beautifully temple which also relates to the first university in Vietnam. Better to go with a guide that will tell you more about it.

reviews.author: Lee Thoo Hai
reviews.title: Beautiful, serene place of historical value
reviews.content: A great site to visit while in Hanoi, historical place keep as a heritage for Vietnamese cultural legacy.

reviews.author: Clue7
reviews.title: Insightful
reviews.content: Really interesting past on the first university in Vietnam. Neat to see that the Vietnamese were so (and same as now) into education. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Bugbitten
reviews.title: Holiday
reviews.content: This tour was very informative on the way that the first university had developed and is still held in high regard today.  Many ancient features and history were revealed.  School children were there as a day trip to inspire them to work hard and work towards honouring their past by studying hard to achieve great results.

reviews.author: haplo89
reviews.title: A nice temple in Hanoi
reviews.content: The temple of literature (30k entrance fee pp) is a nice historical sight in Hanoi. Some parts are 1000 years old, others only 20 years, but everything is beautiful.Expect lots of Vietnamese children who want to talk to you, they come here with their summer school to practice their English. (tell the teachers if you have had enough😉)

reviews.author: bradmichelle1964
reviews.title: Lovely Visit
reviews.content: Interesting temple.Enjoyable visit highlighted by the many happy children dressed in their graduation robes having photos.

reviews.author: mariecorner1
reviews.title: Well kept museum

reviews.author: Ernest W
reviews.title: Wonderful!
reviews.content: This place is incredibly steeped in history and shows the incredibly complex relationship Vietnamese intellectuals had with the history and culture of their Chinese overlords. Here, like in other parts of the Sinosphere, Vietnamese intellectuals were educated in civics, classics, and other subjects using the language of Classical Chinese. Classical Chinese is plastered all over the walls, columns, and stone tablets in the temple complex. After hearing the tour guides and reading the descriptions, it was clear that this was a place where distinctly Vietnamese (and not Chinese) history and culture were taught. Yet with the medium of instruction and scholarly communication being Classical Chinese, it was clear that Vietnamese intellectuals had inherited many ideas about Chinese history and culture. From what I could gather, the prevailing view at the time among Vietnamese intellectuals toward Chinese history and culture was one of veneration but not worship, assimilation but not cooptation. Chinese history and culture were not perfect, and it was clear Vietnamese intellectuals did not agree with everything Chinese, but, like everything else, it had good and bad, and Vietnamese intellectuals were quick to celebrate and embrace the good while discarding the bad. They respected it for what it could teach them about their history and culture but never lost sight of what it meant to be Vietnamese.

reviews.author: Patrick D
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) built in 1070 by the 3rd emperor of the Ly dynasty, Lý Thánh Tông, at the time when Hanoi was named Thang Long, was dedicated only to Confucius whose influence still plays a role important in Vietnamese culture. The temple honors the best scholars and literary men of Vietnam.The temple housed Quôc Tu Giám), built in 1076 under the dynasty of King Ly Nhan Tong, (son of Lý Thánh Tông), as the first university of Vietnam, It is here that the sons of Royal blood, the sons of mandarins and aristocracy continued their studies to become literate and high officials, that is to say the "Sons of the Nation" (Quốc Tử Giám).The temple is divided into five inner courtyards. , with gardens, ponds. The third courtyard contains 82 stone steles recording the names of more than 1,000 doctors of humanities, most of whom have become Mandarin. Each stele erected  on the shell of a turtle, a symbol of longevity and wisdom ,  and also a symbol of union. from the earth and the skyThe Temple of Literature is a 30-40 minute walk from the Old City, close to Hanoi Railway Station and the Museum of Fine Arts.It is an ideal place to walk, relax and discover the many pavilions, pagodas, courtyards and gardens ..It is a high place of cultural memory .. A must to see30,000 VDN entry

reviews.author: mitochondria2007

reviews.author: JohnsonIV

A calligrapher is on location to write at your request. Recommended.

reviews.author: Brigit S
reviews.title: Beautiful any time
reviews.content: This is a peaceful and educational site. No entrance fee. Very good photo ops and a highlight when visiting Hanoi.

reviews.author: Toroshan S
reviews.title: One of the oldest University. .....
reviews.content: I went there by my own. One of the sophisticated special area in Hanoi. Most go and must visit. Inside younwill find and discober a red colored Buddhist temple, turtle statues, several large size pools.

reviews.author: Deeptakshar D
reviews.title: University
reviews.content: This is the oldest university of hanoi. Entry fee is 40,000dong i guess. Students can get a discount. This place is divided into four courtyards and was the place of learning for the vietnamese.

reviews.author: Helge L
reviews.title: You could feel the Pride..
reviews.content: .. From our tour guide when we walked through the literature temple.Actually this is a very nice place even to relax 1-2h from the hectic street life and noise.

reviews.author: antantchan
reviews.title: A historical and ancient site
reviews.content: I had a good time visiting the first university of Vietnam where I got to learn the history behind its literature and key individuals that contributed to this historical site.

reviews.author: Ls L
reviews.title: Temple should be quiet!
reviews.content: This is not only a tourist spot but also the temple- place for praying, studying...so that it should be quiet. Stop using the very loudly speaker ...

reviews.author: JudgeJer
reviews.title: Amazing and informative
reviews.content: A brilliant repository of Vietnamese history culture and literature. Several hours well spent learning about the formative years of Vietnam.

reviews.author: Seppdedepp
reviews.title: Beautiful temple, but be aware of scam
reviews.content: The temple complex itself is very much worth the visit. However, be aware when paying for the tickets as they will try to scam you with the change.

reviews.author: Andrew H
reviews.title: Confucius says...
reviews.content: Worth a visit for the lovely gardens and bonsais alone. There is the Confucius temple at the very top of the gardens. Lots of pre school children in graduation dress... I suppose you got to start them somewhere. Interesting architecture in a lovely setting.

reviews.author: goodguyjas
reviews.title: Pleasant enough temple and garden walk about
reviews.content: This doesn’t take that long to walk through - 50 minutes or so and some of the water features were not looking that great when I was there, which may have been season related. The courtyards and pavilions are of course very reminiscent to what you see in China and are tastefully laid out. The main interest here is the link with Confucius and his teachings with lots of displays and things to read about him. The grand interiors and displays are truly beautiful and there is a lot of attention paid to them. One had a small musical group playing traditional instruments and was very relaxing. Plus the usual gift and snack stops.

reviews.author: Barney S
reviews.title: Short walk arouns
reviews.content: Didn't get audio tour so possibly missed out on interesting information. Nonetheless a beautiful old area of architecture.

reviews.author: SteveT666
reviews.title: Not quite as expected
reviews.content: An interesting 30 - 60 minutes meeting up with Confucius and his mates.   It is more a museum of scholarship and its virtues and pit falls should you not toe the party line than a museum of the written word. Well worth a visit and beautifully kept and presented for visitors.

reviews.author: Mariana B
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: We went to the temple on a rainy day and it was nice to look around and walk through the various gardens

reviews.author: JRKSA
reviews.title: Beautiful Historic University
reviews.content: The Temple of Literature was built about a 1000 years ago based upon the teachings of Confucius.  The Chinese-style architecture and gardens are beautiful. Students that passed the rigorous program had their names carved in stone... that’s a bit more substantial than the diplomas granted by universities today.

reviews.author: John M
reviews.title: You know to really admire and respect a culture when you see see how revered this 'Temple of Literature, etc' is!!
reviews.content: You know to really admire and respect a culture when you see see how revered their 'Temple of Literature & National University' is - and especially a place that as relevant today as it was in years past. The history that is celebrated here is incredible, as are the stone graves, the magnificent buildings and the beautifully maintained surrounds.  On the day we visited there were 2-4 separate student graduations making place.  Most were adorable kindergarten graduates about the ages of 3-5years old; and what a great place to reward their transition into a new phase of lifelong learning and respect for their history and culture.  There were also senior primary students (?) visiting too; and I really felt an education aura in this fabulous place right in the heart of the old city of Hanoi.  One of the highlights of our recent to trip to Vietnam and highly recommended

reviews.author: Jane Bednall
reviews.title: Peaceful historic site in busy city
reviews.content: Beautiful historic site, walk through series of courtyards to arrive at temple shrine ,then a centre with plenty of interest and information.Definitely worth a visit. Craftlink near by with beautiful homemade crafts.

reviews.author: AshakUn N
reviews.title: Old is Gold
reviews.content: Once this was an university now a place to worship. You can still see the list of graduates scripted in stones. Amazing.

reviews.author: Ignace B
reviews.title: Beautiful site in Hanoi
reviews.content: The place where the respectable Confucius is honoured for the wisdom he brought to the students who were selected to get into this ancient university.

reviews.author: Albywon
reviews.title: Pollution spoils
reviews.content: Right in the heart of Hanoi near the Ancient Quarter. Quite expansive and many building to look at. Unfortunately spoiled by both noise and airbourne pollution. Good signage for individual exhibits and this is definitely worth a visit if you are in Hanoi.

reviews.author: BrianJ0
reviews.title: Great for a morning free of hustle and bustle
reviews.content: Fabulous old temple, nice and spacious with lots of nice open spaces as well as the inner temples with their colour and grandeur. Nice reasonably priced gift shops.Nice clean and modern cafe just opposite the exit near the big drum

reviews.author: Eatsmilesleep
reviews.title: Quite a boring place
reviews.content: Seems boring if not for those graduates taking their grad photos. Just statues of Confucius and other gods. Graduating students liven up the compound on weekends.

reviews.author: George O
reviews.title: Photos of Graduates
reviews.content: The temple of Literature was very interesting and celebrated education.  School groups were there celebrating various events, each taking photos. Our tour guide facilitated our understanding of the temple.

reviews.author: Gordo4037
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: We enjoyed strolling around the grounds and enjoyed reading about the purpose of this facility. Great for photo opportunities and a very relaxed atmosphere. Small entrance fee of approx 30000 dong and kids under 15 free. We spent about 45 minutes here.

reviews.author: lizcraven
reviews.title: Outstanding place to visit - not to be missed!
reviews.content: 1,000 years old - a university dedicated to Confucius.It is outdoors and delightful to walk through.   Fascinating - and especially the stone stelae on the backs of tortoises.

reviews.author: Maggie S
reviews.title: Do you like Confucius?
reviews.content: You’ll be happy to find him and his 4 most important scholars here. This temple is the site of Vietnam’s first university, started here in 1076. Important starred attraction in Hanoi.

reviews.author: JTM1511
reviews.title: Well worth a visit.
reviews.content: Very interesting series of old temple buildings and quarters.  Probably best to go with a guide who can explain the various periods of its history.

reviews.author: Leann S
reviews.title: Interesting tour and beautiful setting in busy city
reviews.content: We opted to pick up two audio guides to help us understand more about the location. I am so glad that we did as it gave us a better understanding of the history and importance of the temples and items in display. We enjoyed talking with the touring school children- they had a lot of questions for us. I would recommend visiting first thing in the morning before the tour groups arrive.

reviews.author: Shawn_Bob
reviews.title: Beautiful temple and garden
reviews.content: Lovely gardens and beautiful temple and so worth the visit. Many students drawing and interesting area nearby.

reviews.author: Andreaobrien1
reviews.title: Another 5 layered pagoda
reviews.content: If you have seen other pagodas or temples then this won’t be exciting. It dates to 1050 AD but most is rebuilt.

reviews.author: Keith J
reviews.title: So peaceful
reviews.content: My wife and I recently visited The Temple of Literature while in Hanoi, we found it to be peaceful and our guide was excellent,we would recommend a visit

reviews.author: HarveyCapeTown
reviews.title: Oasis in the city
reviews.content: Lovely buildings, serene gardens and interesting detail. I would recommend taking an audio guide if you don't have a human guide or much knowledge of the philosophy as I'm sure I missed a lot of info and only knew what the guide book told me.

reviews.author: leytay
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: Interesting  and informative tour with Sang . Came away with a deeper understanding of  the hardships involved in early Vietnam  to obtain education.

reviews.author: mikki973
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Seemingly obvious, but still interesting for someone who grew up in Europe, and was educated in the western self-obsessed view on history. To say the least - the northern Vietnamese rulers established an university, perhaps not for the love of science, but the utilitarian value of educated administration, and the university was granting doctorates before universities such as at Oxford or Bologna started to operate.

reviews.author: Immanuel R
reviews.title: Island of serenity
reviews.content: This place provides a nice respite from the bustle of the city. It has a walkway leading up to the temple, flanked on both sides by greeneries. If you have seen other temples, this will not be very different but the place provides a good break from the hustle and bustle of the city.

reviews.author: Nicolas P
reviews.title: Temple of Literature & National University
reviews.content: Rich historical and interesting of Ho Chi Minh story. The very first university in Vietname and till now when the university student finish from the college they came for take picture at this university for memoral. That is lovely habit of Vietnmese.

reviews.author: SeeMoreLiveMore
reviews.title: I'd recommend this ...
reviews.content: For its history and importance to Vietnamese culture, this place is definitely worthy of a visit. It is still a popular place of worship and hence, pretty authentic. Quintessential exemplar of Vietnamese temples.

reviews.author: Mariano
reviews.title: Just OK
reviews.content: Nothing spectacular. If you are nearby, it might be interesting, but not worth going out of your way for...

reviews.author: WillemvZ
reviews.title: Recommended visit if you want to experience some culture
reviews.content: The temple complex exists of multiple areas with the most impressive ones in the back. It can get very crowded but due to its space that's OK. Admission fee is worth it as you can easily spend half an hour here.At the time when we were there, I think a graduation ceremony was taking place. Very cool to see!All the way in the back is a toilet, which might be nice to know :-)

reviews.author: JeffCypress
reviews.title: Best sight in Hanoi
reviews.content: This is by far the most beautiful and interesting of the sights to visit in Hanoi. It is very large, but you can exit at the far end so you don’t have to retrace your steps.

reviews.author: rambling_renaissance
reviews.title: A Must for a Perspective on Vietnamese Culture and Confucianism / Do the Audio Tour
reviews.content: All visitors to Hanoi should take time to visit the Temple of Literature for a valuable window into Vietnamese culture and history. It is also visually striking, and a spacious breath of air in the middle of booming Hanoi.You should plan for several hours to fully walk the Temple grounds, and definitely get the audio tour. It is extensive and well-made, providing background on all aspects of the temple and its history. Time spent here will illuminate any other experiences you have in Vietnam.

reviews.author: ZBH88
reviews.title: Gem of a place
reviews.content: A very cheap and worthwhile place to enter. The grounds themselves are buggy and disabled friendly but the buildings themselves not. Peaceful given the busy roads around and very popular with locals, tourists and school tours too. There are plenty of toilet of available and refreshment areas available. A lovely bit of history and some fish ponds with lillies also.

reviews.author: Steve C
reviews.title: A place of gravitas - a lovely calm way to spend a Sunday morning
reviews.content: The history of the place is fascinating.It has suffered over its long history but still retains a proud dignity.Signage is in English and the headset guides are a must to extract full value from the visit.It helped me better understand some of the history and the culture of Vietnam.Ceremonies still occur there and I was fortunate enough to witness a group of graduates dressed in their formal attire preparing to celebrate passing their exams - a really pleasant site to visit and a fine way to spend a Sunday morning.

reviews.author: David G
reviews.title: Highly recommended
reviews.content: This university was built in 1070. The grounds are incredible, and as an educator, it gives one an appreciation of education over the ages.  The architecture is spectacular. The temples are very impressive.  They have audio and tour guides available. The audio guide is good.

reviews.author: Nonapama
reviews.title: Interesting but very crowded
reviews.content: Love seeing the historic buildings and always the many very old bonsai pots around. The gardens and pond are well tended and very attractive. Many school groups through at the time of our visit so difficult to get clear photos but worth the visit.

reviews.author: mugisele
reviews.title: Lots of tourists!
reviews.content: Its an interesting complex but when its invaded by groups and groups of tourists along with their selfie stick, its transformed into another gong show! Go the the Museum of Fine Arts one block away...no one there and very interesting art and artifacts!

reviews.author: williamkassel
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: Interesting architecture dating from 11th century.  Pagodas and levels of entrance that increase according to what your status was at the time.  Inner most for children of royal regime.

reviews.author: Rodney Y
reviews.title: Worth the walk
reviews.content: This was one of the highlights of Hanoi although a long walk from the old town. It reminded me of a smaller version of the forbidden city in Beijing. There are a number of buildings with interesting shrines and other artifacts.

reviews.author: Carol B
reviews.title: Must See in Hanoi
reviews.content: This is a must see on the Hanoi list.  It is a beautiful site which embodies the history of the royal regimes.  It is worth getting the audio guide, though not necessary to listen to all the descriptions.

reviews.author: Laura C
reviews.title: Picturesque and historic sight in Hanoi
reviews.content: Dating back to 1070 there is plenty of history and tradition here to feast your eyes.  The sight is popular with locals on holidays and tour groups and was crowded when we visited.  Nonetheless it was a stunning and beautiful sight.

reviews.author: Akumuk
reviews.title: Culture, History and Education
reviews.content: This historic temple is a must see for visitors to Hanoi.  It holds some stunning treasures and the architecture is well worth the visit too.  It is of such importance in the history of education in Vietnam that it attracts large crowds, but visitors should not be put off by this.

reviews.author: Maree H
reviews.title: Treasures of Vietnam intrepid Tour visit
reviews.content: This temple was part of our Tour. The temple of literature is a temple of Confucius In Hanoi. The temple was built in 1070 and was reconstructed during the Tran dynasty (1225-1400). I would suggest going with a tour guide or opt for the audio tour as there is very little signposted. The temple is still used today for teaching. Very peaceful place if you can get away from all the tourist. Tickets 30,000 VND children under 15 are free and people with a disability.

reviews.author: 142JanetH
reviews.title: Beautiful gardens and buildings
reviews.content: I am glad we went to this Temple of Literature to understand the significance of it for the Vietnamese people.  One of our waitresses at a hotel restaurant, Daisy, was saying that the Vietnamese people go here before sitting exams asking for a good result. A very peaceful place and we enjoyed going here.

reviews.author: tenamydcanada
reviews.title: Lovely quick visit
reviews.content: The temple is one of my favorite places to visit in Hanoi: central, beautiful and of a small manageable size so you don’t feel sweaty and tired at the end.  1 hour is sufficient.

reviews.author: Liz C
reviews.title: Education & History
reviews.content: Went with a tour guide who made it easy to follow the history. This institution was peaceful and enjoyable.  Learned about Confucius and the many scholars of the Vietnamese culture. The exhibits are large and some are interactive where you can climb into the houses and really see how each room was used (functionality).

reviews.author: AnniK0210
reviews.title: Probably only interesting with a guide
reviews.content: We went there with a guide from Hanoi kids. Got lots of info which made it interesting. Otherwise probably not much to it.

reviews.author: ISP
reviews.title: Good place to visit with audio guide available
reviews.content: Audio guide was easy to use. Calm And peaceful spot were one can learn about the influence of Confucious philosophy and education on Vietnamese culture

reviews.author: Tim S
reviews.title: Rich history
reviews.content: This place has a rich history being the first university in Vietnam. Lots of traditional items to see throughout the exhibit. The exhibit is very large and takes a bit of time to get through but you should be observing and enjoying it all the time. Before you know it, you’ve seen a lot and are probably fulfilled but tired.

reviews.author: lmo3
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: We were taken around by our own guide who was most knowledgeable and gave us an insight into the history of the series of buildings. Interestingly, the names of the top scholars in first and second place were recorded on headstones erected in the grounds but only if they were deemed to have been brilliant enough! Many years passed when no scholars achieved this accolade and during the Vietnamese war these precious objects were buried and protected from destruction. An interesting place to visit with a guide.

reviews.author: Ana
reviews.title: Impressive!
reviews.content: I think this was my favourite sightseeing place in Hanoi! Enjoyed history of this place and it felt so peaceful there. Definitely must do!You’ll spend there a few hours without the tour guide. You can get audio tour if you wish.

reviews.author: tinkerbell539
reviews.title: Not as expected
reviews.content: There isn't much to see at all, we were in and out within 20 minutes. I wouldn't recommend wasting your time.

reviews.author: researcher59
reviews.title: A rare area of peace and tranquility in Hanoi
reviews.content: One of the more interesting sights in Hanoi.  Large 'temple' complex where Vietnamese students graduate and have good luck services.  It was very busy on the Sunday we went with smiling groups of smartly dressed school children taking part in ceremonies.  We walked from the Old Quarter, took about 30 minutes.  A couple of hours enjoyably spent in an oasis of quiet in the hassle and noise that is Hanoi.There is a small entrance fee which probably amounts to about a $/person.

reviews.author: Lars
reviews.title: Nice getaway from Hanoi traffic
reviews.content: Hanoi traffic can be overwhelming and very noisy. This place offers tranquility in the middle of the “chaos”. Fine park with temples. Absolutely worth a visit.

reviews.author: sandflopper j
reviews.title: four courtyards and a Temple
reviews.content: Bit disappointed , the courtyards are just that = courtyards.  The Confuscioun temple is dedicated to early followers and teachers after Confusciu.s

reviews.author: Bezi
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: If you haven't been to many temples before you might like this place but it is nothing special. It was pretty crowded when we were there, mainly with students getting their group photos done before the exams.Given the choice between this or Train street I would choose Train street every time. If you are heading down to Hue you will see much better temples.

reviews.author: Sue B
reviews.title: Lovely place of calm in the city
reviews.content: A beautiful and serene garden and ancient buildings in the heart of Hanoi. It is a relic of an ancient past when the buildings housed the first university and was dedicated to learning and recognizing the achievements  of its alumni. It's still used as a functioning temple and is worth visiting for the garden and sense of peace in a crazy busy city.

reviews.author: Joan D
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds to stroll
reviews.content: Interesting artifacts and scenery through the grounds of this temple. Very cheap, just a few $. Very easy to walk.

reviews.author: Periscope
reviews.title: A mustto visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: Named the Temple of Litterature but in fact the oldest university in Vietnam. Walk around and enjoy the different pagodas.

reviews.author: sherreedalton
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: It is a short tour and easily accessible. Our guide was able to give us a great history lesson and guidance through. Not the most significant temple but worth a quick look.

reviews.author: faboio
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Found a visit to this place, very interesting. We had a prebooked tour with guide, this was good as we learnt so much more about the temple. Worth a visit if in Hanoi.

reviews.author: DAN
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.content: Take time to visit this museum and take in some history of the country. Great way to spend a couple of hours

reviews.author: Marshall C
reviews.title: Make This A Priority On Your Trip To Hanoi It Is Not To Be Missed
reviews.content: This place oozes history and education.  Higher learning has been going on at this site for 2,000 years and is not stopping now.  There is a peace and tranquility that will transport you to another time and place.  Relax when you walk in, take a deep breath and let the energy wash over you.  There are places in the World you should see in your life and this is one of them, do not miss even if you just spend 1/2 and hour it will be worth the effort.

reviews.author: Bryanvdk1
reviews.title: very cool
reviews.content: different from many temples, the stones showing the list of PhDs alone was worth it. highly recommend a visit.

reviews.author: ubtravels
reviews.title: Temple that imbibes the quality of being respectful to Teachers
reviews.content: We were fortunate to see a class of young graduates in their gowns and hats coming to pay respect to the teachers and lighting and incense stick at the temple. It has a rich history where prices used to come for there studies. It has idol of Confucius and his followers.

reviews.author: montecarla
reviews.title: ok
reviews.content: this was something different to see, but it wasn't anything special.  The highlight for me was seeing all the school children that go there for day trips.  Their traditional Vietnamese clothing was beautiful!

reviews.author: Robbie B
reviews.title: inspiring
reviews.content: a must, so interesting to learn about Confusious and the temple is regal and beautiful. lots of monks around too

reviews.author: JaniJermans
reviews.title: Visit
reviews.content: This is a temple of literature, this has great respect among the learned this is the place of wisdom and learning

reviews.author: Mafalda Pinto Portugal
reviews.title: A not to miss attraction
reviews.content: This is a unique place, Confucius temple where education and talent are celebrated for many years. The trees and the building are absolutely stunning

reviews.author: Julia
reviews.title: Beautiful buildings and park
reviews.content: It is very nice to walk around the park and visite the different buildings of the Temple of Literature. I didn't have a guide but find my way thought the different buildings as there are many panels with explanations.It is a bit difficult to find the entrance if you walk from the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum but just follow other tourists and you will find it!

reviews.author: Alan P
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Well worth a visit and a pittance of an entrance fee. Lovely architecture and temple. It's a little oasis within the madness. There is also a little café where you can buy most things, including beer if you fancy one.

reviews.author: Paulrichmond
reviews.title: Facinating
reviews.content: Went with a guide and learned all the history of Confucius. Beautiful gardens and certainly worth a visit. Do read all the signs!

reviews.author: guncle08210
reviews.country: Cape May Court House, New Jersey
reviews.title: History in stone
reviews.content: Interesting for a history lesson.  Did not spend a lot of time. The statues were colorful as were the offerings.  Chico pies?

reviews.author: Shane Huth
reviews.title: Beautiful Temple
reviews.content: Easy to get to. A quick 20 minutes to visit. I'd advise incorporating the "Hanoi Hilton" into this part of town as they are close by.

reviews.author: John and Diane
reviews.title: Interesting Tour
reviews.content: We went to the temple as part of a guided tour.  Without the guide we would not have appreciated everything we saw albeit there are lots of informative English signs.

reviews.author: Lindy L
reviews.title: An oasis in Hanoi
reviews.content: A visit to the temple provides a fascinating glimpse of the teachings of Confucius and a welcome calm space in the hectic pace that is Hanoi.  We spotted delightful groups of school children, some little ones at their "graduation" wearing brightly coloured gowns and mortar boards!The cafe isn't well advertised but it's well worth calling in. There's excellent loos too!

reviews.author: Willem B
reviews.title: First place of higher learning
reviews.content: An interesting museum with a beautiful garden housed in a temple which is well curated with infirmative English labels.

reviews.author: BC
reviews.title: Interesting and Scenic
reviews.content: We spend maybe an hour here and took in the sights, taking a few photos as we ambled around. It is a really scenic temple and interesting too.

reviews.author: druidwicklow
reviews.title: Confucius and club
reviews.content: Imperial grounds of top minds of Vietnam for 1000 years history , temple , turtles and altars looks so royal stile with golden turtle on left side altar, plenty of suvenire shops on grounds, I did lite incenses felling was a monent of  immense power😀🐢🐢🐢Ante G

reviews.author: anitaneff
reviews.title: Visit
reviews.content: I had a wonderful experience but mostly because of the school children who were there.  They were all wanting to practice thier English and were super cute and fun, giving high fives, saying hello, and other basics.  All super darling.

reviews.author: TessaPolis
reviews.title: Historic site with lots to see
reviews.content: Our visit coincided with students going to pray for success in their exams. This was most interesting.  Not a Buddhist place of worship, but to Confucius.

reviews.author: Avery.Rufina
reviews.title: Beautifulllll!
reviews.content: My family went there as suggestion from hotel receptionist. It was really nice and peaceful. We will be back again if we have chance.

reviews.author: Johnny
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: Nice and beutiful ereas with historical. Will recommend to friends and family come here next time. Good for photoes

reviews.author: DianaH
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: I really enjoyed our time at the Temple of Literature.   It combines beautiful architecture, significant cultural insight, and details of history.   I have a better understanding of Vietnamese culture and history from my visit there.

reviews.author: Ivanmil
reviews.title: Very interesting place
reviews.content: It is an amazing place that everyone must visit. However you need a guide to explain you what you observe.

reviews.author: Darian R
reviews.title: Beautiful place to walk through
reviews.content: Very nice place to walk through and relax from the hussle bussle of Hanoi. Can get quite busy but the complex is large so crowds aren't to noticeable.

reviews.author: Lin W
reviews.title: Feels like temple of Confusions
reviews.content: The temple of literature feels like a Temple for Confusions where you see the status of Confusions and some of its teaching. Not my favourite on this visit.

reviews.author: MHurfurt
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit to this lovely Temple.  It is easily walkable from the Old Town.  You can spend 30 minutes to an hour here

reviews.author: Ted G
reviews.title: Cultural Experience
reviews.content: Amid the cacophony of Hanoi traffic, the Temple of Literature was a wonderful escape and experience.  The Audio Guide assisted you through the various stages of the Temple and provided very good information.  A wonderful experience.

reviews.author: Fran P
reviews.title: interesting
reviews.content: not a dusty old building with books! take tour woth a looka very old place in Hanoi and lots of acient history. on the flat and not expensive entry.

reviews.author: Mak Kim Weng
reviews.title: Temple of Literature
reviews.content: I would say that a must visit tourist spot. Very beautiful ancient buildings and surrounded by flowers and some fruit trees.

reviews.author: susieQ321_12
reviews.title: Fabulous temple
reviews.content: This is a unique,  historical  temple, not to be missed. The temple  area  is so colourful. We arrived  around  2.30 and it was busy, our Guide said  it would be  bustling  later, so choose  your  time to visit, carefully.

reviews.author: Jane W
reviews.title: Audio tour guide a must.
reviews.content: Interesting site with well kept gardens. The audio tour and map are well thought out and definitely worth the small charge. There will be some large tour groups passing through quickly but it's easy to take your time and soak in the atmosphere.

reviews.author: Paula G
reviews.title: Historic temple
reviews.content: Beautiful temple of ancient oriental architecture and history . The first university in Vietnam . Very much enjoyed visiting .

reviews.author: 真美子 古
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: If you want to learn vietnamese culture. Go here there are many interesting history and old building during 1010 centery. We will recommend to friends

reviews.author: Bersc
reviews.title: Good spot to walk around
reviews.content: We did the audio tour and walked around on our last day in the city. It was not too busy and was an interesting experience with some good views. We were there for about an hour in total. Entrance fee was about 30,000 dong (£1).

reviews.author: EgbertHerts
reviews.title: Important visit
reviews.content: Very attractive architecture and garden. Important in understanding the history of Vietnam with a lot of information in English.

reviews.author: Maria T
reviews.title: Tranquil haven
reviews.content: There is a wonderful calm and peaceful feeling to this place, which is amazing when you consider you're in the heart of the city.The tortoise stelae are interesting and it really shows how Vietnam has come to respect learning.The temple is a riot of colour and incense burning. Courtyards lead from temple to temple and the architecture is interesting with turtles at the base of the columns.

reviews.author: Benjamin K

reviews.author: GWYN33
reviews.title: All templed out ? But this is special

reviews.author: Lyndal C

reviews.author: Dr.Dipak agrawal

reviews.author: Julianna D

reviews.author: Savy Explorer
reviews.title: Great little place to visit in the city

reviews.author: Chas L
reviews.title: Great to hear some non War history

reviews.author: David S

reviews.author: Gayatri R

Avoid this and come early or very late and enjoy walking the courtyards, listening to birdsong and being....

reviews.author: woonthierallang82
reviews.title: Hanoi in one or two days?

reviews.author: Barbara T
reviews.title: Very Interesting
reviews.content: If you get the chance please go and have a walk around we were lucky we had a guide explaining everthing to us if was very very interesting

reviews.author: auswes11
reviews.title: Hanoi free tour cisit

Beautiful courtyards that mixed spirituality with academics, symbolism with intellectual pursuit. There was a peacefulness to the area that made it worth visiting. Would have appreciated a little more information in English on the signs to enhance our understanding.

reviews.author: Roger N
reviews.title: A lovely bit of calm in the middle of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Kelly
reviews.title: Peaceful
reviews.content: A beautiful and peaceful temple, we were lucky enough to visit around tet so there was a lot going on and many people visiting in their finery. The gardens and pretty and just opposite there is a lake which is also worth a visit.

reviews.author: Jenny G
reviews.title: Gardens are a joy
reviews.content: Was expecting another 'temple' but this a delightful oasis in the middle of the city. Gardens are joy, and the history is moving.

reviews.author: Kami M

reviews.author: Dilip P

reviews.content: This was Vietnam's first university, constructed in 11th century. It will be of intrest if you are knowledgeable and interested in Confucius.

reviews.author: kartor

reviews.author: Sarah b
reviews.title: Confucious he say

reviews.author: Janka K

reviews.author: Marco P
reviews.title: Very nice

reviews.author: abetv_2020
reviews.title: Interesting Place
reviews.content: What is notable about this place is that the Imperial Academy (aka the 1st university in Vietnam) is alsolocated in the Temple complex. The Academy is located in the 5th courtyard. It consists of  2 main pavilions and a secondary pavilion on each side. But the Academy, as it stands today, is a reconstruction as it was destroyed by the French in 1946. But there were actually 6 more pavilions in ancient times (circa mid-1000s) within the compound. Children of the elite, princes and princesses were schooled here.The 2nd of the main pavilion houses the statues of the 3 kings that contributed the most to the establishment of the Temple (which was dedicated to Confucius) and the Imperial Academy. The 4th courtyard houses the Sanctuary where the statue of Confucius and his 4 closest disciples are venerated. For me, the main take away is the fervent desire of the leaders of Hà Nội to rule their subjects well in accordance with the Confucian ethics. The Greek idea of the philosopher king comes to mind which suggests that this ideal is universal, not necessarily a western construct.

reviews.author: pink00flamingo
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: One of the highlights of Hanoi, it takes about 1.5-2 hours to see everything properly.  I would recommend taking a tour so you know exactly what you're looking at and more about the history, otherwise it's a bit of a maze and could be a bit boring.  Lots of great photo opportunities when it's sunny.  For the kids, you can purchase fish food and feed the koi in the main pond.

reviews.author: Suwatchara
reviews.title: Very old but quite boring
reviews.content: Although there is a lot of history here we found it very boring, there are so many of these types of places in Asia.

reviews.author: SwindonMitch
reviews.title: Mandarins and all you need to know
reviews.content: Very interesting and well preserved with some interesting srchitecture and artefacts. Well worth incorporating into your visit to Hanoi

reviews.author: cjkranz
reviews.title: Totally Worth It - Go With a Tour Guide
reviews.content: I would never have understood the history and significance of the Temple of Literature and National University without a tour guide. There are many subtleties and interesting facts that one would have no idea without a guide. So, it’s worth a stop while in Hanoi, but just make sure to go with a guide.

reviews.author: Claire H
reviews.title: Best place in Hanoi
reviews.content: I loved the Temple of Literature - it was my favourite place in Hanoi. Amazing buildings and courtyards, with some history added in. Definitely worth spending a couple of hours here wandering around.

reviews.author: Jalal Iqbal
reviews.title: worth visiting
reviews.content: it is a nice small museum. located a bit far from the old quarter but can be reached there by 10 mins walk. colourful, bright and clean compound. i liked the green lawn and garden in front of it.

reviews.author: Ricky A
reviews.title: Interesting middle ages university
reviews.content: Very interesting to visit such an ancient university. I was impressed with the statues made for each graduate student, called stellae of doctors crafted in the 15th century. Each one features a marmor turtle with a large inscription, stating the name of the doctor, what examinations he passed, name of the reigning king, and  much more information including the  name of the calligrapher.

reviews.author: Malte Boetel
reviews.title: Very interesting insight in culture and society
reviews.content: This museum is located in a very nice garden and gives a good insight in Thai culture. Absolutely worth a visit.

locationDesc: Bun Cha Ta is a Vietnamese dish of grilled pork and noodle, which is thought to have originated from Hanoi, Vietnam. Bun cha is served with grilled fatty pork (cha) over a plate of white rice noodle (bun) and herbs with a side dish of dipping sauce. The dish was described in 1959 by Vietnamese food writer Vu Bang (1913–1984) who described Hanoi as a town transfixed by bun cha Hanoi Bun Cha Ta ’s first bun cha restaurant was on Gia Ngu street, Hoan Kiem District, in Hanoi's Old Quarter and moved to 21 Nguyen Huu Huan street now Bun cha is popular in the Northern region of Vietnam. In the South, a similar dish of rice vermicelli and grilled meat is called bun thit nuong

reviews.author: Alfonso
reviews.title: The best Bún Chả in Hanoi: Michelin star and quality absolutely deserved!
reviews.content:
If you want to taste an authentic Bún Chả in Hanoi, this place at number 21 Nguyễn Hữu Huân is an absolutely mandatory stop. Everything was simply "top" from the first to the last minute!
The recognition in the Michelin Guide is totally deserved: the grilled meat is tender, flavorful, and has that fantastic, perfect smokiness, immersed in a delicious warm broth that is perfectly balanced between sweet and savory. The portions are generous, accompanied by very fresh rice noodles, an abundance of aromatic herbs, and crispy, delicious nem (fried spring rolls), including seafood and vegetarian ones.
The environment is welcoming, clean, and well-organized over several floors, while the staff proved to be very fast, kind, and always ready to explain how to best enjoy the dish.
Excellent value for money for a gastronomic experience of this level in the heart of the Old Quarter. Highly recommended with all my heart!

reviews.author: Jolapine

reviews.author: Wand3ring Har3

reviews.content: The bun cha was delicious and the service was very friendly.

reviews.author: Jessica P

reviews.content: We all had the original Bun Cha - enormous serving we all couldn’t finish. Great vibes, great value, fast and very fresh.

The flavors are there and the scenery is guaranteed.

Highly recommend

reviews.author: Ted bagley

reviews.author: UrsulaB

reviews.author: Zoltán S
reviews.title: Fantastic array of Bun Cha in Hanoi

reviews.author: PatriAdL
reviews.title: Must-see in Hanoi
reviews.content: Bun Cha, a soup based on pork meatballs, noodles and vegetables, is one of Hanoi’s must-see specialties. And to do so, this restaurant is the ideal place. A tiny, very clean place with a menu focused on this recipe and with friendly and attentive service. The best? The price! It doesn’t reach about 4€ per person.

reviews.author: Ian G
reviews.title: Bun Cha ta
reviews.content:
Managed to get here on our last day in Hanoi, and it didn't disappoint.had to go up the tight staircase to the second floor,  take off the shoes and climb in as people were leaving. 
 It had been busy all day, and the unfortunate couple that arrived after us, had been sitting on 2 beers for about 30 minutes when they were told that they had run out of Bun Cha. 
Our order of 2 bun cha and spring rolls to share between 3 of us arrived after about 30 minutes, reasonably priced and very nice food.

reviews.author: Laura M

You put some broth and pork in your bowl then add the noodles garlic lime and chili and dig in.  We will go back very simple place some tables inside but we sat outside beaches it was quite hot and stuffy inside.

reviews.author: Hannah T
reviews.title: Gluten Free Deliciousness!
reviews.content: This restaurant was excellent for gluten free! There is no gluten in the kitchen so it was great to order without the worry! I went for the veggie spring rolls and it came with a soup broth, rice noodles and greens. It was delicious and was lovely to experience traditional Vietnamese food! My partner also thoroughly enjoyed it and he isn’t gluten free. I would definitely recommend paying a visit!

reviews.author: BhRobin

reviews.author: Lee_family_219053

Aircon and with proper seating that maybe allows us to enjoy the meal without the hassle of someone standing behind, waiting for the table and stressing us to quickly finish up and leave. We ordered #1 and 2 and the food arrived quickly but the broth was not hot thus it was not very satisfying as we needed to dip the noodles in it. We asked for a second basket of vegetables as the mix goes well with the meat, noodle and broth. Good and satisfying.

reviews.author: Aran L
reviews.title: Absolutely delicious! 100% recommended
reviews.content: We went on the recommendation of a friend who had been recently and had repeated several times. Don't be wrong!!! We asked for the recommended offer which was a Bu Cha with a chicken fried spring roll. The truth couldn't be better!!!! Absolutely delicious, 100% recommended!!!

reviews.author: MichaelaLock

reviews.author: Furtif007

reviews.author: Stephanie M

reviews.content: I really recommend this place for people who haven’t tried Bun cha and want to make sure that their first experience will be a good one. The service is great and atmosphere very relaxed. Price is to be expected for the quality.

reviews.author: Maria Anna M
reviews.title: Simple, comfortable and Fairly priced
reviews.content: Authentic bun cha in a more comfortable setting, especially on a hot humid day like today. It was not intimidating to eat the soup since they have a friendly staff, especially Nam, who enthutiastically taught me the best way to enjoy it. I loved the soup as is, just the right sweetness plus the smoky flavor of grilled pork. The noodles thin and soft. The fried spring rolls were good and filling.
