There are a couple of interactive things to do on the viewing deck and a great 'walk of faith' - basically a clear glass floor that protrudes from the main tower and allows views straight down to the ground, 65 floors below.

reviews.author: Tripod
reviews.title: What a shame
reviews.content: Lotte Management should be ashamed. Not even enough chairs, no bar stools, no entertainment and lousy drinks. Plus point is the well trained and accomondating staff who deserve a lot of credit to manage the the busy evenings. How can it be that such a large hotel with such great potential has no feeling for ambience? The Hotel Lobby dead quiet, no music, no entertainment and you feel walking into a funeral. Sorry Lotte, brush up your skills as it is not only about building a high rise building but providing genuine hospitality and ambience which the customer will pay for!

reviews.author: hannahmckay78
reviews.title: Night visit was average and overpriced
reviews.content: We found this place pretty underwhelming, there were only fast food restaurants and coffee shops up there which didnt make for much atmosphere. There were also bright screens everywhere which meant when you were looking out to the city the reflection of screens were very visible and took away from the view. Wonder bother going, wish we had gone to top of hanoi bar

reviews.author: Andrew V
reviews.title: Very modern, limited facilities
reviews.content: Get the night ticket, you'll pay less and you'll get to see Day and night versions of Hanoi. The 67th floor bar/restaurant is a seperate ticket. It wasn't crowded at all when I went at around 17:30

reviews.author: kirsi_nessu
reviews.title: Great view over Hanoi
reviews.content: Took a walk from old quarters, easy route Lifts and ticket desk is located 1BF floor one down from ground level. Tickets 230000 Not many people up on the deck. Coffee and fast food available also gift shop and possibly to take pictures on a glass floor.Btw if you are more interested to have a drink and a view top of Hanoi roof top restaurant opens 5 pm

reviews.author: Koen B
reviews.title: Superb place
reviews.content: Away from the city.   Good music and good drinks.  Prices are ok and it's a nice atmosphere. But there was no coffee because the machine was broken ?????   For such a place.  Nice for all visitors and especially business visitors. I'll come back for sure.

reviews.author: Theminimalistbackpacker
reviews.title: Great views and quiet
reviews.content: We went up at night it was great views of Hanoi at night. Standing on the sky deck is a must although it took me a while to actually get on there. Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: Rhonwyn H
reviews.title: Amusing!
reviews.content: This was a nice way to kill the hot afternoon. It gives you a better grasp of how big Hanoi is. Plenty of places to sit and relax. There is also a Lotteria in case you get hungry. Don't forget to try the skydeck!

reviews.author: Jack_OrionYgn
reviews.title: Exhilarating Memories
reviews.content: We went there at night and was greeted with one of the most spectacular night views of Hanoi. The four or five features up there, be it romance or family, made our visit very much memorable. The sky walk is definitely something you have to experience! Me and my girlfriend's heart were racing when we were standing up there. Go there around 9 PM as there will be less crowds and you have plenty of time to enjoy the view.

reviews.author: Girinath
reviews.title: Exciting
reviews.content: The skywalk is soo awsom! Definitely have to go., the attendant gave a nice walkthrough and took lot pics. Very nice to have a freaky experience

reviews.author: Washant
reviews.title: Very scary sky deck
reviews.content: What a wonderful view over the city.I fully enjoyed the the calm of the observation deck. most spectacular is the sky deck completely made out of glass where you are actually stand on glass above the ground. This gifts a very weird feeling to your senses. It's absolutely a good price and I would say go! Downstairs is very good food.

reviews.author: Justin S
reviews.title: Can't understand the poor reviews.....!
reviews.content: I'm surprised at the poor reviews. We loved it here!! I find it amusing that someone stood on the platform for 30mins whilst being ignored. I wonder if this person is either massively exaggerating, or perhaps didn't think to simply ask for their photo to be taken! And for those going up when visibility is poor, try looking 'up' before you decide to pay to ascend 272m!Anyway, some facts....* Taxi from Opera House to Lotte Hotel should be approx VND 50,000 (as per the meter, so barter for that or less)* We went at night. Fascinating views. * Yes, the entrance is down the lift or escalator to the very smart shopping mall. It's all of 20ft once inside the door (not sure why another reviewer found this an issue!?)* The photo booth en route in is optional. If you don't want your 'ride photo', a polite 'kong kam-own' ("no thank you") is all it takes* Lots to do at the top. Of course, wander round for 360 views, but also, have a coffee in the cafe, and take some selfies lying down on the glass platform. Look through the free binoculars, or type a message to appear digitally on a huge wall before standing in front to take a photo. Half an hour at the top for £3.50 ish is a bargain if you ask me!!!Then, do dinner at the dim sum restaurant next door in the hotel.

reviews.title: Amazing view of Hanoi!
reviews.content: No tourists, great spot to relax, read, enjoy the views! Don't miss it, you ll get a different image of the city :)

reviews.author: Sarah H
reviews.title: Tourist exploitation alert
reviews.content: We visited the observation deck at 5:45pm hoping to see the sunset and get a cocktail. Had to pay the 'summer' and 'day visit' rate which was 230,000 each. Not exorbitant, but still pricy for this city. Obviously geared to tourists, there's the standard blue screen group photo opp as you enter the attraction. Unfortunately when we reached level 65 the visibility wasn't great, but can imagine the view would be impressive on a clear day. The glass bottomed platforms are fun and attract the kids. Stay back from these if you're scared of heights!There's a cafe and fast food outlet (not exactly what we had in mind). Only stayed 20 minutes or so.Worth a visit but I wouldn't rush back. The hunt continues for a good rooftop bar in Hanoi!

reviews.author: Lara B
reviews.title: Beautiful view
reviews.content: It was cloudy but good to see. a little bit expensive for the time spent and far from the center. not sure to come back

reviews.author: Philtown
reviews.title: Great view of Hanoi
reviews.content: Amazing views from the top of the Lotte building. Given the average height of the buildings in Hanoi it can feel like a smaller city than it actually is. This view will show you how far it sprawls.Hot tip: skip the glass floor top of hanoi viewing platform which has an entry free and put that money towards enjoying a beer on the open air rooftop bar. It's open from 5pm and access is free via the 65th floor. Use the lift in the hotel lobby.The view gets this 5 stars. The service can be hit or miss.

reviews.author: Samuel_Vu
reviews.title: good but not great
reviews.content: The welcome gate which is at the basement floor and near a crowded supermarket made it unattractive to me at the first sight. The view at the 65th floor is absolutely breathtaking. Except for taking some photos, there is no other activities to do. It would be great if they add some more interesting things to keep guests busy and stay longer

reviews.author: Stan
reviews.title: Feel like high -@-
reviews.content: Quite empty in the middle of Thursday.It was cloudy so that I couldn't see clear city.And it was occupied with Lotte franchises.

reviews.author: RodGowrieSmith
reviews.title: Great views of the city - average drinks and service
reviews.content: The views cannot be beaten, interesting to watch the sunset. Service and music could be better, for drinks it is ok but food is not great. Music is too loud and not suitable for the venue - but the views cannot be beaten.

reviews.author: colossalboards
reviews.title: Great views of the city
reviews.content: We love a good skybar and this has great views over the city. The only down side is, they allow kids, now i don't want to ban families from enjoying the views, but when you are trying to enjoy a nice drinks in a bar with your gf and you have kids jumping around the furniture. It's the only down side.

reviews.author: Peter
reviews.title: Fun to do!
reviews.content: We went in the night time, 7-8:15 we were there maybe. Starting at the cool elevator which does 65 floors in around 45 seconds, feels kinda cool. There were not a lot of people luckily so we could make lots of photos on the glass floor, on which I needed a minute to go on. Because it may be scary for some who got height scare. We found it fully worth the entrance fee although it is also around 90k vnd from old quarter.

reviews.author: Hodges1991
reviews.title: Incredible views over the city
reviews.content: I went here on my birthday after having a haircut downstairs in the department store, it was just by chance that we decided to go up...I got a discount because it was my birthday which is always nice! As it was morning and during the week, we were practically the only people there! You get incredible 360 views over the city and there is a glass platform, you can stand on. I would recommend it especially if you are close by.

reviews.author: Franklyn E
reviews.title: Fantastic Views of the city of Hanoi
reviews.content: This is the tallest building in Hanoi with the observatory deck on the 65th floor. It costs 230,000 Dongs the equivalent of about $10US. The view of Hanoi is spectacular but make sure that it is a clear day before you venture up otherwise you might be disappointed with what you can actually see.There is a space walk deck made out of glass, quite eerie but I gave that a miss. They also have some cafes where you can relax and watch Hanoi from the deck.Enjoyed the visit and would most definitely recommend it. The Lotte tower also have some pretty exclusive shops on the lower floor.

reviews.author: Neil
reviews.title: Spectacular views
reviews.content: Got it on a clear day and was mesmerised by the views after stepping off the elevator! Glass floors in the observation deck are unnerving but make for a great experience, worth the 230k VND admission.

reviews.author: Joel C
reviews.title: Great place to see the skyscraper
reviews.content: Just to see the skyscraper, it might be a little pricy but it defers to individual opinion. You could actually view the whole of Hanoi 360 degree

reviews.author: pqphan
reviews.title: It could be better if it was more organized.
reviews.content: The ticket price is 250.000 dong ($11) for day time and 150.000 ($6) for night time.Overall, it is OK and the Skywalk is quite interesting.The entire thing this completely unorganized, Young clients are running rampage and making so much loud noise. Down to it is: you paid for the ticket, get the elevator to the deck, wondrous on your own, then... go home. You can easily spend around 5 minutes for this. The organizer can easily make the trip more interesting and memorable, but I guess this is not a part of their goal.Service is very low and bare down basic.

reviews.author: cbepdyche
reviews.title: One shot view of Hanoi
reviews.content: Very well organised for the tourist to view Hanoi.. Amazing view... esp if you have happen to go during evening where you can visit the evening as well night view of Hanoi... Some interactive display of name is also interesting.

reviews.author: jslo27
reviews.title: Worth it, though better on a clear day
reviews.content: It was quite foggy when we went up, but we were able to see quite a distance. We wished we could have seen further. The sky walk was nice, but other than that, not a whole lot going on up top. There were only a handful of other people there which was nice (mid-afternoon). There was a strange relationship test to do to see how compatible you and your partner are. We were rated at 92 degrees C, so I guess we're in pretty good shape. Lol. We did see some swan paddle boats in a lake below from on top the tower. We later ended up doing that and had a great time.

reviews.author: Phillip m
reviews.title: Unplanned visit while out shopping
reviews.content: Very good views of the city and would be spectacular on a clearer day! Unfortunately clear days in Hanoi are very rare, I have been living here 3 years and have seen maybe 10 so if it's not raining and cloudy I would recommend going.

reviews.author: Bridgewaterboy
reviews.title: Great views of city
reviews.content: We visited early in the day and were rewarded by only having two other tourist there at the same time.  You can get a spectacular view of the city, its parks and lakes.  There is a 360 picture of the view which allows you to see how good the view is on the day you visit, we were lucky and could see a fair distance.  I don't know if it would ever be possible to see to the horizon considering the smoke haze of the city.  The best item on the deck is the glass walk way, which is fantastic and does not come with an extra charge.  You can also have your picture taken and leave a message for free.  A coffee shop and fast food outlet are available on the level, but are not open until later.  The entrance to the elevator to the deck is in the basement which you enter from the street.  Cost 230,000VD each for tourist, much cheaper for locals.  Cheaper at night 130,000VD each, tourist.

reviews.author: Nikki E
reviews.title: Great view but boring place
reviews.content: There's a great view and a small area where you're standing on a glass floor but otherwise there's nothing to do up there.  It's a little pricey to get up there for just the view but that's what it is.

reviews.author: Kelliejane
reviews.title: Ask about the view before you pay to go up
reviews.content: Because I paid, on what looked like an overcast but clear morning, and had almost no visibility once I was at the top. It's a beautiful building and once it clears, it's great. The glass skywalk will leave you shaking in your boots. There are two and one is free, just take your shoes off first. Other items are a selfie cam and you can take your photo and write a comment for a giant electronic board. Had a bit of fun with that one too. Well worth it if you have a semi clear day - enjoy :)

reviews.author: Josie M
reviews.title: The most amazing view!
reviews.content: We visited the Lotte Observation Deck around 6pm and it was such a nice relaxing atmosphere with the most amazing view of Hanoi. The sky bar was not too busy so we got great comfortable sofa to sit on. The cocktails were probably some of the nicest we have had in the city and not too expensive. The staff were very friendly and even gave us a blanket as it did get a little chilly up there. Would definitely recommend this place and the view is not to be missed!

reviews.author: Johnson_Lam
reviews.title: Nice View!
reviews.content: One of the tallest building here. Great view.However, don't visit during hazy days (like today) or rainy days. At night, enjoy the view, air and some cocktails here.

reviews.author: Lewis H
reviews.title: Clear Days are rare
reviews.content: The Hanoi haze often limits visibility to a few kilometers, so you may wish to choose your visit day carefully, since the ride up the elevator is not cheap by VN standards. But once there, the views can be stunning and provide some interesting time for contemplation of life and the city. the full circumference windows provide good views, with a couple of translucent skywalk areas for special effect photos. Seats for conversation and pondering the views are also provided along with optical assist items. The fare at night is lower for some reason, but I expect the view would be more spectacular with the many lights.

reviews.author: YunJooChan
reviews.title: Must go!
reviews.content: We were not aware that there is a Lotte in Hanoi until our Hanoi City Tour bus passed by the second tallest building in Hanoi! I wanted to go there to see how is it to be in Lotte since I haven't been to Korea before. Who knows they have an observation deck there! It was not very pricey compared to the one I visited in Singapore. So we decided to try our luck! Amazing view on top and guess what?!! they have sky walk! at the 65th floor! Of course i tried to stand and sit and take photos on the transparent floor! It was not so crowded up there since it is just 2-year-old building. You have to go! I spent around 1 hour hanging around the whole building.

reviews.author: TallChris51
reviews.title: A must-see for the view
reviews.content: After a day admiring the thrift and cheap prices of Hanoi, why not go the the 68th floor of the Lotte Tower and order a very expensive (though not against London prices) cocktail?! Great setting, very modern, nice atmospheric music, NICE cocktails and I guess a rooftop restaurant if you're feeling especially rich. Great views across this very spready city, and a chance to mingle with Hanoi's metro elite. Would have happily stayed there all evening if my cocktail budget had allowed. Vertigo not a problem, plenty of space to stand back.

reviews.author: Michael T
reviews.title: Amazing views of Hanoi
reviews.content: This is an amazing views of Hanoi especial at night.You can enjoy your favourite drink at the rooftop bar and i guess this is the highest bar in Hanoi ao far.Will be there on my next visit to Hanoi.

reviews.author: Jun
reviews.title: Lotte Observation Deck 65F
reviews.content: Best place to see all the scenery of Hanoiand the first sky walk in SouthEast Asia which I could see through bottom from the too on the glass was amazing

reviews.author: Puppy
reviews.title: Lot of time in Lotte
reviews.content: My daughter and I spend a bit of time in Lotte, because it was very hot in Hanoi in June so we found respite from the heat at, of all places, the mall. The observation deck is great for view and we were lucky as it rained (hard but briefly) before we went up so the skies were clear and the view amazing. The mall is good with excellent food places, good shopping (but not cheap, and not low quality). We went to the mall on two different occasions and it was never busy.

reviews.author: andrewjohnson90
reviews.title: Amazing nighttime views of Hanoi in an upscale atmosphere
reviews.content: We went to the top of the Lotte hotel for drinks after a long day of exploring Hanoi. The atmosphere was very cool, with good seats on the roof. The bar had a great selection of cocktails, beers, and wines. Although the prices were more like that of a fancy hotel or bar, you pay for the incredible views. I would highly recommend.

reviews.author: MRBP
reviews.title: Heights and views
reviews.content: See Vietnam's metro and its lakes around this building. Try their sky walk, a see-through flooring in two of the segments of the building

reviews.author: Bagpuss19
reviews.title: Great views
reviews.content: Visited here late afternoon and it wasn't busy.  Great views across Hanoi and there is a digital map to help you reference points of interest.   There is a sky ledge platform where you take your shoes off to walk across the glass floor.We stayed for sunset and got some great photos of the city.   Recommend a visit here.

reviews.author: Barry S
reviews.title: Lotte's Has Lots To See
reviews.content: Friends told us how great the views are from the observation deck and they absolutely were. Hanoi is a city of lakes with fine landscapes and views of the Red River. Walking 360 degrees on Lotte's 65th floor you'll agree. We went on a week day and the crowds were minimal. The sky walk is exciting walking out on and some teens promptly, but nicely informed me to take off my shoes. The elevator is a quick and quiet ride to the top. There's plenty of seating and food service is available. To get a feel for the city visit the tower.    On the ground level Lotte has a contemporary department store of five floors and in their basement is a wonderful super market of Vietnamese produce and products. There are admission discounts for seniors and students.

reviews.author: clritz
reviews.title: Great view from above
reviews.content: Great place from which to view Hanoi city and the kids loved the "Skywalk"--where one can step out onto a glass plate floor and literally stand above the city!  We went during a weekday so the place was quiet (except for our noisy group!)  There is a Lotteria and a coffee shop so this would be a great venue for a date without the kids as well!

reviews.author: Quang N
reviews.title: Hanoiiiii!
reviews.content: Nicely good. It has an awesome view of Hanoi and a funny skywalk. You could visit here frequently for relaxing and chilling.

reviews.author: David M
reviews.title: Tallest Building in Hanoi ..WOW what a view
reviews.content: Hanoi is a very densely populated city and the busy traffic and winding streets make this city difficult to go from one site to another easily...but from the 65th floor of this beautiful new landmark Lotte Center you can walk around and see the city with a 360 degree view... and all for a 100,000.00 viet dong fee for the elevator (5 dollars},.    There are hours after dark which would be fun also, but I went during the day and it was painless, no waiting line, and the top floor was empty ...so fun.

reviews.author: Teresa W
reviews.title: Take the time to walk along the wall - many entrance points and you can walk as much or little as you want
reviews.content: An interesting art work in Hanoi - we passed it often on the bus or grab - so finally had an up close look - really enjoyed the art work

reviews.author: abella c
reviews.title: It's worth a visit.
reviews.content: Great initiative this mosaic wall created for the 1000 years of Hanoi. My only regret is that it is along a very busy road and that we lack back up and calm to enjoy it but it is worth the detour

reviews.author: Andibuchbar
reviews.title: Impressively long mosaic wall
reviews.content: Impressively long mosaic wall, Guinness book excellent. Beautiful motifs. Unfortunately unkempt and out of age. Many stones are missing

reviews.author: BorntocruiseUK
reviews.title: Stunning and goes on for miles!!!
reviews.content: We only got to do a short stretch of the mosaic wall but it was amazing. Each panel is so different to the next each telling their own story. Just be careful as you walk along the street as the pavements are not very wide and the traffic does move fast. Start in the middle and choose your direction of travel and you will see enough to keep you busy or start at the beginning and keep walking.I don’t think I have ever seen anything as big as this, it appears to go on and on. To think the pictures are made from little pieces of colourful tiles all carefully placed to make stunning art pieces.

reviews.author: Sue M
reviews.title: Along the Dyke Wall
reviews.content: We saw many sections of the ceramic mosaic mural as we traveled on the main road along side of it.  It was built to commemorate the 1,000 years existence of Hanoi.  And is in the Guiness Book of World records as the longest ceramic mosaic mural.

reviews.author: Maria Eugenia A
reviews.title: Go visit
reviews.content: It is long and not easily accesible. It is really beautiful thought. Nice to watch, a lot of traffic around and not easy to cross the street

reviews.author: Panagiotis S.
reviews.title: Amazing art wall, worth visit it!
reviews.content: Amazing, impressive, worth visiting. I walked about 3 km of it and took a lot of pictures. The only negative is that is along a heavy traffic road, but is a must visit in Hanoi!

reviews.author: Mug
reviews.title: Love Along the Ceramic Mile
reviews.content: Each tile tells a story, and we couldn't help but take silly photos matching the mural's patterns. The sunset walk here became our daily ritual, complete with street coffee and endless selfies.

reviews.author: kate
reviews.title: A colorful journey
reviews.content: It's a beautiful and vibrant piece of art that stretches for miles. However, we noticed it’s not well-maintained, with some tiles missing and faded sections. Despite this, it’s still a colorful and inspiring sight to see!

reviews.author: dianedinky
reviews.title: See it if you can
reviews.content: As mentioned already, the mural is not in a good location, however, it is a thing of beauty and I would have liked to see it close up.  I didn't have time to investigate but feel that at nearly 4,000 metres long there must be a part of it that is accessible on foot?Was still nice to see from our bus a few times and interesting to see the traditional narrow houses that are along this stretch that are so typical of Vietnam.

reviews.author: BrakiWorldTraveler
reviews.title: Such a pity for the location and maintenance neglect
reviews.content: This is the world's longest ceramic tiles mural - some call it mosaic, but imo mosaic is something else.Nevertheless, the location where it is installed was chosen so unfortunately.It's by a very busy road - the main city center throughfare which is constantly under heavy traffic.In that way you cannot see it properly as you have absolutely no desire to walk along that road. Hanoi is one of the most polluted cities in the world, so besides the previous fact, that also contributes to the mural damage, dirt and neglection. We only saw it from taxi several times.

reviews.author: Marion B
reviews.title: Yeah
reviews.content: Pretty ceramic wall but in front of a highway...You can't really walk in front otherwise you'll get run over.May prefer other activities in Hanoi

reviews.author: MizuhoK
reviews.title: See from distance
reviews.content: This mosaic art is at the north side of Long Biên station. This was the project to commemorate the county’s 1000th anniversary, started in 2007 and completed in 2010. It lasts about 6.5km, Guinness Records. We only saw mosaic art from distance. We saw from the bus on the way to hotel from AP. We saw from the bus from hotel to HaLong. The north of Long Bien station is a key point for major transport so you may come across here on during your move.We feel fine to see from distance since you cannot see the whole mosaic anyway. Rather, you can see the whole picture from distance. It’s a pretty colorful art which cheers the people.

reviews.author: Shelley M
reviews.title: unfortunate placement
reviews.content: A bit of a shame something this beautiful is not maintained and able to be viewed easily.  The traffic is crazy, so you dont dare cross over to check it out. Looks lovely from a distance, just in the wrong sport to be enjoyed.

reviews.author: Lee A
reviews.title: Longest ceramic road in the world
reviews.content: It must be a beautiful road with many meaningful pics. But it's pity that some ceramic pieces are fade and peeled of. Needs to be cared and maintained regularly .

reviews.author: palawanismyhome
reviews.title: Guinness world record
reviews.content: The ceramic wall is about 6 kms long and was the idea of Nguyen Thu Thuy in order to hide the dykes. The ceramics come from Bat Trang, the pottery village about 10 kms away. The idea was to complete it for the Hanoi millennium in 2010, and it depicts scenes from the history of Vietnam: Phùng Nguyên culture; Đông Sơn culture; Lý dynasty; Trần dynasty; Lê dynasty and Nguyễn dynasty. It is in the record books as the longest ceramic wall.

reviews.author: srimanone
reviews.title: LONG WALL ON BUSY ROAD
reviews.content: This is a long wall of many designed ceramics. Poorly maintained and very busy road. Plus the walkway is very dangerous, I suggest you pass this by in a taxi or bus for easy viewings

reviews.author: dianne c
reviews.title: beautiful walls that did not age well
reviews.content: It's a really long wall(at least a kilometer?) and right beside the huge busy road. It's a bit scary to walk but the mosaic designs are really nice and made well. Unfortunately it has not aged well. But it is still worth a visit, but just once.

reviews.author: Liam F
reviews.title: Conceptually impressive but difficult to experience
reviews.content: The mural itself is quite remarkable but the only way to see it on foot is by walking directly in front of it on a narrow path with 4 lanes of non-stop traffic right behind you. If your taxi or bus goes past it then it's nice to look at, but I don't recommend walking there.

reviews.author: David
reviews.title: TIP: Look at the pictures rather than visit!
reviews.content: The mural is impossibile to appreciate on foot. It is reportedly miles long and is adjacent to a busy road. So hard to approach, and impossible to take it all in!So, id reccomend looking at the photos online rather than visiting!

reviews.author: Linda B
reviews.title: Amazing piece of art!
reviews.content: The mural is 4 miles long and holds the Guinness World Record for longest ceramic mural (2010). We were only able to view it on our way to the airport as we were leaving Vietnam after two weeks. Wish I could have visited it in person!

reviews.author: David E
reviews.title: A Highlight of Hanoi
reviews.content: The largest mosaic in the world entrances visitors for over 10 years along Au Co, the dyke road wall. Artists from many nations and organizations completed this majestic celebration of Hanoi's 1000 year anniversary under the leadership of artist Thu Thuy,  certainly one of the finest public artists in the world.

reviews.author: dekalbill
reviews.title: Impressive Story in Mosaic Tiles
reviews.content: The miles long mural is worth driving along to appreciate the creative artistic work depicting the history of Hanoi.  This impressive work is dedicated to Hanoi's celebration of 1000 years.

reviews.author: Ev_kka
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Few kilometers long, goes around the street, we saw it many timese - on our way from the airport, etc. It is a masterpeace, be sure to see it at least from the car / motorbike.

reviews.author: WileyCoyote2
reviews.title: Amazingly creative,a joy to the eye
reviews.content: Take a taxi,stop at a convenient locationThen walk to get the best views + pictureTaxi will pick you up ,after your stroll

reviews.author: Vicki E
reviews.title: Pretty impressive
reviews.content: Lovely to look at as you are driving around.  It is the longest mosaic in the world and crafted by many people.  Awesome work.

reviews.author: chiangmaicharlies
reviews.title: Hard to see, but unforgettable if you do
reviews.content: We saw much of this from our taxi from the city to the airport.It would be most difficult to see this in much detail as it's on such a busy road - but we really enjoyed what we saw of it. Sadly, none of my photos from the taxi did it justice.Typical of many Hanoi streets which are now given over to a lot of artwork. Great for visitors and great for the soul.

reviews.author: Nejolla
reviews.title: Very nice mural
reviews.content: A bit overrated a tourist attraction so don't know why it is listed on trip advisor. The mural is lovely yet sits in the middle of a busy street.  Nice to pass by I guess.

reviews.author: RASHIDA HUSAIN
reviews.title: 4km of amazing mosaic art work
reviews.content: truly very inspiring art work from all over the world. in one look it may seem like graffiti but its all amazing art work made of small tiles and mosaic. very nice.!

reviews.author: edenxo1212
reviews.title: Hanoi Ceramic Mosaic Mural
reviews.content: Runs along through many streets in Hanoi. Better experience if you get yourself a bike or motorbike in order to see the whole. But, if you want to have a closer look at it you should have walk on foot

reviews.author: Samuel Piette
reviews.title: Mural street
reviews.content: Those picture on the wall was the most aesthetic things you will ever seen in your life. Not like any other exhibition or art gallery, those picture has its own beauty to display

reviews.author: Brilliant Pottery
reviews.title: Handmade Walls of Tiles
reviews.content: Very interesting the first few meters.  Then it get a little much to see especially with the bikes and traffic.

reviews.author: Susan M
reviews.title: Marvellous
reviews.content: A great attraction despite the whizzing traffic! Close to bus station so go have a look then head out to Ba Trang the ceramic village....

reviews.author: Raymondale
reviews.title: Very long mural
reviews.content: It is a very long mural,i tried to walk from the beginning,but gave up around Long Bien bridge,very long,and dont know where is the ending.if have time will continue to explore it.it is hard to take photos too,the pedestrian street too narrow,and very dangerous if take from the busy main road.i tried to take from the opposite side,but a bit far,and so many vechiles passing by,you have to wait till no vechiles and shoot.some topics of the mosaic mural are funny,come here and have a look.

reviews.author: Iris T
reviews.title: amazing work
reviews.content: It was amazing to see all different works of Mosaic and it was quite long way on the wall. I wish I had time to walk along to see them.It is worth going there to see.

reviews.author: Janice M
reviews.title: Put this on your list
reviews.content: What a beautiful Mural. It has so much detail made from tiny glass tiles.  It goes for such a long way.  We saw it a few times from a taxi and from the back of a motorcycle.  If I had of had more time I would have walked along it to appreciate it even more.  This has taken so much time to do and is really beautiful.  There is some wall not completed, so in future years it would be good to go back and see if it has been completed.

reviews.author: susan1819
reviews.title: Don't try to walk it
reviews.content: The mosaic mural was done to mark the 100th anniversary of Vietnam. It runs along a main road - so don't try to walk it! You can't miss it if you're in a bus, cab or car. There are different stories depicted in the mural. If you want to get up close to the mural, you can do so in the Old Quarter, when walking to the Wholesale market and Old Citadel gate.

reviews.author: Michael D
reviews.country: La Manga del Mar Menor, Spain
reviews.title: DO NOT MISS IT
reviews.content: We have been passed this mosaic a number of times, still not sure how long it is in total but it is long. We were also fortunate to see people adding to the mosaic.

reviews.author: AngiWong
reviews.title: Games for children
reviews.content: Love the mosaic along the road. It has become a game for the children to spot the country or animal or design. Intricate and beautiful

reviews.author: Tonya057
reviews.title: Pretty
reviews.content: Pretty , but hard to see it well, it runs along very busy street. Great work by artists all over the world.

reviews.author: Aliz A.
reviews.title: Nice Highlight of Hanoi
reviews.content: Colourful interesting detail along a road nearby the river. Be aware the trafic. These photos were taken in unsafe conditions.  But its worth to risk;)

reviews.author: Colline D
reviews.title: Beautiful, well worth a look
reviews.content: This world record wall was gorgeous when it was first completed. On this specific trip, nevertheless, I realized many areas of the framework are missing tiles or even crumbling and cracking. Def a must see, but also hoping in many more seasons it won't have disappeared.

reviews.author: Julian E
reviews.title: The longest ever
reviews.content: This mural I believe is the longest in the word. I walked a few miles of it and it is just amazing to see. Well done if you walk all of it.

reviews.author: steven e
reviews.title: A real suprise
reviews.content: Mosaic runs  along the side of a typical very busy road. You will probably see it as you travel to Hanoi from the Airport. Impressive when you think of the work involved

reviews.author: Cristina P.
reviews.title: Wall
reviews.content: It s a mosaic wall that has been said is in the Records Book as the longest wall made from mosaic. A street art you can admire from any vehicle.

reviews.author: Cliff C
reviews.title: Hanoi ceramic mural wall
reviews.content: This wall goes for quite a few kilometres on both sides of the road and depicts the life and history of Vietnam. NO GRAFFITI!Very professional and makes a drive from/to the airport very pleasant and welcoming.

reviews.author: Pennie B
reviews.title: Very public art
reviews.content: Wonderful, lengthy mosaic mural tells many tales along the way. Brilliant! Saw it on several drive bys. Wish there were a fold out book to give the entire view

reviews.author: Sandra
reviews.title: walking along the Hanoi mosaic wall
reviews.content: I walked along the wall for 2 miles south of the Chuong Duong Bridge, took photos and lived to tell about. The sidewalk is narrow, but wide enough to step back (if you are careful) and take photos. The easiest way to get across the chaotic road next to the wall is to hire a Grab motorcycle and have him drop you next to the wall.

reviews.author: gastronaut_11
reviews.title: Extensive
reviews.content: Depicts Vietnam in a kaleidoscope of colour and imagination. Seems to go on forever, mostly ignored, but a great insight.

reviews.author: Nonapama
reviews.title: Good attempt at beautifying
reviews.content: This has transformed an otherwise sad looking concrete wall and not so interesting neighbourhood into a place of art and cultural heritage. Best to drive by as not so easy or safe to walk past.

reviews.author: Nguyễn K
reviews.title: Smell and dirty
reviews.content: So sad!This ceramic road must be a symbol of Hanoi but there are too many broken parts :((Also, it was very smelly with busy trafic around there.

reviews.author: Lisa S
reviews.title: Wow better than graffiti!
reviews.content: We have driven by this numerous times during our stay in Hanoi.  Some very cool, colorful mosaics here.  Our local guide said it used to be graffiti on the concrete wall and then someone came up with the idea to beautify it by using mosaics and I’d say they succeeded!

reviews.author: fizzy1991
reviews.title: Drive by but don't get out of the car
reviews.content: This is a great mural to view along your drive in Hanoi but don't try and get out of your car to see it up close.  The traffic is so crazy here and you will get hit if you try.  Your best bet is to get in the far lane closes to the wall and take pictures as you go.  Or maybe there will be a jam up and you can see them for a longer period of time.

reviews.author: Willem B
reviews.title: Great public art
reviews.content: A proud celebration of the history of the country. Not too easy to access on foot but you will see it going to the airport it Halong Bay

reviews.author: TessaPolis
reviews.title: Longest mosaic in the world.
reviews.content: Saw this on our way out of Hanoi from the car windows.  Very, very long and in a variety of artistic styles.

reviews.author: RovingSoraSon
reviews.title: Along the way
reviews.content: Meet this mural along the way from the airport to the city center. I didnot think it is a thing, just some fun decoration. But there are parts looks amusing and made me want to keep looking to see what is next.

reviews.author: ferretbadger
reviews.title: Intricate and Beautiful
reviews.content: This mural cheers up travellers along the road by providing a bit of color in an otherwise mostly gray city. It features designs from Vietnamese mythology, childrens' art, and quilt patterns and is a delight to pass by.

reviews.author: WireWrapGems2
reviews.title: Worth choosing a route that goes by this mural wall
reviews.content: Local artisans have created a beautiful ceramic tile wall depicting local scenes.  It is difficult to get a good picture if you are riding in a bus.  It is quite long and beautiful to see, day or night.

reviews.author: TheLeongOhana
reviews.title: A Beautiful Mural along a Busy Road
reviews.content: We drove by this beautiful mosaic mural on the way to the airport after a short stay in Hanoi.  It was little tough at times to take a photo from a moving van but I managed to capture a few good photos.  It was colorful and looked like a lot of effort went into the design and construction.  The mural contained a number of different themes and landmarks both local and international, like the Merlion from Singapore.  There also was quite a bit of advertisement on the mural and personally I don’t know why they allowed it.I may try to walk along part of it next time since it extends for a couple miles.

reviews.author: Janka K
reviews.title: Nice view qhen you ride a motorbike
reviews.content: This is a nice scenery when you ride a motorbike at day - I passed the wall when taking passenger seat on the Grab motorbike ride. The decorated wall is long and it's obvious that someone made an effor. I liked it a lot.

reviews.author: Elina Ermakova
reviews.title: Colourful
reviews.content: Together an incredibly frantic interstate, you turn up at a beautiful mural painstakingly assembled by artists which are local and a further master artist out of a number of areas across the world - a tribute to their 1000 season birthday celebration. a genuine must see in this beautiful city.

reviews.author: JnVSydney
reviews.title: Best seen by car
reviews.content: We had planned to walk the length of Hanoi’s Ceramic mosic mural - at 3.85 km it holds the Guiness World Record the longest ceramic mosaic mural in the world.  It was created to celebrate the millenial anniversary of Hanoi and 35 artists from around the world contributed to it. Fortunately the Grab ride to a temple showed us around 60% of it from the taxi and it turns out it runs the length of a (very noisey) highway... so not ideal for gentle and enjoyable strolling.

reviews.author: kpiddy
reviews.title: Longest ceramic mosaic wall in the world
reviews.content: The Hanoi Ceramic Mosaic Wall is pretty hard not to miss on a commute from the city to the Noi Bai International Airport, local and international artists came together to add colour and decorate the Red River dyke wall in preparation for the celebration of Hanoi's 1000th in 2010.  The wall has been recognised by the Guiness Book of Records as the longest ceramic mosaic wall in the world measuring just under four kilometres long.  Accessing the wall would be difficult by foot simply due to the chaotic roads, best viewed from within a vehicle.

reviews.author: FrequentTrooper
reviews.title: Beautiful piece of work
reviews.content: Not a place you can walk to and admire. If you are in a vehicle, ask the driver to slow down and enjoy the mural depicting Hanoi.

reviews.author: Laura T
reviews.title: only drove past when transferring to/from the airport, looked amazing so would love to be able to see in more detail
reviews.content: This colourful 4 mile long mural runs along along the Red River dike wall, following the roads of Au Co, Nghi Tam, Yen Phu, Tran Nhat Duat, Tran Quang Khai and Tran Khanh Du. Stretching along the main road leading out of Hanoi and towards the airport, so most transfers will drive past portions of the mural. Due to the very busy traffic and narrow pathways, it is recommended to view from a car or motorbike, which is what we did. Having read more reviews now though, it sounds like people are able to walk along parts of it? although the pavement must be very very narrow! Apparently, one section is next to the historic Long Bien Bridge where it may be easier to look at in more detail?This mural was created in 2010 to celebrate the 1000 year anniversary of Hanoi. Local and international artists were assigned different sections. The artwork is beautiful and creative in many different styles, showing Vietnamese ethnic and cultural motives. Listed in the Guinness World Records as the longest ceramic art road in the world. I would have liked to have been able to look at in more detail.

reviews.author: Manfred H
reviews.title: interesting
reviews.content: Seeing there is no infrastructure ,no trains,no trams and  gridlock traffic there might have been a better way to celebrate 1000 years Hanoi however the wall is artistic and you have plenty of time admiring as u r stuck in traffic

reviews.author: Kimmie
reviews.title: Colourful Mosaic
reviews.content: The 2 km colourful mosaic was interesting. Showing the ancient time and how they kings shifted the capital. After visiting the different tombs and looking at the mosaic it gives one a better understanding.. awesome and worth the nice walk.

reviews.author: Sharmistha Ghosh Das
reviews.title: Interesting concept... Difficult to capture pictures though
reviews.content: Our Hanoi guide first showed us this Mosaic mural and mentioned about it's length and place in Guiness Book of Records. It's a very interesting concept. We actually walked along the wall but it was very difficult to capture photos of the mosaics since the pedestrian walkway is narrow and there are millions of motorbikes running next to it who hardly stop for anyone on road. Given Vietnam's reputation of bikers snatching phones, we did not want to take a risk with the phone either. But some of the murals are really nice and give a sneak peek into Vietnam's most important landmarks and culture. Worth a visit if you have some time to walk along.

reviews.author: TravelingFamilyTrip
reviews.title: Pretty cool
reviews.content: I noticed this long mosaic wall during my cab ride to the airport.  It was pretty interesting to view it and I appreciated the work that went into it. I wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to find it, but it was a nice addition to Hanoi.

reviews.author: Jana
reviews.title: Long...
reviews.content: Interesting to see if you have time to stroll along. It's well done and very artsy and since it's close to the Old Quarter, it's easy to walk to.

reviews.author: ron b
reviews.title: 4 mile long ceramic mural that straddles Gustav Eiffel's historic Long Bien bridge
reviews.content: This mural was created in 2010 to celebrate the 1000 year anniversary of Hanoi, along the Red River dike wall. Apparently different artists were assigned different sections. The art work is uniformly beautiful and creative. Unfortunately the mural is on a narrow sidewalk on a very busy street so is a bit awkward to visit. One section is next to the historic Long Bien bridge, the oldest bridge across the Red River, built in 1899 by the legendary Gustav Eiffel, bombed by America but since restored, a must-see sight in Hanoi.

reviews.author: igor Š

The Mural is best appreciated on foot, but in case time is short, a vehicle/taxi provides a great option. Appreciate this special outdoor art exhibit! Extremely colourfully decorated' mosaic wall' lining the course to the airport for over a mile. Probably best observed from a taxi.

reviews.author: Chris S

reviews.author: RyanLChicago

reviews.author: Ian G

reviews.author: rlh
reviews.title: Remarkable Ceramic Artwork For The World
reviews.content: Vietnam’s capital city, Hanoi (a/k/a “Thang Long” its historic name which means Ascending Dragon) celebrated its 1000th anniversary as the nation’s capital on October 10, 2010. One of the standout symbols of the city’s celebration back in 2010 was the 4km+ long ceramic mosaic wall running from the An Duong border gate  to the Van Kiep border gate. It has about  6500 square meters of ceramic artwork in 21 mosaic sections that honor Vietnamese forefathers and their various dynasties, the cultures of VN’s 54 ethnic groups, and generally the history and international relations that are part of the nation’s history.  The multi-year project attracted the participation & enthusiasm of local & international artists who used many types of ceramics from craft villages throughout Vietnam to complete the wall. As part of the celebration, the Guinness World Records Organization also certified the collaborative work of art as the longest ceramic art road in the world. The wall is somewhat difficult to view as a pedestrian due to the heavy traffic alongside its length but if you do walk a portion of the route, use the sidewalk opposite the artwall (carefully avoiding the obstructions of foliage, trash, etc) to gain the best views. Again, it will be a dicey walk so remain safety conscious—-a suggestion borne from personal experience!! It is more easily and quickly viewed from a car, taxi or bus but using this means reduces the opportunity to photograph or study the ceramic art.

reviews.content: Great little gems in the city.  Stretches of beautiful ceramic mosaic with different themes and sponsorship from different companies.

reviews.author: Ella K
reviews.title: When you consider the many artisans who put their efforts forward
reviews.content: A large scale, long community effort depicting the symbolic, and historic aspects of Nth Vietnam, which certainly liven up the roadside with colour and meaningful decoration - fun and interesting.

reviews.author: Jen78703
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: This was amazing but I am not sure it's worth a separate trip. We did it as part of our general tour of Hanoi. The mosaic is the longest in the world (3,850 linear meters) and was created by many different people so sections are quite different.

reviews.author: SueL41589
reviews.title: Outstanding murals
reviews.content: These murals were done by individuals and corporations.  They depict all kinds of life, past and present in the area.  A wonderful way to beautify the city.

reviews.author: sandrach1961
reviews.title: Most beautiful mosaic designs
reviews.content: We where travelling back to the airport and saw this it is so amazing the designs. The amount of work that someone has done is outstanding. It really makes the area stand out instead of watching traffic.

reviews.author: MattC1995
reviews.title: Beautiful addition to brighten things up
reviews.content: Places alongside one o the busiest streets in Hanoi, this beautiful mosaic mural is well worth seeing, with its vibrant colours and stories.

reviews.author: Amethyst E
reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.content: We loved driving by this from Tay Ho to Hoan Kiem every day, and trying to spot something we hadn't seen before. Five stars, no complaints!

reviews.author: Muddgirl
reviews.title: WOW!
reviews.content: This is seriously an amazing work of art....when you can see it in entirety.  I had to go early in the a.m.  This is the only way to really see it without "constant" traffic.  What a work of art.  The time it took to create this masterpiece was many years.  It's colorful and detailed.  I just read it's in the World Records book for largest Mosaic.  I believe it.

reviews.author: David Capper
reviews.title: They spanned a long way
reviews.content: My wife and I always enjoy murals and these were very impressive spanning quite a length of one of the major roadways.

reviews.author: TilakDissanayake
reviews.title: Longest Mural in the World
reviews.content: this mural  is as i can remeber 11 Km long and is in the Guiness book of record as the longest in the World.

reviews.author: Mee N
reviews.title: Interesting!
reviews.content: I love the way they used primary schools' students' drawings on the ceramics. The road looks more attractive than before

reviews.author: minimize940314
reviews.title: Good artwork
reviews.content: This mural art is very long! You can see this mural on the way from the airport to city center. It has many symbols and meaningful moments of vietnam history and culture.

reviews.author: rondas2020
reviews.title: The longest ceramic mural ever.....
reviews.content: More of a phenomenon than a destination, this wall of ceramic tile murals stretches for several miles, and the subject matter depicted ranges from everyday flora and fauna, to cityscapes to pure fantasy. It can be walked or biked from end to end, but the boulevard it runs along is very busy, so we drove it. We had a wow moment upon first seeing it, as in "Wow, Can you believe that!" Followed by successive waves of, "look at the fish", "oh, cute birds", etc. Colorful and fun it punctuates the landscape nicely and is really nice mural work.

reviews.author: Raymond W
reviews.title: It's a Mosaic. It's Long
reviews.content: The title of this review says it all. This long mosaic runs along the side of a busy road in central Hanoi. Different sections have different themes. The main monuments and sights of the country from Hoi An and My Son to Hue are represented, as are wildlife and flora. But basically it's long and it's a mosaic.

reviews.author: Janine F
reviews.title: Adds interest to a busy city
reviews.content: Travelling along in a taxi is probably the only way to see this as it is along a very busy road.  Well done and good to look at instead of the tooting motorbikes and cars!

reviews.author: babiesquuensland
reviews.title: very well done
reviews.content: saw this a lot of work has gone into this and looks great, would be very hard to walk this with all the traffic

reviews.author: CYY_sg
reviews.title: Colourful and breaks the monotony while traveling along this road
reviews.content: Colourful mosaic pictures line this stretch of road. It is entertaining for people traveling here. Probably recommended only for the most hardcore fans of such an art-form if you intend to plan a visit here as part of your itinerary.

reviews.author: Nunngo
reviews.title: A masterpiece of community art
reviews.content: I had been to Hanoi twice previously, and both times admired the mural from the road in a car sitting in traffic.  When I was there in 2010 Hanoi was celebrating 1000 years.  The mural was completed as part of the 1000 year celebration.  This trip I was determined to walk the entire length of the mural and photograph as much as possible.  We walked the mural wall on two separate days, the heat was the limiting factor in not doing the entire length in one day.  There were sections that were difficult to get to given the location and the 'madness' of the traffic.  If you have the time to walk even some of the mural it is very much worthwhile viewing up close. The sections have been completed by community groups, and various local schools, including international schools.  The art work is magnificent with elaborate mosaic detail, intense colour and texture.  Unfortunately there are parts of the mural that are already damaged and worn but it is mostly intact and well worth the effort to walk in the heat and traffic.

reviews.author: Wayfaring N
reviews.title: Beautiful welcome to Hanoi
reviews.content: Only saw it on the bus from the airport but remembered it from my last trip here because it's really unforgettable and a great taste of what vietnam is ready to offer

reviews.author: Lydia Farmer L
reviews.title: beautiful mural!
reviews.content: Driving along the crowded congested main road, this is a welcome and attractive sight. We passed it many times during our Hanoi stay. Going to Halong Bay, over to the Westlake district, and several shorter trips. It is a good distraction from the craziness of Vietnamese traffic!

reviews.author: Robert Q
reviews.title: Mosaic Mural on the Red River flood wall.
reviews.content: Hard to see without getting killed by speeding traffic, this project was completed by collage art students celebrating Vietnamese culture.  Still, seen from a distance, or form a moving taxi, it is an impressive sight.

reviews.author: firach
reviews.title: love love love this wall
reviews.content: read on the internet that this wall is 6.5km long and is in the World Guinness Records for being the longest ceramic mosaic wall. Couldn't walk through the whole one as it was too hot, but passing by parts of it on a motorbike gave a glimpse into the the artsy side of vietnam, as well as the things important to them, such as the recurrent drawing of a turtle and a sword in its mouth

reviews.author: jenabaintheworld
reviews.title: beautiful urban art
reviews.content: I see this very long mural going to and from work every day.   Incredible art from ceramic tiles---and done in Ba Trung ceramic village outside Hanoi and then put on display as nice wall to beautify the roadway.    This was done to commemorate 1000 years for the city of Hanoi.    Great idea for beautiful urban art

reviews.author: Jane D
reviews.title: in a vehicle
reviews.content: but looked amazing! Are there tours to see it, because it is on a busy road? I would have paid. Next time!

reviews.author: Lim T
reviews.title: Not the same as photograph
reviews.content: Look from the photo very nice. But actually, have many traffic that side. Look old and not really ok. Dissapointed

reviews.author: Mary M
reviews.title: Interesting mosaic
reviews.content: Passed this wonderful mosaic, depicting Vietnamese culture, every time we took the taxi into the old quarter.

reviews.author: NathaPushpa d
reviews.title: Very nice fine mosaic mural on one side of the road
reviews.content: Excellent art work using Cermic Mosaics. Very fine art work. The length of the mural is about 2km. Nicely done. This is located in a very busy road and very hard to photographed unless vehicle stops in a traffic sign. otherwise use video recording . I have done that and it has come up nicely as I have told my driver to drive slowly. Lots of hard work done by vietnamese young artists. Seems to be taken 4yrs to complete this art work. Its worth it..rather than graffiting the blank walls..it stops also doing that...Thanks for young artitic people of Vietnam..You all have done marvelous job which I have not seen any where else.

reviews.author: Shawn S
reviews.title: The world's longest piece of art
reviews.content: This is one of the things that makes Hanoi Hanoi. It lines one side of a very large and busy road, so it's not the easiest thing to access on foot. This mural is still expanding and has recently added an homage to Hugo Chavez of Venezuela as far West as Xuan Dieu st. There are community contributions to the design of the mural; it's obvious that students in primary schools were commissioned to contribute designs, and they are charming. The sheer variety of styles is inexhaustible, meaning you can pass by the mural many, many times and still see something new. The best way to visit the mural is to hire a taxi or xe om and tell them "Di Cham" while pointing at the mural. They'll get the  message and do what they can to drive slow while you view it.

reviews.author: AADSWJ
reviews.title: Creative
reviews.content: It's along roadside in main road right outside the Old Quarter.  Somehow you will pass it. It was created by those villages in trade to promote their historical handcraft skills.  Some designs are cute,  some are kiddy like. It's better than go to museums!

reviews.author: Rengarajan S
reviews.title: Mosaic mural on roadside
reviews.content: As you head towards the long bridge, you can see very nice mosaic artwork on either sides of the road.... very artistic and so nice to see.....It was commissioned to commemorate the millennium of Hanoi

reviews.author: AAS619
reviews.title: Nice to see from a moving car
reviews.content: We only saw that from the car but I really thought it was beautiful. It goes for quite a distance. I am not sure if I would recommend walking along the sidewalk, unless you desire to contemplate each piece. I liked to have a little bit of perspective and see it change, also it runs along a busy artery road and I would not care to walk around there. That’s why I am glad we saw that from a moving car when we were coming to and leaving Hanoi a few times.

reviews.author: sue5290
reviews.title: Such an interesting art installation
reviews.content: There is such much to look at as you travel along this mural. Many hands created different images of this country and it has some fascinating detail. We really enjoyed studying it and imaging the many different people who took part in it's design and installation.

reviews.author: Toni S
reviews.title: Miles of mosaics on busy streets
reviews.content: This was a recent initiative to celebrate Hanoi millennium by having several streets decorated by mosaics from hundreds artists. It was an original plan but the execution is questionable. The streets decorated are busy with car and scooters and pedestrian unfriendly and there are a few spots where one can enjoy them.

reviews.author: BrakiWorldTraveler
reviews.title: Pity it's on a busy and unattractive street
reviews.content: We saw this beautiful mosaic stretching for hundreds of meters because it was just across our hotel. It's very long and we looked at it while going on bus tours from the hotel.I think it deserves a much better place than on this very busy and uninviting street. You can hardly approach it and walk by due to heavy traffic around.

reviews.author: Lengyelek
reviews.title: Very good initiative from the city
reviews.content: It can bee seen the best from the car or motorbike when passing, more difficult to get close on foot, but worth to do it.

reviews.author: denglander
reviews.title: Loved this !
reviews.content: Awesome ceramic mosaic spanning a huge distance, colourful and great art telling wonderful stories. really worth taking a look if you like art !

reviews.author: palawanismyhome
reviews.title: So many mosaic pieces
reviews.content: Construction began in 2007 of the Ceramic Mosaic Mural which stretches about 6 kms along several roads and ends at Long Bien Bridge. It was the brainchild of  journalist Nguyen Thu Thuy who won a contest for transforming the dyke system in Hanoi to this beautiful mosaic wall. It celebrates the Millennial anniversary of Hanoi which took place in 2010. Vietnamese artists, foreign embassies and cultural centers all helped to construct the wall. All the porcelain came from the village of Bat Trang, otherwise known as the pottery village. The mosaic consists of scenes from Hanoi, modern art and children's drawings, and is now in the Guinness Book of World Records as being the biggest mosaic on the planet.

reviews.author: ailenroc13
reviews.title: It's a must
reviews.content: I wish several cities in the world (including mine) follow this example of decorating highway walls. This one is fab, with different themes all along, so it's a real pleasure to slowly drive along (on your way to the airport) or walk along for a while(it's 4 km long) to discover the various themes. Great idea beautifully realized!

reviews.author: Skimsa
reviews.title: A nice mosaic you will travel past it.
reviews.content: A huge and nice mosaic. You will see it often whilst travelling around (we passed it on our way to Halong) so no need to make a special visit to see it.

reviews.author: Q1578LVsandrat
reviews.title: Fun murals to celebrate 1000 years of Hanoi being the capital
reviews.content: Fun to see going to and from the airport. We traveled on part of our trip with someone from Vietnam and they were quite proud of this and the new bridge in Hanoi ( trying to ease some of the congestion.)

reviews.author: Tiddy W.
reviews.title: Mosaic art along the main road of Hanoi
reviews.content: Just mosaic art but the lenght is alomg the road in Hanoi. Includes famous places in ASEAN country and vietnam places and story. Street art in Hanoi. Colorful and maybe interesting if you have time to see some spots. Nice but isn't the must see must visit place, however you sure will be see this when travelling in Hanoi.

reviews.author: RaRa
reviews.title: Great view while riding a taxi or on the back of a motorcycle...
reviews.content: The mosaic mural stretched for miles and it was a great view from our taxi ride. It was astonishing how they were able to conceptualize and create such art work with the use of mosaic tiles and how each picture depicted had its own story to tell about the rich culture and past of Vietnam.It's a refreshing view amidst the herds of motorcycles zooming past each other in the busy streets of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Omaandopa17
reviews.title: Amazing Mosaic for miles
reviews.content: I love driving pass this, it goes on for miles and some of the work is incrediable.  Best on the back of a motor bike, You can walk it too but its a quite long but worth it.

reviews.author: Tommy-Levandosky
reviews.title: Normal
reviews.content: I like looking at the patterns on these walls. But it seems they have not been cared for long enough.

reviews.author: alisssnow
reviews.title: Very cool!
reviews.content: It's amazing how much time and effort this must have taken! there are so many tiles! A very interesting walk.

reviews.author: Julie M
reviews.title: Very difficult to view.
reviews.content: This mural is on the walls of a freeway! The best you can do is see it from a car or motorbike or do as we did, see it from a distance from the Long Bien bridge.

reviews.author: John C
reviews.title: the great wall of vietnam
reviews.content: We only noticed the wall on our way to the airport to go home but thought it was beautifully done. Dont know the story of it but you could see many different themes as you drove along. Was very impressed

reviews.author: zycieipodroze
reviews.title: Amazing, beautiful and unique ceramic mosaic in Hanoi.
reviews.content: Hanoi Ceramic Mosaic Mural is amazing. It has a length of 4.1 kilometers, which measured the driving engine :) Ceramic mosaic wall is one of the projects developed on the occasion of the millennium uprising Hanoi. Ceramic mosaic wall depicts the history of Vietnam throughout history and includes more than 1,000 years. We admire presented on the history of different dynasties, and scenes from the legends and stories.

reviews.author: Lorenzo R
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: We saw this impressive wall of mosaics when we first entered the city.The aim of the mural was to transform the urban stretches of the Red River Dyke, an essential flood defence that had been subjected to illegal graffiti and advertising.The mural had been in construction since 2007 and involved 35 professional artists from Vietnam and 10 other countries

reviews.author: Djodi
reviews.title: Mosaic murals
reviews.content: I didn't realize they were a thing but in fact we passed them daily on our way to Tay Ho district. As a major fan of mosaics these were varied, colorful and a delight gracing the highway.

reviews.author: Jim M
reviews.title: Awesome wall!
reviews.content: Beautiful ceramic wall, very long! Colorful, lots of activity.  Much traffic!  Worth walking to.  That's all!

reviews.author: KimberleyInOz
reviews.title: The longest mosaic wall in the world - keep your eye out for it in your travels
reviews.content: Worth keeping your eye out for this little gem as you travel - running from near the Old Quarter out to near West Lake / Tay Ho.A lovely touch of colour in the city. It features flashes of history and aspects of life in Hanoi.

reviews.author: marcopolo0979
reviews.title: Km after km of ceramic mosaic murals
reviews.content: Km after km of ceramic mosaic murals - almost 4 km - completed in 2010 in time for Hanoi's 1,000 bday celebration. A very interesting and at times beautiful work of art considered the largest ceramic mosaic on earth, that is a challenge to view, given the horrendous vehicular traffic on the road it's located on.

reviews.author: danliew
reviews.title: surprise to see the miles of mosaic along the busy traffic...
reviews.content: i was going to spend a few hours taking pictures of the Mosaic, but have to stay in bed after eating street foods... major regret !

reviews.author: Snowjunkie7
reviews.title: Wall Art
reviews.content: Found out this wall is the history of Vietnam and what their culture believes. It is difficult to view this art piece as it spans over 10km and there is heavy traffic, but on the drive it is something awesome to look at.

reviews.author: Bob M
reviews.title: 2 km long
reviews.content: This is an astonishing piece of work -- it seem sto stretch for ever. Nice to see such art in a fairly grimy city.

reviews.author: BigChiefMountain
reviews.title: Mosaic wall and see markets
reviews.content: Easy way to view and see local markets.  You can walk along mural is quite spectacular.  At the end is the farmers market that will allow you to taste local fruits and vegetables.

reviews.author: patriciafA8013AE
reviews.title: Just beautiful!
reviews.content: This mosaic wall is so pretty and the mural is very long and constantly changes. It is a wonderful work of art.

reviews.author: AntonioAGSC
reviews.title: a change in the Hanoi street landspace
reviews.content: The road where the ceramic mosaic mural is is a quite wide one and with a lot of traffic but it gives us a different look that must be seen

reviews.author: gracecatherineh
reviews.title: Especially Cool if youre driving by on the back of a moto!
reviews.content: Our guide took us along a length of this on the back of her moto - pretty cool. Apparently it was built in 1010 AD to keep the sea out of Hanoi and so in 2010 they gave it a makeover!

reviews.author: cmbreuer2016
reviews.title: A celebration of 1000 years of being a city!
reviews.content: We have been to Hanoi many times and every time we visit another part of the mural. It would be overwhelming to try and see it all in one visit. Different artists from different countries created this mural along with schoolchildren and companies. To us this is the celebration of Vietnamese people and their appreciation of all types of art.

reviews.author: Emellee
reviews.title: Beautiful, huge, worth a walk
reviews.content: I saw part of the mural on the way in to the city but didn't realize that it was the worlds largest ceramic mosaic mural!The length and detail is extremely impressive. The colors are vibrant and each section of the wall depicts something different about Vietnam and the culture.It is located on a busy road, but the sidewalk is wide enough for a person to walk safely and look at it at the same time.And best of all, it's free!

reviews.author: easterntreker
reviews.title: So Artistic
reviews.content: We say this from our tour bus and I have to say it is one of the most stunning  street wall art I have ever seen .

reviews.author: seetheworld010
reviews.title: Lovely!
reviews.content: Long ago it was nothing but an ugly wall until the renovation came about. It makes the city more pleasant and attractive. Just drive along it.

reviews.author: On the road
reviews.title: place need to visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: The best wtime to visit its after the...rain, the watter clean all the dirtything on mosaic wall. Early morning, when stress not noisy, busy and too dirty, you can feel true Hanoi throught this road. They spend lot of works to finished long raod, but really feel said when they do not spend money to repair every year, some places start damaaged, with weather in Hanoi, easy to fall when no one take care. This road laying on one side of qui, has lot gates go through to other side next to Hong river, all those ugly gate, with block betton no paint, nothing to fix with this beautiful wall, make you feel like eat one stone in spoon of smooth yoghurt. I don't understand why town hall do not spend money to pain, to make those gates become more better looking. Two poor garders standing take care miss beauty!

reviews.author: Ltp_BKK
reviews.title: Nice if you looking form the footpath opposite the mosaic work.
reviews.content: It is a nice pieces of art. However, you should admire these art form the opposite footpath because the pathway which the mosaic work located is really dirty smell and disgusting. There are some people pee here!!! So it will be safe if you just be at the opposite footpath of the street.

reviews.author: Adam S
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: We basically just drive past it on our way out of Hanoi but it is amazing to see. It's feking huge and beautifully done.

reviews.author: theandrews031
reviews.title: Makes a lovely change from Graffiti
reviews.content: In our transfer from the airport to the old quarter of Hanoi our driver pointed out this mural and explained each piece to us. This is a great idea and more cities around the world should take on this idea as it brightens up the route and makes a change to graffiti.

reviews.author: Jacqui B
reviews.title: A spash of colour
reviews.content: We drove past this mural a couple of times while driving around the city. It made the coach stops and starts very interesting as you looked at the different styles on the mosaic. Please to see there was no graffiti on it too.

reviews.author: Lee S
reviews.title: An Amazing Sight To Behold
reviews.content: This mosaic was built to commemorate the 1000th year of the City of Hanoi in 2010. And mark that occasion they did with this beautiful and colorful 4km piece of art and culture. I had a chance to view this magnificent mosaic and see the stories of ancient Vietnamese history and legend depicted as I was riding from my hotel to the Noi Bai Airport to catch my flight home. I cannot even imagine all the thousands of hours planning and executing to create this display that should hopefully stand for centuries.

reviews.author: Maughin L
reviews.title: So beautiful - an absolute must see!
reviews.content: This is the longest mosaic in the Guinness Book of Records, and it is absolutely gorgeous. Be sure to take the time to walk past part of it (it is kms and kms long) or get a taxi to drive you along the road to see it - the colours and the stories that have been captured are just so lovely!

reviews.author: chris1689
reviews.title: Amazing Artwork
reviews.content: Other the course of the few days in Hanoi we passed this everyday on the way to our morning adventures as well as on the way back to our hotel. It made sitting in traffic a little more bearable. It is really amazing to see that something like this could be build and it is an enormously long Mosaic Mural. There are so many different types of events, places, people etc depicted on it. it is definitely something to see. What also amazed me was how well kept it was. In a city that was not very clean it was kept in great condition. I don't know if it is needed to actually walk the whole thing because it is a long mural. but is cool passing by it everyday and seeing all the different artwork on it.

reviews.author: Dushi-NY
reviews.title: Many different styles.
reviews.content: We passed the mosaics wall twice while sitting on a tour bus.  There are so many different styles depicted - traditional, modern, floral, people, etc.  We got stuck in traffic so the slow ride enabled us to appreciate the mosaics.  Amazing that the mosaics are relatively clean and that people are respectful enough to not damage the artwork.  It was even more fun watching the scooters laden with tires, supplies, groceries and people zipping past the mosaics.

reviews.author: Sherry7656
reviews.title: Amazing Mosaic
reviews.content: Absolutely stunning collection of different styles of art work - they merge beautifully as you drive along - amazing that something this gigantic designed by so many different people could actually be created.   Makes the drive through Hanoi so interesting!

reviews.author: maxscuba
reviews.title: Such a long mosaic
reviews.content: Built to celebrate one thousand years from the foundation of Vietnamese reign, it is an almost 5km long mosaic depicting most aspects of local culture.A not to be missed attractions ... but don't go on foot or you'll be likely to be killed by exhaust fumes! The road is extremely busy, maybe the best way to enjoy it is by scooter with multiple stop and goes to take captivating photos.

reviews.author: Lyndaanne16
reviews.title: Street Art with a difference.
reviews.content: Lovely street art featuring different styles of workmanship as sections done by different people along it's 6 km length.  It's a recent work, but depicts the city's history.  It made it into the Guinness Book of Records for largest mosaic.

reviews.author: Jerry N
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: This is a collaboration of many artistss.   Next time I'm in Hanoi I hope to spend more time sturying the works.

reviews.author: bajanboy46
reviews.title: amazing
reviews.content: Unfortunately we did not see this until we were leaving Hanoi.If I ever return it will be worth the walk to see it.

reviews.author: Susan L
reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.content: Wonderful display of public art. It run 4km along a busy road so if you are nervous crossing and walking the streets you'll need to view from a taxi. A quick walk from Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Vanessa Q
reviews.title: Goes on forever
reviews.content: Hobby of mine massive piece of art work .  Well worth strolling along to get a better idea of the scope of the work.

reviews.author: Roddy S
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: Not much to see really and the directions are unclear. No one knew about it and Google's location is wrong. We later passed by it on another taxi trip. It's nice to see for 2 mins on a taxi. Not worth going "there".

reviews.author: The Gypsy Club
reviews.title: Great artwork!
reviews.content: Not much to review here, only that it's a very long stretch of mosaic art along a busy road. Still nice though!

reviews.author: Carol Blue Mountains
reviews.title: Take time to look out of your taxi window at the murals
reviews.content: Its easy to miss these murals, but once you see them you'll appreciate the variety of subject material, styles and lack of graffiti

reviews.author: pauline o
reviews.title: Awesome 4 Km street rmural
reviews.content: Took a ride along this mural in a cyclo.  Amazing, very varied themes and certainly some humour there.  We also passed it in a bus when on day trips out of Hanoi itself, but you need to see it in a slow-moving vehicle to really appreciate it, and it is not possible to walk along the road safely.  Highly recommend.

reviews.author: riahijihan14
reviews.title: nice place
reviews.content: you can come here and walk along the road .You will feel how Vietnamese people working here.very hard and friendly .The sell all good fruites and natural staff.Very cheap.

reviews.author: Severine & Lukasz
reviews.title: A long piece of art
reviews.content: The wall is part of an expressway but there is a sidewalk for those who wish to walk along it. We drove alongside it by bus. It is a very long wall and beautifully decorated. It must have taken a long time to make this.

reviews.author: PORhibido
reviews.title: Nice but No Need to Make a Detour
reviews.content: Celebrating Hanoi's millennial anniversary (2010), this colourful mosaic mural tells the history of Vietnam, but don't be surprised if you can spot ASEAN landmarks (e.g. Cambodia's Angkor Wat and Myanmar's Shwedagon) or even Simón Bolívar.  If you're staying in the Old Quarter, you will very likely see it on the way from/to the airport so unless you want to take close-up photos there's no need for a detour.

reviews.author: Robert L
reviews.title: Something different
reviews.content: This ceramic mosaic mural is a work of art in its own right. It brighten up the road as we traveled into Hanoi.

reviews.author: Linda M
reviews.title: worth seeing
reviews.content: some of the detailed work in this mosaic is amazing can be hard to see due to the volumn of traffic,try to view it from above ie the railway bridge

reviews.author: robeja32
reviews.title: Amazing Street
reviews.content: I was cry when i seen that street. Actually beautiful, i told with my friends that: "you will must came Ha Noi in the future "

reviews.author: ranranran
reviews.title: Interesting!
reviews.content: The mosaic mural was wonderful to see, and so beautiful! Every time we passed the road I couldn't take my eyes off to see the wonderful mural.
