reviews.content: hotel could have told cab driver where we wanted to go, ended up  wandering around. no one indicated correct path

reviews.author: spktravels
reviews.title: Interesting stop
reviews.content: The Silk Village which is now part of Hanoi is  limited to several streets but it is worth a visit.We stopped at one family owned shop which still operates its own looms. Apparently most of the shops in the Silk Village are merely retailers.We learned the process of making silk fabric from the start, silk worms, to designing patterns, to the actual weaving.Next to the manufacturing area is a nice sized shop. There is a large selection of completed garments such as dresses, pajamas and scarfs all reasonably priced. in addition for those who are so inclined there is a wide array of silk fabrics from which you have have clothes made on your own.This shop is modern and the owners were friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: 175MOM
reviews.title: Great silk shopping experience
reviews.content: I enjoyed the visit to the silk village. The entire area is not big, but I still did not get to see all the stores in 2 hours we had.   I see mixed reviews and I can see why. If you are not interested in silk, you should probably skip it.  All the stores are selling silk fabric/scarves, so I can see why people may get bored if you are not interested.  My husband was...but I loved the place as I love fabrics.   Is this "touristy" place?  Sure, I don't think the  locals would pay those prices.  But entire Hanoi is kind of touristy.  Also some may be disappointed that many products are not made there at the silk village.  "Authentic" or not, this is the place to go for silk shopping. I really wanted to see how silk is made in old fashioned way.  I assumed we could see it right in the middle where a small pond/arch are.  But this courtyard is just surrounded by shops.  At one of the stores we bought a scarf, and asked about it.  The store lady pointed to go to the residential area.  So we did, walked for a while but did not see anything.  Maybe they have closed down, or maybe we would have seen if we wondered off smaller streets.  We went back to the silk village and browsed more stores.  At another store where I bought fabric, a very helpful lady, who also made the fabric I bought (and her father dyed it), said her home where she makes fabric is 30 min away, but told as to go to store called Mao and showed us where.  She also advised us that their fabrics are more expensive.  Mao was a larger store in this area, and there is factory/house right next to it.  The store ladies said we could take a look at the factory, so we did that first.  Our kid thought it was interesting. I am not an expart, but theier fabric seemd to be better quality. Some are 100% silk and some are not, and they are clearly marked.  I bought the one my kid liked.   Also some stores also sell non-silk souvenirs in small quantities.  I found some beautiful fans. We did not bargan.  Coming from the U.S., I thought the price was already reasonable, and felt barganing was not appropriate. But I guess you could if you wanted.  We did "cheap" silk shopping in HCMC, but shopping in Van Phuc Silk village was something compeltely different and I enjoyed it.

reviews.author: nickal06
reviews.title: A dying place... unfortunately
reviews.content: Well, well well...This place tries (sadely) to survive with the tourist but there not that much left.Far away, surrounded by the constructions, no need of crytal ball to predict its future...

reviews.author: elna m
reviews.title: Nothing extraordinary
reviews.content: This was just another commercial outlet, nothing unique about it.  If in the area, worth a visit but do not expect anything authentic.

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: Not what I was expecting
reviews.content: Loads of places selling silk, however they are all selling the same stuff. However we did get to see the old style weaving machines that I would say come from the era of our industrial revolution, very noisy and the health and safety people would have a fit lol.The area for the dyeing of the silks was also available to see, didn't get too close didn't want to inhale the fumes.

reviews.author: WAprof
reviews.title: Buying silk fabric
reviews.content: If you'd like to buy silk fabric then make sure and visit Van Phuc. They also have scarves, and other clothing but one of my goals in visiting was fabric and I found a lovely selection here.

reviews.author: LaraDay1993
reviews.title: Van Phuc Silk village
reviews.content: If you have some extra time to kill while you're in Hanoi - the silk village is a nice trip. It's not too far away and the drive is a scenic one of the city. I would recommend that you spend 2 hours there. You probably won't need more time than that. There are no real restaurants there, however one cafe for drinks. I'd recommend that if you're keen to know more about the silk village, try and get hold of a tour guide, there are no information centres or plaques up explaining anything (I may have missed them though ).  Everyone is relatively chilled, you can walk straight into the factories with beautiful old looms still in use. You may even be lucky and see them in use. The silk products are stunning , however the shops become repetitive and some products say 100% silk and then when you ask, the shop assistant will tell you that it's actually not 100%.  There is a stunning shop at the top of the street with silk clothing and scarves that are to die for so definitely take your time and shop around. You can buy various types of silk as well, and you can buy it in meters. The prices aren't too bad, you're looking at $10-$20 a scarf and a bit more for a silk shirt. There is a lovely garden and shrine there as well so have a look at that is well. I think that if you have the time, it's a nice place to visit.

reviews.author: FaithMY
reviews.title: Not worth the visit
reviews.content: We were greatly disappointed at what the silk village has to offer. Shops all selling almost same things . Poor design and price not great either. Not worth the visit.

reviews.author: Kathy K
reviews.title: Skip if limited on time
reviews.content: It was interesting to see how silk is made. I had no idea the amount of labor involved. I wisely left my credit card in the car.This was my second time in Hanoi. I would not recommend this if time is limited. There are far more interesting things to see in the Hanoi area

reviews.author: Annemarie V
reviews.title: lots of silk
reviews.content: it's nice to take a tour, let someone else do the organising, get a bit of info on the area. Lan, our guide was lovely and happy to chat about local culture. we made some nice purchases. some satin silk aud$14 per meter, I have paid 40 at home for lower quality. everyone friendly and no pressure.

reviews.author: Grazbee
reviews.title: Nice for 1-2hours
reviews.content: This Silk Village is really beautiful and the people are so nice. It is nice to see it if you are in Hanoi for 1week. :)

reviews.author: sally a
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.content: My expectations of visiting the silk village as part of the tour I was on were certainly not met. It seemed to be geared to providing a venue for shopping - fair enough -  but some of what was on offer appeared to be cheap reproductions you can find anywhere. There was some nice silk and we did get to see a mechanised weaving set up which showed how the patterns were woven - you could do with ear plugs at this point as it is very noisy. For me it was a very disappointing visit.

reviews.author: Kiko
reviews.title: Very nice products but not sold in all shops
reviews.content: We visited the silk village this month and saw some amazing offers for silk ties and pashminas! You just need to check almost every shop in order to find the right quality- really worth the effort going there.

reviews.author: Justin S
reviews.title: Was a good trip. Maybe worth an arranged tour
reviews.content: Easy to get there by taxi. Approx 190,000 VND from Hanoi Opera House. Bargain given is takes 30-40mins due to traffic. We fancied just wandering around so didn't book any guides/tours. For our needs it worked well. We got to watch a lady working a loom and then wandered the quiet streets, in and out of shops. Some really lovely products. If you want the full run down of the area, how it all works etc, you may want to research in advance or consider a guide. However I don't think it's necessary to spend $$$ on guides. We were there about 70-80 mins. Plenty of time for a leisurely stroll. Our cab driver offered to wait for us, but no need as it's close to a very main road where hailing a cab was easy. Worth a look.

reviews.author: Jean Ann F
reviews.title: Shopping Heaven!!!
reviews.content: More shops and pretty things to buy than anyone could dream of!!!  Prices are VERY affordable.  I enjoyed the history of silk and watching the looms.

reviews.author: Yevgeniya K
reviews.title: Good place to buy fabric
reviews.content: Dont expect to find beautifull silk clothes there. The clothes are not that beautifull and they are not silk. But its the place to find the best silk fabrics ever. Its not that cheap ( the best silk is about 25$ a meter) but still cheaper than in europe. I suggest to come with a lighter so you can check if the fabric is real. They can easily sell you viscose for silk and you will never know, it looks so similar.

reviews.author: Brayden_byn
reviews.title: High quality product silk!!!
reviews.content: From 10km from our hotel in Old Quater, we visited Van Phuc Silk village which is amazing village with helpful and friendly local people and beautiful sightseeings, but impressed thing with me is high quality product silk which is made by hand of local people . It's amazing experiences, thanks Hanoi Free Walking Tours to support us during our trip.You can catch bus 02 and 21 to travel to there.

reviews.author: Su H
reviews.title: Silk village
reviews.content: The name is Silk village, so I expected to see a variety of silk fabric.  But reality is far from expectation.Nothing much to see, all the shops are selling almost the same items. You need to ask for discount in most of the shops as the shops mark up the price especially to the foreigners.Just 40 minutes drive from Hanoi old quarter.

reviews.author: Tania P
reviews.title: Nice silks,nice setting
reviews.content: Nice silks,but most shops all carry same selections, so very repetitive .. The nicer shops were quite expensive & no real bargaining .. Enjoyed seeing silk worms and the looms,but not much else to do. The little park nearby is nice for a wonder.

reviews.author: Adan c
reviews.title: Outstanding white silk dress
reviews.content: Travelling Van Phuc village in lately afternoon, i surprised before the beauty of Van Phuc silk like the rainbow. Furthermore, Hung uncle who is enthusiastic local people told us the history of the village and how to make special of Van Phuc silk. 10km from Hanoi Old Quater, you can travel buy bus or hire moto.

reviews.author: TravelforScuba
reviews.title: Silk Scarves, Silk Worms, and That's About It
reviews.content: Went here looking for inexpensive silk items. Most of what we saw was scarves, a few dresses, and shirts. Most shops have the same items so you can haggle to get the best price. We were a bit underwhelmed there was no one demonstrating the silk weaving just a bunch of old machines set up to show the process. This was interesting but a live demonstration would have been great. It's about a $5 cab ride from old town so cheap to get there. So if you have an hour to kill it's not a complete waste.

reviews.author: agrippina1952
reviews.title: perhaps the high season is better here
reviews.content: We visited in winter, and many of the shops were shut. We had been told that we could see silk weaving and manufacturing in process, but that was not to be. The place seemed rather bleak and deserted. All the silk products on display were very similar, and not cheaper than in the Old Quarter or Hang Gai. I wouldn't bother, but then perhaps a visit in summer might be very different.

reviews.author: KeepMemories
reviews.title: Quiet pleasant walk
reviews.content: The place was really quiet, huge contrast with the busy preparation for Ted New Year in the Old Quarter. The shops sell similar things to Old Quarter silk shops but since it's so quiet, we had a leisurely walk and browse.

reviews.author: shocar
reviews.title: It worth the trip for clothes. Be aware sellers to follow you everywhere
reviews.content: We had here a nice day with a friend shopping around and checking for nice clothes made in silk.Most fancy shops use to charge more, so expect to find more western designs and prices too.Some sellers are not kind and follow you in all the shop what I found very uncomfortable, but I understand is a culture misunderstanding.If you are big size, XL for Europe or US I suggest better go to Hue to buy clothes where they have more sizes due the lot of tourists there.

reviews.author: annalee2403
reviews.title: amazing attraction
reviews.content: Arrive Van Phuc village I was impressed by typical manner of an ancient village in the north of Vietnam with banyan tree, well, communal house, and the sound of power-looms everywhere. There are very much silk with various products like shirts, ties, crafts, dresses…

reviews.author: Beaumaris32
reviews.title: A Great Day Out
reviews.content: At the end of our walking/touring visit to N Vietnam, the 10 of us had to to do a craft village tour.    So, combined with the Bat Trang Ceramic village (see my review) we had a splendid day out - Bat Trang in the morning, back to Hanoi for lunch, then Vin Phuc Silk village in the afternoon.    You start off with a close look at were they spin the silk and make the cloth on looms - very interesting.    Then you can stroll around the large number of places selling all sorts of silk items from scarves to shirts and blouses etc.   Do the usual, expected bargaining and, bingo, souvenir/gift problems solved !   A very pleasant day out.

reviews.author: kdk1965
reviews.title: Up-thumb on the insight and down-thumb on bargains
reviews.content: We stopped here as part of a private tour and while we enjoyed seeing how silk is made, the rest of the visit was simply ok.  It felt "canned" and more like an amusement park area in terms of the approach.  Shops were lovely, the ladies selling items in the shop were lovely, but this is not a free market area.

reviews.author: Dylan G
reviews.title: Great insight into silk manufacturing
reviews.content: Friendly locals, free tour through a silk manufactory. Many silk toys and clothes purchasable. There's a small marketplace next door that sells cheaper items, so it's worth shopping around.

reviews.author: dccollyer
reviews.title: Don't Miss It
reviews.content: As a lace maker I was keen to buy silk thread which is not something they normally sell.  However the management kindly agreed and I came away very satisfied. This is a wonderful place which needs more promotion!

reviews.author: MsAnnHanoi
reviews.title: Touristy but still have a story
reviews.content: Van Phuc silk village , now in Van Phuc ward, Ha Dong disrict, Hanoi, 10km from the city centre, has been the most famous and long lasting silk weaving village in Vietnam with various patterns.Since its first appearance, silk from Van Phuc village became a favorable product thanks to the skilful and sopisticated hans and souls of weavers which were crystallized in each piece of silk. Van Phuc silk was always provided for mandarins to make official clothes. Despite historical changes, Van Phuc silk weaving has still been growing for the last 10 centuries. Itnitially , Van Phus silk was produced only for upper and middle feudal classes. The late 19th century the Nguyen dynasy encouraged people to use domestic products and craftsmen of Van Phuc Viallage quickly collected, learnt, and innovated to “popularize” silk and satin product.

reviews.author: Sebastian L
reviews.title: Touristy
reviews.content: Unless you are very keen to know the intricate process of silk making, the few stalls selling silk products are less appealing than the shops at Old quarters. An optional tour in my opinion.

reviews.author: ColinGJ
reviews.title: Mostly shopping
reviews.content: This is mostly a couple of streets of silk shops selling very nice items. At the back of one of the shops, you can go into a room where they are making some silk objects, and watch the old machines working. Mostly of interest if you want to buy clothes or souvenirs, but not that different to what you can buy in the centre of Hanoi, really.

reviews.author: pw0867
reviews.title: Nice silk and a factory to visit how they make silk clothes
reviews.content: It would be boring for young kids.  With the exception of the factory that you could visit where they showed you how they made silk garments, it was just a bunch of shops selling silk clothing items.  Some were not cheaper than I could have gotten at home, but the wide variety and selection of items was good.It was better than the ceramic village, but not much to see, unless you were in the mood to buy silk.

reviews.author: fickle_flower
reviews.title: Touristy, but more variety than at the Old Quarter
reviews.content: Probably a visit is in place if your intention is to buy silk goods in Hanoi. There are more variety in terms of fabric selection than in the Old Quarter. Prices appear more reasonable, although you still have to bargain hard. They close pretty early, around 7pm

reviews.author: AppreciateAdvice
reviews.title: Can't understand the glowing reviews... not worth visiting
reviews.content: The village is a few streets of "shops" selling silk.  There's nothing interesting, original, compelling or otherwise worthy of spending the time to get there, walk-around and go back to Hanoi.  Sure, there's a working mill where you can learn about how silk is made and watch-it, but it's really not so exciting.  And I didn't find anything that was either special or value-priced or both to make a visit worthwhile.  Pass...

reviews.author: happywanderer1954
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Visited the Village, unfortunately it was at lunch time, so didn't see a lot of activity but it was interesting see the looms and the shopping was good.  Went with a private guide and this was just a cheap as going with an organised tour but we were able to fit in a little more during the day.  Some tour companies advertise an admission fee...don't believe it.  There is not admission fee, you can just walk in.

reviews.author: EmillyStephenie
reviews.title: good for shopping
reviews.content: A place has so much shirt, dress,...which are made from silk by hand made. . everything in here are very cheap and special !

reviews.author: GeciDC
reviews.title: Nothing much here
reviews.content: We went here as part of our day tour to Doung Lam Ancient Village. What to do? Nothing much. You just take a peak on how they make silk and then you will visit a shop that sell their finished silk products and you'll realize after that it is cheaper to get them in the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Phua W
reviews.title: Not worth the time
reviews.content: Went there as part of a day tour. Just a short street was shops selling silk products.  Totally not interesting and not worth the time.  I'd you are looking for silk products,  shops in the old quarters are more interesting.

reviews.author: TravellingMouse2014
reviews.title: Interesting program that showed us the process of silk making from the silk worms eating to finished silk
reviews.content: We watched silk worms eating mulberry leaves, saw the cocoons, saw spinners spinning silk, saw operators winding silk on spools, watched the weavers following elaborate paper cutout patterns on the looms, and saw the beautifully patterned silk emerging from the looms.

reviews.author: msinwdc
reviews.title: Not Worth It
reviews.content: Oh how I wish I listened to most of the reviews here on T.A. I just can't hear the word "village" and not think that it will be a charming and quiet locale full of locals working on their handicraft. And after going to Ba Trang pottery village, which is just that, I was hoping Van Phuc would be the silk equivalent.But alas, it is as many previous reviewers have commented - nothing special or interesting. I couldn't even find the shops that actually spin the silk. Perhaps it's less busy in November (I was the only non-Vietnamese person there) and this activity is not done all year?If you must go, it's worth hiring a guide or asking a local Vietnamese friend to take you, just to make sure you see all there is to see. As already noted, you only need an hour or two. I think this place is of most interest to people who want to buy fabric rather than ready-made items, because the latter are more readily available in Hanoi's Old Quarter. While I didn't see a lot of fabric, what I did see was beautiful and soft.

reviews.author: Brenda R
reviews.title: Small, not much to see or do
reviews.content: I expected the silk village to be more like the colorful, bustling center or Hoi An, so it was a bit of a disappointment. There were significantly fewer shops, and the merchandise was rather limited. Primarily only ready made clothing (as opposed to the custom shops you can find in other parts of Vietnam) and scarves. Not really any decorative items for the home. We had intended to spend a few hours here and maybe grab lunch as well, but other than 1 or 2 fruit vendors and a few small pharmacies, there weren't really any other dining options. We were able to pop into the 2 temples and all of the silk kiosks (around 25) in just over an hour. This is definitely not a full day or even half day excursion if you plan to work it into your schedule.

reviews.author: Nhu_Phuong
reviews.title: Genuine and cheap silk!
reviews.content: It's very easy to get here. Take xe ôm (motorbike taxi) for about 4-5 dollars each way. A lot more expensive by taxi.Here, you'll get to see how they produce silk products. And you can purchase good quality and cheap silk here. This is my go-to place when I need to by gifts for my international friends. About 5 dollars for a silk scarf, That's a good bargain, right?

reviews.author: CHUN C
reviews.title: LIKE A MARKET - THAT'S ALL
reviews.content: Go there if your purpose is to buy silk fabrics and scarf. Otherwise, do not come here coz nothing for your visit. The good thing is the price of silk is cheaper than Dong Xuan market and not crowded.

reviews.author: lastlyvn
reviews.title: A silk village you can see people weaving silk cloth
reviews.content: This is originally a village people produce silk and silk products.  However, it seems the business has come down and nowadays not so many silk factories.  Most products can be found in Hoan Kiem Area and even cheaper there.  Products not exceedingly cheap and this place is quite far away from the city.  Not a particular attraction for tourists or even local people.  Especially do not go right after lunch, most shops are closed for afternoon sleep.

reviews.author: Mervyn C
reviews.title: Not interesting enough
reviews.content: When I heard about "Village", it crossed in my mind that it is very old and traditional, but in fact, it is modern. One minor of this village :(Also there are many silk shops there, but the real silk is little. Silk there might make in China, not from Van Phuc. If you have to use the good product, you should go to folk person there to ask for the special and good one.

reviews.author: Clare Y
reviews.title: Not worth seeing
reviews.content: Perhaps we missed something but all we could see were the silk shops near the main street. The name is misleading as it isn't a village at all and was just in Hanoi.There was construction on the street which I guess hid the looms and silkworm workshop. The city should put up a map near the 'welcome to Silk vilalge' sign to define some kind of walking path.Disappointing.

reviews.author: Ann T
reviews.title: Listen for the sound of the looms
reviews.content: This is a village full of silk shops but one which is no longer surrounded by mulberry trees. However, if you can hear the sound of the looms, go in and watch people at work weaving silk. We visited this on an Urban Adventure Village tour which was a great way to get insight into the place.

reviews.author: PALTravel
reviews.title: Good for purchasing gifts; some shops are more friendly than others.
reviews.content: You really need to shop around ... and if you want an authentic silk or 'pashmina', then you need to know your stuff as some shops slap labels on polyester and which says pashmina.  So, take the time to look at things in a variety of shops before you purchase.That said, the prices are very good and you can easily find something for everyone back home!  It's fun to walk the streets and, if you're interested, you can actually see the entire process (from silk worm to final, woven product.  We'd seen this in Turkey, so didn't bother on this trip.You can find scarfs in all prices.  The finer silk scarves are around $25usd.  Check out each piece before purchasing to make sure there aren't any snags or an damage to the item.We actually took a taxi to the village and he waited while we shopped.  Nice to not have to find a taxi when we were finished!If you have time to shop, this is a great place to do so!

reviews.author: Rafie K
reviews.title: Maybe March is the best time to visit Van Phuc
reviews.content: I was here last week and my sole purpose is to buy silk fabrics and scarf. My wife suggested this place to buy all things silk as she was here in March 2009.Good things:- You can see the silk worm and the process of making the fabric- Considerably low in price compared to Hanoi (and Don Xuan market)- Not that crowdedNot so good:- Less options of silk fabrics and scarf (Maybe due to the cold season)- The fabric options is more inclined towards the celebration of the lunar new yearDespite, I believe this will be better during hot season on whenever the silk worm is active producing the silk thread. I hope someone travel to this place in March or hotter season to supply with more information. Overall, it's a silk village for sure.

reviews.author: beachlady32927
reviews.title: Interesting stop over and nice people
reviews.content: I took a motorbike taxi out of Hanoi just to ride around. I saw the statue and small pond first and didn't know it was the silk village. It was a lovely stop. I have never seen this process or the machines. As a teacher and still a learning child myself I truly immersed myself into the machinery and people. The good we're QUALITY and I literally bought the silk that was on the machine. This was priceless to me. Worth seeing was the granite stones and shrine to the Vietnam war losses for this tiny town. Prices w o haggling were better than old town. I don't haggle much. I look at my life and paychecks and I look at theirs. I can afford 5$ more :)

reviews.author: Upperny
reviews.title: Great prices for silk scarves, but a small venue
reviews.content: We found ourselves with mixed feelings.  The scarves were inexpensive and beautiful ($5-10), but the extraoidinary ones were $25 and we should have bought those.  There are many shops ostensibly selling the same class of goods.  The people are lovely and the walk is short.  The demonstration of weaving isn't worth the trip, if you've seen such things before, but the prices are great and the selection is amazing, given the twenty or so shops.

reviews.author: kandl
reviews.title: Recommended for silk fabric lovers.
reviews.content: As a silk lover, I enjoyed seeing the process from silk worm to silk fabric. The old weaving machines were fascinating. Every type of silk in every colour and pattern available by the meter and some ready made clothes. A pleasant village only a short distance from frantic Hanoi.

reviews.author: DragonCrew
reviews.title: not as my expectation
reviews.content: It's on the way from Mai Chau to Hanoi and sure a good reststop if you want smth strange. There you can see the process of making silk but only at a tiny corner of the village communal house. In contrast, there are hundreds of "modern" things with lots of shops, street hawkers, cars and streetside food stalls. If you are fond of silk, we suggest you go for shopping at Hang Gai "silk" street inside Hanoi old quarter instead.

reviews.author: Anna T
reviews.title: Ideal place for buy silk products
reviews.content: We took private car in around 3 hours from Hanoi centre to the Van Phuc Village. These are many silk products hanging on boutique shops: Crafts, ties, dress, tissus..To be attracted by multiple color of silk products, we bought a lot of things: 10 crafts, 5 ties, somes dress.One thing have to be mentioned that we has made bargaining before settle the payment.It was nice expericence to see how the silkworm makes the fibers and how the spinner makes the tissus.Coming to this village is chance to discover the genuine traditional silk-making industry. Bisides that, this is ideal place for buying vietnamese silk.Recommended for everyone traveling to Hanoi.

reviews.author: BobBonHere
reviews.title: Not worth visiting
reviews.content: This was a bit of a disappointment. Our guide obviously had his preferred shops which were were 'encourage' to buy. Prices were OK but buying anything you didn't really want is expensive.

reviews.author: Mike
reviews.title: Not worth the hassle
reviews.content: We got the impression from Lonely Planet that this village this village was out of Hanoi in the country a little bit so hired a driver for the day to see this and the Thay and Tay Phuong Pagodas.The silk village was the big disappointment of the trip.  We felt like we were still in the middle of Hanoi when we turned off a main road and down a non-descript street lined with silk shops and into a courtyard, where we saw a few silkworm cocoons on a screen, what looked like some raw silk that had been unwould from cocoons some time ago, and into an old silk weaving room where there a few old looms, one of which was being operated.  We walked back out through the connected silk shop and down the street trying to find something else of interest, before getting back in the car and driving on to the pagodas.  Perhaps we missed something?

reviews.author: pngocduong1
reviews.title: Beautiful Silk Village Experience
reviews.content: We visited Van Phuc Silk Village during our Hanoi trip,  Our driver recommended that we visit, and we’re so glad he did!It was very interesting to walk around the village and see the variety of silk products. There were so many beautiful silk clothes, scarves, and other items to choose from. We ended up purchasing quite a few pieces for ourselves and as gifts.It was a great experience and a nice opportunity to see something beyond the typical Hanoi attractions. I would definitely recommend stopping by Van Phuc Silk Village if you have time during your Hanoi visit.

reviews.author: Muriel B
reviews.title: Sumptuous clothes for a more than reasonable price
reviews.content: We don't know what to choose because all the clothes are beautiful and inexpensive. A magical place that can even be discovered by taking the metro (1 km 4 from the metro stop).

reviews.author: Dal S
reviews.title: See how silk is made, woven, dyed
reviews.content: Lots of vendors, makers, suppliers with a dizzying array of wares.  From bolts of fabric to finished product.  What a fun place to see weaving to finished product.

reviews.author: Adrian Villanueva
reviews.title: Handicraft Village
reviews.content: I really enjoyed this trip. The itinerary was perfect, hotels were comfortable, and the food was delicious. Thank you for such a memorable experience.

reviews.author: George E
reviews.title: Super great for social media content - but otherwise is mid
reviews.content: I might have come at the wrong time of day or wrong season - but this was mid. We were there midday, midweek.There was very few sight seers there when we went - despite many of the shops being open. There was a relatively pretty pagoda, and several well-painted murals to get a photo in front of. Overall the silk village made for some colourful and fun Instagram content (with all the umbrellas and murals) but did not necessarily provide a super fulfilling experience in itself. Maybe there is an on-season or on-time, but i guess we missed it.Most of the silk shops appeared to carry the same products (they were quite well priced). The main factory we could see into and appeared staffed and busy, but I think you'd want a guide to take you through there rather than showing yourself through.

reviews.author: Ightham1
reviews.title: Really enjoyable look into silk making
reviews.content: We took a Grab from the old quarter, which took 35 minutes. Lots of great shops as well as the sound of the looms producing the silk. The higher end stores were honest about whether an item was 100% silk or a silk linen mix, although they wouldn’t budge on price. We paid cash first our purchases which I think is the preferred route for the shops.

reviews.author: michelle B
reviews.title: WELL WORTH A VISIT
reviews.content: We really enjoyed our visit to Yan Phuc Silk Village.  It is very pretty as you enter under a sea of suspended pastel coloured umbrellas.  We wandered down an alley and into a small factory where we were welcomed by the two workers despite no one speaking the same language.  They indicated for us to come and look at them work, showed us their patterns and were happy for us to photograph...it was fascinating !!  As some have said there is a lot of similarity between the shops but as an experience we found it quite magical.

reviews.author: Mincimoo
reviews.title: Pretty colours but nothing special
reviews.content: I would avoid visiting on a Sunday, some shops closed. A nice experience to walk through but all the shops have similar fabrics. Nothing special and for tourists.

reviews.author: Scott V
reviews.title: FAKE FAKE FAKE
reviews.content: FAKE FAKE FAKE... they should call it "70% Silk Village. And either cotton or polyester blend cuz I don't know Village. Poor quality clothes for dumb tourists. It's all repeat cheap fake Chinese made clothing, some with fake brand names and all the same tags no matter what. It's swap meet and fake market goods made elsewhere. Better off at the markets in old quarter.

reviews.author: Saf Traveler
reviews.title: Greaqt experience, good shopping, great photos to be taken
reviews.content: Well priced silk items outside of the normal tourist areas.So cool to walk around here and just see all the beautiful things on display. If you've come to Vietnam to buy good stuff to take home as gifts and just generally for yourself, then you have to visit here.This is a 1-2 hour experience in a part of the city you may not always see.great photo opportunities

reviews.author: emmajfitzgerald
reviews.title: Umbrella Street is beautiful
reviews.content: We visited the Silk Village to see Umbrella Street, which is stunning. Other than that, there are places to buy silk here. It was a fair way from the centre of Hanoi so we had to get a taxi.

reviews.author: Dave
reviews.title: Good prices if you want clothes/materials
reviews.content: As someone noted, make sure you go to the right van phuc as this is not a unique place name.Accessible by grab (and return). We  got more or less what was wanted with some materials. Was a bit quiet with a few shops shut (time of day I think - mid afternoon). Fairly picturesque with less traffic than main roads and some street decorations. But yeah this is just a shopping trip to get best prices and options, was not looking for a history of silk making or something like that so think it does the trick as long as the shopping is what you want.

reviews.author: 672highf
reviews.title: Just A Shopping Trip
reviews.content: A very disappointing visit to Van Phuc Silk Village. My expectations where to see the production of silk from silk worm to finished product. Unfortunately the only facility for the production of silk was one example of an old working loom and some explanations of the processes by the in house guide.There are many shops/stalls selling silk products but very little of the silk for sale is manufactured in Vietnam and is readily available in any market just about anywhere in Asia. I found nothing that was unique to Vietnam.Much of the product for sale was labelled "Silk Like" and in fact was not pure silk but a blend and/or man made fibre.

reviews.author: Wanderlust3710
reviews.title: Great 1/2 day activity
reviews.content: We took a taxi from the old district to Van Phuc Village and shopped up a storm...  taxi ride was about $6 and takes about 45 mins....  make sure you have the Vietnamese translation for village as there is a Van Phuc street.  Prices tended to drop as we got further in....   not much for cafes but great selection of silk scarves, dresses etc.By going ourselves and not on a tour though, we didn't get to see the manufacturing process which I'm sure would have been cool...   btw most places only accept local currency

reviews.author: Jo-Ann
reviews.title: Beautiful Silk
reviews.content: Stalls and stalls of silk textile and clothes for sale. There are silk accessories for sale as well. If you are a silk lover, you must visit. I was more interested in watching them spin silk thread and weave silk textile. Very interesting. Loved the red silk thread.

reviews.author: leep700
reviews.title: I would skip this
reviews.content: Unless you are in the market for yards of silk I would skip this. It is one lane of shops all with basically the same wares. There is a loom working but I doubt the silks are made there! There were 2 displayed boards of silk worms. It is HOT! No place to sit down. Perhaps the tour was more interesting. We took a grab cab( like Uber) to the village. The silk scarfs and souvenirs are available in the old quarter or at any of the museums for the same price.

reviews.author: Steph B
reviews.title: A real insight into how hand and simple wooden machinery crafts work
reviews.content: I was astounded by how much beautiful cloth could be created by simple wooden looms in a tiny room. So much more wholesome and rewarding than big mechanised machine led operations. The factory owner we visited was really happy with his work.

reviews.author: rssunderwirth
reviews.title: cab driver didn't show us more interesting sights
reviews.content: hotel could have told cab driver where we wanted to go, ended up  wandering around. no one indicated correct path

reviews.author: spktravels
reviews.title: Interesting stop
reviews.content: The Silk Village which is now part of Hanoi is  limited to several streets but it is worth a visit.We stopped at one family owned shop which still operates its own looms. Apparently most of the shops in the Silk Village are merely retailers.We learned the process of making silk fabric from the start, silk worms, to designing patterns, to the actual weaving.Next to the manufacturing area is a nice sized shop. There is a large selection of completed garments such as dresses, pajamas and scarfs all reasonably priced. in addition for those who are so inclined there is a wide array of silk fabrics from which you have have clothes made on your own.This shop is modern and the owners were friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: 175MOM
reviews.title: Great silk shopping experience
reviews.content: I enjoyed the visit to the silk village. The entire area is not big, but I still did not get to see all the stores in 2 hours we had.   I see mixed reviews and I can see why. If you are not interested in silk, you should probably skip it.  All the stores are selling silk fabric/scarves, so I can see why people may get bored if you are not interested.  My husband was...but I loved the place as I love fabrics.   Is this "touristy" place?  Sure, I don't think the  locals would pay those prices.  But entire Hanoi is kind of touristy.  Also some may be disappointed that many products are not made there at the silk village.  "Authentic" or not, this is the place to go for silk shopping. I really wanted to see how silk is made in old fashioned way.  I assumed we could see it right in the middle where a small pond/arch are.  But this courtyard is just surrounded by shops.  At one of the stores we bought a scarf, and asked about it.  The store lady pointed to go to the residential area.  So we did, walked for a while but did not see anything.  Maybe they have closed down, or maybe we would have seen if we wondered off smaller streets.  We went back to the silk village and browsed more stores.  At another store where I bought fabric, a very helpful lady, who also made the fabric I bought (and her father dyed it), said her home where she makes fabric is 30 min away, but told as to go to store called Mao and showed us where.  She also advised us that their fabrics are more expensive.  Mao was a larger store in this area, and there is factory/house right next to it.  The store ladies said we could take a look at the factory, so we did that first.  Our kid thought it was interesting. I am not an expart, but theier fabric seemd to be better quality. Some are 100% silk and some are not, and they are clearly marked.  I bought the one my kid liked.   Also some stores also sell non-silk souvenirs in small quantities.  I found some beautiful fans. We did not bargan.  Coming from the U.S., I thought the price was already reasonable, and felt barganing was not appropriate. But I guess you could if you wanted.  We did "cheap" silk shopping in HCMC, but shopping in Van Phuc Silk village was something compeltely different and I enjoyed it.

reviews.author: nickal06
reviews.title: A dying place... unfortunately
reviews.content: Well, well well...This place tries (sadely) to survive with the tourist but there not that much left.Far away, surrounded by the constructions, no need of crytal ball to predict its future...

reviews.author: elna m
reviews.title: Nothing extraordinary
reviews.content: This was just another commercial outlet, nothing unique about it.  If in the area, worth a visit but do not expect anything authentic.

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: Not what I was expecting
reviews.content: Loads of places selling silk, however they are all selling the same stuff. However we did get to see the old style weaving machines that I would say come from the era of our industrial revolution, very noisy and the health and safety people would have a fit lol.The area for the dyeing of the silks was also available to see, didn't get too close didn't want to inhale the fumes.

reviews.author: WAprof
reviews.title: Buying silk fabric
reviews.content: If you'd like to buy silk fabric then make sure and visit Van Phuc. They also have scarves, and other clothing but one of my goals in visiting was fabric and I found a lovely selection here.

reviews.author: LaraDay1993
reviews.title: Van Phuc Silk village
reviews.content: If you have some extra time to kill while you're in Hanoi - the silk village is a nice trip. It's not too far away and the drive is a scenic one of the city. I would recommend that you spend 2 hours there. You probably won't need more time than that. There are no real restaurants there, however one cafe for drinks. I'd recommend that if you're keen to know more about the silk village, try and get hold of a tour guide, there are no information centres or plaques up explaining anything (I may have missed them though ).  Everyone is relatively chilled, you can walk straight into the factories with beautiful old looms still in use. You may even be lucky and see them in use. The silk products are stunning , however the shops become repetitive and some products say 100% silk and then when you ask, the shop assistant will tell you that it's actually not 100%.  There is a stunning shop at the top of the street with silk clothing and scarves that are to die for so definitely take your time and shop around. You can buy various types of silk as well, and you can buy it in meters. The prices aren't too bad, you're looking at $10-$20 a scarf and a bit more for a silk shirt. There is a lovely garden and shrine there as well so have a look at that is well. I think that if you have the time, it's a nice place to visit.

reviews.author: FaithMY
reviews.title: Not worth the visit
reviews.content: We were greatly disappointed at what the silk village has to offer. Shops all selling almost same things . Poor design and price not great either. Not worth the visit.

reviews.author: Kathy K
reviews.title: Skip if limited on time
reviews.content: It was interesting to see how silk is made. I had no idea the amount of labor involved. I wisely left my credit card in the car.This was my second time in Hanoi. I would not recommend this if time is limited. There are far more interesting things to see in the Hanoi area

reviews.author: Annemarie V
reviews.title: lots of silk
reviews.content: it's nice to take a tour, let someone else do the organising, get a bit of info on the area. Lan, our guide was lovely and happy to chat about local culture. we made some nice purchases. some satin silk aud$14 per meter, I have paid 40 at home for lower quality. everyone friendly and no pressure.

reviews.author: Grazbee
reviews.title: Nice for 1-2hours
reviews.content: This Silk Village is really beautiful and the people are so nice. It is nice to see it if you are in Hanoi for 1week. :)

reviews.author: sally a
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.content: My expectations of visiting the silk village as part of the tour I was on were certainly not met. It seemed to be geared to providing a venue for shopping - fair enough -  but some of what was on offer appeared to be cheap reproductions you can find anywhere. There was some nice silk and we did get to see a mechanised weaving set up which showed how the patterns were woven - you could do with ear plugs at this point as it is very noisy. For me it was a very disappointing visit.

reviews.author: Kiko
reviews.title: Very nice products but not sold in all shops
reviews.content: We visited the silk village this month and saw some amazing offers for silk ties and pashminas! You just need to check almost every shop in order to find the right quality- really worth the effort going there.

reviews.author: Justin S
reviews.title: Was a good trip. Maybe worth an arranged tour
reviews.content: Easy to get there by taxi. Approx 190,000 VND from Hanoi Opera House. Bargain given is takes 30-40mins due to traffic. We fancied just wandering around so didn't book any guides/tours. For our needs it worked well. We got to watch a lady working a loom and then wandered the quiet streets, in and out of shops. Some really lovely products. If you want the full run down of the area, how it all works etc, you may want to research in advance or consider a guide. However I don't think it's necessary to spend $$$ on guides. We were there about 70-80 mins. Plenty of time for a leisurely stroll. Our cab driver offered to wait for us, but no need as it's close to a very main road where hailing a cab was easy. Worth a look.

reviews.author: Jean Ann F
reviews.title: Shopping Heaven!!!
reviews.content: More shops and pretty things to buy than anyone could dream of!!!  Prices are VERY affordable.  I enjoyed the history of silk and watching the looms.

reviews.author: Yevgeniya K
reviews.title: Good place to buy fabric
reviews.content: Dont expect to find beautifull silk clothes there. The clothes are not that beautifull and they are not silk. But its the place to find the best silk fabrics ever. Its not that cheap ( the best silk is about 25$ a meter) but still cheaper than in europe. I suggest to come with a lighter so you can check if the fabric is real. They can easily sell you viscose for silk and you will never know, it looks so similar.

reviews.author: Brayden_byn
reviews.title: High quality product silk!!!
reviews.content: From 10km from our hotel in Old Quater, we visited Van Phuc Silk village which is amazing village with helpful and friendly local people and beautiful sightseeings, but impressed thing with me is high quality product silk which is made by hand of local people . It's amazing experiences, thanks Hanoi Free Walking Tours to support us during our trip.You can catch bus 02 and 21 to travel to there.

reviews.author: Su H
reviews.title: Silk village
reviews.content: The name is Silk village, so I expected to see a variety of silk fabric.  But reality is far from expectation.Nothing much to see, all the shops are selling almost the same items. You need to ask for discount in most of the shops as the shops mark up the price especially to the foreigners.Just 40 minutes drive from Hanoi old quarter.

reviews.author: Tania P
reviews.title: Nice silks,nice setting
reviews.content: Nice silks,but most shops all carry same selections, so very repetitive .. The nicer shops were quite expensive & no real bargaining .. Enjoyed seeing silk worms and the looms,but not much else to do. The little park nearby is nice for a wonder.

reviews.author: Adan c
reviews.title: Outstanding white silk dress
reviews.content: Travelling Van Phuc village in lately afternoon, i surprised before the beauty of Van Phuc silk like the rainbow. Furthermore, Hung uncle who is enthusiastic local people told us the history of the village and how to make special of Van Phuc silk. 10km from Hanoi Old Quater, you can travel buy bus or hire moto.

reviews.author: TravelforScuba
reviews.title: Silk Scarves, Silk Worms, and That's About It
reviews.content: Went here looking for inexpensive silk items. Most of what we saw was scarves, a few dresses, and shirts. Most shops have the same items so you can haggle to get the best price. We were a bit underwhelmed there was no one demonstrating the silk weaving just a bunch of old machines set up to show the process. This was interesting but a live demonstration would have been great. It's about a $5 cab ride from old town so cheap to get there. So if you have an hour to kill it's not a complete waste.

reviews.author: agrippina1952
reviews.title: perhaps the high season is better here
reviews.content: We visited in winter, and many of the shops were shut. We had been told that we could see silk weaving and manufacturing in process, but that was not to be. The place seemed rather bleak and deserted. All the silk products on display were very similar, and not cheaper than in the Old Quarter or Hang Gai. I wouldn't bother, but then perhaps a visit in summer might be very different.

reviews.author: KeepMemories
reviews.title: Quiet pleasant walk
reviews.content: The place was really quiet, huge contrast with the busy preparation for Ted New Year in the Old Quarter. The shops sell similar things to Old Quarter silk shops but since it's so quiet, we had a leisurely walk and browse.

reviews.author: shocar
reviews.title: It worth the trip for clothes. Be aware sellers to follow you everywhere
reviews.content: We had here a nice day with a friend shopping around and checking for nice clothes made in silk.Most fancy shops use to charge more, so expect to find more western designs and prices too.Some sellers are not kind and follow you in all the shop what I found very uncomfortable, but I understand is a culture misunderstanding.If you are big size, XL for Europe or US I suggest better go to Hue to buy clothes where they have more sizes due the lot of tourists there.

reviews.author: annalee2403
reviews.title: amazing attraction
reviews.content: Arrive Van Phuc village I was impressed by typical manner of an ancient village in the north of Vietnam with banyan tree, well, communal house, and the sound of power-looms everywhere. There are very much silk with various products like shirts, ties, crafts, dresses…

reviews.author: Beaumaris32
reviews.title: A Great Day Out
reviews.content: At the end of our walking/touring visit to N Vietnam, the 10 of us had to to do a craft village tour.    So, combined with the Bat Trang Ceramic village (see my review) we had a splendid day out - Bat Trang in the morning, back to Hanoi for lunch, then Vin Phuc Silk village in the afternoon.    You start off with a close look at were they spin the silk and make the cloth on looms - very interesting.    Then you can stroll around the large number of places selling all sorts of silk items from scarves to shirts and blouses etc.   Do the usual, expected bargaining and, bingo, souvenir/gift problems solved !   A very pleasant day out.

reviews.author: kdk1965
reviews.title: Up-thumb on the insight and down-thumb on bargains
reviews.content: We stopped here as part of a private tour and while we enjoyed seeing how silk is made, the rest of the visit was simply ok.  It felt "canned" and more like an amusement park area in terms of the approach.  Shops were lovely, the ladies selling items in the shop were lovely, but this is not a free market area.

reviews.author: Dylan G
reviews.title: Great insight into silk manufacturing
reviews.content: Friendly locals, free tour through a silk manufactory. Many silk toys and clothes purchasable. There's a small marketplace next door that sells cheaper items, so it's worth shopping around.

reviews.author: dccollyer
reviews.title: Don't Miss It
reviews.content: As a lace maker I was keen to buy silk thread which is not something they normally sell.  However the management kindly agreed and I came away very satisfied. This is a wonderful place which needs more promotion!

reviews.author: MsAnnHanoi
reviews.title: Touristy but still have a story
reviews.content: Van Phuc silk village , now in Van Phuc ward, Ha Dong disrict, Hanoi, 10km from the city centre, has been the most famous and long lasting silk weaving village in Vietnam with various patterns.Since its first appearance, silk from Van Phuc village became a favorable product thanks to the skilful and sopisticated hans and souls of weavers which were crystallized in each piece of silk. Van Phuc silk was always provided for mandarins to make official clothes. Despite historical changes, Van Phuc silk weaving has still been growing for the last 10 centuries. Itnitially , Van Phus silk was produced only for upper and middle feudal classes. The late 19th century the Nguyen dynasy encouraged people to use domestic products and craftsmen of Van Phuc Viallage quickly collected, learnt, and innovated to “popularize” silk and satin product.

reviews.author: Sebastian L
reviews.title: Touristy
reviews.content: Unless you are very keen to know the intricate process of silk making, the few stalls selling silk products are less appealing than the shops at Old quarters. An optional tour in my opinion.

reviews.author: ColinGJ
reviews.title: Mostly shopping
reviews.content: This is mostly a couple of streets of silk shops selling very nice items. At the back of one of the shops, you can go into a room where they are making some silk objects, and watch the old machines working. Mostly of interest if you want to buy clothes or souvenirs, but not that different to what you can buy in the centre of Hanoi, really.

reviews.author: pw0867
reviews.title: Nice silk and a factory to visit how they make silk clothes
reviews.content: It would be boring for young kids.  With the exception of the factory that you could visit where they showed you how they made silk garments, it was just a bunch of shops selling silk clothing items.  Some were not cheaper than I could have gotten at home, but the wide variety and selection of items was good.It was better than the ceramic village, but not much to see, unless you were in the mood to buy silk.

reviews.author: fickle_flower
reviews.title: Touristy, but more variety than at the Old Quarter
reviews.content: Probably a visit is in place if your intention is to buy silk goods in Hanoi. There are more variety in terms of fabric selection than in the Old Quarter. Prices appear more reasonable, although you still have to bargain hard. They close pretty early, around 7pm

reviews.author: AppreciateAdvice
reviews.title: Can't understand the glowing reviews... not worth visiting
reviews.content: The village is a few streets of "shops" selling silk.  There's nothing interesting, original, compelling or otherwise worthy of spending the time to get there, walk-around and go back to Hanoi.  Sure, there's a working mill where you can learn about how silk is made and watch-it, but it's really not so exciting.  And I didn't find anything that was either special or value-priced or both to make a visit worthwhile.  Pass...

reviews.author: happywanderer1954
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Visited the Village, unfortunately it was at lunch time, so didn't see a lot of activity but it was interesting see the looms and the shopping was good.  Went with a private guide and this was just a cheap as going with an organised tour but we were able to fit in a little more during the day.  Some tour companies advertise an admission fee...don't believe it.  There is not admission fee, you can just walk in.

reviews.author: EmillyStephenie
reviews.title: good for shopping
reviews.content: A place has so much shirt, dress,...which are made from silk by hand made. . everything in here are very cheap and special !

reviews.author: GeciDC
reviews.title: Nothing much here
reviews.content: We went here as part of our day tour to Doung Lam Ancient Village. What to do? Nothing much. You just take a peak on how they make silk and then you will visit a shop that sell their finished silk products and you'll realize after that it is cheaper to get them in the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Phua W
reviews.title: Not worth the time
reviews.content: Went there as part of a day tour. Just a short street was shops selling silk products.  Totally not interesting and not worth the time.  I'd you are looking for silk products,  shops in the old quarters are more interesting.

reviews.author: TravellingMouse2014
reviews.title: Interesting program that showed us the process of silk making from the silk worms eating to finished silk
reviews.content: We watched silk worms eating mulberry leaves, saw the cocoons, saw spinners spinning silk, saw operators winding silk on spools, watched the weavers following elaborate paper cutout patterns on the looms, and saw the beautifully patterned silk emerging from the looms.

reviews.author: msinwdc
reviews.title: Not Worth It
reviews.content: Oh how I wish I listened to most of the reviews here on T.A. I just can't hear the word "village" and not think that it will be a charming and quiet locale full of locals working on their handicraft. And after going to Ba Trang pottery village, which is just that, I was hoping Van Phuc would be the silk equivalent.But alas, it is as many previous reviewers have commented - nothing special or interesting. I couldn't even find the shops that actually spin the silk. Perhaps it's less busy in November (I was the only non-Vietnamese person there) and this activity is not done all year?If you must go, it's worth hiring a guide or asking a local Vietnamese friend to take you, just to make sure you see all there is to see. As already noted, you only need an hour or two. I think this place is of most interest to people who want to buy fabric rather than ready-made items, because the latter are more readily available in Hanoi's Old Quarter. While I didn't see a lot of fabric, what I did see was beautiful and soft.

reviews.author: Brenda R
reviews.title: Small, not much to see or do
reviews.content: I expected the silk village to be more like the colorful, bustling center or Hoi An, so it was a bit of a disappointment. There were significantly fewer shops, and the merchandise was rather limited. Primarily only ready made clothing (as opposed to the custom shops you can find in other parts of Vietnam) and scarves. Not really any decorative items for the home. We had intended to spend a few hours here and maybe grab lunch as well, but other than 1 or 2 fruit vendors and a few small pharmacies, there weren't really any other dining options. We were able to pop into the 2 temples and all of the silk kiosks (around 25) in just over an hour. This is definitely not a full day or even half day excursion if you plan to work it into your schedule.

reviews.author: Nhu_Phuong
reviews.title: Genuine and cheap silk!
reviews.content: It's very easy to get here. Take xe ôm (motorbike taxi) for about 4-5 dollars each way. A lot more expensive by taxi.Here, you'll get to see how they produce silk products. And you can purchase good quality and cheap silk here. This is my go-to place when I need to by gifts for my international friends. About 5 dollars for a silk scarf, That's a good bargain, right?

reviews.author: CHUN C
reviews.title: LIKE A MARKET - THAT'S ALL
reviews.content: Go there if your purpose is to buy silk fabrics and scarf. Otherwise, do not come here coz nothing for your visit. The good thing is the price of silk is cheaper than Dong Xuan market and not crowded.

reviews.author: lastlyvn
reviews.title: A silk village you can see people weaving silk cloth
reviews.content: This is originally a village people produce silk and silk products.  However, it seems the business has come down and nowadays not so many silk factories.  Most products can be found in Hoan Kiem Area and even cheaper there.  Products not exceedingly cheap and this place is quite far away from the city.  Not a particular attraction for tourists or even local people.  Especially do not go right after lunch, most shops are closed for afternoon sleep.

reviews.author: Mervyn C
reviews.title: Not interesting enough
reviews.content: When I heard about "Village", it crossed in my mind that it is very old and traditional, but in fact, it is modern. One minor of this village :(Also there are many silk shops there, but the real silk is little. Silk there might make in China, not from Van Phuc. If you have to use the good product, you should go to folk person there to ask for the special and good one.

reviews.author: Clare Y
reviews.title: Not worth seeing
reviews.content: Perhaps we missed something but all we could see were the silk shops near the main street. The name is misleading as it isn't a village at all and was just in Hanoi.There was construction on the street which I guess hid the looms and silkworm workshop. The city should put up a map near the 'welcome to Silk vilalge' sign to define some kind of walking path.Disappointing.

reviews.author: Ann T
reviews.title: Listen for the sound of the looms
reviews.content: This is a village full of silk shops but one which is no longer surrounded by mulberry trees. However, if you can hear the sound of the looms, go in and watch people at work weaving silk. We visited this on an Urban Adventure Village tour which was a great way to get insight into the place.

reviews.author: PALTravel
reviews.title: Good for purchasing gifts; some shops are more friendly than others.
reviews.content: You really need to shop around ... and if you want an authentic silk or 'pashmina', then you need to know your stuff as some shops slap labels on polyester and which says pashmina.  So, take the time to look at things in a variety of shops before you purchase.That said, the prices are very good and you can easily find something for everyone back home!  It's fun to walk the streets and, if you're interested, you can actually see the entire process (from silk worm to final, woven product.  We'd seen this in Turkey, so didn't bother on this trip.You can find scarfs in all prices.  The finer silk scarves are around $25usd.  Check out each piece before purchasing to make sure there aren't any snags or an damage to the item.We actually took a taxi to the village and he waited while we shopped.  Nice to not have to find a taxi when we were finished!If you have time to shop, this is a great place to do so!

reviews.author: Rafie K
reviews.title: Maybe March is the best time to visit Van Phuc
reviews.content: I was here last week and my sole purpose is to buy silk fabrics and scarf. My wife suggested this place to buy all things silk as she was here in March 2009.Good things:- You can see the silk worm and the process of making the fabric- Considerably low in price compared to Hanoi (and Don Xuan market)- Not that crowdedNot so good:- Less options of silk fabrics and scarf (Maybe due to the cold season)- The fabric options is more inclined towards the celebration of the lunar new yearDespite, I believe this will be better during hot season on whenever the silk worm is active producing the silk thread. I hope someone travel to this place in March or hotter season to supply with more information. Overall, it's a silk village for sure.

reviews.author: beachlady32927
reviews.title: Interesting stop over and nice people
reviews.content: I took a motorbike taxi out of Hanoi just to ride around. I saw the statue and small pond first and didn't know it was the silk village. It was a lovely stop. I have never seen this process or the machines. As a teacher and still a learning child myself I truly immersed myself into the machinery and people. The good we're QUALITY and I literally bought the silk that was on the machine. This was priceless to me. Worth seeing was the granite stones and shrine to the Vietnam war losses for this tiny town. Prices w o haggling were better than old town. I don't haggle much. I look at my life and paychecks and I look at theirs. I can afford 5$ more :)

reviews.author: Upperny
reviews.title: Great prices for silk scarves, but a small venue
reviews.content: We found ourselves with mixed feelings.  The scarves were inexpensive and beautiful ($5-10), but the extraoidinary ones were $25 and we should have bought those.  There are many shops ostensibly selling the same class of goods.  The people are lovely and the walk is short.  The demonstration of weaving isn't worth the trip, if you've seen such things before, but the prices are great and the selection is amazing, given the twenty or so shops.

reviews.author: kandl
reviews.title: Recommended for silk fabric lovers.
reviews.content: As a silk lover, I enjoyed seeing the process from silk worm to silk fabric. The old weaving machines were fascinating. Every type of silk in every colour and pattern available by the meter and some ready made clothes. A pleasant village only a short distance from frantic Hanoi.

reviews.author: DragonCrew
reviews.title: not as my expectation
reviews.content: It's on the way from Mai Chau to Hanoi and sure a good reststop if you want smth strange. There you can see the process of making silk but only at a tiny corner of the village communal house. In contrast, there are hundreds of "modern" things with lots of shops, street hawkers, cars and streetside food stalls. If you are fond of silk, we suggest you go for shopping at Hang Gai "silk" street inside Hanoi old quarter instead.

reviews.author: Anna T
reviews.title: Ideal place for buy silk products
reviews.content: We took private car in around 3 hours from Hanoi centre to the Van Phuc Village. These are many silk products hanging on boutique shops: Crafts, ties, dress, tissus..To be attracted by multiple color of silk products, we bought a lot of things: 10 crafts, 5 ties, somes dress.One thing have to be mentioned that we has made bargaining before settle the payment.It was nice expericence to see how the silkworm makes the fibers and how the spinner makes the tissus.Coming to this village is chance to discover the genuine traditional silk-making industry. Bisides that, this is ideal place for buying vietnamese silk.Recommended for everyone traveling to Hanoi.

reviews.author: BobBonHere
reviews.title: Not worth visiting
reviews.content: This was a bit of a disappointment. Our guide obviously had his preferred shops which were were 'encourage' to buy. Prices were OK but buying anything you didn't really want is expensive.

reviews.author: Mike
reviews.title: Not worth the hassle
reviews.content: We got the impression from Lonely Planet that this village this village was out of Hanoi in the country a little bit so hired a driver for the day to see this and the Thay and Tay Phuong Pagodas.The silk village was the big disappointment of the trip.  We felt like we were still in the middle of Hanoi when we turned off a main road and down a non-descript street lined with silk shops and into a courtyard, where we saw a few silkworm cocoons on a screen, what looked like some raw silk that had been unwould from cocoons some time ago, and into an old silk weaving room where there a few old looms, one of which was being operated.  We walked back out through the connected silk shop and down the street trying to find something else of interest, before getting back in the car and driving on to the pagodas.  Perhaps we missed something?

reviews.author: Eli
reviews.title: Interesting backstory
reviews.content: An old pagoda in the center of Hanoi. Quite peaceful and carries that traditional charm. Learning more about its historical backstory was quite interesting and surprising. If you’re traveling solo or on your own, you can use the Travellens app to explore it deeper.

reviews.author: Maud M
reviews.title: Nice temple
reviews.content: Very nice temple in Hanoi which for me deserves a look. The temple was little attended at the time we went there.

reviews.author: Sonia
reviews.title: The sacred temple in the heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: Quan Su Pagoda is one of the most famous and sacred pagodas in Hanoi. This is the headquarters of the Vietnam Buddhist Sangha, so the space is always imbued with Buddhist culture. The pagoda has traditional architecture with a large three-door gate, spacious courtyard, and solemn Buddha statues. On major holidays, the pagoda is crowded with people coming to burn incense and pray. The peaceful space here creates a sense of purity and comfort for anyone who visits.

reviews.author: Betsy S
reviews.title: Beautiful Pagoda
reviews.content: Beautiful and ornate. I was there on Vesak Day, which some consider Buddha’s birthday.  Many locals were there to pay respects.

reviews.author: Tc voyageur
reviews.title: Peaceful. Oasis that’s seen a lot of history
reviews.content: Peaceful oasis in a busy city.   Near some grim reminders of inhumanity — “Hanoi Hilton” prison  n the Police Museum Don’t come looking for action.  It’s a majestic temple with a lot of history to it.  My heritage Buddhist traveling companion lit joss sticks for lost family members.

reviews.author: TheLeongOhana
reviews.title: Beautiful Pagoda on A Busy Street
reviews.content: I stopped by this Buddhist pagoda on the way to Train Street.It was a good size building with lots of greenery everywhere.  Large urns with burning incense with statues and more plants filled the middle of the stairs. I did not go inside as there seemed to be some preparations going on for a ceremony so I silently observed from the outside.  The altar was a beautiful arrangement around a large golden Buddha statue.  Smaller altars were setup on each side.Towards the back there was a small store and stairs leading up to the next levels.  Very quiet everywhere.Worth a short stop if near the Police Museum or Hoa Loa Prison.

reviews.author: R M
reviews.title: Bit of peace
reviews.content: I went here to just get a little peace of mind after doing lots of war tourist stuff. Very beautiful space, tranquil and many locals going in and out. Very glad I went.

reviews.author: Rachel P
reviews.title: Lovely and tranquil
reviews.content: A lovely tranquil temple which was a wekcome relief after the emotion of visting Hoa Lo Prison nearby.  It's free to enter and well worth a visit.  The decoration is incredible and almost sensory overload but it is offset by the calmness of the place.

reviews.author: Mehul Kirit Shah
reviews.title: Buddhist Community Headquarter
reviews.content: The monk who hosted the temple then, had corridors built, statues painted, and bell made. The front palace is dedicated to Buddha and the rear palace is dedicated to the king of the Ly Dynasty.

reviews.author: explor246
reviews.title: Beautiful and peaceful
reviews.content: It was great to have a private tour guide. He explained how pagoda and temples vary, the budas, the alters, etc. And answered a lot of our questions. Highly recommend a tour guide (and they are so inexpensive to hire).

reviews.author: R K L
reviews.title: It survived...
reviews.content: The Ambassador's Pagoda (also known as Quan Su Pagoda) had a noticeably serene and peacefully atmosphere, even while it was full of worshippers when we visited. Originally, the pagoda was built specifically to welcome ambassadors from neighboring countries who were all Buddhists. It survived over centuries when other pagodas met with destruction and has served as the Headquarters of the Vietnamese Buddhism Association since the mid-18th century. Visitors were welcome and encouraged to purchase some incense and offer prayers. To do so was actually quite liberating.

reviews.author: j-curv
reviews.title: Peaceful Find
reviews.content: A beautiful piece of architecture and cultural history that has survived despite the numerous conflicts over the centuries.This is well worth a visit, for its tranquility alone.  On the day we called in there was some kind of ceremony and access was limited to the external perimeter courtyard nonetheless it was worth a wander around this area.

reviews.author: jeff1955malaysia
reviews.title: an old buddhist temple
reviews.content: it is located close to the Hoa Lo prison. its entrance has a pagoda shape and it is dark yellow in colour. you will find a number of monks of a non stop of worshippers doing theirs prayers. it is calm and a strong smell of incense.

reviews.author: BrockDaBadger
reviews.title: Lady Monks (Sangha) Chanting When I Visited
reviews.content: This pagoda has some history and is just around the corner from the Hoa Lo Prison (aka the Hanoi Hilton).  When I arrived I could hear chanting and when I looked inside there were probably 40 Sangha monks chanting.  Small area but a pleasant and free attraction.

reviews.author: RET2246
reviews.title: Lovely little find
reviews.content: A lovely, quiet temple. If you're visiting the prison which is just up the road this is definitely worth a visit, especially following the gloom of the prison this is a peaceful heaven. There are still monks in the temple and plenty of locals coming in to worship. Depending on your level of religion it takes between 10-30 mins to look around.

reviews.author: seanworc
reviews.title: Little Jewel Box Pagoda
reviews.content: This is an 17th century temple with an entrance gate in Ha Noi. It was built by visiting Buddhist ambassadors who called on the then emperor of Viet Nam. It is reportedly the central HQ of Buddhism in Viet Nam. It is an active temple so there will be many worshippers paying homage here.  A quick stop , maybe 30 minutes.  It is not a complex such as the Temple Of Literature or the Lama Temple in Beijing. Went in March, 2013.

reviews.author: Chris101111
reviews.title: Peaceful
reviews.content: Happen to come across the temple when out walking, lovely and serene, locals use it regularly, it's well maintained and the Buddhas are ornate and colourful.I would recommend it to visit.

reviews.author: HugoColle
reviews.title: Beautiful temple
reviews.content: A beautiful temple which is very peaceful once you enter. Not that big but very nice statues and ornaments here. Alot of locals using this temple for offerings and prayers. Still monks and nuns living here. Is called the Ambassadors pagode because in the earlier years it was a guesthouse for the ambassadors of the Budhist countries. Worth a stop..

reviews.author: Porgester
reviews.title: Quiet & peaceful
reviews.content: Its a little off the beaten track but a very beautiful temple & worth the visit. You can pass by it on your way to the prison & temple of literature

reviews.author: Leo D
reviews.title: headquarters for the Vietnam Central Buddhist Congregation.
reviews.content: vietnam has many pagodas and temples and Quan Su is one of the most important temples in the country. Constructed in the 15th century along with a small house for visiting Buddhist ambassadors, in 1934 it became the headquarters of the Tonkin Buddhist Association, and today it is headquarters for the Vietnam Central Buddhist Congregation.Since 1942, the pagoda has been restored and expanded many times with a larger and better architectural structure. It's an active pagoda and usually thronged with worshippers; the interior is dim and smoky with incense.

reviews.author: BabyCParis
reviews.title: Very nice place
reviews.content: Nice Pagoda to visit if you have done all the other sightseing sites in Hanoi. Very peaceful, not crowded and mainly locals.

reviews.author: esopus35
reviews.title: A quick stop
reviews.content: I had my rickshaw driver take me here. It was pretty empty.  I loved the Temple with various shrines. When I was there they had large areas of flower petals spread on the ground. It made for some good photos.

reviews.author: PhongTien
reviews.title: The heritage of Le dynasty
reviews.content: The temple was renovated several times, and now both local worshipers and curious visitors can enjoy the calm, the beauty, the bits and pieces of history. If you’re the talkative kind, the locals will tell you stories.

reviews.author: unREMb
reviews.title: Didn't look like a pagoda
reviews.content: We spent around 15 minutes looking for the place with a map but were unable to recognize it despite passing it by on a few occasions. We had expected a pagoda but it was actually a temple. Bring a picture.We entered it unknowingly and spent around 5 minutes looking around.We didn't see any tourists but there were many locals offering prayers and incense.Bring a guide as there were no English descriptions of the place.

reviews.author: OurFamily
reviews.title: History and modernity
reviews.content: 500 years of history here and a large teaching staff  make this an important place for the city. Pity they replaced the grounds with parking lots and commerce,  Go any time to see the people who are involved with the society. Go After Tet to see a frenzy of prayer.  And rad the Ho Xuan Huong Poem about the duplicity of religious figures, preferably in the Balaban translation

reviews.author: Chai P
reviews.title: Vietnam shall be interesting more if the pepplo concern to hygiene
reviews.content: I visited many time for pray on early of month with my wife

reviews.author: annieandbob
reviews.title: A beautiful pagoda
reviews.content: Take the time to go in and look at the altars and decorations - great photo opportunities.

reviews.author: JOELBRANSYDNEY
reviews.title: VERY NICE AND BIGGEST ONE IN HANOI
reviews.content: We vist many places in Hanoi and one of them is Quan Su pagoda. we like buddit and we cam here listen all the saying from nuns and they pray for the best and good luck. you come here not easyto take photo but you can be offered by some guides and they will let you take photo. it is really nice place to see in Hanoi.

reviews.author: PICHNICH009
reviews.title: gread experience about Buddhism
reviews.content: Quan Su temple is a very old pagoda in Vietna. A lot of event about buddhism was happend there. The design of the temple very ancient. This pagoda is very near to the centre and very near to Hoa Lo prison. I see alot of of the Buddhist are came to this pagoda. I also must queue to come in.
