reviews.content: I was there twice, in summer and winter. It was a drizzling day in the winter of Hanoi and the wood was foggy looking like Alice's wonderland. In summer it would be a bit too hot but its still worth trying. The cactus garden was awesome. Most of the time the gate will be locked but if you re lucky then you'll be able to get in and see the treasure inside :)Bad campers left trash and p**pings in some places so pls beware. There are cleaners but its hard to keep the place all clean and natural without the supportive practices of campers/visitors. Pls dont be like those crappy visitors :(

reviews.author: Yoyo H
reviews.title: great day out of hanoi
reviews.content: we were  tired of hanoi and took a private car+driver for 45$ for the day for a trip to ba vi park. Great  weather up the top, great views and plants

reviews.author: K W T
reviews.title: Cool Air, Beautiful Scenery
reviews.content: Almost 2 hours up to the parking area. A bit of a winding road, make sure you get an experienced driver. But once up there, you'll see that its worth going up. Cool fresh air, beautiful scenery and you can hear the birds chirping. The tour guide mentioned 5000 steps or approximately 1 hours to climb up to the hill top to visit the pagoda and another 1 hour down. After 8-9 minutes, we gave up and went back down!!! And we feel so ashamed we couldn't finish the trip because on the way up, we saw a group of old ladies (maybe 60-70 years old who made it to the top, prayed and came down). Nevertheless, we had some great photo opportunities up on there. On the way down, we pit stop at a hotel (closed during winter) but the restaurant was open. Plenty of photo ops again. Downside to it is that they allow smokers (some Vietnamese group) to smoke inside the restaurant with the windows closed....kinda choking in there (luckily we found a place to sit outside with fresh air!)

reviews.author: Brayden_byn
reviews.title: Outstanding Sightseeing!!!
reviews.content: It's wonderful place for 1 day break to travel around Hanoi by motobike. When standing on the top of Ba Vi moutant, I feel like at Sapa which is so imposing and beautiful sightseeing. High recommend!

reviews.author: Adan c
reviews.title: Ba Vi Trekking Tour!
reviews.content: I had one more outstanding weekend. We had a day very tired because trekking 3 moutant of Ba Vi national park, but it's a amazing. After long climbing with my friend, we drank delicious milk, What's a fantastic feeling. Furthermore, i am heared about Thanh Giong stories by my Vietnamese friends when we drank milk. We spend more hour from Hanoi to Ba Vi by motobike. This place is very suitable for trekking and sightseeing with group friends.

reviews.author: Tri-Jimmy
reviews.title: Weekend break
reviews.content: Great views of the area and a nice way to see some beautiful Vietnamese countryside. Hard to find decent food nearby but we didn't go hungry!

reviews.author: Chu H
reviews.title: Fantastic national park
reviews.content: Ba Vi national Park is located near Hanoi, 60 km far from the city. It's seem to be a good trip with our motorcycles, easy to ride, climb up and walk around  the mountain. Good choice for weekend!

reviews.author: billyroo
reviews.title: Lovely day out away from hustle and bustle of Hanoi
reviews.content: We did a private motorbike trip to Ba Vi National Park. Great fun ride out took about 90 minutes. Beautiful cool air, lovely scenery, great food in the restuarant. We walked up 600 steps to the top to visit Ho Chi Min Temple well worth the climb, had a lovely cup of green tea up the top, made extra special by our two guides Kim and Ken from Funny Travel  Gia Ngu street Hanoi Old quarter.

reviews.author: tuananhhoang
reviews.title: Excellent national park, beautiful nature and environment
reviews.content: I, my wife and some friends love to travel to this attraction and we do it every year. It is simply an excellent national park with amazing trail for driving uphill, beautiful nature and environment. Good for sightseeing, trekking to the sacred Tan Vien temple and Ho Chi Minh temple on top of the mountains.

reviews.author: Jitze B
reviews.title: Great views, cool air.
reviews.content: Today we visited Ba Vi national park which is located some 65 kilometers away from Hanoi. Driving there takes around one hour, not counting driving up the mountain. Entrance fee for a car with two adults and two children is 140.000 vnd, just around 5 euro. The road leading to the main car park next to the top is good with some small parts but nothing scary. Once you make it to the car park you can climb another 200 meters on good rock stairs to get to the top. Admire the temple and the stunning views if it's not too cloudy. The temperature at the top is at least 5 degrees lower than at the entrance of the park which makes it quite refreshing. Recommended for a day trip if you did Ha Long bay and have a day extra when you are in Hanoi.

reviews.author: TallChris51
reviews.title: Enjoy the views
reviews.content: Lovely and under-used national park, with a good mix of scenery and a good road leading up to the summit. Some interesting diversions including ruined church and other buildings. Very atmospheric.  Plan well as there's nothing else around!

reviews.author: BurmeseDays
reviews.title: Hanoi day trips - Ba Vi National Park
reviews.content: Ba Vi National Park is a common day trip from Hanoi, but it seems to be difficult to find much information about it. We hired a driver for the day (~$50 US) and headed there. Trick 1: Get a map when you enter at the base of the mountain …. because there are none up the top. The map shows a couple of walks. The first one you pass, on the way up the hill, to a cave, was ok … cool to be in the jungle, but beyond the cave it got a bit overgrown. On the other side of the road there was another walking track which we attempted to follow … but this was super overgrown and turned into quite a mission. Trick number 2: Wear insect repellent because there are leaches. There are heaps of butterflies though, which is cool. Don't expect to see animals. We did see a couple of birds though. Lonely Planet had suggested there was an orchid garden and a bird garden, I had the ticket lady mark them on the map, but we did not find them - despite lots of looking around. There were plenty of facilities main parking area, mid way up the mountain. A couple of restaurants, accommodation etc…. although the main restaurant waved us away (possibly because there was another function on, possibly because we were not looking to sharp after our bushwalking adventures). Nevertheless, you can get food there.The main attractions seem to be the ruins of the french summer camp - which are pretty cool, and being overgrown by jungle. The tracks here are pretty good. And at the top of the mountain there is a temple dedicated to Ho Chi Minh. Again, the track is good, so easy enough to get there (if you don't mind the 1000+ steps). You'll either be up in the clouds, or have a good view. We had the former.Finally there are some really old and rare pine trees. There is a sign to these off the road on the way up to the HCM temple. These are also worth the walk (up) for nature nerds. The track was getting overgrown when we visited though.

reviews.author: Patty B
reviews.title: Wonderful Place To Visit
reviews.content: This is a lovely place to see while visiting Hanoi.  We met a couple in Saigon who told us about it.  It was a nice walk from the Capella Hotel.  We walked along the lake went over the red  bridge and found wonderful sights.  We watched a man making a beautiful scroll, the famous turtles, beautiful flowers, birds and more.  A woman was selling small items and I got a nice small bike to use for my summer display,  it even had a real chain.  This is a great way to explore this special area.  I am glad we did not miss it.

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: Very characteristic
reviews.content: The Ngoc Son Temple is one of the classic visits to make in the center of Hanoi, especially for its beautiful location: it is located on a small island in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake and is connected to the shore by the characteristic red The Huc bridge, one of the most photographed spots in the city.The temple dates back in its current form mainly to the 19th century and is dedicated to various figures of the Vietnamese tradition, including General Tran Hung Dao, a national hero famous for his victories against the Mongol invasions in the 13th century. The complex reflects an interesting mix of Confucian, Taoist, and traditional Vietnamese religious influences.Inside there are altars, incense, and various rooms dedicated to worship. Particularly curious is the presence of a preserved specimen of one of the enormous turtles that lived in the lake, animals linked to the famous legend of the returned sword that gave its name to Hoàn Kiếm, the "Lake of the Returned Sword."The entrance ticket costs 50,000 VND and during our visit we had to pay in cash.The visit does not take much time, but it is interesting and, above all, allows you to enter one of the symbolic places of Hanoi. It is also very evocative to simply cross the red bridge and observe the lake and the city from there.Considering also that it is located in the heart of Hanoi and a few steps from the Old Quarter, it is a visit that I definitely recommend including during a walk around Hoàn Kiếm Lake.

reviews.author: sannamoo
reviews.title: Small temple in Hoan Kiem
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple in Hanoi is a prominent spiritual site situated on a small island in Hoan Kiem Lake. Accessible by crossing the red Huc Bridge, it venerates national heroes and scholars, offering a peaceful retreat from the bustling city. An entry fee of approximately $2 applies, as it is not a free attraction.Notable features include a glass case displaying a large, taxidermied softshell turtle from the lake, a powerful symbol of national independence, spiritual protection, longevity, and wisdom. This connects the site to the legendary Golden Turtle God, who played a crucial role in defending against foreign invaders.The main shrines feature altars dedicated to the military leader Tran Hung Dao and esteemed scholars, underscoring the site’s historical and cultural importance.

reviews.author: William Tan
reviews.title: a special pagoda
reviews.content: Hanoi is a city rich in historical landmarks and stories. This particular pagoda is very special, as it preserves the actual remains of a giant turtle inside. A lot of people come here to pray

reviews.author: The Wandering Pair
reviews.title: Culture, History and Serenity on the Lake
reviews.content: We visited Ngoc Son Temple this afternoon, and our leg covers came in handy again following our earlier excursion to another religious site.Crossing the red bridge over the lake to the island temple, leaving the busy Hanoi streets behind us, made for a beautiful transition to a more spiritual place. The temple itself is wonderfully decorated, with flowing plants and wildlife to see all around. We spotted herons and turtles across the lake, while the courtyard featured huge, brightly coloured floral displays.The external pagoda, with its Vietnamese flag flying proudly above it, made for quite a spectacle. Turning to look out across the water towards the ancient tower was equally stunning.Moving inside the temple, signs highlighting the no-photography rule were not exactly being adhered to by most visitors. Naturally, we respected the request and took no photographs ourselves. The atmosphere inside the main temple was peaceful and reverent, with people actively praying, making it a truly memorable experience.Alongside the main temple is a small outbuilding where two preserved turtles are housed in special display cases. The information boards explained that only six of these turtles remain in the wild, and the story of the turtle providing a sword to an ancient king made for particularly interesting reading.A cultural must when visiting Hanoi. At 100,000 VND (£2.82) for both of us, it was excellent value and well worth the time we spent exploring the island.

reviews.author: Libertalie Bastiat
reviews.title: Beautiful and peaceful
reviews.content: Must have seen. We did it after a wslk around the beautiful lake

reviews.author: jstrommen
reviews.title: Serene island to visit
reviews.content: Serene site to visit and learn about religious significance, traditions, and lore.

reviews.author: CarolineLanc
reviews.title: Iconic temple on Hoan Kiem lake
reviews.content: Iconic temple on Hoan Kiem Lake. Worth a visit but be prepared for crowds. Very scenic setting.

reviews.author: Dimenson X
reviews.title: So Beautiful 🩷🩷
reviews.content: The Ngoc Son Temple is located on an island on Hanoi's Hoan Kiem Lake in the middle of the city.Built in the 19th century, the temple is a blend of Confucianism, Taoism, and Buddhism.The temple primarily honors General Trần Hưng Đạo (who led the 13th-century resistance against Mongol invaders), Văn Xương Đế Quân (the God of Literature and Education), and La To (the patron saint of medicine).To access the temple you need to cross the red footbridge, the Húc.

reviews.author: Jeremy C
reviews.title: Island Temple
reviews.content: Cross the very pretty Red Bridge which in itself gives excellent views of the lake and enter a compact and typically beautiful temple that is frequented by worshippers and tourists alike. It is a little haven within the bustling city and a chance to get away from it for a little while.

reviews.author: Richard T
reviews.title: Great to mix with the locals going about their religious beliefs
reviews.content: Extremely busy during New Year. We were advised by the hotel to take care due to pick pockets but we saw no evidence at all. Worth the wait to go over the walkway to the Temple. Many people doing their New Year picture posing. A very religious facility for the locals, with many making offerings, burning “money” etc, adding to the local emphasis. The local experts were painting their messages on red paper to signify happiness, good luck etc.We were only there 30 minutes or so, but a great local experience.

reviews.author: Talant2007
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: The temple is built on Ngoc Island on Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi. Originally existing in the 11th century, it later declined. In the present saw built in the 19th century.

reviews.author: Francois T
reviews.title: Worth a visit but not spectacular
reviews.content: Small temple complex on Hoàn Kiém Lake and worth a visit. Cost about VND50 000 to enter and we spent about 45minutes there. Nothing spectacular but still very spiritual and beautiful surrounds. Would recommend a visit if you in the area.

reviews.author: GlobetrotterMSK
reviews.title: Beautiful temple complex
reviews.content: Beautiful temple complex in the heart of Hanoi. Well maintained, popular with the public - also as a photo backdrop. Manageable, but still worth visiting.

reviews.author: Wanderlustaustralia
reviews.title: Beautiful and filled with plants
reviews.content: This is a really beautiful temple with lots of plants. It is kept really clean, and the entry fee is reasonable. Recommend a visit!

reviews.author: TheLush101
reviews.title: Famous turtle and temple
reviews.content: As others have right said, it's busy here day and night. You pay a small amount to be able to cross the red bridge and head to the temple. Inside there is some information about the story of the turtle and the reason that the temple was built to say thank you. The bridge looks more picturesque at night due to the lighting, so probably best to time your visit around dusk so that the temple is still open, grab a drink / food nearby, then take some photos at night.

reviews.author: Eli
reviews.title: Interesting backstory
reviews.content: A temple on Hoan Kiem Lake. Quite peaceful and has that classic old charm. Learning more about its historical backstory was really interesting and surprising. If you’re traveling solo or on your own, you can use the Travellens app to explore it deeper.

reviews.author: NilsM73
reviews.title: Mostly for the evening photo
reviews.content: We came (during the day), we saw, we took the photo and that was more or less it. The best part is really the view during the night. Not a biggie if you don't visit, and you will be happy if you do so, with a guide.

reviews.author: Stanley H
reviews.title: Holy Land of Hanoi, Cambridge
reviews.content: Since ancient times, Hanoi has been the political center of Vietnam. So, most of the things related to ancient dynasties can be found in Hanoi and its surroundings. This time, on New Year's Eve, come to the Old Town of Hanoi. Our team did get to the last attraction of the journey, the Yui Temple. This is a temple in the lake of Tambor. The temple is dedicated to Wen Cheng and the heroes of the 13th-century Dauphin army. Of course, the most important thing is to look at the specimens of reptile already extinct in 2016.The location of the Yuzhou Temple is Yuzhou Lake near the old town of Hanoi. The correct location is one of the lake islands in this lake. There are also two islands in Lake Cambridge. One is the home of the "Yu Mountains" "Yu Mountains", the second is a small island called "Turtle Tower". "Turtle Island" is one only for the wild animals in the lake and swordsmen to enjoy.The former "Yu Mountain Temple", was built during the Chinese dynasty (about the 13th and 14th centuries). But today we are visiting the Yujing Temple, which was built in 1865 during the Mongol Dynasty (about the 19th century) under the supervision of the then Chunxian Chunxian.There is a building called the "peat tower" in "Yu mountain temple". On the tower are inscribed three large words "Writing the sky". A tribute to literature.After passing the "peat tower", there was a door called the "grand tower". This door is a stand. Since there is a "pen", it is necessary to "Ink" so there is such a relative design.After passing through the "Great Canyon", we officially reached the scope of the "Yu Mountain Temple". We go to the lake side to see. That day, it was evening, and it was the evening of Easter. The entire surrounding area of Cambridge has been preparing for the Annual Party. The lights taken and the lights of the surrounding buildings make the night view of Lake Cambridge more colorful.And where we enjoy the lake view, it is located in front of the temple, a building called "Town Booth". There is not much information on this apartment on the Internet. In short, this is the best location to enjoy the whole of Cambridge.And "Toh Moon Building" is the inner gate of "Toh Moon Temple", which means tower that can receive the moonlight.Go to the main temple of "Yu Shan Temple". The first temple on the north side is dedicated to Chen Hengdu and Wen Cheng. In the temple, the knives are believed to be the royal members and generals known for defeating the invasion of the Yunnan army three times.Not very interested in Vietnam's ancient history. So, what we spend the most time admiring is the two remains of the sword that are preserved in the Temple.And the sword, also called Lili. According to the classification of Vietnamese scholars, this is a species of spleen. Today, the last remaining swordfish died in 2016. The same samples as those that died in 1967 were made and kept in the temple. It also means that even swordfish have been extinct.But according to international research, swordfish are the same kind. There are only 4-5 known live spots.A fisherman caught a ancient sword while fishing in the lake of the Rainbow Marine Network, with the words "Good day" inscribed on it, and the fisherman handed it to the leader of the Liberal Army at the time, Li Li Li, and then Li obtained a matching hand of the sword, so they assembled a sword. During the Decade of War, Liu Liu continued to carry the sword around him, eventually defeating the army of the Jin and establishing the post-Li Dynasty. Shortly thereafter, Lili came to the Lake of the Marine to ride the boat to play, and a giant lion emerged from the lake and sank under the sword. Lili believes that this is the sword given to him by the giant during the war against the Ming to help him defeat the enemy, and the giant seems to be willing to take back the sword after the restoration of peace under the sky. Lili decided to rename the Lake of the Navy to "Lake of Cambridge," which meant to return the Sword of God.A pleasant tour. Learn about the ancient history of Vietnam and see the beast of Vietnam. Also in the temple to enjoy the beautiful view of the Cambridge lake. It can be said that it is three. It would have been a missed attraction, here, thank you for the insistence of the guide, which allows the team to quickly close the door and visit the temple.

reviews.author: lilybt
reviews.title: It's changed a lot.
reviews.content: This shrine was built on an island in the northwestern part of Hoan Kiem Lake. It started its history as a temple and has continued to exist as Guandi Mausoleum, then as a temple, then as an educational publishing institution. After crossing the red bridge called Asahisashi Bridge, you reach the small main hall, which is scattered with various gates and towers. It displays stuffed turtles decorated with legends of saving the country, giving a sense of the city's history as it developed into a city center. The admission fee, or rather, the admission fee, was raised significantly the year before last to 50 thousand VND (about 300 yen).

reviews.author: VoyagerZ5533OA
reviews.title: A bubble of peace if you come early
reviews.content: I was a child when I first heard about the legend of the turtle, the king, and the magic sword. As an adult coming here with my own family, it felt a bit surreal, new yet nostalgic. We came here on the first and last days of our Hanoi visit, and the key is to come when they first open, at 7 am. The tranquility you'll find here in the early hours offers a welcomed reprieve from the Old Quarter's nighttime crowd and cacophony. Take your time, observe the markings engraved in the rocks as you first walk in, and notice other forms of life here. You may even have a cat come sit--just sit--next to you when there's no one around. Also try to spot a (live) turtle or two, and tell yourself that it's a sign of good luck. If you still believe in magic, this is the place to keep it alive.

reviews.author: BorntocruiseUK
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: The bridge is beautiful and gives great views over the lake. It’s only a small entrance fee to go in and I believe it’s worth it. You only need about 40 mins to go in and walk all the way around.Unfortunately it was raining whilst we were there but it didn’t really spoil it but made the bridge a tad slippery.The toilet if you need one is on the far side of the island.

reviews.author: Kishor D
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Oldest bridge in Hanoi. Beautiful view of the lake from bridge. Very reasonable entrance fee. Beautiful temple inside. Cannot take photos inside the temple but everything surrounding you can. Worth visiting

reviews.author: CJ
reviews.title: Good history and sightseeing and really peaceful
reviews.content: Very nice temple and a good place to come and learn more about the history of Hà Nội and Ho Kiếm. They have the two turtles displayed which hold a key significance for the people in this region. It costs 50,000VD entry and is a good spot for sightseeing. We visited at night time which is quieter. You get a panoramic view of the city.

reviews.author: akio9jp
reviews.title: The Tortoise and the Hero
reviews.content: Entrance fee is VND 50,000 for a temple on a small island north of the lake. Upon entering the temple grounds, there is a mural of a turtle carrying a treasure sword, named after the legend.Also on display was a taxidermy giant tortoise found in Hoan Kiem Lake, about two meters long.

reviews.author: Daniel B
reviews.title: come here if you are an explorer…
reviews.content: A mysterious temple located in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake.Everything is very beautiful and there are many solemn objects bearing many religious colors of Vietnam.A place worth visiting cultural features when coming to Hanoi

reviews.author: Christina W
reviews.title: Part of a Walking Tour
reviews.content: Very pretty area. A great place to take pictures. Add it to your walking tour of Hanoi. There is a temple at the end of the bridge and a man who sells plaques with Asian symbols on them.

reviews.author: Liliane M
reviews.title: INTERESTING VISIT WITH YOUR LEGEND.
reviews.content: The temple is located on the island of HOAN KIEM Lake which means restituted sword lake.Two turtles said to have lived in the lake are depicted. It's a symbol of longevity.Legend has it that the turtle protects the temple place of worship for the Vietnamese.The legend of the sword turtle is interesting.To access the temple, you have to cross the red bridge another symbol of Hanoi city.I recommend your visit and read your legend.

reviews.author: dennisalexandrov1976
reviews.title: Jade Mountain Temple on Lake of the Returned Sword, led by the Rising Sun Bridge
reviews.content: There's a small lake on which there's an island, there's a temple on it, a bridge leads to it, and in the middle of Lake Turtle Tower. What's not a beautiful combination? We took a great walk around the lake, visited the temple, learned the interesting history of turtles, generally touched on the history of Vietnam, the history of Hanoi. I think it's absolutely necessary to visit this place. And it's hard to write a lot, because you have to see it and learn about it yourself.

reviews.author: LSQRD1
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: This is an interesting and lovely temple on one of the lakes in Hanoi.  It has great importance as it relates to the turtle pavilion in the lake and houses the preserved bodies of the last two great turtles that lived here.  The story itself is fascinating and to see it in real life was very interesting.

reviews.author: BTS1972
reviews.title: Nice Temple in the Middle of Hanoi
reviews.content: A nice temple celebrating a Vietnamese general who fought the Chinese in the Middle Ages. The buildings and figurines are very fine as is the architecture. The temple is surronded by a lake and accesible via a nice bridge. One of the must sees in Hanoi.

reviews.author: sweetpearl88
reviews.title: Beauty of Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: Beautiful Ngoc Son Temple is a famous attraction in Hanoi, which features traditional architecture and the spiritual life of Vietnamese people. It is a serene place to admire the beauty of Hoan Kiem Lake.There are the preserved bodies of 2 big turtles that once lived in Hoan Kiem Lake. They are placed inside glass boxes for preservation and reverence.These turtles hold significant cultural and historical importance in Vietnam, particularly in relation to the legend of the lake's mystical turtle. According to folklore, a magical turtle surfaced from the lake and returned a mythical sword to Emperor Le Loi, who led Vietnamese forces against invaders! Very interesting historical site indeed.

reviews.author: Ightham1
reviews.title: A nice escape
reviews.content: A very pleasant hour spent exploring this well appointed temple. Lots of opportunities to take pictures and escape the hustle and bustle of the busy streets.

reviews.author: Alessandro
reviews.title: Normal Eastern Temple
reviews.content: Normal oriental temple with no particular positive or negative points. Characteristic the bridge to reach it and beautiful orchid pots

reviews.author: Russ Lacuata
reviews.title: Famous Temple in the Middle of the Lake
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is a famous attraction in Hanoi that features traditional architecture and the spiritual life of the Vietnamese people. The temple boasts unique architecture and a good view of the famous Hoan Kiem Lake.

reviews.author: Kirikouette
reviews.title: Things to do when you're in Hanoi
reviews.content: Very nice site to visit if you are in Hanoi on the lake of the restored sword. Made with a friend as part of a tour organized by agencies

reviews.author: Zurdar
reviews.title: Over crowded
reviews.content: Very busy and a little over rated … educational though. The turtle was pretty interesting. Everyone wants to take pictures ok that bridge …

reviews.author: OHKSO
reviews.title: Inside Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: It was a temple standing in Hoan Kiem Lake. When I was walking around the perimeter of the lake, I went to the precinct as one of the Things to do. If you cross the Teh Phuc Bridge to the "island", you will find a ticket box where you had to pay VND 50,000. After visiting the shrine, we were surprised at the size of the corner adjacent to the shrine where giant stuffed soft-shelled turtles are on display. Incidentally, kanji characters are written around the shrine, making it possible to recognize that it was once a kanji area.

reviews.author: Crumpled Nomad | Travel Intelligence
reviews.title: A piece of history
reviews.content: I believe this is one of the most visited tourist spot in Hanoi. Of course, we needed to visit it due to its popularity. One has to pay a fee and cross the bridge which was very scenic to get to the island.There was some legends about how this place was said to have came about. Two real models of the turtles which were previously living in the lake were on display here. Apparently they managed to preserved the bodies after they had passed on. Pretty interesting though.

reviews.author: Onas
reviews.title: Photogenic
reviews.content: Cute, but nothing special. There is a cute bridge and "island" for photos. In the center a temple. It's cool to take photos, but don't have high expectations.

reviews.author: mfilcol2014
reviews.title: Only for location
reviews.content: Temple located in the middle of the lake with access via a highly photogenic bridge. It's worth visiting just for its location. The temple itself is very small and of no great interestInteresting views from the temple to the lake and the city of HanoiIt's not really worth it

reviews.author: Shelley M
reviews.title: Views are nice
reviews.content: The bridge is lovely all lit up at night and we couldn't help wanting to cross it and see what the temple was like on the other side.  Not a lot there to be fair and the turtles were not there when we visited.  Nice to see a different perspective of the lake and it is a nice area of Hanoi but not a lot to see.  I would visit just for the views.

reviews.author: The-Mong-Melbourne-Australia
reviews.title: The lights off the bridge and go to our beautiful at night
reviews.content: I’ve been to this bridge during the day and night, but at night from the edge of the lake, you can take some beautiful photographs. Thoroughly recommend if it’s a nice evening a walk around the top part of the lake, including sitting on one of the park benches and chilling out for a few minutes, watching the beautiful lights of the pagoda and bridge.

reviews.author: Higuma 2017
reviews.title: Try to figure that out.
reviews.content: This is all about the turtle(s). And worthwhile the visit. A rather average, but reasonably cute temple, displaying two dead turtles, quite massive, to be honest. These poor creatures used to live at the bottom of that lake in the middle of Hanoi. Their kind is gone, forever. Their stories can be found on the wall, available in English. Although Vietnamese scholars like to classify them as a unique local species, they are part of the Yangtze Giant Softshell Turtle species... which does not make the whole survival of the species any more bright, as there are only two known individuals alive in the whole planet - both males. Back to the temple, displayed in each of the two glass boxes, there is an item, quite unrecognisable. Looks like a clawed hand. In one of them there is an explanation that suggests it's the reproductive apparel.  Check that and try to figure it out... If those two specimens on display were indeed males and those things are what is suggested, no wonder all the females are dead and the species is functionally extinct.

reviews.author: Inna
reviews.title: Red Bridge and Holy Place
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple 🛕is located on Ngoc Island in Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi. It is also a special national monument of Vietnam. The temple is dedicated to the warlord Tran Hung Dao (one of Vietnam's 14 national heroes), who repelled two of the three major Mongol invasions in the late 13th century. The island is called Jade Island and is connected to the shore by the red Morning Sunlight Bridge.It was very crowded here, calm music was playing, and the red lighting of the bridge conveyed an unusual atmosphere.Entrance to the temple is paid, but not expensive. I advise you to come here several times - during the day and in the evening. You can take very atmospheric and beautiful photos as a keepsake.

reviews.author: Livsnyderen2014
reviews.title: An oasis in the middle of the city
reviews.content: If you want to get away from the noise and traffic in the surrounding streets, the lake in the middle of the city is the perfect place to take a 'break' in the city tour.On a small island in the middle of the lake is the Ngoc Son Temple, and via the famous red bridge, you are led out to the temple, where the silence and tranquility sinks into your soul. When darkness falls over the city, the bridge is illuminated in red colors, while the temple is illuminated in yellow colors. A beautiful sight in the evening picture.Around the lake there is a lively life from morning to evening with joggers, dancers, exercisers of all kinds and lots of people playing, dancing and enjoying themselves. Fantastic place where cafes and food places are located side by side.If you want a trip to the temple, a ticket costs approx. 1.5 euro or dollar. The amount is used for the maintenance of the temple.

reviews.author: Angeles Echevarria
reviews.title: It is an island inside the lake in the center of the ancient city
reviews.content: It was next to our hotel so we visited it at night and day with the guide.There are two turtles important to the city that lived there in the lake and that symbolize longevity.For centuries there were turtles but now there are no moreIt is a place of worship for the VietnameseAnd above all, a place where young people go to take photos.

reviews.author: DotsGirl2
reviews.title: A turtle legend temple
reviews.content: This is a lovely little temple that has a legend to tell about it’s origins.  You cross over a lovely red bridge to get to it.

reviews.author: BrakiWorldTraveler
reviews.title: Amazing location of an ordinary Temple
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is located on a small island on Hoan Kiem Lake in the very center of Hanoi. It's reachable via a small picturesque bridge paying a small fee.Temple is quite ordinary, like many others we saw all over Vietnam, however its position on the lake is so beautiful and that's the reason it's so popular.Come at night as well, when it's beautifully illuminated.

reviews.author: kohechin
reviews.title: Temple in the lake
reviews.content: We crossed a red bridge to the temple in the lake. There are similar temples in Japan, aren't there? But before crossing the bridge, there was a gate with a dragon and a tiger painted on it, and beyond that was a gate with a kirin and a turtle painted on it. Inside was a Chinese-style temple. There was a stuffed turtle on display. The view of the opposite bank from the temple was beautiful.

reviews.author: Sophie G 🏖🧚🏻‍♀️☀️🌴
reviews.title: Very beautiful in the evening because it is well lit!
reviews.content: We saw the red bridge in the evening, unfortunately it was too late to visit but that will be for next time…In the evening around the lake, the view is magnificent because everything is lit!Go there, plus you will be in the old quarter and you will love shopping until 11 p.m.!!

reviews.author: Mohit Mangal
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: The place is absolutely amazing. It is very peaceful and at awesome location.We visited the place twice as in the evening with all the lighting, the place looks amazingIt is very close to Old quarter area so if you are staying there mostly u can walk to the temple. It is directly opposite to the puppet show theatre, which is also a must visit.

reviews.author: Roger W
reviews.title: beautiful location on a lake
reviews.content: This temple is certainly unique due to its location in Hoan Kiem Lake. It can be reached via a beautiful bridge. There is a typical temple on the island itself. It is certainly worth seeing due to its location, and it is also located in the old town of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Katie2690
reviews.title: Beautiful temple
reviews.content: Well worth a visit. Interesting local history, beautiful views and the temple is absolutely worth a visit. A beautiful place to visit.

reviews.author: André K
reviews.title: Not worth the visit
reviews.content: The lake where this temple is situated is more worth the visit then the temple. This is also a waste of time to visit as this temple has nothing special and is just a very small building on an island. Nothing spectacular here.

reviews.author: Justin H
reviews.title: Nice, though somewhat unremarkable temple.
reviews.content: It's interesting because it is on the lake, but otherwise it is fairly similar to a lot of other temples. Nice for a shorter stop, but not somewhere to spend a lot of time. Murals are nice, but lots of people taking photos everywhere.

reviews.author: smfac
reviews.title: In the setting sun
reviews.content: Small temple located on Sword Lake. Not to be missed, which offers a beautiful view of the lake. Instead, visit at the end of the day at sunset. Price 30,000 dong per person.

reviews.author: loonylou78
reviews.title: Beautiful temple.
reviews.content: This was such a fantastic temple to visit. It was our first Vietnamese temple we visited during our recent travels. Situated on Hoan kiem lake it provided a little bit of peace and quiet away from the craziness of the old quarter! Costing less than £1 to get in ,the place is stunning. Lots of artwork at the entrance and a bridge to walk over. The temple itself is small but so colourful and well maintained, you can take pictures from the outside but not inside, but trust me it's beautiful. Also inside the grounds is a small room which features 2  lake turtles which are believed to be the last ones ever to come from the lake and they help to keep the story of the lake turtles and the magical sword alive ( the lake which the temple stands is also known as sword lake). Please visit when you're in Hanoi even if for a short while.

reviews.author: Thanh An
reviews.title: Highlight in our journey!
reviews.content: This place for us is a good destination because it's located on one beautiful island of Hoankiem lake. We stayed there for a couple of hours and exlored a lot. Historical values of Hanoi gave us a hard pass to leave this wonderful country.

reviews.author: Art S
reviews.title: calm and cozy environment
reviews.content: Beautiful surroundings. A nice place to walk. Beautiful bridge, temple. you can walk for about an hour.

reviews.author: John Smirth
reviews.title: Den Ngoc Son
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple with its unique ancient features attracts everyone visiting Hanoi for the first time. I go in the evening, there is a ticket to get through the gate!

reviews.author: Dinh Trung-Tin
reviews.title: A Cultural Jewel in the Heart of Tourist Bustle
reviews.content: My visit to Ngoc Son Temple in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi was a memorable experience despite the crowds of tourists. This temple offers a fascinating insight into Vietnamese history and culture, and there are less crowded corners worth exploring.The temple itself is an architectural gem, with its glazed tile roofs, detailed carvings and elegant pagodas. The view of the lake from the Huc Bridge that leads to the temple is breathtaking, creating an atmosphere of serenity even among the crowds of visitors.One of the disadvantages of this place is indeed the tourist crowds, especially during peak hours. However, I found that as I explored the back part of the temple, there were fewer people and a more peaceful ambiance. This allowed me to better appreciate the spirituality of the place and take wonderful photos without the crowds.The history and cultural significance of Ngoc Son Temple is fascinating, and there are informative signs that provide interesting details. I also enjoyed the collection of historical artifacts on display in the temple.

reviews.author: Alokmili77
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: The temple surrounded by Lake very good lively atmosphere at nearby market hustle & bustle on walking street goid time to spend at evening

reviews.author: Mélanie M
reviews.title: Magnificent temple to visit
reviews.content: First visit upon our arrival in Vietnam and really not disappointed. The ornaments of the buildings are truly magnificent, and the setting is superb. A layer of serenity in the middle of the Capital!And the huge turtles are truly impressive to see!

reviews.author: Akshay Sharma
reviews.title: Visit this place during night time for better view
reviews.content: This is a  temple built alongside Lake Hoan Kiemabout 200 years old, and named after Saint Van Xuong. It is lit during night time and gives a unique appearance.

reviews.author: cramac
reviews.title: Nice for deck and bonsai
reviews.content: Very small but worth the visit. The bonsai trees and the bridge are beautiful and are illuminated in the evening. Located in the most pleasant area of central Hanoi.

reviews.author: Renato505
reviews.title: safety pin
reviews.content: The Ngọc Sơn temple is located on the island in Hoàn Kiếm Lake, it is very beautiful at night because of the lights that highlight its appearance from the entrance through the bridge

reviews.author: Hedthree G
reviews.title: Cheap thrill with lots of legend behind it
reviews.content: There's a great view of the lake from Cafe Pho Co top floor.  Enjoy good food, a breeze , and the view.  The Hoan Kiem Lake itself is actually pretty big and picturesque.  You have to buy a ticket to go over the bridge to the temple, but it amounts to a few US pennies.  There are several photo opportunities here.  We did get to see written prayers being burned so the gods can receive them.  Cool!

reviews.author: fishidmg
reviews.title: If You're Already Nearby, Might As Well Visit
reviews.content: Quite a quick visit and was very hot when we visited during day time.  Decently maintained with some nice view.  Just go if you are already in the area.

reviews.author: ctm7944
reviews.title: NGOC Son Temple - Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is located on Hoan Kiem Lake open 7AM to 6PM cost 30KVND. It is lit up at night which makes for a beautiful photo. On weekends the walking street and weekend night market are nearby.

reviews.author: Craig R
reviews.title: Vietnam Holiday 2023
reviews.content: A small temple located on an island on the Hoan Kiem Lake. After paying an entrance fee you walk across this bridge to the temple. The area is well maintained, and you get a nice view of the lake from the temple.The entrance to the temple is near the Water Puppet Theater.

reviews.author: Shruti V
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Very nice place to visit, its on hoan kiem lake..very beautiful temple,over all area around was excellent..specially in the evening..must visit

reviews.author: OneTrip with local
reviews.title: A nice place with lots of history.
reviews.content: The temple has beautiful bonsai trees and a peaceful lake nearby. You can relax and reflect here. There are also old things to see, like a giant turtle that has been in the lake for many years. You can visit until 6 PM every day. A student ticket costs 15,000 VND and an adult ticket costs 30,000 VND. However, it can be very busy with lots of tourists and locals on the weekends.

reviews.author: Luv2Go56
reviews.title: Small Peaceful Temple on the Lake
reviews.content: We were strolling around Hoan Kiem Lake and decided to get off the beaten path to tour the Ngoc Son Temple. There is a small entrance fee, and it is important to be respectful, and dress appropriately as it is an active place of worship.  It is a very quick stroll around the temple.  Highlights include the stunning red bridge, the impressive pagoda, and the beautiful varied foliage.  It was also fun to see Hanoi Old Town and the lake from this vantage point.  Very serene and tranquil.

reviews.author: hzari3949
reviews.title: Good for a quick visit
reviews.content: Small temple on the lake. Nice views and well maintained. Entry fee of 30,000vnd. It's a quick visit. Right out of old quarter and has benches and a park nearby to sit and relax for a bit.

reviews.author: dianne c
reviews.title: small temple with a nice view
reviews.content: Temple in the middle of the Hoan Kiem Lake. You need to pay a fee to go to it, 20-30K VND.It's just a small temple, most people go there to take pictures on the bridge. It is a beautiful temple though, has many different plants and flowers. The view is pretty nice when it'snearing sun down too.

reviews.author: CRISTINA Z
reviews.title: Another beautiful temple in Hanoi
reviews.content: Another popular temple in Hanoi to see.  Each part of this complex possesses a unique charm and meaning, so just go and see the most visited temple of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Harrison F. Carter
reviews.title: Well worth a look
reviews.content: Nice to see of an evening, can't comment on during the day as didn't see, but once dark, the temple and lake looked really pretty and well worth a little look.

reviews.author: TheLeongOhana
reviews.title: Small Island Temple
reviews.content: This was one of the most popular attractions the day I walked around Sword Lake.  Entrance fee was only 30k VND so a bargain.  So many people were taking photos on the bridge that it required a little weaving around.  At night the bridge was framed in red lights so a popular photo opportunity.Once on the other side, I turned left and walked to the edge of the island.   It was a popular spot for people to hang out as there was a lot of seating under the pagoda and facing the lake.Entering the temple on the left side were the famous Ho Guom Turtle models and a little story on their claim for fame.  I thought they were the most interesting item inside the temple.

reviews.author: Ly ly
reviews.title: Great choice to visit in Ha Noi
reviews.content: This a great palace for children to visit there.My child, they like this place a lot, so it help them to know more about our history.Quite busy at weekend but it's Ok.My child wasn't need to buy entrain ticket because they under 14 years old!

reviews.author: David
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Visited on a Monday. Was very busy - lots of photo taking going on! Entry cost me 30K.Despite being busy it is a pleasant site. The island gardens are well maintained. It's interesting on visit whilst at the lake.

reviews.author: Katy Santos
reviews.title: a little island
reviews.content: I visited this place before the pandemic - After having lunch in Lake View Side Restaurant and Cafe, we walked across to visit Ngoc Son Temple which is a temple standing in the middle of the lake. You can explore inside the premises to take photos of the Buddhist temple.

reviews.author: Stacy K
reviews.title: Island in the Lake
reviews.content: Temple in the middle of the lake in the Old Quarter. There is a giant mummified turtle. There are free public bathrooms, however, there are two toilets without privacy partitions and both must be used at the same time.

reviews.author: LuizDutraNeto
reviews.title: The little Temple of the Jade Mountain ...
reviews.content: At the Northeastern part of "Hoàn Kiêm" (the "Lake of the Restored Sword") and after crossing a beautiful vermillion painted bridge ("Thê Hûc" - the "Welcoming Morning Sunlight Bridge"), you will find the "Jade" islet. Right there, on a small hill, stands "Ngoc Son" (the "Temple of the Jade Mountain"), dedicated to Confucian and Taoist philosophers and to Vietnam's national hero, Tràn Hung Dao. The temple was built between the 18th and 19th centuries and is one of the most visited and revered ones in Vietnam, combining both ancestors' worship and Buddhist practices. So, whenever around Hanoi's "Old Quarter", do not miss "Ngoc Son". Opens daily from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Enjoy!

reviews.author: TravelinGypsey
reviews.title: Perfect!
reviews.content: Beautiful, peaceful & interesting history of this sacred place! A great place to visit and scope out in old quarter area; it’s cheap, doesn’t take too much time at all but is relaxing. Located on beautiful Hoan Kiem Lake; tons of things to do in this area! Follow @travelingypsey on Instagram & GoogleMaps!!!

reviews.author: Pedro Raffainer
reviews.title: Temple in Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: This is the Temple of the Jade Mountain and is located on the Jade Islet in Hoan Kiem Lake. This temple is small, but it's unique location makes it a must visit in Hanoi.

reviews.author: amanda5805
reviews.title: Stunning all lite up in the evening. Must see!
reviews.content: We arrived here later one afternoon around  4:15pm and spent about an hour. It cost 30,000VND (about $1.75CAD). They close at 5pm but didn't r rush people out but didn't let anyone else in.This has the most picturesque bridge. There  was so many people here when we got there and everyone wanted the same picture on the stunning red bridge. It is located in the Old Quarters and is a small island on Hoam Siem Lake.There was so many people all sitting around like bumps on a log. it was really weird. Then all of a sudden they lite the whole place up. So It all started to make sense  that is what most of the people were there for that. So it might be better to go at a different time of day. Who knows maybe it’s nuts all day. The temple was very nice with fresh flowers every where. The temple was built in the 18th century on the Island in the middle of the Lake of the Returned Sword. Legend has it the emperor was given a magical sword which helped him defeat the Chinese Ming Dynasty. When he defeated the Dynasty the Golden Turtle returned to the lake.  There are endangered large soft-shell turtles still swimming in the lake.Lots of locals were there to make their offerings. The grounds and temple are well maintained. It has a beautiful view over the lake.

reviews.author: Khushbu Mehta
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Located right in d centre of Hoan Kiem Lake. Its a beautiful sight to behold,esp in the evenings when its all lit up. U have to walk through the red bridge to reach the temple. Its closed by 6pm. Can spend half an hour here. Quite peaceful.

reviews.author: Gmglcfc
reviews.title: Small Temple
reviews.content: Nice looking Temple on a small island in the lake visited via a bridge . Small entrance fee.Not a lot to see but worthwhile even if just for the photos

reviews.author: skyisblu
reviews.title: Beauty in simplicity - visit in the morning
reviews.content: If you want a more authentic experience at this temple, visit right at opening. Locals come here to make their offerings before continuing their work day, so the morning is when you will witness people releasing birds to the sky, of bags of eels to the lake. You will see piles of incense smoking at every alter, and offering jar in between. You will see the hearth at the back smoldering with the papers of so many students, or symbolic money, or other papers. You will also witness the opening of the temple, the gardeners watering the simple-yet-beautiful gardens surrounding the small island complex. It's a different place than the mid-afternoon tourist destination. I also recommend walking by in the evening, to see the island, and its neighboring red bridge, glowing in the night and reflecting magically on the surface of the water. Quite the sight.

reviews.author: timmind
reviews.title: Picturesque temple and grounds, important history
reviews.content: Sitting on a lakeside bench away from the noise of the traffic, seeing people cross the lovely red bridge to the temple, how could we not go?  I think this temple is more for tourists now, as many westerners in shorts and skimpy tops were admitted. Still, it is worth seeing. The bodhi trees, the miniature rock gardens and the colorful murals are photo-worthy. Poor endangered turtles - long gone from their now polluted lake home. Worth noting: very clean Western style toilets.

reviews.author: Justnitid
reviews.title: The lake temple
reviews.content: The Temple of the Jade Mountain, as it is known in English, is on an island at the northern end of Hoan Kiem lake. The temple is dedicated to Confucius and Grand Prince Hung Dao - a celebrated general who repelled multiple invasions by the Mongols under Kublai Khan.The temple complex is small but deeply venerated.For tourists, the highlight is the red coloured pedestrian bridge to the island. It is one of the most popular selfie and photography spots.

reviews.author: G2Kpauly
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: I went here around sunset and it was just a quick walk around, afew good photos and nothing special the temple. But for 30000 it was cool.

reviews.author: Kim G
reviews.title: Accessed by Huc Bridge Across Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: Another interesting and lovely treasure of Vietnamese culture, built in the 18th century. Here you will find a preserved giant turtle, artifacts and alter. Translated: "Temple of the Jade Mountain" is accessed by the beautiful red, wooden Huc Bridge which spans from the banks of Hoan Kiem Lake, to the Temple on Jade Island. There is a fee to cross the bridge and visit the temple, but we felt it to be a worthwhile visit.

reviews.author: missjdaniels
reviews.title: Beautiful views.
reviews.content: The red bridge is obviously the main attraction of this temple and the view is lovely. There are a few spots inside to take some nice photos. The temple is beautiful and quite serene. I especially liked the bonsai scattered around the temple grounds. We spent around 20 minutes taking photos and enjoying the view. For 30,000VND (around $2 AUD) it is well worth the photo opportunity.

reviews.author: Travelaround59
reviews.title: Quietly located on an island
reviews.content: Lovely place: the temple is buzzing with worshippers and incense smoke and nevertheless the tourists still keeps a holy atmosphere.  We went late afternoon and with the mist coming out of the lake and the fog coming down from the sky everything was very suggestive.

reviews.author: Keith W
reviews.title: Quick visit
reviews.content: Very interesting buildings with so much to see , some walking is required but worth the effort , part only of day needed

reviews.author: LoBommer
reviews.country: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
reviews.title: Very small ornate temple on the lake
reviews.content: Average small ornate temple accessed via a red painted bridge over the lake. A small entrance fee to get in. Interesting facts and history about the lake and the turtles.

reviews.author: Chris S
reviews.title: Just on the lake - very attractive
reviews.content: This temple is accessed by wooden bridge onto small island (entrance £1 per person) and is lovely to visit. Very ornate temple, lots of character, takes 15 to 20 mins - quick easy visit

reviews.author: TinaQ
reviews.title: Lovely temple
reviews.content: A lovely little temple, it's largest selling point is the beautiful red bridge you have to cross to get there. The entrance fee is just over a euro and there are lovely views from the temple island.

reviews.author: Peleg Shlomo
reviews.title: Really nice place to visit
reviews.content: A great place to visit if you have free time in Hanoi, really small entrance fee of 30k and you can get some really beautiful pictures there and see a well preserved clean and stunning temple in the middle of the water.

reviews.author: dekalbill
reviews.title: Jade Mountain Temple
reviews.content: My guide related an interesting story about the history of the lake and temple which made the visit to this small but beautiful site worthwhile.  I was impressed with the local visitors who were there to pray creating a respectful, peaceful location. The iconic red bridge (beautifully illuminated at night) must be crossed to reach the temple.

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: Good but not a must see
reviews.content: Fairly small temple and only 30k dong to enter so very cheap.Temple is located within the lake and you need to cross a lovely red bridge to enter temple.Temple itself is very small and nothing amazing just nice.I would go at night time with everything lit up it’s very nice visually and great for photos.I would do but it’s not a must do while in Hanoi so if you are time poor give it a miss.

reviews.author: Herbert C
reviews.title: Peaceful respite
reviews.content: Located on Jade Island on the popular Hoan Kiem Lake, this temple is the perfect respite for those seeking a moment of peaceful solitude or certain divine blessing. Accessible by the arching Huc Bridge and with a nominal entrance fee, this temple is a good stopover whilst you’re visiting Hoan Kiem Lake or the adjacent Old Quarters. Go with a low expectation to avoid any disappointment.

reviews.author: digitalroc
reviews.title: Temple of the Jade Mountain
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple translates into the Temple of the Jade Mountain and resides on an island in Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi.  The temple was built to commemorate the 13th century military leader Tran Hung Dao who was known for battling the Chinese Yuan Dynasty.  The cost was only 30K VND, there was no line up, and it wasn’t too busy.  If you are near the lake, take the time out of your day to check it out, as it makes for some good photo opportunities.

reviews.author: Praveen K
reviews.title: Cute temple in a great location
reviews.content: The temple itself is not different than many of the others you'd see in the capital itself, but the setting in the middle of the lake with a charming bridge leading to it makes it special... We visited the place twice while just walking around the lake. Entrance fees 30000 dong.

reviews.author: Myra Brian
reviews.title: Thousand years of civilization
reviews.content: Very good place that allows you to find everything you need. The sellers are very nice, welcoming and hard-working, they even allow themselves to laugh with us and put us at ease. Good place that I recommend for any consideration. I am very happy with this store and this service

reviews.author: Joe Kemchi
reviews.title: Folklore best heard from a tour guide or a local
reviews.content: I was in Hanoi for work for a few days and only had a half day to sight see. The Ngoc Son Temple is worthwhile to add to any visit to Hanoi. There is a nice folklore story about this temple and the surrounding lake. There are signs inside the temple describing the story, although it is much more interesting to hear it from either a tour guide or a local.

reviews.author: augustwest11
reviews.title: A Must See
reviews.content: Go early and be respectful. I thought it was a fascinating temple with a neat story and beautiful workmanship.

reviews.author: Steve_of_N21
reviews.title: Small temple on the lake but worth a visit.
reviews.content: This one will not keep you long but as it is only 30K Dong to enter and cross the bridge to the island it’s worth doing, especially after dark when it is well lit. Pleasant enough shrine and the tortoise was probably the highlight.

reviews.author: Thomas Vedel
reviews.title: Meh..
reviews.content: The temple is nice and admissions are very cheap, but it’s nothing special. It’s perhaps a little hyped up? Anyways, we didn’t have to wait in line, the admissions were very cheap, so it’s not like we’re dissapointed. Just not very impressed either?

reviews.author: baghdadlian
reviews.title: Excellent Place
reviews.content: I went to the temple of Jade Mountain temple it was near my hotel paid an entrance fee and the whole area was so beautiful.  There is the Huc Bridge you cross to go toward temple and it is so beautiful.  Stayed and enjoyed the area for 2 hours and going back it had gotten dark and the whole area light up and it is so beautiful.

reviews.author: 422iana
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: When you first walk to over the bridge and get on the island, my first thoughts there was not much here. We went around in a anti-clockwise direction. It was not till we went 270 degrees around that we came upon the temple entrance and made it worth visiting. Nice views over the lake and interesting to see the giant turtle.

reviews.author: Johnfrisbee
reviews.title: Besutiful place
reviews.content: We visited this temple, accessed by the Red Bridge, as we strolled around thd lake and the old quarter of Hanoi.A beautiful place to see, although as we were there on a fine Sunday, around 12.00, it was rather busy. I'd suggest earlier in the day to avoid the throng if you can. But hey. It's a lovely 20-min place to visit as you meander around this lovely, vibrant part of the city.You pay a small entrance charge - not much.Loved this place: it's a "must-do" if you have the time, strolling around at your own pace.

reviews.author: Raymondale
reviews.title: Temple of the hade mountain
reviews.content: The name of the temple means ‘Temple of the Jade Mountain’ and is dedicated to war hero General Tran Hung Dao who defeated an armed force of Mongolian Emperor in the 13th century to invade Vietnam.there is a preserved specimen of a giant turtle found in the lake weighing 250kg.it is located at hoan kiem lake,beautiful lake.

reviews.author: Deepak DB
reviews.title: Lake Temple
reviews.content: 19th Century temple built in the middle of the lake on a busy centre of Hanoi. Just off the busy street you are welcome to this serene temple which can be accessed by a colorful bridge. One has to pay for the entry into the temple. However the garden and the surrounding are open to all.Dress modestly as its a religious place. Good location to spend in the evening when the weather is good.

reviews.author: Pushpal P
reviews.title: Nice temple over the lake
reviews.content: Nice temple over the lake. We visited in the night and it was lit up with lights. Goid for taking some pictures

reviews.author: Susan E
reviews.title: 30k VND ok
reviews.content: Cool little temple over the bridge. It's peaceful in a very bustling city. 30 minutes to see it all. Some cool turtles

reviews.author: Michael A
reviews.title: Nice temple
reviews.content: It is quite a nice and cute little temple that it over a small red bridge which is nice for photos. Entry is 10,000 VND for students or 30,000 VND for adults, definitely worth visiting.

reviews.author: Fazal Mahmud Roni
reviews.title: Small yet crowded temple over hoan keam lake
reviews.content: This lake would come out as one of the major tourist spot at trip advisor. So even though it small its more or less crowded all the time. This small place will offer you to sit under a big roof and enjoy the lake. It has two sculptures of giant turtles. There is a myth that this Ho Guom Tortoise carried the precious sword and buried deep inside of the lake. Ticket required to enter for adult, probably cost VND 30000/pax. Kids under certain age is free.

reviews.author: MarjofromBrissie
reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.content: We paid the small entrance fee to walk across the famous red Huc Bridge to the Ngoc Son Temple which contained a shrine with many offerings to the gods inside and the outside was surrounded by a variety of huge bonsai trees. It offered a good viewpoint of the lake to the south.

reviews.author: KGB777
reviews.title: Small temple at Lake Hoan Kiem
reviews.content: Also known as the Jade Mountain temple, this is located in the centre of lake Hoan Kiem and is accessible via a pedestrian bridge (after payment of a small fee). It gets quite crowded and there's not that much to see, apart from a few large turtle statues. Nice views out over the lake.

reviews.author: doctorfoxtrot
reviews.title: Temple at the Lake
reviews.content: This is a Buddhist temple located at the middle of the Hoan Kiem sword lake connected by the red Huc bridge.  Good place to visit and meditate a little . Be wary however of the huge influx of tourists. Located near the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Piki_cat
reviews.title: Temple on a lake
reviews.content: A temple sitting in the middle of the lake. With a taxidermy turtle that's really huge. Didn't read much about the history and we have to pay an entrance fee. Didn't bring home much memory. If you like Chinese temples this place is peaceful and nice.

reviews.author: Sharif Razi Al Mahmud
reviews.title: Temple means place of Religion but it is more than that
reviews.content: Very common visiting place in the heart of Hanoi. Tourist always use to visit there. So many beautiful statue in the temple. Temple is situated in middle of Hoan Kiem Lake connected with HUC bridge.

reviews.author: Govindan N
reviews.title: Beautiful Place
reviews.content: This temple is located in the old quarter on a small island in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake. To enter the temple, we will have to go over The Huc Bridge, a beautiful red-painted wooden bridge. Ngoc Son temple -Pagoda is peaceful and quite. The island on which the temple stands is called Jade Island. This is a Buddhist temple.The turtle displayed inside Ngoc Son Temple is one of 4 giant turtles which lived in Hoan Kiem Lake. The turtle is attached to the legend King Le Loi, who led Vietnamese people to fight back and expel Ming invaders from the national border. According to legend, Le Loi had the sword named Heaven's Will given to him by the Golden Turtle God, Kim Qui. He used this sword in the battle against the aggressors.Not long after Vietnam got independence, Le Loi was out boating on the lake. Suddenly the Golden Turtle God surfaced, prompting Le Loi to return Heaven's Will. The Golden Turtle God got back the sword and disappeared into depths of the lake. Le Loi then renamed the lake Hoan Kiem Lake, meaning “The Lake of the Returned Sword”.Ngoc Son Temple Entrance Fee:Adults: 30.000 VND Children: 15.000 VND Ngoc Son Temple Opening HoursMonday – Friday: 7 am to 6 pmSaturday and Sunday: 7 am to 9 pm

reviews.author: Daniel19721972
reviews.title: nice to visit. can be crowded
reviews.content: near the old quarter.cheap to visit. takes you half an hour can be crowdedplace is illuminated at night.especially the bridge is then niceduring weekends area around is free of cars and motorcycles

reviews.author: Steven H
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: This temple is small so doesn't take long to do but is a must do, after walking over the lovely bridge, you'll find the interior is beautifully decorated and just amazing to see.

reviews.author: Phuong N
reviews.title: Double
reviews.content: It's an interesting place to visit with the age is up to 1000 years old. Many things to learn when you are here.

reviews.author: tlynn63
reviews.title: Lovely place
reviews.content: We had been looking at this area from the balcony where we had lunch and so decided to see where that pretty red bridge led to.  The entrance was 30.000 dong (very little!).  We enjoyed walking around and eventually found benches, sat, and enjoyed the atmosphere.  Worth a look if you are in the area but not a must do sight.  We were there on a Tuesday in May in the late afternoon and the place was crowded with all ages.

reviews.author: hem0116
reviews.title: Busy
reviews.content: small fee . Accessed over a small bridge on an island in the middle of the popular lakeSeveral levels of devotional icons

reviews.author: MaxChin
reviews.title: Small Temple With Nothing Much To See
reviews.content: The temple is located nearby the old quarter, situated in the middle of the lake, facing the Water puppet show theater nearby. You will see a bridge linking the mainland to the temple, that is the place you are looking for. It require an entry fee of less than VND 100,000 per person, it does not really have a lot of things to see so if your group is quite a large group, you may need to think about it as the total fee will be quite high and you probably finish in less than 20 minute.

reviews.author: aaong86
reviews.title: Temple in the middle of Hoan Kien Lake
reviews.content: This is a beautiful temple located in the middle of Hoan Kien Lake. It's popular among the locals as well as tourist. Worth checking it out.

reviews.author: Liekehanna
reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.content: One of the prettiest temples I visited in Hanoi. Very serene and beautiful to see how the locals also visit the temple despite the many tourists roaming the sight.

reviews.author: Albywon
reviews.title: Limited Access
reviews.content: Beautiful from the edge of the lake, particularly at night when illuminated. It is undergoing renovations at the moment so you see almost as much for free as you do when you pay for entry.

reviews.author: williamkassel
reviews.title: quick visit to Ngoc San Temple
reviews.content: While walking around the lake of the Sword be sure to visit the Ngoc Son Temple.  It is worth the nominal charge to check out this monastery?  Great view of the lake and it tells you the story of the Sword and of the Giant turtles that were suppose to inhabit the lake.

reviews.author: BuzDriver
reviews.title: The Bridge and the Atmosphere
reviews.content: This is a good starting point for a visit to Hanoi. Best time to visit is in the evening before it closes at 6pm. The bridge and the lighting of the temple are quaint and interesting.

reviews.author: ZBH88
reviews.title: Small but interesting
reviews.content: The temple itself is very small bit given the  entrance fee 20,000 the same as a coke you may as well stop and take a look. Open until 6pm every day. Very lovely and lit up in beautiful orange and red lights in the evening.

reviews.author: john
reviews.title: You must visit!
reviews.content: Interesting temple located on the lake, if you are visiting the city you will surely see it since it is located in the historic center of the city and on the lake, which is an area you have to visit! the best time to visit this temple is very early in the morning, I visit it at 7:30 am since otherwise it is always full of visitors

reviews.author: David H
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Entrance was 30000 dong and it took about 15 minutes to visit. A lot of tourists but it was easy to walk around. Well worth a look.

reviews.author: Andres HC
reviews.title: Nice place to visit in a short visit to Hanoi
reviews.content: Location of place is near at the old quarter, perfect location to gif shopping, bars and restaurants.I come in March and 5:30pm is the perfect time to take some pictures with day light 6pm place close but if you already inside can take nice photos  6:30 is already dark with lights..

reviews.author: IanWithington
reviews.title: Small , quiet temple in the lake
reviews.content: A small , quiet temple in the lake.Been to quite a few temples across South East Asia and this one definitely won’t be on the list of ones I remember the most.Worth a visit but will only need 30 minutes max there.

reviews.author: Sarah b
reviews.title: Last day in Hanoi
reviews.content: We visited here during our last full day in the city and as part of our sightseeing tour. This is a small temple but worth a look. It is obviously very popular and many people were worshiping here during our visit.Very photogenic location across a lovely little bridge across the lake. There are loos here too which is very thoughtful.We spent around 30 minutes here but would say it is worth a look if you have the time and are passing.

reviews.author: Lisado976
reviews.title: Cute little temple on Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: This is a cute little temple on Hoan Kiem lake. We visited this place on the 1/15 lunar new year celebration, so it was a bit crowded. The ticket cost is 30k VND per adult. What makes this temple unique is it is located on the lake so the backdrop is excellent for picture/photo.

reviews.author: Jalal Iqbal
reviews.title: cool temple in the lake
reviews.content: very highlights and much pictured small temple located in the cool lake. connected with a nice bridge and much visited. at night due to good lighting, it appears very bright.  the whole lake area is nice and u must visit both at day and night. surely u gonna love the whole place and the vibe of the area.

reviews.author: sudeep912
reviews.title: temple
reviews.content: It is on the side of the lake and is well decorated in the traditional golden cladding.near to the square huge turtle statue is worshiped.people pray for long life.

reviews.author: Beverley B
reviews.title: Really pretty at night.
reviews.content: You do have to pay to access the temple. The walk takes you across a red bridge which is a popular place for people to take selfies! The temple site offers good views across the lake and is interesting in its own right. At night it is illuminated and the reflections in the lake are enchanting.

reviews.author: kpiddy
reviews.title: Particularly beautiful pagoda by night
reviews.content: Down on a small island known as Jade Island in Hoan Kiem Lake is a beautiful pagoda connected to the mainland via a gorgeous red painted wooden Huc Bridge, also known as the Rising Sun Bridge. We did not visit the pagoda/temple, more than happy just to view from across the lake or from the bridge which we could access for free.   The temple and Huc Bridge are memorable structures on the lake to photograph.

reviews.author: Laura T
reviews.title: Felt tricked as paid entrance fee but whole island was under construction - not worthwhile visiting at the moment
reviews.content: The temple sits on a small island in the centre of Hoan Kiem Lake and is linked by a beautiful red wooden bridge, which would make a lovely background for photos apart from the never-ending hoards of crowds!! Soo soooo soooo busy! :-SCurrently there is a LOT of restoration work taking place at the temple, so a visit in late December was not worthwhile, we would recommend to wait until the construction has finished before you try to visit. We were annoyed as there were no signs about the maintenance and you are not told when you buy the tickets, so even though the tickets were very little money (about £1 each), we still felt rather ripped off! and certainly wouldn't have bothered buying the tickets if we had known. There are free clean toilets at the rear of the temple if you do buy a ticket. There was really nothing to see at the temple on the island in December, as completely taken over by construction. You could see the giant turtle in the glass display cabinet, but that was all. I was rather annoyed as there is literally nothing to see, except a couple of bonsai and a view across the lake, which you can see from anywhere... That is until my husband discovered a back door through to the temple near to the toilets! There was no-one else inside here, so not sure if we were really allowed! but inside the temple was nice, brightly coloured with fresh coats of paint... Just a shame we couldn't see the flower gardens or large tree garden mentioned in previous reviews or view the temple from the front... and there were still crowds and crowds of people queuing to get across the bridge... to see nothing very much!The bridge that leads to the Ngoc Soc Temple is illuminated at night and very photogenic so just walk around and take photos - most people seem to hang around on the bridge without buying tickets to take photos, which is fair enough... but... the bridge is just crazy crazy busy all the time! :-STickets are purchased from a booth at the left hand side just after crossing the bridge for 30,000VND (£1) each. Open 7am to 6pm weekdays and until 9pm on weekends. We would recommend admiring the stonework and sculptures before the bridge and walking on the red wooden bridge to take photos, but then turning back at the ticket booth - at least until the extensive construction has finished.

reviews.author: Mark-Breck-StPete
reviews.title: Just saw from the outside - beautiful
reviews.content: The lake area is the place to be in Old Town Hanoi.  If you are lucky, you will be there on the weekend...when they close the streets down.  People are everywhere...strolling, dancing, exercising, singing...it is great.This temple is in the lake, there is very becautiful bridge you can walk on without paying admission and if it is closed.  Great photo opps!

reviews.author: Florian B
reviews.title: closed because of maintenance and nobody tells you ....
reviews.content: Yes, the Ngoc Son Temple is beautiful (I know because I have been there before) but now it is closed because of maintenance work and nobody tells you . The Lady at the desk still asks for the entrance fee (ok not too much but you feel yourself tricked. It´s now only the Bridge and one of the turtles and the view to the lake. Now please ask whether the maintenance is already finished - otherwise it is not worth to go there But: If it is back to normal it is a must

reviews.author: Caroline
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Impressed with the ancient architecture. It is located in the centre of Hoan Kiem Lake  which has really beautifull view

reviews.author: Lusse
reviews.title: Might be nice but
reviews.content: Beautiful island and bridge.We paid entrsnce fee and walked over the bridge then we noticed that whole island was under a maintenance and could acces only turtle display.When we went outside we double checkked and there weren't any information about maintenance before ticket sell point.

reviews.author: Nitsnath123
reviews.title: Uniquely positioned
reviews.content: This is very auspicious place and has many legends associated with it. They charge VND 30K as entry fees which could be only worth if you wish to click some pictures and read details about the temple. Nothing very unique except the bridge access to the temple,  a good place to click pictures and view the lake.

reviews.author: Avinash Chandra A
reviews.title: Beautiful temple in the middle of Hoan Kiem lake
reviews.content: Temple of the Jade Island located near the northern shore of beautiful Lake Hoan Kiem, built in 18th century to honour the 13th century military leader Trang Hung Dao. The beauty is in its location, beautiful surrounding and the red colour bridge called  The Hug Bridge. Looks beautiful in the night,  well illuminated. One can sit on the benches near by and relax.

reviews.author: neilhassall
reviews.title: Currently under renovation / nice views but best to visit when reopened
reviews.content: I visited the island and Ngoc Son Temple early one morning (it opens at 7am) as I'd tried to visit the previous day but had been put off by coachloads of tourists. Admission is only £1 / 30k VND but there isn't much to see and soak up, other than the history as the main temple is closed for renovation - you can see a hall whereby a large turtle found in the lake fro 1968 has been preserved and put on display, but other than views across the lake, there is very little else to see.

reviews.author: Václav B
reviews.title: Tourist trap
reviews.content: It is impossible not to take a picture from this spot.
