It “floats” on the lake and holds a piece of history inside.There is a golden casket in the shape of a turtle that contains two dead bodies of a real turtles. They were sacred animals and so-told ancestors of THE one that returned the sword. But these two were not able to mate. Sad story indeed.But the temple itslef is crowded with tourists taking selfies on the bridge, when we visited the building was under huge reconstruction and is pretty dirty.

reviews.author: Eski701
reviews.title: Visit with teenagers
reviews.content: Ok I have to admit my kids have a very short attention span when it comes to temples and pagodas , but the way around this I find is to give them a camera and they are more than happy then to snap away which is what they did here. This place was ok but tbh unless your nearby I wouldn’t make a special trip .

reviews.author: Hardvision
reviews.title: Beautiful temple. Looks even better at night from a distance.
reviews.content: It is a beautiful temple by the lakeside. Worth a visit. There are lot of shopping and eating places around this central spot. At night, the temple is all lit and looks beautiful from the other side of the lake.

reviews.author: PerttiHar
reviews.title: Nice temple under renovation
reviews.content: Relaxing place of worship. Unfortunately under renovation at this time and full of tourists going around.

reviews.author: Mark M
reviews.title: Renovation
reviews.content: Entry to the temple costs 30k and you access it over a wooden bridge that is full of tourists taking scenic selfies.The temple is being renovated as of November 2018 so doesn't look pretty from the outside. Inside is a colourful Confucian temple which is still used by locals for prayer. So be mindful when taking pictures.

reviews.author: dlam626
reviews.title: Total waste of $
reviews.content: This temple is currently under renovation! Which they don’t tell you when you purchase the ticket. You can walk across the bridge and take photos with the murals outside the temple for free! Once inside there’s nothing to see except for the preserved tortoise. You can take a small side entrance to see the alter as well, but it it certainly wasn’t worth an admission ticket.

reviews.author: Michelle S
reviews.title: Under renervation
reviews.content: It is the most visited temple in Hanoi and currently undergoing extensive renovation.  There's still a lot to see if you fight through the thong of tourists but currently I would say say the entrance fee and visit one of the many other temples that Hanoi has to offer.  Many of which are cheaper or free.

reviews.author: lissyundthomas
reviews.title: Nice view
reviews.content: The small Island is Nice to visit but you are quickly done. At the moment they are renovating so most of the Island is hidden.

reviews.author: Marcin M
reviews.title: The biggest nothing in Hanoi
reviews.content: We went to this place inspired by travel guide. The biggest nothing to see, building place under construction, nobody informed about it. 30 k to see what you can find on the pictures

reviews.author: UNNIMAYA
reviews.title: Debatable whether worth the entry fee
reviews.content: You have to pay an entrance fee to visit this temple situated across a bridge on Hoan kier lake in old quarter of Hanoi. There is a lot of renovation work going on right now and there is nothing much to see other than the views of Hanoi across the lake. Although  it is only 30000 VND to get in , it is debatable whether it is worth even that particularly because of the construction works in progress currently. May be it will be a much better place once the renovation works are over.

reviews.author: saul g
reviews.title: well , if only .......
reviews.content: Located on a very nice spot on Hoan Kiem lake . The temple is under some restorations , Still , there are entry fees . The Bridge leading to the temple from the lake shore , and the garden around it are very nice , lots of tourists and local . Considered "good luck" to visit here . when restorations are over  - the title MUST-SEE will probably justified .

reviews.author: carloscharmy
reviews.title: Under renovation
reviews.content: For 30,000 VND you can get into this temple. Right now they are renovating it (no idea when they are going to finish). As many other travelers say there isn't much to see but I did not mind paying the money to stroll around the small island.

reviews.author: ExperienceLifeLove
reviews.title: Ho hum :/
reviews.content: I didn’t really the significance is. There’s a pretty view across the lake. From all the people on the bridge (taking selfies etc), I thought it must be something special to see inside.As the other reviews point out, it’s under renovation. Maybe it’ll be more impressive once they’re finished.If you’re pushed for time, my advice is to do something else instead.

reviews.author: ngo r
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: Only people who understand about the harmony of The red bridge and the pagoda would see it's beautiful.

reviews.author: Becky & James
reviews.title: Building works - what a dump!
reviews.content: Apart from a pretty view across the lake, the rest of this tiny island was a complete dump. Dirty, rubbish everywhere, building work going on, grumpy staff. As a female I was expected to show respect and cover up, but it seems they have no pride in this little temple, or it is just used as a money machine.

reviews.author: iwona
reviews.title: Stunning @ night
reviews.content: Sadly, we got there after 6 pm when it closes at 6 pm still, as it’s outdoors you can enjoy the site from far and near! The photos we took are amazing 😉 It’s a great, really wonderful attraction to see then you can continue strolling, either around the lake or to the OQ. Worth seeing - I guess it’s a must, a Hanoi landmark!

reviews.author: Lisa M
reviews.title: Pretty, but not worth the entrance fee
reviews.content: It was an attractive temple, but quite small and took very little time to explore. I would not recommend this if you are in a rush or looking to save a couple dollars.

reviews.author: joshbrandon
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Good place to visit in weekdays. In weekends it is over crowded. Beautiful temple with many Chinese tourist. They throw trash everywhere. Authority needs to control & improve the cleanliness measure. Specially holy places.

reviews.author: iliketomoveandsee
reviews.title: Not worth paying to go inside
reviews.content: We paid for a ticket each before crossing the very crowded red bridge, I'm not sure what we expected on the other side, but this wasn't it. The little island is a complete mess, rubbish everywhere. It looks like they are doing renovations, but even the renovations looked a mess. A real shame, I don't mind paying a small amount to see something in progress, I'm always pleased to see renovations - so that future generation can enjoy something, but this was just a mess.

reviews.author: Alchemy
reviews.title: Lovely temple to visit
reviews.content: This is a great place to visit and is conveniently situated near the lakeside. It is a wonderful gathering place and has the red bridge nearby too. Good to spend some time looking around.

reviews.author: RayICue
reviews.title: Gathering Spot
reviews.content: I visited on a Sunday afternoon and enjoyed the crowd of people coming and going across the red bridge.  Great photo stop for people watching.  The street in front was closed and made walking there even more enjoyable.  Less trash on this lake ,  good to see as well.

reviews.author: fluffymonkey
reviews.title: Temple of the Jade Mountain
reviews.content: Its not hard to see why this is Hanoi's most visited temple. Whilst its modest in size the location on the lake and the 'legend' of the magical sword and turtle god draw the crowds. We didnt find it a particularly peaceful place as it was packed when we visited but the temple is great to see, and there is also the opportunity to see one of the elusive lake turtles - unfortunately this ones not alive anymore!

reviews.author: pjcot1
reviews.title: Nicely situated temple, under renovation
reviews.content: I’d imagine this place being one of the best small temples to visit if not being renovated. As of 15th September around half of the temple is closed for renovation. Having said that, the entrance fee is only 30,000 VND and still plenty of serene photo opportunities. Situated in the Hoan Kiem lake, walk accross the red wooden bridge and enjoy the views around the lake and of Turtle Tower. Not a must see until renovations are finished

reviews.author: nellielim
reviews.title: Small temple with lovely views
reviews.content: Located on an islet on Hoan Kiem Lake, this temple can be reached by a red bridge. Though the temple is small and parts of it are under renovation, lovely views across the lake can be seen from it's grounds. There is an entrance fee charge and modest dressing is required for a visit. In the evenings, the temple is brightly lit up making it a nice photo backdrop.

reviews.author: TravelAroundBug
reviews.title: Nothing much to see. A bit of a rip off due to reconstruction
reviews.content: There was no signage of whatever that highlighted the fact almost half of the temple is closed for renovation. The prevailing entry fee still applies but there is nothing much to see. The place is very small and I think we do have more interesting temples in Singapore. The walk on the bridge to the temple is nice though and picture worthy.Will definitely need more English explanation on the board.

reviews.author: Hawkdai007
reviews.title: Not much too see
reviews.content: Probably it was not the best time to go there as it is currently under the renovation so large part of temple was closed down.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Local History & Legends
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple, or the  'Temple of the Jade Mountain', is Hanoi's most visited temple.It is small island in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake, reached  by an elegant red bridge of classical Vietnamese construction. The temple is dedicated to General Tran Hung Dao (who defeated the Mongols in the 13th century), La To (patron saint of physicians) and the scholar Van Xuong.There is also a large taxidermied turtle in a glass case, homage to the legend of King Le Loi returning the sword he used to vanish the Chinese invaders to the turtle in the lake.

reviews.author: pratikjoshi448
reviews.title: Night visit at the Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: Listening to the legend of the Ngoc Son Temple was really intriguing. There was also a huge turtle on display. The turtle has its own legend but it had died recently and they preserved the turtle. It's a tourist attraction now.

reviews.author: Nicola C
reviews.title: Small but nice
reviews.content: This temple is much smaller than other ones in Hanoi, but has great views over the lake. Its 30,000 dong for adults and 15,000 dong for students. It would be hard to spend more than about an hour here. It was quite busy so made it hard to relax and enjoy the temple.

reviews.author: AMC286
reviews.title: The Temple of the Jade Mountain
reviews.content: The Temple of the Jade Mountain locally known in Vietnam as Den Ngoc Son is located on Hoan Kiem Lake in central Hanoi, Vietnam.  Being built on the Jade Islet and dedicated to Confucian Taoist philosophers and the national hero, Tran Hung Dao, the small temple was expanded in 1865.From the shore, the Welcoming Morning Sunlight Bridge leads to the island.  Buildings of the temple include the Pen Tower, the ink slab, the Moon Contemplation Pavilion and the Pavilion against Waves, all of which have symbolic meaning.Show respect to these temples by dressing appropriately as the locals and tour guides will remind tourists before they go to the place.

reviews.author: Natalie B
reviews.title: See it at night
reviews.content: Once the sun goes down, this temple is lit up beautifully. Take a stroll around the lake for lovely photos. You can walk over the bridge and visit the little temple but it closes after dark so keep that in mind if you actually want to go inside.

reviews.author: Rachel P
reviews.title: Lovely and tranquil
reviews.content: A lovely, tranquil small temple in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake.  It was interesting to discover the legend of the lake, see the incredible views from the temple and see the intricate decoration in the temple.  The temple is not big and won't take long to visit but it is worth it.

reviews.author: Larry007_007
reviews.title: So-So
reviews.content: As a tourist I couldn’t really recommend this place.   High Fee to go to the temple, and not much to see (small).   If you are there to take a picture on the lake, do it on the bridge for free.     The temple was fine and well-kept.  If you are there for prayers, there more worthwhile.   As a tourist I would skip it

reviews.author: Muguncjb
reviews.title: A temple in the middle of lake
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is located in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake. To reach the temple one has to cross Cau The Huc, a red wooden bridge for about 1-2 min by slow walk. To enter the Cau The Huc bridge one has buy a entrance ticket which is collected for visiting Ngoc Son Temple as well as to walk on the Cau The Huc bridge.  The temple is small. May be 5 to 10 minutes is sufficient to cover the premises. On the land side are a huge tree garden with paved way for walk on one side and a small flower garden on the other side located. Totally a good 30 to 40 minutes can be spent here. The nearest attraction is Old Quarter.  All can be covered in the evening.

reviews.author: Best Angkor Guide dot com
reviews.title: Just a temple
reviews.content: Ancient temple in Hanoi you should visit. It was not much to see. But if you have nothing to do, just do it.

reviews.author: ruthandvern
reviews.title: Dress with modesty
reviews.content: It was so wicked hot when we went to the lake the evening of our arrival it wasn't until we actually started to get our tickets I decided I'd feel better coming back with covering for my shoulders and knees. It isn't much but it does show respect to the Vietnamese citizens. Crossing the red bridge provided super photo ops. The island and temple can get quite congested. For some reason a group our tour group tourists manage to monopolize about every square inch of photo prime shot areas. That was frustrating but the serenity of the trees, temples, shrines, and Bonsai made it a very pleasant visit.

reviews.author: 127Fred
reviews.title: With the legend of the turtles.
reviews.content: When in Kindergarten, I may recall that we kids were told about a legend regarding turtles and a lake. Unfortunately, I have missed this day, maybe I had smallpox. Otherwise I would have been quite excited to see the place where the legend and beautiful story comes from. Without this legend in mind, a lot of the magic is lost to the average visitor.There remains a lake, which gives an impression of quietness and some great sunset views.There remains a small Buddhist temple. It hardly compares with the temples of Kyoto, Japan. However, it is well kept and quiet.

reviews.author: kenl461
reviews.title: Hoan Kiem Lake & the Ngoc |Son Temple in the middle of the lake.
reviews.content: We walked around Hoan Kem Lake with a pagoda & the Ngnoc Son Temple in the middle of the lake, as part of our tour.  You can access the island where the temple is located by crossing the Rising Sun Bridge.  A nice break from the noise, hustle & bustle of the city.  Lots of locals milling around.  Very peaceful & tranquil.  Nice photo ops here!I would say that this is a better than average visit, GOOD.

reviews.author: zenu
reviews.title: Tranquil and much to admire....
reviews.content: Opposite the Puppet theatre, this temple is accessed via a quaint red wooden bridge.Lovely views of the lake and the Turtle Pagoda.The temple is small and its architecture is delightful.Locals come to pray.Peaceful and far from the madding crowds and the hustle and bustle of Hanoi.

reviews.author: blackeaglejim
reviews.title: Hoan Kiem's island temple
reviews.content: The island called Jade Mountain, at the top end of Hoan Kiem Lake, now is the site of a temple dedicated to Tran Hung Dao, the 13th century general who led the Vietnamese defeat of three Mongol invasions. It's a good example of how Vietnamese deify their national heroes.  In the 17th-18th centuries the island was the site of a palace of the ruling Trinh Lords, who watched naval exercises on the lake which, at that time, was bigger and still connected to the Red River.  It was cut off from the river in the early 19th century.  The island is accessible via a beautiful, comb-shaped, red wooden bridge, built in the 19th century.  Hoan Kiem Lake used to be the abode of very large turtles that lived for centuries.  A preserved sample of one of these is in the temple compound.

reviews.author: JLM3080
reviews.title: interesting but only if passing
reviews.content: This is an interesting building on the lake island, and tells quite a good story about the returned mystical sword, shame the turtles are have died out. Its also a great place to take pictures of the surrounding area

reviews.author: 2littletime2seeitall
reviews.title: Glad I went early
reviews.content: I ventured out early on Sunday morning, and it was quite peaceful at the temple except for a few groups holding up foot bridge traffic for pictures.   The visit cost 30,000 dong, which sounds prohibitive but actually was $1.32.  Pictures are allowed, so I got pictures of the altars and one of the amazing bonsai.  After waiting for a few men who were fascinated by looking at the underside of the turtle to clear out, I got a picture of the preserved legendary giant turtle of Hoan Kiem Lake without anybody in it.  The temple is worth the visit, but it had gotten much busier by the time I left.  Go early.

reviews.author: santo t
reviews.title: Icon of the lake
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple was built in the 18th century on Jade Island in the centre of the ‘Lake of the Returned Sword’ or Hoan Kiem Lake. This small island is accessible by the iconic Huc Bridge or Rising Sun Bridge, a charming red painted wooden bridge  The pagoda is also guarded by two towering posts decorated with Chinese writing. The lake and temple are probably the most famous places in Hanoi Old Quarter to enjoy the surrounding view and are a great place to sit back and watch the locals.Ticket to visit sold at the left hand side before crossing the bridge for VND 30000 / adult, open from 7am to 6pm. The lake and the temple offer plenty of trees and shaded spots to escape from the surrounding busy city streets. This site is not too far from the other famous attraction, at the opposite side of Thang Long Water Puppet.

reviews.author: finesilver
reviews.title: The temple on the lake, great photo ops
reviews.content: The is an extremely popular place, you walk across the iconic red bridge and then you can walk all around the temple grounds and then go inside to check it out.   There are photo ops every few feet, vibrant flowers, trees, the lake itself, and the temple too and its altar and offerings. There are great orchids out in front, same for fruit trees too.The place is quite crowded at all times. It costs a little to go see it, but like $2.  Not sure why anyone would complain about that as an entry fee.  Photo ops also at dusk when the bridge and the temple itself are both lit and reflect in the lake's water too.

reviews.author: mickknap
reviews.title: 19TH Century Temple on the Lake
reviews.content: Beautiful, and historical temple built on a small island on Hoan kiem lake . Get your ticket before you walk over the ornate red bridge which links it to the city,On entering the grounds of the Temple of Jade you will pass through an ornately designed Vietnamese gateway ,leading you round to  the large lakeside pagoda ,some beautiful bonsai trees here and the entrance to the Jade temple , very peaceful and spiritual temple ,where people still come to pray and give offerings ,you can walk round inside and see the beautifully designed statues and murals depicting  Buddha , and Vietnamese history , there is also a large mummified  giant turtle  on show , on exiting the temple you can walk around the  outside through a small garden area , well worth a visit , relaxing and enjoyable .

reviews.author: Greg S
reviews.title: Beautiful ceremony
reviews.content: Don't know if this happens all the time....but just the most beautiful ceremony was occuring at the time we visited the island temple at Hoan Kiem Lake.

reviews.author: loudini56
reviews.title: Beautiful Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: Built in the 19th century on a small island on the northern end of the lake. You cross a crimson bridge to reach the island the temple is located on. It means Temple of the Jade temple and is dedicated to General Tran Hung Dao (who defeated the Mongols in the 13th century), La To (patron saint of physicians) and the scholar Van Xuong. People come and pray to it and leave offerings to Buddha. A beautiful example of a temple built in the Vietnamese style and is well worth visiting.

reviews.author: Mehul Kirit Shah
reviews.title: Jade Mountain Temple
reviews.content: The temple is located on a small island in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake, connected to the lakeshore by an elegant scarlet bridge, constructed in classical Vietnamese style. It extends out into the lake, with small but attractive grounds, displays on Vietnamese history and, more memorably, displays on the giant turtles, including a mummified specimen.

reviews.author: John L
reviews.title: Not much to see and they collect your money for it.
reviews.content: Crawling with people all the time, you can skip it, take your picture outside of the place and go elsewhere.

reviews.author: mapleleaf2727
reviews.title: Giant stuffed turtle
reviews.content: We went there for the stuffed turtle. Apparently it was one of the four that used live in the lake. Other than that, there's nothing very much to see. Can give this a miss if you are pressed for time.

reviews.author: Cocko22
reviews.title: Under renovation but worth a look at the entry price
reviews.content: We thought it would be important to see such a significant temple...it’s under renovation and this detracted significantly from the experience. Worth a look, nominal entrance fee.

reviews.author: Ernest W
reviews.title: Not much interesting going on...except for the cat!
reviews.content: Quite frankly, there isn't much exciting going on in this temple. As a fan of classical Chinese, I like reading the inscriptions on the walls, pillars, rooftops, and ceilings. Some are proverbs, some are poems, some are teachings...But for the average visitor who cannot read the many inscriptions, I'd say there's not much of interest here. There's a big statue of a tortoise encased in glass in one of the buildings. I can't remember what it was made of. But it was pretty unspectacular. Plus, being smack in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake, which is smack in the middle of the most touristy area of Hanoi, this place sees A LOT of tourists. Tourists by the busload come through the gates, and it can be hard to get a picture of anything but tourists. My advice is if you can score a half priced admission by presenting a student ID (any type of student ID will do), then go for it. Otherwise, just skip it...UNLESS you want to play with the resident cat...who is extremely cute, friendly, and pettable. God, I can't believe she can sleep so much despite all those tourists trying to disturb her (myself included).

reviews.author: ReneMacQ
reviews.title: Very Busy
reviews.content: Situated on an island at the lake. Unfortunately if you go on your own, do some homework. There are no signs explaining exactly what is special about this temple. Was very busy.

reviews.author: E8887TZmartinp
reviews.title: Tranquility in the lake
reviews.content: Pleasant wander across the red 19c bridge past the pay booth (nominal) you come to the temple on the island with its 3 chambers. The outer chamber is dedicated to the God of Literature (note the pens and books) while the middle is dedicated to a general who defeated Ming invades 3 times on the 13c.  As with most temples there is a hearth for sending gifts (mainly fake cash) to ones ancestors by incineration on the left as you enter. Nice break from the bustling old town

reviews.author: ASougy
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: Located on the lake it's worth a look. The red bridge is a nice spot for a photo and the temple is interesting. I liked the bonsai trees.

reviews.author: harvint2016
reviews.title: boring and cheated
reviews.content: The temple is very small and charges USD2 per entry. I don't think it is worth it to see this place, pretty boring. Taking pictures at the red bridge for free is enough. Inside the temple its not amazing and nothing out of the ordinary. Plenty of better Hanoi temples are out there. So, after we paid and entered the temple, about 10minutes someone came up to us and asked to give us back the torn ticket. We were hesitant but this guy showed us a lanyard 'ID' card to prove he works here. But he seemed sneaky and anxious... Anyway we gave it to him and he walked off. After our tour we went back to the counter and saw other tourists coming in without passing back the torn tickets. We guessed the sneaky guy actually took our tickets to sell it to other people to make money and the buyers can come in showing our torn tickets to prove they went in before and they wanted to go in again..

reviews.author: Alex B
reviews.title: Interesting feature in Hoan Kiem
reviews.content: I came by Ngoc Son Temple while walking around Hoan Kiem.  I can't really say much since all the information is in Vietnamese.  There's a prominent read bridge that's a feature in the lake, leading to the temple.  I went in out of curiosity but it is neither here nor there really.  That's mainly due to my lack of knowledge of Vietnamese.

reviews.author: Xanerin
reviews.title: Quaint Temple
reviews.content: I have visited many temples from huge ornate ones to lovely small ones.  This is the latter however I thoroughly enjoyed my visit.  Take your time to explore every little nook and cranny and also ask questions so you can understand it in more detail.  I saw many people just walk in and out and not really enjoy what is being offered.  Cost a couple of Aus dollars and is worth every little cent.  There are also clean toilets at the rear of the temple (no charge).

reviews.author: linh y
reviews.title: The ancient temple is beautiful
reviews.content: I visited the Ngoc Son temple for the first time but felt very familiar. The temple with old trees like Dinh Chua my home. Standing in the temple courtyard view beautiful and peaceful Hoan Kiem Lake

reviews.author: Damien G
reviews.title: A Nice Stop
reviews.content: I enjoyed this visit - it’s a small temple on the lake - pretty bridge - nice grounds. Entry fee - around 1 USD. Don’t expect a huge temple with lots to do - more a photo opportunity and a little stop on a sightseeing day.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Bridging the Gap
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is a Confucian and Taoist temple sitting on a small island in the middle of Hanoi's Hoan Kiem Lake.I found the temple itself relatively mundane, but the red painted bridge that connects the island to the north eastern shore of Hoan Kiem Lake is picture-postcard perfect.  It is poetically called "Welcoming Morning Sunlight Bridge", but I didn't get there until late afternoon, so I cannot vouch for that.The temple dates back at least 200 years, with restorations and additions being recorded in 1865.The temple is a popular spot for both locals and visitors to Hanoi..Being built on the Jade Islet and dedicated to Confucian and Taoist philosophers and the national hero, Trần Hưng Đạo, the small temple was expanded in 1865.The temple is a popular spot for visitors to Hoan Kiem Lake and Hanoi.

reviews.author: Wistraveller365
reviews.title: Nice visit
reviews.content: The temple is not as over the top like the one's in Myanmar.  Great place to stop in and soak up some history.  Has a lot of great picture opportunities with the red bridge to enter and the buildings.

reviews.author: Esther R
reviews.title: So sweet
reviews.content: Walk around 15 minutes from my hotel and can enjoy beautifull scenery of the temple after cross the Red Bridge (Hoan Kiem Lake).. one of the famous place must visit in Hanoi.. full of history and such amazing place.

reviews.author: ErickaERK
reviews.title: A place to come
reviews.content: I see quite a lot of tourists as well as Vietnamese come here to visit, a little cramped travel but I found this place worth to come, inside there are many or very good example of looking directly to the image of turtles gold, some antiques from many years ago, I see the solemn atmosphere here

reviews.author: PandaHouston
reviews.title: Entrance is 30000 dong
reviews.content: To walk on the bridge and enter the temple, entrance is 30,000 dong.  The temple area is small and it won't take more than 20 minutes to walk the perimeter.

reviews.author: Kenny Lee Chia Sern
reviews.title: Very scenic place for both day and night
reviews.content: I went to this place by chance during the day as it's located on Hoan Kiem Lake. The view is fantastic and it has a small entry fee of VND 30000 for tourist to step into the temple across the bridge. The night scene will be the best for photo taking with the bridge well lit. Good camera and skills needed to take perfect pictures.

reviews.author: GD365
reviews.title: Not much to see, but but beautiful view of the lake
reviews.content: A very small temple, translated as 'Temple of the Jade Mountain'.The beautiful red bridge across Hoan Kiem lake is the main attraction. On the downside, I saw no information on display about the legend of the giant turtle who carried the magical sword to give to the emperor. so he could defeat his enemies. (you have to research that yourself!)I learned about the legend in detail only because I had a guide with me from Hanoifreewalkingtours.I'm giving it only a '3' rating because of this lack of information. It would be really appealing to children.

reviews.author: Cekeysh
reviews.title: A temple by the water
reviews.content: The temple is interesting because of the red color is the majority of the decoration. Built in one side of the lake it with bridge and water pool, the temple itself is very nice

reviews.author: Gary
reviews.title: Pretty and ornate, particularly inside
reviews.content: The temple is reached via a curved footbridge that is lit up red at night and looks beautiful. On the other side of the bridge you pay 30k VND to enter inside, and while it’s not the most extravagant or huge temple, it was beautifully ornate inside and we were unexpectedly walked round by a local who was keen to show us how he pays his respects, despite the complete lack of any common language! Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: Yvonne a
reviews.title: Quaint
reviews.content: Nothing spectacular about the temple, except that it is located in the heart of Hanoi across the red bridge in the middle of the lake.  You only need 20 minutes here, but lots of photo opportunities.  Very peaceful away from the noise of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Andrea W
reviews.title: A pretty temple reached across a brilliant red bridge
reviews.content: Wear something sensible, if not they'll lend you a coverall: this IS a temple. Didn't go in, but the entrance, the bridge and the lake all add to the charm of this place.

reviews.author: moviegeekjn
reviews.title: Photo Op
reviews.content: Highlighted by the red bridge (lighted at night), this site along the beautiful Hoan Kiem Lake is strictly a photo opportunity (especially for westerners).  Don't expect much explanations in English, so research beforehand to find out the significance.  I used my very bad French to get a general idea about the importance of the turtle and sword from the posted information.If you just want a photo of the bridge, you can get good ones without crossing and paying the small fee.

reviews.author: Jesse F
reviews.title: Pretty good
reviews.content: The big red bridge at the Hoan Kiem Lake. Makes for a gorgeous photo opportunity as the vibrant red bridge creates great contrast on the green hues of the lake and it’s surrounds. You can cross the bridge for free but on the other side is the temple which costs 30k dong per person. There is not much to see or learn once over there. No board with information or guides etc, so not a rich experience overall. The rooms were small and quite crowded but still a very special and sacred place. There are great photo opportunities from around the back of the temple which made it worth the visit. The bridge is great, you get a good view of the whole lake, but the temple wasn't really for me.

reviews.author: DAVID L
reviews.title: Turtle Temple
reviews.content: Nice picturesque temple on an island in Hoan Kiem lake, reached by crossing a bright red bridge. Dedicated to the famous turtle in the legend of the lake.

reviews.author: roandknight
reviews.title: Good temple
reviews.content: Temple near Hoan Kiem lake. Ticket the price 30.000VND/ per person.  The red bridge is nice whether it's day.  Hight recommended it

reviews.author: Teamchampions
reviews.title: Not a must see.
reviews.content: If by the lake and you want to follow the crowds, then this is the place to visit, but not essential. It’s more about the red bridge and the view than the temple itself.

reviews.author: J T
reviews.title: Another old temple in a lake
reviews.content: This is called the Temple of the Jade Mountain. The "Welcoming Morning Sunlight" Bridge leads to the temple from the banks of the lake.This is the most visited temple in Hanoi. Luckily when we visited, it's free admission :-) Don't forget to take a look at the legendary turtle :-)

reviews.author: Trumpboyer86
reviews.title: Temple by the Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: Nothing special other than a good view of the lake from the temple. The red bridge is nice whether its day or night time.

reviews.author: TheTopTier
reviews.title: Great Bonsai
reviews.content: Picturesque and some beautiful bonsai in the grounds overlooking the lake.  Lots of activity and a wedding on the day we were there.  The offerings at the alter were amazing and adundant.

reviews.author: R K L
reviews.title: Smack-dab in the middle of everything...
reviews.content: We could understand why Ngoc Son Temple was the most visited temple in Hanoi. It is perfectly situated on an island in the middle of beautiful Hoan Kiem Lake smack-dab in the middle of everything touristic in Hanoi. Unless we went somewhere by taxi, it was virtually impossible not to walk past Ngoc Son or at least have it in sight. It would be hard to miss the bright red footbridge which conneced the island to the shore. At the very least, curiosity would lead one to visit the temple which is why we checked it out. Although fairly small, it was colorful and ornate like most Buddhist temples. The obvious difference was its picturesque setting and was great for a short visit.

reviews.author: Coryy20
reviews.title: @ hoan lake
reviews.content: If you are at Hoan lake then the small temple that is acoss the red  bridge is the Son temple. There is a very minimal fee to have access to this temple. It is more or less on a small separatied islands because of the lake. Be sure to visit when you are at this lake

reviews.author: Penguins15
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Beautiful situation on lake at Hoag Kiem very interesting old temple easy access , you can light offerings - prayers or Incense sticks , beautifully lit up at night

reviews.author: Debbie W
reviews.title: Worth a quick pop in
reviews.content: On the island on the lake over the red bridge. We popped in for 10 minutes wander around Which as it’s so cheap isn’t a big issue. A lovely pergoda and some nice trees in a calm setting.Would recommend that you go at night to see it as well though as is all lit up and looks lovely. Not sure whether you can actually go in then though.

reviews.author: Bhatman
reviews.title: Cool spot for a quick stop
reviews.content: We were staying around the lake so started a walking tour on our own here.Temple is quaint and has some nice views as well as some cool plants.Don't need more than 15-20 minutes to see the whole thing - but its not out of your way either

reviews.author: Julie
reviews.title: Ngoc Son temple
reviews.content: I visited Ngoc Son temple with my friends. Sightseeing is very wonderful, we can see the Hoan Kiem lake, Turtle Tower. Ticket price is cheap, 30.000VND/per person.

reviews.author: Xerxes R
reviews.title: Peaceful and serene
reviews.content: We visited the temple yesterday and were happy with the serenity and history of the temple. As we walked in, there was a ceremony being organised. It looked that a weekend thing as it was Sunday. Ladies were dancing offering prayers to the temple diety. There is an entrance fee of 30thousand dong as well.  Enjoy your visit.

reviews.author: cottagegyrl
reviews.title: Nice views
reviews.content: This is visible at night and quite pretty from the waterfront downtown. We went in for more views of the temple, women take note, you must cover your shoulders. Once inside you get views of Turtle Tower.

reviews.author: Wandering Traveler
reviews.title: Beautiful temple
reviews.content: It's located in Hoàn Kiếm Lake. You have to cross the Huc Bridge to reach it. It's quite and peaceful. Beautiful works of aged materials. They have one if the turtles from the lake stuffed. It's huge and weight over 900 pounds. It's a must see.

reviews.author: moshiyana
reviews.title: Temple within the Hoan Kiem lake
reviews.content: You got to pay 30,000 VND and dress modestly to enter the temple (you can rent somme clothes as cover-up). This place is accessible via the famous red bridge. We didn't enter though as we've seen several free temples in Ha Noi.

reviews.author: Nev Tickner
reviews.title: nice to see
reviews.content: its a nice place to visit ...  and to worship in the pagoda or on the lake.  There is a comprehensive souvenir sop to browse.

reviews.author: heinzhuynh
reviews.title: Not worth going the temple
reviews.content: Agree  with most. You can view the lake from the shore and no need to pay extra entrance to go inside the temple.Not much to see but red color temple

reviews.author: vampslayer01
reviews.title: Bit pricey
reviews.content: Must pay a price to enter and while the temple is really nice it is not really worth it, just look from afar

reviews.author: Laura P
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: Doesn't worth going to that temple. The entrance fee is 30'000 vnd. The view from the bridge is ok but the temple is under construction.

reviews.author: julienx2k2
reviews.title: Under construction, nothing worth to see
reviews.content: Have a look at it from the bridge. Best views are probably by night from the lake shore.We paid 30k per person to take a 5 min walk in a construction site. Not worth it.

reviews.author: Nunngo
reviews.title: Sweet little temple
reviews.content: This is a must see temple over the bridge on Hoan Kiem Lake.  It is a little beauty with so much colour and history.  You can read about the history of the temple, the lake, the turtle and its sword.  Fascinating and ancient folklore worthy of knowing.  There are many locals who pray at the temple so please be respectful of their space.  A beautiful place to visit during the day but an absolute must to see at night, the lighting is truly spectacular.

reviews.author: Jessie T
reviews.title: Near to the lake
reviews.content: A good historical place to visit, nice for photo taking as well. Recommend to visit when sunny day. Stay in Old Quarter by walking distance only.

reviews.author: tanzlcaro
reviews.title: Local sight
reviews.content: Been there and heard that this place is always busy at the weekend. Lots of local people coming here to pray and also tourits coming here to visit

reviews.author: Julie L
reviews.title: Quick stopover
reviews.content: See local pray in this small island in the middle of the Ho Hoan Kiem lake. Entrance fee is 30K Dong. In case you are wearing shorts or spags top don't worry they will provide you a coverup for free.

reviews.author: AlexanderF85
reviews.title: Nice temple by Hoa Kiem Lake
reviews.content: This is a very nice but overcrowded temple at Hoa Kiem lake. The location makes it a nice sight but the many tourists can be a bother

reviews.author: Jane B
reviews.title: Sweet little temple
reviews.content: A lovely temple on a little Hoan Kiem island on Hoan Kiem lake.  You walk over the red bridge to get there, there is a little gift shop where I bought some beautiful book marks for about 18,000 VD (60p) each.  The kids bought turtles with swords to follow the story of the turtle in the lake. The temple itself is small and very like other temples around Vietnam with offering of foods and flowers. Lovely grounds and view over lake too. A peaceful part of a very busy city.  Beware the persistent cyclo drivers!

reviews.author: aadst11
reviews.title: Very nice temple in the old quarter
reviews.content: Even though it was under construction, this is a very nice temple to visit in the old quarter.  Take a stroll around the lake to experience the entire site

reviews.author: JeanS
reviews.title: Nice but too many selfie-tourists.
reviews.content: Visited this temle last week, a friend wanted to enter so i thought, why not... The price was really not high (30.000 VND, 1.32 § pp) but not worth it. Maybe it was bad luck but i had to visit the temple together with way to many selfie-tourists. The whole island was crowded.The temple itself is pretty nice and the island would be too if there wasn't a building lot blocking a lot of space. Oh and by the way, women have to cover their shoulders.If you are into buying plastic souvenirs and smelling hundred people sweating then go for it. If not a look from the coast of the lake is maybe enough.

reviews.author: minimize940314
reviews.title: Small but important
reviews.content: This is the place that explains the origin of the name of hoan kiem lake. If you love story, visit the temple. It is really easy. Find the red bridge, pay the ticket, get inside, read the description, enjoy the view, take some pictures, done!

reviews.author: Mike P
reviews.title: A pretty temple at the lake.
reviews.content: We popped here to explore on our first day. We paid about a pound to get onto the island and it is very pretty. Worth popping into for a quick stop but not going to blow you away

reviews.author: apatasaurus
reviews.title: Perfect Photo Opportunity
reviews.content: We got some great photos taken from the red bridge over to the temple and at the temple itself overlooking the lake.  The temple was very interesting and everyone on the staff was very pleasant.  The shop was good to have a browse in.  The entry fee was very cheap.

reviews.author: MHeredia
reviews.title: Go at Night!!!
reviews.content: This beautiful temple on Hoi Kiem Lake is best seen at night. Take a  walk all around the lake and when you arrive at the temple entrance you will walk across a bridge and we got in for free. In the evening there are no guards and it is well lit. Great picture opportunities as well.

reviews.author: MsMK
reviews.title: If you go and you are a woman, don't wear shorts!
reviews.content: We were denied entrance because we were wearing shorts. We needed to rent a long cover to enter. I completely respect the traditions of the temple, but they should have a sign letting people know. Also, it was PACKED. We asked for a refund and then went for coffee at The Note Cafe. Which had AMAZING coffee! :)

reviews.author: Paul T
reviews.title: ANCIENT VIETNAM
reviews.content: Ancient Temple of Chinese-Vietnamese origin located close-by the Lake. Unique photo opportunities abound.

reviews.author: Angela W
reviews.title: Peaceful
reviews.content: Went because it was one of those things you have to do. You pay a small entry fee. There are light coats available to cover yourself with if needed for free. You walk over a beautiful red bridge. The temple is small and not much different to other temples inside. There is a beautiful small open area overlooking the lake and a gift shop. If you miss it on your visit then no big deal

reviews.author: QuinnyGG
reviews.title: Peaceful and calm
reviews.content: Early morning visit. We were glad to have a helpful guide who explained the significance of the Buddhas and other figures. Pretty view over the lake

reviews.author: Brayan M
reviews.title: great to visit
reviews.content: - Walk through The Huc bridge then get inside the temple. The Huc is a small, historic bridge with impressive red colour.- Ngoc Son is a sacred religious and historical site, for paying homage to Tran Hung Dao (a hero in Tran dynasty) and some gods. In addition, a big turtle template is displayed. (Hoan Kiem lake is famous for hundred-year turtle)- It's educational to learn more about Hanoi history and culture.- I'm Hanoian =))

reviews.author: Keith S
reviews.title: Small temple in the lake
reviews.content: Accessed via the red bridge- surrounded by beautiful bonsai trees and full size banyan trees. Quite crowded when we went, but still had some quieter areas on the other side of the island from the entrance. One small annoyance- when we got to the entrance of the red bridge, it seemed clear that you needed to buy tickets (although most people walked right past), but when we asked - we were told to buy them at the temple entrance. We got to the temple entrance and we're told to go back and buy tickets! We didn't seem to be the only ones who were given the same advise!

reviews.author: SidneyFace
reviews.title: Interesting to walk around
reviews.content: This is a well visited location on the lake in Hanoi.  Admission is pretty cheap and the interior of the temple inside is quite extraordinary.

reviews.author: Sue S
reviews.title: Small temple and grounds
reviews.content: The temple is on a small island accessed via a bridge on the Hoan Kiem lake. Small charge to view. Interesting place with bonsai trees and small gardens.

reviews.author: thd007
reviews.title: average and you have to pay to go in
reviews.content: small average temple and you have to pay to go in, not much on display to see really. can be missed.

reviews.author: yasirriraz
reviews.title: just an ordinary temple
reviews.content: this place attracts a lots of tourist, probably because this is the only temple in the city.has a bit of histroy arond it and besides that, there is nothing to see there.

reviews.author: grampsxpress
reviews.title: very old temple/pagoda
reviews.content: built around 1054? still used by the monks, very popular with the locals. many pay respects by offering joss sticks/incense etc. i found the aroma a bit overpowering, otherwise nice way to spend an hour on the lake

reviews.author: gfwanderlust2017
reviews.title: Good Energy - Good Views
reviews.content: When we walked the bridge and entered the temple there were some men playing a board game on one side. Some woman were walking around with essence sticks, other man were lighting big pots of essence.. The atmosphere was just very nice.. like we stept back in time.The temple itself is very well kept. Even though it is obviously used on a every day basis. There are some paths you can follow to walk around the temple island. And take pictures of the view. The views are amazing..

reviews.author: wlamb123
reviews.title: Okay While Strolling Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: Touristy and smallish, however, interesting in a fashion.  Some of the nearby vendors are worth watching and patronizing.  Expect throngs by mid-morning.

reviews.author: Kelly W
reviews.title: Beautiful temple!
reviews.content: This is a beautiful temple. Highly recommended when you visit Hoan Kiem Lake. There are turtle statues inside for visitors to appreciate.

reviews.author: Carol-Anne E
reviews.title: Temple exemplifies everything the Vietnamese believe in.
reviews.content: Set at the end of a beautiful Lake, this Temple provides peace to the locals, a place to worship and offer fruit/gifts to the gods. On a misty day, the lake seems quite gloomy, locals believe the turtle still lives in the lake. The Temple itself has many artefacts to look at indoors, with picturesque gardens perfectly manicured lawns surround nearby lake. There is a fee to enter, (Not much) close to many shops, cafes, restaurants.

reviews.author: HappySnappyGirls
reviews.title: Busy, but worth a visit
reviews.content: This is a great little temple but it's super busy with locals and tourists. It's VND30,000/adult. There's a lovely breeze on the island so if it's hot and you're flagging, it's worth the walk just to cool down. There's beautiful deities/idols and photography isn't an issue inside. It's fairly commercial with 3 souvenir shops plus a calligraphy artist doing fast calligraphy wall hangings for VND100,000. There's no stairs to speak of but the bridge to the island isn't particularly smooth if mobility is an issue for you. Watch the pesky touts trying to sell you fans, cards, even lonely planet guide books around the entrance. Only buy your entrance ticket at the booth on the bridge....don't buy from one of the guys who try to tell you you need to buy a ticket from them.

reviews.author: Stephane L
reviews.title: A peaceful place on Sword Lake
reviews.content: First place we visited in Hanoi. On a lake there is this old temple you can can visit. Since it is still in use by the locals, you have to respect the prayers and the offerings. But definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: TravelEatXplore
reviews.title: Famous temple over looking the lake
reviews.content: Give it a 3.5 stars. This is a famous temple that over looking the lake. It is well kept. It does get busy with the tourists and locals too.  It is peaceful even though it is busy with cars and scooters. If you want to cross over the bridge you will have to pay. There is 2 prices. One for locals and one for foreigners.

reviews.author: ImaginativeNameHere
reviews.title: Crowded but worth a visit
reviews.content: Lovely small temple on Hoan Kiem lake in Hanoi.  Cheap and pretty so it's well worth a visit but please be respectful.  We saw several Vietnamese people praying at the altar area (I'm sorry I don't know exactly what it's called!) so it's obviously still in use as a religious place and there were a lot of tourists taking their photo and almost leaning over them.  It was obviously disrespectful and the locals were annoyed so when visiting please don't give tourists a bad name and keep your distance from people who are praying/worshipping!

reviews.author: Tiddy W.
reviews.title: Famous temple in the lake
reviews.content: Another famous temple in the lake of restored sword. The other side of red bridge, famous photo spot in Hanoi. Temple isn't that big but not too small. Mainly worship to guan yu for the sake of wealth and business (ask from local people anyway). Full of visitors, yet full of worship from local people to foreigners. Please notice and carefully dress properly, no shorts or skirts above your knees. The stuffed turtle inside which related to the believing story of sword restoration.

reviews.author: ChrissyLew
reviews.title: Small Temple in a prominent position
reviews.content: Hard to avoid the Ngoc Son Temple given its position at the Old Quarter end of Hoan Kiem Lake. It's a pleasant spot to spend half an hour look around and take some photos. There isn't that much space on the 'island' so try to pick a quiet time.

reviews.author: palawanismyhome
reviews.title: Don't miss Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: Nearly all tourists visiting Hanoi wander round Hoan Kiem lake in the center of the city, just south of the Old Quarter and many of them spend an hour or so at the picturesque temple at the NE corner. The temple is situated on a small island called Jade Island and is accessible by crossing a lovely little bridge called the Rising Sun Bridge (Huc Bridge). There is a small entrance charge to visit this famous temple that was constructed nearly 300 years ago to commemorate Tran Hung Dao's 13th century victory over the Yuan Dynasty. Inside one of the rooms you can see a stuffed  turtle which was 250 kgs and said to be 900 years old. In the temple grounds there are lots of shady areas to rest, and also many small ponds with bonsai trees and small carved figures of Vietnamese, their shacks etc. It is also makes for a great photograph when it is dark as the whole area is illuminated.

reviews.author: Ryan G
reviews.title: Worth a few minutes.
reviews.content: A very small temple that you can walk around in a matter of minutes. There was a very small cost for  a ticket and was an interesting shrine to visit as it is in the centre of the lake. Worth a go.

reviews.author: Kris B
reviews.title: If you are walking around the lake and have a few extra dong....
reviews.content: Nothing special but worth a peek if you are already walking around the lake and want some photo ops on the bridge.

reviews.author: Saibhuvi
reviews.title: Nice bridgeview temple during night
reviews.content: Good view of the lake and the temple during night time, need entrance ticket to get into the temple, lot of people in the weekend.

reviews.author: Lynn S
reviews.title: Cycling through the countryside
reviews.content: We had a great trip to this temple and our guide was excellent. After the temple we cycled through the countryside for 11km and then took a river trip to An area known locally as Ha Long on land.

reviews.author: StephenHoang
reviews.title: Walking on evening, beautiful temple with colorful light
reviews.content: This old temple is situated in Hoan Kiem lake near the Old Quarter. The red bridge on the night very beauty but very crowded, hard to take photo without stranger people on your picture.Recommended you should visit this temple around 5pm to 7pm. Less tourist and local people in here

reviews.author: PierreMalmaison
reviews.title: Quaint and popular
reviews.content: A rather quaint little temple accessed over the iconic Cau The Huc Bridge. Rather extravagant decoration but no surprises. Offers nice views down the lake. Heaving with tourists.Open 8:00-18:00 and entrance costs 30,000 VND (15,000 for students).

reviews.author: ber357
reviews.title: Visit in the Evening
reviews.content: During daytime the bridge and temple itself are packed with worshipers and tourists.  It's the same in the evening, but in the evening the place takes on a magical aura.  The walkways are lighted in soft red and the bridge itself is magnificent in the red glow.  Be sure to walk to the north end of Hoan Kiem Lake to view the bridge at night.  If you're there on a weekend, day or evening, the lake area is traffic-free.  You'll find families and children playing and strolling, but mercifully, no motorcycles!

reviews.author: Mercedes C
reviews.title: Lovely budist temple
reviews.content: Also called the jade temple, the lake surrounds Ngoc Son Temple, a pagoda sitting in the centre on a small island. The temple was built in commemoration of the 13th century military leader Tran Hung Dao who was renowned for his bravery in the battle against the Yuan Dynasty.

reviews.author: Nomad_Chris_1975
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Old temple in the middle of Hanoi. Lots of history, a really big, big turtle, some amazing prayer rooms with displays of gold. Quiet and restful. Nice walk around the temple with great views of the city and the temple in the centre of the lake. Amazing display of bonsai on the pagoda overlooking the lake. Small fee to enter the temple.

reviews.author: owlesey
reviews.title: Nice for photos
reviews.content: The temple itself is nothing amazing but the 30vnd entry few is well worth it to be able to get some lovely photos of the lake and surrounds.

reviews.author: MaHoKu
reviews.title: tempe of the turtle...
reviews.content: model of the last turtle is to been seen there. can be quite crowded and a bit noisy. but nice view over the lake and the bridge.

reviews.author: amlo84
reviews.title: Stunningly pretty
reviews.content: This is one of my favourite places we visited in Hanoi. It's beautiful during the day and stunning at night when all lite up. The legend behind the lake and the reason for the temple itself are both charming and interesting. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: ironian
reviews.title: A smaller temple for a quick visit if you are in the neighbourhood
reviews.content: It’s a small temple in the middle of the lake.  It’s OK if you are walking around the area if you want to pop your head in for a quick look.  There are larger and much nicer temples to see than this one

reviews.author: Denise F
reviews.title: Treasure
reviews.content: What an amazing and spiritual place to visit and explore beautifully kept and maintained . Beautiful piece of history

reviews.author: litseyk
reviews.title: Nice views of the lake if you are walking by.
reviews.content: I was walking around the lake and decided to take a look since I was in the area. It was beautiful inside and had some good photo opportunities. I wouldn't go out of my way to visit this site, but if you happen to be walking by then stop in.

reviews.author: Carlene A
reviews.title: Small but nice
reviews.content: Have to pay for admission. I heard that the spotlights of this temple are golden turtle and the related tale ( I had a local guide). The view of temple from lakeside walkway is so pretty. Worth to take a look.

reviews.author: Ira G
reviews.title: Most visited temple in Hanoi
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is located at the northern shore of Hoan Kiem Lake on Jade Island. hence, the temple is known as the Temple of the Jade Mountain. It was erected in the 18th century to honor a 13th century military leader.

reviews.author: coffeemavenswife
reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.content: This Buddhist temple is interesting to visit, both for its architecture and its decorations.  If you know its background, so much the better.  (We had a guide.)

reviews.author: Mitchelllafrance
reviews.title: Peaceful Oasis
reviews.content: This is a nice oasis in the middle of the city, on the lake.  It is well worth the visit to see the temple, the grounds, pagoda, etc.

reviews.author: Helen K
reviews.title: accessble temple
reviews.content: well worth a visit - beautiful temple with many statues and lots of worshippers - people rub money on statues and then on themselves for prosperity and luck

reviews.author: Dewi R
reviews.title: Good See Through
reviews.content: If you go to Hoan Kiem Lake, you can go through here and spend a few minutes. Unless if you want to pray.

reviews.author: CuriousTraveler007
reviews.title: Fascinating place, but very busy
reviews.content: This temple sits on a small island on the Hoam Kiem Lake in downtown Hanoi. You access it through a very picturesque wooden bridge. The temple is a typical Buddhist temple, we visited right after Tet and it was full of offerings (flowers and food) which made it very colourful.It can get pretty busy, so maybe an early morning visit is better. The price is very reasonable (30K ~ 1.3 USD)

reviews.author: Asia Journey T
reviews.title: Yes, do it
reviews.content: Generally nice place, entrance fee 30.000vnd is a little high. If you can reduce entrance fee for all other tourist attractions, it would be better for tourists and a good way to attract more visitors.

reviews.author: ssvikas
reviews.title: The Bridge is attractive at Night. Can get crowded during the day
reviews.content: Easily the most recognizable landmark in the heart of Hanoi. The bridge across the Hoan Kiem lake to the Ngoc Son Temple looks great at anytime during the day. To visit this place during the day, one would need to buy a ticket for 30,000 VND. Since tickets are checked at the entrance, it means that you can walk the bridge for free. Visited this place different at points in the day. While the daytime visitors can visit the temple and click pictures on the outside and with a lake in the background, I got a chance to visit the place at night and walk through the sparsely crowded bridge

reviews.author: Adam G
reviews.title: Worth a visit, can get busy
reviews.content: Interesting old temple, reached by crossing a beautiful old bridge, good photo opportunities. Can get a bit crowded, but worth an hour of your time. Photos of lake and temple best taken during daytime, but the bridge is lit up at night and looks splendid

reviews.author: QuinnTheInuit
reviews.title: SMALL AND CROWDED — FOR A FEE
reviews.content: If you've ever been to a Buddhist temple, then the only special thing you'll notice about Ngoc Son Temple is that it's more crowded than most temples — and there's an admission charge. Save yourself the fee and admire the temple from the lakeside walkway.

reviews.author: Immerenga
reviews.title: Very busy during tet
reviews.content: Wow, what a crowd there was during the tet holiday. But a spectacle worth your time and money (30k entry fee). The palace itself however is really nothing special. It's neither very old nor particularly beautiful. It actually looks like it could really use some of the money people are burning here for some upkeeping work.

reviews.author: Adam S
reviews.title: Temple on the lake
reviews.content: Presumably you are staying in the old quarter so you have to do a lap of the the lake and go to the temple. There's a funny tortoise thing in there and is very pretty.

reviews.author: Gerard S
reviews.title: Great place to relax
reviews.content: It is probably not a good idea to go there on Sunday afternoon as this Temple attracts a lot of people, but if you choose the right moment this is a divine place to be. The wooden characters inside the Temple are beautiful and the outside is charming with a beautiful view of the lake. An ideal place to relax and stay away from the honking and the crazy driving. If you are spiritual this is perfect for meditation. Nobody will bother you.

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: Interesting but chaotic
reviews.content: We visited on the 1st day of the Tet new Year holiday and it was chaotic.The bridge over the lake to access the Temple was filled with people crossing in both directions.Inside it was pretty much single file pedestrian traffic,making it quite difficult to take reasonable photos.Fortunately because of the day there was no entry fee.

reviews.author: theandrews031
reviews.title: Visit this at night
reviews.content: This is a lovely area on the lake. We visited this at night with all the lights on it made it quite mystical plus there was and singer entertaining with traditional music on a stage. We did visit here on a Friday night.

reviews.author: LucasrkM
reviews.title: Nice place to check out
reviews.content: This temple can sometimes be a bit full of tourist, however you should stop by and check it out. The bridge that takes you there is nice, and the temple itself is a little space of quietness and peace in the hectic city of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Fiona B
reviews.title: Photogenic peaceful temple
reviews.content: Peace and quiet and beauty in the middle of Hoan Kiem lake. Great to have in the middle of chaotic busy central Hanoi

reviews.author: FaeMarieS
reviews.title: Just Right
reviews.content: You can appreciate the scenic view of this place better at night when the lights on. There's an entrance fee by the way if u want to go inside the Temple. So most people were only walk until the bridge. The entrance fee is just right.

reviews.author: Thecatsmum4
reviews.title: Nice stop for photographs if you are in the area
reviews.content: Photogenic place by the Hoan Kiem Lake to stop if you are in the area, it was very busy though as everyone seems to be doing the same thing, so don't expect to be the only people there.

reviews.author: faysie2015
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: Came across this temple while walking around Lake Kiem on a Friday night - it cost a little to go in but the history was actually fairly well written. It was quite small but had an interesting and quite large taxidermy turtle with a story about it.

reviews.author: easterntreker
reviews.title: Good for a quick stop
reviews.content: We came upon this while strolling around the lake , it is worth a stop . The temple is small but lovely . The only problem for me is the smoke from the incense,

reviews.author: Kyle L
reviews.title: Great lake scenery from the temple
reviews.content: There's a small entrance fee (can't remember how much). It's a Taoist temple and it's not as big as Confucius and Buddhist temple in Hanoi. The lake view is stunning and windy when I visited

reviews.author: mike_4m30nd
reviews.title: nice place for photograph
reviews.content: there's nothing much, but this site is perfect who travel with expensive camera. simple yet traditional temple with a lot of trees which made it very comfortable for a short break photograp session

reviews.author: Alamgir Farhad
reviews.title: Peacefull temple in the middle of Lake of Restored Sword
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is an interesting temple on an island in Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi. It is right near the famous roundabout, and you need to cross the iconic Red bridge leading to this temple in the middle of the green lake. Entrance fee is 3000 dong per person. This temple truly makes you feel a sense of peace and tranquility from the bustling streets of Hanoi, it's located right near the roundabout within the lake. It's a lovely place to visit religious or not just to get a sense of culture and see a lovely bit of history.

reviews.author: James G
reviews.title: A lovely temple to visit -- surrounded by the lake on three sides.
reviews.content: This temple is primarily interesting because of its location on the lake. However, it also has an 11 level pagoda that is very attractive. All parts of the temple are colorful and interesting.

reviews.author: JLQ
reviews.title: Pretty and relaxing but...
reviews.content: It's located on the lake and gives some lovely views across the area. That being said, you can get similar views from anywhere around the lake - and that's free! The red bridge is also accessible without needing to buy a ticket. There's not much inside other than the main temple itself and I didn't spend more than 15 minutes here after taking some photos and relaxing.

reviews.author: NinoLeeZhongPing
reviews.title: My very firs temple in Hanoi
reviews.content: Ngoc Son temple was the closest to my lodging in Hanoi. This is one temple with so much in store within it and out. Inside you have a lot of pavilions to rest in and ponder your thoughts for the day. The temple proper is very well kept, spend a few time to pray if you can. The temple is awash with things to photograph, it also shows a preserved turtle which heavily populated Hoa Kim Lake.  Outside you will pass through the Morning Sunlight bridge to get to the temple. There are a lot of small shops outside and across the street (don’t get distracted by those). There is another temple across the street which is equally old yet less visited. Both are close to a monument where a lot of people mill around at night.A must see in Hanoi.

reviews.author: ScotlandRosslea
reviews.title: Beautiful Setting.......Quaint Temple
reviews.content: Wonderful setting and location for this Temple.  Accessed by pedestrian bridge (red).  Temple itself is quite simple compared to some other similar Temples in the city.  This Temple is set apart from others purely by its location on the Lake.Visiting at night becomes a completely different location......lighting changes the view completely.Well worth visiting when in this area of the city but it does become very, very busy at times and photo opportunities become 'difficult'.

reviews.author: WendyH678
reviews.title: Peaceful Temple
reviews.content: The temple is on the island in Hoan Kiem Lake so plan your visit combining both sights.  You will hardly miss it since it is the 'entrance' to the bridge. The temple contains the turtle relic, associated with the legend of the lake.

reviews.author: Sander8011
reviews.title: Peacefull temple on island in middle of Lake of Restored Sword
reviews.content: The temple is on the island in Lake of the Restored Sword, plan your visit combining both sights. The temple contains the turtle relic, associated with the legend of the lake.

reviews.author: Wulan_Dewi
reviews.title: Nice at night
reviews.content: We visited Hoan Kiem Lake at night, a location of this Ngoc Son Temple. There a red bridge to go to this temple. Lights at night made the bridge also the temple became beautiful. Nice spots for photography.Quite crowd when we visited there. Many tourists and locals came to explore the lake and surrounding including this temple.If you like photography, try to visit here and capture some beautiful night photo.

reviews.author: Eli O
reviews.title: Place to visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: This place is included into the city tour, so you can participate in (9am-3pm or so) or visit by yourself.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Refuge in the Lake
reviews.content: Ngoc Son means the Temple of the Jade Mountain, and it is one of the most picturesque shrines in Hanoi, sitting as it does on a small island on Hoan Kiem Lake.It is reached by an equally picturesque curved bridge, painted bright red.This temple is dedicated to Tran Hang Dao, a 13th century Vietnamese army hero, and to  Van Xuong  and Nguyen Van Sieu,  Confucian scholars.This is a very small temple, so it doesn't take long to tour around it.   But it is a great place to sit in the gardens surrounding it and contemplate the peaceful setting and the tranquility of the lake.

reviews.author: Gavina G
reviews.title: Such a huge turtle mummy
reviews.content: This temple has a well location which is on Hoan Kiem lake and right opposite to Water puppet theater. We were attracted by the crowded groups took picture in the Red bridge. It was nice to stand there and look around. This temple is also a common one for students come and pray as it related to feudal education. The one we got shock that is the giant turtle mummy which is around 1.5m in length. People said that there are a lot of turtle in the lake which are sometime emerge on the water surface in special events. It is lovely visit.

reviews.author: 957daphneh
reviews.title: Nice temple, but very busy
reviews.content: Great old temple with excellent location; Try visit on a sunday; I was there a sunday and that was really interesting as the road was closed and many vietnamese make lots of activities in the area around the lake and close to the temple. Good insight on what the locals do on a sunday - even if crowded.

reviews.author: jeannightingale
reviews.title: Beautiful setting, fantastic pagoda
reviews.content: We stopped and spent about an hour a the Ngoc Son Temple.  It has a beautiful setting on the lake and a stunning pagoda. It is well worth visiting!

reviews.author: fireysunrise
reviews.title: Quaint little temple
reviews.content: This charming temple is situated in Hoan Kiem lake near the Old Quarter. The red bridge leading to it is very picturesque, but so crowded it was difficult to cross. The temple itself is enjoyable. Definitely worth the small entrance fee.

reviews.author: Patrick H
reviews.title: Worth a detour
reviews.content: This interesting temple situated in the middle of the lake Hoan Kiem can be reached over a red painted bridge.  This is probable the finest Buddhist temple in Hanoi is well preserved and shines in red, gold, yellow and black colours. Some illustrations and decorations refer to the story of the returned sword.

reviews.author: Oldjack
reviews.title: An Interesting Small Temple On Lake Hoan Kiem
reviews.content: There is a small entry fee of VND 30,000 to enter this small Temple  which translates to Temple of Jade Mountain but it is worth it. It sits  on a small peninsula at the top end of Hoan Kiem Lake and is very populat=r with locals.It was built in 1865.

reviews.author: Boschagirl
reviews.title: Small Temple in Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: It is just a small temple. You can reach this temple by walk through red bridge. A myth said there are giant turtle lives in lake. If you can see the turtle, you will have good fortune in life. The temple have a figure of the turtle in big size too.

reviews.author: Ross M
reviews.title: Magic at Night
reviews.content: Beautiful location with very heavy daytime traffic.Night visit is best...its beautifully lighting really lifts it to a different level.Not to be missed!

reviews.author: AyeMyaMyaCho
reviews.title: Temple on Restored Sword Lake
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple was located on Restored Sword Lake. Entrance fee was 30,000VND per person. Nice to take photos on the bridge connected to Temple. Very crowded with many tourists especially in the evening.

reviews.author: Kou X
reviews.title: Spirtual
reviews.content: The temple is another must see in Hanoi. It is lit at night and features a very sacred temple. You must pay to get in but I highly recommend going there, especially at night.

reviews.author: maxscuba
reviews.title: Charming place
reviews.content: A small  temple in the middle of the lake that is well worth a visit to appreciate the views around. A red bridge links it to the land and allows for great photo opportunities, especially at night when it is illuminated by soft lights.Noteworthy the big embalmed turtle inside as well as the big lacquered horses.

reviews.author: angelfish2222
reviews.title: Convenient & pretty temple in centre of hanoi
reviews.content: The Ngoc Son Temple is conveniently situated at the North side of the lake in Hanoi. It's worth a visit if you're in the area as it gives you some lovely views of the lake but is very pretty itself too. You get to it across a picturesque red bridge. You pay for the ticket before you cross the bridge. There is an outdoor area with bonsi-eque trees, and inside the temple is the altars and incense. There is also a large statue of the turtle which supposedly took the sword to the gods in the lake.

reviews.author: Kimberly B
reviews.title: Nice temple on Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: For only VND 30,000 you can visit this temple. First you cross the red bridge and it's nice to walk around on the small island. It's interesting to read about the history and see locals pray. It can be quite crowded. In the evening it's very beautiful to watch the temple and especially the bridge when it's all lighted up.

reviews.author: Paulo R
reviews.title: Peacefull
reviews.content: Amazing view, to Hanói. A little bit peace away from the busy streets meters away. You pay to get in, but honestly its not that much, and the view only, pays it. It close at 18h. Personal experience, go near that hour. 17h or near that. You'll get almost nobody there, they turn the lights on, and its even prettier.

reviews.author: Iulian L
reviews.title: Very nice temple
reviews.content: Very nice temple. The first one I have seen. They don't have any more tourtles alive. The last one died last year. You can enjoy the nice view of the lake. A peaceful place.

reviews.author: The Gypsy Club
reviews.title: Out of a magazine!
reviews.content: The area in general is just lovely! Crossing the red Huc Bridge takes you to this charming little temple in the middle of the lake. Entrance around 30,000VND. Totally worth a visit!

reviews.author: KiwiKerry53
reviews.title: Just cross the Huc Bridge and you are there
reviews.content: Cross the Huc bridge and you are at the temple which is situated on a small island.  On the border of the  old quarter, it is in the high tourist zone.30,000 VND seems to be the typical entry price to the treasures of Hanoi.  The oldest structure in the complex dates back to 1225 although most of what you see was reconstructed in the 19th century.  Very peaceful and relaxing.

reviews.author: TheShis
reviews.title: A nice little temple.
reviews.content: This is a nice temple, located in the middle of a lake on a little islet.A beautiful red bridge leads to the temple.The temple itself is simple and can get very crowded.Try visiting in the late afternoon, when the crowds are already gone.

reviews.author: Nick A
reviews.title: Temple On the Edge Of Beautifull Lake
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple, is Located on the Northern Edge, of the Beautiful Hoan Kiem Lake. This is just a Five Minute Walk, from the Centre of "The Old Quarter", of Hanoi. Entry to the Temple itself, is Over a Very attractive and Visually popular walking bridge.As you Cross the Bridge, Expect to be Harassed by Camera Toting Sales Types, Very Pushy, and almost "In Your Face". These people will insist on taking photos of you and your partner, "For A Price". Unfortunately, they Dont seem to Understand a Polite "No Thanks". If you continue On, and make it into the Temple, You will be asked to Pay a 30,000 VND Entry Fee per person. Not Really All that Much, And the Temple, is an Ancient Tao Structure,that is perched literally, on the very edge of the Beautifull Hoan Kiem Lake. Worth a Look See.

reviews.author: JanneJ_83
reviews.title: After other temples..
reviews.content: After seeing other temples in Hanoi, we weren't that impressed with this one. Lots of ppl praying here and plenty of tourists. The location (island & bridge) are beautiful though.

reviews.author: Santiago T
reviews.title: Nice Temple!
reviews.content: Temple is on a small Island on the Hoan Kiem Lake. Peaceful area and favourite place for old men playing chess!!!

reviews.author: Łukasz S
reviews.title: Very nice temple
reviews.content: You should go there after dusk - the temple is lightened and full light and shadows. It's very romantic...

reviews.author: colin h
reviews.title: A small temple
reviews.content: A small temple which is cheap to visit. It is very well kept and seems to attract a lot of visitors from around the world. If you have an hour to kill this is the place to visit. Ity gives you a insight to the religion of the region. Not the most inpressive but one of the most traditional.

reviews.author: DelanA82
reviews.title: Taoist Temple
reviews.content: The Temple of the Jade Mountain is built on an islet. It is a Chinese style Taoist Temple that was dedicated to Tran Hang Dao.You enter via a series fo 3 gates and then cross a red wooden bridge which represents the Rising Sun.The preserved body of a giant soft backed turtle is also there.

reviews.author: Asimofee
reviews.title: An ancient temple with a commercial twist
reviews.content: While the gateways, wooden bridge and the temple itself give nostalgic references to ancient Taosim worshipping practices, a shop is set set up within the temple building to sell tourist souvenirs. Toilets are free and clean, but the ticket to enter the temple proper costs VND 60,000 per person.Overall, an interesting destination when you are very free, but perhaps not a must-stop destination.

reviews.author: jeff1955malaysia
reviews.title: nice small temple
reviews.content: it is located inside the Hoan Kian lake. you need to cross the Red bridge to get to the temple. a very small temple but an unusual temple. it is popular with the locals. you will find a lot of touts at the entrance.

reviews.author: Joy C
reviews.title: interesting place
