reviews.content: we really enjoyed this temple it was a bit different to the usual as we were a bit 'templed out' by now, would recommend this one and go back

reviews.author: Paul C
reviews.title: Great introduction to Hanoi and Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: Lots to see and the area has little bridges and more to explore around the Temple. Inside is very interesting and very popular with locals. Always lots occurring, and the temple is very ornate. The views inside are stunning  but it is a small temple. The problem is that there is so many temples in Hanoi that it can be a case of been there done that and oh no not another temple. Spend some here as it has history, position and stunning views across the lake.

reviews.author: Komator
reviews.title: Interesting temple
reviews.content: Interesting temple in the Hoàn Kiếm. The temple itself it's not a killer one, it's quite small. But the views of the lake and the tranquility you have there make this visit worth

reviews.author: Radu P
reviews.title: Nice view, disappointing temple
reviews.content: Small temple located on a little island on the Hoan Kiem Lake, in the very centre of the old town in Hanoi. To reach the temple one has to cross a nice and very photogenic red wooden bridge.The entry fee is really symbolic but in accordance with what the temple can offer: nothing really interesting, except the nice view of the lake and the red bridge. The temple is kind of disappointing although if not crowded could ne a nice and quiet place to meditate and admire the view for a short time.

reviews.author: minhanhvvv66
reviews.title: ''Very amazing''
reviews.content: Though this place isn't very clean, it is in the central of Hanoi. Inside, you can look closely at Hoan Kiem Lake or pray. You can also see a model of the Turtle and the story of it. However, a few months ago, the turtle died. It had lived for a long long time so it is very old now. This attraction is the best one for new visitors!

reviews.author: Richard E
reviews.title: Get in line...Great for your EGO
reviews.content: Very beautiful, very photogenic, very  crowed.,Being tall, Blonde and AMERICAN I had my picture taken with more people than I can count in weeks......bigger attraction than the atttraction

reviews.author: Emma C
reviews.title: Nice location, but nothing to write home about
reviews.content: You get here by crossing the red bridge at the top end of the lake. It's on an island. To be frank, the only thing it really has going for it in my mind, is its location. The temple itself is a bit blah.

reviews.author: Tom R
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: This temple looked very interesting but after paying a small entrance fee it proved to be very disappointing. The best part of this temple is the bridge to access it! The actual temple is very disappointing with shops being the biggest part - really not worth going over for. The actual temple is very small with no guidance about anything. There is a large garbage area -  including a broken toilet, which blights the view somewhat. This temple is not impressive at all and if you have visited any others I would suggest giving this a miss.

reviews.author: 健太 伊
reviews.title: ハノイで一番有名な寺院
reviews.content: 13世紀にホアンキエム湖のゴックソン島で創建された寺院。18世紀に再建された。Ngoc Son TempleIn century 13,The temple was built in Ngoc Son Island.In century 18,It was built again.玉山祠在13世紀，該廟始建於玉山島。在18世紀，它再次被建造。玉山祠在13世纪，该庙始建于玉山岛。在18世纪，它再次被建造。Ngoc Son TempleSa siglo 13, Ang templo ay itinayo sa Ngoc Son Island.Sa siglo 18, Ito ay binuo muli.ວັດ Ngoc Sonໃນ ສະຕະວັດທີ 13 , ໃນພຣະວິຫານ ໄດ້ຖືກສ້າງຂຶ້ນ ໃນ Ngoc Island Son .ໃນ ສະຕະວັດທີ 18 , ໄດ້ມີການສ້າງ ອີກເທື່ອຫນຶ່ງ .　右に龍、左に虎の絵を配した門がある。ここでは昔、科挙(官吏登用試験)合格者たちの名を貼り出していた。虎も龍も、長くこもって勉強してきた人たちが「今まさに科挙に合格して世の中に出て活躍する」という、儒教の考えを示している。Right to the dragon , there is a tiger picture of a gate to the left . Here was a long time ago , I put up the name of the civil service examination (officials appointed test)who passed us . Tiger also dragon also , that long muffled person who has been studying the " be active out in the world to pass on now just imperial examination " , shows the Confucian thought.右龍，還有一個大門左側的老虎照片。這裡有一個很久以前，我就忍了誰通過科舉制度(官員任命的測試)的名稱。虎龍也還那麼長悶悶的人誰一直在研究“被激活了在世界傳遞現在只是科舉” ，顯示了儒家思想。右龙，还有一个大门左侧的老虎照片。这里有一个很久以前，我就忍了谁通过科举制度(官员任命的测试)的名称。虎龙也还那么长闷闷的人谁一直在研究“被激活了在世界传递现在只是科举” ，显示了儒家思想。Karapatan sa ang dragon , mayroong isang tigre larawan ng isang gate sa kaliwa. Narito ay isang mahabang oras nakaraan , ko bang ilagay up ang pangalan ng civil service examination ( opisyal itinalaga test) na nakapasa sa amin. Tiger din dragon din kita, na ang haba muffled tao na ay pag-aaral ng " maging aktibo out sa mundo upang pumasa sa ngayon lamang imperial examination ", ay nagpapakita ng mga Confucian -iisip.ສິດທິໃນການ ມັງກອນ, ມີຮູບພາບ tiger ຂອງ ປະຕູຮົ້ວກັບ ເບື້ອງຊ້າຍເປັນໄດ້ . ທີ່ນີ້ແມ່ນ ການໃຊ້ເວລາ ຍາວກ່ອນຫນ້ານີ້ , ຂ້າພະເຈົ້າ ເອົາໃຈໃສ່ເຖິງ ຊື່ ຂອງການກວດກາ ການບໍລິການ ພົນລະເຮືອນ ( ການແຕ່ງຕັ້ງ ການທົດສອບ ) ຜູ້ທີ່ຜ່ານການ ພວກເຮົາ. Tiger ຍັງ ມັງກອນ ຍັງ , ໃຫ້ບຸກຄົນທີ່ muffled ຍາວ ຜູ້ທີ່ໄດ້ຮັບ ການສຶກສາ " ມີການເຄື່ອນໄຫວ ອອກໄປໃນໂລກ ທີ່ຈະຜ່ານໃນ ປັດຈຸບັນ ພຽງແຕ່ ການກວດສອບ imperial " , ສະແດງໃຫ້ເຫັນ ຄວາມຄິດ ຂົງຈື້ .

reviews.author: Caliope T
reviews.title: A walk in the park
reviews.content: We did this as part of our private tour, so I'm not sure how much the entrance fee was. Though, guessing from the price of other places in Hanoi, it must have been about $2-3US.It was nice to slowly walk around the place, with the guide filling us information before we did. It is very scenic and its refreshing to see a temple in a different place. It is a very calming place.  We went in the mid-afternoon and it was fairly busy. It is lovely and I recommend you take maybe an hour to visit here!

reviews.author: maivillaruel18
reviews.title: Like the scenery
reviews.content: I like the scenery and the location. You can just stop one afternoon seat in one corner and look at how the temple just seat at the center of the lake.

reviews.author: Kai Ng
reviews.title: Interesting 3.5 stars
reviews.content: It's set on island in middle of hoan kiem lake. It's old and interesting, but it's rather small and not much except tourist shop inside building. Nice bridge and views.

reviews.author: Mirage O
reviews.title: Worth a visit on a quiet day
reviews.content: Visited on a fairly quiet morning before too many visitors arrived, not noticing the ticket booth before the bright red bridge until we got across the bridge and informed by the ticket collector. Entry price is very cheap - 30,000 VND (approx USD1.35) p.p. and certainly good value for money. This historical temple on a small islet in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake is very picturesque with interesting relics of bygone days and the lovely bonzai plants in huge pots outside added to its charm.   .

reviews.author: Cymruchris
reviews.title: A must visit destination if you're in Hanoi
reviews.content: I think the best time to visit is late afternoon/early evening so that you can see the transition of the lake view from day into night. There are lots of details to be seen throughout the temple - some quite unusual pieces. I spent a couple of hours here photographing. It did rain - but there was plenty of shelter.

reviews.author: Karl L
reviews.title: Gorgeous temple
reviews.content: A stunning temple set in the lake in a very busy city.   It is a hop skip and a jump across from the old quarter and well worth visiting.  Make sure you spend some time in the gardens to take in the ambience and don't forget to stroll around the temple and look at the trees and flowers.  Was gorgeous.

reviews.author: The Travelling Piggy
reviews.title: Haven in a busy city!
reviews.content: This temple truly makes you feel a sense of peace and tranquillity from the bustling streets of Hanoi, it's located right near the roundabout within the lake. It's a lovely place to visit religious or not just to get a sense of culture and see a lovely bit of history.

reviews.author: tubefeed
reviews.title: Easy to get to, very interesting and you get to cross the famous red bridge!
reviews.content: This is an interesting temple on an island in Hoan Kiem Lake. It is right near the famous roundabout, and you cross the iconic red bridge to get to it.This is very central and if you are visiting Hanoi it is a 'must do' for your itinerary.

reviews.author: 317yolandam
reviews.title: Beautiful Temple
reviews.content: his beautiful historic temple is a must see for all tourists to Hanoi, whether religious or not. be respectful.

reviews.author: Narasimha Prasad G
reviews.title: Ngos Son - The Great Warrior
reviews.content: Ngoc son is not a God but why Vietnamese built temple for him yes,we must know that he was a Great warrior he defeated Chengizkhan's soldiers two times .Salute to Ngos son and salute to Vietnamese war spirit

reviews.author: maggie19562016
reviews.title: Lovely location on lake
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple situated by the lake in Hanoi,very peaceful area away from the hustle and bustle of city.

reviews.author: JasonNguyen24
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: there is a very big turtle inside the temple. Good to visit. Temple is located in the center of Hanoi .THanks novntravel.com for great tour

reviews.author: Tony Smith
reviews.title: Nice little Temple
reviews.content: It is nicest in the morning when there is not so many visitors. A good place to make nice photo of Hoan Kiem lake.

reviews.author: Utopia16
reviews.title: Must see place in Hanoi
reviews.content: Lovely little temple on the lake, good value for the entrance fee. Nice history and on day of visit there were not that many people so had good photo opportunity. Recommended as a must see on a visit to Hanoi.

reviews.author: Similtiades
reviews.title: Ticketing disaster and badly maintained
reviews.content: The little island shrine on Hanoi's central lake is obviously a must-see for tourists. We visited first on a late night walk after dinner on the evening of our arrival, and were encapsulated by the views of the building lit up in the dark, and the famous red bridge casting its reflection into the water. It was a little crowded even then, but commanded a very scenic night time view.In the day time, despite the absence of contrasting illumination the shrine is no less enticing. We walked over the bridge... Only to be told by the security guard that we needed to buy tickets at an office at the other end which was not signposted. We got to the front of the queue and bought two student tickets after being told they accepted US Dollars. Then when handing over money she asked only for Dong. Then she changed the amount of Dong. Then she said Dollars were fine; then she gave them back and asked for Dong. Then we had overpaid and she needed to give some back.The ticketing was a nightmare, much to the amusement of a group of Australians behind us, but not to the Asian tourists forming a very long queue by this point. Apparently the woman being the desk ranted about us irritably to the Australians while they were buying their tickets.Finally though, we were inside. The island is rather small, as is the temple. The walkways are nice, the the rear side leaves a lot to be desired in terms of cleanliness. It looks like a centre for fly tipping, and the building is visibly rotting around the back. There is a nice miniature garden by the front entrance, however, and the shrine itself is nice. More on the history of the place would be recommended though, as there was none here. The whole visit took less than an hour, which we didn't think justified the ticket price; especially after coming from the more expensive city of Hong Kong, where the Buddhist temples are all free to enter.

reviews.author: charesthenry
reviews.title: center location
reviews.content: The temple is located on side of Hoan Kiem lake, I went to this place in the evening, so couldn't see anything clearly, but the atmosphere was more cool  while the weather of Hanoi was so hot and sticky

reviews.author: chrisandun
reviews.title: Unique location!
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple can be reached by crossing a red bridge to an island on the lake where the setting is idyllic.  The temple itself, however, is not really much in size or scope and is quite plain, but  it is frequented by many.  You do need to buy a ticket from a booth prior to crossing the bridge and this, in turn, is taken by someone on the other side before you can pass on to the little island proper. Also, you have to run the gauntlet of souvenir sellers hawking their wares. If you can find a shady spot to sit for a few minutes, you can view the other places across the lake.

reviews.author: MartinKaye
reviews.title: Beautiful little place
reviews.content: As you approach the gate to Huc Bridge (the red coloured bridge over the lake to the island where the temple is situated) you will see a rock with a shrine to your left.  You'll probably see a few local people lighting incense and praying by the shrine.  Entrance to the temple is 30,000 Vietnamese Dong.  And as beautiful as the temple and the grounds around it, you probably won't want to stay for too long, unless you want to meditate.  Another plus is that you get a stunning view of Hoàn Kiếm Lake from the island.

reviews.author: K Tan
reviews.title: Poorly maintained
reviews.content: This attraction is located right in the heart of Hanoi, on the lake. With a relatively steep entrance fee, in comparison to other attractions like the Hoa La prison, you would expect this place to be better maintained, but it's not. Most of the "sights" within the temple has no translation from Vietnamese, which makes it very hard to understand what you're looking at.

reviews.author: Greyhound77
reviews.title: 5 minutes only in here
reviews.content: The only thing of interest to us in here was the cast of the giant tortoise. I'm not a real fan of temples it's fair to say, and if you are there are better ones nearby.

reviews.author: Emily D
reviews.title: Worth a quick visit
reviews.content: Ask for the student discount if you have you're ID and it's only 15,000. It's a great tranquil little spot amongst the bustle of the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: travelbonkers44
reviews.title: Nice temple
reviews.content: Entrance is paid which is quite unusual. And furthermore, given the entry fee, it's quite disappointing to see it not very well preserved. Nevertheless it's a pretty temple and it's nice just to sit on the bench and enjoy the views of the lake around.

reviews.author: doctorse7en
reviews.title: Gives good views of the city
reviews.content: Although the temple isn't that much, it offers a great view of the Hoan Kiem Lake and with it the city. It is VND 30000 to get in (not 20000 as advertised elsewhere)

reviews.author: jaybeeFL
reviews.title: Good Photo Op
reviews.content: Picturesque temple at end of Hoa Kiem Lake with red bridge leading across to the island that the temple sits on. Great photo op from lakeside below the temple. The park around the lake is also quite scenic.

reviews.author: KhongLoon
reviews.title: Temple by the Lake
reviews.content: As Hanoi are famous with a lot of lake, the nature landscaping of this lake is awesome. There;s a lot of student went to the temple to pray as it is famous among locals to be blessed and get good exam result, so you might expect some young peoples over there. Night time view was excellent, Hanoi is a destination which you wont't missed to bring along your camera.

reviews.author: atraveller2011189458
reviews.title: Lovely to visit and enjoy the views across the lake
reviews.content: This was the first temple we visited on a full day out walking around Hanoi. We didn't book a 'city' tour, we just took the map our hotel kindly provided and walked from 11am to 6pm around the majority of Hanoi.This temple is worth a visit to, it has a nominal entrance fee and is very peaceful with lovely views across the lake.

reviews.author: Wenhan Y
reviews.title: An good place to see how locals practice their either religious or superstitious worship
reviews.content: I went to this temple simply to see how the locals pray. It was a sunny and hot afternoon, a large number of young people, especially women, presumably visiting Hanoi from the provinces, gathered at the temple to pray. Everyone seemed happy and content. It is apparently a place of assembly and for hanging out. There may not be many such public places in Hanoi for the locals. The design and architecture of the temple reflect traditional southern Chinese style with small Vietnamese alteration.

reviews.author: Sarah Jane M
reviews.title: Taoist Temple
reviews.content: Lovely little Taoist temple. Very relaxing although not much in the way of information. Giant turtle around the back....

reviews.author: Collin578
reviews.title: Quant little temple in the lake
reviews.content: Nice little temple situated on an island in the lake. Accessible by red bridge. Must visit when strolling around the lake

reviews.author: Jenny T
reviews.title: A deep insight into Vietnamese culture
reviews.content: First, I found this temple a very simple place and there is not much to see but after knowing about its culture value, I changed my mind. Every decoration is full of symbolic meaning, for example, a little altar was built up in the past and people needed to stand there and prayed to ask for permission before entering the temple.Highly recommend Hanoi Audio Guide, this app is very useful to understand about the cultural sites.

reviews.author: Adam J
reviews.title: just a temple in a nice location
reviews.content: I paid the VND30,000 to go in. It was okay. I live in Hong Kong where we have a lot of temples and I find them all the same. Tran Quoc Pagoda on West Lake is a bit more interesting and no cover charge.

reviews.author: nir0sh
reviews.title: Heart of Hanoi Old Quarter
reviews.content: This  is the most  attractive place  of Hanoi situated closer to Old quarter. The view from the templ towards the Lake is excellent. I have visited there in a evening and lake and surrounding were beautiful in night time.

reviews.author: Michelle C
reviews.title: Nice Lake view esp at night!
reviews.content: Good thing that the entrance fee is free for kids below 15 yrs old!Nothing much inside except that it's just a small temple and at a huge lake. For a price of VN30K p/adult, you wont visit in there again for second time.

reviews.author: Mai S
reviews.title: Take a Pass on This Attraction
reviews.content: Our family of 5 visited Ngoc Son Temple in May 2016. Honestly, the temple is fairly average. If you happen to be taking a stroll around Hoan Kiem Lake, by all means, snap a photograph by this temple. But architecturally speaking, there isn't much inspiration here.

reviews.author: huonghoagiay764
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: Ngọc Sơn Temple is in the center of Hà Nội on a small island in the middle of Hoàn Kiếm Lake. The lake is also called Hồ Gươm (Sword Lake) and was previously named Lục Thuỷ (Green Water) because its water is always green. In the 15th century, the lake was renamed Hoàn Kiếm (Returned Sword) because of a legend relating to Lê Lợi’s resistance war against Ming invaders.

reviews.author: Robert K
reviews.title: Good pictures
reviews.content: This temple is the one on an island in Hoan Kiem Lake reached by a small picturesque bridge. The temple itself isn't very different from a lot of the other temples in Vietnam but there are a lot of good photo opportunities of the bridge and the lake. It is also interesting to see the locals burning fake money and other offerings there. There is definitely a mix of tourists and real worshippers at the temple. I would recommend paying the modest fee to visit the temple.

reviews.author: Iolanda G
reviews.title: Special place just for local people
reviews.content: It is not a traditional temple, actually it is just an open area in a bridge with some prays written in chinese and a statue in a corner where some local people go to make little prays or wishes. If you are not inside of the culture you dont find it really interesting, if you are nearby it you ca have a look. But don't go until there just to see it.

reviews.author: Stephen M
reviews.title: Another temple...
reviews.content: This was part of the tour but my guide paid for my entrance and abandoned me to go it alone from there - nice location but without a story it was just another temple. Sorry guys and girls.

reviews.author: Frangipani5
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: My husband and I visited Hanoi in March, a nice temple to visit. Can get very busy in  the afternoon. Entry  is only 20,000 Dong for Adults. The red bridge can get crowded as well  with people taking photos. It was nice to walk around Hoan Kiem Lake late in the afternoon.

reviews.author: Jason G
reviews.title: Pretty at night
reviews.content: Even if you don't visit the temple during the day, make sure to at least see the bridge lit up at night. Even in the rain the reflection in the lake is very picturesque, and there are some pretty willow trees around the lake that provide a nice foreground. The street where the night market sets up runs right into the lake so it isn't very difficult to find.

reviews.author: Charlotte N
reviews.title: Interesting temple in the heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: A nice little temple on the lake. You have to pay entry fee (~$1), but I guess they need to maintain the facility. There is a little back yard with benches and nice shades for you to take a break and enjoy the lake view.

reviews.author: Keely J
reviews.title: Interesting but not a must
reviews.content: Interesting story behind the temple however not sure how true this is. Not alot else to see as it is very small. It's in the middle of the lake but I couldn't help feel they could do more with the place. Not worth 30,000 VND for this small temple. Very crowded.

reviews.author: siewkhim
reviews.title: Temple in the middle of the lake
reviews.content: Just another temple at the lake, you get to experience their cultures and see how the temple is like.

reviews.author: Sylvia D
reviews.title: Another Temple
reviews.content: They all look a bit alike but this one did have a top location in the middle of the lake. Shame about the people selling turtles to release into the lake (so they could catch them and sell them to someone else). Seems a bit cruel to have them in little containers with little water in the hot sun.

reviews.author: Karthic
reviews.title: Nice temple in the lake
reviews.content: This temple is in the hon kiem lake . Well preserved . In the evenings the lights are really so beautiful to watch in the temple and around the lake

reviews.author: Sreenaphang S
reviews.title: A sanctuary
reviews.content: A sanctuary There are many people who have shelled giant flow pray in a very large box can stroll around the temple . It is surrounded by cool water . There are trees down to the water, you can take photos .

reviews.author: Sandlab
reviews.title: So much to understand
reviews.content: A short walk from the Old Quarter, along the east side of Hoan Kiem lake, Ngoc Son Temple has recently been designated as a Special National Relic.The lake walk is fairly pleasant and the entrance to the temple, via the red wooden bridge on painted concrete stilts, switches off most of the noise from the road and introduces a much calmer scene. At least it does if there are not too many tourists around.The whole temple is full of symbolism. The approach to the main temple is via three gates. The first gate is marked by the red Chinese characters for happiness and prosperity, the second by a painted dragon and a tiger, the third by a carved inkstand. The gates also reflect feng shui philosphy and a host of other ideas that I only discovered later. To the left of the gates is the 'But Tower' (Quill Pen). Look at the tower then write your name on the blue sky!Sadly, a funeral was taking place in the main temple and we were restricted entry so our visit was curtailed. Perhaps another time...The first impression is of yet another slightly jaded Hanoi temple, but there is a lot to read about here about the temple, the lake and the surrounds, before you go or after you return. This temple is far better researched before the visit. The tour guides don't cover half the story. Many of the poorer guide books are just as bad.

reviews.author: Ngan H
reviews.title: Nothing exceptional
reviews.content: The temple is dedicated to the turtle that once lived in Hoan Kiem Lake. The entrance to the temple is not free. You can see the carcass of the turtle in the temple. The temple is small.

reviews.author: BijanTehran_Iran
reviews.title: Go there at late afternoon
reviews.content: Small but very lovely place.full of tourists and locals.Very near to old quarter,may be the best place to wonder at night.

reviews.author: 720jackson5
reviews.title: Lovely Setting
reviews.content: Nothing special, however it is a good way to see the Hoan Kiem Lake.  Some lovely Bonsai trees in the complex and on approach lots of ladies selling terrapins and fish to throw into the lake for good luck, not to be encouraged.

reviews.author: Rainie Green
reviews.title: Don't miss it!
reviews.content: The bridge is really great with it special red color. I and my friend take a lot of photos with the bridge but not get inside the temple. You can buy a ticket about 2$ and have a look or just wander around and enjoy the view. A must-be-visited place when you travel to Hanoi!

reviews.author: Hannah
reviews.title: Nice view
reviews.content: very cute bridge in the middle of the lake.  well worth the $2? for crossing and taking pics.  They also have a temple after the bridge.

reviews.author: Yekuu Y
reviews.title: Bridge is great
reviews.content: Cross the red bridge on the lake and get to the temple. There is an entrence fee end of the bridge before enter the temple. Take lots of pics also night. Great view on the bridge

reviews.author: mingle888
reviews.title: Views around the lake
reviews.content: Walk around Hoan Kiem Lake and then cross the iconic red Rising Sun bridge to the Temple and find a spot to contemplate. It is a small temple but with beautiful views around the lake and the bonsai trees, worth the small entrance fee

reviews.author: Kenneth
reviews.title: Looks great at night
reviews.content: This is a good place for a short visit during the day if you want to go inside and take a look at the temple, but not really different inside from other temples. At night the lights make it look very nice, can get nice photos.

reviews.author: Ulrikbuchert
reviews.title: Quite nice place...
reviews.content: This is probably one of the most iconic Hanoi tourist attractions. The temple sits on a tiny island in the Hoan Kiem-lake and is accesible via a red wooden bridge. You should stop by if you're in the vicinity and enjoy the 'island' the temple and the views of the lake.

reviews.author: phoibee
reviews.title: must-see
reviews.content: This is a must go to place when you are in Hanoi, Vietnam. You can see Hoan Kiem lake around it. However, this place is full of tourists besides those who really went there to pray.

reviews.author: Trypp Adams
reviews.title: Worth a visit. Picturesque bridge and temple
reviews.content: For $1.35 US you can cross the red bridge and make your way through the Ngoc Son Temple. The massive Bonsai trees here are impressive along with the turtle which reminded me a bit of the Loch ness monster. This is a bit more scenic at night when lit up but worth a visit during the day.

reviews.author: multi v
reviews.title: Lovely temple in the middle of Hoam Kiem Lake
reviews.content: This temple is reached via a bridge - the Sunbeam bridge. There is a small entrance fee and is well worth a visit. It is not far from the old quarter.  A giant turtle that died in the lake in 1968 is preserved in the back Lovely decorations and peaceful in the middle of such a busy city.

reviews.author: Nat S
reviews.title: Very busy around Chinese New Year but a nice place to visit
reviews.content: Visited mainly because I visited the lake so much and could see many Chinese tourists in the area around the New Year. The temple has beautiful views of the lake once you pass the entrance and has a long bridge you can walk over to get there. I imagine when it's not the New Year, the temple is very peaceful.

reviews.author: Onur Akin
reviews.title: Very Interesting Temple
reviews.content: You can easily find the temple it is very near to the town center.  There are different kinds of bonsai trees. İt is one of the must be seen places

reviews.author: Mayur S
reviews.title: In the middle of the lake
reviews.content: The temple is on an island in Hoan Kiem Lake connected by Huc (Rising Sun) Bridge.  Nearby is Martyrs’ Monument for those who died fighting for Vietnam’s independence. Budget half hour to see.

reviews.author: Diane VOC
reviews.title: Lovely Confucian Temple in Hanoi
reviews.content: We happened upon this temple, while walking through the Historic Old Quarter of Hanoi.  The door was open, so we went in.  We were then invited from the courtyard into the temple proper, which was charming, elegant, and mysterious to us.  The local guardians of the temple were friendly, asking only that we leave our shoes at the door.  The space is full of decorations, flowers, statues, and traditional motifs and furniture.  As it was almost empty while we were here, we took some time to sit and enjoy the experience.  We would recommend this to anyone interested in Vietnamese history, religion, or culture.

reviews.author: Valerie W
reviews.title: So beautiful and peaceful inside
reviews.content: Convinced my husband to cross the bridge and see one last temple. So glad we did as it is lovely with a nice calm about it. Great bonsai outside and lovely views over the lake

reviews.author: Milette V
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple, a must-see
reviews.content: With Hoan Kiem Lake less than a 15-minute walk away from our hotel in the Old Quarter, visiting Ngoc Son Temple (or “Temple of the Jade Mountain”) was a given for us. You can’t miss it! Traverse the beautiful crimson bridge in the northern part of the lake that links the shore to the temple which sits on a small island. There were many people, both locals and tourists, who had the same idea. My husband, daughter and I paid VND 30,000 each to enter the temple. We passed through four picturesque gates or archways with interesting carvings of Vietnamese characters and symbols.  The temple had many buildings that featured massive and colorful altars. There was an old male calligraphist inside the main building who could write your preferred wish (for prosperity, luck, success, etc.) in Hán characters. Ngoc Son Temple is a must-see if only for the preserved body of what is said to be a five-century-old giant tortoise in the main temple.

reviews.author: GioSousa
reviews.title: Good for history lovers
reviews.content: Another thing to add to your day tour in Hanoi. Try to go earlier to have time to look around and take good photos before the other tour buses arrive

reviews.author: JuhiZZZ
reviews.title: Beautiful temple on a beautiful lake
reviews.content: Must see place when visiting Hanoi. Peaceful temple in the middle of the hectic city. It is not free, but tickets are cheap so it does not matter.

reviews.author: Brian L
reviews.title: Temple of the People for the People
reviews.content: Badly damaged during the fighting many decades ago, the people of Ha Noi made donations for the temple to be rebuilt in this very old site. The Bodi tree in the centre of the visiting area was donated and planted during the visit by the Indian President and is from the original bodi tree where the Buddha obtained his enlightenment

reviews.author: chiallasiatravel
reviews.title: The Temple that link with the History of the Lake
reviews.content: The Temple is right on the Hoan Kiem Lake, where they show the giant turtle and Tran Hung Dao, a historical hero of Vietnam.  The TEmple is very nice because it is locate on the small islet on the lake that link with the main land by a red wooden bridge call Cau The Huc.  The Temple is very popular to people who live in the Old quarter.

reviews.author: Jegsy
reviews.title: A Hectic Break From the Hectic Pace
reviews.content: Whilst the lake itself is a lovely spot for a fume filled stroll dodging motorcycles on the pavements, this place thrusts you straight back into hectic Hanoi in the most incongruous of settings. It should be peaceful - it's a temple, a temple on a lake no less, right? A place for quiet reflection, to pause for thought, and get lost in silent revery as you gaze across the rippling waters and the trees drifting in the breeze, the incense floating around the religious paraphernalia, making you consider the nature of belief. Instead, you get selfie-sticks galore, the never ending cycle of walking into photos because that's all people do these days, and the inane squawking of tour groups standing five abreast on a tiny bridge leading to a minuscule island that they then shuffle about on disinterestedly taking photos of each other.  I left after five minutes feeling stressed out and irritated.

reviews.author: Paul R
reviews.title: Quiet oasis in middle of lake
reviews.content: The temple is on an island in a lake accessed by an attractive bridge. It's free to walk onto & over the bridge but you need a ticket to enter the island on the other side. The tickets are sold from a booth on the land side of the bridge & cost 30,000 dong (~£1).The temple internally is very ornate (no need to remove shoes). Outside are many large bonsai trees with views across the lakeProbably not worth going out of your way to visit but if you are passing it's worth a 15 min detour

reviews.author: Yori W
reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.content: Small temple in the middle of the lake. you will need to walk across a red bridge to go inside (a beautiful picturesque one). I see a lot of locals come here for spiritual purpose but it’s actually a good place to see the lake from a unique view. Entrance fee at 30.000 (1.5 USD). A small peaceful oasis just in the busy Old.

reviews.author: ufsnook
reviews.title: Uninspiring
reviews.content: Stopped here during my walk around the lake. 30k to get in, and I spent about five minutes inside. Very small, crowded, and without much to see. If you're walking by, I guess it's worth stopping by, but don't go out of your way to get here

reviews.author: Adventureglo61
reviews.title: Worth going to see
reviews.content: It is worth going to see this temple, but it is not outstanding.  I enjoyed taking a few pictures but it does not take long to see it.

reviews.author: Kim R
reviews.title: Great Style
reviews.content: This whole area is old and reflective of the history of Vietnam. It has managed to survive all the wars and communism and still stands today. Well worth a visit

reviews.author: julierayhancock
reviews.title: intertesing place
reviews.content: lots of history here. great photos beware of hawkers... every where!!! best go with a guide. not alot of walking

reviews.author: Andrzej W
reviews.title: Very nice
reviews.content: The temple is not big but it's very nice. If you are lucky you can hear traditional music and see people in traditional clothes. At night the template is lights and looks even more beautiful. The price for a ticket is pretty low.

reviews.author: Bluegrasstravel88
reviews.title: I feel in love with this place
reviews.content: Beautiful and peaceful, and definitely worth a visit if you are near by. A tranquil little spot in the middle of a very busy city! I had a lovely little relaxing sit down looking over the water.

reviews.author: Angela B
reviews.title: Nice Little Temple
reviews.content: Easily accessed by the red bridge, it's a nice quiet place to visit with good views over the lake. It's quite small but worth visiting if you're in the area.

reviews.author: jamesmK3843ZV
reviews.title: Temple on the lake
reviews.content: Nice temple with nice grounds. Has good views across the lake. There is an entrance fee, but it is not much.

reviews.author: Se0ulist
reviews.title: Center of Hanoi
reviews.content: This temple is one of the most beautiful place where you can see the sword lake. It makes you feel that you're in the middle of the lake. Accessed by red bridge which presents amazing views either day time or in the evening.

reviews.author: Chris_DJ_Bear_Acton
reviews.title: Beautiful History in the heart of Hanoi.
reviews.content: When you're standing on Ngoc Son you get a real sense you are standing on history; the love that the Vietnamese feel towards this ancient shrine is palpable, they've not simply restored it, they've maintained it throughout its long life.Many people just wandered across the bridge and didn't go on to the island as there's a small fee (about 75p at the time of writing), but I would say that's a massive mistake; the wonder and beauty you experience walking the landscaped island or gazing on the shrine is certainly worth a quid.

reviews.author: JasonDoz
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: A nice temple sitting on the lake in Hanoi. It's close to the market streets and definitely worth a visit if you have some time.

reviews.author: travelnomadNZ
reviews.title: Temple on a lake - pleasant surprise
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is very unique. It's a small temple that has character. An added bonus is the lake with the turtle. Turtles are looked on with respect by Vietnamese people . It is very peaceful and relaxing.Tip :  recommend you visit on the morning and at sunset , sunscreen, sunhat , water, camera

reviews.author: Martha V
reviews.title: The history of the lake is better than the temple it's self
reviews.content: Small temple, for relaxing and sit at the afternoon it's nice.According to history, the temple was built around the 18th century and is dedicated to a hero named Tran Hung Dau, who had sword from the lake who taken by the turtle (pardon me if i mistake)so there's a turtle, and sword inside the temple

reviews.author: yeunju
reviews.title: Small and quiet
reviews.content: Amongst the business of the Hoan Kiem area full of bustling bodies, this temple was a nice small adventure to see the culture of the Vietnamese tales of their gods/ turtle spirits. It was very interesting since I haven't had a chance to see an actual temple in Vietnam. There were many foreigners, and the entrance price was not expensive. It's a great place to check out if you already plan on visiting Hoan Kiem Lake. It's like an additional plus!

reviews.author: Serena C
reviews.title: Temple on the lake
reviews.content: This is a quiet temple located on the central Hoan Kiem Lake.  You can look for the giant turtle/tortoise here and also see where they burn items of everyday use - made of paper - so that those who have moved to the other side still have their creature comforts!

reviews.author: amoachaim
reviews.title: A temple!
reviews.content: Go, walk around, it's certainly in a beautiful place with beautiful plants and beautiful temple things. Nothing really new except maybe the giant tortoise preserved in memoriam to all the beautiful tortoises that used to live in the lake. Cool place!

reviews.author: Minh Tuan P
reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.content: Take a trip on the aerly morning, at that time there will be less tourists than usuall. You will have your won time there. Providing a nice view to the lake and the turtle tower.

reviews.author: ExNewYorker
reviews.title: Neither old nor unusual
reviews.content: This temple has an attractive location but it is enough to look at it from the outside. The interior has nothing to distinguish it from other temples.

reviews.author: mdns
reviews.title: Worth a visit!
reviews.content: Great looking small temple, access through a small bridget on Hoan Kiem Lake.This temple is not just a tourist attraction, but locals come and do their prayers as well as made their offerings, too. So that's interesting to experience/watch.Unfortunately, there were just no explanations whatsoever in English, so unless you're here with a Tour Guide, it's kinda hard to find out more about the history...

reviews.author: Cassie W
reviews.title: A small oasis amidst the chaos
reviews.content: Hoan Kiem Lake is quite beautiful and over a short bridge is the Ngoc Son Temple.  We paid 30000 dong to enter - kids were free up to 15.There were some amazing bonsai type creations and a huge tortoise that I think was originally from the lake. There were also people worshiping in this temple.It is worth a quick stop if you are walking around the lake.  There were a lot of guys on bikes trying to take tourists places - this was really the only "touristy" spot we came across in Ha Noi.

reviews.author: putneyhouse
reviews.title: Excellent if you catch the music performances.
reviews.content: It is accessed across a small causeway on Hoan Kiem Lake, it is very colourful and offers excellent views over the lake into town. When we visited (mid-morning) there was a group giving renditions of revolutionary songs and music, they were all middle aged to elderly and performed with great vigour and zest, it was both interesting and uplifting. At the end of the show they changed out their costumes, business clothes and presumably went back to work.

reviews.author: LoganOwens
reviews.title: View of lake and Son Temple
reviews.content: We visited a Jade Mountain, it is located on a small island of HoanKiem Lake Vietnamese construct a classical elegant scarlet bridge which is connected to the lake shore. We were enjoyed here very much. The place had good views of the lake. Temple was not that much attractive that i was imagine ... Lake makes them good !

reviews.author: MJL
reviews.title: Great little temple
reviews.content: Located in the middle of the Kiem Lake, this little temple offers a small touch of history and a place of tranquel prayer

reviews.author: Graham S
reviews.title: Beautiful setting on the Lake.
reviews.content: Situated on an island at the northern end of the Hoan Kiem Lake, this temple complex is very interesting and offers some great views across the lake. Visited by locals as well as tourist, there is a small charge to enter across the famous Huc Bridge, which is a very prominent feature with its red paint work. There are plenty of interesting bonsai plants as well as the temple features which gives lots of photo opportunities. I personally liked the new ticket booth which is one of the best I have seen, it goes so well with the features of the area.The Huc Bridge is illuminated at night and is a great sight against the backdrop of the city. Its a beautiful setting on the lake by day or by night. Well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Oscar M
reviews.title: Part of Lake complex
reviews.content: Although historically and culturally significant, this was not an impressive temple even by Vietnam standards.  It deserves to be visited in the context of the lake complex.

reviews.author: Antonis M
reviews.title: Just good
reviews.content: It looked better from the outside. Nothing  really special or religious inside. Just nice view to the lake.

reviews.author: Neil D
reviews.title: Swell worth a visit
reviews.content: As part of any walk in the Old Town / Sword lake area this temple is well worth a visit. Beautiful arching walkway bridge gives access to great views of the lake and this significant old temple.

reviews.author: Dishaa S
reviews.title: ngoc son temple
reviews.content: a landmark on the sword lake, it can be reached through the brideg which looks stunning at night when it is lit up. there is an entry fee to go inside but the view from the bridge makes every penny spent worthwhile.

reviews.author: schmango
reviews.title: Great view of the lake and city
reviews.content: I enjoyed this but again, wouldve loved more information about what its origins were and why? Perhaps some nostalgic photos of its past in use. Very pretty for a non tour visit i left wanting more information

reviews.author: Bev B
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple--Temple of the Jade Mountain
reviews.content: This Temple is a landmark in Hanoi and located in the Hoan Kiem Lake, accesible through a lovely red bridge. The location is scenic and perfect for taking pictures of the Turtle Temple. Lovely architecture and art adorns the temple and beautiful trees with intricate roots stretch into the river.

reviews.author: LucyCarvalho
reviews.title: Not just a pretty setting...
reviews.content: We hesitated to pay 30,000 VD each to visit a religious site but we are glad we did. It was feast day - which happens every 1st and 15th day of the lunar calendar month. The temple was busy with worshipers placing offerings on the altars and burning fake money notes. These notes represent all kinds of material things like furniture, car and actual money that a deceased person/god would need in the afterlife - it is burnt so that it can reach the heavens. The "notes" are specifically made for this purpose by certain members of the community and they have to be burnt in an allocated place just before the entrance to the temple. The religion is a mix between Taoism and Confucianism with a few rituals borrowed from Buddhism. The relics themselves are interesting and the setting of the temple very calming but what really made the visit was to observe the believers practicing their rituals. So time your visit well and you will have an enriching experience.

reviews.author: Matt K
reviews.title: Nice start of the day
reviews.content: You pay a little entrance fee and can walk around the temple. Good place to start the day walking around the Old Quarter

reviews.author: Tasker S
reviews.title: Hanoi city tour and 0$ food tour
reviews.content: We had an amazing day in Hanoi visiting many local places with the Free Hanoi Food Tour. We visited this temple and find that as the most memorable part of our journey and our guide spend 1 hour explaining many things for us.The temple outside came with a special Pen tower, a Chinese Ink container.Entering the temple, there is a wonderful red bridge that we had to cross, Getting into the sight, Our tour guide showed us all the corner of the place with the Chinese God, the Vietnamese king who defeated the Mongolia... The next room to the temple is the giant turtle that also comes along with many other stories of old time.The most special part of the temple is actually the outside with the 4 colums where our guide translated the Chinese poem that describe the beauty of Hanoi. It is also a wonderful place (maybe the best we had) to take some picture of the city center and also the place to feel safe in the noisy city.Our last activity of the day is the 0$ food tour we got for our deal. We got around 10 dishes and then we had to come back home early as we got tired after a long meaningful day in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Oliver R
reviews.title: Nice but not really worth the fee
reviews.content: Ngoc Son temple is located on an island on Hoan Kiem Lake and it's a nice sight. The entrance fee is a little steep given that it's not an exceptional temple and it's actually better observed from afar in my opinion.

reviews.author: renata e
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple visit
reviews.content: It's a short but nice walk around the Ngoc Son Temple. I enjoyed the visit and the photos I was able to take looking out onto the lake.

reviews.author: lukemec674
reviews.title: Lovely example of a temple
reviews.content: Good place to visit to hear all about the faith of the vietnamese people and see a typical temple. Easy access but take a guide to make it a more worthwhile experience.

reviews.author: Sarah J
reviews.title: Good place to visit '
reviews.content: We had choose a local travel agent to book a day trip in Hanoi with this attraction in the trip, firstly we took a cyclo to go around Hoan Kiem Lake then the cyclo driver drop us in front of the temple for an expose this attraction. It has a very big tortoise inside a big glass box, nice panoramic to lake, the temple was small and so crowded when we there but every thing was good for a day trip.!

reviews.author: dhankar66
reviews.title: "Mystic place"
reviews.content: Is a nice place for walking around, nice architecture and it looks amazing on the lake.  You can make a small picnic in front of the temple in the park.

reviews.author: Zarin S
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: Another name for it is the temple on Jade Mountain.  It is Hanoi's most visited temple. Its nice standing on the bridge and letting the breeze go through your hair.  This temple is dedicated to General Tran Hung Dao.

reviews.author: blavine
reviews.title: Go early
reviews.content: We were lucky to arrive before the tourist hoards, so we experienced the peacefulness of the temple and grounds for a while.

reviews.author: Barb F
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: This is a nice little temple on the lake.  It's surrounded by the lake and park setting.  The entire area is a nice, peaceful area to relax.  The entrance fee is 30,000 VND.

reviews.author: Haytham Abu Firas
reviews.title: Cross the lake
reviews.content: Visiting this temple is through a bridge over Hoan Kiem lake. Nice and quite. Many things to hear about especially the golden turtle statue. A good short visit

reviews.author: lauren2592
reviews.title: Good for a quick stop off on wider tour
reviews.content: The temple is undeniably beautiful and well preserved. Once you pay to get onto the Temple, there isn't a huge amount to see but it still offers good views of the lake and space for a seat in the shade in a picturesque setting.Incorporate it in to a bigger day of sightseeing as the city has so much more to offer.

reviews.author: david j
reviews.title: OK to visit as a quick temple visit
reviews.content: We visited this temple late in the day, the temple is nice and was originally next to the lake, but land has been reclaimed around it now. I wasn't blown away but still interesting as a temple.

reviews.author: Colin O
reviews.title: Have a stroll around..
reviews.content: Set right next to West Lake, Hanoi it has great charm. There are of course a great many such Temples/Pagoda all over Vietnam, this one has a charm of it own, on a site dating back many years. Regardless of your religious faith one cannot avoid thinking of the durability of this one.

reviews.author: SaranaeeSaa
reviews.title: Nice temple
reviews.content: Good history, quiet cool and nice temple. Very enjoy to looking inside the temple, good view by the lake.

reviews.author: Yuval H
reviews.title: Short visit, not one of the impressive temples in Hanoi
reviews.content: It's one of the most touristic temples in Hanoi. Being such, I would spend too much time there, just a short visit.

reviews.author: IndianTraveller122
reviews.title: Small Temple
reviews.content: Situated on the Hoan Kiem lake, this is a very small temple, with a beautiful altar and a well preserved turtle. One can have a  good view of the lake from the small bridge connecting to the temple and also from the inside of the temple

reviews.author: ayanamatsuda19
reviews.title: short break visiting
reviews.content: It is situated on the Hoan Kiem Lake and we dropped by when we visited the lake. Wouldn't go out of my way to see the place. There was a small, peaceful area outside the temple, where you can relax and enjoy a nice view of the lake.

reviews.author: Ashley_w1986
reviews.title: Another tourist trap with a make believe story to go with
reviews.content: Felt a bit ripped off when we visited this temple. 30,000 to get in and it's no different to the rest of the temples. Unless you really want to look at a preserved turtle which is part of the mythical lake story. Really don't think tourist should be charged to visit these sort of places. Especially if the money isn't needed to preserve.

reviews.author: Jack E
reviews.title: Seen one, seen them all
reviews.content: We went here as part of an organised general tour. As is the case with most tours in and around Vietnam 'temples' form the greater part of these tours and to be honest, once you see one temple the others all look just the same; gold leaf, plenty of red, dark timber and the such like. However, the grounds were nice to see here but we wouldn't have been too upset if the tour had gone elsewhere.

reviews.author: Erica P
reviews.title: Simply Delightful
reviews.content: The Temple is located on the famous Hoan Kiem Lake and is accessed by crossing the lovely scarlet Rising Sun bridge seen in many photos of Hanoi. The bridge connects Jade Island where the temple is located to the lake shore. The inside of the temple is not as ornate as other temples we visited but the turtle that is preserved and on display is something to see. It is absolutely huge and supposedly weighs 250kg.This is a peaceful place to visit, a place where you can sit under the shade of a tree, and escape the busy streets of Hanoi.

reviews.author: abbottpotter
reviews.title: Beautiful temple in the middle of the lake
reviews.content: The temple opens very early in the morning (7 am) so this is a great  starting point to start your journey in Hanoi. The morning sun shines the temple area beautifully. The red bridge connecting the lake and the temple is also a popular spot for taking pictures.

reviews.author: Sebastienvo
reviews.title: Great view in night but closed and too small
reviews.content: We have a nice walk with mr. Steven Cong - who is really nice and funny. He buy for us a couple of ice creams and donut. Then she come to the front of this temple. It is quite nice and charming in the night time but what a pity for me this place was already closed at the 7pm. We hope to come back it soon.

reviews.author: 246marly
reviews.title: pagoda worth visiting
reviews.content: Drizzly rain so many saleswomen hassling to sell rain covers and umbrella but once past the gates it was interesting to see the work put into building these structures in recognition of past people of worship and the monks

reviews.author: Leonard S
reviews.title: Another view to enjoy Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: A small island in the middle of Hoan Kiem lake, basically the island only consist of a temple and majority of people coming here is to do their spiritual ritual. But actually this is a great place to enjoy the lake from another view, from the middle of it . Also the same ambience here as with the lake, really chill if not even more peaceful here :) Cost 30,000 dong for the entrance fee. Going to this island you will go through the famous red bridge, another plus point!

reviews.author: Gina H
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Worth a visit while in Hanoi. The grounds have a lovely area to sit and watch others or look at the lake. Cost is now 30,000 dong for adults.

reviews.author: Veena M
reviews.title: Meh
reviews.content: It was alright. Was not the ancient temple that we were expecting to see. It is situated on the Hoan Kiem Lake and we dropped by when we visited the lake. Wouldn't go out of my way to see the place. There was a small, peaceful area outside the temple, where you can relax and enjoy a nice view of the lake.

reviews.author: Sale J
reviews.title: Little island
reviews.content: A very little island with a small bridge in the city.vietnamese style and peacful nice place.The opening hours until 5.30pm!!

reviews.author: strafElga
reviews.title: Nice location!
reviews.content: The temple is located in the middle of the Special National Vestige Sword Lake and had a beautiful view on the lake. It was interesting to see local people playing a local traditional game there. You can also enjoy the sunset on the lake from there.

reviews.author: Daniel B
reviews.title: A temple on an island
reviews.content: If you have reached the Hoan Kiem lake, you can't miss the small red bridge leading to a tiny island with a temple on it. There is a nice story about a huge tortoise related to this temple and apparently there are many turtles in the lake surrounding the temple island. We have not seen them but we did see a lot fish jumping out of the water all the time. The temple itself is another nice temple of which we have seen a lot on our trip already. What we enjoyed was watching the locals and tourists of many kind crossing the bridge towards the temple. There was a very nice atmosphere.

reviews.author: vmimartins
reviews.title: Location
reviews.content: The building of the temple is a simple one. As a temple itself, the place does not stand out. The most beautiful and interesting part of this temple is  it location.

reviews.author: Lyndsey B
reviews.title: Worth the small entrance few
reviews.content: This is a beautiful little temple set out on Hoan Kiem lake that requires a walk over the red bridge. There is a small entrance fee but it's worth it to escape the traffic & chaos of the Old Town for a little while.

reviews.author: Vitieddie
reviews.title: Lake temple
reviews.content: Nice peaceful temple that you walk across the red bridge to get to. Have to buy a ticket at the entrance. Looks lovely at night.

reviews.author: WK Liew
reviews.title: Old temple at Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: A small temple at Hoan Kiem Lake.  It's very peaceful inside the temple grounds.  It also provides a great opportunity for photos of the lake.  When we visited, entrance was free

reviews.author: Evgeny P
reviews.title: Nothing inside
reviews.content: We paid an entrance for this temple but there is nothing in there...We expected to see an antic temple and what we discovered there is a touristic shop with some views... Very poor for the main temple of Hanoi...

reviews.author: clairmontjeff
reviews.title: If you have time
reviews.content: Located on Hoan Kiem Lake, this temple offers some good photo opportunities of the lake. There's a legend of a turtle told here so be sure to ask about it.

reviews.author: pcg551
reviews.title: Peaceful walk round the island
reviews.content: A peaceful walk across the bridge onto the island.  There are amazing bonsai trees to see providing an interesting photographic foreground to the lake.

reviews.author: Miec
reviews.title: Beautiful bridge, peaceful setting
reviews.content: This is quite a small temple and doesn't take that long to look around. However the architecture is interesting and it provides a great opportunity for photos of the lake. Definitely worth a quick visit whilst wandering round the lake.

reviews.author: Puppy
reviews.title: History of Hanoi
reviews.content: At the northern end of the lake is Jade Island, where the Temple of the Jade Mountain (Ngoc Son) stands. Erected in the 18th century to honour the 13th-century military leader Tran Hung Dao who distinguished himself in the fight against the Yuan Dynasty, Van Xuong, a scholar, and Nguyen Van Sieu, a Confucian master and famous writer in charge of repairs made to the temple in 1864. It was Tran Hung Dao who invented the spikes in the pit and rotating spikes defences that were used by peasants to initially hold back 3 different Mongol invasions, later the Chinese and American invasions.  The Emperor posthumously bestowed Trần Hưng Đạo the title of "Hưng Đạo Đại Vương" (Great Lord Hưng Đạo). You approach by the wooden red-painted Huc Bridge, meaning Morning Sunlight Bridge.  Small fee to get in  but you get to visit the small museum on Jade Island which holds the second to last large soft-shell turtle, of the species Rafetus leloii in honor of the emperor. At least one has been sighted in the lake.  This individual affectionately known as Cụ Rùa, meaning ‘Great Grandfather Turtle’ enjoys this popular lake almost as much as countless locals and tourists. On June 2, 1967, a Hoàn Kiếm turtle died from injuries caused by an abusive fisherman that was ordered to net the turtle, but instead hit the turtle with a crowbar. The turtle was preserved and placed on display in the temple. That particular specimen weighed 200 kg and measured 1.9m long. Until that time, no one was sure if the species still lived. The species is critically endangered and the number of individuals in the lake is unclear.

reviews.author: Sandra
reviews.title: over red bridge
reviews.content: ok for a short visit pay 30k to go in, quite small but interesting. can go over bridge without paying.

reviews.author: 1Dale1
reviews.title: Good for a look.
reviews.content: This little place is tucked away amongst the tree's good little piece of history. Have a look if your in the area.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Good vantage point and worth a trip
reviews.content: This temple, situated in the lake is a pleasant sojourn as you walk through central Hanoi. It is not particularly impressive when compared to other temples but the interior is beautiful. The entrance price is just 30,000. It is also located opposite the water puppet show theatre. It is worth popping over to buy tickets at the same time.

reviews.author: keykatbryan
reviews.title: Go in if you are walking around the lake
reviews.content: We stopped by one of the mornings we were exploring Hanoi. It was cheap to get it (I can't quite remember but I believe less than $1), and was a really beautiful area to spend around 30 minutes. Make sure to be respectful as many people are praying inside.

reviews.author: Re1nard
reviews.title: A Peaceful Place in the Middle of Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: This place was near to my hotel so I paid a short visit in the evening. The place is peaceful If you are walking around the lake, you may want to stop for a brief visit. Very small temple. Nice lake views. Worth a few photos. Probably are better temples to see around the city but I only had a brief stay in Hanoi. Close to my homestay.

reviews.author: Chris101111
reviews.title: Peaceful
reviews.content: Beautiful temple at the north part of the lake, with it's icon red bridge it make a good stop with the beauty of the green park near it.Great spot for photos.

reviews.author: 198jennyl
reviews.title: A peaceful setting in the heart of the city.
reviews.content: We stopped into the temple to take a few photos of the picturesque red bridge. It was boiling hot and sitting inside the grounds of the temple alongside the lake in the shade was welcome relief. It was here that we learned of the story of the restored sword and so the children enjoyed trying to spot a tortoise from the lake's edge. In all, we were only there for 40 mins or so and that was all the time we needed to spend. The price of entry was cheap. Definitely worth a stop.

reviews.author: Rev-D
reviews.title: Best bridge in the city
reviews.content: I loved this temple. You have to walk around it to understand. The island temple on the lake is a perfect location. Go see, it's worth the visit.

reviews.author: ptyduke
reviews.title: Not Much to See
reviews.content: If you are walking around the lake, you may want to stop for a brief visit. Very small temple. Nice lake views. Worth a few photos. Probably are better temples to see around the city but I only had a brief stay in Hanoi. Close to my homestay.

reviews.author: Lucylou03
reviews.title: Peaceful spot in the hustle and bustle of hanoi
reviews.content: We stumbled across this temple when we were walking around the lake. It is 30000 dong which you pay before you cross over the bridge. It is extremely peaceful there and one should enjoy the surroundings. It is very small but worth the visit when you want to enjoy the peacefulness of the Buddha religion.

reviews.author: Vnvet68
reviews.title: This is a great place to visit and easy access.
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is a great little temple located on Hoan Kiem in the middle of Hanoi's Old Quarter. It is one of the easiest places to find. I must preface this by saying that I love temples and I visit them all. On a recent tour, one of the tourists complained that because he was not a Buddhist, he did not enjoy visiting all the temples. Well....I'm not a Christian, but I thoroughly enjoyed visiting all the cathedrals in Europe and I loved the Vatican, so I guess I'm more well rounded or at least tolerant. Ngoc Son Temple is very small and you can see it in about 20 minutes, but take time to just sit and enjoy the energy. It is a very nice place to do that.

reviews.author: HugoColle
reviews.title: Lovely small temple
reviews.content: Cross the famous red bridge and you will find a small but nice temple here. Alot of statues and art. A place where many locals come to pray and give offerings. A small garden next to the temple and ofcourse a beautiful view over the lake Hoan Kiem. You can hear the story here how the name was given. Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Kyla L
reviews.title: Nothing Special
reviews.content: The temple is in a beautiful location, but I think I enjoyed it more when seen from afar strolling along the lake. The inside is very small, and had nothing of great interest compared to other temples. The entrance fee is quite cheap at 30,000 dong so worth a look if you're in the area perhaps, but not a must see in my opinion.

reviews.author: Menahem S
reviews.title: I love this place
reviews.content: The guide brought us here on the 1st day of Lunar calender month and I found that people came here to pray for their children to pass the exam (????). All explanation written in Chinese but we still understood since the ATT Asia Travel guide knew the history and she told us everything. Ngoc Son Temple is in the middle of the Lake and it gave us a deep feeling about Hanoi!

reviews.author: Stephstraveldiary
reviews.title: The bridge
reviews.content: The red bridge was more exciting for me than the temple. We went there a few days after the Vietnamese New Year, so it was very crowded with locals! I liked the big mural paintings at the entrance....

reviews.author: JafaOL
reviews.title: In the area
reviews.content: I was wandering around the Hoan Kiem Lake so stopped in at the temple too. It's very quaint and there's not a lot to see but it's really inexpensive so I would check it out if you are near by.

reviews.author: johnsobenj
reviews.title: Meh!
reviews.content: We walked by so we thought "why not?" It was inexpensive to get in but not super exciting. People watching was the only drawcard - seeing local Vietnamese tourists posing for photos was quite entertaining. One thing I've noticed in my travel is that the Vietnamese have managed to ruin a lot of cultural heritage with shops/markets. Why does everything have to be turned into a sales pitch?

reviews.author: G C
reviews.title: A lovely place of worship at a historic location
reviews.content: The Ngoc San Temple is located on an island within historic Hoan Kiem Lake, and is reached via its beautiful arched, red traditional Vietnamese bridge.  The building is colorfully adorned (including the "good luck" colors of red and gold) and displays fine examples of classic architecture.  The main interior shrine includes beautiful worship items, all under the serene gaze of Buddha.  A small room off to the side contains an enormous and wizened turtle... There is also a covered pavilion on an elevated platform towards the lake, which offers very nice views of this famous water body.  My favorite time to visit this place is during the morning -- before the large crowds arrive -- so as to savor its tranquil setting... The Ngoc Son Temple is an easy historic site to see when you're in the Old Quarter, and I would highly recommend a visit -- enjoy :)

reviews.author: Joanna S
reviews.title: Beautiful Temple
reviews.content: This little temple was full of beautiful cultural statues and gardens. It has a divine smell of incense. Gorgeous views of the Hoan Kiem Lake and the Old quarter. Highly recommend visiting this temple, and visit the Water Puppet Show at night, which is right across from the lake and it explains the Sword Lake story.

reviews.author: Lindsay T
reviews.title: Nice Temple
reviews.content: Chinese temple, Nice relaxing gardens, good view of the lake, very photographic especially at night.

reviews.author: IamChiChi
reviews.title: Local Hangout
reviews.content: Interesting to see a lot of old people come here to play board games whilst enjoying the breeze coming from the lake. I stayed and watched them play some games.

reviews.author: Daniel A
reviews.title: Location, Location, Location
reviews.content: The only reason we visited here is because of the excellent location. If it were anywhere else, the temple, I would not have visited. However, since it's centrally located we went. I wasn't thoroughly impressed but what else does one do around a lake during the day? I'd go again.

reviews.author: guppygirl21
reviews.title: Nothing too special...
reviews.content: At first I was very impressed by the concept of the temple, given how old it is and the neat story behind it. However, up against the temples and shrines I had seen in Japan and the other ones in Hoi An (further down the coast of Vietnam), Ngoc Son temple isn't that special. It's quite small, and whilst it was only 20,000 VND to visit, you don't really get much for that except a very short walk around the small island, some kumquat trees, bonsai trees and a view of the lake from the middle. I'd still visit again if I went back with different tourists but don't be devastated if you miss it! :)

reviews.author: Ruby Rose
reviews.title: Dive into the local culture
reviews.content: The first place we visited on arrival. A wonderful way to get a feel for Hanoi straight away. We were lucky enough to see a large group of temple devotees, chanting.

reviews.author: Willbooth
reviews.title: Top spot in Hanoi in my opinion
reviews.content: On historic lake Hoan Kiem, or lake of the returned sword, just across the ancient morning sunlight bridge rebuilt in 1864 to the Temple of the General who warded of the attacks of invaders 3 times and who wrote a few famous books on warfare. This temple is unique as it is on a tiny very well maintained island. There is also a preserved tortoise, one of the last few remaining in the world here, indigenous to Vietnam  Probably the most sought attraction in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Aussiegirltravels
reviews.title: Okay.. Nice view of lake
reviews.content: The temple itself is good. I was more fascinated by the view of the lake though... And also the local Vietnamese men playing chinese checkers (I think) outside. It's worth it to see it though. It's spectacularly decorated in reds and golds and provides many good photo opportunities.

reviews.author: Dr_Iris_B
reviews.title: temple on the lake
reviews.content: We walked here as part of our walking tour around the lake. Everything eas so beautifuuly decorated as part of the New Year festivities. Walking in with the guide we got a nice review of the culture, the rituals and the history of the place. Very nice!

reviews.author: FormerCaliBoy
reviews.title: Temple on the lake
reviews.content: Outside of the entrance is a large tower you should view before paying your fee and heading inside.  Cross over the red bridge and enjoy the view as you go.  Enter the second gate and enjoy the island full of hanging roots from trees, bonsai plants and a great view of the entire lake.Inside the red temple there is a Buddha and also a large incased golden turtle.  There are also restrooms on the back side of the building.  A visit is recommended.

reviews.author: Ramie E
reviews.title: Good place to see
reviews.content: It's quite interesting when we walk through The Huc Bridge to set foot on the temple. We can see lots of beautiful sites from here. The most special thing is a real turtle which was stored in the temple about 500 years ago.

reviews.author: Zee S.Puad
reviews.title: The turtle! It's real..
reviews.content: 30,000VND for adult.. Love the temple a lot.. Can see the turtle tower from afar.. The temple also stored the real turtle from the lake.. It amazing to see the part of Hanoi's history.. ^^

reviews.author: Sebastian L
reviews.title: Well....
reviews.content: Not a must go as the temple on the lake offers little except a nice view at night and perhaps a feast by mosquito especially during the summer.

reviews.author: rlavorgna
reviews.title: Small, tourist packed, cheap, uneventful, no great view
reviews.content: This was not worth the $ (which wasnt much) because there's basically nothing there. Better experience is just walking around the lake people watching.

reviews.author: Leo D
reviews.title: A temple floating on Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: The island on which the temple is built is known as Jade Island and is accessible by the iconic Huc Bridge or Rising Sun Bridge which is a charming scarlet-painted wooden bridge of classical Vietnamese design. The pagoda is also guarded by two towering posts decorated with Chinese writing. The lake and temple are probably the most famous places in Hanoi city in which to rest and enjoy the view and are a great place to sit back and watch the locals.The lake and the temple offer plenty of trees and shaded spots in which to escape the busy city streets.

reviews.author: Rich M
reviews.title: If you're in Hanoi - go see it
reviews.content: There are numerous temples in Vietnam - many larger and more ornate that this one.  However, with the red bridge, location on an island in the lake, and very nice grounds, this is very much worth a visit.  Don't expect St. Peter's Basilica, but you will find a quaint, peaceful little temple and if you go in the morning light you can get some great photos.

reviews.author: r00m_with_a_view
reviews.title: Lake Temple
reviews.content: The Ngoc Son Temple is situated in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake - there is a small admission charge.You reach the temple by way of a bright red bridge ( Welcoming the Morning Sunrise Bridge )The temples are named the Ink slab , the Pen Tower, the Pavilion Against Waves and the Moon Pavilion.Worth a visit when in the area.

reviews.author: Insearch0fadventure
reviews.title: Lovely Temple in middle of lake
reviews.content: Very beautiful and worth a visit. Good photo opportunity at lake both at day and night. Can get crowded with couples with romantic or further romantic intentions - or action seekers wanting the same.

reviews.author: Draghignazzo
reviews.title: Nothing much
reviews.content: To be honest its a tiny time with not much to see, besides depending of the time it can be crowded by mosquitoes... you cn easily skip it.

reviews.author: Barbara Y
reviews.title: Nice little temple
reviews.content: I can't resist visiting anything from a previous era and it seemed like I passed this temple several times because of its central location so I had to stop in to see it. This temple built in the 1700s has such a nice location and offers pretty views of the lake that I think it is worth a visit. Don't forget to look for the giant turtle who is supposed to live in the lake!

reviews.author: akonopl
reviews.title: "The lucky pagoda"
reviews.content: The largest and one of the oldest pagodas in Hanoi which is supposed to bring luck according to the locals.

reviews.author: jaci55555
reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.content: Not good compared to rest of Vietnams pagodas. Interesting story. Lights on lake pretty at night. You week walk past it at some point anyway. Full of local tourists on the weekend.

reviews.author: travellinga1000miles
reviews.title: Temple inside the Lake
reviews.content: Its a nice temple if you want to have a trip to a small temple and don't have a lot of time. Its in the famous lake and just next to Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Sunny D
reviews.title: Worth seeing
reviews.content: This temple is located on an island in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake located in the Old Quarter. There's a small fee to go into the temple during the day. At night the temple is lit up and the red bridge to the island looks like it glows. Worth the walk around the lake during the day and night. Very beautiful at night!! It also looks beautiful from many of the rooftop restaurants.

reviews.author: RealHoltyboy
reviews.title: Preferred the Tram Quoc Pagoda/temple on West Lake
reviews.content: A bit underwhelmed with this, yes it is close to the old town so I guess most tourists will see this and the bridge and setting are nice, but too be honest there are far better temples to visit in Hanoi. Not really worth the 20,000 VND entrance fee.

reviews.author: Tom B
reviews.title: Lake temple
reviews.content: Perched on an island in the middle of the lake is the temple. There are wonderful views across the shimmering surface and even a preserved giant turtle.

reviews.author: chitownsam
reviews.title: Worth a quick pop-in if convenient
reviews.content: Nice little temple a short walk on a bridge in to Hoan Kiem Lake.    Can be quite crowded.   20K entry.   Wouldn't make it a special trip but you're sure to be in the area anyways, particularly if seeing the Water Puppet show close by.

reviews.author: NinaTom
reviews.title: Temple on lake.
reviews.content: There's nothing immediately remarkable about this temple, apart from it being slap bang in the middle of a lake slap bang in the middle of Hanoi. It's picturesque enough and the entry fee is small, so why not.

reviews.author: Alexperience
reviews.title: Nice little temple
reviews.content: The temple is nice, nothing extraordinary. Gives you a nice view of Hoan Kiem Lake. In combination with a stroll around the splendid Hoan Kiem Lake definitely worth a visit. On it's own not really impressive but nice enough.

reviews.author: Vandieman111
reviews.title: A lovely temple in the middle of the city
reviews.content: Although only quite small this temple has the advantage of being surrounded by water with fantastic trees along the water's edge. The entry fee is minimal and it is a great place to sit and look out across the water and also watch the workings of the temple.

reviews.author: Teeshau
reviews.title: More of a gift shop than a temple
reviews.content: This site was located in the lake and when I arrived there with my friends we felt a bit underwhelmed. The temple didn't really feel like a significant religious site. It was more a place to buy a souvenir and there was very little information available of the cultural significance of the building. It's still something with that's probably worth seeing because there are some beautiful things in and around it but it's not a must do in terms of highlights of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Simon C
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: A key part of Hanoi’s heritage, this impressive and revered ancient temple sits in the middle of the lake and bears witness to much of the culture and legends of Vietnam.  There are useful informative displays  - in English.  Well worth a visit to understand a little more about the history of Hanoi, which is really two words Han Oi . Don’t be put off by the very nominal entrance fee of £1.

reviews.author: Linhlinh2014
reviews.title: Place to visit right in Hoan Kiem Lake, if lucky, maybe you will see our great grandfather turtle
reviews.content: This brings you a good feeling when you visit any pagoda/temple in Hanoi. It is surrounded with water.

reviews.author: bryan61
reviews.title: Nice temple
reviews.content: We walked around Hoam Kiem Lake and over a small bridge onto the island where the temple is. I guess we were lucky as there weren't huge crowds. We had a look around inside the temple and sat on a bench to people watch. When we went past the following day on a walking tour we couldn't believe how busy it was, but well worth a visit

reviews.author: Mani M
reviews.title: Great location, but crowded
