reviews.content: Set on the Hoam Kiem lake in a stunning location, but over run by tourist.  Not exactly a place to prey or seek peace.  I enjoyed walking around the lake.  Mist hanging around it look stunning. Interesting place to observe local people.

reviews.author: AndrewPreble
reviews.title: Temple proche watter puppet dans vielle ville
reviews.content: A place of historical and cultural significance, situated at Hoan Kiem Lake, this place was not only enlightening but was an elegant place to spectate.

reviews.author: katey28
reviews.title: Looking out over the lake
reviews.content: Stunning views of the lake and if you enjoy taking photos like me, you can get some fantastic shots here. The temple is on an island in the middle of the lake and looks out to the spirit house. Its kind of magical standing in the middle of the lake and watching the world rush past on their motorbikes.  It was cheap to get into (I don't think there should be a price) and a nice peaceful 'home away from home' feel.

reviews.author: lastlyvn
reviews.title: Nothing special except for its location
reviews.content: It's situated on Hoan Kiem Lake.  You need to go across the red bridge on the lake to go to this temple.  This makes it so special.  In Hanoi there are many lakes but none of them has any bridge on it.  This red bridge is the only one ever found on a lake in Hanoi.  However, even this lake is not built to go across the whole lake, it only goes as far as 1/3 of the lake.  Vietnamese likes to keep their lakes intact.  No bridge across the lake.   It's beautiful to take pictures on the bridge.  However, it's also a very popular sight-seeing places.  Therefore it may not be easy to take a good picture.

reviews.author: ElmarieM
reviews.title: Small temple
reviews.content: There is a $1 entrance fee payable when visiting this temple. A red bridge across the water leads to this temple. Some nice photo opportunities. Relaxing and peaceful atmosphere.

reviews.author: Puppy
reviews.title: Very calm
reviews.content: In a frenetic ancient capital mega-city such as Hanoi it is nice to find a lake (Hoan Kiem) with a clam temple at the center. While in Vietnam remember there is no social welfare system so it wont hurt to give a little to the right people, namely those who are trying to help themselves but must deal with a disability such as the amazing blind man playing the flute or the man with no face because of chemical burns who is cleaning shoes or the old lady looking after the young girl with downs syndrome while she sells prayer sheets, all are worthy.  Dont let anyone tell you that you should not give money to people.  Do what you think is right and be Ok with saying 'No' when you dont think you should give.

reviews.author: Raintree_Thailand
reviews.title: Serenity amidst insanity
reviews.content: This is the place to escape (even momentarily) the chaos and crazy fast pace of Hanoi.  The temple is on a small island in Hoan Kiem Lake, accessed via the fabulous wooden Huc bridge.  Peaceful, quiet (when not overrun with tourists), and lovely.  Especially enjoyable in the early morning or late afternoon/evening.  The lighted bridge if wonderful at night.

reviews.author: Jacqueline P
reviews.title: Morning Paradise
reviews.content: This temple is translated as the Jade Mountain, in English. It is located at the heart of the Hanoi Old Quarter. If you're lucky enough, you may find old people doing tai chi near the hoan kiem lake area as early as 5:00 in the morning.. This Ngoc Son Temple is just right at the middle of the Hoan Kiem Lake. There is a bright red bridge (called "Welcoming Morning Sunlight Bridge") connecting the side of of Hoan Kiem Lake and the Ngoc Son Temple.This Ngoc Son Temple is open 7:30 AM til 5:30 PM. The entrance fee is just VND 20,000.I went there and spent more time in taking great pictures before the bridge, at the bridge and right after the bridge (at the temple). Overall, it was a great experience to be at a temple which is located at the middle of a lake.. ^^,

reviews.author: CanisHan
reviews.title: Small temple beside lake
reviews.content: CC ( 2014.08.01 ) The entrance fee was very cheap, so I and my son visited there on passing by. Not bad place, but not many to see. On passing by, it was worth to visit and rest with view of lake. There was some old people enjoying Vietnam's chess. This chess was very similar to Korean's one with a little difference.

reviews.author: wallaceandgromits
reviews.title: Worth a visit at just $1.
reviews.content: The locals were very friendly here and there are a few nice photo opportunities to be had. A nice addition to a walk around the lake.

reviews.author: Vikas Singh
reviews.title: Ancient temple of the 18th century
reviews.content: Near the northern shore of the Hoan Kiem Lake lies Jade Island on which the Temple of the Jade Mountain (Ngoc Son Temple) stands. The temple was erected in the 18th century in honour of the 13th-century military leader Tran Hung Dao who fought heroically against the Yuan Dynasty. Jade Island is connected to the shore by the wooden red-painted The Huc Bridge

reviews.author: Audric_Kam
reviews.title: A Point of Interest
reviews.content: A place of historical and cultural significance, situated at Hoan Kiem Lake, this place was not only enlightening but was an elegant place to spectate.

reviews.author: SteveJacksonnufc
reviews.title: Hanoi - Ngoc Son Temple - Great little temple on Jade Island
reviews.content: I am surprised this place isn't higher on TA rankings. It is a super little temple built in the 19th century on Jade Island which is located within Hoan Kiem Lake. It is accessed via the most beautiful Huc Bridge. All of these combine to create a super attraction just to the south of Hanoi's Old Quarter. Inexpensive to visit the temple is small but detailed and offers some peaceful time away from the hustle and bustle elsewhere. On the island there are many little areas to visit with great gardens and a wonderful small pagoda where locals play board games. The views from the island back across the lake to Hanoi are superb. This is exactly what you want to see in such a city. Something different and in the heart of the action. Then, at night the whole place comes alive once more as it is wonderfully lit up with different colours with the Huc Bridge really standing out in a strong bright red. Go to see this as it is small and doesn't take much time but it is also intricate and beautiful.

reviews.author: Tony W
reviews.title: Great bridge and fantastic views of the lake
reviews.content: While walking around the lake in Ha Noi we came across the Bridge of the Rising Son that lead to this temple. A small inexpensive admittance fee allows you to cross the bridge and enter the temple. Worth the effort for small investment of time but the bridge can be crowded.

reviews.author: Ellemay 🍹🐠🐳
reviews.title: Worth the time to visit.
reviews.content: In the middle of the lake sits Ngoc Son Temple on Jade island. The pretty 14th century temple is dedicated to the Military Leader Tran Hung Dao, who defeated a force of 300,000 troops sent to invade Vietnam by the Mongol Emperor Kublai Khan The red wooden bridge Huc connects the island to the lakeshore. Tickets are purchased at a booth located on the left-hand side before you cross the bridge. The temple opens at 08:00 and closes at 5pm. We loved walking back to our hotel from the Old Quarter via the lake as the breeze was welcoming & there is plenty of trees to escape under from the blistering heat & sun.

reviews.author: Stefan J
reviews.title: Cozy temple
reviews.content: A cozy and quite temple on an island. Beautiful temple with an interesting statue of a turtle. Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Vua T
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: If walking to Hoan Kiem lake, you can go visit the small temple often crowded with people. To see: the Golden TurtleMay 2014

reviews.author: CosmosTravelVietnam
reviews.title: Nice place to walk
reviews.content: When you visit Hanoi capital, Ngoc Son temple awaits for you. Our travelers told that Cosmos Travel Vietnam Co., Ltd did a great job while recommending this site, Hoan Kiem Lake and Water Puppet Show

reviews.author: docfeedback
reviews.title: ok if you have time
reviews.content: Very pleasant location and well worth a stroll to this attraction if your accommodation is nearby.The temple itself is rather small and not tending to show anything different to the many other temples: except for the rather large preserved tirtle

reviews.author: GeciDC
reviews.title: Morning walks
reviews.content: We stayed for a week in Ly Thai To st., 2 minutes away from this temple, the most visited temple in Ha Noi I supposed. Every morning, it is filled by local people. Elderly doing their morning exercise, students practicing their english, etc. Its a small place with such a significance for the people and a nice place to visit and observe the locals too! I enjoyed every morning I walk by this place!

reviews.author: Penelope_Brasil
reviews.title: Nice view from the lake
reviews.content: This little pagoda sits on a small island at the heart at the city with a nice view from the lake. It holds the lake legend of the returned sword and there is a side room containing a glass case with a stuffed giant turtle.One or more large turtles still inhabit the lake. look into its waters, looking for a sight of a giant turtle, as it is considered a sign of good luck to glimpse the head rising above the water

reviews.author: AntarcticBound
reviews.title: Temple on an island
reviews.content: This is a lovely Chinese temple on an island in Hoan Kiem Lake.  It is entered via a footbridge from the pedestrian walkway that circumnavigates the lake on the northern side of the lake.  The temple is dedicated to a general and the patron saint of physicians.  There is the usual shrine, some ceramics and some reading material.  There is also a glass case with a stuffed turtle in it which is supposed be one of two that inhabited the lake.  (The other is still supposed to be in the lake but nobody has seen it recently.)  It is easy to pop into the temple when visiting the area.

reviews.author: Alexander Shalin
reviews.title: Small Temple
reviews.content: Small Chinese temple on the island in the heart of the city. Entering fee is ~$1 only. Anyway you'll be somewhere near, so it's worth to visit it.

reviews.author: FireSpitter
reviews.title: Just another place of worship
reviews.content: Unfortunately most temples around Hanoi does not have a signboard in English to explain it's significance.  Nevertheless, if you are around and always wondered how the locals worship their deities, this would be one of the many places to do so.

reviews.author: Michael4067
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Story goes that there were two very old turtles living in the Hoàn Kiém Lake.  One died and was stuffed and is on display in the temple. Checked out the temple and stuffed turtle, did not see the surviving turtle in the lake.  The legend is that if you see the surviving turtle it will bring good luck! however it may be a case of similar circumstances to the Loch ness monster!Beautiful temple and very nice outlook over the lake.Well worth the $1 US ( approx. entry fee).Closed in the evening.

reviews.author: JohnBlechl
reviews.title: Nice pagoda
reviews.content: Nice little pagoda on the lake. We had to wait a little bit because they were closed for lunch but it was worth the 20 minute wait. If you are in the area, check it out. But you might not want to make a special trip for it.

reviews.author: Christina P
reviews.title: great
reviews.content: this is a very small temple called ngoc son. i don't know why i keep pronounce and try to remember the name. just like it.

reviews.author: Lukas B
reviews.title: Same same, but different
reviews.content: This temple is same as most of the others in Vietnam, but yet different. Maybe there is the atmosphere thanks to the surrounding lake.

reviews.author: Shai S
reviews.title: Quite little place
reviews.content: Quite little place in the heart of Hanoi. The temple it's nice and you can read in English and French about the history of this place.

reviews.author: DMon13
reviews.title: Really Need to Visit
reviews.content: Came here as part of a tour, but my hostel was so close I'd been around the lake several times.  The temple itself is well worth going in to see, especially as it holds the history of the lake and the story of the turtle and sword that Hanoi still holds dear.  On top of which, the view from within the temple onto the lake is well worth it.

reviews.author: Jamie_YuAJ
reviews.title: Great view of Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: This temple can be reached though a footbridge from one side of Hoan Kiem Lake. With a small fee, you can come and visit. One side of the temple is directly facing the lake where you can take a picture of the Tortoise Tower. A foggy late afternoon picture was a perfect time as the temple and the lake looked magical and mystical. Definitely worth an hour of stay in Hanoi.

reviews.author: pierre b
reviews.title: very nice
reviews.content: nice place on the lac, nice gate and many things to see inside, many people there so we could not take many pictures, but the location is good.

reviews.author: Carla_Thiago
reviews.title: Turtles!
reviews.content: You reach the temple by a beautiful red wooden bridge (Huc), over the Hoan Kiem lake. One of the most preserved temples in Hanoi. There, you can fin a giant stuffed turtle, found in the lake in 1968. The legend says that a turtle brought a sword to one of the generals to help him defeat his war opponents, it was then returned to the lake after his success.This temple is dedicated to the war hero Tran Hung Dao(and other spirits), who defeated the mongolians.

reviews.author: Eunice_Lau
reviews.title: Small temple at Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: It is a temple situated at Hoan Kiem Lake with a red bridge. That day i didn't go inside the temple because it is closed at 5pm and the admission fee is 6000 VND. The decoration in front of the temple is beautiful, so just taking photos outside the temple is still nice.

reviews.author: Fredrik N
reviews.title: The temple with the red bridge
reviews.content: According to my guide book (Berlitz Vietnam) this is one of the sites you should visit when in Hanoi. This is a small nice temple that is sitting right on the lake and has a few wall paintings/sculptures that I really liked but the rest is pretty average. The surrounding lake and the red bridge over to the island is whats giving this temple its specificity.

reviews.author: Michelle C
reviews.title: A Little Temple
reviews.content: It seems that every day tour in Vietnam includes a temple (not to mention the ubiquitous bus stop/shop.  It starts to take on the same mind shut down as a trip in Europe's "not another cathedral"This was a little different in that there was no guide herding me through as quickly as possible, nor was it huge and chaotic.  It reminded me of the small chapel in the west that is filled with the presence of past pray and worship.

reviews.author: donmacintyre1954
reviews.title: nice and tranquill
reviews.content: it costs 60 pence to visit and is a small oasis of peace and calm in the middle of the chaotic frenzy of Hanoi.

reviews.author: Smirth A
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: This is a nice temple in the Hanoi. This is nice temple beside Hoankiem lake. It had a lot of the local culture there.

reviews.author: Doron G
reviews.title: Nice but not very interesting
reviews.content: A very small temple. Not much to see and a bit overpriced.Note that you can walk across the red bridge without paying admission to the temple.  So maybe instead of waisting your money just go on the bridge and take your picture with the lake instead.

reviews.author: Jordan C
reviews.title: A small quaint temple on the lake
reviews.content: We stopped by the temple as we were taking a nice stroll around Hoan Kiem Lake. For $2 you can get entrance into the temple, but I find it a little religiously vacuous to pay for something considered holy; it makes it less so (at least for me). If I was to do it again, I would not have paid to go.

reviews.author: Samantha Minnaar
reviews.title: Worth a visit if in the area
reviews.content: This is a pretty temple located in the hoan kiem lake in the old quarter. Not particularly amazing but worth popping in if you are walking around the lake which is very pretty. Some nice photo opportunities too and just under USD2 per person entry.

reviews.author: Mike H
reviews.title: Not worth the admission fee
reviews.content: There's just very little to see. Save your money and go to the Tran Quoc Pagoda instead which is bigger, better and free.

reviews.author: DrNeko
reviews.title: Fine for a short visit
reviews.content: We were curious about that temple so we paid the 20,000 DNG entrance fee to have a closer look at it. Well, there is not much to say about it. It's small but offers a quite relaxing atmosphere in the middle of the loud and chaotic Hanoi.A nice-to-see location, but nothing unforgettable.

reviews.author: jamescheshunt
reviews.title: good for a short visit
reviews.content: Walking around Hoan Kiem Lake and the red Huc Bridge stood out and is quite impressive so decided to walk over it to the temple. It was worth the VND20,000 ( us$1.00 ) just to walk over to see the temple in the lake. It was quite a nice small temple but didn't particulary stand out over others i have seen.

reviews.author: Name N
reviews.title: Ngoc Son temple
reviews.content: I went to there in March 2013. I liked temple's style. It's very ancient and solemn. I'm also impressed with the Huc bridge.

reviews.author: ScottThorley
reviews.title: Beautiful temple but very crowded
reviews.content: Really nice chinese style temple connected by the Huc bridge (red). Gets very crowded around midday so avoid that time. The red bridge seems to be more of an attraction though. Makes very nice photographs.

reviews.author: Jana C
reviews.title: Like all the others
reviews.content: This temple is so similar to all the others. It is quite small and the only difference is that it is connected to dry land by a red bridge. Only visit if you are in the Hoan Kiem Lake area.

reviews.author: Octovianus G
reviews.title: Beautiful Chinese style Temple .......
reviews.content: This beautiful Chinese style Temple located in the Jade Island is really worth to visit. However, be warned that this Temple is also one of the touristic places in Hanoi. Thus, be prepared that the place is very crowded. If you are a Buddist like my sisters-in-law and nieces, then this is your chance to pray also in this Temple. Otherwise, you can try to take some photo's of the beautiful view here .......

reviews.author: Gypsy057
reviews.title: Picturesque Temple
reviews.content: Getting to the temple via the red wooden bridge is a delight in itself. Photo opportunities galore. The gardens of the temple are beautifully laid out with many interest spot tucked away for you to sit and relax and enjoy the vista.The temple itself is amazing and is used by many people for pray and meditation it was great to see the living working temple and not just a tourist sight.Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: podrozniczka60
reviews.title: Jade Island Temple.
reviews.content: Temple of the Jade Mountain (Ngoc Son Temple) is a picturesque 18th century Chinese style temple on Jade Island . Jade Island is connected to the shore by the wooden red-painted The  Morning Sunlight Bridge.The walk to the temple is lovely and the bridge creates a lot of photo opportunities. Very worth visiting.

reviews.author: CHUN C
reviews.title: PEACEFUL &BEAUTIFUL TEMPLE
reviews.content: This temple is located in a small island at the center of the lake. It is quite small but peaceful temple.Although the view of the lake and bridge is very nice and perfect to take the photos but it is difficult since there is a lot of people :(

reviews.author: Wanderingwolfchild
reviews.title: Beautiful temple in a beautiful setting
reviews.content: Escape the hustle and bustle of the city in this peaceful temple. It's situated on the lake so has wonderful views and a serene atmosphere. The shrines are really magnificent with little plaques explaining the history. It was really nice as our introduction to Hanoi. Definitely worth a visit, you can get some great pictures and the classic one on the entrance bridge!

reviews.author: 8Nikki8
reviews.title: Cool little Temple in the Lake
reviews.content: It was quite small but the views of the lake are nice and if you can find a seat amongst the trees it can be quite relaxing. It is a bit crowded, which is in part due to the temple being on a small island. Great little place to stop by before you go wandering around the lake.

reviews.author: RoamingRuss
reviews.title: Can't not really.
reviews.content: Visiting Hanoi and not going to this temple is like going to London and not going to Leicester Square. Per se, the temple doesn't contain much, tends to be crowded and is rather small with better temples and pagodas nearby. Having said that, the bridge to the temple is a great photo shot and the views of the lake are stunning. Also pop back in the evening as it is floodlit and looks gorgeous.

reviews.author: beestows
reviews.title: good but small temple
reviews.content: it is located within hoan kiem lake. for a fee of 15k VND, you can go inside the temple, take pictures and say your prayers. It's hard to take photos of the bridge to the temple, there's a lot of people waiting outside. there's nothing much to see inside but it's a good attraction to visit. Don't forget to be respectful since most local go there to say prayers.

reviews.author: MrBunnsBangkok
reviews.title: Better from the Outside
reviews.content: This temple is beautiful on the lake. Yet, the temple itself is not that impressive. The inside of the temple is the standard for Vietnamese temples. The outside does have a nice bridge though. Essentially, you pay the entrance to hang out on the bridge. I think this place is best enjoyed from afar.

reviews.author: liamskennedy
reviews.title: I came, I saw and still not sure
reviews.content: Maybe its my fault for a lack of research but we went in here and I am no closer to understading what it is. It fine, its cheap.

reviews.author: Tom O
reviews.title: OK
reviews.content: The things to see do not justify the entry price (10,000 Dong for a student), but the Temple is beautiful enough and the embalmed Tortoise is an impressive sight. Only takes about half an hour at most to visit.

reviews.author: npham722
reviews.title: Religious site
reviews.content: Cool place to stop by and see. Shows Chinese influence on Vietnam's past. The mummified tortoise was pretty neat... and if you stand over the bridge, you can see live tortoises swimming in the lake.

reviews.author: AfriqueSoleil
reviews.title: Nice to visit, on Hoan Kiem lake
reviews.content: Nothing special but nice to visit.  Only costs $1, so worth it.  Great place to take pictures.  This temple is very peaceful and provides many offerings....it's a Buddhist temple, therefore nice to see the difference b/w Buddhist and Confucius

reviews.author: Nats13
reviews.title: nothing special
reviews.content: looks better from the other side of the lake, the bridge is nice, I could say that is the best, but the temple hasnt any special thing , you have to pay a ticket to go inside, this is ok, its just 20.000 D, but they should use that money to renovate it

reviews.author: Adnora
reviews.title: A Temple Among Many
reviews.content: I love the temples I have visited in Asia and Indonesia, but this is one of the more photogenic .  The feeling of timelessness is in the atmosphere and this is a kind of time-travle trip for me

reviews.author: fsenada
reviews.title: Elegant red bridge...
reviews.content: Located on the Lake of Hoan Kiem, accessible by this elegant red looking brigde and is a shrine which is dedicated to General Tran Hung Dao, who defeated the Mongols in the 13th century. Ideal spot to take picture of Hoan Kiem district. Admission is just for 20,000VND.

reviews.author: Traveladventures2727
reviews.title: Scenic
reviews.content: I like the vistas of the bridge and temple and also those from the bridge and temple. Lovely place to escape the city mayhem for a little, to sit by the lake, smell the incense and reflect.

reviews.author: sugiphang
reviews.title: a spot at Hoan Kiem Lake
reviews.content: very easy to found this place, yes because very eye catching when you stop at Hoan Kiem Lake. With red bridge and the pagoda. Nice to capture from around the lake.

reviews.author: Vietdragonflytravel
reviews.title: Nice place to visit
reviews.content: This place is located in small island of Hoan Kiem lake, it is easy for you to visit after your water puppet show or before the water puppet show. That is lovely island where you can see the body of tortoise which is very big and very old. See the Vietnamese culture of praying and worship saints.

reviews.author: susanr0se
reviews.title: Meh
reviews.content: Basically, this is just a little outcrop into Hoan Kiem Lake.  It's $1 and you will be done with it in less than an hour.  If you have kids, it might be nice to go over the bridge with them, but honestly I didn't really get the point.

reviews.author: Ronald G
reviews.title: AKA Jade Hill Temple
reviews.content: Small but very old temple that sits on the north corner of Hoam Lake.  It has an interesting history & was dedicated to the God of Literature (Van Xuong).  You'll want to step onto the wooden Sunbeam Bridge.  While in the area take a look at the beautiful white marble sculpture also known as the Martyr's Monument.  It was dedicated to the Vietnamese who died fighting to retain their freedom.

reviews.author: Madtwo
reviews.title: Another Temple
reviews.content: Vibrant and busy yes but you can just get a bit templed out. Dont miss it out talk to your giude understand more about offering. Its interesting but its just another temple

reviews.author: Jensen T
reviews.title: A temple
reviews.content: it is the centre of Hanoi and Vietnam, you can see a lot of intteresting things there, and the surrounding is nice too. Best visited with a tour guide thats knowledgeable about this gem of a place. Take some time to appreciate the history and culture of Hanoi, Vietnam.

reviews.author: OurFamily
reviews.title: Center City, Center Nation
reviews.content: This temple has been at the center of the lake and the nation for near 800 years. It is not the most beautiful, not the largest, but the significance and the view of the lake make it a good stop on your walking tour. Go at dawn to see the real neighborhood people using this public space.

reviews.author: Monika F
reviews.title: One more temple
reviews.content: The interesting part of this temple is probably the conserved turtle. From what we gathered the turtle lived in Hoan Kiem Lake (where the temple is locaded) and died at the age of somewhere around100 years.There are some pretty nice mangrove trees (great photo op) on that temple island.We visited on a Sunday and it was quite busy.The bridge leading over to the temple makes great photo op as well.

reviews.author: Sarah C
reviews.title: Looks like all the others
reviews.content: small little temple with the usual decor and alters. Due to the dense trees, you can't get a good view of the lake from the island. The bridge to get there makes a nice photo.

reviews.author: arborantics
reviews.title: Nice to sit with Bonsai and trees
reviews.content: I enjoyed the opportunity to be outside and away from the street.Sitting amongst the trees and bonsai surrounded by the lake was a nice change.I found the history surrounding this special temple to be interesting and worth the 20vnd entry fee.

reviews.author: Bibsterina
reviews.title: Just a temple in the city
reviews.content: Just a nice temple in the Hoan Kiem district visited by locals on the 1st and 15 day of the month.  'There is a fee to enter this temple but the exterior of the temple is good enough for a photo.

reviews.author: lightupthedarkness
reviews.title: it's a temple
reviews.content: Its an attractive place, quiet and with the usual locals in a an easy to get to location.i watched the guys diving in the lake to fix some pilings on one of the jetties. its not somewhere i would want to go swimming to be fair

reviews.author: Backmansinhanoi
reviews.title: An oasis on the lake
reviews.content: This is a nice getaway when you get tired of the trafic around Hoan Kiem lake and all the hustlers who want´s to take you for a cyclo ride or clean your shoes. To just sit down in the company of old men playing board games and look out over the lake and smell the incense sticks from inside the temple is very nice.

reviews.author: Don L
reviews.title: Great Place for Kids and Families
reviews.content: I made sure to take my kindergarten class here and we had a great conversation about buildings, lakes, turtles....and all the things that kids come up with. I really was hoping to have the Viet kids talk about going to the Temple with their family, which some did.As a heads up, you can walk across the bridge without paying the entrance fee.For best effect, go on a lunar day, either during the new moon, or a full moon. The temple will be packed with people burning in sense and offerings to the ancestors. This is far from the most impressive temple, but it's age, and it's proximity make it a must-see. Keep your eye peeled for the allusive turtle....

reviews.author: toon-of-macktoon
reviews.title: nice oasis in a sea of traffic
reviews.content: This rwmple is built on an island on one of the many lakes in Hanoi.  This is one small temple and a shop.  Interesting story of why the turtle is so common in the city.  Was a nice peaceful place to go and relax after dodging the traffic

reviews.author: My reviews
reviews.title: The cultural sights in Hanoi are so boring!
reviews.content: Is it me or are the cultural sights in Hanoi at all worth looking at?They are neither magnificent nor awe-inspiring. Not worth the walk there

reviews.author: jyansg
reviews.title: nothing great
reviews.content: there's nothing much to see in the temple. the view is great from far away. in the morning, you could see runner taking a breather at the bridge, a group of ladies doing taichi at the gate, local praying to a small tablet placed on top of a stone craving.

reviews.author: terryjose
reviews.title: A nice temple in the heart of the city
reviews.content: If you are in Hanoi, there is no reason why one should not miss this. It does not require a big effort to go to this temple which is walking distance from tourist area of the city where most of the tourists would stay. The red bridge that takes you from banks of the lake to the temple is very impressive and is an ideal location for taking some photos. Inside the temple it is very calm and peaceful area and one can spend some time walking around.

reviews.author: Travworld
reviews.title: Were very good non slip shoes , Algae everywhere very Slippery
reviews.content: Almost all the temples in Vietnam have some slippery green substance on the steps and paths , They have not been introduce to a pressure cleaner yet .be careful

reviews.author: phuonglam
reviews.title: Ngoc Son temple
reviews.content: It’s located right in the heart of the city. There are many people comes there every day. You could see old people playing chess in the afternoon inside the temple. Very nice place to come to visit.

reviews.author: Salma56
reviews.title: A central, significant part of Hanoi's cultural precinct.
reviews.content: Well situated on Lake Ho Hoan Kiem, this in many ways symbolises the Old City and is perhaps the most recognisable of photos of Hanoi. Early mornings it is frequented by those quietly praying and presenting alms, throughout the day it is a stopping point for tourists and in evenings a meeting place for families and friends.  Over four days we found ourselves frequently drawn to this part of the Old Quarter to share the cultural traditions and lifestyle of the people.

reviews.author: Jon C
reviews.title: Neat little temple
reviews.content: Worth the price of admission (only 20,000 dong or $1) located of course in the middle of the beautiful Hoan Kiem lake

reviews.author: Lashley88
reviews.title: Magnificent
reviews.content: Hoan Kiem Lake is really the heart of Hanoi and is where you can see the locals (especially the energetic elderly) hang out. Crossing the quintessential Asian red wooden bridge you reach Ngoc Son Temple. It costs roughly $2 to enter the small island and check your change once you pay. Even though the ticket booth is very official, due to the large currency it is easy to be taken for a ride. Once you through walking in around the temple is a great way to see Vietnamese people practicing their faith and interacting with each other. You are sure to see incense burning, ancestor worship and a local game of checkers. It was a wonderful way for me to learn more about the people, culture and belief. Make sure you have some water with you and spend a bit of time on the temple island interacting with the locals or simply people watching. It also provides a great spot to take some pictures.

reviews.author: VickiLouise
reviews.title: Nice Surrounds For An Ordinary Temple
reviews.content: At 20,000 VND it's an inexpensive sight to visit and although the temple itself is nothing special inside, the view of the lake from the terraced area at the back is worth the entrance fee. Note that you can cross the bridge and take photos without it costing a penny - you buy your ticket at one side of the bridge and show it to the person on the other side as you go into the temple itself, but there were plenty of people on the bridge who didn't want to spend the money but still wanted their holiday pic and this didn't seem to be a problem at all

reviews.author: benzberry
reviews.title: OK ....
reviews.content: The fees kept out the crowd; both locals and cheap tourists.The temple may not be much but it is worth the 20,000VN (USD1) admission for a moment of peace and clean latrines. The is a huge stuffed turtle there (authentic) that was supposedly the last turtle caught in the lake. In 2011, another similar turtle was caught an released in the lake, weighing 200kg.

reviews.author: cerka
reviews.title: Not a neccesary site to see
reviews.content: I think we paid something like 30,000D each to get in so it was nothing expensive. The thing is there is really not much in there to see that we hadn't seen already. There's temples aplenty in Vietnam. The view of the lake is great but you can see that at any other vantage point around Hoan Kiem Lake. It was nice seeing old men huddled around playing Chinese Chess and the big replica 250kg tortoise but that was pretty much it. Nice during sunset and there were so many tourists there.

reviews.author: tamali71
reviews.title: Not much to visit
reviews.content: Like any other temples, i hate the idea to pay for administration fee to access a small place (while many local access with no fee). The only interesting things are the temple locates on the lake and you can enjoy a amazing view to the lake and streets nearby. There is a history hundred years old mummy turtle is displayed inside the temple.

reviews.author: lockyHanoi
reviews.title: MUST DO
reviews.content: it is the centre of Hanoi and Vietnam, you can see a lot of interesting things there, and the surrounding is nice too.

reviews.author: Judie
reviews.title: Worth a visit, small temple
reviews.content: It is a small temple but worth a visit to walk across for a view of the lake.  The temple itself is very small.

reviews.author: czhunty
reviews.title: Packed
reviews.content: Packed with tourists, possibility to buy souvenirs inside of the temple..disgusting, it can't serve as a holy place anymore..Just compare the price.. 20.000d for amazing Hoa Lo prison museum and 20.000d for this 'nothing'..

reviews.author: kgbGeneva
reviews.title: Lovely temple on Hoam Kiem lake
reviews.content: Best visited with a tour guide thats knowledgeable about this gem of a place. Take some time to appreciate the history and culture of Hanoi, Vietnam.

reviews.author: amitchella
reviews.title: A wonder at night
reviews.content: Visiting the Temple was a pure joy.  Just outside is the wood bridge that is a must-see at night.

reviews.author: S. Ali
reviews.title: Turtle Story
reviews.content: Apologies to anyone that finds that observation offensive.Small Temple on an island reached by red bridge on the edge of Hoan Kiem Lake. Admission is 20,000 VND (1 US$), I did not think it's worth a visit unless you have enough time

reviews.author: atwistedwarmembrace
reviews.title: A Peaceful Spot To Escape The Old Town
reviews.content: Ngoc Son Temple is a temple located on a small island in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake. We paid an entrance fee of 20,000 Dong (~1 USD) to cross the bridge and access the temple. The prices seem to fluctuate a bit according to reports and reviews from other people, but 20,000 Dong seems to be the most common price. I believe there was also a student price of 10,000 Dong if you are fortunate enough to be a student.We visited the temple on a weekday in the early afternoon and found the island itself to be uncrowded and peaceful with plenty of shaded seats amongst the trees to escape the relentless midday sun and frenetic atmosphere of the Old Quarter. However, we found the temple to be a fairly unremarkable sight, with the only feature of interest being the embalmed giant tortoise.It is an inexpensive sight at 20,000 Dong, but if you are looking to save a bit of pocket money then you would not be missing out by skipping over this and just taking a stroll around the lake.

reviews.author: Safariholic
reviews.title: Great photo opportunity when not mobbed by Tourists
reviews.content: Apologies to anyone that finds that observation offensive - not intentional.Visit either very early in the morning or late afternoon/evening (pre-Sunset), when the light is at its best. We were there in mid-afternoon and it was a very grey, heat haze, pollution clouded day, which was a shame.Otherwise a pleasant small Temple on an island reached by a bright red 'monkey bridge' (aka the Huc), on the edge of Hoan Kiem Lake. I belive the original commemorates a great battle way back in the 1300s, although there is a strong suspicion that as recently as the 1800s some improvements renovations were carried-outAdmission is 3,000 VND, so roughly 16 US Cents or 10p (GBP Sterling) - a sound investment.Suggestion - visit here, then go straight to the Green Tangerine Restaurant (Booking strongly recommended - see my Review), a few hundred yards away for Aperitifs and Dinner.

reviews.author: Douglas A
reviews.title: I found crush.
reviews.content: Lack of conservation in these momumentos Hanoi. I did not think it's worth a visit unless you have enough time.

reviews.author: 122Puspawati
reviews.title: Nothing to see
reviews.content: included in our tour itinerary we had a chance to visit this Temple, nothing to see just a Temple.But in here is the Beautiful Hoan Kiem Lake with an Old Tree and good for sight seeing.

reviews.author: WarwickshireMonty
reviews.title: Ornate and Peaceful
reviews.content: Just like the temple of literature this temple is a place of quietness in noisy Hanoi. We felt very peaceful here.

reviews.author: Tribs_Tribdino
reviews.title: Crowded but nice
reviews.content: Vietnam seems to be a historical and cultural trip always. Listening to what happened in Ngoc Son tells me a lot about Vietnamese animism and their wonderful culture.

reviews.author: Linda J
reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.content: Go either on the full moon or new moon to watch the locals burn joss money for success in business.

reviews.author: rsindelar
reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.content: Beautiful temple sitting on the lake in Hanoi city centre! For $1 you can walk through and see all the artifacts as well as relax on an island in the lake. The artwork within and surrounding the temple are absolutely beautiful

reviews.author: Shrenik M
reviews.title: Nice Temple
reviews.content: 5 temples in & around Hanoi. All look similar. Nice to visit just 1-2 of them.

reviews.author: Sara J
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Cross the lovely red bridge onto the island to visit this beautiful little temple. There is a small entrance fee, you buy tickets at the kiosk on the left just before crossing the bridge. Once on the island there are several benches you can relax on, and often elderly men playing Chinese Chess.

reviews.author: Rebecca A
reviews.title: Guards theiving from donations
reviews.content: The actual temple doesn't really have much on it compared to other temples in Hanoi, but the stuffed turtle is definitely impressive. The shocking thing was the people working there quite openly stealing from the donations from the shrine- do not donate anything it will only be stolen!

reviews.author: SmurfSingapore
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Known as the Temple of the Jade Mountain, 20,000 dong for entrance fees and 10,000 dong for local students, but was also charged 20,000 dong each for the 2 Hanoi kids even though they tried talking to the ticket person. Was also given 1 less ticket for the 10 of us which I didn't realise till we were requested to show my ticket after crossing the bridge, luckily I was not asked to pay for another ticket. Do count your tickets upon your purchase. The only attraction of this temple to me is the huge turtle which contributes to the Hoan Kiem lake legend and of course the great view of the lake you can observe from the temple which is in the centre of the lake.

reviews.author: Junie14
reviews.title: the temple in Hoan kiem lake
reviews.content: Small temple in Hoan Kiem lake, easy for walk and visit from the hotel. Only 5 minute by walk. after visit the temple and pray. you can relax and walk around Hoan Kiem lake. Nice place

reviews.author: dubbs2012
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: Beautiful temple with embalmed remains of one of the giant tortoises key to the legend of Hoan Kiem Lake. Not too expensive and right on the lake, so you can see two things at once.

reviews.author: MEtraveller
reviews.title: Nice spot on the lake
reviews.content: Costs 20000 VND ($1US) to get on the little island on Hoan Kiem Lake but it has a pretty temple, good views of the lake and you get to see a 250kg lake turtle. Gift shop has some interesting stuff but the shop on the lake shore on them Old Quarter side has more interesting stuff.

reviews.author: AkihiroHirayama
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: I saw it while being taken to our hotel. Since the hotel was very near Hoankiem lake, we took a walk to Ngoc Son temple. But I found it nothing special. It's a small temple, very crowded with tourists. If you visit this place, be aware of pock picker.

reviews.author: Bethhess00
reviews.title: Okay to skip, but if you're looking for something to do, why not?
reviews.content: We got out of the 2pm water puppet show nearby and the sun was out, so we decided to walk out to the temple. The temple itself was nothing too impressive, but we got some  photos on the red bridge and it was nice to people-watch. If you didn't have to pay an entrance fee, I would recommend going there, but because you have to (even though it's only 20,000VND) I think it would be okay to skip and get your photos from the lakeside.

reviews.author: travelbugAmsterdam
reviews.title: Small temple surrounded by a nice scenery
reviews.content: The temple is not very big, but it is set on the lake and is very colourful. Some images of tiger on one of the entry red doors and. Bridge leading to the temple. It is pretty but nothing spectacular.  From  the bridge you grt a very romantic picture with the smaller Tempe in the middle of the lake.

reviews.author: Foodgloriousfood88
reviews.title: Mediocre
reviews.content: Nothing too interesting.the fee is Only vnd20000Might be worth a visit if u have nothing else to do

reviews.author: raph e
reviews.title: Its cheap admission so worth wandering in
reviews.content: at VND20,000 its pretty cheap to enter. Not a massive amount to see, but if you are wandering around the lake, ts worth stopping by.

reviews.author: harry_mdj
reviews.title: awesome little temple
reviews.content: the temple located in Hoan Kiem Lake, what a great view with the red bridge. many great spot inside the temple and the view from the temple to Hoan Kiem Lake is great.

reviews.author: Vijay M
reviews.title: Temple in the lake
reviews.content: There is nothing special about this temple across the little red bridge and paying the 20,000VND to have a look at the Ngoc Son Temple. However wandering around the lake, the temple and the old quarter is the best thing one can do. More so,  if you happen to spot the big turtle in the lake you will be in luck, as the saying goes, it brings luck to all those that spot it.

reviews.author: Sato_Seitak
reviews.title: Very nice temple in Hanoi
reviews.content: from hotel may devile We go there 2 min . Ngoc son temple location in side the Hoan kiem lake. It is very nice.

reviews.author: lorna2011
reviews.title: It okay...
reviews.content: Its a nice temple in the lake but its not anything special I thought, but after being in Thailand I haven't been particularly impressed with any of the temples in Vietnam. The general atmosphere of Hanoi is great and its all the different bits that add up to make it so good so wandering around the lake and old quarter and the temple is the best thing to do, try to see as much of it as you can.

reviews.author: nanootoronto
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: We arrived on a high Buddist holiday. All the pomp and ceremony was incredilble The old people who attended had faces with a million stories to tell. Would have loved to take their picture was did not want to be rude.

reviews.author: robynvk
reviews.title: I love temples
reviews.content: To see that the Vietnamese people's devotion to the past survives all outside influences is wonderful

reviews.author: LDM24
reviews.title: Interesting little island
reviews.content: It is worth a trip across the little red bridge and paying the 20,000VND to have a quick look at the Ngoc Son Temple, even if it is just to see the giant turtle that used to live in the lake. There is still meant to be one alive in the lake, it brings luck to all those that spot it.

reviews.author: SergeyFr0mM0sc0w
reviews.title: Very beauty!
reviews.content: We walked a lot in the old quarter of the city. There is no reason not to admire the old temple.

reviews.author: hwagg
reviews.title: a beautiful view, they have a preserved turtle...
reviews.content: It is a pretty temple, and a very popular destination since it's in the heard of the old quarter. The day we were there old men were playing a game in the courtyard in front of it, which seemed to indicate it's not only for the tourists. It isn't really something to wow you, however, if you've seen temples before. The preserved turtle is something, though.

reviews.author: Monica
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: A temple for scholars. Interesting architecture with a pond set in tranquil surrounding

reviews.author: Georgia721
reviews.title: Quaint
reviews.content: A quaint little temple located across the red bridge in the middle of the lake.  Only need 20mins there.

reviews.author: Michael D
reviews.title: small but worth a gander
reviews.content: This small temple on Hoan Kiem is interesting.  I was fond of the trees growing on the lake's edge, which no one minds if you climb into for a photo.

reviews.author: Siqueira J
reviews.title: Authentic
reviews.content: It's only 3 minutes walk from the Gondola Hotel - where I stayed.

reviews.author: TramTranTrails
reviews.title: Picturesque
reviews.content: We were the first tourist to enter the gates, inside the grounds the views of the city is beautiful. Besides the interesting history of the turtle and magic sword, it's a quiet place to escape the hustle of Hanoi. So peace peaceful and serene, with the fragrant incense inducing calm.

reviews.author: Lamings
reviews.title: Atmospheric
reviews.content: Enjoyed watching the men playing drafts (?) in the forecourt and seeing the incense coiling skyward in the afternoon sunshine. Clearly a significant temple for local visitors.

reviews.author: alicevarren
reviews.title: Peaceful little place with a big turle
reviews.content: I visited this temple on my own (without a tour package) one afternoon and sat in peace observing the visitors for quite some time. This was my favorite part - sitting on a bench with the temple on one side and the lake on another. It's a good place to meditate if not too crowded. If you go right after lunch, it is not as crowded as it gets after 2:00. The enormous (approximately 7 ft long) preserved turtle inside the temple is something worth seeing as well. It's too bad that they have it enclosed in a glass casing that doesn't allow for good pictures.

reviews.author: Tommy L
reviews.title: Ngoc Son Temple
reviews.content: Ngọc Sơn Temple is in the center of Hà Nội on a small island in the middle of Hoàn Kiếm Lake. The lake is also called Hồ Gươm (Sword Lake) and was previously named Lục Thuỷ (Green Water) because its water is always green. In the 15th century, the lake was renamed Hoàn Kiếm (Returned Sword) because of a legend relating to Lê Lợi’s resistance war against Ming invaders.

reviews.author: AlineZhoo
reviews.title: Nice to visit
reviews.content: Nothing spectacular about this temple except that it is located in the heart of Hanoi. It is a good walk and things to see if you happen to stay at a hotel around the Old quarter.

reviews.author: AnnieNZ
reviews.title: Picturesque
reviews.content: Small... loads of tourists!  Good photo opportunities.

reviews.author: Rowan H
reviews.title: Oooopps! I dropped my sword!
reviews.content: Located on an island in the Northern section of Hoan Kiem lake this houses a small temple and the remains of a gigantic tortoise of the species which inhabits the lake. The legend was that in the mid-15th century, heaven (yes heaven!) gave emperor Ly Thai To (Le Loi) a magical sword. With this sword he drove the Chinese out of Vietnam. However one day after the war, while boating on the lake he came upon a giant golden tortoise who grabbed the sword and disappeared into the depths of this lake. That's why it's called the Lake of the restored sword (Ho Hoan Kiem).LOGISTICSWithin walking distance of the tourist area of Hanoi. I would recommend you do it as part of a larger walking tour of the city featuring Old quarter sites (Ngoc Son, Memorial house, Bach Ma, St Josephs cathedral) > History museum > Hao lo prison museum > Temple of literature.REVIEWI don't know about you but after reading the mythological story above I was suspicious. I reckon that guy was just a klutz who was boating on this lake and accidently dropped his sword in it. So he came up with this tall tale. Regardless the tourists love it. This place is ridiculously packed to the rafters with people taking pictures on the bridge. Once you get over it you find a very small and underwhelming temple with more people than space. It's cheap entry fee and proximity to old quarter are it's best attributes.CONCLUSIONDue to it's proximity to the tourist area it's worth a look but choose what time you go carefully as it can get very crowded.CONCLUSION

reviews.author: prettygirl1990
reviews.title: Small temple but huge spirit
reviews.content: I visited this temple on the first day of lunar month, there were many local people to pray. quiet atmosphere, lovely temple

reviews.author: annieandbob
reviews.title: Worth fighting the crowd over the bridge
reviews.content: Walking over the bridge itself is quite an experience and the temple is beautiful as are the views across the lake to the surrounding streets

reviews.author: JFKtravel
reviews.title: It is like going back in time
reviews.content: Worth a visit if you are passing by; 20 minutes is all you'll need here

reviews.author: MaikoG
reviews.title: Nice place to visit, especially for kids
reviews.content: We paid 10,000 dong each to visit (about 50 cents) the temple on a Monday.  It was fairly crowded with tourists and locals alike.  The temple is located across the red bridge, a great spot for taking photos.  It's free to go on the bridge and from the bridge you can see the Turtle Pagoda.  The temple itself is simple and doesn't take long to view.  Their is a pathway around the temple, including some benches to sit on and a goldfish pond.  There is also a large embalmed turtle.  There are two small gift shops.  I liked the fact that the temple is located next to a park with lots of pathways so it is a great place to walk and let kids run around while taking a break from the Hanoi traffic madness.

reviews.author: Philip0011
reviews.title: Unbelievable experience
reviews.content: Through our guide, Mr. Tan from DELUXE VIETNAM TOURS, we learnt that 3 religions live happily together in on temple. I have traveled to many countries in the world and this is the only one like this

reviews.author: trong d
reviews.title: Center place for hanoi Beauty!
reviews.content: Wherever you go, this is simply the best place to visit. Fresh air, good view and of course the meaning of the 500 years old turtle with the legend giving it the name Restored Sword Lake.

reviews.author: WinnieNg77
reviews.title: nothing much
reviews.content: nothing much inside there except a temple for praying, but need to pay VND10,000 each person

reviews.author: surater89
reviews.title: Very nice place In Hanoi
reviews.content: Ngoc son temple location in side the Hoan kiem lake. In side very large very beautiful  view and had a lot of the local culture there.  from hotel We go there 5 min .

reviews.author: Brad 🇭🇰
reviews.title: Ok temple, nice gates and bridge leading to the temple
reviews.content: We found the Ngoc Son Temple to be just an average attraction in Hanoi, nothing particularly special to write about.  However, we did enjoy its setting in middle of the Hoan Kiem Lake on a small island.  It made for nice photos from the shore walkway around the actual lake.  There is a nice, small bridge that leads from the mainland over to the small island which houses the temple.  The bridge is nice and the gates are very attractive.  We really liked the dragon mural particularly.  This was worth a quick stop to see, even if you don't feel like going over the bridge to the actual temple. The temple was not particularly special, making it difficult to recommend as a must see in Hanoi.  However, its worth taking a few pictures from the outside of the lake, near the Water Puppet Show Theater.  We recommend just doing this before or after you see the water puppet show.  It does cost a few Dong to go over to the temple but can't recall the price, it wasn't much.

reviews.author: lchina
reviews.title: Nice temple beside Hoankiem lake
reviews.content: This is a nice temple in the Hanoi. The temple was built in the 19th century. Initially called Ngoc Son Pagoda (玉山寺), the temple was called Ngoc Son temple for the worship only god Wenchang is the star sent home the scientific literature and church Tran Hung Dao, a hero of the Army original 13th century.When King Ly Thai To moved his capital to Thang Long Ngoc Tuong is named the temple, to the life renamed Tran Ngoc Son. Here was erected a temple to worship the smiles heroic martyrs who sacrificed in the resistance against the Mongolian Highlands. Later he collapsed house long, up to the Le Huu Vinh (1735 - 1739), lord Trinh Thuy Giang Khanh and also covering up the mountain land on the east coast facing the mountain called Ngoc Son Dao Tai and Ngoc Boi. Later in life the Le Thuy Khanh also Chieu Thong was destroyed. A charity named Tin Trai, the same old people have established a temple called Ngoc Son Pagoda.

reviews.author: Amanda k
reviews.title: very nice temple at Hoan Kiem lake
reviews.content: Ngoc son temple location in side the Hoan kiem lake. In side the temple had the 100 year old turtle of Hoan kiem lake. Inside also very beautiful and had a lot of the local culture there.I like the view of this temple to the lake and the design of this temple

reviews.author: Flower53_10
reviews.title: Genuine show
reviews.content: This is a must do experience in Hanoi. Genuine culture of Vietnam. The story of puppets is that when the rice fields we fool of water the villagers invented the entertainment for themselves. They carved puppets and were presenting the stories and showing performances on the water over the rice fields. Nowadays the actors are very good, and even though the show is in Vietnamese, the music, the songs etc is fabulous. We booked our tickets directly from the box office, just make sure to come earlier or a day or two before to get good seats.

reviews.author: Odyssey24193778568
reviews.title: must see
reviews.content: A must-see in Hanoi! Our flight changed due to the weather, and the staff immediately helped us reschedule. Even on a busy weekend, we got great seats with a good view. The music was incredible and the puppets were so vivid and full of life. Excellent service and a wonderful performance—we really enjoyed it!

reviews.author: Almira
reviews.title: Waterpuppet
reviews.content: Interesting if you are interested in tradional culture, show lasted around 50 mins, quite a

reviews.author: 301隊長
reviews.title: Doll's movement
reviews.content: Since I didn't use the audio guide, I didn't understand the content of the songs, but I was thoroughly entertained just by watching the movements of the puppets synchronized with the live music.

reviews.author: Eve G
reviews.title: Nice cultural experience
reviews.content: A cultural experience.  Worth getting the VIP ticket.   Music and singers were phenomenal.   Interesting story.

reviews.author: polarsonneHH
reviews.title: A must when visiting Hanoi
reviews.content: That was interesting, but in the end too long...

reviews.author: marcsheridan59
reviews.title: Well worth a visit and very reasonable but don’t take cards!
reviews.content: Very entertaining, colorful and air conditioned.Historical Vietnamese cultural entertainment and a great place to be out of the summer heat and humidity.

reviews.author: Nicnack35
reviews.title: Good puppetry and music
reviews.content: Nice to see a local tradition. Good puppetry and music. Just wished we’d looked up the story beforehand! Lasts an hour.

reviews.author: Nicnack35
reviews.title: Worth a watch
reviews.content: The music and puppetry were really good and nice to see traditional art form. We knew we wouldn’t follow the story of the show however it was rather bizarre!

reviews.author: dennys34
reviews.title: Was nice
reviews.content: A very unique heritage experience - must do in Hanoi

reviews.author: dennys34
reviews.title: Was nice
reviews.content: A bit long - take a translated - great action

reviews.author: Pathfinder430464
reviews.title: Awesome!
reviews.content: It was amazing! Spend the money for the headset to hear in English if you do not know the language!

reviews.author: mvanroy
reviews.title: Tourist but beautiful and nice
reviews.content: Like so many tourists, we wanted to discover Hanoi's famous water puppet theatre. We bought our tickets for the 4th row 2 days before the show (200k VND pp; the higher the seat, the cheaper). Ten minutes before the performance, the doors opened, the room was full and we had a perfect view of the ‘stage’. You could rent an audio guide but we didn't do this so we couldn't always follow the full story. Nevertheless, we enjoyed the show because of the live music (some 8 musicians with some special instruments) and live voices (in Vietnamese), the fun and beautiful puppets, the humor and also the story that clearly told the origin and history of the nearby Hoa Hoan Kiem lake with its beautiful temple. The whole show lasted 50 min and was really worth the experience.

reviews.author: Eve
reviews.title: Definitely go!
reviews.content: Beautiful show with ancient Vietnamese art form. This is not one to miss in Hanoi, we loved it. Short and sweet show, amazing value for money at £5 each and we had a great view!

reviews.author: Wendy T
reviews.title: A Must visit if you’re in Han Noi
reviews.content: Probably the cheapest way of buying your ticket, there are 3 prices depending where you sit.  It was clean, the seats were spacious & very comfortable, it was raised seating so everyone can see. There was air conditioning and the show was brilliant as were the puppeteers, narrator/singers and all the musicians.  There were a number of steps to climb and I’m not sure if there were any lifts!  There was a little museum at the top of the stairs with lots of past puppets in show.  I would highly recommend a visit it was lovely.

reviews.author: David G
reviews.title: A unique Vietnamese art form
reviews.content: This was one of the two main highlights of our visit in Hanoi during our Vietnam trip. The water puppet show is performed in the modern Thang Long water puppet theatre, near Hoan Kiem Lake, in the center of Hanoi. This 45 minute indoor show is it is truly a unique Vietnamese art form (depicting scenes from rural life and episodes of national history). The puppets are controlled by puppeteers arge rods and hiding behind a bamboo screen.at the back of the pool. This 45+ minute indoor show is truly a unique Vietnamese art form (depicting scenes from rural life and episodes of national history).

reviews.author: Kath
reviews.title: Water puppet theatre
reviews.content: This was an interesting look at theatrical Vietnamese culture

reviews.author: Alice
reviews.title: Fun Hanoi stop with a few quirks
reviews.content: I went to the Thang Long Water Puppet show on a rainy Hanoi evening and ended up really enjoying it. The puppets were clever, the live music had that sharp, twangy sound that stuck in your head, and I liked seeing the water splash around the stage. It felt very local and different from the usual tourist stuff. That said, the theater was packed, the seats were a bit cramped, and if you don’t know the stories already, some parts go by fast. The show is also pretty short, so it doesn’t take up much of an evening. Still, I’d definitely recommend it if you’re in Hanoi, just go in expecting a simple cultural stop rather than a big production.

reviews.author: blanche482
reviews.title: 【Almost the center seat in the front row】
reviews.content: Viewing on Wednesday, April 22nd in the first activity of my first trip to Hanoi, 6 days and 4 nights.When I made a reservation, they told me where to find it, and to my surprise, it was almost the middle seat in the front row.I was able to film everything on a tripod on that day.Also, if you go to the theater on the day, the seats sold out after the evening,It is recommended to book early.Note that the audio guide is almost inaudible due to the volume of live music,It is unnecessary because you can understand the story by the movement of the puppet.

reviews.author: Travel Girl GR
reviews.title: Moderate
reviews.content: I watched the show without understanding much because it is in their language.Hold on for an hour.It reminded me more of a children's play rather than an adult.Something different I've never seen before but at some point I got bored.

reviews.author: The Wandering Pair
reviews.title: Chaos in the Foyer, Magic on the Water
reviews.content: The purchase of the tickets was straightforward through Tripadvisor. However, on arrival, things felt rather chaotic. Organisation appeared to be in short supply and the crowd gathering outside created some concern, particularly for Megan, as there was a real risk of people being crushed in the rush to enter. Thankfully, we made it inside safely in the end.Once seated, we quickly discovered that the theatre makes very efficient use of its available space. The seats are quite cramped, so if you’re particularly tall or broad-shouldered, you may find yourself getting to know your neighbours better than expected.As English visitors, some of the folktales were difficult to follow in detail, and we found the audio guide a little sparse at times. However, this did not detract significantly from the overall experience. The skill and artistry involved in the water puppetry are genuinely impressive, and it is easy to appreciate the tradition even when some of the finer story details are lost in translation.The live music and singing added greatly to the atmosphere and authenticity of the performance. The musicians were excellent, and the cast appeared to be thoroughly enjoying themselves, which helped make the show even more engaging.Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed the performance and would recommend spending an evening experiencing this unique aspect of Vietnamese culture.Audio guides are available in other languages for 50,000 VND per person.Tickets cost us 858,156VND (£24.42), when we collected the tickets from Viator we noticed the price listed was 200,000VND each so for both it was 400,000VND (£11.20) We checked this against the sales desk and can confirm it is cheaper to buy from the theatre than online.

reviews.author: Derya Yağız
reviews.title: A great option for the evening in Hanoi.
reviews.content: It was a lot of fun. Local music and live performances, and it's very easy to get around.

reviews.author: Drud Murdock
reviews.title: A beautiful, creative showcase of Vietnamese culture
reviews.content: A truly captivating way to immerse yourself in Vietnamese traditions and artistic expression! The performance is wonderfully entertaining, highly imaginative, and visually breathtaking.

reviews.author: Safari38865575367
reviews.title: Great show
reviews.content: Very original, immersive, original. I did not regret to add the audio guide, (too bad they are not offered for sale tickets). it gives context to the show and the scenes of life played.

reviews.author: Pippa Jones
reviews.title: Unique and fascinating
reviews.content: I’ve never seen anything like it. Never known anything like it. My friend and I booked this after a recommendation from a colleague. We didn’t know what to expect at all, and it completely blew our minds. It was touching, funny, cheeky and had amazing visual storytelling. We absolutely loved it. It was all in Vietnamese, but the visual storytelling was easy to understand what was happening. It was so unbelievably unique and enjoyable. I’d recommend to anyone that will be visiting Hanoi.

reviews.author: Indigo
reviews.title: Touristy but a must-do & book ahead!
reviews.content: This is a must-do!We recommend booking directly at the theatre and booking in advance because every show sells out. If you do book on a different platform you have to pick your tickets up before the show as they only accept their paper tickets.It lasts around 45 minutes and we really enjoyed it. The live music adds so much to the experience, and when you think about this being performed hundreds of years ago… it’s actually amazing.You can get a listening pack which translates the story for you for just 50,000 (£1.45). However, mine didn't work but they refunded with no issues and the story was just as beautiful.Definitely worth doing while in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Ya-Wun L
reviews.title: Scam
reviews.content: A scam. I booked 4 tickets of skip the line/ first class seats and paid 64 USD. But when we arrived at the entrance, we were told a story that sounded like a scam, which said that the first class seats were unavailable due to the computer issue when we booked. We were given the random seats instead and were told that they would refund us in 2 days. They didn’t eventually. I wrote 2 letters to the ticket office and to the agent, but never ever got any response. That’s why I claimed that it was a scam!

reviews.author: Rana
reviews.title: Quite a unique show
reviews.content: Very nice show, a nice blend of stories, show and music

reviews.author: Mon
reviews.title: Interesting Cultural Experience
reviews.content: This was one of the activities we wanted to see in Hanoi, and it was a great way to get out of the sun and see something totally new. The only reason I would recommend getting "better" seats is so you can be closer to the stage, and thus have fewer tourists holding their phones in front of your face for the entire show.We were glad we bought our tickets in advance, as it appeared like a number of shows had sold out. The pricing onlineseemed pretty accurate too compared to buying in person. (Heads up, if you buy your tickets in advance through TripAdvisor, DON'T stand in the long confusing ticket line -- head towards the entrance to the theater and there should be a staff member with your name and paper tickets. You can't get in with just the digital tickets.)

reviews.author: dennys34
reviews.title: Was very nice
reviews.content: Nice to get an idea of the culture of Vietnam very cool arrangements with the water puppets. It’s worth to buy a translation so you will get the story.

reviews.author: Tom&NikkiTravel
reviews.title: A Great Experience - Worth It? Seating Tips, Audio Guide & What to Expect
reviews.content: We purchased our tickets online via GetYourGuide, which was a smooth process overall. However, it’s worth noting that ticket collection is not at the theatre itself—you’ll need to pick them up from a location approximately a 5–10 minute walk away, so allow a little extra time for this.Our show was scheduled for 9:15pm, and we recommend arriving at least 15 minutes early to secure your seat. While we had pre-booked front-row tickets (Rows A–E), seat selection is not assigned in advance. This can be slightly frustrating, as you might expect reserved seating when booking ahead.If you’re not seated within the first two rows, be prepared for potential obstructions. Audience members moving around or using phones and cameras can impact your view. For reference, we were seated in Row D (Seats 7 and 8), and we’ve included a photo to give a realistic perspective of the view.We highly recommend renting the audio guide (50,000 VND per person), especially for English speakers, as the performance is conducted in Vietnamese. It adds valuable cultural context and enhances the overall experience. That said, the audio volume can be quite low compared to the live music and sound effects, which occasionally makes it difficult to follow.The show itself is of a very high standard—engaging, unique, and deeply rooted in Vietnamese culture. At around 45 minutes long, it’s the perfect length, and the seating is reasonably comfortable throughout.Overall, this is a highly enjoyable and worthwhile experience, and we’d absolutely recommend adding it to your itinerary when visiting  Hanoi

reviews.author: Toby G
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: Great but stupid Americans kept filming

reviews.author: AussiExpatinHongKong
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.content: If you’re in Hanoi, the Water Puppet Show is an absolute must-see. It’s fascinating from start to finish—the skill of the puppeteers is incredible, especially considering everything is performed behind the scenes in water.The whole production is very well presented and thoughtfully put together, with music and storytelling that really bring it to life. Set in a beautiful old theatre, you can almost feel the history around you as you watch.The show runs for about 45 minutes and is performed in Vietnamese, but audio guides are available if you want more context.Best of all, it’s very cheap entertainment for such a unique cultural experience. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: susanna t
reviews.title: Thang long water puppet theatre
reviews.content: What a fantastic experience. Booking through trip advisor was so easy and we were able to collect our paper tickets at the booking office. We chose the vip seats, which gave us a really good view. The audio guide finished off the experience nicely.

reviews.author: Jazz Gumbo
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: Not really my cup of tea, but it is fascinating & very clever too. An interesting story very expertly played out by puppeters who come ou at the end. The show rans approx 45 mins & gives you the history of the lake.

reviews.author: craigleepaulsen
reviews.title: Bit Boring
reviews.content: I understand it’s Vietnamese culture on display, but even if I’d watched this in 1965, I’d still have found it boring.  My wife enjoyed it, but I don’t understand why it’s so highly rated and recommended.  On the plus side, we had VIP tickets and front row seats, and the air‑conditioned theatre was comfortable, but the actual puppet show and music just weren’t great.

reviews.author: Dimenson X
reviews.title: Must visit place!!
reviews.content: The water puppet show was truly enjoyable! So unique and a culturally rich performance! It’s unlike anything I’ve seen before and a must‑see for visitors. I do think tourists would benefit from an audio guide so they don’t miss the storyline. Although, the headset volume was quite low and I had to press it against my ear to catch the translation. At the same time, I didn’t want to miss the beautiful live sounds of the performance itself. Overall, a fascinating and memorable experience! ❤️❤️❤️

reviews.author: JoEastMidlands
reviews.title: Fantastic traditional show
reviews.content: We booked tickets via Get Your Guide, and Charming Vietnam Travel (who were great at getting our tickets moved whwn our flight was cancelled and our journey rearranged).  The show was delightful and entertaining and we used the audio guide to help us better understand the historical story being told.   With live music and singing it really is one to see.

reviews.author: Tyrrell68
reviews.title: Silly but cool. Great live music.
reviews.content: It’s good. At times quite silly and I did catch myself laughing but just as often I was intrigued and wondering how they were actually managing the movements. The music alone is worth it. Air conditioning is very effective so make sure to wear an appropriate extra layer. Try to be flexible and book a show with seats available at the front as it’s tricky seeing past too many heads.

reviews.author: Berrys
reviews.title: Unique show to see when in Hanoi
reviews.content: This was an interesting show.  It was amazing to see the skill.  I'm sure it's much harder than they make it look.  Small theatre.  A nice truly Vietnamese experience.  Show runs about an hour.  Suggest to stop and buy tickets a couple days before and pick front row seats.  No need to get an audio guide.

reviews.author: Tony B
reviews.title: Rude ticket office
reviews.content: I tried to buy tickets from the ticket office and was dealing with a lady with purple hair. Three times I asked for tickets for my chosen date which were showing as available but on each occasion she entirely ignored me. There was a long line behind me and after 5 minutes of this I gave up and left. She has been the rudest person that I have met during my 5 weeks in Vietnam.

reviews.author: WillRod321
reviews.title: A new experience seeing a water puppet show.
reviews.content: This is a different form of puppet show, not your typical Punch and Judy show,  doesn't matter that you cannot speak Vietnamese it is still an enjoyable show and worth the visit.

reviews.author: Susan A
reviews.title: Puppet show Hanoi
reviews.content: They are a very talented group of performers. The singers and musicians were obviously very good. We would advise that you do get the audio guide so that you have some idea on the folklore behind the performances. We did appreciate the professionalism that went into the show, but it wasn’t our thing.

reviews.author: Leigh D
reviews.title: Water puppet show
reviews.content: This was a great experience. My whole family loved it ❤️

reviews.author: Marco
reviews.title: Do not rent the audio guide
reviews.content: The water puppet theatre offers a unique experience where you can witness the talent of the puppeteers. The musical and visual show is well worth experiencing. However, I don’t recommend renting the audio guide because, at 50,000 dong per person, it’s really not worth it. It’s difficult to hear, and you don’t learn much.

reviews.author: Jeremy C
reviews.title: A Glorious Escape From Reality
reviews.content: Whether or not you are interested in the cultural history behind the water puppets I would thoroughly recommend that you take in this 45 minute show just for the sheer fun of it and as a short escape from boring reality. I don't think I've enjoyed puppets quite so much since being part of the original Thunderbirds generation.

reviews.author: Françoise J
reviews.title: So much to rearrange!
reviews.content: Definitely an experience to live when you are in Hanoi. It’s a great show with excellent musicians and singers but there are some very BIG downsides: 1- Unfortunately the doors are not closed when the show begins so for 10 minutes (out of 50) it is a mess... the latecomers settle... forcing those who are installed to get up to let them sit because the passage is EXTREMELY narrow between the rows so if you are not in the first row we see nothing.... Totally disrespectful especially for the artists but also for those who arrived on time!2 - Spectators, arms up, photograph and above all film throughout the show so prevent the visibility of the scene...  SHAMEFUL and as DISRESPECTFUL as those who arrive late!3- The seats are quite uncomfortable and the space extremely narrow; the quantity of the show deserves greater comfort to enjoy!4- I dare not even imagine what would happen in the event of a fire... Leaving the venue after the show was long and laborious... obstructing the only possible way out of the venue...

reviews.author: AHERVASI
reviews.title: Beautiful spectacle, mistreated
reviews.content: It is astonishing that it is allowed to film the performance, but even more to notice no few foolish tourists using their smartphones most of the time, what they probably do not do on their own countries, disturbing the experience of others more interested in enjoying an artistic performance not through a 6 inches display. Guys, watch it on YouTube, save your money, and above all, respect others.The spectacle itself is nice, creative and worth

reviews.author: Hrothmir
reviews.title: Entertaining. Brief. Get headsets for translation. Glad I included in my Hanoi visit.
reviews.content: If you are interested in Vietnamese culture and a 45 minute puppet show sounds entertaining, then add this to your list.We purchased VIP tickets in advance via the Klook.com Website. Tickets were expensive compared to other sites in Vietnam but still very reasonably by U.S. standards (less than $10 per person). We opted for the audio headsets to explain/translate in English. Purchased as you enter the theater, this added to the cost (under $2) and was worthwhile.
