reviews.content: Very Artistic & Unique Puppet Show, in which the puppets are all performing in a stage comprising of a water pond. Very artisticly done & depicting Vietnamese lifestyle of sowing & harvesting & also Vietnamese dance forms,all to the accompaniment of traditional Vietnamese music. There are 3 or 4 shows virtually daily & one must see one. A must see for children.

reviews.author: Sotontraveller
reviews.title: I would like to say I enjoyed this ....
reviews.content: This attraction is in a very busy part of Hanoi with rather bossy security inside and out so no hanging around eg chatting to friends at the beginning or end of a show.  Our viewing was early afternoon.Regrettably the rake is so shallow that if you sit behind a tall person hardly anything can be seen.  This was my experience.  I think it was quite amusing and possibly even a little educational in terms of Vietnamese culture.I was disappointed but would go again in the hope of actually seeing something.

reviews.author: Nicolea Deppen
reviews.title: Distinct from the additional temples
reviews.content: I genuinely loved the water puppet theater. With a combination of regular music, local stories along with the fascinating solutions combined with the bathtub puppets this was a great cultural experience. I received the ticket of mine in the first morning for a night show but there is tickets left. Price tag is completely great for almost one hour show.

reviews.author: Patty B
reviews.title: Near The Mausoleum and Nice
reviews.content: Since this is part of the area where the mausoleum is, we went to see it.  It was worthwhile, but getting busy.  The grounds are nice and so was the pagoda we saw.

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: Lacking atmosphere
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is certainly one of the symbols of Hanoi and, being located inside the Ho Chi Minh complex, it is worth stopping to see it during your visit.Personally, however, I did not find it particularly evocative. The pagoda is very small and the large number of visitors makes it difficult to appreciate the religious atmosphere and the significance of the place.When we were there, there was practically a continuous line of people waiting for their turn, mainly to take photographs and selfies in front of the pagoda. Seeing a place of worship turn almost into a photo shoot inevitably makes it lose much of its charm and spirituality.The structure remains unique, however, built on a single pillar in the center of a small pond and with a history that dates back to the 11th century.It is worth seeing if you are already visiting the Ho Chi Minh complex, also because it requires little time, but personally I do not consider it among the most exciting places visited in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Travel Girl GR
reviews.title: Visit after the mausoleum
reviews.content: The pagoda is in the mausoleum so you will see it as you go out.It's on a pen that makes it special.No entrance required.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: A pagoda on one pillar
reviews.content: This pagoda is hidden in a little park. It is surrounded by a pond with lotus flowers. The pagoda can be entered after climbing a steep staircase. Coming down is more challenging. The chapel area is quite beautiful.

reviews.author: David L
reviews.title: Inspired by the lotus flower
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is one of Hanoi’s most iconic monuments, famous for its unique lotus-flower inspired architecture and deep spiritual significance.  This historic Buddhist temple stands on a single stone pillar and symbolizes the purity, enlightenment and cultural heritage of Vietnam.  Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Jeremy C
reviews.title: Iconic Little Temple
reviews.content: Located within the mausoleum complex this novel little temple sits like a lotus flower on a small lake. I would imagine that it is often mobbed with tourists but still worth looking out and taking a moment of contemplation.

reviews.author: Talant2007
reviews.title: Pagoda on one column
reviews.content: This pagoda was originally built in 1046g and is an iconic Buddhist temple. The original was destroyed during the French occupation in 1954. But in 1955 it was restored.

reviews.author: Steve_Grant1
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: This is an interesting structure clearly based on one pillar. Nive to look at when you are in the overall area with its various sites.

reviews.author: FyingKiwi
reviews.title: An Enigma
reviews.content: A rather strange pagoda containing a statue of Buddha in a manner never previously observed by this traveller throughout his extensive travels. While clearly a place of worship, perhaps because of its location, it also appears to be a shrine that is more visited by tour groups than used by locals. Even after subsequently sharing with a local about this pagoda after visiting, resulted in a non-cholent response.

reviews.author: sekjr0521
reviews.title: If you have something better to do...
reviews.content: The pictures make it look better than it actually is it's a hike to get to because it's behind one of the major buildings there.

reviews.author: Wanderlustaustralia
reviews.title: Beautiful to look at
reviews.content: We spent about two minutes at this pagoda, as it is very small and you won’t have much luck climbing it with the crowds. It was very beautiful and just a short walk from the Ho Chi Minh Museum, definitely worth a look.

reviews.author: TheLush101
reviews.title: Peaceful pagoda
reviews.content: Part of the palace and mausoleum grounds, this is a very serene place. The pond with waterlilies surrounds the pagoda itself. There are steps up to the pagoda itself and it's well organised - you walk up one side, a few people can stand at the top, then you walk back down the other side.

reviews.author: francisco r
reviews.title: Good experience
reviews.content: Very nice, right behind the Ho Chi Min mausoleum.Watch out for the tangancito and the very bad coffee. The pagoda and the temple are worth visiting.

reviews.author: vodka
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: This is a very beautiful place with many stories attached. Not only is it a place with beautiful and unique architecture, I really like this place.

reviews.author: doctorfoxtrot
reviews.title: Part of the Ho Chi Minh complex
reviews.content: Nice to go up and observe. And take photos. Made in observance and respect for the Buddha. Part of the Ho Chi Minh complex where there is tight security coming in

reviews.author: linece91
reviews.title: Beautiful! Soothing site

You can get a little crowded in July but not insurmountable either The site is quiet and soothing.A real moment of disconnection.You can find bamboo sculptures from this pagoda up to the bixtenco tower

reviews.author: Stanley H
reviews.title: A Pillar Temple
reviews.content: Beyond the building blocks of the Presidium, we reached a small temple called the "Temple of One Pillar". The temple was built in 1049. According to the legend, Li Tai Song dreamed of watching the Buddha's hand-to-hand baby, standing on the water pool flower table, soon to be born, it was ordered to build a temple like water flower, so that a column of the temple looked like a water flower. Therefore, the one-pillar temple is dedicated to observance Buddha.Although, the whole journey is definitely a horse ride to see flowers. But in a few short hours, I felt that I went to a history class again. And for Vietnam this part of Hong Kong, Western history will not go deep into teaching an era, to learn more.

reviews.author: divya
reviews.title: Tiny and interesting pagoda
reviews.content: * Entrance : no fees* Parking : could not find a designated parking spot . We parked near the shops/cafes. An old lady charges 20,000 and we only paid 15,000 . She verbally abused us in Vietnamese.No receipt. It’s a scam, she isn’t allowed to charge for parking. * Walkable from Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. It’s in the same compound. * Scooter hire : 1,50,000 per day (Hired close to our hotel)

reviews.author: Amy B
reviews.title: Wow, Just Wow! A Tiny Treasure with a Big Story...
reviews.content: Okay, so I took a little detour from exploring the charming streets of Hội An (yes, I know it's a bit of a trip to Hanoi!) and I had to see the One Pillar Pagoda. I'd seen pictures, but honestly, they don't do it justice.Standing there, this little gem of a temple just gracefully rising out of the water... it's kind of magical. It feels ancient and peaceful all at the same time. I loved hearing the story about Emperor Lý Thái Tông and the dream. It makes the whole place feel even more special.It's definitely smaller than I expected, but that almost makes it more intimate. You can really take it all in. I spent a few quiet moments just soaking up the atmosphere. It was a really nice contrast to the energy of the markets and the tailor shops.Honestly, even if you only have a short time in Hanoi (or if you're making a bit of a journey like I did!), make the effort to see the One Pillar Pagoda. It's a little piece of Vietnamese history and beauty that really stuck with me. So glad I made the trip!

reviews.author: MrDream688
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is one of the most famous pagodas in Vietnam, located in the heart of Hanoi. With its unique architecture resembling a lotus flower blooming on the water, the pagoda is an important spiritual and cultural symbol of the capital.

reviews.author: Sue M

reviews.author: alessandra_biondi3

reviews.content: Chua Mot chot Pagoda was rebuilt because it was demolished. Its peculiarity is to stand on a single pillar, externally you can see the roof from the corners upwards to recall the shape of the boats. Internally, the Buddhist Goddess representing Mercy is venerated.

reviews.author: Liliane M

reviews.author: TravelingAnnK

reviews.author: Nikhat Shahin Khan
reviews.title: Interesting structure

A short visit to this beautiful and historic place is recommended for anyone in Hanoi!

reviews.author: Alberto G

reviews.author: Karen
reviews.title: Symbol of Vietnamese culture and history

The pagoda was built in the 11th century under King Ly Thai Tong, with the shape of a lotus blooming on the water. Despite its small area, the surrounding space is very peaceful and airy, creating a relaxing feeling in the middle of the bustling city. This is a great stop for those who want to learn more about the history and ancient architecture of Vietnam

reviews.author: Yvonne S

This is located close to the Mausoleum of Ho Che Min.

reviews.author: Ludo V
reviews.title: A legend is kept alive here
reviews.content: The Chua Mot Cot (Single Column Pagoda), like the Cot Co, is one of the symbols of Hanoi. Originally built in 1049 under Emperor Ly Thai Tong goose in wood. The concept depicts a lotus flower growing towards the sky from a lotus pond.  She is considered important in connection with the legend that the emperor - who was childless - still had a son here. The post of the pagoda has been restored several times over time, with the original wooden post being replaced by a concrete column with a diameter of 1.25 m. Burned one last time by the French during their retreat in 1954..

reviews.author: LuizDutraNeto
reviews.title: A symbol of Buddhist faith in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Not far from "Ba Dinh Square", "Ho Chi MInh Mausolem" and "Ho Chi Minh Museum", you will find "Chùa Môt Côt", as "One-Pillar Pagoda" is locally known. It was originally built by Emperor Lý Thái Tông, in 1049, and has been restored many many times along the centuries. Its last restoration dates from 1955, as it was severely destroyed by French Union Forces while withdrawing Vietnam after the First Indochina War. The three square meter wooden pagoda stands on a single stone pillar (1,25 m in diameter) in the middle of a pond and is surrounded by beautiful gardens. The pagoda supposedly ressembles a lotus blossom, a Buddhist symbol of purity, enlightenment and rebirth. Inside "One-Pillar Pagoda", Vietnamese Buddhist deity "Quam Am" is enshrined and brings blessings of fertility and health. Visiting the pagoda can be easily combined with other nearby attractions in the "Ho Chi Minh Complex". Dress properly, queue respectfully and be silent, as prayers take place continuously inside this beautiful small temple. Say a little prayer, burn an incense and may "Quam Am" bless your visit to Vietnam. Enjoy!

reviews.author: Cindy Marie Azur
reviews.title: A must visit/view place
reviews.content: Definitely must visit/see if when you’re already within this area along with museum, mausoleum. Have to remember that wearing shorts is forbidden to enter the pagoda. So either you stay outside and take photos or wear some Long pants or covered it with sarong or Long shawl.

reviews.author: UrsulaHans
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: A very nice and interesting pagoda (buddhist temple). When getting there beaware of the traffic - it is dangerous!

reviews.author: Olivier D
reviews.title: Quite a unique place
reviews.content: This was a great moment, especialy becaus ewe were alone for 5min. Then a bus of tourist arrived and it became difficult to take any picture or even relax...

reviews.author: Steve
reviews.title: Do some background reading before you visit
reviews.content: You could easily miss the history of this place and dismiss it as a concrete pillar topped by a wooden structure in the middle of a grubby pond. However its significance as a thousand year old Buddhist temple and one of Vietnams iconic structures should not be overlooked. A shame about the plastic flowers which adorn the base of the pillar

reviews.author: Sharif Razi Al Mahmud
reviews.title: Religious Place
reviews.content: Religious person must visit this place and other people can visit only to watch and taking picture. Small place and average attraction.

reviews.author: giji365
reviews.title: A good attraction
reviews.content: Worth a visit. Beautiful and historic. Warning - don't buy anything from the shops around it. They charge more than double of normal price.

reviews.author: Chandrashekar Naik
reviews.title: Pretty interesting Pagoda...
reviews.content: We had been to this place and it’s has it’s own history behind this, Pagoda door is opened at north facing which has very interesting story. There is one plant which was brought from India a century ago and planted just in front Of Pagoda. Pagoda place is very close to lakeside in fact just a corner of the lakeside.Very nice view for photos. Prefer to visit evening time.

reviews.author: John Q
reviews.title: Interesting structure
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is close to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. This structure represents the lotus flower (symbol of enlightenment). It was destroyed by the French on their evacuation in 1954 and was subsequently reconstructed.

reviews.author: michelle b
reviews.title: worth taking a look
reviews.content: this was an amazing place, the pagoda is amazing, just astounded as how old everything is, the gardens are beautiful and there are shops where you can get something to eat or buy a gift . there are beautiful ponds full of fish & lotus flowers.

reviews.author: Govindan N
reviews.title: Beautiful Pagoda
reviews.content: This Pagoda is built of wood on a single stone pillar. It resembles a lotus blossom.The French before leaving Hanoi had destroyed this Pagoda which has been rebuilt by the government. This Pagoda was originally built by emperor Ly Thai Tong in 1049.This is near Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.This is a nice place to visit in Hanoi

reviews.author: Tran Ngoc Qui
reviews.title: Outstanding architecture pagoda!
reviews.content: It is worth seeing, a place where local people come to visit and pray for the good fortune! Still remember how it is look like with the very special design, 1 pillar to keep it stand above a lake! Do not miss!

reviews.author: Steven H
reviews.title: Unique Pagoda
reviews.content: The one pillar pagoda has an interesting back story and is unique. Nice for a quick photo in a beautiful setting. Part of the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum site.

reviews.author: Mario&Sandy
reviews.title: Nice Pagoda
reviews.content: Nice Pagoda with plenty of tourists as there are several tourists sights near by. Beautiful koi pond surrounds this Pagoda for taking some nice photos. My wife and were more interested in giving thanks and blessings, so we purchased some incense and walked through the side where there are actual small Buddha temples for giving your offerings. A nice experience all around as we enjoyed our quiet time giving thanks.

reviews.author: Slk T
reviews.title: Sightseeing
reviews.content: The place is not easily accessible unless you have Ho Chin Minh Mausoleum as one of your must-see list as you have to go through security checkpoint and walk pass by the Mausoleum to get to the Stilt House and the Pagoda behind the Mausoleum. Then you’ll take a side exit to leave the place.

reviews.author: emirati_nomad
reviews.title: The lady selling fruits
reviews.content: Beautiful place and next to it there is a lady selling fruits. I bought 2 packs of fruits and she gave me 3 extra for free and refused to take any money for it. I was shocked and I wish I can do something to make that lady happy. Kind people still exist. I pray she always be happy and blessed.

reviews.author: Francis Martino
reviews.title: Place where the One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Space is small but it is an icon of Hanoi capital. If you’re in the area to see Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum.Interesting architecture, can be quite beautiful with the right lighting given the pond it sits on. Definitely something to see. Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Tuseef
reviews.title: Like a heaven
reviews.content: Awesome view, just loved the trip. Highly recommend. I must visit again in coming months. Never forget my this trip

reviews.author: tlynn63
reviews.title: Walk up the steps and peer inside
reviews.content: If you are visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum then it is  just a short stroll to the One Pillar Pagoda, a small wooden pagoda built on one stone pillar and made to resemble a lotus blossom.  You are free to go up the steps and take a look inside.  The pagoda is located in a park like setting with a few food vendors around and some benches.  It was nice to sit and take in the atmosphere.

reviews.author: Sarah
reviews.title: Good for a quick stop
reviews.content: This pagoda is located on the grounds of the Hoi Chi Minh Mausoleum. It’s good to snap a quick pic but you will not need to spend more than a couple of minutes here.

reviews.author: Tenaj & Tino
reviews.title: Good Spot To Visit
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is actually part of a bigger attraction, Ho Chi Min. The Pagoda sits right next to it, so you really can’t miss it. There is also a food court and some vendors. This area seems to be more like a park, but with less grass and more people mingling around. As you can see by our picture, Tenaj became the main attraction and not the Pagoda. It’s free of charge to walk the grounds of Ho Chi Min, so defiantly give it a try and bring an umbrella to get some shade from the sun. For more in-depth video reviews check us out on Youtube at: Tenaj and Tino

reviews.author: henry
reviews.title: Great place to visit
reviews.content: I have a tour with my little family. it is really old, historical place,.               It will be my best trip to visit hanoi

reviews.author: Melissa P
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: I enjoyed seeing something a bit unusual here.  You don’t need much time and can visit here while you’re on the way from the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum or museum.  You can get some nice photos and find a place to sit in the shade, too.

reviews.author: Hemant01
reviews.title: An Iconic Buddhist Temple of the 10th Century
reviews.content: This small Pagoda is built on just One Pillar. The fact that it was built in the 10th Century,itself makes it a marvel.It is surrounded by a water pond & a lot of old trees. There is also a tree,the sapling of which was presented to Ho Chi Minh by Mahatama Gandhi. This is The Baudh Tree,the same species of tree under which Buddha meditated & gained enlightenment !!

reviews.author: Kim G
reviews.title: Revered Eleventh Century Historic Buddhist Temple (Recreation)
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is the most highly revered Vietnamese Buddhist Temple, and architecturally unique.  Originally constructed in 1049 by the Emperor Ly Thai Tong for finally being blessed with a son, the temple resembles a lotus flower (the Vietnamese National Flower), standing on one pillar, as seen in his prophetic dream promising the son.  Rising above a small square pond with lotus flowers (Asian Water Lilies), the Temple is accessed by stone steps which reveal a shrine in its small interior. Unfortunately, the French destroyed the original sacred temple upon their withdrawal from Hanoi in 1954. Nearby are the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the Presidential Palace, just a short stroll away and also worth a visit.

reviews.author: Debra R
reviews.title: Iconic Pagoda
reviews.content: Lovely shrine and interesting history.  Simple in comparison to other pagoda's, but the background is what makes it interesting.

reviews.author: Jean-Marie G
reviews.title: Unique architecture
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda (Chua Mot Cot) is at one end of the large Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.  It is a tiny structure built on stilts and is considered one of 2 most iconic temples in Vietnam. A series of steps lead to a small alter where offerings have been left.  Patience and respect is required as there are always people kneeling and praying.

reviews.author: Rschagrin
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: Definitely something to see. In the complex where Ho Chi Minh's stilt house is located and his Mausoleum.Unique that it is built on 1 pillar.

reviews.author: Gillian V
reviews.title: Praying for babies
reviews.content: Predictably rather crowded with tourists, this little pagoda was built in thanksgiving for a royal child, so people still come to pray for a baby. Visitors should respect this and make way for these folk.

reviews.author: Dilimdi
reviews.title: Nothing much
reviews.content: It is literally a one pillar pagoda in the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex, nothing much to see. You could just drop by to see and leave.

reviews.author: aaong86
reviews.title: One pillar temple
reviews.content: Understand this temple has a quite a long history. It's very popular among the locals as well as tourists. You will definitely see this temple when you are visiting Ho Chi Minh mausoleum.

reviews.author: cnomis
reviews.title: small but beautiful
reviews.content: near to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum complex , this place attracts a lot of visitors who all want to tread the steps taking selfies on the steps as they go which can make it a little precarious, however its worth the struggle up the steps past these people to admire the shrine and all its beauty

reviews.author: ruhi
reviews.title: Small but worth the time
reviews.content: The place is located right next to the Ho Chi Minh Museum. Very peaceful place, surrounded with several shops, access to pay and use washroom (not very clean unfortunately). Dress code is important, do not wear shorts and cover shoulders to demonstrate respect to the holy place.

reviews.author: AshakUn N
reviews.title: Still in One piller
reviews.content: Though it was rebuild but its in one piller. Just beside the Ho Chi Minh Musoliam inHanoi. Original must be more beautiful.

reviews.author: goodguyjas
reviews.title: Small but iconic Buddhist Temple
reviews.content: Mere tourists like me perhaps don’t get all the fuss about this small Pagoda aloft its one pillar. But this site is an important part of Vietnamese history so worth respect and a proper look. It’s part of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex so you will come across it on your tour or walkabout. Not sure if it needs its own review as judging by other reviews it is a bit underwhelming when you see it. Still it is worth climbing the steps and admiring the shrine and its elaborate decor. The surrounding pond looked a bit grubby when I was there. Perhaps it stands out in high season.

reviews.author: Gordo4037
reviews.title: Worth the 10 minutes
reviews.content: A small pagoda style temple designed to reflect a lotus flower. Nice little area with lots of souvenir shops about. Really only a 10 minute visit required.

reviews.author: gastronaut_11
reviews.title: Pretty insignificant
reviews.content: Didn't really get it. Small. Situated atop what could have been a motorway concrete support. Just walk round it within the Ho Chi Minh complex, take a photo, then move on. Hanoi has much more to offer.

reviews.author: williamkassel
reviews.title: Quick stop at the One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Yes it is an elevated Pagoda supported by one Pillar.  200 year old pagoda surrounded by pond.  Lots of people watching and is worth a quick visit.

reviews.author: HarveyCapeTown
reviews.title: Nice to see
reviews.content: Built in the 1800s over a lotus pond, it's a quaint pagoda with important symbolism and function. It's a 5 to 10-minute visit maximum and you have to compete with many others to climb up the stairs, but it's a nice place and you can sit in the park and just rest for a bit. It's part of the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum complex and close to the only paid toilets I came across in Vietnam!

reviews.author: SeeMoreLiveMore
reviews.title: Part of Ba Dinh Square complex ...
reviews.content: One of the key sites within the complex that includes many important buildings. Hordes of tourists, which can be a tad off-putting. However, this simple temple is really beautiful, and worthy of a visit. Important historically and many Vietnamese still worship there.

reviews.author: Nice smile@
reviews.title: I came here
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda. The temple has a unique architecture. I came here. I want to sit down and watch everyone

reviews.author: Akumuk
reviews.title: More than just a pillar!
reviews.content: This is a venue that is on the tourist track for those visiting Hanoi.  The Pagoda has its own unique history and the setting is well worth the effort to go and see it.  However the hidden gems to be found in the adjacent buildings leave the visitor gasping in wonder and awe.  They are a must as they hold the essence of the Country within their walls.

reviews.author: ALISON A
reviews.title: Beautiful gardens
reviews.content: It was warm, drizzly day and I had a few hours to kill. I headed off in the direction of the mausoleum. I'm not sure what I expected to find, but it was all so poignant and beautiful.  I was surprised at how formal the entry procedure was, but once inside it was easy to navigate.  You were corralled through the entire exhibit, until you found yourself at the pagoda.  The light that day did nothing to dampen its beauty.  There were koi in the pond below too.

reviews.author: Tran Quoc Tuan (Daniel)
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda - 1000 years old story
reviews.content: This is the symbol of Hanoi which you cant find in another places. It has a balance structre so although the pagoda's very big and the pillar's small, they can stay safe. That's a nice symbol of pagoda architecture in Vietnam. This pagoda is in the central Vietnamese Political Place so you can see many places related around.

reviews.author: Tshen S
reviews.title: One pillar temple
reviews.content: Not that easy to find, it took us awhile to find it, which is in the same block of the Ho Chi Minh National Museum... definitely is one of the highlights in the city... but a popular sight that is inevitably too crowded 😫😣😖

reviews.author: JenniSor
reviews.title: Well-hidden pagoda
reviews.content: The pagoda is hidden deep in the mausoleum complex and you can only reach it after a long walk. The place do not have anything special, you cannot go inside the pagoda,  only looking and taking picture from outside.

reviews.author: Dobanjare
reviews.title: A lot of things to see here
reviews.content: This place is located in Ba Dinh square. There’s also Mausoleum, temple , pond and this pagoda. It’s beautiful and unique.

reviews.author: LuShTa
reviews.title: Nice environment
reviews.content: One pillar pagoda is at the same location with Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. There is no entrance fees charges to visit one pillar pagoda. Worth a quick visit to the pagoda and surrounding area.

reviews.author: Anna
reviews.title: Must come
reviews.content: This is a very famous place in Hanoi. Mot Cot pagoda has a long history. A symbol of Vietnam culture

reviews.author: Kevin Stapleton
reviews.title: One pillar pagoda
reviews.content: Was in the garden next to Ho Chi Minh mausoleum. Worth a quick visit to the pagoda and surrounding area. Full of people wanting photos of the temple. Nice to take a couple of pictures for your visit.

reviews.author: Janka K
reviews.title: Tangerine threes in flowerpots decorating the place
reviews.content: One of the places that just surprice you. The stairs up to the payring place were decorated by beautiful tangerine threes in flowerpots. The whole place was green and naturally colorful. I recommend to go to visit the place after New Year, as I did.

reviews.author: Diverdanperth
reviews.title: Love Ba Dinh Square, the One Pillar Pagoda, but not the taxi scam
reviews.content: For a sense of this area by night, see my review for Ba Dinh Square, "Visit night AND day but beware the taxi scammers". This review continues that review: Two days after photographing the pink lotus and mausoleum by night, on the morning of our departure for Hoi An, our hotel flagged down a 'legitimate' taxi to take us to The One Pillar Pagoda - imagine our surprise at being dropped at Ba Dinh Square - we hadn't realised how close we'd been two nights earlier. In daylight hours, we had to go through security check points and metal detectors - it was quite a different experience to our 'casual' evening visit. Having reinforced our memories and added a few new ones, we had to get back to the hotel. At the southern end of the square, taxis were coming and going regularly. It had cost us 28 000 dong ($2) to get there in a metered taxi, so we grabbed the one that seemed to be at the front of the queue - this is where the taxi scam story begins: this 'taxi' drove past our hotel with us yelling at him to stop. We realised afterwards he's done it on purpose so we couldn't call for help. He pulled over about 200m down the road and I realised the taxi meter was reading 480 000 dong ($30) !!! YEP. We were in a car set up to LOOK like a taxi with the roof light, the meter, a badge on the side, BUT it was NOT A LEGITIMATE TAXI. My family had exited the taxi, we had a flight to catch, and as I argued, the driver just said, "NEW RATE after 12." I thought about it, I felt bitter about it, afterwards I wondered if I hadn't had the pressure of meeting the airport driver (who was waiting for us!) whether I might have opened the door and screamed, "Help, Police". I paid and was bitter about it for two days – it was an unnecessarily unpleasant end to our pleasant memories of Hanoi. There are similar stories all over Trip Advisor - BE WARNED.Hanoi police traffic-controllers could have an inspector standing at the southern end of Ba Dinh square discouraging these ‘illegitimate’ taxis - even seasoned travelers can be duped. I’ve read that the Vietnamese themselves believe they are a country full of thieves and don't trust each other; however, a flourishing tourism industry demands trust i.e. tourists can trust that the government is doing what it can to stamp out the 'illegitimate' thievery, and the government trusts that the flood of foreign money entering the country in the pockets of tourists will grow. The lesson in Hanoi is: wait for a GREEN Mai Linh TAXI.A few days later in Hoi An, I happily coughed up 600 000 dong in a spur of the moment transaction beside a rice paddy; my entire family sat on a water buffalo in memory of a favourite childhood story about a water buffalo called 'Dahbitse’. Only then, did I finally release the tension the taxi incident had caused in me. I'd spent as much as I'd lost on an experience I valued and was happy to pay it.

reviews.author: Jalal Iqbal
reviews.title: unique
reviews.content: simple and small pagoda. very unique and beautiful. located within the Ho Chi Min complex and u need to follow the security check-up while entering in. over all a unique pagoda and u gonna like it.

reviews.author: JnVSydney
reviews.title: Nice for a rest
reviews.content: Located within the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex it is a nice place to have a rest in between walking/exploring the complex. This is a pretty pagoda designed to represent a blossoming lotus flower, we could see that. Worth a look when in the area

reviews.author: sudeep912
reviews.title: worship
reviews.content: this one pillar pagoda is very ancient and is worshiped for begetting children by childless couple. no shoes inside.

reviews.author: Wanderlusting888
reviews.title: Time to rest
reviews.content: After coming out of the mausoleum we headed to the one pillar pagoda. Kind of complicated directions to find initially but glad we went. It’s a lovely little area with a small lake and the pagoda. Tours come in and swarm the area and some of the Chinese tourists were pretty aggressive (ironic considering it’s a place of worship essentially) but they are only there for a few minutes before they are moved on to their next stop. It’s nice to grab some fetch fruit from the vendors selling there and sit at one of the benches and watch the world pass by.

reviews.author: kpiddy
reviews.title: Be respectful and remove your shoes
reviews.content: This beautiful small pagoda located in the near vicinity of Ho Chi Minh Mausoluem is free to visit but please read the sign and do as it asks and be respectful, 'Remove your shoes', we see so many ignoring the sign or not observing others while they were removing their shoes.  The pagoda is said to resemble a lotus flower, it stands on a pillar over a small pond partially filled with water, a short staircase can be climbed for free leading you up to the temple where it is possible to pray or view the alter.

reviews.author: Angela P
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: This pagoda looked so pretty in the photos before we got there.In reality it is tiny- run down - and not worth spending time on it. sorry

reviews.author: Kalpana D
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda- See a lotus bloom
reviews.content: Peaceful and tranquil. One point of interest is a bo tree that grows behind the pagoda. It is said to be an offshoot of the one under which Buddha became enlightened.The tree was given as a gift from India.

reviews.author: Laura T
reviews.title: just far far too crowded, in our opinion the entire Ho Chi Minh Complex is simply over-rated
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is part of the Ho Chi Minh Complex, located near the lake in the gardens of the Presidential Palace, along with The Outbuildings, The Stilted House, The Bunker and the nearby The Mausoleum. I had read that this was 'a place of contemplation, prayer and peace', however this was certainly not the case with the hundreds of tourists everywhere! Located within a small man made lake and up a small number of steps - if you can be bothered to battle the crowds to get close, which we could not.

reviews.author: Cheryl S
reviews.title: Beautiful Pagoda
reviews.content: We saw this on our city tour and it was very interesting. It is a beautiful building and it is amazing that it is all built around one pillar into the lake.

reviews.author: Vivien
reviews.title: Unqiue
reviews.content: Nice structure and history! Pretty unique structure! Its right behind the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum! Could visit if you're in the area!

reviews.author: Berenice A
reviews.title: Good opportunity to see and listen to a locals Buddhist temple prayers Nice park to walk
reviews.content: An interesting historical spot to visit. One pillar pagoda seems to be a small Buddhist temple on top of a pond. People climb the stair to reach its altar and pray. There are several benches in the surrounding quiet park. But the most interesting place is a larger Buddhist temple before the One Pillar Pagoda. Don't miss going inside its porch from where you might be able to catch a chants Buddhist prayer by the locals. Its altar is very ornamented and astonishing.

reviews.author: Arty1st
reviews.title: Unless you are Buddhist - avoid
reviews.content: The pagoda is in the grounds of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum so the visit is not a waste of time, but really 5 mins is plenty for most people.The site is very uninspiring. The pagoda is small, rebuilt (so not old at all) and the "pillar" is modern day solid concrete.

reviews.author: Chi C
reviews.title: Amazing trip
reviews.content: Lovely place, I have never seen a pagoda like that before I will come back with my friends. Really love VietNam

reviews.author: KeithNH2016
reviews.title: Pretty disappointing
reviews.content: This Pagoda is in the precinct of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. It is obviously of importance to the Vietnamese people but as a tourist attraction it is really disappointing.The original architecture is spoilt by what appears to be a modern concrete pier on which the very small timber structure is perched. the surrounding lake/moat was very low on water and the exposed banks were covered with litter and it looked very unkept.The day we visited there was no entry for viewing the interior. The whole experience was flat and the real life item does not live up to the brochure images.In our opinion not worth the walk.

reviews.author: veronica@
reviews.title: Famous temple
reviews.content: A famous temple in Hà Nội, this is a special temple in the world. This pagoda is associated with the history of the vietnammese people.

reviews.author: puchka
reviews.title: Interesting story
reviews.content: This one pillar Pagoda stands in the Mausoleum complex.  As the story goes the King built the Pagoda as Thanksgiving for birth of his son after a long time.  Hence it is associated with fertility.  Tourists offer flowers and incense stick praying for fertility.

reviews.author: Avinash Chandra A
reviews.title: Beautiful Architecture in the form of blooming Lotus
reviews.content: The pagoda is close to the presidential residence and Mausoleum and was built between 1028 and 1054 during kung My Thai Tong with prayers to have a child. The Pagoda is like giant lotus flower in bloom in the middle of a pond and supported on a single stone pillar. There is no entrance fee and visitors are expected to cover shoulders and legs as a mark of respect to the deity. The temple is said to bring bless us of fertility and health.

reviews.author: Batupahat1947
reviews.title: Pagoda overview
reviews.content: More like a very private pagoda. Slightly small for more or less people. Steep steps make ascending up to the prayer hall quite challenging to elderly. Otherwise very suitable for praying sessions

reviews.author: JSTrip_77
reviews.title: Beautiful and Interesting - Recently Rebuilt
reviews.content: Although this pagoda's history is long and storied, the current structure only dates from the 1950s and 1960s.  But that's only because the French destroyed the original on their way out of town. The first one was built in 1049 and then renovated in the 1100s. Either way, the pagoda is really beautiful. One the day that I visited, there were very few visitors. I think that the large groups of (mainly Chinese) tourists skip the pagoda and simply take a few pretty pictures. But, either way, I've never seen such a structure like this. Legend goes that it was the result of an ancient king's dream. It's certainly worth a look...

reviews.author: Heng How N
reviews.title: One pillar temple
reviews.content: It is situated on Chua Mot Cot, Ba Dinh district and behind Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. But the entrance is not behind it and has to walk one big round to go through secruity screening as the museum is besides it as well.The pagoda is going through renovation on the pond area. Don't know why it is called a pagoda but it is more a temple to me on top of one pillar.

reviews.author: TFonTA
reviews.title: Unusual
reviews.content: Took in the one pillar pagoda. We were lucky to find it free of crowds. I went up the steps to the shrine where some locals were praying and an artist drawing. Back on the ground I also visited one of the stalls nearby for a refreshing chilled coconut water, straight from the nut.

reviews.author: kawafamily
reviews.title: 普通 OK
reviews.content: ホーチミン廟に隣接する ホーチミンの家などがある有料エリアの中にあります。半パンやノースリブでは中には入れないので、拝みたい方は肌の露出の少ない服で。割と小さいので外から充分に見れます。It is a small temple you can see inside from outside.But if you wish to pray inside , must wear something cover your thighs and shoulders.

reviews.author: Ben G
reviews.title: Fascinating and stunning temple
reviews.content: An interesting pagoda within an amazing temple complex with intricate and detailed decorations. Well worth a visit while you are in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Naina-Damani
reviews.title: TRANQUIL BUDDHIST TEMPLE
reviews.content: Most historic beautiful Buddhist temple rising from one pillar in the centre of an elegant square shaped lotus flower from the pond.

reviews.author: Hoaido
reviews.title: The architecture
reviews.content: Its architecture is very special. It was built based on the dream of King Ly Thai Tong of the reign Ly.

reviews.author: UNNIMAYA
reviews.title: Worth a quick peek when you visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: Situated in the complex housing Museum and Uncle Ho's residence and gardens , this unique pagoda is a small buddhist temple initially built in 1049 is worth a quick peek although you may not be very impressed by the size. The lines to go up could be long - in which case you just take your pics standing below.

reviews.author: AH79_NL
reviews.title: Visit when around
reviews.content: The story of this Pagoda is worthwhile listening to, but the Pagoda itself is not as big as I expected. Although beautiful on the inside to see, I wouldn’t wait in line in case you have to. Come early and you might be lucky to hardly have any other tourists around.

reviews.author: knightjackie
reviews.title: Average and access a long walk
reviews.content: To get to this Pagoda you have to walk to the opposite side of the block and enter via security at the back of the museum.   Many maps show the correct location but you can only exit the area at that point.  Once you go through security there is about a 400 metre walk around the museum building to get to the pagoda.   On the way you pass a temple complex that was more interesting than the one pillar pagoda itself.   The pagoda is unique in structure but it bit small.

reviews.author: AquaticHawk
reviews.title: Not as exciting as it looks, but still interesting
reviews.content: You might be expecting something a bit bigger, but it isn't as big as you think. It's still very interesting, but it was probably better before the french colonial forces destroyed it. Apparently it was built to look like a lotus, but no longer looks like that because it was rebuilt.

reviews.author: shiraziwine
reviews.title: Did not like it
reviews.content: before i visit one pillar Pagoda i had this imagination that it should be a kind of master art or a wonder, but it is just a very small Pagoda in the middle of a pond with no attraction.but any way, it is the last thing you can visit in that complex

reviews.author: Wildcat7400
reviews.title: A Unique Pagoda
reviews.content: It is located in Ba Dinh Square & next to Ho Chi Minh’s house on stilts.  It is a Buddhist temple & one of Vietnam’s most iconic temples.  The pagoda was built in 1049 during the reign of Emperor Ly Thai Tong of the Ly Dynasty.  Accordingly, the Emperor was childless for a long time. But he dreamt that he was given a baby boy & not long after, his wife became pregnant.  Thus, it could be said that the temple was built out of gratitude & its structure was similar to what he had seen in his dream.  From a single pillar in the middle, the Buddhist temple was built on a square shape platform constructed in the middle of a pond to resemble a lotus flower.  There are steps going up to the temple & in the temple lies a shrine.  The French army had damaged the structure in 1954.  However, restorations have been made in 1955.  Offerings can be made for those who wish to do so but please dress appropriately as a sign of respect.

reviews.author: blackeaglejim
reviews.title: a Hanoi icon
reviews.content: The One-Pillar Pagoda is one of the icons of Hanoi, rivaling the Turtle Tower in Hoàn Kiếm Lake.  Originally built in the 11th century Lý Dynasty, it is the most unusual religious structure in the city.  The shrine is barely three square meters and perches on a tall pillar in the middle of a small pond.  The shape was intended to resemble a lotus, the favorite flower of Buddhists.  A concrete staircase provides access to the temple now, but in the past, both originally and after its periodic renovations, the wooden pillar was about twice as high and the temple staircase, also wooden was higher and steeper.  In a last act of cultural vandalism, the French blew up the pagoda as they were departing Hanoi in 1954.  The new Vietnamese government rebuilt it, but not as high, and with a pillar of concrete rather than wood.       It doesn’t take long to appreciate the One-Pillar Pagoda and for many visitors it’s a stopover on the way to the Hồ Chí Minh Museum or the Mausoleum.  However, the neighborhood is interesting in the other direction, back towards the old quarter or to the Temple of Literature.  Many embassies and government offices are located around here, in what were once colonial mansions designed by Vietnamese architects in the 1930s.  In a variation of the Indochinese Style, they differ from the earlier colonial buildings like the present-day Presidential Palace and Ministry of Finance.

The wooden pagoda sits on a single stone pillar in an elegant lotus pond.During the time of our visit in February it was overcrowded and exceptionally cold!

reviews.author: Seevali D

The pagoda as in the dream resembles a lotus flower in and coming out of the surface of water.  There are live lotus flowers in the water around the pagoda too.   I wish I could make my dreams come true!!You pass this unique structure when you come out of the gates of Ho Chi Ming Mausoleum.  It is almost next to it.  Do not miss it if you visit the Mausoleum.  Although small in size, the Architecture here is quite distinctive and unique in that the Pagoda sits on a single large stone pillar.  The pagoda is also historic having been constructed 17centuries ago in the first century a.d.This is a place of veneration for Vietnamese Buddhists.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Dreams Come True
reviews.content: Legend has it that Emperor Ly Thai Tong, (1028-1054) was childless, but had a dream where he was handed a baby son while seated on a lotus flower.   He married a peasant girl and she bore him the son of his dream.Th emperor then built the temple in thanks for his son, and constructed it in the middle of a lotus pond, similar to the one of his dream.The temple is built of wood on a single stone pillar, hence its popular name of One Pillar Pagoda.

reviews.author: Ernest W
reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.content: Previous to my visit, I had read that this sight may seem underwhelming to some. Well, low and behold, that is exactly the feeling I got when I saw it. Yes, it is built on one single pillar. But the construction seems so cheap that probably anyone can do it. Just go find a phone pole or a freeway pillar with nothing on top of it. Place a square wooden board on top of it. Then construct some walls and a little cute sloping roof and poof! You have yourself a one pillar pagoda. The cheapness was actually highlighted by the observation that the pillar itself resembles a concrete pillar used to support a freeway. There was nothing decorative or aesthetic about it. Under the pagoda roof was an altar that was also highly underwhelming. Overall, take a gander if you happen to be in the area. But don't make a special trip just to see it. You will for sure be disappointed. Also, if you wear shorts, make sure your shorts cover your knees. I saw a couple try to walk up the stairs. The guy was wearing knee length shorts. The girl was wearing mini shorts. Needless to say, she got yelled at by the cleaning lady.

reviews.author: 203pawelb
reviews.title: Little, beautiful and free to visit
reviews.content: Chua Mot Cot or the One Pillar one of Hanoi’s icons, worth a quick visit. Constructed by Emperor Ly Thai Tong in AD 1049. As a symbol of his gratitude to Goddess of Mercy for giving him a son. Over the centuries Pagoda has been damaged and reconstructed numerous times last time after being destroyed by French in 1954. “Modern” pagoda is built from wood and as the name suggests, on a single stone pillar, standing in a small pond. It’s an example of a beautiful architecture. The little shrine is located inside the pagoda which can be accessed via stone steps. Pagoda is often visited by tourist but also by local people to take prayers throughout the day. Therefore, appropriate attire should be worn if you are entering the temple; The One Pillar Pagoda is situated in the park behind Ho Chi Minh mausoleum (5min walk) open daily and free to visit.  There is a couple of stalls nearby with souvenirs and refreshments.  Before you leave the take time to visit the Dien Huu Pagoda which is located close by with a courtyard full of bonsai trees or Bo tree that grows behind the pagoda which legend says is an offshoot of the tree under which Buddha became enlightened.

reviews.author: Ami7878
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Nice pagoda with an historical background. Nice area. Quiet neighborhood. You can even have here a break and ask people about the history of this pagoda: they will willingly tell you.

reviews.author: currie4743
reviews.title: Beautiful and iconic spot
reviews.content: This is on the the complex of the Ho Chi Minh’s mausoleum. I didn’t get that part when I first read about it as something to see in Hanoi. I recognized it as we were standing in line to see the mausoleum and we paid the fee to go back into the park after seeing the mausoleum. It is small but serene. I think reading up on the historic significance would help to better understanding why it’s worth seeing.

reviews.author: cwfan
reviews.title: Iconic pagoda
reviews.content: Situated near the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum it is a replica of the original one.  Locals praying here believe it will invoke well-beings and properity.

reviews.author: hannostamm
reviews.title: A must-see but don't expect too much
reviews.content: Of course this pagoda is an important part of the history of Ha Noi and I really liked visiting when I first moved to Ha Noi 20 years ago.Today, it is surrounded by souvenir stands and absolutely awash in noisy and pushy tour groups. Do go but pick your time wisely.

reviews.author: Gidons51
reviews.title: Very small , very symbolic
reviews.content: A very small Buddhist pagoda ,staying only in one pillar. Built in the 11 century by the emperor. According to legend , people come here to pray for the birth of their son .

reviews.author: Adventure beyond imagination
reviews.title: Unique and extraordinary
reviews.content: One of the most popular sites for all Hanoi tourists. Very unique and extraordinary but overcrowded the most of time.

reviews.author: TheExplorerFamily
reviews.title: Meaningful, but Not Memorable
reviews.content: After reading so much about this one-of-a-kind Pagoda, we were expecting something much larger, but it turned out to be a tiny and quaint, but charming Buddha Shrine on the top of a single pillar, set within a lotus and fish – filled pond. The Temple on the top is made of wood, and people who want sons, or want to say a prayer for their sons, climb up a few steps and say a prayer.The construction is unusual. It was built about a 1000 years ago, and resembles a lotus flower – signifying purity in Buddhism. It was the tiniest Buddha temple we have visited, but it forms a lovely backdrop for a memorable photo. The Gardens around it are part of the palace, and are lovely. There is an entire row of street-food tents where people seemed to relax after their visit to the shrine. We were told that this place holds a revered spot in the hearts of the Vietnamese. There is no need to spend too much time here. You will pass it anyway while exiting the Ho Chi Minh Palace Grounds, so you can say that you were really there.

reviews.author: Chonee
reviews.title: OK
reviews.content: It was a nice Pagoda, however in my opinion not one of the best.  Near the HCM Mausoleum/Presidential Palace but a tad bit tucked so just looked around if you don't see immediately.  Worth the visit but was honestly expecting more.

reviews.author: BLtrvl
reviews.title: Interesting replica structure near HCM mausoleum
reviews.content: Tucked around the corner from the mausoleum, this is a beautifully restored pagoda. A nice shaded area to get out of the afternoon sun.

reviews.author: Esther R
reviews.title: Peacefull
reviews.content: One of most famous place to visit. Its around the hochiminh complex. Many people would like to come for pray and pay respect to their God.

reviews.author: Twoyorkie
reviews.title: different
reviews.content: the famous 1 pillar pagoda ...  photo oportunities are loads in the region and yet anther eyeopening place to visit in 'Nam

reviews.author: LazyRose
reviews.title: Interesting Structure
reviews.content: If you're in the area already (like for the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum/park) then it's worth stopping by. We were here in the afternoon and it was extremely busy, so much so that we didn't want to wait to go inside. It's unique and different from other pagodas that I have seen, so it was worth seeing, but as an attraction in its own right - I'd say you don't need to make a special trip unless you're already nearby.

reviews.author: XavierBB
reviews.title: Hard to find!
reviews.content: It took me a lot of time to find it! although I asked several times. It is easy to find when you enter the park where it is located, but I walked in front of the park's gate several times up and down until I realized that I had to get into the park.When you find it, it is nice to see it and the sorrounding atmosphere.

reviews.author: VIP29
reviews.title: Cultural Awakening
reviews.content: Beautiful architecture and explanation of the various little structures within this venue. Amazing culture kept alive to this day.

reviews.author: dlamtran
reviews.title: A little over rated.
reviews.content: By all mean this is a very popular place to visit by foreigner.  Too crowded and not much to see but I would not miss it if you are planning to visit Ha Noi.

reviews.author: JohanVanGreuning
reviews.title: Vietnam Family Holiday - Hanoi
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is a historic Buddhist temple in Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam. It is regarded alongside the Perfume Temple, as one of Vietnam's two most iconic temples.

reviews.author: Dreemotrua
reviews.title: Peaceful pagoda
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is one of the most iconic temples in Vietnam, situated in Hanoi, it was built by Emperor Ly Thai Tong in honour of the Lady Buddha. Emperor Ly Thai of the Ly dynasty had been longing for a son, he had a dream where he envisioned a baby son lying on a lotus leaf. Shortly after this dream, he was blessed with a son, and in gratitude he commissioned the building of this temple. It is located on a single concrete pillar. Inside is a shrine that is dedicated to Lady Buddha, also known as Quan Am and the Goddess of Mercy. The pond is located in a peaceful area with benches around to sit in quiet contemplation.

reviews.author: Topman4
reviews.title: Good attraction.
reviews.content: We visited as part of a walking tour with a guide and found this place very interesting. It’s very busy but worth the experience. Only about £3 to visit.

reviews.author: Paul h
reviews.title: Ok but not worth a special visit
reviews.content: This is in the gardens of the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and although a little different it wasn’t exactly that interesting but as you are already in the gardens have a look

reviews.author: Cekeysh
reviews.title: Just that
reviews.content: Really just small built temple on the water, supported with one pillar, you can hike up in less than ten second, see the gods in another ten second and go down in another less than ten second. Please dont scold me, but I was not understand.

reviews.author: Andy F
reviews.title: Worth Visiting
reviews.content: Quaint little Buddhist shrine atop a single pillar, set within a fish-filled pond.  You can climb up the steps & look right inside the (active) shrine itself.  Very photogenic.  Fairly old, but variously damaged & restored.  Complete contrast to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum just around the corner.

reviews.author: Lisa W
reviews.title: Good for a quick stop over!
reviews.content: This is a charming, ornate small wooden pagoda built over a lotus pond that you can enter and pray if you wish just walk the steps but make sure first you are dressed appropriately as you will not be allowed to enter.Lovely back story to the building of the pagoda by an emperor after bearing a son. Worth a visit but you don’t need to leave much time as there is not a lot to see.

reviews.author: Andrea W
reviews.title: Pouring with rain but still nice
reviews.content: We did a gallop along past Mausoleum, Presidential palace, HCM memorial and ended up here. It's a pretty place, though it was hard to see that because of the weather. Very unusual pagoda construction. The Vietnamese hold a great reverence for all these areas.

reviews.author: tibet71
reviews.title: This is the signature of Hanoi.
reviews.content: You can't visit Hanoi without visiting one pillar pagoda. It is a must, because it is part of history. The temple is very small, but it has been restored and you can walk up the step to pay your respect.

reviews.author: mkh77
reviews.title: Quick stop
reviews.content: This is worth a short 5 minute visit if you are walking around the area. It is a lovely small pagoda which you can walk around the perimeters of. Dueto it's proximity to the mausoleum it gets very crowded

reviews.author: Tony H
reviews.title: Temple in Pagoda
reviews.content: There is a small temple housing a wooden god in the pagoda. Many people Q to take photo and to play respect the god. It is made of wooden and you can spend 10mins here/

reviews.author: DAVID L
reviews.title: Special Pagoda ...
reviews.content: Charming small pagoda near Ho Chi Minh Memorial which has great significance to the Vietnamese people - dress appropriately for it. Interesting history and legend surrounding it. Enjoy.

reviews.author: Roland I
reviews.title: short stop
reviews.content: interesting Pagoda.  great spot for pictures.  I wish there was a little more information about the history of this place. Be aware that if you want to go up to see inside you have to have your shoulders covered and no shorts.

reviews.author: Grandvisitor
reviews.title: Thought this was over rated.
reviews.content: We had visited many temples and pagodas so were probably over these attractions. The pagoda has significance to Vietnamese people but I found it of little interest. Because it was in the vicinity of the presidential palace and Ho Chi Minhs various residences we visited but wouldn't go again for choice.

reviews.author: Evelynne G
reviews.title: Interesting story about this Pagoda
reviews.content: Four of us went on a tour that encompassed this one Pillar Memorial It was interesting to learn the story of the meaning behind the original one. It has been restored however

reviews.author: JEKOnthego
reviews.title: Adjacent to the grounds of the Presidential site
reviews.content: This is known as Lady Buddha Temple and is in the grounds adjacent to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and Presidential Site.  Dress appropriately and climb the steps to the Pagoda.  Very small overhanging a lake.

reviews.author: SueL41589
reviews.title: Make sure to dress appropriately
reviews.content: You must have clothing that covers your knees and your shoulders otherwise you are denied entrance to this attraction.  It was very crowded when we were there.

reviews.author: ShariWestSussex
reviews.title: read the wall of punishments for certain behaviours
reviews.content: The king was blessed with a son after years of barrenness so built this pagoda in homage. People come here to pay and queue to walk up the steps. It felt wrong to get in the queue just to gawk so we watched from a far.The most interesting aspect for us was the wall where graphic picture show you what will happen if you behave in certain ways. Rather like parables. Some were amusing.Again if you are going up the stairs be respectful and cover knees and shoulders.

reviews.author: Tony M
reviews.title: Quick site when at Ho Chi Minh Mausaleum/Temple of Literature area
reviews.content: Worth the quick step over here if you are in the area. Not anything fancy, but nice backdrop. Complete with Coi pond and gift shops/stalls.

reviews.author: hogsted
reviews.title: not much to see
reviews.content: it was a pagoda, and you see a number of those in Vietnam, this one was small, but of course different resting on only one leg. Close to Ho chi minh mausuleum. So from there it takes not much efford to see it.

reviews.author: cool_satchmo
reviews.title: Nothing special about this pagoda
reviews.content: Apart from the fact that the pagoda is built on one triangular pillar, there is nothing special about this place. It is a place of worship and therefore we need to respect it. However, from a touristic viewpoint, there is not much to see here. It is next to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and therefore tourists visit both places together

reviews.author: Shaz1000
reviews.title: Cute little pagoda, but treat with respect
reviews.content: This is a religious place so shorts are not allowed.  It is rater quaint and interesting and well worth a look.

reviews.author: kerrie212
reviews.title: wow
reviews.content: this is a must but was very busy we still got to take photos and see everything this is another place to cover up ladys out of respect.

reviews.author: Ian D
reviews.title: A curiosity, but well worth a look
reviews.content: A curiosity, but well worth a look. Too many others trying desperately to get photos. So pleased that no artificial light was in use.

reviews.author: TheTopTier
reviews.title: One Pillar, Too Busy
reviews.content: We came along here after visiting the Presedential Palace area.  Despite the heavy monsoonal rain this area was extremely busy and impossible to get any good photos a a result.  The queue into the Pagoda didn't seem worth it.

reviews.author: Tangoj63
reviews.title: Worth a look if in the area
reviews.content: Don’t wear shorts above the knee or you won’t be allowed into the temple part.  You can get into the garden area OK

reviews.author: trisy65
reviews.title: Interesting place but not too impressive
reviews.content: This attraction is somewhat underwhelming. Nice area surrounding and quite near to Ho Chi Minh’s testing place. There are some tourist shops selling goods and the area had clean toilets. It was nice visiting on a cool day

reviews.author: Lotus312
reviews.title: Interesting building
reviews.content: This is one of Vietnam's most iconic temples and was interesting to see and is still in excellent condition. It is in a tranquil garden setting but our visit was unfortunately spoiled by a very overzealous woman, who seemed to be assembling and/or selling joss sticks, opposite the steps up to see inside the pagoda.  She yelled if you looked at her, tried to take any photos of anything and even leapt up the stairs to yell at some other unfortunate tourists, who didn't appear to have done anything wrong!  Such a shame to have, what should have been a peaceful visit, shattered by this woman's actions.

reviews.author: GMW
reviews.title: The interest is the story behind the Pagoda
reviews.content: I visited in Oct 2017 as a solo visitor.The story behind the reason for the Pagoda and why it is built on one pillar helps to appreciate the Pagoda.It is worth stopping by if you are touring around the city - but probably not worth a visit just to see this and nothing else.

reviews.author: MattC1995
reviews.title: Pretty and worth seeing
reviews.content: For something that is free, this little Pagoda is worth a visit, especially if you're visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum next door. The beautiful decorative features of it are nice on a warm and sunny day.

reviews.author: bankim_ms
reviews.title: Very hyped place
reviews.content: One pillar pagoda is a very hyped place. Can be avoided. Nothing great about the place. Though it is old

reviews.author: Patrick B
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Interesting but not overly exciting. Would be of interest to those who practice buddhism and have an interest in it's history.

reviews.author: mhlee1990
reviews.title: A relatively small pagoda
reviews.content: A relatively small pagoda which resembles the shape of a blossom lotus flower. Within walking distance to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and Ho Chi Minh Museum. Worth to pay a visit but do not put high expectation.

reviews.author: Viv A
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: Another temple and of interest to many people, it came about by a dream. Lots of little stores at this site

reviews.author: Ray M
reviews.title: The Lotus Pagoda
reviews.content: A simple structure with religious and folkloric connotations - that is, if you desire a Son, this is the place to wish for it. Walking distance from the HCM Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Thảo Vy N
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: This is the most famous pagoda in Vietnam. The enterring is free. With the unique architecture was built in many years ago, this pagoda is the one of symbols to present Vietnam Capital. Its free for visit. The place is near HoChiMinh's Mausoleum

reviews.author: Peter H
reviews.title: A worthwhile diversion
reviews.content: This is an interesting cultural site in the Ho Chi Min complex. Not good enough to go out of your way for, but close to the House on Stilts, the Ho chi Min museum, the presidential palace, and the associated temples.There is a good arts and crafts market nearby for those who like their souvenirs

reviews.author: MarLyn007
reviews.title: One pillar padoga
reviews.content: A site that was included in our tour. Our guide told us about its history; very interesting and well preserved

reviews.author: moshiyana
reviews.title: Iconic Pagoda in Ha Noi
reviews.content: This is a pretty attraction because of its uniqueness. It is actually a temple so anyone who wants to visit must wear modest clothes. No entrance fees needed.

reviews.author: Carol R
reviews.title: A Lovely Pagoda.
reviews.content: A nice pagoda in a very tranquil setting, the pond around it is filled with poi fish, A beautiful Buddhist pagoda.

reviews.author: kat
reviews.title: Old, nice to see
reviews.content: Old pagoda next to Ho Chi Minh museum and around the corner from presidential palace.Not much to look at really, small. No info boards around to tell you. One wall around the little lake it's in has fully collapsed and no sign of repairing it which is a shame. Lots of market sellers to tourists here which detracts from the pagoda

reviews.author: khm2412
reviews.title: Attractive Religious Site
reviews.content: We visited as part of a full day Hanoi tour. Interesting architecture and very photogenic.  It is essential to wear modest clothing to visit the pagoda.

reviews.author: Iara Errika P
reviews.title: Must Visit
reviews.content: The place is a must visit, but please make sure you are decently dressed. Wearing shorts are not allowed. The place can be easily reached and since it is near the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum it is heavily guarded.

reviews.author: John A
reviews.title: Buddhist temple monument
reviews.content: My guide also said that this is an icon of Vietnam.  Not much to discover as it sits on its own and you can get much of the information of this temple from a Google search.

reviews.author: Patsykennedy57
reviews.title: The Ladybird of Pagodas or Pagodas Made Simple!
reviews.content: The accessibility and centrality of this particular Pagoda is its real attraction. As the name suggests it lacks the complexity of many other pagodas. It is also in a busy tourist part of Hanoi and captures the essence of the vast array of pagodas to be seen throughout Vietnam. Definitely worth a visit as you won't get easier access to any other pagoda in Vietnam.

reviews.author: graham t
reviews.title: Interesting but!
reviews.content: This is a 19th century reconstruction of the original.  Not much to see that you cant see from a photo of the site.  I wold not go to see it if it were not next to Uncle Ho's Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Kamil B
reviews.title: Only if you have it on your path
reviews.content: Not qorth going only to see it. However it is near Cho Chi Minh mausoleum and his museum, so you can make some steps to see it.Original, small but no so amazing.

reviews.author: Jazzy1995
reviews.title: Lovely pagoda
reviews.content: Really pretty pagoda located near the Ho Chi Minh museum with a large pond at the bottom. Quite busy but a nice photo opportunity. To actually go inside the pagoda you need to be covered but nonetheless was very nice.

reviews.author: helgre2016
reviews.title: Tourist spot
reviews.content: Simple pagoda but you have to be "covered" including men to climb the steps. Not a lot to see set in a pleasant square where you can grab a little shade an refreshment

reviews.author: Jessie T
reviews.title: Unique design pagoda
reviews.content: Legend says that people who wishes to get pregnant can pray in this one pillar pagoda. Very unique structure and highly recommended.

reviews.author: apocalipse
reviews.title: nice xtra to a beautiful day
reviews.content: It was nice to see the Pagoda, it was crowed and people praying , the smell of the incense was divine ground clean and lots of green which makes it nice and also refreshing .

reviews.author: TravellingVolup
reviews.title: Beautiful Legend, Disappointing in Reality
reviews.content: I had great interest in the One Pillar Pagoda after reading the legend behind it's inception.  Having been originally built by Emperor Ly Thai Tong so long ago based on a dream and in gratitude for a son, I felt a sense of compassion and awe.  However, upon entering the temple area, I was struck by how different it looked from all of the images I had imagined or seen.  Not the actual structure of the Pagoda, that was beautiful.  But, the area seemed to be really in need of some care and I couldn't make out the square shaped lotus pond as having real connection because of this. Maybe it was the stark contrast directly next to the well kept Presidential area that included a huge sign saying, 'No Gum'.  I am not sure if the rain is the cause of this, but the waters were gloomy and muddy with the fish seeming to gasp for air; yet, it also seemed that there wasn't enough water.  There were a lot of visitors when we went and maybe this made it seem more difficult to appreciate- as there were also stalls and shops selling drinks and other items that were loud.  It was not as I thought it would be offering a space of quiet contemplation; however, the steps leading to the Buddhist Deity, Quan Am, were easy enough to navigate and people were respectful and quiet.  I am glad that we did visit, though.  It would have been a shame to miss this special site for Hanoi.

reviews.author: Vjay S
reviews.title: Good place to visit
reviews.content: Slightly away from the old quarter, better if you take a taxi (beware of swindlers). Beautiful place though it's small and over run by tourists. Beautiful temple at the top, def walk up the few steps and take a look. Nothing else much around there besides the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Neraj W
reviews.title: Nice to see
reviews.content: Since it is located close to the Ho chin Minh mausoleum it is worth swinging by.  It is not worth going all the way just to see this but given its close proximity to all the other tourist attractions it's a nice to see.

reviews.author: 190748JoF
reviews.title: Nice to see if passing
reviews.content: A unique pagoda but in my opinion needs a bit of TLC the area around it is in a state of disrepair. It's in the presidential grounds, I'm glad we saw it but also glad we didn't make a special hornet just to see this. Steps slippy when wet so be careful

reviews.author: AlexanderF85
reviews.title: Beautiful Unique Pagoda
reviews.content: We visited this one of a kind Pagoda while on a tour at the Ho Chi Minh Memorial. It is very different from other pagoda's visited. Even the Buddha representation inside is unique. A must visit

reviews.author: Katrina B
reviews.title: Beautifully restored
reviews.content: Worth the visit.  It is beautifully restored  and you can climb the stairs to see the statue of Budha. It is still used today.

reviews.author: cmike1786
reviews.title: The unique pagoda!
reviews.content: This pagoda is really look like a beautiful picture. It locate in the middle of the lotus lake with the special architecture for one pillar.this is also famous for people come to pray and offer to god.

reviews.author: wildparadox
reviews.title: Worth swinging by
reviews.content: It's a nice, quick, stop if you're in the area, but not worth going out of your way for. There are a few other things nearby you can walk to too, so pick a couple to check out at once.

reviews.author: minimize940314
reviews.title: meaningful, but not spectacular
reviews.content: This temple was built about 1000 years ago. It resembles lotus flower which represents purity in Buddhism. It was destroyed by french and then rebuilt afterward.

reviews.author: Catkin31
reviews.title: Quaint
reviews.content: The one pillar pagoda is within the Presidential palace complex and is quite picturesque.There is a sign about attire which says no shorts and as I had a knee length skirt on I thought I would be able to climb the steps up to the pagoda but no, I was stopped and directed to some coats for hire which I declined. Funny how a "local" was allowed to go up the steps in some very short shorts!!

reviews.author: MHeredia
reviews.title: Picturesque
reviews.content: The name is way cooler than it really is. There is also a line to get up to it. Don't wait in line. Just take a picture from anywhere and that is sufficient. The inside is very small and looks like every other temple. It is in the Ho Chi Minh Complex so you will see it if you visit the Mausoleum or the Presidential Place.

reviews.author: Mun Onn L
reviews.title: Personally, it wasn't interesting.
reviews.content: Let me preface this by saying this is my personal view and it depends a lot on personal tastes. I found this Pagoda to be very small and not interesting at all.I could see many who went there to offer prayers. So perhaps for them, it was a more meaningful experience.

reviews.author: JanaK123
reviews.title: Good Photo
reviews.content: This was, for us anyway, simply a photo opp while walking through the HCM palace gardens. If you are there anyway, definitely go buy and take a picture.

reviews.author: Guna R
reviews.title: Not impressed
reviews.content: I went there expecting something big or unique. But the pagoda didn't impress me at all. It looked very basic to me. But then, this might be due to my high expectations. You won't miss much if you skip this one.

reviews.author: Wanderlusterer17
reviews.title: Within Presidential Palace Grounds
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is within Presidential Palace Grounds. It is a Buddhist temple. It was destroyed during the war and later rebuilt.

reviews.author: Gregory B
reviews.title: Holiday visit
reviews.content: Visited this as it was withing walking distance of our hotel and the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum was closed. Usual street hawkers abound as well as people trying to get you to get a suit  or shirts made. One of the walls around the small moat that surrounds the Pagoda had collapsed. Must wear trousers (legs covered up) to go up to the Pagoda - as I found out.

reviews.author: CookieBaby2010
reviews.title: See it from the ground - very small
reviews.content: Not awed by this, but many went up to offer prayers.  It is a very small structure and you can see everything without going up the stairs - too crowded if you have many praying at the top.

reviews.author: CYY_sg
reviews.title: Can pop by as part of the visit to Ho Chi Minh Museum
reviews.content: Small shrine standing only on one single structural column, which is its unique feature. Since you will already be in the vicinity for the HCM Museum, you might as well drop by anyway.

reviews.author: kamran1975
reviews.title: So so
reviews.content: Not an individual destination for tourists, as a part of a package, worth to see it after mausoleum, citadel and temple of literature.

reviews.author: MichaelDolgy
reviews.title: trip to Vietnam
reviews.content: Very nice historical place, you can feel ancient Vietnam where. you can hear how monks are praying and lot of local souvenirs around.

reviews.author: Robert Q
reviews.title: Disipointing
reviews.content: Part of the Ho Chi Minh complex, it is worthwhile to see as part of a larger tour or visit, but certainly not worth the effort to see by itself.  Unique, but with more souvenir shops than charm.

reviews.author: QuinnyGG
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: In the grounds of the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum so worth visiting this unusual structure if you go there. Only ladies can climb the stairs.

reviews.author: SidneyFace
reviews.title: Try and go when the lotus flowers are out
reviews.content: This Pagoda was a little underwhelming when compared with other Pagoda's and Temple's in Hanoi.  When we visited the lotus ponds had been emptied.  Apparently it is stunning when these ponds are in place

reviews.author: lbhcys
reviews.title: Nice attraction but more maintenance needed
reviews.content: Being one of the main attractions in Hanoi, I was surprised to see that maintenance was lacking in the compound. One stretch of the wall surrounding the pond has collapsed and that part sealed off with raffia string. The pond water was brownish-green and the beautiful lilies as seen in other pictures are nowhere to be found. Weeds have taken root all around the walls of the pond. Not picture worthy at all. I was there in mid-June 2017. Hopefully maintenance have been carried out by the time you visit there.

reviews.author: Mel B
reviews.title: A must see for tourists to Hanoi
reviews.content: A must see for tourists to Hanoi. Close to the mausoleum and Ho Chi Minh museum. Pagodas are a very traditional sight in Vietnam and they are all over the place. This one is the only one built on one pillar. Pretty gardens around.

reviews.author: NathaPushpa d
reviews.title: Never seen a 1 pillar pagoda before - June 2017
reviews.content: Excellent view of the one pillar pagoda. It was surrounded by a water pond full of lotus plants with blooming pink colour flowers. Very nice relaxing environment.There were some Buddha flags and statues I have seen inside.

reviews.author: Nigel R
reviews.title: Unique
