reviews.content: This unique Pagoda is part of the Ho Chi Minh complex and is worth visiting as part of your trip to the Mausoleum. There is not much to see otehr than its unique construction. My wife was able to go up to the alter, unlike me dressed in shorts, no regrets it was hot and humid.

reviews.author: grampsxpress
reviews.title: part of Ho Chi Min complex
reviews.content: found it hard to locate once inside complex, not a lot of english signage etc. heaps of people there on day i visited

reviews.author: vttraveler41
reviews.title: temple on cement
reviews.content: as most of the guide books say - this is really dopey - its a small pagoda sitting on a pillar of cement - clearly not the original - but tis adjacent to the Ho Chi Mien Museum and Mausoleum so stop by

reviews.author: Monika W
reviews.title: Great place to see in Hanoi
reviews.content: Fantastic place to wander around and take photos. You can sense the place is full of culture and history. Recommended!

reviews.author: Kelly W
reviews.title: Beautiful Must See!
reviews.content: Very unusual pagoda, which was built on only one pillar! Located in a very quiet & serene beautiful location, it is a great place to visit and enjoy!

reviews.author: Anil B
reviews.title: An ancient temple
reviews.content: It's a small temple but built 1000 years back and people have lot of faith in the shrine but nothing spectacular and can omit if short of time

reviews.author: Sonata_ResortandSpa
reviews.title: Unique Pagoda
reviews.content: It is like a Lotus locates on the lake. should visit in Ha Noi. Also it is a sacred and ancient pagoda

reviews.author: Barbara M
reviews.title: Not worth a trip on its own
reviews.content: but if you're visiting the Mausoleum anyway, then by all means walk past for a quick look on your way to the exit.

reviews.author: An C
reviews.title: Special constructuion!
reviews.content: There is nothing much special but the construction. I like to visit the old constrution of temple in my Hanoi trip.

reviews.author: Manny B
reviews.title: Tiny one pillar temple
reviews.content: Unless you are on the grounds of the Presidential Palace, it would be a waste of time and energy visiting this one pillar pagoda. This is a tiny Buddhist temple built on a single stone pillar. I understand that ladies need to cover bare shoulders, as this is a religious shrine. You may experience a line, as there is only one set of stairs leading up and down. One minute is all you need here.

reviews.author: Janet O
reviews.title: Pretty if you have time
reviews.content: We visited the One Pillar Pagoda and it was nice if you have excess time.  Rather than spending a day seeing the government buildings, the Opera House and the One Pillar Pagoda (all located in close proximity, I would spend the day going to Trang An, Tam Coc or the Perfume Pagoda.

reviews.author: BrakiWorldTraveler
reviews.title: Nice, but miniature
reviews.content: This miniature pagoda is situated at the exit of the Presidential palace complex. After passing a row of souvenir shops you'll notice it on your right hand side.The pagoda is set atop of a pillar which is stuck in a small rectangular pond. There's a line to climb few steps leading to it, it moves quickly, but you can also skip it, you won't miss much.

reviews.author: rodaholiday
reviews.title: Beautiful pagodA
reviews.content: Ladies need to cover arms. Walk up few steps and then you are  at a small temple with  amazing energy  which holds the female buddah.

reviews.author: gdown64
reviews.title: I thought it would be bigger
reviews.content: Due to its proximity to several other attractions it is worth an effort to see, especially if you can learn its story beforehand.It is a very quaint building but surprisingly small.

reviews.author: LovinLifesJourneys
reviews.title: Its a Tiny Little Temple
reviews.content: Still you must be respectfully covered and climb the stairs to see this little gem.  It is a part of the HCM park area in the Presidential Palace area where HCM raised home is and the park area lovely to walk about.  Don't miss it. It just takes 30 seconds to see but worth a peek.

reviews.author: 368stephenn
reviews.title: Pillar Temple
reviews.content: This small temple set art the rear of the Presidential palace, and near the houses and Museum of Ho Chi Minh is very interesting to see

reviews.author: Daty L
reviews.title: Symbol of ancient Hanoi
reviews.content: A must visit attraction upon visiting Hanoi. This is a unique temple all around Asia and well-known sight seeing place to traveler all around the world. Also, the place nearby Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum and President Palace.

reviews.author: Feen63
reviews.title: A little diapoointing
reviews.content: Not a bad attraction, but if you have experienced the many pagodas in asia then this one is nothing special to the eye.

reviews.author: Louisa M
reviews.title: One of Vietnam's iconic temples
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is said to represent a lotus flower growing out of water.  An extremely sacred temple, a visit to the temple and the surrounding gardens provides a quiet escape from the busy Hanoi streets.

reviews.author: palawanismyhome
reviews.title: Originally constructed 1000 years ago
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda was constructed in the early part of the 11th century during the Ly Dynasty and sits in the middle of a lotus pond. It had been reconstructed several times throughout the centuries, the last time in 1955 when the French left. The area of the tiny temple is only 3X3 m.

reviews.author: Robert O
reviews.title: Special
reviews.content: The one pillar pagoda is a nice place for a photograph during a visit in conjunction with a visit to th Ho Chi Minh mauseleum. The pagoda is very small and  to many tourist try to get in on the same time. a small tourist market is close by.

reviews.author: Nury
reviews.title: Curious monument
reviews.content: Diferent pagoda with a Unique history. Worth passing by and checking it. Entrance free, next to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Martin H
reviews.title: must see
reviews.content: it is worth seeing. One of the most interesting momument in Hanoi. Building is in very good condition.

reviews.author: LazyDays4Us
reviews.title: 1 Pillar, a pond, behind HCM complex - Nice to see
reviews.content: Not raveable, but interesting to see. Cute that there is an ever so slight lean to it. All part of the HCM complex, in a little area behind the Mausoleum. Free to view, a few steps up and look inside.

reviews.author: viet4ever
reviews.title: Lake pagoda is a must see 1000 years old
reviews.content: Very beautiful day or night walk around entire lake pagoda is located in the middle of the lake . Buddhist Vitnamese temples is exceptional in the heart or near by old French quarters fantastic place to explore night time is a transformation of the temple lake lights are on very beautiful

reviews.author: Georgie C
reviews.title: Beautiful Building
reviews.content: We made a quick stop here while visiting the rest of the Ho Chi Minh complex, but that's literally all you need. Good for a quick photo, but as it's so small there's no reason to actually go in unless you're looking to pay respect/worship.

reviews.author: ling1931
reviews.title: Unusal
reviews.content: Built in 1049 this one pillar pagoda which is meant to resemble a lotus blossom sits  in a lotus pond unfortunately this pagoda is mostly a replica due to it being destroyed by  the french in 1955.Its a nice place for a quick visit.

reviews.author: BSinPNS
reviews.title: Beautiful Setting
reviews.content: Not only is it constructed on one pillar, it is in a quiet location near HCM Mausoleum with beautiful gardens surrounding it.

reviews.author: Kyaw M
reviews.title: Old Temple
reviews.content: It was built in 11th century but it was rebuilt now.Before it was built on a wood pillar and now it was on a concrete pillar in the middle of a small pond.

reviews.author: Harris L
reviews.title: It's been rebuilt
reviews.content: As it is adjacent to Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum it is packed with tourists and has lost much of it's authenticity. The column is out of concrete and it feels plopped down in it's site due to the plethora of tables and chairs surrounding it.

reviews.author: ChrissyLew
reviews.title: Must see but don't allow much time
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is one of the symbols of Hanoi and hence a must see but it looks much more impressive in pictures and models than in real life. This is an important pagoda to the Vietnamese people but to the average tourist it's a couple of photos and move on.

reviews.author: Peter T
reviews.title: A must
reviews.content: This temple has such a rich history and is a definite part of Vietnamese culture and religion that one needs to visit this when in Hanoi. The piety that is radiated by this temple and it's grounds is flabergasting.

reviews.author: gunner25571
reviews.title: A visit to the Pagoda
reviews.content: We visited the attraction and were a little disappointed that it really wasn't altogether on a single rock. It was difficult to go into the Pagoda as it is very small and the crowd was huge. It would have taken a long time  to get in

reviews.author: headingyonder
reviews.title: Worth a photo stop
reviews.content: A very small pagoda and not much to see - just a quick photo stop. I found the tourists behaviour more interesting than the site - there was a constant small queue of tourists lining up to take a turn at showing respect at the alter in their various ways before taking a photo in front of it.

reviews.author: 528jean
reviews.title: Ancient pagoda one of Hanoi's landmarks
reviews.content: The pagoda is an emblem of Hanoi and dates back to the 11th century and is very small (approx. 3 sq m) and is supported by a single pillar in the middle of a lake. It's very unusual and quite a tourist attraction. There are several folk legends which go with this pagoda so ask you guide to recount them.

reviews.author: Judi L
reviews.title: Historic
reviews.content: Interesting ancient site- not far from HCM mausoleum.Very crowded when we went but worth a look for photography

reviews.author: vjv2007
reviews.title: Best Part: The Children
reviews.content: The Pagoda is beautiful and highly respected.  It is a place of worship.  However, all around this area, on the day we visited was hundreds of school children.  Just as cute as can be.  Made our visit even more memorable.

reviews.author: campfollowerTucson
reviews.title: takes no time to visit
reviews.content: Just a small pagoda on a pillar. Not that interesting but you will be there anyway if you visit Ho Chi Minh's memorial/museum so you just see it in passing

reviews.author: Susana R
reviews.title: Over rated
reviews.content: It is close to Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, so it is an ok thing to see if you are already there but difficult to find and get to as the side of the park that is close to the Mausoleum is closed. I dragged my boyfriend over because I read of it but we were expecting more...

reviews.author: Jane B
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: This was interesting and one of the main points of interest in Hanoi. We were on a guided tour organised within our holiday with Lumley travel. It could probably be done independently. It was busy with visitors but you could still enjoy the venue and history of the place.

reviews.author: Jess
reviews.title: one of the popular sight-seeing site
reviews.content: One of the popular sight seeing sites for tourists. It can be also considerred a historical site as this pagoda has a history story behind it. Check this out.

reviews.author: justvacati0n
reviews.title: OKish - visit only if you are in the area
reviews.content: Worth visiting only if you came to see the entire complex of Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the museum and the gardens. Not special but it is a small nice place to see.

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda - A Symbol of Fertility
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is located adjacent to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.  There is a small market on the plaza adjacent to the pagoda.  According to our guide, the Pagoda is built on a single pillar to represent the Lotus Flower.  It is a tribute built by Ly Thai Tong.  Tong was a childless Emperor who dreamt he was presented a son by a Buddhist god sitting on a lotus flower.  The temple was built after the birth of Tong's son.It is currently a Buddhist temple that sits above a small concrete lotus pond.  There is a large Bodhi tree behind the pagoda that our guide claimed was grown from the very Bodhi tree that Buddha was sitting beneath when he attained enlightenment.This attraction is free.  It is centrally located.  It is also nearby restrooms, shopping and refreshments.  So there is plenty to do nearby.  As one of the two most iconic temples in Vietnam, I would highly recommend that visitors stop by here.

reviews.author: Lesley-Ann M
reviews.title: Pretty but pretty boring
reviews.content: Reasonably unusual structure but that's about all it had going for it. It was at least not that busy and so we were able to get some good photos. The kids only liked trying to spot fish in the pond.

reviews.author: Helperoli
reviews.title: A great one pillar pagoda, but not much else
reviews.content: This was an OK one pillar pagoda, but there was not much to see. This was mainly because there was a box, which you put prayers in, but it was very oriented towards Vietnamese people. If you are not their religion, you can only go up there and do nothing, whereas the Vietnamese do lots of praying. Overall, it was an OK one pillar pagoda, but there was not much to see.

reviews.author: Maria J
reviews.title: One of the best places from Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex
reviews.content: If visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex, this pagoda is one of the most interesting buildings there.

reviews.author: Jongleurgirl
reviews.title: Part of complex
reviews.content: This is part of the Mausoleum complex and you move on to this after you have viewed Ho Chi Minh House.  Interesting to see but would not have gone just to see this

reviews.author: PierreMalmaison
reviews.title: Pretty and worth a brief visit
reviews.content: Accessible for free in Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum Complex (behind the museum). This pretty little piece of architecture is buzzing with tourists but worthy of a brief visit.

reviews.author: Shana_S87
reviews.title: Peaceful Place
reviews.content: When arrive this place I felt so peaceful. Actually its a temple where major Vietnam women always come for praying. Tour guide told us those Vietnam women who hope to have baby they will come for praying. I hope to have my little angel so and I did my praying too.

reviews.author: onelinedrawing
reviews.title: Nice structure
reviews.content: Interesting pagoda with ornate work around it and nice story about why it was built. Not that large and can be crowded so trying to get a 'people free' picture can be challenging. Few stalls around it selling usual 'souvenirs' etc...Worth going as part of a general walk about tour.

reviews.author: Jenny D
reviews.title: Beautiful One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: This tiny pagoda was quite beautiful.  You get in line, walk up the steps, and can only look inside.  It is amazing how it is only on one pillar.

reviews.author: adrian_foxley
reviews.title: Very pretty
reviews.content: It was very busy in the park but it was worth spending a few minutes to see this special pagoda. It would be nice to see it with less people as it loses the peacefulness it should have.

reviews.author: Colint50
reviews.title: Just a small pergoda
reviews.content: Part of the area around the Ho Chi Minh complex.  Nothing special, it's on one pillar. I climbed the steps to look inside.so,

reviews.author: chesterchandler
reviews.title: One of those Hanoi icons
reviews.content: You only need five minutes here to see the pagoda. It is cool--but small and usually super crowded. But then continue on to Ho Chi MInh's house nearby and the museum. All are free and it is worth your time.  This is a good place to get away from the hustle and noise of Hanoi streets.

reviews.author: Veggiemel
reviews.title: Small but iconic temple
reviews.content: Conveniently located to visit as part of a city tour,  the One Pillar Pagoda is situated in the park behind the Ho Chi Minh museum and mausoeum near Ba Dinh Square.The French destroyed this little wooden temple as one of the final act of aggression before quitting Hanoi in 1954, and the regime subsequently rebuilt it (for the umpteenth time).Built on a single stone pillar it is designed to resemble a lotus blossom, the pillars surround it also feature stone lotus flowers (the Buddhist symbol of purity.) The shrine inside the three square metres temple is dedicated to Quan Am - a Vietnamese Buddhist deity and a bo tree grows behind the pagoda (legend has it that this is an offshoot of the one under which Buddha became enlightened)

reviews.author: Sandy
reviews.title: It stands on one strong pillar!
reviews.content: It needs to have a very strong one pillar, as there are gazillion people trying to go up and down the one set of stairs into it! We choose to sit back and watch the goings on and take some picture of it. This was a very crowded place when we were there. Lots of things to see though.

reviews.author: Josine T
reviews.title: Very unique and a great story behind it!
reviews.content: I wish I could remember the exact stry behind this small pagoda, but all I remember is that it had something to do with a child being born into the family... very pretty building in nice surroundings!

reviews.author: Boise_Matt
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: This attraction is part of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum area.It is small and the stairs are very steep.Worth stopping to admire the architecture and surrounding area.

reviews.author: Kashyap S
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: Pagoda is on a single pillar,its a small pagoda than expected. Quite place and looks really peaceful.

reviews.author: Sharon J
reviews.title: Awesome, spiritual
reviews.content: Visited the Pagoda as part of a local tourWas quite moving and certainly memorableVery beautiful and calm

reviews.author: RajanJamuna
reviews.title: Unique Pagoda
reviews.content: Simple and somewhat popular.  Not much to see as the Pagoda is a small structure.  Nice to walk and wander around.

reviews.author: Lorenzo R
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: This is a Buddhist temple in the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex.It is regarded as one of Vietnam's most iconic temples.

reviews.author: marcopolo0979
reviews.title: Historic yet sad reminder
reviews.content: A historic yet sad reminder of the vindictiveness of the French colonial rule. This is not the original, as it was destoyed by the French before they left in 1954, knowing so well this was an icon revered by the Vietnamese. This is a rebuilt version.

reviews.author: Nigel G
reviews.title: Worth a look if passing
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is an old temple that derives from the one pillar that supports it. Sure it's interesting to walk around the square pond in which it stands. However, when you climb the stairs to the temple there is a statue of Guyan Yin with the most gaudily lit LCD backdrop you can imagine. How to make a sacred image look tacky!! A significant building and worth a visit. The temple in front of it is dedicated to Guyan Yin also - the goddess of mercy and is much more attractive and should be visited in conjunction with the One Pillar Pagoda. Both are worth a visit from an historical perspective. The Temple and Pagoda are located halfway between the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the Museum.

reviews.author: litseyk
reviews.title: Long line to view
reviews.content: This is in the ho Chi Minh memorial and there was a long slow line to walk up the stairs so I just took a photo and walked away. Nothing special.

reviews.author: Ltp_BKK
reviews.title: Really small pagoda
reviews.content: It is a small pagoda located in a little pond. Nothing much. However, there is a little Buddhist temple located in front of the pagoda. Which is worth to visit.

reviews.author: soulsease
reviews.title: It's a pagoda on a single pillar!
reviews.content: It is what it says on the tin - a small but perfectly formed pagoda on a single column. Very photogenic. It is not the original, of course - that fell down some years ago, but it is a faithful reproduction. Worth a photo!

reviews.author: bolkin
reviews.title: Nice place to visit
reviews.content: The French destroyed this temple on their way out in 1954.  It was reconstructed and still commemorates the legend of Emperor Ly Thai Tong.  It is said that the childless emperor dreamed that Quan Am, the Buddhist goddess of mercy and compassion, seated on a lotus flower, handed him a baby boy.  Sure enough, he soon met and married and peasant woman who bore him a male hair, and in 1049 he constructed this monument in appreciation.  The distinctive single pillar is meant to represent the stalk of the lotus flower, and sacred Vietnamese symbol of purity.

reviews.author: steve m
reviews.title: 1st Hanoi Visit
reviews.content: This was a very nice shrine to visit, although it was incredibly busy due to the Tet holiday. Worth the walk nonetheless.

reviews.author: jmm73
reviews.title: Cute
reviews.content: Make sure you queue up to go inside as the altar with all the offerings is beautiful. Watch out for the Chinese tourists who don't think they need to queue though or you'll always be at the back of the line :)

reviews.author: QuanLee
reviews.title: Nice small pagoda!
reviews.content: This pagoda is quite smaller than others we did visited before. However we found down that this pagoda is one of the must see in Hanoi, and we believe it was true.This pagoda also had interesting history and architecture. and it was also good for anyone who believe in buddalism.

reviews.author: Ira G
reviews.title: Lovely pagoda on beautiful grounds.
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is didicated to the Vietnamese Buddhist deity Quan Am. It is regarded alongside the Perfume Temple, as one of Vietnam's two most iconic temples, and was built by Emperor Lý Thái Tông, who ruled from 1028 to 1054. In 1954, the French Union forces destroyed the pagoda before withdrawing from Vietnam after the First Indochina War. It was rebuilt afterwards.

reviews.author: AntonioAGSC
reviews.title: A pagoda different form the others
reviews.content: the area where the one pillar pagode is has different pagodas and places to see, the locals and the tourists are all over these places

reviews.author: Helen K
reviews.title: Ancient Pagoda
reviews.content: worth the visit - beautifully situated in grounds with wonderful statues - you can climb the stairs to see the interior - tiny but beautiful

reviews.author: nadia089
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: We wouldn't say it's a must see but if your going to the mausoleum area then it's worth a look ---it's within the grounds. It's only very small with a stairway to go up and see inside --- though it does feel intrusive when people are praying, there is a small moat that runs round it but it was very dirty when we went.

reviews.author: Bryan H
reviews.title: Part of the Ho Chi Minh complex ...
reviews.content: This pagoda was part of our overall complex tour. It is unique architecturally, supposedly. Our guide said it was the only pagoda known to be built on one pillar. I didn't think it look aesthetically that appealing situated on a big ole pillar like it is. Not worth a separate trip, but see it in passing as you are seeing the sights of the complex.

reviews.author: Dewi R
reviews.title: Overrated Pagoda
reviews.content: We were disappointed with this Pagoda since we were expecting a higher pagoda. But the One Pillar Pagoda was accentuate on the foundation only.

reviews.author: Nadnerb2
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: This one pillar pagoda ios exactly what it says. It is a wonderful pagoda and a great setting to take a photo. Well worth the visit.

reviews.author: CuriousTraveler007
reviews.title: Nothing special, but close to Ho Chi Minh Museum
reviews.content: Just worth a photo while you are in the area. Compared to other pagodas, this one is really not special, but worth a very quick visit if you are visiting the Presidential Palace and Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum

reviews.author: deboramontagna
reviews.title: nice
reviews.content: This is a nice place to see, even if not so excitingIf you are travelling in South-East Asia, you will see full of Pagodas, so this one is nothing special, in our opinion

reviews.author: Chris500
reviews.title: One Pillar ... Yes!
reviews.content: But so what?  LOL.  It's a tourist attraction.  Near the Ho Chi Minh residence.  Kind of boring.  It's the kind of thing that once you've seen it, you don't need to see it again.

reviews.author: Rory G
reviews.title: Not very exciting
reviews.content: I wasn't impressed by this location.  I didn't even bother go to up the stairs to the pagoda.  It is very close to the Ho Chi Minh museum, and there are a few little souvenir and snack stands nearby.

reviews.author: BBTrisha
reviews.title: Interesting history behind the Pagoda
reviews.content: We visited the Pagoda as part of a wider tour of Hanoi. It was interesting but a very small attraction. I would suggest factoring it in with more sights rather than a destination on its own.

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.content: This was the spot of an ancient pagoda that I believe was burned down by the French before they abandoned Vietnam.  So really what you are looking at is a reconstruction (I believe it was done in the 50's?).It isn't a must see, but as others have stated, if you're around the presidential complex, you might as well swing by and check it out.  It wasn't busy when I was here in Jan 2017, but I guess that's just luck.

reviews.author: PrettyGreen
reviews.title: Visit on the grounds of Ho Chi Minh's tomb
reviews.content: This lovely pagoda and the story of its origins is worth visiting after you pay your respects at the tomb of Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: davevond
reviews.title: It's a one pillar pagoda
reviews.content: It's a one pillar pagoda. An interesting look if you're doing the circuit around the mausoleum and the museum. Neat little history. Neat to say you've seen a one pillar pagoda.

reviews.author: Jim S
reviews.title: Busy Attraction
reviews.content: Worth spending around 1/2 hour if visiting the presential palace area. Pretty busy attraction. Nice Pagoda.

reviews.author: Kevin W
reviews.title: Worth a look if you are near the Ho Chi Min Complex
reviews.content: The area has multiple sites, one of which is the One Pillar Pagoda. Definitely worth a look if you are in the area.

reviews.author: Kanaena
reviews.title: A woman slapped me
reviews.content: Okay okay I guess I kinda deserved it BUT I did read the warning ahead of time. The rule simply stated that one was not permitted if one was wearing shorts. So I had capris on and made my way into the pagoda where upon snapping a few pictures I was slapped by a Vietnamese woman who then pointed at my shoulders. I had a sleeveless top on so yes, I should of thought it through but she didn't have to slap me and fyi I had my jacket tied around my waist which I then put on. BUT what annoys me more was when I went further in there was a Caucasian lady in shorts with a spaghetti strap on inside... What the heck? I was way more covered than her and obviously she did not get slapped. What gives? Is it because I'm Asian?

reviews.author: Jonahcardiff
reviews.title: Ticks the box
reviews.content: Worth the visit, depends how busy, very popular with locals and visitors so difficult to take photographs

reviews.author: seetheworld010
reviews.title: A lot of people
reviews.content: And not really worth the wait. Climb up a set of steps to see candles burning and go back down. Very very crowded. Be prepared.

reviews.author: denisenice
reviews.title: Worth a look if your wandering and in the area
reviews.content: Really sweet pagoda and if your touring round the city this is close by other sightseeing spots such as the palace and the mausoleum. Definately worth a picture to add to your memories.

reviews.author: Dale10
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda.
reviews.content: The temple is built of wood on a single stone pillar. It is a historic Buddhist temple located in Hanoi. Not a must visit, but do take a look if you’re in the area.

reviews.author: Sherrill B
reviews.title: Religious Worship
reviews.content: Being a Christian I am very interested in religions of the world. I find it fascinating to observe how other people worship. With Vietnam being predominantly Buddhist it was fascinating to me to see the beautiful places of worship and even to observe people worshipping.

reviews.author: Omer H
reviews.title: A Structural Marvel
reviews.content: This structure must be seen to be believed. A single pillar suports the Pagoda in a unique manner. If you are interested in achitecture then you will have to see it.

reviews.author: karen w
reviews.title: Pretty but not a must-see
reviews.content: I had time to kill so I visited this pagoda - which was pretty, but nothing really special. Take a look if you want to include it in a relaxed walk around Hanoi, but leave it off your must-see list.

reviews.author: Josh T
reviews.title: Stunning building. Can really see the resemblance to the lotus flower
reviews.content: Good idea to have a guide take you through to explain the history and reasoning behind the pagoda. The story and history behind this is quiet fascinating

reviews.author: dharmnava
reviews.title: Small temple but with an interesting history
reviews.content: We found this temple hard to locate based on the map we had but eventually found that it was in the Ho Chi Minh Museum complex.  Lots of people visiting but I thought it was a bit of a disappointment as it is quite a tiny temple.

reviews.author: Sandy S
reviews.title: AUSPICIOUS HISTORY
reviews.content: The story behind the One Pillar Pagoda is obscure now but related to an aging emperor who was unable to conceive a child and came here to pray for a son.and dreamed he had a baby boy.  Months later, a son was born to his wife and he built the pagoda to resemble a lotus flower on a stem.  Fascinating with many people climbing the steps to pray.  The pagoda has been destroyed and rebuilt several times.

reviews.author: mwhamburger
reviews.title: one of Vietnam's most iconic Buddhist temples
reviews.content: it is designed to resemble to Lotus blossom and in the middle of a pond. It was built in 1049 by emperor Ly Thy Tong who had married a peasant girl who bore him a son. He constructed this temple in gratitude for this. It's a very popular sight and the lines can be long.

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: Unusual
reviews.content: You can only visit as part of your tour of the Mausoleum complex.It was very busy the day we were there and we didn't bother trying to go inside because of the crowds, however you can get close enough for a photo.

reviews.author: Joe
reviews.title: So so
reviews.content: This is a tiny pagoda.  Located near the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum.  Nice to look at but super small. Much nicer ones in other places

reviews.author: ScotPerth
reviews.title: Attractive spot
reviews.content: A very pleasant temple area in the HCM mausoleum area.  It is quite small but very busy.  If you are in this area, don't miss it.

reviews.author: Alamgir Farhad
reviews.title: An Interesting Pagoda
reviews.content: The One-Pillar Pagoda is located in the western part of the city, near Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum in Hanoi. The pagoda was built by the Emperor Ly Thai Tong, who ruled from 1028 to 1054 . History says... The King dreamed that he had met Quan The Am Bo Tat( Goddess Of Mercy), who, while seated on a lotus flower, handed him a male child. Ly Thai Tong then married a peasant girl he met by chance and had a son and heir a baby. To express his gratitude for this event, he constructed tho One pillar Pagoda in 1049. The whole pagoda looks like a lotus flower. The unique monument reflects the architectural splendor that the country has grown.

reviews.author: Ralf W
reviews.title: Grand Adventure Part II
reviews.content: Some times the story behind the One Pillar Pagoda is better that the actual building its self. I an OK visit. Not a must see.

reviews.author: ChristineBindert
reviews.title: One of the staples in Hanoi
reviews.content: One of the staple attractions for tourist in Hanoi that means it is crowded! Try to go late afternoon when there are less people! or have a quick look before you go to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and decide which one you do first depending on the crowds!

reviews.author: faysie2015
reviews.title: Ancient
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda was built nearly 1000 years ago, standing on one pillar in a fish pond, it is said to bring boy children to those who want them ..... all Vietnamese men! When compared to Australia's caucasian history this is just so ancient!!

reviews.author: kcjar
reviews.title: Small pagoda in a beautiful setting
reviews.content: We saw this pagoda as part of our walking tour of the Ho Chi Minh Palace Gardens.  We had a little wait to get to see the vibrant Buddha shrine, but it was well worth the time.  It sits on a single pillar that is anchored in a small pond.  There is s small staircase to walk-up to the pagoda, not good if you can't handle stairs.  Glad our guide pointed it out to us because we had a good photo opportunity at the top of the staircase.

reviews.author: Michael S
reviews.title: Nice photo, famous landmark
reviews.content: This makes for a nice pic, and very close to Ho Chi Minh museum and mausoleum if you want to combine activities.

reviews.author: Jacqui B
reviews.title: Originally built in 1048
reviews.content: This is built of wood on a single stone pillar and is designed to look like a lotus flower. It was very popular however please note you have to be modestly dressed to go into the pillar. It is a beautiful building that was rebuilt after the `french destroyed the original in 1954. The surrounding gardens are lovely to rest a while

reviews.author: Stan C
reviews.title: Someting to have a quick look at when visiting the HCM Mausoleum
reviews.content: Take a quick look at this little pagoda in a small pond supported by one pillar- hence its name I guess!A small diversion when visiting the HCM Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Richard J
reviews.title: Oustounding
reviews.content: Take care - it is very easy to miss. The pagoda is easily accessible and as you remain outside there is less restrictions on your apparel.

reviews.author: Maughin L
reviews.title: Lovely to see but very busy!
reviews.content: Was super busy so didn't manage to get any photos of the pagoda by itself, rather with lots of tourists sitting on it etc. Wouldn't go out of my way to see it. There are places around it to buy a cool drink if you are thirsty, as well as some souvenir shops.

reviews.author: minnesotans4
reviews.title: Small pagoda
reviews.content: When touring the Ho Chi Minh gardens, stop for a few minutes to see the pagoda.  It was built to resemble a lotus blossom "rising out of a sea of sorrow".  The French destroyed the original in 1954.

reviews.author: BeccaPop
reviews.title: Okay for a quick glance
reviews.content: Not much to see but does what it says on the tin! Recommend combining with a trip to the HCM Mausoleum and museum but don't make a special trip.

reviews.author: JLQ
reviews.title: Not worth it on its own.
reviews.content: Went past the area as part of exploring the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and surrounding grounds. There is quite a bit of history surrounding the pagoda, but despite that, it's not the most impressive pagoda in Asia  and I wouldn't make it a key priority to have to see this. Also the incense around this area is quite heavy and I saw a lady suffer an asthma attack.

reviews.author: AdventureMom16
reviews.title: Nice Pagoda
reviews.content: Nice pagoda to see along with other site in the area.  Not a single destination.  Many people come to take pictures.

reviews.author: KayL2
reviews.title: Good historical sight
reviews.content: This is a good historical site, mentioned frequently in Vietnamese stories and poems.  However, its restoration is overshadowed by the Ho Chi Minh tomb, a monolith that does not fit in the ancient Hanoi.

reviews.author: WendyH678
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Museum
reviews.content: This is located in the HCM Museum.  Plan your visit to the Mausoleum, Museum and the One Pillar Pagoda.  It is all located together.

reviews.author: Jennifer E
reviews.title: Must See
reviews.content: Although on the small side, this is a must see in Hanoi.  Do climb the steps up to the altar.  There are lovely reflection photos.  Some good bargains to be had in the tourist stalls.

reviews.author: Eli O
reviews.title: Worth visiting in Hanoi.
reviews.content: This place is one of the attractions you may want to visit in Hanoi to to fulfill  yourself with with the city spirit and understanding of the local culture and traditions.

reviews.author: Wulan_Dewi
reviews.title: Not good compare to the history
reviews.content: Before visited here we already read about the history, similar with our guide explanation. Unfortunately we found just ordinary pagoda, and looks like poorly maintained.We can't see the beautiful shape of this pagoda like the story behind. Moreover we came here at noon when the sun was very hot and gave us no compromise to take good photos.Below the pagoda is a pool, but the water was dirty, brown-black. And there were o lotus flowers at all. Actually if we really serious to observe the shape of this pagoda, we'll find the unique shape, but we need much much better environment surrounding it to see the beautifulness. One of it is the clear pool with lotus will help our eyes to find the beautifulness :)We found few quite nice spots to take photos not in this pagoda, but the building behind it. Souvenirs in this place is very expensive, twice than normal price. Better buy the souvenirs at other places. There are no unique souvenirs here.

reviews.author: Justin W
reviews.title: Very unusual Pagoda
reviews.content: We visited the grounds around the Presidential Palace and passed by the pagoda on the way around all the sites of the city. We unfortunately did not get to tour it but it was very impressive on the way it was built. I wish we were able to tour inside. It really does look like a lotus blossom.

reviews.author: Spaska2013
reviews.title: Small and different addition to the HO Chi Min house area
reviews.content: The pagoda is the last thing you are shown if you visit the house if Ho Chi Min are. This is nothing special if you have seen other temples before.

reviews.author: JudeLaw
reviews.title: Do not border!
reviews.content: Not worth your time, nothing much to see here. There are a lot more interesting temples to see in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Angi D
reviews.title: Worth a look and photo stop
reviews.content: Part of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex.  It was pretty busy when we were there, but worth a closer look and a photo stop

reviews.author: maxscuba
reviews.title: Weird architecture
reviews.content: A nice and busy pagoda located in the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex, no entrance fees needed. Built on top of one single pillar (the one that you see is rebuilt from concrete) it shows a very peculiar architecture. Many ladies go there and leave their wishes to be pregnant soon.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Thousand Year Old Pagoda
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is regarded by Vietnamese Buddhists as one of the most iconic temples in Vietnam.It was built by Emperor Ly Thai Tong early in the 11th Century, but has been subject to many renovations over the centuries and had to be totally rebuilt after the French destroyed it in a wanton act of vandalism as they withdrew from their former colony.One Pillar Pagoda is located in the Ho Chi Minh historical site, so it is worth paying it a quick visit while you are there.

reviews.author: StefanoRM75
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: Probably the sole Pagoda built on one pillar in the region, situated in the garden surrounding the Ho Chi Min Mausoleum and Museum.The Pagoda is very small but very ancient and very well preserved, and the overall atmosphere surrounding it is quite and peaceful

reviews.author: jalee77
reviews.title: Just an ordinary pagoda
reviews.content: It is what you see in the picture.. a normal pagoda located outside the Ho Chi Minh museum. No admission fees are required.

reviews.author: jamesdorigo
reviews.title: Just a single shrine
reviews.content: It is very near the HCM Museum. So it is worth visisting 2 places at once. This is just a normal srine but sitting on one pillar. So it is unique but nothing so exciting

reviews.author: fireysunrise
reviews.title: Overcrowded
reviews.content: Like much of this area the pagoda was overcrowded with tourists. The history of the building is interesting, but our visit here was pretty brief. Worth it only if you are planning to see all of the other sights in this complex.

reviews.author: YannLavoie
reviews.title: Nice, but super crowded
reviews.content: Very nice little pagoda in themiddle of a pond, but only problem it is super crowded around it and you have to wait in line to go up, so we took a few pictures and skipped the queue.

reviews.author: ShirleeSpice
reviews.title: Sweet...
reviews.content: Beautiful little one pillar pagoda. It certainly attracts a lot of visitors. It was difficult to get some pics as the selfie brigade were out in force, however that didn't put us off. Worth visiting.

reviews.author: Mary W
reviews.title: Over 1,000 years old
reviews.content: This is in the Mausoleum precinct. It is hard to believe it's age. People do worship there.  It was built on one wooden pier, now concrete due to it's restoration after having been destroyed by the French in the 1950's

reviews.author: F4023NZalbertos
reviews.title: learn Vietnamese history
reviews.content: good place to learn more about a grat man, his life, his work his fight for liberty/ the father of todays Vietnam. i respect him like my own father. great man.

reviews.author: Carthy S
reviews.title: An unique pagoda
reviews.content: I visited this place while on a city tour and in a complex of Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. This pillar is quite different from others as it stands on only a pillar. Then I walked around step by step visiting all the attraction in this complex.

reviews.author: Patrick H
reviews.title: Small but nice
reviews.content: This temple somewhat less than one thousand years old is located in the gardens not far from the presidential palace and the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum. The pagoda sits on one single pillar in a small pond. It is not so impressive but nice to have a look at. The place is usually crowded. Maybe you should go there in the early morning.

reviews.author: Oldjack
reviews.title: Small Pagoda On A Single Pillar
reviews.content: The original pagoda was destroyed by the French when they left but this is a replacement which is interesting but not special.It is part of the Ho Chi Minh historical precict and worth seeing.

reviews.author: JohntheLast
reviews.title: It is what is says
reviews.content: Not much here. It is a pagoda and it is supported by one pillar. But the original was burnt and this is in effect a replica.

reviews.author: MsBrownWarrington
reviews.title: Peaceful spot.
reviews.content: A very unusual sight. Lovely gardens with great photo opportunities.There is also a secret temple that's worth a look.There are the usual stalls selling whatever you need.I found that the sellers are not pushy. Lots to buy but no hassle.

reviews.author: Priscilla S
reviews.title: Good add-on to visit to Ho Chi Minh House and Mausoleum
reviews.content: The pagoda itself was interesting in its symbolic representation of a lotus flower, hence the one pillar, but it is relatively new as it was reconstructed after the French destroyed it in 1954.  It is important as well as it is a Buddhist pilgrimage site, though not on the same scale as others in Asia.

reviews.author: Aileen A
reviews.title: list this as optional
reviews.content: It's located just next to the Mausoluem.. if you are short of time.. you could choose to give this a miss.

reviews.author: AyeMyaMyaCho
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: It was the place connected to Ho Chi Minh Museum. Even though nothing much to see, people said that couples who wanted a baby could pray at that pagoda.

reviews.author: Cris-Eshana
reviews.title: Simple but cute
reviews.content: It's a very simple pagoda, but kind of cute... A little taste of the type of buddhism you find in Vietnam...

reviews.author: Charles S
reviews.title: Unusal pagoda
reviews.content: A must see in Hanoi. The setting is quite beautiful. This place attracts huge crowds. Good place to do some shopping for souvenirs.

reviews.author: Yannie L
reviews.title: Hidden passed the shops. Ok for time filler
reviews.content: If you have 10 or so minutes to fill, pay it a visit, it is well hidden passed the shops in the Ho Chi Minh museum areaIt is quite small but looks OhioBe aware you will get annoyed by shop owners

reviews.author: Vanessa Q
reviews.title: Intersting
reviews.content: Lovely place to have a stroll around, small market stall in the area for souvioners. Some history here.

reviews.author: DinnerLadies
reviews.title: A bit of a disappointment
reviews.content: This pagoda is advertised as an amazing attraction but in our view, it was a little disappointing. There were queues of people trying to get up the steps but when they got to the top, they saw just a small altar/shrine and then turned round quickly and came back down again. The structure of the pagaoda was quite interesting but smaller than we expected.

reviews.author: David R
reviews.title: Its fine to visit if you are near by
reviews.content: I found this only mildy interesting to visit as there are more impressive pagodas to visit in vietnam. Only went there was it was near the museum. There are some shops there and shady trees so you can site and have a rest or drink under some nice tree and view the pagoda which was enjoyable.

reviews.author: Chin R
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is hidden at the middle of a garden, yet it's easy to locate and identical. It is small yet beautiful. Many people come here to worship and pray for baby.

reviews.author: Chris H
reviews.title: An average Pagoda
reviews.content: The pagoda is in the grounds of the Ho Chi Minh museum, so if you are going to the museum it is an easy walk to the Pagoda.This Pagoda is free to visit, but having been to many Pagodas this one is just average and if you are not going to the area where it is or the Ho Chi Minh museum i would not waste your time going there to visit it as the Pagoda at the Hoan Kiem Lake is much nicer and has much more to see.My partner and myself were disappointed with this pagoda, it is most likely fine for people that have not visited many Pagodas and will give them an insight into another Pagoda but for someone that has visited many Pagodas do not waste your time even though it is free, you will not need very long to look through the Pagoda about 15 minutes.

reviews.author: worldiscoverer
reviews.title: Nice pagoda
reviews.content: Nice pagoda with peaceful surroundings. In the same place as the mausoleum so can visit both at the same time.

reviews.author: KiwiKerry53
reviews.title: If you come across it go in if you can
reviews.content: Near Ho Chi MInhs complex, so it's easy to find or stumble upon without even trying.  A historic and iconic temple, with great cultural significance.

reviews.author: chi2616
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: If you have a specific religious intent to visit this temple, then by all means pay a visit. Otherwise, you won't miss much. It is a five minute photo stop.

reviews.author: TheShis
reviews.title: Going back to the pagoda.
reviews.content: This is the 2nd time we're visiting this tiny pagoda.It's still not very impressive, but the shrine within it looked more alive this time.Worth a very quick visit when you are in the area.

reviews.author: DaveandDebbieDodd
reviews.title: A quiet place
reviews.content: This is a free to visit site by the Ho Chi Minh museum, and is worth popping in to see and get a couple of photo's. Ludicrous opening hours along with all tourist sites in Vietnam, but if it's open it's worth a 5 min walk around.

reviews.author: Deepika M
reviews.title: Historic
reviews.content: Would have been a better experience with a tour guide, but history is history and that's worth he experience!

reviews.author: Sammy509
reviews.title: Not fussed
reviews.content: The guide made a big fuss about the Pagoda , not sure why , not much to see , very crowded although it is worth going .

reviews.author: Travlintone
reviews.title: Guess what?
reviews.content: A small pagoda with, guess what? one pillar! Quaint but nothing that will distract you for more than a few minutes.

reviews.author: pauline o
reviews.title: Worth a look but not that riveting
reviews.content: Like quite a few sights in Hanoi it's OK and worth a look, but nothing spectacular.  Interesting architecture.

reviews.author: Vivndhugh
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: This place is lovely and is worth a visit. You can take some lovely photos if your patient with people visiting the top of this pagoda to pray.

reviews.author: Jeff Slo
reviews.title: boring, stinky, crowded, and dirty
reviews.content: dirty water, litter, not so interesting story. just a pagoda with industrial incense burning that slightly masks the stagnant water stench. very crowded for unknown reasons. not visually appealing, could use a massive clean up.

reviews.author: 228Kevin
reviews.title: Another pagoda
reviews.content: As part of the Ho experience you see this pagoda. Sitting on a concrete pillar now so not too original.

reviews.author: ianwyj
reviews.title: Be careful on the steps if it's crowded
reviews.content: Apart from it being called a pagoda (it looks nothing like a pagoda), this has to be one of the most peculiar Buddhist shrines anywhere.  It's not just its small size, but also that it was built in the middle of a pond with a steep set of steps leading up to it.  However, the story behind its existence is quite interesting.  Apparently, the original shrine was built in the mid-11th century by a thankful king who had been blessed with a son following a dream about a Buddhist deity who promised him one.  Why it's in the middle of a pond was due to the deity having been seated on a lotus in the middle of one.The shrine is a rather popular one, so expect a queue to get to the top.  However, considering the steps are slightly steep and human traffic trying to go both ways, visitors should be careful to avoid an unfortunate fall into the pond.  At the top of the stairs is the altar, a rather colourful scene with the deity's gold leaf-covered statue flanked by flowers and food offerings.

reviews.author: Khiem Vo
reviews.title: Too many people
reviews.content: There are too many people at the small famous pagoda. Luckily there is another part of the pagoda next to it to explore.It's not too exciting and not that beautiful.However the history value of this attraction is cool and you should read about it.

reviews.author: Łukasz S
reviews.title: Very nice temple
reviews.content: Another very pretty temple in Hanoi with very nice and green surrounding. If you were in Hanoi you must see One Pillar.

reviews.author: ckpeng04
reviews.title: Just a small Pagoda supported by a pillar.
reviews.content: It is just a small temple-like pagoda standing on a stilt with a lotus pond below. Nice garden around but nothing special. If you are around that area visiting other tourist spots nearby like Ba Dinh Square ( museum ), HCM Mausoleum, then it is worth a visit . However, it is popular among the locals as it has very old historical values.

reviews.author: Severine & Lukasz
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: I've never seen a pagoda on one pillar so it was fun to have a look at it, but actually everyone comes for the ho chi minh museum.

reviews.author: Ela P
reviews.title: The temple like the lotus flower on the top of stem
reviews.content: Very small temple! It's very good to compare the temple looks like the lotus flower on the top of stem. Very nice place.

reviews.author: mz4jun
reviews.title: Not much to see!
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is just a small temple. There is not much to see; totally not for someone who is for sightseeing.

reviews.author: FotoMike
reviews.title: Tucked away jewel of Viet Nam
reviews.content: When I first heard of this Pagoda years ago, I imagined it set in peaceful gardens of green amid lotus blossoms. My virst visit I was surprised to see that it was dwarfed by the monumental museum and mausoleum of President Ho Chi Minh.The Pagoda and small temple grounds are in the shadow of the revered former president and leader of the country's liberation. On a recent visit, I discovered a bit of culture I had not read about the Pagoda. For thse desiring a child, this is the place those prayers are best offered. The friend I had brought here asked if it were true! I asked a local resident who was nearby and she confirmed. Suddenly, this little nine century old religious site took on a new sense of wonder and spiritual hope for those who believe in prayer.

reviews.author: jeff1955malaysia
reviews.title: unusual pagoda
reviews.content: it lies within the area of HCM mossleum. it is a pagoda that sits on only one collum. quite unusual. you will find a lot of people taking pic around this area.

reviews.author: Honza P
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.content: As there are reconstruction works all around the pagoda area, it was very hard to find it even with GPS. We have spend couple hours finding it. When we finally succeeded, the tiny pagoda was bit of a disappointment...

reviews.author: tumbleweeds023
reviews.title: A small pagoda
reviews.content: Don't come just for this - you'll be disappointed - but it's part of the larger complex that features the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum, museum, presidential palace and Ba Dinh park. Combined, it makes for a full and interesting day and definitely worth seeing. The pagoda itself will just take a few minutes to see.

reviews.author: Eric C
reviews.title: Smaller than in pictures
reviews.content: The one pillar pagoda was smaller than it appears in pics. It took us 2 minutes to see and snap a few pics.

reviews.author: Steve F
reviews.title: A little disappointing
reviews.content: I wouldn't recommend going specifically to see this but if you're in the area, for the Ho Chi Minh Museum and Mausoleum then it's worth a brief look.

reviews.author: Gordon B
reviews.title: One trick pony
reviews.content: It's okay, but the one pillar was replaced long ago with concrete.. it's handy to Ho Chi Minh's erstwhile place though.

reviews.author: GMV-GotMyVote
reviews.title: A good historical temple
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is one of Vietnam's two most iconic temple in Hanoi. It is believed this is good Buddhist temple to come and ask for a child.下午我們來參觀河內著名的一柱廟。在1049年創建的。此祠廟建在一根柱子之上。造型獨特，外型雖小，但卻是越南的代表古剎，而寺廟立在蓮花池中的優雅姿態已成為河內的一個象徵。這廟又稱求子廟，不少夫妻都會來朝拜。

reviews.author: apmatos
reviews.title: bit desapointing
reviews.content: Thats is not much to see and/or feel in this atraction. Dont wast your time going here, unless you walk nearby.

reviews.author: mjurgeneit
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Well worth seeing and should be included in any tour of Hanoi. Go in the morning to get the best of the sun for photos

reviews.author: roadbum4ever
reviews.title: Popular with worshippers.
reviews.content: Read about this pagoda but saw it accidentally as were were leaving the Ho Chi Ming Mausoleum compound.

reviews.author: worldtravela69
reviews.title: Nice but worth only a quick pass
reviews.content: This isn't the original but it is unique and worth a very quick stop.  the whole area is surrounded by hawkers which take away some of the charm of visiting the area

reviews.author: Heng X
reviews.title: Not worth a visit
reviews.content: The one pillar pagoda is literally just as the name suggests. There is not much to see except for some greenery and the masoleum just around the corner.The pagoda itself is pretty small and honestly, you can see quite a few of such pagoda elsewhere in Vietnam so if your sole purpose is to just see this attraction, don't be greeted with disappointment!

reviews.author: AussieAnniversary
reviews.title: Part of the Ho Cho Minh Mausoleum, house and gardens
reviews.content: Not good enough for a separate visit just to see, however, do take the time while in the beautiful gardens to spend a few minutes there. Is interesting watching the comings and goings of those with offerings and for prayers

reviews.author: Scott W
reviews.title: A nice stop
reviews.content: If you like Pagodas and Temples then go there but best with a guide as it is the story which makes this interesting.

reviews.author: Roger S
reviews.title: Just down from the Mausoleum
reviews.content: A few hundred metres from HCM's Mausoleum, this is worth seeing. The canopy shelters a small shrine still worshipped despite the number of visitors. Lots of little kiosks nearby to get a snack or drink, and the pond is full of fish

reviews.author: TonyCogan
reviews.title: Interesting side visit on Hoan Kien
reviews.content: Quite an interesting pagoda set on a small island on Hoan Kien, reachable via a short bridge. Like most religious sites, it is sometimes a bit hard to have a really good look and take photos when there are quite a few worshippers constantly laying gifts and kneeling in prayer.

reviews.author: Rachel F
reviews.title: Interesting area, but pricye
reviews.content: The pagoda itself is incredible, and the surrounding area is quite beautiful. However, the businesses and vendors near there charge SO much more for everything (even bottles of water), so be sure to bring a snack and water.

reviews.author: ernur
reviews.title: It is Special for Locals - Especiall new married ladies -
reviews.content: we have visited this place with a local guide. Pagoda is very close to Ho-chi minh residental place. It is really one pilar pagoda and very famous for local ladies especially for new married. They went there and pray for happinis and childeren. And dedicate some foods or clothes to pagoda. There is a small lake with lotus flowers and it really interesting. CheersErnur

reviews.author: SomaK95762
reviews.title: A nice little pagoda
reviews.content: This a nice and small pagoda located in the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Nothing great or not a must see but if you are in Ho Chi Minh complex then a quick visit is not bad.

reviews.author: 69clive
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: A lovely pagoda in beautiful grounds with a lot of history and lovely gardens surrounding it. Unfortunately we went on a typhoon day and the rain was torrential so we did not see it at its best

reviews.author: Peter D
reviews.title: It just sits on One Pillar, therefore its name
reviews.content: Around the corner from Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum in the adjoining complex.  It is small and the stairs are steep and crowded.  Just too many people at once trying to view the inside.

reviews.author: Richard E
reviews.title: Very nice
reviews.content: It is called one pillar because it is sitting perched up on one pillar, great name. Close to other attractions

reviews.author: EhudSpe
reviews.title: Nice to visit on the way
reviews.content: Would not go there only to see this pagoda. But if you are visiting HCM Mausoleum and house, it is worth the stop.

reviews.author: andreaswinkler
reviews.title: Landmark of Hanoi
reviews.content: This is a must see and in vicinity of the Ho Chi Minh Museum and Mausoleum. It is located very pretty and very unusual. The Ho chi Minh house and palace and the neraby temple are worth a visit as well.

reviews.author: Karl L
reviews.title: Fascinating architecture.
reviews.content: What a fascinating piece of architecture.   Nestled behind the Museum is this interesting piece that rises out of the water on one pillar.   It's a must see and all you need is to walk over after going through the Mausoleum Must see

reviews.author: amadeus11190382
reviews.title: Unusual temple very popular attraction.
reviews.content: Sadly being renovated when visited in October 2015 ,the works must be finished by now and well worth a visit to this replica one legged pagoda. It is just around the corner from Ho Chi Minh museum.  ,

reviews.author: Girlfitz66
reviews.title: Not something worth your time
reviews.content: Went with my family of four kids to see this. While it has an interesting story, there is nothing special about it. The water around it is dirty and polluted and honestly that just made us all feel a little sad.

reviews.author: SittoK
reviews.title: Centuries preserved
reviews.content: We visited this attraction on a city tour of Hanoi and had a very knowledgeable tour guide relate the story behind the pagoda and it's origins. Set in a beautiful garden, this pagoda is revered by local people as the place to pray for fertility and to bear male children. That it's been rehabilitated to its original structure post the war damage is a wonder since the pagoda was built in the early 1000's.

reviews.author: luckyrabbit1113
reviews.title: Interesting story, but that's about iy
reviews.content: Many travel guides list One Pillar Pagoda as an essential stop in Hanoi, and the Pagoda's history and the legend surrounding it definitely piqued my interest. However, upon arrival, we realized that the pagoda is quite small, and the long line of tourists and oppressive heat led to our decision to forgo closeup pictures with the statue of Quanyin inside. If you would like to go, I suggest going early to beat the crowds and the heat!

reviews.author: Renée D.
reviews.title: Nothing Amazing
reviews.content: Nothing amazing, but it's within walking distance of the museum, the mausoleum, the temple of literature so if you must see, do visit. I guess it's worth checking offf your list.

reviews.author: Paul C
reviews.title: Save your time, there are a myriad of better places to go
reviews.content: Caught the taxi to the complex and thought great time as the place was quiet and very few people around. Walked down street to the entrance and there it was. It is not the original but a rebuilt replica and looks new. In fact it looked like a kids cubby on top of a power pole. Took the time to walk around and view it from all sides, climb the steps and view the altar inside though you can't go in - and there would be no space. I had read the history and this reconstruction devalued the impact. There are so many other places that offer a better experience.

reviews.author: 317yolandam
reviews.title: This pagoda is very delicate and beautiful
reviews.content: This pagoda is very beautiful in its architecture. Do not expect a gigantic pagoda. Look carefully at the details and the setting.

reviews.author: E G
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: Don't expect too much. The pagoda is in area of Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and it is not the original pagoda. Too many tourist and nothing special.

reviews.author: Kschwam
reviews.title: Read the history!
reviews.content: If you're going to the Ho Chi Minh complex, definitely read up on the history of one pillar pagoda! Much more interesting that way. Very famous temple in Vietnam. Rebuilt after the indochina war.

reviews.author: JasonNguyen24
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: One pillar pagoda is the symbol of Vietnam. Visit Hanoi, you should go to this pagoda. It is in the Ho Chi Minh Complex.

reviews.author: A local
reviews.title: rather busy..and small
reviews.content: This is beside an area where a lot sales happen and meeting point- its attractive enough, but just part of  overall visit to the Palace.

reviews.author: HotelKshipram U
reviews.title: one pillar pagoda
reviews.content: one pillar pagoda is in same compound Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and near museaum , its good little architecture to be visited .

reviews.author: d0dge47
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: We found this when we were trying to get to the mausoleum.Very impressive and peaceful - however there was not too many good easy directions to get about the area after visiting the musuem. We also found the mausoleum shuts about 11.30am!

reviews.author: danielstlee
reviews.title: Small pagoda
reviews.content: A small pagoda near the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, may not be a place to catch your attraction but since it is so near with the rest, you may opt to have few minutes there to find any interesting stuff.

reviews.author: Kjell S
reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.content: It is a really small pagoda!You visit it once! And then you have seen it!The history of the pagoda is more interesting than The pagoda!

reviews.author: deejay90210
reviews.title: A small Pagoda
reviews.content: Just a small Pagoda behind the Mausoleum. OK for a quick visit when visiting the Mausoleum. Can sit around the small lake.

reviews.author: Greyhound77
reviews.title: Ok
reviews.content: This forms part of the Ho Chi Minh complex. It's not spectacular, but it's nice to see as you're wading through the crowds.

reviews.author: berver65
reviews.title: When visiting Ho Chi Minh museum
reviews.content: This pagoda deserves a quick look because of its originality. It's on your way when visiting Ho Chi Minh museum or Ho Chi Minh's house. Or just behind the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum.After seeing so many temples, I didn't bother going up to see the inside. I should have because I now read that the godess inside is a lady (another original point). I was curious to read about it in Wikipedia. I copied a part of it here below :The One Pillar Pagoda  is a historic Buddhist temple in Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam. It is regarded alongside the Perfume Temple, as one of Vietnam's two most iconic temples.The temple was built by Emperor Lý Thái Tông, who ruled from 1028 to 1054. According to the court records, Lý Thái Tông was childless and dreamt that he met the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, who handed him a baby son while seated on a lotus flower. Lý Thái Tông then married a peasant girl that he had met and she bore him a son. The emperor constructed the temple in gratitude for this in 1049, having been told by a monk named Thiền Tuệ to build the temple, by erecting a pillar in the middle of a lotus pond, similar to the one he saw in the dream.The temple is built of wood on a single stone pillar 1.25 m in diameter, and it is designed to resemble a lotus blossom, which is a Buddhist symbol of purity, since a lotus blossoms in a muddy pond. In 1954, the French Union forces destroyed the pagoda before withdrawing from Vietnam after the First Indochina War, It was rebuilt afterwards.

reviews.author: MirreL
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: We went to see the residence and museum of Ho Chi Minh and along the way we also saw this pagoda when passing by. It's not the best attraction that keeps you up for an hour but it's quite nice to see for a few minutes.

reviews.author: hardwil
reviews.title: Wow, a pagoda on a pillar
reviews.content: This is a rebuilt copy of a very old small temple which is built on a single upright column. Set in a small park but with a lot of people mingling around.

reviews.author: Paul L
reviews.title: A nice place to visit.
reviews.content: This was a nice place to go for a walk to. A lot to see around the area as you walk. Go have a look.

reviews.author: Deb W
reviews.title: A temple with a female Buddha
reviews.content: People come here to pray for fertilization. The female Buddha was new to me so that made it very interesting.

reviews.author: CFofLL
reviews.title: Interesting but not overwhelming.
reviews.content: Our guide was very enthusiastic about the One Pillar Pagoda but I found it interesting but not overly spectacular.  Apparently the original was built on a pillar in the middle of a swamp about 1000 years ago and it was destroyed in the war with the French in 1954.  It was rebuilt and has the mandatory small Buddhist shrine inside.  Worth a quick look, but lots of more interesting things nearby.

reviews.author: M B
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: We were in the area visiting the mausoleum and found this tiny pagoda. A good place to drop in but there's not much else to see.

reviews.author: Wenhan Y
reviews.title: A symbol of Hanoi, but nothing too spetacular
reviews.content: The one pillar pagoda has almost become the symbol of Hanoi, it's everywhere from fridge magnet to tourism advertisements. When you get there you may be disappointed by the size and the simple structure of the pagoda. In fact I doubt whether this can be called a "pagoda". It is a small pavilion for praying, on a quiet day, sitting on a bench next to the pagoda looking at how the locals and a few other tourists walk about in the small square surrounding it is a joy in itself . Nevertheless it is still a "must-see" of Hanoi, fortunately you can combine it with Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the museum and the Imperial citadel which is about 500 meters away.

reviews.author: Collin578
reviews.title: Nice but a little overhyped
reviews.content: Cute pagoda, but it's really tiny and not much to look at. Worth visiting if you're near the mausoleum anyways

reviews.author: steveuk
reviews.title: Can be done when visiting How Chi Minh complex
reviews.content: It's worth taking a look whilst visiting the mausoleum. A pretty little architectural structure that's inside the HCM grounds

reviews.author: LozArthur
reviews.title: Cute
reviews.content: Nice little pagoda on a pillar surrounded by souvenir shops, bustling tourists and eateries. Really is a two minute visit as you're in the complex.

reviews.author: lisa c
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Very interesting, but not much to see except the pillar.  It was apparently burned by the French.  Nice garden around it

reviews.author: Mai S
reviews.title: Average Structure but Excellent as Part of the HCM Complex
reviews.content: Our family of 5 visited the One Pillar Pagoda in May 2016. On its own, it is quite average, but taken together with the other structures within the HCM Complex, it provides a complete and enjoyable viewing experience.

reviews.author: Larry M
reviews.title: Unique!!
reviews.content: Located within the Ho Chi Minh complex, this small Chinese style pagoda on water is a nice photo op, but can get crowded when a tour bus arrives or at certain busy times...go early in the morning to beat the heat and crowds.

reviews.author: Rigoberto S
reviews.title: Good walking area
reviews.content: There are much better temples in the area then versus One Pillar; but the area is well groomed and kept up. Good for walking and enjoying the surrounding area.

reviews.author: Hyppe
reviews.title: Small pagoda
reviews.content: The pagoda is so small, the whole place was so crowded. There is no way you can take a nice photo. This place is filled with locals and tourists. Go only if you have no where else to go.

reviews.author: Pete
reviews.title: It's alright
reviews.content: Was heading to a museum nearby and this was on the way so decided to have a look. It's a lot smaller than I had imagined and therefore I wasn't as impressed by it. It does look good, so grab a photo, but I'd only visit if passing by this area.

reviews.author: 365Weathers
reviews.title: Cultural experience
reviews.content: Must see old historic site of Hanoi, it's a short walk from the HCM memorial in the park area of Hanoi, worth the vist

reviews.author: Scottiehere
reviews.title: Ok if you're in the area.
reviews.content: This is in the same are as the mausoleum so if you are in the area then pop in and have a look, otherwise no need to make a special trip.

reviews.author: Incense Travel
reviews.title: Small but interesting
reviews.content: Despite being recently restored this pagoda still looks ancient and interesting. This is considered to be the symbol for Buddhism in Vietnam. The whole structure is put on a pillar(like the name). It combines well with another pagoda right next to it. All located in the Ho Chi Minh complex.

reviews.author: Szabin
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: It's part of the peaceful garden next to Ho Chi Minh Maosoleum and Museum, $2 entry fee is applied.Smaller than I expected and bit crowdy and really nice. Tortoises, gold fishes, crabs are in the water, gives you great opportunity for photo shots.

reviews.author: goafishing
reviews.title: Another bit of history
reviews.content: Interesting and visited as part of the city tour, worth visiting to understand some more of the history of Vietnam.

reviews.author: Kev W
reviews.title: Smaller than I expected
reviews.content: It's ok. Go and take some pictures if you happen to be nearby. It's close to the Ho Chi Minh museum and mausoleum so you may as well take a look if you go to either of these attractions.

reviews.author: Maria T
reviews.title: Nice, but busy
reviews.content: It is a really nice place, but so crowded with so many tourists because it's close to the Ho Chi Minh museum, but it's still a nice place to see if you're in the area.

reviews.author: ckychong
reviews.title: One of the local attraction
reviews.content: It's located nearby to the Ho Chi Minh museum. You should drop by if you are around this museum. You may also do some prayer at the pagoda.

reviews.author: John G
reviews.title: Very busy
reviews.content: This is right next to the HCM Museum so expect it to be packed. The pagoda itself is pretty cool but it's nice to just sit on a bench and watch the world go by.

reviews.author: Stephen M
reviews.title: Small pond with a small pagoda
reviews.content: This is usually combined with the Ho Chi Minh visit and there is a pagoda built on a pillar over a small pond (too small to be called a lake really). You can look it but it just seems like another opportunity for people to try and sell you stuff.

reviews.author: Cashkoala
reviews.title: Go if you are in the area
reviews.content: We did because we went to the Ho Chi Minh museum. Actually the museum was closed for lunch so we walked around the corner to the Pagoda.  It's historic and locals were there to pray. It is small. Read up on it first so you know what it is.

reviews.author: Jason G
reviews.title: Cute
reviews.content: If you're looking to save the 30 minutes or so it takes to walk here from the mausoleum, take a few pictures and look inside, then you can probably skip this site, but if you have a little time to spare then it's worth a quick visit. We were in Hanoi for less than a day and easily fit this in. Was actually a little harder to find than I expected, but ultimately if you just follow the crowds from the mausoleum (even during non peak times) you should be able to find it. We were there after the mausoleum had closed, so the pagoda and the surrounding area wasn't too crowded.

reviews.author: Peter N
reviews.title: It's okay
reviews.content: The surrounding area has some very nice attractions, so as long as you're there this is a fun extra, but nothing something super special or a 'must-see'.

reviews.author: Kathy K
reviews.title: Wouldn't make a special trip
reviews.content: It appears most people visit this as part of Uncle Ho's Mauseleum.  The lines were hours long when we were there, so we visited the pagoda only.  This area in general is interesting to witness the loyalty and admiration they have for the great Father.  You may spend 10 minutes at this venue, tops.

reviews.author: Joan S
reviews.title: Quick tour will do
reviews.content: Just a quick tour in this spot will do. But if you want to take some rest from walking, there are shaded areas where you can sit down. However, note that this place is a bit crowded, both by tourists and locals.

reviews.author: Roger W
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: Be prepared for the crowds that gather around this area, having said that  there are numerous  historical attractions nearby. This Pagoda is unusual in its design and its worth seeing.

reviews.author: HDLBruxelles
reviews.title: Ok in the big area of ho chi minh temple
reviews.content: Honestly, you don t have to walk 100 km under the sun for this small temple without any interest except the pilar. One good thing is the area of ambassades: nice local architecture. You are not far too of the mausolee of ho chi minh ( if you are falled in love for this guy). In summary, a lot of reasons to loose a few minutes on the site of thid pagoda

reviews.author: DaleBbB
reviews.title: Queue up to make a wish
reviews.content: Our tour guide advised us that the altar at the top of the stairs is the place to make wish that is guaranteed to come true. So we joined the queue, made our wish and had our photo taken.

reviews.author: Ngan H
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: A bit disappointed when I reached there. Lots of review written about this place but what you can see there is just a small 'pagoda' dedicated to the resident spirit. Maybe important to the locals.

reviews.author: Marcell_54
reviews.title: A Unique Pagoda..
reviews.content: This Pagoda is near the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, or you can say it's in one place. I visit this place after i visit the mausoleum. There are many people come to pray at this Pagoda. For me,  i got an interesting story about this pagoda. The temple was built by Emperor Lý Thái Tông, who ruled from 1028 to 1054. Overall, it is a simple and unique place to visit (but don't expect it will be a "grand" place) .

reviews.author: Chivesdiners
reviews.title: Top ten sight
reviews.content: Sits in a small park. Very busy. Lots of market stalls for tourist needs. Toilets available. pretty temple opposite.

reviews.author: petra354
reviews.title: Must see if you have free afternoon
reviews.content: Pagoda is very cute and looks good on photo. There is nice a park around so you can hide before sun.

reviews.author: Valerietravels2
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: This is very interesting and the story behind it as well. Go early as it gets crowded as the day goes on.

reviews.author: Sandlab
reviews.title: Battered by History
reviews.content: An fascinating  place to read about, with a long and interesting history, but a little underwhelming when finally approached. The structure has been renovated and rebuilt so many times it is hard to feel much awe when one queues for up to one hour (perhaps more) to get inside the Hi Chi Minh complex then has to fight through hordes of visitors and worshipers to finally reach the pagoda.As an aside, Hanoi is full of one pillar transformers and they provide some interest when one is stuck in the traffic in the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Su H
reviews.title: One pillar pagoda
reviews.content: I thought it was a big one in the lake. But it's a small one and the man made lake is also a very small one. Not many particular things to look around.  Very close , or can be said within the same compound, to Ho Chi Minh mausoleum.

reviews.author: LouenStephan
reviews.title: good to have a look
