reviews.content: The very small pagoda is situated nearby Ho Chi Minh mausoleum, museum and house.  It's only some steps away.  Good to take a picture, not more than that

reviews.author: CathyGri
reviews.title: Good to include as part of your sightseeing
reviews.content: This is part of the same complex where Ho Chi Minh's wooden ethnic minority house where he lived from 1954-1069  is located. This temple is an important symbol to the people of Hanoi. It is a small building reached by a flight of steps and only takes a few minutes to visit.  Allow a minimum of an hour though to visit the complex on the single entry ticket and be prepared to queue for entry to the site if coach parties have just arrived.

reviews.author: BijanTehran_Iran
reviews.title: worth a short visit
reviews.content: Just attached to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and inside the complex.A small beautiful Pagoda with a nice legend.

reviews.author: FayeInAmsterdam
reviews.title: Architectural wonder
reviews.content: When in Asia there are a lot of pagodas, monasteries and ancient buildings to visit. This pagoda is small but very special. Sometimes it's very nice to appreciate the small architecture instead of huge buildings and spaces. So you can go on to the next beautiful landmark to visit in Hanoi.

reviews.author: AlHarvey4
reviews.title: Not that Impressive
reviews.content: This is one of the top rated attractions in Hanoi and maybe it is but there wasn't a lot in Hanoi that impressed me and this certainly wasn't one of them.

reviews.author: Pedro C
reviews.title: Not an impresive structure but worth seen as part of the Ho Chi Mi mauseleum trip
reviews.content: We had the occasion of meeting there some ladies from a far away tribe in the mountains who where sight-seen for the first time. Very interesting, like anything else i Vietnam

reviews.author: roskii
reviews.title: Quick stop
reviews.content: Stopped by after visiting the main gardens of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Very small pagoda with an interesting history but not much else.

reviews.author: JerryH9905
reviews.title: Short Stop Near Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum; Quite Nice
reviews.content: January 31, 2016 - Just a short time after visiting Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, his house and grounds, it is worth a brief visit to the One  Pillar Pagoda.  The Pagoda is located over top of water and has some steep steps to climb to get to the entrance.  Once at the entrance, one can see the beautiful religious display.  Of course, it was crowded but everyone was respectful of each other.  Since we were on the property, it was definitely worth the visit.

reviews.author: The_Don_Francisco
reviews.title: Part of the site of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: A bit of a line to view inside but worth it from an historical point of view.  Lots to do throughout the grounds and this is just a small item on the site.

reviews.author: JLC-1972
reviews.title: Quickly viewed
reviews.content: It is a nice little pagoda with an interesting history. It is, however, a shame that it is a replica, due to the French destruction of the original. It is right next to the Ho Chi Minh Museum, so quickly viewed.

reviews.author: Rainie Green
reviews.title: Good place for photos only
reviews.content: They said that One Pillar Pagoda is one of Hanoi's symbol. You can get here for free entrance ticket, take some photos to show that you'd been here and that's all. It's also said that couples shouldn't come here together (they can broke up after that), do you believe that?

reviews.author: Jenny S
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Located at the back of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, it is a pretty area to visit and One Pillar Pagoda was very popular with people lining up just to walk up the steps and to have their photo taken in front of it. A must if you sare visiting the Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Swetha B
reviews.title: Not sure what was the big deal
reviews.content: So I knew before going itself that this place was going to be crowded but I really didn't understand the hype behind this attraction. It may have been better with less tourists all around and a better surrounding environment. But it is in the HCM mausoleum and presidential house vicinity so no harm in passing by and seeing it

reviews.author: Nigel W
reviews.title: One pillar or one Foot?
reviews.content: In the same area as the Mausoleum and a very pretty pagoda surround by water. A nice visit and somewhere to relax in shade if hot.

reviews.author: Travnur
reviews.title: So many people we were unable to go thru this
reviews.content: We were able to see this from the sidewalk but the crowds were heavy and it was very hot and humid.  We did see the areas where Ho Chi Minh lived a very austere life in his later years.   Things were very basic which you have to respect because the country is still poor.

reviews.author: passion4
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Situated in the Ho Chi Min complex.  We were able to walk to this attraction to visit the Muasoleum, Museum, One Pillar Pagoda and Palace.  Very interesting visit and peaceful walk around the garden areas.

reviews.author: soniar26
reviews.title: Pit stop.
reviews.content: Stopped her briefly on our tour. Pretty little temple with market stalls in the vicinity selling tourist tat.

reviews.author: Hannie A
reviews.title: Pretty boring tourist attraction
reviews.content: Everyone seems to get pretty excited about this landmark but be warned that is isn't that interesting.  It is as it is named - a pagoda on one pillar standing in a pond. It isn't even a particularly attractive pagoda, it even kind of looks like a modern construction. We got pretty interested at one point after being told there was an otter in the pond but we didn't see one after many long minutes of eye straining. However there are koi and a big frog hanging out in the water so it wasn't a total loss. If you're in the area go by for a photo so you can say you've seen it but I wouldn't suggest going out of your way.

reviews.author: Glenys W
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: Close to the mausoleum, this pagoda has an interesting history and one that I wasn't aware of.  Fortunately our Buffalo Tours guide could enlighten us on the history behind this building.

reviews.author: DeadlyddPerth
reviews.title: Interetsing but not a lot to see
reviews.content: It was part of our city tour - allow about ten minutes. It was good to see and is close to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum so it can be accessed easy.

reviews.author: Gary C
reviews.title: Ok if you are Buddist
reviews.content: Not an impressive site. Could leave off your visit list. Lots of sounvirs shops. Not much else. Fish pond, well I felt sorry for the fish!

reviews.author: Ulrikbuchert
reviews.title: Interesting structure...but that's about it...
reviews.content: If you're inside the Ho Chi Minh-mausoleum complex anyways, then why not go have a look at the one-pillar pagoda. It's not something you should plan your day around :)

reviews.author: ChrisA2107
reviews.title: Not worth a special visit
reviews.content: Worth a visit if you are in the area, but not worth going out of your way. It is an interesting building, but there is not any more to it than what you see in the photo.

reviews.author: michael p
reviews.title: Worth a photo
reviews.content: This is not an attraction that is worth going out of your way for. If you are near the Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum then it is worth looking at and grabbing a few photos. Good example of 11th century architectue designed to resemble a lotus bloom.

reviews.author: Merc9SLK
reviews.title: Tiny pagoda over run with tourists
reviews.content: This could be much better than it is portrayed.  Over run with soooo many tourists queuing up the staircase to view the adorned alter table - not at all personal and not at all serene.  The small pool at the bottom of the pagoda is very green - not clean water as you might expect and not laden with water lillies or fish.  Around the perimeter of the area leading to the pagoda you have the usual tourist stalls selling the usual tat of hats, t shirts, sweets etc.  Everyone jostling for space for a picture in front of the small structure.The only plus side is that it is not within the parameter of the mausoleum grounds which means it is free to enter however, it is not well sign posted from the road which means you will find it from pure guess work or to follow the crowds.

reviews.author: abi1985
reviews.title: Of little interest
reviews.content: Not worth visiting, unless of course you are there for the mausoleum or museaum. Otherwise fairly unremarkable.

reviews.author: Perry H
reviews.title: Vietnam trip
reviews.content: Fun little Pagoda set inside Ho Chi Minh's garden area. As your walking out from the garden and small lake, it's on your right. Can't miss it and good for a few pictures.

reviews.author: wildtree
reviews.title: Small but interesting
reviews.content: This is an interesting temple. It's small, but has a lot of heart. Lots of locals visiting to pay their tributes and pray. Remember to remove your shoes before entering buildings here - it's a sign of respect. Free to enter and visit. When we visited, a monk was praying and we got to listen while we walked around.

reviews.author: Owlfred W W
reviews.title: Interesting small Pagoda
reviews.content: If you are visiting the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum site then this pagoda is very close and worth looking at. It was much smaller than I was expecting.

reviews.author: AA Mel
reviews.title: Near Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum-Pretty Setting
reviews.content: Would not go out of my way to see this, but if you are visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, it is very close and worth seeing.

reviews.author: Rob M
reviews.title: Ok. You'll be there anyway.
reviews.content: If you are visiting the mausoleum you'll be there anyway. Rude Chinese tourists shove their way in front.  It's pretty and unusual so why not have a look while in the vicinity.

reviews.author: rjonesirv
reviews.title: Very old pagoda
reviews.content: A very colorful and interestingly shaped pagoda.  We were there on a Holiday and it was very crowded, but well used by the locals.  You can see how they pay their respects.

reviews.author: Angela J
reviews.title: Not much to see...just a house, on stilts
reviews.content: You can't go in the rooms and there isn't much to see inside of them anyways. The grounds are nicer and more to look at than this house.

reviews.author: 1william5555
reviews.title: Only can view from shore
reviews.content: Not much info on the one pillar Pagoda so read up on it before going to see it. The Pagoda is not open to the public so it is only a photo spot

reviews.author: EllaYaldwyn
reviews.title: If you're already at the museum or mausoleum you may as well...
reviews.content: Enjoyed seeing it (and is conveniently located im between Ho Chi Minh Museum and Mausoleum) but after taking one photo we'd done pretty much all there was to do there. It didn't help that we visited on a Monday and everything was closed but still good to tick of the list of places to go

reviews.author: angie g
reviews.title: Great look at Vietnam histoty
reviews.content: Great to see such a big piece of history still standing.  Take time to go and look at it and understand significance

reviews.author: NickDavis
reviews.title: On the Mausoleum tour - a quick stop
reviews.content: Its small and can have long lines. Locals believe praying here brings benefits. Its right by the Mausoleum and Museum so probably on the itinerary for all doing those tours. a quick stop is okay + you can get ice cream here if it's a hot day (rather than dull and grey when we visited in February)

reviews.author: June K
reviews.title: Beautiful pagoda with lots of history
reviews.content: This is one of the places travelers tell you to visit.  It was not a disappointment.  Good photo ops if the weather cooperates.

reviews.author: Annmarie B
reviews.title: A Pagoda
reviews.content: In the grounds of the national museum and behind the mausoleum, however, having seen numerous temples and pagados in Vietnam, this one didn't stand out other than the fact it was on a single pillar!!!!

reviews.author: multi v
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: It stands buy an elegant lotus pond. It is well worth the wait to see the inside up the steps. It is very small, but very charming and gives a good view of the area.

reviews.author: Mark C
reviews.title: Good starting point in Hanoi
reviews.content: After seeing this it's easy to walk around the lake and start to get a feel for the city without trying to wade through the streets of the Old Quarter, which is probably best reserved for the evening.

reviews.author: hikkaduwa_10
reviews.title: Very nice area
reviews.content: it's just round the corner from Hochimin masoleum so these 2 sights should definitely come together. The area around the pagoda is like a small park with benches and traditional shopping.

reviews.author: garry468
reviews.title: ummmmm
reviews.content: concrete post with small house on top...well nearly....not what i was expecting...but park of the ho chi minn tour

reviews.author: Mayur S
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is a historic temple dedicated to the Vietnamese Buddhist deity Quan Am. Originally built in 1028, it has been destroyed and rebuilt several times. This Pagoda and the Perfume Temple are Vietnam's two most iconic temples. It is constructed from wood with on a single stone pillar crafted into the shape of a lotus blossom as its base. The temple is set in a tranquil garden with benches provided for comfortable contemplation.

reviews.author: Makbule O
reviews.title: Very nice but dont expect too much
reviews.content: Very nice but dont expect too much.easy to find pagoda.if you are around must check it out ,if not dont sweat it

reviews.author: MrFood&Wine
reviews.title: Nice temple
reviews.content: It was a nice experience to learn about the traditions they practice. The buildings are quite nice to look at. The history and tradition of the one pillar pagoda is interesting.

reviews.author: EarlyRetirementAbroad
reviews.title: Too many tourists
reviews.content: Nice pagoda that so surrounded by the tourists, that hard to enjoy it fully.  Everyone would stop there after the Mausoleum.

reviews.author: davemartin3
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: If you are visiting the presidential palace then you should certainly take the trouble to visit here as well. Not particularly imposing but nonetheless interesting as part of a day trip.

reviews.author: Valerie W
reviews.title: Pretty but long queues
reviews.content: There were long queues to go up into the Pagoda and it is more relevant to those who follow Buddhism

reviews.author: Ross B
reviews.title: This lies right on the edge of the Presedential Palace grounds and is
reviews.content: This pagoda lies right on the edge of the Presedential Palace grounds and as a temple is very small but you just want climb the steps as the Pagola and see inside

reviews.author: GioSousa
reviews.title: I recommend!
reviews.content: It is very important to not only enjoy the food and drinks but also know about the history of the place. I absolutely recommend getting a tour guide to explain the history of this wonderful place.

reviews.author: Anthony S
reviews.title: Not much interest here
reviews.content: This comes at the end of the tour of Ho's mausoleum complex and is pretty much a pass through and not a lot of interest for us.

reviews.author: Miller_KO
reviews.title: Interesting and unique pagoda...
reviews.content: Visited the pagoda with friends which was inspired by a dream the Emperor Ly Thai Tong had in 1409 where he was given a boy by the goddess of mercy and later had a son with the queen. Burnt by the French and rebuilt in 1954 it is supposed to show the Emperors appreciation to the goddess. This pagoda is set inside the imperial grounds close to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and is good to see as apart of the trip, but it is not worth spending to much time on the pagoda.

reviews.author: Jordi N
reviews.title: Nice but not worth for itself
reviews.content: Nice and curious temple close to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and museum. It is very small and if you don't plan to the mausoleum, don't worth to go till there.

reviews.author: Smileydeb
reviews.title: Interesting legend behind the pagoda
reviews.content: The pagoda was built by Emporer Ly Thai Tong in AD 1409.  Legend has it that he had a dream in which he was visited by Queen Ann, Goddess of Mercy, who was sitting on a lotus flower, and presented him with a baby boy.He later married a young queen and had a son.  He built the pagoda, standing in a lotus pond, to show his gratitude. It stands on one pillar and is supposed to represent purity like a lotus blossoming in a muddy pond.The French burnt it in 1954 so it had to be reconstructed. Worth a visit but you need to know the legend to truly appreciate it.

reviews.author: TJA950
reviews.title: Don't Miss the Adjacent Temple
reviews.content: There’s a danger in Vietnam that you can get “templed out” and consider this as just another temple. Yes, it is in a way but this is a unique and unusual one and very pretty. It is never going to be a “wow” building but if you are in the area, then it is definitely worth seeing. There is an adjacent temple which is part of the small complex which I noted was being missed by many of the tourists. Make sure you see this too as it is very interesting.

reviews.author: Z1619WIcarolineb
reviews.title: Wooden one pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Made in the shape of a lotus the wooden pagoda stands on a singlepillar, lots of locals seem to enjoy being near it. Rebuilt in 1955.

reviews.author: bmkh
reviews.title: Interesting architecture, pretty interior, nothing special
reviews.content: We saw the surrounding area including the garden aside and the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. There is no information given at the pagoda itself, therefore I would advise to inform yourself beforehand to have at least some knowledge of why/how and so on the one pillar pagoda is what it is. It is not very impressive and not a must do, though I have to honestly say that none of the visited "standard" tourist sites in Hanoi are groundbreaking or breathtaking. If you're in the area, then go, if not, the visit is not necessary.

reviews.author: Banda-in-Japan
reviews.title: A bit of a letdown
reviews.content: For all its fame, we were disappointed by this "pagoda" and couldn't really feel that it was anything special.  But, given its location, just next to the HCM Museum, it's an easy site to visit.

reviews.author: xfooey
reviews.title: Small pagoda in the same general are as Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and Museum
reviews.content: It's a small pagoda with lot's of visitors.  Plenty of tourists and locals.  Worth a quick stop and a few pics.

reviews.author: Brian L
reviews.title: One of the many Pagodas in Ha Noi
reviews.content: Dedicated to the Goddess of Mercy, Kwan Yin, this is a nice spot to stretch the legs and enjoy the site. And, if you are wanting blessings from Kwan Yin, take the time and pray for what you want

reviews.author: d_gsy
reviews.title: Yeah, it's another pagoda really
reviews.content: If you love temples or haven't really seen many yet, then drop by and you'll see something interesting. We've been all over Vietnam, and it wasn't any different to any of the other small pagodas - not like the impressive stuff around hue.

reviews.author: Jac-and-Jek
reviews.title: Not much
reviews.content: It is just a very small pagoda style building built over one pillar. I think it is nothing impressive. Same overall feeling as the whole Vietnam: overrated

reviews.author: Leonard S
reviews.title: Meditate in the middle of Hanoi
reviews.content: A reconstruction as the French destroyed the pillar when they left Hanoi. The top was not terribly damaged and so we have it here. The Buddha within the pagoda emanates warmth and peace and is worth the climb

reviews.author: Wgou
reviews.title: Just a small attraction
reviews.content: It's only a reproduction of the original, so while slightly interesting, I wouldn't make a special trip to see it.  You'll probably see it on one of the tours you take of Hanoi, and it's worth seeing then.

reviews.author: Badazi V
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: I think this place is good. An old and small pagoda. You should visit it if you visit ho chi minh musoleum

reviews.author: scottyljd
reviews.title: Interesting story
reviews.content: Part of you entry to the Presidential Palace. Interesting story attached to this pagoda and fascinating to see so may people still worshiping there.

reviews.author: Zalsapehuh
reviews.title: Free!
reviews.content: Visit it along the way from the mausoleum. I understand many of the reviews says its nothing special. It's free! And it's not as if you needa travel all the way from somewhere else to see it. It's along the way from the mausoleum to one of the nearby museums. When else would u get to see a one pillar pagoda anyway?

reviews.author: Orcinusmoon
reviews.title: Great backstory
reviews.content: I came here with my tour guide from Hanoi Kids (book them!!) And got to experience this location with the story behind it. Definitely come to this and other places with a guide--so much more meaning

reviews.author: 236Paul
reviews.title: Ineresting pagoda in Hanoi
reviews.content: Very special pagoda to be seen in Hanoi city center, with butiful location and an interesting history, well worth to be seen.

reviews.author: Mark F
reviews.title: Nice Place
reviews.content: I loved this place when I visited it for the first time with my friends. but when I visited second time with my gf it was not at all excited me as it had before. Its nice place when you visit it first.

reviews.author: Joachim O
reviews.title: One column Pagoda
reviews.content: the One Pillar pagoda is a unicque type of pagoda. Origianally it was built on top of a tree trunk wich later was replaced by a concrete column. Placed in the center of a pond it is still worth wile to be visited.

reviews.author: Angela B
reviews.title: Small, But Nice Story
reviews.content: This is a really small pagoda & as suggested by the name, it sits on a single pillar. The story behind it is sweet; built in the 11th Century by an emperor to thank the goddess of mercy for a male heir basically. It's supposed to represent a lotus blossom. Unfortunately the French destroyed it in the '50's so this is a rebuilt version.

reviews.author: PeterSB_11
reviews.title: Unique little Pagoda
reviews.content: We had seen this image on T-shirts and it was a pleasant site to see.  It is part of a bigger complex and thus no extra effort to visit.

reviews.author: Barbara K
reviews.title: Good for a really quick stop
reviews.content: This is one of the sights on the one-day tour of Hanoi.  Cute little pagoda on what's now a cement column--used to be wood, but that deteriorated over the centuries.

reviews.author: Italianshopper
reviews.title: just see it to believe it!
reviews.content: Its along a nice walk through the grounds of Ho Chi Minh's home so just take a quick peak. Charming.

reviews.author: Paspy7711
reviews.title: Small but a main attraction
reviews.content: Located a bit outside but close to the mausoleum of Ho-Chi-Minh you will find pictures of this pagoda everywhere in Vietnam so its one of the must-sees.Rather inimpressive and always photographe from an angle that covers the real surroundong and size. Its really small and more a puddle than a pond in front.Very annoying touts and stalls in the area with the most insane prices of all Vietnam, just ignore them and move on to the mausoleum.

reviews.author: sigerjet
reviews.title: symbol of Vietonam
reviews.content: I hard that is symbolic of blooming lotus.  Indeed it is built with only one pillar.it was surprisingly small temple but so different.it's easy to come there where is close to Hochiminh museum.

reviews.author: TauntonBob
reviews.title: Cute
reviews.content: A very interesting little pagoda, perched on a pillar over a tiny lake.  It is certainly worth climbing the steps to get a view inside.

reviews.author: LPHDK
reviews.title: Cute
reviews.content: I would not make a trip to this pagoda, but if you are in the neighborhood, it is worth a stop and a picture.

reviews.author: Ishadhi R
reviews.title: 1000 years old pagoda
reviews.content: Vietnam is a 80% buddhist country. One king has seen his newly born son is coming out from a lotus flower in a dream and once the queen has given the birth to his son he made this pagoda looks like a lotus flower. that is why it has only a one pillar.

reviews.author: jaybeeFL
reviews.title: Overemphasized! Underwhelmed!
reviews.content: Although it is one of the most photographed sites in all of Hanoi, I found it to be nothing more than a cute pagoda on a single stilt. What do I know???? Took the picture and moved on to the museum.

reviews.author: Mickthexton
reviews.title: Very Interesting
reviews.content: The whole site is very interesting with lots of interesting buildings and beautiful gardens.Recommend using a guide to get the most from your visit

reviews.author: TravelDooey
reviews.title: Stop by after the mausoleum
reviews.content: It's worth 5 minutes of your time after you visit the mausoleum.  You'll be passing by it anyway & it's free

reviews.author: JasonDoz
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: A nice little pagoda located pretty close to the centre of Hanoi. If you're in the area it's worth visiting and getting a few photos

reviews.author: LouJohnson
reviews.title: Underwhelmed
reviews.content: With an interesting history attached I'd expected something grander so came away disappointed. However the locals seemed to enjoy it and watching them was fun.

reviews.author: What We Found Travelling
reviews.title: Not Much To See
reviews.content: This pagoda is small & there is not much to see.  If you're in the area it's worth a look, but no need to go out of your way to see it.  However, it is in a nice location for photos & close to other attractions.

reviews.author: Sarasij M
reviews.title: The Single Pillar Pagoda:-A small beautiful Pagoda
reviews.content: In the MAUSOLEUM complex, you will find a Single Pillar Pagoda-- built by Emperor L.T.Tong, under a divine command, received in a dream, and after it was built, he was blessed with a son.This is possibly the only single Pillar pagoda, in Vietnam.The name of the DEITY, seems to be MARICI--- the GODESS OF LIGHT.In Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism, Marici is a deva or bodhisattva associated with light and the sun. She is known as Molizhitian (摩利支天) or Molizhitian Pusa (摩利支天菩萨) in China and Marishi-ten (摩利支天?) in Japan and in Tibetan as 'Odzer Canma, "Woman Endowed with Rays of Light" (Wylie: 'od zer can ma). She is one of the 20 (or 24) Celestials (二十/二十四諸天). In Taoism and Chinese folk religion, Marici is known under the epithet of the Lady of Dipper Mother (Chinese: 斗母元君; pinyin: Dǒumǔ Yuánjūn) or Doumu, a name sometimes used by Buddhists.She is referred in BUDDHIST, as well as TAOist texts.The origins of Godess Marici are obscure; however, she appears to be an amalgamation of Indic, Iranian and non-Indo-Iranian antecedents spanning 1500 years.The Pagoda, is an example of Craftsmanship,  Ancient Engineering, and Architecture. The Pillar is rising from a small Pool of water, surrounding it, and with colorful Flowers, and Fishes playing in the Pool.

reviews.author: travelnomadNZ
reviews.title: Little Pagoda
reviews.content: After visiting pagodas from Myanmar I was a little disappointed with one pillar pagoda. Conceptually it is very clever but it is very small compared to other pagodas in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh city.Tip : not my first choice to visit if time is an issue. Sunscreen , sunhat, water, camera , suitable footwear and clothing for temples

reviews.author: josieist
reviews.title: Just walk past it - don't go out of your way
reviews.content: This is literally the small pagoda from the pictures. It's a modern "reconstruction" (more like complete rebuild) as the original was destroyed. Don't go out of your way to see the pagoda, just have a look if you're nearby.There are MANY more impressive pagodas in the city.

reviews.author: Namaste24
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: There should be a good after average and before very good.Most people there were part of a tour.It's nice to see.Not sure if there is a fee to see this as it seemed to be in an area in the street.Glad I saw it.

reviews.author: Ines S
reviews.title: beautiful setting
reviews.content: like so many other places, the one pilar pagoda is also hidden in an amazing green setting and its worth a short visit

reviews.author: HeyerFan
reviews.title: Pretty Pagoda
reviews.content: Pretty pagoda (replica - original destroyed). Very small with shrine. Popular visitor attraction. Lots of people in high season

reviews.author: xylasweet
reviews.title: Unique Pagoda
reviews.content: I'm not an architect but I look through buildings and admire the shape. When it comes to the old one - somehow I admire how our predecessor manage to build such a great work with a 'simple' technology. The One Pillar Pagoda is one example - simple idea which turned up into something grace.

reviews.author: M W
reviews.title: Slightly over rated
reviews.content: A beautiful building, and surrounding areas. However it is nice to see, but I wouldn't go out of my way to see it, join it in with seeing other sites.

reviews.author: ACL3112
reviews.title: A place of worship for fertility and health
reviews.content: This is the reconstruction of a Buddhist temple (the original was built in the 11th century and destroyed by the French). A childless emperor who dreamt about a son built the temple as a sign of gratitude when his wife gave birth to the longed for heir. It is built on one pillar in the middle of a pond, its construction akin to a lotus flower. Appropriate dress is required, this is an important place of worship and prayer for the Vietnamese. They come to pray for fertility and health - and they come back when their prayers have been answered. Behind the pagoda is an offshoot of the tree in Bodhgaya (India) where Buddha found enlightenment. It's a gift from India - and coming from Bodhgaya it is of special importance.

reviews.author: Wynand B
reviews.title: Maybe a bit over rated
reviews.content: Was not amazed by it, think it is worth a visit if you have done every other thing there in Hanoi. But don't go out of you way. Free entrance

reviews.author: Wynnermath
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: A bit interesting; vendors nearby; not much to see; pretty gardens surrounding area. Can't even write 100 characters about it!

reviews.author: Hanan B
reviews.title: Skipping it is no Great Loss
reviews.content: Got there as part of guided tour.  Guide told me the story behind it, and I nodded my head wisely.  Who says that I'm not polite?

reviews.author: evakordek
reviews.title: Bellow expectations
reviews.content: Nice but it is totally rebuilt so nothing of the original Pagoda is still there!  The temple right in front is very interesting though.  Dont miss it

reviews.author: MJL
reviews.title: Amazing to See
reviews.content: Now used as a buddhist alter for prayer, this little pagoda is worth seeing if you are within the area visiting the museum and the other local sites

reviews.author: Lesly D
reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.content: This is a small replica of an original One Pillar Pagoda which I found to be less than compelling. I would not go out of my way to see it, but it is next to Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum, which is worth seeing.

reviews.author: Graham S
reviews.title: Quirky li.ttle place
reviews.content: Strange little Buddhist shrine which althought housed on top of a 'single' pillar in the middle of a small lotus pond, the disproporional stone staircase leading up to the shrine tends to distact from its, perhaps intended, solitude.You get the impression the stone stairway was a later addition but who knows. Still, its a quirky little place with a lovely shrine well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Laura T
reviews.title: Tiny and pretty boring
reviews.content: Yes this is a walk past and take a photo. It is right next to HCM's mausoleum, so visit both at the same time.

reviews.author: MicheleColette
reviews.title: Waist OK
reviews.content: One becomes tired of Pagodas and temples and this was no exception. Hanoi is such an interesting town and the people make it so.

reviews.author: Reismeeuw
reviews.title: A gem
reviews.content: Dedicated to Quan Am ( Guan Yin ) this little pagoda is a gem within the complex of the Ho Chi Minh Museum. Even if there are lines do take to time to walk up the steps and look at the statute of the goddess of mercy.

reviews.author: Oscar M
reviews.title: Historically significant but not much there
reviews.content: Rebuilt pagoda that requires just a quick look.  It does have historical significance but is not very impressive.

reviews.author: acpkl
reviews.title: a simple pagoda
reviews.content: Its just a small one in the middle of a small pond but locals revere it as it was imspired by a vision of a king after a successful battle.

reviews.author: Antonis M
reviews.title: Hmm...
reviews.content: I thought was going to see a Pagoda. But this was a small chapel. Maybe it is historic but it is not something more.

reviews.author: seanworc
reviews.title: Iconic Pagoda in Ha Noi
reviews.content: This is a special place for Vietnamese.  Designed as a symbol of a lotus blossom, it is an expression of purity.  Visitors can walk up the stairs to see the inside of the temple and the buddha statue, but cannot go inside.  It dates back to 1100 CE. However, the current version is a replica. It is a brief visit . Maybe 15 minutes.  It gets very crowded because it is small and very popular.  There are snack vendors around it.  Went in March, 2013.

reviews.author: fairtrader
reviews.title: crowded and not that interesting
reviews.content: Went as part of a Hanoi tour, and it was one thing we could have missed out. Lots of tourists clogging up the little temple..

reviews.author: Della G
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: This is a very quaint pagoda supported by one pillar.  You can only fit so many people at the entry way of this pagoda so you actually have to wait your turn to climb up the stairs to peer in.  This attraction is situated not too far from the Ho Chi Minh museum complex and is a worthwhile visit.

reviews.author: K M
reviews.title: Just another pagoda!
reviews.content: Just another one. It's symbolic of being like a lotus flower, with one pillar. Anyway, if you're out and about sure but don't take a special visit.

reviews.author: Dishaa S
reviews.title: one pillar pagoda
reviews.content: standing on a single stone pillar in a lotus pond, this is part of the ho chi minh complex. this is dedicated to the goddess of mercy and  is definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: Kevin6333
reviews.title: It is exactly that, a pagoda built on a post in a pond.
reviews.content: A cute small pagoda in a fish pond. A photo opportunity perhaps but the grounds around it are more interesting.

reviews.author: AnnieAries
reviews.title: A beautiful building
reviews.content: This is well worth a visit and you can take photographs.  However be aware that there are lots of other visitors and tourists who also want to do the same thing.  Nearby there are some fascinating market stalls selling Vietnamese items - we purchased some gorgeous embroidered pictures - beautifully produced.  You only need US dollars - not necessarily Vietnamese dong.

reviews.author: Anca S
reviews.title: An unussual place
reviews.content: A very interesting place to visit and good photo opportunities; one of Vietnam's most iconic pagodas.

reviews.author: ZAR0602
reviews.title: Better Pagodas to visit if no religious intent
reviews.content: As Pagodas go there are many more interesting ones. This one is quite average if you are visiting with no religious intent.

reviews.author: drf53
reviews.title: Stop and look at it
reviews.content: Good place for a special picture sop worthwhile stopping and looking whilst you're walking around the area.

reviews.author: shoemaker_10
reviews.title: simple structure
reviews.content: the simple structure of one pole supports a pagoda of decent size with access steps - sorry no ramp here

reviews.author: Starnosemouse
reviews.title: Chua Dien Hnu
reviews.content: I visited this place on 23/9/15.  Is nothing more  then an wooden altar build on the pond. Don't waste time going there. Is behind the Ho Chi Minh Mansoleum. If you're standing facing the mansoleum. It's on your your left hand side don't walk to the right or you will have to pay the entrance fee to Ho Chi Minh Residence, another lousy attraction.

reviews.author: skl2910
reviews.title: Worth including on your city tour highlights list
reviews.content: A funny little old building with heaps of historical significance and worth including on your visit around all the key highlights in this particular area.

reviews.author: Daniel A
reviews.title: Something uniquely Vietnamese
reviews.content: As part of the Ho Chi Minh complex this is worth seeing. The original has long since been destroyed and what we now see is a modern copy. It's wort a visit all the same.

reviews.author: Jayme B
reviews.title: If you're close by, why not
reviews.content: Located very close to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum the pagoda is just like any other pagoda you will see. However if you're in the area you might as well drop in for a look

reviews.author: Em
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: This place is definitely overrated by travel books. It is just a tiny pagoda without much interesting artistic or historical insights. the good thing is that you practically bump into it, if you have visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. I would not recommend to go there just to visit it, but preferably combine it with the Mausoleum

reviews.author: Robzaza
reviews.title: Just another pagoda
reviews.content: It was nice to see but at the end of the day it's just another pagoda that is happening to be standing on one pillar. If you are going to see it as part of the surrounding sites than it is worth it otherwise not.

reviews.author: MeiXiang88
reviews.title: Not easy to notice
reviews.content: The one pillar pagoda is located inside a temple. Even though it is just beside the Ho Chi Minh Museum, you might take time to notice that the pagoda is over there.

reviews.author: Fred862014
reviews.title: fun
reviews.content: it's part of the ho chi minh mausoleum park! nice to visit! it's not big, but it's good to visit! to do

reviews.author: rosebt
reviews.title: quaint
reviews.content: A unique pagoda on one pillar within the botanic garden complex. The lotus pond that the pagoda stood in were beautiful. Unfortunately, we could not go up to the pagoda because of the huge crowds

reviews.author: Traveler-O-World
reviews.title: A Pagoda on a Single Pillar
reviews.content: In the grounds adjoining the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a Pagoda built on a single pillar. This is a popular temple where people offer prayers and seek favors. It is a nice peaceful place - but fairly crowded.

reviews.author: ramiaj197
reviews.title: Do not go specially for it
reviews.content: It is not a great attraction to visit.. There is not much to see, However, If you are visting Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, it is a few meters away from the entrance of the museum.

reviews.author: renata e
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda is a nice place to visit
reviews.content: Spend some time exploring the One Pillar Pagoda and take some wonderful photos while visiting. I really enjoyed the experience.

reviews.author: Ray T
reviews.title: In the grounds of the Mausoleum
reviews.content: Delightful grounds, gardens and buildings near to the Mausoleum. The weather was lovely and this made a real contrast to the Mausoleum itself.  Worth a visit.

reviews.author: raysonleo
reviews.title: Local Pagoda
reviews.content: The main thing to see is this pagoda only hold by one pillar. And the small temple is stand firm at the middle of small pond.

reviews.author: Vanessa M
reviews.title: Can't believe how old it is!
reviews.content: Not much to see really and we saw it on the way to the Ho Chi Minh museum but it is amazing to think how old his place is. Can take some pretty pictures here but like some other reviews, not much to see so not really worth going out of your way to see it while you're in Vietnam.

reviews.author: MartyPN
reviews.title: Worth visitng in conjunction with Ho Chi Minh Museum
reviews.content: This attraction provides a useful addition to the visit to the Ho Chi Minh Museum.  The visit should not take long as the attraction is quite compact. The steps leading up to the sanctuary are steep and should be negotiated carefully so as not to trip.

reviews.author: RPM
reviews.title: Decent place
reviews.content: This place gives me a feeding of peace but not quite peaceful. In the middle of the hustle bustle of Hanoi, this one pillar pagoda provides the solitude that one needs.

reviews.author: Natallia P
reviews.title: don't get it
reviews.content: i know this place is recommended by all the city guides but i don't get why. The only reason i went there was because it was close to the presidential palace and mausoleum.  Just a tiny pagoda on one pillar. Maybe it has some sacret religious meaning i don't know of

reviews.author: Kim N
reviews.title: Just one pillar
reviews.content: As the name suggest, it has only one pillar but it was a pretty pillar.  It sits above a man made moat.  It's small so not a lot of people can go up to it at once.  The climb is a bit steep so be careful.

reviews.author: Raul N
reviews.title: Picturesque monument
reviews.content: This attraction is inside the complex that also houses the Ho Chi Min Museum and Mausoleum etc...it is a nice structure (although not the original, since it was destroyed during the war and it was rebuilt in the sixties ) with a distinct architecture. The red colour contrasts well with the lush green trees that surround it. It is rather small (at least compared to the idea that you get from photos and souvenirs) but worth a visit nonetheless. It is not uncommon to see local Vietnamese people climbing up the steps to pray and a visitor can do the same. Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Bruce H
reviews.title: Quaint
reviews.content: I did not know what to expect but having heard so much [both good and bad] I had to see for myself and I am glad I did.  Built for a king to pray for a son, I took the opportunity to pray for my son to achieve happiness in his life and for him to realise his dreams.  It is only small but it would have to be sitting on only one pillar. This is one attraction you must see and depending on your life experiences your attitude towards it will vary.

reviews.author: gkemp95
reviews.title: Nice but small...
reviews.content: Beautiful little pagoda in a small "lake", nice to look at but isn't something to plan the day around. Definitely visit if your in the area of the HCM mausoleum and museum but wouldn't bother going just for the pagoda...

reviews.author: Jacqui M
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: This pagoda is part of the presidential complex and definitely not worth a trip out just to see it. There is a monastery beside it but there are better monasteries to visit. An interesting story is that it was built by a king, who kept coming to pray for a son - which he eventually got.

reviews.author: NICK S
reviews.title: The picture tells the (whole) story...
reviews.content: Close to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and his living quarters, this pagoda (rebuilt) is only a short walk from them so you can visit it whilst visiting other sites in Hanoi but the pagoda itself is not really worth a trip in its own right (there are others in Vietnam that are less crowded!)

reviews.author: Zarin S
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: The Pagoda is nice but quite small.  I expected it to be bigger so I was a little bit disappointed. It is a Buddhist temple where people offered prayers and incense too.

reviews.author: achaya
reviews.title: Unimpressed
reviews.content: While it may have significance to locals, the pagoda is not impressive in any way structurally or aesthetically. To top it, it is a replica of the original larger wooden pagoda, so what are we really looking at? You can take a quick snap of it walking from the Ho Chi Minh Museum to the Mausoleum

reviews.author: Shreekant A
reviews.title: Nice pagoda
reviews.content: The pagoda in the lotus shape is worth visiting.The construction and the history of pagoda worth noting.The construction though simple  is still worth insisting to see its basic concept and the architecture.

reviews.author: david j
reviews.title: Part of the Ho Chi Minh complex, interesting place
reviews.content: This pagoda is situated behind the mausoleum, its quite small, so only takes a few minutes to see. There are a lot of stalls selling snacks & drinks and souvenirs here, so its quite buzzy.

reviews.author: Lauren
reviews.title: Enjoyable
reviews.content: Great to see and experience Vietnamese pagoda. Lots of lovely detail and calm surroundings. Easy to get too and you can always stop for a ice cream

reviews.author: trev48962015
reviews.title: This whole area was fasinating.
reviews.content: The one pillar Pagoda wasnt really a feature for me. HAs high interest for Vietnamese people it appeared but seen many one pillar things before. Maybe it's age and apparantly it's breakthrough design. Couldnt get enthused about it. However the area it was in was fasinating so go there and accept the Pagoda is just a piece of the whole area.

reviews.author: pillay15
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Get on to the steps to see the shrine. Crowded but you will manage as the crowd keeps moving. Remember to buy you souvenirs here as the prices are reasonable.Fridge magnets cost US$1  each. Other places will be slightly expensive. Good place to buy your souvenirs.

reviews.author: homedelsac
reviews.title: Curiousity because of the name
reviews.content: That's it. Nothing really exceptional. Curious local attraction more because of the denomination than by any specificity.

reviews.author: Dmp60
reviews.title: Ancient relic
reviews.content: It's amazing that this is still standing,  a very small pagoda from early Vietnam (639) I think if I remember correctly!

reviews.author: Douglas W
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Enjoyed the Pagoda.  Detail, detail.  Amazing structure. The story behind the pagoda was very interesting.

reviews.author: Krishnan A
reviews.title: sight seeing
reviews.content: Interesting place. A small layout with an attractive pagoda. A well maintained and surroundings are neat and clean with good garden around.

reviews.author: danielm232015
reviews.title: Qne pillar pagoda special
reviews.content: The pagoda started being constructed under Ly’s dynasty in 1049. The legend goes that one night in 1049, King Ly Thai Tong dreamed of the Holy Lady (Phat ba Quan Am) sitting on a lotus and leading him to a similar building.

reviews.author: Robert K
reviews.title: INTERESTING
reviews.content: The history of how and why it was built which represents the lotus was far more interesting than the actual building itself.

reviews.author: skiNebraska
reviews.title: Pretty building, nothing else
reviews.content: You get the idea just by looking at it, but climbing the stairs is what you do to fill in the blanks. It's barely worth the climb, as the shrine is underwhelming

reviews.author: CandiesDelaCruz
reviews.title: Cute attraction
reviews.content: Upon exiting the Ho Chi Minh Museum, you can see this structure. It is a cute One Pagoda with lots of people lining up to see whats inside. I decided not to go inside because I felt strange with having to treat a "holy" place as a tourist stop. I dont want to be that kind of tourist.

reviews.author: Erica P
reviews.title: Unique Architecture
reviews.content: Definitely drop in to visit the One Pillar Pagoda located on the Ho Chi Minh Complex. The temple is one of the most iconic in Hanoi and rises out of a lotus pond on a single pillar. The temple at the top of steep steps is very small at approximately 3x3 metres. It is believed that the temple was built as a place of worship for fertility based on a dream by one of the Emperors who wanted a son.We sat underneath the ancient bo tree in the pleasant and serene setting on a very hot day in Hanoi.

reviews.author: platinumSingapore
reviews.title: for photography
reviews.content: located next to ho chi ming museum. built on a small lotus pond with one pillar supporting this small hut. however, it's unique for photography.

reviews.author: 2bumdrifters
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is smaller than I had imagined, but it was still worth to see it in person.  You definitely would need a guide to take you there.

reviews.author: abbottpotter
reviews.title: Not so amazing
reviews.content: I heard that this pagoda is a must see attraction in Hanoi and this is the last place I visited before leaving Hanoi and I have to say I wasn't that impressed. The pagoda is smaller than what I imagined and there were many people lining to make a prayer. It's more like a religious site rather than tourist attraction.

reviews.author: linhvu9x
reviews.title: It is one of the most unique architecture
reviews.content: It is built in one pillar, and its overall architecture looks like a lotus on the lake. It was built since 11th century when King Ly Thai Tong dreamt a Godness guided him to reach her Lotus-like Budda throne. This pagoda is in Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.

reviews.author: 67TravelBug67
reviews.title: A pagoda with a difference
reviews.content: As in the name this is the one pillar pagoda. It is very unusual and is only small but is definitely worth a visit especially due to the close proximity to the HCM Museum and grounds.Nice just to sit in the shade to reflect and people watch.

reviews.author: pk30052011
reviews.title: Another pagoda
reviews.content: To us Aussies, we like to visit really big & different sorts of temples etc. This was just another one, although it was a bit disdaining because it was super tiny. The area is nice though. Take time to walk around here & explore.We parked our scooter just outside the gate for free. The security on the gate try charge you a ridiculous amount to park inside the grounds, just 20m away from free parking!

reviews.author: Ganga D D
reviews.title: Closeup with the deity!
reviews.content: Its a tiny place of worship with great significance of praying here by the locals to beget a son. One can walk right upto the shrine and take selfies or pictures. A lot of trees around so pleasing to the eyes. One can see the yellow buddha fruits that they offer here which dont really have any fruit in them :)

reviews.author: Terry D
reviews.title: Small
reviews.content: Its right next to hcm museum so why not just go in but its smaller and just a good place to chill with a drink after a long walk

reviews.author: MAHENDRANATHAN
reviews.title: EXTRAORDINARY
reviews.content: This is a small quaint little temple sitting on a single pillar and thus its name. There is a myth that if couples want a son then they should come to this temple and pray for divine intervention to give them a son. How far this is true will only lead to speculative conclusions. But it is historical and this was built by the Emperor to whom a son was born following a dream. Hence,the myth.

reviews.author: Phoebe1992
reviews.title: Great value for history but not very attractive for normal tourists.
reviews.content: The temple is very small but having a great value of history and represent typical ancient architecture of Ly dynasty 1000 years ago. However, as a local, an advice for normal tourist to discover Hanoi, it is just a so so place though having a great history

reviews.author: TallChris51
reviews.title: Nice piece of history
reviews.content: Very scenic setting and a lovely structure, although the concrete pillar does detract from the building itself.  You can also walk up the steps to the shrine.  A nice few minutes to build into a bigger trip.

reviews.author: al22tecc
reviews.title: part of the tour, ok
reviews.content: This can be seen after touring the ho chi minh complex. Its supposed to be where people pray and ask for a son. I saw two elderly women go up so i asked my guide what are they doing. Our guide said maybe they are asking for a grandson! Oh well, if people believe in such, it does not hurt.After going around the complex, this place becomes an anti climax because its significance pales in comparison, in my opinion.

reviews.author: Mumble_Swerve
reviews.title: Tragic history of the one pillar pagoda
reviews.content: Unfortunately, the one pillar pagoda on view isn't actually the original pagoda. In one of their last acts before leaving Hanoi (and seriously petty), the French destroyed the pagoda in 1954. The new government rebuilt it.

reviews.author: Dave N
reviews.title: Unique Pagoda
reviews.content: The one and only pagoda in the world build with only one pillar. Not a miss for all buddhists. In the pagoda is famous guan ying statue. My family and I were there to pray for good health.

reviews.author: granthardie2016
reviews.title: Underwhlming
reviews.content: There are so many pagodas around town that are extremely fascinating and are truly amazing. This one was very underwhelming and could easily be skipped.

reviews.author: Emmalene M
reviews.title: Underwhelmed...
reviews.content: Definitely NOT a must. We were going to skip this entirely but had some time to spare and did our own walking tour of Hanoi getting the Flag Tower, Mausoleum, Presidential Palace and the Pagoda into one afternoon (plenty of time). This is the tiniest pagoda ever. I have no idea why its remarkable its on one pillar as any more pillars for somethig this size would look daft... The actual shrine is a bit tacky as its got lots of flashy lights going on.

reviews.author: AbhijitRaja
reviews.title: Old monument, too much hype
reviews.content: One of the oldest pagodas of Vietnam, one does feel underwhelmed on reaching the monument. Though the calm feeling of any pagoda is present here too.Situated right besides the Ho Chih Minh Mausoleum, it is not too much effort to reach the place. Worth 5 minutes of you time.

reviews.author: Dr jayanta
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Visited the One Pillar pagoda in Hanoi, Vietnam. It is near to Mausolium, Hochimin House, main city, additional attraction travel by rickshaw Take half day trip in that area.Better go morning by 8am and finish by 12 noon. other places are there like vietnam museum.

reviews.author: vmimartins
reviews.title: Not a must
reviews.content: Small temple, rebuilt after being destroyed in the Vietnam / American war . The reconstruction was not true to the original,so the current temple  gives an idea of ​​how it would have been before its destruction.

reviews.author: Ron R
reviews.title: Historic attraction.
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is a small and free attraction close to other attractions such as the Ho Chi Minh Museum, Ho Chi Minh's timber house, his mausoleum and the former French presidential palace.  It is constructed of wood on a single stone pillar and was built in 1049 and rebuilt after being destroyed by retreating French forces in 1954.  It is considered a significant Buddhist monument.

reviews.author: Craig M
reviews.title: Worth a visit when combined with something else in this area of Hanoi.
reviews.content: We asked our hotel to book a taxi to the One Pillar Pagoda. They must have assumed this was a mistake with the taxi dropping us off at Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum. We needed to ask directions from other tourists to get to the Pagoda. It is small and on its own not worth a taxi ride. However it is interesting to see. It is also in a lovely part of Hanoi - the diplomatic area. So combined with a walk around the area and to the Mausoleum it is a worthy destination.

reviews.author: Ian M
reviews.title: Intriguing
reviews.content: A fascinating slice of old Vietnam. While it is sad that this amazing little building was destroyed as the French left, it is notable that it has been restored to its former glory. Many locals spent some time praying here, so make sure to respect their privacy.

reviews.author: 1218John
reviews.title: Quiet Retreat
reviews.content: Popular with worshipers, more so than tourists.  Quiet beautiful setting.  Almost a part of Ho Chi Minh Memorial.Comes with a pretty lotus lake with fish.

reviews.author: StephanieP
reviews.title: Nice spot
reviews.content: Enchanting place. Very unique and impressive.The beautiful environment, is a place a little hidden and there are few tourists. Nice.

reviews.author: mushroom001
reviews.title: Lively
reviews.content: The pagoda is small, and people have to queue to pray in it. But it is surrounded by beautiful yet small lotus pond.  A good place to visit and take photos, it's near to Ho Chi Minh mausoleum. If you had a second thought of visiting Ho Chi Minh mausoleum, you can visit this pagoda as it's situated along the long queue to visit Ho Chi Minh. Many stalls of food nearby too.

reviews.author: seedhunter
reviews.title: Small yet unique
reviews.content: Very near to Ho Chi Minh Memorial, this pagoda is very small, rested on a sigle pillar. Very interesting.

reviews.author: Ramram47
reviews.title: Amazing feat
reviews.content: its quite stunning to see how they made 1 Pillar Pagoda its cool inside even on a hot daymay house single family

reviews.author: Núria S
reviews.title: Nice, but so small!
reviews.content: After visiting Ho Chi Minh mausoleum,  we visited the pagoda.  It's nice but very small.  It's a good visit if you are already near

reviews.author: Vietnam Visa Easy
reviews.title: Unique pagoda
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is a popular attractions in Hanoi located between the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the Ho Chi Minh Museum. Its unique design is of a three square meter wooden structure resembling a “lotus blossom”, the Buddhist symbol of Enlightenment, also Vietnamese national flower. The pagoda is a perfect place to sit and relax after a long tour around Ho Chi Minh Mausoluem. Opening time: 6 am to 6 pm. No ticket.

reviews.author: Fun loving Sun Seeker
reviews.title: Unique Pagoda - worth a peek if visiting HCM Mausoleum
reviews.content: Very unusual one pillar pagoda located in the middle of a pond, small staircase leading up to the shrine inside - which you can view but not enter.  The history behind this very cute pagoda is interesting - the pagoda reminds me of a Vietnamese Wendy house placed on a pillar in the middle of a pond - or what I imagine one would look like. There are plenty of benches to sit and relax and do a bit of people watching or contemplating which ever takes your fancy.  I went for people watching always interesting - was watching a local lady with her children who were looking at the pond/pagoda and singing, very cute children, lovely to watch them. Shops/toilets available - a good place for a comfort break, quick look around the pagoda and learn about it's history, which doesn't take long.

reviews.author: Glenita
reviews.title: Worth a look but dont go out of your way
reviews.content: Very small and tucked away on the way to Ho Chi Mihn museum. Well worth the look seeing as your already there

reviews.author: Snorkeller
reviews.title: Worth a look in Hanoi
reviews.content: It is in an area near the pressed entail palace site, mausoleum etc so worth a look while you are there. Charming little Pagoda and we stopped and had a cold drink from the stands at the bottom of it's steps.

reviews.author: Adi R
reviews.title: Nice quick stop while in the HCM complex, but not too special
reviews.content: While I would definitely recommend this as a quick stop as you are walking through the HCM Mausoleum complex, I wouldn't build an itinerary around this--this is a tiny but quaint pagoda neatly set in the area.

reviews.author: Sang P
reviews.title: Unique Buiding in the City
reviews.content: It is small pagoda standing on the lake by just one pillar. Unique architecture with wood in the beautiful garden. But it is very crowded, you must take long time to reach to the stair climb up the pagoda.

reviews.author: Ravi
reviews.title: Nice Place
reviews.content: This Pagoda is in the vicinity of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Its a quaint pagoda and is a nice place to walk around. If you are in the vicinity potter around and enjoy. Nice place to take pics!

reviews.author: Chris101111
reviews.title: Great visit.
reviews.content: Nice little Pagoda set in a small park area, lots of people but you have a good opportunity for some great photos, combine it as it is close to all the attractions near by.

reviews.author: NazmunMita
reviews.title: Hanoi must see
reviews.content: The Ho chi min complex is must see attraction in Hanoi and one pillar pagoda, presidential palace is walking distance from it

reviews.author: Re1nard
reviews.title: One of Landmarks in Hanoi
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda located near to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. After visiting the mausoleum, if you do not want to go to the Presidential Palace and pay VND 25,000, you may go straight to the One Pillar Pagoda for free. This temple is unique and I saw many Buddhist people come and go to pray in the pagoda.

reviews.author: Gladwin August A
reviews.title: Never to Exceed One's Expectations
reviews.content: Unlike what the other glamorous buildings nearby the pagoda, this one is a bit unassuming and has less grandeur. However, there's a certain charm to the petite pagoda, which nevertheless befits its purpose as a praying altar.Strangely juxtaposed with the hustle and bustle of Hanoi, but a memorable stop nonetheless.

reviews.author: BharathiMani
reviews.title: Quaint Pagoda
reviews.content: This Pagoda is right next to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Its a small quaint Pagoda surrounded by a lotus pond. Nice area to walk around.

reviews.author: Vnvet68
reviews.title: One of the historical landmarks of Hanoi. Peaceful surroundings.
reviews.content: One-Pillar Pagoda is very small and it will take you ten minutes to see it, but the area is very nice and peaceful. A very good look into Hanoi's past.

reviews.author: Warwick T
reviews.title: Longevity of architecture
reviews.content: More amazing history in Hanoi.Visited as part of our walking tour. Some times it's hard to imagine the age of some of these relics.

reviews.author: Elton H
reviews.title: Beautiful pagoda
reviews.content: It's a unique pagoda. Lots of tourists taking pictures of the pagoda. Amaze by the architecture and designs.Great one

reviews.author: GAN L
reviews.title: Unique architecture
reviews.content: Built of wood on a single stone pillar, the pagoda resembles a lotus flower. This structure was rebuild by the Vietnamese government after the original pagoda built by Emperor Ly Thai Tong was destroyed by the French.  The pagoda houses an altar with the statue of Bodhisattva of Compassion with a thousand hands .

reviews.author: Ted.s.P
reviews.title: It's a beautiful little pagoda
reviews.content: It's a beautiful little pagoda built on a single pillar. Visit it as part of your stop @ the Ho Chi Minh mosoleum.

reviews.author: Touristasaurus
reviews.title: It is what it says it is
reviews.content: It's a pagoda ... on one pillar. Part of the Ho Chi Minh circuit after his tomb it's an interesting place to see. Just after the stilt house. It's hard to miss.

reviews.author: CTRTeach11
reviews.title: Nice stop in Hanoi
reviews.content: This was a quick stop for our tour in Hanoi.  The area is clean, and an easy walk around to gain a little more knowledge of the Vietnamese Culture.

reviews.author: Nguyen Bom
reviews.title: Nice art of Buddhism in Vietnam
reviews.content: It locates near with Ho Chi Minh mosueum. It has very strange setup with only pillar to hold the pagoda. One of particular place represent for Vietnam culture

reviews.author: Shilpa K
reviews.title: Tiny temple
reviews.content: This place is probably the tiniest temple you would have ever seen in your life. I believe you attract what you believe in, and that includes good and bad both. A few years ago when I stayed in Kuwait, a good friend of mine introduced me to a video on YouTube called 'The mantra of Avalokiteshvara', which as per the YouTube post, was a God of healing/ compassion... Now I'm not a Buddhist, I don't know much about the religion but this belief somehow felt rather appealing to me partly because the mantra was soothing and I used to play it to calm myself down or to relax. Over the years it became sort of my secret escape from stressful situations and I believe it helped me become a more compassionate and tolerant human being.... When I decided to travel to Vietnam, I never imagined that I had in fact attracted this trip to my life over the years... Because over the years I always thought wouldn't it be cool to visit a Buddhist temple of this god (I imagined it would be in Tibet!) and guess what! Hanoi had one of the pagodas of God Avalokiteshvara which is known as The One Pillar Pagoda. It's a tiny temple which cannot accommodate more than 2 people to pray at once... But I felt extremely at peace here! Had a weird déjàvu feeling here and it made my belief in the power of attraction stronger than ever before.... So push away negative thoughts from your life, because your thoughts become actions! May the joy be with you :-) Have an unbelievably happy and inspiring day all of you. Thanks for reading till the end.... I'm really grateful to be connected with all you kind and happy souls out here :-)

reviews.author: Rev-D
reviews.title: Not too much to see but very cool
reviews.content: It's right next to the Ho Chi Minh museum. There are shops and drinks all over the area so it's a good place to stop and appreciate the simple beauty of this small temple.

reviews.author: Andreainalberta
reviews.title: Small, quiet, not worth a visit on its own.
reviews.content: We stopped by this tiny pagoda enroute from Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum up to the lake. The pagoda is small and isn't the original so it wasn't particularly impressive but if it's on your way somewhere then worth taking a look.

reviews.author: Joanna_vigate
reviews.title: it's ok
reviews.content: Looks a lot taller and bigger in the picture in the tourist guide, still a good place to walk around.

reviews.author: Luke D
reviews.title: Worth a picture
reviews.content: It was interesting to see the One Pillar Pagoda, but it would be much better if there was a sign to give a bit of information about it. Call by during your tour of the Mausoleum.

reviews.author: HugoColle
reviews.title: Unique temple
reviews.content: Its a small temple with few statues inside but very famous because of the architecture. Build on one pillar and raising like a lotus flower which is a Budhist symbol. First build in 1049, destroyed in 1954 by the French when they retreated from Hanoi and rebuild afterwards. So it has also a historical value.

reviews.author: Drew Z
reviews.title: It was under restoration!
reviews.content: I was extremely disappointed to find out that the location was under going a restoration project. Hopefully by my next visit all of the construction materials will be removed and not just haphazardly left around for both tourists and locals to have to walk over and around. It ruined the location and I left disappointed.

reviews.author: euniceysh426
reviews.title: Unique historical building
reviews.content: It's worth to see this historical building! You also can take a relax scroll around the park or grab a postcard and post it there.

reviews.author: Kate2013B
reviews.title: Interesting historical site
reviews.content: An interesting complex overall.  It's worth going to but the crowds can be a bit much.  The history of the site is amazing.

reviews.author: Myo M
reviews.title: Not sure why it's so popular
reviews.content: It's a tiny building on one pillar (hence the name of the pagoda) in the middle of a small pond, and you can't even go inside that tiny temple, can only take a peek from outside at the top of the stone steps.  So, I don't know why it's so popular like one of the premium pagodas of the country, maybe only locals know the reason behind the pagoda's popularity :).Pretty close to the HCM Museum which is also in the vicinity of the Mausoleum & the house-on-stilts & the house where HCM lived in the 1950's (with an attached garage), you can do that whole "HCM area" including this pagoda in one morning (about four hours would be enough). About 40 minutes to get to the above-mentioned area from the Hanoi train station (Ga Hanoi) on Le Duan then turning left onto Dien Bien Phu, just be sure you stay on Dien Bien Phu as the road bears left when you get to the fork (with the big Flag Tower on the right) after going past Lenin Park because going right will take you to the Thang Long Citadel instead of the "HCM area" and One Pillar.

reviews.author: redeco
reviews.title: Tiny Pagoda near Presidential Palace
reviews.content: The one-pillar pagoda was built in 1049 by Emperor Ly Thai Tong.  It stands on a single stone pillar above a lotus pond.  Delicate and beautiful, it has survived destruction several times and has been rebuilt.It's easy to find and just near the area where Ho Chi Minh's stilt house sits in the Presidential Palace park.

reviews.author: John K
reviews.title: A piece of Vietnamese history
reviews.content: My second visit here. Last time it was packed with tourists and it was pouring with rain. This time just a few tourists and sunshine. We visited the small temple beside the pagoda as well which is small and has some beautiful statues inside. The pagoda itself is sitting on a single concrete pillar. Well worth a visit and can be combined with a visit to HCM museum next door and the mausoleum. If you found the review helpful please let me know any feedback is welcomed.

reviews.author: TandMoutAndAbout
reviews.title: Pretty, but smaller than expected
reviews.content: I was really excited about seeing this, but it was much smaller than I thought it would be. All the pictures and souvenirs made it feel substantial, instead, it is more of a tree house with no tree. Worth a look, but it is a lot smaller than you are probably thinking!

reviews.author: 216PeterW
reviews.title: Striking Structure
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is an historic Buddhist temple in Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam. It's quite a very impressive structure with interesting markings on the walls. It has a small shrine devoted to the Boddhisatva of Mercy inside the pagoda. The temple is built of wood on a single stone pillar 1.25 m in diameter, and it is designed to resemble a lotus blossom. This visit was part of a 10 day/9 night tour of Vietnam.

reviews.author: saigon75
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: we went here before visiting the nearby HCM museum.it was very crowded. i especially remember the soothing scent of burning incense.the story behind the building is interesting. only a small attraction, it can be done quickly and is worth a peek.

reviews.author: Bert W
reviews.title: Not very impressive
reviews.content: In a tour we visited the One Pillar Pagoda. Luckily we did not go out of our way to see it but combined it with a visit to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Then it is quite nice to see, but not very impressive, certainly not nr. 1 Pagoda to see in Hanoi

reviews.author: Tran Bao An
reviews.title: A Pagoda With One Pillar
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is often mentioned to be one of Hanoi's most beautiful pagodas. Every tourist guidebook mentions it as a must-see. It's more or less the number one sight in Hanoi. You HAVE to see it!Well, do you? It's basically only a pagoda standing on one pillar. While this surely is an interesting way to build a pagoda, Chua Mot Cot (in Vietnamese) is nothing but that. Standing on one pillar in a little dirty pond, supposedly looking like a lotus blossom, and being overrun by hordes of tourists and Vietnamese alike, I'd recommend skipping it. If you want to go there, combine it with a visit to Ho Chi Minh Museum or Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, both of which are just around the corner. Chua Mot Cot is okay, but there are several other pagodas that are more interesting. Furthermore, the original pagoda was destroyed by the French in 1954, so the one you see is only a copy of the original from 1049

reviews.author: CED
reviews.title: Interesting diversion
reviews.content: I wish I had read the last post before visiting this pagoda. It would have made it much more interesting and understandable.

reviews.author: MirindaK
reviews.title: Small yet Iconic Temple
reviews.content: The history behind this temple was most fascinating to me. Interesting to note that the childless Emperor married a peasant woman, who bore him a child which came to him in a dream. The architecture is most amazing considering how ancient this temple is. It is extremely small and reflects, for me, a token of dedication and gratitute. I was told if I wish to have another child, I should place my wish there and then - no thank you.  I stayed at the bottom of the stairs just in case....

reviews.author: MsAnnHanoi
reviews.title: special architectural history!
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is the most unique architecture of Hanoi in particular Vietnam in general. Even through 1000 years One Pillar Pagoda still in Hanoi centre near Ho Chi Minh museum .In Vietnamese architectural history, the architectural style of the one pillar as One Pillar pagoda appeared before the Ly dysnasty. In the front of ths temple was a lotus- shaped hexangonal stone pillar. Today, One Pillar Pagoda includes a square Lotus calyx, each side of One Pillar Pagoda as leghth of 3 meters, the curved roofs set up on a pillar of 4 meters high, the diameter of 1.20 meters with two single stone columns overlapped into a block. Today the One Pillar Pagoda’s stone columns  doesn’t have lotus as desribed in the Ly dynastry, but One Pillar Pagoda buit on stone columns rising from the waterface is still a unique architecture, reflecting the imagine of a lotus rising up straight from a small square pond surrounded by a row of bainsters made of blue enameled glazed bricks. The architecture of pagodas is now close to the architecture of One Pillar Pagoda in the post Le Dynasty.

reviews.author: apritchy
reviews.title: Very small pagoda
reviews.content: This Pagoda has a very interesting story behind it but it is pretty small and there are other, more interesting in the city. But worth a visit if you are visitng the museum.

reviews.author: Brooke R
reviews.title: Meh
reviews.content: You'll walk past it if you are walking around the presidential gardens. A nice looking structure but I'd be disappointed if I had gone out of my way to see it

reviews.author: Steph859
reviews.title: Cute temple
reviews.content: Push your way to the top of the little flight of stairs and pop your deity in the box for Buddha. Nothing fancy, but has character.

reviews.author: Daniel A
reviews.title: Quite tiny
reviews.content: We happened upon this attraction after we visited Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum. Is is actually quite cute and reminded me of a tree house back in the States. For being so small there were many people there. I would never visit it alone but since I had just visited the Mausoleum, I figured why not?

reviews.author: Ramie E
reviews.title: unique pagoda in vietnam
reviews.content: The One-pillar pagoda or Dien Huu pagoda, has one of the most special architectures in Vietnam. The pagoda is situated next to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.The legend about pagoda is very interesting. It is great to see it.

reviews.author: Charlise B
reviews.title: An immortal lotus
reviews.content: The pagoda is often used as a symbol for Hanoi and remains one of the city’s most revered sights in a beautifully tranquil garden setting with benches provided for comfortable contemplation. The shrine inside the pagoda is dedicated to the Vietnamese Buddhist deity Quan Am with her effigy nestled inside the tiny three square metres temple.

reviews.author: Loretta W
reviews.title: Renovations in Progress
reviews.content: At the time could not get access to site as there were renovations is progress..It actually is quite small. Loved to have had more than a peep. Next time.

reviews.author: veturpin
reviews.title: This really is not a separate site.
reviews.content: This building is located in the grounds which have the Ho Chi Minh sites his homes and mausoleum and the president place. It was small but beautiful.

reviews.author: almhuss
reviews.title: A Tiny Gem
reviews.content: You'll get to see this beautiful ancient pagoda, dedicated to The Buddha, if you are touring the Ho Chi Minh presidential compound, and if you ask directions (or ask your guide).The pagoda is very small, and may not be entered, although many people ascend the stairs for pictures in front or to pray and light joss sticks.  The significance of the pagoda is that it is the oldest in Hanoi, dating back to the 11th century.  The French replaced the wooden support pillar with steel during their colonial administration.  They also removed the ancient bell and took it to Paris, where it remains today.

reviews.author: Peter M
reviews.title: A building site
reviews.content: Just a building site.  What a pity, as it looked lovely!  Would be better to close it off from tourists while trying to make it a better site.

reviews.author: Porgester
reviews.title: Very pretty if not surrounded by a building site
reviews.content: It's tucked away at the side of the museum so easily missed but definitely worth a look if you're in the area. It was in the middle of a building site when we went so a bit disappointing, but the interior of the very small pagoda was still beautiful & I would imagine the whole area will be when the wok is finished

reviews.author: Tuan Anh Nguyen
reviews.title: Beautiful architecture
reviews.content: We have a short time to see . A beautiful architecture . A place to respect when entering views. Nice.

reviews.author: FormerCaliBoy
reviews.title: One pagoda, lots of construction
reviews.content: We popped in here in between our tours of the Ho Chi Minh Museum, Mausoleum and the Presidential Palace.   The One Pillar Pagoda was under major construction during our December tour.  The temple was open, so you walk up the stairs to view the multi-armed Buddha inside the temple.  The pagoda sits atop the moat and the surrounding the pagoda grounds are other buildings under construction.  At the rear of the complex, in a shed are more Buddhas’ and shrines with a lot of offerings for prayers.  This area was certainly not recommended (at the time) for wheelchairs; otherwise, spend a few minutes to see this attraction.

reviews.author: Kelley H
reviews.title: Nice-- 5 minutes of viewing
reviews.content: This isn't worth visiting unless you're already going by the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum. Located just behind the mausoleum, it's worth strolling by to take some pictures and learn a bit more about Vietnamese history. It's free to see but the surrounding area is currently undergoing construction so it's not as peaceful as one would hope.

reviews.author: Scalea05
