reviews.title: Combine this with a visit to Ho Chi Minh Palace
reviews.content: Interesting for about 15 minutes. Then move on to the more interesting site of Ho Chi Minh's residence, a short walk away.

reviews.author: Patrick B
reviews.title: Not worth seeing on its own
reviews.content: I was very keen to see this after seeing it on the map. It is part of the mausoleum grounds which you don't technically have to pay for unless you go into the Ho Chi Minh grounds. The Pagoda isn't in itself very impressive and the grounds all around it are under complete renovation so you can only see it through a gap in the construction fencing....There may be some history to it that we missed out on but there was nothing to explain it's meaning.

reviews.author: Shakes C
reviews.title: Worth a quick visit
reviews.content: If visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum dropping by the One Pillar Pagoda is recommended.  We spent 5 minutes taking a few photos and listening to the interesting history.  The serenity is somewhat destroyed as the surrounding gardens are under full reconstruction.  The fruit stall nearby sold the most amazing mango.

reviews.author: Permanenthoneymoon
reviews.title: Small pagoda outside of Ho Chi Mihn memorial
reviews.content: If you are going to see the Memorial, then the one pillar pagoda is steps away and worth a peek.  I wouldn't make a separate trip to visit this small attraction.  When we were there, there was a lot of construction going on and there were not many people there.

reviews.author: Zee S.Puad
reviews.title: Under restoration
reviews.content: Was here few days ago and it is under restoration and still.. Located inside the area of the Mausoleum and HCM museum so you can just stop by to take a peek before going to the museum..

reviews.author: Abhimanyu A
reviews.title: Not really worth seeing.
reviews.content: All a bit underwhelming. The French destroyed the original one on their way out of the country in an act of spite. It was restored In the 50's. But not worth spending the time to visit it (also, hard core earth moving works going on right next to it)

reviews.author: ColinGJ
reviews.title: Worth a quick look
reviews.content: This is in the same complex as the Ho Chi Minh memorial/museum. It is worth a quick look whilst you are in the area, but at present there is lots of building work going on around it so if you are looking to visit a serene temple then this is not the thing!

reviews.author: Barrie L
reviews.title: Careful!
reviews.content: Be careful - the surrounding area is under construction. Bricks, concrete, heaps if demolished masonry, etc. But worth a look with it's charming Oriental architecture.

reviews.author: Leo D
reviews.title: yes, i have come here!
reviews.content: The unique pagoda is located in the western part of the city, near Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum, Ong Ich Khiem St., Ngoc Ha, Ba Dinh District, Hanoi. one pillar pagoda means long lasting happiness and good luck. it is a historic Buddhist temple in Hanoi but the One-Pillar Pagoda reflects the architectural splendour that the country has grown.it is like a lotus blooming on water surface. with a lot of meaning, the one pillar pagoda becomes one of the most sacred temples.

reviews.author: Rich M
reviews.title: walk by
reviews.content: This is worth walking by if you're in the area - and since there are a couple of other attractions right around it you probably will be.  Not much to see, but unusual enough it's worth a swing by.

reviews.author: Draghignazzo
reviews.title: Go.
reviews.content: Even everything around is under construction, I wouldn't miss stopping by. The place is tiny but sens with a lot of power and remeber: life is under construction.

reviews.author: Insearch0fadventure
reviews.title: Interesting story and nice to see it
reviews.content: There is an interesting story of dreams/fertility relating to this that makes a king very happy in 1049 - nice story  - it was being fixed when saw it - just to look and move on.

reviews.author: beentheretooo
reviews.title: not fabulous but interesting
reviews.content: visit this after the Ho Chi Minh memorial - a short walk away. Unfortunately there is restoration of surrounding buildings so the site is a dump right now but in future may be nice. The pagoda itself is small not too interesting but being on a lone concrete pillar makes it a worthwhile short visit.

reviews.author: clamoor
reviews.title: Under construction, muddy when it rains
reviews.content: It was under construction when I visited it so it was a bit disappointing but it can't be helped. It is situated in between Ho Chi Minh Museum and Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum. There might have been a signage that indicated that one is entering the site of the Pagoda but I did not see one. So it was just by luck that I made a right from the Mausoleum to check out why there are lots of people going in and out of this place. Is it a must see? Not really.

reviews.author: Karentipp
reviews.title: Under construction so be careful under foot but it is still worth a visit
reviews.content: I can understand the Vietnamese not wishing to close this beautiful Pagoda to tourists while they are making (what I hope are) necessary repairs to the area but for god sake will ye do something about making it safe under foot for people walking around. Have you no Health and Safety plans at all here ????  Its dangerous and uneven on accessing and egressing the area for the elderly and the young and the steep steps are hard for anyone poor of foot to climb as no one manages the amount of people climbing up and down, how long they stay etc. I have been here three times in 10 years and the dirt of the area and the bloody stall holders in the middle of the whole place is a disgrace. It had beautiful trees and tubs here on my first visit in 2005 so I was so disapointed to see the conditions it has fallen into.  This is a place of worship and the Vietnamese are not showing it the relevant respect so how can you expect foreign tourists to do so.  Yetsagin read up before you go in as the amount fo information about this site is terrible ..in any language. This pagoda falls under the visits to Ho Chi Minh Mauseloum and the palace so dont miss it.

reviews.author: jaci55555
reviews.title: Under construction
reviews.content: It is a construction sight at the moment. The old pictures look beautiful... There is no greenery anymore. Not worth the trip.

reviews.author: Selly29
reviews.title: Interesting history behind pagoda
reviews.content: The pagoda is situated is a very busy touristy area. If you have time you should visit it. It's fascinating to see that they worship a female deity as well.

reviews.author: RealHoltyboy
reviews.title: Building site . . . .
reviews.content: Passing the signs saying "construction,  keep out" does not bode well and too be honest it might be better when they have finished the works. Until then it is hard to appreciate this place amongst the rubble, dirt and general works. Wait until mid 2015 maybe!

reviews.author: Erlan2013
reviews.title: Another heritage in Hanoi
reviews.content: This is an ancient building long time ago, it is not special like Angkor Wat or Borobudur, because its small compare to them. But you can consider it as a package tour if you visit Ho Chi Min Moseleum in Hanoi. It's located very close to the moseleum .

reviews.author: wendyanddavid536
reviews.title: Underwhelming!
reviews.content: Positioned very close to Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum, the One Pillar Pagoda is a place of great importance to Vietnamese Buddhists. However, what you see today is largely a reconstruction after the original was destroyed by the French in the 1950s. The 'One Pillar' is now concrete, not a tree trunk, and the temple is situated in a murky pond in the middle of a building site. Visit if you are going to Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, but be prepared to be disappointed.

reviews.author: BM1986
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: The fact that it was beeing renovated when I was there might contribute to the fact that I didn't like it so much. It wasn't a peacefull place, as many other pagodas.It was just a small pagoda standing on a pillar in a small lake,

reviews.author: HanaDufkova
reviews.title: Under reconstruction
reviews.content: Dont go there as the place is under reconstruction and also the lake is dirty. Yes, pagoda itself is nice and unique, but you cannot enjoy it...

reviews.author: Sharkbait53
reviews.title: Peaceful Setting
reviews.content: A peaceful Pagoda on the lake with plenty of interesting things to see. A pleasant short walk from the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. A square to the rear has other places of worship. It's worth having a guide to make the best of you visit here.

reviews.author: Johnson_Lam
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: It's within walking distance from HCM mausoleum. It was under repairs when I was there. But still can take an awesome picture as it stands bright under the sun while surrounded by trees. A must visit after Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Haamid J
reviews.title: A pilgrimage site near the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum
reviews.content: It is right now under repairs, yet people could access the main point to pray, wish or meditate.  There were many visitors, as it is right near the HCM Mausoleum, where every tourist is brought to.

reviews.author: Brandylady
reviews.title: Small shrine
reviews.content: The pagoda is within walking distance from Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum. Apart from the fact it is rather unique being on one pillar, I wouldnt put myself out to visit it. It is very small. The surrounding area was under construction when in force- take care!

reviews.author: OISEAU_K
reviews.title: it might be special without the story
reviews.content: when my guide took me there, I was just stunned to be there, because, it is just small pavilion supported by cement legs!!! however, when I heard the background of this pavilion's foundation, hum, maybe it is worth to feel Vietnamese history.. One of the King who did not have a child met a girl at country side after a dream where Buddha handed over a baby. In order to commemorate this so called "concubine", he built this small shrine. It is restored recently because  the real "pillar" is now in Paris! I so not know if it was Napolen who shipped to France, ^^;; Anyway, original pillar seems "relocated" in France when they retrieve from Vietnam. The cement pillar seems quite ugly and not get along with the old pavilion. Behind the pavilion, there is big tree, which is related "Buddha". My guide also mentioned if someone makes a turn right side of the pavilion, you get a girl, and if you make a turn left, you get a son from the front of the pavilion. Most of my friends made a left turn but I did right one, because it was shorter way to reach the tree! As other reviewers mentioned it is not special but history makes this pillar special. AT the entrance, there is small stall restaurant, where you can enjoy nice mango, water melon and bananas, with very cheap price.

reviews.author: Chan Sai Keong
reviews.title: Nothing Special
reviews.content: It is just a small temple. Nothing special and nothing much in the surrounding area. Construction is in progress.It is very close to Ho Chi Min Mausoleum and Presidential Palace. Just go and have a look, it only take your 5 minutes there.

reviews.author: Alexperience
reviews.title: Nothing really special
reviews.content: If you're visiting the Ho Chi Minh museum you can pay it a visit, but it is not worth more trouble. Very small, surrounded by construction (at the time of visiting, nov 2014) and a bit crowded.

reviews.author: f0reverdreaming
reviews.title: not what I expected
reviews.content: Considering how many temples and pagodas I have visited I was surprised at how small this pagoda was considering the 'must see' reviews. It is positioned in between HCM museum and mausoleum just incase you cant find it!

reviews.author: Andrea S
reviews.title: Less than expected
reviews.content: I had a different idea about this pagoda and though it would be an interesting place to visit. It is, in fact. But not as special as everyone says. Besides, it was under construction in the sorounding area and it was a litle caotic.

reviews.author: Hannah C
reviews.title: Nice enough but not worth an excursion
reviews.content: The area is currently under construction - muddy, surrounded by construction work. The pillar has little charm as a result, and to be honest it's nice to look at but not really worth taking a huge detour for.

reviews.author: bryan61
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: We were in the area so visited here. Was ok but is being renovated so mess everywhere. Might be worth a visit when finished

reviews.author: Michael P
reviews.title: Construction everywhere!
reviews.content: You can be in and out of this place in a few minutes. In my opinion its nothing special at all. So if your thinking of getting a taxi there because your to far away to walk, you might want to skip this!

reviews.author: Karen
reviews.title: Construction going on. Nothing spectecular
reviews.content: Lucky for me this was part of a day tour so i didnt have to find my way here myself.  Place was under massive construction. From the entrance to footpaths to the pond on which the pagoda sat on, the whole place was being torn down and dusty. I think there was a temple in the compound, saw lotsa other temple matter sadly laid out in sheds at the back.The pagoda is Literally a small shrine atop a flight of stairs.Perhaps it would have been a much nicer visit if the construction wasnt there.

reviews.author: Jeff B
reviews.title: Small but beautifully formed.
reviews.content: Renovation work is still underway but you can now walk all the way around the pagoda and walk up steps to look in. Once all the work is completed I am sure it will be a setting of charm and atmosphere.

reviews.author: 05Iz05
reviews.title: Under construction
reviews.content: A beautiful pagoda, but the surrounding space is under constitution which ruins it a bit.It is a nice space to get away from the noise of the cars!

reviews.author: kcchin
reviews.title: small Buddhist pagoda
reviews.content: at the time of my visit (Sep2014)...., Everything was under renovation......even the walkways. The gift shop was under a large tin shack. Maybe after all the renovations are finished, it will be an attractive place to visit. It was like going to a construction zone with no hard hats..lol

reviews.author: Francesca R
reviews.title: magic place
reviews.content: the one pillar pagoda is so cool!like a lotus, is over the water...if you are in Ha Noi, you have to go!and inside, in the garden, you can buy so many fruits!

reviews.author: Shiran A
reviews.title: Nice and cool to see
reviews.content: A nice pagoda, beautiful from the inside, but I wouldn't say you shouldn't miss it. The gardens around it are beautiful- worth being there

reviews.author: Zhra789
reviews.title: Only if you have time
reviews.content: They are refurshibing the surrondings so it's a bit messy and the pagoda is not impresive. If you have plenty of time have a look but don't to on purpose.

reviews.author: lesliebauman
reviews.title: Interesting historical significance in the midst of alot construction activity presently
reviews.content: Part of the grounds around the Ho Mausoleum sits the one pillar pagoda. Worth a stop while visiting Ho homes and the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Lahiru P
reviews.title: Nice Place
reviews.content: I have visited this beautiful place during my visit to Hanoi Vietnam. Temple and nice place with fantastic architecture..

reviews.author: Erikhjorth
reviews.title: Vktour showed a pagoda
reviews.content: Vktour showed us a winderful pagoda in Hanoi.The one-legged pagoda was built in 1049 by Emperor Ly Thai Tong. The pagoda looks like a lotus flower and is a thank you for him to have a son. Ho Chi Minh Museum is also worth a visit.Pagoda.

reviews.author: hoangvl
reviews.title: Sadly it is being renovated
reviews.content: One pillar pagoda (also known as Dien Huu) is built on a single pillar, rising out in the middle of a pond, resembling a blossoming lotus bud- a symbol of purity in Buddhism. I was very eager to show my Chinese friends this unique piece of architecture, the symbol of the city during their short visit to Ha Noi. Yes, China is big on pagodas but I'm sure that they hadn't seen one with  strange-looking structure like this before. We arrived in the afternoon and much to our disappointment, the pagoda was all covered by tarps and closed to public as it was under another renovation.This pagoda has been destroyed and rebuilt many times over its nearly 1000 years of history and the latest major rebuilding was in 1955, after the French colonists destroyed it before withdrawing from Viet Nam. All we could do is trying to look from afar and check out the adjacent Ho Chi Minh Museum and the B52 lake. From what the guard there told us, the renovation won't be finished unitl next year.

reviews.author: Sam Aldridge
reviews.title: A cute Pagoda!
reviews.content: When visiting Vietnam, you will see a lot of pagodas, this one is located on the lake in the heart of Hanoi and therefore you cant really miss it. Its a nice addition to the view and I am glad I saw it, but would not have been upset if I could not fit in it. All in all if you see it, great! If not, don't worry to much about it.

reviews.author: sakticleaver
reviews.title: Under Construction
reviews.content: Although it is under construction you can still visit the temple and take a few photos. Definitely worth the visit.

reviews.author: Traveller_Chelly10
reviews.title: Another must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is a Hanoi landmark and well worth the visit, it's also a great photo stop, built of wood on a single stone pillar it is designed to resemble the lotus blossom, it is really very beautiful.

reviews.author: Katie C
reviews.title: Unfortunately under construction...
reviews.content: The Pagoda itself is very nice but the surrounding area is under construction and therefore is incredibly loud and messy, which is not the atmosphere you would usually put with a place of worship.What a shame.

reviews.author: rosie1385
reviews.title: Under restoration
reviews.content: I don't want to put this attraction down with rating as it was useless seeing it at this stage. Can go see but it's all covered and water dirtied and construction gear everywhere. Still impressive from the standpoint it's on one pillar. Wish I came at a time it wasn't covered and looking beautiful as suggested by photos. If I ever visit again it better be finished and not ruined by restoration... Maybe in a month or so time. Also maybe get a tour guide to provide some relevance as I researched all my info prior

reviews.author: Vikas Singh
reviews.title: An iconic Vietnamese temple
reviews.content: The One-Pillar Pagoda (Chua Mot Cot) is located between the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the Ho Chi Minh Museum. The pagoda was built in 1049 and resembles a giant lotus blossom. According to a legend, King Ly Thai To was childless and dreamt one night that he met the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara (Goddess of Compassion), who handed him a baby son while seated on a lotus flower. The King later married a young woman and a son was born to them. As a symbol of gratitude, he had the pagoda built and dedicated it to the Goddess. Originally built in 1049 of wood by Emperor Ly Thai To during the Ly Dynasty, the pagoda was vandalised and burned by the French in 1954 as they retreated from Hanoi - only to be rebuilt the following year out of wood again but attached to a concrete pillar.

reviews.author: Sammy J
reviews.title: Symtom of Ha Noi
reviews.content: This structure is very small but it is the symtom of Ha Noi. I heard a local talk the story about this Pagoda. A King of Vietnam dreamed a beautiful lotus which blossom which only one  branch. After he woke up, he asked the fortuneteller and this person said this was a lucky signal. This was the reason of The King built One Pillar Pagoda to illustrate the Lotus in his dream. If you have time, you should visit this structure.

reviews.author: Stefan J
reviews.title: Beautiful old temple, photo opportunity
reviews.content: Beautiful old temple, a recommended visit. A remake of the thousand year old pagoda destroyed in 1954, built to resemble a lotus blossom.

reviews.author: MG1944
reviews.title: Bad timing
reviews.content: Sadly at the time of our visit, the One Pillar Pagoda was a building site. It is part of the larger area that contains Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum and museum.

reviews.author: Francis D
reviews.title: Unique pagoda
reviews.content: This pagoda was designed with unique architecture, was built by wooden structure. It was like a lotus growing the center of lake, looked like simple but beautiful. Water in the lake was calm, made peaceful space.

reviews.author: Lie95
reviews.title: Unique
reviews.content: Yes,, the place was small, but around this place many stalls sell souvenirs, not just keychains and magnets but the handmade card 3D and many many more. Many souvenirs can be bought :)

reviews.author: Lordgin1
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is a very beautiful and serene but small site to visit.  Within steps of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.  It's a ten minute visit with good photo opportunities and a paid opportunity to enter the Pagoda for prayer.  Visit the Pagoda as an addition to other sites but do not spend the whole day just visiting this area.  Small but beautiful.

reviews.author: JohnF47
reviews.title: Unique, and great photo spot
reviews.content: Made sure I visited the One Pillar Pagoda while I was on the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex.It was a Friday, so was not very crowded.Unique architecture, and worth a visit.

reviews.author: Phua W
reviews.title: Renovations
reviews.content: Unable to view the pagoda as renovations is going on. A little disappointed.  The pagoda is actually quite small.

reviews.author: Lesley D
reviews.title: Pagoda
reviews.content: This is a replica rebuilt on a cement pillar, and is a nice photo spot.     Quite an interesting story on the reason for the one pillar, and lots of schoolkids were there seeing it.

reviews.author: SunDancerIII
reviews.title: The best part of this temple..
reviews.content: ..Is the story behind why it was built as told to us by our HanoiKids tour guide. The pagoda is behind Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, at the exit of Ho Chi Minh complex and the area around it gets very crowded.There is a charge to enter the complex. Kids under 12 are free.

reviews.author: kengoi2102
reviews.title: Small Pagoda
reviews.content: This was small but look so beautiful on the pillar. This pagoda was designed with very special architecture , with only 1 pillar carry the whole house on that. Beside that is very nice history with this pagoda. One thing I still wondering till now is : Why? The French army destroyed ,explored this wonderful pagoda before they leave Vietnam?Totally like this pagoda.P.S: Read and research the history about everyplace that you want to visit before you come. It will help you know more about them.

reviews.author: AntarcticBound
reviews.title: At the exit to the Ho Chi Min Complex
reviews.content: As you are leaving the Ho Chi Min complex, you pass by this tiny pagoda - supported by one pillar - in the middle of a pond.  The pagoda is interesting as it is likely to be the only pagoda you will see supported by only one pillar.  It is so small that it is not actually entered, but one views the shrine inside from the "entrance" after climbing up the stairs to it.  See it while in the area, but don't make a special trip to it.  It will take about 10 minutes of your time.

reviews.author: FireSpitter
reviews.title: An interesting site
reviews.content: It's very unlikely that you would make your way to this place just to view this small pagoda as there are many other interesting sites within close proximity of this place.  But yeah, do see this mini sized pagoda.

reviews.author: Mariapeni
reviews.title: Small Pagoda
reviews.content: According to the history, this pagoda build almost 1000 year ago on 1049. Built with the shape of lotus blooming on its stem. Even this pagoda is small compare other pagoda, this pagoda very interesting with its history. Imagine that a thousand year ago they can build a temple like this, with only one pillar on it...amazing. No admission fee to enter this pagoda but donation are accepted.

reviews.author: kmm81
reviews.title: Stop in while you're in the complex
reviews.content: If you do the whole complex it's worth having a look as it's located right near the museum but otherwise it's nothing much on its own.

reviews.author: Nunngo
reviews.title: Under maintenance and hard to find
reviews.content: Seeing the pergoda for the first time over 3 years ago, this visit was disappointing.  Last time it was easy to find, this time because it is fenced and under repair, we walked past it.   Not worth seeing as you cannot get close up, it is covered by scaffolding and a photo of it in its glory is impossible.

reviews.author: Mandromeda
reviews.title: Nothing to write home about
reviews.content: If you've never seen a pagoda/shrine/temple in your life, this will be of interest to you. Otherwise, only swing by if you're already in the area.

reviews.author: MzTaylor88
reviews.title: Do it only if visiting the mausoleum
reviews.content: The Pagoda is really only worth a quick walk past after visiting the mausoleum or the Presidential Palace gardens - it's really not that impressive when you compare it to other structures and temples in Southeast Asia. For some reason it attracts a lot of people though so be prepared for crowds.

reviews.author: Christina P
reviews.title: amazing
reviews.content: amazing to the max. haha. after my trip to ho chi minh president. there is one pagodar with only one pillar and around is full of lotus flowers.

reviews.author: AZGandalf
reviews.title: Near Uncle Ho. Quick stop
reviews.content: Interesting pagoda very near Uncle Ho. Shady rest place with a drink on a hot and humid day. Not worth a trip but well worth as a side trip from mosoleum.

reviews.author: DMon13
reviews.title: Quick stop after Mausoluem
reviews.content: Came here as part of a tour, and admit its not very impressive compared to some structures in Hanoi - but as its in walking distance from HCM's Mausoleum its worth dropping by.  Our tour guide explained the history of the pagoda which was one of the most interesting stories of the day and helped me understand why so many Vietnamese were flocking to pray at the alter.  Well worth seeing if you understand its significance.

reviews.author: ineffa-bul
reviews.title: underwhelming
reviews.content: A concrete pillar with a concrete box on top, standing in a slimy pond, crowded by tourists and surrounded by hawkers. It wasn't even worth the effort of taking my camera out of its bag.

reviews.author: Michael
reviews.title: Interesting building
reviews.content: This is another thing to find someone who knows the background to take you to. While it's interesting to see, to hear the story and background makes it that much more interesting. It's just a short visit, and is located in the HCM sites. Worth swinging by.

reviews.author: Traveller
reviews.title: Basic
reviews.content: A previous King had this place built to pray for a specific purpose (he wanted a son). It is a small, simple and basic pagoda. Tourists visit because it is located close to other attractions (otherwise, not many tourists would bother to see this small and basic place, I reckon).Having seen much larger Pagodas in China, this one pales in comparison.A quick glance, a few photos and that wraps up this rather mundane visit.

reviews.author: C98SueKL
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: One should visit the One Pillar Pagoda while in Hanoi. It is located just next to the Presidential Palace Area.

reviews.author: Natalia-Khm
reviews.title: Very unusual and genuine building!
reviews.content: I like Pagoda as fine architectural construction. It is close to mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh and Lenin Memorial. Near mausoleum Vietnamese people make a training.

reviews.author: roboesGistel
reviews.title: one pillar pagoda-Hanoi
reviews.content: This pagoda is situated in the gardens behind the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.It was constructed in the 11th ventury by the old king Ly Thai To who still had no son. In a vision he saw the Godess of Mercy-sitting on a lotus- with a male child in her lap. She handed the child to the King . Soon after this dream , his wife gave him a son.The gratefull King ordered a pagoda to be built in the shape of a lotus.The Original pagoda has been damaged many times during repeated wars ; even the French burned the pagoda when they retreated from Vietnam in1954 . In1955 a replica was built resting on one concrete pillar instead of the original wooden pillar.The pagoda is much visited by childless couples making offerings to the Godess of Mercy Quan Am. It is also said this pagoda to posess some healing powers. Around the temple is a lilly-pond and this gives much harmony with the Lotus-shaped temple considering that the Lotus is a symbol of purity and regeneration.

reviews.author: Sheryl A
reviews.title: Average pagoda over run with visitors
reviews.content: Like many unusual pieces of architecture this is best photographed when empty - regrettably when we visited today Sunday it had a permanent flow and was surrounded at all angles. Would be lovely if made 'out of bounds'.. Worth a look if you at Ho Chi Minh's resting place... Free to enter.

reviews.author: Carla_Thiago
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: Worth the visit. The pagoda was originally made of wood, but caught fire and was replaced by cement. The story behind it is beautiful. According to the legen, the king Ly Thai Tong did not have any kids and one day he dreamt of a buddha sitting on a lotus flower with a baby boy on her hands. The following year he was granted with a baby boy. As a gratitude action, he ordered the construction of this pagoda.

reviews.author: Thang Guider
reviews.title: An ancient Pagoda!
reviews.content: A very small pagoda on a huge pillar of concrete Furniture support could Easily a hundred more. And you can not enter inside, but the One Pillar Pagoda is quiet spot to relax as no vehicles are allowed in the surrounding area. Not too much pressure from People trying to sell you stuff either. Here is very close to Ho Chi Minh museum or Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, just about 2 minutes walk you can reach the place.

reviews.author: Eunice_Lau
reviews.title: Unique temple
reviews.content: This temple is located on one pillar and its design is unique. This temple is opened whole day and no need to pay for entry. Temple is small and nothing to see actually.

reviews.author: Fredrik N
reviews.title: A pagoda, so what?
reviews.content: The rather small one pillar pagoda might not sound as much, but I think its design sets it apart from your standard pagoda experience. Visiting the Ho Chi Minh residence or mausoleum, stop by and take a look!

reviews.author: Sammi B
reviews.title: Cute little place
reviews.content: Cute little place, very busy, if you are near the area, then have a wee look, if not then do something else.  I do wish people would realise that one side of the stairs is up and one side down, if everyone else is doing that, then don’t push your way up the down side!!

reviews.author: Ntee6603
reviews.title: Iconic symbol of Hanoi and VietNam
reviews.content: For those who have certain knowledge about the culture of the country, the One Pillar Pagoda represents a unique symbol of VietNam.  Dating back in history, it always was a rallying point for the Vietnamese people: a small anecdotal footnote about the present structure- it was completely rebuilt after the French destroyed it before they left the country.  Also being a Buddhist temple, there was a Bodhi tree given as a sapling by the Indian government from the original Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya, India, where Buddha attained enlightenment over 2500 years ago.

reviews.author: mjrg59
reviews.title: Iconic scene representative of Hanoi
reviews.content: Learn about the dream that created the design for this structure and take photographs of others who are being photographed in front of it.  It is the iconic scene of Hanoi architecture.

reviews.author: JamieTanBK
reviews.title: Normal
reviews.content: There is nothing spectacular about this place... come here just to take a photo or two so that you can say "I've been there".

reviews.author: mhburney
reviews.title: Might as well if you're there
reviews.content: The place was talked up so much from the hotel staff that I was expecting be blown away. What a let down!This place is worth a visit ONLY if you're on a HCM mausoleum trip anyways, otherwise it's not advisable to waste your time. Perhaps when the water lilies are out it makes for a more appealing trip, but in December, it was a small structure you'd see anywhere and wouldn't give a second look. One of those places you see because you're already there and can mark it off your seen list. That's about it.

reviews.author: PLP
reviews.title: Nothing Impressive
reviews.content: Most, if not all, tourists are there as part of Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum tour. It is a pagoda built on one pillar and that is it. Nothing impressive and not worth the trip there.

reviews.author: AlnAbroad
reviews.title: You'll be there anyway
reviews.content: The One Pillar Pagoda is in Ba Dihn Square, in amongst with the Presidential Palace and the Mausoleum.  You will probably be there anyway, so there's no reason not to take a couple minutes and check out the Pagoda.  It's not all that impressive though, but it doesn't take any time or effort.

reviews.author: Jordan C
reviews.title: Just a step around the corner from Uncle Ho
reviews.content: I think most people who go to Hanoi make sure to visit Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum (which is closed for most of the day). What people usually miss is the single pillar pagoda just behind the mausoleum. Take a quick stop, it is definitely worth seeing.

reviews.author: konshoe
reviews.title: Ancient rebuilt
reviews.content: We did not arrive in the right season to view the pond in its full splendor, for we only witnessed murky waters bereft of any color apart from the color of mud. In my research online, the lotus pond would be covered by greens punctuated by pinks of lotus flower, an enrapturing sight to most visitors. The pagoda would then blend perfectly well with the pond, a giant artificial lotus in a pond full of originals.We ventured around the temple proper and found other interesting areas within the compound not shared usually on guidebooks. A side to the lotus ponds stood two smaller pagodas, vertical shrines for further offerings to be made by the faithful, one in white and the other in red.Another area worth taking a look would be a sky reaching tree behind the One Pillar Pagoda. A closer look revealed that this was no ordinary tree, but one which was sacred to Buddhism. The bodhi tree hovered protectively over a small statue of Gautama Buddha, with simple and austere adornments of flowers nearby, an incense urn in front for the faithful to offer their prayers. This was another part of the compound nearly untouched by visiting tourists, allowing the faithful to visit Buddha in relative serenity.

reviews.author: Marcia R
reviews.title: Don't make a special trip!
reviews.content: If you're on the grounds, swing by and take a look...the one support pillar is not original.  It's a tiny pagoda on one pillar, hence the name.  That's it.

reviews.author: sez101
reviews.title: Boring
reviews.content: It's a pagoda on one stilt if your in the area take a photo but otherwise it's boring and dull. It's pretty to look at but not a highlight in my book.

reviews.author: teamDunit
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: Unique and a one of a kind building. Worth looking at and listening to history of building the pagoda. To come to vietnam from overseas and not soak up some culture and history is a wasted trip.

reviews.author: pinotchicky
reviews.title: Great introduction to religion
reviews.content: It was very close to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex. It's a small pagoda but very ornate and well preserved.  Our guide shared all the religious history and that made it all the more enjoyable to visit.

reviews.author: MarkAnnaLondon
reviews.title: Ok, but missable
reviews.content: We expected more of this place. It was very much a case of 'Oh, ok, tick, what's next'There really isn't a lot to see or explore more than what you can see on the photo. Essentially that is it.It's worth 15 minutes if you're on a day tour in Hanoi, but there's other stuff that's more interesting.

reviews.author: ScottThorley
reviews.title: Nothing spectatcular, nice fruit by sold by the side!
reviews.content: Worthy of a photo but not much else really. I bought some very tasty fruits from the stall at the side if the pagoda. Nothing more to say really.

reviews.author: Jana C
reviews.title: Different pagoda
reviews.content: This pagoda is really tiny. I couldn't believe when I saw how little it was. There is a tiny sort of a lake around it and few steps if you want to go up. I actually thought this is very pretty despite you don't need much time for your visit. One Pillar Pagoda is very close to the Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum.

reviews.author: Ablingdon
reviews.title: Pretty
reviews.content: This is a pretty Pagoda, and very unusual. We went at Tet and it was very busy. It is also tiny and takes very little time to see.

reviews.author: Octovianus G
reviews.title: In one compund of Ho Chi Minh's complex, nothing special .......
reviews.content: This One Pillar Pagoda is located in the same compund of the Ho Chi Minh's complex. Thus when you are visiting the Mausoleum, Residence & Museum of Ho Chi Minh, the local guide will take you to this place, too. Actually there is nothing special with this place, but since my sisters-in-laws and nieces are Buddhists, they had the opportunity to pray at this One Pillar Pagoda. Besides that, you can also take a break and enjoying some local fruits at some reasonable prices from the nice sellers at site .......

reviews.author: Vianney Y
reviews.title: For picture-taking purposes only
reviews.content: The name says it all. Nothing much can be done here except take pictures or make an offering. Some tourists also simply sit around and take a break.

reviews.author: Geoff A
reviews.title: OK if you need to fill in time.
reviews.content: Having been to Halong Bay and walking and riding around the old quarter, Hoan Kiem lake, the French quarter etc. etc., we were running out of things to do so decided to venture further afield.  However we thought that we had to be a lot more desperate to appreciate the one pillar pagoda which we thought was very ordinary.

reviews.author: 8Nikki8
reviews.title: Interesting Structure
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda is in the compound of all the Ho Chi Minh visit. I visited it as I left the Residence. It was a quick stop before going on to the Museum. I pretty much just took a photo and moved on because the crowds were kind of large. I thought it was an interesting structure, it was a bit different from other pagodas I had seen.

reviews.author: BK18854
reviews.title: Check it if you are nearby
reviews.content: It's a photo spot. Small, and I am not sure I find it very spectacular. If you are in the area for the palace and ho chi minh mausoleum, then stop by.

reviews.author: ChrisGoldy
reviews.title: Part of Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and house complex
reviews.content: Not original as was rebuilt after destructive and spiteful French destroyed everything when leaving. Not even the nazis damaged Paris when they arrived or left. So who is worse. The pagoda itself is unique (or original would have been). In current state it's really just another pagoda. See it because its part of the complex and likely you will be here if visiting Hanoi

reviews.author: RoamingRuss
reviews.title: Photo and Go
reviews.content: Its quaint. Get the photo on passing on the way back from seeing Ho Chi Minh and head off. Other than that its a bit hard to say much else. Far tooooo many other things to go and see!

reviews.author: Whitlam H
reviews.title: Bit disappointed
reviews.content: The one pillar pagoda was really hyped up by the guide books but really it was a bit disappointing and the crowds didn't really allow you to take decent pictures (especially when its raining and their are multi coloured macs and brollies everywhere blocking the view).  The pillar itself has been rebuilt numerous time and is quite simply concrete.  The pagdo is quite pretty in itself and it does give you an impression of what must have stood here once.  The area is hidden away near the Ho Chi Minh musuem and was quite difficult to find (perhaps because we approached it from a different angle).

reviews.author: Tvler8
reviews.title: Worth the visit, but allow time if it is crowded
reviews.content: The One Pillar is part of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. If it is a busy day you will need to wait because it is quite small.

reviews.author: Michelle M
reviews.title: Allow fifteen minutes unless there's a crowd
reviews.content: The original pagoda, constructed around one thousand years ago, was apparently destroyed by the French during their departure from Vietnam in the mid 1950's.  It has been rebuilt and by now, looks quite old, showing character with it's pleasing symmetry and weathered stone work replete with ferns and mosses.  It is built upon a single plinth (pillar) rising lotus like from a small moat and is near to the HCM Museum.   You can climb the steps to inspect it's interior or make an offering.  Taking a photograph without capturing any tourists may prove impossible as the pagoda is located amid the noisy hoopla of a busy market area.  I wandered off to the left and spent a few minutes enjoying looking at pot plants and small gardens.

reviews.author: MelindaMulberry
reviews.title: Visit whilst visiting museum
reviews.content: I wouldn't make a special trip to visit this, but as it's right next to the museum you may as well. It's important to note for historical purposes that this is actually a reproduction of the original, as the French destroyed the original. It's therefore not as old as you may think. As a visitor in a wheelchair I found that ground access was surprisingly good, and flat, if a little rickety with the cobbles. There are steps up to the pagoda, (as usual), but as it's so small, probably not worth the effort to go up. It's a really busy site here, with hundreds of Vietnamese queuing to go up the steps.

reviews.author: EllaOco
reviews.title: nice place to take pictures
reviews.content: It was a nice place to take pictures. But only for 5 minutes or so, because there is nothing else besides the pagoda and the boats on the lake. We sat outside this prayer room but was asked to leave as there was a ceremony or something inside. Like a mass. The way we were asked to leave was not very nice and friendly.

reviews.author: MrBunnsBangkok
reviews.title: Don't go out of your way
reviews.content: A small wooden structure on top of concrete stairs and a small pond. That's it. This place isn't that interesting, but the large number of people selling drinks, food, and touristy knick-knacks might try and convince you otherwise. It is right next to the HoChiMin Musuem.

reviews.author: Jasmine E
reviews.title: just your average pagoda, only smaller, and less photo worthy.
reviews.content: Small pagoda. Near Museum. I basically sits no higher than a house. Nothing special about it, its surroundings , or the museum near by. I didn't even bother getting a photo of either, and didnt think it was worth the walk to visit !!

reviews.author: 194SteveS194
reviews.title: Touristy
reviews.content: Touristy, not of much interest.  Overall underwhelming.  The best thing I can say about the One Pillar Pagoda is that it was near the HCM Mausoleum so it was not far out of our way.

reviews.author: CherryJim
reviews.title: One-pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: A small but the oldest pagoda in VN. The architect of this pagoda is unique. It's worth visiting when you are on the way to visit Ho Chi Minh Museum

reviews.author: peperoni
reviews.title: Not very impressive
reviews.content: A rather small and unattractive pagoda.  The only thing special about it is may be it was erected on a large pillar.

reviews.author: Sabaudia73
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: Very crowded, lots of vendors getting on your back, bus load of kids who just visited the mausoleum.I was very disappointed as I was looking forward to see it, quite small. Not worth visiting.

reviews.author: fsenada
reviews.title: Just an altar...
reviews.content: Wasn't much to see, just making sure I covered my places of interest count for the day. Its an Altar in the midst of the pond where people come to pray and do their offerings.

reviews.author: Backmansinhanoi
reviews.title: Crowded
reviews.content: So many people visiting at the same time take away the charm. It was busy busy and a lot of mobile vendors wanted to sell things outside. For me this was very disappointing. I thought that it was a place of tranquility. It was the opposite. I would much rather visit some other pagoda with less people (outside Ha Noi to get the right feeling).

reviews.author: James B
reviews.title: Smaller than you think..
reviews.content: Not that big, large crowds and to me doesn't look that old! If you've made it to Ho Chi's mausoleum its a very short walk so you may as well go and see it but not worth the effort unless your in the near vicinity.

reviews.author: Bella C
reviews.title: Charming!
reviews.content: A beautifully calm spot after the hugeness of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. The elegant little wooden pagoda rises on its single stone pillar out of a lotus pond.

reviews.author: jsteven8484
reviews.title: One pillar pagoda
reviews.content: It's just a tiny pagoda but with a very special architecture. The One Pillar Pagoda was built in 1049 in the reign of King Ly Thai Tong "Winter in October up Dien Huu Pagoda. Beside the pagoda, there was a small temple which was serving quite a number of Vietnamese and tourists food, which was quite interesting.

reviews.author: Jen D
reviews.title: Look! A pagoda
reviews.content: It's ok, but not a must see.  Quite a pretty spot, but not much else. It can get quite noisy and over run with school children. Close to Ho Chi Minh museum

reviews.author: Jessie810
reviews.title: Sweet little spot!
reviews.content: Was really surprised at the calm, private feeling of this little pagoda. We were there in the evening and didn't have any problems with other people being around us. Loved the symbolism and the significance of this little place. Supposedly if you want your baby to be a boy you have to go to the top of the stairs to say a prayer to the gods. Its just around the corner from the HCM mausoleum and I thought it was much more interesting to see then HCM!

reviews.author: ashkw
reviews.title: Very pretty place, but prepare to be hassled
reviews.content: A very pretty place to visit in Hanoi, which you might as well look at if visiting the mausoleum or museum. The area is not under cover and water drainage is bad, so if it's raining, ensure you bring a brolly :)

reviews.author: unREMb
reviews.title: Small but interesting
reviews.content: The actual pagoda was quite small and housed a small shrine.The grounds around it was quite packed with tourists and there was a short description (in English) on the origins of the pagoda. Unfortunately, due to the size of the pagoda, only one or two persons can climb up to take a closer look at once.Beside the pagoda, there was a small temple which was serving quite a number of Vietnamese and tourists food, which was quite interesting. We didn't stay to find out more though.

reviews.author: Andrew T
reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.content: Unless you are in the immediate area seeing the mausoleum, don't bother making a special trip. Completely underwhelming.

reviews.author: Tommye F
reviews.title: very pretty
reviews.content: One Pillar Pagoda, a historic Buddhist temple built in a style of a lotus emerging out of the water. Very pretty.  Architecturally interesting.

reviews.author: Monika F
reviews.title: Cute but busy
reviews.content: It is a cute little temple at the Ho Chi Minh complex. With the masses of people waiting in line to walk up it is a little hard to enjoy. None the less it is a unique building. The water that surrounds the pillar is pretty disgusting to look at.Once you walk back down the steps and basically walk straight on you will find an entrance to a temple. Very easy to miss. I actually did not realize there was a temple entrance at all. We had exited all together until I noticed the temple from the outside and went back in surch for a way into the temple. Still many people found the way in before we did.

reviews.author: Luv2Travel484
reviews.title: Cute and unique but crowded
reviews.content: This is very unique and cute. Unfortunately I went around noon and it was swarming with tourists (I guess because many places close during lunch hours so the bus tours come here then!) but I was still able to get close and get good pictures. Sadly at this time of year the water around it was just murky with no lotus flowers or other greenery in it. As others have said you can't go inside but you can climb the steps and look. Located right next to the Ho Chi Minh museum and near to the mausoleum. There are bathrooms and drink vendors here as well but I did not experience any aggressive sellers. The pagoda itself is free.

reviews.author: Sarah C
reviews.title: Tiny, easy to miss
reviews.content: cute little pagoda that you can climb up some steep steps and peek inside (too small to enter). It was packed with tourist but still nice. In the same courtyard as the pagoda is the entrance to a small temple but its a bit hidden since the entrance doesn't seem to lead anywhere if you just peer in. If your facing the pagoda stairs, the entrance is over your left shoulder. The pagoda itself it also a bit hidden since its behind vendors that try to sell you things a bit aggressively as you pass so it caused us to walk past the entrance quickly and miss it. FREE.

reviews.author: highfever88
reviews.title: Interesting Little Pagoda
reviews.content: Was there in the afternoon and it was quite quiet, not too many tourists. Nothing much here but its a nice place to see something special, a pagoda with one big round column. You can walk up the stairs and make some offerings at the pagoda. It is believed that you will be granted with a bearing of a son (as Vietnamese still place importance on son than daughter) if you pray at the pagoda. When you visit the pagoda, it is also nearby the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and the museum.

reviews.author: wolfie97
reviews.title: Just a Pagoda
reviews.content: It is said by the locals, those you pay tributes at this pagoda shall be blessed with successful fertility.  This pagoda is located near the Ho Chi Minh complex and it is flooded with tourist traps and souvenir street vendors.  It is heavily crowded when I was there.

reviews.author: Dancingmocha
reviews.title: UNique design
reviews.content: So come if you are praying for a fertility. Also, it is very near the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and museum

reviews.author: Alex D
reviews.title: Religious iconic pagoda
reviews.content: Built in 1049 according to a dream had by the Kinh Ly Thai Tong. The One-Pillar Pagoda in Hanoi has been named as one of the most unique works of architecture on the continent, in the Asia Book of Records. It is a good place to see together with Ho Chi Minh Complex

reviews.author: CarinAsh
reviews.title: A Quick Look
reviews.content: Nice one pillar pagoda and that's about it.  It's a short walk from HCM Mausoleum so it's easy to take a quick look.

reviews.author: AgungI
reviews.title: Just Ok
reviews.content: If you go to the mosseleum of Ho Chi Minh, you can just walk to One Pillar Pagoda only 2 minutes, the location si not far also from Ho Chi Minh house.The area is tidy and clean, not much to see, only the pagoda but it is unique.

reviews.author: blindgeekpoet
reviews.title: It is what it is :-)
reviews.content: It's near the mausoleum so it won't be bad to take a quick peep. A lot of Asian (oriental) tourists ply the few stairs to maybe say a little prayer. It's good for a picture or two, then you can move on.

reviews.author: Lilia_Phan
reviews.title: Unique architecture
reviews.content: It's just a tiny pagoda but with a very special architecture. It was build on a small pond which cover with extremely beatiful flowers named "Hoa Sung". I like to enjoy the atmosphere there.

reviews.author: LigerTravel2012
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda - Hanoi
reviews.content: According to Dai Viet Su Ky Toan Thu, The Complete History of Great Viet, the pagoda was built in the winter of 1049 under the reign of King Ly Thai Tong who dreamed of seeing the Goddess of Mercy sitting in a lotus throne and talking him to it. When awaking, the king told his mandarins about his dream and one of them thought that it was a bad omen. Monk Thien Tue advised him to build a pagoda and a lotus-shaped tower just as he had seen in his dream. When the pagoda was inaugurated, monks went around the pagoda and recited the Buddhist scriptures to pray for longevity of the king. For this reason, the pagoda is also called Dien Huu (long lasting happiness and good luck).

reviews.author: 607AliciaK
reviews.title: Iconic symbol of Hanoi
reviews.content: For whatever reasons, One Pillar Pagoda, which can be found very near Ho Chi Minh’s house, has become an iconic symbol of Hanoi. It is a very tiny little Pagoda outside the Ho Chi Minh Museum. It is a wooden Pagoda built on a single stone pillar in the middle of a very small pond. No entrance fee.

reviews.author: meg l
reviews.title: Don't go to the trouble of getting there.
reviews.content: We rated this place as a most unfortunate experience! We were staying in Hanoi with three of our grandchildren  aged 11, 9 and 8 and we had been  told that this theme park was a fun place for children and that a pool was also available in which they could swim.....no such luck!! .  One  Merry go Round and one Dodge em Car  appeared to be the only 'fun activities' in operation (at a price over and above the initial entrance fee! ). The' Zoo' however was open and was included in the initial entrance fee but what  a shock this turned out to be!  In 93 deg fahrenheit  (34 deg celsius), a  lone lioness was sitting on concrete with no shade or water available, two giraffes and a zebra standing on concrete with no water or shade available, several hippopotamus  sitting together on concrete with only dark green water nearby.  But the most distressing of all were two elephants standing on concrete, each shackled to a post by a chain  approx. 2 feet long. The only movement these elephants appeared capable of was to sway back and forth on the spot. .....once again no water or shade was evident.This place is not worth the trouble or effort of getting to it, let alone warranting  a rating on Trip Advisor

reviews.author: Molly M
reviews.title: Absoloutley Horrible
reviews.content: This was definitely my worst expirience in Hanoi!!!!! They charged a significantly (this following a long expensive taxi ride) large entrace fee and then all the rides/attractions were closed!!!!! There was a zoo that was open so we decided that we may as well go in. The animals were treated horribly. The elephants were chained to the wall and they had no food or water. The walls, floors and rooves were concrete and the animals had nothing to do. We got out as quickly as we could. There was supposed to be a dolphin show, so we looked into it and the dolphin enclosure wasn't even finished. The Bao Son "Paradise" Theme Park is horrible and I strongly recommend that you do not go there.

reviews.author: Steven H
reviews.title: One Pillar Pagoda
reviews.content: Not a lot to see but very interesting.  Go with a local guide to understand the history.  Was destroyed by the departing French in 1954 and rebuilt.

reviews.author: Salma56
reviews.title: Maintenance of the murky water long overdue!
reviews.content: The structure is quaint but sadly is somewhat shabby. It is important that the government maintain such an important part of the country's history, said to have been constructed in the eleventh century. Local people were enjoying the quietness of the surrounding gardens and I was pleased to see were given respect as they were praying.

reviews.author: Julianna M
reviews.title: Views
reviews.content: Beautiful and unique journey.

reviews.author: Zak H
reviews.title: We had the best guide
reviews.content: We really enjoyed our Trang An boat tour. Our guide, Lien, was absolutely lovely. She took the time to introduce herself properly and even pointed out where King Kong was filmed, which was a great added touch.We chose Option 2, which is the shortest route. It took us through three caves and three pagodas. At each pagoda, we had around 10 minutes to get off the boat, explore the area, take photos, and purchase a drink if needed. The boat seats were comfortable, although be prepared for sitting for quite a long period of time. You can help out by choosing to row yourself. The scenery was the real highlight. The mountains and surrounding landscape were absolutely beautiful, with plenty of opportunities to stop and take photos. Inside some of the caves, the ceilings can be quite low, so you occasionally need to duck to avoid hitting your head!There were quite a few crowds, but surprisingly, everything seemed to work well and it didn't take away from the experience. Overall, a beautiful and relaxing way to experience Trang An, with stunning scenery and a lovely guide who made the trip even more enjoyable.

reviews.author: Chris
reviews.title: Pffff it is a long sit in a boat
reviews.content: It is worth it, but do not choose the full or long package from the offered options. We had #3 for 300,000 pp.The rowers have a tough job, it's almost 3 hours of sailing. The longest cave is 1.5 km. But watch out, it's very low!Along the way, you stop at various temples.Is it worth it? Yes and no! It takes a long time and can be extremely hot. On the other hand, the landscape is beautiful and varied.

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: Unmissable experience
reviews.content: One of the absolute must-do experiences in Ninh Binh. The boat trip lasts about two hours and covers a route of about 10 km, so consider the timing carefully before leaving.The boats are small, generally with four passengers plus the person rowing, and the route crosses a spectacular landscape made of rivers, karst mountains, vegetation, and caves.The only real difficulty, at least in summer, is the truly scorching heat. On the boats there are umbrellas to protect yourself from the sun, but you will have to hold them yourselves during the trip. Furthermore, it is mandatory to wear a life jacket, which is noticeable in the heat and humidity. Absolutely bring water, sunscreen, and a hat.There are so many people and during peak times a procession of boats almost forms, making you lose a bit of the magic of the place. Despite this, it is definitely worth it.Trang An is one of the most spectacular places in the region and, in my opinion, one of the must-see attractions in northern Vietnam.

reviews.author: essentialism
reviews.title: Beautiful landscape! But…
reviews.content: We bought tickets for 2 adults and 1 child, and were told it would be 4 people per boat. However, at the pier, the dispatcher didn't count our child as a seat and forced us to share with 2 strangers (5 people total). When we declined, they acted very rudely, and the rower even shouted at our child. We tried to stay polite and treat it as a language barrier, but they just left us waiting on the side. The issue was only resolved after we reported it to the manager, who agreed to send us off after a 20-minute wait.

reviews.author: jh0rnsey
reviews.title: Highly recommend this trip.
reviews.content: To be clear this review is for the No.2 Trang An shared 4 person boat trip (not tour) which takes you through 4 caves and to 3 temples and lasted nearly 3 hours. Our lady boat rower was excellent and made our trip very special.  This experience was like nothing that we had ever experienced before in our 2 visits to Vietnam. We would highly recommend this trip.

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: Superb
reviews.content: A place of great beauty where the film King Kong was notably filmed. A walk of a little less than 1 hour 30 minutes in an idyllic setting. Despite a large number of tourists, the place remains peaceful. All around the site, you will find places to eat and numerous souvenir shops are available.Special mention to the rowers, sometimes elderly people who probably make the trip several times a day by the sole strength of their arms. Giving them a tip at the end of the activity is the least one can do.

reviews.author: Edward N
reviews.title: A Beautiful and Seamless Experience at Trang An
reviews.content: Once we entered the grounds of Trang An, we found it easy to move around, with clear signage, very friendly staff, and a very efficient ticket office. The highlight of the complex, though, was the boat trip. The boat trip was peaceful, beautiful, and relaxing. The views were stunning. Towering limestone mountains covered in lush greenery surrounded us. The water was crystal clear and seemed to reflect everything. We went through many caves, each of different shapes and sizes. Some were very tall, while others were much lower. Each cave had its own special atmosphere. Our boat rowers were very skilled at their job and very gentle with the oars on the water. They were also very knowledgeable about everything we were seeing. They made us feel very safe and were always willing to answer any questions that we had.The area has been preserved so well and must be a huge task to keep it so clean with so many visitors, but it never felt overcrowded, and you can really tell that everyone respects the environment. The whole area has a very peaceful, calm feeling, and every moment we were there was perfect for taking in the views and the fresh air.In summary, Trang An gave us a flawless experience: beautiful natural landscapes, perfect organization, very friendly people, and lots of peace. We can highly recommend it to all travelers visiting Ninh Binh. A wonderful day!

reviews.author: mvanroy
reviews.title: Beautiful rowing between limestone rocks and through caves!
reviews.content: Yes, this is a very tourist activity. Yes, there are many people and there are many boats (boat 1382 was the highest number we have seen). Yes, it is commercially exploited (but also just well organized). Yes, it is not cheap by Vietnamese standards (300,000 months, but 3 hours of fun). But all this doesn't make it any less special and beautiful!We had chosen route 3 because it seemed to give us the most variety with the combination of 3 temple stops and 3 caves. The temples are authentic and are still used (these are stops of about 10 minutes). The caves are very special, especially the dot cave because you sail through the cave for a kilometer in twilight, where you occasionally have to bend down to avoid hitting your head.For the rest, between the caves and temples it is mainly enjoying nature and karst peaks. Our captain was very friendly and patient. Her English was not so good but chapeau to do this daily.

reviews.author: Naks B
reviews.title: Memorable must -do activity in Vietnam
reviews.content: We had a wonderful multi- generational family experience. There are 3 options for the boat rides. We did no 2, lasting for 2.5 hrs, costing 300,000 VD per person. The management is fantastic inspite of it being crowded with locals and tourists alike. Our boat was rowed by a lady with super powers😃. She made the experience more meaningful for us, guiding us where to take pictures etc, assuring our safety inside the caves. The scenic ride is awesome. Has to be in your to-do list if u visit Vietnam.

reviews.author: Jeneva S
reviews.title: Beautiful boat ride, but very crowded
reviews.content: I did the Trang An boat tour on a hot morning and honestly the scenery was stunning. The limestone cliffs rising out of the water, the little caves, and the quiet stretches between the rows of paddling boats felt pretty special. I loved drifting through the grottoes and seeing the green water and all the old temples tucked away in there. That said, it was more crowded and a bit more organized/touristy than I expected, so it didn’t always feel peaceful. The boat ride can also be a little repetitive if you’ve already done other river tours in Vietnam. Still, it’s absolutely worth seeing once, and I’d recommend it with a bit of patience.

reviews.author: Cathi R
reviews.title: Pretty scenery, but the crowds wore me down
reviews.content: I went to Trang An on a cloudy morning and the karst scenery really is beautiful. The boat ride through the caves was calm at first, and I liked the cool air inside the tunnels and the sound of the oars hitting the water. The temples along the way were fine, though nothing that really stood out to me. My main issue was how crowded and organized it felt — lots of waiting, lots of boats, and it moved a bit too much like a process. I also found the whole outing a little long by the end. Glad I saw it, but for me it was more pleasant than memorable.

reviews.author: S G
reviews.title: Family fun and best cave experience.
reviews.content: Forget Ha Long bay - this is so much better with kids!

reviews.author: SALA TAM COC HOTEL & SPA
reviews.title: Trang An , a must do in Ninh Binh!
reviews.content: Nice , Clearn nature but very crowded of tourist.

reviews.author: TIẾN NAM Đ
reviews.title: Page and
reviews.content: I went alone on a day with a little rain, but in general TRANG AN is very nice to go by boat.

reviews.author: fujiiko
reviews.title: Ninh Binh.
reviews.content: Jade green rivers cutting through rice paddies as far as the eye can see, and all around karst mountains popping up everywhere. The boat ride is the experience to have, with low caves and hidden lakes. Total silence and beautiful temples everywhere emerging from the rocks. Afternoons by bike, rice paddies, and mysticism; this is where Vietnam begins to change.

reviews.author: Explorer11280645473
reviews.title: Trang An eco
reviews.content: We had experience very relaxing in Trang An. The river was clean and fresh. Peaceful and happy

reviews.author: Amy T
reviews.title: Beautiful and Relaxing - Go Early to Avoid Crowds
reviews.content: I didn't expect to enjoy this experience as much as I did. I went earlier in the day to try to avoid the crowds which was the right call as we could see the increased traffic on our way back. We did Route 1 because were interested in seeing the caves more than the pagodas and it was fantastic. It was majestic and relaxing. Would recommend for sure if you're visiting the Ninh Binh area. We even saw some monkeys high up in a tree near the end of our trip.

reviews.author: Marc B
reviews.title: Great!
reviews.content: Nice to sail through this beautiful nature reserve in a rowing boat. Personally, I liked this better than Ha Long Bay. Also busy but much less noise.

reviews.author: John W
reviews.title: A magical experience
reviews.content: This is a big operation (2000 boats, I was told) so it has to be well organised, and it is. Each boat takes 3 or 4 people plus the oars(wo)man. The tourists are required to wear life jackets. The rowers don't - are they good swimmers or are they expendable? The cost (300K dong) per adult is expensive for Vietnam but a comparable experience elsewhere would cost far more.There is a choice of three routes, all taking ~3 hours. Route 1 which I took passes through the most caves, each one opening into a new steep sided basin with towering jungle clad slopes and sheer limestone crags. The cave ceilings can be low, so sometimes you need to duck. Stops are made to visit three temples. The second one (Tran temple) is for the fit and strong. It involves a long steep climb to a saddle, then down the other side to a most unimpressive shrine, and return the same way. If I had known what I was in for I would have stayed with the boat. Not much wildlife to be seen; look out for little grebes popping up all over the waters.All in all, a wonderful experience and well worth the money.

reviews.author: bbrady962
reviews.title: Underrated and as impressive as the Grand Canyon
reviews.content: Having been to Halong bay as well, this place is more spectacular and a better experience overall. The scenery is breathtaking and the water in the rivers are pristine as no tourist motor boats are allowed. There is always lots of space between the constant flow of paddle boats so you still get that peaceful experience. You can also join in and paddle with the guide which is fun.  The stops along the way are really interesting surrounded by these steep green mountains like nothing we have seen before.Exceeded our expectations and for us as impressive as the grand canyon or Yosemite. Only advice would be to go early

reviews.author: AlexSwallow
reviews.title: Fantastic- and unique!
reviews.content: This was a unique experience, at least for me.So many amazing things:- being piloted around in such a small boat- going through caves on the water- being dropped off at beautiful temples (at one we saw perhaps the most amazing butterfly we've ever seen) and then picked up again- the general scenery and setting- being out in natureI think what was most clever for me was that despite the fact there were so many people, the fact each boat was small made it feel such a private experience. On our boat there was us and one other couple. We were lucky that they were friendly and considerate (by considerate I mean that despite the fact that they were in the front seats, first, we regularly swapped throughout the experience). We didn't have to queue for long at all- either to buy tickets or to actually get on the boats.An absolute must do in my opinion.

reviews.author: Anna Z
reviews.title: Trang An vs Halong Bay: pick Trang An
reviews.content: An honest review of someone who did both Halong and Trang An: Trang An/Ninh Binh experience is the best. You can scrape Halong.Advantage 1: shorter trip from Hanoi. If you leave at 7, at 9-9:30 you can already be on a boat - unlike with Halong tours, you leave at 7 and get to the boat at 12:15. Less time transferring and waiting. Advantage 2: not so crowded. At Halong, you queue at every attraction,  and spend the night with 20 other boats nearby. At Trang An, there is a constant flow of boats but it still feels peaceful and serene, no generators running at night, no soapy water dumped from boats, no waiting in line for 30 minutes to enter a cave. Advantage 3: extend your experience by staying in a countryside homestay. This is the best part - you can choose your adventure,  your accommodation and your food when you are on land. You can go on a bike or plunge into a pool or get a grab/cheap beer from a local store. When on boat, your options are limited and you have to stay with the tour.Overall, we found the Ninh Binh scenery very similar to Halong bay, except offering a better experience - as you are constantly moving through the mesmerising landscape in your personal boat - the Halong bay tours go for 2 hours, then stop, and then go back the next day...I wish we had spent more time in Ninh Binh and did not go to Halong bay overnight  cruise - Ninh Binh and Trang An are a better experience.

reviews.author: TRẦN SƠN
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: The landscape is wonderful and together with it the temples, temples, spiritual points in this place have created a place of nature with culture in harmony. World Cultural Heritage and Nature

reviews.author: Sightseer34284038841
reviews.title: Must do in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Got to the centre about 8:30am, no queues and picked boat tour 2. Length of tour was perfect, about 2 hours. We were lucky enough to see some monkeys and overall the trip was excellent. We alternated with another couple on the boat for the front position. Take water and sunscreen. Highly recommended this trip and go early .

reviews.author: Katie
reviews.title: Worthwhile but busy
reviews.content: Very busy- boats and life jackets everywhere but overall it was worth it to see the UNESCO heritage site. We took route 3 to see the 1000m cave which was awesome! Our rower was lovely and took photos of us on the boat. Each boat takes 4 people, so we were asked to join another Vietnamese couple. We agreed to switch front/ back seats for every stop which worked really well. Overall, the tour took us the full 3 hours. Make sure you bring lots of water and sunscreen as it gets very hot. Fans and UV reflective umbrellas would also be a great idea.

reviews.author: Daniel F
reviews.title: Beautiful boat tour in the karst rocks with caves and temples
reviews.content: There are three different tours to choose from. We chose Tour No. 2.The price is the same for all tours, it is300000 VND, card payment possible.After deciding on one of the three tours, you will be assigned a maximum of four on a rowing boat.The approximately 3 h tour (No. 2) led through several caves to various temple complexes. This means that you can get out of the boat at the temples and stay there (toilet facilities are available).I highly recommend the tour. The whole area is beautiful with the karst rocks and the lush plant life.I can also recommend the boat tour in Tam Coc (Tam Cốc - Bích Động), where the water runs through the middle of the rice fields, lined with the high and steep karst rocks.

reviews.author: Mai Mai
reviews.title: COLLECTOR TICKETS
reviews.content: Woman searching for MONV 839 STATE ticket scanned her ticket for someone else, leaving her crew waiting between 15:25 and 16:30 to check orange. Our team bought 6 onl tickets, which are 6 QR codes to scan, standing in the middle of our group, there were others, so the first friend asked to get back the bill for each person to scan one, but Dung's sister refused and said, "If you have 6 people right, please go through" to the turn of strangers who passed by, not only said that it was not a team member but she did not listen and let people pass, and as a result, our group was kept one person waiting for the check-in. It’s worth mentioning that for more than three years I’ve been in a service profession and never seen anyone whisper to a customer like you (even if it’s a customer’s fault) but this was your fault, which made our crew have to ask the driver for the fastest route possible and not stop at any spiritual point to catch up with the pre-booked 7pm ride back to HN. We went on March 10 for five days, but the heritage manager of Zhang An still bothered my friend with the desire to remove review 1* on google, though I lazyly wrote more reviews but the party called too much so I decided to rewrite my experience. The attitude of the staff on this side was really bad, even the first-timer management asked us to delete the review and there was no apologies kindly, I always said if my friend got another disturbing call to delete it, I would have another review 1 *, I'm not missing gmail :)))

reviews.author: Ria1104
reviews.title: Boating Through the Unesco World Heritage Site
reviews.content: Trang An complex is listed as a Unesco World Heritage Site and riding a boat is the best way to explore the place. The tickets would cost you around 250k per person for a 2.5 to 3 hour boat ride. If a person wants he can get tickets for a private boat as well. We got tickets for 2, so we had to share our boat with a family from China. We chose Route 3 option and passed 3 caves and few temples on our way. All the caves were breathtaking and the idea of passing through limestone caves on a boat was truly adventurous. The route 3 also happens to have the longest cave of 1km length, in Trang An and this cave had some amazing landscapes. We literally had to bend down properly to avoid our heads getting hit over here.  Other than the caves, the scenery around with the river water flowing, the huge limestone mountains standing at the banks, and little temples situated at the foothills created a magical atmosphere. We also saw the place where Kong: Skull island movie was shot. Basically, there were a few huts in the backdrop of the forest which were used as sets for the movie. We also got few stops to explore the temples where we got time to click nice photos. Overall we had a nice time. If in Nihn Bin, I would strongly recommend this boating experience in Trang An.

reviews.author: Luca Magnanensi
reviews.title: Spectacular
reviews.content: Those passing through Vietnam will hardly miss one of the boat tours in the rivers and canals and caves and undoubtedly those proposed at the site of Trang An are among the most popular. You will have to choose from 3 options, tours 1, 2 or 3, they all last about 2/3 hours more or less, we were told that the best tours were the 2 and 3 and we opted for the 2. Superlative views, you stop to visit several pagodas independently. Bring something for your butt because 3 hours on a bench is a lot

reviews.author: caroleen78
reviews.title: Amazing UNESCO Heritage Class
reviews.content: We arrived very late after a long bike ride from our hotel 15 kms We started the cruise at 3:30 pm The advantage c is that there are few people The scenery is just amazing and the temples Of all beauty The downside c is that it is getting cooler and the last temple was closed On the boats 4 people better be in front but frankly it is to do

reviews.author: Cowmiami
reviews.title: The Great Satisfaction Tour
reviews.content: The facilities are clean and I feel safe and secure. The tour continues with one staff member rowing a boat through beautiful scenery. It was a great satisfaction.

reviews.author: Timea B
reviews.title: Animal mistreat
reviews.content: Hey everyone, we have just visited Trang An. At Khong Temple we have seen 3 little kittens locked in a very small cage without any water, covered by a board. I have attached a photo.We have asked several people about the reason why they are kept like this. We do not think this is the right way, so we have reported this at the information desk, but we did not get any reassuring answer😔.Whoever goes there please check on the kittens.❤

reviews.author: Matthew C
reviews.title: Ruined by others
reviews.content: We were desperately unlucky. The Vietnamese couple we were paired with on our route decided to play loud music on their phones for the entire 3 hours, they put the umbrella up at the front of the boat completely blocking our view, refused to share sitting in the front and back of the boat with us and when I spoke to the boatman using google translate he said something to the couple, they laughed and nothing changed. This completely spoilt our trip, I would advise to either pay more to have a private boat or try to be paired with couples that appear to have genuine interest in seeing the scenery and sharing the experience with you,

reviews.author: Unikuorn
reviews.title: Worth the drive from Hanoi
