reviews.content: Really enjoyed this. Very scenic and we weren't bothered by any hawkers. Entrance tickets are bought on the left of the complex and you get on boats on the right near where you crossed the bridge.

reviews.title: Paradise.
reviews.content: If you're travelling alone you'll have to share a boat with another couple as they take 3-4 people per boat. The water was crystal clear and the scenery was absolutely stunning. 200,000 vnd for boat ticket (worth very penny). It's the kind of place where photos can't do it justice, you've got to see it with your own eyes.

reviews.author: MarSca
reviews.title: The best so far
reviews.content: Finally one really peaceful place without plastic... we really enjoyed the 2 hours on the boat! We took the tour number 2. Most of the other boats went in the other direction. We ended up on our own on the river. Really nice experience. So far the best

reviews.author: cebolzappa
reviews.title: Tranquil & Serene
reviews.content: I was here 2-3 years ago and it took my breath away so i booked a tour for mom and hubby who visited me on a business trip. They loved the place, it is so tranquil and serene. and now, they add additional timeline to the tour to visit the setting for Kong movie.

reviews.author: Nevena K
reviews.title: Beautiful Scenery, Boat Ride OK
reviews.content: The scenery is beautiful and it is 100% worth experiencing this in your life.  I was in awe through the whole trip.  Unfortunately, what can affect the trip significantly, is who you are on the boat with and/or who is around you.  We went around 2pm, and there was not a lot of tourists, with only about 5 boats choosing to go the "long" route 1 with the 9 caves.  So we thought this would be a great, peaceful experience.  We were a couple and we got seated in a boat with another visitor and her local guide, but they traveled in "tandem" with another group of people in the next boat.  They were loud, talked amongst each other the whole time, and made it extremely difficult to enjoy the peace.  They also almost opted out of stopping at one of the temples by "majority vote", which we did not appreciate as it was part of the trip and experience.  Third of a way in, at one of the stops, our fellow visitor and the local guide wanted to sit up front but instead of asking politely to switch (which is only fair and we would have gladly obliged) they made up this story of how the lady manning the boat said we should be in the second row because we may be to heavy and it is easier to row (my husband is 6'1 and 170lb and probably actually too skinny for his frame and I am an average size 5'8 at 150lbs, which is besides the point because there were way heavier or bigger men in those boats and it did not matter).  And worst of all, they implicated the poor lady who was working so hard to steer us around the grotto.  We, of course, called them out on this, and it made for an awkward rest of the trip!  I don't really know how to avoid this situation as it probably is somewhat out of anyone's control, but maybe in situations like this it is would have been nice to split the group traveling together into 3 & 3 and let them go in tandem (and let them be loud and have fun as they should since they are on vacation too), but allow others to fall back or go ahead and ride in their own peace and not just insist to fill boats to capacity.

reviews.author: Ashleigh R
reviews.title: AmaZing
reviews.content: We visited on a motorbike we rented from our hotel and had the best time. We heard this was more underrated and honestly were so glad to go because it wasn't too busy and the views were stunning. Our rower was friendly and took us to temples along the way. Didn't ask for a tip but we gave her one anyway! Two and a half hours going through caves and even helped paddle. Was such an enjoyable experience and so breath taking. Definitely go here if you can!

reviews.author: robstar101
reviews.title: Fantastic experience
reviews.content: After we did the ‘smaller’ peaceful Tam Coc boat trip we decided to also do this one after and it did not disappoint!This was our experience compared with the Tam Coc tour.Trang An-3 hours-Min 3-4 persons-Time to walk, discover temple, King Kong set-Bigger rocks, lower caves-Feedback form at end of trip-Police on boats, life jacket always on -Tip at the end was not asked but provided-Restaurant and shops aroundTam Coc-2 hours-No minimum persons-No walking-Vendors on boat, half way trying to sell stuff-No police, life jacket off after few minutes-Tip was asked-Small harbour, centre with everythingIf you can only do one, we recommend to do Trang An :-)

reviews.author: klmcc2000
reviews.title: A great boat trip with no hassle
reviews.content: We were boating for about 2 hours through incredible karst scenery and a bunch of caves. It was 200k per person and nobody sought additional "drinks/snacks for the rower".   the rower worked hard and also didn't seek a tip but was very nice. A pity she didn't speak English or French. A good tip was well deserved after the work put in.

reviews.author: Amy M
reviews.title: Amazing experience
reviews.content: Not as touristy as Tam Coc, Trang An offers amazing scenery and a rich history. The caves were very low as the water level was high after all the flooding so that was a bit scary but fine. There's lots to see and you can spend hours there if you have the time. The woman bringing us around was very pushy about a tip just to be warned.

reviews.author: David F
reviews.title: Don’t waste your money, seriously
reviews.content: I am taking nothing away from the scenery. Just amazing. However the trip itself was like a theme park. Swarms of people especially morning around 9am. Couldn’t enjoy the tranquility due to screaming and selfies galore. It’s was a like a scene from Godzilla with the amount of Asian tourists. Not to mention the bloke who must run the operations of who goes on each boat. Stood there with his megaphone, absolute A hole who tried to stop us going on a boat with just me and my partner even though when we purchased the ticket they said we could go in 2’s and have the boat privately to ourselves.All in all such a beautiful place ruined by it being an absolute people fest. Instead rent a scooter and drive around in peace and take in this gorgeous place.

reviews.author: Claudia F
reviews.title: Ruined by hundreds of tourists!
reviews.content: We arrived at the river just before 9am, unfortunately at the same time as around 10 bus loads of Asian tourists. Trying to get on the boats was a nightmare with everyone pushing in front of us with also the staff being very rude. We took off into the sea of bright orange life vests and waited in a queue to go through a few very low man made caves where you had to physically lie down to go through them. The scenery is beautiful but is just ruined by too many people going onto the river at once, all shouting and smoking (also throwing their cigarettes into the beautiful river). After reading the reviews I was expecting this trip to be a lot better than it was! Very disappointing.

reviews.author: Yannis L
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Totally beautiful!! There is 2 route you can chose from when u purchase the ticket (200,000 ĐồNg per route per pax). The 1st route where u get to see 9 caves ( but it was close when we are there as the water level was too high due to flood). The 2nd route is where King Kong film the movie, as well as u get to see 3caves. The view was stunning, the boatman will drop u at the temple where u can get down to get some photos and then  hop back the boat again. Overall it’s about 3hrs for the whole journey. Really highly recommended . Worth the visit

reviews.author: Phu N
reviews.title: WOW
reviews.content: Words cannot describe the spectacular view at Trang An. A lovely day on the little wooden boat through the river and caves. An additional tour site of where kong Skull island was film. Just relax and take in the breathtaking view of Trang an. Give the boat lady some tips 👍👍

reviews.author: Lily
reviews.title: A nice place
reviews.content: We were there on Tet holiday but it wasn't crowded.the boat trip through river took around 2.5 hours for round trip.Trang an itself was beautiful.Recommended !

reviews.author: Nery CS
reviews.title: MAKE SURE TO ASK WHO IS THE TOUR OPERATOR
reviews.content: DO NOT GO WITH JOY TOURS OPERATOR!!! EXTREMELY RUDE, ARROGANT TOUR GUIDE, HE PUSHED A 60yr OLD CUSTOMER AND WANTED TO FIGHT WITH ANOTHER CUSTOMER! KICKING PEOPLE PUT OF TH BUS!Trang an was an amazing experience but our trip there and back was a HELL because of the POOR service of JOY TOURS! People on the tour did not even know they were going with Joy Tours since the tours sellers don't provide you that information ASK WHO WILL BE THE TOUR OPERATOR they might tried to avoid to answer. ask again!People on the same tour paid different prices for the same thing! DISHONESTY! They sell you a buffet lunch : IT WAS TERRIBLE ABSOLUTELY BAD QUALITY FOOD.

reviews.author: MarLyn007
reviews.title: Trang an
reviews.content: Our family of 8 did that excursion because trang an is a unesco world heritage site. We were not disappointed; this excursion was so special that it will be one of the highlights of our trip to Vietnam. We will remember that excursion for years! This natural site is absolutely stunning!

reviews.author: Hang Ng
reviews.title: Just AMAZING!
reviews.content: just one word: AMAZING. You definitely have to come, bring with you a raincoat just in case! Ready for the breathless scene, put aside your camera, there is no camera better than your eyes.

reviews.author: ChristianTVC
reviews.title: Nature at its best
reviews.content: Lovely scenic nature attraction, river, lake, mountain and cave!Take a boat (sampan) ride, you will witness magnificent scenery along the way, school of ducks bathing, passing through 2 cave under a mountain where you may need to limbo or duck yourself through these caves. Whole journey go and back takes approx 1.5 hours, do apply sunblock if the sun gets too fierce on the day.I only took the boat ride, there are also some tourist taking kayaking and biking to mesmerize this small town.

reviews.author: Karen-Larry
reviews.title: Beautiful and peaceful
reviews.content: Beautiful scenery enjoyed from our boat which is paddled by the locally ladies. You will see along the shoreline are a number of temples, scenic tree covered mountains and paddle through a number of caves. It took 2 hours to paddle through all the connecting lakes and caves. The guys on our boat felt guilty being paddled around so helped with the rowing. In some of the cave you need to duck and watch your head. Out on the open water it is best to bring a hat or umbrella as it is very warm. Try to get on first so sitting in the front for better views.

reviews.author: kilipi91
reviews.title: Beautiful place in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: It takes 2 hours by bus from Hanoi to get there. We had six people in the group and on the boat. Really enjoyed the landscape with mountains, many grottoes...It is a perfect natural picture. I sure you will completely have a great time in Trang An. Do not hesitate, just get there and enjoy your time

reviews.author: Suzanne L
reviews.title: Boat trip - Trang An
reviews.content: Definitely worth to visit. Fantastic landscape. Beautiful mountain- hard working ladies. So peaceful. Not bad being out of peak season. Amazing going through the caves.

reviews.author: Era Maida
reviews.title: Wonderful Scenery and Great Boat Trip
reviews.content: In this family trip, we did not booking a tour but only renting a car and organised our own trip. It was a lot cheaper compare with my previous visit. We pay for $65 for renting 2 seater car and it can fit 7 people plus a driver. Giving the condition that we had 2 babies with us, then we only decided to visit Tam Coc and Trang An. The first stop was Tam Coc. Unfortunately, the weather was not good when we took the boat in tam coc as 10 minutes after the ride, it was raining so we decided to get back after the 1st cave. After getting lunch in the local restaurant we went to Trang An, it was great experience to visit this Kingkong skull Island shooting location and it managed professionally. I didn't hear any local women asking for tip money after I finish taking the bout tour around the location which is very different with Tam Coc.   The place and the water is clean and managed well.

reviews.author: Kaylee05
reviews.title: Magnificent boat trip
reviews.content: It's the first time I have ever take a boat trip in Trang An Grottoes. It's so amazing landscapes with much caves. I love the way people here tell many stories about this place with much proud. Want to come back here in May so I can admire the beautiful lotus along the way.

reviews.author: andrew-jerusalem
reviews.title: Spectacularly beautiful
reviews.content: We were in tam coc for 2.5 days but after looking at the recommendations, we decided to cycle to Trang An to do the boat ride rather than at Tam Coc. It's a comfortable cycle there (8kms via the small road that goes to Mua cave). The boat ride is very well organized and completely hassle free. No vendors etc. the ladies rowing were very nice and well deserving of a tip, which they didn't ask for. We got there before 10 so only started to get busy on the way back. And the scenery was stunning.....

reviews.author: junjin
reviews.title: beautiful scenery, relaxing 2.5hr boat ride
reviews.content: the beauty and serenity of this place is beyond words. many blogs recommended to visit this place in the morning before the tourist crowds from tour buses arrive. i hired a private car with guide and we reached here about 11am. thank fully, no crowds yet and i got to enjoy the boat ride in peace. the boat waited till it's full (4 passengers) before heading out. luckily my fellow passengers were 2 vietnamese girls who were chatty but not noisy. the water level was good so we can enter the caves. thou we had to sit on the boat bottom and bend down low at certain areas inside the cave. a the water level is too high, the boat won't be able to enter. popular place for wedding photo taking as the natural backdrop is amazing. when our boat ride was heading back, we met the many boats carrying the bus loads of afternoon tourists, some were singing, talking loudly, quite festive.nevertheless, a must visit while its still natural and unspoilt

reviews.author: rachie_xo
reviews.title: Magically couple of hours in the late afternoon :)
reviews.content: I decided to do Trang An over the more popular Tam Coc because of the reviews about the pushy boat rowers at Tam Coc... And I'm so glad I did! I took a motorbike from where I was staying which took about 15 minutes. I was a bit confused about the parking but eventually found it to the left of the car/coach parking, underneath a cover. Cost to park a motorbike is 15,000vnd which you pay when you leave. Entrance fee for the boat is 200,000vnd per person and boat will leave with 3 or 4 people. As I was on my own, there was already a couple waiting so I took a boat with them (so made a boat of 3 plus the rower). We left the dock about 3pm and for me this was a perfect time... the water wasn't too busy (as I assume the bus tours had left by then), it was a little hot to begin with (but I had a hat and umbrella for this) but as the 2.5 hour tour went on the heat subsided and the light towards the end was just magnificent! The rower lady was so sweet, I don't think she spoke a word of English which is fine, she just knew how to say "sit down" when we were in the grottoes (even though we were already "sitting down", she meant "lay down" I think). One thing I will say is make sure you are at the front of the boat! So walk on first and you will be at the front. I was sat behind the other couple in the boat and my view was mostly blocked, doesn't make for great pictures I'm afraid. But other than that it was magically and I really loved it! Oh yeah and the rower did not ask for a tip or try to sell us anything which was appreciated. I gave a tip of 50,000vnd as I assumed the other couple would tip too and I was on my own but unfortunately they didn't and I felt bad that she only got 50k from me (she definitely deserved more with all that rowing and she was so sweet!). All in all a wonderful couple of hours and I would do it again in a heartbeat!

reviews.author: Michèle H
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Wonderfull boattrip in a beautiful environment. Even in the rain it was lovely (and quiet 😀). We rowed trough 9 caves. Loved it!

reviews.author: Kate J
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: It was raining at the beginning but this didn't spoil the trip. It's beautiful. The lady rowing pointed everything out to us and made sure we ducked at the right times in the caves.

reviews.author: DiNg|photographer
reviews.title: Beautiful place.
reviews.content: You need to buy ticket with only 200k/person. You will spend 3 hours (section 1) and 2,5 hours (section 2 which is passed by the Kong film studio). On the boat you will visit the most wonderful place in Viet Nam with high mountain & river with very fresh air and even you can see the water plants and mosses. With the section 2 the boat man will drive you among the driver through 5 caves and stop you at 2 places: a Temple and the Kong studio. On the way you can ask him/her to stop you at any place you want to shoot a photos (don't forget to given tips for them as the appreciation).

reviews.author: Craig F
reviews.title: Not to be missed!
reviews.content: We decided to do 3 boat rides in Vietnam, Halong Bay, Tam Coc, and Trang An. While I loved them all, I think Trang An was the most picturesque. I recommend taking route 2.

reviews.author: Jakub H
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: Totally amazing 2 hours trip on boat in the nature. Staff is nice but they dont speak english so it's better to find out information before you go there.

reviews.author: ClaireBrianNZ
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.content: We did the boat ride on an incredibly hot and sunny day.  It was a great experience and really enjoyed all the amazing caves. Thought I might be a little claustrophobic but i was so glad for some shade and they were so awesome.  The scenery and caves are fantastic.  Only slight thing to know is that it is quite long 2-3 hrs sitting on little wooden seat in the sun.  TIP. take an umbrella for the sun, that really saved us.  They go with 4 people so we had to share which is no problem but it would have been much nicer view sitting at the front as our view ahead was slightly obscured. So if you can score the front two seats, go for it.  We did both this and Tam Coc boat ride. Both were nice and different but probably this one with more caves was the pick if you just had to do one.

reviews.author: Joe Peck
reviews.title: Better than Halong Bay
reviews.content: From Hanoi, we travel some 2-3 hours to trang An. What a beautiful & breathtaking mountains, lakes! To me, so much nicer than Halong Bay. Taking a small boat travelling on the water, seeing the beauty of the mountains by the water, passing thru caves etc. Can't stop taking photos & video during the whole ride on the boat. The movie - 'King Kong' was filmed there.  Go if you are Hanoi.

reviews.author: Timo T
reviews.title: Great experience - but come prepared
reviews.content: We decided last minute to squeeze this into our travel day. Traveling in a family of 4, we got a boat right away. They usually need to have 4 passengers before the boat can depart, so the couple that arrived before us had to wait for another couple to join them. There are 2 route options. Most foreigners choose option 2 because it includes the area where one of the King Kong movies was filmed. We choose option 1 which we were told is slightly longer and more interesting. It took us 3 hours in total.The boat ride starts off very relaxing. Passengers can help paddling (extra oars are on the boat). There are several stops on the tour, small temples with snack and souvenir stalls and a restaurant. The landscape is spectacular and surreal. One of my favorite parts were the actual grottoes. We didn't know what to expect, so when our boat captain told us to"lay down" we thought it was something lost in translation. We quickly realized that this was pretty solid advise. At the lowest parts, the space between the cave ceiling and the boat is maybe a meter/1 1/2 feet. It was pretty amazing, but watch your head.So if you are in the area, and don't suffer from extreme claustrophobia, I would consider this a must do. Don't expect to be alone. Even on slow days there is a constant flow of boats. Bring hats or even umbrellas - the sun can be relentless. And a flashlight - there are lightbulbs in the grottoes, but we had a flashlight and were able to enjoy the grottoes' formations a lot more.

reviews.author: Christabel B
reviews.title: Skip Ha Long bay and do this instead
reviews.content: For about US$10 you get an amazing tour that lasts at least two hours. All the amazing sights of Ha Long without the rip-off prices. It was touristy, of course, but the overwhelming majority were local Vietnamese tourists (because they're in the know about how to see the best sights for the best price, I think).

reviews.author: Lizzy L
reviews.title: Lovely afternoon excursion
reviews.content: We cycled to Trang An, it's a very easy ride. As there were just two of us we had to wait about 15 minutes for another visitor to join our boat. The journey is lovely, very scenic and peaceful. We stopped at a temple and then a strange 'island' which I later learnt was from a King Kong?  movie. The ladies rowing all the boats are really nice and friendly, not pushy like the rowers at Tam Coc. Overall, we really enjoyed our time here.

reviews.author: jenabaintheworld
reviews.title: definitely worth a boat ride!
reviews.content: We toured these caves and others in the area in a very relaxing boat--- highly recommended way to enjoy the mountains and overall scenery.

reviews.author: Rahul A
reviews.title: Trang An over Tam Coc any day!!
reviews.content: Our tour guides suggested to visit Trang An over Tam Coc and thank God we accepted his suggestion. The place is very beautiful and serene. We went this place before lunch and find less crowd over there and hence the trip was more good. The trip is around 10 kms with 8 caves in it. The caves are scary in a good way and enjoyed a lot when boat passes through them. The ride for the entire trip in the water was very nice and view was excellent. We didnt visited any of the temples and the skull island in between as our guide suggested they doesnt have much of the history and we were anyway going to the temple which was built in 1700s.Overall, a must visit place and it will take 6-7 hours of your time as ride to Trang an also takes 2-2.5 hour from Hanoi.

reviews.author: Kirsty W
reviews.title: Beautiful - A must do
reviews.content: We picked Trang An over tam coc as heard it was lest touristy. We got here early to avoid the masses and had a lovely morning meandering down the river through lots of caves. A few stops at a number of temples and you can do a walk one a mountain if you choose at  one of the stops. Suggested tip $100 dong Time 2 - 2.5 hours depending on how long you stop at each stop.

reviews.author: ZoellaBella
reviews.title: Spectacular views including a visit to Skull Island!
reviews.content: We did route 2 and couldn't have been happier. We started at around 10am and there were not many people so it was perfect.The boat took us into caves and through spectacular landscapes, easy to see why this is known as the 'inland Ha Long Bay'.The highlight of the 2.5 hour trip was visiting 'Skull Island' and the film set of the recent King Kong movie. The huts and the plane were there, and there were even local people dressed as the 'natives' (they were happy to be photographed with tourists for a small tip).Highly recommend this activity, much better than boating in the overcrowded Tam Coc river.

reviews.author: Cam C
reviews.title: Really good 2 hours
reviews.content: Went in a group of friends and had a great laugh. You get two routes to choose from, we would recommend route 2. You get on a rowing boat and a woman takes you around. Great scenery for pictures and videos. Water is lovely and clear which is always a bonus. The women didn't speak English but still managed to laugh at us which was nice. A nice chilled couple of hours with amazing views, whats more to want? Spoiler Alert: You get to go on the movie set of 2017 Kong, not too great, but something to tell the friends and family. They have little islands and temples that you stop off and walk around and then continue down-stream. Quite a few caves you go underneath and as you come out, views are just something else. We really enjoyed the trip and gave the woman a hand with the rowing.Gave her a good tip at the end. Definitely worth 200,000 dong each.

reviews.author: Alex V
reviews.title: A bit too long for a hot day
reviews.content: The scenery is impressive but it gets old after 1 hour on a boat under direct sun light. The 3 hours can become an ordeal, and besides some newly built temples and going through some caves on a boat, there is nothing else to see. Best is to see the scenery from above, from the top of a mountain. also, the 200.000 VND are a bit too much for what they offer.

reviews.author: DitaGenier
reviews.title: A quiet 3 hours
reviews.content: Our experience was great. We loved touring the river by unmotored boat rowed a SUPER STRONG local lady (we tipped her well because she def deserved it!!!). paid 200k VND per peson, 3 hours boat ride. We chose Route 1 without the Kong shooting location to avoid overcrowding. It wasnt a very busy Sunday, just enough amount of tourists so it was pretty calm. The grottoes passing was interesting.

reviews.author: jenngreglyon
reviews.title: Ruined
reviews.content: Stuck in a canoe with a family and baby who never stopped yelling at the top of their voices, so zero serenity appreciation. 200000d wasted. Also could do without cheesy fake "wigwam?" village complete with costumed extras wanting tips.

reviews.author: batto i
reviews.title: nice
reviews.content: Trang An is a beautiful sightseeing place and is set in small boats. Here I experienced a rowing boat with her boat. She drove her journey through the small cave to the temple. I just had to climb to Temple Tran not too far.

reviews.author: Pano R
reviews.title: Very busy with tourists
reviews.content: I love the scenery but it is too busy with people. Van Long is a better one as less crowded. The tour from the boat took us to different temples with different views. Tourists were so noisy spoiled the place.

reviews.author: JeansTangent
reviews.title: Not that nice if you have been to Halong Bay
reviews.content: Plenty of positive reviews made me decide to spend one day in Ninh Binh but it is quite disappointing if u have been in Halong Bay before. It has almost the same scenery as Halong in my opinion, except that u can't jump into the water since it is too shallow. U cn skip this trip if you have been in Halong.

reviews.author: Paula K
reviews.title: Great activity to do
reviews.content: We had good fun on this tour.  We were a group of four and rowed ourselves along most of the time to the relief of our lady rower as we were four comparatively large Australian/New Zealanders.  The scenery was fantastic and worthy of lots of photos.  Even a heavy downpour half way along didn't detract from the day.  Much prefer this place to Tam Coc as there was no silly games with trying to extract more money from us and so we were happy to tip our rower at the end.

reviews.author: Alexander K
reviews.title: Absolutely Worth it
reviews.content: Really nice caves and a stunning nature. If you give some money and show to row slower our boat woman did that. It costs 200.000 but you should do that.

reviews.author: DavidPurcell15
reviews.title: Awesome scenery
reviews.content: The scenery that you will see while undertaking a 2hr+ bamboo boat ride will be some of the best you will ever see. The caves that you glide through, some of which will have you almost flat on the boat are stunning!Although not compulsory, helping with the rowing is very appreciated by the little lady at the back as it is a hard task in the heat, so also ensure you give her a tip. A must see location.

reviews.author: MGCC88
reviews.title: Great experience, highly recommended
reviews.content: In our opinion, this trip was much nicer than halong bay. The views are really nice and it's very relaxing to go in the small boat. You need to be careful with the caves as when the water level is high you need to bend yourself a lot.

reviews.author: Kanaena
reviews.title: Really busy
reviews.content: Super busy,  you'll end up joining other people on the boat but if you end up worth locals you can learn from them. Vert cool a definite must see if you're in the area.

reviews.author: Flyer597278
reviews.title: Keep your head down
reviews.content: Over touristed and privately operated King Kong film set tour but the caves are interesting and lit with lamps. Keep your head down n don't rock the boat! Boat ladies expect tips not sure how much of the 200,000 dong per person fee they get so recommend you tip. Locals are dressed up as King Kong village actors on the island n happily let you take photos although I noticed domestic tourists tipped them when they posed beside them.

reviews.author: AJCHO27
reviews.title: Stunning views
reviews.content: I really enjoyed this boat ride. It was stunning going in and out through tiny caves. It is also very long and the man rowed tirelessly which was very impressive. However when it rained the man refused to take us back and continued to show us the views whilst we got drenched. This ended our time here on a sour note but I would recommend going.

reviews.author: Raymond W
reviews.title: Splendid Karst Scenery
reviews.content: Despite having been very sceptical about the whole rowboat-through-the-karst- pinnacles experience before we came here, we ended up enjoying it very much. With high water levels at the moment, we only got to see two caves and two temples, but that was really enough for us. It still amounted to two hours out in a rowboat. I wouldn't have wanted any longer in all honesty.The experience is extremely relaxing. You travel at a placid pace and there are ducks, dragonflies and even the odd mountain goat to look at. Best of all, however, is the splendid karst scenery, which towers above you on all sides. It gets a bit touristic in the "King Kong: Skull Island" section, with some kitschy movie set displays, but overall this is a very good way to see the karst scenery of the Ninh Binh area.I recommend a tip of 40,000 dong per person to the rower. She seemed pleased enough.

reviews.author: RogueSpy
reviews.title: Truly a great experience
reviews.content: Trang An grottoes was an amazing experience. We travelled by private car which costed 1.720K to pick us up at 8 am and we chose to do Trang An (24/07/17 Monday), when arriving at 10.30 we purchased 2 tickets costing 200k each, we were under impression that we can choose which route to choose. When going on the canoe ride sharing with other people there was no communication, she spoke to the couple infront us in Vietnamese. When going under the caves we had to duck down which she signalled for us to do. As we were approaching the shore she was asking for a tip, we were quite confused as there was no mention that only 2 of the 4/9 caves was opened due to heavy rainfall. She then started to poke me in the back 4 times with the paddle stick when rowing demanding a tip before ending. We were more than happy to tip for service I think she deserved 200K however the striking on my backside with the paddle stick was not on! I would understand why some travellers are reluctant to tip such behaviour. I ended up only giving 25K. The caves was memorable but service was atrocious.

reviews.author: perrinecoll
reviews.title: Tam coc or trang an
reviews.content: We went to tam coc following trip advisor advice between the two sites, but unfortunately trang an is very touristic and crowded. Plus, we had to pay 200VND for the tickets where they didn't even ask us the tour we wanted (4 or 9 caves), and we ended up visiting only 2 caves in a 2h tour as the rest was flooded, without anyone telling us as nobody speaks English. It was beautiful with mountains and Temples but no information given and too many tourists.Then we decided to try tam coc at around 4pm, which was very quiet and beautiful, where the 3 caves were open. It costs more or less the same price but is only 1h30 tour. We prefered Tan coc as we didn't feel ripped off, and the landscape was very nice too.

reviews.author: sinclairbgcj
reviews.title: Awesome Trang An
reviews.content: My family and I had a great time. There is no need to book a tour. We caught the train to Ninh Binh then a taxi to Trang Ăn. Then we went to Hoa Lưu and then Bài Đinh. We got back on the train for Hanoi after a huge day. Our taxi driver gave us time to complete each activity and returned to pick us up in time. At that time of the year we were the only non-Vietnamese visiting. I had a great time practising my Vietnamese yelling between boats. You don't have to know Vietnamese with Google Translate nowadays. Of course we tipped our rower well. I read comments about giving 40000 vnd tips and think what cheapskates these tourists are. I'm an Aussie so I don't usually tip. These girls (mostly) row you around for a couple of hours and you tip them $2. Cheapskates.

reviews.author: Gretchen F
reviews.title: I went back another day and did the second route, the BEST thing to see in Ninh Binh!
reviews.content: It is no wonder that this is a UNESCO site, it is stunning! I would highly recommend this to anyone, you won't be dissapointed!

reviews.author: Lenny H
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Two hours of being rowed through stunning scenery and caves with the option of either visiting a temple or Skull Island - the King Kong movie set.

reviews.author: nickyjamieson3
reviews.title: Beautiful, poor service
reviews.content: Beautiful scenery, sadly there was a major storm while we were out on the boat and the boats are not equipped with umbrellas or roofs so we got soaked!Similarly to the Tam Coc boat ride, expect incredibly braisen, greedy local people to scream at you for a tip.Beautiful location, shame about the locals who are involved in the tourism industry.

reviews.author: Katie W
reviews.title: 2.5-3hr tour through rivers, caved, lagoons
reviews.content: We enjoyed our boat tour. Just 3 of us in the boat, if you have a smaller party maybe they join you with others. We did route one, the other route goes to the King Kong Movie set tomorrow - it seems more popular. Beautiful scenery and rowing through the caves is fun.

reviews.author: LAC
reviews.title: Amazing views. Something you won't see unless you come here!
reviews.content: We took a boat out on the lake with a guide and viewed the scenery by boat. It was amazing. Apparently this is where they filmed King Kong 2. Regardless of that, going through caves where you have to duck your head and can admire the beautiful scenery was very surreal!

reviews.author: Melfish13
reviews.title: Nice boat trip with beautiful scenery.
reviews.content: The trip is lovely and the best thing we did in the ninh bin area, but it doesn't compare to other Vietnamese national parks. Worth doing if you're in the area. We tipped our rower 40,000 dong from the four of us. We would have tipped more, but we were very annoyed that she asked us for money. That's not how a tip works. The parking facility, toilet and surrounding restaurants are all very stressful, with people screaming at you to come to their restaurant from every direction.

reviews.author: Tina T
reviews.title: Beautiful, stunning, breathtaking!
reviews.content: If you love nature then this is for you. The beauty of this place was incredible, and the serenity of the boat trip was just lovely. Our visit in July seemed to be well-timed - it was very hot - but it didn't seem to be overly busy. The boat trip took about 2 and a half hours. Our 10 and 8 year old loved it (the views, temples, caves and picking up an oar to row when it took their fancy). Our rower had only a few words of English, but he was kind and caring, especially with our kids. We tipped him at the end - the energy he exerted in that heat was unbelievable!!!

reviews.author: hydrangeasandroses
reviews.title: Very scenic
reviews.content: Worth making the trip there. Took about 1.5 - 2 hours to get there from Old Quarter, Hanoi. We left super early so that we would reach there before the sun came out. We began the boat trip around 8.45am and it had just rained the night before so the weather was perfect. There are two routes to choose from. We followed the newer one (which brings you to the film set of King Kong 2) of which we found very interesting. There weren't too many boats when we were there so it is quite a good season to be visiting Trang An. We had a translator with us (booked via a Asia Eyes Travel agency in Hanoi) so she could translate the things that the rower could share with us which I found was indeed very informative.

reviews.author: cy185
reviews.title: Tranquil and scenic; best during low season
reviews.content: An interesting boat ride through various small caves. There are two routes you can choose from - one has 9 caves, the other has 4 caves + the remainder of the village set they used for shooting Kong: Skull Island. We chose the latter option, which may not have been a great idea since none of us in the group had seen the Skull Island movie. But if you keep your expectations low, it's fine. Don't imagine that it'll look completely like the movie - there's a lot of extra post-production work and on-set work that goes into making the final scenes, so never expect such things to look like they do in the movies (the same would go for other similar attractions around the world). They have locals dressed up as villagers at the Skull Island set and you can take pictures with them too. But I have to say it's not overly impressive. The boat ride itself and the caves and the scenery are really nice though! It's peaceful and quiet. It helps to have your own English-speaking guide with you, though. The rowers (mostly women) don't speak English, so if no one in your party speaks Vietnamese, you'll just be looking at scenery without being able to have any insights at all into the area.Apparently there are as many as two thousand boats available at Trang An, each one taking about 5 adults including the rower. At peak season, the place can be massively packed. So going in June was a good idea as it wasn't stuffed with people and there was no "traffic jam" on the river. I can't imagine the noise level if there were even 500 boats on the river at the same time... When we went, there were maybe about 50+ boats out at one time? I didn't really count but it certainly wasn't over a hundred. If you want high excitement and activity, this is not the place for you. But if you want to see the limestone hills and enjoy a pleasant boat ride through caves, this'll work!* We gave tips to the rowers at the end of our ride, just as a gesture of thanks.

reviews.author: norttraveller2005
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: I never thought to see someplace like this. Just amazing journey. Not long trip from honoi. You can also come with rental car.the weather was raining but you can buy plastic raincoat like 10,000 nvd. And bring umbrellaincase. In June it is always useful to use uvb and spf umbrella.

reviews.author: Fiach B
reviews.title: Best thing I've done in Vietnam.
reviews.content: Just simply incredible. The length of the journey was well worth the money, having the option to hop off at different points to explore was fantastic. The caves so low I was practically lying down was exciting. Our rower had the stamina of an olympian. We got extremely lucky and barely came across other people the whole journey. Just ourselves and the incredible landscape. Absolutely amazing experience and would do it again in a heartbeat. I could write so much more but this place has to be seen to be understood.

reviews.author: Nikiesha M
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: Worth the trip from Hanoi. It has a 11 cave network and is stunning. Takes 2-3 hours but it's worth it.

reviews.author: Buiduong
reviews.title: Trang An-Fantastic UNESCO Heritage site
reviews.content: It is famous for the complex of landscape, evergreen mountains, picturesque river and pagoda. We visited there 1 year ago and enjoyed very much. There are many things to see, to do and to eat. This place is also perfect choice for active family with children because of its various outdoor activities such as: hiking on mountain, biking or try to paddle the bamboo boat if want. It took us 3 hour from Hanoi city to Trang An.

reviews.author: LauraEvans88
reviews.title: Wonderful scenery
reviews.content: We're really pleased we chose to ride out to the Trang An caves. We took the boat just before 4pm, it was quiet on the water. The scenery is wonderful and the caves you go through make the journey exciting and interesting. Watch your head in some of those caves, they're low. We made a few stops along the way and helped to row for some of the trip. A lovely way to spend a few hours.

reviews.author: Thuy Le
reviews.title: Historical, beautiful place
reviews.content: I visited this place in the end of October when lotuses blossomed everywhere in Trang An, it's the most beautiful landscape I have seen.I love sitting on the boat, watching landscape, listening to ferry women sing and tell stories about Trang An.We visited many temples, places which were built from 1000 year ago, it's Vietnam spirit.You have to visit here in Ninh Binh

reviews.author: CHH-pretoria
reviews.title: Nice couple of hours being rowed around
reviews.content: Really relaxing couple of hours being rowed around - the 9 cave route had few visitors in June but was picturesque and very enjoyable. Remember the sun screen.

reviews.author: DenizM
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: We got on a boat for the tour that includes the Kong: Skull Island filming location. The landscape around is amazing.

reviews.author: lasshopper
reviews.title: A thrilling experience
reviews.content: Trang an is known for its scenic boat cave tours.It is far less crowded and less commercial than Halong bay.The experience was thrilling and beyond words.We rowed in and out of caves and at one point we emerged out of a mountain.The boat ride was for almost 2 hours and i lost count of the number of caves and valleys after a while.It started raining after sometime making it the most memorable experience of our trip.

reviews.author: YannNguyen0404
reviews.title: Nice view, most popular but always crowded
reviews.content: This is where people always heard when talking about Ninh Binh. The view is spectacular with a 3 hours boat ride with great experience.However, this is always crowded by tourist. Normally I would choose to go the Thung Nang pier instead of end up with the long queue here. Be careful for tourist trap here as always.

reviews.author: Jenni C
reviews.title: The boat lady was hilarious - King Kong, King Kong!
reviews.content: When we arrived in Ninh Binh we asked about whether we should visit trang An or Tam Coc and the locals all said that only westerners went to Tam Coc so we went with their advice and weren't disappointed. This is a fun activity, despite the obvious areas of development for tourism its abundant and stunningly natural setting soon take you in. There is a clearly signed ticket office. Its 200,000 dong each for tourists and 4 to a boat, tipping is expected and we tipped 50,000 dong for two of us and the rowing lady seemed happy, she had certainly earned it.

reviews.author: steve a
reviews.title: sunday morning on the river
reviews.content: Very relaxing 3 hours on a Sunday morning.  Rain forecast so not too busy.  It's not the cheapest thing to do and it's quite commercialized.  Having said that the passages through the caves are great and the environment is clean.  There are a couple of 20-30 minute stops in the 3 hours.  Rowers expect a tip.  We shared a 4-person boat with 2 locals and we each gave 50,000.

reviews.author: Cati S
reviews.title: Beautiful caves and landscape
reviews.content: The "pier" is approximately 15 km away from city center. You can go by yourself by scooter or car or book a privat motorbike driver. I booked a driver and paid 15$ for the hole day driving me around to different sights. I don't know if this is the cheapest price but renting a scooter per day costs you about 150.000 dong in low season. The Bootstour costs 200.000 dong and takes 2-3 hours. You have to wait till the boot is full (3-4 persons). You see beautiful hills, caves and amazing landscape... you can really say it's the "dry halong bay". Don't forget a hat and sunscreme. The boots are in a good condition. The woman didn't ask me for a tip, like other persons wrote it here.I would recommend it, especially when you want to calm down after a stressful day.

reviews.author: Phuong V
reviews.title: Beautiful scenery is lovely to visit ^^
reviews.content: For us this is so beautiful place to visit, the natural combination of river and mountains there is really fantastic.

reviews.author: Katherine S
reviews.title: Meh
reviews.content: Unless you have ample time, and the weather is cool, I would skip it.  I much preferred the Tam Coc boat ride.The first couple of grotto's were neat, but then it got boring.  While the ride was pretty, it wasn't the prettiest the area has to offer.

reviews.author: lauriel1988
reviews.title: Amazing tour
reviews.content: The boat trip was part of a day tour in the Ninh Binh area we took from Hanoi. We were lucky because although it looked a little busy when we got there, it seemed like all the other boats were doing a different tour, and we ended up completely alone on the river only 10 minutes after leaving. The scenery and the caves were incredible, it was a great experience. The tour was around 2 hours and we loved every minute of it.

reviews.author: Ha P
reviews.title: Such a tourist trap
reviews.content: We were recommended by the person at our hostel to do either the boat tour at Tam Coc or at Trang An. Since we are thinking of visiting all the sites in the Trang An area, we thought we would do the boat tour there which makes more sense. We had to park our motorbike outside. Then the entrance ticket for the tour is 200.000vnd per person. There were 2 of us so we had to wait for 2 more people to be willing to share the boat with us. No one in charge at the boat station was helping us since they were busy with other tour groups. We approached 1 guy and asked if he wanted to share the boat and he was happy to. The scenery was beautiful but all the temples and pagodas lacking a lot of information. It would be better if the rowers are trained with information so they can be the guide for the boat tour too. There was nothing special about the temples we visited during the boat ride. And personally, I think the Kong movie set was such a tourist trap. Nothing special about that either. The sun was very harsh so we spent literally 5 mins for every stops. Being from North America, I'm accustomed to tipping but I don't like when people ask directly for it. I think it could just be me but I felt very awkward. We did give her some tips at the end. But I wasn't very impressed with this boat tour maybe I had such high expectation for Ninh Binh. We ended up going back to our hostel and not visiting anymore temples or pagodas.

reviews.author: Mai Khoi
reviews.title: Definitely a MUST.
reviews.content: Not necessary to promote much abt this place, cuz this is the main reason that you came to Ninh Binh, right? :) Ticket for a boat trip is abt 8-10$, which takes you about 2 hours. The experience is amazing. Don't forget to charge your camera and action cam. In my opinion, this is even more beautiful than the well-known Ha Long Bay.

reviews.author: Alex W
reviews.title: It's a lovely enough boat trip, but can't shake away a sense of guilt
reviews.content: What actually happens is that a group of you get into a small boat and a local rower (man or woman) will row up and down the (Trang An?) river for 2 to 2.5 hours. With warm weather in May, you see them sweating. It seemed like a lot of work for 150,000 dong (US$14) which was what I was told they were paid by the boat station that sold us the boat-ride tickets.The route we had took us through nine grottoes. Since it had rained the previous days, the water level was high, which meant that the grotto ceilings were low. In almost every grotto, we had to duck so as to avoid knocking our heads against the rocks.It was interesting enough at the start, but by the sixth or seventh grotto, it was less so, and I began to wonder if we tourists were being exploitative of the local rowers.The river and valley were peaceful and the sky was generally cloudy (so sunburn wasn't a great concern), making for a pleasant afternoon.Our tour guide mentioned that the 4 or so passengers per boat should jointly cough up 100,000 dong as tip for the rower. We dutifully did so but it left me feeling a little scrooge-like. And after that, I learnt that the rowers don't do more than one trip per day (nor do they work everyday). That didn't add up to much income!There were a lot of boats at the boat station. But on the river, not too many. We certainly were amongst 3 - 4 other boats at any given time, so it wasn't a case of having the whole river to yourself, but if all the boats from the boat station had been put to use (which might be the case during high season) the river might resemble rush-hour on the highway.

reviews.author: Lara B
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Absolutely breathtaking and great little treck out. We saw where they filmed king Kong and another temple was lovely to see

reviews.author: Moreau P
reviews.title: Lovely day out
reviews.content: Trang An complex has recently recognised by Unesco as world heritage. We had a great boat trip sliding through hidden caves system. We loved the feeling being back to green nature and water. Do it

reviews.author: Sonata_ResortandSpa
reviews.title: Great caves and wonderful landscape
reviews.content: Wonderful landscape and i love the feeling of sitting on the boat and go around Trang An lake, go inside the caves

reviews.author: An C
reviews.title: Amazing!!!
reviews.content: Soooooooooooo beautiful!!! I was surprise about it!!!! Next time I will come back here with my family and friends.

reviews.author: Daphne P
reviews.title: Fun!!
reviews.content: Did a 2 hour tour! Tour guide was only Vietnamese speaking but it was beautiful- we went through many caves and the area and scenery was beautiful

reviews.author: Fearless641688
reviews.title: Gorgeous!
reviews.content: Tranquil, beautiful, and breathtaking.  A must visit for anyone visiting Ninh Binh.Views were spectacular,and although they spoke very little English? The boat staff were very friendly and polite.

reviews.author: lucymccain
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: I booked the private tour for my family and my friends' to Trang An with Novn Travel. Everything was perfect. View was really great. Boat trip and the rower were really nice. We had chance to see where King Kong was filmed. Highly recommend this trip

reviews.author: Amy C
reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.content: I thought trang an was extremely overun with tourists - I was wrong! There were probably about 10-15 boats out total, spread over the site. Our rower was lovely - she didn't speak English but was very friendly and keen to make sure we saw everything. The site itself is outstanding - beautiful! The price is good. We had a great day!

reviews.author: Federico G
reviews.title: Natural Highlight of Vietnam !
reviews.content: We arrived early around 7:45am after a night at Tam Coc village. No other tourists in sight ( Wednesday). Avoid weekends when it can get crowded with local tourists.Took a small boat with a local lady rower. She led us through 4 different grottoes and finally stopped at a village where we could use toilets. Then we walked on the trail to see the famous 'scene' from the 2017 King Kong movie known as Skull Island. The local villagers dress themselves up and will pose for a photo with you ( tip expected).We were all alone ! Not a single tourist in sight!And the views of the karstic mountains , green lush tropical forest , and all of the birds & the birdsong made this one of the most magic moments not only in Vietnam, but in my life!Wow! There are not enough words to express my feelings...

reviews.author: I_wander_asia
reviews.title: Overpriced for what it is
reviews.content: I chose the TrangAn boat ride over the Tam Coc boat ride because of the amazing reviews. I was disappointed because for 200,000 dong per person, I was really expecting something spectacular. It was too touristy for me and after paying so much for your ticket, you have to pay to go to the toilet. We passed nice scenery but I wasn't stunned by it. The view from the top is much better so I would recommend visiting the Mua Cave in Tam Coc. If you want to do an awesome boat ride, don't waste your money here, go to Halong Bay instead.

reviews.author: Jon the Scone
reviews.title: Cool place, if a little touristy. Don't forget the sun cream!
reviews.content: Visited as part of a Stray Tour. 5 of us in one boat, and we had a great time. The scenery is stunning; makes you feel very small as you glide through the cave tunnels and between enormous pillars of rocks and greenery.The pagodas you find are interesting, though given that they've all been restored they don't have that quaint feeling of a ruin that you've just discovered. We were told that on Vietnamese New Year the place gets packed!You can also find the island they used to film Kong: Skull Island, on which they've recreated a village manned by the extras from the movie. Nice way to employ some locals, but a bit naff if you haven't seen the film.TAKE SUN CREAM! And a hat. We burned after a morning on the water. Also be prepared to pay 2,000 dong to use the loos - but there isn't any soap (what a rip off!) Water is also a must. There are some places on the way you can stop to buy water, but easier to just take it with you and not worry.Also - don't forget appropriate clothing for the pagodas. Cover your sinful knees and shoulders!

reviews.author: juliana74
reviews.title: Alot closer than Ha Long Bay!
reviews.content: This isn't Ha Long Bay, but it's certainly close. You see the limestone karsts, but not on as expansive a scale as Ha Long Bay. Show up and pay for a boat ride which takes you through several caves. You see what the locals refer to as Ha Long bay "on land". The area used to be full of padi fields it seems, but it's not a preserved UNESCO heritage site. The only slightly bizarre thing about the boat ride is a stop at the movie set for Kong: Skull Island. Or what remains of it. It was bizarre only because they had local folk stand in the sun in "native island garb" (complete with hand made spears) by their huts for photo ops with tourists. Other than that, the area is beautiful and only about a 2 hour ride from Hanoi.

reviews.author: Nguyễn T
reviews.title: Superb Landscape in the North of Vietnam
reviews.content: You guys always heard of Ha Long bay but Trang An is my favorite. I think I like it more than Ha Long bay. And it's cheaper! You have to buy a ticket which costs 150.000vnd (nearly $7) to take a 3-hour tour in Trang An, but it's totally worth it! It's really easy to get to Trang An from Ha Noi. You can search for the information online. There are a lot of them. If I have to choose between Ha Long bay and Trang An, I rather skip Ha Long bay and go to Trang An!

reviews.author: AaronAikWeiJian
reviews.title: 2.5 hours rowing with beautiful scenery
reviews.content: Chose this boat ride over the Tam Coc one based on recommendations by the locals. 100,000VND entrance fee for adults which includes the boat ride. They will start rowing only when there is 4 people so if you are traveling in a smaller group, you have to wait. Boat ride at a good pace and very safe. Stops you at two locations, one of which is the filming of Skull - Kong Island. Those who would like to take a time lapse video, do it when you are about to enter the caves but be careful not to let your camera/go pro drop out of your boat.Only qualms were that the scenery gets a little repetitive to the end and that the rowing lady who we taught at the start was very friendly became a little moody despite us being friendly and tipping her at the end. It can be quite tiring for them to row 4-5 person on a boat so do help out if you can.

reviews.author: john a
reviews.title: A natural & cultural heritage.
reviews.content: We had great day in Trangan, scenery is so imposing and spectacular with hundred of mountains rising from middle of the field. The boat trip is wonderful and peaceful at all times since this is hand rowing boat, caves are amazing but at some of the caves we had to stoop in order to go through, the only thing I felt not so comfortable is the seat, It was too hard for nearly 3 hours.

reviews.author: Alviss P
reviews.title: Impressive view on a relaxing boat ride
reviews.content: I have not been to tamcoc, but from what I read from tamcoc, trang an sounded like a better place. There wasn't anybody trying to sell you stuff during your boat trip, and you get to row through amazing low rise caves. You can also get to train your paddling skills if you want to, with the makeshift paddles provided in the boats.

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: Incredible view
reviews.content: Super positive experience, despite the truly extreme heat and humidity. The climb has about 500 steps and at a certain point it splits toward two peaks: on one side Ngoa Long (Dragon Mountain), with the famous stone dragon on the ridge, on the other the peak with the pagoda.The views are incredible: from the top, a spectacular view opens up over the Ninh Binh river, surrounded by rice paddies, lotus fields, and karst mountains. It is absolutely worth the effort of the climb.An important piece of advice: be very careful if you want to reach the dragon. There were a lot of people in line on the ridge and in some spots the space to wait is narrow, precarious, and without real protection. In my opinion, it is not worth risking a fall just for a photo.Take your time, especially with the heat and humidity, and drink often: along the climb there are also small kiosks where you can stop.Tiring? Yes. But absolutely worth doing: one of the most beautiful views we have seen in Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Eline Mucha
reviews.title: Mua Cave
reviews.content: I loved the stunning mountains and the amazing view from the top. The climb is a little tiring, but definitely worth it for the scenery and photos.

reviews.author: jh0rnsey
reviews.title: Amazing views!
reviews.content: The highlight of this trip were the amazing views from the top of the 500 steep steps. You need to be fit to attempt this climb. Also you can walk on the walkways about the lotus flower fields.

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.content: A magnificent site that deserves 2 hours or even more of your time. Several points of interest are gathered in one place: several viewpoints with a panoramic view of the sumptuous surrounding landscapes, a temple at the very top (which I did not visit), caves, and several spots set up at the bottom of the mountain for photos. The entrance fee is set at 150,000 Dong, which is about $5.50, and it is well worth it.If, like us, you opt for a guided day trip from Hanoi, here is my advice:- Start directly with the climb, which is, I must admit, very physically demanding. The other photo spots at the bottom of the mountain can be done on the way back.- Once you reach halfway up the stairs, you will have the choice between turning right (toward the temple) or left. If you do not have enough time or do not have the energy to do both sides, it is better to turn left. That is where you will have a remarkable panorama of the valley with the river.- A platform is installed on the left side about a hundred steps from the summit. From this platform, you will already have a breathtaking 360-degree view. For our part, we therefore did not deem it necessary to reach the summit.

reviews.author: Kristian M
reviews.title: OK view. Not too demanding.
reviews.content: Not really demanding to go up the stairs. A bit warm at 13:00 but thats it. Took 10 minutes. Beautiful views but not as stunning as other reviews would suggest. The lotus Lake nearby is worth s visit.

reviews.author: mvanroy
reviews.title: Hard climb with a beautiful view as a reward!
reviews.content: Apart from the fact that there is a (very) small Tiger cave at the foot, the Mua caves are more a climb of 500 stairs to some beautiful viewpoints than caves. We started early (7am) to avoid the heat and the masses. We could park the bike in the parking lot at the entrance (5,000 vnd per bike). Buy a ticket (150,000 vnd pp) and then climb the stairs. Halfway you have a fork and you can either go to the dragon or to the small pagoda. Both give a beautiful view of the surroundings and each other. The steps themselves are not always easy because they are fairly irregular and high but there are some intermediate steps in the middle as an aid. The pagoda is easy to reach, the dragon requires some more climbing and scrambling (and is not for the little ones among us). In addition to this climb, there are some restaurants, some nice bonsais and a Lotus boardwalk at the complex.

reviews.author: SALA TAM COC HOTEL & SPA
reviews.title: Watch the dawn.
reviews.content: The dawn looks beautiful from above, but it needs to arrive early before 5am.

reviews.author: hazel
reviews.title: Very beautiful.
reviews.content: I am very impressed with the dance. The space is beautiful and the view from above is amazing. A place not to be missed when arriving in Safe.

reviews.author: TIẾN NAM Đ
reviews.title: Buy a cave
reviews.content: Another beautiful dance cave and walking 500 steps is also very tired

reviews.author: Janice L
reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.content: This moderately difficult hike is beautiful. I have osteo arthritis in my knees but was able to do it just fine. Take your time.  The views are spectacular. (I'm afraid of heights, so I took my photos below the dragon because it was a bit too scary for me). You'll get a workout and you'll lose a lot of sweaty fluid so bring a litre of water! Enjoy! YOLO!

reviews.author: Cheryl L
reviews.title: Get there before 8am - seriously.
reviews.content: Climbing Lying Dragon Mountain is an absolute must — but timing is everything. The steps are steep, the summit areas are small, and the photos are infinitely better without crowds in them. The gates open at 6am (really!), and if you arrive within the first couple of hours, you'll practically have the mountain to yourself. We got there at 7:30 and found it completely empty. Go then. You won't regret it.

reviews.author: theshoppers188052
reviews.title: calm and peaceful
reviews.content: nice organized, friendly people, calm and beautiful

reviews.author: bbrady962
reviews.title: Great views and a good workout too!
reviews.content: Great views and a great workout too so you need a reasonable level of fitness. We left around 4pm so by the time we reached close to the top, it was too crowded to get to the VERY top but we didn't care. We still got up high enough to see the classic view looking in to the steep valleys below. Maybe go earlier in the day if you want to get to the very top but for for us not essential. Defo worth walking around the small lake at the bottom to cool down

reviews.author: roberto p
reviews.title: Breathtaking view
reviews.content: We were in Ninh Binh in the day from Hanoi with Nyna travel guide who accompanied us in the visit of the north of Vietnam, to get to the dragon mountain you have to climb 500 steps carved into the rock that the higher you climb the higher they become, thank goodness that the weather accompanied us during the climbing was cloudy but as in all of Vietnam very humid .Nevertheless we managed to get up to the dragon overlooking the rice fields and the forest with the river flowing .the full ride takes about 1.30 h -2h taking it easy, under a park with fountains and statues and flowers of all kinds very, very nice....

reviews.author: Rosie Travel
reviews.title: Bad experiences
reviews.content: This season, it is very hot in Mua cave. Especially behaviour of venders near by cave, not friendly, very rude

reviews.author: Al M
reviews.title: Dangerous click bait - give it a miss
reviews.content: This is a manufactured click bait – visitors are supposed to see the second feature which is the shrine on top of the hill. The Dragon is a visual display which has been now adapted for tourists but there’s no structure in place – so when you get there, there’s no organised queue system– the walk around the dragon is extremely dangerous and slippery but no safety fence in place on the sides . The exit route is extremely difficult to access and so people , especially with children forced their way back down the difficult access of slipperyslippery rocks with sheer drops fit the only safety is a  bit of  rusty oil chain – there’s no official marshal around the dragon  queue  so people who don’t want to queue entered by the exit and then cause a blockage at the top – it’s an absolute disaster and a complete waste of time unless you go there very early very late -  this is probably the worst tourist trap  I’ve ever come across anywhere in the world .

reviews.author: Olivia M
reviews.title: Not for those with health issues
reviews.content: We attempted this climb in early afternoon and while the views are beautiful, do not attempt if you have health conditions like a heart problem or mobility issue. There are cafes before you go up and a some boardwalks around lotus flowers (which bloom in May). There is also one stall about half way up the mountain selling cold drinks.

reviews.author: Daniel F
reviews.title: Great views
reviews.content: The ascent to the Dragon is exhausting (easily doable), but it is worth it, the view is lovely.The facility below is large and beautifully designed. Especially the water lily field must be great, unfortunately the water lilies were harvested during my visit.Admission costs 100000 VND, tickets can be purchased until 6.00 p.m.The scooter can be parked at the end of the road (at the entrance/ticket office) for 10000 VND.You have to be careful not to get ripped off the scooter by the pushy sellers to park with them.

reviews.author: George Severin
reviews.title: Breathtaking views.
reviews.content: Mua Caves is a tourist attraction in the Tam Cac region.A very nice, well-kept complex with cafe, lotus ponds and many flowers. On a rock, the "Lying Mountain Dragon", there is a pagodaand you will be rewarded with a breathtaking view of the Ngo Dong River.The path up is tedious (about 500 steps). You actually need good fitness. Below are smaller ones but also the large cave (Mua Caves). Our visit was part of an organized day tour we took.

reviews.author: Mr9xx
reviews.title: Limestone Mou
reviews.content: Marvel at the stunning wave-like limestone mountain landscape. Climb the 500 steps for a rewarding panoramic view truly one of the top highlights to discove

reviews.author: Lohit V
reviews.title: Speechless with the views
reviews.content: I’ve been to Mua Cave and it was easily one of the highlights of my trip to Ninh Binh. The climb up the stone steps is a bit of a workout, but totally worth it once you reach the top.  The panoramic view over Tam Coc with the river, rice fields, and limestone mountains is absolutely stunning—especially around sunset. It does get quite hot and crowded, so I’d recommend going early morning or late afternoon.  A must-visit spot if you’re in Ninh Binh and don’t mind a bit of climbing!

reviews.author: 이름안알려줌ㅋ
reviews.title: Difficult but valuable experience
reviews.content: It's so rough, it's hard to go.The view from the top ends.

reviews.author: Anna T
reviews.title: Gain the top and widen your gaze
reviews.content: Taking advantage of a cloudy day, the greeting is tiring but pleasant. We climbed in 1 hour and a half making the two peaks, one with the dragon and one with the tower. There were many beautiful girls in costume with accompanying photographers, perhaps because it is Tet (Vietnamese New Year) week. Beautiful view, even if in February the colors of the different crops are missing, now at the beginning of growth or just planted. Walk ddu wooden walkways. Beautiful bonsai trees on display.

reviews.author: Ria1104
reviews.title: A Nice Hike Leading Up to a Dragon at the Top
reviews.content: When we first heard about the place, we thought it was some sort of cave. But in reality it was nothing like that. Mua Cave is actually a popular destination in Nihn Bin, where you can hike up a limestone mountain to get breathtaking views of the winding river, mountains and rice fields around. There is a dragon statue at the top and if you are comfortable to walk on sharp stones with a steep drop, you will enjoy a magnificent view of the Nihn Bin area.The climb can be tiring and it is advisable to wear proper shoes and exercise caution at the top near the dragon. The area at the bottom is beautifully decorated particularly the lotus field with the winding walkways. We can get cool Instagram shots in this place.

reviews.author: Sharla R
reviews.title: Scenic
reviews.content: Very scenic and beautiful ! I did have concerns  about a dog  that  was in a small cage right at the entrance just above the water ! Can someone tell me if this was a local persons pet ! He had a little water and no food . I fed him some crackers ! Can someone tell me if he is ok or if he belongs to a local person ?

reviews.author: Talant2007
reviews.title: Mua Caves
reviews.content: A tourist attraction.  The main part of it is the ascent up 500 steps to the top of the mountain, which offers panoramic views of the surrounding landscape.

reviews.author: Sandra L
reviews.title: Lovely.
reviews.content: We went first thing in the morning and it was a haven of peace. A boat trip without all the crowds that are after. We did tour C, much more nature and with fewer temples. It's beautiful though it's important to know it's 3 hours. It reminds a little of Ha Long Bay on dry land.

reviews.author: Luca Magnanensi
reviews.title: The most photographed panorama
reviews.content: A popular attraction in the area, the site offers several things including walkways over the lotus flower field, the Mua Cave the climb to the Mountain of the Lying Dragon with its famous staircase of about 500 steps. The curious thing is that despite being called Mua Cave (literally Mua cave), almost no one visits the cave and comes home having only made the climb to the mountain... absurd, but it is the 'power' of social media. There are also some very nice bars at European prices, a SPA, a resortEntry price 100k money them, about 3.5 euros

reviews.author: caroleen78
reviews.title: At the top of the steps
reviews.content: You must arrive early and climb the 489 steps to admire the view. This climb was built 15 years ago. I imagine the construction work. The steps are quite uneven and rather steep but frankly it is worth going to some trouble. I smiled because on the way it plagues in all languages on the difficulty of the course.Splendid view of the winding river and all the boats.I really advise you to take a boat to take this walk between the karst limestone rocks.We were led by a lovely lady And what’s special is that they all row with their feet She offered us on the return of the hand sewn paintings and frankly I found one very nice that I bought 7 euros Yes of course it is very touristy it builds a lot and soon it will have lost a lot of its authentic character but it is a world that moves and all we want to enjoy comfort

reviews.author: Michael W
reviews.title: Views rather than caves. (Well, one tiny cave). But for Dave’s, there are other cool places.
reviews.content: The steps were steep and there were a lot of them! The view was totally worth it. Go to the tail of the dragon only if you are sure footed, agile, and not disturbed by heights.

reviews.author: Designer NC
reviews.title: A fun day out
reviews.content: A fun experience, wear old trainers, I did it in January and would also reccomend wearing a hoody. There are lights in the caves which is helpful

reviews.author: Russell N
reviews.title: As long as you are not expecting caves you will not be disappointed.
reviews.content: Strange name for a place which is actually a fabulous viewpoint. The actual cave is more of an alcove but the walk to the top is worth it. At the fork in the path - go right for the pagoda or left for the dragon.On the approach road people will step out and try and scam you for parking - just swerve around them and keep going. There is parking inside the main gate (5k for a bicycle 10k for a moped). Also parking lot to the right of the main gates at the same price.

reviews.author: Karyne B
reviews.title: Attention bike and motorcycle parking
reviews.content: Watch out for fake parking! Locals force you to park well before entering the mua caves site! They force you in a very authoritarian and borderline threatening way to park at their house and ask you for money by bike or motorcycle. Do not stop even if they will be very threatening and make you understand with threatening gestures and looks that you do not have the right to go further! It’s completely wrong there is a parking lot just to the right of the entrance to visit the site. We were stopped by two Women who were even threatening because we didn’t want to stay and we took our motorcycle back to park at the entrance of the site we were forced to threaten them in turn to call the police if they didn’t return the money they asked us for when they were not allowed to do so.They finally gave it back to us but we understood that they were not happy and surely insulted us in Vietnamese.

reviews.author: Valter C
reviews.title: A climb worth the scenery.
reviews.content: Tiring climb of 500 steps to get to the dragon on top, but there is also the shorter option that leads to the small pagoda on the nearby hillock.Equip yourself with non-slip shoes if there is moisture or rain and even a windproof jacket, because at some point it begins to pull hard.

reviews.author: Enrica R
reviews.title: Visited in October with rain
reviews.content: I visited this place on a rainy day so I practically climbed the 500 high and slippery steps with enormous effort. From up there the view over the rice fields and the Ninh Binh valley is wonderful. Sore note that made me very angry was that you can not pay with the card and not having enough cash my husband could not go up with us. Too bad that in such a tourist place we still do not have the pos.

reviews.author: MM0980
reviews.title: Exhausting climb that is worthwhile
reviews.content: I went there by bike. Parking bike costs 5,000 VND. Admission costs 100,000 VND. The climb was exhausting and seemed like an eternity. I went first the way to the pagoda (15 min) and then the way to the lying dragon (15 min). You can also walk a bit to the starting point. From both viewpoints you have wonderful views of nature. At the lying dragon has been a single human casserole. Nice view. It was worth it.

reviews.author: Masela Fadjar Pratiwi
reviews.title: Must visit in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Hang Múa (Mua Caves) is an absolute must-visit in Ninh Binh! 🏞️✨ The hike up may be challenging with its 500 steps, but the breathtaking panoramic view at the top makes it all worth it. 🌄😍 From the peak, you get an incredible view of the Tam Coc valley, limestone karsts, and rice fields stretching as far as the eye can see.The atmosphere is peaceful, and the scenery is perfect for photos. 📸 Just be sure to wear comfortable shoes and bring water, especially on hot days! Highly recommended for nature lovers and adventure seekers. 🇻🇳⛰️

reviews.author: みるく
reviews.title: I was tired, but I climbed hard
reviews.content: It's called Mua Cave, so I thought it was a cave, but it was completely different. I just climb the stairs and head for the top. There are hundreds of steps, so it's best to avoid them if you're unsure of your legs. I managed to climb it while I was resting. The summit is ... fun to climb.

reviews.author: Marika
reviews.title: Poor dog at the entrance of Mua Cave
reviews.content: There is a poor dog chained in a cage close to the ticket counter of Mua Cave. When you go there please bring some water or appropriate food for the dog if you can. We felt very sorry today and tried to locate the owner to talk to him but couldn’t. The dog is right at the parking space at the waterfront. Given this is a tourist attraction we might be able to help this dog together. Many thanks

reviews.author: mrbrentharris
reviews.title: Absolutely stunning
reviews.content: The views from the top of the mountain are stunning. Depending on your fitness level, it can be a challenging hike, but I highly recommend going to the top if you can. Be patient as it can get very crowded

reviews.author: juliajg93
reviews.title: 520 steps for spectacular views
reviews.content: We visited this venue on our Ninh Binh day trip from Hanoi, this being our last stop of the day before returning to the city.It is worth noting that the famous stairs to climb the viewpoint were built just over 10 years ago as a tourist claim, without what you see at the top having a spiritual or historical value for the locals. However, the views of the Tam Coc River from the heights are beautiful and compensate for the hard climb on foot.To climb the 520 steps it takes around 15 minutes, while the descent is done in just under 10. Between the different levels there are benches to sit on and even a place to buy water (much needed!). Shortly before reaching the top there is a small viewpoint if you do not want to get to the top of everything, where the steps are increasingly irregular. There are a couple of drinking establishments with shaded areas and fans.Perhaps I would not consider it an essential, but if you are in the area, the time accompanies and you have energy, it is worth it.

reviews.author: Autogirogiringiro
reviews.title: So much effort for the ascent but what views! Not to be missed during your stay in Tam Coc
reviews.content: Noticed the day before during the boat trip on the river, we decided to visit this observation point the next day and it was actually worth it. An almost adrenaline-pumping experience for the slope of the steps (appears about 600) and for the overhangs. It is therefore not recommended for those who have problems with vertigo or those who cannot engage in a rather heavy physical commitment, considering also the heat. However, at some point of the climb there are pitches, one where there is also a bar. The views are really breathtaking at both vantage points and if visibility is good you will consume a lot of memory of your smartphone.
