Very nice also the starting village with numerous bars and probably even a hotel inside.

reviews.author: kesit0
reviews.title: Too hot in August after 10 AM
reviews.content: You can have trained and have worked out before, but with a  thermal sensation of +40° C, there are nicer things to do in town.

reviews.author: Explorer56807302709
reviews.title: Beautiful view!
reviews.content: Good workout! We set the alarm at 6am and drove there by scooter. No bother for pushy people telling you where to park.We saw 3 more goats on the path up. Was not crowded and beautiful view as reward after those 500 steps!

reviews.author: Willi S
reviews.content: The steep climb up Mua Cave was worth every step. From the top, we gazed at breathtaking karst landscapes stretching endlessly.@Go early :))

reviews.author: Adventure05703998509
reviews.title: Beautiful viewpoint and lotus field
reviews.content: The whole is made up of a photo area with cafes and a lotus field (very nice but invaded by Vietnamese for their photos but we have room to move), and a hill with 2 peaks so you can see both sides of the hill (the most interesting being the peak with the river, the highest). The highest peak ends on a not very landscaped area where one stands at dragon carving (if you have vertigo or bad shoes, avoid) which gives a very nice view.

reviews.author: absarita
reviews.title: Mua Cave
reviews.content: Amazing trekking session!!! Had the best lotus farm and it's very scenic Always carry a water bottle and keep hydrated.

reviews.author: Bondy Arachnid
reviews.title: Breathtaking View!
reviews.content: It was a challenging climb to the top of Mua Cave, but wow, the panoramic view was our reward. We felt like we were on top of the world, looking out over the stunning Ninh Binh landscape. A must-do for adventurous !

reviews.author: Rens33
reviews.title: Hot as, but fun!
reviews.content: We rode bicycles from Tam Coc- fairly easy commute. We arrived early and ignored the locals trying to get us to park, riding right to the gates to park there- fee 5k per bicycle.Entered the park to do the two climbs. Great views from either side of surrounding rivers and the lotus field.Although we were early- it was still very hot. Steps are high if you are not overly tall. Recommend decent footwear. We left the complex about 11am, the temp was rising and tour buses were arriving

reviews.author: lilybt
reviews.title: Small climb
reviews.content: Many tours from Hanoi combine Hoa Lu with a cruise on Tran An or Tam Coc, and few incorporate Mua Cave here. The stone steps are maintained, but the steps are volatile, which causes unexpected fatigue. There are two courses, one that branches off the summit course and the other that branches off halfway up the mountain, but the summit is difficult to control in the one hour given to the tour. In the final phase, people got stuck for photography, and the stone steps were narrow, so I gave up and went down to enjoy the view on the Tamcoc side.

reviews.author: Dominique P
reviews.title: To be done with caution
reviews.content: The views are magnificent both on the river that leads and on the water lily field.However, it is necessary to climb nearly 400 steps, all uneven, of variable heights and regularly too high and slippery.But if you go up, what a view. You have to choose the climb that goes to the left to see the River.

reviews.author: Rachel H
reviews.title: Stunning views and scenery, worth the sweaty climb up!
reviews.content: Prepare yourself for a sweaty tough climb! We are not the fittest but managed it in the heat of the afternoon with a few stops on the way and plenty of water. We were told the path to the left was trickier but with better views. There are more steps on this route but it it is only the last 10 or so that are not steps and are more of a scramble. However we weren’t fussed about being able to say we went to this bit as the the views would have been very similar and it was so crowded up there it would have been dangerous. The views from the top and the way up are stunning, just as you see in the guidebooks for Vietnam. On your way back to the car park there’s also some lovely walkways over the water and we caught some of the sunset which was very pretty. Definitely recommend making this trip when in Ninh Binh and can buy tickets at the entrance so no need to book ahead.

reviews.author: bine-ich
reviews.title: Well planned a 100% dreamlike experience
reviews.content: Sensational in the early morning when it is cooler and without crowds. I would only do it in dry weather for safety reasons and preferably at lotus flowering time. We were late May and it was hotter than hot, but that was the only downside. Good climbing shoes, sun protection and something to drink. And best to deposit dry extra clothes in the scooter, because after that our clothes were wet with sweat up to the underwear.

reviews.author: thomeson
reviews.title: A Breathtaking Summit Adventure with Dragon Mountain Views
reviews.content: Mua Cave in Ninh Binh was absolutely breathtaking! The 500-step climb to the summit was well worth it for the panoramic views of the rice fields and limestone mountains. Our guide was very helpful, and the dragon statue at the top made for fantastic photos. The cave itself was interesting, but the real highlight was the view from 'Dragon Mountain'. Make sure to go early morning to avoid the heat and crowds!

reviews.author: 1330marc
reviews.title: To do early in the morning
reviews.content: Beautiful. We went there at 6:30 in the morning and we were alone! The climb is not very difficult and there are risers for the highest steps. Beautiful views of the river and lotus fields. We also made the second sanctuary then the lotus fields. At 7am we only met two couples!Do not forget the mosquito spray!

reviews.author: Mike W
reviews.title: Lovely views
reviews.content: We cycled to Mua at 7am. We parked the tickets by the ticket booth and started the 500 plus step climb. It was already hot but there were few people around. The climb was tiring but you have the views to stop and admire. We took the left path to the dragon first and then the right to the lookout. The views are fabulous. A wonderful start to the day and a well earned breakfast.

reviews.author: Christine F
reviews.title: Great reward after strenuous climb
reviews.content: After the strenuous climb, you will be rewarded with a beautiful view over the region. If you come just in time of year when the water lily fields are blooming, it must be even more beautiful.  The stairs are still normal to walk at first, but are becoming increasingly irregular in height and depth. There are no railings, now and then you almost have to climb or shimmy along the edge. Taking a child with a child carrier on his back upwards was something we found very daring in others, as you can not walk upright at all, especially towards the end, in many places, but rather pull yourself up.

reviews.author: Mickey
reviews.title: BEWARE OF PARKING SCAM
reviews.content: As per other reviews, the motorcycle parking scam is still alive and well, operational thanks to a miserable male duo. The pair have been known to destroy bikes if you do not park in their unofficial space, but will more commonly grab bikes, pull riders off the bike, and even slash tires. The charming pair will charge unaware riders hundreds of thousands of VND to park.Being aware of this scam, we parked our bikes about 300m up the road and walked to the entrance. The actual sting is about 80m prior to the official entrance, where you can park your bike safely for 10k.I recommend parking further back along the road, before the Misery Men® to avoid conflict.Having said this the attraction itself is beautiful and well worth a visit!

reviews.author: afroditi18
reviews.title: Awesome views
reviews.content: A nice way to spend an hr and a half! Stairs are steep but not dangerous (if it's dry). Amazing view! Cave definitely underwhelming. 5000 vdn for bike parking; 100K entrance fee.

reviews.author: Kishor D
reviews.title: Amazing place
reviews.content: Amazing place and views with foot pedals on boats. Restaurants opposite the entrance. Go through 3 caves and ancient temples

reviews.author: corinne_prevost
reviews.title: WHAT TO DO ABSOLUTELY
reviews.content: A very nice place. Certainly bcp people but that is to be seen. For the steps it is difficult and we did not do the last 50 a little too dangerous for us. 66 and 75. Well, for my part, it took me two days to clear the pain in my thighs. Really the place is very beautiful and the view superb. We can walk in the lotuses which for us was not in bloom, not the period, and the route is interesting. Restaurants are not excessive and the ride is good.

reviews.author: akio9jp
reviews.title: It's tough in an hour.
reviews.content: It's not a cave, it's a climb. We climbed about 500 steep stone steps to the top of the mountain, Drangon, but with only an hour of free time on the tour, we decided to turn back about half way, considering our over 60th birthday health.Still, the observation space, located about 300 steps away, offered idyllic and beautiful views of rowdy boats floating in the Tamcoc River, steep cliffs and strange rocks.

reviews.author: Anne LM
reviews.title: Magnificent view, the climb is worth it
reviews.content: Very frequented place of tourists, climb quite difficult and dangerous. But the scenery is amazing once you get upstairs, it’s worth it and I find it a must when visiting the region. It allows you to take height and have a beautiful view of the terrestrial halong bay. At the feet you can also walk in the lotus fields (which you can see only when it is the season)

reviews.author: S&O
reviews.title: Definitely 486 steps up
reviews.content: This is a real highlight in the area. The two mountains with pagodas on the top should definitely be climbed. 486 steps to the dragon's tip. Then visit the cave during the descent.  Great bonsais on site and a huge walkable area with lotus plants. Top package.

reviews.author: Kay S
reviews.title: Tamoc & Mua Caves, Minh Binh tour with Cozy Vietnam
reviews.content: Although raining the views were amazing. I would highly recommend. But be aware of when you go as the weekends are crammed, as the locals visit aswell. The boat ride is good and the water is keep clean for once. Also beware trips with cycling as the bikes aren’t maintained, no brakes and one persons pedal fell off. The tour itself is a little disjointed but don’t let this put you off. The guides are great fun

reviews.author: Heather S
reviews.title: Amazing views from the top
reviews.content: Took so many photos!  The views are incredible but the steps seemed never ending!  I have to say that the steps are fairly low and not great big high things that you have to haul yourself up!  These were normal step level I think.  Once near the top, you can choose to to left or right.  We did both!  The right side goes to the small shrine and the left goes to the dragon which is not located on a path.  From the top you can just see the dragons head but people were rock climbing at their own risk to get to this dragon which was a dangerous feat and not to be done in my opinion!

reviews.author: Mork001
reviews.title: Crowded
reviews.content: You get to decide at the half way mark to go to the dragon or temple routes.So slow getting up and the last few metres are ridiculous.The views are brilliant and worth the effort.

reviews.author: Pier F
reviews.title: Don’t miss this gem in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Climbing the 500 steps rewarded us with breathtaking views of Ninh Binh’s karst landscapes—truly a couple’s dream. The adventure activities, from exploring hidden caves to cycling through lush rice fields, kept our hearts racing. Evenings were magical, with traditional cultural performances adding a touch of local charm.

reviews.author: Bel
reviews.title: Worth a visit for sure!
reviews.content: We loved it here…. Has a little village atmosphere about it. Although the 500 steps are steep… please note it requires a few breaks …. It is well worth the effort as the views are lovely. I was rewarded with the dragon at the top!

reviews.author: Nickola Barry
reviews.title: A breathtaking adventure for two!
reviews.content: Climbing the 500 steps to the top of Mua Cave was worth every effort! The panoramic views of Ninh Binh’s limestone karsts and rice fields were unforgettable. A romantic and adventurous spot for couples.

reviews.author: Bénédicte F
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: To be done early in the morning because less people. Be in good physical condition for the 500 steps and take water. Halfway you can buy some

reviews.author: Webster Lee
reviews.title: Ninh Binh's Natural Beauty
reviews.content: The stunning natural beauty left us in awe—the panoramic views from the top were simply breathtaking. The friendly local guides made our visit even more enjoyable, sharing fascinating stories and insights. The welcoming community added a special touch to our experience, making us feel at home. It was the perfect spot for a romantic adventure, and we can't wait to return. Highly recommend this magical place!

reviews.author: Alex
reviews.title: It's a nice view of the mountains. It's recommended to pick a good season and weather.
reviews.content: I saw a lot of reviews about lotus flowers and rice fields, but this season there are no lotus flowers, there is no rice in the rice fields, only a mountain climbing activity, it's a bit boring. The mountain is very good, some steps are high, it is very challenging to climb, the scenery is good, on the mountain you can also see people on the Sangu River on a boat tour, but the air is not good enough to see especially far, it is important to choose a good season and good weather!

reviews.author: Sirisha D
reviews.title: Hard but worth the climb
reviews.content: There are about 500 steps to reach the top. Left side peak is the highest one with the lying dragon on the top. There is no flat surface near the dragon for pictures and it’s risky with many people hanging around. Right side peak is lower one. It has the Instagram-able pagoda and the lotus pond top view. Best pics will be at the time of sunrise on a clear day.

reviews.author: Henry Jackson
reviews.title: Mua Caves is a great place
reviews.content: Mua Caves is a great place to visit with friends! The climb to the summit is challenging, but the panoramic view of the Ninh Bình valley is spectacular. Mountains and rivers look like natural paint. The atmosphere is quiet, perfect for relaxing and taking unforgettable photos. An experience not to be missed in Ninh Bình!

reviews.author: julc130
reviews.title: Mua Caves Parking Beware
reviews.content: Views were good. Stairs not so bad but very busy. Felt a little dangerous on the way down with all the impatient people hurrying to the bottom. Worth it though if you take your time. We were on pushbikes. When parking people try to stop you just keep riding. It’s a con. Don’t stop. We parked right near the gate and agreed 50k for 5 bicycles. They locked our bike and asked for more money when we came back down. Stand your ground and they unlocked for us. We however would not pay until we came back down which helped as no unlock, no money. Con artists but seemed inevitable. We couldn’t readily find any free marking but there may have been. For 50k it wasn’t worth a massive argument. Be warned.

reviews.author: Petitgiaco
reviews.title: A very nice point of view.
reviews.content: First of all go VERY early if you do not want to get into "traffic jams" on the way up. At the arrival breathtaking view but it is only if you do not have to take a ticket to wait until the "staggerers" have finished their shots with or without hat and their different poses, to take his own photo. It's become UNBEARABLE. I advise to go very early because it's really worth a look, I repeat but it doesn't quickly want a hell. It's up to you to judge according to your level of patience.

reviews.author: aimonetti b
reviews.title: A great panorama!!
reviews.content: A big and beautiful effort to make (500 steps not easy to climb) but a breathtaking 360° view. Nice reward

reviews.author: Davies A
reviews.title: Amazing panoramic view
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit on the top but 500 steps are no joke. If you book a tour, ask if they'll do the cave in the afternoon or not cuz around 4-5pm you'll see flock of birds flying back home! Also I hope they can do better with safety signs around. It's kinda dangerous if you go by yourself and got injured. Anyway, I'd still come back next time!

reviews.author: Anne H
reviews.title: Worth the climb !
reviews.content: Amazing views !   Steps were harder going down (for me anyway).    We started at 8.30am and it was perfect - less crowded and not as hot either.

reviews.author: Trina M
reviews.title: MOA CAVES
reviews.content: DID NINH BINH MOA CAVES (TAM COC) ITS A WORTHWHILE DAY, THEY TAKE YOU ON A SMALL BOAT. THE LADY ROWED WITH HER FEET, THE CAVES WERE REFRESHING. THE LADY PUT IT ON US FOR A TIP. WE ENJOYED THE TRIP BUT NOT THE DEMAND FOR A TIP

reviews.author: Nathalie M
reviews.title: The view from above gives chills
reviews.content: Rising to the top this fact!!! We will say that the view from above is worth the climb!!! I recommend!!! Have fun Go at your own pace

reviews.author: Horizon Hugo
reviews.title: Great 360 view !
reviews.content: This is a park where you have lotus fields , the hang mua cave , and also the lying dragon mountain. The view up there is incredible. Not very crowded in the morning , but I've heard that it's very crowded at sunset.

reviews.author: Staci B
reviews.title: Mind blowing beauty!
reviews.content: Unbelievable visit here. Don't rush. Climb the mountain-800 steps- bring water. Give yourself time to descend- enjoy the boat ride! Majestic area of the world not to be missed.

reviews.author: Sunil D
reviews.title: Mua caves visit
reviews.content: Great boat ride and the going through the small caves , ducking your heads to avoid the stalactites and traversing though a series of caves was the highlight of this trip .. a long boat ride around 2 hours though the maze of waterways ...great

reviews.author: JO M
reviews.title: Nice view the rest bof
reviews.content: It's nice but from the beginning we are put in the bath 400m before arriving at the entrance while we drive 2 ladies stand in the way to prevent us from passing and want us to go on foot (paying to leave our bikes in their garage), a few meters later it starts again with new people, and this until reaching the entrance. There we understand that in any case we will have to pay to be able to put our bikes on the side. Then the entrance is paid and gives access to a small park that leads to the steps. Given the present world and the non-maintenance of spaces, we wonder what the entrance fee is for. The view is great from above but if you want to go to the dragon you have to wait your turn to climb.

reviews.author: Alessandro
reviews.title: Very tiring and beautiful view
reviews.content: Assuming that there are about 460 damn steps and that the final part is composed of very dangerous sharp and pointed rocks, the view is very beautiful. The effort to get there is very great

reviews.author: Sue V
reviews.title: Not for the faint hearted
reviews.content: This was hard! Go early to beat the tours otherwise that makes it even harder. The views were spectacular and I was glad I did it. The last bit involved scrambling over the rocks at the very top and that was just too much for me (and I do like heights)

reviews.author: Jonathan Phan
reviews.title: Wonderful moments at Mua Caves
reviews.content: Visited Hang Múa cave on Friday morning. Enjoyed walking and taking photos, even with the heat and humidity. I'd rate the experience a solid 9 out of 10. Would definitely return.

reviews.author: Bngrivett
reviews.title: Go early or late
reviews.content: Crowded during the middle of the day probably negativity impacted on our visit.   Nice grounds and cafes.  Lotus garden next door was a nice surprise.   Wear solid shoes.

reviews.author: Abbie F
reviews.title: Parking not free
reviews.content: The views were incredible but there is not free parking here anymore. We went for sunset and drove straight up to the ticket office to be met with parking people slapping my bike telling me this is where I had to park and to pay 10k. I had read the reviews which instructed to ignore these people however they were not backing down. I ended up going up to the ticket office itself to ask if it's free parking to which they said no. It all felt very hostile and uncomfortable.So please take this into consideration before ignoring the parking people by the ticket office. Also the "scammers" before the actual parking were offering parking for 5k so it may be worth doing that in the future.

reviews.author: Cruiser13V
reviews.title: Wonderful day spent outside!
reviews.content: The location far beyond my expectations. Although there are a lot of pauses and a steep climb, the vistas are well worth the effort, especially in the Vietnamese heat. The entire area is worth visiting for a half-day as there is enough to do and see.

reviews.author: The_lone_rider
reviews.title: Steep steps but worth the view!
reviews.content: The place is set in between picturesque limestone mountains with a breathtaking view from the top of the stairs . The climb is 500 stairs and takes a while to cover given the steps are steep, there are however benches at points on the steps to help ease the journey.The view on top is a  snapshot of Ninh binh with a Vietnamese flag flying high and mighty in the wind.

reviews.author: Anja S
reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.content: Beautiful views, tough climb (+-500 steps) but definitely worth it. Safety could be improved by installing handrails.

reviews.author: Russ Lacuata
reviews.title: Panoramic View
reviews.content: The climb to the top of the twin peaks is exhausting, however, the reward is worth it. The scenic panoramic view of the landscape and rice fields is amazing. An unforgettable experience.

reviews.author: Devid P.
reviews.title: The dragon on the sky….
reviews.content: What a journey!! We arrived early morning and we climbed till the lying dragon… what a view, what a wonderful place. 500 uneven steps are a lot… but completely worth the climb. Thanks to the weather without sun, wasn’t too hard.

reviews.author: Sashila Mahendran
reviews.title: Mua Cave and Ninh Binh visit
reviews.content: Daughter enjoyed the expedition and scenic view from a top.Ninh Binh is truly magicalOur tour guide Jenny was very informative and took care of us

reviews.author: René P
reviews.title: The trip to the top is worth all the effort.
reviews.content: The stairs up to the dragon can be a challenge for many, and probably not suitable for people with difficulty walking.But once you stand on top of the dragon there is a fantastic view.If you have height anxiety, you should probably consider whether you want to foot right up next to the dragon.

reviews.author: Coyote-Travelerz
reviews.title: Hike and Enjoy the views
reviews.content: The journey climbing the mountain is the experience. The steps are well worn and steep, so wear comfortable footwear with a good grip. The sight can be very busy (lots of tours at once) so the earlier you can get there the fewer people you will find. Along the way and atop the mountain there are wonderful views of the surrounding valleys (even on a cloudy day).

reviews.author: Mac
reviews.title: Bds experience
reviews.content: Impossible to visit The Parking Award is at the head of the client Me solo in 2 wheels 20000 dong Two scooters with 4 girls 10000dong Look for the error Not very welcoming Especially as they sit and play cards without even looking at you

reviews.author: Martina S
reviews.title: Wowww experience
reviews.content: Wonderful place with amazing views. One of the most exciting views ever seen! The long effort to face the staircase is absolutely worth it!!

reviews.author: Ovy Q
reviews.title: Nice viewpoint
reviews.content: I visited a cave in the morning and the ticket price was around $4. The weather was good, with sunny skies making for an amazing view. However, as we climbed the mountain, the temperature rose, and we ended up getting hot and sweaty. I believe it would have been better to visit during a cooler season.

reviews.author: Antonia
reviews.title: Nice view
reviews.content: Nice view from the top, but the last few stairs are very uneven and difficult. There also is not a lot of shade to take a break in. The entrance fee is 100.000 VD. If you don't have the time to make it or are not fit enough, you won't miss out on anything spectacular.

reviews.author: Ros
reviews.title: Wonder of nature
reviews.content: The Mua Caves are a must for those visiting Vietnam.I fell in love with it.You have to climb 500 high and bumpy steps, but when you reach the top every effort is rewarded. The panorama below is magical and surreal and gives a great sense of peace.It is absolutely necessary to have comfortable shoes and water (and maybe even a kway!)Super recommended

reviews.author: Benjamin M
reviews.title: Parking Trouble !
reviews.content: Great view over the lotus paddies and river from all viewpoints. Some people tried to stop us on the way, telling us there was no parking, and we had to park there.  Don't fall for it.  There is a parking just at the ticket office.  Inside and outside they charge 10k extra now.

reviews.author: Mgh070
reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.content: The cave itself is not necessarily special. The surroundings are beautiful and the park neatly landscaped. Attraction is the lookout point. Five hundred steps up. Spicy in the heat but then you also have a very nice view.Worth a lot more money than Bufalo Cave!

reviews.author: PGMikk
reviews.title: Not a "should do" in a "hot day@
reviews.content: I arrived at Mua Cave at around 10am, at that time the sky was very clear and blue, the weather was beyond description for a perfect trip. But everything gradually turned into a nightmare when I started climbing up. We should choose to go to this place on a day with lower temperatures. As I climbed halfway up the mountain, it seemed like each step I took became heavier due to the sunlight shining down from above and the melting temperature bouncing back up from the rock below my feet, making it almost impossible to breathe. I had to rest many times even though it wasn't a very high mountain. My clothes were soaked. And believe me, if I hadn't brought electrolyte water that day, I probably would have spent the whole night camping at the summit and would have descended the mountain the next morning.If you are elderly or have a history of heart disease, it is not recommended to try. Especially on hot days.

reviews.author: Belith67
reviews.title: Best views of Vietnam
reviews.content: The experience in Ninh Binh has been amazing, from the climb to see the wonderful views of the river where we were then canoeed and the scenery we saw cycling throughout this area is very worth it, delighted with the experience! Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Francesca A
reviews.title: What a view
reviews.content: The stairs, the view, the place. This will be forever in our hearts As soon as you arrive it seems a bit of a fake/selfie place but when you start walking up the stairs and you reach the top that you understand you couldn't miss this place out

reviews.author: Huỳnh Tấn P
reviews.title: Amazing Ninh Binh experience
reviews.content: IThis trip was truly unforgettable and offered something for everyone. Highly recommend for everyone who wanna visit Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Hoàng H
reviews.title: Well-organized adventure
reviews.content: Without a doubt, this ranks as our best one-day trip yet, leaving us with cherished memories to last a lifetime. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Sue
reviews.title: Views and steps 😀
reviews.content: Steps steps and some more steps 😁You can do this - good footwear and a bottle of water . You have two choices either go left at the dragon side or go right with stunning views . I suggest right for medium fitness level as this is doable . Keep plenty of time on hand and do not rush . The view at top is all worth it . Went as a part of a guided tour to non bhin tam coc and mua  caves , I took a tour with “ local mint travel “ group  ( WhatsApp +84 94 925 96 75 ) who then connect with local guides and they were simply amazing . So if you up for some challenge with stunning views - go for it

reviews.author: EleonoraO75
reviews.title: Mua Caves
reviews.content: Definitely not to be missed! Of course it is very hot and the climb is tiring but the view from the top is absolutely worth it! Better to go early in the morning or late afternoon

reviews.author: Crumpled Nomad | Travel Intelligence
reviews.title: Breathtaking views
reviews.content: Awesome views surrounding the little hill that we climbed. One needs to buy ticket to enter the premises. The climb was pretty physical as the steps were very high. Need to rest along the way to ensure that we were alive when we got to the top. The views up there were simply breathtaking and I could assure you that the climb was definitely worth it. Of course, do make sure your physical condition is good before embarking on the climb. Alternatively, can always take breaks along the way as there were many break stops. Water is sold at certain points but the prices increased as it gets higher.

reviews.author: Jasmin
reviews.title: Be careful when coming down the steps!
reviews.content: It is indeed a beautiful place. The lotus garden was mesmerising. I’d suggest going quite early in the morning or later in the afternoon, when the sun is not yet blazing because it can really affect your experience. Going up to peak, you’d have to brace through steep steps. I’d suggest for those of you who are not too experienced with hiking/trekking, you might want to use a stick to help you keep your balance!

reviews.author: Lana Cooking Class (Tam Cốc - Ninh Bình)
reviews.title: Beautiful view point
reviews.content: It is amazing view point.the most famous tourist site in ninh binh you have to go.In june vs july,lotus lake is blooming flowers

reviews.author: Onas
reviews.title: Many steps
reviews.content: There is a long climb to the temple. If you have difficulty moving around, this is not a good idea. From above the structure is very simple. What's worth is enjoying the climb and the view from the top.

reviews.author: Darian P
reviews.title: Mua Caves - Parking
reviews.content: Great view! There are a LOT of steps, so bring plenty of water. Before getting to the caves/view points, there's a ton of vendors and many places to take a cute photo. It felt a little like an amusement park.I read a few reviews that said parking was free and included in your ticket. This was not my experience. The lady at the ticket booth said parking was not included. I was able to park my bike just outside the gate for 5000. There will be people that try to stop you way before the entrance. I recommend riding all the way to the entrance gate.

reviews.author: Mark T
reviews.title: Park INSIDE. $15k. Not a must, but visit if you are in the area.
reviews.content: Lots of stairs. Quite steep to the dragon lookout. I wouldn’t have been disappointed if I missed this, but since I was there, I’m happy to have completed the walk.Go early. Avoid the heat and crowds.Park your motorcycle inside the gate to the left AFTER THE TICKET BOOTH. Scams on the road coming in from locals blocking the street trying to get you to park at their place. Drive on by.

reviews.author: Jitka K
reviews.title: The only bad experience during the entire vacation
reviews.content: At the entrance to Mua Cave, about 200 m in front of the parking lot, several very arrogant women stand and catch bikers and cyclists. They will make you leave your motorbike in front of their house 15,000.Parking is also free

reviews.author: ボボ
reviews.title: A view worth the climb
reviews.content: You can reach the top by climbing 450 steps, but some of the steps are quite high, so it takes a lot of physical strength. You can also reach the other top by climbing about 300 steps, so if you have the physical strength, you can do both. The view overlooks the town of Ningping.

reviews.author: Chris318i
reviews.title: One of our highlights in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: The Mua Cave was one of our highlights in Ninh Binh. We climbed to the viewpoint in the evening hours to see the sunset. Of course there are a lot of tourists, but we still enjoyed the sunset and view a lot. Definitely a must-see in Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Chris H
reviews.title: Lovely geomorphology
reviews.content: Lovely experience. I think  route 3 is  the best because it goes through the long cave. Busy but that's expected. Cave was low but lights throughout.

reviews.author: Jacky Chen
reviews.title: Featureless
reviews.content: The entire landscape is mainly artificial and decorated, only the view at the top of the mountain looking down is beautiful. Most of them are Vietnamese guests and young people who come to take photos, with few foreign guests.

reviews.author: Meg H
reviews.title: Mau Caves Lookout
reviews.content: 5 starts BUT do not go if you have ANY health issues: mobility/weight/heart, this is a strenuous climb up, also do not try to climb onto Dragon at top, precarious at best!!! Awesome views. Go very first thing in morning or 2.30pm, less crowds. Do NOT park outside of gates, locals will literally stand in front of you to intimidate you to park elsewhere, say No! firmly.

reviews.author: Sophia
reviews.title: Incredible view
reviews.content: Very nice trip. You can hike to the two viewpoints for little money. 500 steps, but absolutely doable! Parking is available directly in front for 10,000 VND.

reviews.author: Neil Mos
reviews.title: Lovely viewpoint
reviews.content: As the other reviews have stated, watch out for all those charging to park. You don't need to park early so can drive right up to the entrance. Entry price was reasonable, we didn't visit the cave but the viewpoint was really amazing. Luckily wasn't too busy and is definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: romain b
reviews.title: Not worth the price + parking scam
reviews.content: Aggressive locals will pressure you heavily to get you to park at their place... we asked the park officials and they told us we needed to pay. The place itself wasn't great, we didn't think it was worth the price. I would recommend avoiding this place, there are much better things to do around

reviews.author: DotsGirl2
reviews.title: Lots of steep steps for a panoramic view
reviews.content: This complex has a rice paddy boardwalk, the cave which has a Buddha in it, another small cave with a tiger statue in it and then a 500 step climb up the side of the mountain. There are two different paths you can chose about three quarters up. The one on the left takes you highest. The steps at the very top are mainly just rocks. It is a beautiful view. We took our time and rested as needed but lots of young people were going up fairly quickly.

reviews.author: Angie H
reviews.title: Caves disappoint, but hike to views was awesome
reviews.content: It's deceiving to call this place Mua Caves as the highlight is the hike up the 500 steps to the viewpoints. Worth the visit for the views ... Make sure to wear proper footwear!

reviews.author: serene l
reviews.title: Mua Cave at Hang Mua village homestay
reviews.content: Magnificient view on Mua Cave overlooking the padi field and mountain view. We stayed in Hang Mua Village homestay in Ninh Binh with best location to all sightseeing point by bicycle.

reviews.author: Gigi C
reviews.title: Mua Caves the best scenery spot
reviews.content: SO COOL! The scenery is very magnificent, although I can't reach the top because of its long stairs. All in all, it's amazing!

reviews.author: LaNyonsaise
reviews.title: Worth a detour.
reviews.content: Added a visit here as we had spare time and we were passing close by. Five hundred steps sounds a lot but in cool weather and plenty of time it didn’t take too long. The steps are steep in places which made coming down worse than going up. We decided to stop at the viewing platform and didn’t climb the rest of the way because it was a grey and murky day so the views were very muted, not worth going higher to see nothing more.

reviews.author: Shannon
reviews.title: Needs some Garbage Control
reviews.content: The cave itself is great but not the main attraction here, the viewpoints are. Climbing difficulty is medium to hard as it's quite steep with narrow step runs. However the amount of littering is shocking, and I blame the tour organisers as they tend to recommend giving lots of water bottles to tourists. And due to exhaustion, tourists tend to throw bottles down the cliffside instead of the nearest bins. Recommend coming in spring as the lotus field below would look exceptional as during winter the fields are all bare. Remember not to litter when visiting!

reviews.author: HkkS
reviews.title: Worth a visit.
reviews.content: Love the hike, plenty of steps and steep especially near the top. Go early to escape crowds. Wear a good shoe and take water.

reviews.author: Dror S
reviews.title: Took our breath away!
reviews.content: Literally. No kidding.After the beauty of the cave we naturally climbed up to the peak view points, the dragon, and the top Pagoda.What a stunning way!What a view!What a perfect excercise for our legs!We sat there on the top, looking down over the valley - beautiful is a small word to describe it. Now add the sense of achievement for climbing the whole thing - and you get a perfect experience, worthy of a nice relaxing break of coconut water :)

reviews.author: roseann
reviews.title: amazing view
reviews.content: amazing place, when you go to the top. It is beautiful view and one of destination in Ninh Binh must to see

reviews.author: Mike B
reviews.title: Don't worry there is a beer stop
reviews.content: Yes Google maps is a bit out on this one, follow the tour buses if lost.. However we really enjoyed making it to the top. We are very unfit, but made it ok( it's trickier coming down, than going up). Not too many people the day we went. A small shop half way up for a beer stop. I don't think the caves exist, we couldn't find them. Really it's called Dragon Mountain.500 steps. If arriving on a motorbike, just pay the small parking fee.

reviews.author: Cheryl W
reviews.title: Busloads of tourists ticking off the supposed "must do"s.
reviews.content: The busloads and busloads of tourists is just horrible. We got to the bottom at about 4pm after some horrible pushy people trying to scam us into parking our bike before we got there. When we saw that we would be climbing bumper to bumper with SO MANY people we left. Generally our experience is that it's best to skip the tourist traps and explore the streets that go "nowhere" on  bikes. Maybe really early in the morning it's worth it.

reviews.author: mirkale9495
reviews.title: Yes!!!
reviews.content: Magical place, even though we had a cloudy day it was still beautiful to admire the whole Ninh Binh area from above.I recommend visiting the site early in the morning (around 7.30 am) during the rainy season, if you are lucky you can see a beautiful sunrise.

reviews.author: axl f
reviews.title: Unfortunately a little disappointed
reviews.content: We arrived at Mua Cave in the afternoon. As mentioned in a review, a uniformed wannabe policeman waits at the entrance and whistles at the tourists to park in his parking space to collect the fee. He was really very unfriendly. It's best to park further up and simply refuse and say that you're only picking up a friend or something similar.The climb is quite strenuous and the steps are sometimes very slippery, but doable if there aren't an estimated 10,000 tourists coming up and down towards you. Of course, everyone wants the best photo. The view is really great but it's almost impossible to take a decent photo because of the number of people.The kite at the high viewing point is unfortunately already damaged because everyone is climbing on it. It's best to come very early!Overall, I was a bit disappointed but a visit was part of it.

reviews.author: Mumma&Co
reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.content: Absolutely stunning & well worth the hike up dragon mountain! The view from the top is just incredible!! Go early in the day to beat the crowds.

reviews.author: TonyB
reviews.title: Come early for some nice views
reviews.content: Nice place to visit in Ninh Binh if you want to see some great views. Come early, there are a lot of people walking up the 500 quite steep steps already 10.30 in the morning.Motorbike parking cost at the area is 10k.

reviews.author: egwanderlust
reviews.title: Beautiful Views!
reviews.content: Mua Caves isn't about the cave at all. The star attraction is the views from the top. 500ish steps to the top are well worth a visit. The steps get steeper and more crumbly the closer to the top you get. If you have a fear of heights I would skip this attraction. On the ground, there are plenty of additional photo ops, vendors with drinks/snacks, and places to relax. The biggest downside is how crowded it gets during nice weather. One visit in a lifetime would be enough to experience the beauty.

reviews.author: Chi N
reviews.title: Great
reviews.content: Beautiful scenery, like a miniature Great Wall, super nice check-in, reasonable prices that don't rip off tourists, there is a service to rent costumes to take photos with the scenery here, friendly and cute people

reviews.author: DomCanada
reviews.title: Worth doing
reviews.content: The hike/steps are a bit hard (especially in the heat), but take the path to the left and you don't even have to go all the way to the top. The best view is of the Tam Coc river from one of the stops along the way. Totally wroth doing, though.

reviews.author: P J
reviews.title: Amazing Views.
reviews.content: Its not the easiest climb in the heat of the day but really worth it for the stunning views that you get from the top. Some of the steps are quite steep so be prepared and bring good footwear and a bottle of water.Tips: Good footwear, water, cycle here from Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Skram66
reviews.title: Different view at every resting spot, wonderfully staggering in many ways!
reviews.content: Easy to reach via moped or bicycle, able to park at one of the local cafes leading up to entrance for a nominal fee...keep your ticket as you have to show when retrieving your bike!! Didn't do the cave, but did climb to the Dragon & well worth it! Take some water & non slip footwear, as steps uneven & varying in depth. Plan to descend before dusk, as dark & uneven in places! Views obviously dependant on weather. Didn't do Tam Coc river cruise which you look down on from the Dragon, preferred to do the superb Trang An one instead.

reviews.author: Niklas Prins
reviews.title: Nice view, be careful when parking
reviews.content: The view is fantastic and the grounds are very well maintained. There are a lot of tourists here. The only problem is the parking. Don't park in the first parking lot you see on the road to the caves. A very aggressive man in uniform with a pipe is waiting there (the outfit is supposed to give an official impression). The guy is unbearable and parking is too expensive. Drive further ahead; parking isn't free there either, but the parking spaces are much closer to the entrance, cheaper and the guy mustn't be successful with his behavior.

reviews.author: zardoz07
reviews.title: A pleasant afternoon at Mua
reviews.content: We decided to walk in from Ninh Binh. About 7 ks. Google did warn 'real' ground conditions might be different to map so we walked down some narrow paths greeting locals in their yards and walking down flooded tracks with fish before us. No problems at Mua. Some paths were flooded and restaurants closed.  Everyone friendly and 500 steps of varying size to pagoda and dragon. Great views from both. A good experience. I am in my 70s but some fitness is required. Nice guy, whom some had difficulties with, organised a taxi for us for 150k back to Ninh Binh.  No tour needed.  Good day. Nothing but a good experience.

reviews.author: orrdin
reviews.title: Probably great except during a storm…
reviews.content: We got here in the middle of a massive storm. Needless to say the views were nonexistent and the climb to the top was very dangerous. When lightning exploded a stone pillar near the dragon I knew it wasn’t a great idea to go up. But definitely seemed worthwhile on a nice day.

reviews.author: Monie001
reviews.title: Hang Mua Viewpoint
reviews.content: Great views at the top. There are 2x main lookouts (dragon and pagoda) with smaller viewpoints on the way. Quite busy at the top as everyone is trying to get a selfie.We arrived at 5pm (park closes at 6pm) but we managed to get to the top in 25 minutes.The steps are quite a workout and are not just an average size step - quite steep. A little rocky and can be slippery in the wet. Watch out for restaurant owners/scammers trying to block your path on the road in the lead up to the entrance. They will blow whistles and tell you that you need to stop here, park your bike and pay for bicycle parking. You don’t do this until the end, just before the gates. There will be 2x ‘official’ gentlemen who will be very aggressive in ensuring you park and pay before you enter - 5,000 Dong per bike. Costs 100,000 Dong to get into the park.

reviews.author: Rosie Travel
reviews.title: Very bad emotion on a nice day in a beautiful place !
reviews.content: That should be a wonderful trip on a beautiful day! Thing was clean, green , on a light sunny day, no rain...But  I had a very very very very very very bad emotion with the gate conductor, while I was very polite, but he still tried to teach me how to life a polite life ? He  thought who he was? Then I lost all the good emotion about that place. They should remember: Customers paid for visiting fees to help that place make money !

reviews.author: Charlotte S
reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.content: Amazing views make the Mua Caves totally worth it but the climb is tough! This is fine if you are in okay health and don’t mind some exercise but do wear sneakers as the steps can be very slippery when rainy. The small path leading up to the dragon is very crowded and a bit dangerous so be careful!

reviews.author: Alokmili77
reviews.title: OK
reviews.content: Most ordinary boat experience its very lengthy tour to see Mua caves which is seen in lights only there are three similar caves & claimed King Kong movie was filmed but rowing boats by foot by ladies is tremendous job

reviews.author: Nicola F
reviews.title: Lovely view but so crowded . Not what I had envisaged.
reviews.content: This had been one of the main places I had wanted to visit since researching a holiday to Vietnam and watching various you tube/ drone videos which looked incredible. Our visit coincided with the Vietnam independence holiday at the start of September so it was always going to be crowded. We also struggled to do a 6am climb and it was so hot that the next option was a 6pm sunset trip. So, we knew we wouldn’t be alone, but we still weren’t prepared for the masses of tourists pouring in - at least hundreds, if not thousands, all trying to get that perfect selfie! We still had some incredible views, but in a strange way I preferred my you tube vision of the place. I’d still recommend visiting, but manage your expectations , especially if visiting at a peak time. A couple of practical considerations; We cycled from Tam Coc- fairly easy and scenic bike ride/ about 20 minutes and flat  ( but I am 50+ and unfit so still struggled a bit in the heat). We encountered the bogus “ you have to park here officials “ including a man in a fake uniform jumping out and blowing a whistle. To be honest , we found him fairly good natured and we’ve just muttered we were staying at the ecolodge ( not true- but this is the hotel which has parking for bikes right next to the entrance) and he laughed and backed off. I know froma few reviews that some people have had really bad encounters with people trying to get them to park, but this seems to be relatively rare. I really wouldn’t have minded paying him twice as much to park in his patch, but I was so knackered that parking as close to the entrance as possible was a priority for me. Given my poor level of fitness I had worried if I’d make the 500 + steps. It was actually slightly easier than I had feared, partly because the sun was going down, but also because I took it slow and steady, had loads of water with me, and I seemed motivated by the  ever increasing views with every step. I ended up going up both mountains ( so more than 600 steps) but this was by accident, and if you can only manage one, when you get to the main fork, head left. I went right first, and it was far too crowded to enjoy . The left fork gives you the classic views and although I pretty much got to the top, there was an additional queue to get on the dragon itself which seemed dangerous and unnecessary to me, although I can see the attraction if it had been quieter.If you go at a busy time, also be prepared for the Vietnamese couples going up for a photoshoot. It seems to be a common thing that the women will dress up to look gorgeous whilst their partners take photographs of them for prolonged periods at every best viewpoint. There’s even a shop at the bottom which hires out beautiful costumes whilst offering free hair and makeup! I was dripping with sweat, and as far from glamorous as you can imagine, but it was hard to find a gap in their photo shoots at times to get my sweaty selfies. Interesting cultural element to see though. I was worried we’d gone too late and would be descending in the dark/ this was parly true, but necessary to avoid the extreme heat and the worst of the crowds, and the path was partly lit when going down and seemed ok. It did mean cycling back in the dark though. Overall, if I hadn’t seen the amazing clips before I’d probably have loved it, but my trip was slightly less magical and overall I found I enjoyed the lower key attractions in Vietnam much more rewarding. Id say it’s definitely worth visiting if you’re in the Nihn Bihn area, but slightly surprisingly I didn’t find it one of the highlights of our trip, so don’t fret it you can’t fit it in, and watch the amazing drone shots instead!

reviews.author: Isabell8785
reviews.title: Sweaty but worth it
reviews.content: You will definitley break out in even more sweat climbing those steep stairs to reach the top of the laying dragon mountain - but the views are worth it!

reviews.author: Jessica P
reviews.title: Mia caves
reviews.content: A good route up to the top, over 400 steps so be prepared to either take it slow or wear appropriate footwear. The views are amazing and if you are lucky enough to see the lotus in bloom, I imagine it is even better. You can walk through the flowers at the bottom over the wooden bridges. The cave is also a good addition to walk through - this about 100m long and in water which was a welcome relief after climbing the steps on the hottest day of our trip!

reviews.author: Laura
reviews.title: worth seeing view
reviews.content: It took us about 15 minutes to climb the stairs. Proper footwear is definitely an advantage. The view from the top is really worth seeing. Even though it rained when we were there, it was worth it. However, it is full of tourists, which is unfortunately normal for such places.

reviews.author: cramac
reviews.title: Panorama
reviews.content: Even though I went there at 5:30 in the morning, the sweat was crazy. The problem is not the stairs but the humid and sultry heat. But once you reach the top the view is spectacular and repays the effort.

reviews.author: Johan S
reviews.title: If only one comment were to remain, summing up the others
reviews.content: What is true:- The view from the summit is splendid (especially around 5pm) if you choose the left-hand path to climb up.- The ridge that runs alongside the stone dragon statue is a real headache, with emptiness almost on either side and crowds of tourists inventing themselves as tightrope walkers and almost crashing into you for a minute of fame on their Tik-Tok profile.- Admission at 100KVND/pers.What isn't true: - The climb isn't all that complicated. Granted, it was hot in July and you're sweating by the time you reach the top, but don't think it's a cross. We reach the top in no more than 10 minutes, and the steps are fairly easy (except for tik-tokers with flip-flops).What's not said: - hornets at the summit make the length of your stay uncertain.How to get out of the oft-mentioned parking scam at the entrance; - either go by taxi/car and not by bike/scooter- … or accept the scam and realize that 10K VND instead of 5K VND is a few cents for you in the end on a journey that will probably cost you more in beers....

reviews.author: OneTrip with local
reviews.title: Amazing View from the top
reviews.content: This is one of the best things to do in Ninh Binh. Mua Cave is even more beautiful if you travel during the harvest season.

reviews.author: Julie A
reviews.title: It's not to be missed and worth every step!
reviews.content: This is an absolute must!  I'm in my 60's and thought the stairs might kill me but took it nice and slow and it wasn't really as hard as i thought  and was worth every step.  We went for sunrise and practically had the place to ourselves, It was breath taking and an absolute feast for the eyes! You don't need to book this with a tour operator.  Just get a grab or do as as we did  and go by scooter the views on the way are breath taking!

reviews.author: André K
reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.content: Absolutely stunning. This is worth the visit , the views are so beautiful. The 500 steps is worth it . I can highly recommend a visit to to this stunning place.

reviews.author: B K
reviews.title: Stunning Views, Strenuous Climb
reviews.content: Hang Mua We started climbing the mountain around 6.30 am as we were staying right there. Other tourists started climbing soon after, around 7 am.The stairs make for a tough climb. If the weather is hot as we had in our case, earliest possible time is highly recommended to avoid scorching sun as much possible.The stairs get rougher and tougher as we reach higher.Honestly we were so bogged down that we didn’t actually go the highest point. But we had stunning views from the higher landings. Fitness levels, good knees and legs are a prime requirement.Keep yourself stocked with water & a hand towel.On the way, we saw a closed shop offering drinks, water and ice creams with a few empty chairs, would probably open later.

reviews.author: campfamily50
reviews.title: Breathtaking views reward those who climb 1,000 steps
reviews.content: Fantastic views, 1,000 steps but worth the climb. We went at sunset and it was so beautiful, breathtaking. In the summer, even going at sunset it was a hot, sweaty, strenuous climb up those steps so I don’t recommend doing this in the heat of the day. But definitely go, you won’t regret it.

reviews.author: swexplorers2018
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: An outstanding experience even for 59+ age group. Be prepared to take it slowly, drink lots of water, have a hat, and enjoy the view as it's worth the climb to the top. Out guide encouraged us to rest along the way. View beautiful. A little trickier coming down but again, take your time.

reviews.author: ArvindSharma2014
reviews.title: Nice climb to.dragon mountain
reviews.content: This ia nice activity if you like walking and hiking. Views from dragon mountain are awesome, however, you need to climb 1000+ steps, please wear walking shoes and hydrate yourself.  It is very humid. Also,  lot of youngsters  comes for photoshot and  they take hours to get clicked in various poses. You have to ask to get one or two selfie. Dont wait ..

reviews.author: gregsf11
reviews.title: Not much more to say than has already been said
reviews.content: Not so bad as they say. 500 steps is doable. Views from the top are sublime. Just remember:Go really early to avoid the heat. The dragon is not exactly stable in parts, and the whole area around it is dodgy. Don't get into one of those "famous last selfie" compilations. And whatever they may scream at you, don't park your bike until you get inside the ticket gate. Why walk more than you have to?

reviews.author: TIT Adventure
reviews.title: Trang An boat trip and Mua viewpoint
reviews.content: a wonderful day trip from Hanoi to Hang Mua viewpoint & Trang An landscape with lovely team from Emirate organised by TÍT Adventure

reviews.author: Hetzel
reviews.title: Climbing up is the highlight
reviews.content: It was a great thing to do, is less challenging than I expected,,, the view from the top is actually so nice, I found it a bit confusing that the place is marketed as Mua Caves, however , in my personal experience, the caves aren't impressive, but the climb to the top of the mountain with the steps is a nice experience.I didn't do a tour, just went by cab with my friends. Use meter, don't accept price offer.Taxi driver will offer to wait for you to take you wherever else you are going. You can accept that, but again, with meter (meaning he will stop the meter when you arrive there, and restart it when you come back, is his choice to wait for you.I highly recommend to be there at 7 am as it just opens, temperature is nice and less exhausting, very little people...( only thing is that the little shops or stands are closed to buy drinks or so, but you are not missing out) much better barely any people...nice to go at your own pace and take pictures easily.If you have bad knees, or are very overweight, this is maybe not a good option to do.

reviews.author: Shelley M
reviews.title: What a view
reviews.content: We had a guide drop us here, so did not have to battle with the parking touts, which made our life easier.  Take your time hear and wear comfy shoes as the stairs are very steep and slippery in places.  Some steps are very high for little legs.  Its not a race to the top, stop and look around and enjoy the views, they are stunning.  May not be worth doing on a really overcast day as you wont see a great deal.  My family enjoyed this and you come to a fork in the path - left to the dragon and view of rowers in Tam Coc and we decided to do both.  There is a place to get a cold drink half way up which is really nice, they have a seat with a fan set up for the hot sticky days.  There is also places to get cold drinks and ice-cream at the bottom.  Be very careful with young children as not a lot of safety rails, but common sense applies.  Well worth the trip to the top, the views are stunning.

reviews.author: TheGrebes
reviews.title: Lovely climb and views ... Very persistent parking touts
reviews.content: Great experience. Stunning views, but a very steep climb. Relatively quiet when we were there but could be a bit dangerous if crowded as steps very steep and narrow in p!aces. A few people blocking parts of the climb getting their breath back quite awkward to safely manouver around.The parking scam is very evident and even knowing about it we still got caught out by an official looking guy in a u inform of some kind right at the entrance gate. The official parking (cycles and scooters) is inside the gate behind the ticket office. Just say NO loudly to all the touts that try to stop you on the road approaching the gate.

reviews.author: ctm7944
reviews.title: Hang Mua - Wow The Views!
reviews.content: Rode FREE bicycle from accommodations (Tam Coc Wonderland Bungalows). Arrived Hang Mua about 10AM (Open 6AM-7PM).Couldn't have picked a better day to have some morning sunshine. Yes, it is 500 steps. Some of the many stone steps are quite high. But, I enjoyed the challenge/exercise. Eventually you come to a fork in the road. The path to the Left goes up to the highest point (dragon). On this path is where you see the Tam Coc boats passing on the water below. This being the higher path, you can also get great photos of the Pagoda + the countryside.The Right side path leads to the Pagoda with nice views as well.Yes, the RICE fields are GREEN in April.And of course there were lots of tourists there; doing tourist things - just like me.Hang Mua entry is 100KVND. Bicycle parking 10VND.Previous TA reviews were helpful. Advised to ignore people waving me to parking. Some stand in the road and a few had on uniforms to appear as some type of official.Parked at the lot at the end of the road (on the right side), which is immediately before the ticket office.Took photos along the way to & from; people working the fields, buffalo and limestone formations etc. Very scenic!

reviews.author: mabellan
reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.content: Great views. I couldn’t see a good sunset as there was a bit misty but it was totally worth it. The mountain opposite was less crowded and had a few less steps but we decided to do Mua anyway. Best in mind that you need to get a ticket and it’s cash only

reviews.author: Jaroslav Nečas
reviews.title: Spectacular views
reviews.content: To see fantastic views you need to walk up several hundreds steep stairs but it's definitely worth it. There are 2 peaks, higher is more crowded lesser not so much. You probably would need to wait some time to get position for good photo.

reviews.author: Thuy
reviews.title: Hang Mua should be in favorite list if you travel to Ninh Binh
reviews.content: This is nice place to see almost of Tam Coc from the top. Also is natural place for travelers can take photos to save memories

reviews.author: Kelly B
reviews.title: Beautiful viewpoint, but be aware of aggression and scams
reviews.content: The viewpoint is stunning and well worth the short climb (15 mins if you are reasonably fit) but as other reviewers have said, it's important to know what to expect regarding the parking scams on the entrance road.I had several people jump in front of my bike trying to force me to stop before the entrance gate, a woman grabbed my arm as I cycled past her and tried to pull me off my bike, and eventually ended up with 5 men surrounding my bike, screaming at me and kicking my bike very aggressively while I was still sitting on it. As a woman on my own it was intimidating and I ended up parking in their area just to diffuse the situation as I was worried they were about to hit me. Even though I was expecting some of this behaviour (from reading other reviews), I was scared and quite shaken by how furious the men were and how unsafe they made me feel.  Don't let this put you off visiting the beautiful viewpoint - but be prepared for some aggression and go with a friend for extra safety if you can.

reviews.author: must_travel_soon_10
reviews.title: Majestic views are worth climbing the steps
reviews.content: There are approx. 500 steps and they lead to beautiful vistas of the surrounding areas with limestone peaks. We went mid afternoon and didn't encounter excessive crowds. The base area is also very scenic and beautiful. One of three must sees in Ninh Binh

reviews.author: Allison G
reviews.title: Beautiful viewpoint worth the stairs
reviews.content: Great view point worth the stairs. Very hot so bring water. There’s a scam with a man and woman with a whistle who will try to get you to park your scooter or bike and pay for parking (do not do this). Go straight to the ticket counter!

reviews.author: Madiyya
reviews.title: A place to escape the hustle and bustle of Hanoi
reviews.content: This hidden gem offers stunning views of the limestone mountains and rice fields, as well as a chance to explore the mysterious caves that lie beneath. You'll need to climb 500 steps to reach the top of the mountain, but trust me, it's worth it. The view from the peak is breathtaking, especially at sunset. You'll feel like you're in a fairy tale.

reviews.author: Romain H
reviews.title: Parking scam
reviews.content: Do not park outside it’s a scam! Park inside the gate (to the left side after the entrance)5000 VND for bike 10.000 VND for motorbike

reviews.author: Marta R
reviews.title: Worth every step!
reviews.content: We rode a scooter out in the morning. Had read earlier reviews about the parking scam but didn’t find it to be an issue this morning. There was a woman trying to wave us down, but we were able to ride past her easily.There are shops selling dresses on the street as you lead in. Wish I had taken a bit more notice as it’s traditional dress that you can wear up the steps and take some beautiful photos in. It’s only about 600,00 Duong for the dresses so if you want something extra special for your photo have a look at them. Definitely Instagram worthy. Yes there are about 1000 steps and everyone of them is worth it. Due to the beautiful nature you stop every 20-40 steps to take photos and take it all in so you don’t feel completely out of breath (a little sweaty depending on the temperature).The view at the top is magnificent and worth the effort. The dragon is not all that accessible but the view is still spectacular.

reviews.author: majorstu
reviews.title: Beautiful views - definitely a must do when in the area
reviews.content: Our family of 5 ( 2 adults, 3 kids - 14. 11, 8) biked from Tam Coc - a pretty steady flat ride.  Be prepared for the parking fee - a slightly irritating common feature in the area at most attractions, followed by your entrance fee.  I’ve read the parking hassle other reviewers had - we just bypassed the early offerings and parked right outside the entrance gate and paid up.  The caves were OK (nothing compared to those experienced on the Trang An boat tour), but the viewpoint makes it, with beautiful views across the lush rice paddies, waterways and towering limestone cliffs.  As in many places rubbish is a sad accompaniment as is poor maintenance, but  the view really showcases the beauty of the area.  If you’ve got reasonable fitness climbing the 500 steps takes about 15-20 minutes.

reviews.author: Leannie
reviews.title: Worth the steps
reviews.content: Came here as a family of four, and as we arrived by car we did not get any of the hassle described by previous reviewers arriving by car. Once you have paid and entered there are some nice viewing seats/swings with good views, as well as bathrooms which are fine if you bring your own toilet roll.  We started the climb to the viewing point about 4.30m, it was not too busy, we liked the fact that the stairs were very wide allowing two way traffic without it being too busy. I appreciated the many stop points on the way up for breath and taking photos. Didn't make it right to the top, but seeing as I was q hot mess by that point and have no intracranial account to add photos too that was just fine

reviews.author: Christelle Z
reviews.title: Agressive and violent people for parking in front
reviews.content: Very nice view but scam at the entrance on the price of parking.  2 people in fake police ask 10k VND to park motorbike/bicycle.  I refused to pay as I knew there was official parking inside.  One of the two people attacked me, he became violent and kicked my bike 3 times.  I also specify that they looked clearly in a state of intoxication, they were drinking in front of the entrance.  One of the two then wanted to hit me but the park staff intervened.  He then insulted me in Vietnamese and I ended up parking my bike in the official parking lot for 5k VND. On the other hand, no one came to help me afterwards to call the police, the park staff did not want to get involved because they were afraid of reprisals;  and when I finally found the number of the police they told me that they could not come and that I had to go to the station. Really a shame because the point of view is exceptional, but to fear for her safety in Vietnam (especially as a woman) - I pass my turn. Knowing economy relies on tourism, I don’t understand how the police doesn’t take care of this issue, it really stains my memory of Vietnam

reviews.author: Yann Renaud
reviews.title: Breathtaking sceneries
reviews.content: Definitely a place to visit when in the area. From Tam Coc, the place is easily accessible.on bike or motorbike. When arriving, many people try to stop you in order for you to park at their place. The further you can go with your bike/motorbike, is just before the gate before the ticket office. The parking.spot.costs between 10-15kD.The entrance costs 100kD/person, and it is absolutely worth it! You will have to climb around 500 uneven stairs, made of a slippery rock. At a given point you can turn left and reach the top, with the Dragon and a wonderful view over Tam Coc, or right and have another impressive view.

reviews.author: Davina M
reviews.title: READ THE ONE STAR REVIEWS- DANGEROUS! AVOID!
reviews.content: When driving up towards the entrance, locals literally stand in front of out motorbikes and forcefully tried to stop us to pay for parking. We kept swerving around them, as we knew that it was free parking through the gate. At the entrance to buy the tickets, there were two men, very aggressive, who stopped us and were screaming at us that we couldn't go through the gate to park and we had to pay them. Having been in South East Asia for a while we know not to get angry and were calmly saying to them we are going through the gate, it's free parking. They physically would not let us and the older man became so aggressive he got right in front of my face and appeared like he was ready to punch me in the face. My boyfriend got off his bike and walked through the gate to talk to the kiosk for tickets and for them to let us through. While this was happening, the same guy who I thought was going to hit me, grabbed a large metal chain and was swinging it at my boyfriends motorbike and looked like he intended to hit it and lock it up. I started yelling at him to back off, which he did before starting to get back in my face yelling. The ticket people didn't care and were super apathetic. We decided to leave, I didn't want to support people  who were so violent. Before you go here - read the one star reviews from 2019. There is a photo of the same bloke and other foreigners who did get hit, threatened with the chain and knives.

reviews.author: Elisabeth N
reviews.title: Taxing climb for the unfit, but the top is worth the sweat
reviews.content: Over 400 steps, some .5m high!!! This is not an easy climb. The stairs are all different levels, but plenty of place to rest along the way, and the view at the top is so worth the effort.

reviews.author: Alex H
reviews.title: A great viewpoint of Tam Coc river
reviews.content: Parking with your scooter costed us 15,000. Make sure you just drive right up to the entrance and don’t use the shop vendors earlier on, no matter how much they wave at you and walk in front of your scooter.There are two viewpoints to see, one with the pagoda and one with the dragon overlooking the river. Can be done with moderate fitness and well worth the hike to the top.

reviews.author: Bill B
reviews.title: Do if in the area
reviews.content: Mua caves has a very nice entrance area leading up to the stairs.  Do ignore the people trying to flag you down as you get close to the attraction.  We simply said "No" and veered around them and they didn't bother us.  We were charged 10k each to park our bikes just outside the entrance to the attraction.  The stairs are steep and uneven so should be attempted by relatively fit people.  Gorgeous view from the top.  I recommend this attraction if you're in the area.

reviews.author: Polly
reviews.title: The lying dragon mountain
reviews.content: We cycled to the Mua Caves from our local accommodation, it is 5 vnd parking per bike. The entry fee is 100 vnd and soo worth it. When you enter the complex it is beautiful with little decorative ponds, views and swings and restaurants. It is a short walk to the start of the lying dragon mountain steps (view point). There are 500 steps, although wide, it is quite a steep ascend to the top and quite uneven. It is perfectly do able with good footwear and water and shouldn’t take too long if you have a good fitness level. The views are next level beautiful, really breathtaking. You have a view across the mountains but also down to the river where you can see the boats pass! A very rewarding climb! We would recommend getting there early to best the sun and the crowds for a more leisurely time.

reviews.author: DGSmanila
reviews.title: great view + sunset
reviews.content: for older guys - 500 stairs are not so easy as you might think :-)the climb is nice and the view from top is rewarding.We finished the day there so the sunset view is beautiful.

reviews.author: fal3
reviews.title: Great views at the top
reviews.content: We went in December so we couldn’t enjoy the green rice field’s however the view was still nice but rather brown. The steps are a bit slippery are poorly maintained. Weird given you pay a decent amount to get in. Overall I would consider this a must do in the Ninh Binh area along with the Trang An boat tour. It’s the only place here that gives a high vantage point.

reviews.author: Rickiray
reviews.title: Amazing views and worth it
reviews.content: The hike up isnt to tough, i would say moderate fitness you will be fine. We went for sunrise on a sunny day and were not disappointed, spectacular. WARNING about the parking area if you come by scooter or bicycle. Vendors will try to get you to park in their spots. There is parking inside the gate but it is limited   So the vendors outside do provide a needed service. Unfortunately they are way over aggresive and some not all that honest. They charge 15000 dong for a scooter “it is 10000 inside the gate”. A couple gave buddy 150000 dong by mistake and soon realized it he and pretended not to know what they were taking about. A big argument but it was pointless he didnt give back any change. We were parked in his stall and the scooter was still there when we got back so thats a plus. A shame as you could tell his parking spot is taken care of, it is the one on the right just as you reach the gate. They will jump right out in front of you and yell to get you into their stall. Be aware and try not to be intimidated.

reviews.author: Chris
reviews.title: Go for the top!
reviews.content: Every step on those 500 stairs we’ll get you closer to magnificent views! A very good exercise I’d do every day. Go early to avoid the tours coming from Hanoi. Also do the little Peak too, so you’ll have a better view of the tallest one.

reviews.author: MatthewTheCoder
reviews.title: Mua caves - day trip
reviews.content: We visited this site as part of the Ninh Binh day tours which cover Hoa Lu, Trang An and Mua caves.Mua caves has to be highlight of the 3 sites as part of the Ninh Binh day tour package. There are about 500 steps to the top. There are 2 climbs, one climb will lead you to a small feature token pagoda (not one where it can house people). The other climb is to the Dragon. The Dragon climb has a statue of Goddess of Mercy in front of the dragon's head.Some of the stairs are quiet steep. The overall climb can be a bit strenuous physically and that we were instructed by the tour guide to be back in the bus after 40 mins did not help.There were many tourists in this site. It is impossible when we were there to take a photo without someone being it it. There was also a queue on the way up the top of the Dragon peak.If you are short of time, the Dragon climb is better one, it is higher and has more challenging steps.The 40min given to us by the tour guide was simply not enough. I would spend perhaps 2 hours for this site alone, to adequately cover both peaks, catch your breath and enjoy the scenery. Pros: High recommended for the physical activity and the view at the top of the climb.  One of the many reasons to visit Ninh Binh.Cons: Too many tourists. There is literally a human traffic jam on the way up the 2 peaks.

reviews.author: Long H
reviews.title: Amazing view from Mua Cave
reviews.content: Mua Cave is so amazing, we had a great time to enjoy the panoramic view of Ninh BInh. 500 steps to reach the peak of mountain, definitely worth visiting. In the next visit, we will travel in the lotus season, cant' wait

reviews.author: Lorna M
reviews.title: A TIP I WAS GLAD TO KNOW!
reviews.content: Great view definitely worth the trip altough the locals as you the road that leads down to it run out pretending/demanding you park your bikes and pay. They blow whistles to look official and almost stand in your way not letting you by but make sure you just say no and keep driving past them until you get right upto the entrance. No matter how much they insist keep going. And then do not pay more than 5/10 thousand to park your bike (motorbike) bicycles should be less, either inside the gates at the official place which is 10 or you can haggle the guys at the entrance to 5/10. I seen some people paying 300/500! Or if you don't want to pay at all park before you turn onto the road somewhere and walk 5/10 minutes down the road and in.

reviews.author: Jocelyn C
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: Our group of seven aged 13-60+ visited Hang Mua. We all climbed to the peak. The views were worth the 400+ steps with great photo opportunities. The grounds and surrounds are lovely. It was quiet the morning we visited.

reviews.author: 630ph_ngl
reviews.title: Not like advertising
reviews.content: I guess it's nice to see the view once you reach the top, but when I was there it was incredibly busy, making the hike unpleasant. Also, the ride to this place is a complete tourist trap. When driving towards the ticket booth, locals will jump in front of your bike stating aggressively that you need to buy a parket ticket.. I'd advice people to keep on driving towards the ticket booth, as parking should be free there I believe, one more thing is not fair here is you have to pay for any time using toilet, not pleasant at all

reviews.author: hm777
reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.content: Did not visit the caves, but visited Hang Mua peak, which provided beautiful views over the town landscape one side, and into a valley on the other side. The walk from the car park was full of interesting photo points, such as views over a lotus lake, swings, heart-shaped-vine structures, and statues you could sit on and pose with. There were lots of places to buy food and water and eat, and even water stops halfway up the mountain. To get to the mountain, you take the right fork at the path through the resort area. There are 2 peaks, and halfway up the mountain, you choose a path. Take the left fork to visit the tallest peak, with a dragon statue, or the right fork to visit a padoga on a narrow rocky outcrop. From the dragon peak, you can look over the pagoda peak, so if you don't have the energy for both, I'd recommend taking the left fork for the dragon. Note that there will likely be people climbing all over the rocks around the dragon statue!

reviews.author: Gabi C
reviews.title: Not a cave but excellent lookout point
reviews.content: You have to climb up steps to get to a couple of different lookout platforms, views are stunning! You can look over Ninh Binh or over the Tam Coc river ride and rice paddies.
