The old pagoda with around 250 stone stairs to climb will give you an amazing view of the place. Walka bit further inside, you will find an old gate of an ancient palace. The big lake with fresh green water which you can see the fish and the weeds. You will have many best photos in this place.

reviews.author: Big Asian Choice
reviews.title: Beautiful Place for A Short Visit
reviews.content: Tuyet Tinh Coc is a cave with a shrine inside, in Ninh Binh province, near to Mua Caves. Outside of this cave, there is a lake between the valley of limestone hills. To get there, one must walk through a short tunnel through the hill. There are steps to walk up to the cave. Outside the cave, there is a lookout to view the valley from high elevation. There are also walkway around the lake. The place was clean and had no crowd during my visit, might be because it did not coincide with large tour group visiting the place. There were several stalls on the way in and inside the location as well. May be worthwhile to drop by if travelling around the area.

reviews.author: Adrienne A
reviews.title: Beautiful quick stop
reviews.content: The cave is gorgeous, not to be missed. We had the whole place to ourselves the morning we went. We spent about an hour here. Easy to navigate, no need for a guide.

reviews.author: Minh T
reviews.title: Amazing place to see on lonely planet
reviews.content: It was so nice place to visit one time in your life. There was so green lake in the middle of the mountainous valley. After taking pictures of the beautiful lake, we climb up to see Am Tien cave and pagoda, Then take overview pictures of the lake. I saw there were many couples who took wedding picture there. It was so romantic place for couples

reviews.author: Tom V
reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.content: We went on the boat tour around the caves and the shooting of the king kong movie. The sight was absolutely amazing. Recommend this activity for anyone. Bring waterproof clothing and don't bring anything you do not want to get wet.

reviews.author: Minh T
reviews.title: So so
reviews.content: The entrance fee is 20,000 per person and motorbike parking fee is 10,000.You will experience 205 limestone steps to reach the Am Tien Temple but the trekking is not hard like Mua Cave (Hang Mua). The cave is small and has some altars.There is a large lake in front of the cave gate, folk called Ao League. The water is green and it’s a good place to see sunset.The last point of the lake is a gate. It is constructed like the model of ancient gate. Not many people know this place.

reviews.author: LuongParadise
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: I must to say it's nothing speacial. But the view is beautiful. For someone who like to selfie it would be a nice place.

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: Too many people
reviews.content: Hoa Lư Ancient Capital is certainly an interesting place from a historical point of view and is worth a visit if you are in Ninh Binh. Unfortunately, however, our experience was strongly affected by the huge number of people present.There are so many organized groups, practically all with their own guide in tow, and at times it even becomes difficult to move in the spaces and get close to the temples. The amount of people is truly impressive and, in my opinion, makes you lose almost completely the charm of the place.It is a shame especially because some of the buildings are places of worship, but with hundreds of people entering and exiting continuously, guides talking and groups crowding, it is very difficult to perceive any atmosphere of contemplation or religiosity.To this are added numerous vendors who try to offer practically everything and who, in some cases, we found rather insistent.In conclusion, Hoa Lư is certainly interesting and important for understanding the history of Vietnam, but mass tourism has reached such a level as to seriously compromise the visiting experience. Probably, by managing to arrive very early or at a less crowded time, the feeling would be completely different.

reviews.author: PavalikaV
reviews.title: Past Glory
reviews.content: One can give a pass. Nothing spectacular, but for the large complex, though fairly neatly maintained. Indeed if one is TamCoc area, better option would be to do the circuit of Trang An boat ride, then the Bai Dinh Pagoda, Hao Lu Ancient Capital or just take rest in the afternoon; head up to Hao Lu Old Town, which is very similar to Hoi An in its environment.

reviews.author: Mr9xx
reviews.title: Hoa Lu
reviews.content: The site features two main temples dedicated to King Le Dai Hanh and King Dinh Bo Linh. While some of the older structures may be less visually appealing, it is still a worthwhile place to visit.

reviews.author: TravelingFoodie
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: We visited Hoa Lu Ancient Capital and found it to be an interesting and atmospheric historical site. The temples are well kept and set among limestone scenery, creating a calm, traditional feel. It’s easy to walk around and learn about Vietnam’s early history. Not the most dramatic attraction in the area, but a worthwhile cultural stop in Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Emily
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Very well maintained & preserved.Beautiful shrines & temples. Limited written information, but we had a guide to fill in the gaps.Did get quite busy, and be prepared if wearing revealing clothes you will need to cover up with provided fabric.

reviews.author: みるく
reviews.title: It's a laid-back ancient city.
reviews.content: Chan An and Hoa Loo came here for an optional tour. It was fun to ride a little bike before coming here. This one was well maintained and easy to walk. It's hot with not much sun, so parasols, hats and drinks are essential.

reviews.author: lilybt
reviews.title: Taste of Ancient Capitals
reviews.content: Major destinations that can be visited on day tours from Hanoi are "Ha Long Bay Cruise" and "Ninh Binh". The former is a natural heritage site famous for its landscape of steep islands in the bay, while the latter is a mixed heritage site consisting of landscapes and ruins of ancient capitals, also known as "Haron Bay on Land". While many visitors to either may choose the prominent former, they chose the latter because of the flexibility of time and itinerary, and were caught up in the unusual occurrence of being separated from the guide at the arrival point of the river cruise.The first stop is the Hoa Lu ruins, where the Đồng dynasty briefly established the capital before the transfer of the capital to Tân Long, and almost no original structures remain, but it has a unique landscape as a historical heritage.

reviews.author: GhostofMars
reviews.title: Disappointing. Could be so much more.
reviews.content: This could be so much better. The temple they have is good enough, but unfortunately there’s not much else other than an open field. There was a small museum but it only had a few items. They really could turn this into something special showing what has been unearthed here. The confusing map for he area doesn’t help. Don’t get a bicycle from the street vendors. It is unnecessary. In the end didn’t spend much time here.

reviews.author: May G
reviews.title: Beautiful illumination to visit in the evening
reviews.content: A visit in the evening to enjoy the illumination, it is small and perhaps does not deserve a detour. There is a bustling market with local produce sales and traditional dishes in the evening.

reviews.author: akio9jp
reviews.title: Capital 1,000 years ago
reviews.content: Hoa Lu became the capital of Vietnam in 968, when it gained independence from the Southern Han of China, but only functioned as the capital for 42 years, as the capital was moved to Thang Long (now Hanoi) in 1,010. We were able to visit historical buildings, including ancient temples and the ruins of royal palaces.

reviews.author: Eve
reviews.title: Total tourist trap and completely overrated.
reviews.content: This place is overcrowded and really loud.It’s one of the worst tourist traps I’ve ever been to.I left after 10 minutes.

reviews.author: Sean Alicante
reviews.title: Skip. Lots of pushy sales people and it’s kind of in the middle of no where. Not worth the trouble
reviews.content: Not really worth visiting. Go to a Pho ca Hoa Lu ( old town) instead.  This area is kind of grimey with SUUUPER pushy people trying to have you buy their services. I would avoid Unlv’s you really just have so much time in ninh binh where you wanted to see every single thing. Skip the Hoa Lu Ancient Town

reviews.author: Gus b
reviews.title: Not worth it. Too much hassle.
reviews.content: Not worth the fuss. On your way in you will try to be scammed into parking, just ignore them. Ticket price is 20,000 and once you walk towards entrance you’ll be harassed by people trying to get you to rent a bike, again you do NOT need to rent a bike as it’s no way near the 2 hour walk they claim. We walked up some stairs to a cool view but that was about it.Wouldn’t recommend tbh.

reviews.author: Marriet d
reviews.title: Scam! Avoid 'free parking' ahead of Hoa Lu's entrance
reviews.content: Parking scams are everywhere around Ninh Binh. No need to be unpleasant to anyone, but do be strong and continue to your destination with confidence.Your first stop is the ticket booth on the main road's right hand side.Next you'll drive your scooter/bicycle/motorbike across the street  (and ever-so-slightly back the way you came) into Hoa Lu. Present your ticket as you ride through the gate where everyone's entering on foot. If your experience is like mine, five or six scammers will tell you to stop or park where they want you to park. Now's a good time to show off your ice cold nerves! Give the bike some gas and head for the entrance. If you ask employees of Hoa Lu about parking, they'll tell you to do exactly what you want to do, which is park inside the complex for free.

reviews.author: Mark
reviews.title: Important historic site for Vietnamese but not a lot to see. Unpleasant, pushy 'free parking' scammers outside.
reviews.content: Undoubtedly an historic site from the Vietnamese point of view but there's not really much to see. It's in a pleasant, green area not far from Trang An. We hired a motor scooter from our accommodation close to Tam Coc and took the scenic route through Hang Mua, which follows the river and is a nice quiet road. This road emerges not far from Trang An where we spent the morning on a boat trip. Don't be scammed by the 'free parking' places close to the entrance to the 'ancient capital' - they tell you that it's not permitted to take a motor scooter on to the site but, it is. Then they want you to hire a bike to go round it but the bikes are pretty clunky. We agree with other reviewers who recommend cycling from Tam Coc if you have the energy. Then you can use your own bike to ride around the site. Anyway, back to the ancient city: there's some typical old architecture and quite an extensive series of small roads winding through the village - pleasant but not really interesting. So, in conclusion, visit if you want to tick it off but don't worry if you miss out - just look at the pictures online. Enough said?

reviews.author: Catherine F
reviews.title: Interesting site to visit for a couple of hours
reviews.content: We enjoyed our visit to Hoa Lu. We drove by scooter and parked (for free) outside and hired bicycles to visit the different locations within the city. If you are staying in Tam Coc or Trang An and have access to a decent bicycle, I would recommend cycling to Hoa Lu from your hotel and using that bicycle as the ones available there are very basic. You can walk around the site, but if it's a hot day, cycling is better as it is a fairly large site. You are not given a map (and there are just a few on signboards in the centre of the site) and the signage isnt great so make the most of your unintended detours. It is easy to.cycle out of the site onto the main road, so keep Google maps to hand.

reviews.author: Russ Lacuata
reviews.title: Ancient Capital
reviews.content: Located in Ninh Binh, Hoang Lu Ancient Capital of an ancient Vietnamese Kingdom.The ancient city is surrounded by the Trang An limestone mountains and Yen Ngua limestone hills that provided good defense for the kingdom.

reviews.author: Sashila Mahendran
reviews.title: Hoa Lu Ancient Citadel
reviews.content: Hoa Lu Ancient citadel brought to life by our tour guide Jenny.Very interesting historical stories retold during our excursion.Jenny got everyone in the bus well acquainted

reviews.author: Coyote-Travelerz
reviews.title: Disappointing, but interesting
reviews.content: Of the 3 sites on our tour, this was the least interesting.I want to stress this is not a bad place to visit, but there are not many buildings to visit, can be large crowds, and leaves a lot to the imagination. Unless you are a true diehard history buff, you may not get too much from here, making it a waste of your time to visit versus other places in the area.

reviews.author: EleonoraO75
reviews.title: Hoa Lư Ancient Capital
reviews.content: Not having much time and since we also had a visit to the Hue Citadel planned, we only saw two temples. Maybe they aren't the most beautiful we saw in Vietnam but I'm still happy I went. To be done only if you have a lot of time available!

reviews.author: Chris318i
reviews.title: Not a must-see in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: From our point of view Hoa Lu' Ancient Capital is not a must-see. During our visit there were a lot of big tourist groups. The entrance fee is only 20.000 VND per adult. Our highlight was the viewpoint.

reviews.author: Sonje M
reviews.title: Disappointing experience
reviews.content: I was very excited to visit Vietnam’s ancient capital as I’m fascinated with history. However, the experience was extremely disappointing to us, so much so that we did a quick speed walk through the place and cut our visit short. It seems like people are living on the grounds and there is debris and old discarded items lying around in places such as an old billboard/signage, ladder chair, scrubbing brush, etc. It seemed like we accidentally walked into someone's messy backyard. There are also scooters driving around in the “ancient capital”. There are two entrances and it seems locals are using it as a shortcut. This really does not help to transport you to by gone eras.Although the entry fee is not very high, it feels like a bit of a rip off to pay to enter a place with so-called historical importance where people live (and display their debris) and scooters a free to drive like it any other road. There are other much more interesting place that are much better looked after that is completely free to enter.If you have an exceptional imagination I guess it still mildly interesting to imagine how it might have been like years ago.

reviews.author: LaNyonsaise
reviews.title: Few remains to see.
reviews.content: There’s not a lot to see so it doesn’t take long to walk to a couple of temples. The entry ticket is only 20VND and there are some drinks stands nearby.

reviews.author: must_travel_soon_10
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: Although there might be great history here, there's not much to see and wouldn't bother unless all the other major sights have been enjoyed.

reviews.author: Jkim SNieva
reviews.title: Hoa Lu, Vietnam's former Capital
reviews.content: It was a short but sweet visit. I think the reason why our family had a great time visiting the site is that we did it through a packaged tour of Nin Binh, and so we had a guided tour of the place (kudos to our great guide Hoa!). The place has such a fascinating story and though it doesn't loo grand, its ancient vibes made up for it. The gardens are well kept and there's a pond with fishes. It would be a nice place to roam around.

reviews.author: Phi Somchai
reviews.title: Well maintained and spacious
reviews.content: The ancient city is spread over a large area.  We crossed the bridge and walk through the main entrance of the walled city.   The main highlights that remained in the city were the temples and gardens.  They were well maintained.  There were many historical events relating to this city, so it is recommended to read up about this place for a better understanding before the visit.

reviews.author: Eamon G
reviews.title: Just keep on riding by.
reviews.content: Road to & past this so called historic place and then kept on going ! Not worth going into the bull #&-! that goes on outside the entrance which is enough to put off  any sane tourist. With a location with apparent historical importance you would think again the authorities would crack down on it, if they want tourists to enjoy the visit. And I stood around for a further 10 mins just to watch further shenanigans unfold.

reviews.author: hm777
reviews.title: Interesting site, but not a smooth experience
reviews.content: The site itself is not large and does not take much time to go around. It was very pretty and interesting, even if there were not many English explanations. (e.g. I still have no idea what a "dragon's bed" is, despite attempting to google it).It was a rather chaotic experience, however. Once we entered, the people at the clothing stand were loudly shouting at, and literally chasing, all the people wearing shorts, trying to get them to cover up. There were unfortunately so many people wearing shorts that this meant continuous shouting. There were people on motorcycles saying we needed to hire one/take a ride with them to get around the site (definitely not; it was small). It was unclear where the site began and ended. Finally, we walked up a long flight of steep steps to the left of the entrance to see the emperors tomb and were scammed into buying incense at 10,000 dong each by a lady who lit it in front of us despite us saying "no".

reviews.author: Liesel
reviews.title: Dissapointed
reviews.content: While the history and beauty are enjoyable, I'm afraid there were too many negatives for us. Thousands of people. Difficulty getting through very large tour groups who hold everybody else up in order to take their group photos. Paid an entry fee per person but then were demanded additional fee each time we needed to use the toilet once we were inside. Be warned to cover your shoulders and knees to enter (they have clothing wraps to borrow if you don't come prepared). No English explanation boards to explain what we were looking at. People jump in front of our motorbike in order to stop us and told us free bike parking. Then on return to the bike, told us we had to eat there because we parked there.

reviews.author: Meenakshi
reviews.title: Skip this one
reviews.content: Totally worth skipping. Don't waste your time on this one. Has mostly different old pagodas...saw better ones across Vietnam. Lots of better places to visit in Vietnam and around ninh binh.Also beware of the bike taxis outside. Had a bad experience where 2 of them agreed to take my husband and me on a quick tour of the ancient capital with stops across all key landmarks inside for 70k VND  but once we completed the trip they asked for more and created a nuisance.

reviews.author: Tiago M
reviews.title: Just a good photo at the entrance and that´s it
reviews.content: Nothing to see here. The descriptions are bad or non existent and the buildings are not well taken care of. Just don´t spend your time here.

reviews.author: digitalroc
reviews.title: Ancient Capital
reviews.content: The Hoa Lu Ancient Capital was part of the group itinerary that I was on, so normally I would not have made a visit here.  Although we only stayed an hour, so it wasn’t too bad to gain a history lesson about the Ancient Capital of Hoa Lu.

reviews.author: Teresa
reviews.title: not much to see
reviews.content: I went here and there is not much here it looks like the rest of Asia. Was not rely worth coming. Might be good if you are new in Asia.

reviews.author: Durga M
reviews.title: Nothing much to see
reviews.content: We went to the ancient capital in Hao lu city there is nothing great about the place an ancient place renovated couple of times the tour guide explained the story of the king and its history.

reviews.author: green_gecko917
reviews.title: Pleasant ride there, nice for an hour or so.
reviews.content: Giving this 4 stars mainly because the bicycle ride there (about 16km one way) from where we stayed in Tam Coc was spectacular. The ancient capital itself is ok - I'd probably give it 3 stars. Take your bicycles (or motorbikes etc) inside. You are allowed.  We even saw cars in there. Don't park at the "free parking" across the road as they would likely just hold your bikes for ransom afterwards. They were fairly aggressive trying to get us to park but we refused. It is also extremely hot in July so walking through this place would not be pleasant.You can actually get in for free if you go in the other way. There is a main gate where you pay, and then you go straight a few hundred meters towards the first temple and turn right before going in. If you keep going that way, it just turns into a little street that opens up into the town. We might have gone that way if we had known about this "secret" entrance.You can spend maybe 1 hour here, but lots more time cycling around nearby attractions and views.

reviews.author: Vietnamese Dinner Experience in Tam Coc
reviews.title: Where can learn history
reviews.content: I often send my children here at least once a year at the beginning of the year or summer holidays to visit and learn about the history of King Dinh and Le's life in Vietnam. The space here is spacious and airy, we can enjoy as a sunny, windy picnic and immerse in nature.

reviews.author: Shimnik
reviews.title: One day - more than enough
reviews.content: If you think to spend more than 2 days in Hoa Lu (Tam Coc), think about it twice. There is not much to see and do except 2 temples dedicated to the first emperors, rice fields, boat ride and cycling on an old bike. Everything can be realized in one day!

reviews.author: Albywon
reviews.title: Quick Stop
reviews.content: We came here from Hanoi as short stop on the way to Tam Coc. Unfortunately we were rushed through and would have liked to have had more time. Still worth a look and we may return on our own for a better look.

reviews.author: Vnvet68
reviews.title: A look into Vietnam's past.
reviews.content: I loved this place. It is old and not shiny but the feelings and architecture and history is well worth seeing.

reviews.author: ozvpm_andy
reviews.title: Not a destination on its own
reviews.content: We visited Hoa Lu on a day trip to Binh Ninh province as we love all that old historical stuff. While the stop was interesting enough (mainly because our guide told us the history) the site itself is a little underwhelming.Worth a stop if on your way to somewhere else, but not really a tourist destination on its own

reviews.author: Peter V
reviews.title: Onevof the capitals old old Bietnam
reviews.content: We went on the capitals of vietnam tour and visited all of them. Not just hanoi or hue but all thevothrrsctoo andvthis onebof the mostvromantic ones, setbin a beautiful scenery that adds up tomits uniqueness, for hostory buffs a must

reviews.author: nishal p
reviews.title: Most visitors would not be interested in this cultural visit
reviews.content: Nothing fancy and little nostalgic - however there is an ancient charm and some very old artefacts - this site is worth a visit during quiter periods to fully view the collection.  it does get very crowded which makes for a poor site visit.  It is not an eloborate or very distinguished site but it does hold a unique charming old or ancient feel to it.  It will only be appreciated by the true cultural boffins - the general public would overlook the essence of the site.

reviews.author: Eimear
reviews.title: Don’t bother
reviews.content: Compared to all the other sites in the area this one is a complete waste of time. There is nothing really to see and we left very disappointed

reviews.author: Alice W
reviews.title: Don't bother
reviews.content: This site is fake artifacts and not worth the detour. Luckily we motor cycled there and got out quick. I would hate to have been on an organised tour. The touts here are also particularly pushy. We are pretty used to them and generally a friendly no (khong) with a smile is OK.  But these touts were agressive. Even tried to get AUD off us. When we said we didn't carry they tried to sell us an Australian $5 note. They also were forcibly placing hats on my head too, they were just scammy and rude. Avoid stress, avoid this site.

reviews.author: Jean T
reviews.title: Not a lot to see
reviews.content: Interesting in a way  but if ylu want temples & meaningful ruins, this is perhaps not the place for you.

reviews.author: kyy0te
reviews.title: Interesting and beautiful, but not very informative
reviews.content: I was never sure if any part of this was original, either in structure or design. I understood the history of who built it and why, but was left mystified archaeologically. The little museum had a fascinating portion of an excavation and a few artifacts. Bicycling there through the little village off the main highway was the best part.

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: Too many people
reviews.content: Hoa Lư Ancient Capital is certainly an interesting place from a historical point of view and is worth a visit if you are in Ninh Binh. Unfortunately, however, our experience was strongly affected by the huge number of people present.There are so many organized groups, practically all with their own guide in tow, and at times it even becomes difficult to move in the spaces and get close to the temples. The amount of people is truly impressive and, in my opinion, makes you lose almost completely the charm of the place.It is a shame especially because some of the buildings are places of worship, but with hundreds of people entering and exiting continuously, guides talking and groups crowding, it is very difficult to perceive any atmosphere of contemplation or religiosity.To this are added numerous vendors who try to offer practically everything and who, in some cases, we found rather insistent.In conclusion, Hoa Lư is certainly interesting and important for understanding the history of Vietnam, but mass tourism has reached such a level as to seriously compromise the visiting experience. Probably, by managing to arrive very early or at a less crowded time, the feeling would be completely different.

reviews.content: Parking scams are everywhere around Ninh Binh. No need to be unpleasant to anyone, but do be strong and continue to your destination with confidence.Your first stop is the ticket booth on the main road's right hand side.Next you'll drive your scooter/bicycle/motorbike across the street  (and ever-so-slightly back the way you came) into Hoa Lu. Present your ticket as you ride through the gate where everyone's entering on foot. If your experience is like mine, five or six scammers will tell you to stop or park where they want you to park. Now's a good time to show off your ice cold nerves! Give the bike some gas and head for the entrance. If you ask employees of Hoa Lu about parking, they'll tell you to do exactly what you want to do, which is park inside the complex for free.

reviews.author: Mark
reviews.title: Important historic site for Vietnamese but not a lot to see. Unpleasant, pushy 'free parking' scammers outside.
reviews.content: Undoubtedly an historic site from the Vietnamese point of view but there's not really much to see. It's in a pleasant, green area not far from Trang An. We hired a motor scooter from our accommodation close to Tam Coc and took the scenic route through Hang Mua, which follows the river and is a nice quiet road. This road emerges not far from Trang An where we spent the morning on a boat trip. Don't be scammed by the 'free parking' places close to the entrance to the 'ancient capital' - they tell you that it's not permitted to take a motor scooter on to the site but, it is. Then they want you to hire a bike to go round it but the bikes are pretty clunky. We agree with other reviewers who recommend cycling from Tam Coc if you have the energy. Then you can use your own bike to ride around the site. Anyway, back to the ancient city: there's some typical old architecture and quite an extensive series of small roads winding through the village - pleasant but not really interesting. So, in conclusion, visit if you want to tick it off but don't worry if you miss out - just look at the pictures online. Enough said?

reviews.author: Catherine F
reviews.title: Interesting site to visit for a couple of hours
reviews.content: We enjoyed our visit to Hoa Lu. We drove by scooter and parked (for free) outside and hired bicycles to visit the different locations within the city. If you are staying in Tam Coc or Trang An and have access to a decent bicycle, I would recommend cycling to Hoa Lu from your hotel and using that bicycle as the ones available there are very basic. You can walk around the site, but if it's a hot day, cycling is better as it is a fairly large site. You are not given a map (and there are just a few on signboards in the centre of the site) and the signage isnt great so make the most of your unintended detours. It is easy to.cycle out of the site onto the main road, so keep Google maps to hand.

reviews.author: Russ Lacuata
reviews.title: Ancient Capital
reviews.content: Located in Ninh Binh, Hoang Lu Ancient Capital of an ancient Vietnamese Kingdom.The ancient city is surrounded by the Trang An limestone mountains and Yen Ngua limestone hills that provided good defense for the kingdom.

reviews.author: Sashila Mahendran
reviews.title: Hoa Lu Ancient Citadel
reviews.content: Hoa Lu Ancient citadel brought to life by our tour guide Jenny.Very interesting historical stories retold during our excursion.Jenny got everyone in the bus well acquainted

reviews.author: Coyote-Travelerz
reviews.title: Disappointing, but interesting
reviews.content: Of the 3 sites on our tour, this was the least interesting.I want to stress this is not a bad place to visit, but there are not many buildings to visit, can be large crowds, and leaves a lot to the imagination. Unless you are a true diehard history buff, you may not get too much from here, making it a waste of your time to visit versus other places in the area.

reviews.author: EleonoraO75
reviews.title: Hoa Lư Ancient Capital
reviews.content: Not having much time and since we also had a visit to the Hue Citadel planned, we only saw two temples. Maybe they aren't the most beautiful we saw in Vietnam but I'm still happy I went. To be done only if you have a lot of time available!

reviews.author: Chris318i
reviews.title: Not a must-see in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: From our point of view Hoa Lu' Ancient Capital is not a must-see. During our visit there were a lot of big tourist groups. The entrance fee is only 20.000 VND per adult. Our highlight was the viewpoint.

reviews.author: Sonje M
reviews.title: Disappointing experience
reviews.content: I was very excited to visit Vietnam’s ancient capital as I’m fascinated with history. However, the experience was extremely disappointing to us, so much so that we did a quick speed walk through the place and cut our visit short. It seems like people are living on the grounds and there is debris and old discarded items lying around in places such as an old billboard/signage, ladder chair, scrubbing brush, etc. It seemed like we accidentally walked into someone's messy backyard. There are also scooters driving around in the “ancient capital”. There are two entrances and it seems locals are using it as a shortcut. This really does not help to transport you to by gone eras.Although the entry fee is not very high, it feels like a bit of a rip off to pay to enter a place with so-called historical importance where people live (and display their debris) and scooters a free to drive like it any other road. There are other much more interesting place that are much better looked after that is completely free to enter.If you have an exceptional imagination I guess it still mildly interesting to imagine how it might have been like years ago.

reviews.author: LaNyonsaise
reviews.title: Few remains to see.
reviews.content: There’s not a lot to see so it doesn’t take long to walk to a couple of temples. The entry ticket is only 20VND and there are some drinks stands nearby.

reviews.author: must_travel_soon_10
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: Although there might be great history here, there's not much to see and wouldn't bother unless all the other major sights have been enjoyed.

reviews.author: Jkim SNieva
reviews.title: Hoa Lu, Vietnam's former Capital
reviews.content: It was a short but sweet visit. I think the reason why our family had a great time visiting the site is that we did it through a packaged tour of Nin Binh, and so we had a guided tour of the place (kudos to our great guide Hoa!). The place has such a fascinating story and though it doesn't loo grand, its ancient vibes made up for it. The gardens are well kept and there's a pond with fishes. It would be a nice place to roam around.

reviews.author: Phi Somchai
reviews.title: Well maintained and spacious
reviews.content: The ancient city is spread over a large area.  We crossed the bridge and walk through the main entrance of the walled city.   The main highlights that remained in the city were the temples and gardens.  They were well maintained.  There were many historical events relating to this city, so it is recommended to read up about this place for a better understanding before the visit.

reviews.author: Eamon G
reviews.title: Just keep on riding by.
reviews.content: Road to & past this so called historic place and then kept on going ! Not worth going into the bull #&-! that goes on outside the entrance which is enough to put off  any sane tourist. With a location with apparent historical importance you would think again the authorities would crack down on it, if they want tourists to enjoy the visit. And I stood around for a further 10 mins just to watch further shenanigans unfold.

reviews.author: hm777
reviews.title: Interesting site, but not a smooth experience
reviews.content: The site itself is not large and does not take much time to go around. It was very pretty and interesting, even if there were not many English explanations. (e.g. I still have no idea what a "dragon's bed" is, despite attempting to google it).It was a rather chaotic experience, however. Once we entered, the people at the clothing stand were loudly shouting at, and literally chasing, all the people wearing shorts, trying to get them to cover up. There were unfortunately so many people wearing shorts that this meant continuous shouting. There were people on motorcycles saying we needed to hire one/take a ride with them to get around the site (definitely not; it was small). It was unclear where the site began and ended. Finally, we walked up a long flight of steep steps to the left of the entrance to see the emperors tomb and were scammed into buying incense at 10,000 dong each by a lady who lit it in front of us despite us saying "no".

reviews.author: Liesel
reviews.title: Dissapointed
reviews.content: While the history and beauty are enjoyable, I'm afraid there were too many negatives for us. Thousands of people. Difficulty getting through very large tour groups who hold everybody else up in order to take their group photos. Paid an entry fee per person but then were demanded additional fee each time we needed to use the toilet once we were inside. Be warned to cover your shoulders and knees to enter (they have clothing wraps to borrow if you don't come prepared). No English explanation boards to explain what we were looking at. People jump in front of our motorbike in order to stop us and told us free bike parking. Then on return to the bike, told us we had to eat there because we parked there.

reviews.author: Meenakshi
reviews.title: Skip this one
reviews.content: Totally worth skipping. Don't waste your time on this one. Has mostly different old pagodas...saw better ones across Vietnam. Lots of better places to visit in Vietnam and around ninh binh.Also beware of the bike taxis outside. Had a bad experience where 2 of them agreed to take my husband and me on a quick tour of the ancient capital with stops across all key landmarks inside for 70k VND  but once we completed the trip they asked for more and created a nuisance.

reviews.author: Tiago M
reviews.title: Just a good photo at the entrance and that´s it
reviews.content: Nothing to see here. The descriptions are bad or non existent and the buildings are not well taken care of. Just don´t spend your time here.

reviews.author: digitalroc
reviews.title: Ancient Capital
reviews.content: The Hoa Lu Ancient Capital was part of the group itinerary that I was on, so normally I would not have made a visit here.  Although we only stayed an hour, so it wasn’t too bad to gain a history lesson about the Ancient Capital of Hoa Lu.

reviews.author: Teresa
reviews.title: not much to see
reviews.content: I went here and there is not much here it looks like the rest of Asia. Was not rely worth coming. Might be good if you are new in Asia.

reviews.author: Durga M
reviews.title: Nothing much to see
reviews.content: We went to the ancient capital in Hao lu city there is nothing great about the place an ancient place renovated couple of times the tour guide explained the story of the king and its history.

reviews.author: green_gecko917
reviews.title: Pleasant ride there, nice for an hour or so.
reviews.content: Giving this 4 stars mainly because the bicycle ride there (about 16km one way) from where we stayed in Tam Coc was spectacular. The ancient capital itself is ok - I'd probably give it 3 stars. Take your bicycles (or motorbikes etc) inside. You are allowed.  We even saw cars in there. Don't park at the "free parking" across the road as they would likely just hold your bikes for ransom afterwards. They were fairly aggressive trying to get us to park but we refused. It is also extremely hot in July so walking through this place would not be pleasant.You can actually get in for free if you go in the other way. There is a main gate where you pay, and then you go straight a few hundred meters towards the first temple and turn right before going in. If you keep going that way, it just turns into a little street that opens up into the town. We might have gone that way if we had known about this "secret" entrance.You can spend maybe 1 hour here, but lots more time cycling around nearby attractions and views.

reviews.author: Vietnamese Dinner Experience in Tam Coc
reviews.title: Where can learn history
reviews.content: I often send my children here at least once a year at the beginning of the year or summer holidays to visit and learn about the history of King Dinh and Le's life in Vietnam. The space here is spacious and airy, we can enjoy as a sunny, windy picnic and immerse in nature.

reviews.author: Shimnik
reviews.title: One day - more than enough
reviews.content: If you think to spend more than 2 days in Hoa Lu (Tam Coc), think about it twice. There is not much to see and do except 2 temples dedicated to the first emperors, rice fields, boat ride and cycling on an old bike. Everything can be realized in one day!

reviews.author: Albywon
reviews.title: Quick Stop
reviews.content: We came here from Hanoi as short stop on the way to Tam Coc. Unfortunately we were rushed through and would have liked to have had more time. Still worth a look and we may return on our own for a better look.

reviews.author: Vnvet68
reviews.title: A look into Vietnam's past.
reviews.content: I loved this place. It is old and not shiny but the feelings and architecture and history is well worth seeing.

reviews.author: ozvpm_andy
reviews.title: Not a destination on its own
reviews.content: We visited Hoa Lu on a day trip to Binh Ninh province as we love all that old historical stuff. While the stop was interesting enough (mainly because our guide told us the history) the site itself is a little underwhelming.Worth a stop if on your way to somewhere else, but not really a tourist destination on its own

reviews.author: Peter V
reviews.title: Onevof the capitals old old Bietnam
reviews.content: We went on the capitals of vietnam tour and visited all of them. Not just hanoi or hue but all thevothrrsctoo andvthis onebof the mostvromantic ones, setbin a beautiful scenery that adds up tomits uniqueness, for hostory buffs a must

reviews.author: nishal p
reviews.title: Most visitors would not be interested in this cultural visit
reviews.content: Nothing fancy and little nostalgic - however there is an ancient charm and some very old artefacts - this site is worth a visit during quiter periods to fully view the collection.  it does get very crowded which makes for a poor site visit.  It is not an eloborate or very distinguished site but it does hold a unique charming old or ancient feel to it.  It will only be appreciated by the true cultural boffins - the general public would overlook the essence of the site.

reviews.author: Eimear
reviews.title: Don’t bother
reviews.content: Compared to all the other sites in the area this one is a complete waste of time. There is nothing really to see and we left very disappointed

reviews.author: Alice W
reviews.title: Don't bother
reviews.content: This site is fake artifacts and not worth the detour. Luckily we motor cycled there and got out quick. I would hate to have been on an organised tour. The touts here are also particularly pushy. We are pretty used to them and generally a friendly no (khong) with a smile is OK.  But these touts were agressive. Even tried to get AUD off us. When we said we didn't carry they tried to sell us an Australian $5 note. They also were forcibly placing hats on my head too, they were just scammy and rude. Avoid stress, avoid this site.

reviews.author: Jean T
reviews.title: Not a lot to see
reviews.content: Interesting in a way  but if ylu want temples & meaningful ruins, this is perhaps not the place for you.

reviews.author: kyy0te
reviews.title: Interesting and beautiful, but not very informative
reviews.content: I was never sure if any part of this was original, either in structure or design. I understood the history of who built it and why, but was left mystified archaeologically. The little museum had a fascinating portion of an excavation and a few artifacts. Bicycling there through the little village off the main highway was the best part.

reviews.author: Quinten Jiskoot
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: A bit disappointing, you almost don´t see any bear. Far away they roam.

reviews.author: Adrienne G
reviews.title: Incredible hidden gem, still some love in the world
reviews.content: An amazing experience! Well worth the entry fee and the slightly long drive from Tam Cok. The team there do an incredible job saving bears that are victims of the horrific bear bile trade. We were so lucky to see a bear super close (he just turned his head as I took the photo but he was looking straight at us and clearly as curious as we were!) Feeding time is at 4pm which is your best chance to see the bears and you can either watch from the sky walk by yourself for only 50,000 Dong or join a tour for a bit more. Thao in the visitor house was so helpful and kind and gave us all the information we needed. She was an absolute gem! Four Paws is the project that funds and runs the rescue centre. I can’t commend them all there enough for the incredible work they do to rescue the bears who are treated so appallingly by humanity. Clearly there is still some love in the world.

reviews.author: Elaine
reviews.title: A great day out with bears
reviews.content: They begin with a comprehensive and touching film about the bears. There is a sky walk overlooking the bear enclosures. Then the guide will take you on a more comprehensive walk at ground level for the full experience. They use earpieces so that the bears are not frightened by noise. These are frail bears who have suffered in the past but are flourishing now rescued and treated well. An uplifting experience and well worth the ticket. The onside restaurant is also very good.

reviews.author: Veronika R
reviews.title: Musst see!
reviews.content: Beautiful place for rescued bears, with high professional care they deserve.The stories of the bears are very sad. But it's very educational and nice to see that there are changes in progress and people who really care.Go. Enjoy the bears and support the sanctuary.

reviews.author: Wanderer03451888431
reviews.title: Bear Sanctuary Ninh Binh Vietnam
reviews.content: This sanctuary (not a zoo) was established to rescue Asiatic Black and Sun bears from bile milking ( used in Chinese medicine) and hunting. The sanctuary has dedicated staff that work tirelessly for the welfare of theses bears that have been victims of much cruelty in their lives. If you love bears and are passionate about supporting authentic organisations like Four Paws- Bear Sanctuary then you will enjoy seeing the bears being looked after on this amazing site. We did the immersive tour with a member of staff who walked around showing us the food preparation areas and talking with great knowledge about how try to balance their diets whilst offering stimulating ways for the bears to find food. All staff were very knowledgeable and passionate about the bears. This was the best experience and tour we have had in Vietnam and would highly recommend it. The government fully support the excellent work being done to protect these bears and offer them a peaceful life

reviews.author: Katie
reviews.title: Worthwhile trip
reviews.content: Staff are very passionate about helping the bears and raising awareness about boycotting bear bile products. Staff also had amazing English skills- definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area! Sadly we didn’t have time to do a full tour but imagine it would be great if you have the time!

reviews.author: JUDY M
reviews.title: Great work done here..highly recommend
reviews.content: Highly recommend this place.  Our guide was so enthusiastic... she loves those bears.  Very informative and spoke very clear English. Great work on education as a means of stopping the illegal trapping of bears and, worse, bile extraction.  Do take the full tour ..so worth it

reviews.author: Offmefarm
reviews.title: Best day!
reviews.content: Best day of all in Vietnam! 4 Paws is doing amazing work to rehabilitate the bears they so lovingly care for and importantly, to educate about safe alternatives to bear bile- reduce demand and less bear farms will follow. A couple of things to help those wishing to visit:1. Book a tour directly with the centre before you go and take a cab there. We arrived early but the first tour was booked out so we went on to the endangered primate and turtle centre in Cuc Phuong NP which is also excellent. The tour guide we had at both centres were so knowledgeable and passionate2. Buy well priced souvenirs to support the centre3. Have an excellent lunch in the restaurantSpread the news and have an uplifting albeit sad day

reviews.author: Bussereau A
reviews.title: Go there!!
reviews.content: We chose the first formula with a one-hour tour of the sanctuary with a great Ha guide!It was exciting and we had the chance to see all the bears in their enclosures. We could see how fulfilled they were and finally free to self-determination.Education was one of the most important levers it is essential to relay the actions of free paws with this project.We also understood what was at stake for bear owners and why they started wanting to sell their bile.There is still a lot of work to be done in Vietnam but the progress is significant and 46 bears live under care as a result of torture and will end their lives here. So they need us. The capacity of the center is 100 bears so there are still many bears to free from their ordeal. It is a pleasure to see them evolve after the terrible images of their previous living conditions. A very important visit, do not hesitate a second.

reviews.author: Alexandra F
reviews.title: Well worth the visit to support their efforts in rescuing bears from the bile trade industry in Asia
reviews.content: It was a very eye opening and unique experience. The staff recognise each of the bears by name and their favourite foods 😭 I did the immersive tour which was 250k and included a guided sanctuary tour and self guided access to the sky bridge which stretches over the enclosures. The tour begins with a short video outlining the sanctuary and its efforts. The staff are so caring and respectful of the bears and their individual needs. Tragic to find out that all of the bear residents spent a minimum of 15 years in captivity in cages no bigger than a large dog crate.

reviews.author: Viet Exquisite Travel
reviews.title: Amazing experience with kids!
reviews.content: We came there in a cold day but our kids were really excited to see the bears. This place is 100% worth coming to if you visit Ninh Binh, especially families with kids.😊. You  will not only have a good time here, but can also learn a lot about animal rescue. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Глеб К
reviews.title: Best place in Ninh Bihn❤️(best place in Ninh Bihn)
reviews.content: Visited the place together with his wife, there was a sea of experiences left for life❤️ together with a guide managed to dive deeper into the lives of the goateed residents of the shelter, got acquainted with their history, saw how each pet is cared for, fed and given attention. Visitors are also cared for - guests are invited to walk along the SkyWalk trail, where you can see the inhabitants from the stage (by the way, everything is done very safely, no one can hurt each other); there is a cafe where the staff can prepare something delicious for you, a large area of the shelter, which you can walk around with the fascinating history of a guide with great experience, and there is a gift shop with a great range.This place is 100% worth coming to if you happen to be in Nin Bing) can safely advise shelter to everyone you know, visit and you😊P.s. from us advise to arrive early and also take the IMMERSE package, definitely won't regret😉[Also duplicated in English and Korean:][I'll repeat it in English and Korean too:] We visited this place as a couple, and it left us with a lifetime of unforgettable impressions ❤️ Together with the guide, we were able to dive deeper into the lives of the bears living in the sanctuary. We learned their stories and saw how they are cared for, fed, and given attention individually.The staff are also very caring toward visitors. Guests can walk along the SkyWalk trail, where you can observe the animals from an elevated platform (everything is designed very safely, so no one can harm each other). There is also a café where the staff can cook something tasty for you, a large sanctuary area where an experienced guide can take you on a fascinating tour, and a souvenir shop with a wide selection of items.This place is definitely worth visiting if you find yourself in Ninh Binh. SkyWalk 트레일을 따라 걸으며 위에서 곰들을 안전하게 볼 수 있고, 카페에서는 직원들이 맛있는 음식을 준비해 줍니다. 또한 넓은 보호소를 경험 많은 가이드와 함께 흥미로운 설명을 들으며 둘러볼 있고, 다양한 기념��을 판매하는 상점도 있습다.닌빈에 오게 된다면 이곳�은 꼭 방문해 볼 만한 곳�입니다. 누구에게나 자신 있게 추천할 수 있습니다 😊추신: 가능하다면 조금 일찍 방문하고 IMMERSE 패키지를 선택하는 것을 추천합니다. 정말 후회하지 않을 거예요 😉

reviews.author: Татьяна Т
reviews.title: Best thing I've seen in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Having visited almost all the main attractions of Ninh Binh, I can safely say - this place has become the most memorable for me. Definitely worth your attention.My husband and I came here just to see the bears, and we thought we'd spend a little time here. But in the end, they stayed for almost three hours - so interesting.The area is very large and green. We walked long distances over the suspension bridge above the spacious enclosures and watched the bears. There are many of them here, and everyone has their own habits: someone plays, someone relaxes, someone explores the territory. You can watch them for a very long time - it's really fascinating.They gave us a tour and told us about the shelter. Particularly touching was the fact that the staff explained in detail how the bears got here and the difficulties they had experienced before. Now they have a safe place to be cared for.The staff here are incredibly friendly and sympathetic. You can see that people genuinely love their work and treat the bears with great care and warmth. They are also very attentive to visitors and happy to share knowledge.If you're in Ninh Binh, be sure to come. Not only will you have a good time here, but you will also learn a lot about animal rescue

reviews.author: USUKAU
reviews.title: Great place doing great work
reviews.content: Great insight into the work done to help these animals.  We organised a car and driver to take us from our hotel.  The sanctuary offers three types of admission - we opted for the one that includes a tour of the sanctuary.  This was the correct choice!  Our guide showed us around the facility and shared information about the many bears we saw.  We then watched a short film, had a break at the cafe (additional cost but inexpensive) and then went to the tree walk to watch them give the bears lunch.  The tour was far and away the best way to see and learn about the bears.  Entry including the tour was 250k (less than $15 Aud) which goes to help support the bears.  Highly recommend for anyone who likes animals

reviews.author: Matthew C
reviews.title: Fantastic work that needs our support and help
reviews.content: What a great morning we had at this sanctuary. We opted for the full tour, this gave us a guided walk around the enclosures with our guide that answered our questions as we walked. We stopped off at the food preparation area and were lucky to see a few bears (it is set up for the bears rather than for tourists viewing them so you might not see anything), we then watched a film about the sanctuary, the work they do and they very sad situation lots of bears are still in in Vietnam who continue to be kept at bear farms even though its illegal to extract the bile. We then had a self guided walk on a glass walkway. Definitely worth a visit if you are in the area.

reviews.author: Karen - Veiled Valley
reviews.title: Well managed sanctuary, not easy to sight bears
reviews.content: The bear sanctuary is a great place for the bears. They are well taken care of, well protected. They live in a rather natural habitat with lots of space and flora. Food is hidden so that they can use their hunting skills. They are not forced to be in front of visitors. However, because of the protection for the bears, there is really no guarantee that you would see the bear close up or in action. For the cheaper tickets, you can only walk on the sky bridge, which is not that long of a walk. For the guided tours, they also have long movies / talking before and after, which can be boring for young children. It is a very well maintained place. I appreciate their mission and work. It will probably be very fun to volunteer at the place. In terms of bear sighting, it is not as spectacular.

reviews.author: JamesXX_007
reviews.title: This is not to be missed
reviews.content: This is not to be missed. Well organized as we had a private guide for just under an hour.  I tip my hat to the government of Vietnam for leading the way in helping bears.

reviews.author: Jarod S
reviews.title: Must Visit
reviews.content: Amazing experience! Our visit to the bear sanctuary was an absolute highlight of our trip. The staff were kind, knowledgeable, and helpful. The work at the sanctuary is awe-inspiring, as they have nearly eradicated bear farms in Vietnam. They even helped us book a ride back to Hanoi when we were having issues finding one.

reviews.author: Riet-Francis
reviews.title: Impressive reception centre
reviews.content: If you are in Ninh Binh you MUST visit this shelter. Very professional approach to these traumatized animals. There is still a long way to go so that the law against these illegal practices can be fully applied. The Vietnamese government supports this project. Chapeau for the patience and care of all employees.

reviews.author: sarpor
reviews.title: Excellent day visit
reviews.content: I am in complete admiration of the people who work here, who have a clear love for the bears in their care. After such a horrific start in life, these bears now spend their days at what is effectively the best version of a 5 star resort. The staff are very knowledgeable and committed to helping the bears’ mentally and physically. Quality enclosures too. I opted for the 250,000k ticket and with this you get to see into the back areas including the kitchen, vets and enrichment.  I arrived about 9am , just after the first feed so the bears were still actively looking for food as I wandered along the skywalk. Then heading bad and joined my tour about 9:45. This took us to other areas to see different bears and ended a couple of hours later. I had lunch at the onsite restaurant (there’s an enclosure opposite and two bears sat and watched me eat lunch). Then I headed back to the skywalk about 1pm to see the bears called back home so that the caretakers can then put their food out. Shortly after the bears were allowed back out and I watched them forage for a while. Excellent day and if I was ever back here I would return. Cannot recommend this place enough.

reviews.author: tanzania2009186361
reviews.title: Bear sanctuary - and absolute must
reviews.content: Absolutely inspiring visit. The staff knowledge of these rescued bears, their psychological and physical needs, was very apparent. Also a reminder of how much damage we as hu.ans do to our fellow creatures.

reviews.author: Gerda V
reviews.title: Impressive.
reviews.content: Great reception. The bears have plenty of space and are well cared for.  They've come from hell to heaven.  The guide knew a lot to tell.  Highly recommended for every animal lover.

reviews.author: Rens33
reviews.title: Great complex
reviews.content: Complex is great. Guides are very knowledgeable and you can tell they have a real love and passion for the bears rescued. We visited early on a very hot day. Not ideal for bear watching- but we did still see some.  Recommend the full tour for 250k.We got a grab out to the sanctuary, but needed them to call us a taxi to return to Tam Coc as no drivers were accepting.

reviews.author: Tim Anderson
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Our visit to the sanctuary was amazing, the tour guides were very knowledgeable and spoke good English. Our guide on the 21/5/2025 for the 1.30 pm tour was great, although we could not remember her name unfortunately.The short film we were shown was produced quite well and also very informative.The bear feeding times are 9am, 1pm and 4pm I believe, it is best to begin your guided tour (if you chose that option) around 30 minutes after feeding time as this is when the bears will be most active. The sanctuary provide hats and umbrellas for sun protection if necessary.It's great to see how much work is currently being done caring for these bears and  rescuing bears still in captivity.

reviews.author: Phil R
reviews.title: A truly Worthy Cause
reviews.content: We did the full tour which I recommend as the best way to experience this sanctuary.  The pace was good, we saw lots of bears an learnt all about the inhumanity shown towards these bears before they were saved.  A truly worthwhile visit and cause.  hank you Four Paws

reviews.author: Andrea
reviews.title: Absolutely fantastic and educative tour, please support this hard work the team makes by saving bears
reviews.content: Huge thanks for everyone for this hard work! This is amazing what you do for the bears. Animal cruelty needs to end, we have absolutely no right to exploit them! I went to the immersive tour and it was totally worth it. I got so many more information, it was so educative. Thank you for this amazing experience. It was actually one of the best programmes I have taken part in while staying in Ninh Binh. THANK YOU!

reviews.author: James A
reviews.title: Excellent location for conservation
reviews.content: I cycled to the bear sanctuary on a warm but rainy day in early July and found it to be a real highlight on the Ninh Binh area. Four Paws are doing excellent work and I really enjoyed the ambience and beautiful surroundings of the sanctuary. I think I would recommend a visit as a highlight of my time in Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Naomi B
reviews.title: Support the bears - great on a rainy day
reviews.content: We were looking for an outing on a rainy day in Ninh Binh and this sanctuary came up on my search. The bears like the drizzling  rain so we saw plenty from the skywalk. I recommend the guided tour, Ninh provides insights about the individual bears and you get to walk in the lower level near the enclosure. Plus the funds are going to care for the rescued bears.

reviews.author: jbschmor
reviews.title: An important and good place to visit in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: My driver from Tam Coc suggested going here and I am very glad that I did.  This place is well worth your time.  It begins with a short film that in some places may be difficult for some viewers to take.  But the information is important.  What I really like about this place is that the emphasis is on education, not on photo opps with the bears.  I learned a lot and I got to see some beautiful bears who are being well taken care of and protected.

reviews.author: Narelle Z
reviews.title: Highly recommend visiting and supporting this bear sanctuary. So special!
reviews.content: We love visiting the Bear Sanctuary. The Moon bears were so beautiful, and it's just very special what they do there. If you love animals this is a must see. Such a great sanctuary to support too!

reviews.author: Darragh O
reviews.title: Do the Immersive tour. 250k. You won't regret it!
reviews.content: Excellent experience. They do amazing work to rescue bears from cruel bile farming practices.They offer three tours. 50k to self guide yourself through a "skywalk" viewing platform which has three viewings houses with written information about the bears in the viewable enclosures.150k for a guided tour of the skywalk viewing platform where a member of staff gives further info about the day to day running of the sanctuary and info about bile farming.250k for the "immersive experience". We did this one and it is absolutely worth the extra cost!! Do not hesitate. You get access to the viewing platform yourself for as long as you want. Immersive tours start at irregular intervals depending on how many people are they and if the staff are free. For this tour, then bring you for a walk along the pathways between the various enclosures where you can easily see the bears only metres from where you stand, through the enclosure fences. We had Ninh and she was very knowledgeable and had great English and explained all about the sanctuary, bile farming and knew a lot about each individual bear. It is clear the staff really care about the bears as they know them by name.10/10 would thoroughly recommend this experience!!

reviews.author: CJ
reviews.title: Four paws! Great work with bears
reviews.content: I recommend visiting the bear sanctuary to learn about the work that Four Paws and their team is doing to prevent the ill-treatment of bears and the harvesting of bear bile for medicinal purposes. I went there on a Thursday afternoon and there were only a 6 other guests. Entry to the sanctuary starts from 50,000VD for the skywalk (basically you get access to view the bears and sanctuary from several others enclosed platforms) and progress up to 150,000 and 250,000VD which includes a dedicated guide and tour of the premises (you get to go into the sanctuary), an overview of the history of bears in Vietnam, key information about some of the bears that are currently at the sanctuary, and an educational video at the end.The venue is modern and there is a nice vegetarian cafe with a great drink selection. I got an iced coffee and it was amazing! Reasonably priced! I am staying at a Homestay near the Bai Định Pagoda. It’s about a 20minute drive away. I ended up using a rental scooter to get here and had to drive on dirt roads but still made it. It is recommended that you have a 2WD to get up the road but I saw a lot in d scoters parked up which May have belonged to workers. You can also use Grab and I did run into another couple that got a ride from a Luxury Van and loaded their mountain bikes into the back of it. I enjoyed it, saw heaps of bears, learnt a lot and felt good about my fees going back into a good cause. It also beats going to the usual tourist places around here and the queues and waiting times to see the same things.

reviews.author: Amélie L
reviews.title: Best experience in Ninh binh bear sanctuary
reviews.content: The Bear Sanctuary in Ninh Binh is truly an incredible place! They rescue bears from the horrific cruelty of bear bile farming, giving them a second chance at a happy and healthy life. Seeing these rescued bears thriving in a safe, natural environment is both heartwarming and inspiring.The staff here are absolutely amazing—kind, passionate, and deeply dedicated to their mission. They take the time to educate visitors about the realities of bile farming and the importance of conservation efforts. Their hard work and commitment have already saved so many bears, giving them the care and freedom they deserve.Visiting this sanctuary is a must for anyone who cares about animal welfare. It’s not just a place to see bears; it’s a place of hope, healing, and change. I highly recommend supporting this wonderful organization in any way you can.Thank you to the entire team for the incredible work you do you are all so amazing ❤️❤️Also a special thanks for Trang ! She is so passionate and was an incredible guide toward the sanctuary 🥰!!

reviews.author: Fearless546825
reviews.title: Nihn bihn bear sanctuary, amazing.....
reviews.content: An amazing organisation doing some incredible work for these poor  bears here in Vietnam and around the world. Please go and visit and learn about the horrible bear bile farming industry,  knowledge is key to stop this cruelty.There are different entrance fees ranging from 50.000d to 250.000. I recommend paying the 250.000 getting a full guided tour from the carer's there and access around the complex .Should be advertised more in Tam Coc and surrounding areas so more tourists know that wonderful place is here....

reviews.author: Mae G
reviews.title: Memorable visit
reviews.content: Highly worthwhile visit. The bears are all so well cared for. Would recommend the tour option to learn more about the day to day operations of the sanctuary. Very informative tour guide also.

reviews.author: sueanne_nicol
reviews.title: Worthwhile visit
reviews.content: Fabulous sanctuary with great set up for the bears- so much effort put into the bear's enrichment, relationships and wellbeing.Unfortunately we arrived too early for the guided tour, but the skydeck had great installations and was very informative.The park is being expanded and is definately worth the visit.Great shop and cafe too.

reviews.author: James O
reviews.title: Worthy cause we'll worth a half day visit
reviews.content: This sanctuary is little known and about 30 km fron Tam Coc with a number of separate compounds housing a varying number of bears.There are 2 options available for viewing the bears, both of which include a skywalk and the more expensive tour (only an extra $4), includes a walk on the service roads around the compounds, which may or may not increase your viewing chances.Both trips commence with an educational talk and finish with a video of the work the sanctuary does.Obviously, how many bears you see and how close you get to the bears is at the will of the bears themselves. However, planning your visit around one of the 3 daily feeding times increases your chances of some interaction,  09.00, 13.00, and 16.00.There were a number of families visiting during our time there, and the children seemed very excited.It's a worthy cause well worth a half day visit with all  the moneyspent going directly to the care of the bears.

reviews.author: HJ
reviews.title: A great cause and 1/2 day trip
reviews.content: We had a lovely visit to the bear sanctuary, it's a little out of the way and not very well known but it is worth the trip to support such a good cause and see the bears happy and healthy. We did the immersive tour and would recommend it, you visit the sky walk and watch the bears as well as having a private tour closer to the spacious enclosures whilst learning about the charity and why it is needed and how they help. It finishes with a film about the sanctuary.

reviews.author: Davies A
reviews.title: Worth half a day trip
reviews.content: The place is not very big with many activities but worth a visit, and make sure you chose a guided tour so you can see bears on the way. At first they suggest us it's free to walk to their glass bridges to find bear, but I feel grateful that we chose a guide trip, or else we won't know which area to look for bear on the bridge. The guide provide a lot of knowledge and we saw lots of bear on the way so it was a successful. Also don't forget to buy some souvenir to support their organisation helping more unfortunate creatures like these.

reviews.author: Lynn W
reviews.title: Save the Bears
reviews.content: Very well run Sanctuary.Well run, good tour & information. So sad what us humans have done & still do to the beautiful animals of this planet. These Sanctuaries save as many as they can, to at least give them a safe & well looked after rest of their life after such torture.Very important to support these Sanctuaries & learn from our old bad ways & stop it happening in the future.

reviews.author: Claire H
reviews.title: A place to visit if you care about animals.
reviews.content: A place where rescued bears can live out their lives in peace and happiness. It’s a lovely place to see and learn about how they are being rescued. It is however, also very difficult to hear about the stories of their captivity but I saw this as a way to engage with the issue and provide funds to them directly once I’m back home. It’s operated by Four Paws registered charity and the quality input is evident. I just wish all the bears could be freed!

reviews.author: Pamela B
reviews.title: Fascinating yet sad visit
reviews.content: Amazing place where staff are totally dedicated to the care of the bears rescued from bile farms.  Definitely worth booking in advance for the full visit which lasts around 2 hours then after that you are free to spend as long as you want there. We felt we could have stayed all day but stayed around three and half hours. Probably best done on your own with scooter or a driver then you can stay as long as you want

reviews.author: Valerie S
reviews.title: Very impressive rescue facility for Asian bears
reviews.content: I did not know much about the bear bile trade before my husband and I went to this incredible place in Ninh Binh for rescued bears. I highly recommend going on a guided tour to get to see the bears up close. The tour was very informative and I couldn’t help, but cry for those bears still suffering on bear bile farms. I bought as many awesome items from the gift shop that I could fit into my luggage. I will continue to support the Four Paws animal organization now that I’ve returned home and was able to look up all the great work they have done already to help animals around the world. Look forward to following Four Paws online to see what they accomplish next!

reviews.author: Sue V
reviews.title: Support the work of this great place
reviews.content: We took a guided tour, which was very informative and interesting. The cruel treatment these animals have suffered is heart breaking. But the enclosures they live in now are top rate and their treatment excellent. We were very happy to be supporting this charity.

reviews.author: Kaz
reviews.title: An organisation doing fantastic work
reviews.content: Did the tour learning about these poor bears and where they have come from.  This organisation are doing amazing work and the bears are really well cared for.  A worthwhile experience to learn about them.  We had a lovely lunch there and bought a few things from the gift shop, proceeds going to the bears

reviews.author: sixpence04
reviews.title: A beautiful experience. Must visit!
reviews.content: One of the biggest highlights of our trip to Vietnam! These bears have been through heartbreaking things and are now being cared for so beautifully. You can tell the staff really do care. Definitely do the guided tour to learn more and see these gorgeous animals up close. The cafe also has some lovely options. You absolutely have to visit if you're in the area!

reviews.author: Anna C
reviews.title: Impressive sanctuary doing great work!
reviews.content: Great to visit, enlightening, Vietnam is very proactive and the care of the rescued bears is admirable, now if only China & South Korea will ban it too.

reviews.author: Pippa
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: An amazing place doing amazing work. So glad we decided to come and visit the sanctuary, you can really see how much the staff care for the bears. We did the immersive experience which I'd highly recommend as we got to see quite a few of the bears even though it was a very hot day. Definitely a must do if you are visiting Ninh Binh

reviews.author: Jan M
reviews.title: Bear visit on a wet day.
reviews.content: On a rainy day we decided to visit the bear sanctuary, it was well worth it and we saw quite a few bears. They are doing a great job there.

reviews.author: Anne M
reviews.title: Great afternoon out
reviews.content: Great experience, learn about how they rescue bears and take care of them. Staff are friendly and welcoming and willing to share knowledge about what they do. Bears are fed around 1pm so good to time for that

reviews.author: Inspire40202899371
reviews.title: Incredible Experience and Must Do in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Incredible experience and so uplifting to see all of the hard work they are doing and the thoughtfulness they put into the enclosures and the day to day lives of the bears to give them enrichment and a better life.

reviews.author: Laura L
reviews.title: An extraordinary experience, to do absolutely!
reviews.content: A wonderful experience, it was very exciting visit this center and see with how much love and dedication these suffering animals are cared for and protected. I chose the "immerse" program in order to have a complete information about this activity. The ideal time of visit is 9 am, book before you go. The center is a bit isolated and there are no buses, from Ninh Binh you can reach in an hour by taxi.agree with the driver also the return because you will not find transport in that area.

reviews.author: MathildaS
reviews.title: Recommended. Should not be missing from the Vietnam trip!
reviews.content: The facility was very professional, the leadership great. Definitely worth a visit even with children. Keep it up!!!

reviews.author: Antonia
reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.content: This is an amazing sanctuary! The bears have a lot of space and are very well taken care of. You can really tell all the love and affection the staff has for them. You get a great view of the bears from the Skywalk, but if you want more information and support the sanctuary even more, I highly recommend booking the guided tour for 250.000 VD. You can just book the tour when you arrive, no need to book it in advance. The best time to see them is after they had their food (8am, 1pm, and in the evening) There is also a nice vegetarian bistro onsite for a delicious snack.Thank you to the lovely staff for giving these bears a new life!

reviews.author: Bauerin
reviews.title: The bears' past gets under their skin
reviews.content: We had booked a tour for the late morning and a good English speaking lady told us about the bears whose background can impart a lot of knowledge.Because of the heat we hardly saw bears, but for us the visit was worth it. The bears have a terrible past and are cared for here in very large natural enclosures.Finally, there was a movie to watch.Something is really being done here for animal welfare by Western standards, and a visit helps maintain the station.Card payment is possible and a vegetarian restaurant is also on site.

reviews.author: tomerw94
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: We took the guided tour and the lady explained us widely about the place and answered our questions. She and the rest of the staff were nice and easy the understand.It seem like they really give the bears the best condition possible. We been there on a day woth good weather. They can give you umbrellas for the tour if you need.We were lucky to see many bears from a short distance through the fence. At 1 place we saw 8 of them at the same time, but we were told it is considered really lucky.

reviews.author: Navigate544160
reviews.title: Great place - make time to visit
reviews.content: We visited July 24 after reading reviews on TripAdvisor and so glad we did, this is a beautiful place, spotlessly clean and well maintained doing great work for the 45 bears they have rescued. Lovely staff who are really knowledgeable about the bears and the bile trade. We are so glad we came to visit and see the work Four Paws is doing here.

reviews.author: Trail56165823723
reviews.title: A true sanctuary for these beautiful bears
reviews.content: This is a true sanctuary. You can feel the love and care for these bears from all of the staff. Their work and advocacy for protecting bears from bile farming is inspiring. The skywalk is an incredible way to view the enclosures - with the enclosures so big it can be hard to spot the bears. I recommend doing the full guided tour for behind the scenes viewing and different angles to view the enclosures and bears. Come later in the day when it’s not so hot for the bears or they’ll mostly be hiding in the bushes and hard to see

reviews.author: bobby
reviews.title: Life changing experience
reviews.content: We visited a bear sanctuary 🐻 which I have to say is the most ethical sanctuary I’ve ever been to. The list of rules and regulations were long and rightly so, in fact it was a privilege and not a given right to see any bears at all. No loud noises. No calling their names. No strong fragrances.No touching the fences. The lists went on, and I couldn’t have been happier for it. The enclosures are built for them and their comfort not tourists and bratty children smashing on glass walls that you’d typically see at a zoo. In fact out of 47 bears we only managed to see 3 as they roam freely as they please. The footage and facts we were shown on each bear was absolutely heart breaking, in fact I cried so hard a volunteer even offered me a hug.  Honestly if you have the chance to go. GO and support the work they do

reviews.author: Daydream4444
reviews.title: Beautiful sanctuary
reviews.content: Such a wonderful place for the bears with a cruel, sad past. The Sanctuary is has quite great enclosures. The bears are doing very well.
